For then, <s>Brahman</s> and the knowledge of it would not qualify as the subject-matter and purpose [respectively], because of the impossibility of establishing the authoritativeness of the <s>Vedānta</s>s for such a meaning, due to the contradiction with the ego-cognition that has not been superimposed [upon the self]. Or [alternatively], there would be the possibility that [the <s>Vedānta</s> texts] would be grasped through the injunction of self-study — like [texts] with figurative meanings serving the purpose of <s>karma</s>-engagement, or like those serving the purpose of recitation (<s>japa</s>), or like [syllables such as] '<s>hum</s>' etc. whose meanings are not intended — even though their meanings are not intended. Therefore, '<s>jijñāsā</s>' — which indicates doubt and purpose — is to be intended here as primary, both from the individual words and from the sentence [as a whole]. And it is not something to be commenced, because it is not being proposed [as a topic]. Hence the word '<s>atha</s>' combined with it would not be in the sense of commencement. However, the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, which qualifies '<s>jijñāsā</s>,' could be [something] commenced. But even that is not connected with the word '<s>atha</s>,' due to its non-primacy. And '<s>jijñāsā</s>' is not [identical to] '<s>mīmāṃsā</s>' (inquiry), such that it would be commenced like [the topic in] '<s>atha yogānuśāsanam</s>.' For the word '<s>mīmāṃsā</s>,' derived — with the desiderative suffix in the sense of non-desire, through [the rule] '<s>mān-bandha-</s>' etc. — from either the root '<s>māṅ māne</s>' (to measure) or '<s>māna-pūjāyām</s>' (to honor), ending in [the suffix] '<s>anta</s>,' denotes revered inquiry; whereas the word '<s>jijñāsā</s>' denotes the desire for knowledge. For '<s>jijñāsā</s>' would be the motivator toward '<s>mīmāṃsā</s>.' And there is no identity between the thing motivated and the motivator, since, if they were one, that relation would be impossible. And when a self-referential interpretation is possible, the assumption of a reference to something else is not justified, due to the absurd consequence of over-extension. Therefore, it is well said: 'because <s>jijñāsā</s> is not something to be commenced.'

body.text:
atha maṅgalārtho 'thaśabdaḥ kasmānna bhavati ? tathā ca maṅgalahetutvāt pratyahaṃ brahmajijñāsā kartavyeti sūtrārthaḥ saṃpadyata ityata āha- maṅgalasya ca vākyārthe samanvayābhāvāt /
padārtha eva hi vākyārthe samanvīyate, sa ca vācyo lakṣyo vā /
na ceha maṅgalamathaśabdasya vācyaṃ vā lakṣyaṃ vā, kiṃ tu mṛdaṅgaśaṅkhadhvanivadathaśabdaśravaṇamātrakāryam /
na ca kāryajñāpyayorvākyārthe samanvayaḥ śabdavyavahāre dṛṣṭa ityarthaḥ /
tatkimidānīṃ maṅgalārtho 'śabdaḥ teṣu teṣu na prayoktavyaḥ ? tathā ca oṅkāraścāthaśabdaśca dvāvetau brahmaṇaḥ purā /
body.translated_text: Why should the word '<s>atha</s>' not be in the sense of auspiciousness (<s>maṅgala</s>)? And if so, the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> would be: 'The desire to know <s>Brahman</s> should be undertaken daily because it is a cause of auspiciousness.' To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Because there is no syntactic connection (<s>samanvaya</s>) of auspiciousness with the sentence-meaning.' For only a word-meaning is syntactically connected with the sentence-meaning, and that [word-meaning] is either denotative (<s>vācya</s>) or indicative (<s>lakṣya</s>). And here, auspiciousness is neither the denotative nor the indicative meaning of the word '<s>atha</s>'; rather, [the auspiciousness is] merely the effect of hearing the word '<s>atha</s>' — like the sound of a drum or a conch. And in linguistic usage, no syntactic connection of cause and effect is observed in the sentence-meaning — this is the point. Then should the word '<s>atha</s>' in the sense of auspiciousness not be used in those [contexts] at all? And thus [there is the verse]: 'The syllable <s>Oṃ</s> and the word <s>atha</s> — these two, in ancient times, from <s>Brahman</s>,

body.text: kaṇṭhaṃ bhittvā viniryātau tasmānmāṅgalikāvubhau //
body.translated_text: Burst forth, splitting the throat — therefore both are auspicious.' //

body.text:
iti smṛtivyākopa ityata āha- arthāntaraprayukta eva hyathaśabdaḥ śrutyā maṅgalaprayojano bhavati /
arthāntareṣvānantaryādiṣu prayuktaḥ athaśabdaḥ śrutyā śravaṇamātreṇa veṇuvīṇādhvanivanmaṅgalaṃ kurvan maṅgalaprayojano bhavati anyārthamānīyamānodakumbhadarśanavat /
tena na smṛtivyākopaḥ /
tena ca iha ānantaryārthasya sataḥ śravaṇamātreṇa maṅgalārthatetyarthaḥ /
body.translated_text: Would this not contradict the <s>Smṛti</s> (traditional text)? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'For the word <s>atha</s>, employed in another meaning, becomes auspicious in purpose by mere hearing (<s>śruti</s>).' The word '<s>atha</s>,' employed in other meanings such as sequence etc., by mere hearing — like the sound of a flute or a <s>vīṇā</s> — produces auspiciousness and thus becomes auspicious in purpose, like the sight of a water-pot brought for another purpose. Therefore there is no contradiction with <s>Smṛti</s>. And thereby, [the point] here is that [the word '<s>atha</s>'], having the meaning of sequence, becomes auspicious by mere hearing — this is the meaning.

body.text:
syādetat /
pūrvaprakṛtāpekṣo 'thaśabdo bhaviṣyati vinaivānantaryārthatvam /
tadyathā- iyamevāthaśabdaṃ prakṛtya vimṛśyate 'kimayamathaśabda ānantarye athādhikāre' iti /
atra vimarśakavākye 'thaśabdaḥ pūrvaprakṛtamathaśabdamapekṣya prathamapakṣopanyāsapūrvakaṃ pakṣāntaropanyāse /
na cāsyānantaryamarthaḥ, pūrvaprakṛtasya prathamapakṣopanyāsena vyavāyāt /
na ca prakṛtānapekṣā, tadanapekṣasya tadviṣayatvābhāvena asamānaviṣayatayā vikalpānupapatteḥ /
na hi jātu bhavati- kiṃ nitya ātmā, atha anityā buddhiriti /
tasmādānantaryaṃ vinā pūrvaprakṛtāpekṣa ihāthaśabdaḥ kasmānna bhavatītyata āha-
body.translated_text: One might say this: the word '<s>atha</s>' will be taken as referring to something previously mentioned, without having the meaning of sequence at all. For instance: this very word '<s>atha</s>' is being deliberated upon — 'Is this word <s>atha</s> in the sense of sequence, or of commencement?' In this deliberative sentence, the word '<s>atha</s>' refers to the previously mentioned [word] '<s>atha</s>' and introduces an alternative position after the presentation of the first position. And its meaning is not sequence, because of the intervening first-position-presentation separating it from what was previously mentioned. Nor is there non-reference to what was previously mentioned, for without such reference, [the deliberation] would lack a common subject-matter and the alternatives would be impossible. For indeed, [a disjunction like] 'Is the self eternal, or is the intellect impermanent?' never occurs. Therefore, why should the word '<s>atha</s>' here not refer to something previously mentioned, without [having] the meaning of sequence? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says —

body.text:
pūrvaprakṛtāpekṣāyāśca phalata ānantaryāvyatirekāt /
asyārthaḥ- na vayamānantaryārthatāṃ vyasanitayā rocayāmahe, kiṃ tu brahmajijñāsāhetubhūtapūrvaprakṛtasiddhaye /
sā ca pūrvaprakṛtārthāpekṣatve 'pyathaśabdasya sidhyatīti vyartha ānantaryārthatvāvadhāraṇāgraho 'smākamiti /
tadidamuktam 'phalataḥ' iti /
paramārthatastu kalpāntaropanyāse pūrvaprakṛtāpekṣā ; na ceha kalpāntaropanyāsa iti pāriśeṣyādānantaryārtha eveti yuktam /
body.translated_text: 'Because the reference to something previously mentioned does not differ in result from sequence.' The meaning of this is: we do not favor the sense of sequence out of obsession; rather, [we hold it] for the sake of establishing what was previously done (<s>pūrvakṛta</s>) that is the cause of the desire to know <s>Brahman</s>. And that [establishment] is achieved even if the word '<s>atha</s>' merely refers to something previously mentioned — thus, our insistence on establishing the meaning of sequence is pointless. This is what is stated by 'in result' (<s>phalataḥ</s>). In ultimate truth, however, reference to something previously mentioned [occurs when there is] the introduction of an alternative; and here there is no introduction of an alternative — so by elimination, the meaning of sequence alone is appropriate.

body.text:
bhavatvānantaryārthaḥ, kimevaṃ satītyata āha- sati cānantaryārthatva iti /
na tāvadyasya kasyacidatrānantaryam iti vaktavyam, tasyābhidhānamantareṇāpi prāptatvāt /
avaśyaṃ hi puruṣaḥ kiñcitkṛtvā kiñcitkaroti /
na cānantaryamātrasya dṛṣṭamadṛṣṭaṃ vā prayojanaṃ paśyāmaḥ /
tasmāttasyātrānantaryaṃ vaktavyaṃ yadvinā brahmajijñāsā na bhavati, yasminsati tu bhavantī bhavatyeva /
tadidamuktam- yatpūrvavṛttaṃ niyamenāpekṣata iti /
body.translated_text: Let it be in the sense of sequence — what follows from this? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Given the sense of sequence' etc. First, one should not say 'sequence to just anything,' since that would be obtained even without stating it. For necessarily a person does something after having done something else. And we do not see any seen or unseen purpose in mere sequence [to anything]. Therefore, the sequence stated here must be to that without which the desire to know <s>Brahman</s> does not arise, and given which it does arise — it necessarily arises. This is what is stated: 'that which, having occurred prior, is necessarily required [by it].'

body.text:
syādetat /
dharmajijñāsāyā iva brahmajijñāsāyā api yogyatvāt svādhyāyādhyayanānantaryam, dharmavadbrahmaṇo 'pyāmnāyaikapramāṇagamyatvāt /
tasya cāgṛhītasya svaviṣaye vijñānājananāt, grahaṇasya ca 'svādhyāyo 'dhyetavyaḥ' ityadhyayanenaiva niyatatvāt /
tasmādvedādhyayanānantaryameva brahmajijñāsāyā apyathaśabdārtha ityata āha- svādhyāyānantaryaṃ tu samānaṃ dharmabrahmajijñāsayoḥ /
atra ca svādhyāyena viṣayeṇa tadviṣayamadhyayanaṃ lakṣayati /
tathā ca 'athāto dharmajijñāsā' ityanenaiva gatamiti nedaṃ sūtramārabdhavyam ; dharmaśabdasya vedārthamātropalakṣaṇatayā dharmavadbrahmaṇo 'pi vedārthatvāviśeṣeṇa vedādhyayanānantaryopadeśasāmyādityarthaḥ /
body.translated_text: One might say this: Just as for the desire to know <s>dharma</s>, so too for the desire to know <s>Brahman</s>, the sequence should be to the study of the <s>Veda</s> (<s>svādhyāya-adhyayana</s>), since — like <s>dharma</s> — <s>Brahman</s> too is knowable only through scripture (<s>āmnāya</s>) as the sole means of knowledge. And without that [scripture] being grasped, it cannot produce knowledge regarding its own subject-matter; and the grasping [of scripture] is determined solely by the study [enjoined] in '<s>svādhyāyo 'dhyetavyaḥ</s>' (the <s>Veda</s> is to be studied). Therefore, the meaning of the word '<s>atha</s>' for the desire to know <s>Brahman</s> too should be nothing but sequence to <s>Vedic</s> study. To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'But the sequence to <s>Vedic</s> study is common to both the desire to know <s>dharma</s> and the desire to know <s>Brahman</s>.' And here, by '<s>svādhyāya</s>' (self-study) as the qualifier, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] indicates the study that has it as its object. And thus [the point is:] since this is already conveyed by '<s>athāto dharmajijñāsā</s>' (now, therefore, the desire to know <s>dharma</s>), this <s>sūtra</s> need not have been commenced [if that were its meaning] — since the word '<s>dharma</s>,' being indicative of the entire meaning of the <s>Veda</s>, and since <s>Brahman</s> too, like <s>dharma</s>, is equally a Vedic meaning, the instruction of sequence to Vedic study would be the same [for both] — this is the meaning.

body.text:
codayati - nanviha karmāvabodhānantaryaṃ viśeṣaḥ dharmajijñāsāto brahmajijñāsāyāḥ /
asyārthaḥ- 'vividiṣanti yajñena' iti tṛtīyāśrutyā yajñādīnāmaṅgatvena brahmajñāne viniyogāt, jñānasyaiva karmatayā icchāṃ prati prādhānyāt, pradhānasaṃbandhāccāpradhānānāṃ padārthāntarāṇām /
tatrāpi ca na vākyārthajñānotpattāvaṅgabhāvo yajñādīnām, vākyārthajñānasya vākyādevotpatteḥ /
na ca vākyaṃ sahakāritayā karmāṇyapekṣata iti yuktam ; akṛtakarmaṇāmapi viditapadapadārthasaṃbandhānāṃ samadhigataśābdanyāyatattvānāṃ guṇapradhānabhūtapūrvāparapadārthākāṅkṣāsaṃnidhiyogyatānusaṃdhānavatāmapratyūhaṃ vākyārthapratyayotpatteḥ /
anutpattau vā vidhiniṣedhavākyārthapratyayābhāvena tadarthānuṣṭhānaparivarjanābhāvaprasaṅgaḥ /
tadbodhatastu tadarthānuṣṭhānaparivarjane parasparāśrayaḥ, tasmin sati tadarthānuṣṭhānaparivarjanaṃ tataśca tadbodha iti /
na ca vedāntavākyānāmeva svārthapratyāyane karmāpekṣā na vākyāntarāṇāmiti sāṃpratam, viśeṣahetoḥ abhāvāt /
body.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises [this objection]: 'But here, the distinguishing feature of the desire to know <s>Brahman</s> from the desire to know <s>dharma</s> is the sequence to the understanding of <s>karma</s> (ritual action).' The meaning of this is: since, by the third-case <s>Śruti</s> '<s>vividiṣanti yajñena</s>' (they desire to know through sacrifice), sacrifices and the like are enjoined as accessories (<s>aṅga</s>) to the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>; and since knowledge itself, being a [form of] action, has primacy with respect to desire; and since subsidiary things — other word-meanings — [derive significance] from their connection with the principal. And therein, it is not [the case] that the sacrifices and the like serve as accessories to the arising of the knowledge of the sentence-meaning, since the knowledge of sentence-meaning arises from the sentence itself. Nor is it reasonable that the sentence requires actions as auxiliaries. For even those who have not performed [ritual] actions — but who know the meanings of words and their connections, who have understood the principles of scriptural reasoning, and who investigate the mutual expectancy, proximity, and fitness of principal and subsidiary word-meanings — experience the arising of the knowledge of sentence-meaning without obstruction. Or alternatively, if [knowledge of sentence-meaning] did not arise [without ritual action], then — due to the absence of understanding the meaning of injunctive and prohibitive sentences — there would be the absurd consequence that their corresponding performance and avoidance would not occur. But if [one claims that understanding] comes from that [ritual performance], while the performance and avoidance of its meaning [comes from understanding], there would be mutual dependence — understanding depending on performance, and performance depending on understanding. Nor is it reasonable [to say] that only <s>Vedānta</s> sentences require action for conveying their own meaning, while other sentences do not — due to the absence of a distinguishing reason.

body.text:
nanu 'tattvamasi' iti vākyāt tvaṃpadārthasya kartṛbhoktṛrūpasya jīvātmano nityaśuddhabuddhodāsīnasvabhāvena tatpadārthena paramātmanaikyamaśakyaṃ drāgityeva pratipattuṃ āpātato 'śuddhasattvaiḥ, yogyatāvirahaviniścayāt /
yajñadānatapo 'nāśakatanūkṛtāntarmalāstu viśuddhasattvāḥ śraddadhānāyogyatāvagamapuraḥsaraṃ tādātmyamavagamiṣyantīti cet, tatkimidānīṃ pramāṇakāraṇaṃ yogyatāvadhāraṇamapramāṇātkarmaṇo vaktumadhyavasito 'si, pratyakṣādyatiriktaṃ vā karmāpi pramāṇam /
vedāntāviruddhatanmūlanyāyabalena tu yogyatāvadhāraṇe kṛtaṃ karmabhiḥ /
tasmāt 'tattvamasi' ityādeḥ śrutamayena jñānena jīvātmanaḥ paramātmabhāvaṃ gṛhītvā, tanmūlayā copapattyā vyavasthāpya, tadupāsanāyāṃ bhāvanāparābhidhānāyāṃ dīrghakālanairantaryavatyāṃ brahmasākṣātkāraphalāyāṃ yajñādīnāmupayogaḥ /
yathāhuḥ- 'sa tu dīrdhakālanairantaryasatkārāsevito dṛḍhabhūmiḥ' iti /
brahmacaryatapaḥśraddhāyajñādayaśca satkārāḥ /
ata eva śrutiḥ- 'tameva dhīro vijñāya prajñāṃ kurvīta brāhmaṇaḥ' /
iti /
vijñāya tarkopakaraṇena śabdena prajñāṃ bhāvanāṃ kurvītetyarthaḥ /
atra ca yajñādīnāṃ śreyaḥparipanthikalmaṣanibarhaṇadvāreṇopayoga iti kecit /
puruṣasaṃskāradvāreṇetyanye /
yajñādisaṃskṛto hi puruṣaḥ ādaranairantaryadīrghakālairāsevamāno brahmabhāvanāmanādyavidyāvāsanāṃ samūlakāṣaṃ kaṣati ; tato 'sya pratyagātmā suprasannaḥ kevalo viśadībhavati /
ata eva smṛtiḥ- 'mahāyajñaiśca yajñaiśca brāhmīyaṃ kriyate tanuḥ' /
iti, 'yasyaite 'ṣṭācatvāriṃśatsaṃskārāḥ' iti ca /
apare tu ṛṇatrayāpākaraṇena brahmajñānopayogaṃ karmaṇāmāhuḥ /
asti hi smṛtiḥ- 'ṛṇāni trīṇyapākṛtya mano mokṣe niveśayet' /
iti /
anye tu 'tametaṃ vedānuvacanena brāhmaṇā vividiṣanti yajñena' ityādiśrutibhyaḥ tattatphalāya coditānāmapi karmaṇāṃ saṃyogapṛthaktvena brahmabhāvanāṃ pratyaṅgabhāvamācakṣate, kratvarthasyeva khādiratvasya vīryārthatām, 'ekasya tūbhayārthatve saṃyogapṛthaktvam' iti nyāyāt /
ata eva pāramarṣaṃ sūtram 'sarvāpekṣā ca yajñādiśruteraśvavat' iti /
yajñatapodānādi sarvam, tadapekṣā brahmabhāvanetyarthaḥ /
tasmāt yadi śrutyādayaḥ pramāṇaṃ yadi vā pāramarṣaṃ sūtraṃ sarvathā yajñādikarmasamuccitā brahmopāsanā viśeṣaṇatrayavatī anādyavidyātadvāsanāsamucchedakrameṇa brahmasākṣātkārāya mokṣāparanāmne kalpata iti tadarthaṃ karmāṇyanuṣṭheyāni /
na caitāni dṛṣṭādṛṣṭasāmavāyikārādupakārahetubhūtaupadeśikātideśikakramaparyantāṅgagrāmasahitaparasparavibhinnakarmasvarūpatadadhikāribhedaparijñānaṃ vinā śakyānyanuṣṭhātum /
na ca dharmamīmāṃsāpariśīlanaṃ vinā tatparijñānam /
tasmātsādhūktam 'karmāvabodhānantaryaṃ viśeṣaḥ' iti /
karmāvabodhena hi karmānuṣṭhānasāhityaṃ bhavati brahmopāsanāyā ityarthaḥ /
body.translated_text:
One might object: From the sentence '<s>tattvamasi</s>' ('You are That'), the identity of the referent of 'you' — the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>) in the form of agent and enjoyer — with the referent of 'That' — the supreme Self (<s>paramātman</s>) whose nature is eternally pure, awakened, and dispassionate — cannot be immediately grasped by those of impure <s>sattva</s> (constitution), due to the ascertainment that they lack fitness.
But those of purified <s>sattva</s>, whose inner impurities have been attenuated by sacrifices, gifts, and austerities, with the faithful apprehension of fitness as the precondition, will comprehend the identity — if so, then is this ascertainment of fitness, which is the cause of valid cognition, something you are prepared to derive from action (<s>karman</s>), which is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge)? Or is action too a means of knowledge beyond perception and the like?
Rather, the ascertainment of fitness is accomplished by actions through the force of reasoning rooted in and not contradicting <s>Vedānta</s>.
Therefore, having grasped through knowledge consisting of hearing (<s>śrutamaya</s>) from [statements like] '<s>tattvamasi</s>' that the individual self has the nature of the supreme Self, and having established this through reasoning rooted therein, the utility of sacrifices and the like lies in the practice of meditation (<s>upāsanā</s>) — also called <s>bhāvanā</s> (contemplation) — which is continuous over a long period and which has as its fruit the direct realization (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>) of <s>Brahman</s>.
As they say: 'That [practice], cultivated with reverence, without interruption, over a long period, becomes firmly grounded.'
And <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy), austerity (<s>tapas</s>), faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), sacrifices, and the like are the marks of reverence.
Hence the <s>Śruti</s>: 'Having known That alone, the wise <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should cultivate wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>).'
The meaning is: 'having known' — through verbal testimony aided by reasoning — 'should cultivate wisdom,' that is, contemplation (<s>bhāvanā</s>).
In this regard, some hold that the utility of sacrifices and the like is through the removal of impurities that obstruct the highest good.
Others say it is through the refinement (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of the person.
For indeed, a person refined by sacrifices and the like, cultivating the contemplation of <s>Brahman</s> with reverence, without interruption, and over a long period, uproots the beginningless impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>s) of <s>avidyā</s> completely from the root; thereupon, his innermost Self (<s>pratyagātman</s>) becomes supremely serene, isolated, and luminous.
Hence the <s>Smṛti</s>: 'Through great sacrifices and [ordinary] sacrifices, this body is made fit for <s>Brahman</s>.'
And: 'For one who has these forty-eight <s>saṃskāra</s>s...'
Still others speak of the utility of actions for <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge through the discharge of the three debts (<s>ṛṇatraya</s>).
For there is a <s>Smṛti</s>: 'Having discharged the three debts, one should fix the mind on liberation.'
Yet others, from <s>Śruti</s>s such as 'The <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s seek to know Him through Vedic recitation, through sacrifice,' etc., declare that even actions enjoined for their respective fruits, by the principle of <s>saṃyogapṛthaktva</s> (separation from conjunction), serve as auxiliaries (<s>aṅga</s>) to the contemplation of <s>Brahman</s> — just as the <s>khadira</s>-wood quality [of the sacrificial post], though serving the rite's purpose, also serves the purpose of strength — by the maxim: 'When a single [element] serves two purposes, there is separation from conjunction.'
Hence the aphoristic <s>sūtra</s> of [<s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>]: 'And the requirement of all [auxiliaries], because of the <s>Śruti</s> on sacrifice and the like — like a horse.'
'All' means sacrifices, austerities, gifts, and the like; the contemplation of <s>Brahman</s> requires them — this is the meaning.
Therefore, whether the <s>Śruti</s>s and the like are the <s>pramāṇa</s>, or the aphoristic <s>sūtra</s> [of <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>] — in every way, the meditation on <s>Brahman</s>, conjoined with sacrificial and other actions, endowed with the three qualifications [of reverence, continuity, and long duration], leading to the direct realization of <s>Brahman</s> — also called liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) — serves that end through the gradual eradication of beginningless <s>avidyā</s> and its impressions; and for that purpose, actions must be performed.
And these [actions] cannot be performed without knowledge of the distinct nature of each action, the distinctions among the persons qualified for them — encompassing the entire group of auxiliaries (<s>aṅga</s>) up to and including instructive and analogical sequences — [which are] mutually distinct actions with visible and invisible [results] combined as causes.
And without thorough study of <s>Dharma-mīmāṃsā</s>, that knowledge is not possible.
Therefore, it is well said: 'The distinguishing feature is [its] sequence after the comprehension of action (<s>karmāvabodha</s>).'
For through the comprehension of action, the performance of action becomes conjoined with the meditation on <s>Brahman</s> — this is the meaning.

body.text:
tadetannirākaroti- na iti /
kutaḥ ? karmāvabodhāt prāgapyadhītavedāntasya brahmajijñāsopapatteḥ /
body.translated_text:
He refutes this — 'No,' [he says].
Why? Because even before the comprehension of action, for one who has studied <s>Vedānta</s>, the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahmajijñāsā</s>) is appropriate.

body.text:
idamatrākūtam- brahmopāsanayā bhāvanāparābhidhānayā karmāṇyapekṣyanta ityuktam /
tatra brūmaḥ- kva punarasyāḥ karmāpekṣā ? kiṃ kārye yathāgneyādīnāṃ paramāpūrve cirabhāviphalānukūle janayitavye samidādyapekṣā ? svarūpe vā yathā teṣāmeva dviravattapuroḍāśādidravyāgnidevatādyapekṣā ? na tāvatkārye, tasya vikalpāsahatvāt /
tathā hi- brahmopāsanāyā brahmasvarūpasākṣātkāraḥ kāryamabhyupeyaḥ /
sa cotpādyo vā syāt yathā saṃyavanasya piṇḍaḥ, vikāryo vā yathāvaghātasya vrīhayaḥ, saṃskāryo vā yathā prokṣaṇasyolūkhalādayaḥ, prāpyo vā yathā dohanasya payaḥ /
na tāvadutpādyaḥ /
na khalu ghaṭādisākṣātkāra iva jaḍasvabhāvebhyo ghaṭādibhyo bhinna indriyādyādheyo brahmasākṣātkāro bhāvanādheyaḥ saṃbhavati, brahmaṇo 'parādhīnaprakāśatayā tatsākṣātkārasya tatsvabhāvyena nityatayotpādyatvānupapatteḥ /
tato bhinnasya vā bhāvanādheyasya sākṣātkārasya pratibhāpratyayavat saṃśayākrāntatayā prāmāṇyāyogāt, tadvidhasya tatsāmagrīkasyaiva bahulaṃ vyabhicāropalabdheḥ /
na khalu anumānāvagataṃ siddhaṃ vahniṃ bhāvayataḥ śītārtasya śiśirabharamantharatarakāyakāṇḍasya sphurajjvālājaṭilānalasākṣātkāraḥ pramāṇāntareṇa saṃvādyate, visaṃvādasya bahulamupalambhāt /
tasmāt prāmāṇikasākṣātkāralakṣaṇakāryābhāvānnopāsanāyā utpādye karmāpekṣā /
na ca kūṭasthanityasya sarvavyāpino brahmaṇa upāsanāto vikārasaṃskāraprāptayaḥ saṃbhavanti /
body.translated_text:
The intended purport here is this — it was said that the meditation on <s>Brahman</s>, also called <s>bhāvanā</s> (contemplation), requires actions as auxiliaries.
To this we say: Where exactly does this meditation require actions? Is it in the effect — just as the <s>āgneya</s> and other [rites] require fuel-sticks and the like for producing the ultimate unseen result (<s>apūrva</s>), whose fruit is long in coming? Or in [its] essential nature — just as those very [rites] require the two-rice-cake oblation (<s>dviravattapuroḍāśa</s>) and other materials, fire, deity, and the like?
Not in the effect, to begin with, since the effect does not admit of alternatives.
For thus: the effect of the meditation on <s>Brahman</s> must be accepted as the direct realization (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>) of the nature of <s>Brahman</s>.
And that [realization] would be either producible — like a lump [produced] from mixing; or modifiable — like rice-grains [from] threshing; or refinable — like the mortar and the like [from] sprinkling; or attainable — like milk [from] milking.
It is not producible, to begin with.
For indeed, the direct realization of <s>Brahman</s>, unlike the direct perception of a pot and the like, cannot possibly be something deposited by the senses and the like, distinct from the inert pot and the like, and then deposited by contemplation — since <s>Brahman</s>, being self-luminous and not dependent on anything else for its manifestation, its direct realization, being of the very nature of <s>Brahman</s>, is eternal and therefore cannot be produced.
Or, if a realization distinct from [<s>Brahman</s>] were to be deposited by contemplation, such a realization — like a flash of intuition (<s>pratibhā</s>) — would be vitiated by doubt and therefore unfit to be a valid cognition (<s>prāmāṇya</s>), since for [cognitions] of that type, produced by that same aggregate of causes, frequent deviation [from truth] is abundantly observed.
For indeed, the direct perception of fire by one who is cold and has inferred the established fire through inference, and is contemplating it — [this perception] in the form of blazing flames bristling with fire — is not corroborated by another means of knowledge, since discordance is abundantly observed.
Therefore, since the effect in the form of a valid direct realization does not exist, the meditation does not require actions for [producing] an effect.
Nor can modification, refinement, or attainment be possible for <s>Brahman</s>, which is immutably eternal (<s>kūṭastha-nitya</s>) and all-pervading, through meditation.

body.text:
syādetat /
mā bhūdbrahmasākṣātkāra utpādyādirūpa upāsanāyāḥ /
saṃskāryastu anirvacanīyāvidyādvayapidhānāpanayanena bhaviṣyati, pratisīrāpihitā nartakīva pratisīrāpanayadvārā raṅgavyāpṛtena /
tatra ca karmaṇāmupayogaḥ /
etāvāṃstu viśeṣaḥ- pratisīrāpanaye pāriṣadānāṃ nartakīviṣayaḥ sākṣātkāro bhavati /
iha tu avidyāpidhānāpanayamātrameva nāparamutpādyamasti, brahmasākṣātkārasya brahmasvabhāvasya nityatvena anutpādyatvāt /
atrocyate- kā punariyaṃ brahmopāsanā ? kiṃ śābdajñānamātrasaṃtatiḥ, āho nirvicikitsaśābdajñānasaṃtatiḥ ? yadi śābdajñānamātrasaṃtatiḥ, na tarhīyamabhyāsyamānāpyavidyāṃ samucchettumarhati /
tattvaviniścayastadabhyāso vā savāsanaṃ viparyāsamunmūlayet, na saṃśayābhyāsaḥ, sāmānyamātradarśanābhyāso vā /
na hi sthāṇurvā puruṣo veti vā, ārohapariṇāhavat dravyamiti vā śataśo 'pi jñānamabhyasyamānaṃ puruṣa eveti niścayāya paryāptam, ṛte viśeṣadarśanāt /
body.translated_text:
One might say this:
Let the direct realization of <s>Brahman</s> not be a producible or other such effect of meditation.
But it will be refinable — through the removal of the covering by the twofold indescribable (<s>anirvacanīya</s>) <s>avidyā</s> — like a dancer concealed behind a curtain, who [is revealed] through the removal of the curtain by one engaged in the theater.
And therein actions have their utility.
But there is this distinction: in the removal of the curtain, the spectators get a direct perception of the dancer as their object.
Here, however, the mere removal of the covering of <s>avidyā</s> alone [is the result], and nothing else is to be produced — since the direct realization of <s>Brahman</s>, being of the nature of <s>Brahman</s>, is eternal and therefore not producible.
To this we say: What, then, is this meditation on <s>Brahman</s>? Is it merely a continuity of verbal knowledge (<s>śābdajñāna</s>), or a continuity of doubt-free verbal knowledge? If it is merely a continuity of verbal knowledge, then even when repeatedly practiced, it cannot eradicate <s>avidyā</s>.
For the ascertainment of reality, or the repeated practice thereof, can uproot erroneous cognition along with its impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>s) — but not the repeated practice of doubt, nor the repeated practice of perceiving merely a general [characteristic].
For indeed, the cognition 'Is it a post or a person?' — or 'It is a substance possessing height and girth' — even if practiced a hundred times, is not sufficient for the certainty 'It is indeed a person,' without the perception of a distinguishing feature.

body.text:
nanūktaṃ śrutamayena jñānena jīvātmanaḥ paramātmabhāvaṃ gṛhītvā yuktimayena ca vyavasthāpyata iti /
tasmānnirvicikatsaśābdajñānasaṃtatirūpopāsanā karmasahakāriṇyavidyādvayocchedahetuḥ /
na cāsāvanutpāditabrahmānubhavā taducchedāya paryāptā /
sākṣātkārarūpo hi viparyāsaḥ sākṣātkārarūpeṇaiva tattvajñānenocchidyate, na tu parokṣāvabhāsena, diṅmohālātacakracaladvṛkṣamarumarīcisalilādivibhrameṣvaparokṣāvabhāsiṣu aparokṣāvabhāsibhireva digāditattvapratyayairnivṛttidarśanāt /
no khalvāptavacanaliṅgādiniścitadigāditattvānāṃ diṅmohādayo nivartante /
tasmāt tvaṃpadārthasya tatpadārthatvena sākṣātkāra eṣitavyaḥ /
etāvatā hi tvaṃpadārthasya duḥkhiśokitvādisākṣātkāranivṛttiḥ, nānyathā /
na caiṣa sākṣātkāro mīmāṃsāsahitasyāpi śabdapramāṇasya phalam, api tu pratyakṣasya, tasyaiva tatphalatvaniyamāt ; anyathā kuṭajabījādapi vaṭāṅkurotpattiprasaṅgāt /
tasmānnirvicikitsavākyārthabhāvanāparipākasahitamantaḥkaraṇaṃ tvaṃpadārthasyāparokṣasya tattadupādhyākāraniṣedhena tatpadārthatāmāvirbhāvayatīti yuktam /
na cāyamanubhavato brahmasvabhāvo yena na janyeta, api tu antaḥkaraṇasyaiva vṛttibhedo brahmaviṣayaḥ /
na caitāvatā brahmaṇo 'pi parādhīnaprakāśatā /
na hi śābdajñānaprakāśyaṃ brahma svayaṃ prakāśaṃ na bhavati /
sarvopādhivihīnaṃ hi svayañjyotiriti gīyate, na tūpahitamapi /
yathāha sma bhagavānbhāṣyakāraḥ- 'na tāvadayamekāntenāviṣayaḥ' iti /
na cāntaḥkaraṇavṛttāvapyasya sākṣātkāre sarvopādhivinirmokaḥ, tasyaiva tadupādhervinaśyadavasthasya svaparopādhivirodhino vidyamānatvāt /
anyathā caitanyacchāyāpattiṃ vināntaḥkaraṇavṛtteḥ svayamacetanāyāḥ svaprakāśatvānupapattau sākṣātkāratvāyogāt /
na cānumitabhāvitavahnisākṣātkāravat pratibhātvenāsyāprāmāṇyam, tatra vahnisvalakṣaṇasya parokṣatvāt /
iha tu brahmasvarūpasya upādhikaluṣitasya jīvasya prāgapyaparokṣatvāt /
na hi śuddhabuddhatvādayo vastutastato 'tiricyante /
jīva eva tu tattadupādhirahitaḥ śuddhabuddhatvādisvabhāvo brahmeti gīyate /
na ca tattadupādhiviraho 'pi tato 'tiricyate /
tasmāt yathā gāndharvaśāstrārthajñānābhyāsāhitasaṃskārasacivaḥ śrotrendriyeṇa ṣaḍjādisvaragrāmamūrchanābhedamadhyakṣamanubhavati, evaṃ vedāntārthajñānābhyāsāhitasaṃskāro jīvaḥ svasya brahmabhāvamantaḥkaraṇeneti /
body.translated_text:
One might say: It has been stated that through knowledge born of hearing, one grasps the individual self's nature as the supreme Self, and through reasoning, one establishes this.
Therefore, meditation in the form of a continuity of doubt-free verbal knowledge, together with action as its auxiliary, is the cause of the eradication of the twofold <s>avidyā</s>.
But that [meditation], without having produced the experience of <s>Brahman</s>, is not sufficient for its eradication.
For an error that has the form of direct perception is removed only by knowledge of reality that also has the form of direct perception, not by one that has a mediate appearance — since in the case of errors that appear as direct — such as directional confusion, the circle of a firebrand, the [apparently] moving tree, and the water of desert mirages — cessation is observed only through direct-appearing cognitions of the reality of direction and the like.
Certainly the errors of directional confusion and the like do not cease for those who have ascertained the reality of direction and the like through trustworthy testimony, inferential marks, and the like.
Therefore, the direct realization of the referent of 'you' (<s>tvaṃpadārtha</s>) as being the referent of 'That' (<s>tatpadārtha</s>) must be sought.
For only thereby is the cessation of the direct perception of the referent of 'you' as suffering, grieving, and the like [achieved] — not otherwise.
And this direct realization is not the fruit of verbal testimony (<s>śabdapramāṇa</s>) even when combined with [<s>Dharma</s>-]<s>mīmāṃsā</s>, but rather of perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), since there is a fixed rule that only perception yields such a fruit — otherwise, there would be the unwanted consequence that even from the seed of a <s>kuṭaja</s> tree, a banyan sprout could arise.
Therefore, it is reasonable that the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), endowed with the refinement (<s>saṃskāra</s>) produced by the maturation of the contemplation of the meaning of the [<s>Vedāntic</s>] sentence free from doubt, makes manifest the nature of the referent of 'you' — which is immediate (<s>aparokṣa</s>) — as being the referent of 'That,' through the negation of the forms of its various limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>s).
And this [realization] is not of the nature of <s>Brahman</s> in terms of being an experience, such that it could not be produced — rather, it is a modification (<s>vṛtti</s>) of the inner organ itself, having <s>Brahman</s> as its object.
Nor does this entail that <s>Brahman</s> too is dependent on another for its manifestation.
For <s>Brahman</s>, though made manifest by verbal knowledge, does not thereby cease to be self-luminous.
For it is celebrated that [<s>Brahman</s>] is self-luminous when free from all limiting adjuncts, but not when [associated with] limiting adjuncts.
As the revered commentator [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] has said: 'It is not that this [<s>Brahman</s>] is absolutely not an object [of knowledge].'
Nor, even in the direct realization occurring as a modification of the inner organ, is there complete freedom from all limiting adjuncts — since that very limiting adjunct [the inner organ], in its perishing state, conflicting with its own and others' limiting adjuncts, is still present.
Otherwise, without the reflection of consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>) falling upon it, the modification of the inner organ — being itself inert — could not be self-luminous, and thus could not be a direct realization.
Nor is this [realization] invalid like the direct perception of fire by one who has contemplated inferred fire — as if a mere intuition (<s>pratibhā</s>) — since in that case, the specific characteristic (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) of fire is mediate.
But here, the essential nature of <s>Brahman</s> — though tainted by limiting adjuncts as the individual self (<s>jīva</s>) — has been immediate (<s>aparokṣa</s>) even before.
For qualities such as being pure and awakened do not in reality differ from it.
The individual self itself, when free from its various limiting adjuncts, is celebrated as <s>Brahman</s>, having the nature of being pure, awakened, and the like.
Nor does the absence of those limiting adjuncts differ from it in reality.
Therefore, just as one who possesses the refinements produced by the practice of knowledge of the science of music (<s>gāndharvaśāstra</s>) directly perceives through the auditory sense the distinctions of scales (<s>mūrchanā</s>s) in the series of notes beginning with <s>ṣaḍja</s>, so too the individual self, possessing the refinements produced by the practice of knowledge of <s>Vedānta</s>, [perceives] its own nature as <s>Brahman</s> through the inner organ.

body.text:
antaḥkaraṇavṛttau brahmasākṣātkāre janayitavye asti tadupāsanāyāḥ karmāpekṣeti cet, na, tasyāḥ karmānuṣṭhānasahabhāvābhāvena tatsahakāritvānupapatteḥ /
na khalu 'tattvamasi' ityādervākyānnirvicikitsaṃ śuddhabuddhodāsīnasvabhāvaṃ akartṛtvādyupetaṃ apetabrāhmaṇatvādijātiṃ dehādyatiriktaṃ ekamātmānaṃ pratipadyamānaḥ karmasvadhikāramavaboddhumarhati /
anarhaśca kathaṃ kartā vādhikṛto vā /
body.translated_text:
If it be said that there is indeed a requirement of actions by that meditation for producing the direct realization of <s>Brahman</s> as a modification of the inner organ — no, because that meditation does not coexist with the performance of action, and therefore cannot have action as its auxiliary.
For indeed, one who, from sentences such as '<s>tattvamasi</s>' ('You are That'), comprehends without doubt the single Self — whose nature is pure, awakened, and dispassionate, endowed with non-agency and the like, transcending the body and the like, free from caste distinctions such as <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-hood — cannot recognize his own qualification for [performing ritual] action.
And how can one who is unable [to recognize his qualification] be an agent or one who is qualified?

body.text:
yadyucyeta niścite 'pi tattve viparyāsanibandhano vyavahāro 'nuvartamāno dṛśyate, yathā guḍasya mādhuryaviniścaye api pittopahatendriyāṇāṃ tiktatāvabhāsānuvṛttiḥ, āsvādya thūtkṛtya tyāgāt /
tasmādavidyāsaṃskārānuvṛttyā karmānuṣṭhānam, tena ca vidyāsahakāriṇā tatsamuccheda upapatsyate /
na ca- karmāvidyātmakaṃ kathamavidyāmucchinatti, karmaṇo vā taducchedakasya kuta ucchedaḥ iti vācyam, sajātīyasvaparavirodhināṃ bhāvānāṃ bahulamupalabdheḥ /
yathā payaḥ payo 'ntaraṃ jarayati svayaṃ ca jīryati, yathā viṣaṃ viṣāntaraṃ śamayati svayaṃ ca śāmyati, yathā vā katakarajo rajo 'ntarāvile pāthasi prakṣiptaṃ rajo 'ntarāṇi bhindat svayamapi bhidyamānamanāvilaṃ pāthaḥ karoti, evaṃ karmāvidyātmakamapi avidyāntarāṇyapagamayat svayamapyapagacchatīti /
body.translated_text: If it be said: even when reality has been ascertained, the transaction rooted in error is observed to continue — just as, even when the sweetness of jaggery has been ascertained, for those whose senses are afflicted by bile, the appearance of bitterness continues, since [they] taste [it], spit it out, and discard [it]. Therefore, through the continuity of the impressions of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), the performance of <s>karma</s> (ritual action) [continues]; and through that [karma], which is an auxiliary to <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), the complete eradication of that [<s>avidyā</s>] will be possible. Nor should it be objected: 'How can <s>karma</s>, which is of the nature of <s>avidyā</s>, eradicate <s>avidyā</s>? And whence the eradication of <s>karma</s>, which is [itself] the eradicator of that [<s>avidyā</s>]?' — because entities that conflict with their own kind, both themselves and others, are abundantly observed. Just as one [portion of] milk digests another milk and is itself digested; just as one poison neutralizes another poison and is itself neutralized; just as the powder of the <s>kataka</s> (clearing nut), when cast into water muddied by other impurities, breaks up the other impurities while itself being broken up, and thus makes the water clear — so too, <s>karma</s>, even though of the nature of <s>avidyā</s>, while removing other [forms of] <s>avidyā</s>, itself passes away.

body.text:
atrocyate- satyam ; 'sadeva somyedamagra āsīt' ityupakramāt 'tattvamasi' ityantācchabdādbrahmamīmāṃsopakaraṇādasakṛdabhyastānnirvicikitse 'nādyavidyopādānadehādyatiriktapratyagātmatattvāvabodhe jāte 'pi avidyāsaṃskārānuvṛttyānuvartante sāṃsārikāḥ pratyayāstadvyavahārāśca, tathāpi tānapyayaṃ vyavahārapratyayānmithyeti manyamāno vidvān ca śraddhatte, pittopahatendriya iva guḍaṃ thūtkṛtya tyajannapi tasya tiktatām /
tathā cāyaṃ kriyākartṛkaraṇetikartavyatāphalaprapañcamatāttvikaṃ viniścinvan kathamadhikṛto nāma ? viduṣo hyadhikāraḥ /
anyathā paśuśūdrādīnāmapi adhikāro durvāraḥ syāt /
kriyākartrādisvarūpavibhāgaṃ ca vidvasyamāna iha vidvānabhimataḥ karmakāṇḍe /
ata eva bhagavān avidvadviṣayatvaṃ śāstrasya varṇayāṃbabhūva bhāṣyakāraḥ /
tasmādyathā rājajātīyābhimānikartṛke rājasūye na vipravaiśyajātīyābhimāninoradhikāraḥ, evaṃ dvijātikartṛkriyākaraṇādivibhāgābhimānikartṛke karmaṇi na tadanabhimānino 'dhikāraḥ /
na cānadhikṛtena samarthenāpi kṛte vaidikaṃ karma phalāya kalpate, vaiśyastoma iva brāhmaṇarājanyābhyām /
tena dṛṣṭārtheṣu karmasu śaktaḥ pravartamānaḥ prāpnotu phalam, dṛṣṭatvāt /
adṛṣṭārtheṣu tu śāstraikasamadhigamyaṃ phalamanadhikāriṇi na yujyata iti nopāsanākārye karmāpekṣā /
body.translated_text: To this we reply: True. Even when, from the scriptural statement beginning with '<s>sadeva somyedamagra āsīt</s>' (In the beginning, dear one, this was Being alone) and ending with '<s>tattvamasi</s>' (You are That) — the instrument of <s>Brahmamīmāṃsā</s> — repeatedly practiced, the unwavering realization of the true nature of the innermost Self (<s>pratyagātman</s>) as distinct from the body and the like — which are the products of beginningless <s>avidyā</s> — has arisen, the <s>saṃsāric</s> cognitions and their corresponding transactions continue through the persistence of the impressions of <s>avidyā</s>. Nevertheless, the wise person, who considers even those transactional cognitions to be false, [merely] acknowledges them — just as one whose senses are afflicted by bile, even while spitting out and discarding the jaggery, [acknowledges] its bitterness. And thus, this [wise person], who ascertains the entire elaboration of action, agent, instrument, procedure, and result as non-ultimate — how can he be called qualified [for ritual action]? For the qualification belongs to the knower (<s>viduṣaḥ</s>). Otherwise, the qualification even of animals, <s>Śūdra</s>s, and the like would be impossible to prevent. And the one who is considered a 'knower' in the <s>Karmakāṇḍa</s> (ritual portion of the <s>Veda</s>) is one who is in the process of knowing the essential distinction of action, agent, and the like. For this very reason, the revered commentator (<s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>) described the <s>śāstra</s> (scripture) as having for its domain the non-knower. Therefore, just as in the <s>Rājasūya</s> sacrifice — which requires an agent who identifies himself as of royal lineage — one who identifies himself as of <s>brāhmaṇa</s> or <s>vaiśya</s> lineage has no qualification, so too, in ritual action — which requires an agent who identifies with the distinctions of twice-born status, action, and instrument — one who does not hold such identification has no qualification. And Vedic <s>karma</s>, even if performed by an unqualified but capable person, does not yield fruit — like the <s>Vaiśyastoma</s> [sacrifice performed] by <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s or <s>kṣatriya</s>s. Therefore, let one who is capable engage in actions that have visible results and obtain the fruit, since it is visible. But for actions with invisible results, the fruit — which is knowable only through scripture — is not appropriate for one who is unqualified. Hence there is no dependence on <s>karma</s> for the purpose of meditation (<s>upāsanā</s>).

body.text:
syādetat /
manuṣyābhimānavadadhikārike karmaṇi vihite yathā tadabhimānarahitasyānadhikāraḥ, evaṃ niṣedhavidhayo 'pi manuṣyādhikārā iti tadabhimānarahitasteṣvapi nādhikriyeta paśvādivat ; tathā cāyaṃ niṣiddhamanutiṣṭhan na pratyaveyāt tiryagādivaditi bhinnakarmatāpātaḥ /
maivam /
na khalvayaṃ sarvathā manuṣyābhimānarahitaḥ, kiṃ tvavidyāsaṃskārānuvṛttyāsya mātrayā tadabhimāno 'nuvartate /
anuvartamānaṃ ca mithyeti manyamāno na śraddhatta ityuktam /
kimato yadyevam ? etadato bhavati- vidhiṣu śrāddho 'dhikārī nāśrāddhaḥ /
tataśca manuṣyādyabhimāne naśraddhadhāno na vidhiśāstreṣvadhikriyate /
tathā ca smṛtiḥ-
body.translated_text: One might say this: Just as in ritual action that is enjoined for one who identifies as a human being, one who lacks such identification has no qualification — so too, injunctive and prohibitive [statements] are also qualified for human beings, and therefore one who lacks such identification would not be qualified for them either, like an animal. And thus, this [person], performing what is prohibited and not [performing what is enjoined], would not suffer the consequences — like an animal. And so there would be the unwanted consequence of heterodox conduct (<s>bhinnakarmatā</s>). Not so! For this [knower] is not entirely devoid of the identification as a human being; rather, through the persistence of the impressions of <s>avidyā</s>, a measure of that identification continues. And it has been said that the [knower], though the identification continues, considers it false and does not put faith in it. What of it, if this is so? From this it follows: for injunctions, the qualified person is one who has faith (<s>śrāddha</s>), not one who lacks faith. Consequently, one who does not have faith in the identification as a human being and the like is not qualified for the scriptures of injunctions. And thus the <s>Smṛti</s> [says] —

body.text: 'aśraddhayā hutaṃ dattam'-
body.translated_text: 'That which is offered and given without faith (<s>aśraddhā</s>)' —

body.text:
ityādikā /
niṣedhaśāstraṃ tu na śraddhāmapekṣate /
api tu niṣidhyamānakriyonmukho nara ityeva pravartate /
tathā ca sāṃsārika iva śraddhāvagatabrahmatattvo 'pi niṣedhamatikramya pravartamānaḥ pratyavaitīti na bhinnakarmadarśanābhyupagamaḥ /
tasmānnopāsanāyāḥ kārye karmāpekṣā /
body.translated_text: and so forth. But the scripture of prohibition does not depend on faith; rather, it operates simply [upon the fact that] 'this is a person inclined toward the prohibited action.' And thus, even one who has understood the reality of <s>Brahman</s>, like a <s>saṃsāric</s> person, transgressing the prohibition and engaging [in the prohibited act], would suffer the consequences — hence there is no acceptance of heterodox conduct. Therefore, there is no dependence on <s>karma</s> for the purpose of meditation.

body.text:
ata eva nopāsanotpattāvapi ; nirvicikitsaśābdajñānotpattyuttarakālamanadhikāraḥ karmaṇītyuktam /
tathā ca śrutiḥ-
body.translated_text: For this very reason, there is no [dependence on karma] even for the arising of meditation; for it has been stated that after the arising of unwavering scriptural knowledge, there is no qualification for <s>karma</s>. And thus the <s>Śruti</s> [says] —

body.text:
'na karmaṇā na prajayā dhanena tyāgenaike amṛtatvamānaśuḥ' /
iti /
body.translated_text: 'Not by <s>karma</s>, not by offspring, not by wealth — by renunciation alone some attained immortality.'

body.text:
tatkimidānīmanupayoga eva sarvatheha karmaṇām ? tathā ca 'vividiṣanti yajñena' ityādyāḥ śrutayo virudhyeran /
na, ārādupakārakatvātkarmaṇāṃ yajñādīnām /
tathā hi- tametamātmānaṃ vedānuvacanena nityasvādhyāyena, brāhmaṇā vividiṣanti, veditumicchanti, na tu vidanti /
vastutaḥ pradhānasyāpi vedanasya prakṛtyarthatayā śabdato guṇatvāt, icchāyāśca pratyayārthatayā prādhānyāt, pradhānena ca kāryasaṃpratyayāt /
na hi 'rājapuruṣamānaya' ityukte vastutaḥ pradhāno 'pi rājā puruṣaviśeṣaṇatayā śabdata upasarjana ānīyate, api tu puruṣa eva, śabdatastasya prādhānyāt /
evaṃ vedānuvacanasyeva yajñasyāpīcchāsādhanatayā vidhānam /
evaṃ tapaso 'nāśakasya /
kāmānaśanameva tapaḥ, hitamitamedhyāśino hi brahmaṇi vividiṣā bhavati, na tu sarvathā anaśnataḥ, maraṇāt /
nāpi cāndrāyaṇādi tapaḥ, tacchīlasya dhātuvaiṣamyāpatteḥ /
body.translated_text: Then is <s>karma</s> entirely useless here? And if so, <s>Śruti</s>s such as '<s>vividiṣanti yajñena</s>' (they desire to know through sacrifice) and the like would be contradicted. No — because <s>karma</s>s such as sacrifices and the like are auxiliaries from afar (<s>ārād-upakāraka</s>). For thus: '<s>brāhmaṇā</s>s desire to know (<s>vividiṣanti</s>) — desire to understand — that Self, through Vedic recitation, through constant self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>)' — they do not [thereby] know [it directly]. In truth, even knowledge (<s>vedana</s>), which is primary, has grammatical subordinacy because it functions as a verbal root-meaning; while desire (<s>icchā</s>), having the function of a verbal suffix-meaning, has primacy; and from the principal, the understanding of [the subsidiary] arises. For just as, when it is said 'bring the king's man,' the king — though in reality primary — being a qualifier of the man, is grammatically subordinate, and it is the man alone who is brought, due to his grammatical primacy — so too, like Vedic recitation, sacrifice too is enjoined as a means [of arousing] the desire [to know]. Similarly, <s>tapas</s> (austerity) [means] fasting (<s>anāśaka</s>). For <s>tapas</s> is indeed the extinction of desires; for one who eats what is wholesome, measured, and pure, the desire to know <s>Brahman</s> arises — but not for one who fasts completely, because of death. Nor is <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> and the like the [intended] <s>tapas</s>, because the habitual practice of that leads to an imbalance of bodily constituents (<s>dhātu-vaiṣamya</s>).

body.text:
etāni ca nityāni upāttaduritanibarhaṇena puruṣaṃ saṃskurvanti /
tathā ca śrutiḥ- 'sa ha vā ātmāyājī yo veda idaṃ me 'nenāṅgaṃ saṃskriyata idaṃ me 'nenāṅgamupadhīyate' iti /
aneneti prakṛtaṃ yajñādi parāmṛśati /
smṛtiśca-
body.translated_text: And these [karmas], being obligatory (<s>nitya</s>), refine the person by destroying accumulated sins. And thus the <s>Śruti</s> [says]: 'He indeed is the self-sacrificer who knows: "By this, this limb of mine is refined; by this, this limb of mine is nourished."' 'By this' refers to the sacrifice and the like under discussion. And the <s>Smṛti</s> [says] —

body.text:
'yasyaite 'ṣṭācatvāriṃśatsaṃskārāḥ' iti /
nityanaimittikānuṣṭhānaprakṣīṇakalmaṣasya ca viśuddhasattvasyāviduṣa eva utpannavividiṣasya jñānottapattiṃ darśayatyātharvaṇī śrutiḥ-
body.translated_text: 'For one who has these forty-eight <s>saṃskāra</s>s (sacraments)' — and so forth. And for one of purified <s>sattva</s> (inner nature) — whose defilements have been destroyed through the performance of obligatory and occasional [rites] — who is not yet a knower but in whom the desire to know has arisen — the <s>Ātharvaṇī Śruti</s> (<s>Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad</s>) shows the arising of knowledge:

body.text: '.................. viśuddhasattvastatastu taṃ paśyati niṣkalaṃ dhyāyamānaḥ' iti /
body.translated_text: '.................. One of purified nature, thereupon, through meditation, sees That which is without parts.'

body.text:
smṛtiśca 'jñānamutpadyate puṃsāṃ kṣayātpāpasya karmaṇaḥ' ityādikā /
kḷptenaiva ca nityānāṃ karmaṇāṃ nityehitenopāttaduritanibarhaṇena puruṣasaṃskāreṇa jñānotpattāvaṅgabhāvopapattau na saṃyogapṛthaktvena sākṣādaṅgabhāvo yuktaḥ, kalpanāgauravāpatteḥ /
tathāhi- nityakarmaṇāmanuṣṭhānāddharmotpādaḥ, tataḥ pāpmā nivartate ; sa hi anityāśuciduḥkharūpe saṃsāre nityaśucisukhakhyātilakṣaṇena viparyāsena cittasattvaṃ malinayati ; ataḥ pāpanivṛttau pratyakṣopapattidvārāpāvaraṇe sati pratyakṣopapattibhyāṃ saṃsārasya anityāśuciduḥsvarūpatvamapratyūhamavabudhyate ; tato 'sya asminnanabhiratisaṃjñaṃ vairāgyamupajāyate ; tatastajjihāsopāvartate ; tato hānopāyaṃ paryeṣate ; paryeṣamāṇaścātmatattvajñānamasyopāya ityupaśrutya tajjijñāsate ; tataḥ śravaṇādikrameṇa tajjānātītyārādupakārakatvaṃ tattvajñānotpādaṃ prati cittasattvaśuddhyā karmaṇāṃ yuktam /
iyamevārthamanuvadati bhagavadgītā-
body.translated_text: And the <s>Smṛti</s> [says]: 'Knowledge arises in persons through the destruction of sinful <s>karma</s>' — and so forth. And since, through the already established purpose of obligatory <s>karma</s>s — namely, the refinement of the person through the destruction of accumulated sins — their subsidiary role (<s>aṅgabhāva</s>) in the arising of knowledge is established, a separate direct subsidiary role through a distinct connection is not reasonable, due to the excessive burden of postulation. For thus: from the performance of obligatory <s>karma</s>s, <s>dharma</s> is produced; from that, sin (<s>pāpmā</s>) is removed. For [sin] defiles the <s>sattva</s> of the mind through the error (<s>viparyāsa</s>) characterized by the apprehension of permanence, purity, and happiness in <s>saṃsāra</s>, which is [in reality] impermanent, impure, and suffering. Therefore, when sin is removed, and the covering [of the truth] is removed through the door of direct experience and reasoning, one apprehends without obstruction, through direct experience and reasoning, the true nature of <s>saṃsāra</s> as impermanent, impure, and suffering. Then the dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) called non-attachment to [<s>saṃsāra</s>] arises in him. Then the desire to abandon it arises. Then he seeks the means of abandonment. And while seeking, having heard that the knowledge of the true nature of the Self is the means, he desires to know it. Then, through the sequence of hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>) and the like, he knows it. Thus, the role of <s>karma</s>s as auxiliaries from afar — through the purification of <s>sattva</s> — for the arising of the knowledge of reality is fitting. This very [point] the <s>Bhagavadgītā</s> restates —

children.translated_text: 'For the sage who desires to ascend to <s>yoga</s>, <s>karma</s> is said to be the means;
For that very one who has ascended to <s>yoga</s>, tranquility (<s>śama</s>) is said to be the means.' //

body.text: iti /
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text:
evaṃ ca ananuṣṭhitakarmāpi prāgbhavīyakarmavaśāt yo viśuddhasattvaḥ saṃsārāsāratādarśanena niṣpannavairāgyaḥ, kṛtaṃ tasya karmānuṣṭhānena vairāgyotpādopayoginā, prāgbhavīyakarmānuṣṭhānādeva tatsiddheḥ /
iyameva ca puruṣadhaureyabhedamadhikṛtya pravavṛte śrutiḥ- 'yadi vetarathā brahmacaryādeva pravrajet' iti /
tadidamuktam, karmāvabodhāt, prāgapyadhītavedāntasya brahmajijñāsopapatteriti /
ata eva na brahmacāriṇa ṛṇāni santi yena tadapākaraṇārthaṃ karmānutiṣṭhet /
etadanurodhācca 'jāyamāno vai brāhmaṇastribhirṛṇavā jāyate' iti gṛhasthaḥ saṃpadyamāna iti vyākhyeyam /
anyathā 'yadi vetarathā brahmacaryādeva' iti śrutirvirudhyeta /
gṛhasthasyāpi ca ṛṇāpākaraṇaṃ sattvaśuddhyarthameva /
jarāmaryavādo bhasmāntatāvādo 'ntyeṣṭayaśca karmajaḍānaviduṣaḥ prati, na tvātmatattvavidaḥ paṇḍitān /
tasmāttasyānantaryamatha-śabdārthaḥ yadvinā brahmajijñāsā na bhavati yasmiṃstu sati bhavantī bhavatyeva /
na cetthaṃ karmāvabodhaḥ /
tasmānna karmāvabodhānantaryamātrāthaśabdārtha iti sarvamavadātam /
body.translated_text: And thus, even one who has not performed <s>karma</s> [in this life], but who — by the force of <s>karma</s> from a previous birth — has purified <s>sattva</s> and has developed dispassion through seeing the futility of <s>saṃsāra</s>, for him the performance of <s>karma</s> as a means to producing dispassion is accomplished, since that [dispassion] is already achieved through the performance of <s>karma</s> in a previous birth. And it is with reference to this distinction among the foremost of persons that the <s>Śruti</s> declares: '<s>yadi vetarathā brahmacaryādeva pravrajet</s>' (or otherwise, one may renounce directly from the stage of studentship). This is what was stated: 'from the understanding of <s>karma</s>' — [meaning that] even before [completing ritual], for one who has studied the <s>Vedānta</s>s, the desire to know <s>Brahman</s> is justified. For this very reason, a <s>brahmacārin</s> (student) does not have the [three] debts, on account of which he would perform <s>karma</s> to discharge them. And in conformity with this, the [statement] '<s>jāyamāno vai brāhmaṇas tribhir ṛṇavā jāyate</s>' (a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is born with three debts) should be interpreted as [referring to one who] becomes a householder. Otherwise, the <s>Śruti</s> '<s>yadi vetarathā brahmacaryādeva</s>' (or otherwise, directly from studentship) would be contradicted. And even for the householder, the discharge of debts is only for the purpose of purifying <s>sattva</s>. The statements about old age and death, about ending in ashes, and the funeral rites pertain to the dull non-knower who is attached to <s>karma</s>, not to the wise person (<s>paṇḍita</s>) who knows the reality of the Self. Therefore, the meaning of the word '<s>atha</s>' is sequence to that without which the desire to know <s>Brahman</s> does not arise, and given which it does arise — it necessarily arises. And the understanding of <s>karma</s> is not of such a character. Therefore, the meaning of the word '<s>atha</s>' is not merely sequence to the understanding of <s>karma</s> — thus everything is clarified.

body.text:
syādetat /
mā bhūdagnihotrayavāgūpākavadarthaḥ kramaḥ ; śrautastu bhaviṣyanti ; 'gṛhī bhūtvā vanī bhavet vanī bhūtvā pravrajet' iti jābālaśrutirgārhasthyena hi yajñādyanuṣṭhānaṃ sūcayati /
smaranti ca -
body.translated_text: One might say this: Let there not be an essential sequence like [the sequence between] the <s>agnihotra</s> and the cooking of the <s>yavāgū</s> (rice gruel); but there will be a scriptural [sequence]. The <s>Jābāla Śruti</s> — '<s>gṛhī bhūtvā vanī bhavet vanī bhūtvā pravrajet</s>' (having been a householder, one should become a forest-dweller; having been a forest-dweller, one should renounce) — indicates the performance of sacrifices and the like through the householder stage. And they also say in <s>Smṛti</s> —

body.text: 'adhītya vidhivadvedānputrāṃścotpādya dharmataḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Having studied the <s>Veda</s>s according to rule, and having begotten sons in accordance with <s>dharma</s>,

body.text: iṣṭvā ca śaktito yajñairmano mokṣe niveśayet //
body.translated_text: And having performed sacrifices according to one's ability, one should direct the mind toward <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation).' //

body.text:
' iti /
nindanti ca-
body.translated_text: And [the <s>Smṛti</s>s] also censure —

body.text: 'anadhītya dvijo vedānanutpādya tathātmajān /
body.translated_text: 'A twice-born who, without having studied the <s>Veda</s>s, without having begotten sons,

body.text: aniṣṭvā caiva yajñaiśca mokṣamicchanvrajatyadhaḥ' //
body.translated_text: And without having performed sacrifices, desires <s>mokṣa</s>, goes downward.' //

body.text:
iti ; āha- yathā ca hṛdayādyavadānānāmānantaryaniyamaḥ /
kutaḥ ? 'hṛdayasyāgre 'vadyati atha jihvāyā atha vakṣasaḥ' ityathāgraśabdābhyāṃ kramasya vivakṣitatvāt /
na tatheha kramo vivakṣitaḥ, śrutyā tayaivānantaramaniyamasya darśitatvāt, 'yadi vetarathā brahmacaryādeva pravrajedgṛhādvā vanādvā' iti /
etāvatā hi vairāgyamupalakṣayati /
ata eva 'yadahareva virajettadahareva pravrajet' iti śrutiḥ /
nindāvacanaṃ ca aviśuddhasattvapuruṣābhiprāyam /
aviśuddhasattvo hi mokṣamicchannālasyāttadupāye 'pravartamāno gṛhasthadharmamapi nityanaimittikamanācaranpratikṣaṇamupacīyamānapāpmā adhogatiṃ gacchatītyarthaḥ /
body.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Just as for the cutting of the heart and the like, the restriction of sequence [obtains].' Why? Because in '<s>hṛdayasyāgre 'vadyati atha jihvāyā atha vakṣasaḥ</s>' (first he cuts from the heart, then from the tongue, then from the chest), by the words '<s>atha</s>' (then) and '<s>agre</s>' (first), the sequence is intended. But here, such a sequence is not intended, since the very same <s>Śruti</s> demonstrates immediately after that there is no restriction: '<s>yadi vetarathā brahmacaryādeva pravrajedgṛhādvā vanādvā</s>' (or otherwise, one may renounce directly from studentship, or from the householder stage, or from the forest). For by this, [the <s>Śruti</s>] indicates dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>). For this very reason, the <s>Śruti</s> [says]: '<s>yadahareva virajettadahareva pravrajet</s>' (on the very day one becomes dispassionate, on that very day one should renounce). And the censuring statement [in the <s>Smṛti</s>] has in view a person of impure <s>sattva</s>. For a person of impure <s>sattva</s> who desires <s>mokṣa</s> but, out of laziness, does not engage in the means to it, and who also does not observe even the obligatory and occasional householder <s>dharma</s>s — accumulating sin at every moment — goes downward. This is the meaning.

body.text:
syādetat /
mā bhūcchrauta ārtho vā kramaḥ ; pāṭhasthānamukhyapravṛttipramāṇakastu kasmānna bhavatītyata āha- śeṣaśeṣitve pramāṇābhāvāt /
śeṣāṇāṃ samidādīnāṃ śeṣiṇāṃ cāgneyādīnāṃ ekaphalavadupakāropanibaddhānāṃ ekaphalāvacchinnānām ekaprayogavacanopagṛhītānām ekādhikārikartṛkāṇāṃ ekapaurṇamāsyamāvāsyākālasaṃbaddhānāṃ yugapad anuṣṭhānāśakteḥ, sāmarthyātkramaprāptau tadviśeṣāpekṣāyāṃ pāṭhādayastadbhedaniyamāya prabhavanti /
yatra tu na śeṣaśeṣibhāvaḥ nāpyekādhikārāvacchedaḥ yathā sauryāryamṇaprājāpatyādīnām, tatra kramabhedāpekṣābhāvānna pāṭhādiḥ kramaviśeṣaniyame pramāṇam, avarjanīyatayā tasya tatrāvagatatvāt /
na ceha dharmabrahmajijñāsayoḥ śeṣaśeṣibhāve śrutyādīnāmanyatamaṃ pramāṇamasatīti /
body.translated_text:
One might say this:
Let neither the scriptural (<s>śrauta</s>) nor the contextual (<s>ārtha</s>) order [apply]; but why should the order based on the textual position (<s>pāṭha-sthāna</s>), which is the primary [criterion] for operation, not obtain? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Because there is no evidence for the subsidiary-principal relation (<s>śeṣa-śeṣitva</s>).'
For the subsidiaries — firewood (<s>samidh</s>) and the like — and the principals — the <s>Āgneya</s> offering and the like — which are bound by a relation of serving a single fruit, delimited by a single fruit, comprehended by the word of a single performance, having a single qualified agent, and connected with a single full-moon and new-moon time — since they cannot all be performed simultaneously, when the order is obtained through their mutual capacity, and when the specific [order] among them is sought, the textual position and the like are capable of determining their specific sequence.
But where there is neither a subsidiary-principal relation nor delimitation by a single qualification — as in the case of the <s>Saurya</s>, <s>Āryamṇa</s>, <s>Prājāpatya</s>, and the like — there, due to the absence of any need for a specific order, the textual position and the like are not evidence for determining a specific order, since [the order] is already understood as inevitable.
And here, none of the [evidences] such as scripture (<s>śruti</s>) and the like is evidence for a subsidiary-principal relation between the desire to know <s>dharma</s> and the desire to know <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text:
nanu śeṣaśeṣibhāvābhāve 'pi kramaniyamo dṛṣṭaḥ yathā godohanasya puruṣārthasya dārśapaurṇamāsikairaṅgaiḥ saha, yathā vā 'darśapūrṇamāsābhyāmiṣṭvā somena yajeta' iti darśapūrṇamāsasomayoraśeṣaśeṣiṇorityata āha- adhikṛtādhikāre vā pramāṇābhāvāt- iti yojanā /
svargakāmasya hi darśapūrṇamāsādhikṛtasya paśukāmasya sato darśapūrṇamāsa-
body.translated_text:
But [one may object:] even in the absence of a subsidiary-principal relation, a fixed order is observed — as in the case of cow-milking (<s>godohana</s>), which serves a human purpose, with respect to the subsidiary rites of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [sacrifices]; or as in '[having sacrificed] with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, one should sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>,' where the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and <s>Soma</s> [sacrifices] are not in a subsidiary-principal relation. To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Or, because there is no evidence for the qualification-within-qualification (<s>adhikṛtādhikāra</s>) [relation]' — this is the syntactic connection.
For indeed, the person desiring heaven — who is qualified for the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> — when desiring cattle, [has] for the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>

body.text:
kratvarthāppraṇayanāśrite godohane adhikāraḥ /
no khalu godohanadravyamavyāpriyamāṇaṃ sākṣātpaśūn bhāvayitumarhati /
na ca vyāpārāntarāviṣṭaṃ śrūyate yatastadaṅgakramamatipatet ; appraṇayanāśritaṃ tu pratīyate, 'camasenāpaḥ praṇayedgodohanena paśukāmāsya' iti samabhivyāhārāt, yogyatvāccāsyāpāṃ praṇayanaṃ prati /
tasmātkratvarthāppraṇayanāśritatvādgodohanasya tatkrameṇa puruṣārthamapi godohanaṃ kramavaditi siddham /
śrutinirākaraṇenaiva iṣṭisomakramavadapi kramo 'pāsto veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text:
qualification in the cow-milking, which depends on the carrying of water that serves the purpose of the sacrifice.
Indeed, the material of cow-milking, when not employed [in a sacrificial context], is not capable of directly producing cattle.
Nor is any other employment heard [from scripture] by which it would transcend the order of a subsidiary rite; but it is understood as dependent on the carrying of water, from the co-occurrence in the statement 'One should carry water with a ladle, by cow-milking, for one desiring cattle,' and because of its fitness for the carrying of water.
Therefore, since the cow-milking depends on the carrying of water that serves the purpose of the sacrifice, the cow-milking for a human purpose also follows that order — this is established.
By the refutation through scripture alone, the order — like the <s>iṣṭi</s>-<s>Soma</s> order — should also be understood as rejected.

body.text:
śeṣaśeṣitvādhikṛtādhikārābhāve 'pi kramo vivakṣyeta yadyekaphalāvacchedo bhavet, yathāgneyādīnāṃ ṣaṇṇāmekasvargaphalāvacchinnānām ; yadi vā jijñāsyabrahmaṇaḥ aṃśo dharmaḥ syāt, yathā caturlakṣaṇīvyutpādyaṃ brahma kenacitkenacit aṃśenaikena lakṣaṇena vyutpādyate, tatra caturṇāṃ lakṣaṇānāṃ jijñāsyābhedena parasparasaṃbandhe sati kramo vivakṣitaḥ, tathehāpyekajijñāsyatayā dharmabrahmajijñāsayoḥ kramo vivakṣyeta ; na caitadubhayamapyastītyāha- phalajijñāsyabhedācca /
phalabhedaṃ vibhajate- abhyudayaphalaṃ dharmajñānam iti /
jijñāsāyā vastuto jñānatantratvāt jñānaphalaṃ jijñāsāphalamiti bhāvaḥ /
na kevalaṃ svarūpataḥ phalabhedaḥ, tadutpādanaprakārabhedādapi tadbheda ityāha- taccānuṣṭhānāpekṣam /
brahmajñānaṃ ca nānuṣṭhānāntarāpekṣam /
śābdajñānābhyāsānnānuṣṭhānāntaramapekṣate, nityanaimittikakarmānuṣṭhānasahabhāvasya apāstatvāt- iti bhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text:
Even in the absence of a subsidiary-principal relation and a qualification-within-qualification [relation], an order might be intended if there were delimitation by a single fruit — as with the six [offerings] beginning with the <s>Āgneya</s>, which are delimited by the single fruit of heaven; or if <s>dharma</s> were a part of the <s>Brahman</s> that is to be known — just as the <s>Brahman</s> to be explained through the four characteristics (<s>catur-lakṣaṇī</s>) is explained by one or another part, by one or another characteristic, and therein, since the four characteristics are mutually related through non-difference with the object of inquiry, an order is intended — so too here, an order between the desire to know <s>dharma</s> and the desire to know <s>Brahman</s> might be intended on the grounds of a single object of inquiry. But neither of these two [conditions] obtains — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'And because of the difference of fruit and of the object of inquiry (<s>jijñāsya</s>).'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] distinguishes the difference of fruit: 'The knowledge of <s>dharma</s> has worldly prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>) as its fruit.'
Since the desire to know, in reality, depends on knowledge, the fruit of knowledge is [also] the fruit of the desire to know — this is the purport.
Not only is there a difference of fruit in essence, but also a difference of the means of producing that [fruit] — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'And that [fruit of dharma-knowledge] depends on performance (<s>anuṣṭhāna</s>).'
But the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> does not depend on any other performance.
From the practice of verbal knowledge [alone], it does not require any other performance, since the co-existence [of Brahman-knowledge] with the performance of obligatory and occasional rites has been rejected — this is the purport.

body.text:
jijñāsyabhedamātyantikamāha- bhavyaśca dharma iti /
bhavitā bhavyaḥ ; kartari kṛtyaḥ /
bhavitā ca bhāvakavyāpāranirvartyatayā tattantra iti tataḥ prāgjñānakāle nāstītyarthaḥ /
bhūtam, satyam ; sadekāntataḥ, na kadācidasadityarthaḥ /
na kevalaṃ svarūpato jijñāsyayorbhedaḥ, jñāpakapramāṇapravṛttibhedādapi bheda ityāha- codanāpravṛttibhedācca /
codaneti vaidikaṃ śabdamāha, viśeṣeṇa sāmānyasya lakṣaṇāt /
pravṛttabhedaṃ vibhajate- yā hi codanā dharmasya iti /
ājñādīnāṃ puruṣābhiprāyabhedānāmasaṃbhavāt apauruṣeye vede codanopadeśaḥ /
ata evoktam- 'tasya jñānamupadeśaḥ' iti /
sā ca svasādhye puruṣavyāpāre bhāvanāyāṃ tadviṣaye ca yāgādau ; sa hi bhāvanāviṣayaḥ, tadadhīnanirūpaṇatvāt prayatnasya bhāvanāyāḥ, 'ṣiñ bandhane' ityasmāt dhātorviṣayapadavyutpatteḥ /
bhāvanāyāstaddvāreṇa ca yāgāderapekṣitopāyatāmavagamayantī tatrecchopahāramukheṇa puruṣaṃ niyuñjānaiva yāgādidharmamavabodhayati nānyathā /
brahmacodanā tu puruṣamavabodhayatyeva kevalaṃ na tu pravartayantyavabodhayati /
kutaḥ ? avabodhasya pravṛttirahitasya codanājanyatvāt /
body.translated_text:
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the absolute difference of the objects of inquiry: 'And <s>dharma</s> is what is yet to be (<s>bhavya</s>).'
'<s>Bhavya</s>' means 'that which will come into being'; the <s>kṛtya</s> suffix is in the sense of the agent.
It will come into being as something dependent on the operation of the producer — hence it depends on that [operation] and therefore does not exist prior [to it], at the time of knowledge — this is the meaning.
'<s>Bhūta</s>' [means] real; absolutely existent — meaning: never at any time non-existent.
Not only is there a difference of the objects of inquiry in essence, but there is also a difference due to the distinct operation of the evidencing <s>pramāṇa</s> — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'And because of the difference in the operation of the injunction (<s>codanā</s>).'
By '<s>codanā</s>' [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refers to the Vedic word, since a genus is defined through a differentia.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] distinguishes the difference of operation: 'The injunction (<s>codanā</s>) that [concerns] <s>dharma</s>...'
Since the distinctions of command (<s>ājñā</s>) and the like — which depend on differences in a person's intention — are impossible in the authorless <s>Veda</s>, the injunction is teaching (<s>upadeśa</s>).
Hence it is said: 'Its knowledge is teaching.'
And that [injunction], in its proper domain — the human effort (<s>puruṣa-vyāpāra</s>) called <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive action) — and in the object of that [<s>bhāvanā</s>], namely sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>) and the like; for that [sacrifice] is the object of <s>bhāvanā</s>, since effort (<s>prayatna</s>) depends for its determination on <s>bhāvanā</s>, and since the word '<s>viṣaya</s>' (object) is etymologically derived from the root '<s>ṣiñ bandhane</s>' (to bind).
The [injunction], making known the status of requisite means of <s>bhāvanā</s> and, through that, of sacrifice and the like — enjoining a person through the channel of desire — teaches <s>dharma</s> in the form of sacrifice and the like only in this way, not otherwise.
But the injunction concerning <s>Brahman</s> only instructs the person — it does not impel [him to action] while instructing.
Why? Because the cognition [of <s>Brahman</s>], which is free from [the need for] exertion, is produced by the injunction.

body.text: nanu 'ātmā jñātavyaḥ' ityetadvidhiparairvedāntaiḥ tadekavākyatayāvabodhe pravartayadbhireva puruṣo brahmāvabodhyata iti samānatvaṃ dharmacodanābhirbrahmacodanānāmityata āha- na puruṣo 'vabodhe niyujyate //
body.translated_text: But [one may object:] by the <s>Vedānta</s>s that take '<s>ātmā jñātavyaḥ</s>' (the self should be known) as an injunction, and by virtue of being a single sentence with that [injunction], the person is impelled toward cognition while being instructed about <s>Brahman</s> — thus [the injunction regarding <s>Brahman</s>] would be the same as the injunctions concerning <s>dharma</s>. To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'The person is not enjoined toward cognition.'

body.text:
ayamabhisaṃdhiḥ- na tāvadbrahmasākṣātkāre puruṣo niyoktavyaḥ, tasya brahmasvābhāvyena nityatvāt akāryatvāt /
nāpyupāsanāyām, tasyā api jñānaprakarṣe hetubhāvasyānvayavyatirekasiddhatayā prāptatvenāvidheyatvāt /
nāpi śābdabodhe, tasyāpyadhītavedasya puruṣasya viditapadatadarthasya samadhigataśābdanyāyatattvasyāpratyūhamutpatteḥ /
atraiva dṛṣṭāntamāha- yathākṣārtha iti /
dārṣṭāntike yojayati- tadvat iti /
api cātmajñānavidhipareṣu vedānteṣu nātmatattvaviniścayaḥ śābdaḥ syāt /
na hi tadā ātmatattvaparāste, kiṃ tu tajjñānavidhiparāḥ, yatparāśca te ta eva teṣāṃ arthāḥ /
na ca bodhasya bodhyaniṣṭhatvādapekṣitatvāt, anyaparebhyo 'pi bodhyatattvaviniścayaḥ, samāropeṇāpi tadupapatteḥ /
tasmānna bodhavidhiparā vedāntā iti siddham /
body.translated_text:
The intent is this: First, the person need not be enjoined toward the direct realization (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>) of <s>Brahman</s>, since that [realization], being natural to <s>Brahman</s>, is eternal and cannot be produced.
Nor [need he be enjoined] toward meditation (<s>upāsanā</s>), since that too — its causal relation to the intensification of knowledge being established through positive and negative concomitance — is already obtained [without injunction] and hence not enjoinable.
Nor [need he be enjoined] toward verbal cognition (<s>śābda-bodha</s>), since for a person who has studied the <s>Veda</s>, who knows the meanings of words and their connections, and who has understood the principles of scriptural reasoning — that [verbal cognition] arises without obstruction.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] gives an illustration for this very point: 'Just as [cognition] regarding the objects of the senses.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] applies it to the case at hand: 'Similarly...'
Moreover, if the <s>Vedānta</s>s were construed as injunctions of self-knowledge, the ascertainment of the reality of the Self (<s>ātma-tattva</s>) from the <s>Vedānta</s>s would not be verbal [i.e., scripture-based].
For then they would not have the reality of the Self as their subject, but rather the injunction of its knowledge, and whatever [texts] are about something, those are their meanings.
Nor, in that case, would the ascertainment of the reality of the Self [come] from other [<s>Vedānta</s> passages] that are construed as subordinate to the injunction — since [such ascertainment] would be possible even through a superimposed [meaning, i.e.,] one that is not the real meaning.
Therefore, since [the cognition of <s>Brahman</s>] is not an injunction of cognition, the <s>Vedānta</s>s do not have an injunction as their intended meaning — this is established.

body.text:
prakṛtamupasaṃharati- tasmātkimapi vaktavyam iti /
yasminnasati brahmajijñāsā na bhavati sati tu bhavantī bhavatyevetyarthaḥ /
tadāha- ucyate- nityānityavastuviveka ityādi /
nityaḥ pratyagātmā, anityāḥ dehendriyaviṣayādayaḥ /
tadviṣayaścedviveko niścayaḥ, kṛtamasya brahmajijñāsayā, jñātatvādbrahmaṇaḥ /
atha viveko jñānamātram, na niścayaḥ ; tathā sati eṣa viparyāsādanyaḥ saṃśayaḥ syāt ; tathā ca na vairāgyaṃ bhāvayet ; abhāvayankathaṃ brahmajijñāsāhetuḥ ? tasmādevaṃ vyākhyeyam /
nityānityayorvasatīti nityānityavastu taddharmaḥ ; nityānityayordharmiṇostaddharmāṇāṃ ca viveko nityānityavastuvivekaḥ /
etaduktaṃ bhavati- mā bhūt idaṃ ṛtaṃ nityam, idaṃ tadanṛtamanityamiti dharmiviśeṣayorvivekaḥ ; dharmimātrayornityānityayostaddharmayośca vivekaṃ niścinotyeva /
nityatvaṃ satyatvaṃ tadyasyāsti tannityaṃ satyam ; tathā cāsthāgocaraḥ /
anityatvamasatyatvaṃ tadyasyāsti tadanityamanṛtam ; tathā cānāsthāgocaraḥ /
tadeteṣvanubhūyamāneṣu yuṣmadasmatpratyayagocareṣu viṣayaviṣayiṣu yadṛtaṃ nityaṃ sukhaṃ vyavasthāsyate tadāsthāgocaro bhaviṣyati ; yattvanityamanṛtaṃ bhaviṣyati tāpatrayaparītaṃ tattyakṣyata iti so 'yaṃ nityānityavastuvivekaḥ prāgbhavīyādaihikādvā karmaṇo viśuddhasattvasya bhavatyanubhavopapattibhyām /
na khalu satyaṃ nāma na kiñcidastīti vācyam /
tadabhāve tadadhiṣṭhānasyānṛtasyāpyanupapatteḥ, śūnyavādināmapi śūnyatāyā eva satyatvāt /
athāsya puruṣadhaureyasyānubhavopapattibhyāmevaṃ sunipuṇaṃ nirūpayataḥ ā ca satyalokāt ā cāvīceḥ jāyasva mriyasva iti viparivartamānaṃ kṣaṇamuhūrtayāmāhorātrārdhamāsamāsartvayanavatsarayugacaturyugamanvantarapralayamahāpralayamahāsargāvāntarasargasaṃsārasāgarormibhiraniśamuhyamānaṃ tāpatrayaparītamātmānaṃ jīvalokaṃ cāvalokya asminsaṃsāramaṇḍale anityāśuciduḥkhātmakaṃ prasaṃkhyānamupāvartate /
body.translated_text:
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] concludes the topic at hand: 'Therefore, something [particular] must be stated' — meaning: that without which the desire to know <s>Brahman</s> does not arise, and given which it necessarily arises.
Thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'It is said — the discrimination of permanent and impermanent things (<s>nityānitya-vastu-viveka</s>)' etc.
The permanent is the inner Self (<s>pratyag-ātman</s>); the impermanent are body, senses, objects, and the like.
If the discrimination regarding these were a definitive ascertainment (<s>niścaya</s>), then there would be no need for the desire to know <s>Brahman</s>, since <s>Brahman</s> would already be known.
But if the discrimination is mere cognition, not ascertainment, then that would be a doubt different from misapprehension; and thus it would not produce dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>); and if it does not produce [dispassion], how can it be the cause of the desire to know <s>Brahman</s>? Therefore, [the definition] should be explained as follows:
That which abides in the permanent and the impermanent is the permanent-and-impermanent thing (<s>nityānitya-vastu</s>), i.e., the properties of each; the discrimination of the permanent and impermanent substrates and of their properties is the discrimination of permanent and impermanent things.
What is stated amounts to this: Let there not be the discrimination 'this is real and permanent, this is unreal and impermanent' regarding specific substrates; but the discrimination of mere substrates — the permanent and impermanent — and of their properties is definitely ascertained.
Permanence and reality — that which possesses these is permanent and real; and as such, it is the object of commitment (<s>āsthā</s>).
Impermanence and unreality — that which possesses these is impermanent and unreal; and as such, it is the object of non-commitment.
Among these experienced things that fall within the scope of the 'you'-cognition and the 'I'-cognition — objects and subjects — whatever is determined as real, permanent, and blissful will become the object of commitment; and whatever will be [determined as] impermanent and unreal, beset by the threefold suffering (<s>tāpatraya</s>), will be abandoned — this is the discrimination of permanent and impermanent things. It arises for one of purified <s>sattva</s> (clarity) from actions in previous lives or in this life, as established by both experience and reasoning.
Indeed, one should not say that nothing whatsoever is real.
For in the absence of that [reality], even the unreal — which depends on it as its substrate — would be impossible, since even for the <s>Śūnyavādin</s>s (proponents of voidness), voidness itself is [accepted as] real.
Now, for this foremost among persons — who, through both experience and reasoning, thus subtly discriminates — surveying himself and the world of living beings revolving [in the cycle of] 'be born, die,' from [the realm of] <s>Satyaloka</s> down to <s>Avīci</s>, ceaselessly tossed by the waves of the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> — measured in moments, <s>muhūrta</s>s, watches, days and nights, fortnights, months, seasons, half-years, years, <s>yuga</s>s, sets of four <s>yuga</s>s, <s>manvantara</s>s, dissolutions, great dissolutions, great creations, and intermediate creations — beset by the threefold suffering, [perceiving everything as] impermanent, impure, suffering, and non-self — contemplation (<s>prasaṃkhyāna</s>) arises.

body.text:
tato 'syedṛśānnityānityavastuvivekalakṣaṇātprasaṃkhyānāt ihamutrārthabhegavirāgaḥ bhavati /
arthyate prārthyata ityarthaḥ, phalamiti yāvat /
tasminvirāgo nāmānābhogātmikopekṣābuddhiḥ /
tataḥ śamadamādisādhanasaṃpat /
