The non-objectifiability of the inner Self (<s>pratyagātman</s>) has [thus] been established by [the passage] 'For when there is the sense...' (<s>sati hīndriya</s>). And how inference based on general observation (<s>sāmānyato dṛṣṭa</s>) also does not operate regarding <s>Brahman</s> — we shall establish this more subtly later. And this has been established by us at length in the <s>Nyāyakaṇikā</s>. And that [the <s>Vedānta</s>s] do not merely reiterate by virtue of being about existing entities — this too we shall establish later. Therefore everything is clarified. And the <s>Śruti</s> shows birth by '<s>yato vā</s>' (from which indeed), sustenance — i.e., persistence — by 'by which, having been born, they live' (<s>yena jātāni jīvanti</s>), and dissolution into that very [<s>Brahman</s>] by 'into which they depart' (<s>yatprayanti</s>). 'And the determining sentence of that' (<s>tasya ca nirṇayavākyam</s>). And here, when there is doubt about whether [the cause is] <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) etc., the determining sentence is: '<s>ānandādhyeva</s>' (from bliss alone). What is stated amounts to this: just as a stream [of appearances], having the rope as its material cause accompanied by ignorance of the rope, exists in the rope when the rope exists and dissolves in the rope alone — so too, the world, having <s>Brahman</s> accompanied by <s>avidyā</s> as its material cause, exists in <s>Brahman</s> alone and dissolves into that alone — this is established.

body.text: jagatkāraṇatvapradarśanena sarvajñaṃ brahmetyupakṣiptam ; tadeva draḍhayannāha-
body.translated_text: By demonstrating [<s>Brahman</s>'s] being the cause of the world, [the proposition that] <s>Brahman</s> is omniscient has been introduced. Consolidating that very [point], [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says —

body.text: #śāstrayonitvāt# //3 //
body.translated_text: '<s>Śāstrayonitvāt</s>' (Because [<s>Brahman</s>] is the source of scripture) // 3 //

body.text:
sūtrāntaramavatārayituṃ purvasūtrasaṃgatimāha- #jagatkāraṇatvapradarśanena#iti /
na kevalaṃ jagadyonitvādasya bhagavataḥ sarvajñatā, śāstrayonitvādapi boddhavyā /
śāstrayonitvasya sarvajñatāsādhanatvaṃ samarthagate- #mahata ṛgvedādeḥ śāstrasya#iti /
cāturvarṇyasya cāturāśramyasya ca yathāyathaṃ niṣekādiśmaśānāntāsu brahmamuhūrtopakramapradoṣaparisamāpanīyāsu nityanaimittikakāmyakarmapaddhatiṣu ca brahmatattve ca śiṣyāṇāṃ śāsanāt śāstramṛgvedādiḥ ; ata eva mahāviṣayatvāt mahat /
na kevalaṃ mahāviṣayatvenāsya mahattvam, api tvanekāṅgopāṅgopakaraṇatayāpītyāha- #anekavidyāsthānopabṛṃhitasya# /
purāṇanyāyamīmāṃsādayo daśa vidyāsthānāni ; taiḥ tayā tayā dvāropakṛtasya /
tadanena samastaśiṣṭajanaparigraheṇāprāmāṇyaśaṅkāpyapākṛtā /
purāṇādipraṇetāro hi maharṣayaḥ śiṣṭāḥ ; taiḥ tayā tayā dvārā vedān vyācakṣāṇaistadarthaṃ cādareṇānutiṣṭhadbhiḥ parigṛhīto veda iti /
na cāyamanavabodhako nāpyarapaṣṭabodhako yenāpramāṇaṃ syādityāha-
body.translated_text: To introduce the next <s>sūtra</s>, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the connection with the previous <s>sūtra</s>: 'By demonstrating [<s>Brahman</s>'s] being the cause of the world' (<s>jagatkāraṇatvapradarśanena</s>). Not only from being the source of the world does this Blessed One possess omniscience — from being the source of scripture (<s>śāstrayonitva</s>) too, it should be understood. Having established that being the source of scripture proves omniscience — 'Of the great scripture, the <s>Ṛgveda</s> and the like' (<s>mahata ṛgvedādeḥ śāstrasya</s>). It is called <s>śāstra</s> (scripture) because it instructs (<s>śāsanāt</s>) students regarding the true nature of <s>Brahman</s>, and regarding the prescribed procedures of obligatory, occasional, and optional <s>karma</s>s — from the sacrament of conception (<s>niṣeka</s>) to the cremation ground — performed from the <s>Brahma-muhūrta</s> (early morning) through evening — appropriate to each of the four <s>varṇa</s>s (classes) and four <s>āśrama</s>s (stages of life). And because it has a vast subject-matter, it is great (<s>mahat</s>). Not only because of its vast subject-matter is it great, but also because of its being supported by numerous subsidiary disciplines (<s>aṅga</s>s) and auxiliary texts — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Augmented by the many branches of learning' (<s>anekavidyāsthānopabṛṃhitasya</s>). The <s>Purāṇa</s>s, <s>Nyāya</s>, <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>, and the like — the ten branches of learning — by these, [the <s>Veda</s>] is supported through various channels. By this, through the acceptance by all learned people, even the suspicion of non-authoritativeness is dispelled. For the great sages who composed the <s>Purāṇa</s>s and the like are learned persons (<s>śiṣṭa</s>s); and by them — who explained the <s>Veda</s>s through various channels and who practiced their meaning with devotion — the <s>Veda</s> has been accepted. And this [<s>Veda</s>] is neither non-communicative nor indistinctly communicative, such that it would be non-authoritative — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says —

body.text:
#pradīpavatsarvārthāvadyotinaḥ# /
sarvamarthajātaṃ sarvathāvabodhayan nānavabodhako nāpyaspaṣṭabodhaka ityarthaḥ /
ata eva #sarvajñakalpasya#sarvajñasadṛśasya /
sarvajñasya hi jñānaṃ sarvaviṣayaṃ śāstrasyāpyabhidhānaṃ sarvaviṣayamiti sādṛśyam /
tadevamanvayamuktvā vyatirekamāha- #na hīdṛśasya#iti /
sarvajñasya guṇaḥ sarvaviṣayatā ; tadanvitaṃ śāsatram, asyāpi sarvaviṣayatvāt /
uktamarthaṃ pramāṇayati- #yadyadvistarārthaṃ śāstraṃ yasmātpuruṣaviśeṣāt#
body.translated_text: 'Illuminating all meanings like a lamp' (<s>pradīpavat sarvārthāvadyotinaḥ</s>). Illuminating the entire range of meanings in every way, [the <s>Veda</s>] is neither non-communicative nor indistinctly communicative — this is the meaning. For this very reason, [it is] 'as if omniscient' (<s>sarvajñakalpasya</s>) — resembling the omniscient. For the knowledge of the omniscient has everything as its object; and the statement of scripture too has everything as its object — thus the resemblance. Having thus stated the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>), [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>): 'For no such [scripture]...' (<s>na hīdṛśasya</s>). The quality of the omniscient is having everything as its object; scripture possesses that, since it too has everything as its object. [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] adduces evidence for the stated meaning: 'Whatever extensive scripture arises from whatever particular person' (<s>yadyad vistarārthaṃ śāstraṃ yasmāt puruṣaviśeṣāt</s>)

body.text:
#saṃbhavati sa#puruṣaviśeṣaḥ #tato 'pi#śāstrāt #adhikataravijñānaḥ#iti yojanā /
adyatve 'pyasmadādibhiryatsamīcīnārthaviṣayaṃ śāstraṃ viracyate tatrāsmākaṃ vaktṛṇāṃ vākyājjñānamadhikaviṣayam /
na hi te te asādhāraṇadharmā anubhūyamānā api śakyā vaktum /
na khalvikṣukṣīraguḍādīnāṃ madhurarasabhedāḥ śakyāḥ sarasvatyāpyākhyātum /
vistarārthamapi vākyaṃ na vaktṛjñānena tulyaviṣayamiti kathayituṃ #vistara#grahaṇam /
sopanayaṃ nigamanamāha- #kimu vaktavyam#iti /
vedasya yasmāt mahato bhūtāt yoneḥ saṃbhavaḥ, tasya mahato bhūtasya brahmaṇo niratiśayaṃ sarvajñatvaṃ sarvaśaktitvaṃ ca kimu vaktavyamiti yojanā /
#anekaśākhā#iti /
atra ca #anekaśākhābhedabhinnasya#ityādiḥ #saṃbhava#
body.translated_text: 'that [person] possesses knowledge even greater than that [scripture]' — this is the syntactic connection. Even in the present day, whatever well-reasoned scripture is composed by us and the like — of us, the speakers, our knowledge has a greater scope than the text. For indeed, those distinctive properties, even when experienced, cannot be verbally expressed. Surely, the distinctions of sweet taste among sugarcane, milk, jaggery, and the like cannot be articulated even by <s>Sarasvatī</s> herself. The word 'extensive' (<s>vistara</s>) is used to say that even an extensive statement does not have the same scope as the speaker's knowledge. [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the conclusion with application: 'What more need be said?' (<s>kimu vaktavyam</s>). Of that great Being — <s>Brahman</s> — which is the source (<s>yoni</s>) from which the <s>Veda</s> arises, its unsurpassed omniscience and omnipotence — what more need be said? — this is the syntactic connection. 'Of many branches' (<s>anekaśākhā</s>). And here, [the passage] from 'divided into many branches' (<s>anekaśākhābhedabhinnasya</s>) to 'arises' (<s>saṃbhava</s>)

body.text:
ityanta upanayaḥ /
#tasya#ityādi #sarvaśaktitvaṃ ca#ityantaṃ nigamanam /
#aprayatnenaiva#iti /
īṣatprayatnena, yathā 'alavaṇā yavāgūḥ' iti /
devarṣayo hi mahāpariśrameṇāpi yatrāśaktāḥ tadayamīṣatprayatnena līlayaiva karotīti niratiśayamasya sarvajñatvaṃ sarvaśaktitvaṃ coktaṃ bhavati /
aprayatnenāsya vedakartṛtve śrutiruktā 'asya mahato bhūtasya' iti /
ye 'pi tāvat varṇānāṃ nityatvamāsthiṣata tairapi padavākyādīnāmanityatvamabhyupāyam /
ānupūrvībhedavanto hi varṇāḥ padam /
padāni cānupūrvībhedavanti vākyam /
vyaktidharmaścānupūrvī na varṇadharmaḥ, varṇānāṃ nityānāṃ vibhūnāṃ ca kālato deśato vā paurvāparyāyogāt /
vyaktiścānityeti kathaṃ tadupagṛhītānāṃ varṇānāṃ nityānāmapi padatā nityā ?
body.translated_text: is the application. From 'Of that' (<s>tasya</s>) to 'omnipotence also' (<s>sarvaśaktitvaṃ ca</s>) is the conclusion. 'Without effort' (<s>aprayatnenaiva</s>) — with slight effort, as in 'unsalted rice-gruel.' For the divine sages, even with great exertion, are unable [to produce] what this [<s>Brahman</s>] does with slight effort, as if in play — thus its unsurpassed omniscience and omnipotence are stated. The <s>Śruti</s> for [<s>Brahman</s>'s] effortless authorship of the <s>Veda</s> is stated as: 'Of this great Being' (<s>asya mahato bhūtasya</s>). Now, even those who maintain the eternality of phonemes (<s>varṇa</s>s) accept the non-eternality of words (<s>pada</s>), sentences (<s>vākya</s>), and the like. For phonemes arranged in a particular order constitute a word. And words arranged in a particular order constitute a sentence. And sequential order (<s>ānupūrvī</s>) is a property of particular instances (<s>vyakti</s>), not of phonemes — since phonemes, being eternal and all-pervading, cannot have temporal or spatial priority and posteriority. And since instances are non-eternal, how can the wordhood of phonemes — even though eternal — that are comprehended through [non-eternal instances] be eternal?

body.text:
padānityatayā ca vākyādīnāmapyanityatā vyākhyātā /
tasmānnṛttānukaraṇavat padādyanukaraṇamapi /
yathā hi yādṛśaṃ gātracalanādi nartakaḥ karoti tādṛśameva śikṣyamāṇānukaroti nartakī, na tu tadeva vyanakti, evaṃ yādṛśīmānupūrvīṃ vaidikānāṃ varṇapadādīnāṃ karotyadhyāpayitā tādṛśīmevānukaroti māṇavakaḥ, na tu tāmevoccārayati, ācāryavyaktibhyo māṇavakavyaktīnāmanyatvāt /
tasmānnityānityavarṇavādināṃ na laukikavaidikapadavākyādipauruṣeyatve vivādaḥ ; kevalaṃ vedavākyeṣu puruṣasvātantryāsvātantrye vipratipattiḥ /
yathāhuḥ- 'yatnataḥ pratiṣedhyā naḥ puruṣāṇāṃ svatantratā' iti /
tatra sṛṣṭipralayamanicchanto jaiminīyā vedādhyayanaṃ pratyasmādṛśaguruśiṣyaparamparāmavicchinnāmanādimācakṣate /
vaiyāsikaṃ tu matamanuvartamānāḥ śrutismṛtītihāsādisiddhasṛṣṭipralayānusāreṇa anādyavidyopadhānalabdhasarvaśaktisarvajñānasyāpi paramātmano nityasya vedānāṃ yonerapi na teṣu svātantryam, pūrvapūrvasargānusāreṇa tādṛśānupūrvīviracanāt ; yathā hi yāgādibrahmahatyādayor'thānarthahetavo brahmavivartā api na sargāntare vipariyanti /
na hi jātu kvacitsarge brahmahatyārthaheturanarthahetuścāśvamedho bhavati, agnirvā kledayati, āpo vā dahanti, tadvat /
yathātra sarge niyatānupūrvyaṃ vedādhyayanamabhyudayaniḥśreyasahetuḥ, anyathā tadeva vāgvajratayānarthahetuḥ, evaṃ sargāntareṣvapīti tadanurodhāt sarvajño 'pi sarvaśaktirapi pūrvapūrvasargānusāreṇa vedānviracayanna svatantraḥ /
puruṣāsvātantryamātraṃ cāpauruṣeyatvaṃ rocayante jaiminīyā api /
taccāsmākamapi samānam, anyatrābhiniveśāt /
body.translated_text: And since words are non-eternal, the non-eternality of sentences and the like is also explained. Therefore, just as with the imitation of dance, so too with the imitation of words and the like. For just as whatever bodily movements etc. a dancer performs are imitated in exactly the same way by a female dancer who is being trained — but she does not manifest those very [movements], so too, whatever sequential order of Vedic phonemes, words, and the like the teacher produces, exactly the same is imitated by the student — but he does not utter those very [sounds], since the instances of the student are different from the instances of the teacher. Therefore, for proponents of both eternal and non-eternal phonemes, there is no dispute about the human authorship (<s>pauruṣeyatva</s>) of mundane and Vedic words and sentences; the disagreement is only about human autonomy (<s>svātantrya</s>) versus non-autonomy regarding Vedic sentences. As they say: 'The autonomy of persons must be carefully negated by us.' Therein, the followers of <s>Jaimini</s>, not accepting creation and dissolution, speak of a beginningless unbroken succession of teachers and students like us for the Vedic study. But those who follow the view of <s>Vyāsa</s>, in conformity with creation and dissolution established in <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, <s>Itihāsa</s>, and the like — [hold that] even for the supreme Self (<s>paramātman</s>), who is eternal and possesses omniscience and omnipotence obtained through the provision of beginningless <s>avidyā</s>, there is no autonomy regarding the <s>Veda</s>s, since [He] composes the sequential order in conformity with each preceding creation. For just as sacrifice and <s>brahmahatyā</s> (killing of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>), though transformations of <s>Brahman</s>, are causes of beneficial and harmful results respectively, they do not reverse themselves in another creation — for never in any creation does <s>brahmahatyā</s> become a cause of benefit and the <s>aśvamedha</s> [sacrifice] a cause of harm, nor does fire wet, nor does water burn — just so. Just as in this creation, Vedic study in the fixed sequential order is a cause of worldly prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>) and the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>), and otherwise [i.e., in wrong order] that very [study] becomes a cause of harm as a verbal thunderbolt — so too in other creations. And therefore, the omniscient and omnipotent [<s>Brahman</s>], composing the <s>Veda</s>s in conformity with each preceding creation, is not autonomous [in this matter]. And the followers of <s>Jaimini</s> too favor merely the non-autonomy of persons as <s>apauruṣeyatva</s> (non-human authorship). And that is the same for us as well — the [disagreement is merely due to] attachment to different [positions].

body.text:
na caikasya pratibhāne anāśvāsa iti yuktam /
na hi bahūnāmapyajñānāṃ vijñānāṃ vā āśayadoṣavatāṃ pratibhāne yukta āśvāsaḥ ; tattvajñānavatastvapāstasamastadoṣasyaikasyāpi pratibhāne yukta evāśvāsaḥ /
sargādibhuvāṃ ca prajāpatidevarṣīṇāṃ dharmajñānavairāgyaiśvaryasaṃpannānāmupapadyate tatsvarūpāvadhāraṇam ; tatpratyayena cārvācīnānāmapi tatra saṃpratyaya ityupapannaṃ brahmaṇaḥ śāstrayonitvam, śāstrasya cāpauruṣeyatvam, prāmāṇyaṃ ceti /
iti prathamavarṇakam /
body.translated_text: Nor is it reasonable [to object] that confidence is not warranted in the intuition of a single [person]. For indeed, confidence is not warranted even in the intuition of many — whether ignorant or knowledgeable — who are tainted by defects of disposition. But in the intuition of even a single person who has realized the truth and is free from all defects, confidence is well warranted. And it is reasonable that the <s>Prajāpati</s>s and divine sages — who are the beings of the [initial] creation and who are endowed with <s>dharma</s>, knowledge, dispassion, and sovereignty — ascertain the true form [of the <s>Veda</s>]. And through their conviction, the conviction of later [persons] too regarding that [<s>Veda</s>] is justified. Thus, the being-the-source-of-scripture (<s>śāstrayonitva</s>) of <s>Brahman</s>, the non-human authorship (<s>apauruṣeyatva</s>) of scripture, and its authoritativeness (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) — all are established. Thus ends the first section (<s>varṇaka</s>).

body.text:
varṇakāntaramārabhate- #atha vā#iti /
pūrveṇādhikaraṇena brahmasvarūpalakṣaṇāsaṃbhavāśaṅkāṃ vyudasya lakṣaṇasaṃbhava uktaḥ /
tasyaiva tu lakṣaṇasyānena anumānatvāśaṅkāmapākṛtya āgamopadarśanena brahmaṇi śāstraṃ pramāṇamuktam /
akṣarārthastu atirohitaḥ /
body.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] begins another section: 'Or alternatively' (<s>atha vā</s>). By the previous <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic), the doubt about the impossibility of a definition of the nature of <s>Brahman</s> was set aside, and the possibility of the definition was stated. By this [current section], rejecting the doubt that the definition is merely inferential (<s>anumānatva</s>), through the presentation of scriptural evidence, scripture is declared the authoritative means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) regarding <s>Brahman</s>. But the literal meaning [of the <s>sūtra</s>] remains concealed.

The scripture-being-the-means-of-knowledge regarding <s>Brahman</s> has been stated by mere assertion; it must be demonstrated by this <s>sūtra</s>. Therefore, the commentator (<s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>) raises an <s>ultra-sūtra</s> (from beyond the current <s>sūtra</s>) objection: 'But how then?' (<s>kathaṃ punaḥ</s>). What is the objection? — [It is this:] since <s>Brahman</s>, being an existing entity whose nature is pure, awakened, and indifferent, is to be disregarded, the <s>Vedānta</s>s — which speak of [such] an existing entity — would suffer the defect of purposelessness, since they would not teach what serves human ends. And since, being about existing entities, they would share the same subject-matter as perception and the like, there would be the consequence of non-authoritativeness, like mundane sentences that merely reiterate what is already known. For indeed, mundane sentences that communicate a meaning within the scope of another means of knowledge are not independently authoritative.

body.text:
evaṃ vedāntā apītyanapekṣatvalakṣaṇaṃ prāmāṇyameṣāṃ vyāhanyeta /
na ca tairapramāṇairbhavituṃ yuktam /
na cāprayojanaiḥ, svādhyāyādhyayanavidhyāpāditaprayojanavattvaniyamāt /
tasmāttattadvihitakarmāpekṣitakartṛdevatādipratipādanaparatvenaiva kriyārthatvam /
yadi tvasaṃnidhānāttatparatvaṃ na rocayante, tataḥ saṃnihitopāsanādikriyāparatvaṃ vā vedāntānām /
evaṃ hi pratyakṣādyanadhigatagocaratvenānapekṣatayā prāmāṇyaṃ ca prayojanavattvaṃ ca sidhyatīti tātparyārthaḥ /
pāramarṣasūtropanyāsaḥ tu pūrvapakṣadārḍhyāya /
body.translated_text: Similarly, even the <s>Vedānta</s>s [would suffer the same defect] — and thus their authoritativeness, characterized by independence, would be undermined. And it is not fitting for them to be non-authoritative. Nor [is it fitting for them to be] purposeless, since the injunction of self-study assigns a necessary purposefulness [to them]. Therefore, [the <s>Vedānta</s>s] have action-orientation (<s>kriyārthatva</s>) — being devoted to teaching the agent, deity, and the like that are required by the respective enjoined <s>karma</s>s. But if [one] is not inclined to accept that devotion [to action] due to the absence of proximity [to injunctions], then the <s>Vedānta</s>s are devoted to activities such as meditation (<s>upāsanā</s>) and the like that are proximate. For thus, authoritativeness — by not having the same subject-matter as perception and the like, and hence by being independent — and purposefulness are both established. This is the intended purport. But the adduction of the <s>sūtra</s> of <s>Jaimini</s> is for the strengthening of the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view).

body.text:
#ānarthakyaṃ#ca aprayojanavattvam, sāpekṣatayā pramānutpādakatvaṃ cānuvādakatvāditi /
#ataḥ#ityādi #vā#ntaṃ grahaṇakavākyam /
asya vibhāgabhāṣyaṃ #na hi#ityādi #upapannā vā#ityantam /
body.translated_text: 'Purposelessness' (<s>ānarthakyam</s>) means lacking purposefulness; and the production of non-independent cognition through being merely reiterative — this is the meaning. [The passage] from 'therefore' (<s>ataḥ</s>) to 'or' (<s>vā</s>) is the position-statement. The commentary on its division [begins with] 'For indeed' (<s>na hi</s>) and extends to 'or is it tenable' (<s>upapannā vā</s>).

body.text:
syādetat /
akriyārthatve 'pi brahmasvarūpavidhiparā vedāntā bhaviṣyanti ; tathā ca 'vidhinā tvekavākyatvāt-'
body.translated_text: One might say this: Even if not action-oriented, the <s>Vedānta</s>s will be devoted to the injunction of the essential nature of <s>Brahman</s>. And thus 'By being a single sentence with the injunction' (<s>vidhinā tvekavākyatvāt</s>) —

body.text:
iti rāddhāntasūtramanugrahīṣyate /
na khalvapravṛttapravartanameva vidhiḥ ; utpattividherajñātajñāpanārthatvāt ; vedāntānāṃ cājñātaṃ brahma jñāpayatāṃ tathābhāvāt , ityata āha- #na ca pariniṣṭhita#iti /
anāgatotpādyabhāvaviṣaya eva hi sarvo vidhirupeyaḥ, adhikāraviniyogaprayogotpattirūpāṇāṃ parasparamavinābhāvāt, siddhe ca teṣāmasaṃbhavāt /
tadvākyānāṃ tvaidaṃparyaṃ bhidyate /
yathā 'agnihotraṃ juhuyātsvargakāmaḥ' ityādibhyo 'dhikāraviniyogaprayogāṇāṃ pratilambhāt, 'agnihotraṃ juhoti' ityutpattimātraparaṃ vākyam /
na tvatra viniyogādayo na santi ; santo 'pyanyato labdhatvātkevalamavivakṣitāḥ /
tasmāt bhāvanāviṣayo vidhirna siddhe vastuni bhavitumarhatīti /
upasaṃharati- #tasmāt#iti /
body.translated_text:
Thus the established-conclusion <s>sūtra</s> will be taken up.
Surely an injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) is not merely the impelling of what has not [yet] commenced [to act]; for the purpose of an origination-injunction (<s>utpatti-vidhi</s>) is to make known what is unknown; and for the <s>Vedānta</s>s, which make known <s>Brahman</s> as hitherto unknown, it is just so. To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Not, however, regarding an established entity (<s>pariniṣṭhita</s>).'
For every injunction should be accepted as having as its domain a yet-to-arise, producible entity, since the [four aspects of an injunction] — qualification (<s>adhikāra</s>), connection (<s>viniyoga</s>), procedure (<s>prayoga</s>), and origination (<s>utpatti</s>) — are invariably concomitant with one another, and since they are impossible with respect to what is already established.
But the purport (<s>aidaṃparya</s>) of those [Vedāntic] sentences is differentiated [from injunctive ones].
Just as, from sentences like 'One who desires heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Agnihotra</s>' and the like, qualification, connection, and procedure are obtained; [so] the sentence '<s>agnihotraṃ juhoti</s>' (he offers the <s>Agnihotra</s>) has its purport solely in origination.
But it is not that connection and the like are absent here; though present, they are merely unexpressed because they are obtained from elsewhere.
Therefore, an injunction — whose domain is <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive action) — cannot apply to an already established entity.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] concludes: 'Therefore.'

body.text:
atrārucikāraṇamuktvā pakṣāntaramupasaṃkramate- #atha#iti /
evaṃ ca sati uktarūpe brahmaṇi śabdasyātātparyāt pramāṇāntareṇa yādṛśamasya rūpaṃ vyavasthāpyate na tacchabdena virudhyate ; tasyopāsanāparatvāt, samāropeṇa copāsanāyā upapatteriti /
prakṛtamupasaṃharati- #tasmānna#iti /
body.translated_text:
Having stated the reason for the unacceptability [of the injunctive interpretation], [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] moves to the alternative position: 'Now (<s>atha</s>)...'
And this being the case, since the scripture's purport is not directed at <s>Brahman</s> of the nature described — whatever nature of it is established by another means of knowledge, that is not contradicted by scripture; because [scripture] would then be directed toward meditation (<s>upāsanā</s>), and meditation is possible even through superimposition.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] concludes the topic at hand: 'Therefore not...'

body.text: sūtreṇa siddhāntayati- #ucyata#iti /
body.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] establishes the conclusion by means of the <s>sūtra</s>: 'It is said...'

body.text:
tadetadvyācaṣṭe- #tuśabda#iti /
tadityuttarapakṣapratijñāṃ vibhajate- #tadbrahma#iti /
pūrvapakṣī karkaśāśayaḥ pṛcchati- #katham#iti /
kutaḥ prakārādityarthaḥ /
siddhāntī svapakṣe hetuṃ prakārabhedamāha- #samanvayāt# /
samyaganvayaḥ samanvayaḥ ; tasmāt /
etadeva vibhajyate- #sarveṣu hi vedānteṣu#iti /
vedāntānāmaikāntikīṃ brahmaparatāmācikhyasurbahūni vākyānyudāharati- #sadeva#iti /
'yato vā imāni bhūtāni' iti tu vākyaṃ pūrvamudāhṛtaṃ jagadutpattisthitināśakāraṇamiti ceha smāritamiti na paṭhitam /
yena hi vākyamupakramyate yena copasaṃhriyate sa eva vākyārtha iti śābdāḥ /
yathopāṃśuyājavākye 'nūcoḥ puroḍāśayorjāmitādoṣasaṃkīrtanapūrvakopāṃśuyājavidhānena tatpratisamādhānopasaṃhāreṇa cāpūrvopāṃśuyājakarmavidhiparatā ekavākyatābalādāśritā, evamatrāpi 'sadeva somyedam' iti brahmopakramāt 'tattvamasi'
body.translated_text:
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] glosses this: 'The word <s>tu</s> (but)...'
The word 'that' distinguishes the proposition of the latter position. [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] analyzes it: 'That <s>Brahman</s>...'
The hard-hearted opponent asks: 'How?'
The meaning is: by what method?
The proponent states the reason and the distinction of method for his own position: 'Because of the harmonious purport (<s>samanvaya</s>).'
'<s>Samanvaya</s>' means proper (<s>samyak</s>) connection (<s>anvaya</s>); because of that.
This very [point] is analyzed: 'For in all the <s>Vedānta</s>s...'
Desiring to demonstrate the exclusive orientation of the <s>Vedānta</s>s toward <s>Brahman</s>, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] cites many sentences: '<s>Sadeva</s>' (Being alone) etc.
But the sentence 'from which indeed these beings [are born]' (<s>yato vā imāni bhūtāni</s>) — having been cited previously — is not cited here because its being the cause of the world's origin, subsistence, and dissolution was already recalled.
For that meaning which introduces a sentence and that which concludes it — that alone is the sentence-meaning, according to the linguists.
Just as in the <s>Upāṃśuyāja</s> passage — where, through the statement of the defect of consanguinity (<s>jāmitā</s>) between the two <s>Anucu</s> and <s>Puroḍāśa</s> oblations, followed by the prescription of the <s>Upāṃśuyāja</s> and the concluding resolution of that [defect] — the purport of the passage as a novel ritual prescription of the <s>Upāṃśuyāja</s> is adopted by the force of sentential unity — so too here, from the introductory [statement] '<s>Sadeva somyedamagra</s>' (Being alone, dear one, was this in the beginning), which introduces with <s>Brahman</s>, and the concluding 'You are That' (<s>tattvamasi</s>),

body.text:
iti ca jīvasya brahmātmanopasaṃhārāt tatparataiva vākyasya /
evaṃ vākyāntarāṇāmapi paurvāparyālocanayā brahmaparatvamavagantavyam /
na ca tatparatvasya dṛṣṭasya sati saṃbhave 'nyaparatā adṛṣṭā yuktā kalpayitum, atiprasaṅgāt /
na kevalaṃ kartṛparatā teṣāmadṛṣṭā, anupapannā cetyāha- #na ca teṣām#iti /
body.translated_text:
which concludes with the individual self (<s>jīva</s>) being identical with <s>Brahman</s> — the sentence is oriented precisely toward that [<s>Brahman</s>].
Similarly, the orientation of the other sentences toward <s>Brahman</s> should be understood through the examination of their beginning and end.
And when the orientation toward that [<s>Brahman</s>] has been observed, it is not reasonable to conjecture an unobserved orientation toward something else, when [the observed orientation] is possible — due to over-extension.
Not only is the orientation toward the agent [of meditation] unobserved in them, but it is also untenable — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Nor for them...'

body.text:
sāpekṣatvenāprāmāṇyaṃ pūrvapakṣabījaṃ smārayitvā dūṣayati- #na ca pariniṣṭhitavastusvarūpatve 'pi#iti /
ayamabhisaṃdhiḥ- puṃvākyanidarśanena hi bhūtārthatayā vedāntānāṃ sāpekṣatvamāśaṅkyate /
tatraivaṃ bhavān pṛṣṭo vyācaṣṭām,
body.translated_text:
Having recalled the seed of the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie position) — [namely,] non-authoritativeness due to dependence [on other means of knowledge] — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes it: 'Even though [<s>Brahman</s>] is of the nature of an established entity (<s>pariniṣṭhita-vastu</s>), nevertheless...'
The intent is this: Through the illustration of human statements (<s>puṃvākya</s>), the dependence of the <s>Vedānta</s>s is suspected on account of their having established entities as their content.
Therein, the honorable [opponent] is asked to explain,

body.text:
kiṃ puṃvākyānāṃ sāpekṣatā bhūtārthatvena, āho pauruṣeyatvena ? yadi bhūtārthatvena tataḥ pratyakṣādīnāmapi parasparāpekṣatvenāprāmāṇyaprasaṅgaḥ ; tānyapi hi bhūtārthānyeva /
atha puruṣabuddhipurvakatayā puṃvākyaṃ sāpekṣam, evaṃ tarhi atatpūrvakāṇāṃ vedāntānāṃ bhūtārthānāmapi nāprāmāṇyaṃ pratyakṣādīnāmiva niyatendriyaliṅgādijanmanām /
body.translated_text:
Is the dependence of human statements due to their having established entities as content, or due to their being authored by a person (<s>pauruṣeya</s>)? If due to their having established entities as content, then perception and the other [means of knowledge] too — being mutually dependent — would suffer the unwanted consequence of non-authoritativeness; for they too have established entities alone as their content.
But if human statements are dependent because they are preceded by the cognition of a person [i.e., person-authored], then for the <s>Vedānta</s>s — which are not preceded by that [personal cognition] and which have established entities as their content — there is no non-authoritativeness, just as there is none for perception and the like, which arise invariably from the senses, inferential marks, and the like.

body.text:
yadyucyeta- siddhe kilāpauruṣeyatve vedāntānāmanapekṣatayā prāmāṇyaṃ sidhyet ; tadeva tu bhūtārthatvena na sidhyati ; bhūtārthasya śabdānapekṣeṇa puruṣeṇa mānāntarataḥ śakyajñānatvādbuddhipūrvaṃ viracanopapatteḥ ; vākyatvādiliṅgakasya vedapauruṣeyatvānumānasyāpratyūhamutpatteḥ /
tasmātpauruṣeyatvena sāpekṣatvaṃ durvāram, na tu bhūtārthatvena /
kāryārthatve tu kāryasyāpūrvasya mānāntarāgocaratayā atyantānanubhūtapūrvasya tattvena samāropeṇa vā puruṣabuddhāvasamārohāt tadarthānāṃ vedāntānāmaśakyaracanatayā pauruṣeyatvābhāvādanapekṣaṃ pramāṇatvaṃ sidhyatīti prāmāṇyāya vedāntānāmapi kāryaparatvamātiṣṭhāmahe /
body.translated_text:
If it be said: Granted, if the authorlessness (<s>apauruṣeyatva</s>) of the <s>Vedānta</s>s were established, then by virtue of their independence, their authoritativeness would be established; but that very [authorlessness] is not established when they have established entities as their content; for since an established entity can be known by a person through another means of knowledge without depending on scripture, a person-preceded composition [of the text] is possible; and the inference of the <s>Veda</s>'s being authored by a person — based on evidence such as its being a sentence (<s>vākyatva</s>) — arises without obstruction.
Therefore, the dependence due to being person-authored is irremovable, but not [the dependence] due to having established entities as content.
But if [the <s>Vedānta</s>s] had as their content [something] to be produced (<s>kārya</s>) — the <s>apūrva</s> (unprecedented [entity]) — since [that <s>apūrva</s>], being beyond the reach of other means of knowledge, has never been experienced before, it cannot truly or even by superimposition arise in a person's mind; therefore, since the <s>Vedānta</s>s having it as their content cannot be composed [by anyone], by the absence of being person-authored, their independent authoritativeness is established — thus, for the authoritativeness of the <s>Vedānta</s>s too, we maintain their orientation toward something to be produced.

body.text: atra brūmaḥ- kiṃ punaridaṃ kāryamabhimatamāyuṣmataḥ yadaśakyaṃ puruṣeṇa jñātum ? apūrvamiti cet, hanta kutastyamasya liṅādyarthatvam ? tenālaukikena saṃgatisaṃvedanavirahāt ; lokānusārataḥ kriyāyā eva laukikyāḥ kāryatayā liṅāderavagamāt /
body.translated_text: To this we reply: What, pray, is this producible thing that your honor considers unknowable by a person? If [you say it is] the <s>apūrva</s> — well then, whence its being the meaning of the <s>liṅ</s> suffix and the like? Because there is no acquaintance with or apprehension of a connection with it, [<s>apūrva</s>] being supramundane; because the <s>liṅ</s> suffix and the like are understood from worldly usage as having [ordinary] action — which is mundane — as their producible meaning.

body.text:
'svargakāmo yajeta' iti sādhyasvargaviśiṣṭo niyojyo 'vagamyate ; sa ca tadeva kāryamavagacchati yatsvargānukūlam /
na ca kriyā kṣaṇabhaṅgurā āmuṣmikāya svargāya kalpata iti pāriśeṣyādvedata evāpūrve kārye liṅādīnāṃ saṃbandhagraha iti cet, hanta caityavandanādivākyeṣvapi svargakāmādipadasaṃbandhādapūrvakāryatvaprasaṅgaḥ ; tathā ca teṣāmapyaśakyaracanatvenāpauruṣeyatvāpātaḥ /
spaṣṭadṛṣṭena pauruṣeyatvena vā teṣāmapūrvārthatvapratiṣedhe vākyatvādinā liṅgena vedāntānāmapi pauruṣeyatvamanumitamityapūrvārthatā na syāt /
anyatastu vākyatvādīnāmanumānābhāmatvopapādane kṛtamapūrvārthatvenātra tadupapādakena /
upapāditaṃ cāpauruṣeyatvamasmābhirnyāyakaṇikāyām ; iha tu vistarabhayānnoktam /
body.translated_text:
From '<s>svargakāmo yajeta</s>' (one who desires heaven should sacrifice), the person to be enjoined is understood as qualified by the [heaven that is] to be attained; and he understands precisely that producible thing which is conducive to heaven.
Nor is [mere] action — being momentary — capable of producing heavenly [reward] in the next world; therefore, by elimination, the apprehension of the connection of the <s>liṅ</s> suffix and the like with the producible <s>apūrva</s> comes from the <s>Veda</s> alone — if [this is your argument], then even in sentences about worshipping a <s>caitya</s> (shrine) and the like, the unwanted consequence of being oriented toward the <s>apūrva</s> as producible [arises], due to the connection with words like '<s>svargakāma</s>' (one desiring heaven); and thus [there would follow] the unwanted consequence of those too being authorless.
Or, if their person-authoredness — which is clearly observed — negates their orientation toward the <s>apūrva</s>, then by the inferential mark of being a sentence (<s>vākyatva</s>) and the like, even the person-authoredness of the <s>Vedānta</s>s — being inferred — would mean that their orientation toward the <s>apūrva</s> should not obtain.
But if, from the other side, the non-evidential character of [the inference from] being a sentence and the like is established, then there is no need to establish it through the orientation toward the <s>apūrva</s>.
And the authorlessness has been established by us in the <s>Nyāyakaṇikā</s>; but here it is not stated out of fear of prolixity.

body.text:
tenāpauruṣeyatve siddhe bhūtārthānāmapi vedāntānāṃ na sāpekṣatayā prāmāṇyavighātaḥ /
na cānadhigatagantṛtā nāsti yena prāmāṇyaṃ na syāt, jīvasya brahmatāyā anyato 'nadhigamāt /
tadidamuktam - #na ca pariniṣṭhitavastusvarūpatva'pi#iti /
body.translated_text:
Therefore, when the authorlessness [of the <s>Veda</s>] is established, even for the <s>Vedānta</s>s that have established entities as their content, there is no obstruction of authoritativeness through dependence.
Nor is there an absence of conveying what is not otherwise known, such that there would be no authoritativeness — because the individual self's identity with <s>Brahman</s> is not ascertainable from any other [source].
This is what is stated: 'Even though [<s>Brahman</s>] is of the nature of an established entity...'

body.text:
dvitīyaṃ pūrvapakṣabījaṃ smārayitvā dūṣayati- #yattu heyopādeyarahitatvāt#iti /
vidhyarthāvagamāt khalu pāramparyeṇa puruṣārthapratilambhaḥ /
iha tu 'tattvamasi' ityavagatiparyantādvākyārthajñānāt bāhyānuṣṭhānāyāsānapekṣātsākṣādeva puruṣārthapratilambhaḥ, 'nāyaṃ sarpo rajjuriyam' iti jñānādiveti /
so 'yamasya vidhyarthajñānāt prakarṣaḥ /
body.translated_text:
Having recalled the second seed of the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> and refuting it, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Because [<s>Brahman</s>] is devoid of what is to be rejected and what is to be adopted (<s>heyopādeya</s>)...'
Indeed, from the understanding of an injunctive meaning, the attainment of the human goal (<s>puruṣārtha</s>) comes indirectly.
But here, from the knowledge of the sentence-meaning culminating in the realization of 'You are That' (<s>tattvamasi</s>) — directly, without depending on the effort of external performance — the human goal is attained, just as from the cognition 'This is not a snake, this is a rope.'
This is its superiority over the knowledge of an injunctive meaning.

body.text:
etaduktaṃ bhavati- dvividhaṃ hīpsitaṃ puruṣasya ; kiñcidaprāptam, yathā grāmādi ; kiñcitpunaḥ prāptamapi bhramavaśādaprāptamityavagatam, yathā svagrīvāvanaddhaṃ graiveyakam /
evaṃ jihāsitamapi dvividham ; kiñcidahīnaṃ jīhāsati, yathā valayitacaraṇaṃ phaṇinam ; kiñcitpunarhīnameva jihāsati, yathā caraṇābharaṇe nūpure phaṇinamāropitam /
tatrāprāptaprāptau cātyaktatyāge ca bāhyopāyānuṣṭhānasādhyatvāt tadupāyatattvajñānādasti parācīnānuṣṭhānāpekṣā /
na jātu jñānamātraṃ nastvapanayati /
na hi sahasramapi rajjupratyayā vastusantaṃ phaṇinamanyathayitumīśate /
samāropite tu prepsitajihāsite tattvasākṣātkāramātreṇa bāhyānuṣṭhānānapekṣeṇaiva śakyete prāptumiva hātumiva /
samāropamātrajīvite hi te ; samāropitaṃ ca tattvasakṣātkāraḥ samūlaghātamupahantīti /
tathehāpyavidyāsamāropitajīvabhāve brahmaṇyānande vastutaḥ śokaduḥkhādirahite samāropitanibandhanastadbhāvaḥ 'tattvamasi' iti vākyārthatattvajñānādavagatiparyantānnivartate /
tannivṛttau prāptamapyānandarūpamaprāptamiva prāptaṃ bhavati ; tyaktamapi śokaduḥkhādyatyaktamiva tyaktaṃ bhavati /
tadidamuktam - #brahmātmāvagamādeva#jīvasya sarvakleśasya savāsanasya viparyāsasya- sa hi kliśnāti jantūnataḥ kleśaḥ- tasya prakarṣeṇa hānāt #puruṣārthasya,#duḥkhanivṛttisukhāptilakṣaṇasya #siddheḥ#iti /
body.translated_text:
What is stated amounts to this: The desired of a person is of two kinds: something not [yet] attained, like a village and the like; and something already attained but understood as if not attained due to the force of delusion, like a necklace [already] fastened on one's own neck.
Likewise, what is desired to be abandoned is also of two kinds: something that has not [actually] departed, which one desires to abandon, like a coiled hooded serpent; and something that has [already] departed, which one desires to abandon, like a serpent superimposed upon an anklet.
Therein, for [actually] attaining what is not attained and for [actually] abandoning what has not departed, since they are accomplishable through the performance of external means, there is a need for performance subsequent to the knowledge of the truth regarding the means.
Mere knowledge never removes what exists.
For not even a thousand cognitions of 'rope' can alter a real serpent.
But when the desired [object] and the undesired [object] are superimposed, by the mere direct realization of reality — without depending on external performance — they can be attained as if [for the first time] and abandoned as if [for the first time].
For they have their life in superimposition alone; and superimposition is utterly destroyed by the direct realization of reality, root and all.
So too here: when the state of being a <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) — superimposed by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — is [attributed] to <s>Brahman</s>, which is in reality bliss and free from grief, suffering, and the like — the state of being a [suffering] entity, whose basis is superimposition, ceases through the knowledge of the reality of the sentence-meaning 'You are That' (<s>tattvamasi</s>), culminating in realization.
Upon the cessation of that, [<s>Brahman</s>'s] nature as bliss — though already attained — is attained as if [for the first time]; and grief, suffering, and the like — though already abandoned — are abandoned as if [for the first time].
This is what is stated: 'From the realization of <s>Brahman</s> as the Self alone' — of the <s>jīva</s>'s every affliction (<s>kleśa</s>), together with its latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) — the error (<s>viparyāsa</s>), for it afflicts beings and hence is called <s>kleśa</s> — its complete cessation constitutes 'the attainment of the human goal' — characterized by the cessation of suffering and the attainment of bliss — 'is established.'

body.text: yattu 'ātmetyevopāsīta', 'ātmānameva lokamupāsīta'
body.translated_text: But [one may object:] 'Meditate on [it] as the Self' (<s>ātmetyevopāsīta</s>), 'One should meditate on the Self alone as the world' (<s>ātmānameva lokamupāsīta</s>)

body.text: ityupāsanāvākyagatadevatādipratipādanenopāsanāparatvaṃ vedāntānāmuktaṃ taddūṣayati- #devatādipratipādanasya tu#
body.translated_text: — the claim that the <s>Vedānta</s>s are oriented toward meditation, through the teaching of deities and the like contained in meditation-sentences, is refuted by [<s>Śaṅkara</s>]: 'But regarding the teaching of deities and the like...'

body.text:
ātmetyetāvanmātrasya #svavākyagatopāsanārthatve 'pi na kaścidvirodhaḥ# /
yadi na virodhaḥ, santu tarhi vedāntā devatāpratipādanadvāreṇopāsanāvidhiparā evetyata āha- #na tu tathā brahmaṇa#iti /
upāsyopāsakopāsanādibhedasiddhyadhīnopāsanā na nirastasamastabhedaprapañce vedāntavedye brahmaṇi saṃbhavatīti nopāsanāvidhiśeṣatvaṃ vedāntānāṃ tadvirodhitvāt ityarthaḥ /
body.translated_text:
'Even if [the word] "Self" alone, to that extent, has the purpose of meditation contained in its own sentence, there is no conflict.'
If there is no conflict, then let the <s>Vedānta</s>s be oriented toward injunctions of meditation through the teaching of deities — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'But not thus regarding <s>Brahman</s>...'
The meaning is: Meditation — which depends for its establishment on the distinctions of the object of meditation, the meditator, the meditation, and the like — is not possible with respect to <s>Brahman</s> as known from the <s>Vedānta</s>s, in which all elaboration of distinctions has been negated; therefore, the <s>Vedānta</s>s cannot be subsidiary to an injunction of meditation, since they are in conflict with that.

body.text:
syādetat /
yadi vidhivirahe 'pi vedāntānāṃ prāmāṇyam, hanta tarhi 'so 'rodīt' ityādīnāmapyastu svatantrāṇāmevopekṣaṇīyārthānāṃ prāmāṇyam ; na hi hānopādānabuddhī eva prāmaṇasya phale, upekṣābuddherapi tatphalatvena prāmāṇikairabhyupetatvāt ; iti kṛtam 'barhiṣi rajataṃ na deyam' ityādiniṣedhavidhiparatvenaiteṣāmityata āha- #yadyapi#iti /
svādhyāyavidhyadhīnagrahaṇatayā hi sarvo vedarāśiḥ puruṣārthatantra ityavagatam /
tatraikenāpi varṇena nāpuruṣārthena bhavituṃ yuktam ; kiṃ punariyatā 'so 'rodīt' ityādinā padaprabandhena /
na ca vedāntebhya iva tadarthāvagamamātrādeva kaścitpuruṣārtha upalabhyate /
tenaiṣa padasaṃdarbhaḥ sākāṅkṣa evāste puruṣārthamudīkṣamāṇaḥ /
'barhiṣi rajataṃ na deyam' ityayamapi niṣedhavidhiḥ svaniṣedhyasya nindāmapekṣate ; na hyanyathā tataścetanaḥ śakyo nivartayitum /
tadyadi dūrato 'pi na nindāmavāpsyattato niṣedhavidhireva rajataniṣedhe ca nindāyāṃ ca darvihenatasvasya sāmarthyadvayamakalpayiṣyat /
tadevamuttaptayoḥ 'so 'rodīt' iti ca 'barhiṣi rajataṃ na deyam' iti ca padasaṃdarbhayorlakṣyamāṇanindādvāreṇa naṣṭāśvadagdharathavat parasparaṃ samanvayaḥ /
na tvevaṃ vedānteṣu puruṣārthāpekṣā, tadarthāvagamādevānapākṣātparamapuruṣārthalābhādityuktam /
body.translated_text:
One might say this:
If the <s>Vedānta</s>s have authoritativeness even without an injunction — well then, let even [passages like] '<s>so 'rodīt</s>' (he wept) and the like also have authoritativeness, though they are independent [of injunctions] and have meanings that are [seemingly] indifferent [i.e., not useful]. For the fruits of a means of knowledge are not solely the cognitions of acceptance and rejection; the cognition of indifference too is accepted by epistemologists as a fruit of a means of knowledge. So let those be [explained as] oriented toward prohibitions and injunctions [like] '<s>barhiṣi rajataṃ na deyam</s>' (silver should not be given on the sacrificial grass) — enough [with this objection]! To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Even if...'
For since, through the dependence [of the Veda] on the injunction of self-study, the entire body of the <s>Veda</s> is understood to be oriented toward the human goal (<s>puruṣārtha</s>).
Therein, it is not reasonable for even a single syllable to be without human purpose — how much more so for an entire passage like '<s>so 'rodīt</s>' and the like.
Nor is any human purpose obtained from them merely through the understanding of their meaning, as it is from the <s>Vedānta</s>s.
Therefore, this string of words remains expectant, looking for a human purpose.
And this prohibition '<s>barhiṣi rajataṃ na deyam</s>' (silver should not be given on the sacred grass) also requires the censure of its prohibited object; for otherwise, a conscious person cannot be turned away from it.
Now, if [the passage '<s>so 'rodīt</s>'] does not receive censure even remotely, then the prohibition-injunction alone, regarding both the prohibition of silver and the censure, would have attributed to itself a twofold capacity — like [the charioteer who has] lost his horse and [whose] chariot is burned.
Thus, when these two passages — '<s>so 'rodīt</s>' and '<s>barhiṣi rajataṃ na deyam</s>' — are both heated [i.e., pressed for interpretation], through the implied censure [conveyed by '<s>so 'rodīt</s>'], like [the proverb of] the lost horse and the burned chariot, there is a mutual syntactic connection.
But for the <s>Vedānta</s>s, there is no such need for a human purpose [beyond themselves], since from the very understanding of their meaning alone, the supreme human goal is obtained without remainder — this has been stated.

body.text:
nanu vidhyasaṃsparśino vedasyānyasya na prāmāṇyaṃ dṛṣṭamiti kathaṃ vedāntānāṃ tadaspṛśāṃ tadbhaviṣyatītyata āha- #na cānumānagamyaṃ#iti /
abādhitānadhigatāsaṃdigdhabodhajanakatvaṃ hi pramāṇatvaṃ pramāṇānām ; tacca svata ityupapāditam /
yadyapi caiṣāmīdṛgbodhajanakatvaṃ kāryārthāpattisamadhigamyam, tathāpi tadbodhopajanane mānāntaraṃ nāpekṣante nāpīmāmevārthāpattim, parasparāśrayaprasaṅgāditi svata ityuktam /
īdṛgbodhajanakatvaṃ ca kārye iva vidhīnām, vedāntānāmapi brahmaṇyastīti dṛṣṭāntānapekṣaṃ teṣāṃ brahmaṇi prāmāṇyaṃ siddhaṃ bhavati /
anyathā nendriyāntarāṇāṃ rūpaprakāśanaṃ dṛṣṭamiti cakṣurapi na rūpaṃ prakāśayediti /
prakṛtamupasaṃharati- #tasmāt#iti /
body.translated_text:
But one might object: no authority has been observed for a part of the <s>Veda</s> that is untouched by injunction — so how will that apply to the <s>Vedānta</s>s, which are untouched by injunction? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Nor is it knowable through inference.'
For the authority (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) of the means of knowledge consists in their capacity to generate un-sublated, previously-unattained, and undoubted cognition; and that [authority] is self-established (<s>svataḥsiddha</s>) — this has been demonstrated.
And although this capacity of theirs to generate such cognition is ascertained through the presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>) from the effect, nevertheless, in generating that cognition, they do not depend on another means of knowledge, nor on this very presumption — since that would lead to mutual dependence — hence [the authority] is said to be self-established.
And this capacity to generate such cognition exists in the <s>Vedānta</s>s regarding <s>Brahman</s>, just as it does in the injunctions regarding [ritual] action — thus their authority regarding <s>Brahman</s> is established without requiring a parallel example.
Otherwise, [one would have to say:] 'Since the manifestation of form has not been observed in other senses, the eye too does not manifest form' — [which is absurd].
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] concludes the topic at hand: 'Therefore.'

body.text:
ācāryaikadeśīyānāṃ matamutthāpayati- #atrāpare pratyavatiṣṭhante#iti /
tathā hi-
body.translated_text:
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises the view of those who are partial followers of the Teacher (<s>ācārya</s>): 'Here, others take a stand' — thus.
That is as follows —

body.text: ajñātasaṃgatitvena śāstratvenārthavattayā /
body.translated_text: Because the relation [of the Vedānta words with Brahman] is unknown, because of [the Vedānta's] being scripture, because of [its] purposefulness,

body.text: mananādipratītyā ca kāryārthadbrahmaniścayaḥ //
body.translated_text: And because of the cognition of meditation (<s>manana</s>) and the like — the ascertainment of <s>Brahman</s> has action (<s>kārya</s>) as its purpose. //

body.text:
na khalu vedāntāḥ siddhabrahmarūpaparā bhavitumarhanti, tatrāviditasaṃgatitvāt /
yatra hi śabdā lokena na prayujyante na tatra teṣāṃ saṃgatigrahaḥ /
na cāheyamanupādeyaṃ rūpamātraṃ kaścidvivakṣati prekṣāvān, tasyābubhutsitatvāt /
abubhutsitāvabodhane ca prekṣāvattāvidhātaḥ syāt /
tasmāt pratipitsitaṃ pratipipādayiṣannayaṃ lokaḥ pravṛttinivṛttihetubhūtamevārthaṃ pratipādayet, kāryaṃ cāvagate taddheturiti tadeva bodhayet /
evaṃ ca vṛddhaprayogāt padānāṃ kāryaparatāmavagacchati /
tatra kiñcitsākṣāt kāryābhidhāyakam, kiñcittu kāryārthasvārthābhidhāyakam, na tu bhūtārthaparatā padānām /
api ca narāntarasya vyutpannasyārthapratyayamanumāya tasya ca padaśabdabhāvābhāvānuvidhānamavagamyaya śabdasya tadviṣayabodhakatvaṃ niścetavyam /
na ca bhūtārtharūpamātrapratyaye paranaravartini kiñcilliṅgamasti /
kāryapratyaye tu narāntaravartini pravṛttinivṛttī sto hetū ityajñātasaṃgatitvānna brahmarūpaparā vedāntāḥ /
body.translated_text:
Surely the <s>Vedānta</s>s cannot be oriented toward the established nature of <s>Brahman</s>, because the relation [of words to meanings] therein is unknown.
For where words are not used by people [in ordinary discourse], the comprehension of their relation [to meanings] is not possible there.
Nor does any discerning person intend to communicate a mere form that is neither to be avoided nor adopted, since that is not desired to be known.
And in communicating what is not desired to be known, there would be a violation of the [speaker's] discerning nature.
Therefore, this [discerning] world, wishing to communicate what is desired to be known, would communicate only a meaning that is a cause of engagement or disengagement; and when an action is understood, its cause too [is understood] — so it is that alone that [the world] would communicate.
Thus, from the usage of the learned (<s>vṛddha</s>), one understands the orientation of words toward action (<s>kārya</s>).
Therein, some [words] directly denote action, while some denote their own meaning that serves the purpose of the action — but there is no orientation of words toward established facts (<s>bhūtārtha</s>).
Moreover, one must ascertain the communicative capacity of a word regarding its object by inferring the cognition of a meaning in another person who has [already] learned [the language], and by observing that [cognition's] conformity to the presence and absence of the word.
But there is no evidence (<s>liṅga</s>) in another person for a cognition of the mere form of an established fact.
However, in the case of a cognition of action in another person, engagement and disengagement serve as evidence — therefore, because the relation [of words to Brahman] is unknown, the <s>Vedānta</s>s are not oriented toward the nature of <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text:
api ca vedāntānāṃ vedatvācchāstratvaprasiddhirasti /
pravṛttinivṛttiparāṇāṃ ca padasaṃdarbhāṇāṃ śāstratvam /
yathāhuḥ-
body.translated_text:
Moreover, since the <s>Vedānta</s>s are part of the <s>Veda</s>, their being scripture (<s>śāstratva</s>) is well-established.
And it is textual sequences oriented toward engagement and disengagement that constitute scripture.
As they say —

body.text: pravṛttirvā nivṛttirvā nityena kṛtakena vā /
body.translated_text: Engagement or disengagement, whether with respect to something permanent or produced,

body.text: puṃsāṃ yenopadiśyeta tacchāstramabhidhīyate //
body.translated_text: That by which it is taught to people — that is called <s>śāstra</s> (scripture). //

body.text:
iti /
tasmācchāstratvaprasiddhyā vyāhatameṣāṃ svarūpaparatvam /
body.translated_text:
Thus.
Therefore, the orientation [of the Vedāntas] toward their own essential nature [of Brahman] is contradicted by their well-established status as scripture.

body.text:
api ca na brahmarūpapratipādanaparāṇāmeṣāmarthavattvaṃ paśyāmaḥ /
na ca 'rajjuriyaṃ na bhujaṅgaḥ' iti yathākathañcillakṣaṇayā vākyārthatattvaniścayādyathā bhayakampādinivṛttiḥ, evam 'tattvamasi' iti vākyārthāvagamānnivṛttirbhavati sāṃsārikāṇāṃ dharmāṇām. śrutavākyārthasyāpi puṃsasteṣāṃ tādavasthyāt /
body.translated_text:
Moreover, we do not see the purposefulness of these [Vedāntas] if they are oriented toward conveying the nature of <s>Brahman</s>.
And it is not the case that just as, from the sentence 'This is a rope, not a snake,' the ascertainment of the true meaning of the sentence — however figuratively — brings about the cessation of fear, trembling, and the like, so too from the comprehension of the sentence-meaning 'You are That' (<s>tattvamasi</s>), there is cessation of <s>saṃsāric</s> properties. For even for a person who has heard the sentence-meaning, those [saṃsāric properties] remain just as they were.

body.text:
api ca yadi śrutabrahmaṇo bhavati sāṃsārikadharmanivṛttiḥ kasmāt punaḥ śravaṇasyopari mananādayaḥ śrūyante ? tasmātteṣāṃ vaiyarthyaprasaṅgādapi na brahmasvarūpaparā vedāntāḥ, kiṃ tvātmapratipattiviṣayakāryaparāḥ /
tacca kāryaṃ svātmani niyojyaṃ niyuñjānaṃ niyoga iti ca mānāntarāpūrvatayāpūrvamiti cākhyāyate /
na ca viṣayānuṣṭhānaṃ vinā tatsiddhiriti svasiddhyarthaṃ tadeva kāryaṃ svaviṣayasya karaṇasyātmajñānasyānuṣṭhānamākṣipati /
yathā ca kāryaṃ svaviṣayādhīnanirūpaṇamiti jñānena viṣeyeṇa nirūpyate, evaṃ jñānamapi svaviṣayamātmānamantareṇāśakyanirūpaṇamiti tannirūpaṇāya tādṛśamātmānamākṣipati tadeva kāryam /
yathāhuḥ- 'yattu tatsiddhyarthamupādīyate ākṣipyate tadapi vidheyamiti tantre vyavahāraḥ' iti /
vidheyatā ca niyogaviṣayasya jñānasya bhāvārthatayānuṣṭheyatā ; tadviṣayasya tvātmanaḥ svarūpasattāviniścitiḥ /
body.translated_text:
Moreover, if the cessation of <s>saṃsāric</s> properties occurs for one who has heard [about] <s>Brahman</s>, why then are meditation (<s>manana</s>) and the like prescribed in scripture beyond hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>)? Therefore, because of the absurd consequence of their purposelessness, the <s>Vedānta</s>s are not oriented toward the essential nature of <s>Brahman</s>, but rather oriented toward an action (<s>kārya</s>) pertaining to the realization of the Self.
And that action is an injunction (<s>niyoga</s>) — a command enjoining [something] upon a person who is to be enjoined — and is called '<s>apūrva</s>' (unprecedented), since it is unprecedented by any other means of knowledge.
And without the performance of its content, it cannot be accomplished; hence for its own accomplishment, that very action implies the performance of its own content — the instrument of self-knowledge.
And just as an action is dependent on its content for its determination, and is thus determined by knowledge as its content, so too knowledge — being incapable of determination without its own content, i.e., the self — implies such a self for its determination; that very action [implies it].
As they say: 'That which is taken up or implied for the accomplishment of that [injunction] is also to be enjoined — such is the convention in the system.'
And the status of being enjoined consists in the performability of the knowledge — which is the content of the injunction — through its being a <s>bhāvārtha</s> (positive act); while the determination of its content, the self, consists in the ascertainment of its essential existence.

body.text:
āropitatadbhāvasya tvanyasya nirūpakatve tena tannirūpitaṃ na syāt /
tasmāttādṛgātmapratipattividhiparebhyo vedāntebhyaḥ tādṛgātmaviniścayaḥ /
tadetatsarvamāha- #yadyapi#iti /
vidhiparebhyo 'pi vastutattvaviniścaya ityatra vidarśanamuktam- #yathā yūpa#iti /
'yūpe paśuṃ badhnāti' iti bandhanāya viniyukte yūpe, tasyālaukikatvātko 'sau yūpa ityapekṣite 'khādiro yūpo bhavati', 'yūpaṃ takṣati', 'yūpamaṣṭāśrīkaroti' ityādibhirvākyaistakṣaṇādividhipapairapi saṃskārāviṣṭaṃ viśiṣṭasaṃsthānaṃ dāru yūpa iti gamyate /
evamāhavanīyādayo 'pyavagantavyāḥ /
pravṛttinivṛttiparasya śāstratvaṃ na svarūpaparasya, kārya eva ca saṃbandho na svarūpo, iti hetudvayaṃ bhāṣyavākyenopapāditam- #pravṛttinivṛttiprayojanatvāt#ityādinā #tatsāmānyādvedāntānāmapi tathaivārthavattvaṃ syāt#ityantena /
na ca svatantraṃ kāryaṃ niyojyamadhikāriṇamanuṣṭhātāramantareṇeti niyojyabhedamāha- #sati ca vidhiparatve#
body.translated_text:
But if the determination [of the self] were by something else upon which [the nature of the self] has been superimposed, then [the self] would not be truly determined by it.
Therefore, from the <s>Vedānta</s>s — which are oriented toward the injunction of such self-realization — comes the ascertainment of such a self.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states all of this: 'Although...' etc.
An illustration has been given for the point that even from [texts] oriented toward injunction, the ascertainment of the reality of a thing [is possible]: 'Just as [with] the sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>)' etc.
In 'One binds the sacrificial animal to the <s>yūpa</s>,' when the <s>yūpa</s> — being appointed for the binding — is [queried] 'What is this <s>yūpa</s>?' since it is not a worldly [term], from the sentences 'The <s>yūpa</s> is made of <s>khadira</s> wood,' 'One fashions the <s>yūpa</s>,' 'One makes the <s>yūpa</s> octagonal,' and the like — which are subsidiary injunctions of fashioning and the like — it is understood that the <s>yūpa</s> is a piece of wood that has been fashioned into a specific shape and sanctified by ritual preparation.
The <s>āhavanīya</s> [fire] and the like should be understood in the same way.
The two reasons — that scripture pertains to engagement and disengagement, not to essential nature, and that the relation [of words to established meanings] pertains only to action, not to essential nature — have been justified by the <s>Bhāṣya</s> statement beginning with 'because of its having engagement and disengagement as its purpose' and ending with 'so too, by analogy, the <s>Vedānta</s>s would have purposefulness.'
And since an independent action [i.e., an injunction] does not [exist] without a person to be enjoined who is to perform [it], [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the different [types of] persons to be enjoined: 'And if [the Vedāntas] are oriented toward injunction'

body.text:
iti /
'brahma veda brahmaiva bhavati' iti siddhavadarthavādādavagatasyāpi brahmabhavanasya niyojyaviśeṣākāṅkṣāyāṃ brahma bubhūṣorniyojyaviśeṣasya rātrisatranyāyena pratilambhaḥ /
piṇḍaputṛyajñānyāyena tu svargakāmasya niyojyasya kalpanāyāmarthavādasyāsamavetārthatayātyantaparokṣā vṛttiḥ syāditi /
brahmabhāvaścāmṛtatvamiti #amṛtatvakāmasya#ityuktam /
amṛtatvaṃ ca amṛtatvādeva na kṛtakatvena śakyamanityamanumātum, āgamavirodhāditi bhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text:
— thus.
From the <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passage) stating an established fact — 'One who knows <s>Brahman</s> becomes <s>Brahman</s> indeed' — even though the becoming-<s>Brahman</s> is understood, when there is an expectation for the specific person to be enjoined, the specific person to be enjoined — one who desires to become <s>Brahman</s> — is obtained through the principle of the night-long rite (<s>rātrisatra-nyāya</s>).
But if, by the principle of the <s>piṇḍapitṛyajña</s>, a person desiring heaven were to be postulated [as the one to be enjoined], then the <s>arthavāda</s> would have an extremely remote function, being one whose meaning has not been connected [with the injunction].
And the becoming-<s>Brahman</s> is immortality (<s>amṛtatva</s>) — hence [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] has said 'of one who desires immortality.'
And immortality, by virtue of being immortality itself, cannot be inferred as impermanent [i.e., produced], since that would contradict scripture — this is the purport.

body.text:
uktena dharmabrahmajijñāsayorvailakṣaṇyenana vidhyaviṣayatvaṃ codayati- #nanu#iti /
pariharati- #nārhatyevam#iti /
atra cātmadarśanaṃ na vidheyam /
taddhi dṛśerupalabdhivacanatvāt śrāvaṇaṃ vā syāt pratyakṣaṃ vā /
pratyakṣamapi laukikamahaṃpratyayo vā, bhāvanāprakarṣaparyantajaṃ vā /
tatra śrāvaṇaṃ na vidheyam, svādhyāyavidhinaivāsya prāpitatvāt, karmaśrāvaṇavat /
nāpi laukikaṃ pratyakṣam, tasya naisargikatvāt /
na caupaniṣadātmaviṣayaṃ bhāvanādheyavaiśadyaṃ vidheyam, tasyopāsanāvidhānādeva vājinavadanuniṣpāditatvāt /
tasmādaupaniṣadātmopāsanā amṛtatvakāmaṃ niyojyaṃ prati vidhīyate /
'draṣṭavyaḥ' ityādayastu vidhisarūpā na vidhaya iti /
tadidamuktam- #tadupāsanācca#iti /
body.translated_text:
Through the previously stated difference between the desires to know <s>dharma</s> and <s>Brahman</s>, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises the objection that [<s>Brahman</s>] is not the content of an injunction: 'But...' etc.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] resolves it: 'It does not deserve [to be so construed]' etc.
And here, the seeing of the Self (<s>ātmadarśana</s>) is not something to be enjoined.
For that [seeing], since the root '<s>dṛś</s>' (to see) has the meaning of apprehension, would be either scriptural [cognition] or perceptual [cognition].
Perceptual [cognition] too would be either the ordinary 'I'-cognition or that which arises at the culmination of meditative practice.
Among these, the scriptural [cognition] is not something to be enjoined, since it has already been obtained through the injunction of self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>) itself, just like the scriptural cognition of [ritual] action.
Nor is the ordinary perceptual [cognition] [to be enjoined], since that is innate (<s>naisargika</s>).
Nor is the clarity dependent on meditative practice (<s>bhāvanā</s>) to be enjoined regarding the <s>Upaniṣadic</s> Self, since that is already accomplished through the very injunction of meditation (<s>upāsanā</s>), like [the meditation on] horses (<s>vājina</s>) [in the <s>Aśvamedha</s>].
Therefore, the meditation on the <s>Upaniṣadic</s> Self is enjoined with respect to the person to be enjoined — one who desires immortality.
'It should be seen' (<s>draṣṭavyaḥ</s>) and the like, however, are merely injunction-like in form (<s>vidhisarūpa</s>), not [actual] injunctions — this is the meaning.
This is what was stated: 'And from meditation' etc.

body.text: arthavattyā mananādipratītyā cetyasya śeṣaḥ prapañco vidajavyākhyātaḥ /
body.translated_text: The elaboration of the remainder — [the arguments from] purposefulness and the cognition of meditation and the like — is explained by the running gloss (<s>nigadavyākhyāta</s>).

body.text:
tadekadeśimataṃ dūṣayati- #atrābhidhīyate-na#ekadeśimatam /
kutaḥ? #karmabrahmavidyāphalayorvailakṣaṇyāt# /
puṇyāpuṇyakarmaṇoḥ phale sukhaduḥkhe /
tatra manuṣyalokamārabhya ā brahmalokātsukhasya tāratamyamadhikādhikotkarṣaḥ /
evaṃ manuṣyalokamārabhya duḥkhatāratamyayā cāvīcilokāt /
tacca sarvaṃ kāryaṃ ca vināśi ca /
ātyantikaṃ tvaśarīratvamanatiśayaṃ svabhāvasiddhatayā nityamakāryamātmajñānasya phalam /
taddhi phalamiva phalam, avidyāpanayanamātreṇāvirbhāvāt /
etaduktaṃ bhavati- tvayāpyupāsanāvidhiparatvaṃ vedāntānāmabhyupagacchatā nityaśuddhabuddhatvādirūpabrahmātmatā jīvasya svābhāvikī vedāntagamyāsthīyate /
sā copāsanāviṣayasya vidherna phalam, nityatvādakāryatvāt /
nāpyanādyavidyāpidhānāpanayaḥ, tasya svavirodhividyodayādeva bhāvāt /
nāpi vidyodayaḥ, tasyāpi śravaṇamananapūrvakopāsanājanitasaṃskārasacivādeva cetaso bhāvāt /
upāsanāsaṃskāravadupāsanāpūrvamapi cetaḥsahakāri ; dṛṣṭaṃ ca khalu naiyogikaṃ phalamaihikamapi, yathā citrākārīryādiniyogānāmaniyataniyataphalānāmaihikaphaleti cet, na ; gāndharvaśāstrārthepāsanāvāsanāyā ivāpūrvānapekṣāyāḥ ṣaṭjādisākṣātkāre vedāntārthopāsanāvāsanāyā jīvasya brahmabhāvasākṣātkāre 'napekṣāyā eva sāmarthyāt /
tathā cāmṛtībhāvaṃ pratyahetutvādupāsanāpūrvasya nāmṛtatvakāmastatkāryamavaboddhumarhati /
body.translated_text:
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes the view of those partial followers: 'Here it is said: No' — [i.e.,] not the view of the partial followers.
Why? 'Because of the difference between the fruits of the knowledge of <s>karma</s> and of <s>Brahman</s>.'
The fruits of meritorious and demeritorious <s>karma</s> are pleasure and pain [respectively].
Therein, from the human world up to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>, there are increasingly higher degrees of pleasure.
Likewise, from the human world, with increasingly [greater degrees] of pain, up to the <s>Avīci</s> [hell].
And all of that is produced and perishable.
But the absolute state of being without a body (<s>aśarīratva</s>) — unsurpassable, naturally established and therefore eternal, unproduced — is the fruit of Self-knowledge.
For that fruit is like a fruit [only figuratively], since it manifests merely through the removal of the covering of <s>avidyā</s>.
What is stated amounts to this: Even you, who accept the orientation of the <s>Vedānta</s>s toward the injunction of meditation, accept that the individual self's (<s>jīva</s>'s) nature as the Self of <s>Brahman</s> — eternally pure, conscious, and the like — is naturally inherent and knowable from the <s>Vedānta</s>s.
And that [nature] is not the fruit of the injunction of meditation, since it is eternal and therefore unproducible.
Nor is [it produced by] the removal of the covering of beginningless <s>avidyā</s>, since that [removal] occurs only through the arising of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) that is opposed to it.
Nor is the arising of <s>vidyā</s> [the fruit], since that too occurs only through the mind's being assisted by the impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) generated by meditation preceded by hearing and reflection.
The pre-meditation [activities] too, like the impressions of meditation, are auxiliaries of the mind. And it is indeed observed that a proximate fruit [can be] mundane — just as for those obligatory rites such as painting and the like that have an unspecified or specified worldly fruit. If one objects that [the fruit is] mundane, [we reply:] No — because of the capacity of the impression (<s>vāsanā</s>) of the contemplation of the meaning of <s>Vedānta</s> to produce the direct realization of the individual self's nature as <s>Brahman</s>, independently of <s>apūrva</s> (unseen potency), just as the impression of contemplation of the science of music (<s>gāndharva-śāstra</s>) [produces] the direct perception of the notes beginning with <s>ṣaḍja</s>.
And thus, since it is not the cause of the attainment of immortality, the <s>apūrva</s> of meditation is not fit for one who desires immortality to comprehend as its effect.

body.text:
anyadicchatyanyatkarotīti hi vipratiṣiddham /
na ca tatkāmaḥ kriyāmeva kāryamavagamiṣyati nāpūrvamiti sāṃpratam ; tasyā mānāntarādeva tatsādhanatvapratītervidhervaiyarthyāt /
na cāvaghātādividhitulyatā, tatrāpi niyamāpūrvasyānyato 'navagateḥ /
na ca brahmabhūyādanyadamṛtatvamārthavādikaṃ kiñcidasti, yena tatkāma upāsanāyāmadhikriyeta /
viśvajinnyāyena tu svargakalpanāyāṃ tasya sātiśayatvaṃ kṣayiṣṇutvaṃ ceti na nityaphalatvamupāsanāyāḥ /
tasmādbrahmabhūyasyāvidyāpidhānāpanayamātreṇāvirbhāvāt, avidyāpanayasya ca vedāntārthavijñānādavagatiparyantādeva saṃbhavāt, upāsanāyāḥ saṃskārahetubhāvasya saṃskārasya ca sākṣātkāropajanane manaḥsācivyasya ca mānāntarasiddhatvāt. 'ātmetyevopāsīta' iti na vidhiḥ ; api tu vidhisarūpo 'yam ; yathopāṃśuyājavākye 'viṣṇurupāṃśu yaṣṭavyaḥ' ityādayo vidhisarūpā na vidhayaḥ-iti tātparyārthaḥ /
#śrutismṛtinyāyaprasiddham#ityuktam /
tatra śrutiṃ darśayati- #tathā ca śrutiḥ#iti /
nyāyamāha- #ata eva#iti /
yatkila svābhāvikaṃ tannityam, yathā caitanyam ; svābhāvikaṃ cedam ; tasmānnityam /
body.translated_text:
'He desires one thing and does another' — this is indeed contradictory.
Nor is it appropriate [to say] that such a desirer will understand merely the action as what is to be done, and not the <s>apūrva</s> — since the awareness that [action] is a means to that [fruit] comes from another means of knowledge itself, [rendering] the injunction purposeless.
Nor is there parity with injunctions such as killing (<s>avaghāta</s>) and the like, since even there, the restrictive <s>apūrva</s> is not knowable from any other [source].
Nor is there any other <s>arthavāda</s>-based (laudatory) [notion of] immortality, different from becoming <s>Brahman</s>, by which one desiring that [lesser immortality] would be qualified for meditation.
But if, by the principle of the <s>Viśvajit</s> [sacrifice], a desire for heaven were to be postulated, then [that fruit] would be surpassable and perishable — so meditation would not have an eternal fruit.
Therefore, since the becoming-<s>Brahman</s> manifests merely through the removal of the covering of <s>avidyā</s>; since the removal of <s>avidyā</s> is possible through the realization of the meaning of <s>Vedānta</s> — which culminates in understanding alone; since the causal role of meditation is as a generator of impressions, and the impressions' [role is] as an auxiliary of the mind in producing direct realization — [all of which] are established by other means of knowledge — 'One should meditate on the Self as the Self' (<s>ātmetyevopāsīta</s>) is not an injunction; rather, it is injunction-like in form. Just as, in the <s>upāṃśuyāja</s> sentence, 'One should sacrifice to <s>Viṣṇu</s> with the <s>upāṃśu</s> [offering]' and the like are injunction-like in form, not [actual] injunctions — this is the purport.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] has said: '[This is] well-established in <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, and reasoning.'
Therein, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] shows the <s>Śruti</s>: 'And thus the <s>Śruti</s>' etc.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the reasoning: 'For this very reason' etc.
Namely: whatever is natural (<s>svābhāvika</s>) is eternal, like consciousness; and this [nature as Brahman] is natural; therefore it is eternal.

body.text:
pare hi dvayīṃ nityatāmāhuḥ-kūṭasthanityatā pariṇāminityatāṃ ca /
tatra nityamityukte mā bhūdasya pariṇāminityatetyāha- #tatra kiñcit#iti /
pariṇāminityatā hi na pāramārthikī /
tathā hi-tatsarvātmanā vā pariṇamate ekadeśena vā ? sarvātmanā pariṇāme kathaṃ na tattvavyāhṛtiḥ ? ekadeśapariṇāme vā sa ekadeśastato bhinno vā abhinno vā ? bhinnaścet kathaṃ tasya pariṇāmaḥ ? na hyanyasmin pariṇamamāne 'nyaḥ pariṇamati, atiprasaṅgāt /
abhede vā kathaṃ na sarvātmanā pariṇāmaḥ ?
body.translated_text:
For others speak of a twofold eternality: the eternality of the immutable (<s>kūṭastha-nityatā</s>) and the eternality of the transforming (<s>pariṇāmi-nityatā</s>).
Therein, lest [<s>Brahman</s>] have the eternality of the transforming, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Therein, something...' etc.
For the eternality of the transforming is not ultimately real.
That is as follows: Does it transform in its entirety or in part? If it transforms in its entirety, how is there no contradiction with its essential nature? Or if it transforms in part, is that part different from it or non-different? If different, how is that its transformation? For when one thing transforms, another does not transform — [that would lead to] over-extension.
Or, if non-different, how is there not transformation in its entirety?

body.text:
bhinnābhinnaṃ taditi cet ; tathā hi-tadeva kāraṇātmanābhinnam, bhinnaṃ ca kāryātmanā, kaṭakādaya ivābhinnā hāṭakātmanā bhinnāśca kaṭakādyātmanā /
na ca bhedābhedayorvirodhānnaikatra samavāya iti yuktam /
viruddhamiti naḥ kva saṃpratyayaḥ ? yatpramāṇaviparyayeṇa vartate /
yattu yathā pramāṇenāvagamyate tasya tathābhāva eva /
'kuṇḍalamidaṃ suvarṇam' iti sāmānādhikaraṇyapratyaye vyaktaṃ bhedābhedau cakāstaḥ ; tathā hi-ātyantike 'bhede 'nyatarasya dviravabhāsaprasaṅgaḥ ; bhede cātyantike na sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ gavāśvavat ; ādhārādheyabhāve ekāśrayatve vā na sāmānādhikaraṇyam ; na hi bhavati kuṇḍaṃ badaramiti ; nāpyekāsanasthayoścaitramaitrayoścaitro maitra iti ; so 'yamabādhito 'saṃdigdhaḥ sarvajanīnaḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyapratyaya eva kāryakāraṇayorbhedābhedau vyavasthāpayati ; tathā ca kāryāṇāṃ kāraṇātmatvāt kāraṇasya ca sadrūpasya sarvatrānugamāt, sadrūpeṇābhedaḥ kāryasya jagataḥ ; bhedaḥ kāryarūpeṇa goghaṭādineti ; yathāhuḥkāryarūpeṇa nānātvamabhedaḥ kāraṇātmanā /
body.translated_text:
If it be said that it [the effect] is both different and non-different [from the cause] — for thus: it is non-different from the cause insofar as it has the nature of the cause, and different insofar as it has the nature of the effect — just as bracelets and the like are non-different insofar as they have the nature of gold, and different insofar as they have the nature of bracelets etc.
Nor is it reasonable [to say] that because difference and non-difference are contradictory, they cannot co-inhere in one thing.
Contradictory — where do we have this conviction? In that which obtains contrary to the means of knowledge.
But that which is apprehended just as it is by a means of knowledge — its being thus is [established] precisely so.
In the co-referential cognition (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya-pratyaya</s>) 'this earring is gold,' both difference and non-difference are clearly manifest. For thus: if there were absolute non-difference, one of the two would appear twice [redundantly]; and if there were absolute difference, there would be no co-referentiality, as with a cow and a horse; nor is there co-referentiality in a container-contained relation or in a single-substrate relation — for one never says 'the bowl is the jujube [fruit]'; nor do two persons sitting on one seat [warrant saying] '<s>Caitra</s> is <s>Maitra</s>.'
This unsublated, undoubted, universally recognized co-referential cognition alone establishes both difference and non-difference of cause and effect. And thus, since effects have the nature of the cause, and since the cause in the form of Being (<s>sat</s>) pervades all [effects], the world as effect is non-different from [its cause] in the form of Being; and different in the form of the effect — cow, pot, and the like. As they say: 'Multiplicity in the form of the effect; non-difference in the nature of the cause;

body.text: hemātmanā yathābhedaḥ kuṇḍalādyātmanā bhidā //
body.translated_text: Just as non-difference in the nature of gold, and difference in the nature of earring and the like.' //

body.text: iti /
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text:
atrocyate-kaḥ punarayaṃ bhedo nāma, yaḥ sahābhedenaikatra bhavet ? parasparābhāva iti cet, kimayaṃ kāryakāraṇayoḥ kaṭakahāṭakayorasti na vā ? na cet, ekatvamevāsti, na ca bhedaḥ /
asti cet bheda eva, nābhedaḥ /
na ca bhāvābhāvayoravirodhaḥ, sahāvasthānāsaṃbhavāt /
saṃbhave vā kaṭakavardhamānayorapi tattvenābhedaprasaṅgaḥ, bhedasyābhedāvirodhāt /
api ca kaṭakasya hāṭakādabhede yathā hāṭakātmanā kaṭakamukuṭakuṇḍalādayo na bhidyante evaṃ kaṭakātmanāpi na bhidyeran, kaṭakasya hāṭakādabhedāt /
tathā ca hāṭakameva vastusat na kaṭakādayaḥ, bhedasyāpratibhāsanāt /
body.translated_text:
To this we reply: What, then, is this 'difference' that would coexist with non-difference in one thing? If [you say] it is mutual absence (<s>parasparābhāva</s>) — does this mutual absence exist between the cause and effect, the bracelet and gold, or not? If not, then there is only identity, and no difference.
If it does exist, then there is only difference, and no non-difference.
Nor is there non-contradiction between existence and non-existence [of difference], since their co-existence is impossible.
Or, if [their] co-existence [were] possible, then even a bracelet and a <s>vardhamāna</s> [ornament] would, in reality, be non-different — since difference would not contradict non-difference.
Moreover, if the bracelet is non-different from gold, then just as bracelets, crowns, earrings, and the like are not different from one another insofar as they have the nature of gold, so too they should not be different insofar as they have the nature of a bracelet — since the bracelet is non-different from gold.
In that case, gold alone would be the real entity, not bracelets and the like, since difference would not manifest.

body.text: atha hāṭakatvenaivābhedo na kaṭakatvena ; tena tu bheda eva kuṇḍalādeḥ /
body.translated_text: If [it be said that] non-difference is only insofar as [they have] the nature of gold, not insofar as [they have] the nature of a bracelet; and in the latter respect, there is only difference of earring and the like [from the bracelet] —

body.text:
yadi hāṭakādabhinnaḥ kaṭakaḥ kathamayaṃ kuṇḍalādiṣu nānuvartate ? nānuvartate cet kathaṃ hāṭakādabhinnaḥ kaṭakaḥ ? ye hi yasminnanuvartamāne vyāvartante te tato bhinnā eva, yathā sūtrātkusumabhedāḥ /
nānuvartante cānuvartamāne 'pi hāṭakatve kuṇḍalādayaḥ ; tasmātte 'pi hāṭakādbhinnā eveti /
sattānuvṛttyā ca sarvavastvanugame 'idamiha nedam, idamevaṃ nedam' iti vibhāgo na syāt, kasyacit kvacit kadācit kathañcidvivekahetorabhāvāt /
api ca dūrātkanakamityavagate na tasya kuṇḍalādayo viśeṣā jijñāsyeran, kanakādabhedātteṣām, tasya ca jñātatvāt /
body.translated_text:
If the bracelet is non-different from gold, how does it not persist in earrings and the like? And if it does not persist, how is the bracelet non-different from gold? For those things that disappear when something [else] persists are different from it — just as flowers are different from the thread [of a garland].
And earrings and the like do not persist even when the nature of gold persists; therefore they too are different from gold.
And if, by the persistence of Being (<s>sattā</s>), all things would be pervaded [equally], the distinction 'this is here, not that; this is thus, not that' would not exist — since there would be no ground for discrimination of anything from anything at any time or in any way.
Moreover, if one apprehends from a distance 'this is gold,' the particular forms of it — earring and the like — would not be desired to be known, since they are non-different from gold and [gold] is already known.

body.text: atha bhedo 'pyasti kanakāt kuṇḍalādīnāmiti kanakāvagame 'pyajñātāste /
body.translated_text: If [it be said that] there is also difference of earrings and the like from gold — then even when gold is known, they remain unknown.

body.text:
nanvabhedo 'pyastīti kiṃ na jñātāḥ ? pratyuta jñānameva teṣāṃ yuktam ; kāraṇābhāve hi kāryabhāva autsargikaḥ ; sa ca kāraṇasattayā apodyate /
asti cābhede kāraṇasatteti kanake jñāte jñātā eva kuṇḍalādaya iti tajjijñāsājñānāni cānarthakāni syuḥ /
tena yasmin gṛhyamāṇe yanna gṛhyate tattato bhidyate ; yathā karabhe gṛhyamāṇe 'gṛhyamāṇe rāsabhaḥ karabhāt /
gṛhyamāṇe ca dūrato hemni na gṛhyante tasya bhedāḥ kuṇḍalādayaḥ ; tasmātte hemno bhidyante /
body.translated_text:
One might say: But non-difference also exists — so why are they not known? On the contrary, their being known is exactly what is reasonable. For in the absence of a cause [of non-existence], the non-existence of an effect is the general rule; and that [general rule of non-existence] is removed by the existence of a cause.
And since, given non-difference, the cause's existence [as known entails the effect's being known], when gold is known, earrings and the like are known; and thus the desires to know and the cognitions regarding them would be purposeless.
Therefore, whatever is not cognized when something else is being cognized — that is different from it. Just as, when a young camel is being cognized, a donkey that is not being cognized is different from the young camel.
And when gold is cognized from a distance, its particular forms — earrings and the like — are not cognized; therefore they are different from gold.

body.text:
kathaṃ tarhi hema kuṇḍalamiti sāmānādhikaraṇyam iti cet, na hyādhārādheyabhāve samānāśrayatve vā vā sāmānādhikaraṇyamityuktam /
athānuvṛttivyāvṛttivyavasthā ca hemni jñāte kuṇḍalādijijñāsā ca katham ? na khalvabhede aikāntike 'naikāntike caitadubhayamupapadyate ityuktam /
tasmādbhedābhedayoranyatarasminnavaheye 'bhedo pādānaiva bhedakalpanā, na bhedopādānābhedakalpaneti yuktam /
