bhidyamānatantratvādbhedasya, bhidyamānānāṃ ca pratyekamekatvāt, ekābhāve cānāśrayasya bhedasyāyogāt, ekatvasya ca bhedānadhīnatvāt, nāyamayaṃ iti ca bhedagrahasya pratiyogigrahasāpekṣatvāt, ekatvagrahasya cānyānapekṣatvāt, abhedopādānaivānirvacanīyabhedakalpaneti sāṃpratam /
tathā ca śrutiḥ 'mṛttiketyeva satyam' iti /
tasmāt kūṭasthanityataiva pāramārthikī. na pariṇāminityateti siddham /
body.translated_text:
If it be asked: How then is there the co-referentiality 'gold is an earring'? — [the answer is:] it has already been said that co-referentiality does not [require] a container-contained relation or a single-substrate relation.
And how would the arrangement of persistence and exclusion, and the desire to know earrings etc. when gold is already known, [be explained]? For it has been said that in neither absolute non-difference nor [mere] non-absolute [non-difference] are both of these possible.
Therefore, when one of the two — difference and non-difference — must be adopted, it is reasonable to adopt non-difference [as primary] and postulate [a merely apparent] difference — not to adopt difference [as primary] and postulate [a merely apparent] non-difference.
Because difference depends on what is differentiated, and each differentiated thing is individually one, and in the absence of oneness, difference — being without a substrate — is impossible; and because oneness is independent of difference; and because the apprehension of difference — 'this is not this' — requires the apprehension of a counter-correlate, while the apprehension of oneness does not require another — therefore, [the position that] upon the basis of non-difference, an indescribable (<s>anirvacanīya</s>) difference is postulated, is correct.
And thus the <s>Śruti</s>: 'Clay alone is the reality' (<s>mṛttiketyeva satyam</s>).
Therefore, it is established that immutable eternality (<s>kūṭastha-nityatā</s>) alone is ultimately real, not the eternality of transformation (<s>pariṇāmi-nityatā</s>).

body.text:
#vyomavat#iti ca dṛṣṭāntaḥ parasiddhaḥ, asmanmate tasyāpi kāryatvenānityatvāt /
atra ca #kūṭasthanityam#iti nirvartyakarmatāmapākaroti /
#sarvavyāpi#iti prāpyakarmatām /
#sarvavikriyārahitam#iti vikāryakarmatām /
#niravayavam#iti saṃskāryakarmatām /
vrīhīṇāṃ khalu prokṣaṇena saṃskārākhyoṃ'śo yathā janyate, naivaṃ brahmaṇi kaścidaṃśaḥ kriyādheyo 'sti, anavayavatvāt ; anaṃśatvādityarthaḥ /
puruṣārthatāmāha- #nityatṛptam#iti /
tṛptyā duḥkharahitaṃ sukhamupalakṣayati /
kṣudduḥkhanivṛttisahitaṃ hi sukhaṃ tṛptiḥ /
sukhaṃ cāpratīyamānaṃ na puruṣārtha ityata āha-
body.translated_text:
'Like space' — and this illustration is established [only] from the opponent's standpoint; in our view, even that [space] is a product and hence non-eternal.
Here, 'immutably eternal' (<s>kūṭastha-nitya</s>) — by this, the status of being a producible object (<s>nirvartya-karmatā</s>) is refuted.
'All-pervading' (<s>sarvavyāpī</s>) — by this, the status of being an attainable object (<s>prāpya-karmatā</s>) [is refuted].
'Devoid of all transformation' (<s>sarva-vikriyā-rahita</s>) — by this, the status of being a modifiable object (<s>vikārya-karmatā</s>) [is refuted].
'Without parts' (<s>niravayava</s>) — by this, the status of being a refinable object (<s>saṃskārya-karmatā</s>) [is refuted].
For just as in rice-grains, through sprinkling (<s>prokṣaṇa</s>), a portion called refinement (<s>saṃskāra</s>) is produced — no such portion is possible in <s>Brahman</s>, since it is without parts; meaning: because it is without constituent elements.
He states [<s>Brahman</s>'s] nature as a human goal (<s>puruṣārtha</s>): 'Eternally satisfied' (<s>nitya-tṛpta</s>).
By 'satisfaction' (<s>tṛpti</s>), happiness that is free from suffering is indicated.
For satisfaction is happiness accompanied by the cessation of the suffering of hunger.
And happiness, if not experienced, would not be a human goal — therefore he says:

body.text: #svayañjyotiḥ#iti /
body.translated_text: 'Self-luminous' (<s>svayañjyotiḥ</s>).

body.text: tadevaṃ svamatena mokṣākhyaṃ phalaṃ nityaṃ śrutyādibhirupapādya kriyāniṣpādyasya tu mokṣasyānityatvaṃ prasañjayati-
body.translated_text: Having thus established by his own view (<s>svamata</s>) that the fruit called liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) is eternal, [supported] by <s>Śruti</s> and the like, he raises the consequence of impermanence for liberation that would be produced by action:

body.text:
#tadyadi#iti /
na cāgamabādhaḥ, āgamasyoktena prakāreṇopapatteḥ /
api ca jñānajanyāpūrvajanito mokṣo naiyogika ityasyārthasya santi bhūyasyaḥ śrutayo nivārikā ityāha- #api ca brahma veda#iti /
avidyādvayapratibandhāpanayamātreṇa ca vidyāyā mokṣasādhanatvam, na svato 'pūrvotpādena vā ityatrāpi śrutirudāharati- #tvaṃ hi naḥ pitā#iti /
na kevalamasminnarthe śrutyādayaḥ, api tvakṣapādācāryasūtramapi nyāyamūlamastītyāha- #tathā cācāryapraṇītam#iti /
ācāryaścoktalakṣaṇaḥ purāṇe-
body.translated_text:
'If that [liberation were produced]' — [this is the objection].
Nor is there contradiction with scripture (<s>āgama</s>), since scripture is supported by the method stated.
Moreover, there are numerous <s>Śruti</s> passages that refute the position that liberation, produced by an <s>apūrva</s> (unseen potency) generated by knowledge, is a necessary consequence [of action] — thus he says: 'Moreover, one who knows <s>Brahman</s>...'
And <s>vidyā</s>'s (knowledge's) being the means to liberation consists merely in the removal of the obstruction of the twofold <s>avidyā</s>, not through its own [power] or through the production of an <s>apūrva</s> — for this too he cites a <s>Śruti</s>: 'For You are our father...'
Not only <s>Śruti</s>s and the like [support this] in this matter; there is also a <s>sūtra</s> authored by the <s>Ācārya</s> (teacher) that serves as the foundation of logic — thus he says: 'And thus the <s>sūtra</s> composed by the <s>Ācārya</s>...'
And the <s>Ācārya</s> of the stated characteristics [is defined] in the <s>Purāṇa</s>:

body.text: ācinoti ca śāstrārthamācāre sthāpayatyapi /
body.translated_text: He gathers (<s>ācinoti</s>) the meaning of the <s>śāstra</s>s; he establishes [them] in practice (<s>ācāra</s>);

body.text: svayamācarate yasmādācāryastena cocyate //
body.translated_text: Since he himself practices [what he teaches] — therefore he is called an <s>ācārya</s>. //

body.text:
iti /
tena hi praṇītaṃ sūtram-'duḥkhajanmapravṛttidoṣamithyājñānānāmuttarottarāpāye tadanantarāpāyādapavargaḥ' iti /
pāṭhāpekṣayā kāraṇamuttaram, kāryaṃ ca pūrvam ; kāraṇāpāye kāryāpāyaḥ, kaphāpāye iva kaphodbhavasya jvarasyāpāyaḥ /
janmāpāye daḥkhāpāyaḥ ; pravṛttyapāye janmāpāyaḥ ; doṣāpāye pravṛttyapāyaḥ ; mithyājñānāpāye doṣāpāyaḥ /
mithyājñānaṃ cāvidyā rāgādyupajananakrameṇa dṛṣṭenaiva saṃsārasya paramaṃ nidānam /
sā ca tattvajñānena brahmātmaikatvavijñānenaivāvagatiparyantena virodhinā nivartyate /
tato 'vidyānivṛttyā brahmasvarūpāvirbhāvo mokṣaḥ ; na tu vidyākāryastajjanitāpūrvakāryo vā- iti sūtrārthaḥ /
tattvajñānānmithyājñānāpāya ityetāvanmātreṇa sūtropanyāsaḥ ; na tvakṣapādasaṃmataṃ tattvajñānamiha saṃmatam /
tadanenācāryāntarasaṃvādenāyamartho dṛḍhīkṛtaḥ /
body.translated_text:
Thus.
For the <s>sūtra</s> composed by him [<s>Akṣapāda</s>/<s>Gautama</s>] states: 'Through the successive cessation of suffering, birth, activity, defect, and false knowledge — each being removed upon the removal of the one following it — there is liberation (<s>apavarga</s>).'
According to the order of the text, the later [in the list] is the cause, and the earlier is the effect; upon the cessation of the cause, the effect ceases — like the cessation of fever produced by phlegm upon the cessation of phlegm.
Upon the cessation of birth, the cessation of suffering [follows]; upon the cessation of activity, the cessation of birth; upon the cessation of defect, the cessation of activity; upon the cessation of false knowledge, the cessation of defect.
And false knowledge is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), which — through the sequence of giving rise to passions (<s>rāga</s>) and the like — is the ultimate root cause of <s>saṃsāra</s> as directly observed.
And that [<s>avidyā</s>] is removed by its opposite — the knowledge of reality, i.e., the realization of the identity of <s>Brahman</s> and the Self, culminating in direct experience (<s>avagati</s>).
Thereupon, through the removal of <s>avidyā</s>, the manifestation of <s>Brahman</s>'s own nature is liberation; it is neither the product of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) nor the product of an <s>apūrva</s> generated by it — this is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>.
The <s>sūtra</s> is cited merely to the extent that 'through the knowledge of reality, the cessation of false knowledge [follows]'; it is not that the view of reality accepted by <s>Akṣapāda</s> is accepted here.
By this concordance with another <s>Ācārya</s>, this meaning is strengthened.

body.text:
syādetat /
naikatvavijñānaṃ yathāvasthitavastuviṣayam, yena mithyājñānaṃ bhedāvabhāsaṃ nivartayanna vidhiviṣayo bhavet ; api tu saṃpadādirūpam /
tathā ca vidheḥ prāgaprāptaṃ puruṣecchayā kartavyaṃ sat vidhigocaro bhaviṣyati; yathā vṛttyantaratvena manaso viśvedevasāmyādviśvāndevānmanasi saṃpādya mana ālambanamavidyamānasamaṃ kṛtvā prādhānyena saṃpādyānāṃ viśveṣāmeva devānāmanucintanam, tena cānantalokaprāptiḥ ; evaṃ cidrūpasāmyājjīve brahmasvarūpaṃ saṃpādya jīvamālambanamavidyamānasamaṃ kṛtvā prādhānyena brahmānucintanam, tena cāmṛtatvaphalaprāptiḥ /
adhyāse tvālambanasyaiva prādhānyenāropitatadbhāvasyānucintanam ; yathā 'mano brahmetyupāsīta', 'ādityo brahmetyādeśaḥ' ; evaṃ jīvamabrahma 'brahmetyupāsīta' iti /
body.translated_text:
One might say this:
The cognition of oneness [of <s>Brahman</s> and the Self] does not have an actually existing entity as its object, such that, by removing the false knowledge whose manifestation is difference, it would not be the object of an injunction (<s>vidhi</s>); rather, it has the form of a meditation (<s>saṃpad</s>) and the like.
And thus, being something to be done (<s>kartavya</s>) that is not already obtained before the injunction, and being producible by the person's will, it will come within the scope of injunction. Just as — by way of [the mind] being a different modification — having superimposed the nature of the <s>Viśvedeva</s>s upon the mind by [its] similarity to the <s>Viśvedeva</s>s, and having made the mind — the substrate — one [seemingly] possessing a non-existent similarity, the contemplation (<s>anucintana</s>) is principally of the <s>Viśvedeva</s>s as the things superimposed, and the fruit is the attainment of infinite worlds — so too, having superimposed the nature of <s>Brahman</s> upon the individual self (<s>jīva</s>) by [its] similarity to the consciousness-nature [of <s>Brahman</s>], and having made the individual self — the substrate — one [seemingly] possessing a non-existent similarity, the contemplation is principally of <s>Brahman</s>, and the fruit is the attainment of immortality.
But in [the case of] superimposition (<s>adhyāsa</s>), the contemplation is principally of the substrate itself upon which the [other's] nature has been superimposed — as [in the meditation] 'One should meditate on the mind as <s>Brahman</s>,' 'The Sun is <s>Brahman</s> — this is the instruction.' Similarly, 'One should meditate on the individual self, which is not <s>Brahman</s>, as <s>Brahman</s>.' — [this is the proposed interpretation].

body.text:
kriyāviśeṣayogādvā, yathā 'vāyurvāva saṃvargaḥ', 'prāṇo vāva saṃvargaḥ' ; bāhyā khalu vāyudevatā saṃvargaḥ ; bāhyā khalu vāyudevatā saṃvargaḥ ; sa hi vahnyādīn saṃvṛṅkte ; mahāpralayasamaye hi vāyurvahnyādīnsaṃvṛtya saṃhṛtyātmani sthāpayati /
yathāha draviḍācāryaḥ- 'saṃharaṇādvā saṃvaraṇādvā svātmībhāvādvāyuḥ saṃvargaḥ' iti /
adhyātmaṃ ca prāṇaḥ saṃvarga iti ; sa hi sarvāṇi vāgādīni saṃvṛṅkte ; prāyaṇakāle hi sa eva sarvāṇīndriyāṇi saṃgṛhyotkrāmatīti /
seyaṃ saṃvargadṛṣṭirvāyau prāṇe ca daśāśāgataṃ jagaddarśayati yathā, evaṃ jīvātmani bṛṃhaṇakriyayā brahmadṛṣṭismṛtatvāya phalāya kalpata iti /
tadeteṣu triṣvapi pakṣeṣvātmadarśanopāsanādayaḥ pradhānakarmāṇi, apūrvaviṣayatvāt, stutaśastravat; ātmā tu dravyaṃ karmaṇi guṇa iti /
saṃskāro vātmano darśanaṃ vidhīyate /
yathā darśapūrṇamāsaprakaraṇe 'patnyavekṣitamājyaṃ bhavati' iti samāmnātam, prakaraṇinā ca gṛhītamupāṃśuyāgāṅgabhūtājyadravyasaṃskāratayā, avekṣaṇaṃ guṇakarma vidhīyate, evaṃ kartṛtvena kratvaṅgabhūte ātmani 'ātmā vā are draṣṭavyaḥ' iti darśanaṃ guṇakarma vidhīyate, 'yaistu dravyaṃ cikīrṣyate guṇastatra pratīyeta' iti nyāyāt /
ata āha- #na cedaṃ brahmātmaikatvavijñānam#iti /
kutaḥ ? #saṃpadādirūpe hi brahmātmaikatvavijñāne#iti /
darśapūrṇamāsaprakaraṇe hi samāmnātamājyāvekṣaṇaṃ tadaṅgabhūtājyasaṃskāra iti yujyate /
na ca 'ātmā vā are draṣṭavyaḥ' ityādi kasyacitprakaraṇe samāmnātam /
na cānārabhyādhītamapi 'yasya parṇamayī juhūrbhavati' ityavyabhicaritakratusaṃbandhajuhūdvāreṇa juhūpadaṃ kratuṃ smārayadvākyena yathā parṇatāyāḥ kratuśeṣabhāvamāpādayati, naivamātmāpyavyabhicāritakratusaṃbandhaḥ, yena taddarśanaṃ kratvaṅgaṃ sadātmānaṃ kratvarthaṃ saṃskuryāt /
tena yadyapyayaṃ vidhiḥ, tathāpi 'suvarṇaṃ hiraṇyaṃ bhāryam' itivat viniyogabhaṅgena pradhānakarmaiva, apūrvaviṣayatvāt, na guṇakarmeti sthavīyastayaitaddūṣaṇamanabhidhāya sarvapakṣasādhāraṇaṃ dūṣaṇamuktam /
tadatirohitārthatayā na vyākhyātam /
body.translated_text:
Or, [it could be] through connection with a particular ritual action — as [in the texts] 'Wind (<s>Vāyu</s>) indeed is the absorber (<s>saṃvarga</s>),' 'Breath (<s>Prāṇa</s>) indeed is the absorber.' The external deity <s>Vāyu</s> is the absorber; the external deity <s>Vāyu</s> is the absorber — for he absorbs fire and the rest; at the time of the great dissolution (<s>mahāpralaya</s>), <s>Vāyu</s> absorbs fire and the rest, withdraws them, and establishes them in himself.
As <s>Draviḍācārya</s> says: 'Because of absorption (<s>saṃharaṇa</s>), or because of gathering in (<s>saṃvaraṇa</s>), or because of making [them] part of himself, <s>Vāyu</s> is the absorber (<s>saṃvarga</s>).'
And in the individual context (<s>adhyātma</s>), <s>Prāṇa</s> is the absorber — for he absorbs all [faculties] such as speech and the rest; at the time of death (<s>prāyaṇakāla</s>), he alone gathers up all the sense-faculties and departs.
This <s>saṃvarga-dṛṣṭi</s> (meditation on absorption) shows the world as contained in the ten directions, [absorbed] in <s>Vāyu</s> and <s>Prāṇa</s>; similarly, through the activity of expansion (<s>bṛṃhaṇa-kriyā</s>), the meditation on <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahma-dṛṣṭi</s>) applied to the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>) serves the purpose of being remembered [as efficacious].
In all three of these positions, self-vision (<s>ātma-darśana</s>), meditation (<s>upāsana</s>), and the like are the principal actions, since they have an unprecedented entity (<s>apūrva</s>) as their object — like laudatory and prescriptive [passages]; but the Self is the substance (<s>dravya</s>) [and] a subsidiary (<s>guṇa</s>) in the action.
Either a refinement (<s>saṃskāra</s>) or a vision (<s>darśana</s>) of the Self is enjoined.
Just as in the context of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [rites] it is taught: 'The clarified butter (<s>ājya</s>) is that which the wife has looked upon,' and when taken by the principal [rite], the looking-upon is enjoined as a subsidiary action (<s>guṇa-karma</s>) serving as the refinement of the butter-substance that is a subsidiary of the <s>upāṃśu</s> offering — so too, with respect to the Self, which as agent is a subsidiary of the sacrifice, in 'The Self indeed, O dear one, is to be seen' (<s>ātmā vā are draṣṭavyaḥ</s>), the seeing is enjoined as a subsidiary action — according to the principle 'Where one wishes to accomplish the substance, the subsidiary is understood [to apply] there.'
Therefore he says: 'This cognition of the oneness of <s>Brahman</s> and Self is not [a subsidiary action].'
Why? 'For in the cognition of the oneness of <s>Brahman</s> and Self, which takes the form of a meditation (<s>saṃpad</s>) and the like...'
For in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> context, the looking upon butter that is taught there is reasonably [understood as] the refinement of butter that is a subsidiary [of the rite].
But 'The Self indeed, O dear one, is to be seen' and such [passages] are not taught in the context of any [particular rite].
Nor [can it be argued] that even though not studied as part of a [specific rite], just as [the passage] 'He whose ladle is made of <s>parṇa</s> wood' — through the word 'ladle' that has an unfailing connection with a sacrifice, reminds one of the sacrifice, and thereby assigns the quality of being made of <s>parṇa</s> wood to the status of a subsidiary of the sacrifice — so too the Self does not have an unfailing connection with a sacrifice, such that its seeing, being a subsidiary of a sacrifice, would refine the Self for the purpose of the sacrifice.
Therefore, even if this is an injunction, still — like 'gold, wealth, a wife' — due to the breakdown of specific assignment (<s>viniyoga</s>), it is only a principal action, since it has an unprecedented entity as its object, and not a subsidiary action. Without stating this weightier objection, a general objection common to all positions has been stated.
That [objection], being of transparent meaning, has not been explained [further].

body.text:
kiṃ ca jñānakriyāviṣayatvavidhānamasya bahuśrutiviruddhamityāha- #na ca vidikriya#iti /
śaṅkate- #aviṣayatve#iti /
tataśca śāntikarmaṇi vetālodaya iti bhāvaḥ /
nirākaroti- #na# /
kutaḥ? #avidyākalpitabhedanivṛttiparatvāt#iti /
sarvameva hi vākyaṃ nedantayā vastubhedaṃ bodhayitumarhati /
na hīkṣukṣīraguḍādīnāṃ madhurarasabhedaḥ śakya ākhyātum /
evamanyatrāpi sarvatra draṣṭavyam /
tena pramāṇāntarasiddhe laukike evārthe yadā gatiridṛśī śabdasya, tadā kaiva kathā pratyagātmanyalaukike /
adūraviprakarṣeṇa tu kathañcitpratipādanamihāpi samānam /
tvaṃpadārtho hi pramātā pramāṇādhīnayā pramityā prameyaṃ ghaṭādi vyāpnotītyavidyāvilasitam /
tadasya aviṣayībhūtodāsīnatatpadārthapratyagātmasāmānādhikaraṇyena pramātṛtvābhāvāt tannivṛttau pramāṇādayastisro vidhā nivartante /
na hi pakturavastutve pākyapākapacanāni vastusanti bhavitumarhantīti /
tathā hi-
body.translated_text:
Moreover, the enjoining of this [Self-knowledge] as the object of the action of knowing contradicts many <s>Śruti</s> passages — thus he says: 'Nor is the act of knowing (<s>vidi-kriyā</s>)...'
He raises an objection: 'If it were not an object...'
And thus [the consequence would be] like the raising of a <s>vetāla</s> (vampire) in a pacificatory rite — this is the purport.
He refutes: 'No.'
Why? 'Because [the texts] are directed toward the cessation of the difference superimposed by <s>avidyā</s>.'
For every statement, through its negating function, is capable of communicating [only] the distinction among entities.
For the difference in sweet taste among sugarcane, milk, and jaggery cannot be expressed [in words].
This should be seen thus everywhere in other cases as well.
Therefore, when the capacity of words is such even regarding a worldly object established by other means of knowledge, what need even be said regarding the innermost Self (<s>pratyagātman</s>), which is beyond the world?
But through a not-too-distant approximation, some kind of communication is possible here as well.
The referent of 'you' (<s>tvam-padārtha</s>), i.e., the knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>), through cognition (<s>pramiti</s>) dependent on a means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), reaches the knowable object (<s>prameya</s>) such as a pot — this is a display of <s>avidyā</s>.
When that [knower-status] is negated through co-referentiality with the innermost Self (<s>pratyagātman</s>) — which is the referent of 'that' (<s>tat-padārtha</s>), indifferent and not an object [of cognition] — since the status of being a knower ceases, upon its cessation the three modes — means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) and the rest — also cease.
For if the cook is unreal, the cookable, the cooking, and the act of cooking cannot be real either.
Thus indeed —

body.text: vigalitaparāgvṛttyarthatvaṃ padasya tadastadā tvamiti hi padanaikārthatve tvamityapi yatpadam /
body.translated_text: When the word's function of [denoting] an object (<s>arthatva</s>) that involves [the distinction of] subject and predicate has dissolved, then in [the statement] 'that art thou' (<s>tat tvam</s>), if the word 'thou' (<s>tvam</s>) has no separate meaning [from 'that'],

body.text: tadapi ca tadā gatvaikārthyaṃ viśuddhacidātmatāṃ tyajati sakalānkartṛtvādīnpadārthamalānnijān //
body.translated_text: Then that [word 'thou'] too, having attained oneness of meaning with 'that' (<s>tat</s>), reaches the nature of pure consciousness (<s>viśuddha-cid-ātmatā</s>), abandoning all its own impurities of word-meaning such as agency (<s>kartṛtva</s>) and the rest. //

body.text:
ityāntaraślokaḥ /
atraivārthe śrutīrudāharati,- #tathā ca śāstram-yasyāmatam#iti /
prakṛtamupasaṃharati- #ato 'vidyākalpita#
body.translated_text:
This is an interpolated verse (<s>āntara-śloka</s>).
To illustrate this very point, he cites <s>Śruti</s> passages: 'And thus the scripture — "He to whom it is not known..."'
He concludes the topic at hand: 'Therefore, [that which is] superimposed by <s>avidyā</s>...'

body.text: iti /
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text:
parapakṣe mokṣasyānityatāmāpādayati- #yasya tu#iti /
kāryamapūrvaṃ yāgādivyāpārajanyam ; tadapekṣate mokṣaḥ svotpattāviti /
#tayoḥ pakṣayoḥ#iti ; nirvartyavikāryayoḥ /
kṣaṇikaṃ vijñānamātmeti bauddhāḥ /
tathā ca viśuddhavijñānotpādo mokṣa iti nirvartyo mokṣaḥ /
anyeṣāṃ tu saṃskārarūpāvasthāmapahāya yā kaivalyāvasthāvāptirātmanaḥ sa mokṣa iti vikāryo mokṣaḥ ; yathā payasaḥ pūrvāvasthāpahānenāvasthāntaraprāptirvikāro dadhīti /
tadetayoḥ pakṣayorna nityatā mokṣasya, kāryatvāt, dadhighaṭādivat /
body.translated_text:
He shows the impermanence of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) that would follow from the opponent's position: 'But for whom...'
A product (<s>kārya</s>) is an <s>apūrva</s> (unseen potency) generated by the operation of sacrifice and the like; liberation requires that [<s>apūrva</s>] for its own origination.
'Of those two positions' — namely, the producible (<s>nirvartya</s>) and the modifiable (<s>vikārya</s>).
The Buddhists (<s>Bauddhā</s>) hold that momentary consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) is the Self.
Accordingly, the arising of purified consciousness is liberation — thus liberation is a product (<s>nirvartya</s>).
But for others, liberation consists in the Self's attainment of the state of isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>) by abandoning its condition characterized by mental impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) — thus liberation is a modification (<s>vikārya</s>); just as milk's acquisition of a new state by abandoning its previous state is a modification [called] curd.
In both of these positions, liberation is not eternal, because it is a product — like curd, a pot, and so forth.

body.text:
'atha yadataḥ paro divo jyotirdīpyate' iti śruterbrahmaṇo vikṛtāvikṛtadeśabhedāvagamādavikṛtadeśabrahmaprāptisvarūpāsanādividhikāryā bhaviṣyati ; tathā ca prāpyakarmatā brahmaṇa ityata āha- #na cāpyatvenāpi#iti /
anyadanyena vikṛtadeśaparihāṇyāvikṛtadeśaṃ prāpyate /
tadyathopavelaṃ jaladhiratibahalacapalakallolamālāparasparāsphālanasamullasatphenapuñjastabakatayā vikṛtaḥ, madhye tu praśāntasakalakallolopasargaḥ svacchaḥ sthiratayāvikṛtaḥ, tasya madhyamavikṛtaṃ pautikaḥ potena prāpnoti /
jīvastu brahmaiveti kiṃ kena prāpyatām? bhedāśrayātvātprāpterityarthaḥ /
body.translated_text:
From the <s>Śruti</s> 'Now, that light which shines beyond this heaven' (<s>atha yadataḥ paro divo jyotirdīpyate</s>), one might understand a distinction in <s>Brahman</s> between a modified and an unmodified region, and [argue that] the injunction of practices such as reaching unmodified-region-<s>Brahman</s> and being seated [in meditation] will [validly] apply; and thus <s>Brahman</s> would have the status of something to be reached (<s>prāpya-karmatā</s>) — therefore he says: 'Nor even as something to be reached...'
One thing reaches another — [namely] the unmodified region — by leaving the modified region.
For example, the ocean near the shore is modified, with clusters of foam-heaps splashing up from the mutual collision of exceedingly dense and restless waves; but in the middle, free from the disturbance of all waves, it is clear, and in its stillness is unmodified — a sailor reaches that middle unmodified [region] by means of a boat.
But the <s>jīva</s> (individual self) is <s>Brahman</s> itself — so what is to be reached by what? Because reaching depends on difference — this is the meaning.

body.text: atha jīvo brahmaṇo bhinnastathāpi na tena brahmāpyate, brahmaṇo vibhutvena nityaprāptatvādityāha - #svarūpavyatiriktatve 'pi#iti /
body.translated_text: If the <s>jīva</s> is different from <s>Brahman</s>, even so <s>Brahman</s> is not reached by it, since <s>Brahman</s>, being all-pervading (<s>vibhu</s>), is eternally already reached — thus he says: 'Even if there were a difference in essential nature...'

body.text:
saṃskārakarmatāmapākaroti- #nāpi saṃskārya#iti /
dvayī hi saṃskāryatā, guṇādhānena vā, yathā bījapūrakusumasya lākṣārasāvasekaḥ ; tena hi tatkusumaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ lākṣārasasavarṇaṃ phalaṃ prasūte ; doṣāpanayena vā ; yathā malinamādarśatalaṃ nighṛṣṭamiṣṭakācūrṇenodbhāsitabhāsvaratvaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ bhavati /
tatra na tāvadbrahmaṇi guṇādhānaṃ saṃbhavati /
guṇo hi brahmaṇaḥ svabhāvo vā bhinno vā ? svabhāvaścet kathamādheyaḥ, tasya nityavāt /
bhinnatve tu kāryatvena mokṣasyānityatvaprasaṅgaḥ /
na ca bhede dharmadharmibhāvaḥ, gavāśvavat /
bhedābhedaśca vyudastaḥ, virodhāt /
tadanenābhisaṃdhinoktam- #anādheyātiśayabrahmasvarūpatvānmokṣasya#iti /
dvitīyaṃ pakṣaṃ pratikṣipati- #nāpi doṣāpanayanena#iti /
aśuddhiḥ satī darpaṇe nivartate ; na tu brahmaṇi asatī nivartanīyā, nityanivṛttatvādityarthaḥ /
body.translated_text:
He refutes the status of being an object of refinement (<s>saṃskārya-karmatā</s>): 'Nor is it refinable...' (<s>nāpi saṃskārya</s>).
Refinability is of two kinds: either through the addition of a quality (<s>guṇādhāna</s>) — as when a pomegranate (<s>bījapūra</s>) flower is sprinkled with lac-dye (<s>lākṣā-rasa</s>), whereby that flower, thus refined, produces a fruit of the same color as the lac-dye; or through the removal of a defect (<s>doṣāpanaya</s>) — as when a dirty mirror-surface, polished with brick-powder, becomes refined, its brilliance made manifest.
Now, the addition of a quality to <s>Brahman</s> is not possible.
For is a quality [to be added to] <s>Brahman</s> its own nature or something different? If its own nature, how can it be 'added,' since it is eternally [present]?
If different, then since [the result would be] a product, there would be the unwanted consequence of liberation being non-eternal.
Nor is there a property-property-bearer relation in [mere] difference — like a cow and a horse.
And [the position of simultaneous] difference-and-non-difference has been refuted, because of contradiction.
With this intention it is said: 'Because liberation is of the nature of <s>Brahman</s>, to which no excellence can be added' (<s>anādheyātiśaya-brahma-svarūpatvāt mokṣasya</s>).
He rejects the second alternative: 'Nor through the removal of a defect...'
An impurity, when present, is removed from a mirror; but an impurity that does not exist in <s>Brahman</s> cannot be removed, since it is eternally absent — this is the meaning.

body.text:
śaṅkate- #svātmadharma eva#iti /
brahmasvabhāva eva mokṣo 'nādyavidyāmalāvṛta upāsanādikriyayātmani saṃskriyamāṇe 'bhivyajyate, na tu kriyate /
etaduktaṃ bhavati- nityaśuddhatvamātmano 'siddham, saṃsārāvasthāyāmavidyāmalinatvāditi /
śaṅkāṃ nirākaroti- #na# /
kutaḥ ? #kriyāśrayatvānupapatteḥ# /
nāvidyā brahmāśrayā, kiṃ tu jīve ; sā tvanirvacanīyetyuktam ; tena nityaśuddhameva brahma /
abhyupetya tvaśuddhiṃ kriyāsaṃskāryatvaṃ dūṣyate /
kriyā hi brahmasamavetā vā brahma saṃskuryāt, yathā nigharṣaṇamiṣṭakācūrṇasaṃyogavibhāgapracayo nirantara ādarśatalasamavetaḥ ; anyasamavetā vā /
na tāvadbrahmadharmaḥ kriyā, tasyāḥ svāśrayavikārahetutvena brahmaṇo nityatvavyāghātāt /
anyāśrayā tu kathamanyasyopakaroti, atiprasaṅgāt /
na hi darpaṇe nighṛṣyamāṇe maṇirviśuddho dṛṣṭaḥ /
#taccāniṣṭam#iti /
tadā bādhanaṃ parāmṛśati /
body.translated_text:
He raises an objection: 'It is a property of the Self itself...'
[The objector argues:] Liberation, being <s>Brahman</s>'s own nature, is covered by beginningless <s>avidyā</s>-impurity, and when the Self is refined through the activity of meditation (<s>upāsana</s>) and the like, [liberation] is manifested — not produced.
What is being said is this: the eternal purity of the Self is not established, since in the state of <s>saṃsāra</s> it is stained by <s>avidyā</s>.
He refutes the objection: 'No.'
Why? 'Because it is impossible for [<s>Brahman</s>] to be the substrate of action (<s>kriyāśrayatva</s>).'
<s>Avidyā</s> does not have <s>Brahman</s> as its substrate, but rather the <s>jīva</s>; and that [<s>avidyā</s>] is indescribable (<s>anirvacanīya</s>) — as has been said; therefore <s>Brahman</s> is eternally pure.
But even granting the impurity [for argument's sake], the status of being refinable by action is refuted.
For would the action that refines <s>Brahman</s> inhere in <s>Brahman</s> — as rubbing, being the accumulation of contacts and separations with brick-powder, continuously inheres in the mirror-surface — or would it inhere in something else?
To begin with, the action is not a property of <s>Brahman</s>, because, since action causes transformation of its own substrate, it would contradict <s>Brahman</s>'s eternality.
But if [the action] inheres in something else, how would it benefit another [i.e., <s>Brahman</s>]? — there would be overextension (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>).
For it has never been observed that when a mirror is polished, a gem becomes purified.
'And that is undesirable' — here he considers the further refutation.

body.text: atra vyabhicāraṃ codayati- #nanu dehāśrayayā#iti /
body.translated_text: Here he raises a counter-example (<s>vyabhicāra</s>): 'But surely, [action] whose substrate is the body...'

body.text:
pariharati- #na dehasaṃhatasya#iti /
anādyanirvācyāvidyopadhānameva brahmaṇo jīva iti ca kṣetrajña iti cācakṣate /
body.translated_text:
He responds: 'Not [so] for [<s>Brahman</s>] conjoined with the body...'
<s>Brahman</s>, having beginningless and indescribable <s>avidyā</s> as its limiting adjunct (<s>upādhāna</s>), is designated as the <s>jīva</s> (individual self) and as the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field).

body.text:
sa ca sthūlasūkṣmaśarīrendriyādisaṃhatastatsaṃghātamadhyapatitastadabhedenāhamitipratyayaviṣayībhūtaḥ ; ataḥ śarīrādisaṃskāraḥ śarīrādidharmo 'pyātmano bhavati, tadabhedādhyavasāyāt ; yathā aṅgarāgadharmaḥ sugandhitā kāminīnāṃ vyapadiśyate /
tenātrāpi yadāśritā kriyā sāṃvyavahārikapramāṇaviṣayīkṛtā tasyaiva saṃskāro nānyasyeti na vyabhicāraḥ /
tattvatastu na kriyā na saṃskāra iti /
sanidarśanaṃ tu śeṣamadhyāsabhāṣye eva kṛtavyākhyānamiti neha vyākhyātam /
#tayoranyaḥ pippalam#iti /
anyo jīvātmā /
pippalaṃ karmaphalam /
#anaśnannanya#iti /
paramātmā /
saṃhatasyaiva bhoktṛtvamāha mantravarṇaḥ- #ātmendriya#iti /
anupahitaśuddhasvabhāvabrahmapradarśanaparau mantrau paṭhati- #eko deva#iti /
śukraṃ dīptimat ; avraṇaṃ duḥkharahitam ; asrāviraṃ avigalitam, avināśīti yāvat /
upasaṃharati- #tasmāt#iti /
body.translated_text:
And he [the <s>jīva</s>], conjoined with the gross and subtle bodies, sense-faculties, and the rest, fallen into the midst of that aggregate, becomes the object of the 'I'-cognition through non-difference from that [aggregate]; therefore, the refinement of the body and the rest, though a property of the body and the rest, belongs also to the Self, because of the conviction of non-difference from them — just as the property of bodily ornamentation, namely fragrance, is attributed to women.
Thus here too, the action whose substrate [is the body] — being made an object of conventional valid cognition (<s>sāṃvyavahārika-pramāṇa</s>) — is the refinement of that [body-complex] alone and not of another; hence there is no counter-example.
But in reality (<s>tattvataḥ</s>), there is neither action nor refinement [of the Self].
The remainder, being accompanied by examples, has already been explained in the <s>Adhyāsabhāṣya</s> (preface on superimposition) itself, and so is not explained here.
'Of these two, the other one eats the fruit' (<s>tayoranyaḥ pippalam</s>) — the other is the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>).
<s>Pippala</s> (the fruit) is the fruit of action (<s>karma-phala</s>).
'The other who does not eat' (<s>anaśnann anyaḥ</s>) — [that is] the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>).
The text of the <s>mantra</s> states that enjoyership belongs only to the one who is conjoined [with the body]: '<s>Ātman</s>, sense-faculties...'
He recites [two] <s>mantra</s>s that serve to demonstrate <s>Brahman</s> in its unqualified, pure essential nature: 'The one God (<s>eko devaḥ</s>)...'
<s>Śukra</s> means luminous; <s>avraṇa</s> means free from suffering; <s>asnāvira</s> means not decaying, that is to say, indestructible.
He concludes: 'Therefore...'

body.text:
nanu mā bhūnnirvartyādikarmatācatuṣṭayī ; pañcamī tu kācit vidhā bhaviṣyati, yayā mokṣasya karmatā ghaṭiṣyata ityata āha- #ato 'nyat#iti /
ebhyaḥ prakārebhyo na prakārāntaramanyadasti, yato mokṣasya kriyānupraveśo bhaviṣyati /
etaduktaṃ bhavati- catasṛṇāṃ vidhānāṃ madhye 'nyatamatayā kriyāphalatvaṃ vyāptam ; sā ca mokṣādvyāvartamānā vyāpakānupalabdhyā mokṣasya kriyāphalatvaṃ vyāvartayatīti /
tatkiṃ mokṣe kriyaiva nāsti ? tathā ca tadarthāni śāstrāṇi tadarthāśca pravṛttayo 'narthakānītyata upasaṃhāravyājenāha- #tasmājjñānamekam#iti /
body.translated_text:
One might say: Let it not be the fourfold object-status of being producible and the rest; but there will be some fifth mode by which the object-status of liberation [with respect to action] will be established — therefore he says: 'Other than these...'
From these [four] modes, there is no other, fifth mode by which liberation would come within the scope of action.
What is being said is this: among the four types [of object-relation], the status of being a result of action is pervaded by [being] one or another of them; and that [pervasion], being excluded from liberation, through the non-apprehension of the pervader, excludes the status of being a result of action from liberation.
Then is there no action at all with respect to liberation? And [if so], would the scriptures directed toward it and the endeavors directed toward it be purposeless? — To address this, he says by way of conclusion: 'Therefore, knowledge alone...'

body.text:
atha jñānaṃ kriyā mānasī kasmānna vidhigocaraḥ ? kasmācca tasyāḥ phalaṃ nirvartyādiṣvanyatamaṃ na mokṣaḥ ? iti codayati- #nanu jñānam#iti /
pariharati- #na# /
kutaḥ ? #vailakṣaṇyāt# /
ayamarthaḥ-satyam, jñānaṃ mānasī kriyā ; tviyaṃ brahmaṇi phalaṃ janayitumarhati, tasya svayaṃprakāśatayā vidikriyākarmabhāvānupapatterityuktam /
tadetasminvailakṣaṇye sthite eva vailakṣaṇyāntaramāha- #kriyā hi nāma sā#iti /
#yatra#viṣaye #vastusvarūpanirapekṣaiva codyate#- yathā devatāsaṃpradānakahavirgrahaṇe devatāvastusvarūpānapekṣā devatādhyānakriyā ; yathā vā yoṣiti agnivastvanapekṣāgnibuddhiḥ- #yā sā kriyā hi nāma#iti yojanā /
na hi 'yasyai devatāyai havirgṛhītaṃ syāttāṃ dhyāyedvaṣaṭkariṣyan' ityasmādvidheḥ prāgdevatādhyānaṃ prāptam /
prāptaṃ tvadhītavedāntasya viditapadatadarthasaṃbandhasyādhigataśabdanyāyatattvasya 'sadeva somyedam' ityādeḥ 'tattvamasi' ityantātsaṃdarbhāt brahmātmabhāvajñānam, śabdapramāṇasāmarthyāt, indriyārthasaṃnikarṣasāmarthyādiva praṇihitamanasaḥ sphītālokamadhyavartikumbhānubhavaḥ /
na hyasau svasāmagrībalalabdhajanmā manujecchayānyathākartumakartuṃ vā śakyaḥ, devatādhyānavat, yenārthavānatra vidhiḥ syāt /
na copāsanā vānubhavaparyantatā vāsya vidhergocaraḥ, tayoranvayavyatirekāvadhṛtasāmarthyayoḥ sākṣātkāre vā anādyavidyāpanaye vā vidhimantareṇa prāptatvena puruṣecchayānyathākartumakartuṃ vā aśakyatvāt /
tasmādbrahmajñānaṃ mānasī kriyāpi na vidhigocaraḥ /
puruṣacittavyāpārādhīnāyāstu kriyāyā vastusvarūpanirapekṣitā kvacidavirodhinī, yathā devatādhyānakriyāyāḥ ; na hyatra vastusvarūpeṇa kaścidvirodhaḥ ; kvacidvastusvarūpavirodhinī, yathā yoṣitpuruṣayoragnibuddhiḥ-ityetāvatā bhedena nidarśanāmithunadvayopanyāsaḥ /
#kriyaiva#ityevakāreṇa vastutantratvamapākaroti /
body.translated_text:
Now, [one objects:] knowledge is a mental action — why should it not be the domain of an injunction? And why should its fruit not be <s>mokṣa</s> — being one among the producible and the like? Thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises the objection: 'But is not knowledge...' (<s>nanu jñānam</s>).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes: 'No.'
Why? 'Because of the dissimilarity' (<s>vailakṣaṇyāt</s>).
The meaning is this: True, knowledge is a mental action; but it cannot produce a fruit with respect to <s>Brahman</s>, since — <s>Brahman</s> being self-luminous — the status of object (<s>karma</s>) of the action of knowing is untenable — this has been stated.
Having established this dissimilarity, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states a further dissimilarity: 'For that which is called action...' (<s>kriyā hi nāma sā</s>).
In the domain 'where it is enjoined as independent of the true nature of the object' (<s>vastusvarūpanirapekṣaiva</s>) — for example, the action of meditating on a deity, which is independent of the true nature of the deity, at the time of taking the oblation destined for a deity; or again, the cognition of fire regarding a woman, which is independent of the real nature of fire — 'that which is called action' — this is the syntactic connection.
For meditation on a deity is not already obtained before the injunction 'When the oblation destined for a deity has been taken, one should meditate on that deity, being about to utter <s>vaṣaṭ</s>.'
But for one who has studied the <s>Vedānta</s>s, who knows the meanings of words and their connections, and who has understood the principles of scriptural reasoning — from the textual sequence beginning with '<s>sadeva somyedam</s>' (Being alone, dear one, was this in the beginning) and ending with '<s>tattvamasi</s>' (You are That) — the knowledge of the Self's identity with <s>Brahman</s> is already obtained, by the capacity of verbal testimony as a means of knowledge, just as the perception of a pot in the middle of ample light [is obtained] for one whose mind is attentive, by the capacity of the contact of sense and object.
For that [knowledge], born from the capacity of its own causal complex, cannot be made otherwise or prevented by the will of a person — unlike the meditation on a deity — such that an injunction here would serve a purpose.
Nor is meditation (<s>upāsanā</s>) or [the requirement of] culmination in direct experience the domain of this injunction, since both of these — their capacity being established through positive and negative concomitance with regard to either direct realization or the removal of beginningless <s>avidyā</s> — being already obtained without an injunction, cannot be made otherwise or prevented by the will of a person.
Therefore, the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, even though a mental action, is not the domain of an injunction.
But for an action that depends on the mental operation of a person, independence from the true nature of the object is sometimes non-conflicting — as in the case of the action of meditating on a deity, where there is no conflict with the true nature of the object; and sometimes conflicting with the true nature of the object — as in the case of the cognition of fire regarding a man and a woman — thus, with this much distinction, the presentation of two pairs of illustrations [is made].
'Action alone' — by the [restrictive] particle '<s>eva</s>' (alone), [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] removes the object-dependence [of knowledge].

body.text:
nanu 'ātmetyevopāsīta' ityādayo vidhayaḥ śrūyante /
na ca te pramattagītāḥ ; tulyaṃ hi sāṃpradāyikam ; tasmādvidheyenātra bhavitavyamityata āha- #tadviṣaye liṅgādaya#iti /
satyaṃ śrūyante liṅgādayaḥ ; na tvamī vidhiviṣayāḥ, tadviṣayatve 'prāmāṇyaprasaṅgāt /
heyopādeyaviṣayo hi vidhiḥ /
sa eva ca heya upādeyo vā, yaṃ puruṣaḥ kartumakartumanyathā vā kartuṃ śaknoti /
tatraiva ca samarthaḥ kartādhikṛto niyojyo bhavati /
na caivaṃbhūtānyātmaśravaṇamananopāsanadarśanānīti viṣayatadanuṣṭhātrorvidhivyāpakayorabhāvādvidherabhāva iti prayuktā api liṅādayaḥ pravartanāyāmasamarthā upala iva kṣurataikṣṇyaṃ kuṇṭhamapramāṇībhavantīti /
#aniyojyaviṣayatvāt#iti ; samartho hi kartādhikārī niyojyaḥ ; asāmarthye tu na kartṛtā ; tato nādhikṛtaḥ, ato na niyojya ityarthaḥ /
body.translated_text:
But [one objects:] injunctions such as 'One should meditate on [it] as the Self' (<s>ātmetyevopāsīta</s>) and the like are heard [in scripture].
And they are not the ravings of a madman; for the tradition is equally [authoritative].
Therefore, there must be something enjoinable here — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'The <s>liṅ</s> suffix and the like regarding that subject...' (<s>tadviṣaye liṅgādayaḥ</s>).
True, the <s>liṅ</s> suffix and the like are heard; but these are not within the domain of an injunction (<s>vidhi</s>), since if they were, the unwanted consequence of non-authoritativeness would follow.
For an injunction has as its domain what is to be rejected or adopted.
And only that is to be rejected or adopted which a person is able to do, not to do, or to do otherwise.
And only with respect to such [an object] is a competent agent qualified and enjoinable.
But hearing, reflection, meditation, and realization of the Self are not of such a nature — therefore, since both the object [of the injunction] and the person who would perform it — the two pervasive elements of an injunction — are absent, the injunction itself is absent. Thus, even though the <s>liṅ</s> suffix and the like are employed, being incapable of impelling [action], they become pointless, like a razor's edge [applied to] a stone — they become non-authoritative.
'Because the object cannot be enjoined' (<s>aniyojyaviṣayatvāt</s>) — for a competent agent is the qualified person who is to be enjoined; but in the absence of competence, there is no agency; hence he is not qualified, and therefore not enjoinable — this is the meaning.

body.text:
yadi virodhābhānna vidhivacanāni, kimarthāni tarhi vacanānyetāni vidhicchāyānīti pṛcchati- #kimarthāni#iti /
na cānarthakāni yuktāni, svādhyāyavidhyadhīnagrahaṇatvānupapatteriti bhāvaḥ /
uttaram- #svābhāvika#iti /
anyataḥ prāptā eva hi śravaṇādayo vidhisarūpairvākyairanūdyante /
na cānuvādo 'pyaprayojanaḥ, pravṛttiviśeṣakaratvāt /
tathāhi- tattadiṣṭāniṣṭaviṣayepsājihāsāpahṛtahṛdayatayā bahirmukho na pratyagātmani manaḥ samādhātumarhati /
ātmaśravaṇādividhisarūpaistu vacanairmanaso viṣayasrotaḥ khilīkṛtya pratyagātmasrota udghāṭyata iti pravṛttiviśeṣakaratā anuvādānāmastīti saprayojanatayā svādhyāyavidhyadhīnagrahaṇatvamupapadyata iti /
body.translated_text:
If [the injunctive statements] are not injunctions because of [their] contradiction [with the nature of the object], then for what purpose are these injunction-like statements? — [the objector] asks: 'For what purpose...?' (<s>kimarthāni</s>).
And they cannot be purposeless, since their being grasped through the injunction of self-study would be untenable — this is the purport.
The answer: 'Natural' (<s>svābhāvika</s>).
For hearing and the like, already obtained from another [source], are merely reiterated (<s>anūdyante</s>) by the injunction-like statements.
And even a reiteration (<s>anuvāda</s>) is not without purpose, since it effects a special engagement.
This is as follows: One whose heart is carried away by the desire and aversion for various pleasant and unpleasant objects, being outward-turned, is unable to fix the mind on the inner Self (<s>pratyag-ātman</s>).
But through the injunction-like statements about hearing of the Self and the like, the outward-flowing stream of the mind is dammed up and the inward-flowing stream is opened — thus the reiterative statements have the capacity to effect a special engagement; and since they have a purpose, their being grasped through the injunction of self-study is justified.

body.text:
yacca coditamātmajñānamanuṣṭhānānaṅgatvādapuruṣārtha iti tadayuktam ; svato 'sya puruṣārthatve siddhe yadanuṣṭhānānaṅgatvaṃ tadbhūṣaṇaṃ na dūṣaṇamityāha- #yadapi#iti /
#anusaṃjvaret#śarīraṃ tapyamānamanutapyeta /
sugamamanyat /
prakṛtamupasaṃharati- #tasmānna pratipatti#iti /
body.translated_text:
And the objection that was raised — that the knowledge of the Self, not being an auxiliary of [ritual] performance, is without human purpose — that is inappropriate; since, when its human purposefulness is established independently, its non-subsidiarity to performance is an ornament, not a defect — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'And as for the [objection]...' (<s>yadapi</s>).
'Would have fever' (<s>anusaṃjvaret</s>) — the body, being heated, would have sympathetic fever.
The rest is straightforward.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] concludes the topic at hand: 'Therefore, realization is not...' (<s>tasmānna pratipatti</s>).

body.text:
prakṛtisiddhyarthamekadeśimataṃ dūṣayitumanubhāṣate- #yadapi kecidāhuḥ#iti /
dūṣayati- #tanna#iti /
idamatrākūtam-
body.translated_text:
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] restates the view of the partial followers in order to refute it, for the purpose of establishing his own position: 'And as some say...' (<s>yadapi kecidāhuḥ</s>).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes: 'That is not so' (<s>tanna</s>).
The intent here is —

body.text: kāryabodhe yathā ceṣṭā liṅgaṃ harṣādayastathā /
body.translated_text: Just as in the cognition of what is to be produced (<s>kārya</s>), activity [of the body] and the <s>liṅ</s> suffix [serve as evidence], so too joy and the like [serve as evidence for cognition of existing facts].

body.text: siddhabodher'thavattaivaṃ śāstratvaṃ hitaśāsanāt //
body.translated_text: The cognition of an established fact (<s>siddha-bodha</s>) has purposefulness in just the same way — hence its status as scripture (<s>śāstratva</s>) [is established] through teaching what is beneficial. //

body.text:
yadi hi padānāṃ kāryābhidhāne tadarthasvārthābhidhāne vā niyamena vṛddhavyavahāre sāmarthyamabadhṛtaṃ bhavet, na bhavedaheyānupādeyabhūtabrahmātmatāparatvamupaniṣadām ; tatrāviditasāmarthyatvātpadānāṃ loke, tatpūrvakatvācca vaidikārthapratīteḥ /
atha tu bhūte 'pyarthe padānāṃ loke śakyaḥ saṃgatigrahaḥ, tata upaniṣadāntatparatvaṃ paurvāparyaparyālocanayāvagamyamānamapahnutya na kāryaparatvaṃ śakyaṃ kalpayitum, śrutahānyaśrutakalpanāprasaṅgāt /
tatra tāvadevamakāryer'the na saṃgatigrahaḥ, yadi tatparaḥ prayogo na loke dṛśyeta, tatpratyayo vā vyutpannasyonnetuṃ na śakyete /
na tāvattatparaḥ prayogo na dṛśyate loke,
body.translated_text:
If indeed the capacity of words — to denote action-oriented meanings or their own meanings that serve the purpose of action — were ascertained with certainty in the usage of the learned, then the <s>Upaniṣad</s>s could not be oriented toward the Self's identity with <s>Brahman</s>, which is neither to be rejected nor adopted; because the capacity of words is unknown in the world [as oriented toward established facts], and because Vedic comprehension of meaning is preceded by that [worldly capacity].
But if the apprehension of the relation [of words] to established entities too is possible in the world, then the orientation of the <s>Upaniṣad</s>s toward that — understood through the examination of their beginning and end — cannot be denied and replaced by an orientation toward action, due to the absurd consequence of abandoning what is heard and conjecturing what is not heard.
Therein, firstly, there is no [inability to] apprehend the relation regarding meaning that is not action-oriented, if an utterance devoted to that [meaning] is observed in the world, or if the cognition of a learned person [regarding that meaning] can be inferred.
Firstly, it is not the case that an utterance devoted to that [meaning] is not observed in the world,

body.text:
kutūhalabhayādinivṛttyarthānāmakāryaparāṇāṃ padasaṃdarbhāṇāṃ prayogasya loke bahulamupalabdheḥ /
tadyathā- ākhaṇḍalādilokapālacakravālādhivasatiḥ siddhavidyādharagandharvāpsaraḥparivāro brahmalokāvatīrṇamandākinīpāthaḥpravāhaprapātadhautakaladhautamayaśilātalo nandanādipramadāvanavihārimaṇimayaśakuntakamanīyaninadamanoharaḥ parvatarājaḥ sumeruriti ; naiṣa bhujaṅgo rajjuriyamityādiḥ /
nāpi bhūtārthabuddhirvyutpannapuruṣavartinī na śakyā samunnetum, harṣāderunnayanahotoḥ saṃbhavāt /
tathā hi- aviditāryajanabhāṣārtho draviḍo nagaragamanodyato rājamārgābhyarṇaṃ devadattamandiramadhyāsīnaḥ pratipannajanakānandanibandhanaputrajanmā vārttāhāreṇa saha nagarasthadevadattābhyāśamāgataḥ paṭavāsopāyanārpaṇapuraḥsaraṃ 'diṣṭyā vardhase devadatta putraste jātaḥ' iti vārttāhāravyāhāraśravaṇasamanantaramupajātaromāñcakañcukaṃ vikasitanayanotpalamatismeramukhamahotpalamavalokya devadattamutpannapramodamanumimīte ; pramodasya ca prāgabhūtasya tadvyāhāraśravaṇasamanantaraṃ prabhavatastaddhetutām ; na cāyamapratipādayan harṣahetumarthaṃ harṣāya kalpata ityanena harṣaheturartha ukta iti pratipadyate ; harṣahetvantarasya cāpratīteḥ putrajanmanaśca taddhetoravagamāttadeva vārttāhāreṇābhyadhāyīti niścinoti /
evaṃ bhayaśokādayo 'pyudāhāryāḥ /
tathā ca prayojanavattayā bhūtārthābhidhānasya prekṣāvatprayogo 'pyupapannaḥ /
evaṃ ca brahmasvarūpajñānasya paramapuruṣārthahetubhāvādanupadiśatāmapi puruṣapravṛttinivṛttī vedāntānāṃ puruṣahitānuśāsanācchāstratvaṃ siddhaṃ bhavati /
tatsiddhametat- vivādādhyāsitāni vacanāni bhūtārthaviṣayāṇi, bhūtārthaviṣayapramājanakatvāt ; yadyadviṣayapramājanakaṃ tattadviṣayaṃ, yathā rūpādiviṣayaṃ cakṣurādi ; tathā caitāni ; tasmāttatheti /
tasmātsuṣṭhūktam- #tanna; aupaniṣadasya puruṣasyānanyaśeṣatvāt#iti /
upanipūrvātsaderviśaraṇārthātkvipyupaniṣatpadaṃ vyutpāditam, upanīya advayaṃ brahma savāsanāmavidyāṃ hinastīti brahmavidyāmāha ; taddhetutvādvedāntā apyupaniṣadaḥ ; tato viditaḥ aupaniṣadaḥ puruṣaḥ /
body.translated_text:
because utterances of strings of words oriented toward non-action — for the purpose of removing curiosity, fear, and the like — are abundantly observed in the world.
For example: 'The king of mountains, <s>Meru</s>, is the dwelling place of the circle of world-guardians beginning with <s>Indra</s>, attended by <s>Siddha</s>s, <s>Vidyādhara</s>s, <s>Gandharva</s>s, and <s>Apsaras</s>es, with its base of golden rock washed by the cascade of the stream of the <s>Mandākinī</s> descending from the world of <s>Brahmā</s>, delightful with the charming sounds of jeweled birds sporting in pleasure-groves beginning with <s>Nandana</s>' — and so forth; and 'This is not a snake, it is a rope' — and the like.
Nor is it impossible to infer the cognition of an established fact in a learned person, since joy and the like — which are its indicators — are possible.
This is as follows: A <s>Drāviḍa</s> (South Indian) person, who does not understand the language of the noble people (<s>āryajana</s>), [but] who is eager to go to the city, is seated near the house of <s>Devadatta</s> on the royal road. [He sees] a news-bearer who has learned that <s>Devadatta</s> has had a son — the cause of the father's joy — arrive near <s>Devadatta</s> in the city. Having offered a gift of a cloth-wrapping as a greeting, [the news-bearer says]: 'Congratulations to you, <s>Devadatta</s>! A son has been born to you!' — and immediately upon hearing the news-bearer's utterance, [the <s>Drāviḍa</s>], observing <s>Devadatta</s> with his body covered in goosebumps, his eyes blossoming like blue lotuses, his face beaming and radiant like a great lotus, infers <s>Devadatta</s>'s arising delight; and [infers] the causal relation of that delight — which was non-existent before — [to what arose] immediately upon hearing the utterance; and [reflects:] 'This [utterance] is not fit to produce joy without communicating a meaning that is the cause of joy'; and thereby he understands that a meaning which is the cause of joy has been stated; and since no other cause of joy is perceived, and since the birth of a son — being a cause of joy — is understood, he ascertains that that alone was communicated by the news-bearer.
Similarly, fear, grief, and the like should also be illustrated.
And thus, since the communication of established facts by discerning persons is purposeful, its usage by the discerning is also justified.
And thus, this is established: The statements at issue [i.e., the <s>Vedānta</s>s] are about established facts, because they are generators of valid cognition whose content is established facts; whatever generates valid cognition regarding a certain content has that very content — like the eye and the like regarding form and the like; and these [<s>Vedānta</s>s] are such; therefore, [they are] so.
Therefore, it is well said: 'That is not so; because the <s>Upaniṣadic</s> person is not subsidiary to anything else' (<s>aupaniṣadasya puruṣasyānanyaśeṣatvāt</s>).
The word '<s>upaniṣat</s>' is etymologically derived from the prefix '<s>upa-ni</s>' and the root '<s>sad</s>' in the sense of dissolution, with the suffix '<s>kvip</s>'; it denotes the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, which, having brought [the aspirant] near, destroys <s>avidyā</s> together with its impressions and [leads to] the non-dual <s>Brahman</s>; and because the <s>Vedānta</s>s are the cause of that [knowledge], they too are called <s>Upaniṣad</s>s; the person known from them is the <s>Upaniṣadic</s> person (<s>aupaniṣada puruṣa</s>).

body.text:
etadeva vibhajate- #yo 'sāvupaniṣatsveva#iti /
ahaṃpratyayaviṣayādbhinatti- #asaṃsārī#iti /
ata eva kriyārahitatvāccaturvidhadravyavilakṣaṇaḥ /
ataśca caturvidhadravyavilakṣaṇo yadanyaśeṣaḥ /
anyaśeṣaṃ hi bhūtaṃ dravyaṃ cikīrṣitaṃ sadutpattyādyāpyaṃ saṃbhavati, yathā 'yūpaṃ takṣati' ityādi /
yatpunaranyaśeṣaṃ bhūtabhāvyupayogarahitam, yathā 'suvarṇaṃ bhāryam', 'saktūn juhoti' ityādi, na tasyotpattyādyāpyatā /
body.translated_text:
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] analyzes this very [point]: 'That which is [known] from the <s>Upaniṣad</s>s alone...' (<s>yo 'sāvupaniṣatsveva</s>).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] distinguishes [this person] from the object of the I-cognition: 'Non-<s>saṃsāric</s>' (<s>asaṃsārī</s>).
For this very reason — because of being devoid of action — [this person] is different from the four kinds of substance.
And hence, being different from the four kinds of substance, it would be subsidiary to something else only if [it could be].
For an existing substance that is subsidiary to something else — being producible, being something to be brought about by origination and the like — is possible, like 'One fashions the sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>)' and the like.
But that which is subsidiary to something else — [yet] devoid of any utilization, whether existing or to-be-produced — like 'gold is a wife' (<s>suvarṇaṃ bhāryam</s>), 'one offers <s>saktū</s>s' (<s>saktūn juhoti</s>) and the like — for that, there is no susceptibility to origination and the like.

body.text:
kasmātpunarasyānanyaśeṣatetyata āha- yataḥ #svaprakaraṇasthaḥ# /
upaniṣadāmanārabhyādhītānāṃ paurvāparyaparyālocanayā puruṣapratipādanaparatvena puruṣasyaiva prādhānyenedaṃ prakaraṇam /
na ca juhvādivadavyabhicaritakratusaṃbandhaḥ puruṣa ityupapāditam /
ataḥ svaprakaraṇasthaḥ so 'yaṃ tathāvidha upaniṣadbhyaḥ pratīyamāno na nāstīti śakyo vaktumityarthaḥ /
body.translated_text:
Why then is this [<s>Upaniṣadic</s> person] not subsidiary to something else? — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: Because 'it stands in its own context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>)' (<s>svaprakaraṇasthaḥ</s>).
The <s>Upaniṣad</s>s, having been studied without being [formally] inaugurated [as a separate topic], through the examination of their beginning and end — being oriented toward the teaching of the person — this is primarily the context of the person alone.
And it has been established that the person [taught in the <s>Upaniṣad</s>s] does not have an invariable connection with ritual, like the ladle (<s>juhū</s>) and the like.
Therefore, standing in its own context — this [<s>Upaniṣadic</s> person] of such a nature, as understood from the <s>Upaniṣad</s>s, cannot be said not to exist — this is the meaning.

body.text:
syādetat /
mānāntarogocaratvenāgṛhītasaṃgatitayā apadārthasya brahmaṇo vākyārthatvānupapatteḥ kathamupaniṣadarthatetyata āha- #sa eṣa neti netyātmetyātmaśabdāt# /
yadyapi gavādivanmānāntaragocaratvamātmano nāsti, tathāpi prakāśātmana eva satastattadupādhiparihāṇyā śakyaṃ vākyārthatvena nirūpaṇam, hāṭakasyeva kaṭakakuṇḍalādiparihāṇyā /
na hi prakāśaḥ svasaṃvedano na bhāsate ; nāpi tadavacchedakaḥ kāryakaraṇasaṃghātaḥ /
tena 'sa ena neti netyātmā' iti tattadavacchedaparihāṇyā bṛhattvādāpanācca svayaṃprakāśaḥ śakyo vākyāt brahmeti cātmeti ca nirūpayitumityarthaḥ /
body.translated_text:
One might say this:
Since <s>Brahman</s>, being beyond the reach of other means of knowledge, has an unascertained relation [with words], and hence is a non-word-meaning — how can it be the meaning of [<s>Vedānta</s>] sentences? — and [therefore] how can it be [known] from the <s>Upaniṣad</s>s? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'That Self, [described as] "not this, not this" (<s>neti neti</s>) — from the word "Self" (<s>ātmaśabda</s>)...'
Although the Self does not have accessibility to other means of knowledge like a cow and the like, nevertheless, being of the nature of luminosity (<s>prakāśa</s>) and existing [as such], through the removal of each limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>), it can be defined as the sentence-meaning — like gold (<s>hāṭaka</s>) [determined] through the removal of earrings, bracelets, and the like.
For luminosity, being self-cognized, does shine.
Nor does the aggregate of effects and instruments (<s>kāryakaraṇasaṃghāta</s>) that delimits it [fail to shine].
Therefore, 'That Self, [described as] "not this, not this"' — through the removal of each delimiting adjunct, and through the attribution of greatness (<s>bṛhattva</s>) and the like — the self-luminous [Self] can be determined from the sentence as <s>Brahman</s> and as the Self — this is the meaning.

body.text:
athopādhinirāsavadupahitamapyātmarūpaṃ kasmānna nirasyata ityata āha- #ātmanaśca pratyākhyātumaśakyatvāt# /
prakāśo hi sarvasyātmā tadadhiṣṭhānatvācca prapañcavibhramasya /
na cādhiṣṭhānābhāve vibhramo bhavitumarhati ; na hi jātu rajjvabhāve rajjvāṃ bhujaṅga iti vā dhāreti vā vibhramo dṛṣṭapūrvaḥ /
api cātmānaḥ prakāśasya bhāsā prapañcasya prabhā /
tathā ca śrutiḥ 'tameva bhāntamanu bhāti sarvaṃ tasya bhāsā sarvamidaṃ vibhāti' iti /
na cātmanaḥ prakāśasya pratyākhyāne prapañcaprathā yuktā /
tasmādātmanaḥ pratyākhyānāyogādvedāntebhyaḥ pramāṇāntarāgocarasarvopādhirahitabrahmasvarūpāvagatisiddhirityarthaḥ /
body.translated_text: Now, why is the form of the Self — even though conditioned by limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) — not negated, just as the limiting adjuncts are negated? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Because the Self cannot be repudiated' (<s>ātmanaśca pratyākhyātumaśakyatvāt</s>). For luminosity (<s>prakāśa</s>) is the Self of everything, and [it is] the substrate (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) of the illusion of the phenomenal world (<s>prapañca</s>). And in the absence of the substrate, illusion cannot arise — for never has an illusion of 'this is a snake' or 'this is a stream' been previously seen when the rope is absent. Moreover, by the radiance (<s>bhāsa</s>) of the Self — which is luminosity — the phenomenal world shines forth (<s>prabhā</s>). And thus the <s>Śruti</s>: 'Everything shines after That which shines; by the light of That, all this is illuminated' (<s>tameva bhāntam anubhāti sarvaṃ tasya bhāsā sarvam idaṃ vibhāti</s>). And if the Self — which is luminosity — were repudiated, the manifestation of the phenomenal world would not be possible. Therefore, since the Self cannot be repudiated, the ascertainment of the essential nature of <s>Brahman</s> — free from all limiting adjuncts and beyond the scope of any other means of knowledge — is established from the <s>Vedānta</s>s. This is the meaning.

body.text:
upaniṣatsvevāvagata ityavadhāraṇamamṛṣyamāṇa ākṣipati- #nanvātmā#iti /
sarvajanīnāhaṃpratyayaviṣayo hyātmā kartā bhoktā ca saṃsārī, tatraiva ca laukikaparīkṣakāṇāmātmapadaprayogāt /
ya eva laukikāḥ śabdāḥ, te eva vaidikāḥ,
body.translated_text: Unable to tolerate the restrictive assertion that [<s>Brahman</s>] is understood only in the <s>Upaniṣad</s>s, [the opponent] objects: 'But surely, the Self...' (<s>nanvātmā</s>). For the Self — which is the object of the 'I'-cognition universal to all people — is an agent, an enjoyer, and a transmigrating being (<s>saṃsārin</s>); and it is precisely in that [sense] that ordinary people and critical thinkers use the word 'Self' (<s>ātmapadaprayoga</s>). And since the very same mundane words are also Vedic words,

body.text: te eva ca teṣāmarthā ityaupaniṣadamapyātmapadaṃ tatraiva pravartitumarhati, nārthāntare tadviparīte ityarthaḥ /
body.translated_text: and since their meanings too are the same — therefore, even the <s>Upaniṣadic</s> word 'Self' should be applied to that very [agent-enjoyer-transmigrator], not to a contrary meaning. This is the meaning.

body.text:
samādhatte- #na#ahaṃpratyayaviṣaya aupaniṣadaḥ puruṣaḥ /
kutaḥ ? #tatsākṣitvena#-ahaṃpratyayaviṣayo yaḥ kartā kāryakaraṇasaṃghātopahito jīvātmā-tat sākṣitvena, paramātmano 'haṃpratyayaviṣayatvasya #pratyuktatvāt# /
etaduktaṃ bhavati- yadyapi 'anena jīvenātmanā' iti jīvaparamātmanoḥ pāramārthikamaikyam, tathāpi tasyopahitaṃ rūpaṃ jīvaḥ ; śuddhaṃ tu rūpaṃ tasya sākṣi ; tacca mānāntarānadhigatamupaniṣadgocara iti /
etadeva prapañcayati- #na hyahaṃpratyayaviṣaya#iti /
body.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] resolves [the objection]: 'No' — the <s>Upaniṣadic</s> person is not the object of the 'I'-cognition. Why? 'By being the witness of that' (<s>tatsākṣitvena</s>) — the agent, the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>) conditioned by the aggregate of effects and instruments, who is the object of the 'I'-cognition — by being the witness of that, the supreme Self's (<s>paramātman</s>'s) being the object of the 'I'-cognition has been 'already refuted' (<s>pratyuktatvāt</s>). What is stated amounts to this: although there is ultimate identity of the individual self and the supreme Self — as in '<s>anena jīvenātmanā</s>' (by this individual self) — nevertheless, the conditioned form of that [Self] is the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul); while its pure form is the witness (<s>sākṣin</s>); and that [pure form], being unattained by any other means of knowledge, is the domain of the <s>Upaniṣad</s>s. [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] elaborates this very [point]: 'For the object of the I-cognition...' (<s>na hyahaṃpratyayaviṣaya</s>).

#vidhiśeṣatvaṃ vā netuṃ#na śakyaḥ /
kutaḥ ? #ātmatvādeva# /
na hyātmā anyārthaḥ, anyattu sarvamātmārtham /
tathā ca śrutiḥ 'na vā are sarvasya kāmāya sarvaṃ priyaṃ bhavati ātmanastu kāmāya sarvaṃ priyaṃ bhavati' iti /

etadupapādayati- #sarvaṃ hi vinaśyadvikārajātaṃ puruṣāntaṃ vinaśyati# /
ayamarthaḥ- puruṣo hi śrutismṛtītihāsapurāṇatadaviruddhanyāyavyavasthāpitatvātparamārthasan ; prapañcastvanādyavidyopadarśito 'paramārthasan /
yaśca paramārthāsan asau prakṛtiḥ rajjutattvamiva sarvavibhramasya vikārasya /
ata evāsyānirvācyatvenādṛḍhasvabhāvasya vināśaḥ /
puruṣastu paramārthasan ; nāsau kāraṇasahasreṇāpyasan śakyaḥ kartum /
na hi sahasramapi śilpino ghaṭaṃ paṭayitumīśata ityuktam /
tasmādavināśipuruṣānto vikāravināśaḥ śuktirajjutattvānta iva rajatabhujaṅgavināśaḥ /
puruṣa eva hi sarvasya prapañcavikārajātasya tattvam /
na ca puruṣasyāsti vināśo yato 'nantaḥ /
vināśaḥ syādityata āha- #puruṣo hi vināśahetvabhāvāt#iti /
na hi kāraṇāni sahasramapyanyadanyathayitumīśata ityuktam /
atha mā bhūtsvarūpeṇa puruṣo heya upādeyo vā ; tadīyastu kaściddharmo hāsyate, kaściccopādāsyata ityata āha- #vikriyāhetvabhāvācca kūṭasthanityaḥ# /
trividho 'pi dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāmalakṣaṇo vikāro nāstītyuktam /
api cātmanaḥ paramārthasato dharmo 'pi paramārthasanniti na tasyātmavadanyathātvaṃ kāraṇaiḥ śakyaṃ kartum /
na ca dharmānyathātvādanyo vikāraḥ /
tadidamuktam- #vikriyāhotvabhāvāt#iti /
sugamamanyat /
body.translated_text: 'Nor can [<s>Brahman</s>] be construed as subsidiary to an injunction' (<s>vidhiśeṣatvaṃ vā netuṃ na śakyaḥ</s>). Why? 'Because of its very nature as the Self' (<s>ātmatvādeva</s>). For the Self does not exist for the sake of another; rather, everything else exists for the sake of the Self. And thus the <s>Śruti</s>: 'It is not for the sake of all, indeed, that all is dear; rather, it is for the sake of the Self that all is dear' (<s>na vā are sarvasya kāmāya sarvaṃ priyaṃ bhavati ātmanas tu kāmāya sarvaṃ priyaṃ bhavati</s>). Moreover, precisely because it is the Self of all, [<s>Brahman</s>] is neither to be rejected nor to be adopted. For the reality (<s>tattva</s>) — the Self — of the entire class of phenomenal entities is <s>Brahman</s> alone. And one's own nature cannot be rejected, since it is impossible to abandon; nor can it be adopted, since it is already possessed. Therefore, injunctions and prohibitions, whose domain is what is to be rejected and adopted, cannot have as their object the reality of the Self, which is the contrary [of what is to be rejected or adopted] — thus, the Self alone is the reality of the entire class of phenomenal entities. [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] establishes this: 'For the entire class of modifications (<s>vikāra</s>s), being perishable, perishes — terminating in the person (<s>puruṣa</s>).' The meaning is this: the person (<s>puruṣa</s>) — being ultimately real, established by <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, <s>Itihāsa</s>, <s>Purāṇa</s>, and reasoning not contradicting them — is ultimately existent; but the phenomenal world, displayed by beginningless <s>avidyā</s>, is not ultimately existent. And that which is not ultimately existent is the <s>prakṛti</s> (material cause) — like the reality of the rope — of every modification, which is an illusion. For this very reason, being indescribable (<s>anirvācya</s>) and of unstable nature, it is subject to destruction. But the person is ultimately existent; it cannot be made non-existent even by a thousand causes. For it has been said: 'Not even a thousand artisans can make a pot into a cloth.' Therefore, the destruction of modifications terminates in the indestructible person — just as the destruction of the [illusory] silver and snake terminates in the reality of the nacre and the rope. For the person alone is the reality of the entire class of phenomenal modifications. And the person has no destruction, since it is infinite. Lest [one object that] there could be destruction, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Because the person has no cause of destruction' (<s>puruṣo hi vināśahetvabhāvāt</s>). For it has been said that not even a thousand causes can make one thing into another. Now, let the person not be rejectable or adoptable in its essential nature; but some property of it will be abandoned, and some will be adopted — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'And because there is no cause of modification, [the Self] is immutably eternal (<s>kūṭastha-nitya</s>).' What is stated is that the threefold modification — characterized by property-change (<s>dharma</s>), temporal-state-change (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), and condition-change (<s>avasthā</s>) — does not exist [for the Self]. Moreover, since the property of the Self, which is ultimately real, is also ultimately real, it — like the Self — cannot be made otherwise by [any] causes. And there is no modification other than the alteration of a property. This is what is stated: 'Because there is no cause of modification' (<s>vikriyāhetvabhāvāt</s>). The rest is easy [to understand].

body.text:
yatpunarekadeśinā śāstravidvacanaṃ sākṣitvenānukrāntaṃ tadanyathopapādayati- #yadapi śāstratātparyavidāmanukramāṇam#iti /
'dṛṣṭo hi tasyārthaḥ prayojanavadarthāvabodhanam' iti vaktavye, dharmajijñāsāyāḥ prakṛtatvāddharmasya ca karmatvāt 'karmāvabodhanam' ityuktam /
na tu siddharūpabrahmāvabodhanavyāpāraṃ vedasya vārayati /
na hi somaśarmaṇi prakṛte tadguṇābhidhānaṃ parisaṃcaṣṭe viṣṇuśarmaṇo guṇavattām /
vidhiśāstraṃ vidhīyamānakarmaviṣayam ; pratiṣedhaśāstraṃ ca pratiṣidhyamānakarmaviṣayamityubhayamapi karmāvabodhanaparam /
api ca 'āmnāyasya kriyārthatvāt' iti śāstrakṛdvacanam /
tatrārthagrahaṇaṃ yadyabhidheyavāci tato bhūtārthānāṃ dravyaguṇakarmaṇāmānarthakyamanabhidheyatvaṃ prasajyeta ; na hi te kriyārthā ityata āha- #api cāmnāyasya#iti /
yadyucyeta- na hi kriyārthatvaṃ kriyābhidheyatvam, api tu kriyāprayojanatvam ; dravyaguṇaśabdānāṃ ca kriyārthatvenaiva bhūtadravyaguṇābhidhānam, na svaniṣṭhatayā /
yathāhuḥ śāstravidaḥ 'codanā hi bhūtaṃ bhavantam' ityādi /
etaduktaṃ bhavati, kāryamarthamavagamayantī codanā tadarthaṃ bhūtādikamapyarthaṃ gamayatīti-tatrāha- #pravṛttinivṛttivyatirekeṇa bhūtaṃ cet#iti /
ayamabhisaṃdhiḥ-na tāvatkāryārthā eva svārthe padānāṃ saṃgatigraho nānyārtha ityupapāditaṃ bhūte 'pyarthe vyutpattiṃ darśayadbhiḥ /
nāpi svārthamātraparataiva padānām /
tathā sati na vākyārthapratyayaḥ syāt /
na hi pratyekaṃ svapradhānatayā guṇapradhānabhāvarahitānāmekavākyatā dṛṣṭā /
tasmātpadānāṃ svārthamabhidadhatāmekaprayojanavatpadārthaparatayaikavākyatā /
tathā ca tattadarthāntaraviśiṣṭaikavākyārthapratyaya upapanno bhavati /
body.translated_text: Now, the statement of a one-sided knower of the <s>śāstra</s>, which was cited as a witness, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] explains otherwise: 'And what is cited by those who know the purport of the <s>śāstra</s>...' (<s>yadapi śāstratātparyavidāmanukramāṇam</s>). Instead of saying 'its purpose is seen to be the communication of meaningful and purposeful content,' [the author] said '<s>karmāvabodhanam</s>' (the communication of action), because the desire to know <s>dharma</s> is the topic at hand and <s>dharma</s> is action. But this does not preclude the function of the <s>Veda</s> in communicating the established nature of <s>Brahman</s>. For when <s>Somaśarman</s> is the topic, the statement of his qualities does not exclude the quality-possessing-ness of <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s>. The scripture of injunctions has as its domain the action being enjoined; and the scripture of prohibitions has as its domain the action being prohibited — thus both are devoted to the communication of action. Moreover, '<s>āmnāyasya kriyārthatvāt</s>' (because scripture has action as its purpose) is the statement of the author of the [<s>Mīmāṃsā</s>] <s>sūtra</s>s. Therein, if the word '<s>artha</s>' means 'referent' (<s>abhidheya</s>), then the absurd consequence would be that established entities such as substances (<s>dravya</s>), qualities (<s>guṇa</s>), and actions (<s>karma</s>) would be purposeless and non-denotable — for they are not action-oriented. To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Moreover, [regarding the statement] of scripture...' (<s>api cāmnāyasya</s>). If it be said: action-orientedness is not the denoting of action, but rather having action as its purpose; and words for substances and qualities denote established substances and qualities only by virtue of their action-orientedness, not self-referentially — as the knowers of <s>śāstra</s> say: 'For the injunction [communicates] what exists [and] what is to come into being' etc. What is stated amounts to this: the injunction, while communicating the producible meaning, also communicates the established meaning such as substances etc. for the sake of that [producible meaning]. To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'But if [the Veda communicates] an established entity apart from engagement and disengagement...' (<s>pravṛttinivṛttivyatirekeṇa bhūtaṃ cet</s>). The intent is this: First, it has been established by those who show that verbal competence (<s>vyutpatti</s>) applies even to established entities that the comprehension of the relation of words with their own meanings [occurs] in their own [domain], not only for the purpose of action. Nor are words devoted solely to their own meaning. If that were so, there would be no sentence-meaning cognition. For sentential unity has never been observed among [words] that are each independently primary, without a principal-subordinate relation. Therefore, the sentential unity of words — which denote their own meanings — [arises] through being oriented toward a word-meaning that serves a single purpose. And thus the sentence-meaning cognition, qualified by various subsidiary meanings, is justified.

body.text: yathāhuḥ śāstravidaḥ-
body.translated_text: As the knowers of <s>śāstra</s> say —

body.text: sākṣādyadyapi kurvanti padārthapratipādanam /
body.translated_text: Even though words directly communicate the meanings of their terms,

body.text: varṇāstathāpi naitasminparyavasyanti niṣphale //
body.translated_text: the word-elements (<s>varṇa</s>s) do not rest in this fruitless [isolated meaning]. //

body.text: vākyārthamitaye teṣāṃ pravṛttau nāntarīyakam /
body.translated_text: In their operation for the purpose of sentence-meaning, inevitably,

body.text: pāke jvāleva kāṣṭhānāṃ padārthapratipādanam //
body.translated_text: the communication of word-meaning is like the flame of firewood in cooking. //
