#na jñānapratibandhakāraṇarahitasyeti# /
saṃsāriṇāṃ vastuto nityajñānatve 'pyavidyāyāḥ pratibandhakāraṇāni santi, natu īśvarasyāvidyārahitasya jñānapratibandhakāraṇasaṃbhava iti bhāvaḥ /
na tasya kāryamāvaraṇādyapagamo vidyate, anāvṛttatvāditi bhāvaḥ /
jñānabalena kriyā /
pradhānasya tvacetanasya jñānabalābhāvājjagato na kriyetyarthaḥ /
body.translated_text:
Thus.
'By <s>tapas</s>' — by knowledge whose object is the unevolved (<s>avyākṛta</s>) name and form — [<s>Brahman</s>] 'is augmented' (<s>cīyate</s>), i.e., becomes as if wishing to manifest that [name and form]. Just as a weaver and the like, having sketched in the mind the unmanifest cloth and so on, wishes to produce it.
One who possesses one attribute is said to be 'augmented' (<s>upacita</s>) by the generation of a second attribute.
And when augmentation in the form of the wish to manifest has occurred, from that — name and form, [i.e.,] 'food' (<s>anna</s>), the edible, the common [substrate] of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration), the intended-to-be-manifested — is born.
From that unevolved, intended-to-be-manifested food, <s>Prāṇa</s> — <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, the substratum of <s>Brahman</s>'s powers of knowledge and action, the thread-self (<s>sūtrātman</s>) of the world — is born in the common [substrate], just as from the unevolved, intended-to-be-manifested cloth, an intermediate product such as two-threaded yarn and the like [is born].
And from that <s>Prāṇa</s>, mind (<s>manas</s>) — named the faculty of determination (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) and conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>), whose nature is differentiation (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) — is born.
From that mind, whose nature is differentiation, the entities denoted by the word '<s>satya</s>' (truth) — <s>ākāśa</s> (space) and the rest — are born.
And from those [entities] called '<s>satya</s>,' in sequence, the worlds — <s>Bhūḥ</s> and the rest — [are born]; in them, living beings such as humans and the like, and in accordance with the order of <s>varṇa</s>s and <s>āśrama</s>s, actions (<s>karma</s>s) of the nature of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> are born.
And in actions, 'immortality' (<s>amṛta</s>) — the fruit, [namely] heaven, hell, and the like.
And that [fruit], as long as its own causes — <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> — exist, does not perish — hence 'immortal' (<s>amṛta</s>).
[That is to say:] as long as <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> last.
'He who is omniscient' — in general; 'all-knowing' — in particulars.
'Whose <s>tapas</s> is of the nature of knowledge' — whose <s>dharma</s> is not of the nature of exertion — from that former, prior <s>Brahman</s>, this subsequent, produced (<s>kārya</s>) <s>Brahman</s> [is born].
Moreover, name, form, and food — rice, barley, and the like — are born.
Therefore — since <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter), in its state of equilibrium, lacks the capacity to see (<s>anīkṣitṛtva</s>); since the <s>kṣetrajña</s>s (individual selves), even though possessing consciousness, do not see objects at the beginning of creation; since when a primary meaning is possible, figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>) is inappropriate; since false instruction to a seeker of liberation is untenable; since [false instruction] would contradict liberation; since it is logically established that for fire (<s>tejas</s>) and the rest, figurative usage is resorted to because primary meaning is impossible; and since in a doubtful case, the preponderance of [passages supporting the] primary reading is determinative; and since here, when the primary meaning is established by being the default (<s>autsargika</s>), there is no doubt — otherwise, even a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> by descent (<s>brāhmaṇāyana</s>) living in a land mixed with hundreds of <s>Kirāta</s>s (tribals) would incur the consequence of being a <s>Kirāta</s> —
<s>Brahman</s> alone, assisted by beginningless, inexpressible <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), is the material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) of the world — as mother-of-pearl [is the cause] of the superimposed silver, as heat-waves [are the cause] of [illusory] water, as the [single] moon [is the cause] of [the illusion of] a second moon.
But not the insentient <s>Pradhāna</s>, atoms, and the like.
For those are without scriptural authority (<s>aśabda</s>).
Nor is <s>Pradhāna</s> or atoms — supervised by an omniscient <s>Īśvara</s> distinct from them — the material cause of the world — because [the world] is an effect.
Because there is no difference of effects from their cause, and because the complete knowledge of all effects through the knowledge of the cause has been established by scripture through the illustration of clay and the like, and because in [the case of] difference, that [complete knowledge] would be untenable.
And directly, by [<s>Śruti</s>s such as] 'One alone, without a second,' 'There is no multiplicity here whatsoever,' 'From death to death goes [he who sees multiplicity]' and the like — since the phenomenal world (<s>prapañca</s>) other than <s>Brahman</s> is negated — the world has a conscious material cause alone, like a rope [being the cause] of the superimposed snake — this is the established conclusion.
For when the [world's] having an existent (<s>sat</s>) material cause is established, one should inquire — raising the doubt — whether that material cause of the world is conscious or unconscious.
Even now, the [world's] having an existent material cause has not been established — hence [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#That which is denoted by the word "this" (<s>idam</s>)#' and so on, up to '#[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] shows#.'
Even so, the seer (<s>īkṣitṛ</s>) will be an <s>Īśvara</s> distinct from the ultimate <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>kṣetrajña</s> — as the <s>Hairaṇyagarbha</s>s (followers of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>) say. Hence the <s>Śruti</s> is cited: 'One alone, without a second.'
'Let me become many' — this [<s>Śruti</s>] speaks of the insentient cause itself wishing to become many.
By this too, the non-difference of the effect from the conscious cause is accepted.
Even though the creation of elements begins with <s>ākāśa</s> (space), nevertheless, since the triplication (<s>trivṛtkaraṇa</s>) of fire, water, and food alone is intended [in the <s>Chāndogya</s>], and since fire has primacy there, fire is mentioned first.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] cites another <s>Śruti</s> [to establish] that the one without a second is the material cause of the world: '#Similarly elsewhere#.'
<s>Brahman</s> has four feet and eight hooves, sixteen parts.
Thus: east, west, south, north — these are the four parts; the first foot of <s>Brahman</s> is called <s>Prakāśavān</s> (the luminous).
Half [of each part] is a hoof.
Likewise, earth, atmosphere, heaven, ocean — these are another four parts; the second foot is called <s>Anantavān</s> (the infinite).
Likewise, fire, sun, moon, lightning — these are four parts; the third foot is called <s>Jyotiṣmān</s> (the radiant).
<s>Prāṇa</s>, eye, ear, speech — these are four parts; the fourth foot of <s>Brahman</s> is called <s>Āyatanavān</s> (the abode-possessing).
Thus, <s>Brahman</s> with sixteen parts, sixteen members, is to be meditated upon — this is established.
One might object:
By [the word] '<s>īkṣateḥ</s>' (from seeing), the bare verbal root-form is stated with the verbal suffix <s>tip</s>.
And it is not possible that the bare verbal root-form, whose meaning is not intended [as the main point], could serve as proof for a conscious material cause — hence [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#From <s>īkṣateḥ</s>#' — what is intended is the indication of the verbal root-meaning, [which points to] the possessor of the object by [its] characteristic of [denoting] an object.
And this characteristic is well-known — so [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Just as in <s>yajateḥ</s>#' (just as in [the verbal form] 'he sacrifices').
'He who is omniscient' — in general; 'all-knowing' — in particulars.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>], having presented the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> resolution of their own view, refutes it: '#But what was said regarding the attribute of <s>sattva</s>#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> objection again: '#But it was said#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes: '#That too#.'
To begin with, <s>sattva</s> (the quality of goodness) is not operative in the aggregate sense — because the disequilibrium of the <s>guṇa</s>s [is needed for operation, and] equilibrium is untenable [as a basis for seeing].
Nor is knowledge connected with [<s>sattva</s>] in its unmanifest form, because <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> — even in their subtle form — exist as obstructions to it — this is the meaning.
Moreover, the [verbal root] '<s>jānāti</s>' (knows) has its primary usage in [the context of] a consciousness-dominated activity, and is not seen in ordinary usage in [the context of] a mere [insentient] activity — hence [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Moreover, not without a witness#.'
Then how [to explain] the omniscience of yogins arising from the predominance of <s>sattva</s>? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#But of yogins#.'
For the predominance of <s>sattva</s> assists the yogins' capacity of the eye of consciousness, not [the capacity of] blind <s>Pradhāna</s> — this is the meaning.
But if, abandoning the <s>Kāpila</s> (Sāṃkhya) view, one adopts the <s>Hairaṇyagarbha</s> (Yoga) view, against that too [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#But if, on the other hand, a witness-cause#.'
For them too, the omniscience belongs to a special <s>Puruṣa</s> alone — one untouched by afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>s), actions (<s>karma</s>), fruitions (<s>vipāka</s>), and latent deposits (<s>āśaya</s>) — whose material cause is predominant <s>sattva</s> — not to the insentient <s>Pradhāna</s>.
And that [view] too is rejected by the <s>Śruti</s>s of non-duality — this is the import.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] restates the seed of the prima facie view: '#And what was further said — of <s>Brahman</s> too#.'
Even though consciousness in its pure form is eternal, [<s>Brahman</s>] conditioned [by <s>upādhi</s>s] is impermanent, an effect — like space delimited by a pot — having intended [this], [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes: '#This much, O sir#.'
'In the sun, whose nature is extended heat and light' — this too [has the import that] the light delimited by the object is an effect — this is the intent.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises the objection of asymmetry: '#But surely, of the sun#.'
Does the venerable [objector] state the asymmetry with reference to the real absence of action [in <s>Brahman</s>], or with reference to the non-intention [of describing action]?
Therein, if with reference to the non-intention [of describing action], then: let there not be symmetry through 'he illuminates' (<s>prakāśayati</s>), but through 'it shines' (<s>prakāśate</s>) there is [symmetry].
For here, the action is not intended.
And yet, the nature of the sun — which has light as its essence and whose autonomy is well-established — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] resolves: '#No. Even without action#.'
'Even without' — meaning 'even without it being intended.'
Or, if the asymmetry is stated with reference to the real absence of action, that is not so, because the absence of action is unestablished and because action is intended here — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes: '#But when action is required#.'
The meaning is: those <s>Śruti</s>s that are tenable when action is not intended are all the more tenable when action is intended.
'#By whose grace#' — by the grace of <s>Īśvara</s>, the Lord; His eternally established knowledge is eternal — what more need be said? — this is the construction.
As the authors of the <s>Yoga-śāstra</s> [say]: 'Thence [arises] the attainment of the inner consciousness, and also the absence of obstacles.'
And their commentators [say]: <s>Īśvara</s>, won over by a special devotion, favors him with knowledge, dispassion, and the like.
'#Like the light of the sun#.'
Having stated, in terms of the real [nature], the independence [of <s>Brahman</s>'s knowledge] from any cause — by virtue of its eternality — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] also states [the same] by way of contrast (<s>vyatireka</s>): '#Moreover, [<s>Brahman</s>] being free from <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and the like#.'
By the word 'and the like' (<s>ādi</s>), desire (<s>kāma</s>), action (<s>karma</s>), and so on are included.
'#Not of one free from the cause of obstruction to knowledge#.'
Even though beings in <s>saṃsāra</s> possess in reality eternal knowledge, the causes of obstruction — belonging to <s>avidyā</s> — exist; but for <s>Īśvara</s>, who is free from <s>avidyā</s>, the possibility of causes of obstruction to knowledge does not arise — this is the import.
His [<s>Īśvara</s>'s] effect is not the removal of covering and the like, since He is uncovered — this is the import.
[<s>Brahman</s>'s] action is by the power of knowledge.
But <s>Pradhāna</s>, being insentient and lacking the power of knowledge, cannot create the world — this is the meaning.

body.text:
apāṇirgṛhītā, apādo vegavān viharaṇavān /
atirohitārthamanyat /
syādetet /
anātmani vyomni ghaṭādyupādhikṛto bhavatvavacchedakavibhramaḥ, na tu ātmani svabhāvasiddhaprakāśe sa ghaṭata ityata āha- #dṛśyate cātmana eva sata# #iti /
abhiniveśaḥ#mithyābhimānaḥ /
#mithyābuddhimātreṇa pūrveṇeti# /
anenānāditā darśitā /
mātragrahaṇena vicarasahatvena nirvacanīyatā nirastā /
pariśiṣṭam //5 // //6 //
body.translated_text:
[<s>Brahman</s> is] 'without hands, [yet] grasping; without feet, [yet] swift and moving.'
The rest has an obvious meaning.
One might object: in the non-self, namely space, let there be the delusion of delimitation caused by <s>upādhi</s>s such as pots and the like; but in the <s>Ātman</s>, whose nature is self-established luminosity (<s>prakāśa</s>), how can that [delusion] be possible? Hence [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#And it is seen that of the <s>Ātman</s> itself, being existent#.'
'<s>Abhiniveśa</s>' (clinging) means false identification (<s>mithyābhimāna</s>).
'#By the preceding false cognition alone#.'
By this [the word 'preceding'], the beginninglessness [of <s>avidyā</s>] is shown.
By the word 'alone' (<s>mātra</s>), the inexpressibility (<s>nirvacanīyatā</s>) [of <s>avidyā</s>] — in the sense of its inability to withstand scrutiny — is indicated.
The remainder [of the commentary is self-explanatory]. //5// //6//

children.translated_text: '#Because of the instruction of liberation to one who abides in That [<s>Brahman</s>]#.'

children.text: śaṅkottaratvena vā svātantryeṇa vā pradhānanirākaraṇārthaṃ sūtram /
children.translated_text: The <s>sūtra</s> is for the purpose of refuting <s>Pradhāna</s> — either as a response to an objection or independently.
And the objection has been stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>. //7//

body.text: syādetat /

children.text: brahmaiva jñīpsitaṃ, tacca na prathamaṃ sūkṣmatayā śakyaṃ śvetaketuṃ grāhayitumiti tatsaṃbaddhaṃ pradhānameva sthūlatayātmatvena grāhyate śvetaketurarundhatīmivātīva sūkṣmāṃ darśayituṃ tatsaṃnihitāṃ sthūlatārakāṃ darśayatīyamasāvarundhatīti /
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> alone is what is desired to be known; and since it cannot at first be made apprehensible to <s>Śvetaketu</s> because of its subtlety, [therefore] <s>Pradhāna</s> itself — which is related to it [<s>Brahman</s>] and is grosser — is first made apprehensible as <s>Ātman</s> to <s>Śvetaketu</s>, just as one who wishes to show [the star] <s>Arundhatī</s>, which is exceedingly subtle, first shows a grosser star near it, [saying] 'This is <s>Arundhatī</s>.'
To this objection, the reply is the <s>sūtra</s>: '#And because of the non-statement of [<s>Pradhāna</s>] as something to be rejected (<s>heya</s>)#.'
The word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) has the purpose of including what is not [explicitly] stated.
And what is not stated [in the <s>sūtra</s>] has been stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>. //8//

body.translated_text: One might object:

body.text: api ca jagatkāraṇaṃ prakṛtya svapitītyasya niruktaṃ karvitī śrutiścetanameva jagatkāraṇaṃ brūte /

children.translated_text: If the word '<s>sva</s>' (own) denotes the <s>Ātman</s> (self), even then the untenable consequence is that the conscious <s>Puruṣa</s> [would be identified with] the insentient <s>Pradhāna</s>.

If [the word '<s>sva</s>'] denotes 'what belongs to the self' (<s>ātmīya</s>), even then — [since <s>Pradhāna</s> would be] what belongs to the self and serves the purpose of the conscious [<s>Puruṣa</s>] — the dissolution of the conscious [<s>Puruṣa</s>] into the insentient [<s>Pradhāna</s>] that belongs to it is untenable.

children.text: nahi mṛdātmā ghaṭa ātmīye 'pi pāthasi pralīyate 'pi tvātmabhūtāyāṃ mṛdyeva /
children.translated_text: For a pot, whose essence is clay, does not dissolve into water that belongs to it, but only into clay, which is its [material] self.

children.text: naca gajatamanātmabhūte hastini pralīyate, kintvātmabhūtāyāṃ śuktāvevetyāha- #svāpyayāt# //9 //
children.translated_text: Nor does a [superimposed] elephant dissolve into a [real] elephant that is not its [material] self, but only into the mother-of-pearl that is its [material] self — hence [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Because of [the etymological analysis of] <s>svāpyaya</s> (return to one's own self)#.' //9//

body.translated_text: Moreover, with reference to the cause of the world, the etymology of [the word] '<s>svapiti</s>' (he sleeps) [as '<s>svaṃ apīta</s>' — 'gone to one's own self'] — this <s>Śruti</s> declares that the cause of the world is conscious alone.

body.text:
#gatisāmānyāt# /
gatiravagatiḥ /
#tārkikasamaya iveti# /

children.text: yathā hi tārkikāṇāṃ samayabhedeṣu parasparāhatārthatā, naivaṃ vedānteṣu parasparaparāhṛtiḥ, api tu teṣu sarvatra jagatkāraṇacetanyāvagatiḥ samāneti /
children.translated_text: For just as among the logicians there is mutual contradiction of meaning in their doctrinal differences, such mutual refutation does not exist among the <s>Vedānta</s> texts; rather, in all of them the understanding of consciousness as the cause of the world is the same.
"Just as the eye etc. with regard to form etc." (<s>cakṣurādīnām iva rūpādiṣu</s>).

children.text: yathā hi sarveṣāṃ cakṣū rūpameva grāhayati, na punā rasādikaṃ kasyaciddarśayati kasyacidrūpam /
children.translated_text: For just as the eye of all [beings] apprehends only form, and does not show taste etc. to one person and form to another,
so also with the tongue etc., this uniformity of purport should be understood. //10//

body.translated_text:
'#Because of the commonality of the designation (<s>gati</s>)#.'
<s>Gati</s> means cognition (<s>avagati</s>).
'#Just as in the system of the logicians (<s>tārkika</s>s)#.'

children.translated_text: "Because it is heard" (<s>śrutatvāt ca</s>).

children.text: 'tadaikṣata ityatra īkṣaṇamātraṃ jagatkāraṇasya śrutaṃ na tu sarvaviṣayam /
children.translated_text: In the passage 'It willed' (<s>tad aikṣata</s>), only the willing of the cause of the world is stated, not [its] omniscience directly.

children.text: jagatkāraṇasaṃbandhitayā tu tadarthātsarvaviṣayamavagataṃ, śvetāśvatarāṇāṃ tūpaniṣadi sarvajña īśvaro jagatkāraṇamiti sākṣāduktamiti viśeṣaḥ // 11 //
children.translated_text: But through its relation to being the cause of the world, omniscience is understood from its meaning. However, in the <s>Upaniṣad</s> of the <s>Śvetāśvatara</s>s, it is directly stated that the omniscient Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) is the cause of the world — that is the distinction. //11//

body.text:
uttarasūtrasaṃdarbhamākṣipati- #janmādyasya yata ityārabhyeti# /
brahma jijñāsitavyamiti hi pratijñātaṃ, tacca śāstraikasamadhigamyaṃ, śastraṃ ca sarvajñe sarvaśaktau jagadutpattisthitipralayakāraṇaṃ brahmaṇyeva pramāṇaṃ na pradhānādāviti nyāyato vyutpāditam /
na cāsti kaścidvedāntabhāgo yastadviparītamapi bodhayediti ca gatisāmānyāt ityuktam /
tatkimaparamavaśiṣyate, yadarthāntarasūtrasaṃdarbhasyāvatāraḥ syāditi /
#kimutthānamiti# /
kimākṣepe /
samādhatte-
body.translated_text: He raises the question about the purpose of the subsequent <s>sūtra</s>s: "Beginning from 'That from which the origin etc.'" (<s>janmādy asya yataḥ ity ārabhya</s>). For it was proposed that <s>Brahman</s> is to be inquired into, and that it is knowable only through <s>śāstra</s>, and that <s>śāstra</s> is a valid means of knowledge only regarding <s>Brahman</s> — which is omniscient, omnipotent, and the cause of the origination, sustenance, and dissolution of the world — and not regarding <s>Pradhāna</s> etc.; this has been established through reasoning. And it was stated through 'uniformity of purport' (<s>gatisāmānyāt</s>) that there is no portion of <s>Vedānta</s> that would teach anything contrary to this. Then what else remains, for which there would be occasion for a series of <s>sūtra</s>s on other topics? "What is the occasion?" (<s>kim utthānam</s>) — this is the objection. He resolves it —

body.text:
#ucyate-dvirūpaṃ hīti# /
yadyapi tatvato nirastasamastopādhirūpaṃ brahma tathāpi na tena rūpeṇa śakyamupadeṣṭumityupahitena rūpeṇopadeṣṭavyamiti /
tatra ca kvacidupādhirvivakṣitaḥ /
tadupāsanāni #kānicit abhyudayārthāni#manomātrasādhanatayātra paṭhitāni /
#kānicitkramamuktyarthāni, kānicitkarmasamṛddhyarthāni# /
kvacitpunarukto 'pyupādhipavivakṣitaḥ, yathātraivānnamayādaya ānandamayāntāḥ pañca kośāḥ /
tadatra kasminnupādhirvivakṣitaḥ kasminneti nādyāpi vivecitam /
tathā gatisāmānyamapi siddhavaduktaṃ, na tvadyāpi sādhitamiti tadarthamuttaragranthasaṃdarbhārambha ityarthaḥ /
syādetat /
parasyātmanastattadupādhibhedaviśiṣṭasyāpyabhedātkathamupāsanābhedaḥ, kathaṃ ca phalabheda ityata āha- #eka eva tviti# /
rūpābhede 'pyupādhibhedādupahitabhedādupāsanābhedastathā ca phalameva ityarthaḥ /
kratuḥ saṃkalpaḥ /
nanu yadyeka ātmā kūṭasthanityo niratiśayaḥ sarvabhūteṣu gūḍhaḥ, kathametasmin bhūtāśraye tāratamyaśrutayā ityata āha- #yadyapyeyaka ātmeti# /

children.text: yadyapi niratiśayakameva rūpamātmana eśvaryaṃ ca jñānaṃ cānandaśca, tathāpyanādyātamaḥ samāvṛtāṃ teṣu teṣu prāṇabhṛdbhedeṣu kvacidasadiva, kvacitsadiva, kvacidapakṛṣṭamiva, kvacitprakarṣavat, kvacidatyantaprakarṣavadiva bhāsate, tatkasya hetoḥ, avidyatamasaḥ prakarṣanikarṣatāratamyāditi /
children.translated_text: Although the form of the Self is solely unsurpassable — its lordship, knowledge, and bliss — nevertheless, being enveloped by beginningless darkness (<s>anādy ātamas</s>), in the various living beings it appears in some as if non-existent, in some as if existent, in some as if diminished, in some as if excellent, and in some as if supremely excellent. What is the cause of this? It is due to the gradation of intensity and diminution of the darkness of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>).

children.text: tathottamaprakāśaḥ savitā dihmaṇḍalamokarūpeṇaiva prakāśenāpūrayannapi varṣāsu nikṛṣṭaprakāśa iva śaradi tu prakṛṣṭaprakāśa iva prathate, tathedamapīti /
children.translated_text: Similarly, the sun, which has the highest luminosity, though filling the entire sphere of the sky with its own form of light, appears as if of diminished luminosity during the rainy season and as if of excellent luminosity in autumn — so too is this [Self], the meaning is.
"With regard to the connection with limiting adjuncts" (<s>apekṣitopādhisaṃbandham</s>) — as the object of meditation (<s>upāsya</s>).
"With the connection with limiting adjuncts removed" (<s>nirastopādhisaṃbandham</s>) — as the object of knowledge (<s>jñeya</s>). //11//

body.translated_text: "It is said — for it has two forms" (<s>ucyate — dvirūpaṃ hi</s>). Although in reality <s>Brahman</s> is devoid of all limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>), nevertheless, since it cannot be taught in that form, it must be taught through its conditioned form. And in that, sometimes the limiting adjunct is intended — some of those meditations (<s>upāsana</s>s) are "for the sake of prosperity" (<s>abhyudayārthāni</s>), being taught here as achievable through mind alone; some are "for the sake of gradual liberation" (<s>kramamuktyarthāni</s>), and some are "for the sake of perfecting ritual action" (<s>karmasamṛddhyarthāni</s>). But sometimes, even when mentioned, the limiting adjunct is not intended, as here with the five sheaths (<s>kośa</s>s) from <s>annamaya</s> to <s>ānandamaya</s>. So in which [passages] is the limiting adjunct intended and in which is it not — this has not yet been discriminated. Likewise, the uniformity of purport was stated as if already established, but has not yet been proven — for that purpose is the beginning of the subsequent textual series; this is the meaning. One might object: since even though the supreme Self is qualified by various limiting adjuncts, there is non-difference, how can there be difference of meditations, and how can there be difference of results? To this he says: "Though indeed one" (<s>eka eva tu</s>). Even though the form is non-different, due to difference of limiting adjuncts there is difference of the conditioned, hence difference of meditations, and likewise of results — this is the meaning. <s>Kratu</s> means intention (<s>saṃkalpa</s>). But if the one Self is immutable, eternal, unsurpassable, and hidden in all beings, how can there be a teaching of gradation regarding this being-dependent [Self]? To this he says: "Although this one Self" (<s>yady apy eka ātmā</s>).

children.translated_text: "<s>Ānandamaya</s>, because of repetition" (<s>ānandamayo 'bhyāsāt</s>).

There, first he constructs the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> according to the view of the partial-truth proponent (<s>ekadeśin</s>): "In the <s>Taittirīyaka</s>, '<s>annamaya</s>' etc." (<s>taittirīyake annamayam ity ādi</s>).
"Even when there is the flow of secondary [meaning], primary examination is appropriate;
But when both primary [meanings] are equal, the contextual preponderance determines the distinction." //

body.text:
' ānandamaya iti hi vikāre prācurye ca mayaṭastulyaṃ mukhyārthatvamiti vikārārthānnamayādipadaprāyapāṭhādānandamayapadamapi vikārārthameveti yuktam /
na ca prāṇamayādiṣu vikārārthatvāyogātsvārthiko mayaṅiti yuktam /

children.text: prāṇādyupādhyavacchinno hyātmā bhavati prāṇādivikārāḥ, ghaṭākāśamiva ghaṭavikārāḥ /
children.translated_text: For the Self delimited by the limiting adjunct of <s>prāṇa</s> etc. becomes the modifications of <s>prāṇa</s> etc., just as pot-space (<s>ghaṭākāśa</s>) becomes the modifications of the pot.
And the use of the suffix in its own sense [of abundance] is not appropriate for a real entity.
"But being inner to four sheaths (<s>kośa</s>s) does not make it the innermost of all;

children.text: priyādibhāgī śarīro jīvo na brahma yujyate //
children.translated_text: The embodied individual soul (<s>jīva</s>), which partakes of joy (<s>priya</s>) etc., is not reasonably [identified as] <s>Brahman</s>." //

body.translated_text: Since the suffix <s>mayaṭ</s> equally has primary meaning in both the sense of modification (<s>vikāra</s>) and abundance (<s>prācurya</s>), it is reasonable that the word <s>ānandamaya</s> also has the sense of modification, given the preponderant usage of words like <s>annamaya</s> etc. in the sense of modification. Nor is it reasonable [to say] that the suffix <s>mayaṅ</s> is used in its own sense [of abundance] because modification-meaning is inapplicable to <s>prāṇamaya</s> etc.

body.text:
' na ca sarvāntaratayā brahmaivānandamayaṃ, na jīva iti sāṃpratam /
nahīyaṃ śrutirānandamayasya sarvāntaratāṃ brūte api tvannamayādikośacatuṣṭhayāntaratāmānandamayakośasya /
na cāsmādanyasyāntarasyāśravaṇādayameva sarvāntara iti yuktam /
yadapekṣaṃ sasyāntaratvaṃ śrutaṃ tattasmādevāntaraṃ bhavati /
nahi devadatto balavānityukte sarvānsiṃhaśārdūlādīnapi prati halavānapratīyate 'pi tu samānajātīyanarāntaranapekṣya /
evamānandamayo 'pyannamayādibhyo 'ntaro na tu sarvasmāt /
na ca niṣkalasya brahmaṇaḥ priyādyavayavayogaḥ, nāpi śarīratvaṃ yujyata iti saṃsāryevānandamayaḥ /
tasmādupahitamevātropāsyatvena vivakṣitaṃ, na tu brahmarūpaṃ jñeyatveneti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ /
api ca yadi prācuryārtho 'pi mayaṭ, tathāpi saṃsāryevānandamayaḥ, na tu brahma /
ānandaprācurya hi tadviparītaduḥkhalavasaṃbhave bhavati na tu tadatyantāsaṃbhave /
na ca paramātmano manāgapi duḥkhalavasaṃbhavaḥ, ānandaikarasatvādityāha- #na ca saśarīrasya sata iti# /
aśarīrasya punarapriyasaṃbandho manāgapi nāstīti prācuryārtho 'pi mayaṅ nopapadyayata ityarthaḥ /
#ucyate# /
ānandamayāvayavasya tāvadbrahmaṇaḥ pucchasyāṅgatayā na prādhānyaṃ, api tvaṅgina ānandamayasyaiva brahmaṇaḥ prādhānyam /
tathāca tadhikāre paṭhitamabhyasyamānamānandapadaṃ tadbuddhimādhatta iti tasyaivānandamayasyābhyāsa iti yuktam /
jyotiṣṭomādhikāre 'vasante vasante jyotiṣā yajeta' iti jyotiḥpadamiva jyotiṣṭomābhyāsaḥ kālaviśeṣavidhiparaḥ /
api ca sākṣādānandamayātmābhyāsaḥ śrūyate- 'etamānandamayamātmānamupasaṃkrāmati' iti /
pūrvapakṣabījamanubhāṣyaṃ dūṣayati- #yattūktamannamayāditi# /
na hi mukhyārundhatīdarśanaṃ tattadamukhyārundhatīdarśanaprāyapaṭhitamapyamukhyārundhatīdarśanaṃ bhavati /
tādarthyātpūrvadarśanānāmanyadarśanānuguṇyaṃ natu tadvirodhiteti cet, ihāpyānandamayādāntarasyānyasyāśravaṇāt, tasya tvannamayādisarvāntaratvaśrutestatparyavāsānāttādarthyaṃ tulyam /
priyādyavayavayogaśarīratve ca bhāṣyeṇa samāhite /
priyādyavayavayogācca duḥkhalavayoge 'pi paramātmana aupādhika upapāditaḥ /
tathācānandamaya iti prācuryārthatā mayaṭa upapāditeti //12 // //13 // //14 //
body.translated_text: Nor is it correct [to say] that <s>ānandamaya</s> is <s>Brahman</s> alone and not the <s>jīva</s>, on the ground of being the innermost of all. For this <s>śruti</s> does not declare the innermost-of-all status of <s>ānandamaya</s>, but rather [only] the innerness of the <s>ānandamaya</s> sheath relative to the four sheaths beginning with <s>annamaya</s>. And it is not reasonable [to argue] that since no other inner [entity] beyond it is heard, this one alone is the innermost of all. For that with respect to which its innerness is stated — it is inner only to that. Just as when it is said '<s>Devadatta</s> is strong,' one does not understand him to be stronger than all, including lions and tigers, but rather relative to other men of the same kind — so too <s>ānandamaya</s> is inner to <s>annamaya</s> etc., but not to everything. And the partless <s>Brahman</s> cannot have parts like joy (<s>priya</s>) etc., nor is embodiment appropriate for it — therefore <s>ānandamaya</s> is the transmigrating soul (<s>saṃsārin</s>) alone. Hence, what is intended here as the object of meditation is the conditioned [<s>Brahman</s>], not the true nature of <s>Brahman</s> as the object of knowledge — this is the prior position (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>). Moreover, even if the suffix <s>mayaṭ</s> means abundance, still <s>ānandamaya</s> is the transmigrating soul alone, not <s>Brahman</s>. For abundance of bliss exists where there is the possibility of a trace of the opposite, namely suffering — but not where that is entirely impossible. And for the supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), not even the slightest trace of suffering is possible, since it is of the sole essence of bliss — thus he says: "And for an embodied being" (<s>na ca saśarīrasya sataḥ</s>). But for the bodiless one, there is not even the slightest contact with the unpleasant — so even the suffix <s>mayaṅ</s> in the sense of abundance is not applicable; this is the meaning. "It is said" (<s>ucyate</s>). As for the part of <s>ānandamaya</s> that is <s>Brahman</s> — since the 'tail' (<s>puccha</s>) serves as a subordinate limb, it is not primary; rather, <s>ānandamaya</s> itself, which is <s>Brahman</s> as the possessor of the limb, is primary. And thus the word <s>ānanda</s>, being read and repeated in that context, conveys the understanding of that [<s>Brahman</s>] — hence it is reasonable that the repetition is of <s>ānandamaya</s> itself. Just as in the context of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, the word <s>jyotiḥ</s> in 'One should sacrifice with the <s>Jyotiḥ</s> in every spring' is a repetition of <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and pertains to the injunction of a particular time. Moreover, the repetition of the <s>ānandamaya</s> Self is directly heard: 'He approaches this <s>ānandamaya</s> Self' (<s>etam ānandamayam ātmānam upasaṃkrāmati</s>). He restates and refutes the seed of the prior position: "But what was said, '<s>annamaya</s> etc.'" (<s>yat tūktam annamayādi</s>). For the primary showing of <s>Arundhatī</s> does not become a non-primary showing of <s>Arundhatī</s> merely because it is read in the context of prior non-primary showings of <s>Arundhatī</s>. If [the objection is that] the prior showings are subordinate to the purpose of the final one and thus must conform to the other showing, not contradict it — here too, since no other inner [entity] beyond <s>ānandamaya</s> is heard, and since it is heard as the innermost of all beginning from <s>annamaya</s>, the culmination being in that, the subordination is equal. And the possession of parts like joy (<s>priya</s>) etc. and embodiment have been resolved by the <s>bhāṣya</s>. And from the possession of parts like joy etc., even the trace of suffering in the supreme Self has been shown to be due to limiting adjuncts (<s>aupādhika</s>). And thus the suffix <s>mayaṭ</s> in <s>ānandamaya</s> in the sense of abundance has been established. //12// //13// //14//

children.translated_text: Moreover, because of the agreement between the <s>mantra</s> and <s>brāhmaṇa</s> portions — which serve as the goal (<s>upeya</s>) and the means (<s>upāya</s>) respectively — <s>Brahman</s> alone is the referent of the word <s>ānandamaya</s>.

children.text: mantre hi punaḥ 'anyo 'ntara ātmā' iti parabrahmaṇyāntaratvaśravaṇāt, tasyaiva ca 'anyo 'ntara ātmānandamayaḥ' iti brāhmaṇe pratyabhijñānāt, parabrahmaivānandamayamityāha sūtrakāraḥ- #māntravarṇikameva ca gīyate# /
children.translated_text: For in the <s>mantra</s>, since innerness is stated of the supreme <s>Brahman</s> with 'There is another inner Self' (<s>anyo 'ntara ātmā</s>), and since that very [<s>Brahman</s>] is recognized in the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> as 'There is another inner Self that is <s>ānandamaya</s>' (<s>anyo 'ntara ātmā ānandamayaḥ</s>), the <s>sūtrakāra</s> says: "That which is described in the <s>mantra</s> is also sung [in the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>]" (<s>māntravarṇikam eva ca gīyate</s>).

children.text: māntravarṇikameva paraṃ brahma brāhmaṇe 'pyānandamaya iti gīyata iti //15 //
children.translated_text: The very supreme <s>Brahman</s> that is described in the <s>mantra</s> is also sung in the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> as <s>ānandamaya</s>. //15//

children.text: api cānandamayaṃ prakṛtya śarīrādyutpatteḥ prāksraṣṭṛtvaśravaṇāt, 'bahu syām' iti ca sṛjyamānānāṃ sraṣṭurānandamayādabhedaśravaṇāt, ānandamayaḥ para evetyāha /
children.translated_text: Moreover, since creatorship is stated prior to the origination of the body etc. with reference to <s>ānandamaya</s>, and since non-difference of the creator of those being created from <s>ānandamaya</s> is stated through 'Let me become many' (<s>bahu syām</s>), he says that <s>ānandamaya</s> is the supreme [<s>Brahman</s>] alone.
The <s>sūtra</s>: "The other [i.e., the <s>jīva</s>] is not [<s>ānandamaya</s>], because of the impossibility" (<s>netaro 'nupapatteḥ</s>).
The other, namely the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>), is not <s>ānandamaya</s>, because of the impossibility [of attributing the described qualities to it]. //16//

body.text:
#bhedavyapadeśācca# /
rasaḥ sāro hyayamānandamaya ātmā 'rasaṃ hyevāyaṃ labdhvā'nandī bhavati' iti /
so 'yaṃ jīvātmano labdhṛbhāvaḥ, ānandamayasya ca labhyatā, nābheda upapadyate /
tasmādānandamayasya jīvātmano bhede parabrahmatvaṃ siddhaṃ bhavati /
codayati- #kathaṃ tarhīti# /
yadi labdhvā na labdhavyaḥ, kathaṃ tarhi paramātmano vastuto 'bhinnena jīvātmanā paramātmā labhyata ityarthaḥ /
pariharati- #bāḍham /
tathāpīti# /
satyam, paramārthayo 'bhede 'pyavidyāropitaṃ bhedamupāśritya labdhṛlabdhavyabhāva upapadyate /
jīvo hyavidyayā parabrahmaṇo bhinno darśitaḥ, na tu jīvādapi /
tathā cānandamayaścejjīvaḥ, na jīvasyāvidyayāpi svato bhedo darśita iti na labdhṛlabdhavyabhāva ityarthaḥ /
bhedābhedau ca na jīvaparabrahmaṇorityuktamadhastāt /
syādetat /
yathā parameśvarādbhinno jīvātmā draṣṭā na bhavatyevaṃ jīvātmano 'pi draṣṭurna bhinnaḥ parameśvara iti jīvasyānirvācyatve parameśvaro 'pyanirvācyaḥ syāt /
tathā ca vastusannityata āha- #parameśvarastvavidyākalpitāditi# /
rajataṃ hi rāmāropitaṃ na śuktito bhidyate /
na hi tadbhedenābhedena vā śakyaṃ nirvaktum /

children.translated_text: But the mother-of-pearl, being ultimately real, is indeed different from the indeterminable (<s>anirvacanīya</s>) [superimposed] silver, which is itself indeterminable.
For this very [point], he gives a merely analogous illustration: "Just as with the magician" (<s>yathā māyāvinaḥ</s>).
Not being satisfied with that, he gives a perfectly analogous illustration: "Or just as with pot-space" (<s>yathā vā ghaṭākāśāt</s>).
The rest is of transparent meaning. //17// //18//

body.translated_text: "And because of the declaration of difference" (<s>bhedavyapadeśāt ca</s>). For the essence (<s>rasa</s>) — the core — is this <s>ānandamaya</s> Self: 'For having obtained this essence (<s>rasa</s>), one becomes blissful' (<s>rasaṃ hy evāyaṃ labdhvā ānandī bhavati</s>). This [status of] being the obtainer belongs to the individual soul (<s>jīvātman</s>), while being what is obtained belongs to <s>ānandamaya</s> — non-difference is not tenable. Therefore, when the difference of <s>ānandamaya</s> from the individual soul is established, its nature as the supreme <s>Brahman</s> is proven. He raises an objection: "How then" (<s>kathaṃ tarhi</s>). If [<s>Brahman</s>] having been obtained is not to be obtained [again], how then is the supreme Self obtained by the individual soul that is in reality non-different from the supreme Self? — this is the meaning. He resolves: "Indeed so, nevertheless" (<s>bāḍham, tathāpi</s>). True, even though there is non-difference in the ultimate sense, the relationship of obtainer and obtained is tenable by resorting to the difference superimposed through ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>). For the <s>jīva</s> is shown as different from the supreme <s>Brahman</s> through <s>avidyā</s>, but not [shown as different] from itself. And thus, if <s>ānandamaya</s> were the <s>jīva</s>, no difference of the <s>jīva</s> from itself is shown even through <s>avidyā</s> — hence the obtainer-obtained relationship would not hold; this is the meaning. And that difference and non-difference do not [truly] belong to the <s>jīva</s> and the supreme <s>Brahman</s> — this has been stated below. One might object: just as the individual soul as seer is not different from the supreme Lord, so too the supreme Lord is not different from the individual soul as seer — hence if the <s>jīva</s> is indeterminable (<s>anirvācya</s>), the supreme Lord too would be indeterminable. And thus [everything] would be a real entity — to this he says: "But the supreme Lord, from that which is projected by ignorance" (<s>parameśvaras tv avidyākalpitāt</s>). For silver superimposed on mother-of-pearl does not differ from the mother-of-pearl. For it cannot be described either as different or as non-different from it.

children.translated_text: In order to adopt his own position, he refutes the view of the partial-truth proponent (<s>ekadeśin</s>): "But here this is to be said" (<s>idaṃ tv iha vaktavyam</s>).

children.text: eṣa tāvadutsargo yat- brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭheti brahmaśabdātpratīyate /
children.translated_text: This is the general rule: that from the word '<s>Brahman</s>' in '<s>Brahman</s> is the tail, the support' (<s>brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā</s>), pure <s>Brahman</s> is understood;
But from the word <s>ānandamaya</s>, a modified [form of <s>Brahman</s>] is understood. //

body.text:
' tatra kiṃ pucchapadasamabhivyāhārāt annamayādiṣu cāsyāvayavaparatvena prayogāt, ihāpyavayavaparatvātpucchapadasya tatsamānādhikaraṇaṃ brahmapadamapi svārthatyāgena kathañcidavayavaparaṃ vyākhyāyātām /
ānandamayapadaṃ cānnamayādivikāravāciprāyapaṭhitaṃ vikāravāci vā, kathañcitpracurānandavāci vā, brahmaṇyaprasiddhaṃ kayācidvṛtyā brahmaṇi vyākhyāyātām /
ānandapadābhyāsena ca jyotiḥ padeneva jyotiṣṭoma anandamayo lakṣyatāṃ, utānandamayaṃ vikārārthamastu, brahmapadaṃ ca brāhmaṇyeva svārthe 'stu, ānandamapadābhyāsaśca svārthe, pucchapadamātramavayavaprāyalikhitamadhikaraṇaparatayā vyākriyatāmiti kṛtabuddhya eva vidāṅkurvantu /
tatra 'prāyapāṭhaparityāgo mukhyatritayalaṅghanam /
pūrvasminnuttare pakṣe prāyapāṭhasya bādhanam /
pucchapadaṃ hi vāladhau mukhyaṃ sadānandamayāvayave gauṇameveti mukhyaśabdārthalaṅghanamavayavaparatāyāmaṅikaraṇaparatāyāṃ ca tulyam /
avayavaprāyalekhabādhaśca vikāraprāyalekhabādhena tulyaḥ /
brahmapadamānandamayapadamānandapadamiti tritayalaṅghanaṃ tvadhikam /
tasmānmukhyatritayalaṅghanādasādhīyānpūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ /
mukhyatrayānuguṇyena tūttara eva pakṣo yuktaḥ /
api cānandamayapadasya brahmārthatve, brahma puccham iti na samañjasam /
na hi tadevāvayavyavayavaśceti yuktam /
ādhāraparatve ca pucchaśabdasya, pratiṣṭhetyetadapyupapannataraṃ bhavati /
ānandamayasya cāntaratvamannamayādikośāpekṣayā /
brahmaṇāstvāntaratvamānandamayādarthādgamyata iti na śrutyoktam /
evaṃ cānnamayādivadānandamayasya priyādyavayavayogo yuktaḥ /
vāṅmanasāgocare tu parabrahmaṇyupādhimantarbhāvya priyādyavayavayogaḥ, prācuryaḥ ca, kleśena vyākhyāyeyātām /
tathā ca māntravarṇikasya brahmaṇā eva brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā iti svapradhānasyābhidhānāt, tasyaivādhikāro nānandamayasyeti /
so 'kāmayeta' ityādyā api śrutayo brahmaviṣayā ityarthasaṃkṣepaḥ /
sugamamanyat /
#sūtrāṇi tvevaṃ vyākhyeyānīti# /
body.translated_text:
In that case, should [one say]: because of the co-occurrence with the word '<s>puccha</s>' (tail/support), and because in the <s>annamaya</s> and other [sheaths] it is used in the sense of a limb, here too, since the word '<s>puccha</s>' means a limb, the word '<s>Brahman</s>' which is in co-ordinate predication with it should also be explained, by abandoning its own meaning, as somehow denoting a limb?
And should the word '<s>ānandamaya</s>' — being listed alongside terms like <s>annamaya</s> that predominantly denote modifications (<s>vikāra</s>) — be taken as denoting a modification, or somehow as denoting one abundant in bliss, and though not well-known as referring to <s>Brahman</s>, be explained as [referring to] <s>Brahman</s> through some secondary usage?
And should <s>ānandamaya</s> be indicated through the repetition of the word '<s>ānanda</s>' (bliss), just as <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> [is indicated] by the word '<s>jyotis</s>' (light)? Or should <s>ānandamaya</s> be taken in the sense of modification, and the word '<s>Brahman</s>' retain its own meaning as in the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [portion], and the repetition of the word '<s>ānanda</s>' retain its own meaning, and only the word '<s>puccha</s>' — which is predominantly written in the sense of limb — be explained in the sense of support (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>)? Let those of formed judgment decide.
Therein: 'In the first [view], there is abandonment of the predominant textual usage and violation of the primary meanings of three [terms]. In the latter view, there is overriding of the predominant textual usage [only of <s>puccha</s>].
For the word '<s>puccha</s>' is primary in the sense of tail, and only secondary in the sense of a limb of <s>ānandamaya</s> — thus the violation of the primary word-meaning is equal whether [<s>puccha</s> is taken] in the sense of limb or in the sense of support.
And the overriding of the predominant writing [of <s>puccha</s>] as limb is equal to the overriding of the predominant writing [of <s>ānandamaya</s>] as modification.
But the violation of three [primary meanings] — of the word '<s>Brahman</s>,' the word '<s>ānandamaya</s>,' and the word '<s>ānanda</s>' — is additional [in the first view].
Therefore, the first view is more difficult to sustain because of the violation of three primary meanings.
Rather, the latter view alone is fitting, being in accordance with the primary meanings of all three [terms].
Moreover, if the word '<s>ānandamaya</s>' meant <s>Brahman</s>, then '<s>Brahman</s> is the <s>puccha</s> (tail)' would be incoherent, for it is not reasonable that the very same thing be both the whole and its own part.
But if the word '<s>puccha</s>' means support (<s>ādhāra</s>), then '<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>' (foundation) also becomes more fitting.
And the interiority of <s>ānandamaya</s> is [established] in relation to the sheaths beginning with <s>annamaya</s>.
But the interiority of <s>Brahman</s> relative to <s>ānandamaya</s> is understood only by implication, not stated by <s>śruti</s>.
Thus, the connection of <s>ānandamaya</s> with parts such as <s>priya</s> (pleasure) and the rest is fitting, just as with <s>annamaya</s> and the others.
But in the case of the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, which is beyond speech and mind, the connection with parts such as <s>priya</s> and the abundance [of bliss] would have to be explained with difficulty by subsuming them under limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>).
And thus, since the <s>Mantra</s>-passage's own principal teaching is that '<s>Brahman</s> is the <s>puccha</s> (tail/foundation),' the topic of inquiry is <s>Brahman</s> itself, not <s>ānandamaya</s>.
The <s>śruti</s> passages beginning with 'He desired' (<s>so 'kāmayata</s>) also pertain to <s>Brahman</s> — this is the summary of the meaning.
The rest is easy [to understand].
The <s>sūtras</s>, however, should be explained as follows:

body.text:
vedasūtrayorvirodhe 'guṇe tvanyāyyakalpanā' iti sūtrāṇyanyathā netavyāni /
ānandamayaśabdena tadvākyasya brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā ityetadgataṃ brahmapadamupalakṣyate /
etaduktaṃ bhavati- ānandamaya ityādivākye yat brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā iti brahmapadaṃ tatsvapradhānameveti /
yattu brahmādhikaraṇameveti vaktavye brahma puccham ityāha śrutiḥ, tatkasya hetoḥ, pūrvamavayavapradhānaprayogāttatprayogasyaiva buddhau saṃnidhānāt tenāpi cādhiraraṇalakṣaṇopapatteriti /
#māntravarṇikameva ca#
body.translated_text:
When there is a conflict between the <s>Veda</s> and the <s>sūtras</s>, [the principle is] 'when there is a secondary meaning, an unjustified construction [should be attributed to the <s>sūtras</s>]' — thus the <s>sūtras</s> should be interpreted otherwise.
By the word '<s>ānandamaya</s>,' the word '<s>Brahman</s>' occurring in the sentence '<s>Brahman</s> is the <s>puccha</s> (tail), the foundation' is indicated.
What is stated amounts to this: in the sentence beginning with '<s>ānandamaya</s>,' the word '<s>Brahman</s>' in '<s>Brahman</s> is the <s>puccha</s>, the foundation' is itself the principal [referent].
But as to why the <s>śruti</s> says '<s>Brahman</s> is the <s>puccha</s>' when it should have said '<s>Brahman</s> is the <s>adhikaraṇa</s>' (substratum) — the reason is that due to the prior usage of [<s>puccha</s>] as primarily meaning a limb, that [limb-meaning] usage was present in the mind, and through that [usage] too the characteristic of substratum is established.

body.text: #gīyate# // 1.9 //
body.translated_text: The <s>Mantra</s>-passage itself is sung [as referring to <s>Brahman</s>]. // 1.9 //

children.text: yat satyaṃ jñānam' ityādinā mantravarṇena brahmoktaṃ tadevopāyabhūtena brāhmaṇena svapradhānyena gīyate- brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā iti /
children.translated_text: The <s>Brahman</s> that is spoken of by the <s>Mantra</s>-passage 'That which is truth, knowledge...' (<s>yat satyaṃ jñānam</s>) — that very same [<s>Brahman</s>] is sung with its own primacy by the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [portion], which serves as the means — [namely in the statement] '<s>Brahman</s> is the <s>puccha</s>, the foundation.'

children.text: avayavavacanatve tvasya mantre prādhānyaṃ, brāhmaṇe prādhānyamityupāyopeyayormantrabrāhmaṇayorvipratipattiḥ syāditi /
children.translated_text: But if [<s>puccha</s>] meant a limb, there would be a contradiction between the <s>Mantra</s> and the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — [since <s>Brahman</s> would have] primacy in the <s>Mantra</s> [but] primacy [would belong to <s>ānandamaya</s>] in the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — thus there would be a conflict between the means and the end, namely the <s>Mantra</s> and the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
[<s>Sūtra</s>:] Not the other, because of impossibility. // 1.1.16 //

children.text: atra 'itaścānandamayaḥ iti bhāṣyasya sthāne itaśca brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā iti paṭhitavyam /
children.translated_text: Here, in place of the <s>bhāṣya</s> reading 'And from this, <s>ānandamaya</s>...,' one should read '<s>Brahman</s> is the <s>puccha</s>, the foundation.'
[<s>Sūtra</s>:] And because of the declaration of difference. // 1.1.17 //

children.text: atrāpi itaścānandamayaḥ ityasya ca ānandamayādhikāre ityasya ca bhāṣyasya sthāne brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā iti brahmapucchādhikāre iti ca paṭhitavayam /
children.translated_text: Here too, in place of the <s>bhāṣya</s> readings 'And from this, <s>ānandamaya</s>...' and 'in the section on <s>ānandamaya</s>,' one should read '<s>Brahman</s> is the <s>puccha</s>, the foundation' and 'in the section on <s>Brahma-puccha</s>.'
[<s>Sūtra</s>:] And because of desire, there is no dependence on inference. // 1.1.18 //

body.text: #asminnasya ca tadyogaṃ śāsti# // 1.9 //
body.translated_text: [<s>Sūtra</s>:] In this [<s>Brahman</s>], [the <s>śruti</s>] teaches the connection of this [individual soul] with that [<s>Brahman</s>]. // 1.1.19 //

children.text: ityanayorapi sūtrayorbhāṣye ānandamayasthāne brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā iti pāṭho draṣṭavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the <s>bhāṣya</s> on these two <s>sūtras</s> also, in place of '<s>ānandamaya</s>' one should see the reading '<s>Brahman</s> is the <s>puccha</s>, the foundation.'
[<s>Sūtra</s>:] And because of the declaration of [<s>Brahman</s>] as the cause of that. // 1.1.14 //

children.text: vikārasyānandamayasya brahma pucchamavayavaścetkathaṃ sarvasyāsya vikārajātasya sānandamayasya brahma pucchaṃ kāraṇamucyeta idaṃ sarvamasṛjata /
children.translated_text: If <s>ānandamaya</s>, which is a modification, had <s>Brahman</s> as its <s>puccha</s> (limb), then how could <s>Brahman</s> — being a <s>puccha</s> (limb) of this entire class of modifications including <s>ānandamaya</s> — be called the cause [of everything] by the <s>śruti</s> 'It created all this,
whatever there is'?

children.text: nahyānandamayavikārāvayavo brahma vikāraḥ san sarvasya kāraṇamupapadyate /
children.translated_text: For <s>Brahman</s>, being a modification that is a limb of the <s>ānandamaya</s> modification, cannot reasonably be the cause of everything.

children.text: tasmādānandamayavikārāvayavo brahmeti tadavayavayogyānandamayo vikāra iha nopāsyatvena vivakṣitaḥsa kintu svapradhānamiha brahma pucchaṃ jñeyatveneti siddham // 1.9 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Brahman</s> is not a limb of the <s>ānandamaya</s> modification, and hence <s>ānandamaya</s> as a modification — which would be fit to have [<s>Brahman</s>] as its limb — is not intended here as the object of meditation (<s>upāsya</s>). Rather, <s>Brahman</s>, being its own principal [referent] here as the '<s>puccha</s>' (foundation), is what is to be known — this is established. // 1.1.14 //

body.text:
#antakarastaddharmopadeśāt# /
pūrvasminnadhikaraṇe 'pāstasamastaviśeṣabrahmapratipattyarthamupāyatāmātreṇa pañca kośā upādhayaḥ sthitāḥ, natu vivakṣaitāḥ /

children.text: brahmaiva tu pradhānaṃ brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā iti jñeyatvenopakṣiptamiti nirṇītam /
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> alone is the principal [teaching], introduced as what is to be known — '<s>Brahman</s> is the <s>puccha</s>, the foundation' — this has been determined.

children.text: saṃprati tu brahma vivakṣitopādhimupasyatvenopakṣipyate, natu vidyākarmātiśayalabdhotkarṣo jīvātmādityapadavedanīya iti nirṇīyate /
children.translated_text: Now, however, <s>Brahman</s> with an intended limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) is introduced as the object of meditation (<s>upāsya</s>), and it is determined that [this] is not the individual soul (<s>jīvātman</s>) — [a being] who has attained eminence through the excellence of knowledge and <s>karma</s> — to be known through the word '<s>āditya</s>' (sun).

children.text: tatra maryādādhārarūpāṇi saṃsāriṇi pare na tu /
children.translated_text: Therein: [the characteristics of] being limited, having a support, and having form belong to embodied beings in <s>saṃsāra</s>, not to the Supreme [<s>Brahman</s>].
Therefore, the object of meditation is the embodied being in <s>saṃsāra</s> — the sun (<s>Ravi</s>), who is subject to <s>karma</s>.

body.translated_text:
[<s>Sūtra</s>:] The one within [the sun is <s>Brahman</s>], because the attributes of that [<s>Brahman</s>] are taught.
In the preceding <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic), the five sheaths (<s>kośas</s>) are established as mere limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>) serving as means for the apprehension of <s>Brahman</s> devoid of all distinctions — they are not themselves the intended [objects of teaching].

body.text:
piraṇyaśmaśruḥ ityādirūpaśravaṇāt, ya eṣo 'ntarāditye, ya eṣo 'ntarakṣiṇī iti cādhārabhehaśravaṇāt, ye cāmuṣmātparāñco lokāsteṣāṃ ceṣṭe devakāmānāṃ ca ityaiśvaryādāśruteśca saṃsāryeva kāryakāraṇasaṃghātātmako rūpādisaṃpanna ihopāsyaḥ, natu paramātmā aśabdamasparśam ityādiśrutibhiḥ apāstasamastarūpāśca, sve mahimni ityādiśrutibhirapākṛtādhāraśca, eṣa sarveśvaraḥ ityādiśrutibhiradhigatanirmaryādaiśvaryaśca śakya upāsyatveneha pratipattum /
sarvapāpmavirahaścādityapuruṣe saṃbhavati, śāstrasya manuṣyādhikāratayā devatāyāḥ puṇyupāpayoranadhikārāt /
rūpādimattvānyānupapattyā ca kāryakāraṇātmake jīve upāsyatvena vivakṣite yattāvadṛgādyātmakatayāsya sarvātmakatvaṃ śrūyate tatkathañcidādityapuruṣasyaiva stuturiti ādityapuruṣa evopāsyo na paramātmatyevaṃ prāptam /
anādhāratve ca nityatvaṃ sarvagatatvaṃ ca hetuḥ /

children.text: anityaṃ hi kāryaṃ kāraṇādhāramiti nānādhāraṃ, nityamapyasarvagataṃ ca yattasmādadharabhāvenāsthitaṃ tadeva tasyottarasyādhāra iti nānādhāraṃ, tasmādubhayamuktam /
children.translated_text: For an impermanent thing, being an effect, has its cause as its support — thus it has differentiated supports. And even a permanent thing, if it is not all-pervading, being situated through the relation of being supported by that [which is above it] — that [higher entity] is its support — thus it too has differentiated supports. Therefore, both [statements about differentiated support] are accounted for.
This being the preliminary view, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] states: '<s>antaḥ taddharmopadeśāt</s>' — the one within [is <s>Brahman</s>], because the attributes of that [<s>Brahman</s>] are taught.
'It is spoken of here on account of being the Self of all and being free from all evils.
<s>Brahman</s> alone, through these two unfailing [characteristics], is the cause of all, like a modification.'

body.translated_text:
[The opponent argues:] Because of the mention of form such as 'having golden beard' (<s>hiraṇyaśmaśru</s>) and the like; because of the mention of distinction of support in 'He who is within the sun' (<s>ya eṣo 'ntarāditye</s>) and 'He who is within the eye' (<s>ya eṣo 'ntarakṣiṇī</s>); and because of the mention of sovereignty in 'Those worlds that are beyond that [sun], and the desires of the gods' — [it follows that] the object of meditation here is a being in <s>saṃsāra</s> who is an aggregate of cause and effect, endowed with form and the like, not the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>). For [the <s>Paramātman</s>] is devoid of all form according to <s>śruti</s> passages like 'Without sound, without touch' (<s>aśabdam asparśam</s>); is devoid of support according to <s>śruti</s> passages like 'In His own glory' (<s>sve mahimni</s>); and possesses unlimited sovereignty according to <s>śruti</s> passages like 'He is the lord of all' (<s>eṣa sarveśvaraḥ</s>) — [such a being] cannot be apprehended here as the object of meditation.
And freedom from all sins is possible for the <s>Āditya-puruṣa</s> (the Person in the sun), [since] the scripture's instructions are addressed to human beings...

body.text:
' nāmaniruktena hi sarvapāpmāpādānatayasyodaya ucyate /
na cādityasya devatāyāḥ karmānadhikāre 'pi sarvapāpmavirahaḥ prāgbhavīyadharmarūpapāpmasaṃbhave sati /
na caiteṣāṃ prāgbhavīyo dharma evāsti na pāpmeti sāṃpratam /
vidyākarmātiśayasamudācāre 'pyanādibhavaparaṃparopārjitānāṃ pāpmanāmapi prasuptānāṃ saṃbhavāt /
naca śrutiprāmāṇyādidātyaśarīrābhimāninaḥ sarvapāpmaviraha iti yuktaṃ, brahmaviṣayatvenāpyasyāḥ prāmāṇyopapatteḥ /
naca vinigamanāhetvabhāvaḥ, tatra tatra sarvapāpmavirahasya bhūyobhūyo brahmaṇyeva śravaṇāt /
tasyaiva ceha pratyabhijñāyamānasya vinigamanāhetorvidyamānatvāt /
apica sārvātmyaṃ jagatkāraṇasya brahmaṇa evopapadyate, kāraṇādabhedātkāryajātasya, brahmaṇaśca jagatkāraṇatvāt /
ādityaśarīrābhimāninastu jīvātmano na jagatkāraṇatvam /
naca mukhyārthasaṃbhave prāśastyalakṣaṇayā stutyarthatā yuktā /
rūpavattvaṃ cāsya parānugrahāya kāyanirmāṇena vā, tadvikāratayā vā sarvasya kāryajātasya, vikārasya ca vikāravato 'nanyatvāttādṛśarūpabhedenopadiśyate, yathā '---gandhaḥ saḥ iti /
naca brahmanirmitaṃ māyārūpamanuvadacchāstramaśāstraṃ bhavati, apitu tāṃ kurvat iti māśāstratvaprasaṅgaḥ /
yatra tu nirastasamastopādhibhedaṃ jñeyatvenopakṣipyate, tatra śāstram-'aśabdamasparśamarūpamavyayam' iti pravartate /
body.translated_text:
For by the etymological explanation of the name [<s>Āditya</s>], His rising as the remover of all sins is stated.
And freedom from all sins is not possible for the deity <s>Āditya</s>, even if not subject to <s>karma</s> [in this life], since sins in the form of <s>dharma</s> from previous births are possible.
Nor is it valid [to claim] that these [deities] have only <s>dharma</s> from previous births and no sin — this is [merely] an assertion [without proof].
For even when there is an abundance of excellence in knowledge and <s>karma</s>, sins accumulated through the beginningless series of births — though dormant — are still possible.
Nor is it reasonable [to establish] freedom from all sins for the one identified with the solar body merely on the authority of <s>śruti</s>, since that <s>śruti</s>'s authority is also established if it pertains to <s>Brahman</s>.
Nor is there an absence of a reason for determination [in favor of <s>Brahman</s>], since freedom from all sins is taught again and again in each context...

body.text:
tasmādrūpavattvamapi paramātmanyupapadyate /
etenaiva maryādādhārabhedāvapi vyākhyātau /
api cādityadehābhimāninaḥ saṃsāriṇo 'ntaryāmī bhedenoktaḥ, sa evāntarāditya ityantaḥ śrutisāmyena pratyabhijñāyamāno bhavitumarhati /
#tasmāte dhanasanaya iti# /
dhanavanto vibhūtimanta iti yāvat /

children.translated_text: As to why the possession of abundance is fitting when [the referent] is the Supreme Lord — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Whatever is endowed with abundance...' (<s>yad yad vibhūtimat</s>).

Even though everything has [<s>Brahman</s>] as its Self, the manifestation of the Supreme Lord's own nature occurs only in those endowed with abundance (<s>vibhūtimat</s>), not in those lacking abundance, whose Supreme Lord-nature is concealed by the darkness of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — this is the meaning.
[<s>Śruti</s> also teaches:] 'And the sovereignty over the worlds and desires...'
Therefore, by the principle of absolute unsurpassability, [<s>Brahman</s> possesses] unchecked sovereignty — this is the meaning. // 1.1.20 //

body.translated_text:
Therefore, the possession of form is also established as pertaining to the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>).
By this very [reasoning], the distinctions of limitation and support are also explained.
Moreover, the inner controller (<s>antaryāmin</s>) of the being in <s>saṃsāra</s> who identifies with the solar body has been mentioned as distinct [from that being], and that very same [controller], being recognized as identical through the similarity of the <s>śruti</s> statements, 'He who is within the sun' (<s>ya eṣo 'ntarāditye</s>), ought to be the one within.
[<s>Śruti</s> says:] 'Therefore they are wealthy' (<s>tasmāt te dhanasanayaḥ</s>) — that is, they are endowed with abundance.

body.text:
#ākāśastalliṅgāt# /
pūrvasminnadhikaraṇe brahmaṇo 'sādhāraṇadharmadarśanādvivakṣitopādhino 'syaivopāsanā, na tvādityaśarīrābhimānino jīvātmana iti nirūpitam /

children.text: idānīṃ tvasādhāraṇadharmadarśanāttadevodgīthe saṃpādyopāsyatvenopadiśyate, na bhūtākāśa iti nirūpyate /
children.translated_text: Now, however, it is determined that because of the observation of unique attributes, that [<s>Brahman</s>] alone is taught as what is to be meditated upon after being identified with the <s>Udgītha</s> — not the elemental <s>ākāśa</s> (physical space).

children.text: tatra 'ākāśa iti hovāca' iti kiṃ mukhyakāśapādānurodhena 'asya lokasya kā gitaḥ' iti, 'sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtāni' iti 'jyāyā' itica 'parāyaṇam' iti ca kathañcidvyākhyāyatāṃ, utaitadanurodhenākāśaśabdo bhaktyā parātmāne vyākhyāyatāmiti /
children.translated_text: Therein [the question arises]: Given that [the <s>śruti</s> says] '<s>Ākāśa</s>, indeed, he said' (<s>ākāśa iti hovāca</s>), should [the passages] 'What is the <s>Udgītha</s> of this world?' and 'All these beings indeed' and 'the greater' and 'the final resort' be somehow explained in conformity with the primary meaning of the word <s>ākāśa</s> (space)? Or should the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' be explained in a secondary sense as [referring to] the Supreme Self, in conformity with those [other passages]?
Since the earth and other [elements mentioned in the passage] are subordinate, <s>ākāśa</s> in its primary sense is [the subject] for us.
It is our firm conclusion that the other [terms] should be explained in conformity with that [primary meaning of <s>ākāśa</s>].

body.translated_text:
[<s>Sūtra</s>:] <s>Ākāśa</s> [is <s>Brahman</s>], because of the indicatory marks of that [<s>Brahman</s>].
In the preceding <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, it was determined that because of the observation of attributes unique to <s>Brahman</s>, the meditation pertains to [<s>Brahman</s>] with its intended limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>), not to the individual soul (<s>jīvātman</s>) identified with the solar body.

body.text:
' 'asya lokasya kā gatiḥ' iti praśnottare 'ākāśa iti hovāca' ityākāśasya gatitvena pratipādyatayā prādhānyāt, 'sarvāṇi ha vā' ityādīnāṃ tu tadviśeṣaṇatayā guṇatvāt, 'guṇe tvanyāṭyakalpanā' iti bahūnyapyapradhānāni pradhānānurodhena netavyāni /
apica 'ākāśa iti hovāca' ityuttare prathamāvagatamākāśamanupajātavirodhi, tena tadanuraktāyāṃ buddhau yadyadeva tadekavākyagatamupanipatati tattajjaghanyatayā upasaṃjātavirodhi tadānuguṇyenaiva vyavasthānamarhati /
naca kkacidākāśaśabdo bhaktyā brahmaṇi prayukta iti sarvatra tena tatpareṇa bhavitavyam /
nahi gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣa ityatra gaṅgapadamanupapattyā tīraparamiti yādāṃsi gaṅgāyāmityatrāpyanena tatpareṇa bhavitavyam /
saṃbhavaścobhayatra tulyaḥ /
naca brahmaṇyapyākāśaśabdo mukhyaḥ, anaikārthatvasyānyāṭyatvāt, bhaktyā ca brahmaṇi prayogadarśanopapatteḥ /
loke cāsya nabhasi nirūḍhatvāt, tatpūrvakatvācca vaidikārthapratītervaiparītyānupapatteḥ /
tadānuguṇyena ca 'sarvāṇi ha vā' ityādīni bhāṣyakṛtā svayameva nītāni /
tasmādbhūtākāśamevātropāsyatvenopadiśyate, na paramātmeti prāptam /

children.translated_text: This being the prima facie view, the conclusion is stated: 'By the word <s>ākāśa</s>, <s>Brahman</s> is grasped' (<s>ākāśaśabdena brahmaṇo grahaṇam</s>).
Why? 'Because of the indicatory marks (<s>liṅga</s>) of That [<s>Brahman</s>]' (<s>talliṅgāt</s>).
For thus — 'Through co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) of the question and its corresponding answer,
From the consideration of context (<s>paurvāparya</s>), even when there is primacy [of the word <s>ākāśa</s>], there is figurative meaning.' //

body.translated_text: In the question-and-answer 'What is the destination of this world?' — 'He said: <s>Ākāśa</s> (space)' — since <s>ākāśa</s> has primacy by being presented as the destination (<s>gati</s>), while [the passages] '<s>sarvāṇi ha vā</s>' (all indeed) and the like have subordinacy as qualifiers of that, [one may argue that] by the principle 'regarding the subordinate, there is the assumption of figurative meaning' (<s>guṇe tvanyāṭyakalpanā</s>), even many subordinate [passages] must be guided in conformity with the principal. Moreover, in the answer '<s>ākāśa iti hovāca</s>' (He said: <s>Ākāśa</s>), the <s>ākāśa</s> first apprehended is without any [subsequent] conflict; and since the intellect is attached to that, whatever else falls within the same sentence — being secondary and having a subsequently arisen conflict — should be settled in conformity with that [first-apprehended meaning]. And it is not the case that the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' is always used figuratively (<s>bhaktyā</s>) for <s>Brahman</s>, such that it should everywhere be taken as referring to that [<s>Brahman</s>]. For it is not the case that because the word '<s>Gaṅgā</s>' in 'a village on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>' has, by impossibility [of literal meaning], the bank as its referent, therefore in 'fish in the <s>Gaṅgā</s>' too, it should have [the bank] as its referent. And the possibility [of both literal and figurative meanings] is equal in both [cases]. Nor is the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' primary (<s>mukhya</s>) even when applied to <s>Brahman</s>, since non-univocity constitutes figurative usage (<s>anyāṭya</s>), and since figurative usage in application to <s>Brahman</s> is justified by observed [instances]. And in the world, this [word] has its established (<s>nirūḍha</s>) meaning as the sky (<s>nabhas</s>); and since the apprehension of Vedic meanings is preceded by mundane [usage], a reversal is unjustified. And the commentator (<s>Bhāṣyakṛt</s>) himself has guided [the passages] '<s>sarvāṇi ha vā</s>' etc. in conformity with that [elemental <s>ākāśa</s>]. Therefore, the prima facie view (<s>prāpta</s>) is that only elemental <s>ākāśa</s> (physical space) is here taught as the object of meditation, not the supreme Self (<s>paramātman</s>).

body.text:
' yadyapyākāśapadaṃ pradhānārthaṃ tathāpi yatpṛṣṭaṃ tadeva prativaktavyam /
na khalvanunmatta āmnānpṛṣṭaḥ kovidāsanācaṣṭe /
tadiha, 'asya lokasya kā gatiḥ' iti praśno dṛśyamānanāmarūpaprapañcamātragativiṣaya iti tadanurodhādya eva sarvasya lokasya gatiḥ sa evākāśaśabdena prativaktavyaḥ /
naca bhūtākāśaḥ sarvasya lokasya gatiḥ, tasyāpi lokamadhyapātitvāt /
tadeva tasya matirityanupapatteḥ /
na cottare bhūtākāśaśravaṇādbhūtākāśakāryameva pṛṣṭamiti yuktaṃ, praśnasya prathamāvagato 'nupajātavirodhino lokasāmānyaviṣayasyopajātavirodhinottareṇa saṃkocānupapattestadanurodhenottaravyākhyānāt /
naca praśnena pūrvapakṣarūpeṇānavasthitārthenottaraṃ vyavasthitārthaṃ na śakyaṃ niyantumiti yuktaṃ, tannimittānāmajñānasaṃśayaviparyasānāmanavasthāne 'pi tasya svaviṣaye vyavasthānāt /
anyathottarasyānālambanatvāttervaiyadhikaraṇyāpattervā /
api cottare 'pi bahvasamañjasam /
tathāhi-'sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtānyakāśādeva samutpadyante' iti sarvaśabdaḥ kathañcidalpaviṣayo vyākhyeyaḥ /
evamevakāro 'pyasamañjasaḥ /
na khalvapāmākāśa eva kāraṇamapi tu tejo 'pi /
evamannasyāpi nākāśameva kāraṇamapi tu pāvakapāthasī api /
mūlakāraṇavivakṣāyāṃ tu brahmaṇyevāvadhāraṇaṃ samañjasam /
asamaḍhjasaṃ tu bhūtākāśe /
evaṃ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ layo brahmaṇyeva /
evaṃ sarvebhyo jyāyastvaṃ brahmaṇa eva /
evaṃ paramayanaṃ brahmaiva /
tasmātsarveṣāṃ lokānāmiti praśnopakramāt, uttare ca tattadasādhāraṇabrahmaguṇaparāmarśāt pṛṣṭāyāśca gateḥ paramayanamityāsādhāraṇabrahmaguṇopasaṃhārāt, bhūyasīnāṃ śrutīnāmanugrahāya 'tyajedekaṃ kulasyārthe' itivadvaramākāśapadamātramasamañjasamastu /
etāvatā hi bahu samañjasaṃ syāt /
na cākāśasya prādhānyamuttare, kintu pṛṣṭārthatvāduttarasya, lokasāmānyagateśca pṛṣṭatvāt, 'parāyaṇam' iti ca tasyaivopasaṃhārābrahmaiva pradhānam /
tathāca tadarthaṃ sat ākāśapadaṃ pradhānārthaṃ bhavati, nānyathā /
tasmādbrahmaiva pradhānamākāśapadenehopāsyatvenopakṣitaṃ, na bhūtākāśamiti siddham /
#api ca# /

children.translated_text: At the very beginning of this [passage], '<s>antavat kila te sāma</s>' (finite indeed is your <s>Sāman</s>) — 'through the defect of finiteness, [<s>Śālāvatya</s>] said to him' (<s>antavattvadoṣeṇa śālāvatyasyeti</s>).

children.text: na cākāśaśabdo gauṇo 'pi vilambitapratipattiḥ, tatra tatra brahmaṇyākāśaśabdasya tatparyāyasya ca prayogaprācuryādatyantābhyāsenāsyāpi mukhyavatpratipatteravilambanāditi darśanārthaṃ brahmaṇi prayogaprācuryaṃ vaidikaṃ nidarśitaṃ bhāṣyakṛtā /
children.translated_text: Nor is the word '<s>ākāśa</s>', even if figurative (<s>gauṇa</s>), one that delays comprehension — because of the abundant usage of the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' and its synonyms for <s>Brahman</s> in various [passages], the comprehension [of its figurative meaning] is as unhesitating as [that of] the primary meaning, due to extreme habituation (<s>atyantābhyāsa</s>). To demonstrate this, the commentator (<s>Bhāṣyakṛt</s>) has shown the abundant Vedic usage [of <s>ākāśa</s>] for <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: tatraiva ca prathamāvagatānuguṇyenottaraṃ nīyate, yatra tadanyathā kartuṃ śakyam /
children.translated_text: And in that very [passage], the answer is guided in conformity with what was first apprehended, where it is possible to make [the answer] otherwise [i.e., where the answer can accommodate the first-apprehended meaning].

children.text: yatra tu na śakyaṃ tatrottarānuguṇyenaiva prathamaṃ nīyata ityāha- #vākyopakrame 'pīti# //22 //
children.translated_text: But where it cannot be [made otherwise], there the first-apprehended [meaning] is guided in conformity with the answer — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Even at the beginning of the passage' (<s>vākyopakrame 'pi</s>). // 22 //

body.translated_text: Although the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' has primacy in meaning, nevertheless, what is asked must be answered accordingly. Surely a person who is not insane, when asked about mangoes, does not speak of the <s>kovidāra</s> tree. So here, since the question 'What is the destination of this world?' is about the destination of the entire visible phenomenal world of name and form, in conformity with that, the very one who is the destination of the entire world is to be answered by the word '<s>ākāśa</s>.' And elemental <s>ākāśa</s> is not the destination of the entire world, since it too falls within the world. 'That alone is its mind (<s>mati</s>)' — [this too] would be unjustified [for elemental <s>ākāśa</s>]. Nor is it reasonable [to say] that because elemental <s>ākāśa</s> is heard in the answer, what was asked about is only the effect of elemental <s>ākāśa</s> — since the question, which was first apprehended without conflict as referring to the world in general, cannot be contracted by the answer, which has a subsequently arisen conflict; rather, the answer is to be explained in conformity with the question. Nor is it reasonable [to say] that the answer — whose meaning is established — cannot be restricted by the question — whose meaning is not established, being in the form of a prima facie position — since, even when the occasions [for a question] — ignorance, doubt, and misapprehension — are not established, [the answer] is established regarding its own subject-matter. Otherwise, the answer would lack a foundation, or there would be the unwanted consequence of addressing different topics (<s>vaiyādhikaraṇya</s>). Moreover, even in the answer, much is problematic. For thus: in '<s>sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtāni ākāśādeva samutpadyante</s>' (all these beings indeed arise from <s>ākāśa</s> alone), the word '<s>sarva</s>' (all) would have to be explained as having a restricted scope. Likewise, the particle '<s>eva</s>' (alone) is also problematic. For water does not have <s>ākāśa</s> alone as its cause, but also fire. Similarly, food too does not have <s>ākāśa</s> alone as its cause, but also fire and water. But when the ultimate cause (<s>mūlakāraṇa</s>) is intended, the restriction [of 'alone'] is appropriate only for <s>Brahman</s>; it is problematic for elemental <s>ākāśa</s>. Similarly, the dissolution of all beings [is appropriate] only in <s>Brahman</s>. Similarly, the being-greater-than-all is [appropriate] only for <s>Brahman</s>. Similarly, the supreme abode (<s>paramayana</s>) is <s>Brahman</s> alone. Therefore, since [the passage] begins with the question about the [destination of] all worlds, and since in the answer there is reference to attributes exclusive to <s>Brahman</s> in various places, and since the asked-about destination concludes with the exclusive <s>Brahman</s>-attribute of 'supreme abode' (<s>paramayanam</s>) — for the sake of supporting the majority of <s>Śruti</s> passages, by the principle 'one should sacrifice one [member] for the sake of the family,' let only the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' be [slightly] problematic — for by that much, much [else] becomes unproblematic. And there is no primacy of <s>ākāśa</s> in the answer — rather, since the answer is about what was asked, and since the destination of the world in general was asked about, and since that alone is concluded with '<s>parāyaṇam</s>' (supreme abode), <s>Brahman</s> alone is primary. And thus, the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' has primacy [only] insofar as it serves that [<s>Brahman</s>] purpose, not otherwise. Therefore, <s>Brahman</s> alone — primary, introduced by the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' as the object of meditation — is established, not elemental <s>ākāśa</s>. 'Moreover' (<s>api ca</s>) —

#ata eva prāṇaḥ# /
udgīthe-'yā devatā prastāvamanvāyattā' ityukramya śrūyate-'katamā sā devateti prāṇa iti hovāca' uṣastiśkrāyaṇaḥ /
udgīthopāsanaprasaṅgena prastāvopāsanamapyudgītha ityuktaṃ bāṣyakṛtā /
prastāva iti sāmno bhaktiviśeṣastamanvāyattā anugatā prāṇo devatā /
atra prāṇaśabdasya brahmaṇi vāyuvikāre ca darśanātsaṃśayaḥ-kimayaṃ brahmavacana uta vāyuvikāravacana iti /

children.text: tatra ata eva brahmaliṅgādeva prāṇo 'pi brahmaiva na vāyuvikāra iti yuktam /
children.translated_text: Therein, for this very reason — because of the indicatory marks (<s>liṅga</s>) of <s>Brahman</s> itself — <s>Prāṇa</s> too is <s>Brahman</s> alone, not a modification of <s>Vāyu</s> — this is appropriate.
If so, then since the matter is already resolved by that [previous <s>adhikaraṇa</s>] alone, what is the purpose of beginning another <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic)?
To this it is said: 'In a matter where meaning is accessible only through scripture, we respect scripture alone;
But in a matter accessible through another means of knowledge, the determination is guided by that [other means].' //

body.translated_text: 'For this very reason, <s>Prāṇa</s> [is <s>Brahman</s>]' (<s>ata eva prāṇaḥ</s>). In the [<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>] on the <s>Udgītha</s>, after introducing 'whichever deity is connected with the <s>Prastāva</s> [portion of the <s>Sāman</s>],' it is heard: 'Which deity is that? — <s>Prāṇa</s> (the vital breath), he said,' [thus spoke] <s>Uṣasti Cākrāyaṇa</s>. The commentator (<s>Bhāṣyakṛt</s>) has stated that in the context of meditation on the <s>Udgītha</s>, the meditation on the <s>Prastāva</s> is also [designated as] <s>Udgītha</s>. The <s>Prastāva</s> is a specific portion (<s>bhaktiviśeṣa</s>) of the <s>Sāman</s>; the deity connected with it — i.e., following it — is <s>Prāṇa</s>. Here there is doubt, since the word '<s>prāṇa</s>' is seen [to apply] both to <s>Brahman</s> and to a modification of <s>Vāyu</s> (wind): does this [word] denote <s>Brahman</s> or a modification of <s>Vāyu</s>?

body.text:
' brahmaṇo vāsarvabhūtakāraṇatvaṃ, ākāśasya vā vāṭvādibhūtakāraṇatvaṃ prati nāgamādṛte mānāntaraṃ prabhavati /
tatra paurvāparyaparyālocanayā yatrārthe samañjasa āgamaḥ sa evārthastasya gṛhyate, tyajyate cetaraḥ /
iha tu saṃveśanodgamane bhūtānāṃ prāṇaṃ pratyucyamāne kiṃ brahma pratyucyate āho vāyuvikāraṃ pratīti viśaye 'yadā vai puruṣaḥ svapiti prāṇaṃ tarhi vāgapyeti' ityādikāyāḥ śruteḥ sarvabhūtasārendriyasaṃveśanodgamanapratipādanadvārā sarvabhūtasaṃveśanodgamanapratipādikāyā mānāntarānugrahalabdhasāmarthyāyā balātsaṃveśanodgamane vāyuvikārasyaiva prāṇasya, na brahmaṇaḥ /
api cātrodgīthapratihārayoḥ sāmabhaktyorbrahmaṇo 'nye ādityaścānnaṃ ca devate abhihite kāryakāraṇasaṃghātarūpe, tatsāhacaryātprāṇo 'pi kāryakāraṇasaṃghātarūpa eva devatā bhavitumarhati /

children.translated_text: This very point was indeed settled in the <s>Īkṣati-adhikaraṇa</s> (the topic of 'seeing'), but is restated here to reinforce the previously stated reasons for the prima facie view.
Therefore, the prima facie view (<s>prāpta</s>) is that the meaning of the word '<s>Prāṇa</s>' here is a modification of <s>Vāyu</s> (wind).
This being the prima facie view, the conclusion is stated: 'The force of a human statement [derives from] its concordance with another means of knowledge;
But for an authorless (<s>apauruṣeya</s>) statement, what can such concordance do?' //

body.translated_text: Whether <s>Brahman</s>'s being the cause of all beings, or <s>ākāśa</s>'s being the cause of beings such as wind and the like — for neither of these does any means of knowledge other than scripture (<s>āgama</s>) prevail. Therein, through the consideration of context, whichever meaning makes scripture coherent (<s>samañjasa</s>) — that meaning of it is adopted, and the other is rejected. But here, when the sleeping and waking of beings with respect to <s>Prāṇa</s> is being stated, [the question is:] is it being stated with respect to <s>Brahman</s> or with respect to a modification of <s>Vāyu</s>? In this matter, the <s>Śruti</s> '<s>yadā vai puruṣaḥ svapiti prāṇaṃ tarhi vāgapyeti</s>' (when indeed a person sleeps, then speech merges into <s>Prāṇa</s>) — by its capacity to teach the sleeping and waking of all beings through the channel of teaching the sleeping and waking of all the sense-faculties — having acquired its power through the support of another means of knowledge — forcefully [establishes] that the sleeping and waking [are to be understood] with respect to <s>Prāṇa</s> as a modification of <s>Vāyu</s>, not <s>Brahman</s>. Moreover, here, for the <s>Udgītha</s> and <s>Pratihāra</s> — the [other] portions of the <s>Sāman</s> — deities other than <s>Brahman</s>, namely <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) and <s>Anna</s> (Food), have been stated as having the form of the aggregate of effects and instruments; by their association, <s>Prāṇa</s> too, as deity, should be of the form of an aggregate of effects and instruments [i.e., physical <s>prāṇa</s>].

body.text: ' no khalu svataḥsiddhapramāṇabhāvamapauruṣeyaṃ vacaḥ svaviṣayajñānotpāde vā tadvyavahāre vā mānāntaramapekṣate, tasyāpauruṣeyasya nirastasamastadoṣāśaṅkya svata eva niścāyakatvāt, niścāyakatvāt,
body.translated_text: Surely, an authorless statement (<s>vacas</s>), whose status as a means of knowledge is self-established, does not depend on another means of knowledge either for the generation of the cognition of its own subject-matter or for the worldly transaction [based on that cognition] — since that authorless [statement], being free from all suspicion of defect, is by its own nature determinative;

niścayapūrvakatvādvyavahārapravṛtteḥ /
tasmādasaṃvādino vā cakṣuṣa iva rūpe tvagindriyasaṃvādino vā tasyaiva dravye nādārḍhyaṃ vā dārḍhyaṃ vā /
