children.text: tathā copāsakasya prāṇaprāptiḥ karmasamṛddhirvā phalaṃ bhavatīti /
children.translated_text: And thus, for the meditator, the attainment of <s>Prāṇa</s> [i.e., <s>Brahman</s>] or the prosperity of [ritual] action is the fruit.
'By the force of the remainder of the sentence' (<s>vākyaśeṣabalena</s>) —
The meaning is: proximity from the [Vedic] sentence is weak.
But the other illustration is refuted by the commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>) which is explained by the running gloss (<s>nigada</s>). // 23 //

body.translated_text: and because worldly transaction is preceded by [such] determination. Therefore, just as a conflicting visual sense has neither lack of firmness nor firmness regarding the color of an object — [i.e., one ignores] even a concordant tactile sense — so too with this [authorless statement]: there is neither lack of firmness nor firmness based on [concordance with] the mere sense-experience of the sleeping and waking of the senses in the modification of <s>Vāyu</s> that is <s>Prāṇa</s>. But regarding the sleeping and waking of all beings, that is not apprehended from that [sense-based] statement. Or, if it is apprehended, then there too <s>Prāṇa</s> would be <s>Brahman</s> alone, not a modification of <s>Vāyu</s>. As in the sentence '<s>yadā suptaḥ svapnaṃ na kañcana paśyati athāsmin prāṇa evaikadhā bhavati</s>' (when the sleeping person sees no dream, then in this [self], [everything] becomes one in <s>Prāṇa</s> alone), the word '<s>prāṇa</s>' denotes <s>Brahman</s>. And the sleeping and waking of all beings in [the <s>Prāṇa</s> that is] a modification of <s>Vāyu</s> is not seen by another means of knowledge. Nor, because of the firmness of the [Vedic] statement about the sleeping and waking of the senses that is concordant with another means of knowledge, should the [Vedic] statement about the sleeping and waking of all beings be somehow explained as pertaining to the senses — since for [a text] whose status as a means of knowledge is self-established and whose nature is inherently firm, another means of knowledge is of no use. Nor does this [statement about the senses] form a single sentence with that [statement about all beings]. And if it were a single sentence, then that too would be about <s>Brahman</s> alone — this has been stated. But the sleeping and waking of the senses can be accommodated through subordination and reiteration — like 'he chooses one, he chooses two.' But the meaning of the word '<s>sarva</s>' (all) does not deserve contraction. Therefore, one should meditate on the <s>Prastāva</s> portion [of the <s>Sāman</s>] with the vision of <s>Brahman</s> as denoted by the word '<s>Prāṇa</s>', not with the vision of a modification of <s>Vāyu</s> — this is established.

idamāmananti-'atha yadataḥ paro divo jyotirdīpyate niśvataḥpṛṣṭheṣu sarvataḥ pṛṣṭheṣvanuttameṣūttameṣu lokeṣvidaṃ vāva tadyadidamasminnantaḥ puruṣe jyotiḥ' iti /

asaṃkucadvṛttirayaṃ viśvaśabdo 'navayavatvena saṃsāramaṇḍalaṃ brūta iti darśayitumāha- #sarvataḥpṛṣṭheṣūttameṣu# /
na cedamuttamamātraṃ apitu sarvottamamityāha- #anuttameṣu#nāstyebhyo 'nya uttama ityarthaḥ /
'idaṃ vāva tadyadidamasminpuruṣe 'ntarjyotiḥ' tvagrāhyeṇa śārīreṇoṣmaṇā, śrotragrāhyeṇa ca pihitakarṇena puṃsā ghoṣeṇa liṅgenānumīyate /
tatra śārīrasyoṣmaṇastvacā darśanaṃ dṛṣṭiḥ, ghoṣasya ca śravaṇaṃ śrutiḥ, tayośca dṛṣṭiśrutī jyotiṣa eva, talliṅgena tadanumānāditi /

children.text: atra saṃśayaḥ-kiṃ jyotiḥśabdaḥ teja uta brahmeti /
children.translated_text: Here there is doubt: does the word '<s>jyotis</s>' (light) [denote] fire (<s>tejas</s>) or <s>Brahman</s>?
What, to begin with, is the prima facie view? — That it denotes fire (<s>tejas</s>).

Why? Because in a context where both figurative (<s>gauṇa</s>) and primary (<s>mukhya</s>) comprehension are possible, the primary comprehension is the default (<s>autsargika</s>); and because of the perception of an indicatory mark of fire (<s>tejas</s>) within the sentence.
Since there is no restriction by another sentence, and since [the listener] does not connect that meaning [with <s>Brahman</s>] //

body.translated_text: '<s>Jyotiścaraṇābhidhānāt</s>' (Because of the mention of [its] feet). They declare this: 'Now, that light (<s>jyotis</s>) which shines beyond the heaven, on the backs of all, on the backs of everything, in the highest of the highest worlds — this very [light] is that which is the light within a person' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.13.7). That light (<s>jyotis</s>) which shines — i.e., illuminates — beyond the heaven, on the backs of all. This word '<s>viśva</s>' (all), having an unrestricted scope, speaks of the entire realm of <s>saṃsāra</s> without any part [being excluded] — to show this, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'on all backs, the highest' (<s>sarvataḥpṛṣṭheṣu uttameṣu</s>). And this is not merely the highest, but the unsurpassed — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'unsurpassed' (<s>anuttameṣu</s>) — meaning: there are none higher than these. 'This very [light] is that which is the light within a person' (<s>idaṃ vāva tad yad idam asmin puruṣe antar jyotiḥ</s>) — [this is inferred] by the evidence (<s>liṅga</s>) of the bodily warmth, which is tangible, and the sound heard by a person with ears covered — which is audible. Therein, the perception of the bodily warmth by touch is 'seeing' (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>); and the hearing of the sound is 'hearing' (<s>śruti</s>); and both the seeing and hearing are of the light (<s>jyotis</s>) alone — through its indicatory mark, it is inferred.

children.text: yadyapyādhārabahutvaśrutirbrahmaṇyapi kalpitopādhinibandhanā kathañcidupapadyate, tathāpi yathā kārye jyotiṣyatiśayenopapadyate na tathātretyata uktam- #upapadyetatarāmiti /
children.translated_text: Although the <s>Śruti</s> about multiplicity of supports can somehow be justified regarding <s>Brahman</s> too, through being based on imagined limiting adjuncts, nevertheless, it is more fitting regarding fire as an effect than regarding <s>Brahman</s> — hence it was said: 'It would be more fitting' (<s>upapadyetatarām</s>).
'<s>Prākṛta</s>' means 'born from <s>prakṛti</s>' (primordial matter) — that is, an effect.
Thus being the prima facie conclusion, it is said [in verse] — 'That which is well-known as the meaning of the pronoun, obstructing the meaning to be established,
Requiring well-knownness, standing in the preceding sentence — [this] overrides [the proposed meaning].' //

body.translated_text:
Indeed, the words '<s>ākāśa</s>' (space) and '<s>prāṇa</s>' (breath), through the incidence of a powerful sublating factor, were displaced from their primary meaning and established elsewhere.
But here, if the word '<s>jyotis</s>' (light) has fire as its primary meaning, there is firstly no sublating factor within its own sentence.
On the contrary, the [phrase] 'it shines' (<s>dīpyate</s>) is itself an indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of fire.
And the similarity with the light within the belly, and [the fact that] 'one who has eyes (<s>cakṣuṣya</s>) becomes renowned (<s>viśruta</s>), possessed of form (<s>rūpavān</s>)' — indicating a minor fruit — are heard within its own sentence.
Shining (<s>dīpti</s>), which is another name for blazing, is never possible in <s>Brahman</s> without fire.
Nor is the similarity with the light within the belly possible for <s>Brahman</s> without external fire.
Nor is the indicatory mark of heat and sound — seeing and hearing — tenable for <s>Brahman</s> apart from fire that is within the belly.
Nor is the great-fruited meditation on <s>Brahman</s> suited for a minor fruit.
But if [the meditation] is on fire that is within the belly, having superimposed external fire [upon it], this meditation — being commensurate with its fruit — is fitting.
This is the indicatory mark of fire.
And to corroborate this, even though [the argument about] the multiplicity of supports has been set aside, it is presented here because here the reason for its dismissal is absent.
Nor is the possession of limits impossible for a mass of fire, since the solar [fire] and the like, being possessed of parts, have limits at their respective parts, and since their meditation is prescribed as such; but for <s>Brahman</s>, which is partless, the meditation on a part is untenable, and if parts were to be postulated, they would not be postulated when [the entity] has been [shown to be] partless.
Nor can another sentence — 'One quarter of it is all beings; three quarters of it are the immortal in heaven' — which teaches <s>Brahman</s>, be used to establish the word '<s>jyotis</s>' in '<s>yadataḥ paraḥ</s>' (that which is beyond this) as referring to <s>Brahman</s>.
For a <s>Śruti</s> occurring in another sentence cannot, merely by proximity, be used to override the primary meaning of yet another sentence.
Nor can the heaven heard in the other sentence as a substratum be recognized in the limit-expression 'of heaven' (<s>divaḥ</s>).
Moreover, even the orientation of that other sentence toward <s>Brahman</s> is [something] still to be established and is not yet established — so how can the sentence 'that which is beyond this' be constrained by it as oriented toward <s>Brahman</s>?
Therefore, '<s>jyotis</s>' is fire alone, not <s>Brahman</s> — this is the prima facie conclusion.
The mention of darkness in the context of speaking about fire is for the purpose of [generating] a firm conviction regarding the opposite side, by presenting the counter-argument — this is its purpose.
'Obstructing the operation of the eye' (<s>cakṣurvṛtternirodhakam</s>) — by virtue of being an obstructor.
The objector says: 'But surely, even of an effect...' (<s>nanu kāryasyāpi</s>).
The partial supporter of the established view responds: 'Let it be so, then' (<s>astu tarhi</s>).
That fire which is unmixed with water and food — that is said to be not tripartite (<s>trivṛtkṛta</s>).
The objector refutes: 'No' (<s>na</s>).
For that [unmixed fire] is not useful anywhere; in all practical activities, only the tripartite [fire] is useful — this is the meaning.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the doubt of the partial supporter: 'This very...' (<s>idameva</s>).
The objector dismisses it: 'No; because of another purpose' (<s>na; prayojanāntara</s>).
The <s>Śruti</s> 'Each one I shall make tripartite' (<s>ekaikāṃ trivṛtaṃ trivṛtaṃ karavāṇi</s>) — which has as its sole domain the meditation on fire and the like — should not be narrowed [in scope] — this is the meaning.
Thus, when the partial supporter has been refuted, the ultimate respondent — the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> — says: 'Let it then be the tripartite [fire] alone' (<s>astu tarhi trivṛtkṛtameva</s>).
The sharing [of portions among elements] is fitting.

children.translated_text: 'By the force of that [pronoun], even the indicatory marks of fire must certainly be interpreted',

children.text: brahmaṇyeva pradhānaṃ hi brahmacchando na tatra tu //
children.translated_text: 'As referring to <s>Brahman</s> alone — for <s>Brahman</s> is the main [topic], not fire, in that [passage].' //

body.text:
' autsargikaṃ tāvadyadaprasiddhārthānuvādakatvaṃ yadvidhivibhaktimapyapūrvārthāvabodhanasvabhāvātpracyāvayati /
yathā 'yasyāhitāgneragnirgṛhāndahet' 'yasyobhayaṃ havirārtimārcchet' iti /
yatra punastatprasiddhamanyato na kathañcidāpyate, tatra vacanāni tvapūrvatvāditi sarvanāmnaḥ prasiddhārthatvaṃ balādapanīyate /
yathā 'yadāgneyo 'ṣṭākapālo bhavati' iti /
tadiha 'yadataḥ paro divo jyotiḥ' iti yacchabdasāmarthyāt dyumaryādenāpi jyotiṣā prasiddhena bhavitavyam /
naca tasya pramāṇāntarataḥ prasiddhirasti /
pūrvavākye ca dyusaṃbandhitayā tripādbrahma prasiddhamiti prasiddhyapekṣāyāṃ tadeva saṃbadhyate /
naca pradhānasya prātipadikārthasya tattvena pratyabhijñāne tadviśeṣaṇasya vibhaktyarthasyānyatāmātreṇānyatā yuktā /
evaṃ ca tadvākyasthāni tejoliṅgānyasamañjasānīti brahmaṇyeva gamayitavyāni, gamitāni ca bhāṣyakṛtā /
tatra jyotirbrahmavikāra iti jyotiṣā brahmaivopalakṣyate /
athavā prakāśamātravacano jyotiḥśabdaḥ prakāśasya brahmeti brahmaṇi mukya iti jyotirbahmeti siddham /
#prakṛtahānāprakṛtaprakriye iti# /
prasiddhyapekṣāyāṃ pūrvavākyagataṃ prakṛtaṃ saṃnihitaṃ, aprasiddhaṃ tu kalpyaṃ na prakṛtam /
ata evoktam- #kalpyata iti# /
saṃdaṃśanyāmāha- #na kevalamiti /

children.translated_text: Even for the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, like a name and the like, [fire can function as] a symbol (<s>pratīka</s>) [for meditation].

children.text: kaukṣeyaṃ hi jyotirjīvabhāvenānupraviṣṭasya paramātmano vikāraḥ, jīvabhāve dehasya śaityāt, jīvataścauṣṇyājjñāyate /
children.translated_text: For the light within the belly is a modification of the supreme Self (<s>paramātman</s>) who has entered [the body] as the individual self (<s>jīva</s>); since the body is cold in the state of being a <s>jīva</s>, [but] heat is known to be [present] while [the being] is alive.
Therefore, the meditation on a symbol of that [supreme <s>Brahman</s>] is fitting.
The rest of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> is explained by the running gloss (<s>nigadavyākhyāta</s>). // 24 //

body.translated_text:
As a general rule, the capacity of restatement of a well-known meaning [belonging to a pronoun] — which displaces even the injunctive case-ending from its unprecedented-meaning function.
For example: 'If the fire of one who has established the [sacrificial] fires were to burn his house,' 'If both his oblations were to reach misfortune' — [in such cases, the indicative mood is used for a well-known event, not enjoining anything new].
But where that well-known [meaning] cannot be obtained from any other source, then the statements — being unprecedented — forcefully override the well-knownness of the pronoun.
For example: 'When there is an <s>Āgneya</s> eight-<s>kapāla</s> [offering]' — [here '<s>yad</s>' introduces something new].
Accordingly, here in '<s>yadataḥ paro divo jyotiḥ</s>' (that light which is beyond this, beyond heaven), by the force of the word '<s>yad</s>' (that which), there must be a light that is well-known, beyond the [celestial] boundary too.
And there is no well-knownness of that from another means of knowledge.
But in the preceding sentence, the three-quartered <s>Brahman</s> is well-known as connected with heaven (<s>dyu</s>); therefore, when well-knownness is required, that alone is connected.
Nor, when the primary meaning — the <s>prātipadika</s>-meaning (nominal stem-meaning) — is recognized in its reality, is it reasonable that its qualifier — the case-ending meaning of 'otherness' — would become different merely because of its otherness.
And thus, the indicatory marks of fire occurring in that sentence are discordant [with fire] and must be interpreted as referring to <s>Brahman</s> alone — and they have been so interpreted by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (commentator).
Therein, [regarding] '<s>jyotis</s> is <s>Brahman</s>' — '<s>jyotis</s>' being a modification of <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Brahman</s> is indicated (<s>upalakṣyate</s>) by '<s>jyotis</s>.'
Or alternatively, the word '<s>jyotis</s>' denotes mere luminosity (<s>prakāśamātra</s>); and since luminosity is <s>Brahman</s>, [the word] is primary in [its application to] <s>Brahman</s> — thus '<s>jyotis</s> is <s>Brahman</s>' is established.
'Because of the abandonment of the topic at hand and the introduction of what is not the topic at hand' (<s>prakṛtahānāprakṛtaprakriye</s>) — when well-knownness is required, what stands in the preceding sentence is the topic at hand and proximate; but what is not well-known and must be postulated is not the topic at hand.
Hence it was said: 'It is postulated' (<s>kalpyate</s>).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the tongs-principle (<s>saṃdaṃśanyāya</s>): 'Not only...' (<s>na kevalam</s>).

body.text:
#chandobhidhānānneti cet na tathā cetorpaṇanigadāttathāhi darśanam# /
pūrvavākyasya hi brahmārthatve siddhe syādetadevaṃ, natu tadbrahmārthaṃ, apitu gāyatryartham /
'gāyatrī vā idaṃ sarvaṃ bhūtaṃ yadidaṃ kiñca' iti gāyatrīṃ prakṛtyedaṃ śrūyate-'tripādasyāmṛtaṃ divi' iti /
nanu 'ākāśastalliṅgāt' ityanenaiva gatārthametat /
tathāhi-'tāvānasya mahimā' ityasyāmṛci brahma catuṣpāduktam /
saiva ca 'tadetadṛcābhyanūktam' ityanena saṃgamitārthā brahmaliṅgam /
evaṃ 'gāyatrī vā idaṃ sarvam' ityakṣarasaṃniveśamātrasya gāyatryā na sarvatvamupapadyate /
naca bhūtapṛthivīśarīrahṛdayavākprāṇātmatvaṃ gāyatryāḥ svarūpeṇa saṃbhavati /
naca brahmapuruṣasaṃbandhitvamasti gāyatryāḥ /
tasmādgīyatrīdvārā brahmaṇa evopāsanā na gāyatryā iti pūrveṇaiva gatārthatvādanārambhaṇīyametat /
naca pūrvanyāyasmāraṇe sūtrasaṃdarbha etāvānyuktaḥ /
atrocyate-astyadhikā śaṅkā /
tathāhi-gāyatrīdvārā brahmopāsaneti kor'thaḥ, gāyatrīvikāropādhino brahmaṇa upāsaneti /
naca tadupādhinastadavacthachinnasya sarvātmatvaṃ, upādheravacchedāt /
nahi ghaṭāvacchinnaṃ nabho 'navacchinnaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text:
'If it be said [that the reference is] not [to <s>Brahman</s>] because of the mention of a meter (<s>chandas</s>) — no, [it is] not so, because of the direction of the mind [toward <s>Brahman</s>], as stated in the running text; for thus is the teaching (<s>darśana</s>)' [BS 1.1.25].
For if the previous sentence's orientation toward <s>Brahman</s> were established, it would be so [i.e., '<s>jyotis</s>' would refer to <s>Brahman</s>]; but that [previous sentence] is not oriented toward <s>Brahman</s> — rather, it is oriented toward the <s>Gāyatrī</s> [meter].
[The <s>Śruti</s>] 'The <s>Gāyatrī</s> is indeed all this, whatever exists here' — having introduced <s>Gāyatrī</s> as the topic, this is heard: 'Three quarters of it are the immortal in heaven.'
But [one may object:] is this not already dealt with by '<s>ākāśas tal-liṅgāt</s>' [BS 1.1.22]?
This is so: In the <s>Ṛk</s> 'Such is its greatness' (<s>tāvānasya mahimā</s>), four-quartered <s>Brahman</s> is stated.
And that very [<s>Ṛk</s>], connected in meaning [with the prose passage] by '<s>tadetadṛcābhyanūktam</s>' (this is reiterated by this verse), is an indicatory mark of <s>Brahman</s>.
Thus [in that earlier topic it was shown that] '<s>Gāyatrī</s> is indeed all this' cannot be justified for the <s>Gāyatrī</s> in the form of a mere arrangement of syllables as having all-ness.
Nor can the <s>Gāyatrī</s>'s being of the nature of elements (<s>bhūta</s>), earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>), body (<s>śarīra</s>), heart (<s>hṛdaya</s>), speech (<s>vāk</s>), <s>prāṇa</s>, or Self be possible for the <s>Gāyatrī</s> in its own form.
Nor does the <s>Gāyatrī</s> have a connection with <s>Brahma-puruṣa</s> (the <s>Brahman</s>-person).
Therefore, it is through the <s>Gāyatrī</s> [as a symbol] that the meditation is on <s>Brahman</s> alone, not on the <s>Gāyatrī</s> — so this is already dealt with by the previous [<s>sūtra</s>] and should not have been commenced [as a new topic].
Nor is this much textual sequence of <s>sūtra</s>s warranted for the mere recollection of the previous reasoning.
To this it is said: there is an additional objection.
This is as follows: 'The meditation on <s>Brahman</s> through the <s>Gāyatrī</s>' — what does this mean? It means: the meditation on <s>Brahman</s> conditioned by the <s>Gāyatrī</s> as a limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) that is its modification.
But for [<s>Brahman</s>] conditioned by that limiting adjunct and delimited by that delimitation, all-selfhood (<s>sarvātmatva</s>) is impossible, since the limiting adjunct itself delimits.
For space delimited by a pot is not undelimited.

body.text:
tasmādasya sarvātmatvādikaṃ stutyarthaṃ, tadvaraṃ gāyatryā evāstu stutiḥ kathācitpraṇāḍyā /
'vāgvai gāyatrī vāgvā idaṃ sarvaṃ bhūtaṃ gāyati ca trāyate ca' ityādiśritibhyaḥ /
tathāca 'gāyatrī vā idaṃ sarvam' ityupakramya gāyatryā eva hṛdayādibhirvyākhyāya ca 'saiṣā catuṣpadā ṣaḍvidhā gāyatrī' ityupasaṃhāro gāyatryāmeva samañjaso bhavati /
brahmaṇi tu sarvamatadasamañjasamiti /
'yadvai tadbrahma' iti brahmaśabdaśchandoviṣaya eva, yathā 'etāṃ brahmopaniṣadam' ityatra vedopaniṣaducyate /
tasmādgāyatrichandobhidhānānna brahmaviṣayametaditi prāptam /
evaṃ prāpte 'bhidhīyate- #na# /
kutaḥ, #tathā cetorpaṇanigadāt# /
gāyatryākhyacchandodvāreṇa gāyatrīrūpavikārānugate brahmaṇi cetorpaṇaṃ cittasamādhānamanena brahmaṇavākyena nigadyate /
etaduktaṃ bhavati /
na gāyatrī brahmaṇo 'vacchedikā, utpalasyeva nīlatvaṃ, yena tadavacchinnatvamanaytra na syādavacchedakavirahāt /
kintu yadetadbrahma sarvātmakaṃ sarvakāraṇaṃ satsvarūpeṇāśakyopadeśamiti tadvikāragāyatrīdvāreṇopalakṣyate /
gāyatryāḥ sarvacchandovyāptyā ca savanatrayavyāptyā ca dvijātidvitīyajanmajananīyatayā ca śrutervikāreṣu madhye prādhānyena dvāratvopapatteḥ /
na cānyatropalakṣaṇābhāvena nopalakṣyaṃ pratīyate /
nahi kuṇḍalenopalakṣitaṃ kaṇṭharūpaṃ kuṇḍalaviyoge 'pi paścātpratīyamānamapratīyamānaṃ bhavati /
tadrūpapratyāyanamātropayogitvādupalakṣaṇānāmanavacchedakatvāt /
tadevaṃ gāyatrīśabdasya mukhyārthatve gāyatryā brahmopalakṣyata ityuktam /
saṃprati ti gāyatriśabdaḥ saṃkhyāsāmānyādgauṇyā vṛttyā brahmaṇyeva vartata iti darśayati- #apara āheti# /
tathāhi-ṣaḍakṣaraiḥ pādairyathā gāyatrī catuṣpadā, evaṃ brahmāpi catuṣpāt /
sarvāṇi hi bhūtāni sthāvarajaṅgamānyasyaikaḥ pādaḥ /
athavā divyākāśe trayaḥ pādāḥ /
tathāhi śrutiḥ-'idaṃ vāva tadyo 'yaṃ puruṣādākāśaḥ'
body.translated_text:
Therefore, the all-selfhood and the like [attributed to it] are for the purpose of praise (<s>stuti</s>); it would be better to let the praise — however exaggerated — be of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> itself.
From <s>Śruti</s>s such as: 'Speech is indeed <s>Gāyatrī</s>; speech indeed is all this that exists — it sings and protects.'
And thus, having introduced [the topic] with '<s>Gāyatrī</s> is indeed all this' and having explained the <s>Gāyatrī</s> by the heart and the like, the conclusion 'This four-footed, sixfold [entity] is the <s>Gāyatrī</s>' is fitting with regard to the <s>Gāyatrī</s> alone.
But with regard to <s>Brahman</s>, all of this would be discordant.
And the word '<s>Brahman</s>' in '<s>yadvai tat brahma</s>' (that which is indeed <s>Brahman</s>) is used regarding the meter (<s>chandas</s>) itself, just as in '<s>etāṃ brahmopaniṣadam</s>' (this <s>Brahma</s>-<s>Upaniṣad</s>), [where] a Vedic <s>Upaniṣad</s> is intended.
Therefore, because of the mention of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter, this [passage] is not about <s>Brahman</s> — this is the prima facie conclusion.
This being the prima facie conclusion, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'No' (<s>na</s>).
Why? 'Because of the direction of the mind, as stated' (<s>tathā cetorpaṇanigadāt</s>).
Through the meter called <s>Gāyatrī</s>, the directing of the mind (<s>cetorpaṇa</s>) — the concentration of thought (<s>cittasamādhāna</s>) — upon <s>Brahman</s>, which is present in the form of the modification that is the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, is declared by this sentence about <s>Brahman</s>.
What is stated amounts to this:
The <s>Gāyatrī</s> is not a delimiter of <s>Brahman</s> — like blue-ness in a lotus — such that [<s>Brahman</s>] delimited by it would not [have all-selfhood] elsewhere due to the absence of the delimiter.
Rather, this <s>Brahman</s> — which is the Self of all and the cause of all — being impossible to teach in its own form, is indicated through the modification [that is the] <s>Gāyatrī</s>.
And the fitness of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> as the primary mediating symbol among modifications [is due to]: its pervading all meters, its pervading the three <s>savana</s>s (pressings of <s>Soma</s>), and its being the mother of the twice-born's second birth — hence the fitness of its being the primary mediating symbol, as taught by <s>Śruti</s>.
Nor, in the absence of the indicatory symbol elsewhere, is what is indicated not cognized.
For the face-form indicated by an earring is not uncognized even after the removal of the earring, when perceived later.
Because indicatory symbols — their sole function being the initial cognition of the form [of what is indicated] — are not delimiters.
Thus, when the word '<s>Gāyatrī</s>' is taken in its primary meaning, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] has stated that <s>Brahman</s> is indicated through the <s>Gāyatrī</s>.
Now [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] shows that the word '<s>Gāyatrī</s>' itself applies to <s>Brahman</s> through a figurative usage (<s>gauṇī vṛtti</s>) based on the similarity of number: 'Others say' (<s>apara āha</s>).
This is as follows: Just as the <s>Gāyatrī</s> [meter] is four-footed with six-syllable feet, so too <s>Brahman</s> is four-footed.
For all beings — stationary and moving — are one foot of it.
Or alternatively, in the celestial space (<s>divyākāśa</s>), there are three feet.
Thus the <s>Śruti</s>: 'This indeed is that — [the space] which is here within the person — [is the same as] the space' (<s>idaṃ vāva tadyo 'yaṃ puruṣādākāśaḥ</s>).

body.text:
taddhi tasya jagaritasthānam /
jāgratvakhalvayaṃ bāhyānpadārthānveda /
tathā-'ayaṃ vāva sa yo 'yamantaḥ puruṣa ākāśaḥ' /
śarīramadhya ityarthaḥ /
taddhi tasya svapnasthānam /
tathā-'ayaṃ vāva sa yo 'yamantarhṛdaya ākāśaḥ' /
hṛdayapuṇḍarīka ityarthaḥ /
taddhi tasya suṣuptisthānam /

children.translated_text: This is what is stated [by the <s>Śruti</s>]: 'Three quarters of it are the immortal in heaven' (<s>tripādasyāmṛtaṃ divi</s>).
Thus, by the similarity of being four-footed, <s>Brahman</s> is referred to by the word '<s>Gāyatrī</s>.'
On this view, <s>Brahman</s> alone is what is denoted [by the word '<s>Gāyatrī</s>'].
Because [the passage] is oriented toward <s>Brahman</s>, [<s>Brahman</s>] is what is denoted — this has been stated. // 25 //

body.translated_text:
For that is its waking state (<s>jāgaritasthāna</s>).
For indeed, in the waking state, one knows external objects.
Likewise: 'This indeed is that — the space within the person' (<s>ayaṃ vāva sa yo 'yamantaḥ puruṣa ākāśaḥ</s>).
The meaning is: within the body.
For that is its dream state (<s>svapnasthāna</s>).
Likewise: 'This indeed is that — the space within the heart' (<s>ayaṃ vāva sa yo 'yamantarhṛdaya ākāśaḥ</s>).
The meaning is: within the lotus of the heart.
For that is its deep-sleep state (<s>suṣuptisthāna</s>).

body.text:
#ṣaḍvidheti# /
bhūtapṛthivīśarīrahṛdayavākprāṇā iti ṣaṭ prakārā gāyatryākhyasya brahmaṇaḥ śrūyante /
#pañca brahmapuruṣā iti ca, hṛdayayasuṣiṣu brahmapuruṣaśrutirbrahmasaṃbandhitāyāṃ vivakṣitāyāṃ saṃbhavati# /
asyārthaḥ-hṛdayasyāsya khalu pañca suṣayaḥ pañca chidrāṇi /
tāni ca devaiḥ prāṇādibhī rakṣyamāṇāni svargaprāptidvārāṇīti devasuṣayaḥ /
tathāhi-hṛdayasya yatprāṅmukhaṃ chidraṃ tatstho yo vāyuḥ sa prāṇaḥ, tena hi prayāṇakāle saṃcarate svargalokaṃ, sa eva cakṣuḥ, sa evāditya ityarthaḥ /
'ādityo ha vai bāhyaḥ prāṇaḥ' iti śruteḥ /
atha yo 'sya dakṣiṇaḥ suṣistatstho vāyuviśeṣo vyānaḥ /
tatsaṃbaddhaṃ śrotra taccandramāḥ, 'śrotreṇa sṛṣṭā viśaścandramāśca' iti śruteḥ /
atha yo 'sya pratyaṅmukhaḥ suṣistatatstho vāyuviśeṣo 'pānaḥ sa ca vāksaṃbandhādvāk, 'vāgvā agniḥ' iti śruteḥ /

children.text: atha yo 'syodaṅmukhaḥ suṣistatstho vāyuviśeṣaḥ sa udānaḥ, pādatalādārabhyordhvaṃ nayanāt /
children.translated_text: Now, the particular vital air stationed in the northward-facing aperture is <s>Udāna</s>, [so called] because it leads upward beginning from the soles of the feet.
That vital air, its support, is space (<s>ākāśa</s>), [which is] the deity.
These indeed are the five apertures.

children.text: tatsaṃbaddhāḥ pañca hārdasya brahmaṇaḥ puruṣā na gāyatryāmakṣarasaṃniveśamātre saṃbhavanti, kintu brahmaṇyeveti //26 //
children.translated_text: The five <s>puruṣa</s>s of the <s>Brahman</s> residing in the heart — connected with those [apertures] — are not possible in the <s>Gāyatrī</s> as a mere arrangement of syllables, but only in <s>Brahman</s> itself. // 26 //

body.translated_text:
'Sixfold' — thus.
Beings, earth, body, heart, speech, and <s>prāṇa</s> — these six kinds of the <s>Brahman</s> named <s>Gāyatrī</s> are heard [in scripture].
'And the five <s>Brahma-puruṣa</s>s — the <s>Śruti</s> statement of <s>Brahma-puruṣa</s>s in the apertures of the heart is possible when the relatedness to <s>Brahman</s> is intended.'
The meaning of this is: This heart indeed has five apertures (<s>suṣi</s>), five openings.
And they, being guarded by the deities — <s>Prāṇa</s> and the rest — are the gateways to the attainment of heaven, hence they are called divine apertures (<s>devasuṣi</s>).
That is as follows: The vital air (<s>vāyu</s>) stationed in the eastward-facing opening of the heart is <s>Prāṇa</s>; for by it, at the time of departure [from the body], one travels to the heavenly world. That itself is the eye, and that itself is the sun (<s>Āditya</s>) — this is the meaning.
Because of the <s>Śruti</s>: 'The sun is indeed the external <s>Prāṇa</s>.'
Now, the particular vital air stationed in the southern aperture is <s>Vyāna</s>.
The ear is connected with it, and that [ear] is the moon — because of the <s>Śruti</s>: 'Through the ear were emitted the peoples and the moon.'
Now, the particular vital air stationed in the westward-facing aperture is <s>Apāna</s>; and that, by virtue of its connection with speech, is speech — because of the <s>Śruti</s>: 'Speech is indeed <s>Agni</s> (fire).'

body.text:
#yathā soka iti# /
yadādhāratvaṃ mukhyaṃ divastadā kathañcinmaryādā vyākhyeyā /
yo hi śyeno vṛkṣāgre vastuto 'sti sa ca tataḥ paro 'pyastyeva /
arvāgbhāgātiriktamapyaparabhāgasthasya tasyaiva vṛkṣātparato 'vasthānāt /
evaṃ ca bāhyadyubhāgātiriktaśārīrahārdadyubhāgasthasya brahmaṇo bāhyāt dyubhāgātparato 'vasthānamupapannam /

children.text: yadā tu maryādaiva mukhyatayā prādhānyena vivakṣitā tadā lakṣaṇayādhāratvaṃ vyākhyeyam /
children.translated_text: But when the boundary itself is intended primarily and principally, then the support-relation should be explained figuratively (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>).
Just as in 'the settlement is on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,' [where the meaning is] by proximity — thus.
This is what was stated: 'Another says' — thus.
For this very reason, it was said 'even beyond heaven.' // 27 //

body.translated_text:
'As a falcon' — thus.
When the support-relation of heaven (<s>div</s>) is primary, the boundary [i.e., limit] must somehow be explained.
For a falcon that is actually on the top of a tree — it also exists beyond that [point].
Even though [the falcon] exceeds the near side, its being situated beyond the tree [is established] by the fact that the very same [falcon], situated on the far side, is beyond the near portion.
Similarly, it is fitting that <s>Brahman</s> — which, though exceeding the external celestial portion, is situated in the bodily and cardiac celestial portion — has its position beyond the external celestial portion.

children.translated_text: '<s>Prāṇa</s> [is <s>Brahman</s>], because of the consistent pursuit [of indicatory marks].'
'When many indicatory marks are mixed together, which prevails?
The indicatory mark of the indicated — this is the question, not previously examined.' //

' mukhyaprāṇajīvadevatābrahmaṇāmanekeṣāṃ liṅgāni bahūni saṃplavante, tatkatamadatra liṅgaṃ, liṅgābhāsaṃ ca katamadityatra vicāryate /
na cāyamarthaḥ 'ata eva prāṇaḥ' ityatra vicāritaḥ /

tathā 'eṣa sādhu karma kārayati' 'eṣa lokādhipatiḥ' ityādyapi /

tathāpi paramapuruṣārthasyāpavargasya parabrahmajñānādanyato 'navāpteḥ, paramānandarūpasya mukhyasyāmṛtatvasyājaratvasya ca brahmarūpāvyabhicārāt, adhyātmasaṃbandhabhūmnaśca parācīndre 'nupapatteḥ, indrasya devatāyā ātmani pratibuddhasya caramadehasya vāmadevasyeva prarabdhavipākakarmāśayamātraṃ bhogena kṣapayato brahmaṇa eva sarvametatkalpata iti vigrahavadindrijīvaprāṇavāyuparityāgena brahmaivātra prāṇaśabdaṃ pratīyata iti pūrvapakṣābhāvādanārabhyametaditi /

jīvaśca prajñātmā /

children.text: yatpunarbhedadarśanaṃ 'saha hyetau' iti, tajjñānakriyāśaktibhedena buddhiprāṇayoḥ pratyagātmopādhibhūtayornirdeśaḥ pratyagātmānamevopalakṣayitum /
children.translated_text: As for the indication of duality — 'For these two together' — this is a reference to the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) and <s>Prāṇa</s>, [which are] the two limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) of the inner Self (<s>pratyagātman</s>), [distinguished] by the distinction of the powers of knowledge and action, [mentioned] in order to indicate the inner Self itself.

children.text: ata evopalakṣyasya pratyagātmasvarūpasyābhedamupalakṣaṇaṃ bhedenopalakṣayati-'prāṇa eva prajñātmā' iti /
children.translated_text: For this very reason, the non-difference of the inner Self — which is the thing indicated (<s>upalakṣya</s>) — is indicated through the distinguishing indicatory mark (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) of duality: '<s>Prāṇa</s> alone is the conscious Self.'
'Therefore, because of following the <s>Brahman</s>-indicatory marks that are not otherwise explicable,
By the force of sentential unity, the indicatory marks of <s>Prāṇa</s> and the individual soul are explained [as referring to <s>Brahman</s>]' — this is the summary. // 28 //

body.translated_text:
The indicatory marks of the chief vital air (<s>mukhyaprāṇa</s>), the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>), a deity, and <s>Brahman</s> — many [of them] flow together regarding these multiple [candidates]. Which among them is the [genuine] indicatory mark, and which is a semblance of an indicatory mark? — this is what is examined here.
Nor has this question been examined in [the section] 'For this very reason, [it is] <s>Prāṇa</s>.' [BSBh 1.1.5]
One might say this:
The attainment of the highest human goal, the non-involvement with all sins such as killing a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> embryo and the like, the nature of being consciousness (<s>prajñātman</s>), and bliss (<s>ānanda</s>) and the like — these are not possible in the chief vital air.
Likewise, 'He causes one to perform good action,' 'He is the lord of the worlds,' and the like.
In the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>), the nature of being consciousness is somehow possible, but the others are not.
Speech (<s>vaktṛtva</s>) — i.e., having the operation of speech as an instrument — although not possible in the supreme Self (<s>paramātman</s>) in its essential nature, nevertheless, to resolve the contradiction with the many <s>Brahman</s>-indicatory marks that are not otherwise explicable, it must be explained as [applying to] <s>Brahman</s> itself through the medium of the individual soul, since the individual soul is non-different from <s>Brahman</s>.
And thus the <s>Śruti</s>: 'That which is not spoken by speech, by which speech is uttered — know That alone as <s>Brahman</s>' — states that <s>Brahman</s> is the cause of speaking.
Even the sustaining of the body, though belonging to the chief vital air, is [attributable] to the supreme Self alone, since the operation of <s>Prāṇa</s> depends on the supreme Self.
Even though there is here an indicatory mark of <s>Indra</s> as a deity with a personal form — for indeed, <s>Indra</s> spoke to <s>Pratardana</s> who had come to <s>Indra</s>'s abode, saying, beginning with 'Know Me alone,' [and then] 'I am <s>Prāṇa</s>, the conscious Self' — using the word <s>Prāṇa</s> with reference to himself;
and the nature of being consciousness is appropriate for him, since deities have unobstructed powers of knowledge;
and because of <s>Indra</s>'s supremacy of power, [he can be] the cause of the highest human goal;
and since scripture has jurisdiction over human beings and does not operate toward deities, the non-involvement with sins such as killing a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> embryo is fitting;
and the lordship over the worlds [belongs to <s>Indra</s>] because he is a world-guardian;
and the nature of being bliss and the like [belongs to <s>Indra</s>] because heaven itself is blissful;
and immortality [belongs to <s>Indra</s>], because of the <s>Smṛti</s>: 'The state [of lasting] until the dissolution of all beings is declared to be immortality';
and the praise with reference to a personal form, 'I killed <s>Tvāṣṭra</s>' and the like, is fitting precisely for him [<s>Indra</s>];
nevertheless, since the supreme human goal of liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) cannot be attained from any [source] other than the knowledge of the supreme <s>Brahman</s>; since the supreme bliss, the primary [meaning of] immortality, and agelessness invariably apply to the nature of <s>Brahman</s> alone; and since the preponderance of references to the inner Self (<s>adhyātma-saṃbandha</s>) does not fit <s>Indra</s> as a deity — all of this is appropriate only for <s>Brahman</s>, just as for <s>Indra</s> as a deity who has realized [himself in] the Self and, like <s>Vāmadeva</s> in his final body, is merely exhausting through experience the residual latent impressions of <s>karma</s> whose fruits have begun to ripen.
Thus, abandoning [the references to] <s>Indra</s> as a deity with personal form, the individual soul, and the vital air, it is <s>Brahman</s> alone that is understood here by the word <s>Prāṇa</s> — hence there is no <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view) [to be established]; therefore this [topic] should not be commenced.
To this we reply: 'That which is <s>Prāṇa</s> — that is <s>Prajñā</s> (consciousness); that which is <s>Prajñā</s> — that is <s>Prāṇa</s>. For these two together dwell in this body and together depart' — thus, for the very <s>Prāṇa</s> whose nature as the conscious Self (<s>prajñātman</s>) is said to be the object of meditation, the departure together with consciousness is stated.
But in <s>Brahman</s> — being non-dual — the dual number is not possible, nor co-existence, nor departure.
Therefore, the vital air (<s>vāyu</s>) alone is <s>Prāṇa</s>.
And the individual soul is the conscious Self (<s>prajñātman</s>).
The figurative identity of these two through their co-occurring engagement and disengagement is expressed by 'That which is <s>Prāṇa</s>' and the like.
Bliss, immortality, agelessness, freedom from sin, and the like will [be attributed] to <s>Brahman</s> in [the vital air and the individual soul taken as] <s>Prāṇa</s>.
Therefore, as appropriate, three [entities] alone are the objects of meditation here.
Nor does this division of the passage constitute a defect.
Because the comprehension of sentence-meaning is preceded by the comprehension of word-meanings.
And word-meanings, by the method stated, are independent [in their denotation].
Therefore, due to the difference of the objects of meditation, the meditation is threefold — this is the prima facie view.
But the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>) is: True, the comprehension of sentence-meaning is preceded by the comprehension of word-meanings; but the words are not oriented solely toward their own individual meanings — rather, they are oriented toward the meaning of a single sentence.
They are unable to produce that single sentence-meaning without [first] communicating the word-meanings; hence, incidentally, for the sake of that [sentence-meaning] alone, they also communicate those [word-meanings]. Thus, words — whose natural tendency is to communicate a single qualified meaning — are led toward the communication of multiple meanings only by a strong sublating [consideration].
As they say: 'When sentential unity is possible, the division of the sentence is not desired.'
Therefore, just as in the <s>Upāṃśuyāja</s> passage — where, with the introduction of the defect of consanguinity (<s>jāmitā</s>) and the concluding resolution of it — for the sake of sentential unity, '<s>Prajāpati</s>'s <s>upāṃśu</s> [offering] should be performed' and the like are determined to be not separate injunctions but <s>arthavāda</s>s (laudatory passages) — so too here, having begun with 'Know Me alone,' having said 'I am <s>Prāṇa</s>, the conscious Self,' and having concluded with '<s>Prāṇa</s> alone is the conscious Self — blissful, ageless, immortal' — since sentential unity regarding <s>Brahman</s> is understood, the indicatory marks of the individual soul and the chief vital air too are to be led in conformity with that [<s>Brahman</s>].
Otherwise, there would be the absurd consequence of dividing the sentence.

body.text:
#na brahmavākyaṃ bhavitumarhatīti# /
naiṣa saṃdarbho brahmavākyameva bhavitumarhatīti, kintu tathāyogaṃ kiñcidatra jīvavākyaṃ, kiñcinmukhyaprāṇavākyaṃ, kiñcidbrahmavākyamityarthaḥ /
#prajñāsādhanaprāṇāntarāśrayatvāditi# /
prāṇāntarāṇīndriyāṇi, tāni hi mukhye prāṇe pratiṣṭhitāni /
jīvamukhyaprāṇayoranyatara ityupakramamātram /
ubhāviti tu pūrvapakṣatattvam /
brahma tu dhruvam /
#na brahmeti# /
na brahmaivetyarthaḥ /
#daśānāṃ būtamātrāṇāmiti# /
pañca śabdādayaḥ, pañca pṛthivyādaya iti daśa bhūtamātrāḥ /
pañca buddhīndriyāṇi pañca buddhasya iti daśa prajñāmātrāḥ /
tadevaṃ svamatena vyākhyāya prācāṃ vṛttikṛtāṃ matena vyācaṣṭe- #athaveti# /
pūrvaṃ prāṇasyaikamupāsanamaparaṃ jīvasyāparaṃ brahmaṇa ityupāsanātraividhyena vākyabhedaprasaṅgo dūṣaṇamuktam /
iha tu brahmaṇa ekasyaivopāsātrayaviśiṣṭasya vidhānānna vākyabeda ityabhimānaḥ prācāṃ vṛttikṛtām /
tadetadālocanīyaṃ kathaṃ na vākyabheda iti /

children.text: yuktaṃ 'somena yajeta' ityādau somādiguṇaviśiṣṭayāgavidhānaṃ, tadguṇaviśiṣṭasyāpūrvasya vidhiviṣayatvāt /
children.translated_text: It is appropriate that in '<s>somena yajeta</s>' (one should sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>) and the like, there is an injunction of sacrifice qualified by qualities such as <s>Soma</s> and the like, since the <s>apūrva</s> qualified by those qualities is the object of the injunction.

children.text: iha tu siddharūpaṃ brahma na vidhiviṣayo bhavitumarhati, abhāvārthatvāt /
children.translated_text: But here, <s>Brahman</s> — being of an already established nature — cannot be the object of an injunction, since it is of the nature of absence [of action, i.e., not a <s>bhāvārtha</s>].
Because there is the invariable rule that only what has a positive-act meaning (<s>bhāvārtha</s>) is the object of an injunction.

children.text: vākyāntarebhyaśca brahmavagateḥ prāptatvāttadanūdyāprāptopāsanā bhāvārthaḥ vidheyastasya ca bedādvidhyāvṛttilakṣaṇo vākyabedo 'tisphuṭa iti bāṣyakṛtā nodghāṭitaḥ, svavyākhyānenaivoktaprayatvāditi sarvaṃvadātam //31 //
children.translated_text: And since <s>Brahman</s> is understood from other sentences as already established, by restating that [<s>Brahman</s>], the un-obtained meditation — which is a positive act (<s>bhāvārtha</s>) — is what is to be enjoined; and because of the difference of that [meditation into three types], the division of the sentence — characterized by the division of the injunction — is very clear. Hence the commentator (<s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>) did not bring it up, since, being refuted by his own explanation, it is already accounted for — thus everything is well stated. // 31 //

body.translated_text:
'[The passage] cannot be a statement about <s>Brahman</s>' — the meaning is not that this textual sequence cannot be a statement about <s>Brahman</s> at all; rather, as appropriate, some [part of] it is a statement about the individual soul, some about the chief vital air, and some about <s>Brahman</s> — this is the meaning.
'Because it depends on other <s>prāṇa</s>s as the means of <s>prajñā</s> (consciousness)' — the other <s>prāṇa</s>s are the sense organs; for they are established in the chief vital air.
The individual soul or the chief vital air — this is merely the beginning [of the prima facie view].
But [that the passage refers to] both — this is the real prima facie position.
<s>Brahman</s>, however, is certain.
'Not <s>Brahman</s>' — means: not <s>Brahman</s> alone.
'Of the ten material elements' — the five [elements] beginning with sound and the five beginning with earth — these are the ten material elements (<s>bhūtamātrā</s>).
The five cognitive sense-organs are the five 'of consciousness' (<s>prajñāmātrā</s>) — thus ten consciousness-elements.
Having thus explained according to his own view, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] explains according to the view of the ancient commentators (<s>prācāṃ vṛttikṛtām</s>): 'Or alternatively' — thus.
Previously, the objection was raised that there would be a threefold division of the passage — one meditation for <s>Prāṇa</s>, another for the individual soul, and another for <s>Brahman</s> — leading to the division of the sentence.
But here, the view of the ancient commentators is that since a single <s>Brahman</s> alone — qualified by three [types of] meditation — is enjoined, there is no sentence-division.
This should be carefully considered: how is there no sentence-division [on this view]?

body.text: iti śrīvācaspatimiśraviracite bhāṣyavibhāge bhāmatyāṃ prathamasyādhyāyasya prathamaḥ pādaḥ //1 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the first <s>pāda</s> (quarter) of the first <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter) in the <s>Bhāmatī</s>, the exposition of the commentary (<s>bhāṣyavibhāga</s>), composed by the revered <s>Vācaspati Miśra</s>. // 1 //

body.text: #iti prathamasyādhyāyasya spaṣṭabrahmaliṅgaśrutisamanvayākhyaḥ prathamaḥ pādaḥ# //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the first <s>pāda</s> of the first <s>adhyāya</s>, called 'The Harmonious Purport of <s>Śruti</s> Passages with Clear <s>Brahman</s>-Indicatory Marks' (<s>spaṣṭabrahmaliṅgaśrutisamanvaya</s>). //

body.text: #prathamādhyāye dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ# /
body.translated_text: The second <s>pāda</s> of the first <s>adhyāya</s>.

body.text:
atha dvitīyaṃ pādamāripsuḥ pūrvoktamarthaṃ smārayati vakṣyamāṇopayogitayā- #prathame pāda iti# /
uttaratra hi brahmaṇo vyāpitvanityatvādayaḥ siddhavaddhetutayopadekṣyante /
na caite sākṣātpūrvamupapāditā iti kathaṃ hetubhāvena na śakyā upadeṣṭumityata uktam- #samastajagatkāraṇasyeti# /
yadyapyete na pūrvaṃ kaṇṭhata uktāstathāpi brahmaṇo jagajjanmādikāraṇatvopapadānenādhikaraṇasiddhāntanyāyenopakṣiptā ityupapannasteṣāmuttaratra hetubhāvenopanyāsa ityarthaḥ /
#arthāntaraprasiddhānāṃ ceti# /
yatrārthāntaraprasiddhā evākāśaprāṇajyotirādayo brahmaṇi vyākhyāyante, tadavyabhicāriliṅgaśravaṇāt /
tatra kaiva kathā manomayādīnāmarthāntaraṃ prasiddhānāṃ padānāṃ brahmagocaratvanirṇayaṃ pratītyabhiprāyaḥ /
pūrvapakṣābhiprāyaṃ tvagre darśayiṣyāmaḥ /
#sarvatra prasiddhopadeśāt /
idamāmnāyate /
sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ brahmaḥ# /
kutaḥ, #tajjalāniti# /
yatastasmādbrahmaṇo jāyata iti tajjaṃ, tasmiṃśca līyata iti tallaṃ, tasmiṃścāniti sthitikāle ceṣṭata iti tadanaṃ jagat tasmātsarvaṃ khalvidaṃ jagadbrahma /
ataḥ kaḥ kasminrajyate kaśca kaṃ dveṣṭīti rāgadveṣarahitaḥ śāntaḥ sannupāsīta /
#atha khalu kratumayaḥ puruṣo yathākraturasmiṃlloke puruṣo bhavati tathetaḥ pretya bhavati sa kratuṃ kurvīta manomayaḥ prāṇaśarīra ityādi# /
tatra saṃśayaḥ-kimiha manomayatvādibhirdharmaiḥ śārīra ātmopāsyatvenopadiśyate āhosvidbrahmeti /
kiṃ tāvatprāptam /
śārīro jīva iti /
kutaḥ /
'kratum' ityādivākyena vihitāṃ kratubhāvanāmanūdya 'sarvam' ityādivākyaṃ śamaguṇe vidhiḥ /
tathā ca 'sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ brahma' iti vākyaṃ prathamapaṭhitamapyarthālocanayā parameva, tadarthopajīvitvāt /
evaṃ ca saṃkalpavidhiḥ prathamo nirviṣayaḥ sannaparyavasyanviṣayāpekṣaḥ svayamanirvṛtto na vidhyantareṇopajīvituṃ śakyaḥ, anupapadākatvāt /
tasmācchāntatāguṇavidhānātpūrvameva 'manomayaḥ prāṇaśarīraḥ' ityādibhirviṣayopanāyakaiḥ saṃbadhyate /
manomayatvādi ca kāryakāraṇasaṃghātātmano jīvātmana eva nirūḍhamiti jīvātmanopāsyenoparaktopāsanā na paścāt brahmaṇā saṃbaddhumarhati, utpattiśiṣṭaguṇāvarodhāt /
naca 'sarvaṃ khalvidam' iti vākyaṃ brahmaparamapi tu śamahetuvannigadārthavādaḥ śāntatāvidhiparaḥ, 'śūrpeṇa juhoti' 'tena hyannaṃ kriyate' itivat /
na cānyaparādapi brahmāpekṣitatayā svīkriyata iti yuktaṃ, manomayatvādibhirdharmairjīve suprasiddhairjīvaviṣayasamarpaṇenānapekṣitatvāt /
sarvakarmatvādi tu jīvasya paryāyeṇa bhaviṣyati /
evaṃ cāṇīyastvamapyupapannam /
paramātmanastvaparimeyasya tadanupapattiḥ /
prathamāvagatena cāṇīyastvena jyāyastvaṃ tadanuguṇatayā vyākhyeyam /
vyākhyāṃ ca bhāṣyakṛtā /
evaṃ karmakartṛvyapadeśaḥ saptamīpraṇamāntatā cābhede 'pi jīvātmani kathañcidbhedopacāreṇa rāhoḥ śira itivaddraṣṭavyā /
'etadbrahma' iti ca jīvaviṣayaṃ, jīvasyāpi dehādibṛṃhaṇatvena brahmātvāt /

children.text: evaṃ satyasaṃkalpatvādayo 'pi paramātmavartino jīve 'pi saṃbhavanti, tadavyatirekāt /
children.translated_text: Thus, [attributes] such as having true will (<s>satyasaṃkalpatva</s>) etc., though belonging to the <s>Paramātman</s> (supreme Self), are also possible in the <s>jīva</s> (individual self), because of its non-difference from That.

children.text: tasmājjīva evopāsyatvenātra vivakṣitaḥ, na paramātmeti prāptam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is the <s>jīva</s> (individual self) alone that is intended here as the object of meditation, not the <s>Paramātman</s> (supreme Self) — this is what is arrived at [as the prima facie view].
This being the prima facie view, [the <s>siddhānta</s>] is stated: 'A compound whose meaning is that of a universal pronoun (<s>sarvanāma</s>) requires what is proximate;
The meaning of a secondary suffix (<s>taddhita</s>), being general, does not negate the requirement [of proximity].'

body.translated_text: Now, wishing to commence the second <s>pāda</s> (quarter), [<s>Vācaspati</s>] reminds [us] of the previously stated meaning for the sake of what is to follow — 'In the first <s>pāda</s>' etc. For in the sequel, <s>Brahman</s>'s pervasiveness, eternality, and other [attributes] will be taught as established reasons. And since these were not directly demonstrated earlier, how can they be taught as reasons? — to address this, it is said: 'Of [<s>Brahman</s>] which is the cause of the entire universe' etc. Although these were not explicitly stated before, nevertheless, through the demonstration of <s>Brahman</s>'s being the cause of the origin etc. of the world, they were implied by the principle of the established conclusion of the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topical section) — thus their subsequent presentation as reasons is justified. This is the meaning. 'And of those well-known in other senses' — where <s>ākāśa</s> (space), <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), <s>jyotis</s> (light), and other terms that are well-known in other senses are interpreted as referring to <s>Brahman</s>, that is because invariable indicatory marks (<s>liṅga</s>) are heard [in those passages]. In that case, what need is there to speak of the determination that terms like <s>manomaya</s> (mind-made) etc., which are not well-known in another sense, refer to <s>Brahman</s> — this is the intention. But we shall show the intention of the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (objection) later. '[<s>Brahman</s> is the object of meditation] because of the teaching that is well-known everywhere. This is what is handed down in scripture: All this is indeed <s>Brahman</s>.' From what reason? — 'Because of <s>tajjalān</s>.' Because the world is born from That (<s>Brahman</s>), it is <s>tajja</s> (born of That); because it dissolves into That, it is <s>talla</s> (dissolved in That); because it moves and acts during the period of sustenance in That, it is <s>tadana</s> (breathing in That) — therefore all this world is indeed <s>Brahman</s>. Hence, who is attached to whom, and who hates whom? — being free from attachment and aversion, one should meditate in a state of tranquility. 'Now, a person is indeed made of intention (<s>kratumaya</s>). As a person's intention is in this world, so does he become after departing hence. Let him form his intention. [He who is] <s>manomaya</s> (mind-made), having <s>prāṇa</s> as his body' — and so on. Therein arises a doubt: Is the embodied self (<s>śārīra ātman</s>) being taught here as the object of meditation through attributes such as being <s>manomaya</s>, or is it <s>Brahman</s>? What is first arrived at? [The answer is:] the embodied individual self (<s>jīva</s>). Why? Because the sentence beginning with '<s>kratu</s>' (intention) restates the cultivation of intention that has been enjoined, and the sentence beginning with 'all' is an injunction regarding the quality of tranquility (<s>śama</s>). And thus the sentence 'all this is indeed <s>Brahman</s>,' though read first, is actually subsequent in terms of the consideration of meaning, because it subserves the purpose of that [injunction of tranquility]. And thus the first injunction of intention (<s>saṃkalpavidhi</s>), being without an object, not reaching completion, requiring an object, and itself incomplete, cannot be subserved by another injunction, because it would not establish [anything]. Therefore, even before the injunction of the quality of tranquility, it is connected with the passages 'mind-made, having <s>prāṇa</s> as body' etc., which introduce the object [of meditation]. And being <s>manomaya</s> etc. is established only for the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>), which is the composite of cause and effect — therefore the meditation colored by the individual self as the object of worship ought not subsequently to be connected with <s>Brahman</s>, because [the meditation] is restricted to the qualities learned at its inception. Nor is the sentence 'all this indeed [is <s>Brahman</s>],' even though it pertains to <s>Brahman</s>, more than a laudatory statement (<s>arthavāda</s>) serving as a reason for tranquility, being directed toward the injunction of tranquility — like 'one offers with the winnowing basket' and 'for by that, food is produced.' Nor is it proper [to say] that <s>Brahman</s> is accepted as required even from another passage, because the object has already been assigned to the individual self through the well-established attributes of being <s>manomaya</s> etc., and [<s>Brahman</s>] is therefore not required. And being the agent of all actions etc. will pertain to the individual self in due course. And thus the attribute of being subtler than the subtle (<s>aṇīyastva</s>) is also explained. But for the <s>Paramātman</s> (supreme Self), who is immeasurable, that would be inapplicable. And the attribute of being greater than the great (<s>jyāyastva</s>) should be interpreted in conformity with the attribute of subtlety that is first apprehended. And [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] the commentator has given [such] an interpretation. Thus the designation as object and agent, and the use of the locative case, should be seen even in the case of the individual self — which is non-different [from <s>Brahman</s>] — through a figurative attribution of difference, like [the expression] '<s>Rāhu</s>'s head.' And 'this is <s>Brahman</s>' pertains to the individual self, for the individual self too is <s>Brahman</s> because it causes the expansion (<s>bṛṃhaṇa</s>) of the body etc.

children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Brahman</s>, which is required [by the context], must be accepted even from another passage;
And thus the literal truth of [attributes] beginning with having true will (<s>satyasaṃkalpa</s>) etc. [is established].

body.text:
' bhavedetadevaṃ yadi prāṇaśarīra ca sarvanāmārthaṃ saṃprāpya tadabhidhānaṃ paryavasyet /
tatra manomayapadaṃ paryamasitābhidhānaṃ tadabhidhānaparyavasānāyālaṃ, tadeva tu manovikāro vā manaḥpracuraṃ vā kimarthamityadyāpi na vijñāyate /
tadyatraiṣa śabdaḥ samavetārtho bhavati sa samāsārthaḥ /
na caiṣa jīva eva samavetātho na brahmaṇīti, tasya 'aprāṇo hyamanāḥ' ityādibhistadvirahapratipādanāditi yuktam, tasyāpi sarvavikārakāraṇatayā, vikārāṇāṃ ca svakāraṇādabhedātteṣāṃ ca manomatayā brahmaṇastatkāraṇasya manomayatvopapatteḥ /
syādetat /
jīvasya sākṣānmanomayatvādayaḥ, brahmaṇastu taddvārā /
tatra prathamaṃ dvārasya buddhisthatvāttadevopāsyamastu, na punarjaghanyaṃ brahma /

children.translated_text: And the indicatory marks of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahmaliṅga</s>) would also be applicable to the <s>jīva</s>, because of the non-difference of the <s>jīva</s> from <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: tadetadatra saṃpradhāryam-kiṃ brahmaliṅgairjīvānāṃ tadabhinnānāmastu tadvattā, tathāca jīvasya manomayatvādibhiḥ prathamamavagamāttasyaivopāsyatvaṃ, uta na jīvasya brahmaliṅgavattā tadabhinnasyāpi /
children.translated_text: This is what must be deliberated here: Should the <s>jīva</s>s, being non-different from <s>Brahman</s>, possess the characteristics of <s>Brahman</s> through the indicatory marks of <s>Brahman</s> — and thus, since the <s>jīva</s> is first apprehended through [attributes like] being <s>manomaya</s> etc., should the <s>jīva</s> alone be the object of meditation? Or does the <s>jīva</s>, even though non-different, not possess the characteristics indicated by the marks of <s>Brahman</s>?

children.text: jīvaliṅgaistu brahma tadvata, tathāca brahmaliṅgānāṃ darśanāt, teṣāṃ ca jīve 'nupapatterbrahmaivopāsyamiti /
children.translated_text: Rather, <s>Brahman</s> possesses the characteristics indicated by the marks of the <s>jīva</s> — and thus, because marks of <s>Brahman</s> are seen [in the passage], and because those [marks] are inapplicable to the <s>jīva</s>, it is <s>Brahman</s> alone that is the object of meditation.

children.text: vayaṃ tu paśyāmaḥ-'samāropyasya rūpeṇa viṣayo rūpavānbhavetṣa viṣayasya tu rūpeṇa samāropyaṃ na rūpavat //
children.translated_text: But we hold: 'The substrate (<s>viṣaya</s>) becomes endowed with the form of what is superimposed upon it, but the superimposed thing does not become endowed with the form of the substrate.'

body.translated_text: This would be so if '<s>prāṇaśarīra</s>' (having <s>prāṇa</s> as body), having acquired the meaning of a universal pronoun (<s>sarvanāma</s>), were to culminate in that designation. There, the word <s>manomaya</s> (mind-made) has completed its designation, and is sufficient for the culmination of that designation; but whether it means 'a modification of mind' or 'predominantly mental' is not yet known. Where this word has a unified meaning — that is the meaning of the compound. And it is not the case that this word has a unified meaning only in the <s>jīva</s> and not in <s>Brahman</s>, for the <s>Upaniṣad</s>s teach the absence of [mind] in it through passages like 'without breath, without mind' (<s>aprāṇo hyamanāḥ</s>) — this objection is valid. Nevertheless, since [<s>Brahman</s>] is the cause of all modifications, and since modifications are non-different from their cause, and since those [modifications] are of the nature of mind, <s>Brahman</s> as their cause can be called <s>manomaya</s>. One might object: The <s>jīva</s> possesses attributes like being <s>manomaya</s> directly, while <s>Brahman</s> [possesses them] only indirectly through the <s>jīva</s>. In that case, since what is proximate — the intermediary [i.e., the <s>jīva</s>] — is first grasped by the intellect, let that alone be the object of meditation, and not the remoter <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text:
' samāropitasya hi rūpeṇa bhujaṅgasya bhīṣaṇatvādinā rajjū rūpavatī, natu rajjūrūpeṇābhigamyatvādinā bhujaṅgo rūpavān /
tadā bhujaṅgasyaivābhāvātkiṃ rūpavat /

children.text: bhujaṅgadaśāyāṃ tu na nāsti vāstavī rajjuḥ /
children.translated_text: But in the state [of perceiving] the snake, the real rope does not cease to exist.

children.text: tadiha samāropitajīvarūpeṇa vastusadbrahma rūpavadyujyate, natu brahmarūpairnityatvādibhirjīvastadvānbhavitumarhati, tasya tadānīmasaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: Accordingly, here <s>Brahman</s>, which truly exists, is rightly endowed with the form of the superimposed <s>jīva</s>, but the <s>jīva</s> cannot be endowed with the attributes of <s>Brahman</s> such as eternality etc., because the <s>jīva</s> does not [truly] exist at that time.

children.text: tasmādbrahmaliṅgadarśanājjīve ca tadasaṃbhavādbrahmaivopāsyaṃ na jīva iti siddham /
children.translated_text: Therefore, because marks of <s>Brahman</s> are observed [in the passage] and because those [marks] are impossible in the <s>jīva</s>, it is established that <s>Brahman</s> alone is the object of meditation, not the <s>jīva</s>.

children.text: etadupalakṣaṇaṇāya ca 'sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ brahma' iti vākyamupanyastamiti //1 //
children.translated_text: And to indicate this very point, the sentence 'all this is indeed <s>Brahman</s>' has been cited. [End of <s>Sūtra</s>] 1.

body.translated_text: For the rope becomes endowed with the characteristics of the superimposed snake, such as being frightful, but the snake does not become endowed with the characteristics of the rope, such as being approachable. At that time, since the snake itself does not exist, what would be endowed with form?

body.text:
#yadyapyapauruṣeya iti# /
śāstrayonitve 'pīśvarasya pūrvapūrvasṛṣṭiracitasaṃdarbhāpekṣaracanatvenāsvātantryādapauruṣeyatvābhidhānaṃ, tathā cāsvātantryeṇa vivakṣā nāstītyuktam /
parigrahaparityāgau copādanānupādāne ukte, na tūpādayeyatvameva /
anyathoddeśyatayānapapādeyasya grahāderavivakṣitatvena camasādāvapi saṃmārgaprasaṅgāt /
tasmādanupādeyatve 'pi graha uddeśyatayā parigṛhīto vivakṣitaḥ /

children.translated_text: But the oneness contained therein is excluded as a delimiting factor and is unintended.
And desire and non-desire [i.e., intention and non-intention are determined] according to the [textual] division.
This has been stated: 'These two are understood from the purport and non-purport of the Vedic sentence.'

children.text: yatparaṃ vedavākyaṃ tattenopāttaṃ vivakṣitam, atatpareṇa cānupāttamavivakṣitamityarthaḥ //2 //
children.translated_text: That which is the purport of the Vedic sentence — what is adopted by that [purport] is intended; and what is not adopted by a sentence whose purport is different is unintended — this is the meaning. [End of <s>Sūtra</s>] 2.

body.translated_text: 'Although [the <s>Veda</s> is] unauthored' — Even though [<s>Brahman</s>] has scripture as its source (<s>śāstrayonitva</s>), the designation 'unauthored' (<s>apauruṣeya</s>) [for the <s>Veda</s>] is because of [its] lack of independence, since [the <s>Veda</s>] is composed in dependence upon the arrangement fashioned in each preceding creation. And thus it has been said that there is no intended meaning [that is independently determined by <s>Īśvara</s>] through lack of independence. And acceptance and rejection [of meanings] are [defined as] adoption and non-adoption [by the Vedic text], not that [something] should never be adopted. Otherwise, since the <s>graha</s> (sacrificial vessel), being presented as the topic, would be non-demonstrable, and hence unintended, there would be the undesirable consequence of cleaning [the vessel] even for the <s>camasa</s> (cup) etc. Therefore, the <s>graha</s>, even though it is not [independently] to be adopted, is accepted as intended because it is presented as the topic.

children.text: yathā satyasaṃkalpatvādayo brahmaṇyupapadyante, evaṃ śārīre 'pyupapatsyante, śārīrasya brahmaṇo 'bhedāt /
children.translated_text: Just as [attributes like] having true will (<s>satyasaṃkalpatva</s>) etc. are applicable to <s>Brahman</s>, so too they would be applicable to the embodied self (<s>śārīra</s>), because of the non-difference of the embodied self from <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: śārīraguṇā iva manomayatvādayo brahmaṇītyata āha sūtrakāraḥ- #anupapattestu na śārīraḥ# //3 //
children.translated_text: To [the objection] that, just as the qualities of the embodied self [are applicable to <s>Brahman</s>], so too [attributes like] being <s>manomaya</s> etc. [should be applicable] to <s>Brahman</s> — the <s>Sūtrakāra</s> (author of the <s>Sūtra</s>s) says: 'But [it is] not the embodied self, because of the impossibility [of certain attributes applying to it].' [<s>Sūtra</s>] 3.

body.translated_text: [<s>Sūtra</s>] 4.
[<s>Sūtra</s>] 5.

body.text:
yattadavocāma samāropyadharmāḥ samāropaviṣaye saṃbhavanti, natu viṣayadharmāḥ samāropya iti /
tasyeta utthānam /
atrāha codakaḥ- #kaḥ punarayaṃ śārīro nāmeti# /
na tāvadbhedapratiṣedhādbhedavpadeśācca bhedābhedāvekatra tāttvikau bhavitumarhato virodhādityuktam /
tasmādekamiha tāttvikamatāttvikaṃ cetarat, tatra paurvāparyeṇādvaitapratipādanaparatvādvedāntānāṃ dvaitagrāhiṇaśca mānāntarasyābhāvāttadbādhanācca tenādvaitameva paramārthaḥ /
tathā ca 'anupapattestu' ityādyasaṃgatārthamityarthaḥ /
pariharati- #satyamevaitat /
para evātmā dehendriyamanobuddhyupādhibhiravicchidyamāno bālaiḥ śārīra ityupacaryate# /
anādyavidyāvacchedalabdhajīvabhāvaḥ para evātmā svato bhedenāvabhāsate /
tādṛśāṃ ca jīvānāmavidyā, natu nirūpādhino brahmaṇaḥ /
na cāvidyāyāṃ satyāṃ jīvātmavibhāgaḥ, sati ca jīvātmavibhāge tadāśrayāvidyetyanyonyāśrayamiti sāṃpratam /
anāditvena jīvāvidyayorbījāṅkuravadanavakḷpterayogāt /

children.text: naca sarvajñasya sarvaśakteśca svataḥ kuto 'kasmātsaṃsāritā, yo hi paratantraḥ so 'nyena bandhanāgāre praveśyeta, natu svatantra iti vācyam /
children.translated_text: And one should not say: How can the omniscient and omnipotent [<s>Brahman</s>] become a <s>saṃsārin</s> (bound being) by itself, of its own accord, without cause? For one who is dependent can be thrust into a prison by another, but not one who is independent.

children.text: nahi tadbhāgasya jīvasya saṃpratitanī bandhanāgārapraveśitā, yenānuyujyeta, kintvi.manādiḥ pūrvapūrvakarmāvidyāsaṃskāranibandhanā nānuyogamarhati /
children.translated_text: For the <s>jīva</s>, which is a part of That [<s>Brahman</s>], does not have a presently [traceable] entry into the prison, such that one could raise the objection. Rather, [its bondage] is beginningless, grounded in the impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>s) of previous <s>karma</s> and <s>avidyā</s>, one after another, and thus does not warrant the objection [of origination].

children.text: na caitāvatā īśvarasyānīśatā na hyupakaraṇādyapekṣitā kartuḥ svātantryaṃ vihanti /
children.translated_text: Nor does this [fact] make <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) non-sovereign, for the dependence on instruments and other [auxiliaries] does not impede the independence of the agent.
Therefore, whatever [objection is raised], this too [is answered]. [End of <s>Sūtra</s>] 6.

body.translated_text: What we stated — that the attributes of what is superimposed are possible in the substrate of superimposition, but the attributes of the substrate [are not possible] in what is superimposed — this is the basis for that [argument]. Here the objector says: 'Who then is this embodied self?' It has been said that difference and non-difference cannot both be real in one [entity] because of contradiction, since [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] negates difference yet also uses expressions of difference. Therefore, one of the two is real here and the other unreal. Among these, since the <s>Vedānta</s>s are oriented toward establishing non-duality, and since there is no other means of valid knowledge that grasps duality, and since [duality] is sublated by that [non-dual knowledge], non-duality alone is the ultimate truth. And thus [the opponent asks:] the [sūtra] 'but because of the impossibility' etc. would have an incoherent meaning. [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] resolves this: 'This is indeed true. The supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) alone, undivided by the limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>s) of body, senses, mind, and intellect, is figuratively called the embodied self (<s>śārīra</s>) by the ignorant.' The supreme Self alone, having obtained the status of a <s>jīva</s> through the delimitation of beginningless <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), appears as different from its own nature. And <s>avidyā</s> belongs to such <s>jīva</s>s, not to <s>Brahman</s> free from limiting adjuncts. And [one should not say:] 'If <s>avidyā</s> is real, then there is a distinction between <s>jīva</s> and <s>ātman</s>; and if there is a distinction between <s>jīva</s> and <s>ātman</s>, then <s>avidyā</s> rests on that [distinction]' — this is mutual dependence — for that is appropriate, since the beginninglessness of both <s>jīva</s> and <s>avidyā</s>, like the seed and sprout, makes this charge of impossible origination inapplicable.
[<s>Sūtra</s>] 7.

children.translated_text: Instead of saying <s>viśeṣāt</s> ('because of distinction'), the expression <s>vaiśeṣya</s> ('distinctive excellence') is used in order to convey absolute distinction.
For the attachment to pleasure etc. that is imagined through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is appropriate only for one whose nature is <s>avidyā</s>.

But not for the <s>Paramātman</s> (supreme Self), whose nature is pure, enlightened, and liberated, and who has wiped away all <s>avidyā</s> and its impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>s) — this is the meaning.
The rest [of the <s>bhāṣya</s>] has a self-evident meaning. [End of <s>Sūtra</s>] 8.

body.text:
#attā carācaragrahaṇāt /
kaṭhavallīṣu paṭhyate-yasya brahma ca kṣatraṃ cobhe bhavata odamaḥ# /
body.translated_text: '[<s>Brahman</s> is] the eater, because of the mention of [both] the moving and the non-moving. In the <s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> it is read: "For whom both the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and the <s>Kṣatriya</s> classes become food"' —

body.text:
#mṛtyuryasyopasetacanaṃ ka itthā veda yatra sa iti# /
atra cādanīyaudānopasecanasīcitaḥ kaścidattā pratīyate /
attṛtvaṃ ca bhoktṛtā vā saharntṛtā vā syāt /
naca prastutasya paramātmano bhoktṛtāsti, 'anaśrannanyo 'abhicākaśīti' iti śrutyā bhoktṛtāpratiṣedhāt /
jīvātmanaśca bhoktṛtāvidhānāt-'tayoranyaḥ pippalaṃ svādvatti' iti /
tadyadi bhoktṛtvamattṛtvaṃ tato muktasaṃśayaṃ jīvātmaiva pratipattavyaḥ /
brahmakṣatrādi cāsya kāryakāraṇasaṃghāto bhogāyatanatayā vā sākṣādvā /
saṃbhavati bhogyam /
atha tu saṃhartṛtā bhoktṛtā, tatastrayāṇāmagnijīvaparamātmanāṃ praśnopanyāsopalabdheḥ saṃhartṛtvasyāviśeṣādbhavati saṃśayaḥ-kimattā agnirāho jīva utāho paramātmeti /
tatraudanasya bhogyatvena loke prasiddherbhoktṛtvameva prathamaṃ buddhau viparivartate, caramaṃ tu saṃhartṛtvamiti bhoktaivāttā /
tathā ca jīva eva /
'na jāyate mriyate' iti ca tasyaiva stutiḥ /
yadi tu saṃhārakāle 'pi saṃskāramātreṇa tasyāvasthānāt /
durjñānatvaṃ ca tasya sūkṣmatvāt /
tasmājjīva evāttehopāsyata iti prāptam /
yadi tu saṃhartṛtvamattṛtvaṃ tathāpyagnirattā, 'agnirannādaḥ' iti śrutiprasiddhibhyām /
evaṃ prāptebhidhīyate-attātra paramātmā, kutaḥ, carācaragrahaṇāt /
'ubhe yasyodanaḥ' iti 'mṛtyuryasyopasecanam' iti ca śrūyate /
tatra yadi jīvasya bhogāyatanatayā tatsādhanatayā ca kāryakāraṇasaṃghātaḥ sthitaḥ, na tarhyedanaḥ /
nahyodano bhogāyatanaṃ, nāpi bhogasādhanaṃ, api tu bhogyaḥ /
naca bhogāyatanasya bhogasādhanasya vā bhogyatvaṃ mukhyam /
na cātra mṛtyurupasecanatayā kalpyate /
naca jīvasya kāryakāraṇasaṃghāto brahmakṣatrādirūpo bhakṣyaḥ, kasyacitkrūrasattvasya vyāghrādeḥ kaścidbhavet na tu sarvathā sarvajīvasya /
tena brahmakṣatraviṣayamapi sarvajīvasyāttṛtvaṃ na vyāpnoti, kimaṅga punarmṛtyūpasecanavyāptaṃ carācaram /
na caudanapadātprathamāvagatabhogyatvānurodhena yathāsaṃbhavamattṛtvaṃ yojyata iti yuktam /
nahyodanapadaṃ śrutyā bhogyatvamāha, kintu lakṣaṇayā /
naca lākṣaṇikabhogyatvānurodhena 'mṛtyuryasyopasecanam' iti, 'brahma ca kṣatraṃ ca' iti ca śrutī saṃkocamarhataḥ /
naca brahmakṣatre evātra vivakṣite, mṛtyūpasecanena prāṇabhṛnmātropasthāpanāt /
prāṇiṣu pradhānatvena ca brahmakṣatropanyāsasyopapatteḥ, anarthatvācca /
tathāca carācarasaṃhartṛtvaṃ paramātmana eva /
nāgneḥ /
nāpi jīvasya /

children.text: tathāca 'na jāyate mriyate vā vipaścit' iti prakṛtasya na hānaṃ bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: And thus, 'He is not born and does not die — the wise one' — this will not be inapplicable to the one under discussion [the supreme Self].

children.text: 'ka itthā veda yatra saḥ' iti ca durjñānatopapatsyate /
children.translated_text: And 'Who knows where He is?' — [this] will be justified by His being difficult to know.
But for the individual self, who is well-known to everyone, there is no being-difficult-to-know.
Therefore, it is established that the eater is the supreme Self alone. // 9 //

body.translated_text:
'Death is whose condiment — who knows where He is?' //
Here, some eater is understood — being sprinkled with the condiment of food and rice.
And the status of being an eater is either enjoyership (<s>bhoktṛtā</s>) or the capacity to destroy (<s>saṃhartṛtā</s>).
Now, the supreme Self (<s>paramātman</s>) under discussion does not have enjoyership, since the <s>Śruti</s> negates enjoyership: 'The other, not eating, merely looks on.'
And the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>) has enjoyership enjoined: 'The other eats the sweet fruit.'
Therefore, if enjoyership is the meaning of 'eater,' then the individual self alone, free from doubt, must be understood.
And the aggregate of effects and instruments in the form of <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s, <s>kṣatriya</s>s, and the like — either as the locus of enjoyment or directly — can be the object of enjoyment for him.
But if 'eater' means the capacity to destroy, then — since all three: fire, the individual self, and the supreme Self are found presented in the question — because the capacity to destroy is common [to all three], a doubt arises: Is the eater fire, or the individual self, or the supreme Self?
Therein, since rice (<s>odana</s>) is well-known in the world as an object of enjoyment, enjoyership first revolves in the mind, while the capacity to destroy [comes] last — thus the eater is the enjoyer.
And therefore it is the individual self alone.
And 'He is not born and does not die' is a eulogy of that very [individual self].
If, however, [it is argued that the individual self persists] even at the time of dissolution, by virtue of its impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>s) alone.
And its being difficult to know is due to its subtlety.
Therefore, it is the individual self alone that should be worshipped here as the eater — this is the prima facie conclusion.
But if the capacity to destroy is the meaning of 'eater,' even then fire is the eater, because of the well-established <s>Śruti</s>: 'Fire is the eater of food.'
When the matter stands thus, the conclusion is stated: The eater here is the supreme Self. Why? Because of the reference to both moving and non-moving [beings].
'Both of which are His food' and 'Death is whose condiment' — thus it is heard.
Therein, if the aggregate of effects and instruments exists for the individual self as the locus of enjoyment or as the means thereof, then it is not food (<s>odana</s>).
For food is neither the locus of enjoyment nor the means of enjoyment; rather, it is what is enjoyed.
Nor is the primary meaning of 'what is to be enjoyed' applicable to the locus or means of enjoyment.
Nor is death construed here as a condiment.
Nor is the aggregate of effects and instruments in the form of <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s and <s>kṣatriya</s>s something to be eaten by the individual self — it might be so for some fierce creature like a tiger, but not universally for every individual self.
Therefore, the status of being an eater with respect to <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s and <s>kṣatriya</s>s does not extend to every individual self — much less does it extend to [all] moving and non-moving [beings] along with death as condiment.
Nor is it reasonable [to say] that the eater-status should be construed [as enjoyership] only as far as possible, in accordance with the status of being an object of enjoyment first understood from the word 'food.'
For the word 'food' does not convey the status of being an object of enjoyment through direct denotation (<s>śruti</s>), but through secondary indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>).
Nor do the <s>Śruti</s>s 'Death is whose condiment' and '<s>brāhmaṇa</s>s and <s>kṣatriya</s>s' deserve to be restricted in scope by [the status of being an object of enjoyment] which is merely a secondary indication.
Nor are <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s and <s>kṣatriya</s>s alone intended here, since by the mention of 'death as condiment,' all living beings are evoked.
And since the mention of <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s and <s>kṣatriya</s>s is justified as being the foremost among living beings, and because [interpreting it as mere enjoyership] would be purposeless.
Thus, the capacity to destroy moving and non-moving [beings] belongs to the supreme Self alone.
Not to fire.
Nor to the individual self.

body.text:
guhāṃ praviṣṭāvātmānau hi taddarśanāt /
saṃśayamāha- #tatreti# /
pūrvapakṣe prayojanamāha- #yadi buddhijīvāviti# /
siddhānte prayojanamāha- #atha jīvaparamātmanāviti# /
autsargikasya mukhyatābalātpūrvasiddhāntapakṣāsaṃbhavena pakṣāntaraṃ kalpayiṣyata iti manvānaḥ saṃśayamākṣipati- #atrāhākṣepteti# /
ṛtaṃ satyam /
avaśyaṃbhāvīti yāvat /
samādhatte- #atrocyatada iti# /
adhyātmādhikārādanyau tāvatpātārāvaśakyau kalpayitum /
tadiha buddheracaitanyena paramātmanaśca pibacchabdo lakṣayansvārtamajahannicarecarayuktapibadapibatparo bhavatītyarthaḥ /
astu vā mukhya eva, tathāpi na doṣa ityāha- #yadveti# /
svātantryalakṣaṇaṃ hi kartṛtvaṃ tacca pāturiva pāyayiturapyastīti so 'pi kartā /
ata eva cāhuḥ-'yaḥ kārayati sa karotyeva' iti /
evaṃ karaṇasyāpi svātantryavivakṣayā kathañcitkartṛtvaṃ, yathā kāṣṭhāni pacantīti /

children.translated_text: Therefore, even in the primary sense, there is no contradiction.
Having thus resolved the doubt, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] presents the prima facie view: 'The intellect and the field-knower (<s>kṣetrajña</s>).'
'The fixed-substrate-ness of the intellect is not possible;
It is not reasonable to attribute [it] with difficulty to the all-pervading supreme Self. //

body.translated_text:
The two selves that have entered the cave — because of seeing [this in scripture].
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the doubt: 'Therein...'
He states the purpose of the prima facie view: 'If [they are] the intellect and the individual self...'
He states the purpose of the established conclusion: 'But if [they are] the individual self and the supreme Self...'
Thinking that, by the force of the prima facie position that the primary [meaning] is the general rule, since the alternative of the earlier established position is not possible, another alternative will be postulated — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] challenges the doubt: 'Here, the objector [says]...'
'<s>Ṛta</s>' means truth.
That is, what necessarily exists.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] resolves: 'To this we say...'
Since the context pertains to the innermost Self (<s>adhyātma</s>), the two drinkers cannot be postulated as other [than the self and <s>Brahman</s>].
Thus here, the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) — being insentient — and the word 'drinks' (<s>pibat</s>) — denoting the supreme Self through secondary indication by abandoning its own meaning, and without abandoning [the meaning, by being used] in connection with both moving and non-moving [beings as object] — becomes applicable to 'drinking' and 'not-drinking.' This is the meaning.
Or, let it be in the primary sense even so; even then there is no defect — thus he says: 'If...' (<s>yadvā</s>).
For independence is the hallmark of agency; and that [independence] belongs to the causer just as to the doer — hence the causer too is an agent.
As they say: 'One who causes to do, does indeed.'
Similarly, even the instrument, when independence is intended, has a certain kind of agency — as [in the expression] 'the logs cook.'

body.text:
' naca pibantāvitivatpraviṣṭapadamapi lākṣaṇikaṃ yuktaṃ, sati mukhyārthatve lākṣaṇikārthatvāyogāt, buddhijīvayośca guhāpraveśopapatteḥ /
apica 'sukṛtasya loke' iti sukṛtalokavyavasthānena karmagocarānatikrama uktaḥ /
buddhijīvau ca karmagocaraṃmanatikrāntau /
jīvo hi bhoktṛtayā buddhiśca bhogasādhanatayā dharmasya gocare sthitau, na tu brahma, tasya tadāyattatvāt /

children.translated_text: Moreover, 'shadow and sunlight' (<s>chāyātapau</s>) — darkness and light — are stated.

children.text: tatrāpi prete vicikitsāpanuttaye buddherbhedena paralokī jīvo darśanīya iti buddhirucyate /
children.translated_text: Therein too, for the purpose of removing doubt about the afterlife, the individual self should be shown as different from the intellect; hence the intellect is mentioned.
When the matter stands thus, the conclusion is stated: 'The individual self, ascertained by the drinking of truth (<s>ṛtapāna</s>), is his second;

children.text: brahmaṇaiva sarūpeṇa na tu buddhyā virūpayā //1 //
children.translated_text: With <s>Brahman</s> itself, of the same form — not with the intellect, which is of a different form. // 1 //

body.translated_text:
Nor is the word 'entered' (<s>praviṣṭa</s>) to be taken as secondary in the way [the word] 'drinking' [was], since when the primary meaning is possible, the secondary meaning is not justified, and since the intellect and the individual self can indeed enter the cave.
Moreover, 'In the world of merit' (<s>sukṛtasya loke</s>) — by the determination of being situated in the world of merit, the non-transgression of the domain of <s>karma</s> is stated.
And both the intellect and the individual self are within the domain of <s>karma</s>.
