For the individual self, as an enjoyer, and the intellect, as the means of enjoyment, are within the domain of <s>dharma</s>; but not <s>Brahman</s>, since it depends on them [for its apparent involvement].

children.translated_text: When the [Self's] being accompanied by a second — <s>Brahman</s> — has first been understood,
The cave-dwelling-ness, [understood] subsequently, should be explained without contradiction. // 2 //

body.text:
gauḥ sadvitīyetyukte sajātīyenaiva gavāntareṇāvagamyate, na tu vijātīyenāśvādinā /
tadiha cetano jīvaḥ sarūpeṇa cetanāntareṇaiva brahmaṇā sadvitīyaḥ pratīyate, na tvacetanayā virūpayā buddhyā /
tadevam 'ṛtaṃ pibantau' ityatra prathamamavagate brahmaṇi tadanurodhena caramaṃ guhāśrayatvaṃ śālagrāme hariritavadvyākhyeyam /
bahulaṃ hi guhāśrayatvaṃ brahmaṇaḥ śrutaya āhuḥ /

children.translated_text: This is what is stated: 'Because of the seeing of that...'
Because of the seeing [in the <s>Śruti</s>s] of that <s>Brahman</s>'s cave-dwelling-ness.

children.text: evañca prathamāvagatabrahmānurodhena sukṛtalokavartitvamapi tasya lakṣaṇayā chatrinyāyena gamayitavyam /
children.translated_text: And thus, in accordance with the <s>Brahman</s> first understood, even the being-in-the-world-of-merit should be understood through secondary indication, by the 'umbrella principle' (<s>chatrinyāya</s>).

children.text: chāyātapatvamapi jīvasyāvidyāśrayatayā brahmaṇaśca śuddhaprakaśasvabhāvasya tadanāśrayatayā mantavyam //11 //
children.translated_text: And the shadow-and-sunlight [quality] too should be understood — [applied to] the individual self through its having <s>avidyā</s> as its basis, and to <s>Brahman</s> through its nature of pure light and its non-basis in that [<s>avidyā</s>]. // 11 //

body.translated_text:
When it is said that a cow has a companion, [it is understood] to be of the same kind — another cow — not of a different kind, such as a horse and the like.
Thus here, the conscious individual self (<s>jīva</s>) is understood as accompanied by another conscious [entity] of the same form — namely <s>Brahman</s> — not by the insentient intellect, which is of a different form.
Thus, when 'drinking truth' (<s>ṛtaṃ pibantau</s>) has first led to the understanding of <s>Brahman</s>, in accordance with that, the subsequent cave-dwelling-ness should be explained — as [the saying] '<s>Hari</s> [resides] in <s>Śālagrāma</s>.'
For the <s>Śruti</s>s abundantly declare <s>Brahman</s>'s cave-dwelling-ness.

body.text:
imameva nyāyaṃ 'dvā suparṇā' ityatrāpyudāharaṇe kṛtvācintayā yojayati- #eṣa eva nyāya iti# /
atrāpi kiṃ buddhijīvau uta jīvaparamātmānāviti saṃśaṭya karaṇarūpāyā api buddheredhāṃsi pacantītivatkartṛtvopacārābuddhijīvāviha pūrvapakṣayitvā siddhāntayitavyam /
siddhāntaśca bhāṣyakṛtā sphoritaḥ /
taddarśanāditi ca 'samāne vṛkṣe puruṣo nimagnaḥ' ityatra mantre /
na khalu mukhye kartṛtve saṃbhavati karaṇe kartṛtvopacāro yukta iti kṛtvācintāmudghāṭayati- #apara āha# /
sattvaṃ buddhiḥ /
śaṅkate- #sattvaśabda iti# /
siddhāntārthaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ vyācaṣṭa ityarthaḥ /
nirākaroti- #tanneti /
yena svapnaṃ paśyatīti# /
yeneti karaṇamupadiśati /
tataśca bhinnaṃ kratāraṃ kṣetrajñam /
#yo 'yaṃ śārīra upadraṣṭeti# /
astu tarhyasyādhikaraṇasya pūrvapakṣe eva brāhmaṇārthaḥ, vacanāvirodhe nyāyasyābhāsatvādityata āha- #nāpyasyādhikaraṇasya pūrvapakṣaṃ bhajata iti# /
evaṃ hi pūrvapakṣamasya bhajeta, yadi hi kṣetratre saṃsāriṇi paryavasyeta /
tasya tu brahmarūpatāyāṃ paryavasyanna pūrvapakṣamapi svīkarotītyarthaḥ /
apica /
#tāvetau#
body.translated_text:
Having applied this same reasoning to [the passage] 'Two birds' (<s>dvā suparṇā</s>) as well, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] connects it with the [principle of] deliberative reasoning (<s>kṛtvācintā</s>): 'This same reasoning...'
Here too, having raised the doubt whether [the two are] the intellect and the individual self, or the individual self and the supreme Self — and having raised as the prima facie view that the intellect and the individual self [are intended], because even for the intellect, which is an instrument, there is a figurative attribution of agency, as in 'the logs cook' — the established conclusion should be stated.
And the established conclusion has been expressed by the commentator (<s>Bhāṣyakṛt</s>).
And 'because of seeing' — in the mantra 'On the same tree, the person is immersed' (<s>samāne vṛkṣe puruṣo nimagnaḥ</s>).
Since figurative attribution of agency upon an instrument is not reasonable when the primary agency [of the conscious agent] is possible — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises the deliberative reasoning: 'Another says...'
'<s>Sattva</s>' means the intellect.
[The opponent] raises a doubt: 'The word <s>sattva</s>...' (<s>sattvaśabda</s>).
The meaning is: [the opponent] explains the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> passage as serving the purpose of the established conclusion.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes: 'That is not so. [The passage] "By which one sees dreams"...'
'By which' (<s>yena</s>) teaches the instrument.
And from that, the field-knower (<s>kṣetrajña</s>) — distinct from it — is the agent.
'He who is this embodied one, the witness' (<s>yo 'yaṃ śārīra upadraṣṭā</s>).
Then let the meaning of this <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> passage pertain to the prima facie view of this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (section) alone — since in the absence of conflict with scripture, the [seemingly valid] reasoning is [actually] a semblance — to this he says: 'Nor does [the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>] belong to the prima facie view of this <s>adhikaraṇa</s>...'
For it would belong to the prima facie view in this way: if it culminated in the field-knower as a transmigrating being (<s>saṃsārin</s>).
But since it culminates in [the field-knower's] identity with <s>Brahman</s>, it does not even accept the prima facie view — this is the meaning.
Moreover —
'Those two —

body.text:
#sattvakṣetrajñau na ha vā evaṃvidi raja ādhvaṃsata iti# /
rajo 'vidyā nādhvaṃsanaṃ saṃśleṣamevaṃvidi karotīti /
etāvataiva vidyopasaṃhārājjīvasya brahmātmatāparatāsya lakṣyata ityāha- #tāvatā ceti# /
cedayati- #kathaṃ punariti# /
nirākaroti- #ucyate-neyaṃ śrutiriti# /
anaśnan jīvo brahmābhicākaśītītyukte śaṅkate, yadi jīvo brahmātmanā nāśnāti, kathaṃ tarhyanminbhoktṛtvāvagamaḥ, caitanyasamānādhikaraṇaṃ hi bhoktṛtvamavabhāsata iti /

children.translated_text: To refute this, the <s>Śruti</s> says: 'The other eats the sweet fruit.'

children.text: etaduktaṃ bhavati-nedaṃ bhoktṛtvaṃ jīvasya tattvataḥ, apitu buddhisattvaṃ mukhādirupapariṇataṃ citicchāyāpattyopapannacaitanyamiva bhuṅkte natu tattvato jīvaḥ paramātmā bhuṅkte /
children.translated_text: What is stated amounts to this: This enjoyership does not belong to the individual self in reality; rather, the intellect (<s>buddhi-sattva</s>), having transformed into the form of a mouth and the like, endowed with consciousness as if by the reflection of consciousness (<s>citi-chāyā</s>) — eats as it were; but the individual self does not truly eat, nor does the supreme Self eat.
And this has already been explained in the commentary on superimposition (<s>adhyāsa-bhāṣya</s>).
By this, the deliberative reasoning (<s>kṛtvācintā</s>) has been disclosed. // 12 //

body.translated_text:
<s>sattva</s> (intellect) and <s>kṣetrajña</s> (field-knower) — indeed, for one who knows thus, <s>rajas</s> (impurity, i.e., <s>avidyā</s>) does not smear.' //
'<s>Rajas</s>' is <s>avidyā</s>; [saying] 'does not smear' means: one who knows thus does not produce attachment [to <s>avidyā</s>].
With just this much — from the concluding reference to <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) — the culmination of the individual self's identity with <s>Brahman</s> [in this passage] is indicated — thus he says: 'With just that much...'
[The opponent] objects: 'But how then...'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes: 'It is said: This <s>Śruti</s> is not...'
When it is said that the individual self, as identical with <s>Brahman</s>, does not eat — [the objector] asks: If the individual self does not eat as identical with <s>Brahman</s>, then whence the apprehension of its enjoyership? For enjoyership appears as co-referential with consciousness.

body.text:
#antara upapatteḥ# /
nanu 'antastaddharmopadeśāt' ityanenaivaitadgatārtham /
santi khalvatrāpyamṛtatvābhayatvādayo brahmadharmāḥ pratibimbajīvadevatāsvasaṃbavinaḥ /

children.translated_text: Therefore, from the teaching of properties of <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Brahman</s> alone is intended here.
And because the word '<s>Brahman</s>' is directly used.
It is said: 'This [particle] "<s>eṣa</s>" (this) and "<s>dṛśyate</s>" (is seen) — this is used in the sense of direct perception;

children.text: parokṣaṃ brahma na tathā pratibimbe tu yujyate //1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s>, being imperceptible [to the senses], is not [used] thus; but for the reflection [in the eye], it is appropriate. // 1 //

body.translated_text:
'The inner [Self], because of reasoning' (<s>antara upapatteḥ</s>).
One might [object]: Is not this already covered by [the <s>sūtra</s>] 'The inner [Self], because of the teaching of its properties' (<s>antas taddharmopadeśāt</s>)?
For here too there are properties of <s>Brahman</s> — such as immortality, fearlessness, and the like — which are not possible for the reflection-self, the individual self, or the deities.

children.translated_text: By virtue of the opening [context], the description of the others first
Was made by the very reasoning by which — that indeed is to be applied here. // 2 //

body.text:
'ṛtaṃ pibantau ityatra hi jīvaparamātmānau prathamamanagatāviti tadanurodhena guhāpraveśādayaḥ paścādavagatā vyākhyātāḥ, tadvidihāpi 'ya eṣo 'kṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyate' iti pratyakṣābhidhānātprathamamavagate chāyāpuruṣe tadanurodhenāmṛtatvābhayatvādayaḥ stutyā kathañcidvyākhyeyāḥ /
tatra cāmṛtatvaṃ katipayakṣaṇāvasthānāt, abhayatvamacetanatvāt, puruṣatvaṃ puruṣākāratvāt, ātmatvaṃ kanīnikāyatanatvāt, brahmarūpatvamuktarūpāmṛtatvādiyogāt /
evaṃ vāmanītvādayo 'pyasya stutyaiva kathañcinnetavyāḥ /
kaṃ ca khaṃ cetyādi tu vākyamagnīnāṃ nācāryavākyaṃ niyantumarhi /
'ācāryastu te gatiṃ vaktā' iti ca gatyantarābhiprāyaṃ, na tūktapariśiṣṭābhiprāyam /
tasmācchāyāpuruṣa evātropāsya iti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ /
saṃbhavamātreṇa tu jīvadevate upanyaste, bādhakāntaropadarśanāya caiṣa dṛśyata ityasyātrābhāvāt /

children.translated_text: Because it has been refuted by [the <s>sūtra</s>] 'The inner [Self], because of the teaching of its properties.'
When the matter stands thus, the conclusion is stated: 'He who is this...'
'The two pronominal words — <s>eṣa</s> and <s>ya</s> — being applicable when [the referent's] form has not been fully specified,
Having reached the referent of that which is proximate, they [the demonstrative pronouns] would serve as designators.

body.translated_text:
For in 'Drinking truth' (<s>ṛtaṃ pibantau</s>), when the individual self and the supreme Self were first understood, in accordance with that, the subsequent qualities — cave-entering and the like — were explained. Similarly here too, when the reflection-person (<s>chāyāpuruṣa</s>) has first been understood from [the statement] 'This person who is seen in the eye' (<s>ya eṣo 'kṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyate</s>) — because of the directly perceptible reference — the subsequent qualities of immortality, fearlessness, and the like should be explained in some way through eulogistic [interpretation].
Therein, immortality is due to its persisting for a few moments; fearlessness is due to its being insentient; person-hood is due to its having a person-like form; self-hood is due to its being located in the pupil of the eye; and <s>Brahman</s>-nature is due to its possession of the stated [qualities of] immortality and the like.
Similarly, the qualities of being a <s>Vāmana</s> (dwarf) and the like should also somehow be explained through eulogy alone.
But the sentence '<s>kaṃ ca khaṃ ca</s>' (bliss and space) and the like is a statement about the fires [of meditation] and cannot be constrained by the teacher's statement [about the person in the eye].
And 'The teacher will tell you the way' (<s>ācāryastu te gatiṃ vaktā</s>) — this has the intent of a different destination, not [the intent of teaching] the remainder of what has been stated.
Therefore, it is the reflection-person alone that is to be meditated upon here — this is the prima facie view.
The individual self and the deity are presented merely as possibilities, in order to show that there is another [sublating] objection — since 'This [person] is seen' (<s>eṣa dṛśyate</s>) does not apply here.

body.text:
' saṃnihitāśca puruṣātmādiśabdāste ca na yāvatsvārthamabhidadhati tāvatsarvanāmabhyāṃ nārthatuṣo 'bhidhīyata iti kutastadarthasyāparokṣatā /
puruṣātmaśabdau ca sarvanāmanirapekṣau svarasato jīve vā paramātmani vā vartete iti /
naca tayoṣcakṣuṣi pratyakṣadarśanamiti nirapekṣapuruṣapadapratyāyitārthānurodhena ya eṣa iti dṛśṭata iti ca yathāsaṃbhavaṃ vyākhyeyam /
vyākhyātaṃ ca siddhavadupādānaṃ śāstrādyapekṣaṃvidvidviṣayaṃ prarocanārtham /
viduṣaḥ śāstrata upalabdireva dṛḍhatayā pratyakṣavaduparyate praśaṃsārthamityarthaḥ /
api ca tadeva caramaṃ prathamānuguṇatayā nīyate yannetuṃ śakyam, alpaṃ ca /
iha tvamṛtatvādayo bahavaśāśakyāśca netum /
nahi svasattākṣaṇāvasthānamātramamṛtatvaṃ bhavati /
tathā sati kiṃ nāma nāmṛtaṃ syāditi vyarthamamṛtapadam /
bhayābhaye api cetanadharmau nācetane saṃbhavataḥ /
evaṃ vāmanītvādayo 'pyanyatra brahmaṇo netumaśakyāḥ /
pratyakṣavyapadeśaścopapāditaḥ /
tadidamuktam-upapatteriti /
'etadamṛtamabhayametadbrahma' ityukte syādāśaṅkā /
nanu sarvagatasyeśvarasya kasmādviśiṣeṇa cakṣureva sthānamupadiśyata iti, tatpariharati, śrutiḥ-'tadyadyapyasminsārpirvodakaṃ vā siñcati vartmanī eva gacchati' iti /
vartmanī pakṣasthāne /
etaduktaṃ bhavati-nirlepasyeśvarasya nirlepaṃ cakṣureva sthānamanurūpamiti /
tadidamuktam- #tathā parameśvarānurūpamiti saṃyadvāmādiguṇopadeśaśca tasmin#brahmaṇi #kalpate#ghaṭate, samavetārthatvāt /
pratibimbādiṣu tvasaṃvetārthaḥ /
vāmanīyāni saṃbhajanīyāni śobhanīyāni puṇyaphalāni vāmāni /
saṃyanti saṃgacchamānāni vāmānyaneneti saṃyadvāmaḥ paramātmā /
tatkaraṇatvātpuṇyaphalotpattestena puṇyaphalāni saṃgacchante /

children.text: sa eva puṇyaphalāni vāmāni nayati lokamiti vāmanīḥ /
children.translated_text: He alone leads the auspicious fruits of merit (<s>vāmāni</s>) to the world — hence He is called <s>Vāmanī</s>.
This very one is <s>Bhāmanī</s>.
<s>Bhāmanī</s> is so called because He leads the effulgences (<s>bhānāni</s>) to the world.

children.text: taduktaṃ śrutyā-'tameva bhāntamanubhāti sarvaṃ tasya bhāsā sarvamidaṃ vibhāti' iti //13 //
children.translated_text: This has been stated by <s>Śruti</s>: 'Everything shines after Him who shines; by His radiance all this is illuminated.' //13//

body.translated_text:
The words <s>puruṣa</s> (person), <s>ātman</s> (self), and the like are proximate [in the passage], and as long as they do not convey their own meaning, the referent is not adequately expressed by the two pronouns alone — so how can the referent be said to be directly perceived (<s>aparokṣa</s>)?
The words <s>puruṣa</s> and <s>ātman</s>, independently of the pronouns, naturally refer either to the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>) or to the supreme self (<s>Paramātman</s>).
Nor is there direct visual perception of either of these in the eye; hence the expressions 'this one here' and 'is seen' should be interpreted as contextually appropriate, in accordance with the meaning conveyed by the independent word <s>puruṣa</s>.
The usage as if [<s>Brahman</s>] were already established has been explained as dependent on scripture and pertaining to one who has knowledge, serving the purpose of generating interest.
The meaning is that the knower's apprehension through scripture itself, being firm, is praised as if it were direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>).
Moreover, only the final [characterization] is adapted to conform with the initial one, and that too when it can be so adapted, and when there is little [to adapt].
But here, the qualities such as <s>amṛtatva</s> (immortality) and others are many and cannot be adapted [to refer to the reflection or the individual soul].
For mere persistence in one's own existence does not constitute <s>amṛtatva</s> (immortality).
If it did, what indeed would not be immortal? — thus the word 'immortal' would become meaningless.
Fear and fearlessness too are properties of conscious beings and cannot occur in an insentient entity.
Likewise, the qualities of being <s>Vāmanī</s> and the rest cannot be applied to anything other than <s>Brahman</s>.
The designation as directly perceived (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) has also been established.
This is what is stated by [the <s>sūtra</s>] 'because of logical fitness' (<s>upapatteḥ</s>).
When it is said 'This is the immortal, the fearless — this is <s>Brahman</s>,' a doubt might arise:
Since <s>Īśvara</s> is all-pervading, why is the eye specifically taught as His abode? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] replies with the <s>Śruti</s>: 'Even if one pours clarified butter or water on it, it goes only to the eyelids.'
The 'eyelids' means the sides of the eye.
What is thereby stated is this: for <s>Īśvara</s> who is untainted, the eye alone, being itself untainted, is a fitting abode.
This is what is stated — 'thus it is fitting for the supreme Lord' — and the teaching of qualities such as <s>Saṃyadvāma</s> and the rest is appropriate (<s>kalpate</s>), i.e., fits, only in that <s>Brahman</s>, because the meanings are inherently present [in <s>Brahman</s>].
But in the case of reflections and the like, the meanings are not inherently present.
The auspicious fruits of merit (<s>puṇyaphala</s>) — which are worthy of worship (<s>saṃbhajanīya</s>), beautiful (<s>śobhanīya</s>) — are called <s>vāma</s>.
That by which these auspicious things (<s>vāmāni</s>) come together (<s>saṃyanti</s>) is <s>Saṃyadvāma</s>, the <s>Paramātman</s>.
Because He is the agent of their production, the fruits of merit come together through Him.

body.text:
#sthānādivyapadeśācca# /
āśaṅkottaramidaṃ sūtram /
āśaṅkāmāha- #kathaṃ punariti# /
sthānino hi sthānaṃ mahadvṛṣṭaṃ, yathā yādasāmabdhiḥ /
tatkathamatyalpaṃ cakṣuradhiṣṭhānaṃ paramātmanaḥ paramamahata iti śaṅkārthaḥ /

children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] resolves this: 'To this we say...'

children.text: sthānānyādayo yeṣāṃ te sthānādayo nāmarūpaprakarāsteṣāṃ vyapadeśātsarvagatasyaikasthānaniyamo nāvakalpate /
children.translated_text: Those whose locations and the rest are name-and-form manifestations — because of the designation of such things, the restriction of the all-pervading [<s>Brahman</s>] to a single location is not tenable.
But this multiplicity of locations is not [a real plurality], just as space (<s>nabhas</s>) is not [really] in multiple locations such as those [delimited by] a needle-hole and the like.

children.text: viśeṣatastu brahmaṇastāni tānyupāsanāsthānānīti tairasya yukto vyapadeśaḥ //14 //
children.translated_text: Rather, specifically for <s>Brahman</s>, those various [locations] are places of meditation (<s>upāsanāsthāna</s>), and therefore the designation of It by means of those [locations] is appropriate. //14//

body.translated_text:
'And because of the designation of location and the rest' (<s>sthānādivyapadeśācca</s>).
This <s>sūtra</s> addresses an objection and its resolution.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the objection: 'But how...'
For the abode of that which abides [in it] is seen to be large, just as the ocean is [the abode] of aquatic creatures.
How then can the exceedingly small eye be the seat of the <s>Paramātman</s>, who is supremely great? — this is the meaning of the objection.

body.text:
apica prakṛtānusārādapi brahmaivātra pratyetavyaṃ, natu pratibimbajīvadevatā ityāha sūtrakāraḥ #-sukhaviśiṣṭābhādhānādeva ca# /
evaṃ khalūpākhyāyate-upakosalo ha vai kāmalāyanaḥ satyakāme jābāle brahmacaryamuvāsa /
tasmācāryasya dvādaśa varṣaṇyagnīnupacacāra /
sa cācāryo 'nyānbrahmacāriṇaḥ svādhyāyaṃ grāhayitvā samāvartayāmāsa /
tamevaikamupakosalaṃ na samāvartayati sma /
jāyayā ca tatsamāvartanāyārthito 'pi tadvacanamavadhīryācāryaḥ proṣitavān /
tato 'tidūnamānasamagniparicaraṇakuśalamupakosalamupetya trayo 'gnayaḥ karuṇāparādhīnacetasaḥ śraddadhānāyāsmai dṛḍhabhaktaye sametya brahmavidyāsūcire-'prāṇo brahma kaṃ brahma khaṃ brahma' iti /
athopakosala uvāca, vijānāmyahaṃ prāṇo brahmeti, sa hi sūtrātmā vibhūtimattayā brahmarūpāvirbhāvādbrahmeti /
kintu kaṃ ca khaṃ ca brahmetyetanna vijānāmi /
nahi viṣayendriyasaṃparkajaṃ sukhamanityaṃ lokasiddhaṃ khaṃ ca bhūtākāśamacetanaṃ brahma bhavitumarhati /
athainamagnayaḥ pratyūcuḥ-'yadvāva kaṃ tadeva khaṃ yadeva khaṃ tadeva kam' iti /
evaṃ saṃbhūyoktvā pratyekaṃ ca svaviṣayāṃ vidyāmūcuḥ-'pṛthivyagnirannamādityaḥ' ityādanā /
punasta enaṃ saṃbhūyocuḥ, eṣā somya te 'smidvidyā pratyekamuktā svaviṣayā vidyā, ātmavidyā cāsmābhiḥ saṃbhūya pūrvamuktā prāṇo brahma kaṃ khaṃ brahmeti, ācāryastu te gatiṃ vaktā, brahmavidyeyamuktāsmābhirgatimātraṃ tvavaśiṣṭaṃ noktaṃ, tattu vidyāphalaprāptaye jābālastavācāryo vakṣyatītyuktvāgnaya uparemire /
evaṃ vyavasthite 'yadvāva kaṃ tadeva khaṃ yadeva khaṃ tadeva kam' ityetadvyācaṣṭe bhāṣyakāraḥ- #tatra khaṃśabda iti pratīkābhiprāyeṇeti# /
āśrayāntarapratyayasyāśrayāntare prakṣepaḥ pratīkaḥ /
yathā brahmaśabdaḥ paramātmaviṣayo nāmādiṣu kṣipyate /
idameva tadbrahma jñeyaṃ yannāmeti /
tathedameva tadbrahma yadbhūtākāśamiti pratītiḥ syāt /
na caitatpratīkatvamiṣṭam /
laukikasya mukhasya sādhanapāracantryaṃ kṣayiṣṇutā cāmayastena saha vartata iti sāmayaṃ sukham /
tadevaṃ vyatireke doṣamuktvobhayānvaye guṇamāha- #itacaretaviśeṣitau tviti# /
tadarthayorviśeṣitatvācchabdāvapi viśeṣitāvucyete /
sukhaśabdasamānādhikaraṇo hi khaṃśabdo bhūtākāśamarthaṃ parityajya brahmaṇi guṇogena vartate /
tādṛśā ca khena sukhaṃ viśiṣyamāṇaṃ sāmayādvyāvṛttaṃ nirāmayaṃ bhavati /
tasmādupapannamubhayopādānam /
brahmaśabdābhyāsasya prayojanamāha- #tatra dvitīya iti# /
brahmapadaṃ kaṃpadasyopari prayujyamānaṃ śiraḥ, evaṃ khaṃpadasyāpi brahmapadaṃ śiro yayoḥ kaṅkhaṃpadayoste brahmaśirasī, tayorbhāvo brahmaśirastvam /
astu prastute kimāyātamityata āha- #tadevaṃ vākyopakrama iti# /
nanvagnibhiḥ pūrvaṃ nirdiśyatāṃ brahma, 'ya eṣo 'kṣiṇi' ityācāryavākye 'pa tadevānuvartanīyamiti tu kuta ityāha- #ācāryastu te gatiṃ vakteti ca gatimātrābhidhānamiti# /
yadyapyete bhinnavaktṛṇī vākye tathāpi pūrveṇa vaktnā ekavākyatāṃ gamite, gatimātrābhidhānāt /
kimuktaṃ bhavati, tubhyaṃ brahmavidyāsmābhirūpadiṣṭā, tadvidastu gatirnoktā, tāṃ ca kiñcidadhikamādhyeyaṃ pūrayitvācāryo vakṣyatīti /
tadanena pūrvāsaṃbaddhārthāntaravivakṣā vāriteti /
athaivamagnibhirupadiṣṭe proṣita ācāryaḥ kālenājagāma, āgataśca vīkṣyopakosalamuvāca, brahmavida iva te somya mukhaṃ prasannaṃ bhāti, ko 'nu tvāmanuśaśāseti /
upakosalastu hrīṇo bhītaśca ko nu māmanuśiṣyāt bhagavan proṣite tvayītyāpātato 'pajñāya nirbadhyamāno yathāvadagnīnāmanuśāsanamavocat /
tadupakṣutya cācāryaḥ suciraṃ kliṣṭa upakosale samupajātadaryārdrahṛdayaḥ pratyuvāca, somya kila tubhyamagnayo na brahma sākalyenāvocan, tadahaṃ tubhyaṃ sākalyena vakṣyami, tadanubhavamāhātmyāt 'yathā puṣpakarapalāśa āpo na śliṣyanta evamevaṃvida pāpaṃ karma na śliṣyate, ityevamuktavatyācārya āhopakosalaḥ, bravītu me bhagavāniti, tasmai hovācācāryo 'rcirādikāṃ gatiṃ vaktumanāḥ, yaduktamagnibhiḥ prāṇo brahma kaṃ brahma khaṃ brahmeti tatparipūraṇāya 'eṣo 'kṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyate' ityādi /
etaduktaṃ bhavati-ācāryeṇa ye sukhaṃ brahmākṣisthānaṃ saṃyadvāmaṃ vāmanībhāmanītyevaṅguṇakaṃ prāṇasahitamupāsate te sarve 'pahatapāpmāno 'nyatkarma kurvantu mā vākārṣuḥ, arciṣamarcirabhimāninīṃ devatāmabhisaṃbhavanti pratipadyante, arciṣo 'harahardevatāṃ, ahna āpūryamāṇapakṣaṃ śuklapakṣadevatāṃ, tataḥ ṣaṇmāsān, yeṣu māseṣūttarāṃ diśameti savitā te ṣaṇmāsā uttarāyaṇaṃ taddevatāṃ pratipadyante, tebhyo māsebhyaḥ saṃvatsaradevatāṃ, tata ādityaṃ, ādityāccandramasaṃ, candramaso vidyutaṃ, tatra sthitānetānpuruṣaḥ kaścidbrahmalokādavatīryāmānavo 'mānavyāṃ sṛṣṭau bhavaḥ /

children.translated_text: That is to say, one born in <s>Brahmaloka</s>.

children.text: sa tādṛśaḥ puruṣa etānsatyalokasthaṃ kāryaṃ brahma gamayati, sa eṣa devapatho devairarcirādibhirnetṛbhirupalakṣita iti devapathaḥ, sa eva ca brahmaṇā gantavyenopalakṣita iti brahmapathaḥ, etena pathā pratipadyamānāḥ satyalokasthaṃ brahma imaṃ mānavaṃ manoḥ sargaṃ kiṃbhūtamāvartaṃ janmajarāmaraṇapaunaḥ punyamāvṛttistatkartāvarto mānavo lokastaṃ nāvartante /
children.translated_text: Such a <s>puruṣa</s> leads these [souls] to <s>Satyaloka</s>, to <s>Kāryabrahman</s> (the conditioned <s>Brahman</s>). This is the <s>Devapatha</s> (path of the gods), characterized by the guides such as <s>Arcis</s> (flame) and the rest, who are deities. And it is also called <s>Brahmapatha</s> (path of <s>Brahman</s>), being characterized by <s>Brahman</s> as the destination. Those who proceed along this path to <s>Brahman</s> abiding in <s>Satyaloka</s> do not return to this human world (<s>mānava</s>), the creation of <s>Manu</s>, which is characterized by <s>āvarta</s> (the cycle) — the recurrence of birth, old age, and death.

children.text: tathāca smṛtiḥ-'brahmaṇā saha te sarve saṃprāpte pratisaṃcare /
children.translated_text: And thus the <s>Smṛti</s> states: 'All those, together with <s>Brahman</s>, when the dissolution (<s>pratisaṃcara</s>) arrives,
at the end of the highest [cycle], having perfected their selves, enter the supreme abode.' //15//

body.translated_text:
Furthermore, even by following what is being discussed in context (<s>prakṛtānusāra</s>), <s>Brahman</s> alone is to be understood here, and not the reflection, the individual soul, or a deity — so says the author of the <s>sūtra</s>s: 'And because of the statement about one distinguished by happiness not being negated' (<s>sukhaviśiṣṭābhidhānādeva ca</s>).
For the story is narrated thus: <s>Upakosala</s>, the son of <s>Kamala</s>, lived as a <s>brahmacārin</s> with <s>Satyakāma Jābāla</s>.
For twelve years he tended the fires of his teacher.
The teacher, having taught the other <s>brahmacārin</s>s their Vedic studies, dismissed them [with the concluding ceremony].
But he did not dismiss <s>Upakosala</s> alone.
Even when entreated by his wife for <s>Upakosala</s>'s dismissal, the teacher disregarded her words and went away on a journey.
Then the three fires, their hearts overcome with compassion, approached <s>Upakosala</s>, who was exceedingly sorrowful but skilled in fire-tending and full of steadfast devotion, and together imparted to him the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>: '<s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, <s>ka</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, <s>kha</s> is <s>Brahman</s>.'
Then <s>Upakosala</s> said: 'I understand that <s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, for He is the <s>Sūtrātman</s> (the thread-self) and is called <s>Brahman</s> because of His manifestation as divine glory.
But I do not understand [in what sense] <s>ka</s> and <s>kha</s> are <s>Brahman</s>.
For the happiness born of the contact of sense-organs with objects, being impermanent and commonly known, and <s>kha</s> being the insentient elemental space, cannot possibly be <s>Brahman</s>.'
Then the fires replied to him: 'What indeed <s>ka</s> (happiness) is, that alone is <s>kha</s> (space); what <s>kha</s> is, that alone is <s>ka</s>.'
Having thus spoken collectively, they each individually taught their respective knowledge: 'Earth, fire, food, the sun,' and so on.
Then again they said to him together: 'O dear one, this is the knowledge imparted to you by us — each has taught his own respective knowledge, and the knowledge of the self (<s>ātmavidyā</s>) was taught by us collectively at the outset — "<s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, <s>ka</s> and <s>kha</s> are <s>Brahman</s>." But the teacher will tell you the path (<s>gati</s>). This knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> has been taught by us; only the path remains untold, and the teacher <s>Jābāla</s> will tell you that for the attainment of the fruit of this knowledge.' Having said this, the fires became silent.
Things being thus established, the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] explains the passage 'What indeed <s>ka</s> is, that alone is <s>kha</s>; what <s>kha</s> is, that alone is <s>ka</s>' with the intention of the <s>pratīka</s> (transferred designation).
A <s>pratīka</s> is the projection of the cognition belonging to one substrate onto another substrate.
Just as the word <s>Brahman</s>, whose referent is the supreme self (<s>Paramātman</s>), is projected onto name and the like [by saying] 'Name is <s>Brahman</s>.'
Similarly, the understanding would be: 'This very <s>Brahman</s> is what is [called] elemental space.'
But this transferred designation is not intended [here].
Ordinary happiness (<s>mukhasukha</s>) is accompanied by the defects of being impermanent and subject to decay and disease — hence the happiness associated with it is contingent (<s>sāmaya</s>).
Having thus stated the defect in the case of mutual exclusion, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the merit in the case of mutual qualification: 'But the two being qualified by each other...'
Because their referents are qualified [by each other], the two words are also said to be qualified.
For the word <s>kha</s>, being in co-reference (<s>samānādhikaraṇa</s>) with the word for happiness (<s>sukha</s>), abandons its meaning of elemental space and functions with reference to <s>Brahman</s> as a secondary designation.
And happiness, when qualified by such <s>kha</s> [= <s>Brahman</s>], being distinguished from contingent [happiness], becomes free from affliction (<s>nirāmaya</s>).
Therefore, the employment of both [terms] is justified.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the purpose of the repetition of the word <s>Brahman</s>: 'There, the second...'
The word <s>Brahman</s>, being applied above the word <s>ka</s>, is its 'head' (<s>śiras</s>); likewise the word <s>Brahman</s> is the 'head' of the word <s>kha</s>. Those two — the words <s>ka</s> and <s>kha</s> — whose head is <s>Brahman</s>, are called <s>brahmaśiras</s> (having <s>Brahman</s> as their head); their quality is <s>brahmaśirastva</s>.
As to what bearing this has on the topic at hand, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Thus, from the opening of the passage...'
One might object: Let the fires first declare <s>Brahman</s>; but how does one know that in the teacher's statement 'the being in the eye' (<s>ya eṣo'kṣiṇi</s>), the same [<s>Brahman</s>] is being continued? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'And because the teacher will tell you the path, and [the teacher's statement] is merely a declaration of the path.'
Even though these are statements by different speakers, yet because the former speaker establishes a unity of discourse [with the latter], since [the latter] merely declares the path.
What is thereby stated is: 'The knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> has been taught to you by us; but the path for the knower has not been stated; that the teacher will state, completing what little more remains to be studied.'
By this, the intention to speak of something unconnected with what precedes is precluded.
Then, after the fires had thus taught, the teacher who had gone away returned in due course, and upon arrival, observing <s>Upakosala</s>, said: 'O dear one, your face shines like that of a knower of <s>Brahman</s>. Who has instructed you?'
<s>Upakosala</s>, being bashful and afraid, initially dissembled saying 'Who indeed could instruct me, revered sir, while you were away?'; but being pressed, he truthfully recounted the instruction of the fires.
Having heard this, the teacher, whose heart had become soft with compassion toward <s>Upakosala</s> who had suffered for so long, replied: 'O dear one, the fires did not teach you <s>Brahman</s> in its completeness; I shall teach it to you completely.' And because of the greatness of that experience, 'Just as water does not cling to the petal of a lotus, so evil action does not cling to one who knows thus.' When the teacher had spoken thus, <s>Upakosala</s> said: 'Let the revered sir teach me.' Then the teacher, intending to teach him the path through <s>Arcirādi</s> (the path of light), [said] in order to complete what the fires had stated — '<s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, <s>ka</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, <s>kha</s> is <s>Brahman</s>' — 'This being seen in the eye' and so on.
What is thereby stated is this: Those who, as taught by the teacher, meditate upon <s>Brahman</s> as abiding in the eye, as <s>Saṃyadvāma</s>, as <s>Vāmanī</s>, as <s>Bhāmanī</s>, possessing these qualities, together with <s>Prāṇa</s> — all of them, having their sins destroyed, 'let them do other works but not [sinful] ones' — they reach <s>Arcis</s>, the deity presiding over flame; from <s>Arcis</s> to the deity of day; from day to the deity of the bright fortnight; from that to the six months during which the sun travels northward, [reaching] the deity of <s>Uttarāyaṇa</s>; from those months to the deity of the year; from that to the sun (<s>Āditya</s>); from <s>Āditya</s> to the moon (<s>Candramā</s>); from the moon to lightning. There, a certain being (<s>puruṣa</s>), having descended from <s>Brahmaloka</s> — a human being, born from <s>Manu</s> in the human creation —

children.translated_text: And the singular number is used with reference to the class (<s>jāti</s>).
Therefore, the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>) alone is the inner controller (<s>antaryāmin</s>), not <s>Paramātman</s> — thus [concludes the prima facie view].
This being the prima facie position, [the <s>Siddhāntin</s>] states — 'For regulating body and sense organs, it has no other body and sense organs;
If that [body etc.] is acquired through <s>karma</s>, then that world is produced through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance).'

body.translated_text: For activity characterized by regulation is an effect seen [to belong] to a conscious embodied being, either in its own body and sense organs, or through the body in tools such as an adze — it cannot belong to <s>Brahman</s> which is without a body. For a banyan sprout is never born from the seed of a <s>kuṭaja</s> plant. By this, one should understand that the [objection] regarding 'that from which the origin etc. [of this world proceeds]' (<s>janmādyasya yataḥ</s>) is also implicitly raised. Therefore, since <s>Paramātman</s>, being devoid of body, sense organs, and the like, cannot be the inner controller (<s>antaryāmin</s>), the inner controllership must belong either to <s>Pradhāna</s>, or to a deity (<s>devatā</s>) presiding over earth and the like, or to a <s>yogin</s> possessing powers such as speech, or to the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>). Now, although <s>Pradhāna</s> possesses the properties of being unseen, unheard, unthought, and unknown, nevertheless, since it is insentient and lacks the scriptural attributes of being a seer, hearer, thinker, and knower, and since the <s>Śruti</s> 'this is your self' (<s>eṣa ta ātmā</s>) cannot apply to it as it is not the self, <s>Pradhāna</s> cannot be the inner controller. Although a deity presiding over earth and the like possesses selfhood, and the properties of being unseen etc. together with being a seer etc. are possible [for it] due to its connection with body and sense organs — as the <s>Śruti</s> states 'earth alone is its seat, fire its world, <s>manas</s> its light' — nevertheless, since its control is restricted to a particular domain, it contradicts the <s>Śruti</s> 'who controls all worlds from within, who controls all beings from within,' and hence is untenable. As for the <s>yogin</s>, although by entering worlds and beings he is capable of controlling all worlds and all beings through the creation of manifold bodies and sense organs in each place — as the <s>Śruti</s>s state 'he becomes one, he becomes three' etc. — nevertheless, by the principle to be stated later that 'cosmic functions are excluded, because of the context,' since those accomplished through knowledge have no activity regarding modifications [of the world], he too is not the inner controller. Therefore, by elimination, the individual self (<s>jīva</s>) alone — being conscious, possessing body and sense organs, endowed with the capacity of seeing etc., itself unseen etc. due to the impossibility of operating upon oneself — [is the inner controller]. And it is immortal (<s>amṛta</s>), because it does not perish even when body and sense organs perish; otherwise, there would be the unwanted consequence of the destruction of what has been done and the occurrence of what has not been done, due to the absence of experiencing fruits in the next world. The statement 'who abides in the self' (<s>ya ātmani tiṣṭhan</s>) involves a figurative attribution of difference even where there is non-difference, just as in 'O Lord, in what is it established? In its own greatness' (<s>sve mahimni</s>). And 'whom the self does not know' (<s>yam ātmā na veda</s>) is intended to express the impossibility of operating upon oneself. And all such statements as 'whose body is the self' (<s>yasyātmā śarīram</s>) should be construed like 'in its own greatness' (<s>sve mahimni</s>). Moreover, if there were another controller or knower controlling even the self, then there would be another for that one too, leading to an infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>). And the individual self's control over all worlds and beings is through unseen merit (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>); for <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> acquired by it regulate [things], and through this means the <s>jīva</s> controls.

children.translated_text: 'Who in all sacrifices' is <s>adhiyajña</s>.
'Who in all beings' is <s>adhibhūta</s>.
From <s>prāṇa</s> up to the self is <s>adhyātma</s>.
Because the designation is not well-known — this is merely the introduction to the prior view (pūrvapakṣa). [End of sūtra] 19.

body.translated_text: In <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, <s>Itihāsa</s>, and <s>Purāṇa</s>s, the status of being the source of the universe (<s>jagadyonitva</s>) is understood to belong to the revered omniscient, omnipotent supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>). That cannot be denied by a semblance of inference (<s>anumānābhāsa</s>) common to ordinary people that contradicts scripture. And thus, the entire class of modifications is a transformation of his power of <s>avidyā</s>, which functions in the place of his body and sense organs; accordingly, through the respective effects and instruments such as earth, deities, and so on, he is able to control those very entities — earth, deities, and the rest. Nor is there an infinite regress; for he is not controlled by another controller. Rather, the <s>jīva</s> who is known in the world as a controller is none other than <s>Paramātman</s> himself, with difference imagined through limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) — this has been stated repeatedly. So whence another controller, and whence an infinite regress? And thus the <s>Śruti</s> passages such as 'there is no other seer than this' are also vindicated, since in the ultimate sense there is no seer other than the inner controller who is the individual self [in reality <s>Paramātman</s>]. The <s>Śruti</s> passages about the distinction between knower and known, the means of knowledge such as perception, the experience of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and the scriptures of injunctions and prohibitions — all rest upon the difference between <s>jīva</s> and <s>Paramātman</s> that is imagined through <s>avidyā</s>. Thus, the recognition of one and the same inner controller across the <s>adhidaiva</s> and other domains is consistent; the singular 'who' (<s>yaḥ</s>) in 'who [controls] all worlds' and 'who [controls] all beings' is justified. And immortality (<s>amṛtatva</s>) is coherent only with respect to <s>Paramātman</s>, not otherwise. In passages like 'who abides in the self' (<s>ya ātmani tiṣṭhan</s>), there will be no strain in figuratively attributing difference where there is non-difference. Therefore, it is established that <s>Paramātman</s> is the inner controller, not the <s>jīva</s> etc. [The section] from earth up to thunder is <s>adhidaiva</s>. 'Who in all worlds' is <s>adhiloka</s>. 'Who in all <s>Veda</s>s' is <s>adhiveda</s>.

children.translated_text: [Sūtra:] 'Because there is a contradiction in the activity being attributed to the agent of seeing and other actions.'
The meaning is: because there is a contradiction in activity being attributed to the self (<s>ātman</s>) which is the agent. [End of sūtra] 20.

The meaning is: eternally immutable (<s>kūṭastha-nitya</s>).
Transformation or apparent modification (<s>vivarta</s>) is observed [only] of that which has a similar nature [to its effect];
But similarity in nature with insentient things is not possible for that whose nature is consciousness (<s>cit</s>). [Verse 1]

body.translated_text: [Sūtra:] 'Because the qualities such as invisibility etc. are stated as attributes.' [The <s>Śruti</s> states:] 'Now the higher [knowledge] by which that <s>Akṣara</s> (imperishable) is apprehended' — 'that which is invisible' means beyond the range of the intellect and sense organs; 'ungraspable' means beyond the reach of the organs of action; 'without lineage' (<s>agotra</s>) means without cause; 'without <s>varṇa</s>' means devoid of the status of being a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> etc. Not only is it beyond the range of the sense organs alone; it has no sense organs at all — thus [the <s>Śruti</s>] says 'without eyes, without ears.' This indicates the organs of knowledge. 'Without hands, without feet' indicates the organs of action. 'Eternal' — 'all-pervading, extremely subtle,' because it is difficult to know. children.translated_text: Alternatively, if the word 'source' (<s>yoni</s>) refers to the efficient cause (<s>nimittakāraṇa</s>), even then there is no reason for determining that it is <s>Brahman</s> alone and not the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>) that is the efficient cause — this is the prior view based on doubt.
To this it is replied — 'Having stated the imperishable's (<s>akṣara</s>'s) status as source of the universe, immediately thereafter,

children.text: yaḥ sarvajña iti śrutyā sarvajñasya sa ucyate //1 //
children.translated_text: By the <s>Śruti</s> 'who is omniscient,' it is declared to be the omniscient one. [Verse 1]

body.translated_text: Transformations that are observed are indeed of the same nature as that which undergoes transformation. Just as the transformations of a spider's saliva — the spider's threads — are of the same nature as the saliva, so too apparent modifications (<s>vivarta</s>) are only of the same nature as the existing [substrate], not of a dissimilar nature. Just as the apparent modifications of a rope — a streak, a snake, etc. — are of the same nature as the rope; no one ever has the erroneous cognition of an elephant in a rope. Nor does a spider's thread become a transformation of gold. Why? Because of utter dissimilarity. Therefore, only insentient <s>Pradhāna</s> is the source of the insentient world — this is fitting. It is called <s>akṣara</s> (imperishable) as it does not emit its own modifications. And the statement 'who is omniscient, who knows all' (<s>yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavit</s>) is a description of what is beyond <s>Akṣara</s>, as the <s>Śruti</s> says 'higher than the imperishable is the supreme.' For apart from <s>Pradhāna</s>, no other imperishable entity is possible that is prior to the self and beyond the entire class of modifications. Therefore, the <s>Paramātman</s> who is beyond <s>Pradhāna</s> is the omniscient one. But the source of beings is the imperishable <s>Pradhāna</s> alone, and let that be the very <s>Pradhāna</s> accepted by the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>s. Now, if one is not satisfied with that on grounds of its lacking authoritative support, then let it be the unmanifest (<s>avyākṛta</s>), the subtle element of being, which is the seed-power of name and form. It is called <s>pradhāna</s> because modifications are offered by it. That indeed, being insentient and indeterminable (<s>anirvācya</s>), is fit to be the material cause of the indeterminable, insentient phenomenal world, due to similarity of nature. But one might object: the conscious self too is indeterminable — [yet] it is of dissimilar nature. The <s>Bhāṣya</s> statement 'of the insentient things' is intended to establish similarity of nature. One might object: Is not this [view] largely refuted by the very refutation of the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> <s>Pradhāna</s>? Why then is there apprehension [about it]? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Moreover, because it was not seen previously.' The meaning is: where there is a refuting argument, one would not resort to it; but here there is no refuting argument. Therefore, in passages like 'that willed' (<s>tadaikṣata</s>), let <s>Brahman</s>'s being the source of the universe be figuratively attributed through its being the substratum of the power of <s>avidyā</s>.

children.translated_text: Therefore, from the commonality of reference, through recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>), it is clear
That the imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>), being omniscient and the source of the universe, cannot be insentient. [Verse 2]
The <s>Śruti</s> 'higher than the imperishable' is understood to refer to the unmanifest (<s>avyākṛta</s>);
Since [the <s>Śruti</s>] has not spoken of its own effects, therefore the unmanifest is [called] the imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>). [Verse 3]

children.text: yattu sārūpyābāvānna cidātmanaḥ pariṇāmaḥ prapañca iti /
children.translated_text: As for the objection that the phenomenal world cannot be a transformation of the conscious self due to the absence of similarity of nature —
Indeed so.
'But this phenomenal world is an apparent modification (<s>vivarta</s>) of <s>Brahman</s>, which does not undergo [real] transformation;
Arising from beginningless latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), it does not require similarity of nature. [Verse 1]

body.translated_text: Nothing here is hidden, as it were.

plavante gacchanti asthāyina iti plavāḥ /
ata evādṛḍhāḥ /
ke te yajñarūpāḥ /

te tu ṣoḍaśartvijaḥ /
body.translated_text: There is certainly no rule that every error is based solely on external similarity of nature. Error is also seen to arise from internal causes — desire, anger, fear, madness, dreams, and other mental defects — without requiring similarity of nature. Moreover, only with respect to error that has a [specific] cause is the demand for the absence of that [cause] appropriate; but [error] that has fallen into the stream of beginningless <s>avidyā</s> and its latent impressions does not warrant such a demand. Therefore, the phenomenal world, as an apparent modification (<s>vivarta</s>) of <s>Paramātman</s>, has that [<s>Paramātman</s>] as its source, just as a snake, being an apparent modification of a rope, has the rope as its source — but not as a [real] transformation of it. Therefore, from the indicative mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of the attribute of omniscience stated in connection with it, in the passage 'that which is invisible' (<s>yat tad adreśyam</s>), <s>Brahman</s> alone is taught as the object of knowledge, not <s>Pradhāna</s> nor the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>) as an object of meditation — this is established. Not only from indicative marks, but also from the designation 'higher knowledge' (<s>parā vidyā</s>), this very same thing is to be understood — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says 'Moreover, the two kinds of knowledge.' He states another indicative mark: 'In what, O revered one.' Enjoyments are objects of experience; regarding the enjoyer who is distinct from them — for the limited individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>) is indeed distinct from the objects of experience, hence through knowledge of it, not everything becomes known. He states another designation: 'Moreover, he [said] the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> is the foundation of all knowledge.' '[These are] rafts, indeed unsteady, of the form of sacrifice, eighteen [in number].' <s>Plavāḥ</s> (rafts) means those that float, that go, that are impermanent. Hence they are 'unsteady' (<s>adṛḍhāḥ</s>). What are they? 'Of the form of sacrifice' (<s>yajñarūpāḥ</s>) — <s>rūpa</s> means that by which something is characterized; those whose form, i.e., limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>), is sacrifice — they are 'of the form of sacrifice.' They are the sixteen priests (<s>ṛtvij</s>s).

evaṃ yajamāno 'pi yajñopādhireva /

children.translated_text: The meaning is: that upon which [they] depend is the sacrifice.
And that <s>karma</s> is inferior, because it yields inferior fruits such as heaven (<s>svarga</s>) and the like.
<s>Apiyanti</s> means they attain.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s> says:] 'For between the illustration and the illustrated there is not [complete correspondence]' — this is the intended meaning. [End of sūtra] 21.

body.translated_text: The word <s>ṛtvik</s> is derived from the limiting adjunct of performing seasonal sacrifices, hence the priests (<s>ṛtvij</s>s) are defined by the adjunct of sacrifice. Likewise, the sacrificer (<s>yajamāna</s>) too is defined by the adjunct of sacrifice alone. Similarly the wife (<s>patnī</s>), because of the <s>Smṛti</s> statement 'of the husband, not in connection with sacrifice.' These eighteen are 'of the form of sacrifice' — the sacrifice is the <s>karma</s> that is stated in connection with priests and others.

viśeṣaṇaṃ hetuṃ vyācaṣṭe- #viśinaṣṭi hīti# /

children.translated_text: 'From the embodied self' (<s>śārīra</s>) is illustrative; it should be understood [to apply] also to [distinction] from <s>Pradhāna</s>.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] explains the statement of difference: 'Likewise, from <s>Pradhāna</s> also.'
One might object:

children.text: kimāgamikaṃ sāṃkhyābhimataṃ pradhānaṃ, tathāca bahusamañjasaṃ syādityata āha- #nātra pradhānaṃ nāma kiñciditi# //22 //
children.translated_text: Is the <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) accepted by the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> something known from scripture? And in that case, would it be highly consistent? To this he says: 'There is nothing called <s>Pradhāna</s> here.' //22//

body.translated_text: [Sūtra:] 'And because of the distinguishing attribute and the statement of difference, [the inner controller is] not the other two.' [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] explains the distinguishing attribute as the reason: 'For it distinguishes.'

children.translated_text: And when the connection with the subject of the context is established, the author of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> has presented the fact of being placed amidst those being born as the reason for including them among those being born.

children.text: tasmāddhiraṇyagarbha eva bhagavān prāṇātmanā sarvabhūtāntaraḥ kāryo nirdiśyata iti sāṃpratam /
children.translated_text: Therefore it is proper that the Lord <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> alone, as the inner [Self] of all beings through the identity of <s>Prāṇa</s> (vital breath), is being described as an effect (<s>kārya</s>).
Then is the <s>sūtra</s> entirely to be disregarded? No, he says: 'In this view...'
Because of the context. //23//

body.translated_text:
'And because of the description of form (<s>rūpopanyāsa</s>).'
Having explained this through objection and resolution from the opponent's standpoint, he expounds it from his own view: 'Others, however, consider...'
The word 'however' (<s>punaḥ</s>), indicating a distinction from the preceding, signals the acceptability of this [view].
For one who has fallen amidst the class of beings born and who possesses a form with fire as head and so forth, when there is a possibility of [being] among those born, it is not proper to arbitrarily attribute creatorship.
The context here indeed belongs to the source of the universe (<s>viśvayoni</s>), and the proximity belongs to those being born.
If one objects that since context is stronger than proximity, the description of form belongs to the subject of the context — the source of the universe — abandoning those being born, [we reply:] no, because there is a contradiction in attributing embodiment to the subject of the context, which is devoid of body, sense-faculties, and the like.
Nor is it proper to say that on this account alone the <s>śruti</s> passages about head and so forth, due to conflict with the context, abandon their own meaning and refer merely to being the Self of all, because <s>śruti</s> is stronger than context, which conveys a greatly remote meaning.

saṃdeho dehasya madhyabhāgaḥ sa ākāśo bahulaḥ sarvagatatvāt /
bastireva rayiḥ
body.translated_text:
'<s>Vaiśvānara</s>, because of the specific meaning of a common word (<s>sādhāraṇaśabdaviśeṣāt</s>).'
<s>Prācīnaśāla</s>, <s>Satyayajña</s>, <s>Indradyumna</s>, <s>Jana</s>, and <s>Buḍila</s>, having assembled, engaged in deliberation: 'Who is our Self? What is <s>Brahman</s>?'
The question 'What is <s>Brahman</s>?' was added lest, when 'Self' is mentioned, the understanding be directed merely to the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>).
And they, deliberating but unable to reach a conclusion, approached King <s>Aśvapati</s> of <s>Kaikeya</s>, who was learned in the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> knowledge.
Having approached, they said: 'You know this very Self, <s>Vaiśvānara</s> — please tell us about him,' beginning thus and [proceeding through] heaven, sun, wind, space, water, and earth.
The meaning is this: Heaven is the head of the Lord <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, resplendent with light.
The eye is the sun, who is of universal form (<s>viśvarūpa</s>).
The breath is the wind, which has a separate path — 'separate path' means that which has a distinct course, and that very one whose nature (<s>ātman</s>) is of separate path, is called 'one whose nature is of separate path.'
The torso (<s>saṃdeha</s>) is the middle part of the body; that is space (<s>ākāśa</s>), abundant because of its all-pervasiveness.
The bladder (<s>basti</s>) itself is wealth (<s>rayi</s>),
