children.text: evaṃ ca parameśvaradṛṣṭirhi jāṭhare vaiśvānara ihopadaiśyata iti bhāṣyaṃ virudhyeta /
children.translated_text: And thus the statement of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> that 'the vision of the Supreme Lord is taught here regarding the gastric <s>Vaiśvānara</s>' would be contradicted.
And there would be conflict with <s>śruti</s>.

children.text: 'sa yo haitamevamagniṃ vaiśvānaraṃ puruṣaṃ puruṣavidhaṃ puruṣe 'ntaḥpratiṣṭhitaṃ veda' iti vaiśvānarasya hi puruṣatvavedanamatrānūdyate, natu puruṣasya vaiśvanaratvavedanam /
children.translated_text: 'He who knows this fire, <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, who is a person, of human form, established within the person' — here the personhood of <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is being restated (<s>anūdya</s>), not the <s>Vaiśvānara</s>-hood of the person being taught.

children.text: tasmāt 'sa eṣo 'gnirvaiśvānaro yat' iti yadaḥ pūrveṇa saṃbandhaḥ, puruṣa iti tu tatra puruṣadṛṣṭerupadeśa iti yuktam //24 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, in 'This fire is <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, which...,' the word 'which' (<s>yat</s>) connects with what precedes, and the word 'person' (<s>puruṣa</s>) serves as the instruction to see [<s>Vaiśvānara</s>] as a person — this is proper. //24//

body.translated_text:
[which is] water, since from water [comes] food and from food [comes] wealth (<s>rayi</s>); therefore waters are called <s>rayi</s>, and the bladder is the receptacle of those [waters] in the form of urine — thus it is said 'the bladder itself is <s>rayi</s>.'
The feet are the earth, because of being established there.
Thus, among the parts of <s>Vaiśvānara</s> — heaven, sun, wind, space, water, and earth — corresponding to head, eye, breath, torso, bladder, and feet, the censure of the worshippers <s>Prācīnaśāla</s> and others, who had been meditating on each one individually with the understanding of <s>Vaiśvānara</s> in a reversed manner, through the defects of head-falling, blindness, departure of vital breath, bodily disintegration, bursting of the bladder, and loosening of the feet, teaches by condemning their meditations the completeness [of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>] consisting of head and all other parts — as it is declared: 'He who meditates on this one as a span in measure (<s>prādeśamātra</s>).'
He eats food in all worlds beginning with heaven, in all beings both stationary and moving, in all selves — body, sense-faculties, mind, intellect, and individual soul — that is, he obtains the fruit connected with everything.
Then, with the intention of establishing the <s>Agnihotra</s>-nature of the food of <s>Vaiśvānara</s> as eater and food, the <s>śruti</s> says: 'The chest indeed is the altar (<s>vedi</s>)' — because of its resemblance to the altar.
'The body-hair is the sacrificial grass (<s>barhis</s>)' — because of its resemblance to spread sacrificial grass.
'The heart is the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [fire].'
Next to the heart, 'the mind is the <s>Anvāhāryapacana</s> [fire].
The mouth is the <s>Āhavanīya</s> [fire]' — for there indeed that food is offered as oblation.
Now, [the objector argues:] at the beginning [of the passage], with the words 'Who is our Self? What is <s>Brahman</s>?', since the words 'Self' (<s>ātman</s>) and '<s>Brahman</s>' are established in their conventional sense as referring to the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), the words '<s>Vaiśvānara</s>,' 'fire,' and the like, being colored by that [established meaning], can somehow be directed toward the Supreme Self; but it is not proper to redirect the words '<s>Brahman</s>' and 'Self,' which are understood first, in accordance with the words '<s>Vaiśvānara</s>' and the like, which are understood later.
And although in the <s>Vājasaneyin</s> version of the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> knowledge, at the beginning — 'You indeed know <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, please tell us about him' — the words 'Self' and ['<s>Brahman</s>'] do not occur, nevertheless the <s>Chāndogya</s> passage has the same meaning, and since it has the same beginning, the meaning of the <s>Vājasaneyin</s> passage is determined in conformity with the established meaning of the former.
For a passage whose meaning is uncertain is settled by one whose meaning is certain — not a certain meaning by an uncertain one.
And like ritual action (<s>karman</s>), <s>Brahman</s> too, being recognized across all branches [of the <s>Veda</s>], is one and the same.
And having heaven as head and the like is not possible for any one of the gastric fire, the elemental fire, a deity, or the individual self.
Nor is the status of being the support and fruit-recipient of all worlds [possible for them].
Nor is the burning away of all sins [possible]. Therefore, by the method of elimination (<s>pāriśeṣya</s>), <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is determined to be the Supreme Self itself — whence then this doubt? — 'Because of the words, being established within, and so forth, [<s>Vaiśvānara</s> is] not [<s>Brahman</s>]...'
The reply is: that which can be redirected is redirected in accordance with the beginning [of the passage].
But the objector's assumption is that the words '<s>Vaiśvānara</s>' and 'fire' cannot be redirected.
Moreover, being established within and being a span in measure are not possible for the all-pervading and immeasurable Supreme <s>Brahman</s>.
And the status of being the locus of <s>Prāṇāhuti</s> (offerings into the vital breath) is not proper for anything other than the gastric fire.
And the status of being the <s>Gārhapatya</s> and the like for the heart and the like is not possible for <s>Brahman</s>.
Therefore, <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is one or another among the gastric fire, the elemental fire, a deity, or the individual souls, as befits [each reading] — but not <s>Brahman</s>.
And thus the words 'Self' and '<s>Brahman</s>' occurring at the beginning must also be redirected.
And the attributes of being the head and the like are mere praise (<s>stuti</s>).
Alternatively, the objector's intention is that for a deity having fire as its body, the attributes of having heaven as head and the like are tenable due to its lordly power.
To this the reply is: 'No.'
Why? 'Because the instruction is of such a vision (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>).'
What is understood first, being established independently (<s>ananyathāsiddha</s>), [should] redirect what is understood later.
But here there is no independent establishment of the later-understood [terms], because it can be explained either as instruction through a symbol (<s>pratīka</s>) — like 'Mind is <s>Brahman</s>' — or as instruction through a limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) — like 'consisting of mind, having breath as body, having the form of light.'
Or, because the words '<s>Vaiśvānara</s>' and 'fire' denote <s>Brahman</s> by etymology, there is no independent establishment [of a non-<s>Brahman</s> meaning]; and thus, either by transferring the cognition that rests on <s>Brahman</s> to another locus called the gastric <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, or by [understanding] <s>Brahman</s> to be meditated upon with the gastric <s>Vaiśvānara</s> as its limiting adjunct, the combination of the attributes of <s>Vaiśvānara</s> and of <s>Brahman</s> is tenable.
He explains 'because of impossibility' as a part of the <s>sūtra</s>: 'If the Supreme Lord were not intended here...'
He explains 'And they read of him as a person' as a part of the <s>sūtra</s>: 'And if merely [the gastric fire]...'
The meaning is: neither as a limiting adjunct of <s>Brahman</s> nor as a symbol (<s>pratīka</s>).
'Not merely established within, but also a person' — this is the meaning of the word 'also' (<s>api</s>).
By recollecting (<s>anūdya</s>) 'He who is the Person' as a person, <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is not [separately] enjoined.
Were it otherwise, the meditation on <s>Vaiśvānara</s> would be taught as a superimposition on the person.

children.text: ata eva na devatā bhūtaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: For this very reason, [<s>Vaiśvānara</s>] is neither a deity nor an elemental [fire].

For this very reason — that is, because of these grounds: the connection with having heaven as head and the like as known from <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>, being the support and fruit-recipient of all worlds, the burning away of all sins, and the indication through the words 'Self' and '<s>Brahman</s>' at the beginning.

children.text: 'yo bhānunā pṛthivīṃ dyāmutemām' iti mantravarṇo 'pi na kevalauṣṇyaprakāśavibhavamātrasya bhūtāgneramamīdṛśaṃ mahimānamāhaga, api tu brahmavikāratayā tādrūpyeṇeti bhāvaḥ //27 //
children.translated_text: Even the Vedic verse 'He who [illumines] the earth and heaven yonder with radiance' does not declare such greatness for the elemental fire, which possesses merely the power of heat and light; rather, [it refers to <s>Brahman</s>], because [the fire] has such a nature by virtue of being a transformation of <s>Brahman</s> — this is the import. //27//

body.text:
#sākṣādapyavirodhaṃ jaiminiḥ# /
yadetatprakṛtaṃ mūrdhādiṣu cubukānteṣu puruṣāvayaveṣu dyuprabhṛtīnpṛthivīparyantāṃstrailokyātmano vaiśvānarasyāvayavān saṃpādya puruṣavidhatvaṃ kalpitaṃ tadabhiprāyeṇedamucyate 'puruṣavidhaṃ puruṣe 'ntaḥpratiṣṭhitaṃ veda' iti /
atrāvayavasaṃpattyā puruṣavidhatvaṃ kāryakāraṇasamudāyarūpapuruṣāvayavamūrdhādicubukāntaḥpratiṣṭhānācca puruṣe 'ntaḥpratiṣṭhitatvaṃ samudāyamadhyapatitvāttadavayavānāṃ samudadāyinām /
atraiva nidarśanamāha- #yathā vṛkṣe śākhāmiti# /
śākhākāṇḍamūlaskandhasamudāye pratiṣṭhitā śākhā tanmadhyapatitā bhavatītyarthaḥ /
samādhānāntaramāha- #athaveti# /
antaḥpratiṣṭhatvaṃ mādhyāsthyaṃ tena sākṣitvaṃ lakṣayati /
etaduktaṃ bhavati-vaiśvānaraḥparamātmā carācarasākṣīti /

children.translated_text: He uproots the lingering doubt of the objector: 'When it is determined...'
<s>Vaiśvānara</s> is the innermost Self (<s>pratyagātman</s>), because of being the Self of all (<s>viśvātmakatva</s>).
Or, he is the leader (<s>nara</s>) of all (<s>viśva</s>), because the entire manifest world (<s>viśvaprapañca</s>) is his modification.
Or, all living beings (<s>narāḥ</s>), the individual selves (<s>jīvāḥ</s>), are his own Selves — [he is <s>Vaiśvānara</s>] because of identity with them. //28//

body.translated_text:
'Even directly there is no contradiction — [so says] <s>Jaimini</s>.'
What was under discussion — that having composed the parts of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, whose Self is the three worlds, from heaven down to earth, upon the bodily parts of a person from head to chin, the human form was conceived — with that intent it is said: 'He knows [<s>Vaiśvānara</s>] as having human form, established within the person.'
Here, the human form is [established] through the correlation of the parts, and being established within the person is because the constituent parts, being parts of the aggregate which is the person in the form of the totality of cause and effect, fall within [that aggregate], being established within the bodily parts from head to chin.
To this he gives an illustration: 'Just as a branch in a tree...'
A branch established in the aggregate of branches, trunk, root, and stem falls within that [aggregate] — this is the meaning.
He states another explanation: 'Or alternatively...'
'Being established within' indicates being in the middle, and by that, the status of being a witness (<s>sākṣin</s>) is implied.
What is said amounts to this: <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is the Supreme Self, the witness of the moving and the unmoving.

body.text:
#abhivyakterityāśmarathyaḥ# /
sākalyenopalambhāsaṃbhavādupāsakānāmanugrahāyānanto 'pi parameśvaraḥ prādeśamātramātmanamabhivyanaktītyāha- #atimātrasyāpīti# /

children.translated_text: 'Beyond measure' (<s>atimātra</s>) means one who has transcended measure, i.e., magnitude.
'For the sake of the worshippers.'
That is to say, for the purpose of the worshippers.
He states another interpretation: 'In the regions (<s>pradeśeṣu</s>)...' //29//

body.translated_text:
'Because of manifestation — [so says] <s>Āśmarathya</s>.'
Since it is impossible to apprehend [him] in totality, for the sake of gracing the worshippers, the Supreme Lord, though infinite, manifests himself as a span in measure — thus he says: 'Even though beyond measure...'

children.translated_text: 'Because of correlation (<s>saṃpatti</s>) — [so says] <s>Jaimini</s>.'
For the bodily region from the head down to the chin is a span in measure (<s>prādeśamātra</s>).
Correlating the parts of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, whose Self is the three worlds, precisely there [in that span], he shows <s>Vaiśvānara</s> as a span in measure. //31//

body.text:
atraiva jābālaśrutisaṃvādamāha sūtrakāraḥ- #āmananti cainamasmin# /
avimukte avidyopādhikalpitāvacchede jīvātmani sa khalvavimuktaḥ /
tasminpratiṣṭhitaḥ paramātmā, tādātmyāt /

children.text: ata eva hi śrutiḥ-'anena jīvenātmanā' iti /
children.translated_text: For this very reason the <s>śruti</s> [says]: 'Through this individual self (<s>jīva</s>)...'
But the relation of support and supported is based on the difference imagined through <s>avidyā</s>.
<s>Varaṇā</s> is the eyebrow (<s>bhrū</s>).
The rest is of transparent meaning. //32//

body.translated_text:
The <s>Sūtrakāra</s> states the concordance with the <s>Jābāla</s> <s>śruti</s> in this very context: 'And they declare him in this [<s>Avimukta</s>].'
In <s>Avimukta</s> — in the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>) delimited by the limiting adjunct imagined through <s>avidyā</s> — that indeed is <s>Avimukta</s> (the never-forsaken).
The Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) is established in that [<s>jīvātman</s>], because of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>).

body.text: iti śrīvācaspatimiśraviracite śārīrakamīmaṃsābhāṣyavibhāge bhāmatyāṃ prathamasyādhyāyasya dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ //2 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the second <s>pāda</s> of the first <s>adhyāya</s> in the <s>Bhāmatī</s>, the division of the commentary on the <s>Śārīrakamīmāṃsā</s>, composed by the venerable <s>Vācaspati Miśra</s>. //2//

body.text: #iti prathamādhyāyasya upāsyabrahmavācakāspaṣṭaśrutisamanvayākhyo dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ#
body.translated_text: Thus ends the second <s>pāda</s> of the first <s>adhyāya</s>, called 'The Harmonization of <s>Śruti</s> Passages with Unclear Reference to <s>Brahman</s> as the Object of Meditation.'

body.text: #prathamādhyāye tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ# /
body.translated_text: Third <s>pāda</s> of the first <s>adhyāya</s>.

body.text:
#dyubhvādyāyatanaṃ svaśabdāt# /
iha jñeyatvena brahmopakṣipyate /
tatra 'pāravattvena setutvādbhede ṣaṣṭhyāḥ prayogataḥ /
body.translated_text:
'That which has heaven, earth, and the rest as its abode — because of its own word (<s>svaśabda</s>).'
Here <s>Brahman</s> is introduced as that which is to be known.
In that regard: 'Because of being the far shore, because of being the bridge, and because of the use of the genitive case indicating difference,

body.text: dyubhvādyāyatanaṃ yuktaṃ nāmṛtaṃ brahma karhicit //
body.translated_text: it is fitting that [the entity] having heaven, earth, and the rest as its abode [is <s>Brahman</s>] — never is the immortal (<s>amṛta</s>) anything other than <s>Brahman</s>.'

body.text:
' pārāvāramathyapātī hi setuḥ tābhyāmavacchidyamāno jalavidhārako loke dṛṣṭaḥ, natu bandhanahetumātram /
haḍinigāḍādiṣvapi prayogaprasaṅgāt. na cānavacchinnaṃ brahma setubhāvamanubhavati /
na sadbrahmāmṛtasya seturiti yujyate /
naca brahmaṇo 'nyadamṛtamasti, yasya tatsetuḥ, syāt /
na cābhede ṣaṣṭhyāḥ prayogo dṛṣṭapūrvaḥ /
tadidamuktam- #amṛtasyaiṣa seturiti śravaṇāditi# /
amṛtasyeti śravamāt, iti yojanā /
tatrāmṛtasyeti śravaṇāditi viśabdatayā na vyākhyātam /
seturiti śravaṇāditi vyācaṣṭe- #pāravāniti# /
tathāca pāravatyamṛtavyatirikte setāvanuśriyamāṇe pradhānaṃ vā sāṃkhyapārikalpitaṃ bhavet /
tat khalu svakāryopahitamaryādatayā puruṣaṃ yāvadagacchadbhavatīti pāravat, bhavati ca dyubhvādyāyatanaṃ, tatprakṛtitvāt, prakṛtyāyatanatvācca vikārāmāṃ, bhavati cātmātmaśabdasyasvabhāvavacanatvāt, prakāśātmā pradīpa itivat /
bhavati cāsya jñānamapavargopayogi, tadabhāve pradhānādvivekena puruṣasyānavadhāraṇādapavanupargāpatteḥ /
yadi tvasminpramāṇābhāvena na parituṣyasi, astu tarhi nāmarūpabījaśaktibhūtamavyākṛtaṃ bhūtasūkṣmaṃ dyubhvādyāyatanaṃ, tasmin prāmāṇike sarvasyoktasyopapatteḥ /
etadapi pradhānopanyāsena sūcitam /
atha tu sākṣācchutyuktaṃ dyubhvādyāyatanamādriyame, tato vāyurevāstu /
'vāyunā vai gautama sūtreṇāya ca lokaḥ paraśca lokaḥ sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni saṃdṛbdhāni bhavanti' iti śruteḥ /
yadi punarasya dyubhvādyāyatanasya sārvajñyaśruteratrāpi na parituṣyami, bhavatu tato hiraṇyagarbha eva bhagavān sarvajñaḥ sūtrātmā dyubhvādyāyatanam /
tasya hi kāryatvena pāravattvaṃ cāmṛtātparabrahmaṇo bhedaścetyādi sarvamupapadyate /
ayamapi 'vāyunā vai gotama sūtreṇa' iti śrutimupanyasyatā sūcitaḥ /
tasmādayaṃ dyuparbhṛtīnāmāyatanamityevaṃ prāpte 'bhidhīyate /

children.translated_text: The abode of heaven, earth, and the rest is the supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone, not <s>Pradhāna</s>, <s>Avyākṛta</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, the embodied self, or <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>.
Why? Because of its own word (<s>svaśabda</s>).
Whether the state of being a bridge is due to sustaining or due to being the means to immortality,
even in the prima facie view, the word <s>setu</s> (bridge) is not desired in its primary sense.

body.translated_text: A <s>setu</s> (bridge/dam) is seen in the world as that which holds back water, being bounded by both banks — it is not merely a cause of binding, for otherwise the term would absurdly apply to fetters, stakes, and the like. Nor does the unlimited <s>Brahman</s> undergo the state of being a bridge. It is not fitting to say that the ever-existent <s>Brahman</s> is the bridge of the immortal. Nor is there any other immortal entity apart from <s>Brahman</s> of which it could be the bridge. And the use of the genitive case in non-difference has no precedent. Thus it was stated: 'because of the hearing of "this is the bridge of the immortal."' The construction is: 'because of hearing "of the immortal."' There, the phrase 'because of hearing "of the immortal"' is not explained as a separate word. He explains 'because of hearing "bridge"' as meaning 'having a farther shore.' And thus, when a bridge that is distinct from the immortal and has a farther shore is being considered, it could be <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter) as postulated by the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> school. For that indeed has a farther shore inasmuch as it extends up to <s>Puruṣa</s> (spirit) by way of the limit imposed by its own effects; it is also the abode of heaven, earth, and the rest, being their material cause, and modifications having their abode in their material cause; it is also the <s>Ātman</s> (self), since the word 'self' denotes essential nature, like saying 'the lamp is luminous in nature.' Its knowledge also serves liberation, since without it, due to the non-ascertainment of <s>Puruṣa</s> through discrimination from <s>Pradhāna</s>, liberation would not be attained. But if you are not satisfied with this due to lack of proof, then let the <s>Avyākṛta</s> (unmanifest), which is the subtle elements constituting the seed-power of name and form, be the abode of heaven, earth, and the rest, since when that is established as valid, everything stated is accounted for. This too was indicated by the mention of <s>Pradhāna</s>. But if we value what is directly stated by <s>śruti</s> (scripture) as the abode of heaven, earth, and the rest, then let it be <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) alone, because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'By <s>Vāyu</s> indeed, O <s>Gautama</s>, as by a thread, this world and the other world and all beings are strung together.' But if I am still not satisfied even with the <s>śruti</s> declaring omniscience regarding this abode of heaven, earth, and the rest, then let it be the blessed <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> himself, the omniscient <s>Sūtrātman</s> (thread-self), as the abode of heaven, earth, and the rest. For his having a farther shore through being an effect, and his difference from the supreme <s>Brahman</s> which is immortal — all this is accounted for. He too was indicated by the one citing the <s>śruti</s> 'By <s>Vāyu</s> indeed, O <s>Gautama</s>, as by a thread.' Having thus arrived at the position that this is the abode of heaven, earth, and the rest, it is now stated:

body.text:
' nahi mṛddārumayo mūrtaḥ pārāvāramadhyavartī pāthasāṃ vidhārako lokasiddhaḥ setuḥ pradhānaṃ vāvyākṛtaṃ vā vāyurvā jīvo vā sūtrātmā vābhyupeyate /
kintu pāravattāmātraparo lakṣaṇikaḥ setuśabdo 'bhyupeyaḥ /
so 'smākaṃ pāravattāvarjaṃ vidharaṇatvamātreṇa yogamātrādrūḍhiṃ parityajya pravartsyati /
jīvānāmamṛtatvapadaprāptisādhanatvaṃ vatmajñānasya pāravata eva lakṣayiṣyati /
amṛtaśabdaśca bhāvapradhānaḥ /
yathā 'dvyekayordvivacanaikavacane' ityatra dvitvaikatve dvyekaśabdārthau, anyathā dvyekeṣviti syāt /
tadidamuktaṃ bhāṣyakṛtā #amṛtatvasādhanatvāditi# /
tathā cāmṛtasyeti ca seturiti ca brahmaṇi dyubhvādyāyatane upapatsyete /
atra ca svaśabdāditi tantroccaritatamātmaśabdāditi ca sadāyatanā iti sacchabdāditi ca brahmaśabdāditi ca sūcayati /
sarve hyete 'sya svaśabdāḥ /
syādetat /
āyatanāyatanavbhāvaḥ sarvaṃ brahmeti ca sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ hiraṇyagarbhepyupapadyate /
tathāca sa evātrāstvamṛtatvasya seturityāśaṅkya śrutivākyena sāvadhāraṇenottaramāha- #tatrāyatanāyatanavadbhāvaśravaṇāditi# /
vikārarūpe 'nirvācya'bhisaṃdhānaṃ yasyābhisaṃdhānupuruṣasya sa tathoktaḥ /
bhedaprapañcaṃ satyamabhimanyamāna iti yāvat /
tasyāpavādo doṣaḥ śrūyate #-mṛtyoriti /
sarvaṃ brahmeti tviti# /
yatsarvamavidyāropitaṃ tatsarvaṃ paramārtha brahma /
na tu yadbrahma tatsarvamityarthaḥ /
#apara āheti# /
nātra dyubhvādyāyatanasya setunocyate yena pāravattā syāt /
kintu 'jānatha' iti yajjñānaṃ kīrtitaṃ, yaśca 'vāco vimuñcatha' iti vāgvimokaḥ, tasyāmṛtatvasādhanatvena setutocyate /
taccobhayamapi pāradeva /

children.text: naca prādhānyādeṣa iti sarvanāmnā dyubhvādyāyatanamātmaiva parāmṛśyate, na tu tajjñānavāgvimocane iti sāṃpratam /
children.translated_text: And it is not proper to say that because of primacy, the pronoun 'this' refers to the <s>Ātman</s> (self) as the abode of heaven, earth, and the rest, rather than to the knowledge thereof and the release of speech.
Because knowledge of the self and cultivation of release of speech alone have primacy as what is enjoined.
But the <s>Ātman</s> (self), being a substance without activity, is not what is enjoined.
Only by the fitness of the enjoined activity is even a subordinate element referred to.

body.translated_text: For neither <s>Pradhāna</s>, nor <s>Avyākṛta</s>, nor <s>Vāyu</s>, nor the individual self, nor the <s>Sūtrātman</s> is accepted as a bridge in the well-known worldly sense — one made of mud or wood, having physical form, situated between the two banks, and holding back waters. Rather, the word <s>setu</s> must be accepted in a secondary sense, meaning only 'having a farther shore.' For us, it will operate by mere capacity for sustaining, abandoning the conventional meaning in favor of mere fitness, apart from having a farther shore. The having a farther shore will indicate that the knowledge of the self is the means for the attainment of the state of immortality for living beings. And the word 'immortal' has the sense of a state. Just as in 'the dual and singular number for two and one,' the words 'two' and 'one' mean duality and oneness; otherwise it would be 'in twos and ones.' Thus it was stated by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (commentator): 'because of being the means to immortality.' And thus both 'of the immortal' and 'bridge' are appropriate with reference to <s>Brahman</s> as the abode of heaven, earth, and the rest. Here, by the <s>sūtra</s> word <s>svaśabdāt</s> (from its own word), he indicates: from the word <s>Ātman</s>, which is frequently used in the system, and from the word <s>sat</s> (being) in 'that whose abode is <s>sat</s>,' and from the word <s>Brahman</s>. For all these are its own words. One might object: the relation of abode and that which has an abode, and the co-referentiality 'all is <s>Brahman</s>' are also possible with <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>. Anticipating this objection, he answers with a <s>śruti</s> statement containing a restrictive particle: 'because of the hearing of the relation of abode and that which has an abode.' One whose intention is toward the inexpressible in the form of a modification — that is, a person who considers the manifold of differences to be real — is so described. His refutation, the defect, is heard: 'of death.' 'But all is <s>Brahman</s>' — whatever is superimposed through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), all that is in the ultimate sense <s>Brahman</s>. But it does not mean that whatever is <s>Brahman</s> is everything — that is the meaning. 'Another says': here, the bridge of the abode of heaven, earth, and the rest is not spoken of, so that it would have a farther shore. Rather, the knowledge that is praised as 'know!' and the release of speech as 'release your words' — their being the means to immortality is called their being a bridge. And both of these indeed have a farther shore.

body.text:
#muktopasṛpyavyapadeśāt# /
dyubhvādyāyatanaṃ prakṛtyāvidyādidoṣamuktairupasṛtyaṃ vyapadiśyate-'bhijyate hṛdayagranthiḥ' ityādinā /
tena tat dyubhvādyāyatanaviṣayameva /
brahmaṇaśca muktopasṛpyatvaṃ 'yadā sarve pramucyante' ityādau śrutyantare prasiddham /
tasmānmuktopasṛpyatvāt /
dyubhvādyāyatanaṃ brahmeti niścīyate /
hṛdayagranthiścāvidyārāgādveṣabhayamohāḥ /
body.translated_text: The abode of heaven, earth, and the rest is described as that which is to be approached by those who are liberated — freed from defects such as <s>prakṛti</s> (primal nature) and <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — through passages such as 'the knot of the heart is cut.' Therefore, that refers only to the abode of heaven, earth, and the rest. And <s>Brahman</s>'s being approachable by the liberated is well-known in other <s>śruti</s> passages such as 'when all are released.' Therefore, because of being approachable by the liberated, the abode of heaven, earth, and the rest is determined to be <s>Brahman</s>. The knot of the heart consists of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), <s>bhaya</s> (fear), and <s>moha</s> (delusion).

body.text:
mohaśca viṣādaḥ, śokaḥ /
paraṃ hiraṇyagarbhādyavaraṃ yasya tadbrahma tathoktam /
tasminbrahmaṇi yaddṛṣṭaṃ darśanaṃ tasmiṃstadarthamiti yāvat /

children.text: yathā 'carmaṇi dvīpinaṃ hanti' iti carmārthamiti gamyate /
children.translated_text: Just as in 'he kills the leopard for the skin,' it is understood to be for the sake of the skin.
The mention of name and form is with reference to <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance).
'The desires that are lodged in the heart' —
The word 'desires' indicates <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) by way of implication.

body.translated_text: And <s>moha</s> (delusion) means dejection, grief. That <s>Brahman</s> which is higher than <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> and others and lower than which they are, is so described. The vision that is seen in that <s>Brahman</s> — 'in that, for the sake of that' is the meaning.

children.translated_text: 'It is not the inferred entity, because of the absence of that word' —
The word 'inferred' (<s>anumāna</s>) is used as an indication.
It should also be understood as 'not the <s>Avyākṛta</s> (unmanifest),' since the reason applies equally to both.

body.text:
#praṇabhṛcca# /
cenātacchabdatvaṃ heturanakṛṣyate /
svayaṃ ca bhāṣyakṛdatra hetumāha- #na copādhiparicchinnasyeti# /
na samyak saṃbhavati /
nāñjasamityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: For saying that being an abode means being an object of enjoyment is strained.
One might object:

children.text: yadyatacchabdatvādityatrāpi heturanakraṣṭavyaḥ, hanta kasmātpṛthagyogakaraṇaṃ, yāvatā 'na prāṇabhṛdanumāne' ityeka eva yogaḥ kasmānna kṛta ityata āha- #pṛthagiti# /
children.translated_text: If the reason 'because of the absence of that word' is also to be carried forward here, then why is a separate <s>sūtra</s> formulated? Why was not a single <s>sūtra</s> 'the inferred entity and the bearer of <s>prāṇa</s> are not' composed? To this he replies: 'separately' —

children.text: 'bhedavyapadeśāt' ityādinā hi prāṇabhṛdeva niṣidhyate, na pradhānaṃ, taccaikayogakaraṇe durvijñānaṃ syāditi //4 //
children.translated_text: For by the statement 'because of the declaration of difference' and so on, only the bearer of <s>prāṇa</s> (embodied self) is negated, not <s>Pradhāna</s>; and if they were combined in one <s>sūtra</s>, that would be difficult to understand.

body.translated_text: 'And the bearer of <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath)' — by the word 'and,' the reason of 'absence of that word' is carried forward. The <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (commentator) himself states the reason here: 'one limited by adjuncts does not properly' — does not fittingly — that is the meaning.
(Sūtra 5)

children.translated_text: 'Because of the context' —

children.text: na khalu hiraṇyagarbhādiṣu jñāteṣu sarvaṃ jñātaṃ bhavati kintu brahmaṇyeveti //6 //
children.translated_text: Certainly, when <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> and others are known, everything is not known; but only when <s>Brahman</s> is known.

body.text:
#sthityadanābhyāṃ ca# /
yadi jīvo hiraṇyagarbho vā dyubhvādyāyatanaṃ bhavet, tatastatprakṛtyā 'anaśrannanyo 'abhicākaśīti' iti paramātmābhidhānamākasmikaṃ prasajyeta /
naca hiraṇyagarbha udāsīnaḥ, tasyāpi bhoktṛtvāt /
naca jīvātmaiva dyubhvādyāyatanaṃ, tathā sati sa evātra kathyate, tatkathanāya ca brahmāpi kathyate, anyathā siddhānte 'pi jīvātmakathanamākasmikaṃ syāditi vācyam /
yato 'nadhigatārthāvabodhanasvarasenāmnāyena prāṇabhṛnmātraprasiddhajīvātmadhigamāyātyantānavagatamalaukikaṃ brahmāvabodhyata iti subhāṣitam- #yadāpi paiṅgyupaniṣatkṛtena vyākhyāneneti# /
tatra hi 'anaśrannanyo 'abhicākaśīti' iti jīva upādhirahitena rūpeṇa brahmasvabhāva udāsīno 'bhoktā darśitaḥ /
tadarthamevācetanasya buddhisattvasyāpāramārthikaṃ bhoktṛtvamuktam /

children.text: tathā cetthaṃbhūtaṃ jīvaṃ kathayatānena mantravarṇena dyubhvādyāyatanaṃ brahmaiva kathitaṃ bhavati, upādhyavacchinnaśca jīvaḥ pratiṣiddho bhavatīti /
children.translated_text: And thus, by this <s>mantra</s> passage which speaks of the individual self in such a manner, <s>Brahman</s> itself as the abode of heaven, earth, and the rest is spoken of, and the individual self as limited by adjuncts is negated.
There is no contradiction with the <s>Pauṅgi Brāhmaṇa</s> — that is the meaning.
'For the purpose of elaboration' —
Thinking that it is not included in that section, this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topical discussion) was undertaken — that is the meaning.

body.translated_text: 'And because of abiding and eating' — If the individual self or <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> were the abode of heaven, earth, and the rest, then the mention of the supreme self in 'the other, not eating, looks on' would be pointless. Nor is <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> the detached one, for he too is an enjoyer. Nor should one say that the individual self alone is the abode of heaven, earth, and the rest, and that since it is spoken of here, <s>Brahman</s> is also spoken of for the purpose of speaking about it, and that otherwise even in the established doctrine the mention of the individual self would be pointless. For by the natural flow of scripture whose purpose is to make known what is not yet known, <s>Brahman</s> — which is entirely unknown, supramundane — is made known for the sake of knowing the individual self who is well-known merely as a bearer of <s>prāṇa</s>. Thus it is well stated: 'even according to the explanation given in the <s>Paiṅgi Upaniṣad</s>.' For there, in 'the other, not eating, looks on,' the individual self is shown as detached, having the nature of <s>Brahman</s>, in a form free from adjuncts, as a non-enjoyer. For that very purpose, the non-ultimate enjoyership of the insentient <s>buddhi-sattva</s> (intellective substance) is stated.

body.text:
#bhūmā saṃprasādādadhyupadeśāt# /
nāradaḥ khalu devarṣiḥ karmavidanātmavittayā śocyamātmānaṃ manyamāno bhagavantamātmajñamājānasiddhaṃ mahāyoginaṃ sanatkumāramupasasāda /
upasadya covāc, bhagavan, anātmajñatājanitaśokasāgarapāramuttārayatu māṃ bhagavāniti /
tadupaśrutya sanatkumāreṇa 'nāma brahmetyupāstva' ityukte nāradena pṛṣṭaṃ kiṃnāmno 'sti bhūya iti /
tatra sanatkumārasya prativacanam-'vāgvāva nāmno bhūyasī' iti /
tadevaṃ nāradasanatkumārayorbhūyasī /
praśnottare vāgindriyamupakramya manaḥsaṃkalpacittadhyānavijñānabalānnatoyavāyusahitatedonabhaḥ smāraśāprāṇeṣu paryavasite /
kartavyākartavyavivekaḥ saṃkalpaḥ, tasya kāraṇaṃ pūrvāparaviṣayanimittaprayojananirūpaṇaṃ cittam /
smaraḥ smaraṇam /
prāṇasya ca samastakriyākārakaphalabhedena pitrādyātmatvena ca rathāranābhidṛṣṭāntena sarvapratiṣṭhatvena ca prāṇabhūyastvadarśino 'tivāditvena ca nāmādiprapañcādaśāntādbhūyastvamuktvāpṛṣṭa eva nāradena sanatkumāra ekagranthena 'eṣa tu vā ativadati yaḥ satyenātivadati' iti satyādīnkṛtiparyantānuktvopadideśa-'sukhaṃ tveva vijijñāsitavyam' iti /
tadupaśrutya nāradena 'sukhaṃ tveva bhagavo vijijñāse' ityukte sanatkumāraḥ 'yo vai bhūmā tatsukham' ityupakramya bhūmānaṃ vyutpādayāṃbabhūva-'yatra nānyatpaśyati' ityādinā /
tadidṛśe viṣaye vicāra ārabhyate /

children.text: tatra saṃśayaḥ-kiṃ prāṇo bhūmā syādāho paramātmeti /
children.translated_text: There the doubt arises: is <s>Prāṇa</s> (vital breath) the <s>Bhūman</s> (infinite), or is it the supreme self?

The <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (commentator) has stated that the co-referentiality of the two — the state and the one possessing the state — with the intention of expressing identity, is the seed of the doubt.
There, 'in this arrangement of the text, that which is stated as greater than another,
that greater thing is stated preceded by a question.'

body.translated_text: '<s>Bhūman</s> (the infinite), because of the teaching proceeding from <s>saṃprasāda</s> (deep sleep/serenity)' — The divine sage <s>Nārada</s>, being a knower of ritual action but not of the self, considering himself pitiable due to his lack of self-knowledge, approached the blessed <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, who was known to be a knower of the self, a self-realized great <s>yogin</s>. Having approached, he said: 'Blessed one, may you carry me across the ocean of grief born of the lack of self-knowledge.' Upon hearing this, when <s>Sanatkumāra</s> said 'meditate on name as <s>Brahman</s>,' <s>Nārada</s> asked: 'Is there anything greater than name?' <s>Sanatkumāra</s>'s reply was: 'Speech indeed is greater than name.' Thus the extensive question-and-answer between <s>Nārada</s> and <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, beginning with the organ of speech, concluded at mind, will, thought, meditation, understanding, strength, food, water, fire, space, memory, hope, and <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath). <s>Saṃkalpa</s> (will) is the discrimination between what is to be done and what is not; its cause is <s>citta</s> (thought), which is the examination of prior and subsequent objects, grounds, and purposes. <s>Smara</s> means memory. And of <s>prāṇa</s>, having shown its being greater than name and the rest through the tenfold division of the entire range of action, instrument, and result, through its being the self of ancestors and others, through the analogy of the spokes of a wheel-hub, and through its being the foundation of all, and through the status of one who speaks what surpasses — having stated its superiority over the tenfold elaboration beginning with name, even without being asked by <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Sanatkumāra</s> in a single passage taught the series from truth to resolve, saying 'he indeed speaks what surpasses who speaks what surpasses with truth,' and then instructed: 'happiness indeed is to be inquired into.' Upon hearing this, when <s>Nārada</s> said 'Blessed one, I wish to inquire into happiness,' <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, beginning with 'that which is <s>Bhūman</s> (the infinite) — that is happiness,' proceeded to explain the <s>Bhūman</s> through passages such as 'where one sees nothing else.' In such a subject matter, the investigation begins.

body.text:
' naca prāṇāt kiṃ bhūya iti pṛṣṭam /
nāpi bhūmā vāsmādbhūyāniti pratyuktam /
tasmātprāṇabhūyastvābhidhānānantaramapṛṣṭhena bhūmocyamānaḥ prāṇasyaiva bhavitumarhati /
apica bhūmeti bhāvo na bhavitāramāntareṇa śakyo nirūpayitumiti bhavitāramapekṣamāṇaḥ prāṇasyānantaryeṇa buddhisaṃnidhānāttameva bhavitāraṃ prāpya nirvṛṇoti /
'yasyobhayaṃ havirārtimārcchet' ityatrārtivārtaṃ haviḥ /
yathāhuḥ 'mṛṣyāmahe haviṣā viśeṣaṇam' iti /
na cātmanaḥ prakaraṇādātmaiva buddhaistha iti tasyaiva bhūmā syāditi yuktam /
sanatkumārasya 'nāma brahmetyupāstva' iti /
pratīkopadeśarūpeṇottareṇa nāradapraśnasyāpi tadviṣayatvena paramātmopadeśaprakaraṇasyānutthānāt /
atadviṣayatve cottarasya praṣaśnottarayorvaiyadhikaraṇyena vipratipatteraprāmāṇyaprasaṅgāt /
tasmādasati prakaraṇe prāṇasyānantaryāttasyaiva bhūmeti yuktam /
tadetatsaṃśayabījaṃ darśayatā bhāṣyakāreṇa sūcitaṃ pūrvapakṣasādhanamiti na punaruktam /
naca bhūyobhūyaḥ praśnātparamātmaiva nāradena jijñāsita iti yuktam /
prāṇopadeśānantaraṃ tasyoparamāt /
tadevaṃ prāṇa eva bhūmeti sthite yadyattadvirodhitayā vacaḥ pratibhāti tattadanuguṇatayā neyam /
nītaṃ ca bhāṣyakṛtā /
syādetat /
'eṣa tu vā ativadati' iti tuśabdena prāṇadarśino 'tivādino vyavacchidya satyenātilāditvaṃ vadan kathaṃ prāṇasya bhūmānamabhidadhītetyata āha- #prāṇameva tviti /
prāṇadarśinaścātivāditvamiti# /
nāmādyāśāntamatītya vadanaśīlatvamityarthaḥ /
etaduktaṃ bhavati-nāyaṃ tuśabdaḥ prāṇātivāditvādvayavacchinatti, apitu tadativāditvamaparityajya pratyuta tadanukṛṣya tasyaiva prāṇasya satyasya śravaṇamananaśraddhāniṣṭhakṛtibhirvijñānāya niścayāya satyenātivadatīti prāṇavratamevātivāditvamucyate /
tuśabdo nāmādyativāditvadvyavacchinatti /
na nāmādyāśāntavādyativādi, apitu satyaprāṇavādyativādityarthaḥ /
atra cāgamācāryopadeśābhyāṃ satyasya śravaṇam /
athāgamāvirodhinyāyaniveśanaṃ mananaṃ, matvā ca guruśiṣyasabrahmacāribhiranusūyubhiḥ saha saṃvādya tattvaṃ śraddhatte /
śraddhānantaraṃ ca viṣayāntaradarśī niraktastato vyāvṛttastattvajñānābhyāsaṃ karoti, seyamasya kṛtiḥ prayatnaḥ /
atha tattvajñānābhyāsaniṣṭhā bhavati, yadanantarameva tattvavijñānamanubhavaḥ prādurbhavati /
tadetadbāhyā /
apyāhuḥ-'bhūtārthabhāvanāprakarṣaparyantajaṃ yogijñānam' iti bhāvanāprakarṣasya prayanto niṣṭhā tasmājjāyate tattvānubhava iti /
tasmātprāṇa eva bhūmeti prāpte 'bhidhīyate-'eṣa tu vā ativadati yaḥ satyenātivadati' ityuktvā bhūmocyate /
tatra satyaśabdaḥ paramārthe nirūḍhavṛttiḥ śrutyā paramārthamāha /
paramārthaśca paramātmaiva /
tato hyanyatsarvaṃ vikārajātamanṛtaṃ kayācidapekṣayā kathañcitsatyamucyate /
tathāca 'eṣa tu vā ativadati yaḥ satyenātivaditi' iti brahmaṇo 'tivāditaṃ śrutyānyanirapekṣayā liṅgādibhyo balīyasyāvagamitaṃ kathamiva saṃnidhānamātrāt śrutyādyapekṣādatidurbalātkathaṃ citprāṇaniṣayatvena śakyaṃ vyākhyātum /
evaṃ ca prāṇādūrdhvaṃ brahmaṇi bhūtāmavagamyamāno na prāṇaviṣayo bhavitumarhati, kintu satyasya paramātmana eva /
evaṃ cānātmavida ātmānaṃ vividiṣornāradasya praśne paramātmānamevāsmai vyākyāsyāmītyabhisaṃdhimānsanatkumāraḥ sopānārohaṇanyāyena sthūlādārabhya tattadbhūmavyutpādanakrameṇa bhūmānamatidurjñānatayā paramasūkṣmaṃ vyutpādayāmāsa /
naca praśnapūrvatāpravāhapatitenottareṇa sarveṇa praśnapūrveṇaiva bhavitavyamiti niyamo 'stītyādisugamena bhāṣyeṇa vyutpaditam /
vijñānādisādhanaparamparā mananaśraddhādiḥ, prāṇāntare cānuśāsane tatāvanmātreṇaiva prakaraṇasamāpterna prāṇasyānyāyattatocyeta /
tadabhidhāne hi sāpekṣatvena na prakaraṇaṃ samāpyeta /
tasmānnedaṃ prāṇasya prakaraṇamapi tu yadāyattaḥ prāṇastasya, sa cātmetyātmana eva prakaraṇam /
śaṅkate #-prakaramānta iti# /
prāṇaprakaraṇasamāptāvityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes: '#No.
"O Revered One" (<s>sa bhagava</s>)#' — thus.

children.text: saṃdaṃśanyāyena hi bhrūma etatprakaraṇaṃ, sa codbhūmā prāṇaḥ, prāṇasyaitatprakaraṇaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: For we determine this topic by the method of tongs (<s>saṃdaṃśanyāya</s>) — and if that [to which the topic pertains] were the beyond-<s>Prāṇa</s> <s>Bhūman</s>, [and if] this were <s>Prāṇa</s>'s topic, then the <s>Bhūman</s> being [merely] <s>Prāṇa</s> would [make it] <s>Prāṇa</s>'s topic.
And that is inappropriate — as has been stated. //8//

body.translated_text:
Nor was [<s>Nārada</s>] asked 'What is greater than <s>Prāṇa</s>?'
Nor was it replied 'The <s>Bhūman</s> (Plenitude) is indeed greater than it [<s>Prāṇa</s>].'
Therefore, since <s>Bhūman</s> — being stated immediately after the declaration of the greatness of <s>Prāṇa</s>, without being asked about — ought to pertain to <s>Prāṇa</s> itself.
Moreover, <s>Bhūman</s> (plenitude) — being an [abstract] state — cannot be ascertained without [reference to] the entity that possesses it; hence, requiring an entity-possessor, by virtue of <s>Prāṇa</s>'s immediate proximity in the intellect, [<s>Bhūman</s>] reaches that very entity-possessor [<s>Prāṇa</s>] and is satisfied.
'That whose oblation would reach both [hands] in pain' (<s>yasyobhayaṃ havirārtim ārcchet</s>) — here the oblation is [characterized by] pain.
As they say: 'We take "<s>havis</s>" (oblation) as the qualifier.'
Nor is it correct [to argue] that since the Self is the topic (<s>prakaraṇa</s>), the Self alone is present in the intellect, and therefore the <s>Bhūman</s> pertains to that [Self] alone.
[For] <s>Sanatkumāra</s>'s [instruction] 'Meditate upon name as <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>nāma brahmetyupāsva</s>) —
since even <s>Nārada</s>'s question was about the same subject-matter by way of <s>pratīka</s>-instruction (instruction on symbols) in the subsequent [passages], the topic (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) of instruction on the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) has not arisen.
And if the subsequent [passages] were not about that subject-matter [i.e., the <s>Paramātman</s>], then — because of the discrepancy between the question and answer, which would concern different subjects — there would be an absurd invalidity [of the teaching].
Therefore, in the absence of a [relevant] topic, because of the immediate proximity of <s>Prāṇa</s>, it is fitting that the <s>Bhūman</s> pertains to that [<s>Prāṇa</s>] alone.
This very seed of doubt, shown by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>, is the means for establishing the prima facie view — hence it is not repetitive.
Nor is it correct [to say] that <s>Nārada</s> desired to know the <s>Paramātman</s> alone through his repeated questioning.
Because he ceased after the instruction on <s>Prāṇa</s>.
Thus, when it is established that the <s>Bhūman</s> is <s>Prāṇa</s> alone, whatever statement appears to contradict this must be interpreted in conformity with it.
And it has been so interpreted by the author of the <s>Bhāṣya</s>.
One might say this:
'But this one (<s>eṣa</s>) indeed speaks excellently (<s>ativadati</s>) who speaks excellently with <s>Satya</s> (Truth)' — here, by the word '<s>tu</s>' (but), having excluded [the view that] one who sees <s>Prāṇa</s> speaks excellently, and [instead] declaring that speaking excellently is through <s>Satya</s>, how can [the text] be teaching the <s>Bhūman</s> of <s>Prāṇa</s>? — To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#But <s>Prāṇa</s> itself#' — thus.
'#And the speaking excellently of the seer of <s>Prāṇa</s>#' — thus.
The meaning is: the disposition of speaking by transcending [everything] from name up to [and including <s>Prāṇa</s>].
What is being said is this: this word '<s>tu</s>' does not exclude the speaking-excellently that pertains to <s>Prāṇa</s>; rather, without abandoning that speaking-excellently, and indeed drawing it along, [the text teaches that] for the ascertainment of that very <s>Prāṇa</s> — [which is] <s>Satya</s> (Truth) — through hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>), reflection (<s>manana</s>), faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), and the culmination of effort (<s>niṣṭhākṛti</s>), for the sake of realization (<s>vijñāna</s>), [one who] speaks excellently with <s>Satya</s> — [this] is called the 'observance of <s>Prāṇa</s>' (<s>prāṇavrata</s>) as the speaking-excellently.
The word '<s>tu</s>' excludes [only] the speaking-excellently that pertains to name and the rest.
The meaning is: not the speaker-excelling who [merely] speaks of [things] up to name and the rest, but the speaker-excelling who speaks of <s>Satya-Prāṇa</s>.
And here, the hearing of <s>Satya</s> is through scripture and the teacher's instruction.
Then, the embedding oneself in reasoning that does not contradict scripture is reflection (<s>manana</s>); and having reflected, [one] has faith through dialogue with teachers, students, and co-students who are free from envy, about the truth.
After faith, one who has turned away from seeing other objects, having withdrawn therefrom, practices the repetition of the knowledge of reality — this is the effort (<s>kṛti</s>), the exertion.
Then comes the culmination (<s>niṣṭhā</s>) in the practice of the knowledge of reality, immediately after which the realization of reality (<s>tattvavijñāna</s>), the experience, manifests.
This [culmination] is the external [aspect].
As others too say: 'The knowledge of the <s>yogin</s> arises at the culmination of the cultivation of actual reality (<s>bhūtārthabhāvanā</s>)' — the effort is the culmination of cultivation, and from that arises the experience of reality.
Therefore, when the prima facie view that the <s>Bhūman</s> is <s>Prāṇa</s> alone has been established, the reply is given: Having said 'But this one indeed speaks excellently who speaks excellently with <s>Satya</s>,' the <s>Bhūman</s> is stated.
Therein, the word '<s>Satya</s>' (Truth) — having a conventional meaning fixed in [the sense of] ultimate reality — denotes the ultimate reality through <s>Śruti</s> [authority].
And the ultimate reality is the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) alone.
For everything other than That — being the entire product of transformation — is called '<s>anṛta</s>' (unreal), [and] only in some relative sense [and] somehow is it called '<s>satya</s>' (real).
And thus, 'This one indeed speaks excellently who speaks excellently with <s>Satya</s>' — [here,] the speaking-excellently of <s>Brahman</s>, being conveyed by <s>Śruti</s> — which is independent and stronger than <s>liṅga</s> (indicatory marks) and the like — how could it possibly be interpreted as pertaining to <s>Prāṇa</s> merely on the basis of proximity — which is dependent on <s>Śruti</s> and the like [and hence] extremely weak?
And thus, when the <s>Bhūman</s> is understood as [pertaining to] <s>Brahman</s> — which is beyond <s>Prāṇa</s> — it cannot pertain to <s>Prāṇa</s>, but only to the <s>Paramātman</s> who is <s>Satya</s>.
And thus, <s>Sanatkumāra</s> — intending 'I shall explain to <s>Nārada</s>, who does not know the Self and desires to know the Self, the <s>Paramātman</s> itself' — by the method of ascending steps, beginning from the gross, gradually taught the <s>Bhūman</s>, which is supremely subtle and hence extremely difficult to know, through the successive elucidation of each [level's] plenitude.
And there is no rule that every subsequent [statement] must be preceded by a question, just because the entire [series of] answers has flowed from the stream of questions — this and more has been elucidated by the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, which is easy [to understand].
The successive means — reflection, faith, and the like — beginning with realization (<s>vijñāna</s>), and: in the instruction on <s>Prāṇa</s> as the other [entity], the topic is concluded merely by that much — hence <s>Prāṇa</s> is not stated as being dependent on something else [beyond it].
For if it were stated as dependent, the topic would not be concluded, because of its [remaining] expectancy.
Therefore, this is not the topic of <s>Prāṇa</s>, but of that upon which <s>Prāṇa</s> is dependent — and that is the Self — hence this is the topic of the Self.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises a doubt: '#The topic ends#' — thus.
The meaning is: upon the conclusion of the topic of <s>Prāṇa</s>.
