What is other [than the Self] is afflicted (<s>ārtam</s>),
meaning: perishable.
What is other has a concealed purpose. //9//

body.translated_text:
Not only from <s>Śruti</s> is the <s>Bhūman</s> the <s>Paramātman</s>, but also from <s>liṅga</s> (indicatory mark) — the <s>sūtrakāra</s> says: '#And because of the fitness of the attributes (<s>dharmopapatteḥ</s>)#.'
The <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>, having restated what the prima facie view had somehow interpreted, refutes it: '#He who, in the state of deep sleep#' — thus.
In the state of deep sleep, because of the non-connection with the senses and the rest, [the referent] is the Self alone,
not <s>Prāṇa</s>,

body.text:
#akṣaramambarāntadhṛteḥ# /
akṣaraśabdaḥ samudāyaprasiddhyā varṇeṣu rūḍhaḥ /
paramātmani cāvayavaprasiddhyā yaugikaḥ /
body.translated_text:
'#<s>Akṣara</s> (the Imperishable), because of the sustaining up to <s>ambara</s> (space)#.'
The word '<s>akṣara</s>' (imperishable/syllable), by convention based on collective usage, is established [as referring to] syllables/letters.
With respect to the <s>Paramātman</s>, it is etymological (<s>yaugika</s>) — [derived from] the convention based on component-analysis [as 'that which does not perish'].

body.text:
avayavaprasiddheśca samudāyaprasiddhirbalīyasīti varṇā evākṣaram /
naca varṇeṣvākāśasyotatvaprotatve nopapadyete, sarvasyaiva rūpadheyasyanāmadheyātmakatvāt /
sarvaṃ hi rūpadheyaṃ nāmadheyasaṃbhinnamanubhūyate, gaurayaṃ vṛkṣo 'yamiti /
na copāyatvāttatsaṃbhedasaṃbhavaḥ /
nahi dhūmopāyā bahnidhīrdhumasaṃbhinnaṃ bahnimavagāhate dhūmo 'yaṃ bahniriti, kintu vaiyadhikaraṇyena dhūmādvihniriti /
bhavati tu nāmadheyasaṃbhinno rūpadheyapratyayo ḍittho 'miti /
apica śabdānupāye 'pi rūpadheyapratyaye liṅgendriyajanmani nāmasaṃbhedo dṛṣṭaḥ /
tasmānnāmasaṃbhinnā pṛthivyādayo 'mbarāntā nāmnā gratitāśca viddhāśca, nāmāni ca oṃkārātmakāni tadvyāptatvāt /
'tadyathā śaṅkunā sarvāṇi saṃtṛṇṇānyevamoṅkāreṇa sarvā vāk' iti śruteḥ /
ata oṃkārātmakāḥ pṛthivyādayo 'mbarāntā iti varṇā evākṣaraṃ na paramātmeti prāptam /
evaṃ prāpte 'bhidhīyate-akṣaraṃ paramātmaiva, na tu varṇāḥ /
kutaḥ /
ambarāntadhṛteḥ /
na khalvambarāntāni pṛthivyādīni varṇā dhārayitumarhanti, kintu paramātmaiva /
teṣāṃ paramātmavikāratvāt /
naca nāmadheyātmakaṃ rūpadheyamiti yuktaṃ, svarūpabhedāt, upāyabhedāt, arthakriyābheda /
tathāhi-śabdatvasāmānyātmakāni śrotragrāhyaṇyabhidheyapratyayārthakriyāṇi nāmadheyānyanubhūyante /
rūpadheyāni tu ghaṭapaṭādīni ghaṭatvapaṭatvādisāmānyātmakāni cakṣurādīndriyāgrāhyāṇi madhudhāraṇaprāvaṇādyarthakriyāṇi ca bhedenānubhūyante iti kuto nāmasaṃbhedaḥ /
naca ḍittho 'miti śabdasāmānādhikaraṇyapratyayaḥ /

children.text: na khalu śabdātmako 'yaṃ piṇḍa ityanubhavaḥ, kintu yo nānādeśakālasaṃplutaḥ piṇḍaḥ so 'yaṃ saṃnihitadeśakāla ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the experience is not 'This body is of the nature of sound'; rather, the meaning is: 'This body — which was encountered at different places and times — is the same one [now] present at [this] place and time.'

But the conventional name (<s>saṃjñā</s>) — for those who have grasped the [name-referent] connection through extreme habituation — comes to mind through the impact of the awakening of the latent impression (<s>saṃskārodbodha</s>), as if entering into [the cognition of] the body.
As they say: 'The recollection of the name therein [in the body-cognition] is not caused by something other [than the body itself].

children.text: piṇḍa eva hi dṛṣṭaḥ sansaṃjñāṃ smārayituṃ kṣamaḥ //1 //
children.translated_text: For the body itself, being seen, is capable of causing the recollection of the name.' //1//

body.translated_text:
And the convention from collective usage is stronger than that from component-analysis — hence '<s>akṣara</s>' refers to syllables/letters alone.
Nor is it the case that the weaving-in and weaving-through (<s>otatva-protatva</s>) of space into syllables is untenable, because everything that is form (<s>rūpadheya</s>) is of the nature of name (<s>nāmadheya</s>).
For every form is experienced as pervaded by name — [as in] 'This is a cow, this is a tree.'
Nor is the pervading of name [into form] impossible because [name is merely] a means [of cognition].
For the cognition of fire through the means of smoke does not apprehend fire as pervaded by smoke — [as in] 'This smoke is fire' — but rather through a subject-predicate distinction: 'From smoke [one infers] fire.'
But the cognition of form is indeed pervaded by name — [as in] '<s>Ḍittha</s> is this one.'
Moreover, even without [name being] the means, in the cognition of form — which arises from the senses and is [not dependent on name for its production] — the pervading by name is observed.
Therefore, earth and the rest, up to space, are pervaded by name and are strung through by name; and names have the nature of <s>Oṃkāra</s>, because of being pervaded by it.
'Just as by a needle everything is strung through, so by <s>Oṃkāra</s> all speech [is strung through]' — because of this <s>Śruti</s>.
Hence, earth and the rest up to space, having the nature of <s>Oṃkāra</s>, are syllables alone — '<s>akṣara</s>' refers to syllables, not to the <s>Paramātman</s> — this is the prima facie view.
With this prima facie view established, the reply is: '<s>Akṣara</s>' is the <s>Paramātman</s> alone, not syllables.
Why?
Because of the sustaining up to space (<s>ambarāntadhṛti</s>).
For syllables cannot sustain earth and the rest up to space — only the <s>Paramātman</s> can.
Because they [earth etc.] are transformations of the <s>Paramātman</s>.
Nor is it correct [to say] that form is of the nature of name, because of the difference of essential nature, difference of means [of cognition], and difference of functional capacity.
For thus: names are experienced as having the general nature of sound-ness, as graspable by the ear, and as having the functional capacity of producing the cognition of the referent.
But forms — pots, cloths, and the like — are experienced as different, having the general nature of pot-ness, cloth-ness, and the like, as graspable by the eye and other senses, and as having the functional capacity of holding honey, covering, and the like. Hence, what basis is there for the pervading of name?
Nor is '<s>Ḍittha</s> is this one' a cognition of co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) with sound [i.e., name].

children.text: saṃjñā hi smaryamāṇāpi pratyakṣatvaṃ na bādhate /
children.translated_text: 'The name, even when being recollected, does not override the directness (<s>pratyakṣatva</s>) [of the body-cognition].

children.text: saṃjñinaḥ sā taṭasthā hi na rūpācchādanakṣamā //2 //
children.translated_text: For it [the name] is extraneous (<s>taṭastha</s>) to the named [entity] and is not capable of concealing [its] form.' //2//

body.text:
iti /
naca varṇātirikte sphoṭātmani alaukike 'kṣarapadaprasiddhirasti loke /
na caiṣa prāmāṇika ityupariṣṭātpravedayiṣyate /
niveditaṃ cāsmābhistattvabindau /
tasmācchrotragrāhyāṇāṃ varṇānāmambarāntadhṛteranupapatteḥ samudāyaprasiddhibādhanāvayavaprasiddhyā paramātmaivākṣaramiti siddham /
ye tu pradhānaṃ pūrvapakṣayitvānena sūtreṇa paramātmaivākṣaramiti siddhāntayanti cairambarāntadhṛterityanena kathaṃ pradhānaṃ nirākriyata iti vācyam /
atha nādhikaraṇatvamātraṃ dhṛtiḥ tathāpyambarāntadhṛterityanarthakam /
etāvadvaktavyam-akṣaraṃ praśāsanāditi /
etāvataiva pradhānanirākaṇasiddheḥ /
tasmādvarṇākṣaratānirākriyaivāsyārthaḥ /

children.translated_text: Nor should one say that since the attributes 'not gross' (<s>asthūla</s>) and the like are not prima facie applicable to syllables, there is no occasion for doubt regarding syllables.

children.text: nahyavaśyaṃ prāptipūrvakā eva pratiṣedhā bhavanti, aprāpteṣvapi nityānuvādānāṃ darśanāt /
children.translated_text: For it is not the case that negations are necessarily preceded by [the thing being] prima facie established — since [negations] serving as perpetual restatements (<s>nityānuvāda</s>) are seen even for what is not prima facie established.
Just as the negation-restatement in the <s>Agnicayana</s> (fire-altar building): 'not in the intermediate space, not in heaven.'
Therefore, this [objection] is of no consequence. //10//

body.translated_text:
And there is no conventional usage of the word '<s>akṣara</s>' for the <s>sphoṭa</s> (the extra-mundane sound-unit) beyond syllables.
Nor is this [<s>sphoṭa</s>] a valid [entity] — this will be explained later.
And it has been presented by us in the <s>Tattvabindu</s>.
Therefore, since the sustaining of earth and the rest up to space is untenable for the syllables — which are graspable by the ear — the <s>Paramātman</s> alone is '<s>akṣara</s>' (the Imperishable), by the component-analysis convention overriding the collective-usage convention — this is established.
But those who take <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial nature) as the prima facie view and establish the <s>Paramātman</s> as '<s>akṣara</s>' by this <s>sūtra</s> — for them, how does 'because of sustaining up to space' refute <s>Pradhāna</s>? — this must be answered.
If sustaining [means] merely being the substrate, even so, 'because of sustaining up to space' would be meaningless.
This much [alone] would need to be said: '<s>akṣara</s>' [is the <s>Paramātman</s>] because of commanding (<s>praśāsanāt</s>).
Since that alone would suffice for refuting <s>Pradhāna</s>.
Therefore, the meaning of this [<s>sūtra</s>] is the refutation of the letter/<s>akṣara</s> [interpretation] alone.

children.translated_text: '#And that [<s>Akṣara</s> is <s>Brahman</s>], because of commanding (<s>praśāsanāt</s>)#.'

children.text: praśāsanamājñā cetanadharmo nācetane pradhāne vāvyākṛte vā saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: Commanding (<s>praśāsana</s>) is governance (<s>ājñā</s>) — [which is] an attribute of a conscious entity — and is not possible for the insentient <s>Pradhāna</s> or the <s>Avyākṛta</s> (unmanifest [matter]).
And when the primary meaning is possible, figurative usage (<s>bhaktatva</s>) — like 'the bank wishes to collapse' (<s>kūlaṃ pipattiṣati</s>) — is not appropriate — this is the purport. //11//

body.text:
anyabhāvavyāvṛtteśca /
ambarāntavidharaṇalasyākṣarasyeśvarāgadyadanyadvarṇā vā pradhānaṃ vā.vyākṛtaṃ vā teṣāmanyeṣāṃ bhāvalo 'nyabhāvastamatyantaṃ vyavartayati śrutiḥ-'tadvā etadakṣaraṃ gārgi' ityādikā /
anenaiva sūtreṇa jīvasyāpyakṣaratā niṣiddhetyata āha- #tatheti# /
'nānyat' ityādikayā hi śrutyātmabhedaḥ pratiṣidhyate /

children.translated_text: And thus, the <s>jīva</s>s — which are different due to the difference of limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) — are negated by the statement of non-difference — this is the meaning.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states another reason why the embodied self (<s>śārīra</s>) is not [denoted by] the word '<s>akṣara</s>': '#Without eyes (<s>acakṣuṣkam</s>)#' — thus.

children.text: akṣarasya cakṣurādyupādhiṃ vārayantī śrutiraupādhikasya jīvasyākṣaratāṃ niṣedhatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Śruti</s> — which negates the limiting adjunct of the eye and the like for the <s>Akṣara</s> — thereby negates the <s>Akṣara</s>-hood of the <s>jīva</s>, which is [defined by] limiting adjuncts — this is the meaning.

Therefore, since [the <s>Akṣara</s>-hood] of syllables, <s>Pradhāna</s>, <s>Avyākṛta</s>, and the <s>jīva</s> is untenable, and since it is tenable for the <s>Paramātman</s>, it is established that the <s>Paramātman</s> alone is the '<s>Akṣara</s>.' //12//

body.translated_text:
'#And because of the exclusion of the state of being another (<s>anyabhāvavyāvṛtteḥ</s>)#.'
Of the <s>Akṣara</s> that sustains up to space and commands — [whatever is] other than <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), namely syllables, <s>Pradhāna</s>, or <s>Avyākṛta</s> (the unmanifest) — the state of being those others is completely excluded by the <s>Śruti</s>: 'O <s>Gārgī</s>, that <s>Akṣara</s>...' and the like.
Since by this very <s>sūtra</s> the <s>Akṣara</s>-hood of the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) too is negated, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Thus#' — thus.
For by the <s>Śruti</s> 'not another' (<s>nānyat</s>) and the like, the difference of the Self [from <s>Brahman</s>] is negated.

children.translated_text: '#[<s>Brahman</s> is the referent] because of being designated as the object of the seeing (<s>īkṣati-karma-vyapadeśāt</s>) — that [is <s>Brahman</s>]#.'
'Because of being the fruit of the knowledge of the <s>Brahman</s> that is the product, the person who has arrived [at it], and from the difference of purpose,
the lower (<s>apara</s>) <s>Brahman</s> is understood to be the object of meditation and contemplation.' //

body.text:
' 'brahma veda brahmaiva bhavati' iti śruteḥ sarvagataparabrahmavedena tadbhāvāpattau 'sa sāmabhirunnīyate brahmalokam iti na deśaviśeṣaprāptirupapadyate /
tasmādaparameva brahmeha dhyeyatvena codyate /
na cekṣaṇasya loke tattvaviṣayatvena prasiddheḥ parasyaiva brahmaṇastathābhāvāt, dhyāyateśca tena samānaviṣayatvāt, parabrahmaviṣayameva dhyānamiti sāṃpratam, samānaviṣayatvasyaivāsiddheḥ /
paro hi puruṣo dhyānaviṣayaḥ, parātparastu darśanaviṣayaḥ /
naca tattvaviṣayameva sarvaṃ darśanaṃ, anṛtaviṣayasyāpi tasya darśanāt /
naca mananaṃ darśanaṃ, tacca tattvaviṣayameveti sāṃpratam /
mananādbhedena tatra tatra darśanasya nirdeśāt /
naca mananamapi tarkāparanāmāvaśyaṃ tattvaviṣayam /
yathāhuḥ-'tarko 'pratiṣṭhaḥ' iti /

children.translated_text: Therefore, it is the lower <s>Brahman</s> alone that is the object of meditation here.
And its supremacy (<s>paratva</s>) is relative to the body — thus.
This being the prima facie conclusion, [the established view] is stated: 'Seeing and meditation — these two, being related as effect and cause,
Have a single object; the general rule is that [meditation] has reality as its object, as with seeing.' //

body.translated_text:
Because of the <s>Śruti</s> 'One who knows <s>Brahman</s> becomes <s>Brahman</s> indeed' — when, through the knowledge of the all-pervading supreme <s>Brahman</s>, one attains its nature — the [statement] 'He is led upward by the <s>Sāman</s>s to the world of <s>Brahman</s>' [would imply that] the attainment of a specific place is not appropriate.
Therefore, it is the lower <s>Brahman</s> (<s>apara Brahma</s>) alone that is here urged as the object of meditation.
Nor is it appropriate [to say that] since seeing (<s>īkṣaṇa</s>) is well-known in the world as having reality as its object, and since only the supreme <s>Brahman</s> has that nature, and since meditation has the same object as that [seeing], the meditation must be about the supreme <s>Brahman</s> — since the identity of their objects is itself unestablished.
For the supreme Person (<s>para puruṣa</s>) is the object of meditation, while the one beyond the supreme (<s>parātpara</s>) is the object of seeing.
Nor is all seeing necessarily about reality, since seeing is observed even regarding the unreal.
Nor is it appropriate [to say] that reflection (<s>manana</s>) is seeing, and that [seeing] is necessarily about reality.
Because seeing is mentioned separately from reflection in various places.
Nor is reflection — which is another name for reasoning (<s>tarka</s>) — necessarily about reality.
As they say: 'Reasoning is without firm foundation.'

body.text:
' dhyānasya hi sākṣātkāraḥ phalam /
sākṣātkāraścotsargatastattvaviṣayaḥ /
kkacittu bādhakopanipāte samāropitagocaro bhavet /
na cāsatyapavāde śakya utsargastyaktum /
tathā cāsya tattvaviṣayatvāttatkāraṇasya dhyānasyāpi tattatvaviṣayatvam /
apica vākyaśeṣeṇaikavākyatvasaṃbhave na vākyabhedo yujyate /
saṃbhavati ca parapuruṣaviṣayatvenārthapratyabhijñānāt samabhivyāhārāccaikavākyatā /
tadanurodhena ca parātpara ityatra parāditi jīvaghanaviṣayaṃ draṣṭavyam /
tasmāttu paraḥ puruṣo dhyātavyaśca draṣṭavyaśca bhavati /
tadidamuktam- #na cātra jīvaghanaśabdena prakṛto 'bhidhyātavyaḥ paraḥ puruṣaḥ parāmṛśyateḥ#kintu jīvaghanāt parāt paro yo dhyātavyo draṣṭavyaśca tameva kathayituṃ jīvaghano jīvaḥ /
khilyabhāvamupādhivaśādāpannaḥ sa ucyate /
'sa sāmabhirunnīyate brahmalokam' ityanantaravākyanirdiṣṭo brahmaloko vā jīvaghanaḥ /
sa hi samastakaraṇātmanaḥ sūtrātmano hiraṇyagarbhasya bhagavato nivāsabhūmitayā karaṇaparivṛtānāṃ jīvānāṃ saṃghāta iti bhavati jīvaghanaḥ /

children.translated_text: Thus, it is the supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone — whose locus [of meditation] is the three-syllabled <s>Oṃkāra</s> — that is to be meditated upon.

children.text: ata eva cāsya deśaviśeṣādhigatiḥ phalamupādhimattvāt, krameṇa ca samyagdarśanotpattau muktiḥ /
children.translated_text: And for this very reason, the attainment of a specific location is its fruit, because [<s>Brahman</s> is meditated upon] as conditioned by limiting adjuncts; and through the gradual arising of correct realization, there is liberation.

children.text: 'brahma veda brahmaiva bhavati' iti tu nirupādhibrahmavedanaviṣayā śrutiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'One who knows <s>Brahman</s> becomes <s>Brahman</s> indeed' — this <s>Śruti</s>, however, pertains to the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> without limiting adjuncts.
But the lower <s>Brahman</s> — whose locus [of meditation] is the single-syllabled [<s>Oṃ</s>] — should be understood as the [separate] object of meditation. // 13 //

body.translated_text:
For the fruit of meditation is direct realization (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>).
And direct realization, as a general rule, has reality as its object.
In some cases, however, when a sublating [cognition] intervenes, it may have a superimposed content.
But in the absence of an exception, the general rule cannot be abandoned.
And thus, since [direct realization] has reality as its object, meditation — its cause — also has that reality as its object.
Moreover, when sentential unity is possible through the textual sequel, a division of the sentence is not appropriate.
And sentential unity is possible — because of the recognition of meaning as pertaining to the supreme Person, and because of the syntactic connection [of the clauses].
Accordingly, in 'beyond the supreme' (<s>parātpara</s>), the word 'beyond' (<s>parāt</s>) should be taken as referring to the mass of individual souls (<s>jīvaghana</s>).
Therefore, that supreme Person is both the object of meditation and the object of seeing.
This is what was stated: 'Nor is the supreme Person — who is the subject [of meditation] — referred to by the word "mass of individual souls"'; rather, [the word 'mass of individual souls'] is [used] to indicate the individual soul, in order to speak of that very one — who is to be meditated upon and seen — as beyond the supreme that is beyond the mass of individual souls.
The individual soul is so called.
One who has, through the force of limiting adjuncts, assumed the status of being an incomplete portion (<s>khilya</s>) — he is called [a mass of individual souls].
Or, the 'world of <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>brahmaloka</s>) referred to in the immediately following sentence 'He is led upward by the <s>Sāman</s>s to the world of <s>Brahman</s>' is the mass of individual souls.
For that [world of <s>Brahman</s>], being the abode of the revered <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> — the cosmic Self (<s>sūtrātman</s>) who is the totality of all instruments — is the aggregate of individual souls enclosed by instruments, hence it is a 'mass of individual souls.'

body.text:
#dahara uttarebhyaḥ# /
'atha yadidamāsmin brahmapure daharam' sūkṣmaṃ guhāprāyaṃ puṇḍarīkasaṃniveśaṃ veśma 'daharo 'sminnantarākāśastasminyadantastadanveṣṭavyam' āgamācāryopadeśābhyāṃ śravaṇaṃ ca, tadavirodhinā tarkeṇa mananaṃ ca, tadanveṣaṇam /
tatpūrvakeṇa cādaranairantaryadīrghakālāsevitena dhyānābhyāsaparipākena sākṣātkāro vijñānam /
viśiṣṭaṃ hi tajjñānaṃ pūrvabhyaḥ /
tadicchā vijijñāsanam /
atra saṃśayamāha- #tatreti# /
tatra prathamaṃ tāvadevaṃ saṃśayaḥ-kiṃ daharākāśādanyadeva kiñcidanveṣṭavyaṃ vijijñāsitavyaṃ ca uta daharākāśa iti /
yadāpi daharākāśo 'nveṣṭavyastadāpi kiṃ bhūtākāśa āho śārīra ātmā kiṃ vā paramātmeti /
saṃśayahetuṃ pṛcchati- #kuta iti# /
taddhetumāha #-ākāśabrahmapuraśabdābhyāmiti# /
tatra prathamaṃ tāvadbhūtākāśa eva dahara iti pūrvapakṣayati #-tatrākāśaśabdasya bhūtākāśe rūḍhatvāditi# /

children.text: eṣa tu bahutarottarasaṃdarbhavirodhāttucchaḥ pūrvapakṣa ityaparitoṣeṇa pakṣāntaramālambate pūrvapakṣī-athavā jīvo dahara iti prāptam /
children.translated_text: But since this prima facie view is trivial, being contradicted by the very many subsequent passages, the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> — unsatisfied — takes up another position: Or alternatively, the small [space] is the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>) — this is the prima facie conclusion.
[This is] fitting — this is the meaning.
Therein: 'Because of its being a receptacle, and because of the distinguishing [feature], the body is said to be the city of the individual soul.',
'Not of <s>Brahman</s> — this is fitting, because of the absence of both reasons.' //

body.translated_text:
'The small [space is <s>Brahman</s>], because of the subsequent [indicatory marks]' [BS 1.3.14].
'Now, in this city of <s>Brahman</s>, there is a small (<s>dahara</s>)' — subtle, like a cave — 'dwelling in the shape of a lotus. In that [dwelling] there is a small inner space (<s>antara ākāśa</s>). What is within that is to be sought' — through hearing, by means of scripture and the instruction of a teacher; and through reflection, by means of reasoning that does not contradict that [scripture] — that is the seeking.
And through the maturation of the practice of meditation — undertaken with reverence, continuity, and over a long period, preceded by that [hearing and reflection] — direct realization (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>) is special knowledge (<s>vijñāna</s>).
For that knowledge is distinguished from the preceding [stages].
The desire for that [realization] is the desire to know (<s>vijijñāsana</s>).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the doubt here: 'Therein' — thus.
There, the doubt is first as follows: Is what is to be sought and desired to be known something other than the small space (<s>daharākāśa</s>), or is it the small space itself?
Even when it is [accepted that] the small space is what is to be sought, [the question is:] is it the elemental space (<s>bhūtākāśa</s>), or the embodied self (<s>śārīra ātmā</s>), or the supreme Self (<s>paramātman</s>)?
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] asks the cause of the doubt: 'Whence?' — thus.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states its cause: 'Because of the words "space" and "city of <s>Brahman</s>."'
Therein, first, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] presents the prima facie view that the small [space] is the elemental space: 'Because the word "space" is conventionally established as [referring to] elemental space' — thus.

body.text:
' asādhāraṇyena hi vyapadeśatā bhavanti /
tadyathā kṣitijalapavanabījādisāmagrīsamavadhānajanmāpyaṅkuraḥ śālibījena vyapadiśyate śālyaṅkura iti /
natu kṣityādibhiḥ, teṣāṃ kāryāntareṣvapi sādhāraṇyāt /
tadiha śarīraṃ brahmavikāro 'pi na brahmaṇā vyapadeṣṭavyam, brahmaṇaḥ sarvavikārakāraṇatvenātisādhāraṇyāt /
jīvabhedadharmādharmopārjitaṃ tadityasādhāraṇakāraṇatvājjīvena vyapadiśyata iti yuktam /
apica brahmapura iti saptamyadhikaraṇe smaryate, tenādheyenānena saṃbaddhavyam /
naca brahmaṇaḥ sve mahimni vyavasthitasyānādheyasyādhārasaṃbandha kalpate /
jīvastvārāgramātra ityādheyo bhavati /
tasmādbrahmaśabdo rūḍhiṃ parityajya dehādibṛṃhaṇatayā jīve yaugike vā bhākto vā vyākhyeyaḥ /
caitanyaṃ ca bhaktiḥ /
upādhānānupadhāne tu viśeṣaḥ /
vācyatvaṃ gamyatvam /
syādetat /
jīvasya puraṃ bhavatu śarīraṃ, puṇḍarīkadaragocaratā tvanyasya bhaviṣyati, vatsarājasya pura ivojjayinyāṃ bhaitrasya sajñmetyata āha- #tatra purasvāmina iti# /
ayamarthaḥveśma khalvadhikaraṇamanirdiṣṭhādheyamādheyaviśeṣāpekṣāyāṃ purasvāminaḥ prakṛtatvāttenaivādheyena saṃbaddhaṃ sadanapekṣaṃ nādheyāntareṇa saṃbandhaṃ kalpayati /
nanu tathāpi śarīramevāsya bhogāyatanamiti ko hṛdayapuṇḍarīkasya viseṣo yattadevāsya sajñmetyata āha- #manaupādhikaśca jīva iti# /
nanu mano 'pi calatayā sakaladehavṛtti paryāyeṇetyata āha- #manaśca prāyeṇeti# /
ākāśaśabdaścārūpatvādinā sāmānyena jīve bhāktaḥ /

children.text: astu vā bhūtākāśa evāyamākāśaśabdo 'daharo 'sminnantarākāśaḥ' iti, tathāpyadoṣa ityāha- #na cātra daharasyākāśasyānveṣyatvamiti# /
children.translated_text: Or let this word 'space' in 'the small inner space' be about the elemental space itself; even so, there is no fault — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Nor is it the small space that is to be sought here' — thus.

children.text: evaṃ prāpta ucyate-bhūtākāśasya tāvanna daharatvaṃ, 'yāvanvāyamākāśastāvānoṣo 'ntarhṛdaya ākāśaḥ' ityupamānavirodhāt /
children.translated_text: This being the prima facie conclusion, the established view is stated: First, smallness (<s>daharatva</s>) cannot belong to elemental space, because of the contradiction with the comparison: 'As vast as this external space, so vast is this space within the heart.'
That is as follows: 'By that, its being the thing compared [would be] like the battle of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.',

children.text: agatyā bhedamāropya gatau satyāṃ na yujyate //
children.translated_text: 'When there is no [real] distinction, to superimpose distinction by necessity — when there is a [real] distinction — is not appropriate.' //

body.translated_text:
For designations are based on a distinctive [i.e., non-common] [cause].
Just as a sprout — although born from the aggregate of earth, water, wind, seed, and other conditions — is designated by the seed as a 'rice-sprout.'
But not by earth and the like, since those are common to other products as well.
Similarly here, the body — although a modification of <s>Brahman</s> — should not be designated by <s>Brahman</s>, since <s>Brahman</s>, being the cause of all modifications, is excessively common.
Since [the body] is acquired by the merit and demerit belonging to the differences among individual souls, it is rightly designated by the individual soul, due to [the individual soul's] being the distinctive cause.
Moreover, in the locative expression 'in the city of <s>Brahman</s>,' [the body] is remembered as a container (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>); it must be connected with what is contained (<s>ādheya</s>) [in it].
And for <s>Brahman</s> — established in its own greatness, being uncontainable — a container-relation is not conceivable.
But the individual soul, being the size of an atom (<s>ārāgramātra</s>), is containable.
Therefore, the word '<s>Brahman</s>' — abandoning its conventional meaning — should be explained as applying to the individual soul either through a derivative meaning (<s>yaugika</s>) by virtue of [the individual soul's] nourishing the body and the like, or through a figurative usage (<s>bhakti</s>).
And the figurative usage is [based on] consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>).
The distinction between [the two explanations] is: limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) versus non-limiting adjunct.
Denotation [is one mode of signification]; implication (<s>gamyatva</s>) [is another].
One might say this: Let the body be the city of the individual soul; but the being within the lotus-cave will belong to another — just as, in the city of [King] <s>Vatsarāja</s>, <s>Ujjayinī</s>, the dwelling-place (<s>sajña</s>) of <s>Maitra</s> [can exist]. To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Of the owner of the city' — thus.
The meaning is this: The dwelling (<s>veśma</s>) — which is the container, whose contained entity is unspecified — when there is an expectation for a specific contained entity, since the owner of the city is the topic at hand, it is connected with that very contained entity and, being expectant, does not construct a connection with another contained entity.
But even so, [one may object:] the body itself is the abode of enjoyment for the [individual soul] — so what is distinctive about the lotus of the heart such that it alone is [the individual soul's] dwelling? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'And the individual soul has the mind as its limiting adjunct' — thus.
But [one may further object:] the mind too, being mobile, pervades the entire body in turn. To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'And the mind, for the most part' — thus.
And the word 'space' (<s>ākāśa</s>) is figuratively [applied] to the individual soul, through the general [similarity] of being formless and the like.

body.text:
' asti tu daharākāśasya brahmatvena bhūtākāśādbhedenopamānasya gatiḥ /
na cānavacchinnaparimāṇamavacchinnaṃ bhavati /
tathā satyavacchedānupapatteḥ /
na bhūtākāśamānatvaṃ brahmaṇo 'tra vidhīyate, yena 'jyāyānākāśāt' iti śrutivirodhaḥ syāt, api tu bhūtākāśopamānena puṇḍarīkopādhiprāptaṃ daharatvaṃ nivartyate /

children.text: apica sarva evottare hetavo daharākāśasya bhūtākāśatvaṃ vyāsedhantītyāha- #naca kalpitabheda iti# /
children.translated_text: Moreover, all the subsequent reasons refute the elemental-space-ness of the small space — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Nor [can it be elemental space, since] the postulated distinction...' — thus.
Nor is the small space the individual soul — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Even though the word "Self"...' — thus.
'The body is accepted as the locus of the apprehension of <s>Brahman</s>.',
'By virtue of that distinctive [relation], the body can be the city of <s>Brahman</s>.' //

body.translated_text:
But there is a basis for the comparison with elemental space when the small space has the nature of <s>Brahman</s> and is thus different [from elemental space].
Nor does something of unlimited measure become limited.
For if so, the limitation [itself] would be impossible.
[The comparison] does not prescribe for <s>Brahman</s> the measure of elemental space — for that would contradict the <s>Śruti</s> 'Greater than space' — rather, through the comparison with elemental space, the smallness acquired [by <s>Brahman</s>] through the limiting adjunct of the lotus is removed.

body.text:
' dehe hi brahmopalabhyata ityasādhāraṇatayā deho brahmapuramiti vyapadiśyate, na tu brahmavikāratayā /
tathāca brahmaśabdārtho mukhyo bhavati /
astu vā brahmapuraṃ jīvapuraṃ, tathāpi yathā vatsarājasya pure ujjayinyāṃ maitrasya sajñma bhavati, evaṃ jīvasya pure hṛtpuṇḍarīkaṃ brahmasadanaṃ bhaviṣyati, uttarebhyo brahmaliṅgebhyo brahmaṇo 'vadhāraṇāt /
brahmaṇo hi bādhake pramāṇe balīyasi jīvasya ca sādhake pramāṇe sati brahmaliṅgāni kathañcidabhedavivakṣayā jīve vyākhyāyante /
na ceha brahmaṇo bādhakaṃ pramāṇaṃ, sādhakaṃ vāsti jīvasya /
brahmapuravyapadeśaścopapādito brahmopalabdhisthānatayā /
arbhakaukastvaṃ coktam /
tasmāt sati saṃbhave brahmaṇi, talliṅgānāṃ nābrahmaṇi vyākhyānamucitamiti brahmaiva daharākāśo na jīvabhūtākāśāviti /
śravaṇamananamanuvidya brahmānubhūya caraṇaṃ cārasteṣāṃ kāmeṣu caraṇaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ /
syādetat /
daharākāśasyānveṣyatve siddhe tatra vicāro yujyate, natu tadanveṣṭavyam, apitu tadādhāramanyadeva kiñcidityuktamityanubhāṣate- #yadapyetaditi# /
anubhāṣitaṃ dūṣayati-atra brūma iti /
yadyākāśādhāramanyadanyeṣṭavyaṃ bhavettadevopari vyutpādanīyaṃ, ākāśavyutpādanaṃ tu kkopayujyata ityarthaḥ /
codayati- #nanvetadapīti# /
ākāśakathanamapi tadantarvartivastusadbhāvapradarśanāyaiva /
athākāśaparameva kasmānna bhavatītyata āha- #taṃ cedbrūyariti# /
ācāryeṇa hi 'daharo 'sminnantakarākāśastasminyadantastadanveṣṭavyaṃ tadvāva vijijñāsitavyam' ityupadiṣṭe 'tevāsinākṣiptam-'kiṃ tadatra vidyate yadanveṣṭavyam' /
puṇḍarīkameva tāvatsūkṣmataraṃ, tadavaruddhamākāśaṃ sūkṣmatamam /
tasminsūkṣmatame kimaparamasti /
nāstyevetyarthaḥ /
body.translated_text:
For <s>Brahman</s> is apprehended in the body, and by virtue of that distinctive relation, the body is designated as the city of <s>Brahman</s> — not by virtue of being a modification of <s>Brahman</s>.
And thus the meaning of the word '<s>Brahman</s>' is primary.
Or let 'city of <s>Brahman</s>' be 'city of the individual soul'; even so — just as, in the city of [King] <s>Vatsarāja</s>, <s>Ujjayinī</s>, the dwelling of <s>Maitra</s> exists — so too, in the city of the individual soul, the lotus of the heart will be the abode of <s>Brahman</s>, since <s>Brahman</s> is ascertained from the subsequent <s>Brahman</s>-indicatory marks.
For only when there is a stronger means of knowledge that sublates [the reference to] <s>Brahman</s>, and a means of knowledge that supports [the reference to] the individual soul, are the <s>Brahman</s>-indicatory marks explained as referring to the individual soul through the intention of expressing non-difference.
But here, there is no means of knowledge that sublates <s>Brahman</s>, nor one that supports the individual soul.
And the designation 'city of <s>Brahman</s>' has been justified as [meaning] the locus of the apprehension of <s>Brahman</s>.
And the smallness has been accounted for.
Therefore, when [interpretation as referring to] <s>Brahman</s> is possible, it is not fitting to explain [<s>Brahman</s>-]indicatory marks as referring to non-<s>Brahman</s>. Hence the small space is <s>Brahman</s> alone, not the individual soul or the elemental space.
Having sought [<s>Brahman</s>] through hearing and reflection, having directly experienced <s>Brahman</s>, their conduct (<s>caraṇa</s>) — their movement among desires — means: their movement among those desires becomes [free] — this is the meaning.
One might say this: Once the seeking of the small space is established, the investigation regarding it is justified; but what is to be sought is not that [small space], but rather something else that is its support — this is what was said. [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] restates this: 'As for what [was said]...' — thus.
Having restated it, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes it: 'Here we say' — thus.
If something else supported by space were to be sought, that alone would have to be explained in detail; but the detailed exposition of space would serve no purpose — this is the meaning.
[The opponent] objects: 'But is this not also...' — thus.
The description of space too is only for the purpose of showing the existence of a real entity within it.
But why should it not be about space itself? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'If one were to say that...' — thus.
For when the teacher has taught: 'In that [dwelling] there is a small inner space; what is within that is to be sought, that indeed is to be desired to be known' — [the student's implicit objection is:] What is there in that [space] that is to be sought?
The lotus itself is extremely subtle; the space enclosed within it is the most subtle.
In that most subtle [space], what else can there be?
There is nothing — this is the meaning.

body.text:
tat kimanveṣṭavyamiti /
tadasminnākṣepe parisamāpte samādhānāvasara ācāryasyākāśopamānopakramaṃ vacaḥ-'ubhe asmindyāvāpṛthivī samāhite' iti /
tasmātpuṇḍarīkāvaruddhākāśāśraye dyāvāpṛthivyāvevānveṣṭavye upadiṣṭe, nākāśa ityarthaḥ /
pariharati #-naitadevam /
evaṃ hīti# /
syādetat /
evamevaitat /
no khalvabhyupagamā eva doṣatvena ityata āha- #tatra vākyaśeṣa iti# /
vākyaśeṣo hi daharākāśātmavedanasya phalavattvaṃ brūte, yacca phalavat tatkartavyatayā codyate, yacca kartavyaṃ tadicchitīti 'tadanveṣṭavyaṃ tadvāva vijijñāsitavyam' iti taddaharākāśaviṣayamavatiṣṭhate /
syādetat /
dyāvāpṛthivyāvevātmānau bhaviṣyataḥ, tābhyāmevātmā lakṣayiṣyate, ākāśaśabdavat /
tataścākāśādhārau tāveva parāmṛśyate ityata āha- #asminkāmāḥ samāhitāḥ#pratiṣṭhitāḥ /
#eṣa ātmāpahatapāpmeti# /
anena #prakṛtaṃ dyāvāpṛthivyādisamādhānādhāramākāśamākṛṣya# /
dyāvāpṛthivyabhidhānavyavahitamapīti śeṣaḥ /

children.text: nanu satyakāmajñānasyaitatphalaṃ, tadanantaraṃ nirdeśāt, na tu daharākāśavedanasyetyata āha- #samuccayārthena caśabdeneti# /
children.translated_text: But [one may object:] this fruit belongs to the knowledge of '<s>satyakāma</s>' (one whose desires are real), since it is stated immediately after that [passage], not to the meditation on the small space (<s>dahara-ākāśa</s>). To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'By the word "<s>ca</s>" in the sense of aggregation' (<s>samuccayārthena caśabdena</s>).

children.text: 'asminkāmāḥ' iti ca 'eṣaḥ' iti caikavacanāntaṃ na dve dyāvāpṛthivyau parāmnaṣṭumarhatīti daharākāśa eva parāmraṣṭavya iti samudāyārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In this [space] are the desires' and 'this' — being singular in number — cannot refer to the two [separate entities], heaven and earth; rather, it is the small space (<s>dahara-ākāśa</s>) alone that must be referred to — this is the aggregate meaning.

children.text: tadanena krameṇa 'tasminyadantaḥ' ityatra tacchabdo 'nantaramapyākāśamatilaṅgasya hṛtpuṇḍarīkaṃ parāmṛśatatyuktaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: By this reasoning, it is stated that in '<s>tasmin yad antaḥ</s>' (that which is within it), the word '<s>tad</s>' (that), even though passing over the immediately [mentioned] space, refers to the lotus of the heart (<s>hṛt-puṇḍarīka</s>).
The meaning is: that which is the inner space within that lotus of the heart — that is to be sought. // 14 //

body.translated_text:
What then is to be sought? — to this objection, when it has been completed, the teacher's words — introduced by the comparison with space — serve as the resolution: 'In it, both heaven and earth are contained.'
Therefore, heaven and earth — which rest upon the space enclosed in the lotus — are themselves taught as what is to be sought, not the space — this is the meaning.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] resolves: 'This is not so. For thus...' — thus.
One might say this: It is exactly so.
Surely the concessions themselves are not [being presented as] defects — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'In that regard, the textual sequel...' — thus.
For the textual sequel states the fruitfulness of the knowledge of the small space as the Self; and what is fruitful is urged as what is to be done; and what is to be done is desired — hence 'that is to be sought, that indeed is to be desired to be known' stands as referring to the small space.
One might say this: Heaven and earth alone will be the Selves; [<s>Brahman</s>] will be indicated by them alone — like the word 'space.' And thus those two — being [merely] referred to — as resting upon space are what is being pointed to. To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'In it, desires are contained' — i.e., established.
'This is the Self, free from sin' — by this, 'having drawn back to the [small] space — which is the support into which heaven, earth, and the rest are resolved — even though separated by the intervening mention of heaven and earth' — this is the remainder.

body.text:
#gatiśabdābhyāṃ tathāhi dṛṣṭaṃ liṅgaṃ ca# /
uttarebhya ityasya prapañcaḥ etameva daharākāśaṃ prakramya batāho kaṣṭamidaṃ vartate jantūnāṃ tattvāvabodhavikalānāṃ, yadebhiḥ svādhīnamapi brahma na prāpyate /
tadyathā cirantananirūḍhanibiḍamalapihitānāṃ kaladhautaśakalānāṃ pathi patitānāmuparyapari saṃcaradbhirapi pānthairdhanāyadbhirgrāvakhṇḍanivahavibhrameṇaitāni nopādiyanta ityabisaṃdhimatī sādbhutamiva sakhedamiva śrutaḥ pravartate-'imāḥ sarvāḥ prajā aharahargacchantya etaṃ brahmalokaṃ na vindanti' iti /
svāpakāle hi sarva evāyaṃ vidvānavidvāṃśca jīvaloko hṛtpuṇḍarīkāśrayaṃ daharākāśākhyaṃ brahmalokaṃ prāpto 'pyanādyavidyātamaḥ paṭalapihitadṛṣṭitayā brahmabhūyamāpanno 'hamasmīti na veda /
so 'yaṃ brahmalokaśabdastadgatiśca pratyahaṃ jīvalokasya daharākāśasyaiva brahmarūpalokatāmāhatuḥ /
tadetadāha bhāṣyakāraḥ- #itaśca parameśvara eva daharo yasmāddaharavākyaśeṣa iti# /
tadanena gatiśabdau vyākhyātau /
'tathāhi dṛṣṭam' iti sūtrāvayavaṃ vyācaṣṭe- #tathāhyaraharjīvānāmiti# /
vede ca loke ca dṛṣṭam /
yadyapi suṣuptasya brahmabhāve laukikaṃ na pramāṇāntaramasti, tathāpi vaidikīmeva prasiddhiṃ sthāpayitumucyate, īdṛśī nāmeyaṃ vaidiko prasiddhiryalloke 'pi gīyata iti /
yathā śrutyantare yathā ca loke tatheha brahmalokaśabdo 'pīti yojanā /
'liṅgaṃ ca' iti sūtrāvayavavyākhyānaṃ codyamukhenāvatārayati- #nanu kamalāsanalokamapīti# /
pariharati- #gamayedyadi brahmaṇo loka iti# /
atra tāvanniṣādasthapatinyāyena ṣaṣṭhīsamāsātkarmadhārayo balīyāniti sthitameva, tathāpīha ṣaṣṭhisamāsanirākaraṇena karmadhārayasamāsasthāpanāya liṅgamapyadhikamastīti tadapyuktaṃ sūtrakāreṇa /

children.text: tathāhi-lokavedaprasiddhāharaharbrahmalokaprāptyabhidhānameva liṅgaṃ kamalāsanalokaprāptervipakṣādasaṃbhavādvyāvartamānaṃ ṣaṣṭhīsamāsāśaṅkāṃ vyāvartayaddaharākāśaprāptāvevāvatiṣṭhate, naca daharākāśo brahmaṇo lokaḥ kintu tadbrahmeti brahma ca tallokaśceti karmadhārayaḥ siddho bhavati /
children.translated_text: This is as follows: The very statement of the daily attainment of <s>Brahma-loka</s> — well-known in the world and in the <s>Veda</s> — being an indicatory mark that excludes the world of <s>Brahmā</s> [i.e., <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>'s world, which is not reached daily] and confines itself to the attainment of the small space — establishes that the small space is not a world belonging to <s>Brahman</s>, but rather is itself <s>Brahman</s> and itself a world — and the appositional compound (<s>karmadhāraya</s>) is thus established.
'<s>Loka</s>' (world) [means:] that which is seen (<s>lokyate</s>).
That which resides in the lotus of the heart is indeed seen [there].

children.text: yatkhalu puṇḍarīkasthamantaḥkaraṇaṃ tasminviśuddhe pratyāhṛtetarakaraṇānāṃ yogināṃ nirmala ivodake candramaso bimbamatisvacchaṃ caitanyaṃ jyotiḥsvarūpaṃ brahmāvalokyata iti //15 //
children.translated_text: For when the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) stationed in the lotus [of the heart] becomes purified, for <s>yogin</s>s whose other sense organs have been withdrawn — as the reflection of the moon in pure water — the exceedingly transparent consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>), whose nature is luminosity (<s>jyotis</s>) — [which is] <s>Brahman</s> — is seen. // 15 //

body.translated_text:
'Because of the [words] "going" and "world" (<s>gatiśabdābhyām</s>); for thus it is observed (<s>dṛṣṭam</s>); and because of the indicatory mark (<s>liṅgam ca</s>)' [BS 1.3.15].
The elaboration of 'from the subsequent [statements]' (<s>uttarebhyaḥ</s>): Having introduced this very small space, [the <s>Śruti</s>] proceeds — alas! how pitiful is this condition of creatures who lack the realization of truth, that <s>Brahman</s> — though within their own reach — is not attained by them!
Just as gold pieces fallen on the path — covered by dense grime that has been long accumulated — are not picked up even by travelers passing repeatedly over them, [mistaking them] for a heap of gravel-fragments — with such sympathetic intent, the <s>Śruti</s> proceeds as if with wonder, as if with sorrow:
'All these beings, day after day, go to this <s>Brahma-loka</s> (world of <s>Brahman</s>) and do not find it.'
For at the time of sleep, this entire world of living beings — learned and unlearned alike — though having reached the <s>Brahma-loka</s> called the small space (<s>dahara-ākāśa</s>), which has its abode in the lotus of the heart — having attained the state of <s>Brahman</s>, yet with vision covered by the veil of beginningless <s>avidyā</s> — does not know 'I have become <s>Brahman</s>.'
This word '<s>Brahma-loka</s>' (world of <s>Brahman</s>) and the going to it by the world of living beings every day — these declare that the small space alone has the nature of a world that is <s>Brahman</s>.
This is what the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (commentator) states: 'And from this, the supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>) alone is the small [space], since the remainder of the <s>dahara</s>-passage [supports this].'
By this, [the words] 'going' and 'world' have been explained.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] glosses the <s>sūtra</s>-component 'for thus it is observed' (<s>tathāhi dṛṣṭam</s>): 'For thus, day after day, for the living beings...'
It is observed in the <s>Veda</s> and in the world.
Although there is no other worldly means of knowledge for [establishing] the <s>Brahman</s>-nature of one who is in deep sleep, nevertheless, this is stated in order to establish the Vedic well-knownness: such indeed is this Vedic well-knownness that it is even celebrated in the world.
Just as in another <s>Śruti</s>, and just as in the world — so too here, the word '<s>Brahma-loka</s>' also [functions] — this is the syntactic connection.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] introduces the gloss on the <s>sūtra</s>-component 'and the indicatory mark' (<s>liṅgam ca</s>) through the objection: 'But surely, even the world of <s>Brahmā</s> (<s>Kamalāsana</s>)...' (<s>nanu kamalāsanalokam api</s>).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] resolves: 'It would, if "<s>Brahman</s>'s world" [were the meaning]' (<s>gamayed yadi brahmaṇo loka iti</s>).
Here, by the <s>Niṣāda-Sthapati</s> principle, the appositional compound (<s>karmadhāraya</s>) is stronger than the genitive compound (<s>ṣaṣṭhī-samāsa</s>) — this is already established. Nevertheless, here, in addition to dismissing the genitive compound and establishing the appositional compound, there is a further indicatory mark — and this too is stated by the author of the <s>sūtra</s>s.

body.text: #dhṛteśca mahimno 'syāsminnupalabdheḥ# /

children.translated_text: The word '<s>dhṛti</s>' (sustaining) in the <s>sūtra</s> is a nominal derivative (<s>bhāva-vacana</s>) [meaning 'the act of sustaining'].
And because of sustaining, the supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>) alone is the small space (<s>dahara-ākāśa</s>).

children.text: kutaḥ, asya dhāraṇalakṣaṇasya mahimno 'sminneveśvara eva śrutyantareṣūpalabdheḥ /
children.translated_text: Why? Because this greatness — characterized by sustaining — is found (<s>upalabdhi</s>) in this very [supreme Lord] alone, in other <s>Śruti</s> passages.
The <s>Bhāṣya</s> of this is explained by the running gloss (<s>nigadavyākhyāna</s>). // 16 //

body.translated_text: 'And because of sustaining (<s>dhṛteḥ</s>) and its greatness (<s>mahimnaḥ</s>) being found in this alone (<s>asmin upalabdheḥ</s>)' [BS 1.3.16].

body.text:
#prasiddheśca# /
na ceyamākāśaśabdasya brahmaṇi lakṣyamāṇavibhutvādiguṇayogādvṛttiḥ sāṃpratikī, yathā rathāṅganāmā cakravāka iti lakṣaṇā, kintvatyantanirūḍheti sūtrārthaḥ /
ye tvākāśaśabdo brahmaṇyapi mukhya eva nabhovadityācakṣate, taiḥ 'anyāyaścānekārthatvam' iti ca 'ananyalabhyaḥ śabdārthaḥ' iti ca mīmāṃsakānāṃ mudrābhedaḥ /
kṛtaḥ /
labhyate hyākāśaśabdādvibhutvādiguṇayogenāpi brahma /
naca brahmaṇyeva mukhyo nabhasi tu tenaiva guṇayogena vartsyatīti vācyam /
lokādhīnāvadhāraṇatvena śabdārthasaṃbandhasya vaidikapadārthapratyayasya tatpūrvakatvāt /
nanu 'yāvanvā ayamākāśastāvāneṣo 'ntarhṛdaya ākāśaḥ' iti vyatirekanirdeśānna lakṣaṇā yuktā /
nahi bhavati gaṅgāyāḥ kūlamiti vivakṣite gaṅgāyā gaṅgeti prayogaḥ
body.translated_text:
'And because of well-knownness (<s>prasiddheḥ</s>)' [BS 1.3.17].
And this usage of the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' (space) for <s>Brahman</s> is not a current figurative usage (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) — by virtue of the connection with qualities such as all-pervasiveness and the like that are figuratively attributed — as [in the case of] '<s>rathāṅganāmā cakravākaḥ</s>' (the <s>cakravāka</s> bird is named 'chariot-wheel') where the figurative usage [is current]; rather, it is extremely well-established (<s>nirūḍha</s>) — this is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>.
But those who say that the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' is primary even in [its application to] <s>Brahman</s>, just like [its application to] space (<s>nabhas</s>) — by them, the disagreement between the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s>s' [principles] 'The other [interpretation] is [justified] by the multiplicity of meanings' and 'The meaning of a word is not obtainable from another [source]' is resolved.
For <s>Brahman</s> too is obtainable from the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' by the connection with qualities such as all-pervasiveness.
Nor should it be said that [the word] is primary only in [reference to] <s>Brahman</s> and would apply to [physical] space (<s>nabhas</s>) by the same quality-connection.
Because the relation of word and meaning is determined through [its dependence on] worldly usage, and the Vedic cognition of word-meaning is preceded by that.
But [one may object:] the statement of distinction — 'As extensive as this space is, so extensive is this space within the heart' — shows that [the two are different], so figurative usage (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) is not appropriate.
For indeed, when the intended meaning is 'the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,' the usage '<s>Gaṅgā</s>' for '<s>Gaṅgā</s>' [i.e., for the bank] does not occur [in the same form].

body.text:
tatkimidānīṃ 'paurṇamāsyāṃ paurṇamāsyā yajeta' 'amāvasyāyāmamāvāsyayā' ityasādhurvaidikaḥ prayogaḥ /
naca paurṇamāsyāmāvāsyāśabdāvagneyādiṣu mukhyau /
yaccoktaṃyatra śabdārthapratītistatra lakṣaṇā' yatra punaranyārthe niścite śabdāprayogastatra vācakatvameveti, tadayuktam /
ubhayasyāpi vyabhicārāt /

children.translated_text: From the word in '<s>somena yajeta</s>' (one should sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>), a meaning is comprehended.
And therein, nothing is figurative apart from the sentence-meaning.

children.text: naca 'ya evaṃ vidvān paurṇamāsīṃ yajeta ya evaṃ vidvānamāvāsyām' ityatra paurṇamāsyamāvāsyāśabdau na lākṣaṇikau /
children.translated_text: Nor in 'One who knows thus should sacrifice at the full moon; one who knows thus [should sacrifice] at the new moon' are the words '<s>paurṇamāsī</s>' and '<s>amāvāsyā</s>' non-figurative.
Therefore, all this is inconclusive. // 17 //

body.translated_text:
Then what? Is the Vedic usage in 'At the full moon, with the full-moon [sacrifice], one should sacrifice,' 'At the new moon, with the new-moon [sacrifice]' improper?
Nor are the words '<s>paurṇamāsī</s>' and '<s>amāvāsyā</s>' primary in [their application to] the <s>Āgneya</s> and other [offerings].
And the statement — 'Where the comprehension of the word's meaning [occurs], there is figurative usage (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>)'; 'But where, having ascertained another meaning, there is no usage of the word — there it is denotative (<s>vācakatva</s>) itself' — that is inappropriate.
Because of the deviation of both [principles from their intended scope].

body.text:
#itaraparāmarśātsa iti cennāsaṃbhavāt# /
samyak prasīdatyasmin jīvo viṣayendriyasaṃyogajanitaṃ kāluṣyaṃ jahātīti suṣuptiḥ saṃprasādo jīvasyāvasthābedaḥ na brahmaṇaḥ tathā śarīrātsamutthānamapi śarīrāśrayasya jīvasya, natvanāśrayasya brahmaṇaḥ /
tasmādyathā pūrvoktairvākyaśeṣagatairliṅgairbrahmāvagamyate dahārākāśaḥ, evaṃ vākyaśeṣagatābhyāmeva saṃprasādasamutthānābhyāṃ daharākāśo jīvaḥ kasmānnāvagamyate /
tasmānnāsti vinigamaneti śaṅkārthaḥ /
'nāsaṃbhavāt' /
body.translated_text:
'If it be said that [the small space refers to] the other [i.e., the individual soul], because of a reference to it — no, because of impossibility' [BS 1.3.18].
[One might object:] In deep sleep, the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>) becomes composed (<s>saṃprasāda</s>) — it becomes well-settled (<s>samyak prasīdati</s>), i.e., it abandons the turbidity generated by the contact of objects and senses — [hence] <s>saṃprasāda</s> (composure in deep sleep) is a state of the individual soul, not of <s>Brahman</s>. Likewise, the rising up from the body (<s>samutthāna</s>) is [the rising] of the individual soul that has the body as its support, not of <s>Brahman</s>, which has no support.
Therefore, just as from the previously stated indicatory marks belonging to the remainder of the passage, the small space is understood to be <s>Brahman</s>, why should not the small space be understood as the individual soul from these two — <s>saṃprasāda</s> and <s>samutthāna</s> — which also belong to the remainder of the passage?
Therefore, there is no determinate conclusion — this is the purport of the objection.
'No, because of impossibility' (<s>nāsaṃbhavāt</s>).

children.text: saṃprasādasamutthanābhyāṃ hi jīvaparāmarśo na jīvaparaḥ, kintu tadīyatāttvikarūpabrahmabhāvaparaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the reference to the individual soul through <s>saṃprasāda</s> and <s>samutthāna</s> is not oriented toward the individual soul [as such], but toward its true nature as <s>Brahman</s> — the real form [of the <s>jīva</s>].

children.text: tathā caiṣa parāmarśo brahmaṇa eveti na saṃprasādasamutthāne jīvaliṅgam, api tu brahmaṇa eva tādarthyādityagre vakṣyate /
children.translated_text: And thus this reference is to <s>Brahman</s> alone — hence <s>saṃprasāda</s> and <s>samutthāna</s> are not indicatory marks of the individual soul, but rather of <s>Brahman</s> alone, because of their purposefulness [only with reference to <s>Brahman</s>] — this will be stated later.

But the illustrations such as the comparison with space and the like are invariably connected with <s>Brahman</s> and oriented toward <s>Brahman</s> — hence there is a determinate conclusion — this is the meaning. // 18 //

body.text:
#uttarāccedāvirbhūtasvarūpastu# /
daharākāśameva prakṛtyopākhyāyate-yamātmānamanviṣya sarvaṃśca lokānāpnoti sarvāṃśca kāmān, tamātmānaṃ vividiṣantau surāsurarājavindrivirocanau samitpāṇī prajāpatiṃ varivasitumājagmatuḥ /
body.translated_text:
'If [it be said that the individual soul is meant] from the subsequent [passage] — [we say:] no, [the small space is <s>Brahman</s>], because its own nature has become manifest' [BS 1.3.19].
The very small space is further elaborated by a story: 'That Self which is to be sought, [by which one] having searched, attains all worlds and all desires' — desiring to know that Self, <s>Indra</s>, the king of the gods, and <s>Virocana</s>, [the king of the <s>Asura</s>s], came to <s>Prajāpati</s> to serve him, with fuel-sticks in hand.

body.text:
āgatya ca dvātriṃśataṃ varṣāṇi tatparicaraṇaparau brahmacaryamūṣatuḥ /
athaitau prajāpatiruvāca, kiṅkāmāvihasthau yuvāmiti /
tāvūcatuḥ, ya ātmāpahatapāpmā tamāvāṃ vividiṣāva iti /
tataḥ prajāpatiruvāca, ya eṣo 'kṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyate eṣa ātmāpahatapāpmatvādiguṇa, yadvijñānātsarvalokakāmāvāptiḥ /
etadamatṛtamabhayam /
athaitacchutvaitāvaprakṣīṇakalmaṣāvaraṇatayā chāyāpuruṣaṃ jagṛhatuḥ /
prajāpatiṃ ca prapacchatuḥ, atha yo 'yaṃ bhagavo 'psu dṛśyate, yaścādarśo, yaśca svaṅgādau katama eteṣvasau atavaika eva sarveṣviti /
tametayoḥ śrutvā praśnaṃ prajāpatirbatāho sudūraramudbhāntāvetau, asmābhirakṣisthāna ātmopadiṣṭaḥ, etau ca chāyāpuruṣaṃ pratipannau, tadyadi vayaṃ bhrāntau stha iti brūmastataḥ svātmani samāropitapāṇḍityabahumānau vimānitau santau daurmanasyena yathāvadupadeśaṃ na gṛhṇīyātām, ityanayorāśayamanurudhya yathārthaṃ grāhayiṣyāma ityabisaṃdhimānpratyuvāca, udaśarava ātmānamavekṣethāmasminyatpaśyathastadbrūtamiti /
tau ca dṛṣṭvā saṃtuṣṭahṛdayau nābrūtām /
atha prajāpitiretau viparītagrāhiṇau mā bhūtāmityāśayavānpapraccha, kimatrāpaśyatāmiti /
tau hocatuḥ, yathaivāvamicirabrahmacaryacaraṇasamupajātāyatanakhalomādimantāvevamāvayoḥ pratirūpakaṃ nakhalomādimadudaśarāve 'paśyāveti /
punaretayośchāyātmavibhramamapaninīṣuryathaiva hi chāyāpuruṣa upajanāpāyadharmābhedenāvagamyamāna ātmalakṣaṇavirahānnātmaivevamevedaṃ śarīraṃ nātmā, kintu tato bhinnamityanvayavyatirekābhyāmetau jānīyātāmityāśayavān prajāpatiruvāca, sādhvalaṅkṛtau suvasanau pariṣkṛtau bhūtvā punarudaśarāve paśyatamākmānaṃ, yaccātra paśyathastadbratamiti /
tau ca sādhvalaṅkṛtau suvasanau chinnanakhalomānau bhūtvā tathaiva cakratuḥ /
punaśca prajāpatināpṛṣṭau tāmeva chāyāmātmānamūcatuḥ /
tadupaśrutya prajāpatiraho batādyāpi na praśānta enayorvibhramaḥ, tadyathābhimatamevātmatattvaṃ kathayāmi tāvat /
kālena kalmaṣe kṣīṇe 'smadvacanasaṃdarbhapaurvāparyalocanayātmatattvaṃ pratipatsyete svayameveti matvovāca, eṣa ātmaitadamṛtamabhayametadbrahmeti /
tayorvirocano dehānupātitvācchāyāyā deha evātmatattvamiti matvā nijasadanamāgatya tathaivāsurānupadiśyate /
devendrastvaprāptanijasadano 'dhvanyeva kiñcidvaralakalmaṣatayā chāyātmani śarīrahuṇadoṣānuvidhāyini taṃ taṃ doṣaṃ paribhāvayan nāhamatra chāyātmadarśane bhogyaṃ paśyāmīti prajāpatisamīpaṃ samitpāṇiḥ punarevevāya āgataśca prajāpatināgamanakāraṇaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ pathi paribāvitaṃ jagad /
prajāpatistu suvyākhyātamapyātmatattvamakṣīṇakalmaṣāvaraṇatayā nāgrahīḥ, tatpunarapi tatprakṣayāyā carāparāṇi dvātriṃśataṃ varṣāṇi brahmacaryaṃ, atha prakṣīṇakalmaṣāya te ahametamevātmānaṃ bhūyo 'nuvyākhyāyasyāmītyavocat /
sa ca tathā caritatbrahmacaryaḥ surendraḥ prajāpatimupasasāda /
upapannāya cāsmai prajāpatirvyacaṣṭe, ya ātmāpahatapāpmadilakṣaṇo 'kṣaṇa darśitaḥ so 'yaṃ ya eṣa svapne mahiyamāno vanitādibhiranekadhā svapnopabhogān bhuñjāno virahatīti /
asminnapi devendro bhayaṃ dadarśa /
yadyapyayaṃ chāyāpuruṣavanna śarīradharmānanupatati, tathāpi śokabhayādivividhabādhānubhavānna tatrāpyasti svastiprāptirityuktavati maghavati punaraparāṇi cara dvātriṃśataṃ varṣāṇi svacchaṃ brahmacaryamidānīmapyakṣīṇakalmaṣo 'sītyūce prajāpatiḥ /
athāsminnevaṅkāramupasanne maghavati prajāpatiruvāca, ya eṣa ātmāpahatapāpmādiguṇo darśito 'kṣiṇi ca svapne ca sa eṣa yo viṣayendriyasaṃyogavirahātprasannaḥ suṣuptāvasthāyāmiti /
atrāpi nendro nirvavāra /
yathā hi jāgradvā svapnagato vāyamahamasmīti imāni bhūtāmani ceti vijānāti naivaṃ suṣuptaḥ kiñcidapi vedayate, tadā khalvayamacetayamāno 'bhāvaṃ prāpta iva bhavati /
tadiha kā nirvṛtiriti /
eva muktavati maghavati batādyāpi na te kalmaṣakṣayo 'bhūt /
tatpunaraparāṇi cara pañca varṣāṇi brahmacaryamityavocatprajāpatiḥ /
tadevamasya maghonastribhiḥ paryāyairvyatīyuḥ ṣaṇṇāvativarṣāṇi /
caturthe ca paryāye pañca varṣāṇītyekottaraṃ śataṃ varṣāṇi brahmacaryaṃ carataḥ sahasrākṣasya sopedire /
body.translated_text: Having arrived, the two (<s>Indra</s> and <s>Virocana</s>) devoted to serving him, observed <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship) for thirty-two years. Then <s>Prajāpati</s> said to them, 'With what desire do you two dwell here?' They replied, 'We wish to know that <s>Ātman</s> (Self) who is free from evil.' Thereupon <s>Prajāpati</s> said, 'The person who is seen in the eye — he is the <s>Ātman</s>, possessing the qualities of being free from evil and so forth, through whose knowledge one attains all worlds and desires. This is the immortal, the fearless.' Having heard this, these two, because the veil of their impurities had not yet been destroyed, grasped it as referring to the shadow-person (<s>chāyāpuruṣa</s>). They asked <s>Prajāpati</s>, 'O Lord, the one who is seen in water, in a mirror, and in one's own limbs and such — which one among these is he, or is he one and the same in all?' Hearing their question, <s>Prajāpati</s> thought, 'Alas, these two have gone far astray! I taught the <s>Ātman</s> as being located in the eye, yet they have taken it to mean the shadow-person. If I were to say "you are deluded," then, having their pride in their self-attributed learning wounded, they would become dejected and would not properly receive the teaching.' Thus, accommodating their disposition, intending to lead them to the truth gradually, he replied, 'Look at yourselves in a pan of water, and whatever you see there, tell me.' They looked and, with satisfied hearts, said nothing. Then <s>Prajāpati</s>, with the intention 'let these two not remain holders of wrong understanding,' asked, 'What did you see there?' They said, 'Just as we ourselves, through long practice of <s>brahmacarya</s>, have come to possess well-formed bodies with nails, hair, and so forth, so too we saw our exact likeness, complete with nails, hair, and the rest, in the water-pan.' Wishing again to remove their delusion about the shadow-self — for just as the shadow-person, being apprehended without any difference from the properties of origination and destruction, lacks the marks of the <s>Ātman</s> and is therefore not the <s>Ātman</s> itself, so too this body is not the <s>Ātman</s>, but rather something different from it; intending that these two should know this through the methods of agreement and difference (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>) — <s>Prajāpati</s> said, 'Having adorned yourselves well, dressed in fine garments, and groomed yourselves, look again at yourselves in the water-pan, and tell me what you see there.' The two, having adorned themselves well, dressed in fine garments, with nails and hair trimmed, did exactly so. When asked again by <s>Prajāpati</s>, they declared that very shadow to be the <s>Ātman</s>. Hearing this, <s>Prajāpati</s> thought, 'Alas, even now their delusion has not subsided. Well then, let me state the truth of the <s>Ātman</s> as I understand it. In time, when their impurities have diminished, they will realize the truth of the <s>Ātman</s> by themselves through reflecting on the sequential coherence of my words.' Thinking thus, he said, 'This is the <s>Ātman</s>, this is the immortal, the fearless, this is <s>Brahman</s>.' Of the two, <s>Virocana</s>, thinking that the truth of the <s>Ātman</s> is indeed the body since the shadow follows the body, returned to his own abode and taught the <s>Asuras</s> accordingly. But <s>Indra</s>, the lord of the gods, not yet having reached his own abode, while still on the way, because his impurities were only slightly diminished, reflecting on the various defects of the shadow-self which conforms to the defects of the body, thought, 'I do not see any object of enjoyment in this teaching of the shadow-self,' and returned again to <s>Prajāpati</s> with fuel in hand. When he arrived and was asked by <s>Prajāpati</s> the reason for his return, he described what he had contemplated on the way. <s>Prajāpati</s> then said, 'You did not grasp the truth of the <s>Ātman</s>, though it was well explained, because the veil of your impurities had not yet been destroyed. Therefore, practice <s>brahmacarya</s> again for another thirty-two years for its removal, and then, when your impurities have been destroyed, I shall explain that very <s>Ātman</s> to you again.' He (<s>Indra</s>), having thus practiced <s>brahmacarya</s>, approached <s>Prajāpati</s> again. To him who had duly arrived, <s>Prajāpati</s> explained: 'The <s>Ātman</s> who was shown as possessing the marks of being free from evil and so forth, as being in the eye — he is the one who, in dreams, moves about gloriously, enjoying various dream-pleasures with women and others, and then becomes free of them.' In this too, <s>Indra</s> the lord of the gods saw a defect. For although this dream-self does not follow the properties of the body like the shadow-person, nevertheless, because of the experience of various afflictions such as sorrow and fear, there is no well-being attained even there. When <s>Maghavān</s> (<s>Indra</s>) said this, <s>Prajāpati</s> replied, 'Practice another thirty-two years of pure <s>brahmacarya</s>, for even now your impurities have not been destroyed.' Then, when <s>Maghavān</s> had duly arrived after this observance, <s>Prajāpati</s> said, 'The <s>Ātman</s> who was shown as possessing qualities such as freedom from evil, both in the eye and in dream — he is the one who, in deep sleep (<s>suṣupti</s>), is serene due to the absence of contact between the senses and their objects.' Even here, <s>Indra</s> was not satisfied. For just as in waking or in dream one knows 'I am this person, these are beings,' in deep sleep one is not aware of anything at all; then, being unconscious, one seems to have reached non-existence. What happiness is there in that? When <s>Maghavān</s> spoke thus, <s>Prajāpati</s> said, 'Alas, even now your impurity has not been destroyed. Therefore practice another five years of <s>brahmacarya</s>.' Thus, in three cycles, ninety-six years passed for <s>Maghavān</s> (<s>Indra</s>). And in the fourth cycle, with five more years — making one hundred and one years of <s>brahmacarya</s> for the thousand-eyed one — the teaching was completed.

body.text:
athāsmai brahmacaryasaṃpadunmṛditakalmaṣāya maghavate ya eṣo 'kṣiṇi yaśca svapne suṣupte anusyūta eṣa ātmāpahatapāpmādiguṇako darśitaḥ, tameva 'maghavan martyaṃ vai śarīram' ityādinā vispaṣṭaṃ vyācaṣṭe prajāpatiḥ /
ayamasyābhisaṃdhiḥ-yāvatkiñcita sukhaṃ duḥkhamāgamāpāyi tatsarvaṃ śarīrendriyāntaḥkaraṇasaṃbandhi, na tvātmanaḥ. sa punaretāneva śarīrādīn anādyavidyāvāsanāvaśādātmatvenābipratītastadgatena sukhaduḥkhena tadvantamātmānamabhimanyamāno 'nutapyate /
yadā tvayamapahatapāpmatvādilakṣaṇamudāsīnamātmānaṃ caitanyānandaghane rūpe vyavasthitaḥ samastalokakāmān prāpto bhavati /
body.translated_text: Then, to <s>Maghavān</s> (<s>Indra</s>), whose impurities had been crushed by the fulfillment of <s>brahmacarya</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s> had shown the <s>Ātman</s> possessing qualities such as freedom from evil, as being interwoven in the eye, in dream, and in deep sleep. That very <s>Ātman</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s> now explains clearly beginning with '<s>Maghavan</s>, the body is indeed mortal' and so forth. The purport of this is as follows: whatever happiness or suffering there is that comes and goes — all of that belongs to the body, senses, and internal organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), not to the <s>Ātman</s>. However, due to beginningless <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and its <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions), one falsely identifies these very body and other things as the Self, and imagining the Self to possess the happiness and suffering that belong to them, one grieves. But when this one recognizes the <s>Ātman</s> as indifferent, characterized by freedom from evil and the rest, established in the form that is a mass of consciousness and bliss (<s>caitanyānandaghana</s>), then one attains all worldly desires.

children.text: etasyaiva hi paramānandasya mātrāḥ sarve kāmāḥ /
children.translated_text: For all desires are but fractions (<s>mātrāḥ</s>) of this very supreme bliss (<s>paramānanda</s>).
Suffering, however, is a fabrication of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), and therefore the knower does not experience it.
'For those who have not practiced the <s>Upaniṣads</s>, delusion arises in this world.'
For their benefit, I have set forth this narrative (<s>upākhyāna</s>).

body.translated_text:
Thus, from the established subsequent textual sequence of the <s>Prājāpatya</s> (teaching of <s>Prajāpati</s>), in the eye, in dream, in deep sleep, and in the fourth stage — through 'This serene being, having risen from this body' — the <s>Śruti</s> declares the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>) alone as endowed with qualities such as being free from sin (<s>apahatapāpman</s>) etc.
For the supreme [<s>Brahman</s>], a location in the eye is not possible.
Nor is there a connection with states such as dream etc.
Nor is there a rising from the body.
Therefore, that which possesses all of these — that is declared by <s>Śruti</s> as endowed with the qualities of being free from sin etc.
And since all of these pertain to the <s>jīva</s>, it is the <s>jīva</s> alone that is declared by <s>Śruti</s> as endowed with the qualities of being free from sin etc. — hence the supreme <s>Brahman</s> is not indicated by the qualities of being free from sin etc.
But it was stated that being free from sin etc. is impossible for the <s>jīva</s>.
[The objector replies:] It will be so by virtue of the scriptural statement.
What can a [scriptural] statement not accomplish?
There is no excessive burden for a statement.
Nor is there a contradiction with another means of knowledge.
For the <s>jīva</s> is not by nature sinful etc.; rather, sin etc. arises for it from the origination of speech, intellect, and body, and in the absence of body etc., it does not exist — like smoke in the absence of fire — this is the intent of the objection.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes this: 'To him one should reply — but [the Self] whose true nature has become manifest' etc.
The intent is this: Through the consideration of the textual sequence, the purport of the <s>Upaniṣad</s>s is understood as follows — <s>Brahman</s> is one, non-dual, pure, enlightened, free, and without phenomenal elaboration, and everything other than it is its apparent transformation (<s>vivarta</s>), like a snake upon a rope.
Accordingly, the <s>jīva</s> too is a form of <s>Brahman</s> conditioned by the body, senses, and other limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>s) imagined by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), and not its intrinsic nature.
This being so, the qualities of being free from sin etc. are not possible in that [<s>jīva</s> as conditioned by] the limiting adjunct of <s>avidyā</s>.
But in the one whose <s>Brahman</s>-nature has become manifest, free from limiting adjuncts — [those qualities] are possible for <s>Brahman</s> alone, not for the <s>jīva</s>.
Accordingly, it is <s>Brahman</s> alone that is declared by <s>Śruti</s> as endowed with the qualities of being free from sin etc. — hence it is that very [<s>Brahman</s>] that is the <s>dahara</s>-space (the small space [within the heart]), not the <s>jīva</s>.
One might object: If, upon the manifestation of its true nature, it is <s>Brahman</s> and not the <s>jīva</s>, then this statement is contradictory — 'the <s>jīva</s> whose true nature has become manifest' — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Because it has previously gone [through the states of waking etc.]' and 'By the <s>Brahman</s> [seen] in the water-vessel' etc.
Just as the reflections of <s>Indra</s> in the water-vessel, having the properties of arising and perishing, are not the Self — because they lack the characteristics of the Self — so too the body, senses, and the like, having the properties of arising and perishing, are not the Self. Through the illustration of the water-vessel, the disillusionment (<s>vyutthāna</s>) from identifying the body with the Self — i.e., its sublation (<s>bādha</s>) — [is established].
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises an objection: 'But how can one's own form [be manifested]?'
For something that is mixed with another substance and overpowered by it, when separated from it, is manifested — like gold, tin, and the like [separated from alloy].
But for the immutably eternal [Self], which is not mixed with anything else, whence would there be manifestation through separation?
Nor is the <s>jīva</s> un-manifest in the state of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
For seeing (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) and the like are its own nature, and they are manifest in the state of <s>saṃsāra</s> — so how can the <s>jīva</s>'s nature not be manifest? — this is the meaning.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] resolves this: 'Prior to the arising of discriminative knowledge' etc.
The meaning is this: Although this immutably eternal [Self] is not truly mixed with anything else, and although its nature as seeing etc. shines forth even in the state of <s>saṃsāra</s>, nevertheless, due to the force of beginningless, indescribable <s>avidyā</s>, its nature as seeing etc. shines forth as if mixed with the body, senses, and the like imagined by <s>avidyā</s> — though unmixed, as if mixed; though discriminated, as if undiscriminated.
Accordingly, through the afflictions (<s>tāpa</s>) etc. belonging to the body, senses, and the like, [the Self] appears as if possessing afflictions etc.
This has been demonstrated in detail in the <s>adhyāsa-bhāṣya</s> (introduction on superimposition) and is not demonstrated here.
Although crystals and the like, when in proximity to <s>japā</s> (hibiscus) flowers and the like — and that proximity consists of the contact with what is conjoined — and thus they are conjoined [with them], nevertheless they are not directly in contact with the <s>japā</s> flower — by just this much, the illustration has been resolved.
Feelings (<s>vedanā</s>) are joy, fear, grief, and the like.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] applies [the illustration] to the thing illustrated: 'Similarly, [the Self is distinct from] the body etc.' etc.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] divides [the <s>Śruti</s> passage] 'This serene being, having risen from this body and having reached the supreme light, manifests in its own form': 'The discriminative knowledge produced by scripture' etc.
By this, having spoken of discriminative knowledge [produced] through hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>), reflection (<s>manana</s>), and practice of meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), the fruit of that discriminative knowledge is the direct realization of the pure Self alone — the manifestation in its own form. And that direct realization, being a modification [of the mind], dissolving all phenomenal elaboration while itself also dissolving — being of the nature of phenomenal elaboration — like the <s>kataka</s> fruit [which purifies water and itself dissolves], [it too] dissolves.
Accordingly, the light of the Self — free from the entire web of phenomenal elaboration, unobstructed, self-luminous — is established.
This is what is stated: 'Having reached the supreme light' etc.
And here, the use of the <s>ktvā</s> suffix [in '<s>samutthāya</s>'] in referring to reaching, which is subsequent [to rising], should be understood like 'having opened his mouth, he sleeps' — [where opening the mouth and sleeping are not strictly sequential].
And since discriminative direct realization is the 'rising from the body' — not a physical departure from the body — it is possible even for one who still has a body, whose <s>prārabdha karma</s> (karma that has begun to bear fruit) has not yet been exhausted — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Thus, by discrimination and non-discrimination alone' etc.
Not only from <s>Śruti</s>s such as 'He who knows that supreme <s>Brahman</s> becomes <s>Brahman</s> indeed' is the non-difference of the <s>jīva</s> from the <s>Paramātman</s> [established]; through the consideration of the textual sequence of the <s>Prājāpatya</s> [teaching] too, it must be understood in exactly this way — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'And from what [source] is this to be thus understood?' etc.
One might object:

body.text:
praticchāyātmavajjīvaṃ paramātmano vastuto bhinnamapyamṛtābhayātmatvena grāhayitvā paścātparamātmānamṛtābhayādimantaṃ prajāpatirgrāhyati, na tvayaṃ jīvasya paramātmabhāvamācaṣṭe chāyātmana ivetyata āha- #nāpi praticchāyātmāyamakṣilakṣita iti# /
akṣilakṣito 'pyātmaivopadiśyate na chāyātmā /

kiñca dvitīyādiṣvapi paryāyeṣu 'etaṃ tveva te bhūyo 'nuvyākhyāyasyāmi' ityupakramātprathamaparyāyanirdiṣṭo na chāyāpuruṣaḥ, api tu tato 'nyo dṛṣṭātmeti darśayati, anyathā prajāpateḥ pratārakatvaprasaṅgādityata āha- #tathā dvitīye 'pīti# /

chāyāpuruṣo 'sthāyī, sthāyī cāyamātmā cakāsti, pratyabhijñānādityarthaḥ /
#nahi khalvayamevamiti# /
ayaṃ suṣuptaḥ /

'nahi vijñāturvijñāterviparilopo vidyate 'vināśitvāt' ityanenāvināśitvaṃ siddhavaddhetukurvatā suptotthitasyātmapratyabhijñānamuktam, ya evāhaṃ jāgaritvā suptaḥ sa evaitarhi jāgarmīti /
ācāryadeśayamatamāha- #kecittviti# /

na tvetadasti /
vākyopakramasūcitasya parātmanaḥ parāmarśāt /

tadetaddūṣayati- #teṣāmetamiti# /
subodham /
