Only the general direction has been indicated here; the detailed treatment is to be understood in the <s>Tattvabindu</s>.
Or enough with the dispute with the <s>Naiyāyika</s>s.

children.text: santvanityā eva varṇāstathāpi gatvādyavacchedenaiva saṃgatigraho 'vanādiśca vyavahāraḥ setsyatītyāha- #athāpi nāmeti# //28 //
children.translated_text: Even if <s>varṇa</s>s are indeed non-eternal, still the apprehension of their conjunction and the beginningless conventional usage will be accomplished through delimitation by cow-ness and the like — thus he says: 'Even so, by name' (<s>athāpi nāma</s>). //28//

body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: #ata eva ca nityatvam# /

children.text: nanu prācyāmeva mīmāṃsāyāṃ vedasya nityatvaṃ siddhaṃ tatkiṃ punaḥ sādhyata ityata āha- #svatantrasya karturasmaraṇādeva hi sthite vedasya nityatva iti# /
children.translated_text: But if the eternality of the <s>Veda</s> is already established in the prior <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> [i.e., <s>Pūrva Mīmāṃsā</s>], then why is it being established again? To this he says: 'Since there is no memory of an independent author, the eternality of the <s>Veda</s> is established' (<s>svatantrasya kartur asmaraṇād eva hi sthite vedasya nityatva</s>).
For the world cannot originate from something non-eternal, because that [non-eternal thing] too, being subject to origination, would require [a further cause].

children.text: tasmānnityo vedaḥ jagadutpattihetutvāt, īśvaravaditi siddhameva nityatvamanena dṛḍhīkṛtam /
children.translated_text: Therefore the <s>Veda</s> is eternal because it is the cause of the world's origination, just like <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) — thus the eternality is simply confirmed and strengthened by this [<s>sūtra</s>].
The rest is self-evident in meaning. //29//

body.translated_text: 'From this very [reason], eternality' (<s>ata eva ca nityatvam</s>).

body.text:
#samānanāmarūpatvāccāvṛttāvapyavirodho darśanātsmṛteśca# /
śaṅkāpadottaratvātsūtrasya paṭhati- #athāpi syāditi# /
abhidhānābhidheyāvicchede hi saṃbandhanityatvaṃ bhavet /
evamadhyāyapakādhyetṛparaṃparāvicchede vedasya nityatvaṃ syāt /
niranvayasya tu jagataḥ pravilaye 'tyantāsataścāpūrvasyotpāde 'bhidhānābhidheyāvatyantamucchinnāviti kimāśrayaḥ saṃbandhaḥ syāt /
adhyāpakādhyetṛsaṃtānavicchede ca kimāśrayo vedaḥ syāt /
naca jīvāstadvāsanāvāsitaḥ santīti vācyam /
antaḥkaraṇādyupādhikalpitā hi te tadvicchede na sthātumarhanti /
naca brahmaṇastadvāsanā, tasya vidyātmanaḥ śuddhasvabhāvasya tadayogāt /
brahmaṇaśca sṛṣṭyādāvantaḥkaraṇāni tadavacchinnāścha jīvāḥ prādurbhavanto napūrvakarmāvidyāvāsanāvanto bhavitumarhanti, apūrvatvāt /
tasmādviruddhamidaṃ śabdārthasaṃbandhavedanityatvaṃ sṛṣṭipralayābhyupagameneti /
abhidhātṛgrahaṇenādhyāpakādhyetārāvuktau /

children.translated_text: In order to refute the doubt, he introduces the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Here it is stated: because of the sameness of names and forms' (<s>tatredam abhidhīyate samāna-nāma-rūpatvāt</s>).

children.text: yadyapi mahāpralayasamaye nāntaḥkaraṇādayaḥ samudācaradvṛttayaḥ santi tathāpi svakāraṇe 'nirvācyāyāmavidyāyāṃ līnāḥ sūkṣmeṇa śaktirūpeṇa karmavikṣepakāvidyāvāsanābhiḥ mahāvatiṣṭhanta eva /
children.translated_text: Even though at the time of the great dissolution (<s>mahāpralaya</s>) there are no inner organs and the like functioning with active modifications, nevertheless, merged in their cause — the indescribable <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — in the subtle form of potency, along with the impressions of <s>karma</s>, projecting power, and <s>avidyā</s>, they greatly persist indeed.
And thus the <s>smṛti</s> [states]: 'This [universe] was enveloped in darkness, unknowable, without distinguishing marks,
beyond reasoning, beyond knowledge, as if entirely asleep.'

body.translated_text: 'And because of the sameness of names and forms, there is no contradiction even in [the next] cycle [of creation], as is seen from <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>' (<s>samāna-nāma-rūpatvāc cāvṛttāv apy avirodho darśanāt smṛteś ca</s>). He cites the <s>sūtra</s> because it serves as a response to a doubt: 'Even if it were so' (<s>athāpi syāt</s>). For the eternality of the relation [between word and meaning] would hold only if there is no interruption of denotation and denotatum. Likewise, the eternality of the <s>Veda</s> would hold only if there is an unbroken succession of teachers and students. But when the world dissolves without remainder, and when what was entirely non-existent comes into being afresh, denotation and denotatum are completely severed — on what basis could the relation subsist? And when the succession of teachers and students is broken, on what basis could the <s>Veda</s> subsist? Nor can it be said that the <s>jīva</s>s (individual souls) endure, endowed with the impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) thereof. For the <s>jīva</s>s are constructed by the limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) of the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) and the like, and when those are dissolved, they cannot persist. Nor does <s>Brahman</s> have such impressions, since <s>Brahman</s>, being of the nature of knowledge and of pure essence, is incompatible with them. And the <s>jīva</s>s that emerge at the beginning of creation along with their inner organs cannot possess prior <s>karma</s>, <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), and <s>vāsanā</s>s (impressions), because they would be entirely new. Therefore, the eternality of the word-meaning relation and of the <s>Veda</s> is contradicted by the acceptance of creation and dissolution — [this is the doubt]. By the mention of 'denotators' (<s>abhidhātṛ</s>), teachers and students are indicated.

body.text:
' iti /
te cāvadhaiṃ prāpya parameśvarecchāpracoditā yathā kūrmadehe nilīnānyaṅgāni tato niḥsaranti, yathā vā varṣāpāye prāptamṛdbhāvāni maṇḍūkaśarīrāṇi tadvāsanāvāsitatayā ghanaghanāghanāsārāvasekasuhitāni punarmaṇḍūkadehabhāvamanubhavanti, tathā pūrvavāsanāvaśātpūrvasamānanāmarūpāṇyutpadyante /
etaduktaṃ bhavati-yadyapīśvarātprabhavaḥ saṃsāramaṇḍalasya, tathāpīśvaraḥ prāṇabhṛtkarmāvidyāsahakārī tadanurūpameva sṛjati /
naca sargapralayapravāhasyānāditāmantareṇaitadupapadyata iti sargapralayābyupagaṃme 'pi saṃsārānāditā na virudhyata iti /
tadidamuktam- #upapadyate cāpyupalabhyate ca# /
āgamata iti /
syādetat /
bhavatvanāditā saṃsārasya, tathāpi mahāpralayāntarite kutaḥ smaraṇaṃ vedānāmityata āha- #anādau ca saṃsāre yathā svāpaprabodhayoriti# /
yadyapiprāṇāmātrāvaśeṣatātanniḥ śeṣaye suṣuptapralayāvasthayorviśeṣaḥ, tathāpi karmavikṣepasaṃskārasahitalayalakṣaṇā vidyāvaśeṣatāsāmyena svāpapralayāvasthayārabheda iti draṣṭavyam /
nanu nāparyāyeṇa sarveṣāṃ suṣuptāvasthā, keṣāñcittadā prabodhāt, tebhyasya suptotthitānāṃ grahaṇasaṃbhavāt, prāyaṇakālaviprakarṣayośca vāsanocchedakāraṇayorabhāvena satyāṃ vāsanāyāṃ smaraṇopapatteḥ śabdārthasaṃbandhavedavyahārānucchedo yujyate /
mahāpralayastvaparyāyeṇa prāṇabhṛnmātravatartī, prāyaṇakālaviprakarṣau ca tatra saṃskāramātrocchedahetū sta iti kutaḥ suṣuptavatpūrvaprabodhavyavahāravaduttaprabodhavyavahāra iti codayati- #syādetat /
svāpa iti# /
body.translated_text:
Thus, having reached their respective limits, impelled by the will of the supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>), just as limbs hidden in the body of a tortoise emerge from it, or just as the bodies of frogs — having attained the state of clay [i.e., dormancy] at the end of the rainy season — being pervaded by the impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) thereof, nourished by the downpour of dense rainclouds, again experience the state of frog-bodies, so too, by the force of prior impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), names and forms identical to the previous ones arise.
This is what is stated: although the world-cycle (<s>saṃsāra-maṇḍala</s>) originates from the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), nevertheless the Lord, cooperating with the <s>karma</s> and <s>avidyā</s> of living beings, creates in conformity with those alone.
And without the beginninglessness of the stream of creation and dissolution, this cannot be accounted for — hence even upon accepting creation and dissolution, the beginninglessness of <s>saṃsāra</s> is not contradicted.
Thus it is said: 'It is possible, and it is also observed' — from scripture.
One might object: let the beginninglessness of <s>saṃsāra</s> be granted; still, with the great dissolution (<s>mahāpralaya</s>) intervening, whence comes the remembrance of the <s>Veda</s>s? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'And in the beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s>, as in sleep and waking.'
Although there is a difference between the states of deep sleep and cosmic dissolution in that [deep sleep involves] the residuum of <s>prāṇa</s> alone while [dissolution involves] the complete annihilation of that, nevertheless, the state of dissolution — characterized by latency accompanied by the <s>saṃskāra</s>s of <s>karma</s>-projection — should be understood as non-different from the state of sleep, by virtue of their similarity in that a residuum of <s>avidyā</s> remains.
But [one may object:] deep sleep does not occur simultaneously for all beings — since some are awake at that time, and since those who have risen from sleep can learn from them — and because of the absence of the two causes that would destroy impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), namely the time of death and extreme temporal distance, and because remembrance is possible when impressions exist, the non-interruption of the practice of word-meaning-relation and <s>Veda</s> is justified.
But the great dissolution (<s>mahāpralaya</s>) inevitably encompasses all living beings without exception, and at that time the time of death and extreme temporal distance are causes for the complete destruction of <s>saṃskāra</s>s alone — so whence the post-waking practice resembling the pre-sleep practice, as in the case of deep sleep? — thus [the opponent] raises the objection: 'One might say: in sleep...'

body.text:
pariharati- #naiṣa doṣaḥ /
satyapi vyavahārocchenīti# /
ayamabhisaṃdhiḥ-na tāvatprāyaṇakālaviprakarṣau sarvasaṃskārocchedakau, pūrvābhyastasmṛtyanubandhājjātasya harṣabhayaśokasaṃpratipatteranupapatteḥ /
manuṣyajanmavāsanānāṃ cānekajātyantarasahasravyavahitānāṃ punarmanuṣyajātisaṃvartakena karmaṇābhivyaktyabhāvaprasaṅgāt /
tasmānnikṛṣṭadhiyāmapi yatra satyapi prāyaṇakālaviprakarṣādau pūrvavāsanānuvṛttiḥ, tatra kaiva kathā parameśvarānugraheṇa dharmajñānavairāgyaiśvaryātiśayasaṃpannānāṃ hiraṇyagarbhaprabhṛtīnāṃ mahādhiyām /
yathāvā ā ca manuṣyebhya ā ca kṛmibhyo jñānādīnāmanubhūyate nikarṣaḥ, evamā manuṣyebhya eva ā ca bhagavato hiraṇyagarbhajjñānādīnāṃ prakarṣe 'pi saṃbhāvte /
tathāca tadabhivadanto vedasmṛtivādāḥ prāmāṇyamapratyūhamaśruvate /
evaṃ cātrabhavatāṃ hiraṇyagarbhādīnāṃ parameśvarānugṛhītānāmupapadyate kalpāntarasaṃbandhinikhilavyavahārānusaṃdhānamiti /
sugamamanyat /
syādetat /
astu kalpanāntaravyavahārānusaṃdhānaṃ teṣām /
asyāṃ tu sṛṣṭāvanya eva deśaḥ, anya eva caiṣāmarthāḥ, anya eva varṇāśramāḥ, dharmāccānarthor'thaścādharmāt, anarthaścepsitor'thaścānīpsitaḥ apūrvatvātsargasya /
tasmātkṛtamatra kalpāntaravyavahārānusaṃdhānena, atkiñcitkaratvāt /
tathāca pūrvavyavahārocchedācchabdārthasaṃbandhaśca vedaścānityau prasajyeyātāmityata āha- #prāṇināṃ ca sukhaprāptaya iti# /
yathāvastusvabhāvasāmarthyaṃ hi sargaḥ pravartate, natu svabhāvasāmarthyamanyathayitumarhati /
nahi jātu sukhaṃ tattvena jihāsyate, duḥkhaṃ copāditsyate /
naca jātu dharmādharmayoḥ sāmarthyāviparyayo bhavati /
nahi mṛtpiṇḍātpaṭaḥ, ghaṭaśca tantubhyo jāyate /
tathā sati vastusāmarthyaniyamābhāvātsarvaṃ sarvasmādbhavediti pipāsurapi dahanamāhṛtya pipāsāmupaśamayet, śītārto vā toyamāhṛtya śītārtimiti /
tena sṛṣṭyantare 'pi brahmahatyādiranarthaheturevārthahetuśca yāgādirityānupūrvyaṃ siddham /

children.text: evaṃ ya eva vedā asminkalpe ta eva kalpāntare, ta eva caiṣāmarthā ta eva ca varṇāśramāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, the very same <s>Veda</s>s that exist in this cosmic cycle (<s>kalpa</s>) exist in another cosmic cycle, and the very same meanings belong to them, and the very same social classes and life-stages (<s>varṇāśrama</s>s) [obtain].
When similarity with what is observed is possible, the postulation of dissimilarity [between cosmic cycles] is contrary to inference (<s>anumāna</s>) and scripture (<s>āgama</s>).
'And here, many scriptural passages have been shown by the author of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> (<s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>) —
called <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, and <s>Purāṇa</s>; the subversion of those would otherwise result.' //

body.translated_text:
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] resolves: 'This is not a fault. Even when practice is interrupted...'
The intention is as follows: First, the time of death and extreme temporal distance are not causes for the complete destruction of all <s>saṃskāra</s>s, because the experiential recognition (<s>saṃpratipatti</s>) of joy, fear, and sorrow arising in a newborn — connected with the continuity of memory cultivated in previous lives — would be inexplicable otherwise.
And because there would be the unwanted consequence that the impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>s) from human birth — separated by thousands of intervening births — would not be manifested by the <s>karma</s> that brings about another human birth.
Therefore, where even for those of inferior intellect, prior impressions persist despite the time of death and extreme temporal distance, what need is there to speak of the great-minded ones — <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> and others — who are endowed with an abundance of <s>dharma</s>, knowledge, dispassion, and sovereign power, by the grace of the supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>)?
Or alternatively: just as a gradation of knowledge and the like is experienced from humans down to worms, so too a gradation [in the positive direction] is conceivable from humans up to the Lord <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>.
And thus, the statements of <s>Veda</s> and <s>Smṛti</s> that affirm this enjoy unobstructed authority.
Thus, the recollection of all practices connected with other cosmic cycles (<s>kalpa</s>s) is possible for these revered ones — <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> and others — who are favored by the supreme Lord.
The rest is easy to understand.
One might object: let them have recollection of the practices of other cosmic cycles. But in this creation, the country is different, the purposes are different, the social classes and life-stages (<s>varṇāśrama</s>s) are different; and from <s>dharma</s> comes misfortune, and from fortune comes <s>adharma</s>, and misfortune [comes] from what is desired and fortune from what is undesired — because creation is novel.
Therefore, what use is the recollection of practices from other cosmic cycles, since it accomplishes nothing?
And thus, because of the interruption of prior practice, word-meaning-relation and the <s>Veda</s> would turn out to be non-eternal — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'For the sake of the happiness of living beings.'
For creation proceeds according to the capacity of the real nature of things, but the capacity of real nature cannot be altered.
For indeed, happiness is never truly wished to be abandoned, nor is suffering ever wished to be taken up.
And there is never a reversal of the capacities of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>.
For a cloth does not arise from a lump of clay, nor a pot from threads.
If it were so — if there were no constraint based on the capacity of real entities — then everything would arise from everything, and even a thirsty person would fetch fire to quench his thirst, or one afflicted by cold would fetch water [to relieve] his cold.
Therefore, even in another creation, killing of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (<s>brahmahatyā</s>) and the like are causes of misfortune alone, and sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>) and the like are causes of fortune — thus the [invariable] order is established.

children.translated_text: Therefore, it is well said: 'Because of the sameness of names and forms, there is no contradiction even in recurrence.'
'<s>Agni</s> (Fire) indeed desired' — thus [the <s>Śruti</s> states].
Relying on a figurative usage (<s>vṛtti</s>) pertaining to the future, the sacrificer (<s>yajamāna</s>) himself is called '<s>Agni</s>.'
For there is no other deity called <s>Agni</s> apart from <s>Agni</s> [himself]. //30//

body.text:
#madhvādiṣvasaṃbhavādanadhikāraṃ jaiminiḥ# /
brahmavidyāsvadhikāraṃ devarṣīṇāṃ brūvāṇaḥ praṣṭavyo jāyate, kiṃ sarvāsu brahmavidyā svaviśeṣeṇa sarveṣāṃ kiṃvā kāsucideva keṣāñcit /
yadyaviśeṣeṇa sarvāsu, tato madhvādividyāsvasaṃbhavaḥ /
#katham /
asau vā ādityo devamadhvityatra hi manuṣyā ādityaṃ madhvadhyāsenopāsīran# /
upāsyopāsakabhāvo hi bhedādhiṣṭhāno na svātmanyādityasya devatāyāḥ saṃbhavati /
na cādityāntaramasti /
prācāmādityānāmasminkalpe kṣīṇādhikāratvāt /
#punaścādityavyapāśrayāṇi pañca rohitādīnyupakramyeti# /
ayamarthaḥ-'asau vā ādityo devamadhu' iti devānāṃ modahetutvānmadhviva madhu /
bhrāmaramadhusārūpyamāhāsya śrutiḥ-'tasya madhuno dyaureva tiraścīnavaṃśaḥ /
body.translated_text:
'<s>Jaimini</s> [holds that there is] no eligibility [of gods], because of the impossibility in the <s>madhu-vidyā</s> and the like.'
One who asserts the eligibility of divine sages (<s>devarṣi</s>s) for <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge is questioned: is it in all <s>Brahman</s>-meditations without distinction for all [of them], or only in certain [meditations] for certain [beings]?
If without distinction in all, then there is impossibility in the <s>madhu-vidyā</s> and the like.
'How? In "That sun indeed is the honey of the gods" (<s>asau vā ādityo devamadhu</s>), here, human beings would meditate on the sun as honey' — the relation of object-of-meditation and meditator, being founded on difference, is not possible for the deity <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) in relation to himself.
Nor is there another <s>Āditya</s>, because the eligibility of the former <s>Āditya</s>s in this cosmic cycle has been exhausted.
'And further, five [kinds of rays] beginning with the red ones, which depend on the sun, are introduced' — this is the meaning: 'That sun indeed is the honey of the gods' — [the sun is called] honey because it is the cause of delight (<s>moda</s>) for the gods, like honey.
The <s>Śruti</s> states its resemblance to bee-honey: 'Of that honey, heaven indeed is the crossbeam.

athāsyādityamadhuna udīcibhiratikṛṣṇābhī raśmināḍībhirathavedavihitebhyaḥ karmakusumebhya āhṛtyāgnau hutaṃ somādi pūrvavadamṛtabhavamāpannamatharvāṅgirasamantrabhramarāḥ, tathāśvamedhavācaḥ stomakarmakusumāt hatihāsapurāṇamnatrabhramarā ādityamaṇḍalamānayanti /

tadamṛtaṃ maruta upajīvanti /

tā etā ādityavyapāśrayāḥ pañca rohitādayo raśmināḍya ṛgādisaṃbaddhāḥ krameṇopadiśyeti yojanā /
etadevāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvopalabhya yathāsvaṃ samastaijha karaṇairyaśastejahandriyasākalyavīryānnādyānyamṛtaṃ tadupalabhyāditye tṛpyati /
tena khalvamṛtena devānāṃ vasvādīnāṃ modanaṃ vidadhadādityo madhu /
etaduktaṃ bhavati-na kevalamupāsyopāsakabhāva ekasminvirudhyate, api tu jñātṛjñeyabhāvaśca prāpyaprāpakabhāvaśceti /
tathāgniḥ pāda iti /
adhidaivataṃ khalvākāśe brahmadṛṣṭividhānārthamuktam /
ākāśasya hi sarvagatatvaṃ rūpādihīnatve ca brahmaṇā sārūpyaṃ, tasya caitasyākāśasya brahmaṇaścatvāraḥ pādā agnyādayaḥ 'agniḥ pādaḥ' ityādinā darśitāḥ /

children.text: yathā hi goḥ pādā na gavā viyujyatanta, evamagnyādayo 'pi nākāśena sarvagatenetyākāśasya pādāḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the legs of a cow are not separated from the cow, so too <s>Agni</s> and the rest are not separated from space, which is all-pervading — hence they are the quarters of space.

children.text: tadevamākāśasya catuṣpado brahmadṛṣṭiṃ vidhāya svarūpeṇa vāyuṃ saṃvargaguṇakamupāsyaṃ vidhātuṃ mahīkaroti-vāyurvāva saṃvargaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having thus prescribed the meditation on <s>Brahman</s> in the four-quartered space, [the <s>Śruti</s>] proceeds to magnify <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) — which is qualified by the attribute of absorption (<s>saṃvarga</s>) — as the object of meditation in its own form: '<s>Vāyu</s> indeed is the absorber' (<s>vāyur vāva saṃvargaḥ</s>).

children.text: tathā svarūpeṇaivādityaṃ brahmadṛṣṭyopāsyaṃ vidhātuṃ mahikaroti- #ādityo brahmetyādeśaḥ#upadeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise, [the <s>Śruti</s>] proceeds to magnify the sun (<s>Āditya</s>) — as the object of meditation on <s>Brahman</s> in its own form — by the instruction: 'The sun is <s>Brahman</s> — this is the teaching' (<s>ādityo brahmeti ādeśaḥ</s>).
The rest is of transparent meaning. //31//

body.translated_text:
The intermediate space (<s>antarikṣa</s>) is the honeycomb.'
For the covering layer of the intermediate space serves as the honeycomb of the sun-honey, because it is stationed there.
And the oblations of <s>Soma</s>-juice, clarified butter, milk, and the like that are offered into the fire — having been cooked and ripened by the rays of the sun combined with fire — having attained the state of <s>amṛta</s> (immortality) — are carried to the solar orb by the <s>Ṛg-veda</s> mantras.
Just as bees, having gathered nectar from flowers, bring it to their hive, so too the <s>Ṛg-mantra</s>-bees, through the recollection of meaning connected with ritual performance and the like, having gathered from the ritual-flowers prescribed by the <s>Ṛg-veda</s>, bring the nectar produced therefrom to the solar orb through its red eastern rays-channels (<s>raśmi-nāḍī</s>s); that <s>amṛta</s>, the <s>Vasu</s>s subsist upon.
Then, through its white southern rays-channels, the <s>Yajur-veda</s>-mantra-bees bring the <s>Soma</s> and other [oblations] — offered into the fire and attaining the state of <s>amṛta</s> as before — gathered from the ritual-flowers prescribed by the <s>Yajur-veda</s>, to the solar orb; that <s>amṛta</s>, the <s>Rudra</s>s subsist upon.
Then, through its dark western rays-channels, the <s>Sāma-veda</s>-mantra-and-hymn-bees bring the <s>Soma</s> and other [oblations] — offered into fire and attaining the state of <s>amṛta</s> as before — gathered from the ritual-flowers prescribed by the <s>Sāma-veda</s>, to the solar orb; that <s>amṛta</s>, the <s>Āditya</s>s subsist upon.
Then, through its exceedingly dark northern rays-channels, the <s>Atharva-Āṅgirasa</s>-mantra-bees, and likewise the <s>itihāsa</s>-<s>purāṇa</s>-mantra-bees from the <s>Aśvamedha</s>-recitation-<s>stoma</s>-ritual-flower, bring the <s>Soma</s> and other [oblations] — offered into fire and attaining the state of <s>amṛta</s> as before — gathered from the ritual-flowers prescribed by the <s>Atharva-veda</s>, to the solar orb.
In the <s>Aśvamedha</s> and the <s>Vācaḥ Stoma</s>, the <s>pāriplava</s> is recited — hence the <s>itihāsa</s>-<s>purāṇa</s>-mantras too have ritual application.
That <s>amṛta</s>, the <s>Marut</s>s subsist upon.
Then, through its upward rays-channels — which are hidden — the meditation-bees (<s>upāsana-bhramara</s>s) bring [the offerings] from the <s>Praṇava</s>-flower to the solar orb; that <s>amṛta</s>, the <s>Sādhya</s>s subsist upon.
These are the five [kinds of rays] beginning with the red, which depend on the sun, connected with the <s>Ṛg-veda</s> and the rest, taught in sequence — this is the construction.
Having seen and obtained this very <s>amṛta</s>, with all its instruments collectively — glory, splendor, vigor of the senses, strength, and food — having obtained that <s>amṛta</s>, [the deity] is satisfied in the sun.
By that <s>amṛta</s>, the sun — causing delight for the gods, the <s>Vasu</s>s and others — is [called] honey.
This is what is stated: not only does the relation of object-of-meditation and meditator conflict [when applied to] one [and the same being], but also the relation of knower and known, and the relation of goal and seeker.
Likewise, '<s>Agni</s> is a quarter' (<s>agniḥ pādaḥ</s>) — this is stated with reference to the macrocosmic (<s>adhidaivata</s>) level, for the purpose of prescribing the meditation on <s>Brahman</s> in space (<s>ākāśa</s>).
For space, being all-pervading and devoid of form and the like, has resemblance with <s>Brahman</s>; and of this space, which is [a symbol for] <s>Brahman</s>, the four quarters — <s>Agni</s> and the rest — are shown by [the <s>Śruti</s>] beginning with '<s>Agni</s> is a quarter.'

na khalupratyakṣādivyatirikto loko nāma pramāṇāntaramasti, kintu pratyakṣādimūlā lokaprasiddhiḥ satyatāmaśrute, tadabhāve tvandhaparamaprāvanmūlābhāvādvipalvate /
body.translated_text:
If it were said that the eligibility of all gods and sages in all forms of <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge is not unrestricted, but only as appropriate [to each] — to that, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] presents: 'And because of existence in light' (<s>jyotiṣi bhāvācca</s>).
For the ordinary usage and cognition of words such as '<s>Āditya</s>' (sun) and the like are observed [to apply] to the orbs of light and the like. And these [orbs] do not possess consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>). For in them, no purposive activities are seen as in [a person like] <s>Devadatta</s> and the like.
'One might say: From mantras, <s>arthavāda</s>s, <s>Itihāsa</s>s, <s>Purāṇa</s>s, and common usage' (<s>mantrārthavādetihāsapurāṇalokebhyaḥ</s>).
Among these, [the mantras say:] 'He seized the right [arm] of <s>Indra</s> laughing' (<s>jagṛbhmāte dakṣiṇam indra hasatam</s>), and '<s>kāśir</s> [is] <s>Indra</s>' — <s>kāśir</s> means 'fist.' Likewise, 'With strong neck, beautiful belly, good arms, in the ecstasy of food, <s>Indra</s> swallows the <s>Vṛtra</s>s' (<s>tuvigrīvo vapodaraḥ subāhur andhaso made indro vṛtrāṇi jighrate</s>) — thus mantras and <s>arthavāda</s>s declare the deity's possession of bodily form.
Likewise, [passages] such as 'Eat, O <s>Indra</s>, drink of that which is offered' (<s>addhi indra piba ca prasthitasya</s>) and the like show the deity's consumption of oblations.
As for lordship: '<s>Indra</s> is lord of heaven, <s>Indra</s> rules the earth, <s>Indra</s> [rules] the waters, <s>Indra</s> the mountains, <s>Indra</s> the mighty, <s>Indra</s> the wise ones, <s>Indra</s> in welfare and in effort, <s>Indra</s> in the offering.' Likewise: 'The lord of this world, seeing heaven, the lord of <s>Indra</s> of the satisfied ones.'
Likewise, [scripture] shows the deity's grace toward one who serves, and her bestowal of fruits when pleased: 'Through oblations alone one gratifies the gods who eat the offering; to him, pleased, they grant food and strength' (<s>āhutibhir eva devān hutādaḥ prīṇāti tasmai prītā iṣam ūrjaṃ ca yacchanti</s>), and 'Being satisfied herself, <s>Indra</s> satisfies him with progeny and cattle.'
The authors of <s>Dharmaśāstra</s> also say: 'Being satisfied, they satisfy him with all desired auspicious fruits.' And many <s>Purāṇa</s> statements elaborate the five-fold manifestation of the deity — bodily form and the rest.
Ordinary people too remember and worship the five-fold [aspect] of the deity's body and the like. Thus: they depict <s>Yama</s> with a staff in hand, <s>Varuṇa</s> with a noose in hand, <s>Indra</s> with a thunderbolt in hand. And they speak of the deities as eaters of oblations. Likewise, they speak of [the deity's] lordship — 'the village of the god,' 'the field of the god.' And they speak of her grace and her bestowal of fruits when pleased: '<s>Paśupati</s> is pleased with him — a son has been born to him.' '<s>Dhanada</s> (the wealth-giver) is pleased with him — wealth has been obtained by him.'
The <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> (objector) refutes all this: 'No, it is said. For common usage (<s>loka</s>) is not [an independent means of knowledge]' (<s>nahi tāvat loko nāma</s>).
Indeed, there is no separate means of valid knowledge called 'common usage' apart from perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) and the like; rather, the common currency [of an idea], being rooted in perception and the like, derives its truth [from them]. In their absence, however, it collapses — like a blind man following another blind man — due to the absence of a foundation.

children.text: mantrāśca vrīhyādivacchutyādibhistatra tatra viniyujyamānāḥ pramāṇabhāvananupraveśinaḥ kathamupayujyantāṃ teṣa teṣu karmasvityapekṣāyāṃ dṛṣṭe prakāre saṃbhavati nādṛṣṭakalpanocitā /
children.translated_text: And mantras, being assigned to particular ritual contexts through <s>Śruti</s> and the like — just as rice and the like [are assigned to rituals] — participate in the function of being means of valid knowledge [only insofar as they relate to ritual]. When the question arises as to how they are employed in those various rites, [the answer is:] when a visible mode [of functioning] is possible, the postulation of an invisible one is not appropriate.

children.text: dṛṣṭaśca prakāraḥ prayogasamavetārthasmāraṇaṃ, smṛtvā cānutiṣṭhanti khalvanuṣṭhātāraḥ padārthān /
children.translated_text: And the visible mode is the recollection of the meaning connected with the performance (<s>prayogasamavetārthasmaraṇa</s>); and performers, having recalled the meanings of the words, carry out [the rites] accordingly.

children.text: autsargikī cārthaparatā padānamityapekṣitaprayogasamavetārthasmaraṇatātparyāṇāṃ mantrāṇāṃ nānadhigate vigrahādāvapi tātparyaṃ yujyata iti na tebhyo 'pi tatsiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: And since the natural referential function of words is to denote their own objects, for mantras — whose purport is the recollection of the meaning connected with the performance — purport with respect to the unascertained [matter of] bodily form and the like is not justified. Hence, from mantras too, that [five-fold nature of deities] is not established.

Therefore, since there is no valid means of knowledge for apprehending the possession of bodily form and the like by deities, the conclusion arrived at is that [the deity] falls within the scope of the sixth means of knowledge [i.e., <s>anupalabdhi</s>, non-apprehension — meaning the deity's bodily form is negated through absence of evidence]. //32//

body.translated_text:
And perception and the other [means of knowledge] do not constitute valid evidence for bodily form and the like [of deities]. Nor can <s>Itihāsa</s> and the like serve as the basis, since they too, being of human authorship (<s>pauruṣeya</s>), depend on perception and the like, and perception and the like are absent here — so [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '<s>Itihāsa</s> and <s>Purāṇa</s> too...' (<s>itihāsapurāṇam api</s>).
Now, it was said that the five-fold nature — bodily form and the rest — is established from mantras and <s>arthavāda</s>s; to that [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '<s>Arthavāda</s>s too...' (<s>arthavādā api</s>).
<s>Arthavāda</s>s, entering into syntactic unity with an injunction (<s>vidhi</s>), have as their ultimate purport the praise of the subject matter of the injunction, and thus cannot serve as valid evidence for their own [literal] meaning.
For those who know the principles of <s>Śābda</s> (verbal testimony) [say]: 'That for which the word is intended — that is the meaning of the word.'
But where [the arthavāda's own meaning] is also supported by another means of knowledge — such as the swiftness of wind — there it is accepted by virtue of the other means of knowledge, not by the power of the word [alone].
But where there is no other means of knowledge — as in the case of the five-fold nature of bodily form and the like — the meaning is to be understood from the word alone. And a word that is not intended for that [meaning] is insufficient to convey it.
Even if the purport (<s>tātparya</s>) is accepted as extending to that [meaning] as well, the sentence would be split, since a single sentence cannot have two different purports.
And when syntactic unity is possible, splitting the sentence is not justified.
Therefore, the claim that the deity's possession of bodily form, which is not ascertained by any other means of knowledge, can be understood from a word whose purport lies elsewhere — this is mere wishful thinking — that is the meaning.

children.translated_text: Nor does [word-function] terminate in injunction alone in a sentence containing a negative particle (<s>nañ</s>).
If that were so, the negative particle would become meaningless.
As [the authorities] say: 'Even though words directly accomplish the presentation of their referents,
the phonemes do not terminate in this fruitless [intermediate function] alone.

body.translated_text:
This being the conclusion [of the pūrvapakṣa], [the <s>Siddhāntin</s>] states: 'But <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> [holds] there is existence; for there is [evidence]' (<s>bhāvaṃ tu Bādarāyaṇe 'sti hi</s>).
The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) sets aside the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> — and so on — up to '[the word <s>bhūta</s>-] the root <s>bhū</s> [establishes] the insentience of the sun and the like is accepted' — this has transparent meaning.
'From the usage of mantras, <s>arthavāda</s>s, and the like' — the word 'and the like' (<s>ādi</s>) includes <s>Itihāsa</s>s, <s>Purāṇa</s>s, and <s>Dharmaśāstra</s>s. 'The usage of mantras and the like' means their activity; 'from the observation of that' [is the reason].
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] restates the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>: 'What was also said...' (<s>yadapyuktam</s>).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] first refutes with the <s>ekadeśin</s>'s (partial) view: 'Here we say...' (<s>atra brūmaḥ</s>).
Having raised and refuted the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s>, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Here [the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s>] objects' (<s>atrāha</s>).
This is indeed the procedure of verbal testimony (<s>śābdī gatiḥ</s>) — namely, that [a word's] function depends on its purport (<s>tātparya</s>). For a word whose purport lies elsewhere cannot serve as valid evidence for something else. For the sentence 'The white one runs' (<s>śveto dhāvati</s>), whose purport is the washing of a leper, cannot convey the running of a dog.
And in a great sentence containing a negative particle (<s>nañ</s>), the subsidiary sentence-meaning cannot be understood as having the form of an injunction.
Nor does that meaning belong to it merely from the [false] cognition [one might have], since that cognition is erroneous.
But this is not the procedure of perception and the like. For one who opens his eyes in order to see a pot for fetching water does not see only the pot, or only the cloth, or only the cloth — [rather, he sees both pot and cloth].
Thus, when the <s>ekadeśin</s> <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> has been refuted, the proponent of the ultimate conclusion (<s>paramasiddhānta</s>) says: 'Here it is said: the comparison is inappropriate' (<s>atrocyate viṣama upanyāsaḥ</s>).
The intention is this: in ordinary usage, words employed to convey a particular meaning do not terminate merely in the recollection of their own referent alone. For no usage of words merely for the recollection of their own referent has ever been observed in the world.
Rather, it is observed [that words function] for sentence-meaning.
And since these [words], having recalled their own referents, cannot directly convey the sentence-meaning, the recollection of their own referent is posited as an intermediate operation of words, serving as a means to sentence-meaning.
And that which exists for the sake of something [else] does not terminate in that [intermediate function] alone — hence words do not terminate in the mere expression of their own referent alone.

children.translated_text: Their activity, aimed at [conveying] the sentence-meaning, is indispensable —
[just as] the blazing of firewood serves cooking, so does the presentation of word-referents [serve the sentence-meaning].'

children.translated_text: For the <s>yāga-bhāvanā</s> (intention to sacrifice) itself, being fruitful, has as its subsidiary operations particular to its own instrument — namely sacrifice — [activities such as] feeding the deity, [obtaining] the deity's grace, and so on; just as in the case of agriculture, each subsidiary operation serves as a means to obtaining the harvest.

Just as in the view of <s>Bhavana</s> [i.e., the <s>Bhāṭṭa</s> school], the subsidiary operations of <s>Āgneya</s> and other [sacrifices], which are directed toward producing <s>apūrva</s> (unseen merit), serve as means to heaven,

children.text: tasmātkarmaṇo 'pūrvāvāntaravyāpārasya vā devatāprasādāvāntaravyāpārasya vā phalavattvāt pradhānatvamubhayasminnapi pakṣe samānaṃ, natu devatāyā vigrahādimatyāḥ prādhānyamiti na dharmamīmāṃsāyāḥ sūtram-'api vā śabdapūrvatvādyajñakarma pradhānaṃ guṇatve devatāśrutiḥ' iti virudhyate /
children.translated_text: therefore, whether the fruitfulness belongs to the sacrificial act itself or to the subsidiary operation of <s>apūrva</s>, or to the subsidiary operation of the deity's grace, the primacy [of the sacrifice] is the same in both views; but the deity possessing bodily form and the like does not have primacy — thus the <s>sūtra</s> of <s>Dharma-Mīmāṃsā</s>, 'Or rather, since the word comes first, the sacrificial act is primary, and the mention of the deity is [merely] subsidiary' (#<s>api vā śabdapūrvatvād yajñakarma pradhānaṃ guṇatve devatāśrutiḥ</s>#), is not contradicted.
Therefore it is established that deities generally have qualification for <s>brahmavidyā</s> (knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>). //33//

body.translated_text: Thus it is stated. This is the procedure within a single sentence. But where one sentence has a connection with another sentence, there, since the comprehension of factual meaning is established through worldly convention, each sentence having its function completed by conveying its own particular qualified meaning, afterwards, for some reason, when the need for another purpose arises, a syntactic connection is postulated. As for example in: '<s>Vāyu</s> indeed is the swiftest deity; one approaches <s>Vāyu</s> with his own share; he alone leads one to prosperity; one should sacrifice a white [animal] to <s>Vāyu</s>.' For here, if the injunction for studying one's own <s>Veda</s> (<s>svādhyāya</s>) did not accept the collection of <s>Vedas</s> denoted by the word <s>svādhyāya</s> as having the purpose of human goals, then the <s>arthavādas</s> (laudatory passages), being confined merely to factual meaning, would not attain syntactic unity with the injunction. Therefore, by virtue of the injunction of <s>svādhyāya</s>, when the expectation of a unified purpose arises, these passages, being directed toward factual narratives, indicate the excellence of what is enjoined through conveying that [factual content]; but they do not have the power to indicate that [excellence] while having their own primary meaning entirely unintended, for in that case <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication) itself would not occur, since its seed — namely the invariable connection with the denoted meaning — would be absent. For this very reason, in the expression '<s>gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣaḥ</s>' ('the village on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>'), the word <s>Gaṅgā</s> indicates the bank as connected with its own primary meaning, and not the ocean bank — for what reason? Because of the absence of proximity to its own primary meaning [in the latter case]. And all this is not possible if the primary meaning is entirely unintended. For this very reason, where <s>arthavādas</s> are seen whose meaning contradicts other <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge), such as '<s>Āditya</s> indeed is the sacrificial post,' 'the sacrificer is the <s>prastara</s> grass,' and so forth — there, in order to accomplish both non-contradiction with other <s>pramāṇas</s> and the purpose of praise, <s>Jaimini</s> formulated the <s>sūtras</s> '#<s>guṇavāda</s> however#' and '#the establishment of that#.' Therefore, where the meaning of <s>arthavādas</s> contradicts other <s>pramāṇas</s>, there the indication of excellence through <s>guṇavāda</s> (figurative interpretation) constitutes indication based on what is already indicated (<s>lakṣitalakṣaṇā</s>). But where there is agreement with other <s>pramāṇas</s>, there the meaning is established from <s>arthavāda</s> just as from other <s>pramāṇas</s>, since two mutually independent [means of knowledge] operate upon a single object, just like perception and inference. However, from the standpoint of the knower, it is a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>). For an uninstructed knower first comprehends the meaning from perception and other [means] rather than from scripture, since in the latter case there is dependence on [prior] learning and so on. But not from the standpoint of the <s>pramāṇa</s> [itself], since, as stated, both are independent regarding their own object. Now if this is so, why does <s>guṇavāda</s> (figurative interpretation) occur even when there is contradiction with other means of knowledge? Since in a conflict with scripture, why should the other means of knowledge not be overridden instead — just as <s>Vedānta</s> passages concerning non-duality [override] perception and other [means] directed toward the manifold world? Why are <s>Vedānta</s> passages too not subjected to <s>guṇavāda</s> like <s>arthavādas</s>? To this it is replied: From the worldly standpoint, words have two kinds of objects — through a doorway (<s>dvāra</s>) and through purport (<s>tātparya</s>). Just as within a single sentence the word-meanings are the doorway-object and the sentence-meaning is the purport-object, so too in the syntactic unity of two sentences. For example, 'this cow belongs to <s>Devadatta</s>, it should be purchased' is one sentence, and 'it yields much milk' is another — the conveyance of its yielding much milk is the doorway; but the purport lies in the meaning of the other sentence, 'it should be purchased.' There, what serves as the doorway is interpreted otherwise when contradicted by another <s>pramāṇa</s>. Just as the sentence 'eat poison' is taken as having its purport in the meaning of another sentence, 'do not eat at his house.' But where the purport [itself is at stake], there, when contradicted by another means of knowledge, it is the human-authored <s>pramāṇa</s> [that is overridden, not the <s>Veda</s>]. The <s>Vedānta</s> passages, however, when examined in their sequential context, are directed toward establishing <s>Brahman</s> — free from the manifold world of erroneous duality — and being non-human-authored, they are self-established authoritative statements of reality, even though the passage about <s>Āditya</s> being the sacrificial post appears to teach <s>Āditya</s>'s identity as the post, it is actually directed toward praise of the post. Therefore, when contradicted by another <s>pramāṇa</s>, the doorway-object is interpreted through <s>guṇavāda</s>. But where there is no contradicting <s>pramāṇa</s>, as in the case of the bodily forms of deities and the like, there even the doorway-object, being cognized, cannot be abandoned. Nor can it be subjected to <s>guṇavāda</s>, for who would resort to the figurative when the literal is possible? — that would lead to excessive application [of figurative interpretation]. If it be said that in that case, the sentence teaching previously unknown [facts such as] the bodily form [of deities] would be split — indeed it would be split. If it be said that in that case there would also be a difference in purport — no, because even through the doorway, when that [meaning] is cognized, there is no ground for postulating a different purport. And it is not the case that a [sentence] lacks authority regarding that toward which its purport is not directed, for if that were so, a sentence directed toward a qualified meaning would lack authority regarding the qualifiers, and thus it could not convey even the qualified meaning, since it would have no scope over the qualifiers. But if [one says] it has scope through having the qualified [meaning] as its object, then in rejecting [the qualifier] there would be mutual dependence: the cognition of the qualifier depends on the rejection, and the rejection depends on [the sentence] having the qualified meaning as its object. Therefore, just as qualifiers cognized from sentences directed toward qualified meanings must be accepted as belonging to the scope of that very sentence even unwillingly, so too the bodily forms of deities and the like, cognized from <s>arthavāda</s> sentences that are directed toward other purposes, cannot rightly be abandoned when there is no contradiction from another <s>pramāṇa</s>. For <s>guṇavāda</s> is not appropriate when the literal meaning is possible. And it has been stated that a non-human-authored statement, even when conveying factual matters, does not depend on another means of knowledge for its own object — hence it would not lack authority in the absence of another means of knowledge. It might be objected: even if there is unity of purport, if there is still a split of sentences, then how is it one sentence due to unity of meaning? No, because in each case there is the possibility of the cognition terminating in a single meaning qualified by the respective word-meanings. That single meaning, qualified by other word-meanings, is in some cases the doorway-object and in some cases the object reached through the doorway — that is the only difference. But if this is so, then even in 'having eaten rice, he goes to the village,' there would be a split of sentences, since the relation is different in 'having eaten rice' and 'he goes to the village.' No, because the cognition does not terminate in one [part alone]. For 'having eaten' conveys same-agent-ness and temporal priority, and this cognition does not terminate without the cognition of another subsequent action. Therefore, within a sentence of five or six words, there is no danger of multiplicity, since the cognition of the qualified meaning terminates [only] with [all] the words together. Even if there is multiplicity of qualifiers, since the qualified is one, and since the principal [meaning], heard once, cannot be made to recur in accordance with subsidiary qualifiers — but when there is a difference in the principal [meaning], there is indeed a split of sentences. Therefore it is established that the <s>arthavāda</s> sentence is different from the injunctive sentence, and that the two sentences, each having completed its function in conveying its own sentence-meaning, subsequently have mutual connection through some [further] expectancy. #Furthermore, it is through injunctions alone that <s>Indra</s> and other [deities] have their deities.# The body of sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>) consists in relinquishing ownership over the oblation, having designated a deity and selected the offering. A deity that is not inscribed in the mind cannot be designated. And what is formless cannot be inscribed in the mind — therefore, since the injunction of sacrifice itself requires the form of the deity, whatever form is understood from other sources such as <s>mantras</s> and <s>arthavādas</s> is accepted, since there is no means of knowledge for postulating a different form. And because <s>mantras</s> and <s>arthavādas</s> would otherwise become entirely opaque in their function. Just as in 'the <s>Vrātya</s> sacrifices with the <s>Vrātyastoma</s>,' when the nature of the <s>Vrātya</s> is required, what is desired by the injunction and understood from the <s>arthavāda</s> — 'one whose father or grandfather did not drink <s>Soma</s>, he is a <s>Vrātya</s>' — has the injunction as its authority; so too the form of the deity. If it be objected that designation requires knowledge of form but not the actual existence of the form, and that knowledge of a deity's form is possible even through superimposition, so that <s>mantras</s> and <s>arthavādas</s> teach only a superimposed form of the deity — true, it requires knowledge of form, and since this is not possible from other sources, it [must come] from <s>mantras</s> and <s>arthavādas</s> alone. But when there is no overriding [evidence] regarding that form, it would be inappropriate to abandon its status as established through experience and postulate an otherwise — something not experienced and not current. Therefore it is proper that the form of the deity, though presented in the mind through <s>mantras</s> and <s>arthavādas</s> that are directed toward other purposes, has the injunction as its authority, since it is required by the injunction. It might be objected: when required by the injunction, the meaning understood even from a passage directed toward another purpose is accepted; but there is no such requirement, since the deity is not a word-form, and since that [deity] is knowable through other means of knowledge — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: #'And not merely a word' and so forth.# Not only is the establishment of bodily form and the like from <s>mantras</s> and <s>arthavādas</s> [relevant], but also from <s>itihāsas</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and popular tradition — whether rooted in <s>mantras</s> and <s>arthavādas</s> or rooted in perception and the like — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: #'<s>Itihāsa</s>' and so forth.# '<s>Śliṣyate</s>' means 'it is consistent.' The rest is explained by the mere recitation [of the text]. Thus, when the bodily form of deities and the like is established through <s>mantras</s>, <s>arthavādas</s>, and so forth, sacrifice, being of the nature of worship of the deity — like the worship of a teacher and others — becomes fruitful through the grace of the deity and so on. But for something unconscious that cannot receive worship, this would be inexplicable. And it should not be objected that since the sacrifice is subsidiary to the deity, and the result arises from the deity, the scripturally declared fruitfulness of the sacrifice through <s>yāga-bhāvanā</s> (the intention to sacrifice) and the scripturally declared instrumentality of sacrifice toward that result or its fruit-portion would have to be abandoned.

children.translated_text: Or, <s>Jānaśruti</s> was overcome by <s>śuc</s> (grief).
The meaning is: he was seized by grief.
Alternatively, <s>Jānaśruti</s>, due to grief, ran to <s>Raikva</s> — that is, he went [to him].

children.text: tasmāttadādravaṇāditi tacchabdena śugvā jānaśrutirvā raikko vā parāmṛśyata ityuktam //34 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the phrase 'because of that running,' the word 'that' can refer either to the grief, or to <s>Jānaśruti</s>, or to <s>Raikva</s> — thus it has been stated. //34//

body.translated_text:
'[His] grief is indicated by the hearing of that disregard and by [his] rushing toward that' (#<s>śugasya tadanādaraśravaṇāttadādravaṇātsūcyate hi</s>#).
Providing the sub-connection [of this section], [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the purport of the <s>adhikaraṇa</s>: '#As is the eligibility of human beings#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the seed of the doubt: '#There#.'
When there is eternal bliss free from all trace of suffering, what conscious being would not desire it? — so one cannot say that the <s>Śūdra</s> is ineligible due to absence of desire.
Nor is there an absence of capability for <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge in the <s>Śūdra</s>.
For capability is of two kinds — innate and acquired.
Among these, the innate capability of <s>Śūdra</s>s for hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>) and the like is unimpeded, just like that of the twice-born.
If one objects: in the absence of [Vedic] study, the absence of acquired capability [renders the <s>Śūdra</s>] ineligible — well then, in the absence of the establishment of the [sacred] fires (<s>ādhāna</s>), since there is no fire, there would be no eligibility in rites requiring fire either!
And since fire is not an instrument for <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge, why are those who have not established the fires not ineligible [for <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge]?
Nor is it correct [to say] that, because of the absence of [Vedic] study, one is ineligible for <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge as [one would be] for what requires [study] as its instrument.
For it is reasonable [to say]: since the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire is prescribed as the substrate for oblation in 'He offers into the <s>Āhavanīya</s>,' and since the transcendent form of that [fire] — being unobtainable except through the <s>ādhāna</s> (fire-establishment) prescribed by the Vedic passage that must be studied — and since the <s>ādhāna</s> is prescribed as connected with the twice-born alone, therefore the transcendent fire accomplished through that [<s>ādhāna</s>] is not available to the <s>Śūdra</s>; hence the <s>Śūdra</s> is ineligible for rites requiring the <s>Āhavanīya</s> and other [fires].
But in <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge there is no such transcendent instrument that would be unavailable to the <s>Śūdra</s>.
If one says: there is a restriction to [Vedic] study — no,
because it cannot withstand alternatives.
That study would be restricted either for the sake of the person (<s>puruṣārtha</s>), as accepting gifts (<s>pratigraha</s>) and the like are for acquiring wealth;
or for the sake of the ritual (<s>kratvārtha</s>), as threshing (<s>avaghāta</s>) in 'they thresh the rice-grains.'
It is not for the sake of the ritual.
For 'The <s>Svādhyāya</s> (self-study) is to be studied' is not recited with reference to any particular rite, unlike 'they thresh the rice-grains' which is recited with reference to the <s>Darśa-Pūrṇamāsa</s> rite.
Nor does [<s>Svādhyāya</s>], even though studied independently [of a specific rite], bring to mind a rite through an invariable connection with a rite, by which the study would be connected with a rite through that very sentence.
For <s>Svādhyāya</s> (self-study) is not invariably connected with a rite in the way that the <s>juhū</s> (offering-ladle) and the like are.
Therefore, there is no restriction for the sake of the ritual.
Nor for the sake of the person.
[For the activity] is dependent on the person's desire alone.
But in the procedural details (<s>itikartavyatā</s>), activity — both general and specific — is entirely dependent on injunction.
For one who has not learned the distinction of instruments cannot function in the procedural details.
Therefore, because the subsidiary acts depend on injunction for their operation, they serve the purpose of the ritual.
For 'ritual' (<s>kratu</s>) refers back to the injunction that is its subject, through the content of the injunction.
'That for which [something] is desired and made a subject' — that is <s>kratvārtha</s> (ritual-serving).
But study, or <s>Svādhyāya</s>, or the knowledge of meaning arising from that — prior to [any] injunction — has its activity dependent on the person's desire, and is therefore person-serving.
And if by study alone [a restriction] were to be imposed on the understanding of meaning, then there would be contradiction with other means of knowledge,
since that form [of understanding] is obtainable even without [Vedic] study, through reading from manuscripts and the like.
Therefore, just as in 'gold is [to be] heavy' [a separate fruit must be postulated], so too a [separate] fruit should be postulated from study alone.
And thus, since the injunction of study is non-restrictive [regarding knowledge], the <s>Śūdra</s> too, having capability through either study or reading from manuscripts and the like, would be eligible for <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge.
Or let there not be eligibility for <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge everywhere [for the <s>Śūdra</s>] due to the absence of study; but in the <s>Saṃvargavidyā</s> (knowledge of absorption) there will be [eligibility],
since that [<s>Saṃvargavidyā</s>] commences by addressing a <s>Śūdra</s>: '<s>aha hāretvā śūdra</s>' (Come, take away, O <s>Śūdra</s>).
And this word '<s>Śūdra</s>' cannot be made to refer to a non-<s>Śūdra</s> through any etymological analysis of its components, since the conventional meaning of the whole word is stronger due to its independence from the conventional meaning of the parts.
Therefore, just as the <s>Niṣāda-sthapati</s> (chief of the <s>Niṣāda</s>s), who has not studied [the <s>Veda</s>], has eligibility for the <s>Iṣṭi</s> sacrifice by the force of the [Vedic] statement, so too the <s>Śūdra</s> will have eligibility for the <s>Saṃvargavidyā</s> — this is the prima facie conclusion.
This being arrived at, we say: '#The <s>Śūdra</s> has no eligibility, because of the absence of Vedic study#.'
The intent is this: Although the injunction of study — 'The <s>Svādhyāya</s> is to be studied' — is not recited in connection with any particular fruitful rite, nor does it contain a term invariably connected with a rite — for <s>Svādhyāya</s> is not invariably connected with a rite in the way the <s>juhū</s> and the like are — nevertheless, the injunction of <s>Svādhyāya</s>, being the injunction of a purificatory rite (<s>saṃskāra</s>) for study, makes known that study is a requisite means.
Should one then postulate a fruit [for study] — either heaven, like the <s>Piṇḍa-pitṛyajña</s>, or an <s>arthavādic</s> (eulogistic) fruit as in 'gold is heavy' — and then, by breaking the [direct] application, construe [the injunction] as meaning 'one should study through <s>Svādhyāya</s>'? Or should one, taking [the study] as ultimately purposive, determine the requisite [element] that it depends upon, and [then] see [it as serving a purpose]?
When there is the possibility of [explaining the injunction] through a visible means — in the form of obtaining the requisite [element] even indirectly — and when the application as heard [in scripture] is sustainable, the postulation of an unheard, invisible fruit through breaking the scriptural application is not appropriate.
And the purificatory nature of <s>Svādhyāya</s> for study is visible.
For through that [purificatory rite], a person attains [study]; and [study] once attained gives rise to the understanding of fruitful action and <s>Brahman</s>, whose purpose is prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>) and the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>). But in the case of wearing gold and the like, there is nothing requisite [to be attained] even indirectly through the visible means; therefore, conversely, a fruit is postulated from the wearing alone, by breaking the [direct] application.
And when it has been established that <s>Svādhyāya</s>, as a purificatory rite of study, gives rise to the understanding of fruitful action and <s>Brahman</s>, whose purpose is prosperity and the highest good — then for one who has [Vedic] study alone, there is the understanding of action and <s>Brahman</s> whose purpose is prosperity and the highest good, and not for another. And one who has the purificatory rite of initiation (<s>upanayana</s>) alone has [Vedic] study; and that [<s>upanayana</s>] belongs only to the twice-born. Therefore, because of the absence of the purificatory rite of <s>upanayana</s> and consequently the absence of the purificatory rite of study, the understanding of meaning arising from <s>Svādhyāya</s> recited from manuscripts and the like does not serve as the fruit for <s>Śūdra</s>s — hence, due to the absence of scriptural capability, the <s>Śūdra</s> is not eligible for <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge. This is established.
'#Not being ordained in sacrifice#' — the word 'sacrifice' (<s>yajña</s>) is used illustratively.
It should be understood as 'not being ordained in <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge)' as well.
Because the usage-as-if-established (<s>siddhavadabhidhāna</s>) has a prior logical basis (<s>nyāyapūrvakatva</s>), and the logical basis is equal in both cases.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] restates the second <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>: '#As for what was further said about the <s>Saṃvargavidyā</s>#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes: '#That is not an indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>)#.'
Why?
'#Because of the absence of a valid reasoning (<s>nyāya</s>)#.'
The <s>Śūdra</s> is not directly enjoined regarding the <s>Saṃvargavidyā</s>, in the way that the <s>Niṣāda-sthapati</s> is [directly enjoined] in 'One should sacrifice for the <s>Niṣāda-sthapati</s> by this [rite].'
Rather, this word '<s>Śūdra</s>' occurs in an <s>arthavāda</s> (explanatory passage), and an <s>arthavāda</s> illuminates a meaning already established from elsewhere but does not establish [a new meaning] — so say the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s>s of ritual.
But according to us, even from a sentence whose primary purpose is something else, a meaning cognized by another means of knowledge, when it is required by an injunction — in the absence of a sublating cognition — is indeed accepted.
And a sublating reasoning (<s>nyāya</s>) has been stated for this matter.
Nor is there a requirement [for the <s>Śūdra</s>] from any injunction, since the injunction is concluded by the acquisition of eligibility through [the word] 'twice-born' (<s>dvija</s>).
But if [the word <s>Śūdra</s>] were within the scope of an injunction, then this reasoning would be overridden by the force of the [Vedic] statement — as in the case of the <s>Niṣāda-sthapati</s> — but this [<s>Śūdra</s>] is not within the scope of an injunction. This has been stated.
Therefore, the eligibility of the <s>Śūdra</s> is not established merely from an <s>arthavāda</s> — this is the purport.
Moreover, does the force of the <s>arthavāda</s> establish eligibility of the <s>Śūdra</s> for knowledge in general (<s>vidyāmātra</s>), or for the <s>Saṃvargavidyā</s> [specifically]? Not for knowledge in general — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#And even if this were desired#.'
For the <s>arthavāda</s> heard in the context of the <s>Saṃvargavidyā</s> does not extend the eligible person to knowledge in general, because of the consequent absurdity (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>).
Then let the <s>Śūdra</s>'s eligibility be for the <s>Saṃvargavidyā</s> alone — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Because it is situated in an <s>arthavāda</s>#.'
Then is this word '<s>Śūdra</s>' like a madman's song [i.e., meaningless]? That is not reasonable either, for what is traditionally transmitted is of equal [authority] — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#And this word <s>Śūdra</s> can be [explained thus]#.'
The story narrated here is as follows: <s>Jānaśruti Pautrāyaṇa</s> was one who gave abundantly, who was full of faith, who cooked much [for guests], and who was dear to guests.
And in various villages, towns, and crossroads, he had rest-houses built, full of various foods and drinks, for travelers.
'Everywhere, those seeking food and drink from me will partake [of it] in these rest-houses' — [this was his intention].
Then, divine sages, gratified by the magnitude of this generous king's virtues, assuming the form of geese (<s>haṃsa</s>s), flew overhead in a garland formation during the summer nights for his benefit, while he was lying on the terrace of his palace.
Addressing the foremost goose, one goose flying behind him spoke with wonder:
O bright-eyed one! The light of this <s>Jānaśruti Pautrāyaṇa</s> stretches through day and night into the celestial world — do not touch it, lest it burn you!
The leading goose replied to him who had spoken thus:
Whom do you speak of as if he were excellent (<s>vara</s>) — this one who is [merely] like <s>Raikva</s> with the cart (<s>sayugvā</s>)?
The meaning is: He said '<s>vara</s>' (excellent) mockingly.
Or, '<s>vara</s>' means 'poor fellow' (<s>varāka</s>) — this <s>Jānaśruti</s> [is a mere] poor fellow.
'<s>Kam</s>' is used in the sense of reproach.
Since he is a poor fellow, why do you speak of this <s>kam</s> — this person who is a mere living being — as this <s>Jānaśruti</s>?
For the light of <s>Raikva</s> is irresistible, but not that of this mere living being.
For that blessed <s>Raikva</s>, endowed with the accumulated store of merit and knowledge, the knower of <s>Brahman</s>, has the merit of all living beings within the three worlds subsumed in his own merit; but no one's merit enters the domain of <s>Raikva</s>'s merit.
Then <s>Jānaśruti</s>, having heard from the speech of the goose of his own utter inferiority and the supreme excellence of <s>Raikva</s>, became dejected in mind — like a gambler defeated at dice — sighing repeatedly, excessively, somehow managing to pass the night with great difficulty.
Then, hearing the auspicious sound of musical instruments accompanied by thousands of hymns begun by flocks of restless songbirds heralding the end of night, the king, still lying on his bed, at once summoned his charioteer and commanded: 'Friend, search diligently for the one called <s>Raikva</s>, a knower of <s>Brahman</s>, a solitary ascetic, [the one who is] <s>sayugvā</s> (with the cart), in those various extremely secluded forest groves, riverbanks, and similar places, and report to us.'
And searching here and there, [the charioteer] saw, in a certain extremely secluded place, under a cart, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> scratching his scabs.
And seeing him, thinking 'This must be <s>Raikva</s>,' he sat down respectfully and asked: 'Are you, O blessed one, <s>Raikva</s> with the cart (<s>sayugvā</s>)?'
And the charioteer, having inferred <s>Raikva</s>'s confirmation and his desire for household life and wealth through various gestures, reported to the king.
The king, hearing this, taking six hundred cows, a gold necklace, and a chariot drawn by she-mules, hastened toward <s>Raikva</s>.
Having arrived, he addressed [<s>Raikva</s>]:
O <s>Raikva</s>, here are six hundred cows, a gold necklace, and this chariot drawn by she-mules — accept these and teach me, O blessed one.
To him who had spoken thus, <s>Raikva</s> replied with both haughtiness and longing:
'<s>Aha hāretvā śūdra</s>' — Come, take away, O <s>Śūdra</s>! Let the cows together [with the rest] be yours alone.
'<s>Aha</s>' is a particle used in haughty address.
The chariot yoked with she-mules (<s>hāretvā</s>) — having gone (<s>itvā</s>) with the chariot (<s>hāreṇa yuktā</s>) — let it be yours together with the cows. [The sense is:] what use is this amount of wealth to me, who lives without material needs and for whom household maintenance is irrelevant?
But the reading '<s>āharetvā</s>' (bring!) has been rejected by the teachers as being meaningless, and because in that case the absence of the correlative 'together with the cows' [would be a defect].
In this story, the word '<s>Śūdra</s>' can be used to refer to <s>Jānaśruti</s>, even though he is a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, through etymological derivation from [its] components.
For that <s>Raikva</s>, wishing to display his clairvoyant knowledge, indicated the grief (<s>śuc</s>) of <s>Jānaśruti</s> by [calling him] '<s>Śūdra</s>.'
But how does the word '<s>Śūdra</s>' indicate grief? It is said:
'#Because of [his] rushing toward that#' (<s>tadādravaṇāt</s>).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] explains this: <s>Jānaśruti</s> rushed toward (<s>abhidudrāva</s>) grief.
The meaning is: [<s>Jānaśruti</s>] was overtaken by grief.

body.text:
#kṣatriyatvagateścottaratra caitrarathena liṅgāt /
itaśca na jātiśūdro jānaśrutiḥ yatkāraṇaṃ#prakaraṇanirūpeṇa kriyamāṇe kṣatriyatvamasya jānaśruteravagamyate caijñarathena liṅgāditi vyācakṣāṇaḥ prakaraṇaṃ nirūpayati- #uttaratra hi saṃvargavidyāvākyaśeṣe# /
caitrarathenābhipratāriṇā niścitakṣātriyatvena samānāyāṃ saṃvargavidyāyāṃ samabhivyāhārālliṅgātsaṃdigdhakṣatriyabāvo jānaśrutiḥ kṣatriyo niścīyate /
'atha ha śaunakaṃ ca kāpeyamabhipratāriṇaṃ ca kākṣaseniṃ sūdena pariviṣyamāṇau brahmacārī bibhikṣe' iti prasiddhayājakatvena kāpeyenābhiprayāriṇo yogaḥ pratīyate /
brahmacāribhikṣayā cāsyāśūdratvamavagamyate /
nahi jātu brahmacārī śūdrān bhikṣate /
yājakena ca kāpeyena yogādyājyo 'bhipratārī /
kṣatriyatvaṃ cāsya caitrarathitvāt /
'tasmāccaitrarathī nāmaikaḥ kṣatrapatirajāyata' iti vacanāt /
caitrarathitvaṃ cāsya kāpeyena yājakena yogāt /
#etena vai citrarathaṃ kāpeyā ayājayanniti#chandogānāṃ dvirātre śrūyate /
tena citrarathasya yājakāḥ kāpeyāḥ /
eṣa cābhipratāri citrarathādanyaḥ sanneva kāpeyānāṃ rājyo bhavati /
yadi caitrarathiḥ syāt samānānvayānāṃ hi prāyeṇa samānānvayā yājakā bhavanti /

children.translated_text: Therefore, because of being a descendant of <s>Citraratha</s>, <s>Abhipratārin Kākṣaseni</s> is a <s>Kṣatriya</s>.
And because of co-mention with him, <s>Jānaśruti</s> too is presumed to be a <s>Kṣatriya</s>.
And from this too <s>Jānaśruti</s> is a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, he says: '#And because of the connection with sovereignty indicated by the sending of a <s>kṣattṛ</s> (door-keeper)#.'

children.text: kṣattṛpreṣaṇe cārthasaṃbhave ca tādṛśasya vadānyapraṣṭhasyaiśvaryaṃ prāyeṇa kṣatriyasya dṛṣṭaṃ yudhiṣṭhirādivaditi //35 //
children.translated_text: In the sending of a <s>kṣattṛ</s> (door-keeper) and in the presence of wealth, such sovereignty of a generous and renowned person is generally seen to belong to a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, as in the case of <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> and others. //35//

body.translated_text: '#And because of the ascertainment of <s>Kṣatriya</s>-hood further on, through the indicatory mark of <s>Caitraratha</s>#.' Furthermore, <s>Jānaśruti</s> is not a <s>Śūdra</s> by birth, because — explaining that when the context is examined, the <s>Kṣatriya</s>-hood of this <s>Jānaśruti</s> is ascertained through the indicatory mark of <s>Caitraratha</s> — he sets forth the context: '#For further on, in the remainder of the <s>Saṃvargavidyā</s> passage#.' Through the indicatory mark of co-mention in the same <s>Saṃvargavidyā</s> with <s>Abhipratārin</s>, whose <s>Kṣatriya</s>-hood is established through <s>Caitraratha</s>, <s>Jānaśruti</s>, whose <s>Kṣatriya</s> status was uncertain, is determined to be a <s>Kṣatriya</s>. From the passage 'Then a <s>Brahmacārin</s> begged from <s>Śaunaka Kāpeya</s> and <s>Abhipratārin Kākṣaseni</s> while they were being served food,' the connection of <s>Abhipratārin</s> with <s>Kāpeya</s>, who is a well-known sacrificial priest, is understood. And from the <s>Brahmacārin</s>'s begging from him, his non-<s>Śūdra</s> status is ascertained, for a <s>Brahmacārin</s> never begs from <s>Śūdra</s>s. And through the connection with <s>Kāpeya</s> as sacrificial priest, <s>Abhipratārin</s> is the patron of the sacrifice. And his <s>Kṣatriya</s>-hood is due to his being a descendant of <s>Citraratha</s>, from the statement 'Therefore one named <s>Caitrarathī</s>, a ruler, was born.' And his status as a descendant of <s>Citraratha</s> is established through the connection with <s>Kāpeya</s> as sacrificial priest. '#With this [ritual] the <s>Kāpeya</s>s caused <s>Citraratha</s> to perform sacrifice#' — this is heard in the <s>Dvirātra</s> [section] of the <s>Chandoga</s>s. Therefore, the <s>Kāpeya</s>s are the sacrificial priests of <s>Citraratha</s>. And this <s>Abhipratārin</s>, though being different from <s>Citraratha</s>, becomes the patron of the <s>Kāpeya</s>s — if he were a descendant of <s>Citraratha</s>, for generally those of the same lineage have priests of the same lineage.

body.text:
#saṃskāraparāmarśāttadabhāvābhilāpācca# /
na kevalamupanītādhyayanavidhiparāmarśena na śūdrasyādhikāraḥ kintu teṣu teṣu vidyopadeśeṣūpanayanasaṃskāraparāmarśāt śūdrasya tadabhāvābhidhānādbrahmavidyāyāmanadhikāra iti /

children.translated_text: Objection: But the instruction of <s>Brahman</s> is heard even for the uninitiated — 'He taught them even without initiating them.'
To this he responds: '#Even the passage "He taught them without initiating them" shows the prior entitlement to <s>Upanayana</s>#.'
Since prohibition presupposes prior entitlement, <s>Upanayana</s> is negated only for those for whom it was previously applicable.

children.text: tacca dvijātīnāmiti dvijātaya eva niṣiddhopanayanā adhikriyante na śūdra iti //36 //
children.translated_text: And that [prior entitlement] belongs to the twice-born (<s>dvijāti</s>s) alone; therefore only the twice-born whose <s>Upanayana</s> has been suspended are eligible [for such instruction], not the <s>Śūdra</s>. //36//

body.translated_text: '#Because of the reference to <s>saṃskāra</s> (purificatory rite), and because of the declaration of its absence [for <s>Śūdra</s>s]#.' Not only is the <s>Śūdra</s> disqualified through the reference to the injunction of <s>Upanayana</s> and Vedic study for the initiated, but also because in the various teachings of <s>vidyā</s>s there is reference to the <s>Upanayana</s> sacrament, and because of the declaration of its absence for the <s>Śūdra</s>, there is no eligibility of the <s>Śūdra</s> for <s>Brahmavidyā</s>.

body.text:
#tadabhāvanirdhāraṇe ca pravṛtteḥ# /
satyakāmo ha vai jābālaḥ pramītapitṛkaḥ svāṃ mātaraṃ jabālāṃ prapaccha,
body.translated_text: '#And because of the effort being directed toward the ascertainment of the absence of that [<s>Śūdra</s> status]#.' <s>Satyakāma</s>, the son of <s>Jabālā</s>, whose father was unknown, asked his own mother <s>Jabālā</s>:

ahamācāryakule brahmacaryaṃ cariṣyāmī, tadbravītu bhavatī kiṅgotro 'hamiti /
sābravīt /
tvajjanakaparicaraṇaparatayā nāhamajñāsiṣaṃ gotraṃ taveti /
sa cvācāryaṃ gautamamupasasāda /

children.text: tadupaśrutyābhyadhādgautamaḥ, nādvijanmana ārjavayuktamīdṛśaṃ vacaḥ, tenāsminna śūdratvasaṃbhāvanāstīti tvāṃ dvijātijanmānamupaneṣya ityupanetamanuśāsituṃ ca jābālaṃ gautamaḥ pravṛttaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard this, <s>Gautama</s> declared: 'Such straightforward speech does not belong to one who is not twice-born; therefore there is no possibility of <s>Śūdra</s>-hood in him — I shall initiate you, recognizing you as one born of the twice-born.' And <s>Gautama</s> proceeded to initiate and instruct <s>Jābāla</s>.
From this too it is understood that a <s>Śūdra</s> has no eligibility.
'#He did not depart from truth#.'
The meaning is: 'You have not transgressed truth.' //37//

body.translated_text: 'I wish to live the life of a <s>Brahmacārin</s> in the teacher's household; please tell me, revered lady, what is my lineage?' She replied: 'Being devoted to serving your father, I did not know your lineage.' He then approached the teacher <s>Gautama</s>. Having approached, he said: 'O revered sir, I wish to live as a <s>Brahmacārin</s> under you.' He [<s>Gautama</s>] said: 'One whose lineage is unknown is not to be initiated; what is your lineage?' Then <s>Satyakāma</s> replied: 'I do not know my own lineage. I asked my mother <s>Jabālā</s>, and she too did not know.'

children.translated_text: '#Because of the prohibition against hearing, studying, and [performing rituals for] their benefit, and because of <s>Smṛti</s>#.'
This has been explained by the <s>Bhāṣya</s> through its own explicit commentary.
The rest has self-evident meaning. //38//

children.translated_text: '#But whatever limited immortality has been stated with reference to the knowledge of <s>Vāyu</s>, that is relative#.'

children.text: 'apapunarmṛtyuṃ jayati' iti śrutyā hyapamṛtyorvijaya ukto natu paramamṛtyuvijaya ityāpe..kitvaṃ (?), tacca tatraiva prakaraṇāntarakaraṇena hetunā /
children.translated_text: Through the <s>Śruti</s> 'he conquers repeated death,' the conquest of untimely death is stated, but not the conquest of ultimate death — thus it is relative; and that [relativity is established] by the reason that a separate context is created within that very [passage].

children.text: na kevalamapaśrutyā tadāpekṣikamapi tu paramātmānamabhidhāya 'ato 'nyadārtam' iti vāṭvāderārtatvābhidhānāt /
children.translated_text: Not only is that [immortality] relative on the basis of the [secondary] <s>Śruti</s>, but also because, after having spoken of the Supreme Self, [the text] declares 'whatever is other than this is afflicted' — thereby declaring the afflicted nature of <s>Vāyu</s> and the rest.
The implication is: one does not become free from affliction by resorting to what is itself afflicted. //39//

body.translated_text: '<s>Kampanāt</s>' (Because of trembling). Setting aside the passage, the context, and the <s>Śruti</s> references to <s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>Vajra</s>, etc., the objection is raised that what is taught here is <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) in its fivefold function, both internal (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) and external — not <s>Brahman</s>. For indeed, the word '<s>Prāṇa</s>' primarily denotes the internal wind, and the word '<s>Vajra</s>' denotes the thunderbolt. And the thunderbolt is a transformation of <s>Vāyu</s>, for <s>Vāyu</s> as the external [element], combined with smoke, light, and water, transforms into the state of a rain-cloud and manifests as lightning, thunder, rain, and thunderbolt. And although the phrase 'the entire universe' would seem to include <s>Vāyu</s>, nevertheless, even a contextually limited term does not abandon its primary referent but merely contracts its scope. But the words '<s>Prāṇa</s>' and '<s>Vajra</s>,' if taken to refer to <s>Brahman</s>, would altogether abandon their primary meaning. Therefore, contraction of scope is preferable to abandonment of primary meaning, since at least a trace of the primary meaning is preserved. The word '<s>amṛta</s>' (immortal) too, meaning the absence of death, does not denote the eternal absence of death, since it can be explained as [mere] longevity; just as [it is said] 'the gods are immortal.' Therefore, in accordance with the <s>Śruti</s> references to <s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>Vajra</s>, it is <s>Vāyu</s> alone that is intended here, not <s>Brahman</s> — such is the prima facie view. To this established [objection], the reply is given: '#<s>Kampanāt</s>#' (Because of trembling). Because the entire universe including <s>Vāyu</s> trembles [before it], it is the Supreme Self alone that is known from the word — this follows by the method of leaping over intermediate terms (<s>maṇḍūkapluti</s>). From <s>Brahman</s>, this entire universe does not deviate; it proceeds in its activity under a fixed rule and does not transgress the boundary. The meaning is this: mere contraction of <s>Śruti</s> scope is not sufficient reason for abandoning the meaning of <s>Śruti</s>; rather, it is the contraction of <s>Śruti</s> scope combined with the syntactic unity of the preceding and following passages and the context. This is what is stated: '#In the preceding and following portions of the text, we find <s>Brahman</s> alone being indicated. How then could we accept that <s>Vāyu</s> is indicated in the intervening portion?#' By this, the syntactic unity of the passage is demonstrated. '#Also from the context#' — through the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, the context is stated. That which was asked about is the principal topic to be answered, and that constitutes the context. If something other than what was asked about were stated, the scripture would become invalid, as it would amount to irrelevant prattle.
