tadantaḥpātinastu sarve tadanuguṇatayā netavyāḥ, natu śrutyanurodhamātreṇa prakaraṇādapakraṣṭavyā iti hi lokasthitiḥ /
anyathopāṃśuyājavākye jāmitādoṣopakrame tatpratisādhānopasaṃhāre ca tadantaḥ pātino 'viṣṇurupāṃśu yaṣṭavyaḥ' ityādayo vidhiśrutyanurodhena pṛthagvidhayaḥ prasajyeran /
tatkimidānīṃ 'tisra eva sāhnasyopasadaḥ kāryā dvādaśāhīnasya' iti prakaraṇānurodhātsāmudāyaprasiddhibalalabdhamahargāṇābhidhānaṃ parityajyāhīnaśabdaḥ kathamapyavavavyutpattyā sānnaṃ jyotiṣṭomamabhidhāya tatraiva dvādaśopasattāṃ vidhattām /
sa hi kṛtsnavidhānānna kutaścidapi hīyate kratorityahīnaḥ śakyo vaktum /
maivam /
avayavaprasiddheḥ samudāyaprasiddhirbalīyasīti śrutyā prakaraṇabādhanānna dvādaśopakratomahīnaguṇayukte jyotiṣṭome śaknoti vidhātum /
nāpyato 'pakṛṣṭaṃ sadahargaṇasya vidhatte /
paraprakaraṇe 'nyadharmavidheranyāṭyatvāt /
asaṃbaddhapadavyavāyavicchinnasya prakaraṇasya punaranusaṃdhānakleśāt /
tenānapakṛṣṭenaiva dvādaśāhīnasyetivākyena sāhnasya tisra usapadaḥ kāryā iti vidhiṃ stotuṃ dvādaśāhavihitā dvādaśopasattā tatprakṛtitvena ca sarvāhīneṣu prāptā nivītādivadanūdyate /
tasmādahīnaśrutyā prakaraṇabādhe 'pi na dvādaśāhīnasyeti vākyasya prakaraṇādapakarṣa /
jyotiṣṭomaprakaraṇāmnātasya pūṣādyanumantraṇamantrasya yalliṅgabalātprakaraṇabādhenāpakarṣastadagatyā /
pauṣṇādau ca takarmaṇi tasyārthavattvāt /
iha tvapakṛṣṭasyārcirādimārgopadeśe phalasyopāyamārgapratipādake 'tiviśade 'eṣa saṃprasādaḥ' iti vākyasyāviśadaikadeśamātrapratipādakasya niṣprayojanatvāt /
naca dvadaśāhīnasyetivadyathoktātmadhyānasādhanānuṣṭhānaṃ stotumeṣa saṃprasāda iti vacamarcirādimārgamanuvadatīti yuktam, stutilakṣaṇāyāṃ svābhidheyasaṃsargatātparyaparityāgaprasaṅgāt dvādaśāhīnasyeti tu vākye svārthasaṃsargatātparye prakaraṇavicchedasya prāptānuvadamātrasyā cāprayojanatvamiti stutyarthau lakṣyate /
na caitaddoṣabhayātsamudāyaprasiddhimullaṅghayāvayavaprasiddhimupāśritya sāhnasyaiva dvādaśopasattāṃ vidhātumarhati, tritvadvādaśatvayorvikalpaprasaṅgāt /
naca satyāṃ gatau vikalpo nyāṭyaḥ /
sāhnāhīnapadayośca prakṛtajyotiṣṭomābhidhāyinorānarthakyaprasaṅgāt /
prakaraṇādeva tadavagateḥ /
iha tu svārthasaṃsargatātparye noktadoṣaprasaṅga iti paurvāparyālocanayā prakaraṇānurodhādrūḍhimapi pūrvakālatāmapi parityajya prakaraṇānuguṇyena jyotiḥ paraṃ brahma pratīyate /
yattūktaṃ mumukṣorādityaprāptirabhihiteti /
nāsāvātyantiko mokṣaḥ, kintu kāryabrahmalokaprāptiḥ /
naca kramamuktyabhiprāyaṃ svena rūpeṇābhiniṣpadyata iti vacanam /
nahyetatprakaraṇoktabrahmatattvaviduṣo gatyutkrāntī staḥ /
tathā ca śrutiḥ-'na tasmāt prāṇā utkrāmanti atraiva samavanīyante' iti /
naca taddvāreṇa kramamuktiḥ /
arcirādimārgasya hi kāryabrahmalokaprāpakatvaṃ na tu brahmabhūyahetubhāvaḥ /

children.translated_text: For the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), in the case of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) whose cause is the direct realization of its nature as eternally pure, luminous <s>Brahman</s> free from all limiting adjuncts, there is no need for the <s>arcirādi-mārga</s> or attainment of the world of <s>kārya-Brahman</s> (conditioned <s>Brahman</s>).
Here too, [<s>jyotis</s> refers to <s>Brahman</s>] because of the fitness of the knower of <s>Brahman</s> [for this interpretation].

children.text: tasmānna jyotirādityamupasaṃpadya saṃprasādasya jīvasya svena rūpeṇa pāramārthikena brahmaṇābhiniṣpattirāñjasīti śruteratrāpi kleśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is not the case that <s>jyotis</s> means the Sun, and that having attained it, the <s>jīva</s> called <s>saṃprasāda</s> (the serene one) manifests in its own form — that is, in its ultimate nature as <s>Brahman</s> — in a straightforward manner. Thus the <s>śruti</s> poses difficulty [for the opponent's view] here as well.

children.text: apica paraṃ jyotiḥ sa uttamapuruṣa itihaivopariṣṭādviśeṣaṇāttejaso vyāvartya puruṣaviṣayatvenāvasthāpanājjyotiḥpadasya, parameva brahma jyotiḥ na tu teja iti siddham //40 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, [the <s>śruti</s> states] 'the supreme light, that is the highest <s>Puruṣa</s>' — since by this qualification occurring later, [the word <s>jyotis</s>] is distinguished from fire and established as referring to <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Supreme Person), it is proven that the word <s>jyotis</s> denotes the supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone, not fire. //40//

body.translated_text: [Sūtra:] '<s>Jyotis</s> (light), because it is seen [in the context of <s>Brahman</s>].' Here, since the word <s>jyotis</s> has its primary meaning as fire (physical light) and only a secondary meaning as <s>Brahman</s>, and since <s>prakaraṇa</s> (contextual topic) is stronger than <s>śruti</s> (direct textual statement), and since there is no restriction of <s>śruti</s> as in the previous case, and moreover since on the view that <s>jyotis</s> means <s>Brahman</s> there would be the unwanted consequence of distorting the <s>ktvā-śruti</s> (gerundive construction) which denotes prior temporal action, and since the <s>samutthāna-śruti</s> (text about rising up) also [supports] that <s>jyotis</s> is fire alone — for <s>samutthāna</s> means rising up, not discriminative knowledge; and rising up is explained on the fire-view through the <s>arcirādi-mārga</s> (path beginning with flame); and <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun), being the supreme light relative to the flame and other [stages], one attains it, having come near it, and manifests in one's own form — [meaning] upon reaching the world of <s>kārya-Brahman</s> (conditioned <s>Brahman</s>), one is gradually liberated. But on the view that <s>jyotis</s> means <s>Brahman</s>, having become <s>Brahman</s>, what further manifestation of one's own nature could there be? Nor can the direct realization of <s>Brahman</s>'s nature as distinct from the body and so forth, being a mental modification, constitute such manifestation, for that [realization] precedes the state of becoming <s>Brahman</s>, it does not follow it — this is the distortion of the <s>ktvā-śruti</s> in the expression 'having attained.' Therefore, since three <s>śruti</s> passages override the <s>prakaraṇa</s>, it is established prima facie that <s>jyotis</s> here means fire alone. This being the prima facie view, it is stated: '#<s>Brahman</s> alone is denoted by the word <s>jyotis</s>. Why? Because it is seen [in context]. For the continuity of that [<s>Brahman</s>] is seen here in the <s>prakaraṇa</s>#.' Indeed, what is stated as the thesis, what is referred to in the middle, and what is concluded — that alone is the principal meaning of the <s>prakaraṇa</s>. All [statements] falling within it must be construed in accordance with it, and must not be dragged away from the <s>prakaraṇa</s> merely on the strength of [individual] <s>śruti</s> [statements] — such is the established practice. Otherwise, in the <s>upāṃśuyāja</s> passage, where the defect of consanguinity (<s>jāmitā</s>) is introduced and its remedy is concluded, the injunctive statements falling within it such as '<s>Viṣṇu</s> is the <s>upāṃśu</s> deity, one should sacrifice [to him]' and so forth would, by merely following the injunctive <s>śruti</s>, become separate injunctions [unrelated to the context]. Then should the statement 'three <s>upasad</s>s are to be performed for the <s>sāhna</s>, twelve for the <s>ahīna</s>' — setting aside the designation of the <s>mahargaṇa</s> obtained through the force of conventional usage of the aggregate, in accordance with the <s>prakaraṇa</s> — [should] the word <s>ahīna</s>, through some forced etymology, designate the six-day <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and prescribe twelve <s>upasad</s>s for that alone? For it can be said that [the sacrifice] is called <s>ahīna</s> (non-deficient) because, due to its complete ritual procedure, it is not deficient (<s>hīna</s>) in any respect. Not so. Since the conventional meaning of the aggregate is stronger than the conventional meaning of the parts, due to [the principle that] <s>śruti</s> overrides <s>prakaraṇa</s>, it cannot prescribe [twelve <s>upasad</s>s] for the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, which is introduced as a twelve-day [sacrifice] endowed with the qualities of a <s>mahīna</s>. Nor does it prescribe for anything dragged away from this, namely for the <s>ahargaṇa</s> [day-count]. For prescribing the properties of one thing in the context of another is [a case of] being out of place. Because of the difficulty of re-establishing the continuity of a <s>prakaraṇa</s> that has been interrupted by the intervention of unconnected words. Therefore, without any such displacement, through the very statement 'twelve for the <s>ahīna</s>,' in order to commend the injunction that 'three <s>upasad</s>s are to be performed for the <s>sāhna</s>,' the twelve <s>upasad</s>s prescribed for the twelve-day [sacrifice], which are already established for all <s>ahīna</s>s through their being the archetype, are merely restated, like the <s>nivīta</s> [wearing of the sacred thread] and such. Therefore, even when the <s>śruti</s> about <s>ahīna</s> overrides the <s>prakaraṇa</s>, the statement 'twelve for the <s>ahīna</s>' is not displaced from its <s>prakaraṇa</s>. As for the <s>pūṣādi-anumantraṇa-mantra</s> (invocation mantras of <s>Pūṣan</s> and others), which is stated in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> context — its displacement through overriding the <s>prakaraṇa</s> by the force of indicatory marks is unavoidable, because in the <s>pauṣṇa</s> and other rites, that [mantra] has purposefulness. But here, if displaced, since the teaching of the <s>arcirādi-mārga</s> is a very detailed exposition of the means-path for the result, the statement 'this is <s>saṃprasāda</s> (the serene one)' — which conveys only an unclear partial meaning — would be purposeless. Nor is it proper [to say] that, as in the case of 'twelve for the <s>ahīna</s>,' the statement 'this is <s>saṃprasāda</s>' merely restates the <s>arcirādi-mārga</s> in order to commend the practice of meditation on the self as described — because in the case of commendatory interpretation, there would be the abandonment of the purport of connection with its own referent; whereas in the statement 'twelve for the <s>ahīna</s>,' since the purport of connection with its own referent [is maintained] and the interruption of <s>prakaraṇa</s> is merely a restatement of what is already established, there is no purposelessness — hence the commendatory interpretation applies [there]. Nor should one, out of fear of this defect, transgress the conventional meaning of the aggregate and resort to the conventional meaning of the parts to prescribe twelve <s>upasad</s>s for the <s>sāhna</s> alone, because there would be the unwanted option between three and twelve. And when a definite rule is available, an option is not proper. Moreover, the words <s>sāhna</s> and <s>ahīna</s>, which designate the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> under discussion, would become purposeless, since their meaning would already be understood from the <s>prakaraṇa</s> alone. But here, when the purport is connection with its own referent, the aforementioned defects do not arise. Therefore, through deliberation on the sequence [of the text], in accordance with the <s>prakaraṇa</s>, setting aside even the primary meaning [of <s>jyotis</s>] and even the prior-temporal meaning, <s>jyotis</s> is understood as the supreme <s>Brahman</s> in conformity with the <s>prakaraṇa</s>. As for the objection that the attainment of <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) is stated for the seeker of liberation — that is not ultimate <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), but rather attainment of the world of <s>kārya-Brahman</s> (conditioned <s>Brahman</s>). Nor is the statement 'he manifests in his own form' intended for gradual liberation (<s>kramamukti</s>). For one who knows the truth of <s>Brahman</s> as taught in the <s>prakaraṇa</s>, there is no departure or ascent [of the vital breaths]. As the <s>śruti</s> states: 'The vital breaths do not depart from him; they are absorbed right here.' Nor is there gradual liberation through that [path], for the <s>arcirādi-mārga</s> leads to the world of <s>kārya-Brahman</s>, but is not the cause of becoming <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text:
#ākāśor'thāntaratvādivyapadeśāt# /
yadyapi 'ākāśastalliṅgāt' ityatra brahmaliṅgadarśanādākāśaḥ paramātmeti vyutpāditaṃ, tathāpi tadvadatra paramātmaliṅgadarśanābhāvānnāmarūpanirmahaṇasya bhūtākāśe 'pyavakāśadānenopapatterakasmānna rūḍhiparityāgasyāyogāt, nāmarūpe antarā brahmeti ca nākāśasya nāmarūpayornirvahiturantarālatvamāha, api tu brahmaṇaḥ, tena bhūtākāśo nāmarūpayornirvahitā /
brahma caitayorantarālaṃ madhyaṃ sāramiti yāvat /
na tu nirvoḍaiva brahma, antarālaṃ vā nirvāḍhṛ /
tasmātprasiddherbhūtākāśo na tu brahmeti prāptam /
evaṃ prāpta ucyate-paramevākāśaṃ brahma, #kasmāt, arthāntaratvādivyapadeśāt# /
nāmarūpamātranirvāhakamihākāśamucyate /
bhūtākāśaṃ ca vikāratvena nāmarūpāntaḥpāti sat kathamātmānamudvahet /
nahi suśikṣito 'pi vijñānī svena skandhenātmānaṃ voḍhumutsahate /
naca nāmarūpaśrutiraviśeṣataḥ pravṛttā bhūtākāśavarjaṃ nāmarūpāntare saṃkocayituṃ sati saṃbhave yujyate /
naca nirvāhakatvaṃ niraṅkuśamavagataṃ brahmaliṅgaṃ kathañcitkleśena paratantre netumucitam 'anena jīvenātmanānupraviśya nāmarūpe vyākaravāṇi' iti ca sraṣṭṛtvamatisphuṭaṃ brahmaliṅgamatra pratīyate /

children.text: brahmarūpatayā ca jīvasya vyākartṛtve brahmaṇa eva vyākartṛtvamuktam /
children.translated_text: And since the <s>jīva</s> has the nature of <s>Brahman</s>, when the <s>jīva</s> is said to be the fashioner, it is actually <s>Brahman</s> alone that is said to be the fashioner.
And thus, since the intermediary status is established only for the sustainer, the supposition of a distinction — that the sustainer is one thing and the intermediary is another — is not justified.

children.text: tathā ca te nāmarūpe yadantaretyayamarthāntaravyapadeśa upapanno bhavatyākāśasya /
children.translated_text: And accordingly, the designation as something different — 'that which is the intermediary of those names and forms' — is fitting for <s>ākāśa</s> [understood as <s>Brahman</s>].

children.text: tasmādarthāntaravyapadeśāt, tathā 'tadbrahma tadamṛtam' iti vyapadeśādbrahmaivākāśamiti siddham //41 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, because of the designation as something different, and also because of the designation 'that is <s>Brahman</s>, that is the immortal,' it is established that <s>ākāśa</s> is indeed <s>Brahman</s>. //41//

body.translated_text: [Sūtra:] '#<s>Ākāśa</s> (space), because of the designation as something different, and so forth#.' Although in the [sūtra] '<s>Ākāśa</s>, because of its characteristic marks,' it was established that <s>ākāśa</s> is the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) through the observation of characteristic marks of <s>Brahman</s>, nevertheless, since here there is no observation of such characteristic marks of the Supreme Self, and since the fashioning of name and form can be accounted for even in elemental space (<s>bhūtākāśa</s>) through the notion of providing scope, why should the primary meaning be abandoned without reason? And the [<s>śruti</s>] statement '<s>Brahman</s> is the intermediary of name and form' does not mean that <s>ākāśa</s> is the sustainer of name and form in the sense of being intermediate between them; rather, it means that <s>Brahman</s> [is their intermediary]. Thus elemental space is the sustainer of name and form, and <s>Brahman</s> is their intermediary — that is, their middle, their essence, as it were. But <s>Brahman</s> is not merely the sustainer, nor is the intermediary merely the sustainer. Therefore, by established usage, [<s>ākāśa</s> means] elemental space, not <s>Brahman</s> — this is the prima facie view. This being the prima facie position, it is stated: <s>Ākāśa</s> is indeed the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. '#Why? Because of the designation as something different, and so forth#.' What is called <s>ākāśa</s> here is merely the sustainer of name and form. And elemental space, being a modification, falls within the category of name and form — how then could it sustain itself? For even a well-trained intelligent person cannot lift himself by his own shoulders. And the <s>śruti</s> about name and form, having been employed without restriction, cannot, when there is the possibility [of a wider reference], be confined to name and form excluding elemental space. And the sustaining capacity, understood without any restriction, being a characteristic mark of <s>Brahman</s>, should not be forced with difficulty into a dependent meaning. Moreover, [from the <s>śruti</s>] 'Having entered through this <s>jīva</s>-self, let me manifest names and forms' — the creatorship is very clearly perceived here as a characteristic mark of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.translated_text: [Sūtra:] '#Because of the distinction [made] in deep sleep and departure [from the body]#.'
'Since at the beginning, middle, and end, the transmigrating [soul] is presented,
In the textual composition pertaining to that [transmigrating soul], everything should be construed in reference to that alone.'

body.text:
' saṃsāryeva tāvadātmāhaṅkārāspadaprāṇādiparītaḥ sarvajanasiddhaḥ /
tameva ca 'yo 'yaṃ vijñānamayaḥ prāṇeṣu' ityādiśrutisaṃdarbha ādimadhyāvasāneṣvāmṛśatīti tadanuvādaparo bhavitumarhati /
evaṃ ca saṃsāryātmaiva kiñcidapekṣya mahān, saṃsārasya cānāditvenānāditvādaja ucyate, na tu tadatiriktaḥ kaścidatra nityaśuddhabuddhamuktatvabhāvaḥ pratipādyaḥ /
yattu suṣuptyutkrāntyoḥ prājñenātmanā saṃpariṣvakta iti bhedaṃ manyase, nāsau bhedaḥ kintvayamātmaśabdaḥ svabhāvavacanaḥ, tena suṣuptyutkrāntyavasthāyāṃ viśeṣaviṣayābhāvātsaṃpiṇḍitaprajñeva prājñenātmanā svabhāvenā pariṣvakto na kiñcidvedetyabhede 'pi bhedavadupacāreṇa yojanīyam /
yathāhuḥ-'prājñaḥ saṃpiṇḍitaprajñaḥ' iti /
patyādayaśca śabdāḥ saṃsāriṇyeva kāryakaraṇasaṃghātātmakasya jagato jīvakarmārjitatayā tadbhogyatayā ca yojanīyāḥ /
tasmātsaṃsāryevānūdyate na tu paramātmā pratipadyata iti prāptam /
evaṃ prāpte 'bhidhīyate-'suṣuptyutkrāntyorbhedena vyapadeśādityanuvartate /
ayamabhisaṃdhiḥ-kiṃ saṃsāriṇo 'nyaḥ paramātmā nāsti, tasmātsaṃsāryātmaparaṃ 'yo 'yaṃ vijñānamayaḥ prāṇeṣu' iti vākyam, āhosvidiha saṃsārivyatirekeṇa paramātmano 'saṃkīrtanātsaṃsāriṇaścādimadhyāvasāneṣvavamarśanātsaṃsāryātmaparaṃ, na tāvatsaṃsāryatiriktasya tasyābhāvaḥ /
tatpratipādakā hi śataśa āgamāḥ 'īkṣaternāśabdam' 'gatisāmānyāt' ityādibiḥ sūtrasaṃdarbhairupapāditāḥ /
na cātrāpi saṃsāryatiriktaparamātmasaṃkīrtanābhāvaḥ, suṣuptyutkrāntyestatsaṃkīrtanāt /
naca prājñasya paramātmano jīvādbhedena saṃkīrtanaṃ sati saṃbhave rāhoḥ śira itivadaupacārikaṃ yuktam /
naca prājñaśabdaḥ prajñāprakarṣaśālini nirūḍhavṛttiḥ kathañcidajñaviṣayo vyākhyātumucitaḥ /
naca prajñāprakarṣo 'saṃkucadvṛttirviditasamastaveditavyātsarvavido 'nyatra saṃbhavati /
na cetthaṃbhūto jīvātmā /
tasmātsuṣuptyutkrāntyorbhedena jīvātprājñasya paramātmano vyapadeśāt 'yo 'yaṃ vijñānamayaḥ' ityādinā jīvātmānaṃ lokasiddhamanūdya tasya paramātmabhāvo 'nanadhigataḥ pratipādyate /
naca jīvātmanuvādamātraparāṇyetāni vacāṃsi /
anadhigatārthāvabodhanaparaṃ hi śābdaṃ pramāṇaṃ, na tvanuvādamātraniṣṭhaṃ bhavitumarhati /
ata eva ca saṃsāriṇaḥ paramātmabhāvavidhānāyādimadhyāvasāneṣvanupādyatayāvamarśa upapadyate /

children.text: evaṃ ca mahattvaṃ cājatvaṃ ca sarvagatasya nityasyātmanaḥ saṃbhavānnāpekṣikaṃ kalpayiṣyate /
children.translated_text: And thus, greatness and unborn-ness are naturally possible for the all-pervading, eternal Self, and need not be construed as merely relative.
[Sūtra:] '#But that [the reference to the transmigrating self] in the middle, [being interspersed] with descriptions of states such as the waking state and so forth —#'
It is not the state of having stages that is intended to be expressed by this.

children.text: api tvavasthānāmupajanāpāyadharmakatvena tadatiriktamavasthārahitaṃ paramātmānaṃ vivakṣati, uparitanavākyasaṃdarbhālocanāditi //42 //
children.translated_text: Rather, by virtue of the stages possessing the property of origination and destruction, it intends to express <s>Paramātman</s> (the Supreme Self) who is beyond them and devoid of stages — this is understood from examining the connection of the subsequent statements. //42//

body.translated_text: Now, the transmigrating self, accompanied by the vital breaths and other [faculties] which are the seat of ego-sense, is known to all people. And the scriptural passage beginning with 'that which consists of consciousness among the vital breaths' refers to this very [transmigrating self] at the beginning, middle, and end — therefore it should be understood as merely restating that. And thus, the transmigrating self alone, being great in some relative sense, and being called <s>aja</s> (unborn) because of the beginninglessness of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration), [should be the referent] — but no entity beyond that, characterized by eternal purity, consciousness, and freedom, is being taught here. As for your view that a distinction is intended [in the references to] deep sleep and departure [from the body] — 'embraced by the all-knowing Self (<s>prājña</s>)' — that is not a [real] distinction. Rather, the word <s>ātman</s> here denotes one's own nature. Therefore, in the states of deep sleep and departure, due to the absence of objects of particular cognition, with cognition as it were contracted, 'embraced by the all-knowing Self, by one's own nature, he knows nothing' — even though there is no [real] difference, it should be construed figuratively as if there were a difference. As they say: '<s>prājña</s> means one whose cognition is contracted.' And the words <s>pati</s> (lord) and the like should be construed with reference to the transmigrating [self] alone, since the world, consisting of the aggregate of body and senses, is to be construed as being earned by the <s>jīva</s>'s <s>karma</s> and as being the object of its experience. Therefore, it is merely the transmigrating self that is being restated, not the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) that is being taught — this is the prima facie view. This being the prima facie position, it is stated: 'Because of the distinction [made] in deep sleep and departure' — [the word <s>arthāntaravyapadeśāt</s>] is understood to continue [from the previous sūtra]. The intended meaning is as follows: Is there no Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) other than the transmigrating [self], such that the passage 'that which consists of consciousness among the vital breaths' refers to the transmigrating self alone? Or rather, since the Supreme Self is mentioned here as distinct from the transmigrating [self], and since the transmigrating [self] is referred to at the beginning, middle, and end, [does the passage concern] the transmigrating self? In fact, the non-existence of that [Supreme Self] distinct from the transmigrating [self] cannot be maintained. For hundreds of scriptures establish its existence, as demonstrated through the series of <s>sūtra</s>s such as 'Because of [the activity of] seeing, [<s>Brahman</s> is the cause,] not the non-sentient [<s>pradhāna</s>],' 'Because of the commonality of the going [to <s>Brahman</s>],' and so forth. Nor is there an absence of mention of the Supreme Self distinct from the transmigrating [self] in this passage, since such mention is made in the contexts of deep sleep and departure. And the mention of the all-knowing <s>Paramātman</s> (<s>prājña</s>) as distinct from the <s>jīva</s> — when a [literal] possibility exists — should not be construed figuratively, as in the expression '<s>Rāhu</s>'s head.' Nor is the word <s>prājña</s>, which has an established meaning of one endowed with excellence of knowledge, properly interpreted as referring to one who is ignorant. And the excellence of knowledge, being of unrestricted scope — belonging to one who knows all that is to be known, the omniscient — cannot be found elsewhere [than in the Supreme Self]. And the <s>jīva</s> (individual self) is not of such a nature. Therefore, because of the designation of the all-knowing Supreme Self (<s>prājña</s>) as distinct from the <s>jīva</s> in deep sleep and departure, through [the passage] 'that which consists of consciousness' and so forth, the <s>jīva</s> known to common experience is merely restated, and its identity with the Supreme Self, not previously known, is taught. Nor are these statements merely concerned with restating the <s>jīva</s>. For verbal testimony (<s>śabda-pramāṇa</s>) is directed toward communicating what is not previously known, and should not be taken as merely making restatements. And it is precisely for this reason — to teach the Supreme Self-nature of the transmigrating [self] — that the reference [to the transmigrating self] at the beginning, middle, and end is fitting, since it serves as the basis for what is being restated.

body.translated_text: 'That which is inferred [as <s>Pradhāna</s>] also, [is not so] according to some, because of the apprehension [of it] as arranged in the figure of the embodied [self]; and [the scripture] shows [this]' (#<s>ānumānikam apy ekeṣām iti cet na śārīrarūpakavinyastagṛhīter darśayati ca</s>#). One might argue thus: Having proposed the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>, the definition of <s>Brahman</s> was stated as 'that from which the origin etc. [of this world proceed].' This definition does not apply to <s>Pradhāna</s> and such [non-conscious principles], which would make it a faulty definition due to over-extension; rather it applies to <s>Brahman</s> alone — this was established in '[It is not the non-conscious] because of [the mention of] seeing, [and it is] not the unspoken [<s>Pradhāna</s>].' And there is a general tendency of <s>Vedānta</s> statements toward teaching <s>Brahman</s> as the cause, not toward teaching <s>Pradhāna</s> as the cause — this was elaborated through the subsequent series of <s>sūtra</s>s. Then what remains for whose sake the subsequent series is commenced? Nor is there over-extension even if 'the <s>avyakta</s> is beyond the great' and similar [passages] are harmonized with <s>Pradhāna</s>, for these do not teach that <s>Pradhāna</s> is the cause of the world, but merely the existence of <s>Pradhāna</s>. And by the mere existence of that, nothing is diminished from the definition of <s>Brahman</s> as 'that from which the origin etc. [of this world proceed].' Therefore the subsequent series is purposeless — to this he responds: '#Having proposed the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>#.' The passages 'the <s>avyakta</s> is beyond the great' and 'the one unborn' etc. do not merely establish the existence of <s>Pradhāna</s>, but rather [teach] that <s>Pradhāna</s> is the cause of the world. For in 'beyond the great,' the word <s>para</s> (beyond) indicates being temporally prior and remote, and thus causality. And for passages like 'the one unborn' etc., the teaching of causality is quite explicit. Thus, because of the over-extension of the definition, the commencement of the subsequent series for preventing such over-extension is appropriate. He states the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (objection): '#That in those [passages]#.' He states the well-established usage in <s>Sāṃkhya</s> doctrine: '#There, <s>avyakta</s>#.' Not only is there conventional usage from the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> tradition, but this very meaning is also understood from the established meaning of the component parts — he says: '#Not <s>vyakta</s> (manifest)#.' Because it lacks the attributes denoted by words such as <s>śānta</s> (calm), <s>ghora</s> (terrible), and <s>mūḍha</s> (deluding).

body.translated_text: there exists the unmanifest as the cause.' Nor can the word <s>avyakta</s> in 'the <s>avyakta</s> is beyond the great' refer to the body on the grounds of context and elimination, because the body, being characterized by attributes denoted by words like <s>śānta</s> (calm), <s>ghora</s> (terrible), and <s>mūḍha</s> (deluding), cannot properly be called <s>avyakta</s> (unmanifest). Therefore, when it is concluded that what is called <s>avyakta</s> is none other than <s>Pradhāna</s>, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] replies: '#This is not so. For this <s>Kāṭhaka</s> passage [does not refer to <s>Pradhāna</s>]#.' For it is popular, worldly usage — conventional meaning — that serves as the basis for determining the meaning of the <s>Veda</s>, since it is the means for that. As they say: 'The very words that are worldly are also Vedic, and their meanings are the same.' But the technical terminology of philosophers [does not serve this purpose], for it is of human origin and is not established as a basis for determining the meaning of the <s>Veda</s> — just like the conventional usage [of terms] in medicine and the like. Therefore, from conventional usage at least, <s>Pradhāna</s> is not what is understood [by the word <s>avyakta</s>]. And the etymological derivation applies equally elsewhere too. Thus, when the <s>śruti</s> reference to <s>avyakta</s> is otherwise established [as not referring to <s>Pradhāna</s>], through context and elimination, this word <s>avyakta</s> refers to the body. How it properly refers to that will be shown later. Among those — body and the rest — 'know the sense objects as pertaining to them.' Just as a horse moves by relying on the road, so the sense organs, being like horses, function by relying on their respective objects. '<s>Ātman</s> is the enjoyer' — so say the wise. How? When there is the conjunction — the <s>yoga</s> — of the sense organs, mind, and self. For through the contact of sense organs, objects, and mind, the <s>ātman</s> is the enjoyer of smell and the like. The context, as a statement expectant of [identifying] <s>Pradhāna</s>, should be understood [differently]: 'the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is <s>Pradhāna</s>' — he introduces that expectation: '#With those uncontrolled senses etc.#' The statement about lack of control serves to indicate, by way of contrast, the benefit of control. The word <s>para</s> means 'superior.' Now, if superiority means being more internal, then the senses alone would be superior to external objects like smell etc. — to this he says: '#The objects which are sound etc.#' Superiority is not by virtue of being more internal, but by virtue of being predominant, and that depends on what is intended; since the predominance of the objects over the senses (<s>graha</s>s) is intended by the <s>śruti</s>, the superiority of objects over the senses follows. For the <s>śruti</s> has called eight <s>graha</s>s (seizers) — namely the organs of smell, taste, speech, sight, hearing, mind, hands, and skin — as the sense organs. They seize, that is, bring under control, the person who is [like] an animal. But they are not able to bring him under control in his own essential nature, so long as they do not present to this person — who is like a sacrificial animal — smell, taste, form, color, sound, desire, action, and touch. Therefore smell and the rest are the eight <s>atigraha</s>s (over-seizers), because it is by their presentation that the seizing nature of the <s>graha</s>s is established. This is what was stated: '#The seizing nature of the senses and the over-seizing nature of the objects are well-known from <s>śruti</s>#.' Even though the mind is equal to the senses in its seizing nature, he states its superiority over the objects by a distinguishing feature belonging to itself: '#And the superiority of the mind over the objects#.' Why is the person introduced as a charioteer? To this he says: '#Because of the word <s>ātman</s>#.' The meaning is: because of the recognition of that [self]. He states the reason for its superiority: '#And because it is the enjoyer#.' By this, the <s>jīvātman</s> (individual self) is called great (<s>mahān</s>) by virtue of being the master. Alternatively, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says that the <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) pertaining to <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> is designated by the word <s>ātman</s>, according to both <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>: '#Or alternatively. <s>Pūḥ</s> (city)#.' The <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) is the <s>pūḥ</s> (city) because it is the substratum of the entire collection of objects of experience. Thus, since all individual intellects have as their single abode the primordial intellect of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, the intellect of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> possesses greatness and selfhood through encompassing [all others]. Therefore the separate treatment [of <s>mahān ātmā</s>] from <s>buddhi</s> in general is justified. Now, in this interpretation, since the intellect of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> has the status of <s>ātman</s>, there is no mention here of a chariot-rider as the self of the enjoyer — so not merely a chariot remains but also a chariot-possessor. To this he says: '#In this interpretation, however#.' Just as a superimposed reflection does not in reality differ from the original, so too the <s>vijñānātman</s> (cognizing self) does not in reality differ from <s>Paramātman</s> (the Supreme Self). Thus it is <s>Paramātman</s> alone who is taken here as the possessor of the chariot, and therefore only the chariot remains [to be accounted for]. Now, what is the purpose of the figurative construction of the chariot etc. with respect to the body and the rest? To this he says: '#For one who is not conjoined with body, senses, mind, intellect, and objects, there is no experience#.' <s>Vedanā</s> means the experience of pleasure and the like. <s>Pratyagātman</s> (the inner self) here refers to the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), and his attainment of <s>Brahman</s> [is the goal]. And since the identity of the <s>jīva</s> with <s>Brahman</s> is not established through other means of knowledge, so that scripture would not be needed here, he says: '#And thus#.'

The rest is of transparent meaning. //1//

avyākṛtamavyaktamityanarthāntaram /

children.translated_text: That which is its nature as pleasure — that is <s>sattva</s>.
That which is its nature as pain — that is <s>rajas</s>.
That which is its nature as delusion — that is <s>tamas</s>.
And thus the <s>avyakta</s> is admitted to be none other than <s>Pradhāna</s>. //2//

body.translated_text: The <s>sūtra</s> that aims at removing the seed of the lingering doubt of the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> (objector) is: 'But it is subtle, because of the fitness for that.' Because the modifications are non-different from <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), the unmanifest character of <s>prakṛti</s> is figuratively applied to the modifications. Just as in 'prosperous with cows,' the word <s>go</s> (cow) [is applied] to its modification, milk. The evidence that the modifications deserve the designation <s>avyakta</s> by virtue of their non-difference from the cause, the <s>avyakta</s>, he states: '#And thus the <s>śruti</s>#.' <s>Avyākṛta</s> (undifferentiated) and <s>avyakta</s> (unmanifest) are synonymous. Now, if this is so, then <s>Pradhāna</s> itself is admitted, for the world, being of the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion, can only arise from a cause of the same nature, since the effect is of the nature of the cause.

children.translated_text: Nor does the fact that the primary sense does not [directly] refer to that [second referent] prevent the figurative usage from obtaining.
Just as when the word 'crow' is used where only the sense of 'destroyer' is contextually expected, it is understood to refer to all destroyers including dogs and the like.
As they say: 'When a child is told "Protect the food from the crows,"
because the primary intent is warding off harm, he also protects it from dogs and the like, not only [from crows].'

body.translated_text: The <s>sūtra</s> is for the purpose of removing the doubt — #<s>tadadhīnatvād arthavat</s># (Because it is dependent on That, it is purposeful). For the <s>Pradhāna</s> of the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, whether theistic or atheistic, can be described as actually distinct from <s>Īśvara</s> or from the <s>kṣetrajñas</s> (individual souls). But this <s>avidyā</s>-power of <s>Brahman</s>, denoted by words such as <s>māyā</s>, cannot be described either as identical with or as different from [<s>Brahman</s>]. This very indescribability (<s>anirvacanīyatva</s>) is what constitutes its unmanifest nature (<s>avyaktatva</s>). This is the difference between the doctrine of the unmanifest (<s>avyākṛtavāda</s>) and the doctrine of <s>Pradhāna</s> (<s>pradhānavāda</s>). And the <s>avidyā</s>-power is dependent on <s>Īśvara</s>, because it has Him as its substrate. Nor is mere substance without power sufficient for producing an effect — hence the purposefulness of the power. This is what is stated — #<s>arthavat</s># (purposeful). Here one might object: if <s>saṃsāra</s> is experienced through <s>Brahman</s>'s <s>avidyā</s>-power, then there would be the unwanted consequence of re-origination even for the liberated, since that [<s>avidyā</s>] would remain constant like <s>Pradhāna</s>. Or if it were destroyed, there would be the total cessation of all <s>saṃsāra</s>, since the root <s>avidyā</s>-power would be entirely eliminated — to this he says: #<s>muktānāṃ ca punaḥ</s># (And for the liberated, again...) — there is no re-arising of bondage. #Why? Because by <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), that seed-power is burnt.# The intended meaning is this: we do not maintain, as the <s>Pradhānavādins</s> do, that <s>avidyā</s> is one and the same for all <s>jīvas</s>, by which [objection] we would be thus reproached; rather, this [<s>avidyā</s>] is differentiated for each <s>jīva</s>. Therefore, only for the very <s>jīva</s> in whom <s>vidyā</s> has arisen is <s>avidyā</s> removed, not for another <s>jīva</s>, since <s>vidyā</s> and <s>avidyā</s> belonging to different substrates do not conflict — so how could there be the unwanted consequence of total cessation of <s>saṃsāra</s>? But for the proponents of <s>Pradhāna</s>, this is indeed a defect: since <s>Pradhāna</s> is one, its elimination would mean the elimination of everything, and if it is not eliminated, then no one would ever be liberated. Even if <s>Pradhāna</s> were multiple, since bondage and liberation are grounded in the reality and unreality of <s>avidyā</s> characterized as non-discriminative cognition (<s>aviveka-khyāti</s>), then <s>Pradhāna</s> becomes superfluous, since [bondage and liberation] are accounted for by the reality and unreality of <s>avidyā</s> alone. Nor is it valid to say that the differentiation of <s>jīvas</s> depends on the differentiation of <s>avidyā</s> as limiting adjunct, and the differentiation of <s>avidyā</s> as limiting adjunct depends on the differentiation of <s>jīvas</s>, resulting in mutual dependence and hence the non-establishment of both — this is not a problem, because both are established as beginningless, like the seed and sprout. And the figurative usage of oneness is based merely on [the shared nature of] being <s>avidyā</s> — [hence it is called] 'unmanifest' (<s>avyakta</s>) and 'undifferentiated' (<s>avyākṛta</s>). If one objects: 'In this case, <s>avidyā</s> alone is the seed of the world, so what need is there for <s>Īśvara</s>?' — to this he says: #<s>parameśvarāśrayā</s># (having the Supreme Lord as its substrate). For the non-conscious, not presided over by consciousness, is not sufficient for producing an effect — hence [<s>avidyā</s>] depends on the Supreme Lord either as efficient cause or as material cause for accomplishing its own effect. For the substratum of the illusion of the world-appearance is <s>Īśvara</s>, just as the substratum of the illusion of a snake is the rope. Thus, just as the snake-illusion has the rope as its material basis, so the world-illusion has <s>Īśvara</s> as its material basis. Therefore, even though <s>avidyā</s> has the <s>jīva</s> as its locus, it depends on <s>Īśvara</s> as efficient cause and as object — hence it is said to have <s>Īśvara</s> as its substrate; but not as its receptacle, since that would be impossible in <s>Brahman</s> whose nature is knowledge. For this very reason he says: #'In which [<s>avidyā</s>], devoid of the awakening to their own true nature, the transmigrating <s>jīvas</s> sleep.'# — In which <s>avidyā</s>, when it obtains, the <s>jīvas</s> sleep. The true nature of the <s>jīvas</s> is the real <s>Brahman</s>; 'devoid of the awakening to that, they sleep' — thus the [power of] dissolution (<s>laya</s>) is stated. 'Transmigrating' — thus the [power of] projection (<s>vikṣepa</s>) is stated. #Because the state of being a <s>jīva</s> is dependent on the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>).# Although both the <s>jīva</s> and the <s>avyakta</s> are beginningless and hence have no fixed temporal priority, nevertheless, intending to express the priority of the <s>avyakta</s>, this is stated. #'Even though, like the body, the senses and the rest...'# — this should be understood on the analogy of the words 'cow' and 'bull' [as a <s>gaubalīvarda</s> compound denoting a general class]. He states the view of those close to [but not identical with] the <s>Ācārya</s>: #'Others, however...'# He refutes this: #'But by them...'# Since both contextual connection (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) and elimination (<s>pāriśeṣya</s>) are equally applicable in both cases, there is no reason to restrict the reference to only one. He raises an objection: #'For the purpose of the <s>āmnāya</s> (scripture)...'# The meaning of the objection is: the word <s>avyakta</s> itself is the cause of distinguishing [something] from the gross body, since the latter is manifest (<s>vyakta</s>). He refutes: No. #Because of dependence on syntactic unity (<s>ekavākyatā</s>).# When syntactic unity is possible — without abandoning what is contextually relevant and without introducing what is contextually irrelevant — division of the sentence is not justified. And there is no syntactic unity without mutual expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>); and both [the gross and subtle bodies] are contextually relevant — hence both are expected as referents here, and even a single word refers to both bodies.

' iti /
nanu na śarīradvayasyātrākāhkṣā /
kintu duḥśodhatvātsūkṣmasyaiva śarīrasya, natu ṣāṭkauśikasya sthūlasyaṣa etaddhi dṛṣṭabībhatsatayā sukaraṃ vairāgyaviṣayatvena śodhayitumityata āha- #na caivaṃ#
body.translated_text: Thus. But [one might object]: here there is no expectancy for both bodies; rather, because of the difficulty of purifying it, only the subtle body [is meant], not the gross body made of six sheaths — for the latter, being manifestly repulsive, is easy to make a subject of dispassion for the purpose of purification — to this he says: #<s>na caivam</s>#

children.translated_text: #<s>mantavyam</s># (it should not be thought so).

children.text: viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padamavagamayituṃ paraṃ paramatra pratipādyatvena prastutaṃ na tu vairāgyāya śodhanamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: what is contextually intended here as that which is to be taught is the supreme — the highest state of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — to be made known, not purification for the sake of dispassion.

children.text: alaṃ vā vivādena, bhavatu sūkṣmameva śarīraṃ pariśodhyaṃ, tathāpi na sāṃkhyābhimatamatra pradhānaṃ paramityabhyupetyāha- #sarvathāpi tviti# //3 //
children.translated_text: Or enough with disputation — let it be granted that only the subtle body is to be purified; even so, the <s>Pradhāna</s> accepted by <s>Sāṃkhya</s> is not the supreme [entity] referred to here — conceding this, he says: #<s>sarvathāpi tu</s># (In any case, however...) //3//

body.text: #jñeyatvāvacanācca# /

children.translated_text: For this additional reason too, this word <s>avyakta</s> does not refer to the <s>Pradhāna</s> accepted by <s>Sāṃkhya</s>.

children.text: sāṃkhyaiḥ khalu pradhānādvivekena puruṣaṃ niḥśreyasāya jñātuṃ vā vibhūtyai vā pradhānaṃ jñeyatvenopakṣipyate /
children.translated_text: For the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> indeed present <s>Pradhāna</s> as something to be known — either for the purpose of knowing <s>Puruṣa</s> through discrimination from <s>Pradhāna</s>, leading to the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>), or for the purpose of [attaining] supernatural powers (<s>vibhūti</s>).

children.text: na ceha jānīyāditi copāsīteti vā vidhivibhaktiśrutirasti, api tvavyaktapadamātram /
children.translated_text: But here there is no injunctive verbal suffix (<s>vidhivibhakti</s>) in the form 'one should know' (<s>jānīyāt</s>) or 'one should meditate' (<s>upāsīta</s>) in the scriptural text — there is merely the word <s>avyakta</s>.
And by this much alone, recognition of [the categories of] <s>Sāṃkhya</s> <s>smṛti</s> does not obtain — this is the purport. //4//

body.translated_text: #<s>Jñeyatvāvacanāc ca</s># (And because it is not stated as something to be known).

children.text: jñeyatvāvacanasyāsiddhimāśaṅkya tatsiddhipradarśanārthaṃ sūtram- #vadatīti cenna prājño hi prakaraṇāt# /
children.translated_text: Anticipating the objection that the absence of a statement of knowability is not established, the <s>sūtra</s> is for the purpose of demonstrating its establishment: #<s>vadati iti cen na prājño hi prakaraṇāt</s># (If [you say] it does state [knowability], no, because the subject of the context is the Intelligent One).
The <s>bhāṣya</s> on this [<s>sūtra</s>] is explained by [mere] recitation (<s>nigada</s>). //5//

'yeyaṃ prete' iti hi naciketasaḥ praśnamupaśrutya tattatkāmaviṣayamalobhaṃ cāsya pratītya mṛtyuḥ 'vidyābhīpsinaṃ naciketasaṃ manye' ityādinā naciketasaṃ praśasya praśnamapi tadīyaṃ praśaṃsannasminpraśne brahmaivottaramuvāca- #taṃ durdarśamiti# /

children.text: yadi punarjīvātprājño bhidyeta, jīvagocaraḥ praśnaḥ, prājñagocaraṃ cottaramiti kiṃ kena saṃgaccheta /
children.translated_text: If, on the other hand, the Intelligent One (<s>Prājña</s>, the Supreme Self) were different from the <s>jīva</s>, then the question would concern the <s>jīva</s> and the answer would concern the <s>Prājña</s> — how would the one correspond to the other?

children.text: apica yadviṣayaṃ praśnamupaśrutya mṛtyunaiṣa praśaṃsito naciketāḥ yadi tameva bhūyaḥ pṛcchettaduttare cāvadadhyāt tataḥ praśaṃsā dṛṣṭārthā syāt, praśnāntare tvasāvasthāne prasāritā satyadṛṣṭārthā syādityāha- #yatpraśneti# /
children.translated_text: Moreover, if <s>Naciketas</s>, who was praised by <s>Mṛtyu</s> upon hearing his question, were to ask again about the very same topic and [<s>Mṛtyu</s>] were to respond to that very topic, then the praise would serve an evident purpose; but if [the praise were] extended to a different question where it has no proper place, it would serve no evident purpose — hence he says: #'regarding which question...'#
The question about which [topic is raised is] the same as [the topic of] the question [that was praised].
The rest is of transparent meaning. //6//

body.translated_text: #<s>Trayāṇām eva caivam upanyāsaḥ praśnaś ca</s># (The presentation and the question concern only these three). For the progression of the dialogue-passage between <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death) and <s>Naciketas</s>, beginning with the granting of boons, is observed throughout the <s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s>s. <s>Mṛtyu</s>, being pleased, granted three boons to <s>Naciketas</s> who had been sent [to him] by his angry father. <s>Naciketas</s>, with the first boon, wished for his father's goodwill; with the second, knowledge of the [sacrificial] fire (<s>agnividyā</s>); with the third, knowledge of the Self (<s>ātmavidyā</s>) — as stated: 'This is the third of the boons chosen.' Now, in that granting of boons, the question and answer relate to [these three subjects, not to] <s>Pradhāna</s>. Therefore, in the <s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s>s, the textual progression concerns only fire, the <s>jīva</s>, and the Supreme Self — it cannot properly relate to the unintroduced <s>Pradhāna</s> — hence he says: #'And for this reason too, the word <s>avyakta</s> does not denote <s>Pradhāna</s>.'# The syntactical connection is: the reply concerning the <s>jīva</s>, namely 'how the self comes to be after death, O <s>Gautama</s>' and so forth, is connected — though at a distance — with [the verse] 'Come, I shall declare to you this secret, eternal <s>Brahman</s>.' Here the objector asks: Is there only one question concerning both the <s>jīva</s> and the Supreme Self, or is the question 'this [doubt] that exists when a man has departed' about the <s>jīva</s> separately, and [the passage] 'beyond <s>dharma</s>' and so forth about the Supreme Self separately? If one, there is conflict with the <s>sūtra</s> [which says] 'of three.' If distinct, then the question beginning with 'beyond <s>dharma</s>' and so forth would come after the granting of three boons concerning the father's goodwill, knowledge of fire, and knowledge of the Self — [requiring] the postulation of a fourth boon, which would contradict the scripture that says 'third.' Or if the question is not included within the boon-granting, then likewise the mention of <s>Pradhāna</s> too could be [argued to be] not included within the boon-granting — this is the objection, [citing] '<s>mahataḥ param avyaktam</s>' (beyond the great is the unmanifest). He resolves this: #'To this we say: we do not [hold] thus here.'# In reality, since the <s>jīva</s> and the Supreme Self are non-different, there is only one question by virtue of the non-difference of the objects of inquiry. Hence the reply too is one. The <s>sūtra</s>, however, follows the conventional [apparent] distinction. And the real non-difference of the <s>jīva</s> and the Supreme Self has been shown by the blessed <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (commentator) through scriptural citations in various places. Similarly, [he has shown how] the question about the existence and non-existence of the <s>jīva</s> [is really about <s>Brahman</s>], and so forth. For, having heard <s>Naciketas</s>'s question 'this [doubt] that exists when a man has departed,' and perceiving his non-attachment to various objects of desire, <s>Mṛtyu</s>, praising <s>Naciketas</s> with 'I consider <s>Naciketas</s> one who seeks knowledge' and so forth, and also praising his question, gave <s>Brahman</s> itself as the answer to this question: #'that which is hard to see...'#

children.translated_text: #<s>Mahadvac ca</s># (And like [the term] 'great').
By this [<s>sūtra</s>] it is stated that since the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> usage conflicts with the Vedic usage, the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> usage should not be given priority when interpreting the <s>Veda</s>.

children.text: sāṃkhyānāṃ mahattattvaṃ sattāmātraṃ, puruṣārthakriyākṣamaṃ sattasya bhāvaḥ sattā tanmātraṃ mahattattvamiti /
children.translated_text: For the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, <s>mahat-tattva</s> (the Great Principle) is mere existence (<s>sattā-mātra</s>) — the state of being existent (<s>sat</s>) is existence (<s>sattā</s>); that alone is <s>mahat-tattva</s>, [defined as] capable of serving the purposes of <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: yā yā puruṣārthakriyā śabdādyupabhogalakṣaṇā ca sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātilakṣaṇā ca sā sarvā mahati buddhau samāpyata iti mahattattvaṃ sattāmātramucyata iti //7 //
children.translated_text: Whatever purposeful activity for <s>Puruṣa</s> there is — whether characterized as the enjoyment of sound and other [sense objects], or characterized as the discriminative knowledge (<s>khyāti</s>) of the difference between <s>Sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> — all of that is accomplished in the great <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect); hence <s>mahat-tattva</s> is called mere existence (<s>sattā-mātra</s>). //7//

body.text:
#camasavadaviśeṣāt# /
ajāśabdo yadyapi chāgāyāṃ rūḍhastathāpyadhyātmavidyādhikārānna tatra kartitumarhati /
tasmādrūḍherasaṃbhavādyogena vartayitavyaḥ /
tatra kiṃ svatantraṃ pradhānamanena mantravarṇenānūdyatāmuta pārameśvarī māyāśaktistejo 'bannavyākriyākāraṇamucyatām kiṃ tāvatprāptaṃ, pradhānameveti /
tathāhi-yādṛśaṃ pradhānaṃ sāṃkhyaiḥ smaryate tādṛśamevāsminnanyūnānatiriktaṃ pratīyate /
sā hi pradhānalakṣaṇā prakṛtirna jāyata ityajā ca ekā ca lohitaśuklakṛṣṇā ca /
yadyapi lohitatvādayo varṇā na rajaḥprabhṛtiṣu santi, tathāpi lohitaṃ kusumbhādi rañjayati,
body.translated_text: # <s>Camasavad aviśeṣāt</s># (Like a cup/vessel, because of non-distinction). Although the word <s>ajā</s> (unborn) is conventionally established in the sense of a she-goat, nevertheless, since the context pertains to spiritual knowledge (<s>adhyātmavidyā</s>), it cannot be taken in that [conventional] sense. Therefore, since the conventional meaning is inapplicable, it must be interpreted through etymological derivation (<s>yoga</s>). The question then is: does this mantra-verse refer to an independent <s>Pradhāna</s>, or does it speak of the <s>māyā</s>-power belonging to the Supreme Lord — the cause of the manifestation of fire, water, and food? What then is the prima facie view? It is that it refers to <s>Pradhāna</s> itself. For what is described here appears to be exactly like the <s>Pradhāna</s> as conceived by the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> — neither less nor more. For that defining characteristic of <s>Pradhāna</s> is: <s>Prakṛti</s> is unborn (<s>ajā</s>), one, and red-white-black. Although redness and other colors do not literally exist in <s>rajas</s> and the other [<s>guṇas</s>], nevertheless, [just as] red [dye like] safflower colors [things],

body.text:
rajo 'pi rañjayatīti lohitam /
evaṃ prasannaṃ pāthaḥ śuklaṃ, sattvamapi prasannamiti śuklam /
evamāvarakaṃ meghādi kṛṣṇaṃ, tamo 'pyāvarakamiti kṛṣṇam /
pareṇāpi nāvyākṛtasya svarūpeṇa lohitatvādiyoga āstheyaḥ, kintu tatkāryasya tejo 'bannasya rohitvādikāraṇa upacaraṇīyam /
kāryasārūpeṇa vā kāraṇe kalpanīyaṃ, tadasmākamapi tulyam /
'ajo hyeko juṣamāṇo 'nuśete jahātyenāṃ bhuktabhogāmajo 'nyaḥ' iti tvātmabhedaśravaṇāt sāṃkhyasmṛterevātra mantravarṇe pratyabhijñānaṃ na tvavyākṛtaprakriyāyāḥ /
tasyāmaikātmyābhyupagamenātmabhedābhāvāt /
tasmātsvatantraṃ pradhānaṃ nāśabdamiti prāptam /
#teṣāṃ sāmyāvasthāvayavadharmairiti# /
avayavāḥ pradhānasmaikasya sattvarajastamāṃsi teṣāṃ dharmā lohitatvādayastairiti /
#prajāstraiguṇyānvitā iti# /
sukhaduḥkhamohātmikāḥ /
tathāhi-maitradāreṣu narmadāyāṃ maitrasya sukhaṃ, tat kasya hetoḥ, taṃ prati sattvasya samudbhavāt /
tathāca tatsapatnīnāṃ duḥkhaṃ, tat kasya hetoḥ, tāḥ prati rajaṛsamudbhavāt, tathā caitrasya tāmavindato moho viṣādaḥ, sa kasya hetoḥ, taṃ prati tamaḥsamudbhavāt /
narmadayā ca sarve bhāvā vyākhyātāḥ /
tadidaṃ traiguṇyānvitatvaṃ prajānām /
anuśeta iti vyācaṣṭe- #tāmevāvidyayeti# /
viṣayā hi śabdādayaḥ prakṛtivikārastraiguṇyena sukhaduḥkhamohātmāna indriyamano 'haṅkārapraṇālikayā buddhisattvamupasaṃkrāmanti /
tena tadbuddhisattvaṃ pradhānavikāraḥ sukhaduḥkhamohātmakaṃ śabdādirūpeṇa pariṇamate /
citiśaktistvapariṇāminyapratisaṃkramāpi buddhisattvādātmano vivekabudhyamānā buddhivṛttyaiva viparyāsenāvidyayā buddhisthānsukhādīnātmanyabhimanyamānā sukhādimatīva bhavati /
tadidamuktam- #sukhī duḥkhī mūḍho 'hamityavivekatayā saṃsarati# /
ekaḥ /
sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātisamunmūlitanikhilavāsanāvidyānubandhastvanyo jahātyenāṃ prakṛtim /
tadidamuktam- #anyaḥ punariti# /
bhuktabhogāmiti vyācaṣṭe- #kṛtabhogāpavargām# /
śabdādyāpalabdhirbhogaḥ /
guṇapuruṣānyatākhyātirapavargaḥ /

children.text: evaṃ prāpte 'bhidhīyate-na tāvat 'ajo hyeko juṣamāṇo 'nuśete jahātyenāṃ bhuktabhogamajo 'nyaḥ' ityetadātmabhedapratipādanaparamapi tu siddhamātmabhedaṃnūdya bandhamokṣau pratipādayatīti /
children.translated_text: This being the prima facie conclusion, [the established view] is stated: First, 'The unborn one, indeed, the one enjoying, lies with [her]; the other unborn one abandons her whose enjoyments have been consumed' — this [mantra], even though it teaches the duality of selves, does not have the teaching of the duality of selves as its primary purport; rather, presupposing the already-established duality of selves, it teaches bondage and liberation — thus.

children.text: sa cānūdito bhedaḥ 'eko devaḥ sarvabhūteṣu gūḍhaḥ sarvavyāpī sarvabhūtāntarātmā' ityādiśrutibhirātmaikatvapratipādanaparābhirvirodhātkalpaniko 'vatiṣṭhate /
children.translated_text: And that presupposed duality is, because of the contradiction with <s>Śruti</s> passages such as 'The one God hidden in all beings, all-pervading, the inner Self of all beings' and the like — which have as their primary purport the teaching of the oneness of the Self — merely figurative.

children.text: tathāca na sāṃkhyaprakriyāpratyabhijñānamityajāvākyaṃ camasavākyavatpariplavamānaṃ na svatantrapradhānaniścayāya paryāptam /
children.translated_text: And thus, there is no recognition of the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> doctrine [in this mantra]; and the <s>ajā</s>-passage (unborn-passage), being inconclusive like the <s>camasa</s>-passage (cup-passage), is not sufficient for the determination of an independent <s>Pradhāna</s>.
This is what was stated by the author of the <s>Sūtra</s>s: 'Like the cup-passage, because of the absence of a distinguishing [feature]' (<s>camasavadaviśeṣāt</s>) — thus. //8//

body.translated_text:
<s>Rajas</s> too, because it colors (<s>rañjayati</s>), is red (<s>lohita</s>).
Similarly, clear water is white (<s>śukla</s>), and <s>sattva</s> too, being clear, is white.
Similarly, that which covers, such as clouds and the like, is dark (<s>kṛṣṇa</s>), and <s>tamas</s> too, being a covering, is dark.
Even by the opponent, the redness and the like should not be accepted as belonging to the undifferentiated (<s>avyākṛta</s>) in its own form; rather, it should be figuratively applied (<s>upacaraṇīya</s>) to its effects — fire, water, and food — as the cause of redness and the like.
Or, the attribution to the cause by virtue of resemblance with its effect — that is the same for us as well.
'The unborn one (<s>aja</s>), indeed, the one [soul] enjoying, lies with [her]; the other unborn one (<s>aja</s>) abandons her whose enjoyments have been consumed' — but from hearing of the duality of selves [in this mantra], the recognition is of the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> tradition alone in this mantra-passage, not of the <s>avyākṛta</s> (undifferentiated) doctrine.
Because in that [avyākṛta doctrine], with the acceptance of oneness of the Self, there is no duality of selves.
Therefore, it is established that <s>Pradhāna</s> is independent [and] not [established] by scripture — thus the prima facie conclusion.
'By the properties of the constituents in their state of equilibrium' — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s> comments].
The constituents (<s>avayava</s>s) of the single <s>Pradhāna</s> are <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>; their properties are redness and the like — by those [properties, the recognition is possible] — thus.
'The creatures are endowed with the three <s>guṇa</s>s' — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s> comments].
[This means:] they are of the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion.
For example: among the wives of <s>Maitra</s>, <s>Narmadā</s> brings pleasure to <s>Maitra</s> — for what reason? Because <s>sattva</s> predominates in relation to him.
Similarly, his co-wives [bring] pain — for what reason? Because <s>rajas</s> predominates in relation to them. Similarly, <s>Caitra</s>, not obtaining her, [experiences] delusion and despair — for what reason? Because <s>tamas</s> predominates in relation to him.
And by [the example of] <s>Narmadā</s>, all [worldly] experiences are explained.
This is the endowment of creatures with the three <s>guṇa</s>s.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] glosses 'lies with' (<s>anuśete</s>) as: 'Through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) itself' — thus.
For the sense-objects — sound and the like — being modifications of <s>Prakṛti</s>, having the nature of the three <s>guṇa</s>s as pleasure, pain, and delusion, pass through the channel of the senses, mind, and <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego) to the <s>buddhi-sattva</s> (intellect-substance).
Thereby, that <s>buddhi-sattva</s>, being a modification of <s>Pradhāna</s>, having the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion, transforms in the form of sound and the like.
But the power of consciousness (<s>citi-śakti</s>), though not undergoing transformation and not subject to transference, not discriminating itself from the <s>buddhi-sattva</s>, through the mental modification (<s>buddhi-vṛtti</s>) itself, by a misconception that is <s>avidyā</s>, falsely attributing to itself the pleasure and the like that reside in the <s>buddhi</s>, becomes as if possessing pleasure and the like.
This is what was stated: 'I am happy, I am suffering, I am deluded — thus, through non-discrimination, [the soul] transmigrates' — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s> comments].
[This is] the one [soul].
But the other, whose connection with the bondage of all <s>vāsanā</s>s (latent impressions) and <s>avidyā</s> has been uprooted by the discriminative knowledge (<s>khyāti</s>) of the difference between <s>sattva</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>, abandons this <s>Prakṛti</s>.
This is what was stated: 'The other, however' — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s> comments].
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] glosses 'whose enjoyments have been consumed' (<s>bhuktabhogām</s>) as: 'Whose enjoyment and liberation have been accomplished' — thus.
The apprehension of sound and the like is enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>).
The discriminative knowledge of the difference between <s>guṇa</s> and <s>puruṣa</s> is liberation (<s>apavarga</s>).
For by that [knowledge], the <s>puruṣa</s> is released — thus.

body.text:
uttarasūtramavatārayituṃ śaṅkate- #tatra tvidaṃ tacchira iti# /
sūtramavatārayati- #atra brūmaḥ /
jyotirupakramā tu tathā hyadhīyata eke# /
sarvaśākhāpratyayamekaṃ brahmeti sthaitau śākhāntaroktarohitādiguṇayoginī tejo 'bannalakṣaṇā jarāyujāṇḍasvedajadbhijjacaturvidhabhūtagrāmaprakṛtibhūteyamajā pratipattavyā, 'rohitaśuklakṛṣṇām' iti rohitādirupatayā tasyā eva pratyabhijñānāt /
na tu sāṃkhyaparikalpitā prakṛtiḥ /
tasyā aprāmāṇikatayā śrutahānyaśrutakalpanāprasaṅgāt, rañjanādinā ca rohitādyupacārasya sati mukhyārthasaṃbhave 'yogāt /
tadidamuktam- #rohitādīnāṃ śabdānāmiti# /
ajāpadasya ca samudāyaprasiddhiparityāgena na jāyata ityavayavaprasiddhyāśrayaṇe doṣaprasaṅgāt /
atra tu rūpakaklapanāyāṃ samudāyaprasiddherevānapekṣāyāḥ svīkārāt /
api cāyamapi śrutikalāpo 'smaddarśanānuguṇo na sāṃkhyasmṛtyanuguṇa ityāha #-tathehāpīti /
kiṃ kāraṇaṃ brahmetyupakramyeti# /
brahmasvarūpaṃ tāvajjagatkāraṇaṃ na bhavati, viśuddhatvāttasya /
yathāhuḥ-'puruṣasya tu śuddhasya nāśuddhā vikṛtirbavet' ityāśayavatīva śrutiḥ pṛcchati /
kiṅkāraṇam /
yasya brahmaṇo jagadutpattistat kiṅkāraṇaṃ brahmetyarthaḥ /

children.text: te brahmavido dhyānayogenātmānaṃ gatāḥ prāptā apaśyanniti yojanā /
children.translated_text: Those knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, having reached — attained — the Self through the yoga of meditation, saw [it] — this is the construction.
'Who [presides over] each and every source' — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s> comments].

children.text: avidyā śaktiryoniḥ, sā ca pratijīvaṃ nānetyuktamato vīpsopapannā /
children.translated_text: <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance), being a power (<s>śakti</s>), is the source (<s>yoni</s>); and it is different for each individual soul (<s>jīva</s>) — hence the repetition (<s>vīpsā</s>) is justified.
The rest is of transparent meaning. //9//

body.translated_text:
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises an objection in order to introduce the next <s>sūtra</s>: 'But here, that is its head' — thus.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] introduces the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Here we say: But [the passage] beginning with light — for thus some recite' (<s>jyotirupakramā tu tathā hyadhīyata eke</s>).
When [the principle is] established that a single <s>Brahman</s> is the purport of all branches [of the <s>Veda</s>], this <s>ajā</s> (unborn feminine entity) — characterized as fire, water, and food, being the material cause of the four-fold group of living beings born from wombs, eggs, sweat, and sprouts — which is stated in another branch as possessing the qualities of redness and the like, is to be understood [as the <s>avyākṛta</s>]. [This is] because the recognition [is] of that very [entity] through the redness and the like mentioned in 'the red, white, and dark one' (<s>rohitaśuklakṛṣṇām</s>).
But not the <s>Prakṛti</s> imagined by the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>s.
Because, since that [Sāṃkhya Prakṛti] is without valid authority, there would be the fault of abandoning what is heard [in scripture] and postulating what is not heard.
And because the figurative usage of redness and the like through [the analogy of] coloring (<s>rañjana</s>) and the like is inappropriate when a primary meaning is possible.
This is what was stated: 'Of the words red and the like' — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s> comments].
And the word <s>ajā</s> (unborn feminine) — if, abandoning the well-known composite meaning [of the word as a whole], one resorts to the etymological meaning of the component parts as 'that which is not born' (<s>na jāyate</s>) — there would be [the same] fault.
But here, in the figurative interpretation [of the <s>ajā</s>-passage], the well-known composite meaning alone is accepted without any need [for etymological analysis].
Moreover, this scriptural passage too is favorable to our view, not to the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> tradition — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Similarly here too' — thus.
What is the reason? 'Having introduced [the passage] with <s>Brahman</s>' — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s> comments].
The essential nature of <s>Brahman</s> is not the cause of the world, because of its purity.
As they say: 'From a pure <s>puruṣa</s>, an impure modification cannot arise' — the <s>Śruti</s>, as if having this intent, asks.
What is the cause? The meaning is: what is the cause of that <s>Brahman</s> from which the world originates?

body.text:
sūtrāntaramavatārayituṃ śaṅkate- #kathaṃ punariti# /
ajākṛtirjātistejo 'banneṣu nāsti /
naca tejo 'bannānāṃ janmaśravaṇādajanmanimitto 'pyajāśabdaḥ saṃbhavatītyāha- #naca tejo 'bannānāmiti# /
sūtramavatārayati- #ata uttaraṃ paṭhati /

children.translated_text: 'And because of the instruction through a figurative representation (<s>kalpana</s>), there is no contradiction, as with honey and the like' (<s>kalpanopadeśācca madhvādivadavirodhaḥ</s>).

children.text: nanu kiṃ chāgā lohitaśuklakṛṣṇaivānyādṛśīnāmapi chāgānāmupalambhādityata āha- #yadṛcchayeti# /
children.translated_text: Now, [one may object:] is it only a she-goat that is red, white, and dark? Since she-goats of other [colors] are also observed — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'By chance' (<s>yadṛcchayā</s>) — thus.
<s>Bahubarkarā</s> means 'having many offspring (<s>śāva</s>s).'
The rest is explained by the running commentary (<s>nigada</s>). //1//

body.translated_text:
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises an objection in order to introduce another <s>sūtra</s>: 'But how?' — thus.
The form (<s>ākṛti</s>) of a she-goat (<s>ajā</s>) — i.e., the universal goat-ness (<s>jāti</s>) — does not exist in fire, water, and food.
And since there is a <s>Śruti</s> stating the origination of fire, water, and food, the word <s>ajā</s> cannot apply [to them] even in the sense of 'unborn' — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'And fire, water, and food' — thus.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] introduces the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Therefore [<s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>] reads the next [sūtra].'

body.text:
#na saṃkhyopasaṃgrahādapi nānābhāvādatirekācca# /
avāntarasaṃgatimāha- #evaṃ parihṛte 'pīti# /
pañcajanā iti hi samāsārthaḥ pañcasaṃkhyayā saṃbadhyate /
naca 'diksaṃkhye saṃjñāyām' iti samāsavidhānānmanujeṣu nirūḍho 'yaṃ pañcajanaśabda iti vācyam /

evaṃ cātmani pcamanujānāmākāśasya ca pratiṣṭhānamiti nistātparyaṃ, sarvasyaiva pratiṣṭhānāt /

naca ṣoḍaśigrahaṇavadvikalpasaṃbhavaḥ /

vastutattvakathā ceyaṃ nānuṣṭhānakathā, vidhyabhāvāt /

sāṃkhyaiśca prakṛtyādīni /

na cādhāratvenātmano vyavasthānātsvātmani cādhārādheyabhāvasya virodhāt ākāśasya ca vyatirecanāt, trayoviṃśatirjanā iti syānna pañca pañcajanā iti vācyam /
