hirugbhāvena tu teṣāṃ saptaviṃśatitvāvirodhaḥ /
tasmānnāśābdī sāṃkhyasmṛtiriti prāptam /
mūlaprakṛtiḥ pradhānam /
nāsāvanyasya vikṛtirapi tu prakṛtireva tadidamuktam- #mūleti# /
mahadahaṅkārapañcatanmātrāṇi prakṛtayaśca vikṛtayaśca /
tathāhi-mahattattvamahaṅkārasya tattvāntarasya prakṛtirmūlaprakṛtestu vikṛtiḥ /
evamahaṅkāratattvaṃ mahato vikṛtiḥ, prakṛtiśca tadeva tāmasaṃ sat pañcatanmātrāṇām /
tadeva sāttvikaṃ sat prakṛtirekādaśendriyāṇām /
pañcatanmātrāṇi cāhaṅkārasya vikṛtirākāśādīnāṃ pañcānāṃ prakṛtiḥ /
tadidamuktam- #mahadādyāḥ prakṛtivikṛtayaḥ sapta /
ṣoḍaśakaśca vikāraḥ# /
ṣoḍaśasaṃkhyāvacchinno gaṇo vikāra eva /
pañcabhūtānyatanmātrāṇyekādaśendriyāṇīti ṣoḍaśako gaṇaḥ /
yadyapi pṛthivyādayo goghaṭādīnāṃ prakṛtistathāpi na te pṛthivyādibhyastattvāntaramiti na prakṛtiḥ /
tattvāntaropādānatvaṃ ceha prakṛtitvamabhimataṃ nopādānamātratvamityavirodhaḥ /
puruṣastu kūṭasthanityo 'pariṇāmo na kasyacitprakṛtirnāpi vikṛtiriti /
evaṃ prāpte 'bhidhīyate #-na saṃkhyopasaṃgrahādapi pradhānādīnāṃ śrutimattvāśaṅkā kartavyā /
kasmāt nānābhāvāt /
nānā hyetāni pañcaviṃśatitattvāni /
naiṣāṃ pañcaśaḥ pañcaśaḥ sādhāraṇadharmo 'sti# /
na khalu sattvarajastamohadahaṅkārāṇāmekaḥ kriyā dā guṇo vā dravyaṃ vā jātirvā dharmaḥ pañcatanmātrādibhyo vyāvṛttaḥ sattvādiṣu cānugataḥ kaścidasti /
nāpi pṛthivyaptejovāyughrāṇānām /
nāpi rasanavakṣustvakśrotravācām /
nāpi pāṇāpādapāyūpasthamanasāṃ, yenaikenāsādhāraṇenopagṛhītāḥ pañca pañcakā bhavitumarhati /
pūrvapakṣaikadeśinamutthāpayati- #athocyeta pañcaviṃśasaṃkhyaiveyamiti# /
yadyapi parasyāṃ saṃkhyāyāmavāntarasaṃkhyā dvitvādikā nāsti tathāpi tatpūrvaṃ tasyāḥ saṃbhavāt paurvāparyalakṣaṇayā pratyāsattyā parasaṃkhyopalakṣaṇārthaṃ pūrvasaṃkhyopanyasyata iti dūṣayati- #ayamevāsminpakṣe doṣa iti# /
naca pañcaśabdo janaśabdena samasto 'samastaḥ śakyo vaktumityāha- #paraścātra pañcaśabda iti# /
nanu bhavatu samāsastathāpi kimityata āha- #samastatvācceti# /
api ca vīpsāyāṃ pañcakadvayagrahaṇe daśaiva tattvānīti na sāṃkhyasmṛtipratyabhijñānamityasamāsamabhyupetyāha- #na ca pañcakadvayagrahaṇaṃ pañca pañceti# /
na caikā pañcasaṃkhyā pañcasaṃkhyāntareṇa śakyā viśeṣṭum /
pañcaśabdasya saṃkhyopasarjanadravyavacanatvena saṃkhyāyā upasarjanatayā viśeṣaṇenāsaṃyogādityāha- #ekasyāḥ pañcasaṃkhyāyā iti# /
tadevaṃ pūrvapakṣaikadeśini dūṣite paramapūrvapakṣiṇamutthāpayati #-nanvāpannapañcasaṃkhyākā janā eveti# /
atra tāvadrūḍhau satyāṃ na yogaḥ saṃbhavatīti vakṣyate /
tathāpi yaugikaṃ pañcajanaśabdamabhyupetya dūṣayati- #yuktaṃ yatpañcapūlīśabdasyeti# /
pañcapūlītyatra yadyapi pṛthaktvaikārthasaṃvāyinī pañcasaṃkhyāvacchedikāsti tathāpīha samudāyino 'vacchinatti na samudāyaṃ samāsapadagamyamatastasmin kati te samudāyā ityapekṣāyāṃ padāntarābhihitā pañcasaṃkhyā saṃbadhyate pañceti /
body.translated_text:
'Not even from the inclusion of number, because of the plurality [of categories] and because of the excess' [BS 1.4.11].
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the subsidiary connection: 'Even when thus refuted...'
For the compound-meaning of '<s>pañcajanāḥ</s>' (five peoples) is connected with the number five.
Nor should it be said that the word '<s>pañcajana</s>' is conventionally fixed (<s>nirūḍha</s>) in [the sense of] 'human beings,' based on the grammatical rule '<s>diksaṃkhye saṃjñāyām</s>' (directional and numerical [compounds are formed] in the sense of a proper name), which prescribes such compounding.
For if that were so, [the form] would be '<s>pañcamanujāḥ</s>' (five humans).
And thus, [the meaning] 'in the Self, the five humans and space have their foundation' would be purposeless, since everything whatsoever has its foundation [in the Self].
Therefore, since the conventional meaning (<s>rūḍhi</s>) is not possible, it must be abandoned, and the etymological meaning (<s>yoga</s>) should be adopted here.
And the word '<s>jana</s>' (people/beings) must be explained as somehow [applicable] to the <s>tattva</s>s (categories).
Therein too, [the question arises:] are the five [categories] — <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest — that occur in the remainder of the sentence intended, or some others beyond those?
In that matter, upon consideration of the sequence, there is a contradiction between the <s>Kāṇva</s> and <s>Mādhyandina</s> recensions.
For in one, fire is the fifth, but not in the other.
Nor is an option (<s>vikalpa</s>) possible as in the case of the <s>ṣoḍaśī</s>-libation.
For it is [only] practice (<s>anuṣṭhāna</s>) that admits of options, not [matters of] reality (<s>vastu</s>).
And this is a discussion about the reality of things, not about practice, since there is no injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) [here].
Therefore, certain <s>tattva</s>s alone — five in each group, totaling twenty-five when each is fitted with the number five — are [meant] here.
And the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>s remember twenty-five <s>tattva</s>s beginning with <s>Prakṛti</s>.
Since twenty-five <s>tattva</s>s are remembered, [the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>s claim that] it is precisely those that are spoken of by this mantra — hence <s>Pradhāna</s> and the like are not unscriptural.
Nor should it be said that since the Self is established as the substratum, and since the relation of substratum and superstratum within one's own self is contradictory, and since space (<s>ākāśa</s>) is excluded [from the count], [the result] would be 'twenty-three peoples' (<s>trayoviṃśatir janāḥ</s>) and not 'five groups of five peoples' (<s>pañca pañcajanāḥ</s>).
Because even when the Self and space are excluded, the number twenty-five is accounted for by the three parts of the root <s>Prakṛti</s> — <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>.
And if [one objects that] when there are twenty-seven with the Self and space, [saying] 'twenty-five <s>tattva</s>s' would contradict one's own doctrine — no, because the number twenty-five is accounted for by unifying <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> merely under their common character as root <s>Prakṛti</s>.
But when they are taken separately, their being twenty-seven is not contradicted.
Therefore, the conclusion arrived at is that the <s>Sāṃkhya Smṛti</s> is not unscriptural.
The root <s>Prakṛti</s> is <s>Pradhāna</s>.
It is not a modification (<s>vikṛti</s>) of anything else, but is <s>Prakṛti</s> (originary cause) alone — this is what is stated: 'root' (<s>mūla</s>).
<s>Mahat</s> (the Great), <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), and the five <s>tanmātra</s>s (subtle elements) are both <s>prakṛti</s>s (causes) and <s>vikṛti</s>s (effects).
For instance: the <s>mahat-tattva</s> is the <s>prakṛti</s> of <s>ahaṅkāra</s> and another category, but a <s>vikṛti</s> of the root <s>Prakṛti</s>.
Similarly, the <s>ahaṅkāra-tattva</s> is a <s>vikṛti</s> of <s>mahat</s>, and that very [<s>ahaṅkāra</s>], being <s>tāmasa</s> (of the nature of <s>tamas</s>), is the <s>prakṛti</s> of the five <s>tanmātra</s>s.
That very [<s>ahaṅkāra</s>], being <s>sāttvika</s> (of the nature of <s>sattva</s>), is the <s>prakṛti</s> of the eleven sense-organs.
And the five <s>tanmātra</s>s are <s>vikṛti</s>s of <s>ahaṅkāra</s> and <s>prakṛti</s>s of the five [gross elements] — space and the rest.
This is what is stated: '<s>Mahat</s> and the rest — seven are both <s>prakṛti</s>s and <s>vikṛti</s>s.
And the group of sixteen is modification (<s>vikāra</s>) alone.'
The group delimited by the number sixteen is modification alone.
The five gross elements, the five <s>tanmātra</s>s [this is incorrect per Sāṃkhya; correctly: five gross elements and eleven sense-organs], and the eleven sense-organs — this is the group of sixteen.
Although earth and the like are the <s>prakṛti</s>s of cows, pots, and the like, nevertheless, since those [products] are not a separate <s>tattva</s> from earth and the like, [earth etc.] are not [considered] <s>prakṛti</s> [in the technical sense].
And the meaning of '<s>prakṛti</s>' intended here is being the material cause of a separate <s>tattva</s>, not merely being a material cause [of anything] — hence there is no contradiction.
But <s>Puruṣa</s> (the conscious principle), being immutable (<s>kūṭastha</s>), eternal, and non-transforming, is neither the <s>prakṛti</s> of anything nor a <s>vikṛti</s>.
This being the prima facie view, the <s>Siddhāntin</s> states: 'Not even from the inclusion of number should the suspicion of scripturalness arise regarding <s>Pradhāna</s> and the like.
Why? Because of plurality.
For these twenty-five <s>tattva</s>s are diverse.
They do not have a common property shared by groups of five.'
Indeed, there is no single action, quality, substance, or universal (<s>jāti</s>) that is common to <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, <s>tamas</s>, <s>mahat</s>, and <s>ahaṅkāra</s> — that is, which distinguishes them from the five <s>tanmātra</s>s and the like while pervading [only] <s>sattva</s> and the rest.
Nor [is there such a common property] among earth, water, fire, wind, and the organ of smell.
Nor among the organs of taste, sight, touch, hearing, and speech.
Nor among the hands, feet, organ of excretion, organ of generation, and mind — by which single uncommon [property], being included, [these] could form five groups of five.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises the partial objection of the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s>: 'But one might say: this is just the number twenty-five itself.'
Although in a larger number, a subsidiary number such as two and the like does not [independently] exist, nevertheless, since the [subsidiary number] is possible prior to [the larger number], the prior number is mentioned for the purpose of indicating the larger number through the proximity characterized by sequence — this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes: 'This very thing is the fault in this view.'
Nor can the word '<s>pañca</s>' (five), being compounded with the word '<s>jana</s>' (people), be said to be uncompounded — so [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Moreover, the word "<s>pañca</s>" here is...'
But even granting the compound, what then? — to this he says: 'Because of being compounded.'
Moreover, if through distributive repetition (<s>vīpsā</s>) the grasping of two groups of five [were intended], there would be only ten <s>tattva</s>s, and hence no recognition of the <s>Sāṃkhya Smṛti</s> — thus, accepting the non-compound [interpretation], [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Nor is the grasping of two groups of five [possible] — "five, five."'
Nor can a single number five be qualified by another number five.
Since the word '<s>pañca</s>' (five), being a numeral adjective denoting a substance qualified by number, [treats] the number as subordinate, the [subordinate] number cannot be conjoined with a qualifier — so [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Of a single number five...'
Thus, having refuted the partial <s>pūrvapakṣin</s>, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises the ultimate <s>pūrvapakṣin</s>: 'But surely, [these are] peoples who have attained the number five.'
Here, it will be stated that when a conventional meaning (<s>rūḍhi</s>) exists, the etymological meaning (<s>yoga</s>) is not possible.
Nevertheless, accepting the etymological [meaning of] the word '<s>pañcajana</s>,' [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes: 'It is appropriate that the word "<s>pañcapūlī</s>"...'
In '<s>pañcapūlī</s>' (a bundle of five), although there is a number-five that delimits the individuals conjoined in a group, here [in '<s>pañcajana</s>'] it delimits the aggregate, not the [individual members of the] aggregate, which is what the compound-word conveys. Hence, when the question arises 'how many are those aggregates?', the number five stated by another word is connected [to answer] 'five.'

body.text:
pañcajanā ityatra tu pañcasaṃkhyayotpattiśiṣṭatayā janānāmavacchinnatvātsamudāyasya ca pañcapūlīvadatrāpratīterna padāntarābhihitā saṃkhyā saṃbadhyate /
syādetat /
saṃkhyeyānāṃ janānāṃ mā bhūcchabdāntaravāvyasaṃkhyāvacchedaḥ /
pañcasaṃkhyāyāstu tayāvacchedo bhaviṣyati /
nahi sāpyavacchinnetyata āha- #bhavadapīdaṃ viśeṣaṇamiti# /
ukto 'tra doṣaḥ /
body.translated_text:
But in '<s>pañcajanāḥ</s>' (five peoples), since the peoples are delimited by the number five through the suffix-generated [compound meaning], and since [the compound word] does not indicate the aggregate — unlike '<s>pañcapūlī</s>' — a number stated by another word is not connected [here].
One might object: let the peoples — the things to be counted — not have their number-delimitation by another word; but the number five will have its delimitation by that [other word].
For it too is not [independently] delimited — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Even this qualifier [is problematic].'
The fault has been stated here.

body.text:
nahyupasarjanaṃ viśeṣaṇena yujyate pañcaśabda eva tāvatsaṃkhyeyopasarjanasaṃkhyāmāha viśeṣatastu pañcajanā ityatra samāse /
viśeṣaṇāpekṣāyāṃ tu na samāsaḥ syāt, asāmarthyāt /
nahi bhavati ṛddhasya rājapuruṣa iti samāso 'pi tu (pada) vṛttireva ṛddhasya rājñaḥ puruṣa iti /
sāpekṣatvenāsāmarthyādityarthaḥ /
#atirekācceti# /
abhyuccayamātram /
yadi sattvarajastamāṃsi pradhānenaikīkṛtyātmākāśau tattvebhyo vyatiricyete tadā siddhāntavyākopaḥ /
atha tu sattvarajastamāṃsi mitho bhedena vivakṣyante tathāpi vastutattvavyavasthāpane ādhāratvenātmā niṣkṛṣyatām /
ādheyāntarebhyastvākāśasyādheyasya vyatirecanamanarthakamiti gamayitavyam /
#kathaṃ ca saṃkhyāmātraśravaṇe satīti# /
'diksaṃkhye saṃjñāyām' iti saṃjñāyāṃ samāsasmaraṇāt pañcajanaśabdastāvadayaṃ kkacinnirūḍhaḥ /
naca rūḍhau satyāmavayavaprasiddhergrahaṇaṃ, sāpekṣatvāt, nirapekṣatvācca rūḍheḥ /
tadyadi rūḍhau mukhyor'thaḥ prāpyate tataḥ sa eva grahītavyo 'tha tvasau na vākye saṃbandhārhaḥ pūrvāparavākyavirodhī vā /
tato rūḍhyaparityāgenaiva vṛttyantareṇārthāntaraṃ kalpayitvā vākyamupapādanīyam /
yathā 'śyenenābhicaran yajeta' iti śyenaśabda śakuniviśeṣe nirūḍhavṛttistadaparityāgenaiva nipatyādānasādṛśyenārthavādikena kratuviśeṣe vartate, tathā pañcajanaśabdo 'vayavārthayogānapekṣa ekasminnapi vartate /

children.text: yathā saptarṣiśabdo vasiṣṭha ekasmin saptasu ca vartate /
children.translated_text: Just as the word '<s>saptarṣi</s>' (seven sages) functions both in the single [sage] <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and in the seven [sages collectively].
And this [word '<s>pañcajana</s>'] is not conventionally fixed in [the sense of] the <s>tattva</s>s (categories).
[The <s>Sāṃkhya</s>s] wish to apply it to the <s>tattva</s>s in accordance with the number twenty-five.

children.text: rūḍhau satyāṃ pcaviṃśatereva saṃkhyāyā abhāvātkathaṃ tattveṣu vartate //11 //
children.translated_text: But since, when a conventional meaning (<s>rūḍhi</s>) exists, the very number twenty-five is absent [as a referent], how can it function in [the sense of] the <s>tattva</s>s? //11//

body.translated_text:
For a subordinate element (<s>upasarjana</s>) cannot be conjoined with a qualifier. To begin with, the word '<s>pañca</s>' (five) expresses a number that is subordinate to the thing counted — especially in the compound '<s>pañcajanāḥ</s>.'.
But if [the word '<s>pañca</s>'] required a qualifier, there would be no compound, due to incapacity (<s>asāmarthya</s>).
For one does not form the compound '<s>ṛddhasya rājapuruṣa</s>' (the king's servant of the prosperous one); rather, [it remains] a mere word-group: '<s>ṛddhasya rājñaḥ puruṣaḥ</s>' (the servant of the prosperous king).
The meaning is: because of the incapacity arising from [the element's] being dependent [on a qualifier].
'And because of the excess' — [this is] mere abundance [of argument].
If <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> are unified with <s>Pradhāna</s>, and the Self and space are excluded from the <s>tattva</s>s, then there is a contradiction with one's own doctrine.
But if <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> are intended as mutually distinct, then even so — in establishing the reality of things — let the Self be extracted as the substratum.
But the exclusion of space — which is a superstratum — from the other superstrata is pointless — this is to be understood.
'How can [there be recognition], when only a number is heard?' — since the <s>Pāṇinian</s> rule '<s>diksaṃkhye saṃjñāyām</s>' (directional and numerical [compounds are formed] in the sense of a proper name) prescribes compounding in the sense of a proper name, the word '<s>pañcajana</s>' is first and foremost conventionally fixed (<s>nirūḍha</s>) somewhere [i.e., in a particular referent].
And when a conventional meaning exists, the grasping of the meaning derived from [etymological analysis of] the component parts is not [warranted], because [the component-analysis] is dependent [on context], while the conventional meaning is independent.
Thus, if the conventional meaning yields the primary referent, then that alone should be grasped. But if that [conventional referent] is not fit to be syntactically connected in the sentence, or contradicts the preceding and following sentences,
then — without abandoning the conventional meaning — one should, through another semantic function (<s>vṛttyantara</s>), postulate a different referent and thereby explain the sentence.
Just as the word '<s>śyena</s>' (hawk) has its conventional meaning fixed in a particular species of bird, and — without abandoning that [conventional meaning] — through a different function based on the similarity of 'swooping down' (<s>nipāta</s>), functions in [the sense of] a particular sacrifice in '<s>śyenenābhicaran yajeta</s>' (one desiring to harm should sacrifice with the <s>śyena</s> [rite]), so too the word '<s>pañcajana</s>,' independent of its etymological component-meanings, functions even in a single [referent].

body.text:
evaṃ ca ke te pañcajanā ityapekṣāyāṃ kiṃ vākyaśeṣagatāḥ prāṇādayo gṛhyantāmuta pañcaviṃśatistattvānīti viśaye tattvānāmaprāmāṇikatvāt, prāṇādīnāṃ ca vākyaśeṣe śravaṇāttatparityāge śrutahānyaśrutakalpanāprasaṅgātprāṇādaya eva pañcajanāḥ /
naca kāṇḍavamādhyandinayorvirodhānna prāṇādīnāṃ vākyaśeṣagatānāmapi grahaṇamiti sāṃpratam, virodhe 'pi tulyabalatayā ṣoḍaśigrahaṇavadvikalpopapatteḥ /
na ceyaṃ vastusvarūpakathā, apitūpāsanānuṣṭhānavidhiḥ, 'manasaivānudraṣṭavyam' iti vidhiśravaṇāt /
#kathaṃ punaḥ praṇādiṣu janaśabdaprayoga iti# /
janavācakaḥ śabdo janaśabdaḥ /
pañcajanaśabda iti yāvat /
tasya kathaṃ prāṇādiṣvajaneṣu prayoga iti vyākhyeyam /
anyathā tu pratyastamitāvayavārthe samudāyaśabdārthe janaśabdārtho nāstītyaparyanuyoga eva /
rūḍhyaparityāgenaiva vṛttyantaraṃ darśayati- #janasaṃbandhācceti# /
janaśabdabhājaḥ pañcajanaśabdabhājaḥ /
nanu satyāmavayavaprasiddhau samupāyaśaktikalpanamanupapannaṃ, saṃbhavati ca pañcaviṃśatyāṃ tattveṣvavayavaprasiddhirityata āha- #samāsabalācceti# /
syādetat /
samāsabalāccedrūḍhirāsthīyate hanta na dṛṣṭastarhi tasya prayogo 'śvakarṇādivadvṛkṣādiṣu /
tathāca lokaprasiddhyabhāvānna rūḍhityākṣipati- #kathaṃ punarasatīti# /

children.text: janeṣu tāvatpañcajanaśabdaśca prathamaḥ prayogo lokeṣu dṛṣṭa ityasati prathamaprayoga ityasiddhamiti sthavīyastayānabhidhāyābhyupetya prathamaprayogābhāvaṃ samādhatte-śakyodbhidādivaditi /
children.translated_text: As for [the word '<s>pañcajana</s>'], the first usage of the word '<s>pañcajana</s>' is seen in the world [as applied] to peoples — thus the claim 'there is no first usage' is unestablished. Without asserting this with greater emphasis, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] concedes the absence of a first usage and resolves it: 'Like <s>śakyodbhidā</s> (one capable of splitting) and the like.'
Even according to the different views of the followers of the Teacher (<s>ācāryadeśīya</s>s), the twenty-five <s>tattva</s>s are not established [from this mantra].

But the ultimate intent [of <s>Śaṅkara</s>] is that the '<s>pañcajanāḥ</s>' are the very ones occurring in the remainder of the sentence — with this intent, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'But some [say]...' (<s>kaiścit tu</s>).
The rest is of transparent meaning. //12//

body.translated_text:
And thus, when the question arises 'who are those <s>pañcajanāḥ</s>?' — should the <s>prāṇa</s>s and the rest occurring in the remainder of the sentence be grasped, or the twenty-five <s>tattva</s>s? — in this matter, since the <s>tattva</s>s lack valid authority, and since the <s>prāṇa</s>s and the rest are heard in the remainder of the sentence — and abandoning them would entail the faults of 'abandoning what is heard' and 'postulating what is unheard' — the <s>prāṇa</s>s and the rest alone are the '<s>pañcajanāḥ</s>.' 
Nor is it appropriate [to say] that because of the contradiction between the <s>Kāṇva</s> and <s>Mādhyandina</s> [recensions], the <s>prāṇa</s>s and the rest occurring in the remainder of the sentence should not be grasped either — because even when there is contradiction, an option (<s>vikalpa</s>) is tenable due to [their] equal strength, as in the case of the <s>ṣoḍaśī</s>-libation.
Nor is this a discussion about the intrinsic nature of reality; rather, it is an injunction for the practice of meditation (<s>upāsanā</s>), because of the hearing of the injunctive [expression] 'one should contemplate with the mind alone' (<s>manasaivānudraṣṭavyam</s>).
'But how is the word "<s>jana</s>" (people) used for <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest?' — [here,] the word '<s>janaśabda</s>' means 'a word that denotes <s>jana</s>' — that is, the word '<s>pañcajana</s>.' How is its usage [applied] to <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest, which are not [literally] peoples? — this is to be explained.
Otherwise, [if one takes '<s>pañcajana</s>' as having a conventional meaning] in which the component-meanings have become dormant and a collective word-meaning [has emerged], the meaning of the word '<s>jana</s>' does not exist [separately in it] — hence there is no objection at all.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] shows a different semantic function without abandoning the conventional meaning: 'Because of connection with people' (<s>janasaṃbandhāt</s>).
'Those who partake of the word <s>jana</s>' [means:] those who partake of [the meaning of] the word '<s>pañcajana</s>.'
But [one might object:] when the meaning from the component parts is possible, the postulation of a collective semantic power is unjustified; and the component-meaning is possible in the case of the twenty-five <s>tattva</s>s — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'By the force of the compound' (<s>samāsabalāt</s>).
One might object: if the conventional meaning is upheld by the force of the compound, well then, no usage of it [in this sense] is seen — like '<s>aśvakarṇa</s>' (horse-ear) and the like [which conventionally denote] trees and the like.
And thus, because of the absence of well-knownness in common usage, there is no conventional meaning — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises the objection: 'But how, when there is no [well-known usage]?'

body.text:
#kāraṇatvena cākāśādiṣu yathāvyapadiṣṭokteḥ# /
atha samanvayalakṣaṇe keyamakāṇḍe virodhāvirodhacintā, bhavitā hi tasyāḥ sthānamavirodhalakṣaṇamityata āha- #pratipāditaṃ brahmaṇa iti# /
ayamarthaḥ nānekaśākhāgatatattadvākyālocanayā vākyārthāvagame paryavasite sati pramāṇāntaravirodhena vākyārthāgateraprāmāṇyamāśaṅkyāvirodhavyutpādanena prāmāṇyavyavasthāpanamavirodhalakṣaṇārthaḥ /
prāsaṅgikaṃ tu tatra sṛṣṭiviṣayāṇāṃ vākyānāṃ parasparamavirodhapratipādanaṃ na tu lakṣaṇārthaḥ /
tatprayojanaṃ ca tatraiva pratipādayiṣyate /
iha tu-vākyānāṃ sṛṣṭipratipādakānāṃ parasparavirodhe brahmaṇi jagadyonau na samanvayaḥ seddhumarhati /
tathāca na jagatkāraṇatvaṃ brahmaṇo lakṣaṇaṃ, naca tatra gatisāmānyaṃ, naca tatsiddhaye pradhānasyāśabdatvapratipādanaṃ, tasmādvākyānāṃ virodhāvirodhābyāmuktārthākṣepasamādhānābhyāṃ samanvayaḥ evopapādyata iti samanvayalakṣaṇe saṃgatamidamadhikaraṇam /
body.translated_text:
'And because in <s>ākāśa</s> and the like, the statement [designates <s>Brahman</s>] as the cause, as it has been expressed.'
Now, [one might ask:] what is this investigation of contradiction and non-contradiction doing out of place in the <s>samanvaya</s> section (first <s>pāda</s>), since its proper place will be the <s>avirodha</s> section (non-contradiction section)? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'The [nature of] <s>Brahman</s> has been established' (<s>pratipāditaṃ brahmaṇaḥ</s>).
The meaning is this: the purpose of the <s>avirodha</s> section is not [to address contradictions] by examining particular statements from various <s>śākhā</s>s after the meaning of the sentences has been ascertained; rather, [it is] to suspect the invalidity of the ascertained sentence-meaning due to contradiction with other means of knowledge, and then to establish its validity by demonstrating non-contradiction.
Incidentally, in that section, the demonstration of mutual non-contradiction among statements concerning creation will occur, but that is not the [primary] purpose of the section.
The purpose of that [demonstration] will be explained there itself.
But here — if there is mutual contradiction among statements that teach creation, then <s>samanvaya</s> (harmonization) regarding <s>Brahman</s> as the source of the world cannot be established.
And thus, being the world-cause would not be a characteristic of <s>Brahman</s>, nor would there be a common drift toward it, nor would the establishment of <s>pradhāna</s>'s being unscriptural serve that [purpose]. Therefore, it is through the objection and resolution concerning the contradiction and non-contradiction of sentences that <s>samanvaya</s> itself is being demonstrated — hence this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic) fits in the <s>samanvaya</s> section.

children.translated_text: 'Because of the mutual contradiction of statements regarding cause and effect,
<s>samanvaya</s> (harmonization) regarding the supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) as the source of the world is not established.'

body.text:
' 'sadeva somyedamagra āsīt' ityādīnāṃ kāraṇaviṣayāṇāṃ, 'asadvā idamatra āsīt' ityādibhirvākyaiḥ kāraṇaviṣayairvirodhaḥ /
kāryaviṣayāṇāmapi vibhinnakramākramotpattipratipādakānāṃ virodhaḥ /
tathāhi-kānicidanyakartṛkā jagadutpattimācakṣate vākyani /
kānicitsvayaṅkartṛkām /
sṛṣṭyā ca kāryeṇa tatkāraṇatayā brahma lakṣitam /
sṛṣṭivipratipattau tatkāraṇatāyāṃ brahmalakṣaṇe vipratipattau satyāṃ bhavati tallakṣye brahmaṇyapi vipratipatti /
tasmādbrahmaṇi samanvayābhāvānna samanvayāgamyaṃ brahma /
vedāntāstu kartrādipratipādanena karmavidhiparatayopacaritārthā avivakṣitārthā vā japopayogina iti prāptam /

children.translated_text: 'Of sequence and the like' (<s>kramādi</s>).
By the word 'and the like' (<s>ādi</s>), non-sequence (<s>akrama</s>) is included.

children.text: evaṃ prāpta ucyate-'sargakramavivāde 'pi na sa sṛṣṭari vidyate /
children.translated_text: This being the prima facie view, [the <s>Siddhāntin</s>] states: 'Even in a dispute about the sequence of creation, that [dispute] does not exist regarding the Creator;
And the statement of non-being (<s>asat</s>) regarding being (<s>sat</s>) is figurative, [expressing] the absence of [manifest] effects in some [passages].'

body.translated_text:
The statements concerning the cause — such as 'Being (<s>sat</s>) alone, dear one, was this in the beginning' (<s>sad eva somyedam agra āsīt</s>) and the like — are contradicted by [other] statements concerning the cause, such as 'Non-being (<s>asat</s>) indeed was this here in the beginning' (<s>asad vā idam agra āsīt</s>) and the like.
Likewise, there is contradiction among the effect-oriented statements that teach differing sequences and non-sequences of origination.
Thus: some statements declare that the origination of the world is brought about by another [agent]; some [declare it to be] self-caused.
And <s>Brahman</s> is characterized as the cause of the world through the effect, [namely] creation. When there is disagreement about creation, there is disagreement about Its being the cause; and when there is disagreement about <s>Brahman</s>'s characteristic, there is disagreement about <s>Brahman</s> itself, the thing characterized.
Therefore, because of the absence of <s>samanvaya</s> regarding <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Brahman</s> is not to be known through <s>samanvaya</s>.
Rather, the <s>Vedānta</s>s, through their teaching of agents and the like, are either subordinate to injunctions of ritual action with figurative meaning, or have unintended meaning, or are useful for recitation (<s>japa</s>) — this is the prima facie conclusion (<s>prāpta</s>).

body.text:
' na tāvadasti sṛṣṭikrame vigānaṃ, śrutīnāmavirodhāt /
tathāhi-anekaśilpaparyavadāto devadattaḥ prathamaṃ cakradaṇḍādi karoti, atha tadupakaraṇaḥ kumbhaṃ, kumbhopakaraṇaścāharatyudakaṃ, udakopakaraṇaśca saṃyavanena godhūmakaṇikānāṃ karoti piṇḍaṃ, piṇḍopakaraṇastu paṭati ghṛtapūrṇaṃ, tadasya devadattasya sarvatraitāsmin kartṛtvācchakyaṃ vaktuṃ devadattāccakrādi saṃbhūtaṃ tasmāccakrādeḥ kumbhādīti /
śakyaṃ ca devadattātkumbhaḥ samudbhūtastasmādudakāharaṇādītyādi /
nahyastyasaṃbhavaḥ sarvatrāsmin kāryajāte kramavatyapi devadattasya sākṣātkarturanusyūtatvāt /
tathehāpi yadyapyākāśādikrameṇaiva sṛṣṭistathāpyākāśānakālānilādau tatra tatra sākṣāt parameśvarasya kartṛtvācchakyaṃ vaktuṃ parameśvarādākāśaḥ saṃbhūta iti /
śakyaṃ ca vaktuṃ parameśvarādanalaḥ saṃbhūta ityādi /
yadi tvākāśādvāyurvāyosteja ityuktvā tejaso vāyurvāyorākāśa iti brūyādbhavedvirodhaḥ /
na caitadasti /
tasmādamūṣāmavivādaḥ śrutīnām /
evaṃ 'sa imāṃllokānasṛjata' ityupakramābhidhāyinyapi śrutiraviruddhā /
eṣā hi svavyāpāramabhidhānakrameṇa kurvatī nābhidheyānāṃ kramaṃ niruṇāddhi /
te tu yathākramāsthitā evākrameṇocyante-yathā kramavanti jñānāni jānātīti /
tadevamavigānam /
abhyupetya tu vigānamucyate-sṛṣṭau khalvetadvigānam /
sraṣṭā tu sarvavedāntavākyeṣvanusyūtaḥ parameśvaraḥ pratīyate /
nātra śrutivigānaṃ mātrayāpyasti /
naca sṛṣṭivigānaṃ sraṣṭari tadadhīnanirūpaṇe vigānamāvahatīti vācyam /
nahyeṣa sraṣṭṛtvamātreṇocyate 'pi tu 'satyaṃ jñānamanantaṃ brahma' ityādinā rūpeṇocyate sraṣṭā /
taccāsya rūpaṃ sarvavedāntavākyānugatam /
tajjñānaṃ ca phalavat /
'brahmavidāpnoti param' 'tarati śokamātmavit' ityādi śruteḥ /
sṛṣṭijñānasya tu na phalaṃ śrūyate /
tena 'phalavatsaṃnidhāvaphalaṃ tadaṅgam' iti sṛṣṭivijñānaṃ sraṣṭṛbrahmavijñānāṅgaṃ tadanuguṇaṃ sadbrahmajñānāvatāropāyatayā vyākhyeyam /
tathāca śrutiḥ-'annena somya śuṅgenāpo mūlamanviccha' ityādikā /
śuṅgenāgreṇa /
kāryeṇeti yāvat /
tasmānna sṛṣṭivipratipattiḥ sraṣṭari vipratipattimāvahati /
api tu 'guṇe tvanyāyakalpanā' iti tadanuguṇatayā vyākhyeyā /
yacca kāraṇe vigānam'asadvā idamatra asīt' iti, tadapi 'tadapyeṣa śloko bhavati' iti pūrvaprakṛtaṃ sadbrahmaṇākṛṣya 'asadevedamatra āsīt' ityucyamānaṃ tvasato 'bhidhāne 'saṃbaddhaṃ syāt /
śrutyantareṇa ca mānāntareṇa ca virodhaḥ /
tasmādaupacārikaṃ vyākhyeyam /
'taddhaika āhurasadevedamatra āsīt' iti tu nirākāryatayopanyastamiti na kāraṇe vivāda iti sūtre caśabdastvarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: [The <s>sūtra</s>] sets aside the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>.

children.text: ākāśādiṣu sṛjyamāneṣu kramavigāne 'pi na sraṣṭari vigānam /
children.translated_text: Even when there is disagreement about the sequence in the creation of <s>ākāśa</s> and the like, there is no disagreement regarding the Creator.
Why?

children.text: yathaikasyāṃ śrutau vyapadiṣṭaḥ parameśvaraḥ sarvasya kartā tathaiva śrutyantareṣūkteḥ, kena rūpeṇa, kāraṇatvena, aparaḥ kalpo yathā vyapadiṣṭaḥ krama ākāśādiṣu, 'ātmana ākāśaḥ saṃbhūta ākāśādvāyurvāyoragniragnerāpo 'dbhyaḥ pṛthivī' iti, tasyaiva kramasyānapabādhanena 'tattejo 'sṛjata' ityādikāyā api sṛṣṭerukterna sṛṣṭāvapi vigānam //14 //
children.translated_text: Because, just as in one <s>Śruti</s> the supreme Lord is designated as the maker of everything, so too He is stated in other <s>Śruti</s>s — in what manner? — as the cause. The other interpretation [is]: just as the sequence has been designated in <s>ākāśa</s> and the like — 'From the Self arose <s>ākāśa</s>, from <s>ākāśa</s> arose wind, from wind fire, from fire water, from water earth' — by the non-sublation of that very sequence, even the creation stated [in other Śrutis] beginning with 'That created fire' (<s>tat tejo 'sṛjata</s>) etc. [is non-contradictory] — hence there is no disagreement even about creation. //14//

body.translated_text:
To begin with, there is no disagreement about the sequence of creation, because the <s>Śruti</s>s are non-contradictory.
Thus: <s>Devadatta</s>, proficient in multiple crafts, first makes the wheel, staff, and the like; then, equipped with those implements, [he makes] a pot; equipped with the pot, he fetches water; equipped with water, he kneads wheat flour into a ball using a stirring implement; equipped with the ball, he fries it filled with clarified butter. Now, since <s>Devadatta</s> is the agent everywhere in this entire [sequence] of products, it is possible to say: 'From <s>Devadatta</s> the wheel and the like arose, from the wheel and the like the pot and the like [arose].' And it is [also] possible [to say]: 'From <s>Devadatta</s> the pot arose, from that the fetching of water and the like [arose].' For there is no impossibility anywhere in this entire [sequence of] effects, since <s>Devadatta</s>, the direct agent, is continuous throughout, even though [the process] has a sequence.
Similarly here too, although creation proceeds in the sequence of <s>ākāśa</s> (space) and the like, nevertheless, since the supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>) is the direct cause in each case — in <s>ākāśa</s>, fire, wind, and the like — it is possible to say: 'From the supreme Lord, <s>ākāśa</s> arose.' And it is [also] possible to say: 'From the supreme Lord, fire arose,' and so on.
But if, having said 'From <s>ākāśa</s> [arose] wind, from wind [arose] fire,' one were then to say 'From fire [arose] wind, from wind [arose] <s>ākāśa</s>,' there would be contradiction. But this does not occur.
Therefore, there is no dispute among these <s>Śruti</s>s.
Likewise, even the <s>Śruti</s> that begins with 'He created these worlds' (<s>sa imāṃl lokān asṛjata</s>) is non-contradictory.
For this [<s>Śruti</s>], in the course of its own expression, while performing its own function in the order of statement, does not determine the sequence of the things stated.
Rather, those [things], being situated in their own sequence, are stated without [following that] sequence — just as 'he knows sequential cognitions' [does not imply the cognitions are non-sequential].
Thus, there is no disagreement.
But even conceding disagreement, it is said: The disagreement is indeed about creation; but the Creator — the supreme Lord — is understood as continuous throughout all <s>Vedānta</s> statements.
In this regard, there is not the slightest disagreement among the <s>Śruti</s>s.
Nor should it be said that disagreement about creation, [since creation's] determination depends on [the Creator], brings about disagreement regarding the Creator.
For [<s>Brahman</s>] is not spoken of merely by virtue of being the Creator, but rather the Creator is spoken of with the characterization 'Being (<s>sat</s>), knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), infinite (<s>ananta</s>) is <s>Brahman</s>' and so on.
And that characterization of It pervades all <s>Vedānta</s> statements.
And the knowledge of That bears fruit: 'The knower of <s>Brahman</s> attains the highest' (<s>brahmavid āpnoti param</s>), 'The knower of the Self crosses over sorrow' (<s>tarati śokam ātmavit</s>) — from <s>Śruti</s>.
But no fruit is heard for the knowledge of creation.
Hence, by the principle 'In the proximity of what bears fruit, that which is fruitless is its accessory' (<s>phalavat saṃnidhāv aphalaṃ tad aṅgam</s>), the knowledge of creation is an accessory to the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> the Creator, and being subsidiary to that, is to be interpreted in conformity with <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge, as a means of bringing about [that knowledge].
And thus the <s>Śruti</s> says: 'Through food, dear one, as the shoot, trace water as the root' (<s>annena somya śuṅgenāpo mūlam anviccha</s>) and the like.
'Through the shoot' means 'through the tip' — that is, through the effect.
Therefore, disagreement about creation does not bring about disagreement regarding the Creator.
Rather, it is to be interpreted in conformity with that, by the principle 'In the case of a subsidiary, an irregular interpretation is to be adopted [to harmonize with the principal]' (<s>guṇe tv anyāyakalpanā</s>).
As for the disagreement about the cause — [the statement] 'Non-being (<s>asat</s>) indeed was this here' (<s>asad vā idam agra āsīt</s>) — this too, having been drawn into [connection with] the previously mentioned being (<s>sat</s>), namely <s>Brahman</s>, through 'And this verse occurs' (<s>tad apy eṣa śloko bhavati</s>), when stated as 'Non-being indeed was this here,' would be incoherent if it referred to [literal] non-being.
And it would contradict both other <s>Śruti</s>s and other means of knowledge.
Therefore, it is to be interpreted figuratively.
'But some say: "Non-being indeed was this here"' — this is presented [merely] to indicate the absence of [manifest] effects — hence there is no dispute about the cause. And the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) in the <s>sūtra</s> has the meaning of 'but' (<s>tu</s>).

body.text:
nanvekatrātmana ākāśakāraṇatvenoktiranyatra ca tejaḥ kāraṇatvena, tatkathamavigānamiti /
ata āha- #kāraṇatveti# /
hetau tṛtīyā /
sarvatrākāśānalānilādau sākṣātkāraṇatvenātmanaḥ /
prapañcitaṃ caitadadhastāt /
body.translated_text:
Now, [one might object:] in one place, the Self is stated as the cause of <s>ākāśa</s>, and in another, as the cause of fire — how then is there no disagreement?
To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'As the cause' (<s>kāraṇatvena</s>).
The third [case-ending] is used in the sense of reason (<s>hetu</s>).
Everywhere — in [the creation of] <s>ākāśa</s>, fire, wind, and the like — the Self is the direct cause.
And this has been elaborated above.

children.text: vyakriyata iti ca karmakartari karmaṇi vā rūpaṃ, na cetanatiriktaṃ kartāraṃ pratikṣipati kintūpasthāpayati /
children.translated_text: The [middle voice or passive] form 'was manifested' (<s>vyakriyata</s>) is either in the <s>karmakartari</s> (object-as-agent) or <s>karmaṇi</s> (passive) construction, and does not exclude a conscious agent but rather implies one.

children.text: nahi lūyate kedāraḥ svayameveti vā lūyate kedāra iti vā lavitāraṃ devadattādiṃ pratikṣipati /
children.translated_text: For [the expression] 'The field is being harvested' (<s>lūyate kedāraḥ</s>) — whether [stated as] 'by itself' or [simply] 'is being harvested' — does not exclude a harvester such as <s>Devadatta</s> and the like.
Rather, it positively implies [such an agent].
Therefore, everything is clear. //15//

body.text:
#jagadvācitvāt# /
nanu 'brahma te bravāṇi' iti brahmābhidhānaprakaraṇāt, upasaṃhāre ca 'sarvān pāpmano 'pahatya sarveṣāṃ ca bhūtānāṃ śraiṣṭhyaṃ svārājyaṃ paryeti ya evaṃ veda' iti niratiśayaphalaśravaṇādbrahmavedanādanyatra tadasaṃbhavāt, ādityacandrādigatapuruṣakartṛtvasya ca 'yasya vaitatkarma' iti cāsyāsatyavacchede sarvanāmnā pratyakṣasiddhasya jagataḥ paramārśena, jagatkartṛtvasya ca brahmaṇo 'nyatrāsaṃbhavātkathaṃ jīvamukhyaprāṇāśaṅkā /
ucyate-brahma te bravaṇīti bālākinā gārgyeṇa brahmābhidhānaṃ pratijñāya tattadādityādigatābrahmapuruṣābhidhānena na tāvadbrahmoktam /
yasya cājātaśatroḥ 'yo vai bālāke eteṣāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ kartā yasya vaitatkarma' iti vākyaṃ na tena brahmābhidhānaṃ pratijñātam /
na cānyadīyenopakrameṇānyasya vākyaṃ śakyaṃ niyantum /
tasmādajātaśatrorvākyasaṃdarbhapaurvāparyaparyālocanayā yo 'syārthaḥ pratibhāti sa eva grāhyaḥ /
atra ca karmaśabdastāvadvyāpāre nerūḍhavṛttiḥ /
kārye tu kriyata iti vyutpattyā vartate /
naca rūḍhau satyāṃ vyutpattiryuktāśrayitum /
naca brahmaṇa udāsīnasyāpariṇāmino vyāpāravattā /
vākyaśeṣe ca 'athāsmin prāṇa evaikadhā bhavati' iti śravaṇātparispandalakṣaṇasya ca karmaṇo yatropapattiḥ sa eva veditavyatayopadiśyate /
ādityādigatapuruṣakartṛtvaṃ ca prāṇasyopapadyate, hiraṇyagarbharūpaprāṇāvasthāviśeṣatvādādityādidevatānām /
'katama eko devaḥ prāṇaḥ' iti śruteḥ /
upakramānurodhena copasaṃhāre sarvaśabdaḥ sarvān pāpmana iti ca sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāmiti cāpekṣikavṛttirvahūn pāpmano bahūnāṃ bhūtānāmityevaṃparo draṣṭavyaḥ /
ekasmin vākye upakramānurodhādupasaṃhāro varṇanīyaḥ /

children.translated_text: And the distinction of <s>prāṇātman</s> (the self as vital breath), i.e., <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, from the <s>jīva</s> is also explicable.

children.text: tasmājjīvaprāṇayoranyatara iha grāhyo na raparameśvara iti prāptam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the conclusion is that one of the two — <s>jīva</s> or <s>prāṇa</s> — should be understood here, not the supreme Lord.
This being the prima facie view, [the <s>Siddhāntin</s>] replies: 'Having refuted <s>Bālāki</s>, the false claimant of <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge,
how can the king speak something disconnected or false?'

body.translated_text: <s>Jagadvācitvāt</s> (Because it denotes the world). Objection: Since the context is the teaching of <s>Brahman</s> as stated in '<s>Brahma</s> te bravāṇi' ('I shall tell you <s>Brahman</s>'), and since in the conclusion 'having destroyed all sins, he attains supremacy and sovereignty over all beings — he who knows thus,' the mention of an unsurpassable result is impossible anywhere other than in the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, and since the creatorship of the persons residing in the sun, moon, etc. is indicated by 'yasya vaitatkarma' ('whose indeed is this work'), and since, in the absence of any limiting specification, the pronoun 'this' refers to the perceptually established world, and since creatorship of the world is impossible for anyone other than <s>Brahman</s> — how can there be a doubt regarding <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) or <s>mukhyaprāṇa</s> (chief vital breath)? Reply: When <s>Bālāki</s> <s>Gārgya</s> promised to teach <s>Brahman</s> saying 'I shall tell you <s>Brahman</s>,' he did not in fact teach <s>Brahman</s>, since he described non-<s>Brahman</s> persons residing in the sun and other [luminaries]. And <s>Ajātaśatru</s>'s statement 'He who is the maker of these persons, whose indeed is this work' — by this he did not promise to teach <s>Brahman</s>. Nor can one person's statement be constrained by another person's introductory declaration. Therefore, by examining the coherence and sequence of <s>Ajātaśatru</s>'s statements alone, whatever meaning becomes apparent — that alone should be accepted. Here, the word <s>karma</s> (action/work) does not have its conventional meaning (<s>rūḍhi</s>) of activity or operation; rather, it functions in the sense of 'effect' through the etymological derivation (<s>vyutpatti</s>) 'that which is made' (kriyate). And when a conventional meaning exists, it is not proper to resort to etymology. Moreover, <s>Brahman</s>, being indifferent and without transformation, cannot possess activity. And since in the remainder of the passage we hear 'then in this [state], <s>prāṇa</s> alone becomes unified,' and since the entity in which activity characterized by movement is possible is the one being taught as what is to be known — the creatorship of the persons residing in the sun and other [luminaries] is also explicable for <s>prāṇa</s>, because the deities such as <s>Āditya</s> are particular states of <s>prāṇa</s> in the form of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>. As the <s>śruti</s> states: 'Which is the one god? <s>Prāṇa</s>.' And in accordance with the introduction, the word 'all' in the conclusion — in 'all sins' and 'of all beings' — should be understood in a relative sense, meaning 'many sins' and 'of many beings.' The conclusion should be interpreted in conformity with the introduction within a single passage. However, if one holds that <s>Ajātaśatru</s>'s statement, having refuted the proud <s>Bālāki</s> who was attributing <s>Brahman</s>-hood to what is not <s>Brahman</s>, must be about <s>Brahman</s> itself — for otherwise, if he intended to teach something that is not <s>Brahman</s> and not different from what <s>Bālāki</s> had said, his statement would be disconnected — even so, this cannot be a teaching of <s>Brahman</s>; rather, it is a teaching of the <s>jīva</s> alone. The reason is that <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, wishing to enlighten <s>Bālāki</s> who had come to learn about the maker of these persons presented as what is to be known, addressed a sleeping man, and since no response was heard to the call, he demonstrated that <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest are not the experiencer and not the master, and through the man's rising when struck with a stick, he pointed out the <s>jīva</s> — distinct from <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest — as the experiencer and master. And subsequently, from the <s>śruti</s> passage: 'Just as a chief enjoys through his servants, or as servants serve the chief, so does this conscious self (<s>prajñātman</s>) enjoy through these selves, and so do these selves serve this self.' Just as a chief, the principal person, enjoys sense-objects through his servants who function as instruments, or as servants serve the chief — for they serve the chief by providing food, clothing, and the like — so does this conscious self, the <s>jīva</s>, enjoy sense-objects through these selves residing in the sun and other [luminaries]. For <s>Āditya</s> and the rest, by rendering assistance through illumination, rain, and the like, nourish the <s>jīvātman</s>; and <s>Āditya</s> and the others also enjoy the <s>jīvātman</s> who is the sacrificer, through receiving the oblations offered by him. Therefore, it is the <s>jīvātman</s> alone that is taught here as what is to be known, being identical with <s>Brahman</s> due to their non-difference.

evamajātaśatruṇā dṛptabālākerabrahmavādino viśeṣamātmano darśayatā jīvaprāṇābhidhāne asaṃbaddhamuktaṃ syāt /
tayorvābrahmaṇorbrahmābhidhāne mithyābhihitaṃ syāt /
tathā ca na kaścidviśeṣo bālākergārgyādajātaśatrorbhavet /
tasmādanena brahmatattvamabhidhātavyam /

tasmāt 'brahma te bravāṇi' iti brahmaṇopakramāt, sarvān pāpmano 'pahatya sarveṣāṃ ca bhūtānāṃ śraiṣṭhyaṃ svarājyaṃ paryeti ya evaṃ veda' iti ca sati saṃbhave sarvaśruterasaṃkocānniratiśayena phalenopasaṃhārāt, brahmavedanādanyataśca tadanupapatteḥ, ādityādipuruṣakartṛtvasya ca svātantryalakṣaṇasya mukhyasya brahmaṇyeva saṃbhavādanyeṣāṃ hiraṇyagarbhādīnāṃ tatpāratantryāt, 'kkaiṣa etadbālāke' ityāderjīvādhikaraṇabhavanāpādanapraśnasya 'yadā suptaḥ svapnaṃ na kañcana paśyatyathāsmin prāṇa evaikadhā bhavati' ityāderuttasya ca brahmaṇyevopapatterbrahmaviṣayatvaṃ niścīyate /
atha kasmānna bhavato hiraṇyagarbhagocare eva praśnottare,
body.translated_text: Just as when someone who falsely considers himself a knower of gems says of glass 'This is to be known as a gem,' another person, having declared 'This is glass, not a gem, because the defining characteristics do not apply,' and then wishing to demonstrate his own superior knowledge, would give a disconnected teaching if he did not speak about a real gem — attributing gem-hood to what is not a gem does not establish the superiority of the first speaker, since the second speaker would also be speaking falsely. Therefore, the respondent who establishes his superiority over the first speaker must speak about the true nature of the gem. Similarly, if <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, while demonstrating his superiority over the proud <s>Bālāki</s> who was a false teacher of <s>Brahman</s>, were to teach about <s>jīva</s> or <s>prāṇa</s>, his statement would be disconnected; or if he were to attribute <s>Brahman</s>-hood to <s>jīva</s> or <s>prāṇa</s>, which are not <s>Brahman</s>, he would be speaking falsely. In that case, there would be no distinction between <s>Bālāki</s> <s>Gārgya</s> and <s>Ajātaśatru</s>. Therefore, he must teach the true nature of <s>Brahman</s>. And being truthful, there can be no accusation of falsehood against him. Therefore, from the introductory statement 'I shall tell you <s>Brahman</s>,' and from the conclusion with the unsurpassable result — 'having destroyed all sins, he attains supremacy and sovereignty over all beings — he who knows thus' — where, possibility existing, the word 'all' should not be restricted, and from the impossibility of such a result from knowledge of anything other than <s>Brahman</s>, and because the creatorship of the persons in the sun and other [luminaries] — in its primary sense of independent agency — is possible only for <s>Brahman</s> while <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> and others are dependent on it, and because the question establishing the abode of the <s>jīva</s> beginning with 'Where was this person, O <s>Bālāki</s>' and the answer 'When asleep, seeing no dream whatsoever, then in this [state] <s>prāṇa</s> alone becomes unified' are explicable only with reference to <s>Brahman</s> — the subject matter is determined to be <s>Brahman</s>. Now, why should not both the question and the answer pertain to <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> alone?

children.translated_text: For there is no maker without creative activity.
Nor is creative activity — otherwise called <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive force) — possible without <s>bhūti</s> (coming into being), i.e., origination. This is the meaning.

children.text: nanu yadīdamā jagatparāmṛṣṭaṃ tatastadantarbhūtāḥ puruṣā apīti ya eteṣāṃ puruṣāṇāmiti punaruktamityata āha- #etaduktaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: Objection: If this pronoun 'idam' refers to the world, then the persons included within it are also [referred to], so the statement 'the maker of these persons' would be redundant. To this he says: 'This is what is stated:' —
'the maker of these persons' [means that they are mentioned to indicate that he is] the maker not only of the world at large but specifically of these persons as well. [End of sūtra] 16.

body.translated_text: To refute this, [the sūtra] reads: 'From this Self, the <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths) are established according to their respective abodes.' What is stated here amounts to this: the Self alone is the substratum of the <s>jīva</s>, <s>prāṇa</s>, and the rest — not anything else. And although the <s>jīva</s> is not different from the Self, nevertheless, the supreme Self as delimited by limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) being conceived as the <s>jīva</s>, a relation of container and contained should be understood through the superimposition of difference based on the difference of limiting adjuncts. Thus, the supreme Self's being the substratum of the <s>jīva</s>'s existence and being its source is well established. Having thus established that the purport of the dialogue between <s>Bālāki</s> and <s>Ajātaśatru</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, [the objection arises that] 'yasya vaitatkarma' — the mention of activity — does not fit. [In response:] the word <s>karma</s> denotes 'effect,' and the pronoun 'this' (<s>etat</s>) refers to that effect. The pronoun refers to what is proximate, and nothing explicitly stated by words is proximate here. Nor are the persons residing in the sun and other [luminaries] fit to be referred to, despite being proximate, because they are many and masculine in gender, whereas 'etat' denotes a single neuter entity, and because 'the maker of these persons' already accounts for them. Therefore, it is the world — though not explicitly mentioned but perceptually established and fit for connection — that must be referred to. This is the meaning of [the sūtra's words] 'this is what is stated.' The [sūtra's] word 'vā' (or) indicates that what is said — 'the maker of these [persons] residing in the sun and other [luminaries] who are parts of the world' — is too little; rather, the entire world is his effect. The words <s>jīva</s> and <s>prāṇa</s> [in the passage] have <s>Brahman</s> as their referent, since the word <s>jīva</s> serves as a secondary indicator (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) of <s>Brahman</s>. But the word <s>Brahman</s> is not a secondary indicator of <s>jīva</s>, for if it were, it would be improper, as has been stated. Nor is it proper for a word whose natural capacity is to convey unapprehended meaning to convey already apprehended meaning. Nor is it proper for the already apprehended to serve as a secondary indicator of the unapprehended. And when unity of passage is possible, splitting into separate passages is not justified. If one were to follow the remainder of the passage and postulate three meditations — on <s>jīva</s>, <s>prāṇa</s>, and <s>Paramātman</s> — there would be three separate passages. But through examining the coherence and sequence, with the purport being meditation on <s>Brahman</s>, there is unity of passage alone. Therefore, the purport is not <s>jīva</s> or <s>prāṇa</s>, but <s>Brahman</s> alone — this is established. One might say: let the persons be indicated as effects, but the creative activity directed toward them is not indicated, nor is the result; the origin of the effect — 'whose is this work' — will be indicated later, so whence the redundancy? To this he says: 'Nor even of the person-directed [activity].' What is stated here amounts to this: by the very word 'maker' (<s>kartṛ</s>), he designates the maker, and thereby the creative activity and its result are implied, being entailed by [the concept of maker].

api ca sarvavedāntasiddhametadityāha- #suṣuptikāle ceti# /

samudācaradvṛttivikṣepābhāvamātreṇopamānam /
