prathamaṃ bhāṣyakṛtā jīvanirākaraṇāya sūtramidamavatāritam /
tatra mandadhiyāṃ nedaṃ prāṇanirākaraṇāyeti buddhirmā bhūdityāśayavānāha- #prāṇanirākaraṇasyāpīti# /
body.translated_text:
To the objection, 'From the statement beginning with "<s>prāṇa</s> alone becomes unified" and similar passages too, how is the entity distinct from the <s>jīva</s> understood?' — to address this, he cites another passage: #from this Self, the <s>prāṇas</s>#.
Moreover, he states that this is established by all <s>Vedānta</s> texts: #and in the state of deep sleep (<s>suṣupti</s>)#.
By way of concluding the reasoning within the <s>Vedāntic</s> methodology itself, he says: #therefore, where this# — of the Self — since there is absence of awareness, its form is as if of the nature of transparency, but not transparency itself,
because the <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions) of dissolution and distraction are present there.
The simile is merely based on the absence of the manifest activity of mental modifications (<s>vṛtti-vikṣepa</s>).
He elaborates on this very point: if the particular cognition (<s>viśeṣa-vijñāna</s>) — cognition of pot, cloth, and so on — generated by the limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>) such as the internal organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) were removed, and the essential nature of the Self were called simply 'cognition,' then that, being undifferentiated and unlimited, would be nothing but existent <s>Brahman</s> (<s>sat-brahma</s>); and since that is eternal, it is neither produced by limiting adjuncts nor is the essential nature devoid of them, because the nature of <s>Brahman</s> is never relinquished.
Therefore he has said: #particular (<s>viśeṣa</s>)#.
But when the <s>saṃskāra</s> of distraction, reinforced by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) in the form of dissolution, becomes active, then due to the arising of particular cognition, there is a coming forth that is in the nature of a fall from the form of the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) to the states of dream and waking.
Not only in the <s>Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa</s>, but in the <s>Vājasaneya</s> tradition as well, through the same question and answer, they understand the <s>Paramātman</s> as distinct from the <s>jīva</s> — thus he says: #moreover, thus one (<s>eka</s>)#.
To the objection, 'Here <s>ākāśa</s> (space) is the place of sleep, so whence the notion of the <s>Paramātman</s>?' — to this he replies: #and the word <s>ākāśa</s>#.
For it is impossible that physical <s>ākāśa</s> in its primary sense could be the support of the Self.
And as for what is stated about the abiding in the <s>purītat</s> during the state of deep sleep through the passage of seventy-two thousand <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels) called <s>hitā</s>, that too pertains to the internal organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>).
Therefore, just as in 'the small space (<s>dahara</s>) within this,' the word <s>ākāśa</s> should be understood as referring to the <s>Paramātman</s>.
The <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (commentator, i.e. <s>Śaṅkara</s>) first introduced this <s>sūtra</s> for the purpose of refuting the <s>jīva</s> [as the referent].
With the intention that those of dull intellect should not think 'this is only for the refutation of <s>prāṇa</s>,' he says: #the refutation of <s>prāṇa</s> also#.

body.text:
tau hi bālākyajātaśatrū suptaṃ puruṣamājagmatuḥ /
tamajātaśatrurnāmabhirāmantrayāñcakre 'bṛhat pāṇḍuravāsaḥ somarājan' iti /
sa amantryamāṇo nottasthau /

children.translated_text: He then awakened him by pressing him with his hand.
Then he arose.
'Then <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said: "Where was this person when he was thus asleep?"' — and so on.
Thus, through the awakening of the sleeping man, the teaching of an entity distinct from <s>prāṇa</s> and others [is demonstrated]. //18//

body.translated_text:
For those two, <s>Bālāki</s> and <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, approached a sleeping man.
<s>Ajātaśatru</s> called him by names: 'O great one, wearer of white garments, O king <s>Soma</s>.'
But even when being called, he did not rise.

body.text:
#vākyānvayāt# /
nanu maitreyībrāhmaṇopakrame yājñavalkyena gārhasthyāśramāduttamāśramaṃ yiyāsatā maitraiṭyā bhāryāyāḥ kātyāyanyā sahārthasaṃvibhāgakaraṇa ukte maitreyī yājñavalkyaṃ pratimamṛtatvārthinī prapaccha, yannu ma iyaṃ bhagoḥ sarvā pṛthvī vittena pūrṇā syātkimahaṃ tanāmṛtā syāmuta neti /
tatra neti hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ /
yathaivopakaraṇavatāṃ jīvitaṃ tathaiva te jīvitaṃ syādamṛtatvasya tu nāśāsti vittena /
evaṃ vittenāmṛtatvāśā bhavedyadi vittasādhyāni karmāṇyamṛtatve upayujyeran /
tadeva tu nāsti, jñānasādhyatvādamṛtatvasya karmaṇāṃ ca jñānavirodhināṃ tatsahabhāvitvānupapatteriti bhāvaḥ /
sā hovāca maitreyī yenāhaṃ nāmṛtā syāṃ kimahaṃ tenaṃ kuryāṃ yadeva bhagavān veda tadeva me brūhi /
amṛtatvasādhanamiti śeṣaḥ /
tatrāmṛtatvasādhanajñānopanyāsāya vairāgyapūrvakatvāttasya rāgaviṣayeṣu teṣu teṣu patijāyādiṣu vairāgyamutpādayituṃ yājñavalkyo 'na vā are patyuḥ kāmāya' ityādivākyasaṃdarbhamuvāca /
ātmaipādhikaṃ hi priyatvameṣāṃ na tu sākṣāt priyāṇyetāni /
tasmādetebhyaḥ patijāyādibhyo viramya yatra sākṣātprema sa eva #ātmā vā are draṣṭavyaḥ śrotavyo mantavyo nididhyāsitavyaḥ# /
vāśabdo 'vadhāraṇe /
vā are darśanena śravaṇādisādhanenedaṃ jagatsarvaṃ viditaṃ bhavatīti vākyaśeṣaḥ /
yato nāmarūpātmakasya jagatastattvaṃ pāramārthikaṃ rūpamātmaiva bhujaṅgasyeva samāropitasya tattvaṃ rajjuḥ /
tasmādātmani vidite sarvamidaṃ jagattattvaṃ viditaṃ bhavati, rajjvāmiva viditāyāṃ samāropitasya bhujaṅgasya tattvaṃ viditaṃ bhavati, yatastasmādātmaiva draṣṭavyo na tu tadatiriktaṃ jagat svarūpeṇa draṣṭavyam /
kutaḥ /
yato 'brahma taṃ parādāt' brāhmaṇajātirbrahmaṇo 'hamityevamabhimāna iti yāvat /
parādāt parākuryādamṛtatvapadāt /
kaṃ, yo 'nyatrātmano brahma brāhmaṇajātiṃ veda /
evaṃ kṣatriyādiṣvapi draṣṭavyam /
ātmaiva jagatastattvaṃ na tu tadatiriktaṃ kiñcittaditi /
atraiva bhagavatī śrutirupapattiṃ dṛṣṭāntaprabandhenāha /
yat khalu yadgrahaṃ vinā na śakyate grahītuṃ tattato na vyatiricyate /
yathā rajataṃ śuktikāyāḥ, bhujaṅgo vā rajjoḥ, dundubhyādiśabdasāmānyādvā tattacchabdabhedaḥ /
na gṛhyante ca cidrūpagrahaṇaṃ vinā sthitikāle nāmarūpāṇi /
tasmānna cidātmano bhidyante /
tadidamuktam #-sa yathā dundubherhanyamānasyeti# /
dundubhigrahaṇena tadgataṃ śabdasāmānyamupalakṣayati /
na kevalaṃ sthitikāle nāmarūpaprapañcaścidātmātirekeṇāgrahaṇāccidātmano na vyatiricyate 'pi tu nāmarūpotpatteḥ prāgapi cidrūpāvasthānāt tadupādānatvācca nāmarūpaprapañcasya tadanatirekaḥ, rajjūpādānasyeva bhujaṅgasya rajjoranatireka ityetadvṛṣṭāntena sādhayati bhagavatī śrutiḥ-'sa yathārdraidho 'grerabhyāhitasya pṛthagdhūnā viniścarantyevaṃ vā are 'sya mahato bhūtasya niḥśvasitametadyadṛgvedaḥ' ityādinā caturvidho mantra uktaḥ /
itihāsa ityādināṣṭavidhaṃ brāhmaṇamuktam /
etaduktaṃ bhavati-yathāgnimātraṃ prathamamavagamyate śrudrāṇāṃ visphuliṅgānāmupādānām /
atha tato visphuliṅgā vyuccaranti /
na caite 'gnestattvānyatvābhyāṃ śakyantaṃ nirvuktam /
evamṛgvedādayo 'pyalpaprayatnādbrahmaṇo vyuccaranto na tatastattvānyatvābhyāṃ nirucyante /
ṛgādibhirnāmopalakṣyate /
yadā ca nāmadheyasyeyaṃ gatistadā tatpūrvakasya rūpadheyasya kaiva katheti bhāvaḥ /
na kevalaṃ tadupādānatvāttato na vyatiricyate nāmarūpaprapañcaḥ, pralayasamaye ca tadanupraveśāttato na vyatiricyate /
yathā sāmudramevāmbhaḥ pṛthivītejaḥ saṃparkāt kāṭhinyamupagataṃ saindhavaṃ khilyaḥ, sa hi svākāre samudre kṣipto 'mbha eva bhavati, evaṃ cidambhodhau līnaṃ jagacchideva bhavati na tu tato 'tiricyata iti /
etaddṛṣṭāntaprabandhenāha- #sa yathā sarvāsāmapāmityādi# /
dṛṣṭāntaprabandhamuktvā dārṣṭāntike yojayati- #evaṃ vā are idaṃ mahaditi# /
bahuttvena brahmoktam /
idaṃ brahmetyarthaḥ /
bhūtaṃ satyam /
anantaṃ nityam /
apāraṃ sarvagatam /
#vijñānaghanaḥ# /
vijñānaikarasa iti yāvat /
etebhyaḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvena vyavasthaitebhyo bhūtebhyaḥ samutthāya sāmyenotthāya /
kāryakāraṇasaṃghātasya hyavacchedādduḥ khitvaśokitvādayastadavacchinne cidātmani tadviparīte 'pi pratīyante, yathodakapratibimbite candramasi toyagatāḥ kampādayaḥ /
tadidaṃ sāmyenotthānam /
yadā tvāgamācāryopadeśapūrvakamanananididhyāsanaprakarṣaparyantajo 'sya brahmasvarūpasākṣātkāra upāvartate tadā nirmṛṣṭanikhilavāsanāvidyāmalasya kāryakāraṇasaṃghātabhūtasya vināśe tānyeva bhūtāni naśyantyani tadupādhiścidātmanaḥ khilyabhāvo vinaśyati /
tato na pretya kāryakāraṇabhūtanivṛttau rūpagandhādisaṃjñāstīti /
na pretya saṃjñāstīti saṃjñāmātraniṣedhādātmā nāstīti manyamānā sā maitreyī hovāca, atraiva mā bhagavānamūmuhanmohitavān na pretya saṃjñāstīti /
sa hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ svābhiprāyaṃ, dvaite hi rūpādiviśeṣasaṃjñānibandhano duḥkhitvādyabhimānaḥ /
body.translated_text:
#On account of the consistency of the passages (<s>vākyānvaya</s>)#.
Now, at the beginning of the <s>Maitreyī Brāhmaṇa</s>, when <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, wishing to pass from the householder's stage (<s>gārhasthya āśrama</s>) to the highest stage of life, proposed the division of wealth with his wife <s>Maitreyī</s> and <s>Kātyāyanī</s>, <s>Maitreyī</s>, desiring immortality, asked <s>Yājñavalkya</s>: 'Venerable one, if this entire earth filled with wealth were mine, would I become immortal thereby, or not?'
Thereto <s>Yājñavalkya</s> replied: 'No.' 'Your life would be just like the life of those who possess material means, but there is no hope of immortality through wealth.'
Thus, there could be hope of immortality through wealth only if the rituals accomplished by wealth were useful for immortality.
But that is not the case, since immortality is accomplished by knowledge, and since rituals, being opposed to knowledge, cannot possibly coexist with it — this is the purport.
<s>Maitreyī</s> said: 'What shall I do with that by which I do not become immortal? What the venerable one knows, that alone tell me' —
the remainder being: 'the means to immortality.'
Thereupon, in order to present the knowledge that is the means to immortality — since that [knowledge] is preceded by dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) — <s>Yājñavalkya</s> uttered the series of statements beginning with 'It is not for the sake of the husband' and so on, in order to generate dispassion toward those objects of attachment such as husband, wife, and so forth.
For the dearness of these is dependent on the Self (<s>Ātman</s>); these are not directly dear in themselves.
Therefore, withdrawing from these — husband, wife, and so on — where there is direct love, that very #<s>Ātman</s> indeed is to be seen, heard, reflected upon, and deeply meditated upon (<s>nididhyāsitavya</s>)#.
The word '<s>vā</s>' is used in the sense of emphasis.
'By seeing — that is, by the means of hearing and so on — this entire universe becomes known' — this is the remainder of the sentence.
Since the true, ultimate nature (<s>pāramārthika rūpa</s>) of the universe consisting of name and form is the <s>Ātman</s> alone — just as the true nature of a superimposed snake is the rope —
therefore, when the <s>Ātman</s> is known, this entire universe is known in its true nature, just as when the rope is known, the true nature of the superimposed snake is known. Therefore, it is the <s>Ātman</s> alone that is to be seen, not the world as something distinct from it, in its own form.
Why? Because '<s>Brahman</s> abandons him' — the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> caste, i.e. the pride 'I am a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' — that is the meaning.
It would cast him away from the state of immortality — whom? — one who knows <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> caste, as other than the Self.
The same is to be understood regarding <s>Kṣatriyas</s> and others.
The <s>Ātman</s> alone is the true nature of the universe; there is nothing distinct from it — thus.
On this very point, the blessed <s>Śruti</s> presents reasoning through a series of illustrations.
That which cannot be grasped without a particular grasper does not differ from that [grasper] —
just as silver [does not differ] from the mother-of-pearl, or the snake from the rope, or the particular sounds from the generic sound of a drum and so forth.
And names and forms during the period of existence are not grasped without the grasping that is of the nature of consciousness (<s>cit</s>).
Therefore they do not differ from the conscious Self (<s>cid-ātman</s>).
This has been stated: #just as of a drum being struck, and so on#.
By the mention of the drum, the generic sound belonging to it is indicated.
Not only during the period of existence does the manifold of name and form not differ from the conscious Self — because it cannot be grasped apart from the conscious Self — but also because even before the origination of names and forms, there was abiding in the form of consciousness, and because the manifold of name and form has consciousness as its material cause (<s>upādāna</s>), it is non-different from it, just as a snake that has the rope as its material cause is non-different from the rope — this the blessed <s>Śruti</s> establishes through an illustration: 'Just as from wet firewood placed on a fire, smoke issues forth separately, even so from this great Being has been breathed forth the <s>Ṛgveda</s>' — by this, the four kinds of mantras are stated.
By 'history (<s>itihāsa</s>)' and so forth, the eight kinds of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> texts are stated.
The meaning is: just as fire alone is first apprehended as the material cause of sparks that fly forth,
and then from it the sparks issue forth,
and these cannot be determined as either identical with or different from fire,
so too the <s>Ṛgveda</s> and others, issuing forth from <s>Brahman</s> with little effort, cannot be determined as either identical with or different from it.
By the <s>Ṛg</s> and others, name (<s>nāma</s>) is indicated.
And when this is the condition of name, what need be said of form (<s>rūpa</s>) that presupposes it — this is the purport.
Not only because of having it as material cause is the manifold of name and form non-different from it, but also because at the time of dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>) it re-enters into it, it is non-different from it.
Just as ocean water itself, having acquired hardness through contact with earth and fire, becomes a block of salt — for when thrown into the ocean, its own form, it becomes water alone — so too the universe, dissolved into the ocean of consciousness, becomes consciousness alone and does not differ from it.
This he states through a series of illustrations: #just as of all waters, and so on#.
Having stated the series of illustrations, he applies them to the illustrated: #thus indeed this great, and so on#.
By the word 'great,' <s>Brahman</s> is spoken of.
The meaning is: this is <s>Brahman</s>.
'Being' (<s>bhūta</s>) means real (<s>satya</s>).
'Infinite' (<s>ananta</s>) means eternal (<s>nitya</s>).
'Boundless' (<s>apāra</s>) means all-pervading.
#A mass of consciousness (<s>vijñāna-ghana</s>)#.
That is to say, of the sole essence of consciousness.
Rising above these — the elements and so on arranged in the relation of cause and effect — rising in equality (<s>sāmyena</s>).
For because of the limitation by the aggregate of cause and effect, qualities such as being subject to suffering and sorrow are cognized in the conscious Self limited by them, and even in its opposite [i.e. the unlimited Self they appear reflected], just as movements such as trembling belonging to water are [seen] in the moon reflected in water.
This is the rising in equality.
But when, through the culmination of reflection and deep meditation preceded by the teaching of a traditional teacher, the direct realization of the essential nature of <s>Brahman</s> dawns upon him, then — since all the impurities of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) and ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) have been completely removed — upon the destruction of the aggregate of cause and effect, those very elements perish, the limiting adjunct of the conscious Self that was like a block of salt is destroyed.
Thereafter, upon the cessation of the aggregate of cause and effect, there are no cognitions (<s>saṃjñā</s>) such as form, smell, and so on — 'after death there is no [particular] consciousness.'
<s>Maitreyī</s>, thinking from the denial of consciousness as such that the Self does not exist, said: 'Here, venerable one, you have indeed bewildered me — [by saying] after death there is no consciousness.'
Then <s>Yājñavalkya</s> stated his own intended meaning: in duality indeed, the identification with suffering and so on is rooted in particular cognitions of form and so forth.

body.text:
ānandajñānaikarasabrahmādvayānubhave tu tat kena kaṃ paśyet, brahma vā kena vijānīyāt /
nahi tadāsya karbhāvo 'sti svaprakāśatvāt /
etaduktaṃ bhavati-na saṃjñāmātraṃ mayā vyāsedhi, kintu viśeṣasaṃjñeti /
tadevamamṛtatvaphalenopakramāt, madhye cātmavijñānena sarvavijñānaṃ pratijñāya tadupapādanāt, upasaṃhāre ca mahadbhūtamanantamityādinā ca brahmarūpabhidhānāt, dvaitanindayā cādvaitaguṇakīrtanādbrahmaiva maitreyībrahmaṇe pratipādyaṃ na jīvātmeti nāsti pūrvapakṣa ityanārabhyamevedamadhikaraṇam /
atrocyate-bhoktṛtvajñātṛtājīvarūpotthānasamādhaye maitreyībrahmaṇe pūrvapakṣeṇopakramaḥ kṛtaḥ /
patijāyādibhogyasaṃbandho nābhokturbrahmaṇo yujyate, nāpijñānakartṛtvamakartuḥ sākṣācca mahato bhūtasya vijñānātmabhāvena samuttānābhidhānaṃ vijñānātmana eva draṣṭavyatvamāha /
body.translated_text:
But in the non-dual experience of <s>Brahman</s>, which is of the sole essence of bliss and consciousness, by what could one see whom, or by what could one know <s>Brahman</s>?
For then there is no state of being an agent for him, because [<s>Brahman</s>] is self-luminous.
The meaning is this: it is not mere consciousness that I denied, but rather particular consciousness.
Thus, since the passage begins with the result of immortality; since in the middle, having declared that through the knowledge of the Self all things are known, it substantiates this; since at the conclusion, by [the description] 'a great being, infinite,' and so on, the nature of <s>Brahman</s> is described; and since through the censure of duality the virtues of non-duality (<s>advaita</s>) are proclaimed — it is <s>Brahman</s> alone that is taught in the <s>Maitreyī Brāhmaṇa</s>, not the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>); hence there is no <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view), and therefore this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (section) need not be undertaken at all.
To this we reply: The <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> has been raised at the beginning of the <s>Maitreyī Brāhmaṇa</s> for the purpose of reconciling the description of the Self rising as having the nature of an enjoyer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>) and knower (<s>jñātṛ</s>), which is the nature of the <s>jīva</s>.
The connection with objects of enjoyment such as husband, wife, and so forth is not appropriate for <s>Brahman</s>, which is not an enjoyer; nor is the agency of knowing appropriate for that which is not an agent. And [the Śruti's] direct statement about rising as the conscious self (<s>vijñānātman</s>) from this great Being declares that it is the conscious self alone that is to be seen.

children.text: anyathā brahmaṇo draṣṭavyatvapare 'smin brāhmaṇo tasya vijñānātmatvena samutthānābhidhānamanupayuktaṃ syāttasya tu draṣṭavyamupayujyata ityupakramamātraṃ pūrvapakṣaḥ kṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Otherwise — in this <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> that has the seeing of <s>Brahman</s> as its purport — the mention of its rising as the conscious self (<s>vijñānātman</s>) would be pointless; but the 'to be seen' is appropriate for that [conscious self]. Thus the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> is raised only from the introductory portion.
#And because the collection of objects of enjoyment exists for the sake of an enjoyer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>)# — this is merely corroborative support [for the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>].
The <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion), however, has been stated by the <s>Bhāṣya</s> explained through direct gloss (<s>nigada</s>). //19//

body.text: tadevaṃ paurvāparyālocanayā maitreyībrāhmaṇasya brahmadarśanaparatve sthite bhoktrā jīvātmanopakramamācāryadeśīyamatena tāvatsamādhatte sūtrakāraḥ- #pratijñāsiddherliṅgamāśmaradhyaḥ# /

children.text: yathā hi vahnervikārā vyuccaranto visphuliṅgā na vahneratyantaṃ bhidyante, tadrūpanirūpaṇatvāt, nāpi tato 'tyantamabhinnāḥ, vahneriva parasparavyāvṛttyabhāvaprasaṅgāt, tathā jīvātmano 'pi brahmavikāra na brahmaṇo 'tyantaṃ bhidyante, cidrūpatvābhāvaprasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text: Just as sparks, which are modifications of fire issuing forth from it, are not absolutely different from fire — because they are determined as having the nature of fire — nor are they absolutely identical with it — because [if they were,] there would be the absurd consequence of the absence of mutual distinction, just as in the case of fire [itself] — so too the <s>jīvātmans</s> (individual selves), being modifications of <s>Brahman</s>, are not absolutely different from <s>Brahman</s>, because otherwise there would be the absurd consequence of the absence of the nature of consciousness (<s>cid-rūpa</s>).

children.text: nāpyatyantaṃ na bhidyante, parasparaṃ vyāvṛttyabhāvaprasaṅgāt, sarvajñaṃ pratyupadeśavaiyarthyācca /
children.translated_text: Nor are they absolutely non-different, because there would be the absurd consequence of the absence of mutual distinction, and because the teaching addressed to the omniscient [<s>Brahman</s>] would be rendered purposeless.
Therefore, there is in some respect difference and in some respect non-difference of the <s>jīvātmans</s> (individual selves) [from <s>Brahman</s>].

children.text: tatra tadvijñānena sarvavijñānapratijñāsiddhaye vijñānātmaparamātmanorabhedamupādāya paramātmani darśayitavye vijñānātmanopakrama ityāśmaradhya ācāryo mene //20 //
children.translated_text: There, in order to establish the promise that 'by the knowledge of that [<s>Brahman</s>], everything is known,' by taking up the non-difference of the cognitive self (<s>vijñānātman</s>) and the supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), what is to be shown in the <s>Paramātman</s> is commenced through the cognitive self — so the teacher <s>Āśmarathya</s> held. //20//

body.translated_text: Thus, when it has been established through the examination of the sequential coherence (<s>paurvāparya</s>) that the <s>Maitreyī Brāhmaṇa</s> has the vision of <s>Brahman</s> as its purport, and [the objection is raised] that the introductory portion [speaks of] the <s>jīvātman</s> as the enjoyer, the <s>Sūtrakāra</s> first accommodates this according to the view of <s>Ācāryadeśīya</s> (a teacher close to the <s>Ācārya</s>): #the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) for the establishment of the proposition — <s>Āśmarathya</s>#.

body.text: ācāryadeśīyāntaramatena samādhatte- #utkramiṣyata evaṃbhāvādisyauḍulomiḥ# /

children.text: jīvo hi paramātmano 'tyantaṃ bhinna eva san dehendriyamanobuddhyupadhānasaṃparkātsarvadā kaluṣaḥ, tasya ca jñānadhyānādisādhanānuṣṭhānātsaṃprasannasya dehendriyādisaṃghātādutkramiṣyataḥ paramātmanaikyopapatteridamabhedenopakramaṇam /
children.translated_text: For the <s>jīva</s> (individual self), being entirely different from the <s>Paramātman</s>, is always impure due to contact with the conditioning adjuncts (<s>upādhāna</s>) of body, sense-organs, mind, and intellect. And when, through the practice of means such as knowledge, meditation, and the like, it becomes purified and is about to depart from the aggregate of body, sense-organs, and the like, the fitness of its unity with the <s>Paramātman</s> [is established] — hence this commencement with non-difference [is made].
What is stated amounts to this: Taking up the future non-difference [between <s>jīva</s> and <s>Brahman</s>], the non-difference is stated even at the time of difference.

children.text: yathāhuḥ pāñcarātrikāḥ-'āmukterbheda eva syājjīvasya ca parasya ca /
children.translated_text: As the <s>Pāñcarātrika</s>s say: 'Until liberation, there is indeed difference between the <s>jīva</s> and the Supreme;
but for one who has been liberated, there is no difference, because of the absence of the cause of difference.'

body.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] reconciles [the issue] with the view of another near-teacher: '#Because of that nature, it will depart — so [holds] <s>Auḍulomi</s>#.'

body.text:
' iti /
atraiva śrutimupanyasyati- #śrutiścaivamiti# /

children.translated_text: Previously, the impurity of the self caused by the conditioning adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) of body, sense-organs, and the like was stated.

children.text: saṃprati svābhāvikameva jīvasya nāmarūpaprapañcāśrayatvalakṣaṇaṃ kāluṣyaṃ pārthivānāmaṇūnāmiva śyāmatvaṃ kevalaṃ pākeneva /
children.translated_text: Now [it is stated that] the impurity of the <s>jīva</s>, characterized by being the substrate of the phenomenal expansion of name and form (<s>nāmarūpaprapañca</s>), is indeed natural — like the dark color of earthly atoms, [removable] only as if by firing.

children.text: jñānadhyānādinā tadapanīya jīvaḥ parātparataraṃ puruṣamupaitītyāha- #kkacicca jīvākṣayamapīti# /
children.translated_text: Having removed that [impurity] through knowledge, meditation, and the like, the <s>jīva</s> approaches the <s>Puruṣa</s> who is higher than the highest — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#And somewhere, even the imperishability of the <s>jīva</s>#.'
The illustration of the rivers [is from the <s>Śruti</s>]: 'Just as these rivers, O dear one.' //21//

body.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] adduces a <s>Śruti</s> for this very [view]: '#And the <s>Śruti</s> too [supports] this#.'

body.text:
tadevamācāryadeśīyamatadvayamuktvātrāparituṣyannācāryamatamāha sūtrakāraḥ #-avisthiteriti kāśakṛtsnaḥ# /
etadvyācaṣṭe- #asyaiva paramātmana iti# /
na jīva ātmano 'nyaḥ /
nāpi tadvikāraḥ kintvātmaivāvidyopādhānakalpitāvacchedaḥ /
ākāśa iva ghaṭamaṇikādikalpitāvacchedo ghaṭākāśo maṇikākāśo na tu paramākāśādanyastadvikāro vā /
tataśca jīvātmanopakramaḥ parāmātmanaivopakramastasya tato 'bhedāt /
sthūladarśilokapratītisaukaryāyaupādhikenātmarūpeṇopakramaḥ kṛtaḥ /
atraiva śrutiṃ pramāṇayati- #tathāceti# /
atha vikāraḥ paramātmano jīvaḥ kasmānna bhavatyākāśādivadityāha- #naca tejaḥprabhṛtīnāmiti# /
nahi yathā tejaḥprabhṛtīnāmātmavikāratvaṃ śrūyate evaṃ jīvasyeti /
ācāryatrayamataṃ vibhajate- #kāśakṛtsnasyācāryasyeti# /
ātyantike satyabhede kāryakāraṇabhāvābhāvādanātyantiko 'bheda āstheyaḥ, tathāca kathañcidbhedo 'pīti tamāsthāya kāryakāraṇabhāva iti matatrayamuktvā kāśakṛtsnīyamataṃ sādhutvena nirdhārayati- #tatra teṣu#madhye /
#kāśakṛtsnīyaṃ matamiti# /
ātyantike hi jīvaparamātmanorabhede tāttvike 'nādyavidyopādhikalpito bhedastattvamasīti jīvātmano brahmabhāvatattvopadeśaśravaṇamanananididhyāsanaprakarṣaparyantajanmanā sākṣātkāraṇe vidyayā śakyaḥ samūlakāṣaṃ kaṣituṃ, rajjvāmahivibhrama iva rajjutattvasākṣātkāreṇa, rājaputrasyeva va mlecchakule vardhamānasyātmani samāropito mlecchabhāvo rājaputro 'sīti āptopadeśena /
na tu mṛdvikāraḥ śarāvādiḥ śataśo 'pi mṛnmṛditi cintyamānastajjanmanā mṛdbhāvasākṣātkāreṇa śakyo nivartayituṃ, tatkasya hetoḥ, tasyāpi mṛdo bhinnābhinnasya tāttvikatvāt, vastutastu jñānenocchettumaśakyatvāt, so 'yaṃ pratipādayiṣitārthānusāraḥ /
api ca jīvasyātmavikāratve tasya jñānadhyānādisādhanānuṣṭhānāt svaprakṛtāvapyaye sati nāmṛtatvasyāśāstītyapuruṣārthatvamamṛtatvaprāpiśrutivirodhaśca /
kāśakṛtsnamate tvetadubhayaṃ nāstītyāha- #evaṃ ca satīti# /
nanu yadi jīvo na vikāraḥ kintu brahmaiva kathaṃ tarhi tasminnāmarūpāśrayatvaśrutiḥ, kathañca 'yathāgneḥ śrudrā visphuliṅgā' iti brahmavikāraśrutirityāśaṅkāmupasaṃhāravyājena nirākaroti- #ataśca svāśrayasyeti# /
yataḥ pratipādayiṣitārānusāraścāmṛtatvaprāptiśca vikārapakṣe na saṃbhavataḥ, ataśceti yojanā /
dvitīyapūrvapakṣabījamanayaiva trisūtryāpākaroti- #yadapyuktamiti# /
śeṣamatirohitārthaṃ vyākhyātārthaṃ ca /
tṛtīyapūrvapakṣabījanirāse kāśakṛtsnīyenaivetyavadhāraṇaṃ tanmatāśrayaṇenaiva tasya śakyanirāsatvāt /
aikāntike hyādvaite ātmano 'nyakarmakaraṇe 'kena kaṃ paśyet' iti ātmanaśca karmatvaṃ 'vijñātāramare kena vijānīyāt' iti śakyaṃ niṣeddhum /
body.translated_text:
Having thus stated the two views of the near-teachers, not being satisfied with them, the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author of the <s>sūtra</s>s) states the view of the [true] teacher: '#Because of the non-differentiation of status — so [holds] <s>Kāśakṛtsna</s>#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] explains this: '#Of this very <s>Paramātman</s>#.'
The <s>jīva</s> is not other than the Self.
Nor is it a modification (<s>vikāra</s>) of that [Self]; rather, it is the Self itself — a delimitation imagined through the conditioning adjunct (<s>upādhāna</s>) of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance).
Just as space (<s>ākāśa</s>), [appearing as] pot-space or jewel-box-space through the imagined delimitation of a pot, jewel-box, and the like, is not other than the supreme space nor a modification of it.
Therefore, the commencement through the <s>jīvātman</s> is indeed the commencement through the <s>Paramātman</s> itself, because of the non-difference between them.
The commencement was made through the conditional form of the Self by way of the limiting adjuncts, for the ease of apprehension of those who see [things] grossly [i.e., ordinary people].
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] cites a <s>Śruti</s> as evidence for this very [view]: '#And thus#.'
Then, why should the <s>jīva</s> not be a modification of the <s>Paramātman</s>, like space and the like? To this he says: '#And not like fire (<s>tejas</s>) and the rest#.'
For it is not the case that the <s>jīva</s> is heard [in <s>Śruti</s>] as being a modification of the Self in the way that fire and the rest are.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] distinguishes the three teachers' views: '#Of the teacher <s>Kāśakṛtsna</s>#.'
Since, if the non-difference [of <s>jīva</s> and <s>Brahman</s>] were absolute, there would be no cause-effect relationship [and hence no creation]; [therefore] a non-absolute non-difference should be maintained. And thus there is also some kind of difference — having maintained this, and [having presented] the cause-effect relationship on that basis — having stated the three views, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] determines the <s>Kāśakṛtsna</s> view as correct: '#Among those#' — i.e., among them.
'#The <s>Kāśakṛtsna</s> view#.'
For when the non-difference of <s>jīva</s> and <s>Paramātman</s> is absolute and ultimate, the difference — imagined through the conditioning adjunct of beginningless <s>avidyā</s> — can be uprooted root and all by the direct realization (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>) born of the culmination of the teaching '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' (You are That), heard, reflected upon, and deeply meditated upon — just as the delusion of a snake in a rope [is uprooted] by the direct realization of the rope's true nature; or just as the superimposed <s>Mleccha</s>-identity of a prince raised in a <s>Mleccha</s> household [is uprooted] by the authoritative instruction 'You are a prince.'
But a modification of clay, such as a plate and the like, even when contemplated a hundred times as 'clay, clay,' cannot be eliminated by the direct realization of the clay-nature born thereof. For what reason? Because the [plate's nature of being] both different and non-different from clay is itself real. In truth, [it is] because [the modification] cannot be eliminated by knowledge — such is the [correct] presentation of the intended meaning.
Moreover, if the <s>jīva</s> were a modification of the Self, then upon the destruction of its own nature through the cessation of [the modification's] existence through the practice of means such as knowledge, meditation, and the like, there would be no prospect of immortality — and thus there would be both the unwanted consequence of purposelessness and contradiction with the <s>Śruti</s>s that teach the attainment of immortality.
In the <s>Kāśakṛtsna</s> view, these two [problems] do not arise — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#And when this is so#.'
Now, if the <s>jīva</s> is not a modification but is <s>Brahman</s> itself, then how [can one explain] the <s>Śruti</s> about [the <s>jīva</s>] being the substrate of name and form? And how [can one explain] the <s>Śruti</s> about [it being] a modification of <s>Brahman</s>, 'As from a fire tiny sparks [fly forth]'? — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] dispels this doubt under the guise of a conclusion: '#And therefore, of that which is its own substrate#.'
Since the presentation of the intended meaning and the attainment of immortality are not possible in the modification view, 'therefore' — this is the construction.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] dispels the second <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> seed with this very set of three <s>sūtra</s>s: '#What was also said#.'
The rest has transparent meaning and has been explained.
In dispelling the third <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> seed, the emphatic restriction 'by the <s>Kāśakṛtsna</s> [view] alone' [indicates] that only by resorting to that view can it be dispelled.
For in absolute non-duality (<s>advaita</s>), when the Self has no other object of action, 'By whom should one see whom?' [is possible]; and the objecthood of the Self too — 'By whom should the knower be known?' — can be negated.

bhedābhedapakṣe vaikāntike vā bhede sarvametadadvaitāśrayamaśakyamityavadhāraṇasyārthaḥ /
na kevalaṃ kāśakṛtsnīyadarśanāśrayaṇena bhūtapūrvagatyā vijñātṛtvamapi tu śrutipaurvāparyaparyālocanayāpyevamevetyāha- #api ca yatra hīti# /
kasmāt punaḥ kāśakṛtsnasya matamāsthīyate netareṣāmācāryāṇāmityata āha- #darśitaṃ tu purastāditi# /
kāśakṛtsnīyasya matasya śrutiprabandhopanyāsena punaḥ śrutimattvaṃ smṛtimattvaṃ copasaṃhāropakramamāha- #ataśceti# /
kkacitpāṭha ātaśceti /
tasyāvaśyaṃ cetyarthaḥ /
jananajarāmaraṇabhītayo vikriyāstāsāṃ sarvāsāṃ 'mahānajaḥ' ityādinā pratiṣedhaḥ /
pariṇāmapakṣe 'nyasya cānyabhāvapakṣe aikāntikādvaitapratipādanaparāḥ 'ekamevādvitīyam' ityādayaḥ, dvaitadarśananindāparāśca 'anyo 'sāvanyo 'hamasmi' ityādayaḥ, janmajarādivikriyāpratiṣedhaparāśca 'eṣa mahānajaḥ' ityādayaḥ śrutaya uparudhyeran /

atha tvagṛhyamāṇaviśeṣatayā na balābalāvadhāraṇaṃ,tataḥ saṃśaye sati na suniścitārthamātmani jñānaṃ bhavet /

nanu yadi kṣetrajñaparamātmanorabhedo bhāvikaḥ, kathaṃ tarhi vyapadeśabuddhibhedau kṣetrajñaḥ paramātmeti kathañca nityaśuddhabuddhamuktasvabhāvasya bhagavataḥ saṃsāritā /
avidyākṛtanāmarūpopādhivaśāditi cet /
kasyeyamavidyā /

nāpi paramātmanaḥ, tasya vidyaikarasyāvidyāśrayatvānupapatteḥ /
tadatra saṃsāritvāsaṃsāritvavidyāvidyāvattvarūpaviruddhayadharmasaṃsargudbuddhivyapadeśabhedāccāsti jīveśvarayorbhedo 'pi bhāvika ityata āha- #sthite ca paramātmakṣetrajñātmaikatveti# /
na tāvadbhedadābhedāvekātra bhāvikau bhavitumarhata iti viprapañcitaṃ prathame pāde /
dvaitadarśananindayā caikāntikādvaitapratipādanaparāḥ paurvāparyālocanayā sarve vedāntaḥ pratīyante /
tatra yathā bimbādavadatāttāttvike pratibimbānāmabhede 'pi nīlamaṇikṛpāṇakācādyupadhānabhedātkālpaniko jīvānāṃ bhedo buddhivyapadeśabhedau vartayati, idaṃ bimbamavadātamimāni ca pratibimbāni nīlotpalāśaśayāmalāni vṛttadīrghādibhedabhāñji bahūnīti, evaṃ paramātmanaḥ śuddhasvabhāvājjīvānamabheda aikāntike 'pyanirvacanīyānādyavidyopadhānabhedātkālpaniko jīvānāṃ bhedo buddhivyapadeśabhedāvayaṃ ca paramātmā śuddhavijñānānandasvabhāva ime ca jīvā avidyāśokaduḥkhādyupadravabhāja iti vartayati /
avidyopadhānaṃ ca yadyapi vidyāsvabhāve paramātmani na sākṣādasti tathāpi tatpratibimbakalpajīvadvāreṇa parasminnucyate /
na caivamanyonyāśrayo jīvavibhāgāśrayāvidyā, avidyāśrayaśca jīvavibhāga iti, bījāṅkuravadanāditvāt /
ata eva kānuddiśyaiva īśvaro māyāmāracayatyanārthikāṃ, uddeśyanāṃ sargādau jīvānāmabhāvāt, kathaṃ cātmānaṃ saṃsāriṇaṃ vividhavedanābhājaṃ kuryādityādyanuyogo niravakāśaḥ /

yathā pratibimbeṣu bhāsamāneṣu bimbaṃ tadabhinnamapi guhyamevaṃ jīveṣu bhāsamāneṣu tadabhinnamapi brahma guhyam /
astu tarhi brahmaṇo 'nyadguhyamityata āha- #naca brahmaṇo 'nya iti /
ye tu#āśamarathyaprabhṛtayaḥ #nirbandhaṃ kurvanti te vedāntārthamiti# /
brahmaṇaḥ sarvātmanā bhagaśo vā pariṇāmābhyupagame tasya kāryatvādanityatvācca tadaśrito mokṣo 'pi tathā syāt /
yadi tvevamapi mokṣaṃ nityaṅkṛtakaṃ brūyustatrāha #-nyāyeneti# /
evaṃ ye nadīsamudranidarśanenāmukterbhedaṃ muktasya cābhedaṃ jīvasyāsthiṣata teṣāmapi nyāyenāsaṃgatiḥ /
no jātu ghaṭaḥ paṭo bhavati /

evaṃ samudrādapi teṣāṃ bheda eva /
ye tu kāśakṛtsnīyameva matamāsthāya jīvaṃ paramātmanoṃ'śamācakhyusteṣāṃ kathaṃ 'niṣphalaṃ niṣkriyaṃ śāntam' iti na śrutivirodhaḥ /
niṣphalamiti sāvayavatvaṃ vyāsedhi na tu sāṃśatvam, aṃśaśca jīvaḥ paramātmano nabhasa iva karṇanemimaṇḍalāvacchinnaṃ nabhaḥ śabdaśravaṇayogyaṃ, vāyoriva ca śarīrāvacchinnaḥ pañcavṛttiḥ prāṇa iti cet /
na tāvannabho nabhasoṃśaḥ, tasya tattvāt /

naca karṇanemimaṇḍalāvacchinnamaṃśa iti cet, hanta tarhi prāptāprāptavivekena karṇanemimaṇḍalaṃ vā tatsaṃyogo vetyuktaṃ bhavati /

body.translated_text:
In the view of difference-cum-non-difference, or in the view of absolute difference according to the <s>Vaikāntika</s>s, all this, being dependent on non-duality, is impossible — such is the meaning of the emphatic restriction.
Not only through resorting to the <s>Kāśakṛtsna</s> view is the knower-hood [of the Self established] by way of what has been previously discussed, but also through the examination of the sequential connection of <s>Śruti</s> passages — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Also, where indeed#.'
Why then is the view of <s>Kāśakṛtsna</s> adopted and not that of the other teachers? — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#It has been shown earlier#.'
Having shown the <s>Śruti</s>-groundedness and <s>Smṛti</s>-groundedness of the <s>Kāśakṛtsna</s> view through the presentation of the continuous thread of <s>Śruti</s>, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the introduction and conclusion: '#Therefore#.'
Somewhere the reading is '<s>ātaśca</s>' — its meaning is 'necessarily.'
Birth, old age, death, and other modifications — the negation of all of these is [stated] through 'The great unborn one' and so on.
In the view of transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>) or the view that one thing becomes another, the <s>Śruti</s> passages aimed at establishing absolute non-duality, such as 'One only, without a second,' those aimed at censuring the perception of duality, such as 'He is other, I am other,' and those aimed at negating modifications such as birth, old age, and the like, such as 'This great one is unborn' — all these would be obstructed.
Moreover, if both difference and non-difference between the <s>jīva</s> and the <s>Paramātman</s> were maintained, then, since they are mutually contradictory and cannot be combined, if one were to prevail, no unqualified knowledge of the Self could arise, because the stronger one would sublate the knowledge that relies on the weaker position.
But if, due to the inability to discern a distinction [between them], neither can be determined as stronger or weaker, then, since doubt would persist, no knowledge with a firmly ascertained object would arise regarding the Self.
And knowledge with a firmly ascertained object is heard as the means to liberation — '<s>Vedāntavijñānasuniścitārthāḥ</s>' (those whose purpose is firmly ascertained through the knowledge of <s>Vedānta</s>).
This is what [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states: '#Otherwise, for those desiring liberation#.'
'Of one who perceives oneness' — thus says the <s>Śruti</s>, not 'of one who perceives both oneness and multiplicity.'
Objection: If the non-difference between <s>Kṣetrajña</s> (the knower of the field) and <s>Paramātman</s> is real, then how [can there be] the distinction of designation and cognition — '<s>Kṣetrajña</s>' and '<s>Paramātman</s>' — and how can the blessed Lord, whose nature is eternally pure, awakened, and free, be a <s>saṃsārin</s> (transmigrating being)?
If [the answer is:] due to the conditioning adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) of name and form created by <s>avidyā</s> — then whose is this <s>avidyā</s>?
It does not belong to the <s>jīva</s>, because the <s>jīva</s> is not different from the <s>Paramātman</s>.
Nor does it belong to the <s>Paramātman</s>, because it is untenable that one whose sole nature is knowledge could be the locus of <s>avidyā</s>.
Therefore, since there are mutually contradictory properties — being a <s>saṃsārin</s> and not being a <s>saṃsārin</s>, possessing <s>vidyā</s> and <s>avidyā</s> — and since there is distinction of cognition and designation, there is indeed a real difference between the <s>jīva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s> — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#And when the identity of the <s>Paramātman</s> and the <s>Kṣetrajña</s> is established#.'
That difference and non-difference cannot both be real in the same locus — this has been elaborated in the first <s>pāda</s>.
And through the censure of the perception of duality, all <s>Vedānta</s> passages, when examined in their sequential connection, are understood as aimed at establishing absolute non-duality.
Therein, just as when a reflection appears in a clear mirror, though the reflections are non-different from the original in reality, yet due to the difference of the substrates — blue gems, swords, glass, and the like — there is a constructed (<s>kālpanika</s>) difference among the reflections, giving rise to distinctions of cognition and designation — 'This original is clear, and these reflections are tinged blue-lotus-dark, and differ in round, long, and other shapes, and are many' — in the same way, though the non-difference of the <s>jīva</s>s from the <s>Paramātman</s>, whose nature is pure, is absolute, yet due to the difference of the conditioning adjuncts (<s>upādhāna</s>) of beginningless <s>avidyā</s>, which is indescribable (<s>anirvacanīya</s>), there is a constructed difference among the <s>jīva</s>s, and the distinctions of cognition and designation [arise] — 'This <s>Paramātman</s> is of the nature of pure consciousness and bliss, and these <s>jīva</s>s are subject to the afflictions of <s>avidyā</s>, sorrow, suffering, and the like.'
And the conditioning adjunct of <s>avidyā</s>, though it does not directly exist in the <s>Paramātman</s> whose nature is knowledge, is nevertheless predicated of the Supreme through the medium of the <s>jīva</s>, which is like a reflection [of the Supreme].
Nor is there mutual dependence (<s>anyonyāśraya</s>) [in this] — the <s>avidyā</s> depending on the distinction of <s>jīva</s>s, and the distinction of <s>jīva</s>s depending on <s>avidyā</s> — because, like the seed and the sprout, it is beginningless.
For this very reason, the objection — 'For whose sake does <s>Īśvara</s> fashion this purposeless <s>māyā</s>, since the <s>jīva</s>s for whom it would be intended do not exist at the beginning of creation; and how could He make Himself a <s>saṃsārin</s> subject to various sufferings?' — is without scope.
For <s>saṃsāra</s> has no beginning, nor does the distinction of <s>jīva</s>s through <s>avidyā</s> have a beginning, such that one could raise this objection.
And here, by mentioning 'name,' [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] indicates <s>avidyā</s> [as well].
Objection: If the <s>jīva</s> is not different from <s>Brahman</s>, then since the <s>jīva</s> is manifest, <s>Brahman</s> too should be manifest; and in that case, '<s>nihitaṃ guhāyām</s>' (hidden in the cave) would not be tenable — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#For indeed, the real#.'
Just as the caves of the mirror-image are gems, swords, and the like, so too the caves of <s>Brahman</s> are the <s>avidyā</s>s that differ for each <s>jīva</s>.
Just as when reflections are manifest, the original, though non-different from them, remains hidden — so too when the <s>jīva</s>s are manifest, <s>Brahman</s>, though non-different from them, remains hidden.
But then let something other than <s>Brahman</s> be hidden — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#And there is nothing other than <s>Brahman</s>#.' '#But those#' — <s>Āśmarathya</s> and the rest — '#who insist, they [deviate from] the meaning of <s>Vedānta</s>#.'
If the transformation of <s>Brahman</s> — whether wholly or partially — is accepted, then since <s>Brahman</s> would be an effect and hence non-eternal, liberation too, which depends on it, would be the same.
But if even so they were to declare liberation to be eternal and uncreated, then [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#By reasoning#.'
Similarly, those who, by the illustration of rivers and ocean, maintain the difference of the <s>jīva</s> in the state of non-liberation and its non-difference in the state of liberation — for them too, the inconsistency is [shown] by reasoning.
A pot never becomes a cloth.
Objection: But it has been said that just as a river becomes the ocean.
But what does the revered one consider to be the 'river'? Is it the water, the atoms, their spatial configuration, or the composite entity constituted by them?
Among these, since the spatial configuration or the composite entity perishes upon entering the ocean, what achieves identity with the ocean?
The water-atoms of the river are simply different from the water-atoms previously existing in the ocean — there is no non-difference.
Likewise, there is only difference of them from the ocean [atoms].
But those who, adopting the <s>Kāśakṛtsna</s> view itself, declared the <s>jīva</s> to be a part (<s>aṃśa</s>) of the <s>Paramātman</s> — how is there no contradiction with the <s>Śruti</s> 'without fruit, without action, tranquil'?
[If they say:] 'without fruit' negates having parts (<s>sāvayavatva</s>) but not having aspects (<s>sāṃśatva</s>), and the <s>jīva</s> is an aspect of the <s>Paramātman</s> like space delimited by the circumference of an ear-cavity is space suitable for hearing sound, and like <s>Prāṇa</s> (vital breath) delimited by the body has five functions — [in response:]
First, space [delimited by the ear-cavity] is not a part of space, because it is identical with it.
If [they say:] that which is delimited by the circumference of the ear-cavity is a part — well then, by the discrimination of what has reached and what has not reached [a place], what is stated is merely the ear-cavity circumference or contact with it.
And the ear-cavity circumference is not a part of space, because it is different from it.

children.translated_text: For impossibility indeed strengthens [the case for] <s>māyā</s>, since <s>māyā</s> by its very nature involves that which cannot be accounted for.

body.translated_text:
If [they say:] the contact with it, being a property of space, is its part — no, because of impossibility.
For if it were a property of space, then since space is without parts and undivided everywhere, that contact would manifest everywhere.
For there is no possibility that something without parts exists without pervading.
Therefore, if it exists there, it exists only as pervading.
And if it does not pervade there, it simply does not exist there.
If [they say:] it exists only as pervading, but because its ascertainment depends on the correlate, it is not ascertained everywhere — [we reply:] let it indeed not be ascertained everywhere.
But the space conjoined with it would be suitable for hearing everywhere, and thus there would be the unwanted consequence of hearing everywhere.
And a part cannot be explained by either difference or non-difference, nor by both, since contradictory [properties] cannot co-exist in a single locus — thus it has been stated.
Therefore, the part of space is merely constructed (<s>kalpita</s>) through beginningless <s>avidyā</s>, which is indescribable (<s>anirvacanīya</s>), and is not real — this is reasonable.
Nor should it be objected: 'How can something constructed, whose existence depends on knowledge alone, exist while not being cognized? And how can a non-existent part serve a function characterized by hearing sound? Surely a snake not cognized in a rope is not sufficient to produce the effect of fear, trembling, and the like' —
because the non-cognition [of it] is not established, since it is revealed by its effects.
If [they ask:] how can what was not cognized prior to the production of the effect serve as a contributing factor to the production of the effect? — no,
because it is revealed by the production of prior effects, and because even in the absence of [present] cognition, the continuation of its impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) persists, and because the stream of that impression-flow and the construction [based on it] are beginningless.
Or, let there indeed be impossibility — because both cause and effect are of the nature of <s>māyā</s>.

'#And [<s>Brahman</s> is] the material cause, because of the non-obstruction of the declaration and the illustration#.'
Objection: Since the reconciliation (<s>samanvaya</s>) of the <s>Vedānta</s> passages in <s>Brahman</s> has been demonstrated, the topic characterized by reconciliation is complete — what further remains for the sake of which this [discussion] is commenced? — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] dispels this doubt by showing the connection and states the remainder: '#Just as the higher good#.'
And here, having stated the connection of the topic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), the connection of this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (section) with the topic is stated.
What is meant is this: truly, the reconciliation of the <s>Vedānta</s> passages has been stated with regard to <s>Brahman</s> as the cause of the universe.
Therein, since causality is seen in two ways, is the causality of <s>Brahman</s> with respect to the universe merely as the efficient cause (<s>nimittakāraṇa</s>), or also as the material cause (<s>upādānakāraṇa</s>)?
If the first view [is adopted], then in tracing the material cause, the <s>Pradhāna</s> established in <s>Sāṃkhya</s> <s>Smṛti</s> would have to be accepted.
And thus the definition of <s>Brahman</s> as 'that from which origination and the rest [of the universe proceed]' would be faulty, because of over-extension (<s>ativyāpti</s>), since it would apply to <s>Pradhāna</s> as well.
Or [the definition would fail] because of impossibility.

This is what [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states: '#As for the efficient cause alone, to begin with#.'
Since scripture concludes merely with [establishing] causality in general, it does not preclude the restriction of that particular [type of causality] by inference; rather, it actually concurs — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#By elimination, something other than <s>Brahman</s>#.'
When the material causality of <s>Brahman</s>, which was under consideration, is negated, [and] since there is no occasion [for material causality] elsewhere, the inferential <s>Pradhāna</s> well-known from <s>Sāṃkhya</s> <s>Smṛti</s> remains as the residue.

Just as by knowing one <s>Somaśarman</s>, all the <s>Kaṭha</s>s are known.
With this prima facie view established, the reply is given: '#And [<s>Brahman</s> is] the material cause (<s>Prakṛti</s>)#.'

But the efficient cause (<s>nimittakāraṇa</s>) is entirely different from the effect, so knowledge of the effect does not arise from knowledge of it. Therefore <s>Brahman</s> is the material cause of the world. <s>Sat</s> (being) and <s>tyat</s> (that) are the two forms of <s>Brahman</s>.
<s>Sat</s> (the existent), being immediately apprehensible through the universal and the particular, is expressible, and has the nature of earth, water, and fire.

But how can that be a form of <s>Brahman</s> unless <s>Brahman</s> is its material cause? Therefore, from transformation, <s>Brahman</s> is the material source (<s>prakṛti</s>) of the elements. //26//

body.translated_text: 1.4.7.26. #From the transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>) of self-creation (<s>ātmakṛti</s>)#. The mention of material cause (<s>prakṛti</s>) is indicative — it should be understood as including the efficient cause (<s>nimitta</s>) as well, since <s>Brahman</s> is the material cause as the object acted upon and the efficient cause as the agent with respect to it. #'But how?'# — Because the coexistence of what is already established and what is to be established in one locus is contradictory. #'We say: because of transformation'# — The meaning is that even what is already established undergoes transformation in the form of an indescribable (<s>anirvacanīya</s>) modification, and because of its indescribability, the modification is as if not different from the original — thus even what is established can be what is to be established.
