children.translated_text: Even by this much, difference is negated; one should not infer real modification (<s>vikāra</s>) merely from the statement of material causality.
For a part of a sentence does not have independent meaning. //27//

body.translated_text: He refutes the inference of the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> (objector) by showing its conflict with scripture — #'As for what is argued'#. What is said amounts to this: <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) is merely the efficient cause of the world, because He creates the world preceded by deliberation (<s>īkṣā</s>), like a potter (<s>kulāla</s>) who makes pots. In this regard, the reason (<s>hetu</s>) suffers from the fallacy of unestablished substratum (<s>āśrayāsiddha</s>) since the existence of <s>Īśvara</s> is not established, and the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>) has an unestablished qualifier. As they say: 'Logic does not operate regarding what is not perceived.' If it be said that the existence of <s>Īśvara</s> is established from scripture (<s>āgama</s>), well then, <s>Īśvara</s> must be accepted exactly as scripture reveals Him — and scripture reveals <s>Īśvara</s> as both the efficient and the material cause. Since the inference contradicts the scripture that grasps the qualified substratum, the inference cannot prevail — so how can there be a restriction to efficient causality alone? This language of material cause, transformation, etc. is not intended in the sense of real modification (<s>vikāra</s>), but rather just as a rope is the material cause of the apparent snake, so <s>Brahman</s> should be understood as the material cause of the world. Indeed, transformation of the eternal, partless <s>Brahman</s> — whether in its entirety or in part — is impossible, because it is eternal and without parts, as has been stated. And the effects of clay such as pots are neither different from it, nor non-different, nor both different and non-different, but are simply indescribable (<s>anirvacanīya</s>).

children.translated_text: It might be objected:

children.text: mā bhūtpradhānaṃ jagadupādānaṃ tathāpi na brahmopādānatvaṃ sidhyati, paramāṇavādīnāmapi tadupādānānāmupaplavamānatvāt, teṣāmapi hi kiñcidupodbalakamasti vaidikaṃ liṅgamityāśaṅkāmapanetumāha sūtrakāraḥ- #etena sarve vyākhyātā vyākhyātāḥ# /
children.translated_text: Let <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) not be the material cause of the world; still, <s>Brahman's</s> being the material cause is not established, since the proponents of atoms (<s>paramāṇuvādins</s>) also maintain atoms as the material cause, and they too have some supporting Vedic indication (<s>liṅga</s>). To remove this doubt, the <s>sūtrakāra</s> says — #'By this, all are explained, explained'#.
The <s>sūtra</s> is explained by the <s>bhāṣya</s> which paraphrases it.

children.text: 'pratijñālakṣaṇaṃ lakṣyamāṇe padasamanvayaḥ vaidikaḥ sa ca tatraiva nānyatretyatra sādhitam //28 //
children.translated_text: 'The Vedic coordination of words (<s>padasamanvaya</s>), when the referent characterized by the proposition (<s>pratijñālakṣaṇa</s>) is being indicated, pertains to that alone and not to anything else — this has been established here.' //28//

body.text: ' iti śrīmadvācaspatimiśraviracite śrīmacchārīrakabhāṣyavibhāge bhāmatyāṃ prathamādhyāyasya caturthaḥ pādaḥ //4 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth <s>pāda</s> (quarter) of the first <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter) in the <s>Bhāmatī</s>, the exposition of the commentary on the <s>Śārīrakabhāṣya</s> (Embodied-Self Commentary), composed by the illustrious <s>Vācaspati Miśra</s>. //4//

body.text: iti prathamādhyāye 'vyaktādisaṃdigdhapadamātrasamanvayākhyaścaturthaḥ pādaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth <s>pāda</s> of the first <s>adhyāya</s>, called 'the coordination of terms whose referents are in doubt beginning with the Unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) and others.'

body.text: iti śrīmadbrahmasūtraśāṅkarabhāṣye samanvayākhyaḥ prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the first <s>adhyāya</s>, called '<s>Samanvaya</s>' (Coordination), of the commentary on the <s>Brahmasūtra</s> by <s>Śaṅkara</s>.

body.text: #atha dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ# /
body.translated_text: #Now begins the second <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter)#.

body.text:
#smṛtyanavakāśadoṣaprasaṅga iti cennānyasmṛtyanavakāśadoṣaprasaṅgāt# /
vṛttavartiṣyamāṇayoḥ samanvayavirodhaparihāralakṣaṇayoḥ saṃgatipradarśanāya sukhagrahaṇasya caitanyoḥ saṃkṣepatastātparyārthamāha- #prathame 'dhyāya iti# /
anapekṣavedāntavākyasvarasasiddhasamanvayalakṣaṇasya virodhatatparihārābhyāmākṣepasamādhānakaraṇādanena lakṣaṇenāsti viṣayaviṣayibhāvaḥ saṃbandhaḥ /
pūrvalakṣaṇārtho hi viṣaśayastadgocaratvādākṣepasamādhānayoreṣa ca viṣayīti /
tadevamadhyāyamavatārya tadavayavamadhikaraṇamavatārayati- #tatra prathamaṃ tāvaditi# /
tantryate vyutpādyate mokṣasādhanamaneneti tantraṃ, tadevākhyā yasyāḥ sā smṛtistantrākhyā paramarṣiṇā kapilenādividuṣā praṇītā /
anyāścāsuripañcaśikhādipraṇītā smṛtayastadanusāriṇyaḥ /
na khalvamūṣāṃ smṛtīnāṃ manvādismṛtivadanyo 'vakāśaḥ śakyo vaditumṛte mokṣasādhanaprakāśanāt /
tadapi cennābhidadhyuranavakāśāḥ satyo 'pramāṇaṃ prasajyeran /
tasmāttadavirodhena kathañcidvedāntā vyākhyātavyāḥ /
pūrvapakṣamākṣipati- #kathaṃ punarīkṣatyādibhya iti# /
prasādhitaṃ khalu dharmamīmāṃsāyāṃ 'virodhe tvanapekṣaṃ syādasati hyanumānam' ityatra, yathā śrutiviruddhānāṃ smṛtīnāṃ durbalatayānapekṣaṇīyatvaṃ tasmānna durbalānurodhena balīyasīnāṃ śrutīnāṃ yuktamupavarṇanam, api tu svataḥsiddhapramāṇabhāvāḥ śrutayo durbalāḥ smṛtīrbādhanta eveti yuktam /
pūrvapakṣī samādhatte- #bhavedayamiti# /
prasādhito 'pyarthaḥ śraddhājaḍānprati punaḥ prasādhyata ityarthaḥ /
āpātataḥ samādhānamuktvā paramasamādhānamāha pūrvapakṣī- #kapilaprabhṛtīnāṃ cārṣamiti# /
ayamasyābhaisaṃdhiḥ-brahma hi śāstrasya kāraṇamuktaṃ 'śāstrayonitvāt' iti, tenaiṣa vedarāśirbrahmaprabhavaḥ sannājānasiddhānāvaraṇabhūtārthamātragocaratabuddhaipūrvako yathā tathā kapilādīnāmapi śrutismṛtiprathitājānasiddhabhāvānāṃ smṛtayo 'nāvaraṇasarvaviṣayatadbuddhiprabhavā iti na śrutibhyo 'mūṣāmasti kaścidviśeṣaḥ /
na caitāḥ sphuṭataraṃ pradhānādipratipādanaparāḥ śakyante 'nmathayitacum /
tasmāttadanurodhena kathañcicchutaya eva netavyāḥ /
api ca tarko 'pi kapilādismṛtiranumanyate, tasmādapyetadeva prāptam /
evaṃ prāpta āha- #tasya samādhiriti# /
yathā hi śrutīnāmavigānaṃ brahmaṇi gatisāmānyāt, naiṣaṃ smṛtīnāmavigānamasti pradhāne, tāsāṃ bhūyasīnāṃ brahmopādānatvapratipādanaparāṇāṃ tatra tatra darśanāt /
tasmādavigānācchraita evārtha āvastheyo na tu smārto vigānāditi /
tatkimidānīṃ parasparavigānātsarvā eva smṛtayo 'vaheyā ityata āha- #vipratipattau ca smṛtīnāmiti /
na cātīndriyārthāniti# /
arvāgdṛgabhiprāyam /
śaṅkate- #śakyaṃ kapilādīnāmiti# /
nirākaroti- #na /
siddherapīti# /
na tāvatkapilādaya īśvaravadājānasiddhāḥ, kintu viniścatavedaprāmāṇyānāṃ teṣāṃ tadanuṣṭhānavatāṃ prāci bhave 'smiñjanmani siddhiḥ, ata evājānasiddhā ucyante /
yadasmin janmani na taiḥ siddhadyupāyo 'nuṣṭhitaḥ prāgbhavī.vedārthānuṣṭhānalabdhajanmatvāttatsiddhīnām /
tathā cāvadhṛtavedaprāmāṇyānāṃ tadviruddhārthābhidhānaṃ tadapabādhitamapramāṇameva /
apramāṇena ca na vedārtho 'tiśaṅkituṃ yuktaḥ pramāṇasiddhatvāttasya /
tadevaṃ vedavirodhe siddhavacanamapramāṇamuktvā siddhānāmapi parasparavirodhe tadvacanādanāścāsa iti pūrvoktaṃ smārayati- #siddhavyapāśrayakalpanāyāmapīti# /
śraddhājaḍānbodhayati- #paratantraprajñasyāpīti# /
nanu śrutiścetkapilādīnāmanāvaraṇabhūtārthagocarajñānātiśayaṃ bodhayati, kathaṃ teṣāṃ vacanamapramāṇaṃ, tadaprāmāṇye śruterapyaprāmāṇyaprasaṅgādityata āha- #yā tu śrutiriti# /
na tāvatsiddhānāṃ parasparaviruddhāni vacāṃsi pramāṇaṃ bhavitumarhanti /
naca vikalpo vastuni, siddhe tadanupapatteḥ /
anuṣṭhānamanāgatotpādyaṃ vikalpyate, na siddham /
tasya vyavasthānāt /
tasmācchutisāmānyamātreṇa bhramaḥ sāṃkhyapraṇetā kapilaḥ śrauta iti /
syādetat /
kapila eva śrauto nānye manvādayaḥ /
tataśca teṣāṃ smṛtiḥ kapilasmṛtiviruddhāvaheyetyata āha- #bhavati cānyā manoriti# /
tasyāścāgamāntarasaṃvādamāha- #mahābhārate 'pi ceti# /
na kevalaṃ manoḥ smṛtiḥ smṛtyantarasaṃvādinī, śrutisaṃvādinyapītyāha- #śrutiśceti# /
upasaṃharati- #ata iti# /
syādetat /
bhavatu vedaviruddhaṃ kāpilaṃ vacastathāpi dvayorapi puruṣabuddhiprabhavatayā ko vinigamanāyāṃ heturyato vedavirodhi kāpilaṃ vaco nādaraṇīyamityata āha- #vedasya hi nirapekṣamiti# /
ayamabhisaṃdhiḥ-satyaṃ śāstrayonirīśvarastathāpyasya na śāstrakriyāyāmasti svātantryaṃ kapilādīnāmiva /
sa hi bhagavān yādṛśaṃ pūrvasmin sarge cakāra śāstraṃ tadanusāreṇāsminnapi sarge praṇītavān /
evaṃ pūrvatarānusāreṇa pūrvasmin pūrvatāmanusāreṇa ca pūrvatara ityanādirayaṃ śāstreśvarayoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ /
tatreśvarasya na śāstrārthajñānapūrvā śāstrakriyā yenāsya kapilādivatsvātantryaṃ bhavati /

children.text: śāstrārthajñānaṃ cāsya svayamāvirbhavadapi na śāstrakāraṇatāmupaiti, dvayorapyaparyāyeṇāvirbhāvāt /
children.translated_text: And His knowledge of scriptural meaning, though manifesting of its own accord, does not attain the status of being the cause of scripture, since both manifest simultaneously without sequence.

children.text: śāstraṃ ca svatobodhakatayā puruṣasvātantryābhāvena nirastamastadoṣāśaṅkaṃ sadanapekṣaṃ sākṣādeva svārthe pramāṇam /
children.translated_text: And scripture, being self-illuminating, free from dependence on human independence, with all suspicion of defect removed, is directly and independently a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) regarding its own subject matter.

children.text: kapilādivacāṃsi tu svatantrakapilādipraṇetṛkāṇi tadarthasmṛtipūrvakāṇi, tadarthasmṛtayaśca tadarthānubhavapūrvāḥ /
children.translated_text: But the statements of <s>Kapila</s> and others have independent authors like <s>Kapila</s>, are preceded by recollection of their meaning, and those recollections are preceded by experience of that meaning.

children.text: tasmāttāsāmarthapratyayāṅgaprāmāṇyaviniścayāya yāvatsmṛtyanubhavau kalpete tāvatsvataḥ siddhapramāṇabhāvayānepakṣayaiva śrutyā svārtho viniścāyita iti śīghratarapravṛttayā śrutyā smṛtyartho bādhyata iti yuktam //1 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, in order to ascertain the validity of those traditions — which is subsidiary to the cognition of their meaning — as far as recollection and experience can establish it, the Vedic meaning is already determined by <s>śruti</s> alone, whose status as a valid means of knowledge is self-established and independent. Thus it is fitting that the meaning of <s>smṛti</s> is overridden by <s>śruti</s>, which operates more swiftly. //1//

body.translated_text: "If there would be the fault of leaving no scope for <s>smṛti</s> (tradition)" — to show the connection between the two topics, namely the resolution of the conflict regarding the harmonization of what has been stated and what is about to be stated, and for easy comprehension, he states the purport in brief — "In the first <s>adhyāya</s>" (chapter). The relationship of object and cognizer consists in the connection between the characteristic of harmonization established independently by the natural purport of <s>Vedānta</s> sentences and the objection and resolution through the removal of conflicts with that. For the content of the former characteristic is the object, and since the objection and resolution pertain to it, this is the cognizer. Having thus introduced the <s>adhyāya</s>, he introduces the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (section), which is a subdivision of it — "There, the first" etc. A <s>tantra</s> is that by which the means of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) is expounded; that itself is the name of that <s>smṛti</s>, hence 'the <s>smṛti</s> named after the <s>tantra</s>' — composed by the supreme sage <s>Kapila</s> and other ancient sages. And other <s>smṛtis</s> composed by <s>Āsuri</s>, <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, and others follow that. Indeed, no other scope can be stated for these <s>smṛtis</s>, unlike the <s>smṛtis</s> of <s>Manu</s> and others, apart from illuminating the means of liberation. If they did not teach even that, they would become without scope and hence non-authoritative. Therefore, the <s>Vedānta</s> texts must somehow be interpreted in a manner not conflicting with them. He raises the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (objection) — "How then, from words like 'deliberates'" etc. It has been established in <s>Dharmamīmāṃsā</s> in the passage 'when there is conflict, it should be disregarded, for in the absence [of śruti], inference [applies]' that <s>smṛtis</s> that conflict with <s>śruti</s> are to be disregarded due to their weakness. Therefore it is not proper to reinterpret the stronger <s>śrutis</s> to accommodate the weaker ones; rather, it is fitting that the <s>śrutis</s>, whose authority as <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) is self-established, simply override the weaker <s>smṛtis</s>. The <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> (objector) responds — "This could be" etc. The meaning is that even an established point is re-established for those whose understanding is dulled by blind faith. Having stated the resolution superficially, the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> gives the ultimate resolution — "The seer-knowledge of <s>Kapila</s> and others" etc. His intention is this: <s>Brahman</s> has been stated to be the source of scripture — 'because of being the source of scripture' — therefore this mass of <s>Vedas</s>, having <s>Brahman</s> as its origin, preceded by cognition that grasps only unobstructed true objects through innate perfected knowledge — just as it is for the <s>Vedas</s>, so too for <s>Kapila</s> and others, whose innate perfected nature is celebrated in both <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>, their <s>smṛtis</s> arise from cognition pertaining to all unobstructed objects. Hence there is no difference between their traditions and the <s>śrutis</s>. And these cannot be easily shaken off, being clearly devoted to establishing <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and the like. Therefore, the <s>śrutis</s> themselves must somehow be led to conform with them. Moreover, reasoning too supports the <s>smṛti</s> of <s>Kapila</s> and others, hence the same conclusion follows from that as well. When the matter stands thus, he says — "The resolution of that" etc. Just as there is unanimity of <s>śrutis</s> regarding <s>Brahman</s> due to the commonality of their purport, there is no such unanimity of these <s>smṛtis</s> regarding <s>pradhāna</s>, since the majority of them, being devoted to establishing <s>Brahman</s> as the material cause, are seen here and there. Therefore, due to unanimity, one should abide by the Vedic meaning alone, not the traditional one, due to disagreement. Then, should all <s>smṛtis</s> be rejected due to mutual disagreement? To this he says — "And when there is conflict among <s>smṛtis</s>" and "Not about supersensory objects" etc. This is from the standpoint of ordinary perception. He raises a doubt — "It is possible for <s>Kapila</s> and others" etc. He refutes — "No, because even of the perfected ones" etc. <s>Kapila</s> and others are not innately perfected like <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord); rather, for those whose certainty in Vedic authority is established, and who practiced accordingly, their perfection came in a previous birth. For this very reason they are called innately perfected — because in this birth they did not practice the means of perfection; their births were obtained through practicing Vedic teachings in former lives. And for those whose certainty in Vedic authority is established, their assertion of meanings contradicting that is itself invalidated and non-authoritative. And it is not proper to cast excessive doubt on Vedic meaning through what is non-authoritative, since that meaning is established by valid means of knowledge. Having thus stated that the words of the perfected ones are non-authoritative when conflicting with the <s>Vedas</s>, and that even among the perfected ones there is mutual conflict in their statements, he reminds of what was said before — "Even when resorting to the assumption of the perfected" etc. He awakens those dulled by faith — "Even for one whose understanding depends on another" etc. Now, if <s>śruti</s> itself reveals the superiority of knowledge — unobstructed cognition of real objects — of <s>Kapila</s> and others, how can their words be non-authoritative? For if their words were non-authoritative, even <s>śruti</s> would become non-authoritative. To this he says — "But that <s>śruti</s>" etc. The mutually contradictory statements of the perfected ones cannot be authoritative. Nor is there optionality regarding an established fact, since that would be impossible for what is already established. Optionality applies to future actions to be performed, not to established facts, because of the fixed nature of the latter. Therefore, it is merely an error arising from a general reference in <s>śruti</s> that <s>Kapila</s>, the founder of <s>Sāṅkhya</s>, is Vedic. One might say: only <s>Kapila</s> is Vedic, not others like <s>Manu</s>. Then their <s>smṛti</s>, conflicting with <s>Kapila</s>'s <s>smṛti</s>, should be rejected. To this he says — "There is also another <s>smṛti</s> of <s>Manu</s>" etc. And he states its agreement with other scriptures — "And in the <s>Mahābhārata</s> also" etc. Not only is <s>Manu</s>'s <s>smṛti</s> in agreement with other <s>smṛtis</s>, but also in agreement with <s>śruti</s> — "And <s>śruti</s>" etc. He concludes — "Therefore" etc. One might say: granted that <s>Kāpila</s> doctrine conflicts with the <s>Vedas</s>, still, since both arise from human cognition, what reason is there for determining that the <s>Kāpila</s> statement conflicting with the <s>Vedas</s> should not be heeded? To this he says — "For the <s>Veda</s> is independent" etc. The intention is this: true, <s>Īśvara</s> is the source of scripture, yet He has no independence in creating scripture, unlike <s>Kapila</s> and others. For the Lord composed scripture in this creation following the pattern of the scripture He made in the previous creation. Thus, following the earlier creation in the previous one, and that following the one before it — this causal relationship between scripture and the Lord is beginningless. In this, the Lord's creation of scripture is not preceded by knowledge of scriptural meaning, whereby He would have independence like <s>Kapila</s> and others.

body.text:
mahadahaṅkārau tāvadaprasiddhau, ahaṅkāraprakṛtikatvena tanmātrāṇyapyaprasiddhāni smartuṃ na śakyanta ityāha- #itareṣāṃ ceti# /
nanu 'mahataḥ paramavyaktam' itiśrutiprasiddhāni mahadādīnītyata āha- #yadapīti# /

children.translated_text: He states the purport of the <s>sūtra</s> — "Because of being effects" etc.

children.text: sāṃkhyasmṛtermahadādiṣviva pradhāne 'pi prāmāṇyaṃ neti niścīyata ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is that it is determined that the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> <s>smṛti</s> has no authority regarding <s>pradhāna</s>, just as it has none regarding <s>mahat</s> and the rest.

children.text: sāṃkhyasmṛterbādhe 'pi taduktayuktīnāṃ kathaṃ bādha cārṣajñānamatra mūlamupapadyata iti yuktam /
children.translated_text: Even when the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> <s>smṛti</s> is overridden, how can the reasoning stated therein be overridden? The seer-knowledge that is its foundation is well-established — thus it is reasonable to ask.

children.text: tasmānna kāpilasmṛteḥ pradhānopādānatvaṃ jagata iti siddham //2 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that <s>pradhāna</s> is not the material cause of the world according to <s>Kāpila</s> <s>smṛti</s>. //2//

body.translated_text: <s>Mahat</s> (the Great One) and <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle) are not well-known to begin with; and since the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) are described as having <s>ahaṅkāra</s> as their source, they too cannot be well-known enough to be remembered — thus he says "Of the others" etc. Now, one might object that <s>mahat</s> and the rest are well-known through <s>śruti</s> such as 'beyond the <s>mahat</s> is the unmanifest' — to this he says "Even that which" etc.

body.text:
#etena yogaḥ pratyuktaḥ# /
nānena yogaśāstrasya hairaṇyagarbhapātañjalādeḥ sarvathā prāmāṇyaṃ nirākriyate, kintu jagadupādānasvatantrapradhānatadvikāramahadahaṅkārapañcatanmātragocaraṃ prāmāṇyaṃ nāstītyucyate /
na caitāvataiṣāmaprāmāṇyaṃ bhavitumarhati /
yatparāṇi hi tāni tatrāprāmāṇye 'prāmāṇyamaśruvīran /
na caitāni pradhānādisadbhāvaparāṇi /
kintu yogasvarūpatatsādhanatadavāntaraphalavibhūtitatparamaphalakaivalyavyutpādanaparāṇi /
tacca kiñcinnimittīkṛtya vyutpādyamiti pradhānaṃ savikāraṃ nimittīkṛtaṃ, purāṇeṣviva sargapratisargavaṃśamanvantaravaṃśānucaritaṃ tatpratipādanapareṣu, na tu tadvivakṣitam /
anyaparādapi cānyanimittaṃ tatpratīyamānamabhyupeyeta, yadi na mānāntareṇa virudhyate /

children.translated_text: But it has been stated that this conflicts with <s>Vedānta</s> <s>śrutis</s>.
Therefore, even from the <s>Yoga</s> scripture, which is itself authoritative, the existence of <s>pradhāna</s> and the like is not established.

children.text: ata eva yogaśāstraṃ vyutpādayitāha sma bhagavān vārṣagaṇyaḥ-'guṇānāṃ paramaṃ rūpaṃ na dṛṣṭipathamṛcchati /
children.translated_text: For this very reason, the venerable <s>Vārṣagaṇya</s>, while expounding <s>Yoga</s> scripture, has said: 'The supreme form of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) does not come within the range of sight.
But that which comes within the range of sight is mere <s>māyā</s> (illusion), quite insignificant.'

body.translated_text: "By this, <s>Yoga</s> is also refuted." By this, the authority of the <s>Yoga</s> scripture — that of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, <s>Patañjali</s>, and others — is not rejected in every respect. Rather, it is said that it has no authority regarding an independent <s>pradhāna</s> as the material cause of the world and its modifications — <s>mahat</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, and the five <s>tanmātras</s>. Nor should this amount to their complete non-authority. For those texts, being directed toward other purposes, would lose authority only if their authority regarding that primary purpose were denied. And these are not primarily devoted to establishing the existence of <s>pradhāna</s> and the like. Rather, they are devoted to expounding the nature of <s>yoga</s>, its means, its intermediate fruits — the <s>vibhūtis</s> (supernatural powers) — and its ultimate fruit, <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation). And that exposition employs something as an occasion; thus <s>pradhāna</s> with its modifications is used merely as an occasion, just as in the <s>Purāṇas</s> — which are devoted to teaching creation, dissolution, dynasties, <s>Manvantaras</s>, and dynastic chronicles — yet those topics are not their primary intent. Even what is incidentally conveyed while a text is primarily directed elsewhere should be accepted, provided it does not conflict with another valid means of knowledge.

body.text:
' iti /
yogaṃ vyutpipādayiṣatā nimittamātreṇeha guṇā uktāḥ, na tu bhāvataḥ, teṣāmatāttvikatvādityarthaḥ /
alokasiddhānāmapi pradhānādīnāmanādipūrvapakṣanyāyābhāsotprekṣitānāmanuvādyatvamupapannam /
tadanenābhisaṃdhināha- #etena sāṃkhyasmṛtipratyākhyānena yogasmṛtirapi#pradhānādiviṣayatayā #pratyākhyātā draṣṭavyeti# /
adhikaraṇāntarārambhamākṣipati- #nanvevaṃ sati samānanyāyatvāditi# /
samādhatte #-astyatrābhyadhikāśaṅkā# /
mā nāma sāṃkhyaśāstrātpradhānasattā vijñāyi /
yogaśāstrāttu pradhānādisattā vijñāpayiṣyate bahulaṃ hi yogaśāstrāṇāṃ vedena saha saṃvādo dṛśyate /
upaniṣadupāyasya ca tattvajñānasya yogāpekṣāsti /
na jātu yogaśāstravihitaṃ yamaniyamādibahiraṅgamupāyamapahāyāntaraṅgaṃ ca dhāraṇādikamantareṇaupaniṣadātmatattvasākṣātkāra udetumarhati /
tasmādaupaniṣadena tattvajñānenāpakṣaṇāt saṃvādabāhulyācca vedenāṣṭakādismṛtivadyogasmṛtiḥ pramāṇam /
tataśca pramāṇātpradhānādipratīternāśabdatvam /

children.text: naca tadapramāṇaṃ pradhānādau, pramāṇaṃ ca yamādāviti yuktam /
children.translated_text: And it is not reasonable to say that it is non-authoritative regarding <s>pradhāna</s> and the like, but authoritative regarding <s>yama</s> and the rest.
Because if it were non-authoritative in the former, there would be no confidence in it regarding the latter either.

children.text: yathāhuḥ-'prasaraṃ na labhante hi yāvatkkacana markaṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: As they say: 'As long as even a few monkeys do not find their range,
the demons do not rush forth into their own domain.'

body.translated_text: Thus. The <s>guṇas</s> are mentioned here merely as an occasion by one wishing to expound <s>yoga</s>, not in their true reality, since they are not ultimately real — this is the meaning. Even for <s>pradhāna</s> and the like, which are not established in common experience, their being merely restated — having been speculatively posited through semblances of reasoning in the manner of beginningless <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> — is appropriate. With this intention he says — "By this rejection of <s>Sāṅkhya</s> <s>smṛti</s>, the <s>Yoga</s> <s>smṛti</s> too" should be regarded as "rejected insofar as it pertains to <s>pradhāna</s> and the like." He raises the occasion for beginning a new <s>adhikaraṇa</s> — "But if this is so, since the reasoning is the same" etc. He resolves — "There is here an additional apprehension." Let the existence of <s>pradhāna</s> not be known from <s>Sāṅkhya</s> scripture. But from <s>Yoga</s> scripture, the existence of <s>pradhāna</s> and the like will be made known, for the agreement of <s>Yoga</s> scriptures with the <s>Veda</s> is abundantly observed. And the knowledge of reality that is the <s>Upaniṣadic</s> means requires <s>yoga</s>. Surely, the direct realization of the <s>Ātman</s>-reality of the <s>Upaniṣads</s> cannot arise without the external means prescribed in <s>Yoga</s> scripture — <s>yama</s> (restraints), <s>niyama</s> (observances), and the rest — and without the internal means of <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) and the like. Therefore, since <s>Upaniṣadic</s> knowledge of reality depends on it, and because of the abundance of agreement with the <s>Veda</s>, <s>Yoga</s> <s>smṛti</s> is authoritative like the <s>smṛtis</s> concerning the <s>aṣṭaka</s> rites and the like. And since it is authoritative, the cognition of <s>pradhāna</s> and the like derived from it would not be unscriptural.

body.text:
' iti /
seyaṃ labdhaprasarā pradhānādau yogāpramāṇatāpiśācī sarvatraiva durvārā bhavedityasyāḥ prasaraṃ niṣedhatā pradhānādyabhyupeyamiti nāśabdaṃ pradhānamiti śaṅkārthaḥ /
sā #iyamapyadhikāśaṅkātirdeśena nivartyate# /
nivṛttihetumāha- #arthaikadeśasaṃpratipattāvapīti# /
yadi pradhānādisattāparaṃ yogaśāstraṃ bhavet, bhavetpratyakṣavedāntaśrutivirodhenāpramāṇam /
tathā ca tadvihiteṣu yamādiṣvapyanāśvāsaḥ syāt /
tasmānna pradhānādiparaṃ tat, kintu tannimittīkṛtya yogavyutpādanaparamityuktam /
na cāviṣaye 'prāmāṇyaṃ viṣaye 'pi prāmāṇyamupahanti /
nahi cakṣū rasādāvapramāṇaṃ rūpe 'pyapramāṇaṃ bhavitumarhati /
tasmādvedāntaśrutivirodhātprādhānādirasyāviṣayo na tvaprāmāṇyamiti paramārthaḥ /
syādetat /
adhyātmaviṣayāḥ santi sahasraṃ smṛtayo bauddhārhatakāpālikādīnāṃ, tā api kasmānna nirākriyanta ityata āha- #satīṣvapīti# /
tāsu khalu bahulaṃ vedārthavisaṃvādinīṣu śiṣṭānādṛtāsu kaiścideva tu puruṣāpasadaiḥ paśuprāyairmlecchādibiḥ parigṛhītāsu vedamūlatvāśaṅkaiva nāstīti na nirākṛtāḥ, tadviparītāstu sāṃkhyayogasmṛtaya iti tāḥ pradhānādiparatayā vyudasyanta ityarthaḥ /
#na sāṃkhyajñānena vedanirapekṣeṇeti# /
pradhānādiviṣayeṇetyarthaḥ /
#dvaitino hi te sāṃkhyā yogāśca# /
ye pradhānādiparatayā tacchāstraṃ vyācakṣata ityarthaḥ /
sāṃkhyā samyagbuddhirvaidikī tayā vartanta iti sāṃkhyāḥ /
evaṃ yogo dhyānaṃ upāyopeyayorabhedavivakṣayā /
cittavṛttinirodho hi yogastasyopāyo dhyānaṃ pratyayaikānatā /

children.translated_text: And this is merely illustrative.

children.text: anye 'pi yamaniyamādayo bāhyā āntarāśca dhāraṇādayo yogopāyā draṣṭavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Other external aids of <s>Yoga</s> such as <s>yama</s> (restraint), <s>niyama</s> (observance), etc., and internal ones such as <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), etc., should also be understood [as means of <s>Yoga</s>].

By this, the interpretation extends to all the reasonings and traditions of <s>Kaṇabhakṣa</s> (i.e., <s>Kaṇāda</s>), <s>Akṣacaraṇa</s> (i.e., <s>Gautama</s>), and others who accept the authority of the <s>Veda</s>.
The rest is easy to understand. //3//

body.translated_text: Thus ends [the previous discussion]. This demon of the invalidity of <s>Yoga</s> as a means of knowledge, having gained ground with respect to <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and similar doctrines, would become irresistible everywhere — the purpose of the objection is to suggest that <s>Pradhāna</s> is a doctrine not established by a valid means of knowledge, by negating its spread. This additional objection is also refuted by the indication of a further objection. He states the reason for the refutation: 'even upon the partial comprehension of the meaning.' If the <s>Yoga</s> scripture were exclusively devoted to establishing the existence of <s>Pradhāna</s> and such entities, it would indeed be invalid due to its contradiction with direct perception and <s>Vedānta</s> <s>śruti</s> (scripture). And in that case, there would be no confidence even in the <s>yamas</s> (restraints) and other practices prescribed therein. Therefore, that scripture is not devoted to <s>Pradhāna</s> and similar doctrines, but rather its purpose is to teach <s>Yoga</s> by taking those as its occasion — this has been stated. And invalidity in one domain does not undermine validity in another domain. For the eye, which is not a valid means of knowledge regarding taste and similar qualities, cannot thereby become invalid regarding form as well. Therefore, the ultimate meaning is that <s>Pradhāna</s> and similar doctrines are outside the scope of this [<s>Yoga</s> scripture] due to their contradiction with <s>Vedānta</s> <s>śruti</s>, but it is not that [the scripture] lacks validity altogether. One might object: there are thousands of <s>smṛtis</s> (remembered traditions) of the Buddhists, Jains, <s>Kāpālikas</s>, and others dealing with spiritual matters — why are those not refuted as well? To this he says: 'even though they exist.' Since those are largely in conflict with the meaning of the <s>Veda</s>, are disregarded by the learned, and are adopted only by certain degraded persons, those who are little better than animals, <s>Mlecchas</s> (barbarians) and such — there is not even the suspicion that they are rooted in the <s>Veda</s>, so they are not [formally] refuted. But the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s> <s>smṛtis</s>, being the opposite of those, are rejected insofar as they teach <s>Pradhāna</s> and similar doctrines — this is the meaning. 'Not by <s>Sāṃkhya</s> knowledge independent of the <s>Veda</s>' — meaning, [not by knowledge] having <s>Pradhāna</s> and similar doctrines as its object. 'For those <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> and <s>Yogins</s> are dualists' — meaning, those who interpret that scripture as devoted to <s>Pradhāna</s> and similar doctrines. <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> are so called because they conduct themselves according to <s>sāṃkhyā</s>, i.e., correct Vedic understanding. Likewise, <s>yoga</s> means meditation, with the intention of non-difference between means and end. For <s>yoga</s> is the cessation of the modifications of the mind, and its means is meditation, the one-pointedness of cognition.

body.text:
na vilakṣaṇatvādasya tathātvaṃ ca śabdāt /
avāntarasaṃgatimāha- #brahmāsya jagato nimittakāraṇaṃ prakṛtiścetyasya pakṣasyeti# /
codayati- #kutaḥ punariti# /
samānaviṣayatve hi virodho bhavet /

children.translated_text: And there is no identity of subject matter here, because <s>Brahman</s>, which possesses attributes, being beyond the scope of other means of knowledge, is not amenable to reasoning and is accessible solely through scripture — this is the meaning.
He resolves [the objection]: 'this would be [the case].'
'Let <s>dharma</s> (duty), which is beyond the scope of other means of knowledge and which pertains to established reality,
be [beyond reasoning] because of its nature as something to be accomplished; but <s>Brahman</s>, being an established [entity], is within its scope.'

body.translated_text: 'Not, because of dissimilarity; and its being so, from scripture.' He states the internal connection: 'that <s>Brahman</s> is the efficient cause and the material cause of this world — of this position.' He raises the objection: 'from what [basis], then?' For contradiction would arise only if they have the same subject matter.

body.text:
' tasmātsamānaviṣayatvādastyatra tarkasyāvakāśaḥ /
nanvastu virodhaḥ, tathāpi tarkādare ko heturityata āha- #yathā ca śrutīnāmiti# /
sāvakāśā vahvayo 'pi śrutayo 'navakāśaikaśrutivirodhe tadanuguṇatayā yathā nīyante evamanavakāśaikatarkavirodhe tadanuguṇatayā bahvayo 'pi śrutayo guṇakalpanādibhirvyākhyānamarhantītyarthaḥ /
api ca brahmasākṣātkāro virodhitayānādimavidyāṃ nivartayan dṛṣṭenaiva rūpeṇa mokṣasādhanamiṣyate /

children.text: tatra brahmasākṣātkārasya mokṣasādhanatayā pradhānasyānumānaṃ dṛṣṭasādharmyeṇādṛṣṭaviṣayaṃ viṣayato 'ntaraṅgaṃ, bahiraṅgaṃ tvatyantaparokṣagocaraṃ śābdaṃ jñānaṃ, tena pradhānapratyāsattyāpyanumānameva balīya ityāha- #dṛṣṭasādharmyeṇa ceti# /
children.translated_text: There, since the direct realization of <s>Brahman</s> is the means to <s>mokṣa</s>, inference regarding <s>Pradhāna</s>, which pertains to the unseen on the basis of similarity with the seen, is more proximate in subject matter, while scriptural knowledge, which deals with what is entirely remote, is more distal. Therefore, even through the proximity of <s>Pradhāna</s> [to experience], inference alone is stronger — thus he says: 'and through similarity with the seen.'

children.text: api ca śrutyāpi brahmaṇi tarka ādṛta ityāha- #śrutiriti# /
children.translated_text: Moreover, even by scripture, reasoning is valued with respect to <s>Brahman</s> — thus he says: 'scripture [itself].'

children.text: so 'yaṃ brahmaṇo jagadupādānatvākṣepaḥ punastarkeṇa prastūyate-'prakṛtyā ca śrutyāpi vikārāṇāmavasthitam /
children.translated_text: This objection against <s>Brahman</s> being the material cause of the world is now taken up again through reasoning: 'By the nature [of things] and even by scripture, the permanence of the modifications [is established];

children.text: jagadbrahmasarūpaṃ ca neti no tasya vikriyā //
children.translated_text: the world is of the same form as <s>Brahman</s>, and therefore there is no transformation of it.'

body.translated_text: Therefore, because of the identity of subject matter, there is scope for reasoning here. Even if there is no [actual] contradiction, what reason is there for regarding reasoning [as relevant]? To this he says: 'and just as the <s>śrutis</s> (scriptures)...' Just as many scriptures that have [independent] scope are interpreted in conformity with a single scripture that has no [alternative] scope when there is a conflict, so too when there is a conflict with a single reasoning that has no [alternative] scope, even many scriptures deserve to be interpreted through subsidiary interpretation and the like in conformity with that reasoning — this is the meaning. Moreover, the direct realization of <s>Brahman</s>, by dispelling beginningless <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) that stands in opposition, is accepted as a means to <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) through its very manifest nature.

children.translated_text: '<s>Brahman</s> is pure and conscious; the world is insentient and partakes of impurity.
Therefore, because of its similarity to <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter), it is <s>Pradhāna</s> alone that undergoes transformation.'

body.text:
' tathāhi-eka eva strīkāyaḥ sukhaduḥkhamohātmakatayā patyuśca sapartnānāṃ ca caitrasya ca straiṇasya tāmavindato 'paryāyaṃ sukhaduḥkhaviṣādānādhatte /
striyā ca sarve bhāvā vyākhyātāḥ /
tasmātsukhaduḥkhamohātmatayā ca svarganarakādyuccāvacaprapañcatayā ca jagadaśuddhamacetanaṃ ca, brahma tu cetanaṃ viśuddhaṃ ca, niratiśayatvāt /
tasmātpradhānasyāśuddhasyācetanasya vikāro jaganna tu brahmaṇa iti yuktam /
ye tu cetanabrahmavikāratayā jagaccaitanyamāhustānpratyāha- #acetanaṃ cedaṃ jagaditi# /
vyabhicāraṃ codayati-nanu cetanamapīti /
pariharati- #na svāmibhṛtyayorapīti# /
nanu mā nāma sākṣāccetanaścetanāntarasyopakāṣīnt, tatkāryakaraṇabuddhyādiniyogadvāreṇa tūpakariṣyatītyata āha- #niratiśayā hyakartāraścetanā iti# /
upajanāpāyavaddharmayogo 'tiśayaḥ, tadabhāvo niratiśayatvam /
ata eva nirvyāpāratvādakartāraḥ /
tasmātteṣāṃ buddhyādiprayoktṛtvamapi nāstītyarthaḥ /
codako 'nuśayabījamuddhāṭayati- #yopīti# /
abhyupetyāpātataḥ samādhānamāha- #tenāpi kathañciditi# /

children.text: paramasādhānaṃ tu sūtrāvayavena vaktuṃ tamevāvatārayati- #na cetaradapi vilakṣaṇatvamiti# /
children.translated_text: But the definitive resolution is to be stated through a portion of the <s>sūtra</s> (aphorism), and to that end he introduces it: 'and the dissimilarity of the other as well.'
He states the purport of the portion of the <s>sūtra</s>: 'for this, which is not apprehended [otherwise].'

children.text: śabdārthāt khalu cetanaprakṛtitvāccaitanyaṃ pṛthivyādīnāmavagamyamānamupodvalitaṃ mānāntareṇa sākṣācchūyamāṇamapyacaitanyamanyathayet /
children.translated_text: The consciousness of earth and other [elements], which is being apprehended from the meaning of the word, i.e., from the fact that <s>Brahman</s> is a conscious source, even though it is being directly heard through another means of knowledge and is thus corroborated, would [not] be otherwise construed as unconsciousness.

children.text: mānāntarābhāve vārthor'thaḥ śrutyarthenāpabādhanīyaḥ, na tu tadbalena śrutyartho 'nyathayitavya ityarthaḥ //4 //
children.translated_text: In the absence of another means of knowledge, the meaning [derived from reasoning] should be overridden by the meaning of scripture, but the meaning of scripture should not be distorted by the force of that [reasoning] — this is the meaning. //4//

body.translated_text: For example: a single woman's body, being of the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion, brings pleasure, pain, and despondency in alternation to the husband, to co-wives, and to <s>Caitra</s> who is enamored of her. And all states are explained through the woman [metaphor]. Therefore, the world, being of the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion, and being the varied manifestation of heaven, hell, and other high and low [states], is impure and insentient; but <s>Brahman</s> is conscious and pure, because of its unsurpassable nature. Therefore it is reasonable that the world is a transformation of the impure, insentient <s>Pradhāna</s>, and not of <s>Brahman</s>. To those who maintain that the world possesses consciousness because it is a transformation of conscious <s>Brahman</s>, he replies: 'this world is insentient.' He raises the counter-instance: 'but is it not also conscious?' He resolves it: 'not even as between master and servant.' But even if a conscious being does not directly benefit another conscious being, it would do so through the employment of body, senses, intellect, and the like — to this he says: 'for conscious beings are unsurpassable and non-agents.' The possession of qualities that arise and perish constitutes surpassability; the absence of that is unsurpassability. And precisely for this reason, being without activity, they are non-agents. Therefore, they do not even have the capacity to direct the intellect and other [instruments] — this is the meaning. The objector uncovers the seed of the latent impression: 'whoever.' He offers a provisional resolution on the surface: 'even by that, somehow.'

body.text:
sūtrāntaramavatārayituṃ codayati- #nanu cetanatvamapi kkacidapi# /
na pṛthivyādīnāṃ caitanyamāthameva, kintu bhūyasīnāṃ śrutīnāṃ sākṣādevārtha ityarthaḥ /
sūtramavatārayati- #ata uttaraṃ paṭhati-abhimānivyapadeśastu viśeṣānugatibhyām# /
vibhajate- #tuśabda iti# /
naitāḥ śrutayaḥ sākṣānmṛdādīnāṃ vāgādīnāṃ ca caitanyamāhuḥ, api tu tadadhiṣṭhātrīṇāṃ devatānāṃ cidātmanāṃ, tenaitacchutibalena na mṛdādīnāṃ vāgādīnāṃ ca caitanyamāśaṅkanīyamiti /
kasmātpunaretadevamityata āha- #viśeṣānugatibhyām# /
tatra viśeṣaṃ vyācaṣṭe- #viśeṣo hīti# /
bhoktṛṇāmupakāryatvādbhūtendriyāṇāṃ copakāratvāt sāmye ca tadanupapatteḥ sarvajanaprasiddheśca 'vijñānaṃ cābhavat' iti śruteśca viśeṣaścetanācetanalakṣaṇaḥ prāguktaḥ sa nopapadyeta /
devatāśabdakṛto vātra viśeṣo viśeṣaśabdenocyata ityāha- #api ca kauṣītakinaḥ prāṇasaṃvāda iti# /
anugatiṃ vyācaṣṭe- #anugatāśceti# /
sarvatra bhūtendriyādiṣvanugatā devatā abhimāninīrūpadiśanti mantrādayaḥ /
api ca bhūyasyaḥ śrutayaḥ 'agnirvāg bhūtvā mukhaṃ prāviśadvāyuḥ prāṇo bhūtvā nāsike prāviśadādityaścakṣurbhūtvākṣiṇī prāviśat' ityādaya indriyaviśeṣagatā devatā darśayanti /
devatāśca kṣetrajñabhedāścetanāḥ /
tasmānnendriyādīnāṃ caitanyaṃ rūpata iti /

children.text: api ca prāṇasaṃvādavākyaśeṣe prāṇānāmasmadādiśarīrāṇāmiva kṣetrajñādhiṣṭhitānāṃ vyavahāraṃ darśayan prāṇānāṃ kṣetrajñādhiṣṭhānena caitanyaṃ draḍhayatītyāha- #prāṇasaṃvādavākyaśeṣe ceti /
children.translated_text: Moreover, in the continuation of the passage on the debate of the <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths), by showing the activity of the <s>prāṇas</s> as presided over by <s>kṣetrajñas</s> (knowers of the field), just like our bodies, he strengthens [the view] that the consciousness of the <s>prāṇas</s> is due to the presiding <s>kṣetrajña</s> — thus he says: 'and in the continuation of the passage on the debate of the <s>prāṇas</s>.'
'That <s>tejas</s> (fire/light) saw' — this too [is cited].

children.text: yadyapi prathame 'dhyāye māktatvena varṇitaṃ tathāpi mukhyatayāpi kathañcinnetuṃ śakyamiti draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: Although in the first chapter this was described as figurative, it should be understood that it can somehow be taken in the primary sense as well.
He concludes the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view): 'therefore.' //5//

body.translated_text: In order to introduce another <s>sūtra</s>, he raises an objection: 'but consciousness too, in some cases.' The consciousness of earth and other [elements] is not merely inferred, but is rather the direct meaning of numerous scriptures — this is the meaning. He introduces the <s>sūtra</s>: 'therefore the next [<s>sūtra</s>] is read — the designation of one possessing self-awareness, because of the particular and the general.' He divides [the <s>sūtra</s>]: 'the word tu (but).' These scriptures do not directly attribute consciousness to earth and other [elements] or to speech and other [faculties], but rather to the deities who preside over them, who are of the nature of consciousness. Therefore, on the strength of these scriptures, consciousness should not be suspected of earth and other [elements] or of speech and other [faculties]. Why is it to be understood thus? To this he says: 'because of the particular and the general.' There he explains 'the particular': 'for the particular.' Because the enjoyers are to be served, and because the elements and senses serve them, and because in a state of equality [between them] this would be impossible, and because of universal recognition, and because of the scripture 'and consciousness came into being,' the particular consisting in the distinction between sentient and insentient, mentioned earlier, would not hold. Or, the particular referred to by the word 'particular' is the distinction made by the word 'deity' — thus he says: 'moreover, the <s>Kauṣītakins</s>' debate of the <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths).' He explains 'the general': 'and the general [application].' Mantras and other [texts] indicate that deities, as presiding entities, pervade all elements, senses, and the like everywhere. Moreover, numerous scriptures such as '<s>Agni</s> (Fire), becoming speech, entered the mouth; <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind), becoming breath, entered the nostrils; <s>Āditya</s> (Sun), becoming sight, entered the eyes' and so on, show deities associated with particular senses. And the deities are conscious beings, being distinct <s>kṣetrajñas</s> (knowers of the field). Therefore, the consciousness does not belong to the senses and the like in their own nature.

body.text:
siddhāntasūtram- #dṛśyate tu# /
prakṛtivikārabhāve hetuṃ sārūpyaṃ vikalpa dūṣayati- #vilakṣaṇatvena ca kāraṇeneti# /
sarvasvabhāvānanuvartanaṃ prakṛtivikārabhāvāvirodhi /
tadanuvartane tādātmyena prakṛtivikārabhāvābhāvāt /
myamastvasiddhaḥ /
tṛtīyastu nidarśanābhāvādasādhāraṇa ityarthaḥ /
atha jagadyonitayāgamādbrahmaṇo 'vagamādāgamabādhitaviṣayatvamanumānasya kasmānnodbhāvyata ityata āha- #āgamavirodhastviti# /
na cāsminnāgamaikasamadhigamanīye brahmaṇi pramāṇāntarasyāvakāśo 'sti, yena tadupāyāgama ākṣipyetetyāśayavānāha- #yattūktaṃ pariniṣpannatvādbrahmaṇīti# /
yathā hi kāryatvāviśeṣa'pi 'ārogyakāmaḥ pathyamaśrīyāt' 'svarakāmaḥ sikatāṃ bhakṣayet' ityādīnāṃ mānāntarāpekṣatā, na tu 'darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeta' ityādīnām /
tatkasya hetoḥ /
asya kāryabhedasya pramāṇāntarāgocaratvāt /
evaṃbhūtatvāviśeṣe 'pi pṛthivyādīnāṃ mānāntaragocaratvaṃ, na tu bhūtasyāpi brahmaṇaḥ, tasmāmnāyaikagocarasyātipatitasamastamānāntarasīmatayā smṛtyāgamasiddhatvādityarthaḥ /
yadi smṛtyāgamasiddhaṃ brahmaṇastarkāviṣayatvaṃ, kathaṃ tarhi śravaṇātiriktamananavidhānamityata āha- #yadapi śravaṇavyatirekeṇeti# /
tarko hi pramāṇaviṣayavivecakatayā taditikartavyatābhūtastadāśrayo 'sati pramāṇe 'nugrāhyasyāśrayasyābhāvācchuṣkatayā nādriyate /
yastvāgamapramāṇāśrayastadviṣayavivecakastadavirodhī sa mantavya iti vidhīyate /
#śrutyanugṛhīteti# /
śrutyāḥ śravaṇasya paścāditikartavyatātvena gṛhītaḥ /
#anubhavāṅgatveneti# /
mato hi bhāvyamāno bhāvanāyā viṣayatayānubhūto bhavatīti mananamanubhavāṅgam /
#ātmano 'nanvāgatatvamiti# /
svapnādyavasthābhirasaṃpṛktatvam /
udāsīnatvamityarthaḥ /
api ca cetanakāraṇavādibhiḥ kāraṇasālakṣaṇye 'pi kāryasya kathañciccaitanyāvirbhāvānāvirbhāvābhyāṃ vijñānaṃ cāvijñānaṃ cābhavaditi jagatkāraṇe yojayituṃ śakyam /
acetanapradhānakāraṇavādināṃ tu duryojametat /
nahyacetanasya jagatkāraṇasya vijñānarūpatā saṃbhavinī /
cetanasya jagatkāraṇasya suṣuptādyavyavasthāsviva sato 'pi caitanyasthānāvirbhāvatayā śakyameva kathañcidavijñānātmatvaṃ yojayitumityāha- #yo 'pi cetanakāraṇaśravaṇabaleneti# /

children.translated_text: This would not be tenable only for the other [opponent], namely, the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> who advocates an insentient <s>pradhāna</s> as the cause.
#The dissimilarity has already been refuted#.
This was stated by conceding [for the sake of argument] that there is no cause-effect relation where there is dissimilarity.
But in ultimate truth, this is not conceded by us — such is the meaning. //6//

body.translated_text: The <s>siddhānta</s> (conclusion) <s>sūtra</s>: 'but it is seen.' He refutes the option of similarity as a reason for the relationship of material cause and effect: 'and by a cause that is dissimilar.' Not following all characteristics [of the cause] is not incompatible with the relationship of material cause and effect. For if [the effect] followed [all characteristics], there would be identity, and hence the absence of the material cause-effect relationship. The middle [term] however is unestablished. And the third [reason] is uncommon due to the absence of an example — this is the meaning. Now, since <s>Brahman</s> is known from scripture as the source of the world, why should it not be pointed out that inference has its domain overridden by scripture? To this he says: 'but the contradiction with scripture.' And there is no scope for any other means of knowledge regarding this <s>Brahman</s> that is knowable by scripture alone, such that scripture, which is the means to it, could be challenged — with this intention he says: 'as to what was said, that <s>Brahman</s> is fully established.' Just as, despite the general nature of being something to be accomplished, statements like 'one who desires health should eat wholesome food' and 'one who desires a good voice should eat sand' require other means of knowledge, but statements like 'one who desires heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new and full moon rites)' do not — for what reason? Because this particular effect is not within the scope of any other means of knowledge. Similarly, despite the general nature of being an established entity, earth and other [elements] are within the scope of other means of knowledge, but <s>Brahman</s>, even though existent, is not, because it is accessible solely through scripture, having transcended the limits of all other means of knowledge — the meaning is that [its inaccessibility to reasoning is established] from tradition and scripture. If the inaccessibility of <s>Brahman</s> to reasoning is established from tradition and scripture, then how is the injunction of <s>manana</s> (reflection), which is distinct from <s>śravaṇa</s> (hearing), [to be explained]? To this he says: 'as to the [injunction] distinct from hearing.' For reasoning, in its capacity of discriminating the subject matter of a valid means of knowledge, being ancillary to that [means], depends on it; in the absence of a valid means of knowledge, the substrate to be supported is absent, and so [reasoning], being dry [i.e., groundless], is not valued. But that [reasoning] which is based on the valid means of scriptural knowledge, which discriminates its subject matter and is not in conflict with it — that is enjoined as what is to be reflected upon. 'Supported by scripture' — [this means reasoning that is] taken up as the ancillary procedure following upon hearing, i.e., scripture. 'As an accessory to experience' — for what is reflected upon becomes experienced as the object of meditation, and thus reflection is an accessory to [direct] experience. 'The non-association of the self' — meaning its non-involvement with states such as dream and the like; meaning its detachment. Moreover, even those who hold the doctrine of a conscious cause can reconcile [the scripture] 'there was consciousness and non-consciousness' with the cause of the world through the occasional manifestation and non-manifestation of consciousness, despite the dissimilarity of the effect from the cause. But for those who hold the doctrine of an insentient <s>Pradhāna</s> as the cause, this is difficult to reconcile. For it is not possible for an insentient cause of the world to have the nature of consciousness. But for a conscious cause of the world, just as in states like deep sleep where [consciousness] exists but is not manifest, it is quite possible to reconcile its nature as non-consciousness somehow — thus he says: 'whoever, on the strength of hearing that the cause is conscious.'

body.text:
#asaditi cenna pratiṣedhamātratvāt# /
na kāraṇātkāryamabhinnam, abhede kāryatvānupapatteḥ, kāraṇavatsvātmani vṛttivirodhāt, śuddhyaśudadhyādiviruddhadharmasaṃsargācca /
atha cidātmanaḥ kāraṇasya jagataḥ kāryādbhedaḥ, tathā cedaṃ jagatkāryaṃ sattve 'pi cidātmanaḥ kāraṇasya prāgutpatternāsti, nāsti cedasadutpadyata iti satkāryavādavyākopa ityāha- #yadi cetanaṃ śuddhamiti# /
pariharati- #naiṣa doṣa iti# /
kutaḥ, #pratiṣedhamātratvāt# /
vibhajate- #pratiṣedhamātraṃ hīdamiti# /
pratipādayiṣyati hi 'tadananyatvamārambhaṇaśabdādibhyaḥ' ityatra /

children.translated_text: Just as the effect, in its own essential nature, is indeterminable as either existent or non-existent,

children.text: api tu kāraṇarūpeṇa śakyaṃ sattvena nirvaktumiti /
children.translated_text: but can be determined as existent in the form of the cause —

children.text: evaṃ ca kāraṇasattaiva kāryasya sattā na tato 'nyeti kathaṃ tadutpatteḥ prāk sati kāraṇe bhavatyasat /
children.translated_text: and thus the existence of the effect is nothing other than the existence of the cause — how then, prior to its origination, when the cause exists, can it be non-existent?

children.text: svarūpeṇa tūtpatteḥ prāgutpannasya dhvastasya vā sadasattvābhyāmanirvācyasya na sato 'sato votpattiriti nirviṣayaḥ satkāryavādapratiṣedha ityarthaḥ //7 //
children.translated_text: But in its own essential nature, prior to origination, the effect — whether unmanifested or dissolved — being indeterminable as either existent or non-existent, the origination is neither of something existent nor of something non-existent; therefore the refutation of <s>satkāryavāda</s> is without a subject — such is the meaning. //7//

body.translated_text: #If [you say] it is non-existent, [we say] no, because [our position] is mere negation#. The effect is not non-different from the cause, because if there were non-difference, the status of being an effect would be impossible, because like the cause there would be a contradiction of activity upon its own self, and because of the association of contradictory properties such as purity and impurity. If, on the other hand, there is difference of the conscious cause from the world as its effect, then this world-effect, even while the conscious cause exists, does not exist prior to origination, and if it does not exist, then what is non-existent is produced — thus the doctrine of <s>satkāryavāda</s> (pre-existence of the effect) would be undermined. To this he says — #If the conscious [<s>Brahman</s>] is pure#. He resolves this — #This is not a fault#. Why? #Because it is mere negation#. He elaborates — #For this is mere negation#. He will establish this in the [sūtra] 'Its non-difference, from the words "origin" and so forth' (<s>tadananyatvam ārambhaṇa-śabdādibhyaḥ</s>).

body.text:
apītau tadvatprasaṅgādasamañjasam /
asāmañjasyaṃ vibhajate- #atrāha#codakaḥ, #yadi sthaulyeti# /
yathā hi yūṣādiṣu hiṅgisaindhavādīnāmavibhāgalakṣaṇo layaḥ svagatarasādibhiryūṣaṃ rūṣayatyevaṃ brahmaṇi viśuddhyādidharmiṇi jagalliyamānamavibhāgaṃ gacchadbrahma svadharmeṇa rūṣayet /
na cānyathā layo lokasidda iti bhāvaḥ /
kalpāntareṇāsāmañjasyamāha- #api ca samastasyeti# /
nahi samudrasya phenormibudbudādipariṇāmo vā rajjvāṃ sarpadhārādivibhrame vā niyamo dṛṣṭaḥ /
samudro hi kadācitphenormikūpeṇa pariṇāmate kadācidbudbudādinā, rajjvāṃhi kaścitsarpa iti viparyasyati kaściddhāreti /

children.translated_text: And there is no fixed sequential order.
Thus, this fixed order of the divisions of objects of experience and the fixed sequential order are incoherent [on the <s>Advaita</s> view].
He states the incoherence through another alternative — #Moreover, of the experiencers#.
He states the alternative formulation prefaced by an objection — 'Now if this...' //8//

body.translated_text: At dissolution, there would be the same undesirable consequence — [therefore] it is incoherent. He elaborates the incoherence — #Here the objector says#, #If grossness [of the world]#. Just as in broths and similar preparations, the absorption (<s>laya</s>) of <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt), and the like, characterized by non-distinction, corrupts the broth with its own flavors, similarly the world, being dissolved into <s>Brahman</s> which possesses the property of purity and the like, entering into non-distinction, would corrupt <s>Brahman</s> with its own properties. And dissolution is not established in the world in any other way — such is the purport. He states the incoherence through an alternative formulation — #Moreover, of the entire [world]#. For neither in the transformation of the ocean into foam, waves, and bubbles, nor in the illusion of a snake or a stream upon a rope, is any fixed order observed. The ocean sometimes transforms in the form of foam and waves, sometimes in the form of bubbles and so forth; upon a rope, one person erroneously perceives a snake, another perceives a stream.

body.text:
siddhāntasūtram- #na tu dṛṣṭāntabhāvāt# /
nāvibhāgamātraṃ layo 'pi tu kāraṇe kāryasyāvibhāgaḥ /
tatra ca taddharmārūṣaṇe santi sahasraṃ dṛṣṭāntāḥ /
tava tu kāraṇe kāryasya laye kāryadharmarūṣaṇe na dṛṣṭāntalavo 'pyastītyarthaḥ /
syādetat yadi kāryasyāvibhāgaḥ kāraṇe, kathaṃ kāryadharmārūṣaṇaṃ kāraṇasyetyata āha- #ananyatve 'pīti# /
yathā rajatasyāropitasya pāramārthikaṃ rūpaṃ śukti4na ca śuktī rajatameva midamapītyarthaḥ /
api ca sthityutpattipralayakāleṣu triṣvapi kāryasya kāraṇādabhedamabhidadhatī śrutiranatiśaṅkanīyā sarvaireva vedavādibhiḥ, tatra sthityutpattyoryaḥ parihāraḥ sa pralaye 'pi samānaḥ kāryasyāvidyāsamāropitatvaṃ nāma, tasmānnāpītimātramanuyojyamityāha- #atyalpaṃ cedamucyata iti /
asti cāyamaparo dṛṣṭāntaḥ /
yathā ca svapnadṛgeka iti# /
laukikaḥ puruṣaḥ /
evamavasthātrayasākṣyeka iti /
avasthātrayamutpattisthitipralayāḥ /

children.translated_text: He states the resolution of the incoherence raised through the alternative formulation, by means of the existence of illustrations — #Now, as to what was said further#.
Because the power of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is determinate, there is a determinate order of creation — such is the meaning.
#By this#.

children.text: mithyājñānavibhāgaśaktipratiniyamena muktānāṃ punarutpattiprasaṅgaḥ pratyuktaḥ, kāraṇābhāve kāryābhāvasya pratiniyamāt, tattvajñānena ca saśaktino mithyājñānasya samūlaghātaṃ nihatatvāditi //9 //
children.translated_text: By the determinacy of the power of differentiation belonging to false knowledge, the objection regarding the re-emergence of those who are liberated is refuted, because in the absence of the cause there is necessarily the absence of the effect, and because false knowledge along with its power has been uprooted by the knowledge of reality. //9//

body.translated_text: The <s>siddhānta</s> (conclusion) sūtra — #But no, because of the existence of illustrations#. Dissolution is not mere non-distinction, but rather the non-distinction of the effect in the cause. And for the non-corruption [of the cause] by the properties [of the effect] in that [state], there are a thousand illustrations. But for your [<s>Sāṃkhya</s>] position — the corruption [of the cause] by the properties of the effect upon the dissolution of the effect in the cause — there is not even the slightest illustration. This is the meaning. [To the objection:] It might be said — if there is non-distinction of the effect in the cause, how is there non-corruption of the cause by the properties of the effect? To this he says — #Even though there is non-difference#. Just as the apparent form of the superimposed silver is in reality the mother-of-pearl, and the mother-of-pearl is not the silver itself — such is the meaning. Moreover, the <s>śruti</s> (scripture), which declares the non-difference of the effect from the cause in all three times — creation, subsistence, and dissolution — is not to be doubted by any of the <s>Vedavādins</s> (proponents of the <s>Veda</s>). The same resolution that applies to subsistence and creation applies equally to dissolution — namely, that the effect is superimposed through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). Therefore, mere dissolution is not a ground for objection. He says — #Too little is said here#. And there is this further illustration — #Just as a single dreamer# — means an ordinary person. Similarly, a single witness of the three states — the three states being creation, subsistence, and dissolution.

body.text: #svapakṣadoṣācca# /

children.translated_text: The dissimilarity between cause and effect is equally common to both positions.

children.text: prāgutpatterasatkāryavadaprasaṅgo 'pītau tadvatprasaṅgaśca pradhānopādānapakṣa eva nāsmatpakṣa iti yadyapyupariṣṭātpratipādayiṣyāmastathāpi guḍajihvikayā samānatvāpādanamidānīmiti mantavyam /
children.translated_text: The undesirable consequence of <s>asatkāryavāda</s> (the doctrine of the non-pre-existence of the effect) prior to origination, and the same undesirable consequence at dissolution — these apply only to the position of <s>pradhāna</s> as the material cause, not to our position. Although we shall establish this later, nevertheless the present [argument] aims to show the equivalence [of the objection] by way of a <s>guḍajihvikā</s> (retort of equal applicability) — so it should be understood.
This is the ground of pleasure and pain for this person — <s>kleśa</s> (affliction), <s>karma</s> (action), <s>āśaya</s> (latent impression), and the rest — this belongs to this [person].
The rest is easy to understand. //10//

body.translated_text: #And because of the defects in the opponent's own position#.

body.text: #tarkāpratiṣṭhānādapi# /

children.text: kevalāgamagamyer'the svatantratarkāviṣaye na sāṃkhyādivat sādharmyadharmyamātreṇa tarkaḥ pravartanīyo yena pradhānādisiddhirbhavet /
children.translated_text: In matters that are to be known solely through scripture, which are not within the scope of independent reasoning, one should not employ reasoning based merely on similarity and dissimilarity as the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and others do, by which [reasoning] the establishment of <s>pradhāna</s> and the like would follow.
For such reasoning would be dry [groundless], because it has no firm foundation.
As it has been said: 'An object inferred even with effort by skilled reasoners
is demonstrated to be otherwise by others who are more skilled.'

body.translated_text: #Also because reasoning has no firm foundation#.

body.text:
' iti /
naca mahāpuruṣaparigṛhītatvena kasyacittarkasya pratiṣṭhā, mahāpuruṣāṇāmeva tārkikāṇāṃ mitho vipratipatteriti /
sūtre śaṅkate-anyathānumeyamiti cet /
tadvibhajate- #anyathā vayamanumāsyāmaha iti# /
nānumānābhāsavyabhicāreṇānumānavyabhicāraḥ śaṅkanīyaḥ, pratyakṣādiṣvapi tadābhāsavyabhicāreṇa tatprasaṅgāt /
tasmāt svābhāvikapratibandhavalliṅgānusaraṇe nipuṇenānumātrā bhavitavyaṃ, tataścāpratyūhaṃ pradhānaṃ setsyatīti bhāvaḥ /
api ca yena tarkeṇa tarkāṇāmapratiṣṭhāmāha sa eva tarkaḥ pratiṣṭhito 'bhyupeyaḥ, tadapratiṣṭhāyāmitarāpratiṣṭhānābhāvādityāha- #nahi pratiṣṭhitastarka eveti# /
api ca tarkāpratiṣṭhāyāṃ sapalalokayātrocchedaprasaṅgaḥ /
naca śrutyarthābhāsasanirākaraṇena tadarthatattvaviniścaya ityāha-sarvatarkāpratiṣṭhāyāṃ ceti /
api ca vicārātmakastarkastarkitapūrvapakṣaparityāgena tarkitaṃ rāddhāntamanujānāti /
sati caiṣa pūrvapakṣaviṣaye tarke pratiṣṭhārahite pravartate, tadabhāve vicārapravṛtteḥ /
tadidamāha- #ayameva ca tarkasyālaṅkāra iti# /
tāmimāmāśaṅkāṃ sūtreṇa pariharati-evamapyavimokṣaprasaṅgaḥ /
na vayamanyatra tarkapramāṇayāmaḥ, kintu jagatkāraṇasattve svābhāvikapratibandhavanna liṅgamasti /
yattu sādharmyavaidharmyamātraṃ, tadapratiṣṭhādoṣānna mucyata iti /
kalpāntareṇānirmokṣapadārthamāha- #api ca sāmyagjñānānmokṣa iti# /

children.text: bhūtārthagocarasya hi samyagjñānasya vyavasthitavastugocaratayā vyavasthānaṃ loke dṛṣṭaṃ, yathā pratyakṣasya /
children.translated_text: For it is seen in the world that right knowledge, which has a real object, is stable because it has a well-established object as its content — just like perception.

children.text: vaidikaṃ cedaṃ cetanajagadupādānaviṣayaṃ vijñānaṃ vedotthatarketikartavyatākaṃ vedajanitaṃ vyavasthitam /
children.translated_text: And this Vedic knowledge, having the conscious [<s>Brahman</s>] as the material cause of the world as its object, requiring reasoning that follows from the <s>Veda</s>, generated by the <s>Veda</s>, is well-established.

children.text: vedānapekṣeṇa tu tarkeṇa jagatkāraṇabhedamavasthāpayatāṃ tārkikāṇāmanyonyaṃ vipratipattestattvanirdhāraṇakāraṇābhāvācca na tatastattvavyavastheti na tataḥ samyagjñānam /
children.translated_text: But for logicians who seek to establish the diversity of the world's cause through reasoning independent of the <s>Veda</s>, because of their mutual disagreement and because of the absence of a means to ascertain the truth, there is no establishment of truth from that [reasoning], and therefore no right knowledge.
And from the absence of right knowledge, there is no liberation from <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth) — such is the meaning. //11//

body.translated_text: And no reasoning attains firm establishment merely because it is accepted by great men, since the great men who are logicians themselves mutually disagree. In the sūtra, [the opponent] raises a doubt — 'If it is to be inferred otherwise.' He elaborates this — #We shall infer otherwise#. One should not suspect invalidity of inference because of the invalidity of pseudo-inferences, since in the case of perception and other [means of knowledge] too, the same undesirable consequence would follow from the invalidity of their semblances. Therefore, one must be a skilled inferrer who follows the inferential mark possessing a natural invariable concomitance, and then <s>pradhāna</s> will be established without obstruction — such is the purport. Moreover, the very reasoning by which one declares that all reasoning lacks firm foundation — that very reasoning must be accepted as firmly established, for if that [reasoning] too lacked firm foundation, there would be no absence of firm foundation of the others. To this he says — #For no firmly established reasoning itself#. Moreover, if all reasoning lacked firm foundation, there would be the undesirable consequence of the destruction of all worldly activity along with its fruits. And it is not the case that the ascertainment of the true meaning of scripture consists merely in the refutation of the apparent meaning of scripture. He says — #And if all reasoning lacked firm foundation#. Moreover, reasoning in the form of deliberation, by abandoning the examined prior position (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>), accepts the examined established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>). And when this [reasoning] in the form of a prior position is present, it operates without firm foundation; in the absence of that [prior position], deliberation would not proceed. This he states — #And this is the very ornament of reasoning#. With the sūtra he resolves this doubt — 'Even so, there would be the consequence of non-liberation.' We do not validate reasoning elsewhere [outside of scripture]; rather, there is no inferential mark possessing a natural invariable concomitance for the existence of [any specific] cause of the world. But what is mere similarity and dissimilarity — that does not escape the defect of lacking firm foundation. He states the meaning of non-liberation through another alternative — #Moreover, liberation from right knowledge#.

children.translated_text: Where even the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> reasoning, which to some extent follows the <s>Veda</s> and is accepted by the learned such as <s>Manu</s> and others, meets such a fate, what then can be said of the doctrine of <s>paramāṇu</s> (atoms) and the like, which is entirely outside the <s>Veda</s> and disregarded by <s>Manu</s> and others?
#In some respect#.

children.text: sṛṣṭyādayo hi vyutpādyāste na kiñcitsadasadvā pūrvapakṣanyāyotprekṣitamapyudāhṛtya vyutpādyanta iti kenacidaṃśenetyuktam /
children.translated_text: For creation and the like are to be taught, and they are taught by citing [arguments] that are sometimes imagined according to the method of the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prior position), whether existent or non-existent — hence it is said 'in some respect.'
The rest is easy to understand. //12//

body.translated_text: #By this, the [systems] not accepted by the learned are also explained#. The effect is not non-different from the cause, because if there were non-difference, the status of being an effect would be impossible, as it would have the nature of the cause, and because the meaning of 'making' would be impossible. For the meaning of that [making] is bringing into being what did not previously exist. And if it has the nature of the cause, there is nothing that did not previously exist, for the sake of which a person would make effort. If [you say] it is for the purpose of manifestation — no, because that [manifestation] too, having the nature of the cause, already exists; or if it does not exist, by the same undesirable consequence applying to what is to be manifested, the nature-of-cause thesis would be contradicted. For it is not tenable that the very same thing at the very same time both exists and does not exist. What is this — a jewel, a mantra, a herb, or a magic show trained by the effect — that this [thing], possessing unsurpassed unobstructed proximity, is sometimes perceptible and sometimes imperceptible to that very person with those very sense faculties? [By which] its apprehension is sometimes through perception, sometimes through inference, sometimes through scripture. If [you say] the obstruction by other effects is the cause of its imperceptibility — no, because the entire class of effects is eternally existent. And if one were to say that other effects such as sherds, gravel, powder, and particles constitute the pot, and therefore the pot is sometimes imperceptible — that is not so, because since the entire class of effects, having the nature of the cause, is eternally existent, there would always be obstruction, and the pot would be absolutely never perceived. Or if the class of effects is only occasional, it would not have the nature of the cause, because the association of contradictory properties characterized as permanence and impermanence is a differentiator. And it has been said that difference and non-difference, being mutually contradictory, cannot coexist in one thing. Therefore, the effect is absolutely different from the cause. And it is not proper [to say] that if there is difference, the cause-effect relation would be impossible as between a cow and a horse, because it has already been said that even in the case of non-difference, that [relation] is impossible as [the effect] would have the nature of the cause. And in absolute difference, we see the relation of efficient cause between a potter and his pot. Therefore, even though there is no distinction in otherness, it is difference in <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) alone that is the ground for the fixed relation of material cause and material effect. [According to the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>,] those things that come into being from <s>samavāya</s> have a smaller magnitude than cloths and other [products]. But from the supreme, great, conscious material cause, the material effect cannot be extremely small in magnitude. Therefore, that in which this [process of division] rests when it reaches its smallest point, beyond which nothing smaller is possible — that is the root cause of the world, namely, the <s>paramāṇu</s> (atom). The <s>śruti</s>, which declares the world-effect to be smaller than the cause, because it contradicts reasoning whose authority is established, should be interpreted in some secondary sense, like the <s>śruti</s> about the year that has gone to the thousand-year sacrifice. To the one who raises this further objection, he extends the refutation of <s>Sāṃkhya</s> — #By this# — through the sūtra. Its meaning is: We shall refute the difference of the effect from the cause in the [sūtra] 'Its non-difference, from the words "origin" and so forth.' And we shall disregard the greater or lesser magnitude of the effect, by [showing] its superimposition through <s>avidyā</s>, as it is non-consequential. Therefore, since the reasoning accepted by the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> and others is dry [groundless], being without firm foundation — this sūtra extends the refutation of <s>Sāṃkhya</s> [to them as well].

#yathā tvadyatva iti# /
body.translated_text:
'#Because of the objection of the experiencer, and because of non-differentiation — as in the world#.'
Objection: the scope of reasoning does not extend to the profoundly deep subject of the cause of the universe; it has been stated that this is to be known solely through scripture — then how can an objection based on reasoning be raised? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Although <s>Śruti</s> is the authority#.'
For <s>Śruti</s>, having commenced independently and being self-evidently authoritative, does not depend on any other means of knowledge.
But once it has commenced, when it encounters a contradiction from reasoning that is more clearly and firmly established in its authority, it is deflected from its primary meaning and led to a secondary meaning — just as in the case of <s>mantra</s>s and <s>arthavāda</s>s — this is the meaning.
The <s>Bhāṣya</s> has a concealed purport.
'#Just as, however, of the present day#' — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s> comments].
