tasmādākāśavajjīvātmāna utpadyanta iti prāpta ucyate-bhavedevaṃ yadi jīvā brahmaṇo bhidyeran /

children.translated_text: But this is not the case.

Because of the scriptural statements of non-difference such as 'Having created it, it entered into that very thing' and 'Through this individual soul,' and because the difference is due to limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>), the association of contradictory attributes is feasible, just as in the case of the spaces in a pot, a jar, and the like.

children.text: upādhīnā ca manomaya ityādīnāṃ śruterbhūyasīnaṃ ca nityatvājatvādigocarāṇāṃ śrutīnāṃ darśanāt 'upādhipravilayenopahitasya' iti ca praśnottarābhyāmanekadhopapādanādavibhāgasya ca 'eko devaḥ sarvabhūteṣu gūḍhaḥ' iti śrutyaivoktatvānnityā jīvātmano na vikārā na cādvaitapratijñāvirodha iti siddham /
children.translated_text: And because of the scriptural mention of the limiting adjuncts such as 'made of mind' and the like, and because of the observation of more numerous scriptures dealing with eternality, non-origination, and the like, and because of the multiple demonstrations through questions and answers that 'through the dissolution of the limiting adjuncts, that which was conditioned,' and because non-difference itself has been stated by scripture — 'The one God hidden in all beings' — the individual souls are eternal, not modifications, and there is no conflict with the promise of non-duality — thus it is established.
And the <s>Maitreyī Brāhmaṇa</s> has been explained below, and hence is not explained here. //17//

body.translated_text: Let there not be gross origination and destruction for this soul through the rise and fall of the body; but perhaps, like space and the like, at the time of the great creation and at its end, origination and destruction may occur for the individual soul — to remove this further doubt, this section is commenced. 'Not the self, because of the scriptural declaration of its eternality, and from those.' He states the seed of the doubt that is the basis of the inquiry: 'Because of the conflict among scriptures.' He shows that very conflict: 'In certain scriptures.' He takes up the prima facie view: 'In that case, it is established.' First, regarding the supreme self (<s>paramātman</s>), the individual souls are different because of the association of contradictory attributes — being tainted and untainted by evil, and the like. And if they are not modifications, then their being a separate ontological category would conflict with the more numerous scriptures of non-duality. And there would be conflict with the promise that through knowing <s>Brahman</s> everything becomes known. Therefore, the weight of scripture favors their being modifications. And the other means of knowledge has been stated here: because they are differentiated, like space and the like. And the scripture 'As from a fire, tiny sparks' directly shows the individual souls to be modifications of <s>Brahman</s>. And 'As from a blazing fire' directly shows the origination of individual souls from <s>Brahman</s> and their dissolution into it. But one might say that the origination and dissolution from the imperishable are understood for things, not for individual souls — to this he says: 'Of the individual souls.' One might object: in the scriptures about creation, why is the origination of individual souls not mentioned, just as the origination of space and the like is? Therefore, since what is fit to be mentioned is not mentioned, we should understand the absence of origination — to this he says: 'And nowhere is there non-mention.' For otherwise, a ritual that is mentioned in one branch of the <s>Veda</s> together with certain subsidiary elements would not have the subsidiary elements of another branch incorporated into it. Therefore, due to conflict with the more numerous scriptures, the scripture about entering must be explained through the figurative interpretation of modification. Therefore, just as space, the individual souls originate — such is the prima facie view. The conclusion is: this would be so if the individual souls were different from <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text:
#jño 'ta eva# /
karmaṇā hi jānātyartho vyāptastadabhāve na bhavati dhūma iva dhūmadhvajābhāve, suṣuptyādyavasthāsu ca jñeyasyābhāvāttadvyāpyasya jñānasyābhāvaḥ /
tathāca nātmasvabhāvaścaitanyaṃ tadanuvṛttāvapi caitanyasya vyāvṛttiḥ /
tasmādindriyādibhāvābhāvānuvidhānāt jñānabhāvābhāvayorindriyādisaṃnikarṣādheyamāgantukamasya caitanyaṃ dharmo na svābhāvikaḥ /
ata evendriyādīnāmarthavattvam, itarathā vaiyarthyamindriyāṇāṃ bhavet /
nityacaitanyaśrutayaśca śaktyabhiprāyeṇa vyākhyeyāḥ /
asti hi jñānotpādanaśaktirnijā jīvānāṃ, na tu vyomna ivendriyādisaṃnikarṣe 'pyeṣā jñānaṃ na bhavatīti /
tasmājjaḍā eva jīvā iti prāpte 'bhidhīyate-yadāgantukajñānaṃ jaḍasvabhāvaṃ tatkadacit parokṣaṃ kadācit saṃdigdhaṃ kadācidviparyastaṃ, yathā ghaṭādi, na caivamātmanā /
tathāhi-anumimāno 'pyaparokṣaḥ, smarannapyānubhavikaḥ, saṃdihāno 'pyasaṃdigdhaḥ, viparyasyannapyaviparītaḥ sarvasyātmā /
tathāca tatsvabhāvaḥ /
naca tatsvabhāvasya caitanyasyābhāvaḥ, tasya nityatvāt /

children.translated_text: Therefore, the mental modifications (<s>vṛtti</s>), which are of the nature of action, cease in deep sleep and the like when there is no object of action.
Thus it is established that consciousness is the intrinsic nature of the self.

children.text: tathāca nityacaitanyavādinyaḥ śrutayo na kathañcit kleśena vyākhyātavyā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: And thus the scriptures declaring eternal consciousness need not be explained away with any difficulty.
And the sense organs have their purpose in the arising of the modifications pertaining to smell and other objects — thus everything is clear. //18//

body.translated_text: 'The knower, for that very reason.' For the meaning 'knows' is pervaded by action; in its absence, it does not exist, like smoke in the absence of fire. And in states such as deep sleep and the like, due to the absence of the knowable, there is the absence of knowledge which is pervaded by it. And thus consciousness is not the intrinsic nature of the self, for even when the self continues, consciousness ceases. Therefore, since the presence and absence of knowledge conform to the presence and absence of sense organs and the like, consciousness is an adventitious attribute bestowed by the contact with sense organs and the like, not an intrinsic one. Hence the purposefulness of the sense organs and the like; otherwise the sense organs would be purposeless. And the scriptures declaring eternal consciousness should be explained with reference to potentiality (<s>śakti</s>). For the individual souls have an innate capacity to produce knowledge, but unlike space, this capacity produces knowledge upon contact with sense organs and the like, while space does not — such is the prima facie view. The conclusion is: that which has adventitious knowledge and an inert nature is sometimes mediate, sometimes doubtful, sometimes erroneous, like a pot and the like; but the self is not like this. For even when inferring, the self is immediate; even when remembering, it is experiential; even when doubting, it is undoubted; even when in error, it is unerring — the self of all. And thus consciousness is its intrinsic nature. And there is no absence of consciousness which is its intrinsic nature, since it is eternal.

body.text:
2.3.13.19.
#utkrāntigatyāgatīnām# /
yadyapyavikṛtasyaiva paramātmano jīvabhāvastathā cānaṇuparimāṇatvaṃ, tathāpyutkrāntigatyāgatīnāṃ śruteśca sākṣādaṇuparimāṇaśravaṇasya cāvirodhārthamidamadhikaraṇamityākṣepasamādhānābhyāmāha- #nanu ceti# /

children.translated_text: He takes up the prima facie view: 'In that case, it is first established that —'
For separation and conjunction-production are the result of departure and the like.
And these do not exist for that which is all-pervading.

children.text: sarvatra nityaprāptasya vā sarvātmakasya vā tadasaṃbhāvāditi //19 //
children.translated_text: Because these are impossible for that which is eternally present everywhere, or for that which is the self of all. //19//

body.translated_text: 2.3.13.19. 'Of departure, going, and returning.' Although the individual soul's status is that of the supreme self itself unmodified, and thus it has no atomic dimension, nevertheless this section is for the purpose of showing the non-contradiction of the scriptures about departure, going, and returning, and the direct scriptural mention of atomic dimension — thus he states through objection and resolution: 'But is it not so?'

body.text:
#svātmanā cottarayoḥ# /
utkramaṇaṃ hi maraṇe nirūḍham /
taccācalato 'pi tatra sato dehasvāmyanivṛttyopapadyate na tu gatyāgatī /
tayoścalane nirūḍhayoḥ kartṛsthabhāvayorvyāpinyasaṃbhavāditi madhyamaṃ parimāṇaṃ mahattvaṃ śarīrasyaiva /
taccārhataparīkṣāyāṃ pratyuktam /
gatyāgatī ca paramanahati na saṃbhavato 'ta pāriśeṣyādaṇutvasiddhiḥ /
gatyāgatibhyāṃ ca prādeśikatvasiddhau maraṇamapi dehādapasarpaṇameva jīvasya na tu tatra sataḥ svāmyanivṛttimātramiti siddhamityāha- #satyośca gatyāgatyoriti# /
itaśca dehādapasarpaṇameva jīvasya maraṇamityāha- #dehapradeśānāmiti# /
tasmādgatyāgatyapekṣotkrāntirapi sāpādānāṇutvasādhanamityarthaḥ /
na kevalamapādānaśruteḥ,
body.translated_text: 'And by its own self, in the case of the latter two.' For departure is well-known in the context of death. And this is feasible even for something that does not move, being present there, through the mere cessation of the ownership of the body — but going and returning are not so feasible. Since going and returning, which are well-known as involving movement and residing in the agent, are impossible for an all-pervading entity, a medium dimension, namely the magnitude of the body itself, would be appropriate. But that has been refuted in the examination of the <s>Jaina</s> view. And going and returning are impossible for what is supremely small — therefore, by elimination, the proof of atomic dimension is established. And when atomic dimension is established through going and returning, death too is the actual departure of the individual soul from the body, not merely the cessation of ownership while remaining there — thus it is established, as he says: 'And when going and returning exist.' And for this further reason, death is indeed the departure of the individual soul from the body, he says: 'Of the parts of the body.' Therefore, departure too, which presupposes going and returning, establishes atomic dimension through its basis — this is the meaning. Not only from the basis of scripture,

body.text: taccharīrapradeśāntavyatvaśruterapyevamevetyāha- #sa etāstejomātrā iti# //20 //
body.translated_text: but also from the scriptural statement about its being limited to the extent of the parts of the body, he says the same: 'These are the luminous essences.' //20//

body.text:
#nāṇuratacchuteriti cennetarādhikārāt# /
yata utkrāntyādiśrutibhirjīvānāmaṇutvaṃ prasādhitaṃ tato vyāpakātparamātmanasteṣāṃ tadvikāratayā bhedaḥ /

children.text: tathāca mahattvānanyādiśrutayaḥ paramātmaviṣayā na jīvaviṣayā ityavirodha ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus the scriptures about greatness, non-otherness, and the like pertain to the supreme self, not to the individual soul — this is the meaning of non-contradiction.

children.text: yadi jīvā aṇavastato 'yo 'yaṃ vijñānamayaḥ parameṣu' iti kathaṃ śārīro mahattvasaṃbandhitvena pratinirdiśyate iti codayati- #nanviti# /
children.translated_text: If the individual souls are atomic, then how is the embodied soul indicated in connection with greatness in 'this one who is made of knowledge, among the vital breaths' — this he raises as an objection: 'But is it not —'
He resolves it: 'From the standpoint of scripture' — that is, from the ultimate standpoint, the designation is like that of <s>Vāmadeva</s>.

children.text: yathā hi garbhastha eva vāmadevo jīvaḥ paramārthadṛṣṭyātmano brahmatvaṃ pratipede, evaṃ vikārāṇāṃ prakṛtervāstavādabhedāttatparimāṇatvavyapadeśa ityarthaḥ //21 //
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Vāmadeva</s>, the <s>jīva</s>, while still in the womb, realized through the ultimate viewpoint the <s>Brahman</s>-nature of his self, so too — because modifications (<s>vikāra</s>s) are not really different from their cause (<s>prakṛti</s>) — the designation as being of the same measure [as <s>Brahman</s>] [is appropriate] — this is the meaning. //21//

body.translated_text: 'Not atomic, because of the scripture declaring otherwise — if this be said, no, because the other topic is intended.' Since the atomic dimension of the individual souls has been established through the scriptures about departure and the like, their difference from the all-pervading supreme self is established through their being modifications of it.

body.text: #svaśabdonmānābhyāṃ ca# /

children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] analyzes 'its own word' (<s>svaśabda</s>): 'Directly, indeed' (<s>sākṣād eva</s>).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] analyzes 'measure' (<s>unmāna</s>): 'Likewise, the measure too.'

children.text: uddhṛtya mānamunmānaṃ bālāgrāduddhṛtaḥ śatatamo bhāgastasmādapi śatatamāduddhṛtaḥ śatatamo bhāga iti tadidamunmānam /
children.translated_text: 'Measure' (<s>unmāna</s>) means an extracted measurement: 'The hundredth part extracted from the tip of a hair, and the hundredth part extracted from the hundredth part of that' — this is the measure.
A measurement extracted from the tip of an awl — 'merely the size of an awl-tip' — thus. //22//

body.translated_text: 'And from its own [scriptural] word and from the measure (<s>unmāna</s>)' [BS 2.3.22].

children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises an objection in order to introduce another <s>sūtra</s>: 'But if it is partless...' (<s>nanu aguṇatve sati</s>).

children.text: aṇurātmā na śarīravyāpīti na sarvāṅgīṇaśaityopalabdhiḥ syādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: if the self (<s>ātman</s>) is atomic and does not pervade the body, then the experience of cold throughout all limbs would not be possible.
'There is no contradiction, as with sandalwood' [BS 2.3.23].

children.text: tvaksaṃyukto hi jīvaḥ tvakca sakalaśarīravyāpinīti tvagvyāpyātmasaṃbandhaḥ sakalaśaityopalabdhau samartha ityarthaḥ //23 //
children.translated_text: For the <s>jīva</s> is connected with the skin, and the skin pervades the entire body — hence the connection of the self, through the pervading skin, is capable [of accounting for] the experience of cold throughout all limbs — this is the meaning. //23//

body.text:
#avasthitivaiśeṣyāditi cennābhyupagamāddhṛdi hi# /
candanabindoḥ pratyakṣato 'lpīyastvaṃ buddhvā yuktā kalpanā bhavati, yasya tu saṃdigdhamaṇutvaṃ sarvāṅgīṇaṃ ca kāryamupalabhyate tasya vyāpitvamautsargikamapahāya neyaṃ kalpanāvakāśaṃ labhata iti śaṅkārthaḥ /
naca haricandanabindudṛṣṭāntenāṇatvānumānaṃ jīvasya,
body.translated_text:
'If [it be said that there is a difference] because of the particular mode of abiding — no, because of acceptance; for [the self abides] in the heart' [BS 2.3.24].
The intent of the objection is: for a drop of sandalwood-paste, its smallness being perceived directly, the postulation [of pervasion through contact] is reasonable; but for that whose atomicity is doubtful, and whose effect is experienced throughout all limbs, its pervasiveness should be accepted as the default (<s>autsargika</s>), and this postulation does not find scope — setting aside [the default pervasiveness].
Nor is there an inference of the atomicity of the <s>jīva</s> from the illustration of the drop of yellow sandalwood-paste,

children.translated_text: Because of the inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntika</s>) [of the reason], since a counter-example is available — so [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Nor is there here an inference.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] dispels this doubt: 'Here it is said' (<s>atrocyate</s>).
Although the atomicity of the self is established by the previously stated <s>Śruti</s>s, nevertheless, for the sake of abundance [of argument], another <s>Śruti</s> is adduced. //24//

body.text: #guṇādvā lokavat# /

children.text: ye tu sāvayavatvāccandanabindoraṇusaṃcāreṇa dehavyāptirupapadyate na tvātmano 'navayavasyāṇusaṃcāraḥ saṃbhavī, tasmādvaiṣamyamiti manyante tān pratidamucyate guṇādvā lokavaditi /
children.translated_text: For those who think that since a drop of sandalwood-paste, being composite, can pervade the body through the movement of its atoms, but the movement of atoms is not possible for the self which is partless, and therefore [the analogy] is dissimilar — to them this is stated: 'Or from the quality, as in the world.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] analyzes that: 'Consciousness' (<s>caitanya</s>).
Although the <s>jīva</s> is atomic, nevertheless its quality — consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>) — pervades the entire body.
Just as, even though a lamp is small, its quality — radiance (<s>prabhā</s>) — pervades the entire interior of the house. //25//

body.translated_text: 'Or from the quality, as in the world' [BS 2.3.25].

body.text:
etadapi śaṅkādvāreṇa dṛṣayitvā dṛṣṭāntāntaramāha- #vyatireko gandhavat /
akṣīyamāṇamapi taditi# /
kṣayasyātisūkṣmatayānupalabhyamānakṣamiti śaṅkate- #syādetaditi# /
viśliṣṭānāmalpatvādityupalakṣaṇaṃ, dravyāntaraparamāṇūnāmanupraveśādityapi draṣṭavyam /
viśleṣānupraveśābhyāṃ ca sannapi viśleṣaḥ sūkṣmatvānnopalakṣyate iti /
nirākaroti- #nā# /
kutaḥ /

children.translated_text: 'Because of being beyond the senses' [BS 2.3.26].
Because of the extreme subtlety of atoms, fragrance — like form and the like residing in them — would also not be perceived.

children.text: upalabhyamāno vā sūkṣma upalabhyeta na sthūla ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Or, if perceived, it would be perceived as subtle, not as gross — this is the meaning.
The rest is of transparent meaning. //26//

body.translated_text:
Having also shown this through an objection, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states another illustration: 'Separation, as with fragrance' [BS 2.3.26].
'Even though it is not diminishing, that [fragrance]' — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises the objection: 'One might say thus...'
'Because the separated [particles] are small' — this is illustrative; [the point should be understood as:] also because atoms of another substance enter into [the fragrant substance] — this too is to be considered.
And through both separation and entry, even though the separation exists, it is not perceived due to its subtlety.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes: 'No.'
Why?

children.translated_text: 'Because of separate instruction' [BS 2.3.28].
The <s>Bhāṣya</s> of this is explained by the running gloss (<s>nigadavyākhyāta</s>). //28//

body.text:
#tadguṇasāratvāttu tadvyapadeśaḥ prājñavat /
kamṭakatodane 'pīti# /
mahadalpayoḥ saṃyogo 'lpamavaruṇaddhi na mahāntaṃ, na jātu ghaṭakarakādisaṃyogā nabhaso tabho vyaśruvate 'pitvalpāneva ghaṭakarakādīn, itarathā yatra nabhastatra sarvatra ghaṭakarakādyupalambha iti, te 'pi nabhaḥparimāṇaḥ prasajyeranniti /
na cāṇorjīvasya sakalaśarīragatā vedanopapadyate /
yadyapyantaḥkaraṇamaṇu tathāpi tasyatvacā saṃbaddhatvāttvacaśta samastaśarīravyāpitvādekadeśe 'pyadhiṣṭhitā tvagadhiṣṭhitaiveti śarīravyāpī jīvaḥ śaknoti sarvāṅgīṇaṃ śaityamanubhavituṃ tvagindriyeṇa gaṅgāyām /
aṇustu jīvo yatrāsti tasminneva śarīrapradeśo tadanubhavenna sarvāṅgīṇaṃ, tasyāsarvāṅgīṇatvāt /
kaṇṭakatodanasya tu prādeśikatayā na sarvāṅgīṇopalabdhiriti vaiṣamyam /
#guṇatvameva hīti# /
idameva hi guṇānāṃ guṇatvaṃ yaddravyadeśatvam /
ata eva hi hemante viṣaktāvayavāpyadravyagate 'tisāndre śītasparśe 'nubhūyamānepyanudbhūtaṃ rūpaṃ nopalabhyate yathā, tathā mṛgamadādīnāṃ gandhavāhaviprakīrṇasūkṣmāvayavānāmatisāndre gandhe 'nubhūyamāne rūpasparśau nānubhūyete tatkasya hetoḥ, anudbhūtatvāttayorgandhasya codbhūtatvāditi /
naca dravyasya prakṣyaprasaṅgaḥ, dravyāntarāvayavapūraṇāt /
ata eva kālaparivāsavaśādasya hatagandhitopalabhyate /
apica caitanyaṃ nāma na gumo jīvasya guṇānaḥ, kintu rūpabhāvaḥ /
naca svabhāvasya vyāpitve bhāvasyāvyāpitvaṃ, tattvapracyuterityāha- #yadi ca caitanyamiti# /
tadevaṃ śrutismṛtītihāsapurāṇasiddhe jīvasyāvikāritayā paramātmatve, tathā śrutyāditaḥ paramamahattve ca, yā nāmāṇutvaśrutayastāstadanurodhena buddhiguṇasāratayā vyākhyeyā ityāha- #tadguṇasāratvāditi# /
tadvyācaṣṭe- #tasyā buddheriti# /
ātmanā svasaṃbandhinyā buddherupasthāpitatvāttadā parāmarśaḥ /
nahi śuddhabuddhamuktasvabhāvasyātmanastattvaṃ saṃsāribhiranubhūyate /
apitu yo 'yaṃ mithyājñānadveṣādyanuṣaktaḥ sa eva pratyātmamanubhavagocaraḥ /

children.text: naca brahmasvabhāvasya jīvātmanaḥ kūṭasthanityasya svata icchādveṣānupaṅgasaṃbhava iti buddhiguṇānāṃ teṣāṃ tadabhedādhyāsena taddharmatvādhyāsaḥ, upadarāvādhyastasyeva candramaso bimbasya toyakampe kamapvattvādhyāsa ityupapāditamadhyāsabhāṣye /
children.translated_text: And since the <s>jīvātman</s>, whose nature is <s>Brahman</s>, is immutably eternal (<s>kūṭastha-nitya</s>), and since desire, aversion, and the like cannot belong to it inherently, the superimposition (<s>adhyāsa</s>) of those properties of the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) — [which are properties] of that [intellect] — onto it [the self] through the superimposition of non-difference [between self and intellect] is [analogous to] the superimposition of trembling upon the reflected disc of the moon in [trembling] water — this has been demonstrated in the <s>Adhyāsa-bhāṣya</s> (commentary on superimposition).

children.text: tathāca buddhyādyupādhikṛtamasya jīvatvamiti buddherantaḥkaraṇasyāṇutayā so 'pyaṇuvyapadeśabhāgbhavati, nabha iva karakopahitaṃ karakaparimāṇam. tathā cotkrāntyādīnāmupattiriti /
children.translated_text: And thus, the <s>jīva</s>-hood of this [self] is created by the limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) of the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) and the rest; hence, because of the atomicity of the intellect — the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) — it too receives the designation of 'atomic,' just as space [delimited] by a water-vessel is [designated as] of the measure of the water-vessel. And thus the departure [at death] and the like are also accounted for.
The rest is explained by the running gloss (<s>nigada</s>).

At the time of death (<s>prāyaṇa</s>), there would be either non-existence or the state of non-transmigration; and from that, the unwanted consequences of the destruction of what has been done (<s>kṛtavipraṇāśa</s>) and the arising of what has not been done (<s>akṛtābhyāgama</s>) [would follow]. //29//

body.translated_text:
'But the designation [of atomicity] is because of the predominance of the quality of that [intellect], as with the wise one (<s>prājña</s>); even in the prick of a thorn' [BS 2.3.29].
The conjunction of a great [entity] and a small [entity] — the small one restricts [the scope of the great], not the great one [that of the small]. A pot, a water-vessel, and the like — their conjunction with space never restricts space; rather, [it restricts] only the small pot, water-vessel, and the like. Otherwise, wherever there is space, everywhere there would be the perception of pots, water-vessels, and the like, and they too would turn out to be of the same measure as space.
And the experience of sensation (<s>vedanā</s>) throughout the entire body is not possible for the atomic <s>jīva</s>.
Although the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) is atomic, nevertheless, since it is connected with the skin, and the skin pervades the entire body, the <s>jīva</s> — stationed even in one part [of the body] — is able to experience cold throughout all limbs through the skin-organ, as when [bathing] in the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, because the skin pervades the whole body and is thus presided over [by the <s>jīva</s>].
But the atomic <s>jīva</s>, being present only where it is, [can experience sensation only in] that very part of the body — hence the experience is not throughout all limbs, because of its not being present everywhere.
But the prick of a thorn, being localized, does not involve perception throughout all limbs — hence the dissimilarity [between the two cases].
'For this indeed is the quality-nature of qualities' (<s>guṇatvam eva hi</s>) — this indeed is the nature of qualities: that they [can extend to the extent of their] substance's location.
For this very reason, in winter, even though a touch-sensation of extreme cold pervading [all] parts is experienced, the form (<s>rūpa</s>) — though unarisen — is not perceived; similarly, when the extremely concentrated fragrance of musk (<s>mṛgamada</s>) and the like — whose subtle particles have been dispersed by the wind — is experienced, form and touch are not experienced. For what reason? Because those [form and touch] are unarisen, while fragrance is arisen.
Nor is there the problem of the substance's extension [beyond its locus], because [the intervening spaces] are filled by the particles of other substances.
For this very reason, after a period of time, the loss of fragrance is perceived.
Moreover, consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>) is not a quality (<s>guṇa</s>) of the <s>jīva</s> in the manner of qualities that are different [from their substrate]; rather, it is its very nature (<s>rūpabhāva</s>).
And it is not the case that when the essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) pervades, the entity (<s>bhāva</s>) itself does not pervade — for that would be a departure from its true nature — so [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'And if consciousness [were a quality]...' (<s>yadi ca caitanyam</s>).
Thus, since the <s>Paramātman</s>-nature of the <s>jīva</s> — as immutable (<s>avikārin</s>) — is established through <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, <s>Itihāsa</s>, and <s>Purāṇa</s>, and since supreme greatness [of the self] is also [established] from <s>Śruti</s> and the like, those <s>Śruti</s>s that speak of atomicity should be explained, in conformity with [the established view], as [the self being designated as atomic] because of the predominance of the quality of the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) — so [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Because of the predominance of the quality of that [intellect]' (<s>tadguṇasāratvāt</s>).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] explains that: 'Of that intellect' (<s>tasyā buddheḥ</s>).
Because of being presented by the intellect that is connected with it [the self], the ascription (<s>parāmarśa</s>) [of atomicity] to the self [takes place].
For the true nature of the self — which is by nature pure, awakened, and liberated — is not experienced by those in <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigrating beings).
Rather, it is only that [self] which is accompanied by false knowledge (<s>mithyājñāna</s>), aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), and the like that comes within the range of each person's inner experience.

body.text:
#yāvadātmabhāvitvāttu na doṣastaddarśanāt# /
yāvatsaṃsāryātmabhāvitvādityarthaḥ /
samānaḥ sanniti /
buddhyā samānaḥ tadguṇasāratvāditi /
#apica mithyājñāneti# /
na kevalaṃ yaṃvatsaṃsāryātmabhāvitvamāgamataḥ, upapattitaścetyarthaḥ /
ādityavarṇamiti /

children.translated_text: The meaning is: of the nature of luminosity (<s>prakāśarūpa</s>).
'Of darkness' (<s>tamasaḥ</s>) —
The meaning is: of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance).
'Having truly known That, having directly realized [it], one crosses over death' — death means <s>avidyā</s> — this is the construction. //30//

body.translated_text:
'But [this is] not a fault, because [the intellect and self are connected] as long as the self is in [transmigratory] existence; for that is what is seen' [BS 2.3.30].
The meaning is: because [the intellect] exists as long as the self is in the state of a transmigrating being.
'Being the same' — being the same [as the intellect], because of the predominance of the quality of that [intellect].
'Moreover, through false knowledge' (<s>mithyājñāna</s>) — not only is the co-existence [of the intellect] with the transmigrating self [known] from scripture, but also from reasoning — this is the meaning.
'Of the color of the sun' (<s>ādityavarṇam</s>) —

children.translated_text: The <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> brings out the seed [of doubt] concerning the latent state (<s>anuśaya</s>): 'But in deep sleep and dissolution...' (<s>nanu suṣuptapralayayoḥ</s>).
'With the existent' (<s>satā</s>) — with the <s>Paramātman</s>.
The resolution of the seed regarding the latent state: 'Here it is said: Like manhood and the like, because of the possibility of manifestation of that which exists' [BS 2.3.31].
The <s>Bhāṣya</s> of this is explained by the running gloss (<s>nigadavyākhyāta</s>). //31//

body.text:
#nityopalabdhyanupalabdhiprasaṅgonyataraniyamo vānyathā# /
syādetat /
antaḥkaraṇe 'pi sati tasya nityasaṃnidhānāt kasmānnityopalabdhyanupalabdhī na prasajyete /
athādṛṣṭavipākakādācitkatvāt sāmarthyapratibandhāpratibandhābhyāmantaḥ karaṇasya nāyaṃ prasaṅgaḥ /
tāvasatyevāntaḥ karaṇe ātmano vendriyāṇāṃ vā stāṃ, tatkimantargaḍunāntaḥkaraṇeneti codayati- #athavānyatarasyātmana iti# /
athaveti siddhāntaṃ nivartayati /
siddhāntī brūte- #na cātmana iti# /
avadhānaṃ khalvanuvubhūpā śuśrūṣā vā /
na caite ātmano dharmau, tasyāvikriyatvāt /
na condriyāṇam, ekaikendriyavyatireke 'pyandhādīnāṃ darśanāt /
naca te āntaratvenānubhūyamāne bāhye saṃbhavataḥ /

children.translated_text: Therefore, there exists something internal apart from [the self and sense-organs].
And that to which these [attention and eagerness] belong is the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>).
This is what is stated: 'That whose attention...' (<s>yasyāvadhāna</s>).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] shows a <s>Śruti</s> for this very point: 'And thus' (<s>tathā ca</s>). //32//

body.translated_text:
'The unwanted consequence of either eternal perception or eternal non-perception; or the restriction to one [of the two]; otherwise' [BS 2.3.32].
One might object: even when the inner organ is present, because of the eternal proximity [of the self to it], why does not either eternal perception or eternal non-perception result as an unwanted consequence?
But if, because of the occasional nature [of perception], resulting from the occasional ripening of <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit/demerit), the obstruction and non-obstruction of the capacity of the inner organ [is the explanation] — then this problem does not arise.
Then, even without the inner organ — either for the self or for the sense-organs — let there be [the same explanation]. What then is the need for the inner organ, that internal device? — thus [the opponent] raises the objection: 'Or alternatively, of one of the two — the self...' (<s>athavā anyatarasya ātmanaḥ</s>).
The word 'or alternatively' (<s>athavā</s>) reverses the established view.
The <s>Siddhāntin</s> replies: 'Not of the self' (<s>na ca ātmanaḥ</s>).
Attention (<s>avadhāna</s>) is indeed the desire to experience, or the eagerness to hear.
And these are not properties of the self, because of its immutability (<s>avikriyatva</s>).
Nor are they [properties] of the sense-organs, since [attention] is observed even in blind persons and the like when one sense-organ is absent.
Nor are these two [attention and eagerness] possible in an external [entity] when experienced as internal.

body.text:
#kartā śāstrārthavattvāt# /
nanu 'tadguṇasāratvāt' ityanenaiva jīvasya kartṛtvaṃ bhoktṛtvaṃ ca labdhameveti tadvyutpādanamanarthakamityata āha-tadguṇasāratvādhikāreṇeti /
tasyaivaiṣa prapañco ye bhoktaiva na karteti tannirākaraṇārthaḥ /
'śāstraphalaṃ prayoktari tallakṣaṇatvāt' ityāha sma bhagavān jaiminiḥ /
prayoktaryanuṣṭhātari /
kartarīti yāvat /
śāstraphalaṃ svargādi /
kutaḥ /
prayoktṛphalasādhanatālakṣaṇatvāt śāstrasya vidheḥ /
kartrapekṣitopāyatā hi vidhiḥ /
buddhiścetkartrī bhoktā cātmā tato yasyāpekṣitopāyo bhoktuna tasya kartṛtvaṃ yasya kartṛtvaṃ naca tasyāpekṣitopāyā iti kiṃ kena saṃgatamiti śāstrasyānarthakatvamavidyamānābhidheyatvaṃ tathā cāprayojanakatvaṃ syāt /
yathā ca tadguṇasāratayāsyāvastusadapi bhoktṛtvaṃ sāṃvyavahārikamevaṃ kartṛtvamapi sāṃvyavahārikaṃ na tu bhāvikam /
body.translated_text:
'[The self is] the agent, because of the purposefulness of scripture (<s>śāstra</s>)' [BS 2.3.33].
But [one might ask:] the agency and experiencer-ship of the <s>jīva</s> have already been obtained by the [<s>sūtra</s>] 'Because of the predominance of the quality of that [intellect]' (<s>tadguṇasāratvāt</s>) — so the elaboration of that is purposeless — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Under the topic of "because of the predominance of the quality of that [intellect]"...'
This very [topic] is an elaboration thereof — for the purpose of refuting those who [hold that the self] is an experiencer alone but not an agent.
'The fruit of scripture belongs to the performer — because of its being characterized as such' — so declared the revered <s>Jaimini</s>.
'To the performer' — to the practitioner, i.e., to the agent.
'The fruit of scripture' — heaven and the like.
Why? Because scripture — i.e., injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) — is characterized by being the means for accomplishing the goal of the performer.
For injunction is the [presentation of a] means desired by the agent.
But if the intellect were the agent and the self the experiencer, then — [since] the means are desired by the experiencer, [but] the agency belongs to [another entity, the intellect], and the one whose agency it is does not have the desired means — what is connected with what? Thus scripture would become purposeless, having no referent, and consequently pointless.
And just as, through the predominance of the quality of that [intellect], the experiencer-ship [of the self] — though not ultimately real — is conventional (<s>sāṃvyavahārika</s>), so too the agency [is] conventional, not real (<s>bhāvika</s>).

body.text: avidyāvadviṣayatvaṃ ca śāstrasyopapāditamadhyāsabhāṣya iti sarvamavadātam //33 //
body.translated_text: And that scripture pertains to the domain of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) has been demonstrated in the <s>Adhyāsa-bhāṣya</s> — thus everything is clear. //33//

children.translated_text: 'Because of the teaching of movement (<s>vihāra</s>)' [BS 2.3.34].

children.text: vihāraḥ saṃcāraḥ kriyā, tatra svātantryaṃ nākartuḥ saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: <s>Vihāra</s> means movement, action; and independence therein is not possible for a non-agent.
Therefore, from this too, the <s>jīva</s> is an agent. //34//
'Because of taking up (<s>upādāna</s>)' [BS 2.3.35].

children.text: tadeteṣāṃ prāṇānāmindriyāṇāṃ vijñānena buddhyā vijñānaṃ grahaṇaśaktimādāyopādāyetyupādāne svātantryaṃ nākartuḥ saṃbhavati //35 //
children.translated_text: 'Of these <s>prāṇa</s>s (vital breaths), i.e., sense-organs, having taken up (<s>upādāya</s>) the cognitive faculty (<s>vijñāna</s>), i.e., the grasping capacity, through cognition (<s>vijñāna</s>), i.e., through the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>)' — and this independence in taking up is not possible for a non-agent. //35//

body.text:
#vyapadeśācca kriyāyāṃ cennirdeśaviparyayaḥ# /
abhyuccayamātrametatra samgupapattiḥ /

children.translated_text: 'Cognition (<s>vijñāna</s>) is the agent; it performs the sacrifice.'

children.text: sarvatra hi buddhiḥ karaṇarūpā karaṇatvenaiva vyapadiśyate na kartṛtvena, iha tu kartṛtvena, tasyā vyapadeśe viparyayaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: For everywhere the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), being of the nature of an instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>), is designated as an instrument alone, not as an agent. But here [it is designated] as an agent — [if that were the case,] there would be a reversal in its designation.
Therefore, it is the self alone that is designated as '<s>vijñāna</s>' (cognition).
And by that [designation, it is established that the self] is the agent. //36//

body.translated_text:
'And because of the designation in [connection with] action; if [it be said that the intellect is designated as agent] — [we say:] the designation is reversed' [BS 2.3.36].
This is merely an additional argument (<s>abhyuccayamātra</s>); otherwise the connection is easy.

body.text:
sūtrāntaramavatārayituṃ codayati-atrāha yadīti /
prajñāvān svatantra iṣṭamovātmanaḥ saṃpādayennāniṣṭam /
aniṣṭasaṃpattirapyasyopalabhyate /
tasmānna svatantrastathā ca na kartā /
tallakṣaṇatvāttasyetyarthaḥ /
asyottaram- #upalabdhidaniyamaḥ# /
karaṇādīni kārakāntarāṇi kartā prayuṅkte na tvayaṃ kārakāntaraiḥ prayujyata ityetāvanmātramasya svātantryaṃ na tu kāryakriyāyāṃ na kārakāntarāṇyapekṣata iti /

children.text: īdṛśaṃ hi svātantryaṃ neśvarasyāpyatrabhavato 'stītyutsannasaṃkathaḥ kartā syāt /
children.translated_text: For even the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) — the revered one here [in this world] — does not have this kind of [absolute] independence. Thus [all] doubt is dispelled — it [the self] is the agent.

children.text: tathā cāyamadṛṣṭaparipākavaśādiṣṭamabhiprepsustatsādhanavibhrameṇāniṣṭopāyaṃ vyāpārayannaniṣṭaṃ prāpnuyādityaniyamaḥ kartṛtvaṃ ceti na virodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus, this [self], desiring the desired [result] through the maturation of unseen merit (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>), may, through confusion about the means, engage an undesired means and thereby attain the undesired — there is no fixed rule [preventing this]. And [its] agency (<s>kartṛtva</s>) [is also established] — hence there is no contradiction.
'Because [the sense-organs] serve merely to present the objects [to consciousness]' (<s>viṣayaprakalpanamātraprayojanatvāt</s>).

children.text: nityacaitanyasvabhāvasya khalvātmana indriyādīti karaṇāni svaviṣayamupanayanti, tena viṣayāvacchinnameva caitanyaṃ vṛttiriti vijñānamiti cākhyāyate, tatra cāsyāsti svātantryamityarthaḥ //37 //
children.translated_text: For the Self, whose nature is eternal consciousness, has the sense-organs and the like as its instruments, which present their respective objects [to it]. Therefore, consciousness delimited by the object is called 'cognition' (<s>vṛtti</s>) or 'knowledge' (<s>vijñāna</s>), and in that [process] the Self has independence — this is the meaning. //37//

body.translated_text:
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises an objection in order to introduce another <s>sūtra</s>: 'Here one objects: if...' (<s>atrāha yadi</s>).
If the conscious self (<s>prajñāvān</s>) were independent, it would bring about only what is desired for itself, not what is undesired. But the occurrence of undesired [results] is also observed for it. Therefore, it is not independent, and thus it is not an agent — because [agency] is characterized by that [independence] — this is the meaning.
The answer to this: 'The restriction pertains to [the means of] perception' [BS 2.3.37].
The agent employs the other factors of action (<s>kāraka</s>s) — instruments and the like — but this one [the self] is not employed by other factors. This much alone is its independence; but it is not the case that in the activity of producing results it does not depend on other factors.

children.translated_text: 'Because of the reversal of powers' (<s>śaktiviparyayāt</s>).
Previously, the reversal of the causal case-endings (<s>kāraṇaka-vibhakti-viparyaya</s>) was stated.
Now, the reversal of the agentive powers (<s>kāraka-śakti-viparyaya</s>) [is addressed] — hence there is no redundancy.

children.text: aviparyayāya tu karaṇāntarakalpanāyāṃ nāmni visaṃvāda iti //38 //
children.translated_text: But if, to avoid the reversal [of powers], one postulates another instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>), there would be a discrepancy in terminology. //38//

body.text:
samādhyabhāvācca /
samādhiriti saṃyamamupalakṣayati /
dhāraṇādhyānasamādhayo hi saṃyamapadevadanīyāḥ /
yathāhuḥ-'trayamekatra saṃyamaḥ' iti /
atra śrotavyo mantavya iti dhāraṇopadeśaḥ /

children.translated_text: 'It is to be meditated upon' (<s>nididhyāsitavya</s>) — this is the instruction of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation).
'It is to be seen' (<s>draṣṭavya</s>) — this is the instruction of <s>samādhi</s> (absorption).
As [<s>Patañjali</s>] says: 'That very meditation, when shining forth as the object alone, as if empty of its own form, is <s>samādhi</s>.'

children.text: so 'yamiha kartātmā samādhāvupadiśyamāna ātmanaḥ kartṛtvamavaitīti sūtrārthaḥ //39 //
children.translated_text: This agent-self, being instructed here in <s>samādhi</s>, knows the agency of the Self — this is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>. //39//

body.translated_text:
'And because of the absence of <s>samādhi</s>' (<s>samādhyabhāvāc ca</s>).
<s>Samādhi</s> here indicates <s>saṃyama</s> (the combined practice [of concentration, meditation, and absorption]).
For <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and <s>samādhi</s> (absorption) are to be designated by the single term <s>saṃyama</s>.
As [<s>Patañjali</s>] says: 'The three together [constitute] <s>saṃyama</s>.' Here, 'It is to be heard, it is to be reflected upon' — this is the instruction of <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration).

body.text:
#yathā ca takṣobhayathā# /
avāntarasaṃgatimāha- #evaṃ tāvaditi# /
vimṛśati- #tatpunariti# /
pūrvapakṣaṃ gṛhṇāti- #tatreti# /
śāstrārthavattvādayo hi hetava ātmanaḥ kartṛtvamāpādayanti /
naca svābhāvike kartṛtve saṃbhavatyasatyapavāde tadaupādhikaṃ yuktam. atiprasaṅgāt /
naca muktyabhāvaprasaṅgo 'syāpavādakaḥ, yathā jñānasvabhāvo jñeyābhāve 'pi nājño bhavatyevaṃ kartṛsvabhāvo 'pi kriyāveśābhāve 'pi nākartā /
tasmāt svābhāvikamevāsya kartṛtvamiti prāpte 'bhidhīyate /
nityaśuddhabuddhamuktasvabhāvaṃ hi brahma bhūyobhūyaḥ śrūyate /
tadasya buddhatvamasatyapi boddhavye yuktaṃ,
body.translated_text:
'And as with a carpenter, in both ways' (<s>yathā ca takṣobhayathā</s>).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the subordinate connection: 'Thus, to begin with' (<s>evaṃ tāvat</s>).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] deliberates: 'But then, that again...' (<s>tatpunaḥ</s>).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] takes up the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>: 'Therein...' (<s>tatra</s>).
For the reasons such as 'the scripture being purposeful' (<s>śāstrārthavattvādi</s>) and the like establish the agency of the Self.
And when intrinsic agency is possible, without there being a sublation (<s>apavāda</s>), it is not appropriate to [posit] that [agency] as merely adventitious (<s>aupādhika</s>) — because of over-extension.
Nor does the consequence of non-liberation serve as a sublating [argument]: just as one whose nature is knowledge (<s>jñāna-svabhāva</s>) does not become non-knowing even in the absence of objects to be known, so too one whose nature is agency does not become non-agent even in the absence of involvement in action.
Therefore, agency is intrinsic to it alone — when this prima facie view is arrived at, the reply is given.
For <s>Brahman</s>'s nature as eternally pure, enlightened, and liberated is heard again and again [in scripture].
Its being 'enlightened' (<s>buddhatva</s>) is appropriate even in the absence of something to be known,

body.text:
vahnerivāsatyapi dāhye dagdhṛtvaṃ, tacchīlasya tasyāvagamāt /
kartṛtvaṃ tvasya kriyāveśādavagantavyam /
naca nityodāsīnasya kūṭasthasya nityasyāsakṛcchutasya saṃbhavati, tasya ca kadācidapyasaṃsarge kathaṃ tacchaktiyogo nirviṣayāyāḥ śakteraṃsabhavāt tathāca yadi tatsidhyarthaṃ tadviṣaḥ kriyāveśo 'byupeyate tathā sati tatsvabhāvasya svabhāvocchedābhāvādbhāvanāśaprasaṅgaḥ, naca muktasyāsti kriyāyoga iti /
kriyāyā duḥkhatvānna vigalitasakaladuḥkhaparamānandāvasthā mokṣaḥ syādityāśayavānāha- #na svābhāvikaṃ kartṛtvamātmana iti# /
abhiprāyamabudhvā codayati- #nanu sthitāyāmapīti# /
pariharati- #na /
nimittānāmapīti# /
śaktaśakyāśrayā śaktiḥ svasattayāvaśyaṃ śakyamākṣipati /
tathāca tayākṣiptaṃ śakyaṃ sadaiva syāditi bhāvaḥ /
codayati- #nanu mokṣasādhananavidhānāditi# /
pariharati- #na /
sādhanāyattasyeti# /
asmākaṃ tu na mokṣaḥ sādhyaḥ, apitu brahmasvarūpaṃ tacca nityamiti /
uktamabhiprāyamāviṣkaroti- #apica nityaśuddha iti# /
codayati- #para eva tarhi saṃsārīti# /
ayamarthaḥ-paraścetsaṃsārī tasyāvidyapravilaye muktau sarve mucyerannaviśeṣāt /
tataśca sarvasaṃsārocchedaprasaṅgaḥ /
parasmādanyaścetsa buddhyādisaṃghāta eveti, tasyaiva tarhi muktisaṃsārau nātmana iti /
pariharati- #na /
avidyāpratyupasthāpitatvāditi# /
na paramātmano muktisaṃsārau, tasya nityamuktatvāt /
nāpi buddhyādisaṃghātasya, tasyācetanatvāt /
api tvavidyopasthāpitānāṃ buddhyādisaṃghātānāṃ bhedāttattadbuddhyādisaṃghātabhedopadhāna ātmaiko 'pi bhinna iva viśuddho 'pyaviśuddha iva tataścaikabuddhyādisaṃghātāpagame tatra mukta ivetaratra baddha iva yathā maṇikṛpāṇādyupadhānabhedādekameva mukhaṃ nāneva dīrghamiva vṛttamiva śyāmamivāvadātamiva anyatamopadhānavigame tatra muktamivānyatropahitamiveti naikamuktau sarvamuktaprasaṅgaḥ /
tasmānna paramātmano makṣasaṃsārau, nāpi buddhyādisaṃghātāsya kintu buddhyādyupahitasyātmasvabhāvasya jīvabhāvamāpannasyeti paramārthaḥ /
atraivānvayavyatirekau śrutibhirādarśayati- #tathāceti# /
itaścaupādhikaṃ yadupādhyabhibhavodbhavābhyāmasyābhibhavodbhavau darśayati śrutirityāha- #tathā#
body.translated_text:
just as fire's being a 'burner' (<s>dagdhṛtva</s>) [is appropriate] even in the absence of something to be burned — because its nature (<s>tacchīla</s>) is understood [as such].
But the agency of this [Self] is to be understood from [its] involvement in action (<s>kriyāveśa</s>).
And that [involvement] is not possible for one who is eternally indifferent (<s>nityodāsīna</s>), immutably eternal (<s>kūṭastha-nitya</s>), and heard of repeatedly [as such]. And since there is never any contact [of the Self with action], how can there be a connection with the power [of agency]? — for a power without an object is impossible. And thus, if involvement in action is accepted to establish that [agency], then, since such a nature [agency] — once accepted as intrinsic — cannot be destroyed [without destroying the entity itself], there would be the consequence of the destruction of the entity (<s>bhāvanāśa</s>); and for the liberated one there is no connection with action.
Since action is of the nature of suffering, the state of liberation — which is the supreme bliss with all suffering removed — would not be [possible] — with this intent [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Agency is not intrinsic to the Self' (<s>na svābhāvikaṃ kartṛtvam ātmanaḥ</s>).
Without understanding the intent, [the opponent] objects: 'But even when the power remains...' (<s>nanu sthitāyām api</s>).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes: 'No. Even of the causes...' (<s>nimittānām api</s>).
A power resides in the capable and the capable-of-being-done; by its very existence, it necessarily draws forth the capable-of-being-done [i.e., the effect]. And thus, the capable-of-being-done, being drawn forth by it, would always exist — this is the purport.
[The opponent] objects: 'But because the teaching of means to liberation [is given]...' (<s>nanu mokṣasādhanavi dhānāt</s>).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes: 'No. Because [liberation] depends on means...' (<s>sādhanāyattasya</s>).
But for us, liberation is not something to be accomplished (<s>sādhya</s>); rather, it is the very nature of <s>Brahman</s>, and that is eternal.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] reveals the stated intent: 'Moreover, eternally pure...' (<s>api ca nityaśuddha</s>).
[The opponent] objects: 'Then it is the Supreme alone that is the <s>saṃsārin</s> (bound being)' (<s>para eva tarhi saṃsārī</s>).
The meaning is: if the Supreme is the <s>saṃsārin</s>, then upon the dissolution of <s>avidyā</s>, in liberation, all would be liberated — since there is no distinction. And thus there would be the consequence of the annihilation of all <s>saṃsāra</s>.
Alternatively, if there is another [entity] apart from the Supreme, that would be the aggregate of <s>buddhi</s> and the like alone — and then it is that very [aggregate] that has bondage and liberation, not the Self.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes: 'No. Because [the <s>jīva</s>s are] presented by <s>avidyā</s>' (<s>avidyāpratyupasthāpitatvāt</s>).
Bondage and liberation do not belong to the <s>Paramātman</s> (supreme Self), since It is eternally liberated.
Nor do they belong to the aggregate of <s>buddhi</s> and the like, since that is insentient.
Rather, because the aggregates of <s>buddhi</s> and the like that are presented by <s>avidyā</s> are diverse, through the superimposition of those diverse <s>buddhi</s>-aggregates, the one Self — though one — appears as if diverse, though pure appears as if impure. And thus, upon the removal of one <s>buddhi</s>-aggregate, It is as if liberated there, while as if bound elsewhere — just as a single face, through the superimposition of different reflecting surfaces such as gems, swords, and the like, appears as if multiple, as if long, as if round, as if dark, as if fair; and upon the removal of one reflecting surface, it is as if freed there while as if imposed upon elsewhere. Hence, the liberation of one does not entail the consequence of the liberation of all.
Therefore, bondage and liberation do not belong to the <s>Paramātman</s>, nor to the aggregate of <s>buddhi</s> and the like; rather, they belong to the Self that has assumed the state of a <s>jīva</s> through being superimposed upon by <s>buddhi</s> and the like — this is the ultimate truth.
For this very point, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] shows the positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>) from <s>Śruti</s>: 'And thus...' (<s>tathā ca</s>).
And from this [it follows] that [agency] is adventitious — for that whose suppression and emergence [correspond to] the suppression and emergence of the limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) is shown by <s>Śruti</s> — so [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Likewise...'

atraivārthe sūtraṃ vyācaṣṭe- #tadetadāheti# /
saṃprasādaḥ suṣuptiḥ /
syādetat /

yathā svaśarīremodāsīnastakṣā sukhī, nāsyādīni tu karaṇāni vyāpārayan duḥkhī, tathā svātmanātmodāsīnaḥ sukhī, manaḥprabhṛtīni tu karaṇādīni vyāpārayan duḥkhītyetāvatāsya sāmyaṃ na tu sarvathā /
yathātmā ca jīvo 'vayavāntarānapekṣaḥ svaśarīraṃ vyāpārayatyevaṃ manaḥprabhṛtīni tu karaṇāntarāṇi vyāpārayatīti pramāṇasiddhe niyogaparyanuyogānupapattiḥ /
pūrvapakṣahetūnanubhāṣya dūṣayati- #yattūktamiti# /
yatparaṃ hi śāstraṃ sa eva śāstrārthaḥ /
kartrapekṣitopāyabhāvanāparaṃ tanna kartṛsvarūpaparam /
tena yathālokasiddhaṃ kartāramapekṣya svaviṣaye pravartamānaṃ na puṃsaḥ svābhāvikaṃ kartṛtvamavagamayitutsahate, tasmāttattvamasītyādyupadeśavirodhādavidyākṛtaṃ tadavatiṣṭhate /
codayati- #nanu saṃdhye sthāna iti# /
aupādhikaṃ hi kartṛtvaṃ nopādhyapagame saṃbhavatīti svābhāvikameva yujyata ityarthaḥ /
apica yatrāpi karaṇamasti tatrāpi kevalasyātmanaḥ kartṛtvaśravaṇātsvābhāvikameva yuktamityāha- #tathopādāne 'pīti# /
tadetat pariharati- #na tāvatsaṃdhya iti# /
upādhyapagamo 'siddho 'ntaḥkaraṇasyopādheḥ saṃdhye 'pyavasthānādityarthaḥ /

nanu yadi na kevalasya kartṛtvamapi tu karaṇādisahitasyaiva, tathā sati karaṇādiṣvati kartṛvibhaktiḥ syāt /

#sarvakārakāṇāmeveti# /

nanvevaṃ sati tasyāmevātmanaḥ svābhāvikaṃ kartṛtvamastvityata āha- #naca tasyāṃ#ulabdhāvapyasya svābhāvika #kartṛtvamasti#kasmāt #nityopalabdhisvarūpatvāt#ātmanaḥ /
nahi nitye svabhāve cāsti bhāvasya vyāpārityarthaḥ /

nāpi buddhyāderupalabdhikartṛtvamātmanyadhyastaṃ yathā tadgatamadhyavasāyādikartṛtvamityāha- #ahaṅkārapūrvakamapi kartṛtvaṃ nopalabdhurbhavitumarhati# /
kutaḥ /
#ahaṅkārasyāpyupalabhyamānatvāt# /
nahi śarīrādi yasyāṃ kriyāyāṃ gamyaṃ tasyāmeva gantṛ bhavati /
etaduktaṃ bhavati-yadi buddhirupalabdhī bhavet, tatastasyā upalabdhṛtvamātmanyadhyavasyeta /

tasyā jaḍatvenopalabhyamānatayopalabdhikartṛtvānupapatteḥ /
yadā caupalabdhau buddherakartṛtvaṃ tadā yaduktaṃ buddherupalabdhṛtve karaṇāntaraṃ kalpanīyaṃ, tathāca nāmamātre visaṃvāda iti tanna bhavatītyāha- #na caivaṃ sati karaṇāntarakalpanā#
body.translated_text:
'In dream and waking' (<s>svapnajāgaritayoḥ</s>).
For this very point, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] explains the <s>sūtra</s>: 'This is what is stated' (<s>tad etad āha</s>).
<s>Saṃprasāda</s> means deep sleep (<s>suṣupti</s>).
One might object: The carpenter has hands and the like; engaging axes and the like through those, he may be afflicted. But the <s>Paramātman</s> is partless — with what would He engage the mind and the like? Hence the analogy with the carpenter is inappropriate. To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'And the carpenter analogy...' (<s>takṣadṛṣṭāntaś ca</s>).
Just as the carpenter, resting in his own body, is happy, but engaging axes and other instruments is afflicted — so too the Self, resting in its own nature, is happy, but engaging instruments such as the mind and the like is afflicted. The similarity is to this extent only, not in every respect.
And just as the Self, being the <s>jīva</s>, operates the body without requiring intermediate parts, so too it operates the mind and other instruments — since this is established by valid means of knowledge, the demand for justification is inappropriate.
Having restated the reasons of the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes: 'But what was said...' (<s>yat tūktam</s>).
For that which is the purport of scripture is the meaning of scripture. [Scripture] has as its purport the cultivation of means desired by the agent — it does not have the agent's own nature as its purport.
Therefore, just as [scripture], presupposing the agent as ordinarily established, proceeds in its own domain, it cannot convey the intrinsic agency of the person. Hence, due to the contradiction with the teaching of 'You are That' (<s>tat tvam asi</s>) and the like, that [agency] remains as created by <s>avidyā</s>.
[The opponent] objects: 'But in the dream state...' (<s>nanu saṃdhye sthāna</s>).
The meaning is: since adventitious agency is not possible when the limiting adjunct is removed, intrinsic [agency] alone is fitting.
Moreover, even where there is an instrument, the <s>Śruti</s> hears of the agency of the Self alone — hence intrinsic [agency] alone is fitting — so [the opponent] says: 'And likewise in the case of cessation [of instruments]' (<s>tathopādāne 'pi</s>).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes this: 'To begin with, not in the dream state...' (<s>na tāvat saṃdhya</s>).
The removal of the limiting adjunct is unestablished, since the inner organ — the limiting adjunct — persists even in the dream state — this is the meaning.
Moreover, the kind of knowledge that exists in dream, the same kind of activity [exists there] too — so [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'And the activity there too...' (<s>vihāro 'pi ca tatra</s>). 'And likewise in the case of cessation [of instruments]' (<s>tathopādāne 'pi</s>).
Although the agent case-ending is heard for the agent alone, nevertheless the agency of this [Self] is produced by the superimposition of action, instruments, and the like — not [the agency] of the pure [Self]; for one who cuts with the aid of an axe is not a cutter when alone [without the axe].
But [the opponent says:] if the agency does not belong to [the Self] alone but only together with instruments and the like, then the agent case-ending should apply to the instruments and the like too. But this is not so — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'It does occur, not in the world...' (<s>bhavati na loke</s>).
The meaning is: the agent case-ending does sometimes apply to instruments and the like too, depending on the speaker's intention.
Moreover, this <s>Śruti</s> about 'cessation' (<s>upādāna</s>) has as its purport merely the cessation of the activity of instruments — not [the establishment of] independence. And the agent case-ending is figurative.
Because non-purposive cessation of instrument-activity — like 'the bank wants to fall' — is observed. So [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Moreover, in this cessation...' (<s>api cāsminn upādāne</s>). 'But this designation that you [mention]' — what we said, namely that this is merely a compilation — that arises from this.
'Of all agents (<s>kāraka</s>s) indeed' — 'The rice grains soften,' 'the firewood blazes,' 'the pot [cooks]' — thus in their own activities, all [these entities] have agency. Then is it agency alone that belongs to <s>buddhi</s> and the like, and not instrumentality? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'But their instrumentality depends on apprehension (<s>upalabdhi</s>)' (<s>upalabdhyapekṣaṃ tv eṣāṃ karaṇatvam</s>).
But then, [the opponent says:] let there be intrinsic agency of the Self in that very apprehension. To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'And not even in that apprehension does it have intrinsic agency' (<s>na ca tasyām upalabdhāv apy asya svābhāvika kartṛtvam asti</s>) — why? — 'Because of the eternally self-luminous nature of the Self' (<s>nityopalabdhisvarūpatvāt ātmanaḥ</s>).
For in what is eternal and is [the Self's very] nature, the entity has no [additional] activity — this is the meaning.
Thus it has been said: the Self does not have intrinsic agency in apprehension.
Nor is the apprehension-agency of <s>buddhi</s> and the like superimposed on the Self — as its agency of determination and the like belonging to that [<s>buddhi</s>] [is superimposed] — so [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Even agency preceded by the ego-sense (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>) cannot belong to the apprehender' (<s>ahaṅkārapūrvakam api kartṛtvaṃ nopalabdhuḥ bhavitum arhati</s>).
Why?
'Because the ego-sense too is apprehended' (<s>ahaṅkārasyāpy upalabhyamānatvāt</s>).
For the body and the like, which are the object (<s>gamya</s>) in the action of going, do not become the goer (<s>gantṛ</s>) in that very action.
What is stated amounts to this: if <s>buddhi</s> were the apprehender, then its apprehension-agency would be superimposed on the Self.
But this is not so.
Because, being insentient and being itself apprehended, the agency of apprehension is impossible for <s>buddhi</s>.
And when <s>buddhi</s> is non-agent in apprehension, then the claim that 'if <s>buddhi</s> is the apprehender, another instrument must be postulated, and then there would be a discrepancy in terminology' — that does not apply — so [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'And in this case, there is no postulation of another instrument' (<s>na caivam sati karaṇāntarakalpanā</s>)

children.translated_text: — because <s>buddhi</s> is not the apprehender.

children.text: caitanyamidānīmakaraṇaṃ buddhirupalabdhāvātmā cānapalabdha etyata āha- #buddhe karaṇatvābhyupagamāt# /
children.translated_text: [One might then say:] 'Now consciousness is a non-instrument, <s>buddhi</s> is the apprehender, and the Self is the non-apprehender' — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Because of the acceptance of <s>buddhi</s>'s instrumentality' (<s>buddheḥ karaṇatvābhyupagamāt</s>).

children.text: ayamabhisaṃdhiḥ-caitanyamupalabdhirātmasvabhāvo nitya iti na tatrātmanaḥ kartṛtvaṃ, nāpi buddheḥ karaṇatvaṃ, kintu caitanyameva viṣayāvacchinnaṃ vṛttiriti copalabdhiriti cākhyāyate /
children.translated_text: The intent is this: consciousness, which is apprehension (<s>upalabdhi</s>), is the very nature of the Self and is eternal — hence the Self has no agency therein, nor does <s>buddhi</s> have instrumentality therein. Rather, consciousness itself, delimited by objects, is called 'cognition' (<s>vṛtti</s>) and 'apprehension' (<s>upalabdhi</s>).

children.text: tasya tu tattadviṣayāvacchede vṛttau buddhyadīnāṃ karaṇatvamātmanaśca tadupadhānenāhaṅkārapūrvakaṃ kartṛtvaṃ yujyata iti //40 //
children.translated_text: But in its delimitation by various objects — in [the arising of] cognition — the instrumentality of <s>buddhi</s> and the like is appropriate, and the agency of the Self through the superimposition of those [instruments], preceded by the ego-sense (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>), is [also] appropriate. //40//

#parāttu tacchuteḥ# /
yadetajjīvānāmaupādhikaṃ kartṛtvaṃ tatpravartanālakṣaṇeṣu rāgādiṣu satsu neśvaramaparaṃ pravartakaṃ kalpayitumarhati, ati prasaṅgāt /
naceśvaro dveṣapakṣapātarahito jīvān sādhvasādhuni karmaṇi pravartayitumarhati, yena dharmādharmāpekṣayā jagadvaicitryamāpadyeta /
sa hi svatantraḥ kāruṇiko dharma eva jantūn pravartayennādharme /
tataśca tatpreritā jantavaḥ sarve dhārmikā eveti sukhina eva syurna duḥkhunaḥ /
svatantrāstu rāgādiprayuktāḥ pravartamānā dharmādharmaparcayavanto vaicitryamanubhavantīti yuktam /
evañca vidhiniṣedhayorarthavattvamitarathā tu sarvathā jīvā avastatantrā itīśvareṇaiva pravartyanta iti kṛtaṃ vidhiniṣedhābyām /
nahi balavadanilasalilaughanudyamānaṃ pratyupadeśor'thavān /

'eṣa hyeva sādhu karma kārayati' ityādayastāvcachutayaḥ sarvavyāpāreṣu jantūnāmīśvaratantratāmāhuḥ, tadasati pratibandhake na praśaṃsāparatayā vyākhyātumucitam /

nāpi nirghṛṇaḥ /
naca karmapracayasyādirastyanāditvatsaṃsārasya /

children.text: tadanenābhisaṃdhinoktam-parāyatte 'pi hi kartṛtvaṃ karotyeva jīva iti /
children.translated_text: With this intent it was stated: Even though the agency [of the <s>jīva</s>] is dependent on another [<s>Īśvara</s>], the <s>jīva</s> does indeed act.

children.text: tasmādvidhiniṣedhaśāstravirodhāllokasya sthūladarśitvāt 'eṣa hyeva sādhu ka4ma kārayati' ityādiśruteḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, [this is stated] because of the contradiction with the scriptures of injunction and prohibition, because people are gross-sighted [and do not perceive subtle causation], and because of the <s>Śruti</s> 'He alone makes [beings] perform good action' and the like.
'The ignorant creature (<s>jantu</s>), powerless over its own happiness and suffering,
impelled by <s>Īśvara</s>, goes either to heaven or to the abyss.'

body.translated_text:
'#But from the Supreme, because it is heard from that#' (<s>parāt tu tacchuteḥ</s>).
This agency (<s>kartṛtva</s>) of the <s>jīva</s>s is due to limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>); when the impelling factors such as attachment (<s>rāga</s>) and the like exist, one should not postulate <s>Īśvara</s> as yet another impeller — because of the absurd consequence of over-extension (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>).
Nor can <s>Īśvara</s>, being free from hatred and partiality, be the one who impels <s>jīva</s>s toward good and bad actions — for then the diversity of the world in terms of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> would [need to] arise from His will.
For He, being independent and compassionate, would impel beings toward <s>dharma</s> alone, not toward <s>adharma</s>.
Consequently, all beings impelled by Him would be solely righteous and therefore solely happy, not miserable.
But it is reasonable that those who are independent, operating under the impulse of attachment and the like, accumulating <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, experience diversity.
And thus, injunctions and prohibitions (<s>vidhiniṣedha</s>) would be meaningful; but otherwise, if <s>jīva</s>s are entirely dependent [on <s>Īśvara</s>] and are impelled by <s>Īśvara</s> alone, injunctions and prohibitions would be purposeless.
For instruction is not meaningful for one who is being swept away by powerful wind or flood.
Therefore, <s>Śruti</s>s such as 'He alone makes [beings] perform good action' and the like — being contradicted by all <s>Śruti</s>s of injunction and prohibition and by common experience — should be interpreted as directed toward the praise of lordship (<s>aiśvarya</s>). This being the prima facie conclusion, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states:
The <s>Śruti</s>s such as 'He alone makes [beings] perform good action' and the like declare the dependence of beings on <s>Īśvara</s> in all their activities — and when there is no obstructing [counter-evidence], it is not appropriate to interpret them as merely directed toward praise.
Nor does what is established by <s>Śruti</s> require postulation [to be valid], such that the postulation [of <s>Īśvara</s> as impeller] would be contradicted when the impelling factors such as attachment and the like already exist.
Nor is it reasonable [to say] that if agency is dependent on <s>Īśvara</s>, beings would engage only in <s>dharma</s> and hence be only happy, not experiencing diversity.
For even though <s>Īśvara</s> is free from attachment, nevertheless, impelling beings toward <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> with regard to their respective prior <s>karma</s>s, He is neither biased through hatred or partiality,
nor merciless.
And there is no beginning to the accumulation of <s>karma</s>, since <s>saṃsāra</s> is beginningless.
Nor is it correct [to say] that injunctions and prohibitions are purposeless for one whose agency is dependent on <s>Īśvara</s>.
For <s>Īśvara</s> does not impel beings like a powerful wind; rather, accommodating their consciousness, [He impels them] through the medium of attachment and the like.
And thus, injunctions and prohibitions are meaningful for those who seek to attain the desirable and avoid the undesirable.

body.text: ' iti smṛteśceśvaratantrāmāmeva jantūnāṃ kartṛtvaṃ, na tu svatantrāmāmiti siddham /

children.text: īśvara eva vidhiniṣedhayosthāne niyujyeta yadvidhiniṣedhayoḥ phalaṃ tadīśvareṇa tatpratipāditadharmādharmanirapekṣeṇa kṛtamiti vidhiniṣedhayorānarthakyam /
children.translated_text: If <s>Īśvara</s> alone were to be employed in place of injunctions and prohibitions, whatever is the fruit of injunctions and prohibitions would have been accomplished by <s>Īśvara</s> independently of the <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> taught by those [injunctions and prohibitions] — and thus injunctions and prohibitions would be purposeless.

children.text: na kevalamānarthakyaṃ viparītaṃ cāpadyeta ityāha- #tathā vihitakāriṇamiti# /
children.translated_text: Not only would there be purposelessness, but the reverse would also follow — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#And one who performs what is enjoined#.'
And the previously stated defect — the destruction of what has been done and the arrival of what has not been done (<s>kṛtanāśa</s> and <s>akṛtābhyāgama</s>) — would ensue.
The rest has transparent meaning. //41//

body.translated_text: And from this <s>Smṛti</s> too, it is established that the agency of beings is indeed dependent on <s>Īśvara</s>, not independent.

'#[The <s>jīva</s> is] a part (<s>aṃśa</s>), because of the various designations, and otherwise too, since some [<s>Śākhā</s>s] read of [its] being a fisherman, a gambler, and the like#' (<s>aṃśo nānāvyapadeśād anyathā cāpi dāśakitavāditvam adhīyata eke</s>).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the sub-connection: '#Of the <s>jīva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s>#.' The relation of helper and helped (<s>upakāryopakārakabhāva</s>) [means] the relation of directed and director (<s>prayojyaprayojakabhāva</s>).
Here, because of the apparent absence of a determining reason (<s>vinigamana-hetu</s>), indeterminacy (<s>aniyama</s>) has been stated as the established conclusion.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>], showing the semblance of a determining reason by grasping the position of difference, says: 'Or alternatively' (<s>athavā</s>).

children.translated_text: And thus, both worldly and Vedic approval and avoidance, and the distinction of happiness and suffering, liberation and bondage, are justified.

children.text: naca mokṣasyānarthabahulatā, yataḥ pratibimbānāmiva śyāmatāvadātatādirjīvānāmeva nānāvedanābhisaṃbandho brahmaṇastu bimbasyeva na tadabhisaṃbandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Nor does liberation entail great misfortune; for just as the dark or light color belongs to the reflections alone and not to the original, so too the diverse sensations belong only to the <s>jīva</s>s, but not to <s>Brahman</s>, which is like the original.

children.text: yathāca darpaṇāpanaye tatpratibimbaṃ bimbabhāve 'vatiṣṭhate na kṛpāṇe pratibimbatamapi /
children.translated_text: And just as, when a mirror is removed, the reflection [in it] subsists in the state of the original, but does not [subsist] in a sword even though reflected in it,

children.text: evamavidyopadhānavigame jīve brahmabāveti siddhaṃ jīvo brahmāṃśa iva tattantratayā na tvaṃśa iti tātparyārthāḥ //43 //
children.translated_text: so too, upon the removal of the conditioning adjunct of <s>avidyā</s>, the <s>jīva</s> attains the state of <s>Brahman</s>. Thus it is established: the <s>jīva</s> is as if a part of <s>Brahman</s>, being dependent on It, but is not [actually] a part. This is the purport. //43//

body.translated_text:
The relations of controlled and controller, sought and seeker, known and knower, governed and governor, supported and supporter — these cannot be conceived between <s>jīva</s> and <s>Paramātman</s> in the case of non-difference.
Nor can <s>Śruti</s>s such as 'The fishermen of <s>Brahman</s>, the gamblers of <s>Brahman</s>' and the like — which are directed toward teaching that the fishermen are <s>Brahman</s>, the gamblers are <s>Brahman</s>, and so forth — be conceived in the case of difference between <s>jīva</s>s and <s>Brahman</s>.
Nor can the establishment of the <s>jīva</s>s as parts (<s>aṃśa</s>) of <s>Īśvara</s> [be made] through <s>Śruti</s>s that teach both difference and non-difference, together with the mantra-passage directly teaching part-hood — 'A quarter of Him is all beings' (<s>pādo'sya viśvā bhūtāni</s>) — and the <s>Smṛti</s> 'My own part' (<s>mamaivāṃśaḥ</s>) and the like.
And it is reasonable that <s>Īśvara</s>, through the perfection of unsurpassable limiting adjuncts and endowed with divine powers, is the ruler even of His own parts, who have inferior limiting adjuncts.
For to begin with, the <s>jīva</s>s cannot be parts of <s>Īśvara</s> who has no parts [in the literal sense].
Moreover, if the <s>jīva</s>s were parts of <s>Brahman</s>, then the sensation (<s>vedanā</s>) residing in them would belong to <s>Brahman</s> — just as sensation in the foot and the like belongs to <s>Devadatta</s>.
Consequently, for one who has attained the state of <s>Brahman</s>, there would be the consequence of experiencing the sensations of all <s>jīva</s>s — hence <s>saṃsāra</s> itself would be better than liberation! For in <s>saṃsāra</s>, one experiences only one's own sensation and does not suffer greatly.
But the liberated one, being the experiencer of the sensations of all <s>jīva</s>s — liberation should be carefully avoided as being fraught with great misfortune!
Likewise, since difference and non-difference, being mutually contradictory, cannot co-exist in one thing, the <s>jīva</s>s cannot be parts [of <s>Brahman</s>].
Nor is it reasonable that <s>Brahman</s> alone is real while <s>jīva</s>s are not — because of the consequent absence of the distinction of happiness and suffering, liberation and bondage, and the consequent absence of [the validity of] approval and avoidance.
Therefore, the <s>jīva</s>s alone are ultimately real, not the one non-dual <s>Brahman</s>.
The non-duality <s>Śruti</s>s are [to be explained] through figurative usage based on the absence of distinction regarding genus (<s>jāti</s>), place (<s>deśa</s>), and time (<s>kāla</s>) — this being the prima facie conclusion, [the <s>Siddhāntin</s>] states:
Means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>s) convey previously unknown meanings — especially scripture (<s>śabda</s>).
Therein, difference, being already established through worldly experience, need not be taught by scripture.
But non-difference, being previously unknown, deserves to be taught through the restatement of already-known difference.
And that upon which a sentence opens, is touched upon in the middle, and is concluded — therein lies its purport (<s>tātparya</s>).
And the <s>Upaniṣad</s>s, opening with, touching upon in the middle, and concluding with non-duality, are directed toward non-duality alone.
And it is not reasonable that what they are directed toward is figurative; for in repeated use, the meaning gains strength, not weakness — much less does it become figurative. This has been stated.
Therefore, when non-duality is the real [teaching], the <s>jīva</s>-nature of that <s>Brahman</s> [arises] from the differentiation of the conditioning adjunct of beginningless, indescribable <s>avidyā</s> — just as from the differentiation of the limiting adjuncts such as mirrors and the like, the reflections of a single original (<s>bimba</s>) become multiple.

children.translated_text: The group (<s>gaṇa</s>) limited by the number seventeen is the 'group of seventeen' (<s>saptadaśaka</s>).

children.text: tadyathā-buddhikarmendriyāṇi bāhyāni daśa buddhimanasī vṛttibhedamātreṇa bhinne apyekīkṛtyaikamantaḥ karamaṃ śarīraṃ pca viṣayā iti saptadaśako rāśiḥ //47 //
children.translated_text: Namely: the ten external cognitive and active sense-organs (<s>buddhīndriya</s>s and <s>karmendriya</s>s), <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) and <s>manas</s> (mind) — though differentiated only by difference of function — counted as one internal organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), the body, and the five objects [of the senses] — this is the group of seventeen. //47//

children.translated_text: For one who knows the difference of the Self from the body composed of six sheaths (<s>ṣāṭkauśika</s>), but does not know the difference from the entire aggregate of <s>buddhi</s> and the like — for that person there is eligibility for rites having results in the other world.

children.text: samastabuddhyādivyatirekavedinastu karmabhoktṛtvābhimānarahitasya nādhikāraḥ karmaṇi tathāca na yatheṣṭaceṣṭā, abhimānavikalasya tasyā apyabhāvāditi //48 //
children.translated_text: But for one who knows the difference from the entire aggregate of <s>buddhi</s> and the like — being devoid of the conviction of being an agent and experiencer of <s>karma</s> — there is no eligibility for action. And thus there is no acting as one pleases either, because for one who lacks [even] that conviction, even that [arbitrary action] is absent. //48//

body.translated_text:
'#Approval#' (<s>anujñā</s>) is the injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) that is intended — not the incitement of one already engaged.
Because in a non-human-authored [scripture], the accommodation of an author's intention is not possible.
And because the incitement of one already engaged is impossible in the case of the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> sacrifice, where the animal-killing serves the ritual purpose.
Even in [the case of] the person-serving [injunction], regarding the restrictive portion, [the question arises] for one who is already engaged: '#What then is the connection with the body?#'
For the Self, being immutably eternal (<s>kūṭasthanitya</s>) and without measure (<s>aparimāṇin</s>), has no conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>), inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), or any other relation with the body, since it transcends all qualities — this is the intent.
The answer: '#This aggregate of body and the like is the erroneous cognition arisen in the Self [in the form of] "I alone am this"#.'
The meaning is this: True, there is no ultimate relation of the Self with the body and the like; but there is an erroneous modification (<s>vṛtti</s>) — a false cognition, produced by <s>buddhi</s> and the like, directed toward the Self, of the form 'I alone am this aggregate of body and the like.'
In this [erroneous cognition], the aggregate of body and the like appears as identical with the Self.
This is a conventional (<s>sāṃvṛtta</s>) relation characterized by identity — not an ultimate one — this is the meaning.
[The objector], with a hidden intent, raises a doubt: '#For one who sees correctly, then...'
The answer: 'No. Of that [one]...#'
If the correct vision is accepted as: 'I am solely the non-dual <s>Brahman</s>' — when the aggregate of subtle and gross body and the like is displayed by <s>avidyā</s> [as the Self] — then indeed, for the possessor of that [correct vision], injunctions and prohibitions are entirely purposeless.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] clarifies this very point: '#Regarding what is to be avoided and what is to be adopted#.'
The objector reveals the hidden intent: 'For one who sees the difference from the body alone...'
[The objection is that] the eligibility of the agent pertains to rites having results in the other world (<s>āmuṣmikaphala</s>) such as <s>Darśa-Pūrṇamāsa</s> and the like — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises and resolves this: '#No.

kāṇādādīnāṃ tvātmasamavāpyadṛṣṭaṃ pratyātmamasādhāraṇaṃ tatkṛtaśca manasā sahātmanaḥ svasvāmibhāvalakṣaṇaḥ saṃbandho 'nādiradṛṣṭabhedānāmanāditvāt, tathā cātmanaḥsaṃyogasya sādhāraṇye 'pi svasvāmibhāvasyāsādhāraṇyādabhisaṃdhyādivyavasthopapadyata eva /

But for those <s>Sāṃkhya</s>s or <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>s who desire the distinction of pleasure and pain to be ultimately real, and [who hold that] there are many all-pervading selves — for them alone does this intermixture follow.
Therein, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] first states the intermixture against the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>s, preceded by a question: 'How?' — thus.
Whatever kind of relation with the <s>guṇa</s>s exists, that same [relation] is undifferentiated with respect to all <s>puruṣa</s>s — hence the pleasure and pain produced by it are undifferentiated with respect to all.
Nor can the distinction be based on <s>karma</s>, since <s>karma</s> belongs to <s>Prakṛti</s>, and <s>Prakṛti</s> being common [to all], the non-distinction remains unchanged.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises an objection: 'It might be said' — thus.
The meaning is this: <s>Pradhāna</s> does not operate for the sake of displaying its own glory, but rather for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>.
And with respect to whichever <s>Puruṣa</s> the two purposes of <s>Puruṣa</s> — enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) — have been accomplished by it, with respect to that [<s>Puruṣa</s>] it ceases, its task being completed; but with respect to another <s>Puruṣa</s>, whose task is not yet completed, it continues to operate.
Thus, since the distinction between the liberated and the bound is tenable, the distinction of pleasure and pain too will be tenable — [the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> argues]. [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes: 'No' — thus.
Since all <s>puruṣa</s>s are all-pervading, and since <s>Pradhāna</s> is common [to all], the very [claim] that 'the purpose has been accomplished for this <s>Puruṣa</s> by this [<s>Pradhāna</s>]' does not hold.
Therefore, without a reason, the distinction must be maintained by force of purpose alone.
And that is unjustified because of the absence of a reason — this is the meaning.
Let there be non-distinction for the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>s, [since their] <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit) inheres in <s>Pradhāna</s>, and <s>Pradhāna</s> is common [to all].
But for the followers of <s>Kaṇāda</s> and the like, the <s>adṛṣṭa</s> inheres in the self, and is unique to each self; and the relation of the self with the mind — characterized by the owner-owned relation (<s>svasvāmibhāva</s>) — produced by that [<s>adṛṣṭa</s>], is beginningless, since the differences among <s>adṛṣṭa</s>s are beginningless. And thus, even though the conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) of the self [with the mind] is common, because the owner-owned relation is unique, the distinction of intention (<s>abhisaṃdhi</s>) and the like is indeed tenable.
Nor is the conjunction itself common.
For the conjunction that the mind has with other selves is not the same as [the conjunction] with its owner, since the conjunction of a self differs with each individual conjunction.

children.translated_text: For the postulation [of ultimate particularities requires prior] difference, and from that [postulation comes] difference — thus [there is circularity].
This itself is the refutation of the <s>Kaṇāda</s> (Vaiśeṣika) position.

children.text: bhāṣyakṛtā tu prauḍhavāditayā kāṇādān pratyapyadṛṣṭāniyamādityādīni sūtrāṇi yojitāni /
children.translated_text: But the author of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> (<s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>), by way of bold argumentation (<s>prauḍhavāditā</s>), has applied the <s>sūtra</s>s beginning with 'Because of the non-restriction of <s>adṛṣṭa</s>' and the like even against the <s>Kaṇāda</s>s.
But some prefer [the interpretation that those <s>sūtra</s>s] are directed only toward the refutation of the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> position — let that be for now. //50//

body.translated_text:
Therefore, since the oneness of the Self is established by scripture, and since the distinction [of experiences] is tenable even in [the case of] oneness, there is no need for the postulation of multiple selves — [especially] because of the undesirability [of such postulation] due to its cumbersomeness and contradiction with scripture.
And because, in postulating difference through the possession of ultimate particularities (<s>antyaviśeṣa</s>s), there would be the fallacy of mutual dependence.
