children.translated_text: That is as follows: The non-origination of the <s>prāṇa</s>s would be either like the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) — by virtue of being the unmodified Self of <s>Brahman</s> — or by virtue of being a reality other than <s>Brahman</s>.
To begin with, they do not have unmodified <s>Brahman</s>-selfhood like the <s>jīva</s>, because of being insentient.
Therefore, their non-origination should be maintained on the ground of being a reality other than <s>Brahman</s>.

And thus, there would be a contradiction with the promise of 'through the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, everything is known,' and an undermining of the entire <s>Vedānta</s> [corpus] — this is what [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states: 'For in the space-<s>adhikaraṇa</s> indeed' — thus. //2//

body.translated_text:
'Similarly, <s>Prāṇa</s>' — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s> begins].
Although, because of the contradiction with the <s>Śruti</s> of the promise 'through the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, everything is known,' and because of the contradiction with the more numerous non-duality <s>Śruti</s>s, the <s>Śruti</s>s that state the existence of the <s>prāṇa</s>s at the beginning of creation ought to be interpreted otherwise — just like the <s>Śruti</s>s [that state] the non-createdness of space and the like — nevertheless, one who does not know the mode of alternative interpretation, thinking that 'even a single <s>Śruti</s> that cannot be otherwise explained would invalidate the many,' raises the prima facie objection.
And here, because of the great elevation [of the topic], [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] recalls the reasons for the prima facie view of the space-<s>adhikaraṇa</s>: 'Therein, to begin with' — thus.
For the origination of the great elements is knowable only through the single means of valid knowledge that is scripture; and where that scripture is absent, by the very absence of that means of valid knowledge, the non-existence [of origination] is understood.
Just as with the salutation to the <s>caitya</s> (shrine) and its status as a religious duty — this is the meaning.
Here, after raising the prima facie view superficially through the [apparent] conflict of <s>Śruti</s>s and consequent indetermination, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] introduces the [stronger] prima facie view with 'Or alternatively' — thus.
Its intent has been shown [above].
In 'and like the vital breath (<s>prāṇa</s>)' (<s>pānavyāpacca tadvat</s>), the resemblance with the <s>pūrvapakṣa-sūtra</s> meaning of the horse-acceptance (<s>aśvapragraha</s>) and <s>iṣṭi</s> <s>adhikaraṇa</s> was then alluded to.
But the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>) would be [valid] only if the <s>Śruti</s> stating the existence of the <s>prāṇa</s>s at the beginning of creation were not otherwise explainable.
But this [<s>Śruti</s>] is indeed otherwise explainable.
For in the intermediate dissolution (<s>avāntarapralaya</s>), the creation of the instruments presupposing fire and the like needs to be stated — hence the introduction [of the passage] has that as its purpose.
Therein, the eligible person — <s>Prajāpati</s> — is not destroyed; only the three worlds have dissolved. Therefore, the <s>Śruti</s>, with reference to his <s>prāṇa</s>s, is of meaningful purport.
Therefore, for the sake of consistency with the more numerous <s>Śruti</s>s, and for the coherence of the promise of all-knowledge — and since, if the subsequent passage [about creation] were to be taken as secondary, there would be the consequence of the previously promised meaning being unfulfilled and thus [the passage] having no purpose — the <s>prāṇa</s>s too, like space, are modifications of <s>Brahman</s>.
Nor is it the case that the <s>Śruti</s>s entirely deny the origination of the <s>prāṇa</s>s, as with the salutation to the <s>caitya</s> and the like; for in some places there is indeed no mention of their origination, but <s>Śruti</s>s declaring their origination have been shown in various places.
Therefore, there is a difference from the <s>caitya</s>-salutation, the <s>poṣadha</s> (observance), and the like — thus.
Some interpret the <s>sūtra</s> in the context of the space-<s>adhikaraṇa</s> explanation as: 'Because of the impossibility of secondary meaning' — thus.
The secondary meaning is: the <s>Śruti</s> of the non-origination of the <s>prāṇa</s>s is impossible [to maintain] — because of [the necessity of their] origination — thus.
That is unjustified.
Because it cannot withstand the dilemma.

children.translated_text: 'And because of the prior <s>Śruti</s> [stating its origination]' — thus.
The <s>Bhāṣya</s> on this is explained by the running commentary (<s>nigada</s>). //3//

body.text: #tatpūrvakatvādvācaḥ# /

children.translated_text: The word 'speech' (<s>vāc</s>) is a synecdoche (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) for speech, <s>prāṇa</s>, and mind.

children.text: ayamarthaḥ-yatrāpi tejaḥprabhṛtīnāṃ sṛṣṭau prāṇasṛṣṭirnokteti brūṣe, tatrāpyukteti brūmahe /
children.translated_text: The meaning is this: Where you say that in the creation of fire and the rest, the creation of the <s>prāṇa</s>s is not stated — even there, we say it is stated.

children.text: tathāhi-yasmin prakaraṇena tejobannapūrvakatvaṃ vākprāṇamanasāmāmnāyate 'annamayaṃ hi' ityādinā, tadyadi mukhyārthaṃ tatastatsāmānyātrveṣāmeva prāṇānāṃ sṛṣṭiruktā /
children.translated_text: That is as follows: In the passage where the precedence of fire, water, and food for speech, <s>prāṇa</s>, and mind is taught by [the <s>Śruti</s>] beginning with 'For [the body is] made of food' — if that is taken in its primary sense, then by that very generalization, the creation of these very <s>prāṇa</s>s is stated.

children.text: atha gaumaṃ tathāpi brahmakartṛkāyāṃ nāmarūpavyākriyāyāmupakramopasaṃhāraparyālocanayā śrutyantaraprasiddheśca brahmakāryatvaprapañcārthameva prāṇādīnāmāpemayatvādyabhidhānamityuktaiva tatrāpi prāṇasṛṣṭiriti siddham //4 //
children.translated_text: But even if it is taken as secondary, nevertheless — by examining the introduction and conclusion in the context of the differentiation of name and form by <s>Brahman</s> as the agent, and because of the well-known [fact] from other <s>Śruti</s>s that [the <s>prāṇa</s>s] are products of <s>Brahman</s> — the statement of the food-nature and the like of the <s>prāṇa</s>s is for the purpose of elaborating their being products of <s>Brahman</s>. Thus, even there, the creation of the <s>prāṇa</s>s is stated — this is established. //4//

body.translated_text: 'Because speech and the like are preceded by that [<s>Prāṇa</s>]' — thus.

'Seven, because of [scriptural] passages and because of specification' — thus.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the internal connection: 'Regarding the subject of origination' — thus.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the cause of doubt: 'Because of the conflict of <s>Śruti</s>s' — thus.
The subject is the doubt.
'In some places, seven <s>prāṇa</s>s [are mentioned]' — namely: sight, smell, taste, speech, hearing, mind, and skin.
In some places, eight <s>prāṇa</s>s 'are enumerated as seizers (<s>graha</s>s)' — namely: smell, taste, speech, sight, hearing, mind, hands, and skin. These are the seizers, and their objects — the over-seizers (<s>atigraha</s>s) — are also exactly eight: '<s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is a seizer; he is seized by the over-seizer <s>apāna</s>, for by <s>apāna</s> one smells odors' — and so on, as stated in this passage.
'In some places, nine' — namely, 'seven' —

children.translated_text: 'Seven indeed are the <s>prāṇa</s>s in the head' — thus.

children.text: ye sapta śīrṣaṇyāḥ śrotrādayaste prāṇā ityukte itareṣāmaśīrṣaṇyānāṃ hastādīnāmaprāṇatvaṃ gamyate /
children.translated_text: When the seven in the head — hearing and the rest — are said to be the <s>prāṇa</s>s, it is understood that the others — those not in the head, such as the hands and the like — are not <s>prāṇa</s>s.

children.text: yathā dakṣiṇenākṣṇā paśyatītyukte vāmena na paśyatīti gamyate /
children.translated_text: Just as, when it is said 'He sees with the right eye,' it is understood that he does not see with the left.

children.text: etaduktaṃ bhavati-yadyapi śrutivipratiṣedo yadyapi ca pūrvasaṃkhyāsu na parāsāṃ saṃkhyānāṃ niveśastathāpyavacchedakatvena bahvīnāṃ saṃkhyānāmasaṃbhavādekasyāṃ kalpyamānāyāṃ saptatvameva yuktaṃ prāthamyāllāghavācca, vṛttibhedamātravivakṣayā tvaṣṭatvādayo gamayitavyā iti prāptam //5 //
children.translated_text: What is stated amounts to this: Although there is a conflict of <s>Śruti</s>s, and although the earlier numbers do not accommodate the later numbers, nevertheless — since it is impossible for many numbers to serve as the delimiting [count], and since, when one must be chosen, seven is appropriate because of [its] primacy and parsimony — the other numbers such as eight and so on are to be understood as intended merely by difference of function — this is the prima facie conclusion. //5//

body.translated_text:
'indeed are the <s>prāṇa</s>s in the head, and two below' — thus.
Two ears, two eyes, two nostrils, one mouth — these are seven.
The anus and the generative organ — or <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) and <s>manas</s> (mind) — are the two below — thus nine.
In some places, ten:
'Nine indeed are the <s>prāṇa</s>s in a person' — those mentioned [above] — 'the navel is the tenth.'
In some places, eleven: 'Ten are the <s>prāṇa</s>s in a person' — namely: the five cognitive sense-organs (<s>buddhīndriya</s>s) beginning with smell, and the five organs of action (<s>karmendriya</s>s) beginning with the hands; the self is the eleventh — 'the self [which] pervades through the instrument' is the mind — that is the eleventh.
'In some places, twelve.
"Of all contacts, the skin alone is the abode" — in this [passage]' — namely: skin, nose, tongue, eyes, ears, mind, heart, hands, feet, generative organ, anus, and speech.
In some places, these very <s>prāṇa</s>s with the addition of <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego) are thirteen.
Thus, the <s>Śruti</s>s are in conflict regarding the number of the <s>prāṇa</s>s.
Therein, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] takes up the prima facie view preceded by a question: 'What, then, is established?
Seven alone — thus.
Seven alone are the <s>prāṇa</s>s. Whence [this]? From passages' — i.e., from understanding [based on] <s>Śruti</s>s such as 'Seven <s>prāṇa</s>s spring forth' and the like.
Not only is [this] understood from <s>Śruti</s>, but also from specification — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'And because of specification.'

body.translated_text:
With this prima facie view established, the reply is given: '#But the hands and the rest, since it is established from [other sources], it is not so#.'
The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) sets aside the prima facie position.
Not seven alone, but the hands and the rest too are <s>prāṇa</s>s.
Since the eleven-fold nature of the <s>prāṇa</s>s is established from other means of knowledge — when this is established.
The suffix '<s>tasi</s>' is used with all case-endings.
'It is not so' — the meaning of the words is: [the conclusion that there are only] seven is [reached merely] due to brevity and primacy.
What is meant is this: although the <s>Śruti</s> passages are self-evidently authoritative and independent, nevertheless, due to their mutual contradiction, they are not sufficient to determine the true nature of the matter.
Nor is an option (<s>vikalpa</s>) possible regarding an established entity, as it would be in the case of [ritual] performance.
Therefore, they are determined with the help of the meaning furnished by other means of knowledge.
'#For just as#' — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s> comments].
'Even by the <s>sruva</s> ladle' — since cutting portions of a meat <s>puroḍāśa</s> [with the <s>sruva</s>] is impossible, and since cutting liquid portions is possible, it is determined that [what is cut] in the <s>sruva</s>-cutting are liquid [offerings].
Similarly here too, from the functional determination of the five-fold set of cognitions such as form and the rest, the five-fold set of cognitive sense-organs (<s>buddhīndriya</s>s) such as the eye and the rest is determined as instruments.
For the blind and the like do not perceive form and the rest, even when the other [organs] such as the nose and the like — whose existence is inferred from the perception of smell and the like — are present.
Similarly, from the functional determination of the five-fold set of actions characterized by speech and the like, the five-fold set of organs of action (<s>karmendriya</s>s) characterized by voice, hands, and the like is determined.
For the mute and the like never possess speech and the like, even when the feet and the like — whose existence is known from walking and the like — or the cognitive sense-organs are present.
Thus, through the functional determination of activities such as volition and the like, which cannot be accomplished by the organs of action or cognition, the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) is inferred.
And a single inner organ will perform multiple functions, just as a single lamp is the cause of illuminating forms, transforming the wick, and drying up the oil.
Therefore, there is no division of the inner organ.
Rather, the one inner organ is called <s>manas</s> (mind) because of thinking, <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego) because of self-identification, and <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) because of determination.
And due to the difference of functions, though undivided, it is figuratively spoken of as if divided into three.
But in reality it is one alone, because there is no evidence for division.
Thus, since exactly eleven functions are determined, the <s>Śruti</s> that states 'the <s>prāṇa</s>s are eleven' is straightforward.
The other <s>Śruti</s> passages, however, should be interpreted in conformity with this.
Among those, the <s>Śruti</s> passages stating the numbers seven, eight, nine, and ten are [explained] by partial enumeration, in accordance with [the principle] 'one selects one, two, or three.'
But the <s>Śruti</s> passages stating twelve and thirteen should be interpreted as having in view some division based on functional differences, and as being directed toward meditation (<s>upāsanā</s>) and the like.
Therefore, the <s>prāṇa</s>s are eleven alone and no other number — this is established.
Moreover, the statement that the <s>prāṇa</s>s in the head are seven — that too should be determined as referring to [only] four, because of contradiction with other means of knowledge.
For there are not two eyes, since the function characterized by the perception of form is undivided.
But for one whose one eye is closed, the perception of form is not of the same quality as that of one with both eyes intact — therefore, it is really one eye, but figuratively spoken of as divided due to the difference of its seats.
Even for a one-eyed person, perception occurs through a portion of the eye located in the one socket.
By this, the nose and the ears too are explained.
Here is another interpretation of the two <s>sūtra</s>s: '#Only seven <s>prāṇa</s>s#' — the eye, nose, tongue, voice, ear, mind, and skin — would depart [at death].
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises a doubt in order to explain that only seven depart because they are specified: '#But even the word "all" here#.'
The answer to this is: '#Because of being specified#.'
The eye and the rest, up to the skin, are specified in the departure [passage].
Therefore, since the word 'all' is relative to the context, only seven <s>prāṇa</s>s depart, not the hands and the like — thus is the prima facie view.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] objects: 'But here, cognition is the eighth.'
'They say he does not know' — by this [it is] enumerated.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] resolves: 'This is not a defect.'
The established view is stated: '#The hands and the rest, however, are <s>prāṇa</s>s beyond the seven#' — they are understood to partake in departure, because of the <s>Śruti</s> declaring the hands and the rest as seizers (<s>graha</s>s).
For indeed, the <s>Śruti</s> declaration of their seizer-nature (<s>grahatva</s>) would be appropriate only if they bind the self until liberation; otherwise, their seizer-nature would not be proclaimed, as in the case of the body made of six sheaths.
And for this very reason, the <s>Smṛti</s> states that their liberation is bounded [by final release] — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#With the eightfold city (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>)#.'

children.translated_text: Similarly, the <s>Atharva</s> <s>Śruti</s> too speaks of the departure of these eleven.

children.text: tasmācchutyantarebhyaḥ smṛteśca sarvaśabdārthāsaṃkocācca sarveṣāmutkrameṇa sthite 'sminnaivaṃ yaduktaṃ saptaiveti, kintu pradarśanārthaṃ saptatvasaṃkhyeti siddham //6 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, since the departure of all [<s>prāṇa</s>s] is established from other <s>Śruti</s> passages, from <s>Smṛti</s>, and from the non-contraction of the meaning of the word 'all,' it is not so that only seven [depart] as was stated; rather, the number seven is merely illustrative — this is established. //6//

body.text:
#aṇavaśca# /
atra sāṃkhyānāmāhaṅkārikatvādindriyāṇāmahaṅkārasya ca jagnāmaṇḍalavyāpitvātsarvagatāḥ prāṇāḥ /
vṛttisteṣāṃ śarīradeśatayā prādeśikī tannibandhanā ca gatyāgatiśrutiriti manyante, tānpratyāha-aṇavaśca prāṇā anudbhūtarūpaspartā cāṇutvaṃ duradhigamatvānna tu paramāṇutvaṃ dehavyāpikāryānutpattiprasaṅgāttāpadūnasya śiśirahradanimagnasya sarvāṅgīṇaśītasparśopalabdhirastītyuktam /

children.translated_text: What is meant is this: if the sense-organs were all-pervading, then there would be the unwanted consequence of perceiving objects that are separated by an intervening barrier or distant.

children.text: sarvagatatve 'pi dehāvacchinnānāmeva karaṇatvaṃ tena na vyavahitaviprakṛṣṭavastūpalambhaprasaṅga iti cet, hanta prāptāprāptāvivekena śarīrāvacchinnānāmeva teṣāṃ karaṇatvamindriyatvamiti na vyāpināmindriyabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: If [one argues:] even though all-pervading, only those delimited by the body function as instruments, and therefore there is no unwanted consequence of perceiving objects that are separated or distant — well then, by the non-discrimination between what has reached and what has not reached [a place], their instrumentality and organ-hood belong only to those delimited by the body; hence, there is no organ-hood for the all-pervading [portions].

children.text: tathāca nāmamātre visaṃvādo nārthe 'smābhistadindriyamucyate bhavadbhistu vṛttiriti siddhamaṇavaḥ prāṇā iti /
children.translated_text: And thus the disagreement is merely in name, not in substance — what we call 'the sense-organ,' you call 'the function' — therefore it is established that the <s>prāṇa</s>s are atomic.

body.translated_text:
'#And [they are] atomic (<s>aṇu</s>)#.'
Here, the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>s hold that since the sense-organs arise from <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego) and since <s>ahaṅkāra</s> pervades the entire cosmic sphere, the <s>prāṇa</s>s are all-pervading.
Their functioning, being limited to the bodily region, is localized, and the <s>Śruti</s> statements about going and coming are based on that [localized functioning] — so they think. In response to them, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: And the <s>prāṇa</s>s are atomic — their atomic nature means that their form and touch are unmanifest and hence difficult to apprehend, but it does not mean they are of the size of a <s>paramāṇu</s> (ultimate atom), since there would be the unwanted consequence that effects pervading the body could not arise [from them]. It has been stated that one who is heated by fire or immersed in a cold pond perceives cold touch throughout all limbs.

body.text:
#śreṣṭhaśca# /
na kevalamitare prāṇā brahmavikārāḥ /
śreṣṭhaśca prāṇo brahmavikāraḥ /
'nāsadāsīt' ityadhikṛtya pravṛtte brahmasūkte nāsadāsīye sargātprāgānīditi prāṇavyāpāraśravaṇādasati ca vyāpārānupapatte prāṇasadbhāvājjyeṣṭhatvaśruteśca na brahmavikāraḥ prāṇa iti manvānasya bahuśrutivirodhe 'pi ca śrutyoretayorgatimapaśyataḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ /

children.text: rāddhāntastu bahuśrutivirodhādevānīditi na prāṇavyāpārapratipādinī, kintu sṛṣṭikāraṇamānīt jīvati sma āsīditi yāvat /
children.translated_text: But the established view is: because of the contradiction with many <s>Śruti</s> passages, '<s>ānīt</s>' does not teach the activity of <s>Prāṇa</s>; rather, it means 'the cause of creation was alive, existed' — that is all.
Therefore, [that passage] has as its purport the establishment of the existence of that [cause of creation].
And the seniority (<s>jyeṣṭhatva</s>) should be understood as relative to the ear and the other [organs].
Therefore, in accordance with the many <s>Śruti</s> passages, it is established that even the chief <s>Prāṇa</s> is a modification of <s>Brahman</s>. //8//

body.translated_text:
'#And the chief [<s>prāṇa</s>]#.'
Not only are the other <s>prāṇa</s>s modifications of <s>Brahman</s>,
but the chief <s>Prāṇa</s> too is a modification of <s>Brahman</s>.
The prima facie view belongs to one who, taking up [the hymn] beginning with 'Neither non-being existed nor being' in the <s>Nāsadāsīya</s> creation hymn of <s>Brahman</s>, and hearing the mention of the activity of <s>Prāṇa</s> in '<s>ānīt</s>' (it breathed) before creation, and [arguing] that activity is impossible in the case of what does not exist, and from the <s>Śruti</s> declaring its seniority (<s>jyeṣṭhatva</s>), considers that <s>Prāṇa</s> is not a modification of <s>Brahman</s> — [even though this view contradicts] many <s>Śruti</s> passages, and [the proponent] sees no way to reconcile these two [sets of] <s>Śruti</s>s.

body.text:
#na vāyukriye pṛthagupadeśāt# /
saṃprati mukhyaprāṇasvarūpaṃ nirūpyate /
atra hi 'yaḥ prāṇaḥ sa vāyuḥ' iti śrutervāyureva prāṇa iti pratibāti /
athavā 'prāṇa eva brahmaṇaścaturthaḥ pādaḥ sa vāyunā jyotiṣā' iti vāyorbhedena prāṇasya śravaṇādetadvirodhādvaraṃ tantrāntarīyameva prāṇasya svarūpamastu, śrutī ca viruddhārthe kathañcinneṣyete iti sāmānyakaraṇavṛttireva prāṇo 'stu /
na cātrāpi karaṇebhyaḥ pṛthakprāṇasyānukramaṇaśrutivirodho vṛttivṛttimatorbhedāditi pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ /
siddhāntastu-na sāmānyendriyavṛttiḥ prāṇaḥ /
sa hi militānāṃ vendriyāṇāṃ vṛttirbhavet pratyekaṃ vā /
na tāvanmilitānām, ekadvitricaturindriyābhāve tadabhāvaprasabhaṅgāt /
no khalu cūrṇaharidrāsaṃyogajanmāruṇaguṇastayoranyatarābhāve bhavitumarhati /
naca bahuviṣṭisādhyaṃ śibikodvahanaṃ dvitriviṣṭisādhyaṃ bavati /
na ca tvagekasādhyaṃ, tathā sati sāmānyavṛttitvānupapatteḥ /

children.text: apica yatsaṃbhūya kārakāṇi niṣpādayanti tatpradhānavyāpārānuguṇāvāntaravyāpāreṇaiva yathā vayasāṃ prātisviko vyāpāraḥ pañjaracālanānuguṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, when component agents jointly accomplish [something], each contributes its own subsidiary function that is conducive to the principal function — just as the individual function of birds [in a cage] is conducive to the shaking of the cage.

children.text: na cendriyāṇāṃ prāṇe pradhānavyāpāre janayitavye 'sti tādṛśaḥ kaścidavāntaravyāpārastadanuguṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: But the sense-organs have no such subsidiary function conducive to producing <s>Prāṇa</s>, the principal function.

children.text: ye ca rūpādipratyayā na te tadanuguṇāḥ, tasmānnendriyāṇāṃ sāmānyavṛttiḥ prāṇastathā ca vṛttivṛttimatoḥ kathañcidbhedavivakṣayā na pṛthagupadeśo gamayitavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the cognitions of form and the like are not conducive to that [principal function]; therefore, <s>Prāṇa</s> is not the general function of the sense-organs. And accordingly, the separate teaching [of <s>Prāṇa</s>] should not be explained away by positing some kind of difference between the function and the possessor of the function.

children.text: tasmānna kriyā, nāpi vāyumātraṃ prāṇaḥ, kintu vāyubheda evādhyātmāmāpannaḥ pañcavyūhaḥ prāṇa iti //9 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Prāṇa</s> is neither [mere] function nor mere air, but rather a specific modification of air that has assumed an internal (<s>ādhyātma</s>) form with a fivefold arrangement. //9//

body.translated_text:
'#[<s>Prāṇa</s>] is neither [mere] air nor [mere] function, because of the separate teaching#.'
Now the essential nature of the chief <s>Prāṇa</s> is being determined.
For here, from the <s>Śruti</s> 'That which is <s>Prāṇa</s>, that is <s>Vāyu</s> (air),' it appears that <s>Prāṇa</s> is just air.
Alternatively, [from the <s>Śruti</s>] '<s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is the fourth foot of <s>Brahman</s>; it [shines] by air and by light' — since <s>Prāṇa</s> is heard as different from air, and since this contradicts [the former <s>Śruti</s>], let the nature of <s>Prāṇa</s> be that according to another system, and let the two contradictory <s>Śruti</s>s be somehow reconciled — thus let <s>Prāṇa</s> be the general function of the sense-organs.
Nor would there be a contradiction with the <s>Śruti</s> that enumerates <s>Prāṇa</s> separately from the [other] sense-organs, since the function and the possessor of the function are [in some sense] different — this is the prima facie view.
But the established view is: <s>Prāṇa</s> is not the general function of the sense-organs.
For that [general function] would either be the function of the organs combined together, or of each one individually.
Not of the combined organs — because in the absence of one, two, three, or four organs, there would be the unwanted consequence of its absence.
For indeed, the red color produced by the combination of turmeric powder [and lime] cannot exist in the absence of either one of them.
And the carrying of a palanquin, which requires many bearers, cannot be accomplished by two or three bearers.
Nor [is it the function] of a single organ like the skin — because in that case, [it] being the general function would be untenable.

body.text:
syādetat /
yathā cakṣurādīnāṃ jīvaṃ prati guṇabhūtatvājjīvasya ca śreṣṭhatvājjīvaḥ svatantra evaṃ prāṇo 'pi prādhānyāt śreṣṭhatvācca svatantraḥ prāpnoti /

children.text: naca dvayoḥ svatantrayorekasmin śarīre ekavākyatvamupapadyata ityaparyāyaṃ viruddhānekadikkriyatayā deha unmathyeta /
children.translated_text: And since two independent [entities] in a single body cannot have a unified purpose, the body would inevitably be torn apart by contradictory activities in multiple directions.
With this prima facie view established, the reply is given: '#But like the eye and the rest, because of being taught together with them, and so on#.'

children.text: yadyapi cakṣurādyapekṣayā śreṣṭhatvaṃ prādhānyaṃ ca prāṇasya tathāpi saṃhatatvādacetanatvādbhautikatvāccakṣurādibiḥ sahaśiṣṭatvāccaca puruṣārthatvāt puruṣaṃ prati pāratantryaṃ śayanāsanādivadbhavet /
children.translated_text: Although <s>Prāṇa</s> has supremacy and primacy relative to the eye and the other [organs], nevertheless, because it is composite, non-sentient, material (<s>bhautika</s>), taught together with the eye and the rest, and serves the purpose of the <s>puruṣa</s>, it is subordinate to the <s>puruṣa</s> — like a bed, seat, and the like.

children.text: tathāca yathā mantrītareṣu naiyogikeṣu pradhānamapi rājānamapekṣyāsvatantra evaṃ prāṇo 'pi cakṣurādiṣu pradhānamapi jīve 'svatantra iti //10 //
children.translated_text: And thus, just as a minister, though chief among the other court officials, is not independent, being subordinate to the king — so too <s>Prāṇa</s>, though chief among the eye and the other [organs], is not independent, being subordinate to the <s>jīva</s>. //10//

body.translated_text: Objection: Just as the eye and the other [organs] are subordinate to the <s>jīva</s>, and the <s>jīva</s>, being supreme, is independent — so too <s>Prāṇa</s>, due to its primacy and supremacy, would be independent.

body.text:
syādetaccakṣurādibiḥ saha śāsanena karaṇaṃ cet prāṇaḥ /
evaṃ sati cakṣurādiviṣayarūpādivadasyāpi viṣayāntaraṃ vakyavyam /
naca tacchakyaṃ vaktum /

children.text: ekādaśakaraṇagaṇanavyākopaśceti doṣaṃ pariharati- #akaraṇatvācca na doṣastathāhi darśayati# /
children.translated_text: And the enumeration of eleven organs would be disrupted — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] removes this defect: '#And because of not being an instrument, there is no defect — for thus [the <s>Śruti</s>] shows#.'
<s>Prāṇa</s> is not accepted by us as an instrument for discrimination, grasping, and the like, such that some other object would need to be sought for it.

children.text: ekādaśatvaṃ ca karaṇānāṃ vyākupyetāpi tu prāṇāntarāsaṃbhavi dehendriyavidhāraṇakāraṇaṃ prāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the eleven-fold nature of the instruments would be disrupted [if <s>Prāṇa</s> were counted among them]; rather, <s>Prāṇa</s> is the cause of sustaining the body and the sense-organs — something that cannot be accomplished by any other <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: tacca śrutiprabandhena darśitaṃ na kevalaṃ śarīrendriyadhāraṇamasya kāryam //11 //
children.translated_text: And that [function of sustaining] has been shown by the continuous thread of <s>Śruti</s> — not merely the sustaining of the body and sense-organs is its function. //11//

body.translated_text:
Objection: If <s>Prāṇa</s> is an instrument along with the eye and the rest through [being under the same] governance,
then, just as the eye and the rest have their respective objects such as form and the like, some other object should be stated for this [<s>Prāṇa</s>] as well.
But that cannot be stated.

body.text:
apica- #pañcavṛttirmanovadvyapadiśyate# /
'viparyayo mithyājñānamatadrūpapratiṣṭham' yathā marumarīcikādiṣu salilādibuddhayaḥ /
atadrūpapratiṣṭhatā ca saṃśaye 'pyasti tasyaikāpratiṣṭhānāt /
ataḥ so 'pi saṃgṛhītaḥ /
'śabdajñānānupātī vastuśūnyo vikalpaḥ' /
yadyapi mithyājñāne 'pyasti vastuśūnyatā tathāpi na tasya vyavahārahetutāsti /
asya tu paṇḍitarūpavicārāsahasyāpi śabdajñānamāhātmyādvyavahārāhetubhāvo 'styeva /

children.translated_text: As [in the statement] 'consciousness of the <s>puruṣa</s>.'
For here, the sixth case (<s>ṣaṣṭhī</s>) does not denote a relation, because relation is the basis of difference.
Because consciousness is absolutely non-different from <s>puruṣa</s>.

children.text: yadyapi cātrābhāvapratyayālambanā vṛttirneṣyate tathāpi vikṣepasaṃskāralakṣaṇā manovṛttirihāstyeveti sajñavamavadātam //12 //
children.translated_text: And although here a mental modification (<s>vṛtti</s>) having absence as its object is not accepted, nevertheless a mental modification characterized by the impression of projection (<s>vikṣepa-saṃskāra</s>) does exist here — thus the matter is clearly explained. //12//

body.translated_text:
Moreover: '#It is designated as having five functions, like the mind#.'
'<s>Viparyaya</s> (misapprehension) is false knowledge not grounded in the real nature [of the object]' — as in the case of the cognition of water and the like in mirages and the like.
And the character of not being grounded in the real nature exists also in doubt, since [doubt] has no single ground.
Therefore, that [doubt] too is included.
'<s>Vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction) is devoid of a real object and follows upon verbal knowledge.'
Although in misapprehension too there is the absence of a real object, nevertheless it does not serve as a cause of practical activity.
But this [<s>vikalpa</s>], though unable to withstand the scrutiny of the learned, due to the power of verbal knowledge, does serve as a cause of practical activity.

body.text:
#aṇuśca# /
'samāstribhirlokaiḥ' iti vibhutvaśravaṇādvibhuḥ prāṇaḥ, 'samaḥ pluṣiṇā' ityādyāstu śrutayo vibhorapyavacchedādbhāviṣyanti /
yathā vibhuna ākāśasya kuṭakarakādyavacchedātkuṭādisāmyamiti prāpta āha- #aṇuśca# /

children.translated_text: From the <s>Śruti</s>s about departure (<s>utkrānti</s>), going (<s>gati</s>), and returning (<s>āgati</s>), the individual (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) <s>prāṇa</s> is delimited, not all-pervading.

And the designation of 'atomicity' for [<s>prāṇa</s>] — even though it pervades the body — is merely a figurative usage based on [its] being difficult to perceive, not [implying actual] atomicity — this has been stated earlier.

children.text: yattvasya vibhutvānmānaṃ tadādhidaivikena sūtrātmanā samaṣṭivyaṣṭirūpeṇa na tvādhyātmikena rūpeṇa /
children.translated_text: As for the measure indicating its pervasiveness, that pertains to the cosmic (<s>ādhidaivika</s>) <s>Sūtrātman</s> (the thread-self) in its collective and individual forms, not to the individual (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) form.

children.text: tadāśrayāśca 'samaḥ pluṣiṇā' ityevamādyāḥ śrutayo dehasāmyameva prāṇasyāhuḥ svarūpato na tu karakākāśavatparopādhikatayā kathañcinnatavyā iti //13 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>Śruti</s>s such as '<s>samaḥ pluṣiṇā</s>' (equal to a bug) and the like, which are based on that [cosmic form], speak of the equality of <s>prāṇa</s> with the body in its essential nature — not as [equality] in the manner of pot-space being [equal to the pot] through an extraneous limiting adjunct. //13//

body.translated_text:
'And [<s>prāṇa</s> is] atomic' [BS 2.4.13].
Since pervasiveness (<s>vibhutva</s>) of <s>prāṇa</s> is heard in '<s>samās tribhir lokaiḥ</s>' (equal to the three worlds), <s>prāṇa</s> is all-pervading; and the <s>Śruti</s>s like '<s>samaḥ pluṣiṇā</s>' (equal to a bug) and the like would be [explained as referring to] the delimitation of the all-pervading [<s>prāṇa</s>] — just as space (<s>ākāśa</s>), though all-pervading, is [spoken of as] equal in measure to a hut, a water-vessel, and the like through the delimitation of a hut and the like — this being the prima facie view, [the <s>Siddhāntin</s>] says: 'And [<s>prāṇa</s> is] atomic.'

body.text:
#jyotirādyadhiṣṭhānaṃ tu tadāmananāt# /
yaddhi tatkāryaṃ kurvaddṛṣṭaṃ tatsvamahimnaiva karotityeṣa tāvadutsargaḥtha parādhiṣṭhānaṃ tu tasya balavatpramāṇāntaravaśāt. syādetat /
vāsyādīnāṃ takṣādyadhiṣṭhitānāmacetanānāṃ kāryakāritvadarśanādacetanatvenondriyāṇāmapyadhiṣṭhātṛdevatākalpaneti cet /
na /
jīvasthaivādhiṣṭhātuścetanasya vidyamānatvāt /
naca 'agnirvāgbhūtvavā mukhaṃ prāviśat' ityādiśrutibhyo devatānāmapyadhiṣṭhātṛtvamabhyupagantuṃ yuktam /
anekādhiṣṭhānābhyupagame hi teṣāmekābhiprāyaniyamanimittābhāvānna kiñcitkāryamutpadyeta virodhāt /
apica ya indriyāṇāmadhiṣṭhātā sa eva bhokteti devatānāṃ bhoktṛtvena svāmitvaṃ śarīra iti na jīvaḥ svāmī syādbhoktā ca /
tasmādagnyādyupacāro vāgādiṣu prakāśakatvādinā kenacinnimittena gamayitatavyo natu svarūpeṇāgnyādidevatānāṃ mukhādyanupraveśa iti prāptam /
evaṃ prāpte ucyate-nānāvidhāsu tāvacchutiṣu smṛtiṣu ca tatra tatra vāgādiṣvagnyādidevatādhiṣṭhānavagamyate /
naca tadasatyāmanupapattau kleśena vyākhyātumucitam /
naca svarūpopayogabhedajñānavirahiṇo jīvasyendriyādhiṣṭhātṛtvasaṃbhavaḥ, saṃbhavati tu devatānāmindriyādyārṣeṇa jñānena sākṣātkṛtavatīnāṃ tatsvarūpabhedatadupayogabhedavijñānam /
tasmāttāstā eva devatāstattatkaraṇādhiṣṭhātrya iti yuktaṃ na tu jīvaḥ /
bhavatu vā jīvo 'pyadhiṣṭhātā tathāpyadoṣaḥ /
anekeṣāmadhiṣṭhātaṇāmekaḥ parameśvaro 'sti niyantāntaryāmī tadśādvipratipitsavo 'pi na vipratipattumarhanti /
tathā caikavākyatayā na tatkāryotpattipratyūhaḥ /
na caitāvatā devatānāmatra śarīre bhoktṛtvam /
nahi yantā rathamadhitiṣṭhinnapi tatsādhyavijayāderbhoktāpi tu svāmyeva /

children.text: evaṃ devatā adhiṣṭhātryo 'pi na bhoktryastāsāṃ tāvnamātrasya śrutatvāt /
children.translated_text: Thus, even though the deities are presiders, they are not experiencers — since only their presiding function (<s>adhiṣṭhāna-mātra</s>) is heard [in <s>Śruti</s>].
But the experiencer is the <s>jīva</s> alone.

children.text: naca narādiśarīrocitaṃ duḥkhabahulamupabhogaṃ sukhamapyo devatā arhanti /
children.translated_text: Nor do the deities deserve to undergo the experience — which is predominantly painful — that is appropriate for bodies of humans and the like.

children.text: tasmāt prāṇānāmadhiṣṭhātryo devatā iti siddham, śeṣamatirohitārtham //14 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that the deities are the presiders of the <s>prāṇa</s>s [i.e., sense-organs]. The rest is of transparent meaning. //14//

body.translated_text:
'But the presiding [of deities] over light and the rest [i.e., the sense-organs exists], because of their being mentioned (<s>āmanana</s>)' [BS 2.4.14].
For that which is seen to produce its effect does so by its own power alone — this is the default rule. But its being presided over by another [agent] would be [accepted only] by the force of another, stronger means of knowledge.
One might object: Since the adze and the like — being insentient — are seen to produce effects when presided over by a carpenter and the like, and since the sense-organs too are insentient, the postulation of a presiding deity [is warranted].
No — because of the existence of the <s>jīva</s>, a conscious entity, already present as the presider.
Nor is it appropriate to accept from <s>Śruti</s>s such as '<s>Agni</s>, having become speech, entered the mouth' and the like that deities too are presiders.
For if multiple presiders were accepted, then — because of the absence of a reason for restricting [them] to a single purpose — no effect would be produced, due to conflict [among them].
Moreover, whoever presides over the sense-organs is the experiencer — and [if that were the deities, then] the deities, being experiencers and hence masters of the body, the <s>jīva</s> would not be the master and experiencer.
Therefore, the figurative application of <s>Agni</s> and the like to speech and the like should be understood through some reason such as their being illuminators, and not as the actual entry of the deities <s>Agni</s> and the like into the mouth and the like — this is the prima facie conclusion.
This being the prima facie view, it is said: In numerous <s>Śruti</s>s and <s>Smṛti</s>s of various kinds, the presiding of deities — <s>Agni</s> and the like — over speech and the like is understood here and there.
And when there is no logical impossibility making it false, it is not proper to laboriously explain it away.
Nor is it possible for the <s>jīva</s> — which lacks knowledge of the specific nature, use, and distinction [of the sense-organs] — to be the presider over the sense-organs. But it is possible for the deities — who have directly realized [these things] through <s>ārṣa</s> (seeric) knowledge regarding the sense-organs and the like — to possess the knowledge of their specific nature, distinction, and use.
Therefore, those very deities are the presiders over the respective sense-organs — this is fitting, not the <s>jīva</s>.
Or, let the <s>jīva</s> also be a presider — even so, there is no fault.
For there is one supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>) who is the controller and inner ruler (<s>antaryāmin</s>) of the multiple presiders; even those who wish to disagree [with each other] cannot [actually] disagree, being directed by Him.
And thus, through unity of purpose, there is no impediment to the production of their effects.
Nor does this make the deities experiencers here in this body.
For the driver (<s>yantā</s>) who mounts a chariot is not thereby the enjoyer of the victory and the like achieved by it; rather, the master alone [is the enjoyer].

body.text:
#ta indriyāṇi tadvyapadeśādanyatra śreṣṭhāt# /
mā bhūt prāṇo vṛttirindriyāmām /
indriyāṇyevāsya jyeṣṭhasya ca prāṇasya vṛttayo bhaviṣyanti /
tadbhāvābhāvānuvidhāyibhāvābhāvatvamindriyāṇāṃ śrutyanubhavasiddhaṃ, tathāca prāṇaśabdasyaikasyānyāṭyamanekārtvaṃ na bhaviṣyati /
vṛttīnāṃ vṛttimatastattvāntaratvābhāvāt /
tattvāntaratve tvindriyāṇāṃ, prāṇaśabdasyānekārthatvaṃ prasajyeta /
indriyeṣu lākṣaṇikatvaṃ vā /
naca mukhyasaṃbhave lakṣaṇā yuktā ughanyatvāt /
naca bhedena vyapadeśo bhedasādhanam 'etasmājjāyate prāṇaḥ' ityādirmanaso 'pīndriyebhyo 'sti bhedena vyapadeśa ityanindriyatvaprasaṅgaḥ /
smṛtivaśāttu tasyendriyatve indriyāmāmapi prāṇādbhedena vyapadiṣṭānāmapyasti prāṇasvabhāvatve 'hanta asyaiva rūpamasāma' iti śrutiḥ /
tasmādupapatteḥ śruteśca prāṇasyaiva vṛttasya ekādaśendriyāṇi na tattvāntarāṇīti prāptam /
evaṃ prāpta ucyate-mukhyāt prāṇāttattvāntarāṇīndriyāmi, tatra tatra bhedena vyapadeśāt /
mṛtyuprāptāprāptatvalakṣaṇaviruddhadharmasaṃsargaśruteḥ /
arthakriyābhedācca /
dehadhāraṇaṃ hi prāṇasya kriyār'thālocanamanane cendriyāṇām /
naca tadbhāvābāvānuvidhānaṃ tadvṛttitāmāvahati /
dehena vyabhicārāt /
prāṇādayo hi dehānvayavyatirekānuvidhāyino naca dehātmanaḥ /
yāpi ca prāṇarūpatāmindriyāṇāmabhidadhāti śrutiḥ, tatrāpi paurvāparyālocanāyāṃ bheda eva pratīyata ityuktaṃ bhāṣyakṛtā /
tasmādbahuśrutivirodhāt pūrvāparavirodhācca prāṇarūpatābhidhānamindriyāṇāṃ prāṇāyattatayā bhāktaṃ gamayitavyam /
manasastvindriyatve smṛteravagate kkacidindriyebhyo bhedenopādānaṃ gobalīvardanyāyena /
athavā indriyāṇāṃ vartamānamātraviṣayatvānmanasastu traikālyagocaratvādbhedenābhidhānam /
naca prāṇe bhedavyapadeśabāhulyaṃ tathā netuṃ yuktam /
prāṇarūpatāśruteśca gatirdarśitā /
tathā jyeṣṭhe prāṇaśabdasya mukhyatvādindriyeṣu tatastattvāntareṣu lākṣaṇikaḥ prāṇaśabda iti yuktam /
naca mukhyatvānurodhenāvagatabhedayoraikyaṃ yuktaṃ, mā bhūdgaṅgādīnāṃ tīrādibhiraikyamiti /
anye tu bhedaśabdādhyayāhārabhiyā bhedaśruteśceti paunaruktyabhiyā ca tacchabdasya cānantaroktaparamārthakatvādanyathā varṇayāñcakruḥ /
kimekādaśaiva vāgādaya indriyāṇyāho prāṇo 'pīti viśaye indrasyātmano liṅgamindriyaṃ, tathāca vāgādivatprāṇasyāpīndraliṅgamindriyāmiti vāgādivatprāṇo 'pīndriyamiti prāptam /
evaṃ prāpte 'bhidhīyate-indriyāṇi vāgādini śreṣṭhāt prāṇādanyatra /
kutaḥ-tenendriyaśabdena teṣāmeva vāgādīnāṃ vyapadeśāt /
nahi mukhye prāṇā indriyaśabdo dṛṣṭacaraḥ /
indraliṅgatā tu vyutpattimātranimittaṃ yathā gacchatīti gauriti /
pravṛttinimittaṃ tu dehādhiṣṭhānatve sati rūpādyālocanakaraṇatvam /

children.translated_text: And this presiding over the body [means] that its benefit and harm correspond to the benefit and harm of the body.
And thus, there is no unwanted consequence that light (<s>āloka</s>) would be [called] a sense-organ.

children.text: tasmādrūḍhervāgādaya evendriyāṇi na prāṇa iti siddham /
children.translated_text: Therefore, from the conventional usage (<s>rūḍhi</s>), speech and the rest alone are the sense-organs, not <s>prāṇa</s> — this is established.

But the commentator (<s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>'s) [treatment of this] <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic) should be read in the <s>sūtra</s>s beginning with 'because of the <s>Śruti</s> of difference' and so on. //17//

body.translated_text:
'They — the sense-organs — [are distinct from <s>prāṇa</s>], because of the designation [as such], except for the chief (<s>śreṣṭha</s>) [<s>prāṇa</s>]' [BS 2.4.17].
Let <s>prāṇa</s> not be a function (<s>vṛtti</s>) of the sense-organs; rather, the sense-organs themselves will be functions of this chief <s>prāṇa</s>.
For the existence and non-existence of the sense-organs conforming to the existence and non-existence of that [<s>prāṇa</s>] is established by <s>Śruti</s> and experience. And thus, since the word '<s>prāṇa</s>' is one, its [different] meanings would not be many.
Because functions are not a separate category (<s>tattvāntara</s>) from the possessor of functions.
But if the sense-organs were a separate category, then the word '<s>prāṇa</s>' would have multiple meanings.
Or its use for the sense-organs would be figurative (<s>lākṣaṇika</s>).
And when the primary meaning is possible, figurative usage is not appropriate, because [figurative usage] is secondary.
Nor is the separate designation [of <s>prāṇa</s> from the sense-organs] a proof of [their] difference — [for] 'from this are born <s>prāṇa</s>' and the like — there is separate designation of the mind too from the sense-organs, yet [mind's] non-sense-organ-hood would absurdly follow.
But based on <s>Smṛti</s>, when the sense-organ-hood of mind [is accepted], then for the sense-organs too — even though designated as different from <s>prāṇa</s> — there is a <s>Śruti</s> supporting their having the nature of <s>prāṇa</s>: 'Come, let us assume its form' (<s>hanta asyaiva rūpam āsāma</s>).
Therefore, from both reasoning and <s>Śruti</s>, the eleven sense-organs are functions of <s>prāṇa</s> itself and not separate categories — this is the prima facie conclusion.
This being the prima facie view, it is stated: The sense-organs — speech and the rest — are different from the chief (<s>śreṣṭha</s>) <s>prāṇa</s>.
Why? Because by that word 'sense-organ' (<s>indriya</s>), those very [faculties] — speech and the rest — are designated.
For the word '<s>indriya</s>' (sense-organ) is not seen to be used for the chief <s>prāṇa</s>.
As for [the etymological derivation that] '<s>indriya</s>' means 'a sign of <s>Indra</s> (the self)' — that is merely a basis for [etymological] derivation, just as [one says] '<s>gacchati iti gauḥ</s>' ('that which goes is a cow').
But the actual basis for its usage is: being an instrument for perceiving form and the like, while presiding over the body.

body.text:
saṃjñāmūrtikḷptistu trivṛtkurvata upadeśāt /
satprakriyāyāṃ 'tatteja aikṣata' ityādinā saṃdarbheṇa tejo 'bannānāṃ sṛṣṭiṃ vidhāyopadiśyate-'seyaṃ devataikṣata hantāhamimāstisro devatā anena jīvenātmanānupraviśya nāmarūpe vyākaravāṇi tāsāṃ trivṛtaṃ trivṛtamekaikāṃ karavāṇi' iti /
asyārthaḥ-pūrvoktaṃ bahubhavanamīkṣaṇaprayojanamadyāpi sarvathā na niṣpannamiti punarīkṣāṃ kṛtavatī bahubhavanameva prayojanamuddiśya kathaṃ hantedānīmahamimā yathoktāsteja ādyāstisro devatāḥ pūrvasṛṣṭāvubhūtena saṃprati smaraṇasaṃnidhāpitena jīvena prāṇādharaṇakartrātmanānupraviśya buddhyādibhūtamātrāyāmadarśa iva mukhabimbaṃ toya iva candramaso bimbaṃ chāyāmātratayānupraviśya nāma ca rūpaṃ ca te vyākaravāṇi vispaṣṭaṃ karavāṇīdamasya nāmedaṃ ca rūpamiti /
tāsāṃ tisṛṇāṃ devatānāṃ trivṛtaṃ trivṛtaṃ tejo 'bannātmanā tryātmikāṃ tryātmikāmekaikāṃ devatāṃ karavāṇīti /
tatra saṃśayaḥ-kiṃ jīvakartṛkamidaṃ nāmarūpavyākaraṇamāho parameśvarakartṛkamiti /
yadi jīvakartṛkaṃ tataḥ 'ākāśo ha vai nāma nāmarūpayornirvahitā' ityādiśrutivirodhādanadhyavasāyaḥ /
atha parameśvarakartṛkaṃ, tato na virodhaḥ /
tatra ḍitthaḍavitthādināmakaraṇe ca ghaṭapaṭādirūpakaraṇe ca jīvakartṛtvadarśanādihāpi trivṛtkaraṇe nāmarūpakaraṇe cāsti saṃbhāvanā jīvasya /
tathāca yogyatvādanena jīveneti vyākaravāṇīti pradhānakriyayā saṃbadhyate, na tvānantaryādanupraviśyetyanena saṃbadhyate /
body.translated_text:
'But the fabrication of name and form (<s>saṃjñāmūrtikḷpti</s>) is [done] by the one who performs the tripartite combination (<s>trivṛtkaraṇa</s>), because of the instruction (<s>upadeśa</s>)' [BS 2.4.20].
In the <s>Satprakriyā</s> (the teaching-method based on Being), having prescribed the creation of fire, water, and food through the sequence beginning with 'That fire reflected' (<s>tat teja aikṣata</s>), [the <s>Śruti</s>] instructs: 'That deity reflected: "Come, let me enter these three deities with this living self (<s>jīva</s>) and differentiate name and form. Let me make each one of those three tripartite."'
The meaning of this is: The purpose of [the deity's] earlier reflection — namely, 'becoming many' — is not yet fully accomplished in every respect. Hence, [the deity,] having reflected again with the very same purpose of becoming many [in mind, thought:] 'Come, how shall I now, having entered these three aforementioned deities — fire and the rest — which were created earlier, through this living self (<s>jīva</s>) — which was not manifest in the earlier creation but is now brought to mind through recollection, and which is the bearer and agent of <s>prāṇa</s> — having entered as a mere reflection, like a face-image in a mirror or like the disc of the moon in water — differentiate name and form, making them distinct: "this is its name, and this is its form."'
'Of those three deities, let me make each one tripartite' — that is, [make each one] of triple nature, consisting of fire, water, and food.
Therein, the doubt [arises:] is this differentiation of name and form done by the <s>jīva</s>, or by the supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>)?
If done by the <s>jīva</s>, then — because of contradiction with <s>Śruti</s>s like '<s>ākāśo ha vai nāma nāmarūpayor nirvahitā</s>' (space indeed is the differentiator of name and form) — there is no [firm] conclusion.
But if done by the supreme Lord, then there is no contradiction.
Therein, since the <s>jīva</s> is seen in worldly [experience] to be the agent of naming — [calling things] '<s>Ḍittha</s>, <s>Ḍavittha</s>' and the like — and of form-making — [fashioning] pots, cloths, and the like — here too, in the tripartite combination and in the making of name and form, there is a possibility for the <s>jīva</s>.
And thus, because of [the <s>jīva</s>'s] fitness, 'with this living self' (<s>anena jīvena</s>) is syntactically connected with the principal verb 'let me differentiate' (<s>vyākaravāṇi</s>), and not — merely because of proximity — with 'having entered' (<s>anupraviśya</s>).

body.text:
pradhānapadārthasaṃbandho hi sākṣātsarveṣāṃ guṇabhūtānāṃ padārthānāmautsargikastādarthyātteṣām /
tasya tu kkacitsākṣādasaṃbhavātparamparāśrayaṇaṃ, sākṣātsaṃbhavaśca yogyatayā darśitaḥ /
nanu seyaṃ devateti parameśvarakartṛtvaṃ śrūyate /
body.translated_text:
For the direct connection of all subordinate word-meanings with the principal word-meaning is the default, since they exist for the sake of that [principal meaning].
But the indirect connection through intermediaries [is adopted] only sometimes, when direct [connection] is not possible; and the possibility of direct [connection here] has been shown through [the <s>jīva</s>'s] fitness.
But [one might object:] 'That deity' (<s>seyaṃ devatā</s>) — [by this expression,] the creatorship of the supreme Lord is heard [in the <s>Śruti</s>].

body.text:
satyam /
prayojakatayā tu tadbhaviṣyati /
yathā loke cāreṇāhaṃ parasainyamanupraviśya saṃkalayānīti /
yadi punarasya sākṣātkartṛbhāvo bhavedanena jīvenetyanarthakaṃ syāt /
nahi jīvasyānyathā karaṇabhāvo bhavitumarhati /
prayojakakartustatsākṣātkartā karaṇaṃ bhavati pradhānakriyoddeśena prayojakena prayojyakarturvyāpanāt /
tasmādatra jīvasya kartṛtvaṃ nāmarūpavyākaraṇe 'nyatra tu parameśvarasyeti virodhādanadhyavasāya iti prāptam /
evaṃ prāpta ucyate-parameśvarasyaivehāpi nāmarūpavyākartṛtvamupadiśyate na tu jīvasya, tasya pradhānakriyāsaṃbandhaṃ pratyayogyatvāt /
nanvanyatra ḍitthajavitthādināmaka4maṇi ghaṭaśarāvādirūpakarmaṇi ca kartṛtvadarśanādihāpi yogyatā saṃbhāvyata iti cet /
na /
nirinadīsamudrādinirmāṇāsāmarthyenārthāpattyabhāvaparicchinnena saṃbhāvanāpabādhanāt /
tasmāt parameśvarasyaivātra sākṣātkartṛtvamupadiśyate na jīvasya /
anupraviśyetyanena tu saṃnihitenāsya saṃbandho yogyatvāt /

children.translated_text: Nor is there purposelessness [of the mention of <s>jīva</s>], because the statement of its entry is meaningful — the tripartite combination being for the sake of the experiencer-<s>jīva</s>.
One might object:

children.text: anupraviśya vyākaravāṇīti samānakartṛtve ktvaḥ smaraṇāt praveśanakarturjīvasyaiva vyākartṛtvamupadiśyate 'nyathā tu parameśvarasya vyākartṛtve jīvasya praveṣṭṛtve bhinnakartṛkatvena ktvaḥ prayogo vyāhanyetetyatrāha- #naca jīvo nāmeti# /
children.translated_text: 'Having entered, it differentiates' — by the <s>ktvā</s> suffix [implying same-agent continuity], the agent of entry — the <s>jīva</s> — is taught to be the same as the agent of differentiation. Otherwise, if the supreme Lord were the agent of differentiation and the <s>jīva</s> the agent of entry, the usage of the <s>ktvā</s> suffix, which requires the same agent, would be violated. To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'And the <s>jīva</s> is not [a different agent]' (<s>na ca jīvo nāma</s>).
The rest has transparent meaning. //20//

body.translated_text:
True. But that [creatorship of the supreme Lord] would be in the capacity of an instigator (<s>prayojaka</s>).
Just as in the world: 'Through a spy, I shall enter the enemy's army and form alliances.'
But if [the supreme Lord] were the direct agent, then 'with this living self' (<s>anena jīvena</s>) would be purposeless.
For the <s>jīva</s> cannot function otherwise than as an instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>).
The direct agent of the instigating agent's [intended result] becomes the instrument with respect to the principal action, because the instigator governs the instigated agent for the sake of the principal action.
Therefore, the <s>jīva</s>'s agency here is in the differentiation of name and form, while the supreme Lord's [agency] is elsewhere [i.e., in creation proper] — and because of the contradiction [that would otherwise result], there is no [firm] conclusion — this is the prima facie conclusion.
This being the prima facie view, it is said: The supreme Lord's creatorship in the differentiation of name and form is taught here as well, not the <s>jīva</s>'s, because of the <s>jīva</s>'s unfitness for connection with the principal action.
But [one might object:] since the <s>jīva</s> is seen elsewhere to be the agent in naming — [calling things] '<s>Ḍittha</s>, <s>Ḍavittha</s>' and the like — and in form-making — pots, platters, and the like — fitness [for the <s>jīva</s>] is conceivable here too.
No — because the possibility [of the <s>jīva</s> being the agent here] is negated by the <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumptive reasoning) that is delimited by [the <s>jīva</s>'s] incapacity to create rivers, oceans, and the like.
Therefore, the direct creatorship taught here belongs to the supreme Lord alone, not to the <s>jīva</s>.
But [the word] 'having entered' (<s>anupraviśya</s>), being proximate, is connected with this [<s>jīva</s>], because of fitness.

body.text:
#māṃsādi bhaumaṃ yathāśabdamitarayośca# /
atra bhāṣyakṛtottarasūtraśeṣatayā sūtrametadviṣayopadarśanaparatayā vyākhyātam /
śaṅkānirākaraṇārthatvamapyasya śakyaṃ vaktum /
tathāhi-yo 'nnasyāṇiṣṭho bhāgastanmanastejasastu yo 'ṇiṣṭho bāgaḥ sa vāgityatra hi kāṇādānāṃ sāṃkhyānāṃ cāsti vipratipattiḥ /
tatra kāṇādā mano nityamācakṣate /
sāṃkhyāstvāhaṅkārike vāṅmanase /
annabhāgatāvacanaṃ tvasyānnasaṃbandhalakṣaṇārtham /
annopabhoge hi manaḥ svasthaṃ bhavati /
evaṃ vāco 'pi pāṭavena tejaḥsāmyamabhyūhanīyam /
tatredamupatiṣṭhate- #māṃsāditi# /
vāṅmanasa iti vaktavye māṃsādyabhidhānaṃ siddhena saha sādhyasyopanyāso dṛṣṭāntalābhāya /

children.text: yathā māṃsādi bhaumādyevaṃ vāṅmanase api taijasabhaume ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as flesh and the like are [products] of earth and the like, so too speech and mind are [products] of <s>tejas</s> (fire) and earth respectively — this is the meaning.
What is thereby stated is: to begin with, nothing apart from <s>Brahman</s> is eternal.

children.text: brahmajñānena sarvajñānapratijñāvyāghātāt, bahuśrutivirodhācca nāpyāhaṅkārikam, ahaṅkārasya sāṃkhyābhimatasya tattvasyāprāmāṇikatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because [if they were eternal,] the promise of 'through the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, everything is known' would be contradicted, and because there would be a conflict with the many <s>Śruti</s>s [asserting non-duality]. Nor are [speech and mind products] of <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, because the <s>ahaṅkāra</s> — the category (<s>tattva</s>) accepted by the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>s — lacks scriptural authority.

children.text: tasmādasati bādhake śrutirāñjasī nānyathā kathañcinnetumuciteti kañciddoṣamityuktaṃ taṃ doṣaṃ darśayannāha pūrvapakṣī- #yadi sarvameva iti# //21 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the absence of a sublating [cognition], the <s>Śruti</s> is to be taken in its straightforward sense, not otherwise interpreted in any manner — [this would involve] some defect. Showing that defect, the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> says: 'If everything indeed...' //21//

body.translated_text:
'Flesh and the like is [a product] of earth, as [indicated] by the [Śruti] words; and similarly for the other two' (<s>māṃsādi bhaumaṃ yathāśabdam itarayoś ca</s>).
Here, the author of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> has explained this <s>sūtra</s> as a supplement to the following <s>sūtra</s>, with the purport of showing the subject matter.
But it is also possible to say that it serves to remove a doubt.
Thus: in the [<s>Chāndogya</s>] passage 'That which is the subtlest portion of food — that is the mind; and that which is the subtlest portion of <s>tejas</s> (fire/light) — that is speech,' there is a disagreement between the <s>Kāṇāda</s>s (Vaiśeṣikas) and the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>s.
The <s>Kāṇāda</s>s declare the mind to be eternal.
But the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>s [hold that] speech and mind are [products] of <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego).
[They take] the statement about [the mind] being a portion of food as having the purpose of indicating [the mind's] connection with food — for when food is consumed, the mind becomes healthy.
Similarly, the excellence of speech should be inferred from [its] similarity with <s>tejas</s>.
To this, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] presents: 'Flesh and the like' (<s>māṃsādi</s>).
Instead of saying 'speech and mind,' [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says 'flesh and the like' — this is presenting the already-established alongside the to-be-established, for the purpose of obtaining an illustration.

body.text: #vaiśeṣyāttu tadvādastadvādaḥ# //22 //
body.translated_text: 'But because of distinction, it is so designated — that is the designation' (<s>vaiśeṣyāt tu tadvādas tadvādaḥ</s>). //22//

body.text: tribṛtkaraṇāviśeṣe 'pi yasya ca yatra bhūyastvaṃ tena tasya vyapadeśa ityarthaḥ //22 //
body.translated_text: Even though the tripartite combination (<s>trivṛtkaraṇa</s>) is without distinction [i.e., all elements are mixed], that [entity] in which a particular [element] predominates is designated by that [predominant element] — this is the meaning. //22//

body.text: iti śrīmadvācaspatimiśraviracite śrīmadbhagavatpādaśārīrakabhāṣyavibhāge bhāmatyāṃ dvitīyasyādhyāyasya caturthaḥ pādaḥ //4 //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the fourth <s>pāda</s> of the second <s>adhyāya</s> in the <s>Bhāmatī</s>, the elucidation of the revered <s>Śārīraka-Bhāṣya</s>, composed by the venerable <s>Vācaspati Miśra</s>. //4//

body.text: iti śrīmadbrahmasūtraśāṅkarabhāṣye 'virodhākhyo dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ ____________________________Adhyāya 3____________________________ /
body.translated_text:
Thus [ends] the second <s>adhyāya</s>, called <s>Avirodha</s> (Non-contradiction), in the <s>Śārīraka-Bhāṣya</s> of <s>Śaṅkara</s> on the <s>Brahmasūtra</s>s.
____________________________<s>Adhyāya</s> 3____________________________

body.text: #atha tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ# /
body.translated_text: Now the third <s>adhyāya</s> [begins].
