body.translated_text:
'In the interval [between death and rebirth], the [soul,] having obtained that [the subtle body], departs embraced [by the vital breaths and subtle elements] — [this is known] from the question and the explanation' (<s>tad-antara-pratipattau raṃhati saṃpariṣvaktaḥ praśna-nirūpaṇābhyām</s>).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>], showing the connection characterized by causal relation between the second and third <s>adhyāya</s>s and presenting a summary of the content for easy understanding, says: 'In the second <s>adhyāya</s>' — thus.
For by resolving the contradictions with <s>Smṛti</s>, logic (<s>nyāya</s>), and <s>Śruti</s>, the invalidity characterized by indetermination has been removed; and when that is firmly established, the third investigation [<s>adhyāya</s>] becomes possible — otherwise, being rootless, it would not be established.
To show the subordinate connection, it is said: 'Therein, the realities (<s>tattva</s>s) other than the <s>jīva</s> are the instruments of the <s>jīva</s>' — thus.
Having stated the summary of the <s>adhyāya</s>, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the summary of the <s>pāda</s>: 'In the first <s>pāda</s>, to begin with' — thus.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states its purpose: '[It serves] dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>)' — thus.
To prepare the ground for the preceding and following [topics], [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] builds the foundation: 'The <s>jīva</s>, accompanied by the chief vital breath (<s>mukhya prāṇa</s>)...' — 'Because the taking up of elements is not heard, unlike the taking up of instruments' — thus.
Here, since the <s>Śruti</s> on the taking up of instruments already implies — through the elemental nature of those instruments — the taking up of elements as well, the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> is commenced with the intention of [discussing] the taking up of elements beyond the instrument-taking.
[The prima facie view is:] If [the soul] were to depart taking the elements, that too would have been heard of through the <s>Śruti</s> on the taking up of instruments. But it is not heard. Therefore, [the soul] does not depart embraced by elements, but only embraced by instruments.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s> answers:] Regarding a matter that is knowable only through scripture, the absence of [scriptural statement] is not sufficient to determine the absence of the thing to be known.
[The prima facie view continues:] Nor is it correct to postulate the departure embraced by elements based on the impossibility of beginning another body otherwise — so [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Because elemental matter is readily available everywhere' (<s>sulabhāś ca sarvatra bhūtamātrāḥ</s>).
'The celestial realm, rain' (<s>dyu-parjanya</s>) — thus.
For here, the <s>Śruti</s>, intending to teach the meditation on the <s>Agnihotra</s> ritual-merit (<s>apūrva</s>) — transformed into [the stages of] <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) and the like in five-fold division, as [entities] to be offered in the fires beginning with the celestial realm — as a means of attaining the <s>uttara-mārga</s> (northern path), says: 'That yonder world, O <s>Gautama</s>, is the fire' and so on.
Here, the evening and morning <s>Agnihotra</s> oblations, having been offered — in the preparatory [stage] consisting of milk and the like, transformed through <s>śraddhā</s> into the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire's fuel, smoke, flame, embers, and sparks, and also transformed into the agent and other case-relations — gradually ascending through the intermediate space, enter the celestial world as subtle elemental [substances]. Being connected with liquid substance such as milk-like water, they are designated by the word 'water' (<s>ap</s>); and being caused by <s>śraddhā</s> (faith), they are designated by the word '<s>śraddhā</s>.'
Of these two oblations, the substratum is fire, and the fuel, smoke, flame, embers, and sparks are mentioned figuratively.
'That yonder celestial world, O <s>Gautama</s>, is the fire.' Just as the <s>Āhavanīya</s> is the substratum of the <s>Agnihotra</s>, so too the celestial world is the substratum of the subtle waters in the form of <s>Agnihotra</s>-oblation-transformations designated by the word '<s>śraddhā</s>.'
Of this [fire], the sun alone is the fuel, for illuminated by it, the celestial world blazes — hence, from the kindling, [it is called] fuel. The rays of the sun are the smoke, since, like [smoke] from fuel, the rays arise from the sun.
The day is the flame — because of the general similarity of illumination and because [day] is an effect of the sun.
The moon is the embers.
In this fire, the gods — being the vital breaths of the sacrificer, having the form of <s>Agni</s> and the like, on the cosmic (<s>adhidaiva</s>) level — offer <s>śraddhā</s>; and <s>śraddhā</s> has been explained.
'Rain (<s>Parjanya</s>) indeed, O <s>Gautama</s>, is the fire.' <s>Parjanya</s> is the particular deity presiding over the instruments of rain.
Of it, wind alone is the fuel, for <s>Parjanya</s> — [as] the fire — is kindled by wind, since rain is observed when strong winds prevail.
Cloud is the smoke — because of being an effect of fire and because of resemblance to smoke.
Lightning is the flame — because of the general similarity of luminosity.
Thunderbolt is the embers — because of hardness and because of connection with lightning.
Thunder is the sparks — because of the general similarity of being scattered.
In that [fire], the gods — the vital breaths of the sacrificer having the form of <s>Agni</s> — offer <s>Soma</s>, the king; from that oblation of <s>Soma</s>, rain comes into being.
What is thereby stated is: the waters called '<s>śraddhā</s>,' having entered the celestial world as oblations, having been transformed into the form of the moon, in the second cycle enter the <s>Parjanya</s>-fire as oblations and are transformed into rain.
'The earth indeed, O <s>Gautama</s>, is the fire.' Of this fire called earth, the year alone is the fuel — for kindled by the passage of time called the year, the earth becomes fit for the production of rice and the like.
Space is the smoke — for space appears as if rising from the fire of earth.
Night is the flame — being dark like the earth itself, night, through its darkness, is a flame appropriate to the fire [of earth], as a flame is appropriate to [its] fire.
The directions are the embers — because of the observation that, when the flame-like night subsides, the calm and clear directions appear, as embers [appear when the flame dies down].
The sub-directions are the sparks — because of their similarity in being small.
In that fire, the waters — having come through the sequence of <s>śraddhā</s>-<s>Soma</s> transformation, transformed into rain — the gods offer; from that oblation, food — rice, barley, and the like — comes into being.
'The person (<s>puruṣa</s>) indeed, O <s>Gautama</s>, is the fire.' Of him, speech alone is the fuel — for by speech, stationed in the eight locations beginning with the palate, manifesting phonemes, words, and sentences in sequence and thereby illuminating the entire realm of meanings, [the person] is kindled.
Breath (<s>prāṇa</s>) is the smoke — because, like smoke, it issues from the mouth.
The tongue is the flame — because of the similarity of redness.
The eyes are the embers — because of being the locus of radiance.
The ears are the sparks — because of the similarity of being scattered.
Those very waters — having come through the sequence of <s>śraddhā</s> and other transformations, transformed into the form of rice and the like — being offered in the fire of the person, their transformation becomes semen.
'The woman (<s>yoṣā</s>) indeed, O <s>Gautama</s>, is the fire.' Of her, the lap (<s>upastha</s>) alone is the fuel — for by it she is kindled for the production of sons and the like. The invitation [to sexual union] is the smoke — because the invitation arises from [the desire for] the woman. Or alternatively, the body-hair is the smoke. The vulva is the flame — because of its redness.
What [the couple] does internally — sexual intercourse — those are the embers.
The delights — the small pleasures — are the sparks, because of their smallness.

body.text:
tasminnetasminnagnau devā reto juhvati tasyā āhutergarbhaḥ saṃbhavati /
evaṃ śraddhāsomavarṣānnaretohavakrameṇa yoṣāgniṃ prāpyāpo garbhākhyā bhavanti /
tatrāpsamavāyitvādāpaḥ puruṣavacaso bhavanti pañcamyāmāhutāviti /
yataḥ pañcamyāmāhutāvāpaḥ puruṣavacaso bhavanti tasmādadbhiḥ pariveṣṭito jīvo rahatīti gamyate /
etaduktaṃ bhavati-śraddhāśabdavācyā āpa ityagre vakṣyati tāsāṃ trivṛtkatatayā tejo 'nnāvinābhāvenābgrahaṇena tejonnayorapi saṃgraha ityetadapi vakṣyate /
yadyapyetāvatāpi bhūtaveṣṭitasya jīvasya raṃhaṇaṃ nāvagamyate tejobannānāṃ pañcamyāmāhutau puruṣavacastvamātraśravaṇāt, tathāpīṣṭādikāriṇāṃ dhūmādinā pitṛyāṇena pathā candralokaprāptikathanaparayā 'ākāśāccandramasameṣa somo rāṭ' iti śrutyā saha 'śraddhāṃ juhvati tasyā āhuteḥ somo rājā saṃbhavati' ityasyāḥ śruteḥ mānatvādgamyate bhūtapariṣvakto raṃhatīti /
tathāhi-yā evāpo hutā dvitīyasyāmāhutau somabhāvaṃ gatāstābhireṣa pariṣvakto jīva iṣṭādikārī candrabhūyaṃ gataścandralokaṃ prāpta iti /
nanu svatantrā āpaḥ śraddhādikrameṇa somabhāvamāpnuvantu tābhirapariṣvakta eva tu jīvaḥ sendriyamātro gatvā somabhāvamanubhavatu /
ko doṣaḥ /
ayaṃ doṣaḥ /
yataḥ śrutisāmānyātikrama iti /
evaṃ hi śrutisāmānyaṃ kalpeta yadi yena rūpeṇa yena ca krameṇāpāṃ somabhāvastenaiva jīvasyāpi somabhāvo bhavet /
anyathā tu na śrutisāmānyaṃ syāt /
tasmātpariṣvaktāpariṣvaktaraṃhaṇaviśaye śrutisāmānyānurodhena pariṣvaktaraṃhaṇaṃ niścīyate /
ato dadhipayaḥprabhṛtayo dravabhūyastvādāpo hutāḥ sūkṣmībhūtā iṣṭādikāriṇamāśritā nondhanena vidhinā dehe hūyamāne hutāḥ satya āhutimapya iṣṭādikāriṇaṃ pariveṣṭya svargaṃ lokaṃ nayantīti /
codayati- #nanvanyā śrutiriti# /
ayamarthaḥ-evaṃ hi sūkṣmadehapariṣvakto raṃhet yadyasya sthūlaṃ śarīraṃ raṃhato na bhavet /
asti tvasya vartamānasthūlaśarīrayoga ādehāntaraprāptestṛṇajalāyukānidarśanena, tasmānnidarśanaśrutivirodhānna sūkṣmadehapariṣvakto raṃhatīti /
pariharati- #tatrāpīti# /
na tāvatparamātmanaḥ saṃsaraṇasaṃbhavaḥ, tasya nityaśuddhabuddhamuktasvabhāvatvāt /
kintu jīvānām /
paramātmaiva copādhikalpitāvacchedo jīva ityākhyāyate, tasya ca dehendriyāderupādheḥ pradeśikatvānna tatra san dehāntaraṃ gantumarhati /
tasmātsūkṣmadehapariṣvakto raṃhatikarmopasthāpitaḥ pratipattavyaḥ prāptavyo yo dehastadviṣayāyā bhāvanāyā utpādanāyā dīrghībhāvamātraṃ jalūkayopamīyate /
sāṃkhyānāṃ kalpanāmāha- #vyāpināṃ karaṇānāmiti# /
āhaṅkārikatvātkaraṇānāmahaṅkārasya ca jaganmaṇḍalavyāpitvātkaraṇānāmapi vyāpitetyarthaḥ /
bauddhānāṃ kalpanāmāha- #kevalasyaivātmana iti# /
ālayavijñānasaṃtāna ātmā tasya vṛttiḥ ṣaṭ pravṛttivijñānāni /
paścendriyāṇi tu cakṣurādīni abhinavāni jāyante /
kaṇabhukklpanāmāha- #mana eva ceti# /

children.translated_text: The place of enjoyment — the abode of enjoyment — means a new body.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the <s>Digambara</s> (Jain) position: 'The <s>jīva</s> alone leaps' — thus.
By the word 'and the like' (<s>ādi</s>), [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] includes the position of the <s>Lokāyatika</s>s (materialists).

children.text: te hi śarīrātmavādino bhasmībhāvamātmana āhurna kasyacidgamanamiti //1 //
children.translated_text: For they, being proponents of the body-as-self doctrine, declare that the self simply turns to ashes — no one goes anywhere. //1//

body.translated_text:
'In this fire — the woman — the gods offer the semen as an oblation; from that oblation the embryo comes into being.'
Thus, through the sequence of oblations — faith, <s>Soma</s>, rain, food, and semen — having reached the fire that is the woman, the waters become what is called the embryo.
Therein, since the waters are the material cause (<s>samavāyin</s>), they become 'possessing human speech' (<s>puruṣavacas</s>) in the fifth oblation — thus.
Since in the fifth oblation the waters become possessing human speech, it is understood that the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), enveloped by the waters, transmigrates.
What is stated amounts to this: The word <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) denotes waters — this will be said later. And since those [waters] are subject to <s>trivṛtkaraṇa</s> (tripartite combination), by the mention of water, fire and food are also necessarily included since they are inseparable — this too will be said later.
Although even from this much alone the transmigration of the <s>jīva</s> enveloped by the elements is not understood — since only the statement that the waters become possessing human speech in the fifth oblation is heard — nevertheless, from the authority of this <s>Śruti</s> together with the <s>Śruti</s> that narrates the attainment of the lunar world through the path of the fathers via smoke and the like for those who have performed sacrifices and the like — 'From space [they go] to the moon; this is <s>Soma</s>, the king' — it is understood that [the <s>jīva</s>] transmigrates enveloped by the elements.
For: the very waters that, having been offered as the second oblation, attained the state of <s>Soma</s> — enveloped by those [waters], this <s>jīva</s>, the performer of sacrifices and the like, having attained the state of the moon, reached the lunar world — thus.
One might object: Let the waters independently attain the state of <s>Soma</s> through the sequence of faith and the like; but the <s>jīva</s>, consisting merely of the senses, without being enveloped by those [waters], goes and experiences the state of <s>Soma</s>.
What is the defect [in this]?
This is the defect: Because there would be a transgression of the generality of the <s>Śruti</s>.
For the generality of the <s>Śruti</s> would be achieved only if the <s>jīva</s>'s attainment of <s>Soma</s>-hood were in the same form and by the same sequence as the waters' attainment of <s>Soma</s>-hood.
But otherwise, there would be no generality of the <s>Śruti</s>.
Therefore, in the matter of whether the transmigration is enveloped or unenveloped, in conformity with the generality of the <s>Śruti</s>, [the conclusion that] transmigration is enveloped is determined.
Hence, curd, milk, and other liquid substances — having been offered [in ritual], having become subtle — being predominantly water, having attached themselves to the performer of sacrifices and the like, having been offered in the funeral-fire (<s>udhana</s>) when the body is being cremated, having attained the [state of] oblation, having enveloped the performer of sacrifices and the like, they lead [him] to the heavenly world — thus.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises an objection: 'But another <s>Śruti</s>' — thus.
The meaning is this: The <s>jīva</s> would transmigrate enveloped by the subtle body if it did not possess a gross body while transmigrating.
But it does possess a current gross body until the attainment of another body, as illustrated by the analogy of grass and the leech. Therefore, because of the contradiction with the illustrative <s>Śruti</s>, [the <s>jīva</s>] does not transmigrate enveloped by a subtle body.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] resolves: 'Even there' — thus.
To begin with, transmigration is not possible for <s>Paramātman</s> (the Supreme Self), because of Its eternally pure, awakened, and liberated nature.
Rather, [transmigration belongs] to the <s>jīva</s>s (individual souls).
And <s>Paramātman</s> Itself, conditioned by the superimposed limitation [of <s>upādhi</s>s], is called the <s>jīva</s>; and since the <s>upādhi</s> — consisting of body, senses, and the like — is localized (<s>pradeśika</s>), [the <s>jīva</s>] being there [in that location] cannot go to another body.
Therefore, [the <s>jīva</s>] should be understood as transmigrating enveloped by the subtle body, brought forward by <s>karma</s>. The body that is to be obtained — the object of the <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive force) that is to be generated — is compared to the leech only in the sense of [the bhāvanā's] extension (<s>dīrghībhāva</s>).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> position: 'Of the all-pervading sense-organs' — thus.
The meaning is: Since the sense-organs are products of <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), and since <s>ahaṅkāra</s> pervades the entire world-sphere, the sense-organs too are all-pervading — thus.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the Buddhist position: 'Of the mere self alone' — thus.
The <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store-consciousness) continuum is the self; its functions are the six <s>pravṛttivijñāna</s>s (active consciousnesses).
But the later sense-organs — sight and the like — arise anew.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the <s>Kaṇabhuj</s> (<s>Vaiśeṣika</s>) position: 'The mind alone' — thus.

body.text:
codayati- #nanūdāhṛtābhyāmiti# /
atra sūtreṇottaramāha- #tryātmakatvāttu bhūyastvāt# /
tejasaḥ kāryamaśitapītāhāraparipākaḥ /
apāṃ snehasvedādi /
pṛthivyāḥ kāryaṃ gandhādi /
yastu gandhasvedapākaprāṇāvakāśadānadarśanāddehasya pāñcabhautikatvaṃ paśyaṃstejobannātmakatvena tryātmakatve na parituṣyati, taṃ pratyāha- #punaśca tryātmaka iti# /

children.translated_text: Because of the three-constituent nature (<s>tridhātutva</s>) — the body being sustained by the three constituents of wind (<s>vāta</s>), bile (<s>pitta</s>), and phlegm (<s>śleṣman</s>).

children.text: ato na sa deho bhūtāntarāṇi pratyākhyāya kevalābhiradbhirārabdhuṃ śakyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, that body cannot be constructed from waters alone, rejecting the other elements.
Then why the restriction to the mention of water alone? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Therefore, with reference to predominance' — thus.

children.text: pṛthivīdhātuvarjamitarateja ādyapekṣayā kāryasya śarīrasya lohitādidravabhūyastvāttatkaraṇayoścopādānanimittayordravabhūyastvādapāṃ puruṣavacastvoktirna punarbhūtāntaranirāsārthā //2 //
children.translated_text: Excluding the earth-element, because of the predominance of the liquid [element] in the body — [evidenced by] blood and the like — relative to fire and the rest, and because of the predominance of the liquid [element] in its two causes — the material and efficient — the statement of 'possessing human speech' is made with reference to water; but it is not intended to exclude the other elements. //2//

body.translated_text:
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises an objection: 'But from the two cited [<s>Śruti</s>s]' — thus.
Here, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] answers with the <s>sūtra</s>: 'But because of being constituted of three elements, and because of predominance' (<s>tryātmakatvāttu bhūyastvāt</s>).
The effect of fire (<s>tejas</s>) is the digestion of ingested food and drink.
The effect of water (<s>āpas</s>) is moisture, sweat, and the like.
The effect of earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>) is smell and the like.
But to one who, seeing the five-element nature of the body from [the evidence of] smell, sweat, digestion, <s>prāṇa</s>, space-provision, and visibility, is not satisfied with the three-element constitution of fire, water, and food — to that person [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'And again, of three elements' — thus.

body.text: #prāṇagateśca# /

children.text: prāṇānāṃ jīvaddehe sāśrayatvamavagataṃ gacchati jīvaddehe tadanuvidhāyinaḥ prāṇā api gacchantīti dṛṣṭam /
children.translated_text: It is understood that the <s>prāṇa</s>s have their locus in the living body; when the living body departs, the <s>prāṇa</s>s, which follow it, also depart — this is observed.
Therefore, when departing from the body composed of six sheaths (<s>ṣāṭkauśika</s>), they depart in something that departs.

children.text: sa caiṣāmanuvidheyaḥ sūkṣmo deho bhūtendriyamaya iti gamyate /
children.translated_text: And that which they follow is understood to be a subtle body composed of elements and sense-organs.

For [the <s>prāṇa</s>s] are not observed to have their locus in the sense-organs alone, such that [their] departure could be accounted for as [being located] in the <s>tanmātra</s>s (subtle elements) alone. //3//

body.translated_text: 'And because of the departure of the <s>prāṇa</s>s' — thus.

body.text: #agnyādigatiśruteriti cenna bhāktatvāt# /

children.text: śrāvite 'pi spaṣṭe jīvasya prāṇaiḥ saha gamane 'gnyādigatiśaṅkā śrutivirodhotthāpanārthā /
children.translated_text: Even though the departure of the <s>jīva</s> together with the <s>prāṇa</s>s is clearly stated in <s>Śruti</s>, the objection regarding departure to fire and the like is raised for the purpose of generating a [seeming] contradiction with <s>Śruti</s>.
For here, the departure of hair and body-hair to herbs and trees must first be accepted as figurative, because of the contradiction with observation.

And thus, since [the departure of the <s>prāṇa</s>s to fire and the like] falls in between those [figurative statements], for those [too], because of the contradiction with <s>Śruti</s>, figurative meaning alone is appropriate.
And the figurative meaning has been stated as [referring to] the cessation of the function [of those organs]. //4//

body.translated_text: 'If [it be said that] because of the <s>Śruti</s> of departure to fire and the like — no, because of its being figurative' — thus.

body.text:
#prathame 'śravaṇāditi cenna tā eva hyupapatteḥ# /
pañcamyāmāhutāvapāṃ puruṣavacastvaprakāre pṛṣṭe prathamāyāmāhutau anapāṃ śraddhāyā hetavyatābhidhānasaṃbhavaddhamanupapannaṃ ca /

children.text: nahi yathā paśvādibhyo hṛdayādayo 'vayavā avadāya niṣkṛṣya hūyante, evaṃ śraddhā buddhiprasādalakṣaṇā niṣkraṣṭuṃ vā hotuṃ vā śakyate /
children.translated_text: For just as the limbs such as the heart and the like are separated and extracted from animals and the like and then offered, faith — characterized as the clarity of the intellect — can neither be extracted nor offered in that manner.
Nor is the natural conformity of effect to cause appropriate in this way.
Therefore, the word <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) is used figuratively for water — thus.
For this very reason, the <s>Śruti</s> [says]: 'Waters indeed are faith' (<s>āpo hātmai</s>). //5//

body.translated_text:
'If [it be objected that] in the first [oblation] there is no mention [of water] — no, because those very [waters] are [meant], since it is tenable' — thus.
When the mode of waters becoming possessing human speech in the fifth oblation has been asked about, in the first oblation — where the offering of faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) rather than water is stated — [the offering of water] is both possible and [yet] not directly established.

children.translated_text: 'If [it be said that this is] because it is unheard — no, because of the understanding [that it applies] to those who have performed sacrifices and the like' — thus.
The meaning of this has already been stated above.

children.text: agnihotre ṣaṭsūtkrāntigatipratiṣṭhātṛptipunarāvṛttilokapratyutthāyiṣvagnisamiddhūmārciraṅgāravisphuliṅgeṣu praśnāḥ ṣaṭ, teṣāṃ yaḥ samāhāraḥ ṣaṇṇāṃ sā ṣaṭpraśnī, tasyā nirūpaṇaṃ prativacanam //6 //
children.translated_text: In the <s>Agnihotra</s>, regarding the six [stages] — departing, going, remaining, being satisfied, returning, and the world arising — [and] regarding fire being kindled, smoke, flame, embers, and sparks — there are six questions. The collection of these six [questions] is the 'six-fold questioning' (<s>ṣaṭpraśnī</s>); its examination is the answer. //6//

body.text:
sūtrāntaramavatārayituṃ śaṅkate- #kathaṃ punariti /
somaṃ rājānamāpyāyasvāpakṣīyasvetyevamenāṃstatra bhakṣayantīti# /
kriyāsamabhihāreṇāpyāyanāpakṣayau yathā somasya tathā bhakṣayanti somamayāṃllokānityarthaḥ /
ata uttaraṃ paṭhati- #bhāktaṃ vānātmavisttvāttathāhi darśayati# /
karmajanitaphalopabhogakartā hyadhikārī na punarupabhogyastasmāccandrasālokyamupagatānāṃ devādibhikṣyatve 'svargakāmo yajeta' iti yāgabhāvanāyaḥ kartrapekṣitopāyatārūpavidhiśrutivirodhādannaśabdo bhoktṛṇāmeva satāṃ devopājīvitāmātreṇa bhākto gamayitavyo na tu carvaṇanigaraṇābhyāṃ mukhya iti /
atraivārthe śrutyantaraṃ saṃgacchata ityāha- #tathāhi darśayati# /
śrutiranātmavigāmanātmavittvādeva paśuvaddevopabhogyatāṃ na tu carvaṇīyatayā /
yathā hi balīvardādayo bhuñjanā api svaphalaṃ svāmino halādivahanenopakurvāṇā bhogyāḥ, evaṃ paramatattvamavidvāṃsa iṣṭādikāriṇa iha dadhipayaḥpuroṭāśādināmuṣmiṃśca loke paricārakatayā devānāmupabhogyā iti śrutyarthaḥ /
athavā #anātmavittvāttathāhi darśayati#ityasyānyā vyākhyā /
ātmavit pañcāgnividyāvit na ātmavit anātmavit /
yo hi pañcāgnividyāṃ na vedaṃ taṃ devā bhakṣayantīti nindyate pañcāgnividyāṃ stotuṃ tasyā eva prakṛtatvāt /
tadanenopacārasya projanamuktam /

children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the ground for the figurative usage as the impossibility [of the literal meaning]: 'For thus [the <s>Śruti</s>] shows' — thus.
The <s>Śruti</s> [shows] the enjoyer-status [of the <s>jīva</s>].
'Having experienced glory in the world of <s>Soma</s>' — thus.
The rest is of transparent meaning. //7//

body.translated_text:
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises an objection in order to introduce another <s>sūtra</s>: 'But how?' — thus.
'Having reached <s>Soma</s>, the king — "Grow! Diminish!" — thus they consume him there' — thus.
By the simultaneous action (<s>kriyāsamabhihāra</s>) of growing and diminishing, just as with <s>Soma</s>, so too do they consume — they consume the <s>Soma</s>-like worlds — this is the meaning.
Hence [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] reads the next [<s>sūtra</s>]: 'It is figurative, because of the absence of Self-nature; for thus [the <s>Śruti</s>] shows' (<s>bhāktaṃ vānātmavittvāttathāhi darśayati</s>).
For the performer of <s>karma</s> — who has generated fruits through <s>karma</s> — is the agent of enjoyment, not the one to be enjoyed. Therefore, when those who have attained co-residence with the moon (<s>candrasālokya</s>) are said to be consumed by the gods, [this contradicts] the injunctive <s>Śruti</s> 'One who desires heaven should sacrifice' — which has the character of a rule (<s>vidhi</s>) specifying the means desired by the agent. Because of this contradiction, the word 'food' (<s>anna</s>) should be understood figuratively, in the sense of merely being sustained by the gods, even though they are experiencers — not in the primary sense of being chewed and swallowed.
To show that another <s>Śruti</s> confirms this very meaning, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'For thus [the <s>Śruti</s>] shows' — thus.
The <s>Śruti</s> shows [that their being consumed is] due to not being a knower of the Self (<s>anātmavittva</s>) — that is, their being subject to the gods' enjoyment like cattle, not as something to be chewed.
For just as oxen and the like, even while eating themselves, serve their master by pulling the plough and the like, and are thus 'enjoyed' [i.e., used], similarly those who do not know the supreme truth — the performers of sacrifices and the like — are 'enjoyed' by the gods: in this world through curd, milk, and rice-cakes [offered as oblations], and in the other world through servitude — this is the meaning of the <s>Śruti</s>.
Alternatively, there is another interpretation of 'Because of not being a knower of the Self; for thus [the <s>Śruti</s>] shows.'
A knower of the Self is one who knows the <s>Pañcāgnividyā</s> (doctrine of the five fires); one who does not know it is a non-knower of the Self.
One who does not know the <s>Pañcāgnividyā</s> — 'him the gods consume' — this is stated as a censure, in order to praise the <s>Pañcāgnividyā</s>, since that alone is the topic at hand.
By this, the purpose of the figurative usage has been stated.

yathā bhāṇḍasthe madhuni sarpiṣi vā kṣālite 'pi bhāṇḍalepakaṃ taccheṣaṃ madhu vā sarpirvā na kṣālayituṃ śakyamiti dṛṣṭamevaṃ tadanusārādetadapi pratipattavyam /
