evakāre prayoktavye ivakāro guḍajihvikayā prayuktaḥ /
śabdaikagamyer'the na sāmānyatodṛṣṭānumānāvasara ityarthaḥ /
śeṣamatirohitārtham /
pūrvapakṣahetumanubhāṣate- #yadapyuktaṃ prāyaṇamiti# /
dūṣayati- #tadapyanuśayasadbhāveti# /
ramaṇīyacaraṇā kapūyacaraṇā ityādikayānuśayapratipādanaparayā śrutyā viruddhamityarthaḥ /
#apicetyādi# /
iha janmani hi paryāyeṇa sukhaduḥkhe bhujyamāne dṛśyete /
yugapaccedekapraghaṭṭakena prāyaṇena sukhaduḥkhaphalāni karmāṇi vyajyeran /
yugapadeva tatphalāni bhujyeran /
tasmādupabhogaparyāyadarśanādbalīyasā durbalasyābhibhavaḥ kalpanīyaḥ /
evaṃ viruddhajātinimittopabhogaphaleṣvapi karmasu draṣṭavyam /
na cābhivyaktaṃ ca karma phalaṃ na datta iti ca saṃbhavati /
phalopajanābhimukhyaṃ hi karmaṇāmabhivyaktiḥ /

children.text: apica prāṇasyābhivyañjakatve svargarakatatiryagyonigatānāṃ jantūnāṃ tasmiñjanmani karmasvanadhikārānnāpūrvakarmopajanaḥ pūrvakṛtasya kramāśyasya prāyaṇābhivyaktatayā phalopabhogena prakṣayānnāsti teṣāṃ karmāśya iti na te saṃsareyuḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, if the time of death (<s>prāyaṇa</s>) is the manifester [of all <s>karma</s>], then for beings gone to heaven, the <s>Rākṣasa</s>-realm, or animal births — having no eligibility for <s>karma</s> in that birth — there would be no production of new <s>karma</s>; and since their previously accumulated <s>karmāśaya</s> (latent karmic impressions), being manifested at death and exhausted through the enjoyment of their fruit, [would leave] no <s>karmāśaya</s> remaining — they would not transmigrate further.
Nor would they be liberated, due to the absence of Self-knowledge — thus [they would be in] a wretched and inauspicious state indeed!

children.text: kiñca svasamavetameva prāyamenābhivyajyate 'pūrvaṃ na parasamavetaṃ, yena pitrādigatena karmaṇā varteranniti /
children.translated_text: Moreover, generally what is manifested is only what inheres in oneself, not what inheres in another — so one could not operate on the basis of <s>karma</s> inherited from one's father and the like.
The rest is easy to understand. //8//

body.translated_text:
'#When [the fruit of] the performed [karma] has been exhausted, [the soul] descends with residual impression (<s>anuśaya</s>), because of <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>, in that manner alone and not otherwise; having dwelt [in the lunar world] until the exhaustion of [karma]#' (<s>kṛtātyaye 'nuśayavān iṣṭasmṛtibhyāṃ yathetam anevaṃ ca yāvat saṃpātam uṣitvā</s>).
Because of the limiting word 'until' (<s>yāvat</s>).
'#Whatever [karma] one performs here#' (<s>yat kiñceh akarot</s>) — and because of the hearing that 'whatever karma one performs here — [of that] having reached the end,' and because the time of death (<s>prāyaṇa</s>) manifests all <s>karma</s> by a single impulse.
Indeed, it is not reasonable that when the cause of manifestation is common, the manifestation would be restricted [to only some karmas].
And manifestation means the directing of [<s>karma</s>] toward yielding its fruit; therefore all <s>karma</s> must be experienced [in the form of its fruit].
And <s>karma</s> contradicts its own fruit [i.e., exhausted <s>karma</s> cannot produce fruit again].
Therefore, from <s>Śruti</s> and from logical fitness, the descent is for those free from residual impression alone — those whose enjoyment has been experienced — not from <s>karma</s>.
And <s>ācāra</s> (conduct) and <s>karma</s> (action) have a well-known distinction in <s>Śruti</s>.
'As one acts, as one conducts oneself, so one becomes' (<s>yathākārī yathācārī tathā bhavati</s>).
And thus, 'Those of pleasant conduct' and 'those of foul conduct' — [the <s>Śruti</s>] teaches conduct alone as the cause of [the type of] birth, not <s>karma</s>.
Or let both — conduct and <s>karma</s> — be denoted [by the word <s>caraṇa</s>]; even so, without distinction, the residual impression [applies to both]. Nevertheless, although this performer of <s>iṣṭa</s> (Vedic sacrifices) and <s>pūrta</s> (public works) is himself free from residual impression — since his enjoyment has been experienced — still, by virtue of the residual impression inherited from his father and others, he will experience the ripening of that [inherited <s>karma</s>] — birth, lifespan, and enjoyment — after descending from the lunar world.
For it is remembered (<s>Smṛti</s>) that one person's good and bad deeds cause another who is connected to him to share in their fruits — as in 'He whose wife drinks liquor falls [from his position] with half his body' and the like.
Likewise, in the <s>Śrāddha</s> rite, the <s>Vaiśvānarī Iṣṭi</s>, and the like, there are <s>Śruti</s>s about the fruits going to the father, son, and others.
Therefore, in conformity with the opening [statement] 'until the exhaustion [of karma]' and following the other <s>Śruti</s> 'whatever [one] does here,' the quality of 'pleasant conduct' should be understood as figuratively attributed to the performer of <s>iṣṭa</s> and <s>pūrta</s> through [its] connection with another [i.e., the inherited karma].
And thus, the descent is for those free from residual impression alone, whose enjoyment has been experienced — this being the prima facie conclusion, it is said:
[The souls] descend with residual impression even after the <s>karma</s> whose fruit has been enjoyed has passed away.
Why? From <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s> (<s>dṛṣṭasmṛtibhyām</s>).
<s>Śruti</s>, being directly perceived [as scripture], is referred to by the word '<s>dṛṣṭa</s>' (seen).
And <s>Smṛti</s> has been cited.
Alternatively, by the word '<s>dṛṣṭa</s>' is meant enjoyment — of higher and lower [types].
The intent is this: 'Those of foul conduct,' 'those of pleasant conduct' — this qualifies those who have descended.
And when the primary meaning is possible, it is not proper to resort to figurative meaning merely through [association with] a connected person.
Nor is it correct [to say] that the primary meaning is impossible because of contradiction with the opening [statement] and with another <s>Śruti</s>.
For even with reference to <s>iṣṭa-pūrta karma</s> that has already yielded its fruit, the words 'until' (<s>yāvat</s>) and 'whatever' (<s>yat kiñcit</s>) are justifiable.
For 'one should offer the <s>agnihotra</s> as long as one lives' — the [word] 'as long as one lives' does not prescribe oblation even during meals, travel, and the like, but only with reference to the evening and morning times.
[The opponent says:] This is because of the force of the prescription of evening and morning times; and because time, being not-to-be-adopted [as a subsidiary], being a non-subsidiary, still enters [the prescription] as a condition (<s>nimitta</s>) — [the word 'yāvat'] is thus [restricted].
No.
Here too, because of the conformity with the primary meaning of 'those of pleasant conduct' and the like, that [restriction of 'yāvat'] is justified.
Then should the opening [statement] be contracted in conformity with the conclusion?
No, it is said.
For that [opening word 'yāvat'] cannot have an unrestricted scope even in conformity with the conclusion.
For not all the 'descents' (<s>saṃpāta</s>s) of all persons are exhausted through the enjoyment of [only] the performer of <s>iṣṭa</s> and the like there [in the lunar world].
Because of the absurd consequence that the <s>karmāśaya</s>s (latent impressions of <s>karma</s>) residing in other persons would be exhausted through his enjoyment.
And because the removal — through enjoyment in the lunar sphere — of <s>karmāśaya</s>s long-since-enjoyed and [hence] non-existent [would be pointless].
And thus, the <s>Śruti</s> [word 'yāvat'], contracting on its own, accepts even the contraction entailed by conformity with the conclusion.
By this, 'whatever [one] does here' is also explained.
Moreover, the performer of <s>iṣṭa</s> and <s>pūrta</s> [karma] in this birth did not perform only those; he also earned the <s>apūrva</s> (unseen merit) of animal-tending by, for example, drawing water through cow-milking.
Likewise, day and night, through activities of speech, mind, and body, having accumulated merit and demerit to be enjoyed here and hereafter — the [merit/demerit] to be enjoyed in the mortal world and elsewhere cannot be appropriately enjoyed in the lunar world.
And the destruction of residual impression — which contradicts its own fruit — is not possible without either expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) or Self-knowledge.
Therefore, it is fitting that he descends with that residual impression, being one who possesses residual impression.
Nor will the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> say that the <s>karmāśaya</s> (latent impression of <s>karma</s>) belongs to a single birth alone.
But others, thinking that the doubt about descent upon the exhaustion of all <s>karma</s> is baseless, have explained the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> differently — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Some, to begin with, say#.'
Residual impression (<s>anuśaya</s>) here means the remainder of <s>karma</s> that has already yielded its fruit.
Here the question is: Do [the souls] return to this world because of the remainder of <s>iṣṭa-pūrta karma</s> that has yielded its fruit, or do they return after having completely exhausted those [<s>iṣṭa-pūrta karmas</s>] through enjoyment, [driven] by un-enjoyed <s>karma</s>?
Therein — since <s>iṣṭa</s> and the like have been eradicated root and all through enjoyment, [the souls] are free from residual impression and return due to un-enjoyed <s>karma</s> — this being the prima facie conclusion, it is said: They return with residual impression indeed.
Why? From observation (<s>dṛṣṭānusārāt</s>).
Just as when honey or clarified butter stored in a vessel is washed out, the residual smearing of honey or clarified butter on the vessel cannot be washed away — thus is observed; and by analogy with that, this too should be understood.
And merely by virtue of the residual, [the soul], even though wishing to remain in the lunar sphere, cannot remain.
Just as a servant, surrounded by retinues of elephant-riders, horsemen, and foot-soldiers, serving a great king, by the force of time, [when reduced to] only an umbrella and sandals remaining, can no longer serve — this is observed. And worldly <s>Smṛti</s> (common understanding) is rooted in that.
Thus, from observation and <s>Smṛti</s>, they descend with residual impression indeed.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes this: '#And this is not so#.'
The particle '<s>iva</s>' (like) is used in place of '<s>eva</s>' (indeed) — through a dialectal pronunciation (<s>guḍajihvikā</s>).
The meaning is: where the meaning is accessible only through scripture, there is no scope for inference by analogy (<s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s>).
The rest has transparent meaning.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] restates the prima facie reason: '#What was also said about the time of death (<s>prāyaṇa</s>)#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes: '#That too [is refuted] because of the existence of residual impression#.'
The meaning is: this is contradicted by the <s>Śruti</s> that teaches residual impression — 'Those of pleasant conduct,' 'those of foul conduct.'
'#Moreover#' — in this very birth, pleasure and suffering are seen being experienced in alternation.
If all <s>karmas</s> were manifested simultaneously by a single impulse at the time of death, [then] their fruits would also be enjoyed simultaneously.
Therefore, from the observation of alternation in enjoyment, the overpowering of the weaker by the stronger must be postulated.
The same should be seen regarding <s>karmas</s> whose enjoyment-fruits are [of types that] contradict each other [regarding] the kind of birth.
And it is not possible that <s>karma</s> is manifested yet does not yield its fruit.
For the manifestation of <s>karmas</s> is their orientation toward the production of fruit.

children.translated_text: '#If [it be said that <s>caraṇa</s> means] conduct — no, because it serves as an indicator (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>), so [holds] <s>Kārṣṇājini</s>#.'

children.text: anena niranuśayā evāvarohantīti pūrvapakṣabījaṃ nigūḍhamuddhāṭya nirasyati /
children.translated_text: By this, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] uncovers and refutes the hidden seed of the prima facie view that those free from residual impression alone descend.
Although [it is said in <s>Smṛti</s>:] 'Non-anger toward all beings, by action, mind, and speech,
and benevolence and knowledge — the wise know this as <s>śīla</s> (character).'

Thus, from <s>Smṛti</s>, <s>śīla</s> (character) — which is conduct (<s>ācāra</s>) — is different from residual impression (<s>anuśaya</s>). Nevertheless, because conduct serves as a subsidiary to residual impression, the teacher <s>Kārṣṇājini</s> held that [<s>caraṇa</s>] serves as an indicator (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) of residual impression.

And thus, from [the <s>Śruti</s>] 'Those of pleasant conduct,' 'those of foul conduct' — through the indicator of residual impression — it is established that the descent is for those with residual impression alone. //9//

body.text: #ānarthakyamiti cenna tadapekṣatvāt# /

children.text: 'ācārahīnaṃ na punaranti vedāḥ' iti hi smṛtyā vedapadena vedārthamupalakṣayantyā vedārthānuṣṭhānaśeṣatvamācārasyoktaṃ na tu svatantra ācāraḥ phalasya sādhanaṃ, tena vedārthānuṣṭhānopakārakatayācārasya nānarthakyaṃ kratvarthasya /
children.translated_text: For by the <s>Smṛti</s> 'The <s>Veda</s>s do not again accept one who is devoid of conduct (<s>ācāra</s>)' — using the word '<s>Veda</s>' to indicate the meaning of <s>Veda</s> [i.e., Vedic injunctions] — it is stated that conduct is subsidiary to the performance of the meaning of the <s>Veda</s>; but conduct is not independently a means to the fruit. Therefore, because of its being helpful to the performance of Vedic injunctions, conduct — which serves the purpose of the ritual (<s>kratvārtha</s>) — is not purposeless.
By this, the ritual-serving nature of conduct — like that of fuel-sticks (<s>samidh</s>) and the like — has been stated.

Now, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says that even if conduct is person-serving (<s>puruṣārtha</s>) — being a purificatory rite of the person (<s>puruṣasaṃskāra</s>) — like bathing (<s>snāna</s>) and the like, there is no defect: '#Even if conduct is person-serving#.'
Thus it has been stated that by the word <s>caraṇa</s>, which denotes conduct (<s>ācāra</s>), all residual impression (<s>anuśaya</s>) is indicated. //10//

body.translated_text: '#If [it be objected that this leads to] purposelessness — no, because [conduct] is dependent on that [<s>karma</s>]#' (<s>ānarthakyam iti cen na tad apekṣatvāt</s>).

children.text: bādaristu mukhya eva caraṇaśabdaḥ karmaṇītyāha- #sukṛtaduṣkṛte eveti tu bādariḥ# /
children.translated_text: But <s>Bādari</s> [holds that] the word <s>caraṇa</s> is used in its primary sense — referring to <s>karma</s> (action) itself — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Good and bad [deeds] alone — so [holds] <s>Bādari</s>#' (<s>sukṛtaduṣkṛte eveti tu Bādariḥ</s>).
The '<s>Brāhmaṇa-parivrājaka</s> principle' [and] the 'cow-and-bull principle' (<s>gobalīvardanyāya</s>) [are relevant here].
The rest has transparent meaning. //11//

body.text:
#aniṣṭādikāriṇāmapi ca śrutam# /
'ye vai ke cāsmāllokātprayanti candramasameva te sarve gacchanti' iti kauṣītakināṃ samāmnānāt, dehārambhasya ca candralokagamanamantareṇānupapatteḥ pañcamyāmāhutāvityāhitisaṃkhyāniyamāt /
tathāhi-dyusomavṛṣṭyannaretaḥpariṇāmakrameṇa tā evāpo yoṣidagnau hutāḥ puruṣavacaso bhavantītyaviśeṣeṇa śrutam /
na caitanmanuṣyābhiprāyaṃ, kapūyacaraṇāḥ svayonimityamanuṣyasyāpi śravaṇāt /
gamanāgamanāya ca devayānapitṛyāṇayoreva mārgayorāmnānāt, pathyantarasyāśruteḥ, 'jāyasva mriyasveti tṛtīyaṃ sthānam' iti ca sthānatvamātreṇāvagamātpathitvenāpratīteścandralokādavatīrṇānāmapi ca tatsthānatvasaṃbhavādasaṃpūreṇa prativacanopapatteḥ,
body.translated_text:
'#And because it is heard even for those who do not perform <s>iṣṭa</s> and the like#' (<s>aniṣṭādikāriṇām api ca śrutam</s>).
Because of the <s>Kauṣītakin</s> statement: 'All those who depart from this world go to the moon' — and because the commencement of a body is impossible without going to the lunar world, because of the fixed count in [the passage about] the fifth oblation.
Thus: Through the sequence of transformations into [the forms of] sky, <s>Soma</s>, rain, food, and semen — those very waters, offered in the fire of woman, become endowed with the form of a person — this is heard without restriction.
And this is not intended [only] for humans, since even non-humans are heard of — 'those of foul conduct [attain] their [respective] birth.'
And because only two paths — the <s>Devayāna</s> (path of the gods) and <s>Pitṛyāṇa</s> (path of the fathers) — are mentioned for going and returning, and no third path is heard of; and because the statement 'Be born, die — this is the third state' is understood merely as a state (<s>sthāna</s>), not as a path; and because even for those who have descended from the lunar world, that state [of being born and dying] is possible; and because the reply [about the fate of those who follow neither path] is complete even without full elaboration [of a third path],

body.text:
ananyamārgatayā ca tadbhogavirahiṇāmapi grāmaṃ gacchan vṛkṣamūlānyupasarpatītivatsaṃyamanādiṣu yamavaśyatāyai candralokagamanopapatteḥ, 'na katareṇavacana' ityasyāsaṃpūraṇapratipādanaparatayā mārgadvayaniṣedhaparatvābhāvāt, aniṣṭādikāriṇāmapi candralokagamane prāpte 'bhidhīyate-satyaṃ sthānatayāvagatasya na mārgatvaṃ tathāpi vettha yathāsau mārgo na saṃpūryate ityasya prativacanāvasare mārgadvayaniṣedhapūrvaṃ tṛtīyaṃ sthānamabhivadannasaṃpūraṇāya tatpratipakṣamācakṣīta /
yadi punastenaiva mārgeṇāgatya janmamaraṇaprabandhavat sthānamadhyāsīta naitattṛtīyaṃ sthānaṃ bhavet /
nahīṣṭādikāriṇaścandramaṇḍalādavaruhya ramaṇīyaṃ ninditāṃ vā yoniṃ pratipadyamānāstṛtīyaṃ sthānaṃ pratipadyante /
tatkasya hetoḥ /
pitṛyāṇena pathāvarohāt /
tadyadi kṣudrajantavo 'pyanenaiva pathāvaroheyuḥ, naitadeṣāṃ janmamaraṇaprabandhavattṛtīyaṃ sthānaṃ bhavet /
tato 'vagacchāmaḥ saṃyamanaṃ sapta ca yātanābhūmīryamavaśatayā pratipadyamānā aniṣṭādikāriṇo na candramaṇḍalādavarohantīti /
tasmāt 'ye vai ke ca' itīṣṭādikāriviṣayaṃ na sarvaviṣayam /
pañcamyāmāhutāviti ca svārthavidhānaparaṃ na punarapañcamyāhutipratiṣedhaparamapi, vākyabhedaprasaṅgāt /
saṃyamane tvanubhūyeti sūtreṇāvarohāpādānatayā saṃyamanasyopādānāccandramaṇḍalāpādānaniṣedha āñjasaḥ /

children.translated_text: And thus it is the established-view <s>sūtra</s> itself.
But if it were a prima facie view <s>sūtra</s>, [the meaning] would have to be somehow conveyed by supplying another doubt.
'#Born from a living being#' means born from a womb (<s>jarāyuja</s>).
'#Born from moisture#' means born from sweat (<s>saṃsvedaja</s>). //12//

body.translated_text:
And since there is no other path, and since even for those devoid of the enjoyment thereof, going to the lunar world is tenable — as one going to a village approaches the roots of trees [along the way] — for subjection to <s>Yama</s> in <s>Saṃyamana</s> and the like; and since the statement 'by neither of the two paths' has as its purport the teaching of non-fulfillment, not the negation of both paths; when the going to the lunar world even of those who have performed undesirable actions is thus established, [the established view] is stated: True, what is understood as a station does not have the character of a path; nevertheless, when the occasion for answering 'Do you know how that path is not filled up?' arises, [the teacher], while negating the two paths, speaks of a third station — he would declare the counterpart of that [non-fulfillment] for the purpose of [explaining] non-fulfillment.
If, however, [beings] were to come by that very path and occupy the station like the continuum of birth and death, this would not be a third station.
For those who have performed <s>iṣṭa</s> (sacrifices) and the like, descending from the lunar sphere and entering a pleasant or condemned womb, do not attain a third station.
For what reason?
Because of the descent by the path of the ancestors (<s>pitṛyāṇa</s>).
If lowly creatures too were to descend by this very path, this continuum of birth and death would not be a third station for them.
From this we understand that those who have performed undesirable actions, attaining <s>Saṃyamana</s> and the seven places of torment under <s>Yama</s>'s subjection, do not descend from the lunar sphere.
Therefore, 'whoever indeed' refers only to those who have performed <s>iṣṭa</s> and the like, not to everyone.
And 'when offered as the fifth oblation' has as its purport the injunction of its own purpose, not the prohibition of [birth] without the fifth oblation — because there would be the unwanted consequence of splitting the sentence.
But since by the <s>sūtra</s> 'having experienced in <s>Saṃyamana</s>,' <s>Saṃyamana</s> is mentioned as the means of descent, the negation of reaching the lunar sphere is straightforward.

body.text:
sābhāvyāpattirupapatteḥ /
yadyapi yathetamākāśamākāśādvāyumityato na tādātmyaṃ sphuṭamavagamyate tathāpi vāyurbhūtvetyādeḥ sphuṭataraṃ tādātmyāvagamādyathetamākāśamityetadapi tādātmya evāvatiṣṭhate /
na cānyasyānyabhāvānupapattiḥ /
manuṣyaśarīrasya nandikeśvarasya devadeharūpapariṇāmasmaraṇāddevadehasya ca nahuṣasya tiryaktvasmaraṇāt /
tasmānmukhyārthaparityāgena na gauṇī vṛttirāśrayaṇīyā /
gauṇyāṃ ca vṛttau lakṣaṇāśabdaḥ prayukto guṇe lakṣaṇāyāḥ saṃbhavāt /
yathāhuḥ-'lakṣyamāṇaguṇairyogādvṛtteriṣṭā tu gauṇatā' iti /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ-sābhāvyāpattiḥ /
samāno bhāvo rūpaṃ yeṣāṃ te sabhāvāsteṣāṃ bhāvaḥ sābhāvyaṃ sārūpyaṃ sādṛśyamiti yāvat /
kutaḥ- #upapatteḥ# /
etadeva vyatirekamukhena vyācaṣṭe- #nahyanyasyānyabhāvo mukhya upapadyate# /
yuktametadyaddevaśarīramajagarabhāvena pariṇamate, devadehasamaye 'jagaraśarīrasyābhāvāt /
yadi tu devājagaśarīre samasamaye syātāṃ na devaśarīramajagaraśarīraṃ śilpiśatenāpi kriyate /

children.text: nahi dadhipayasī samasamaye parasparātmanī śakye saṃpādayituṃ, tathehāpi sūkṣmaśarīrākāśayoryugapadbhāvānna parasparātmatvaṃ bhavitumarhati /
children.translated_text: For curd and milk cannot be made into each other when they exist simultaneously; similarly here too, since the subtle body and space exist simultaneously, they cannot become identical with each other.
The same should be applied in the case of air and the rest as well.
And thus, the 'becoming that' should be explained as figurative, through similarity with that.

children.text: nanvākāśabhāvena saṃyogamātraṃ lakṣyatāṃ kiṃ sādṛśyenetyata āha- #vibhutvāccākāśeneti# //22 //
children.translated_text: Objection: Let mere contact be indicated by 'becoming space' — why [resort to] similarity? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#And because of the all-pervasiveness of space#.' //22//

body.translated_text:
'<s>Sābhāvyāpatti</s> (the attainment of similarity), because of tenability.'
Although from 'just as into this space, from space into air' and so on, identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) is not clearly understood, nevertheless, from 'having become air' and the like, since identity is more clearly understood, 'just as into this space' too is established as [expressing] identity alone.
Nor is it untenable that one thing becomes another —
because we remember the transformation of the human body of <s>Nandikeśvara</s> into a divine body, and the transformation of <s>Nahuṣa</s>, who had a divine body, into an animal.
Therefore, the secondary meaning (<s>gauṇī vṛtti</s>) should not be resorted to by abandoning the primary meaning.
And in the secondary meaning, the word '<s>lakṣaṇā</s>' (indication) is used, since indication is possible in [what is based on] a quality (<s>guṇa</s>).
As they say: 'The secondary nature of an expression is accepted through the connection with qualities that are indicated.'
With this prima facie view established, we say: <s>Sābhāvyāpatti</s> (attainment of similarity).
Those who have the same form (<s>bhāva</s>) are <s>sabhāva</s>s; their state is <s>sābhāvya</s>, meaning similarity, resemblance.
Why? '#Because of tenability#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] explains this very [point] through the method of exclusion: '#For the becoming of one thing as another is not tenable in the primary sense#.'
It is reasonable that a divine body transforms into the state of a python, because at the time of the divine body, the python body does not exist.
But if the divine and python bodies were to exist at the same time, the divine body could not be made into a python body even by a hundred craftsmen.

children.translated_text: '#Not after a long time, because of a distinction#.'

children.text: 'durniṣprapataram' iti duḥkhena niḥsaraṇaṃ brūte na tu vilambeneti manyate pūrvapakṣī /
children.translated_text: The prima facie view considers that '<s>durniṣprapatara</s>' (more difficult to escape) speaks of escape with difficulty, not of delay.

children.text: vinā sthūlaśarīraṃ na sūkṣmaśarīre duḥkhabhāgīti durniṣprapataraṃ vilambaṃ lakṣayatīti rāddhāntaḥ //23 //
children.translated_text: The established view is that without a gross body, there is no experience of suffering in the subtle body — hence '<s>durniṣprapatara</s>' indicates delay. //23//

body.text:
#anyādhiṣṭhiteṣu pūrvavadabhilāpāt# /
ākāśasārūpyaṃ vāyudhūmādisaṃparko 'nuśayināmukta ihedānīṃ vrīhiyavā oṣādhivanaspatayastilamāṣā iti jāyanta iti śrūyate /
tatra saṃśayaḥ-kimanuśayināṃ bhogādhiṣṭhānaṃ vrīhiyavādayaḥ sthāvarā bhavanti, āhosvit kṣetrajñāntarādhiṣṭhiteṣveṣu saṃsargamātramanubhavantīti /
tatra manuṣyo jāyate devo jāyata ityādau prayoge janeḥ śarīraparigrahe prasiddhatvādatrāpi vrīhyādiśarīraparigraha eva janirmukhyārtha iti vrīhyādiśarīrā evānuśayina iti yuktam /
naca ramaṇīyacaraṇāḥ kapūyacaraṇā itivat karmaviśeṣāsaṃkīrtanāmāttadabhāve vrīhyādīnāṃ śarīrabhāvābhāvātkṣetrajñānantarādhiṣṭhitānāmeva yatsaṃparkamātramiti sāṃpratam /
iṣṭādikāriṇāmiṣṭādikarmasaṃkīrtanāttadabhāve vrīhyādīnāṃ śarīrabhāvābhāvātkṣetrajñāntarādhiṣṭhitānāmeva yatsaṃparkamātramiti sāṃpratam /
iṣṭādikāriṇāmiṣṭādikarmasaṃkīrtanādiṣṭādeśca hiṃsādoṣadūṣitatvena sāvadyaphalatayā candralokabhogāntaraṃ sthāvaśarīrabhogyaduḥkhaphalatvasyāpyupapatteḥ /
naca 'na hiṃsyātsarvā bhūtāni' iti sāmānyaśāstrasyāgnīṣomīyapaśuhiṃsāviṣayaviśeṣaśāstreṇa bādhanaṃ, sāmānyaśāstrasya hiṃsāmānyadvāreṇa viśeṣopasarpaṇaṃ vilambeneti sākṣādviśeṣaspṛśaḥ śāstracchīghratarapravṛttāddurbalatvāditi sāṃpratam /
nahi balavadityeva durbalaṃ bādhate kintu sati virodhe /
na cehāsti virodhaḥ, bhinnagocaracāritvāt /
'agnīṣomīyaṃ paśumālabhet ' iti hi kratuprakaraṇe samāmnātaṃ kratvarthatāmasya gamayati na tvapanayati niṣedhāpāditāmasya puruṣaṃ pratyanarthahetutām /
tenāstu niṣedhādasya puruṣaṃ pratyanarthahetutā vidheścha kratvarthatā ko virodhaḥ /
yathāhuḥ-'yo nāma kratumadhyasthaḥ kalañjādīni bhakṣayet /
na kratostatra vaiguṇyaṃ yathā coditasiddhitaḥ' iti /
tasmājjanermukhyārthatvādvrīhyādiśarīrā anuśayino jāyanta iti prāpte 'bhidhīyate-bhavedetadevaṃ yadi ramaṇīyacaraṇāḥ kapūyacaraṇā itivadvrīhyādiṣvanuśayavatāṃ kamaviśeṣaḥ kīrtyeta na caitadasti /
na ceṣṭādeḥ karmaṇaḥ sthāvaśarīropabhogyaduḥkhaphalaprasavahetubhāvaḥ saṃbhavati, tasya dharmatvena sukhaikahetutvāt /
body.translated_text:
'#In those presided over by others, as before, because of the statement#.'
The similarity with space, the contact with air, smoke, and the like of the <s>anuśāyin</s>s (transmigrating souls) has been stated. Now it is heard: 'They become rice and barley, herbs and trees, sesame and beans.'
Here a doubt [arises]: do rice, barley, and the like — the immobile beings — become the abode of experience for the <s>anuśāyin</s>s, or do the <s>anuśāyin</s>s merely have contact with these [plants] that are presided over by other <s>kṣetrajña</s>s (individual souls)?
Therein, since in usages like 'a human is born,' 'a god is born,' the verb 'to be born' (<s>jan</s>) is well-known in the sense of assuming a body, here too 'being born' as rice and the like should be in the primary sense of assuming rice-bodies and the like — thus it is reasonable that the <s>anuśāyin</s>s have rice-bodies and the like.
Nor [can it be argued:] just as in 'those of pleasant conduct' and 'those of foul conduct,' specific <s>karma</s> is mentioned, and in the absence of such [specific mention], the rice and the like do not become bodies, and hence it is merely contact with those presided over by other <s>kṣetrajña</s>s — this is proper.
For those who have performed <s>iṣṭa</s> (sacrifices) and the like, since their <s>karma</s> is mentioned, and since <s>iṣṭa</s> and the like, being tainted by the fault of <s>hiṃsā</s> (violence) in animal sacrifice, have censurable results, and since it is tenable that the painful result of having an immobile plant-body is [experienced] after the enjoyment in the lunar world —
Nor is it proper [to argue] that the general injunction 'one should not harm any beings' is overridden by the specific injunction regarding the killing of the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> sacrificial animal, [and therefore] the general injunction, approaching the specific [case] through the generality of <s>hiṃsā</s>, is weaker because it is slower compared to the specific injunction that directly touches the specific [case] and has quicker application.
For the stronger does not override the weaker simply by being stronger, but only when there is a contradiction.
And here there is no contradiction, because they operate in different domains.
For 'one should sacrifice the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal' — being recited in the context of the <s>kratu</s> (sacrifice) — conveys its purpose for the sacrifice, but does not remove the harm-causing nature for the person that was established by the prohibition.
Therefore, let there be, due to the prohibition, its character as causing harm to the person, and due to the injunction, its purpose for the sacrifice — what contradiction is there?
As they say: 'If one who is in the midst of a sacrifice were to eat <s>kalañja</s> and the like, there is no deficiency of the sacrifice, because of the accomplishment of what was enjoined.'
Therefore, since 'being born' is in its primary sense, the <s>anuśāyin</s>s are born with rice-bodies and the like — with this prima facie view established, [the established view] is stated: This would be so if, as in 'those of pleasant conduct' and 'those of foul conduct,' a specific <s>karma</s> were mentioned for the <s>anuśāyin</s>s in connection with rice and the like — but this is not the case.
Nor is it possible that <s>iṣṭa</s> and other <s>karma</s>s produce the painful result of having an immobile plant-body for experience, because [<s>iṣṭa</s>] is <s>dharma</s> and hence exclusively a cause of happiness.

body.text:
naca tadgataiyaiḥ paśuhiṃsāyā 'na hiṃsyāt' iti niṣedātkratvarthāyā api duḥkhaphalavatsaṃbhavaḥ /
puruṣārthāyā eva na hiṃsyāditi pratiṣedhāt /
tathāhi-na hiṃsyāditi niṣedhasya niṣedhyādhīnanirūpaṇatayā yadarthaṃ niṣedhyaṃ tadartha eva niṣedho vijñāyate /
na caitat 'nānṛtaṃ vadet' 'na tau paśau karoti' itivatkasyacitprakaraṇe samāmnātaṃ yenānṛtatavadanavadasya niṣedhasya kratvarthate niṣedho 'pi kratvarthaḥ syāt /
paśau niṣiddhayorājyabhāgayoḥ kratvarthatvena niṣedhasyāpi kratvarthatvaṃ bhavet /
evaṃ hi satyājyabhāragaritairapyaṅgāntarairājyabhāgasādhyaḥ kratūpakāro vijñāyate /
tasmādanārabhyādhītena na hiṃsyādityanenābhihitasya vidhyupahitasya puruṣavyāpārasya vidhivibhaktivirodhātprakṛtyarthahiṃsākarmabhāvyatparityāgena puruṣārtha eva bhāvyo 'vatiṣṭhate /
ākhyātānabhihitasyāpi puruṣasya kartṛvyāpārābhidhānadvāreṇopasthāpitatvāt /
kevalaṃ tasya rāgataḥ prāptatvāttadanuvādena nañarthaṃ vidhirupasaṃkrāmati, tena puruṣārtho niṣedhya iti tadadhīnanirūpaṇo niṣedho 'pi puruṣārtho bhavati /
tathā cāyamarthaḥ saṃpadyate-yatpuruṣārthaṃ hananaṃ tanna kuryāditi /
kratvarthasyāpi na niṣedhe hiṃsāyāḥ kratūpakārakatvamapi kalpyate /
naca dṛṣṭe puruṣokārakatve pratyarthini sati tatkalpanāspadam /
naca svātantryapāratantrye sati saṃyogapṛthaktve svādiratādivadekatra saṃbhavataḥ /
tasmātpuruṣārthapratiṣedho na kratvarthamapyāskandatīti śuddhasukhaphalatvameveṣṭādīnāṃ na sthāvaśarīropabhogyaduḥkhaphalatvamapīti /
ākāśādiṣviva karmavyāpāramantareṇābhilāpāt /
anuśayināṃ vrīhyādisaṃyogamātraṃ na tu dehatvamiti /
ayamevārtha utsargāpavādakathanenopalakṣitaḥ /
#apica mukhye 'nuśayināṃ vrīhyādijanmanīti# /

children.text: vrīhyādibhāvamāpannāḥ khalvanuśayinaḥ puruṣairupabhuktā retaḥ sigbhāvamanubhavantī śrūyate /
children.translated_text: For the <s>anuśāyin</s>s, having attained the state of rice and the like and having been consumed by men, are heard [in <s>Śruti</s>] to undergo the state of semen.
This is untenable if the <s>anuśāyin</s>s had rice and the like as their bodies.

children.text: vrīhyādidehatve hi vrīhyādiṣu lūneṣvavahantinā phalīkṛteṣu ca vrīhyādidehavināśādanuśayinaḥ pravaseyuriti kathamanuśayināṃ retaḥsigbhāvaḥ saṃsargamātre tu saṃsargiṣu vrīhyādiṣu naṣṭeṣvapi na saṃsargiṇo 'nuśayinaḥ pravaseyuriti retaḥsigbhāva upapadyate /
children.translated_text: For if rice and the like were their bodies, then when the rice and the like are cut, threshed, and husked, the rice-body and the like would be destroyed, and the <s>anuśāyin</s>s would depart — so how could the <s>anuśāyin</s>s attain the state of semen? But if it is mere contact, then even when the rice and the like — the objects of contact — are destroyed, the <s>anuśāyin</s>s who are in contact would not depart, and hence the attainment of the state of semen is tenable.
The rest has been stated. //24//

body.translated_text:
Nor is it possible that violence in animal sacrifice, because of the prohibition 'one should not harm,' though performed for the sake of the sacrifice, produces a painful result.
Because the prohibition is only of violence for one's own purpose.
For thus: the prohibition 'one should not harm,' since its ascertainment depends on what is prohibited, is understood as pertaining to the very purpose for which the prohibited [act] is performed.
And this [prohibition] is not recited in any [sacrificial] context, as are 'one should not speak untruth' or 'one should not perform [certain rites] on the animal' — so that, just as the prohibition of untruth-speaking being for the sake of the sacrifice, this prohibition too would be for the sake of the sacrifice.
[Nor is it the case that] because the prohibition of the two <s>ājyabhāga</s>s (ghee-portions) regarding the animal is for the sake of the sacrifice, this prohibition too would be for the sake of the sacrifice.
For when that is so, the benefit to the sacrifice that was accomplished by the <s>ājyabhāga</s>s is [still] understood through other subsidiary rites that substitute for the <s>ājyabhāga</s>s.
Therefore, of the person's activity stated by the prohibition 'one should not harm' — which is recited independently without reference [to any sacrificial context] — and which is enjoined by the injunctive verbal suffix, since there is a contradiction [with the verb-root meaning of <s>hiṃsā</s>], by abandoning the root-meaning of the <s>hiṃsā</s>-action as the thing to be accomplished, only the person's purpose remains as what is to be accomplished.
Because the person, even though not expressed by the verbal ending, is brought to mind through the expression of the agent's activity.
However, since [<s>hiṃsā</s>] is already obtained [by people] through attachment, through the restatement of that [already-obtained act], the prohibition-meaning attaches to the injunction — therefore, the prohibited [act] is of the person's purpose, and hence the prohibition too, whose ascertainment depends on it, is of the person's purpose.
And thus this meaning is achieved: 'That killing which is for one's own purpose — that one should not do.'
Even when <s>hiṃsā</s> for the sake of the sacrifice is not prohibited, the capacity of <s>hiṃsā</s> to benefit the sacrifice can be postulated.
But when there is a visible capacity to serve the person's purpose, which is the opponent [of the sacrifice's purpose], there is no scope for such postulation.
Nor can [the two] — independence and subordination — co-exist in a single [act], like conjunction and separateness, or like the <s>sva</s>-suffix and <s>tadīya</s>-suffix.
Therefore, the prohibition pertaining to one's own purpose does not encroach upon the sacrifice's purpose — hence <s>iṣṭa</s> and the like have purely pleasant results, not also the painful result of an immobile plant-body for experience.
Because of the statement [of <s>anuśāyin</s>s' contact with rice etc.] being like [their contact with] space and the like — without the operation of <s>karma</s>.
The <s>anuśāyin</s>s merely have contact with rice and the like, not embodiment in them.
This very meaning is indicated by the statement of the general rule and its exception:
'#Moreover, if birth of the <s>anuśāyin</s>s as rice and the like were in the primary sense#' — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s> comments].

children.translated_text: '#The union with semen#' — thus.

children.text: sadyo jāto hi bālo na retaḥ sigbhavatyapi tu cirajātaḥ prauḍhayauvanaḥ, tasmādapi saṃsargamātramiti gamyate //26 //
children.translated_text: For a just-born child does not produce semen; rather, only one who is born long ago and has attained the prime of youth [does so]. Therefore, from this too it is understood that [the relationship of the <s>anuśāyin</s> with rice etc.] is mere contact. //26//

children.text: tatkimidānīṃ sarvatraivānuśayināṃ saṃsargamātraṃ tathāca ramaṇīyacaraṇā ityādiṣu tathābhāva āpadyeteti netyāha- #yoneḥ śarīram# /
children.translated_text: Then is it the case that everywhere the <s>anuśāyin</s>s have mere contact? And if so, the same state would follow in [the passages] 'those of pleasant conduct' and 'those of foul conduct' — [to show that] this is not so, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#From the womb, the body#.'
This is easy to understand. //27//

body.text: iti śrīvācaspatimiśraviracite śārīkamīmāṃsābhāṣyavibhāge bhāmatyāṃ tṛtīyasyādhyāyasya prathamaḥ pādaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the first <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s> in the <s>Bhāmatī</s>, the division of the commentary on the <s>Śārīrakamīmāṃsā</s> (investigation of the embodied self), composed by the revered <s>Vācaspati Miśra</s>.

body.text: iti tṛtīyādhyāyasya gatyāgaticintayā vairāgyanirūpaṇākhyaḥ prathamaḥ pādaḥ #tṛtīyādhyāye dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ#
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the first <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s>, called the examination of going and coming for the purpose of ascertaining dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>). '#The second <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s>#.'

body.text: #saṃdhye sṛṣṭirāha hi# //1 //
body.translated_text: '#In the state between [waking and deep sleep], [there is] creation, for [the <s>Śruti</s>] says so#.' //1//

children.text: idānīṃ tu tasyaiva jīvasyāvasthābhedaḥ svayañjyotiṣṭvasiddhyartha prapañcayate- #kiṃ prabodha iva svapne 'pi pāramārthikī sṛṣṭirāhosvinmāyāmayīti# /
children.translated_text: Now, the differentiation of the states of that very <s>jīva</s> is elaborated for the purpose of establishing its self-luminous nature (<s>svayañjyotiṣtva</s>): '#Is the creation in dream, like that in the waking state, ultimately real, or is it made of <s>māyā</s>?#'

children.text: yadyapi brahmaṇo 'nyasyānirvācyatayā jāgratsvapnāvasthāgatayorubhayorapi sargayormāyamayatvaṃ tathāpi yathā jāgratsṛṣṭirbrahmātmabhāvasākṣātkārātprāganuvartate /
children.translated_text: Although, since there is nothing other than <s>Brahman</s> that can be described [as ultimately real], both creations — that of the waking state and that of the dream state — are made of <s>māyā</s>, nevertheless, just as the waking creation continues until the direct realization of the identity with <s>Brahman</s>,
but ceases upon the direct realization of the identity with <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text: evaṃ kiṃ svapnasṛṣṭirāhosvit pratidinameva nivartata iti vimarśārthaḥ //
children.translated_text: so the question is: does the dream creation [likewise continue until that realization], or does it cease every day? — this is the purpose of the inquiry.

body.text:
#dvayoḥ#ihalokaparalokasthānayoḥ /
saṃdhau bhavaṃ saṃdhyam /
aihalaukikacakṣurādyavyāpārādrūpādisākṣātkāropajananādanaihalaukikaṃ pāralaukikendriyādivyāpārasya ca bhaviṣyato 'pratyupannatvena na pāralaukikam /
naca na rūpādisākṣātkāro 'sti svapnadṛśaḥ /
body.translated_text:
'Of the two' (<s>dvayoḥ</s>) — of the two stations, this world and the next world.
<s>Saṃdhya</s> (the juncture-state) is that which exists at the juncture (<s>saṃdhi</s>).
Since [the dream state] does not engage the organs of this world such as the eye and the like, and hence does not generate the direct perception of form and the like — it is not of this world. And since the activity of the organs of the next world and the like, being future, is not yet present — it is not of the next world.
And yet, it is not the case that there is no direct perception of form and the like for the dreamer.

body.text:
tasmādubhayorlokayorasyāntarālatvamiti brahmātmabhāvasākṣātkārātprāk tathyarūpaiva sṛṣṭirbhavitumarhati /
ayamabhisaṃdhiḥ-iha hi sarvāṇyeva mithyājñānānyudāharaṇaṃ teṣāṃ satyatvaṃ pratijñāyate /
prakṛtopayogitayā tu svapnajñānamudāhṛtam /
jñānaṃ yamarthamavabodhayati sa tathaiveti yuktam /
tathābhāvasya jñānārohāt /
atathātvasya tvapratīyamānasya tathābhāvaprameyavirodhena kalpanāspadatvāt bādhakapratyayādatathātvamiti cet /
na /
tasya bādhakatvāsiddheḥ /
samānagocare hi viruddhārthopasaṃhāriṇī jñāne virudhyate /
balavadabalavattvāniścayācca bādhyabādhakabhāvaṃ pratipadyete /
na ceha samānaviṣayatvaṃ, kālabhedena vyavasthopapatteḥ /
yathāhi kṣīraṃ dṛṣṭaṃ kālāntare dadhi bhavati, evaṃ rajataṃ dṛṣṭaṃ kālāntare śuktirbhavet /
nānārūpaṃ vā tadvastu /
yadyasya tīvrātapaklāntisahitaṃ cakṣuḥ sa tasya rajatarūpatāṃ gṛhṇāti /
yasya tu kevalamālokamātropakṛtaṃ, sa tasyaiva śuktirūpatāṃ gṛhṇāti /
evamutpalamapi nīlalohitaṃ divā saurībhirbhābhirabhivyaktaṃ nīlatayā gṛhyate /
pradīpābhivyaktaṃ tu naktaṃ lohitatayā /
evamasatyāṃ nidrāyāṃ sato 'pi rathādīnna gṛhṇāti nidrāṇastu gṛhṇātīti sāmagrībhedādvā kālabhedādvā virodhābhāvaḥ /
nāpi pūrvottarayorbalavadabalavattvanirṇayaḥ /
dvayorapi svagocaracāritayā samānatvena vinigamanāhetorabhāvāt /
tasmādapyavaśyamavirodho vyavasthāpanīyaḥ /
tatsiddhametat /
vivādāspadaṃ pratyayāḥ, samyañcaḥ, pratyayatvāt, jāgratstambhādipratyayavaditi /
imamarthaṃ śrutirapi darśayati-'atha rathān rathayogān pathaḥ sṛjate' iti /
naca 'na tatra rathā na rathayogā na canthāno bhavanti' iti virodhādupacaritārthāṃ sṛjata iti śrutirvyākhyeyā /
sṛjata iti hi śruterbahuśrutisaṃvādātpramāṇāntarasaṃvādācca balīyastvena tadanuguṇatayā na tatra rathā ityasyā bhāktatvena vyākhyānāt /
jāgradavasthādarśanayogyā na santi na tu rathā na santīti /
ata eva kartṛśrutiḥ śākhāntaraśrutirudāhṛtā /
prājñakartṛkatvāccāsya pāramārthikatvaṃ viyadādisargavat /
naca jīvakartṛkatvānna prājñakartṛkatvamiti sāṃpratam /
'anyatra dharmādanyatrādharmāt' iti prājñasyaiva prakṛtatvāt /
jīvakartṛkatve 'pi ca prājñadabhedena jīvasya prājñatvāt /

children.translated_text: Moreover, some dream-cognitions are seen to accord with waking-state cognitions.

children.text: tadyathā svapne śuklāmbaradharaḥ śuklamālyānulepano brāhmaṇāyanaḥ priyavrataṃ pratyāha-priyavrata, pañcame 'hani prātarevorvarāprāyabhūmidānena narapatistvāṃ mānayiṣyatīti /
children.translated_text: For example: in a dream, a person wearing white garments and white garlands and unguents, of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> lineage, tells <s>Priyavrata</s>: 'O <s>Priyavrata</s>, on the fifth day, in the early morning, the king will honor you with a gift of fertile land.'

children.text: sa ca jāgrattathātmano mānamanubhūya svapnapratyayaṃ satyamabhimanyate /
children.translated_text: And he, upon experiencing such honor for himself in the waking state, considers the dream-cognition to be true.
Therefore, the creation in the juncture-state [of dream] is ultimately real. //1//

body.translated_text:
Therefore, since [the dream state] is intermediate between both worlds, the creation [in dreams] — prior to the direct realization of the Self as <s>Brahman</s> — must be real.
The intention is as follows: here, all cognitions whatsoever are cited as examples, and their truth is the thesis.
But dream-cognition is cited [specifically] because of its relevance to the topic at hand.
What a cognition reveals as its object is indeed so — this is reasonable.
Because of the [cognition's] arising from that being so [i.e., from the object's actual existence].
But as for its being otherwise — since that [otherwise-ness], being unperceived, is a candidate for [mere] postulation [only] because of its contradiction with what is apprehended [by the cognition] as being so — [one might say:] 'its otherwise-ness follows from a sublating cognition (<s>bādhakapratyaya</s>).'
No — because the sublating character of that [cognition] is unestablished.
For [a sublating cognition] conflicts with a cognition [only] when it attributes a contradictory meaning to the same object.
And due to the uncertainty of which is stronger and which is weaker, they enter into the relationship of sublated and sublating.
But here there is no sameness of object, since an arrangement [of non-contradiction] is possible through temporal difference.
For just as milk that is observed at one time becomes yogurt at another time, so too silver that is observed [in one moment] may become shell at another time.
Or, [alternatively,] that entity has multiple forms.
One whose eye is [affected] by the exhaustion of intense heat — that person grasps its silver-nature.
But one whose [eye] is merely assisted by light alone — that person grasps its shell-nature.
Similarly, a lotus that is both blue and red: manifested in daylight by solar rays, it is grasped as blue;
but manifested at night by lamplight, [it is grasped] as red.
Thus, when sleep is absent, one does not grasp chariots and the like that [actually] exist; but when asleep, one does grasp them — hence, either through the difference of conditions (<s>sāmagrī</s>) or through temporal difference, there is no contradiction.
Nor is there a determination of which is stronger and which is weaker between the prior and the subsequent [cognitions],
because — both being equally operative in their respective domains — there is no reason for deciding [between them].
Therefore, from this [reasoning] too, non-contradiction must necessarily be established.
Thus this is established: cognitions are the subject of dispute; they are valid; because they are cognitions — just like the cognitions of pillars and the like in waking.
The <s>Śruti</s> too shows this meaning: 'Then he creates chariots, chariot-harnesses, and paths' (<s>atha rathān rathayogān pathaḥ sṛjate</s>).
Nor should [the <s>Śruti</s>] 'He creates' be explained as having a figurative meaning on account of the contradiction with 'There are no chariots there, no chariot-harnesses, no paths' (<s>na tatra rathāḥ na rathayogāḥ na panthānaḥ</s>).
For the <s>Śruti</s> 'He creates' — being in accord with numerous other <s>Śruti</s>s and in accord with other means of knowledge — is stronger; and in conformity with that, 'There are no chariots there' must be explained figuratively: [meaning] 'there are none suitable for perception in the waking state, but chariots do exist.'
For this very reason, the <s>Śruti</s> declaring the creatorship [of the self in dreams] from another <s>Śākhā</s> is cited.
And because of the creatorship of the <s>Prājña</s> (the wise/supreme Self), [dream creation] is ultimately real, like the creation of space and the like.
Nor is it appropriate [to object] that because the <s>jīva</s> is the creator, the <s>Prājña</s> is not — 
because the <s>Prājña</s> alone is the topic in 'Other than <s>dharma</s>, other than <s>adharma</s>' and so on.
And even if the <s>jīva</s> is the creator, by virtue of the non-difference of the <s>jīva</s> from the <s>Prājña</s>, [the <s>jīva</s>] is [itself] the <s>Prājña</s>.

body.text:
iti prāpte ucyate- #māyāmātraṃ tu kātsnaryenānabhivyaktasvarūpatvāt# /
idamatrakūtam /
na tāvat kṣīrasyeva dadhi rajatasya pariṇāmaḥ śuktiḥ saṃbhavati /
nahi jātvīśvaragṛhe cirasthitānyapi rajatabhājanāni śuktibhāvamanubhavanti dṛśyante /
na cetarasya rajatānubhavasamaye 'nyo 'nākulendriyo na tasya śuktibhāvamanubhavati pratyeti ca /
na cobhayarūpaṃ vastu /
sāmagrībhedāttu kadācidasya toyabhāvo 'nubhūyate kadācinmarīciteti sāṃpratam /
pāramārthike hāsya toyabhāve tatsādhyāmudānyopaśamalakṣaṇārthakriyāṃ kuryānmarīcisādhyāmapi rūpaprakāśalakṣaṇām /
na marīcibhiḥ kasyacittṛṣṇaja udanyopaśāmyati /
naca toyameva dvividhamudanyopaśamanamatadupaśamanamiti yuktam /
tadarthakriyākāritvavyāptaṃ toyatvaṃ mātrayāpi tāmakurvattoyameva na syāt /
apica toyapratyayasamīcīnatvāyāsya dvaividhyamabhyupeyate taccābhyupagame 'pi na seddhumarhati /
tathāhi-asamarthavidhāpāti toyametaditi manvāno na tṛṣṇayāpi marīcitoyamabhidhāvet yathā marīcīnanubhavan /
athāśaktamabhimanyamāno 'bhidhāvati /
kimaparāddhaṃ marīciṣu toyaviparyāsena sarvajanīnena yattamatilaṅghya viparyāsāntaraṃ kalpyate /
naca kṣīradadhipratyayavadācāryamātulabrāhmaṇapratyayavadvā toyamarīcivijñāne samuccitāvagāhinīsa svānubhavātparasparaviruddhayorbādhyabādhakabhāvāvabhāsanāt /
tatrāpi rajatajñānaṃ pūrvamutpannaṃ bādhyamuttaraṃ tu bādhakaṃ śuktijñānaṃ prāptipūrvakatvātpratiṣedhasya /
rajatajñānātprākprāpakābhāvena śukteraprāptāyāḥ pratiṣedhasaṃbhavātpūrvajñānaprāptaṃ tu rajataṃ śuktijñānamapabadhitumarhati /
tadapabādhātmakaṃ ca svānubhavādavasīyate /
yathāhuḥ-'āgāmitvādabādhitvā paraṃ pūrvaṃ hi jāyate /
pūrvaṃ punarabādhitvā paraṃ notpadyate kkacit' /
naca vartamānarajatāvabhāsi jñānaṃ bhaviṣyattāmasyāgocarayanna bhaviṣyatā svasamayavartinīṃ śuktiṃ gocarayatā pratyayena bādhyate, kālabhedena virodhābhāvāditi yuktam /
mā nāmāsya jñāsītpratyakṣaṃ bhaviṣyattāṃ tatpṛṣṭhabhāvi tvanumānamupakārabhāvahetumivāsati vināśapratyayopanipāte sthemānamākalayati /
asati vināśapratyayopanipāte rajatamidaṃ sthiraṃ rajatatvādanubhūtapratyabhijñātarajatavat /

children.text: tathāca rajatagocaraṃ pratyakṣaṃ vastutaḥ sthirameva rajataṃ gocarayet /
children.translated_text: And thus, the perception having silver as its object would in reality establish that silver alone is stable.

children.text: tathāca bhaviṣyacchuktikājñānakālaṃ, rajataṃ vyāpnuyāditi virodhācchuktijñānena bādhyate /
children.translated_text: And thus, it would pervade even the time of the future shell-cognition — and because of this contradiction, it is sublated by the shell-cognition.
As they say: 'For when silver is being grasped, it is grasped as long-lasting;
It pervades even the time of the future shell-cognition — hence that [silver-cognition is sublated].' //

body.translated_text:
This being the prima facie view, it is said: 'But it is mere <s>māyā</s> (illusion), because of the non-manifestation of its [true] nature in its entirety' [BS 3.2.3].
Here is the essential point:
To begin with, the transformation of silver into shell — like [the transformation of] milk into yogurt — is not possible.
For silver vessels kept for a long time even in the Lord's house are never observed to undergo the state of shell.
Nor does it happen that, at the time of the other person's experience of silver, another person with undisturbed senses does not experience its shell-nature but perceives [only silver].
Nor is it an entity with dual nature.
But [the objection that] 'due to the difference of conditions, at one time its water-nature is experienced and at another time its mirage-nature' [might be put forward] — this is [refuted as follows:]
If the water-nature were ultimately real, it would produce the practical efficacy achievable by water — namely, the quenching of thirst — and also the practical efficacy achievable by the mirage — namely, the illumination of form.
But no one's thirst born of desire is quenched by mirages.
Nor is it reasonable [to say] that water itself is of two kinds — [one] that quenches thirst and [one] that does not.
For water-ness — which is pervaded by [the capacity for] such practical efficacy — if not producing that [efficacy] even slightly, would not be water at all.
Moreover, [the argument that] the duality [of water and mirage] is accepted in order [to maintain] the correctness of the water-cognition — even upon such acceptance, it cannot be established.
For thus: one who, thinking 'This water cannot accomplish [thirst-quenching],' would not even run toward mirage-water despite being thirsty — like one who does not experience mirages [at all].
But if, thinking it capable, one runs toward it —
what wrong have the mirages committed — [when] the universally recognized error of mistaking [mirages] for water [is well-known] — that, overriding that [universal error], another error is postulated?
Nor are the water and mirage cognitions — like the milk and yogurt cognitions, or like the cognitions of a teacher, maternal uncle, and <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [being the same person seen differently] — simultaneously apprehending [the same thing] — [this is known] from one's own experience, since the mutual contradiction between the two [cognitions] appears as a sublated-sublating relationship.
Therein, the silver-cognition, arising first, is sublated, while the later shell-cognition is the sublator — because negation (<s>pratiṣedha</s>) presupposes a prior attainment.
Prior to the silver-cognition, since there was no means of apprehending the shell, the shell — being unattained — could not be negated; but the silver, attained through the prior cognition, can be sublated by the shell-cognition.
And that [shell-cognition] is of the nature of sublation — this is ascertained from one's own experience.
As they say: 'Being subsequent, [the latter cognition], having sublated the former, is born;
But having sublated the latter, the former is never born.'
Nor is it reasonable [to say] that the cognition appearing as present silver is not sublated by a cognition that does not bring within its scope the future nature [of the object] but does bring within its scope the shell existing at its own time, [arguing that there is] no contradiction because of temporal difference.
Let this [later cognition] not directly know the future nature; nevertheless, the inference following upon it — like [the inference] of the causal condition of benefit — in the absence of the occurrence of a cognition of destruction, determines the persistence [of the object].
In the absence of the occurrence of a cognition of destruction, [the inference runs:] 'This silver is stable, because of being silver, like previously experienced and recognized silver.'

' iti /
pratyakṣeṇa cirasthāyīti gṛhyata iti kecidvyācakṣate /
tadayuktam /
yadi cirasthāyitvaṃ yogyatā na sā pratyakṣagocaraḥ śakteratīndriyatvāt /
atha kālāntaravyāpitvaṃ, tadapyayuktaṃ, kālāntareṇa bhaviṣyatendriyasya saṃyogāyogāttadupahitasīmno vyāpitvasyātīndriyatvāt /
naca pratyabhijñāpratyayavadatrāsti saṃskāraḥ yenāvartamānamapyākalayet /
tasmādatyantābhyāsavaśena pratyakṣānantaraṃ śīgratarotpannavinaśyadavasthānumānasahitapratyakṣābhiprāyemeva cirasthāyīti gṛhyata iti mantavyam /
ata evaitatsūkṣmataraṃ kālavyavadhānamavivecayantaḥ saugatāḥ prāhuḥ, dvividho hi viṣayaḥ pratyakṣasya grāhyaścādhyavaseyaśca /
grāhyakṣaṇa ekaḥ svalakṣaṇo 'dhyavaseyaśca /
grāhyakṣaṇa ekaḥ slakṣaṇo 'dhyavaseyaśca saṃtāna iti /
etena svapnapratyayo mithyātvena vyākhyātaḥ /
yattu satyaṃ svapnadarśanamuktaṃ tatrāpyākhyātrā brāhmaṇāyanenākhyāte saṃvādābhāvāt /

children.translated_text: The corroboration with what was told to <s>Priyavrata</s> is merely coincidental (<s>kākatālīya</s>) and cannot establish the dream-cognition as a valid means of knowledge.

children.text: tādṛśasyaiva bahulaṃ visaṃvādadarśadarśitaśca visaṃvādo bhāṣyakṛtā kātsnryenānabhivyaktiṃ vivṛṇvatā /
children.translated_text: And the frequent observation of non-corroboration in cases of that very kind [of dream] is shown — and the non-corroboration has been shown by the author of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> while explaining 'the non-manifestation in its entirety.'
'At night, while asleep' —

children.text: rajanīsamaye 'pi hi bhāratādvarṣāntare ketumālādau vāsaro bhavatīti bhārate varṣa ityuktam //3 //
children.translated_text: For even at the time of night, in a region of <s>Bhārata</s> other than [the one where it is night] — in <s>Ketumāla</s> and the like — it is daytime; hence it is said 'in the <s>Bhārata</s> region.' //3//

body.translated_text:
Some explain: 'It is grasped as long-lasting by perception.'
That is incorrect.
If 'long-lasting' means suitability [for persistence], that is not within the scope of perception, because of the supra-sensory nature of capacity (<s>śakti</s>).
If it means extending over another time-period, that too is incorrect, because the sense-organ — not being in contact with the future [object] — and the pervasiveness delimited by [the sense-organ's] boundaries are supra-sensory.
Nor is there here a <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression) — as in the case of recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) — by which [the cognition] could apprehend even what is not present.
Therefore, it should be understood that — through the force of extreme habituation — immediately after perception, [what is grasped as] 'long-lasting' is [apprehended] with the intention of a perception accompanied by an inference of persistence that arises and perishes extremely rapidly.
For this very reason, the <s>Bauddha</s>s (Buddhists), not discerning this extremely subtle temporal interval, say: the object of perception is twofold — the apprehended (<s>grāhya</s>) and the determined (<s>adhyavaseya</s>). The apprehended instant is a single particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), and the determined is the continuum (<s>saṃtāna</s>).
By this, the dream-cognition is explained as false.
As for the [counter-example of] a true dream-vision that was cited — even in that case, since the narration by the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-descended [person in the dream] lacks corroboration,

body.text:
#sūcakaśca hi śruterācakṣate ca tadvidaḥ# /
darśanaṃ sūcakaṃ tacca svarūpeṇa sat /
asattu dṛśyam /
ata eva strīdarśanasvarūpasādhyāścaramadhātuvisargādayo jāgradavasthāyāmanuvartante /

children.translated_text: But [effects] achievable by [the actual] woman — such as garlands, unguents, tooth-marks, and the like — do not continue [into waking].
'Nor [is it accepted] by us that even in dream there is an activity of the <s>Prājña</s> (the supreme Self).'

children.text: prājñavyāpāratvena pāramārthikatvānumānaṃ pratyakṣeṇa bādhakapratyayena virudhyamānaṃ nātmānaṃ labhata iti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: The inference of ultimate reality based on its being an activity of the <s>Prājña</s> — being contradicted by the sublating cognition (<s>bādhakapratyaya</s>) that is perception — does not sustain itself — this is the purport.
An intermediate third sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>) between bondage and liberation [is what the dream-state represents]. //4//

body.translated_text:
'And [the dream is] indicative (<s>sūcaka</s>), for so the <s>Śruti</s> [says], and those who know declare [it so]' [BS 3.2.4].
The dream-vision is indicative, and that [indication] exists in its own right.
But the [thing] seen [in the dream] is unreal.
For this very reason, [certain effects] that are achievable by the actual form [of the dream-vision] — such as the final seminal emission and the like [resulting from dreaming of a woman] — do continue into the waking state.

children.translated_text: 'But because of meditation on the Supreme, that [sovereignty] is concealed; for from that [meditation] arise [both] his bondage and its opposite [liberation].'
'Or because of connection with the body — that [concealment] too' — these two <s>sūtra</s>s have been explained by us in the first <s>sūtra</s> [commentary].
And the <s>Bhāṣya</s> of these two is explained by the running gloss (<s>nigadavyākhyāta</s>). //5//

body.text:
#tadabhāvo nāḍīṣu tacchuterātmani ca# /
iha hi nāḍīpuritatparamātmāno jīvasya suṣuptāvasthāyāṃ sthānatvena śrūyante /
tatra kimeṣāṃ sthānānāṃ vikalpa āhosvitsamuccayaḥ /
kimato yadyevam /
etadato bhavati /
yadā nāḍyo vā purītadvā suṣuptasthānaṃ tadā viparītagrahaṇanivṛttāvapi na jīvasya paramātmabhāva iti /
avidyānivṛttāvapi jīvasya paramātmabhāvāya kāraṇāntaramapekṣitavyaṃ tacca karmaiva na tu tattajñānaṃ viparītajñānanivṛttimātreṇa tasyopayogāt, viparītajñānanivṛtteśca vināpi tattvajñānaṃ suṣuptāvapi saṃbhavāt /
tataśca karmaṇaivāpavargo na jñānena /
yathāhuḥ-'karmaṇaiva tu saṃsiddhimāsthitā janakādayaḥ' iti /
ata tu paramātmaiva nāḍīpurītasmṛtidvārā suṣuptisthānaṃ tato viparītajñānanivṛtterasti mātrayā paramātmabhāva upayogaḥ /
tayā hi tāvadeṣa jīvastadavasthāno bhavati kevalam /
tattvajñānābhāvena samūlakāṣamavidyāyā akāṣājjāgratsvapnalakṣaṇaṃ jīvasya vyutthānaṃ bhavati /
tasmātprayojanavatyeṣā vicāraṇeti /
kiṃ tāvaprāptaṃ, nāḍīpurītatparamātmasu sthāneṣu suṣuptasya jīvasya nilayaṃ prati vikalpaḥ /
yathā bahuṣu prāsādeṣveko narendraḥ kadācitkkacinnilīyate kadācitkkacidevameko jīvaḥ kadācinnāḍīṣu kadācitpurītati kadācidbrahmaṇīti /
yathā nirapekṣā vrīhiyavāḥ kratusādhanībhūtapuroḍāśaprakṛtitayā śrutā ekārthā vikalpyante, evaṃ saptamīśrutyā vāyatanaśrutyā vekanilayanārthāḥ parasparānapekṣā nāḍyadayo 'pi vikalpamarhanti /
yatrāpi nāḍībhiḥ pratyavasṛpya purītati śeta iti nāḍība3hmaṇorādhārayoḥ samuccayaśravaṇam /
prāṇaśabdaṃ ca brahma 'athāsmin prāṇe brahmaṇi sa jīva ekadhā bhavati' nnirapekṣayoravedhāratvam /
iyāṃstu viśeṣaḥ /
kadācinnāḍya evādhāraḥ kadācinnāḍībhiḥ saṃcaramāṇasya purītadeva /
evaṃ tābhireva saṃcaramāṇasya kadācidbrahmaivādhāra iti siddhamādhāratve nāḍīpurītatparamātmanāmanapekṣatvam /
tathāca vikalpo vrīhiyavavadbṛhadrathantaravadveti prāptam /
prāpte 'bhidhīyate-jīvaḥ samuccayenaivaitāni nāḍyādīni svāpāyopaiti na vikalpena /
ayamabhisaṃdhiḥ-nityavadāmnātānāṃ yatpākṣikatvaṃ nāma tadgatyantarābhāve kalpyate /
yathāhuḥ-'evameṣo 'ṣṭadoṣo 'pi yadvrīhiyavavākyayoḥ /
vikalpa āśritastatra gatiranyā na vidyate' iti /
prakṛtakratusādhanībhūtapuroḍāśadravyaprakṛtitayā hi parasparānapekṣau vrīhiyavau vihitauśakrutaścaitau pratyekaṃ puroḍāśamabhinirvartayitum /
tatra yadi miśrābhyāṃ puroḍāśo 'bhinirvartyeta parasparānapekṣavrīhiyavavidhātṛṇī ubhe api śāstre bādhyeyātām /
na caitau prayogavacanaḥ samuccatumarhati /
sa hi yathā vihitānyaṅgānyabhisamīkṣya pravartamāno naitānyanyathayitaṃ śakroti /
miśraṇe cānyathātvameteṣām /
na cāṅgānurodhena pradhānābhyāso 'gosave ubhe kuryāt' itivadyuktaḥ /
aśruto hyatra pradhānābhyāso 'ṅgānurodhena ca so 'nyāyyaḥ /
na cāṅgabhūtaindravāyavādigrahānurodhena yathā pradhānasya somayāgasyāvṛttirevamatrāpīti yuktam /
'somenayajeta' iti hi tatrāpūrvayāgavidhiḥ /
tatra ca daśamuṣṭiparimitasya somadravyasya 'somamabhiṣuṇoti', 'somamabhiplāvayati' iti ca vākyāntarānulocanayā rasadvāreṇa yāgasādhanībhūtasyendravāyvādyuddeśena prādeśamātreṣūrdhvapātreṣu grahaṇāni pṛthakprakalpanāni saṃskārā vidhīyante, natu somayāgoddeśenendravāyvādayo devatāścodyante, yena tāsāṃ yāganiṣpattilakṣaṇaikārthatvena vikalpaḥ syāt /
naca prādeśamātramekaikamūrdhvapātraṃ daśamuṣṭiparimitasomarasagrahaṇāya kalpate, yena tulyārtatayā grahaṇāni vikalperan /
naca yāvanmātramekamūrdhvapātraṃ vyāpnoti tāvanmātraṃ gṛhītvā pariśaṣṭaṃ tyajyeteti yujyate /
daśamuṣṭiparimitopādānasyādṛṣṭārthatvaprasaṅgāt /
evaṃ taddṛṣṭārthaṃ bhavedyadi tatsarvaṃ yāga upayujyeta /
naca dṛṣṭe saṃbhavatyadṛṣṭakalpanā nyāyyā /
tasmātsakalasya somarasasya yāgaśeṣatvena saṃskārārhatvādekaikena ca grahamena sakalasya saṃskartṛmaśakyatvāttadavayavasyaikena saṃskāre 'vayavāntarasya grahaṇāntareṇa saṃskāra iti kāryabhedādgrahaṇāni samuccīyeran /
ata eva samuccayadarśanaṃ 'daśautānadhvaryuḥ prātaḥ savane grahan gṛhṇāti' iti /
samuccaye ca sati kramo 'pyupapadyate /
'āśvino daśamo gṛhyate tṛtīyo hūyate' /
tathaiva 'aindravāyavāgrāngrahāngṛhṇāti' iti /
teṣāṃ ca samuccaye sati yāvadyaduddeśena gṛhītaṃ tāvattasyai devatāyai tyaktavyamityarthādyāgasyāvṛttyā bhavativyam /

body.translated_text:
'Its absence [is experienced] in the <s>nāḍī</s>s, and from the <s>Śruti</s> of that [absence being] in the Self' (<s>tad-abhāvo nāḍīṣu tac-chuter ātmani ca</s>).
For here, the <s>nāḍī</s>s (channels), the <s>purītat</s> (pericardium/sheath around the heart), and the <s>Paramātman</s> are heard of as locations of the <s>jīva</s> in the state of deep sleep (<s>suṣupti</s>).
The question is: is there an alternative (<s>vikalpa</s>) among these locations, or a cumulation (<s>samuccaya</s>)?
What follows from this? This follows:
If the <s>nāḍī</s>s or the <s>purītat</s> are the location in deep sleep, then even upon the cessation of erroneous apprehension, the <s>jīva</s> would not attain <s>Paramātman</s>-hood. [It would follow that] even upon the removal of <s>avidyā</s>, something additional would be required for the <s>jīva</s>'s attainment of <s>Paramātman</s>-hood — and that would be <s>karma</s> (action) alone, not knowledge of reality, since [knowledge] has its use merely in the removal of erroneous knowledge; and since the removal of erroneous knowledge is possible even in deep sleep without knowledge of reality.
Consequently, liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) would be through <s>karma</s> alone, not through knowledge.
As [the scripture] says: '<s>Janaka</s> and others attained perfection through <s>karma</s> alone.'
But if the <s>Paramātman</s> alone — through the medium of the <s>nāḍī</s>s and the <s>purītat</s> — is the location in deep sleep, then the removal of erroneous knowledge has at least some use for the attainment of <s>Paramātman</s>-hood.
For through that [removal] alone, this <s>jīva</s> abides in that state [of <s>Paramātman</s>-hood] merely. But in the absence of knowledge of reality, since <s>avidyā</s> has not been eradicated with its root, from that [uneradicated <s>avidyā</s>], the <s>jīva</s>'s re-emergence — characterized by waking and dreaming — occurs.
Therefore, this investigation is purposeful.
What, then, is the prima facie conclusion? An alternative among the <s>nāḍī</s>s, <s>purītat</s>, and <s>Paramātman</s> as locations of the <s>jīva</s> in deep sleep.
Just as a single king takes rest sometimes in one, sometimes in another of his many palaces — so too the single <s>jīva</s> sometimes [rests] in the <s>nāḍī</s>s, sometimes in the <s>purītat</s>, sometimes in <s>Brahman</s>.
Just as rice and barley, being heard of as mutually independent material ingredients for the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (sacrificial cake) — an accessory of the rite — having the same purpose, are alternatives, so too the <s>nāḍī</s>s and the like, being heard of through the locative case or through the word 'abode' (<s>āyatana</s>) as having the same purpose — namely, being a single resting-place — and being mutually independent, are worthy of being alternatives.
Even where [the <s>Śruti</s> says] 'having retreated through the <s>nāḍī</s>s, one sleeps in the <s>purītat</s>' — [this is] the hearing of a cumulation of the <s>nāḍī</s>s and <s>Brahman</s> as two substrates.
And [the word] <s>prāṇa</s> [denoting] <s>Brahman</s> — [in the passage] 'Now in this <s>prāṇa</s>, in <s>Brahman</s>, this <s>jīva</s> becomes one' — being mutually independent, they are to be separately ascertained.
But there is this distinction: sometimes the <s>nāḍī</s>s alone are the substrate; sometimes, for one who moves through the <s>nāḍī</s>s, the <s>purītat</s> alone [is the substrate]; and similarly, for one who moves through those [<s>nāḍī</s>s], sometimes <s>Brahman</s> alone is the substrate. Thus it is established that the <s>nāḍī</s>s, <s>purītat</s>, and <s>Paramātman</s> are mutually independent as substrates.
And thus, there is an alternative, as with rice and barley, or as with the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> [<s>Sāman</s>s] — this is the prima facie conclusion.
This being the prima facie view, the reply is given: The <s>jīva</s> enters these — the <s>nāḍī</s>s and the like — at the time of sleep by cumulation, not by alternative.
The intent is this: the optionality that is attributed to [things] described as if permanent is to be posited [only] when there is no other possibility.
As [the authorities] say: 'Even though this eightfold defect exists in the statements about rice and barley, the alternative is resorted to because there is no other possibility.'
For rice and barley, being prescribed as mutually independent material ingredients for the <s>puroḍāśa</s> — an accessory of the rite under discussion — are [each individually] capable of producing a <s>puroḍāśa</s> (sacrificial cake).
Therein, if a <s>puroḍāśa</s> were to be produced from a mixture of both, both scriptures — the one prescribing rice and the one prescribing barley, each being independent — would be violated.
Nor can the performer's directive (<s>prayogavacana</s>) combine them. For he, proceeding by examining the subsidiary elements as prescribed, cannot alter them; and in mixing, these [ingredients] would be altered.
Nor is the repetition of the principal [rite] justified in accordance with the subsidiary elements, as in the <s>Agosava</s> [where they say] 'one should perform both.' For here, the repetition of the principal is unheard of, and [positing it] in accordance with subsidiary elements is irregular.
Nor is it justified that, just as in the case of the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice — where repetition of the principal sacrifice occurs in accordance with the subsidiary <s>Aindravāyava</s> and other <s>graha</s>s (cups) — so too here.
For there [in the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice], '[One should sacrifice] with <s>Soma</s>' is the injunction of an unprecedented sacrifice. And therein, for the <s>Soma</s>-substance measuring ten handfuls, by examining other scriptural sentences such as 'he presses the <s>Soma</s>,' 'he purifies the <s>Soma</s>' — the individual takings [of <s>Soma</s>-juice] through the medium of juice, into hand-span-sized upward vessels, designated for [deities such as] <s>Indra</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, and others as accessories of the sacrifice, are separately arranged and consecrated. But the deities — <s>Indra</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, and the like — are not prescribed for the purpose of the <s>Soma</s>-sacrifice, such that by their having a single purpose — the completion of the sacrifice — there could be an alternative.
Nor can each single hand-span-sized upward vessel accommodate the taking of the juice of all ten handfuls of <s>Soma</s>, such that — by having equal capacity — the takings could be alternatives.
Nor is it correct that one should take as much as one upward vessel can hold and discard the remainder — because of the consequence that the [injunction to take] ten handfuls would serve no perceived purpose.
It would serve a perceived purpose if all of it were used in the sacrifice. And when a perceived purpose is possible, the postulation of an unperceived one is not justified.
Therefore, since all the <s>Soma</s>-juice deserves consecration as a remainder of the sacrifice, and since all of it cannot be consecrated by a single taking, a portion of it is consecrated by one [taking], and another portion by another — thus, because of the difference of function, the takings are cumulated.
Hence the cumulative statement: 'The <s>adhvaryu</s> takes ten <s>graha</s>s (cups) at the morning pressing.'
And when there is cumulation, sequence too is appropriate: 'The <s>Āśvina</s> [<s>graha</s>] is taken tenth, offered third.' And likewise: 'He takes the <s>Aindravāyava</s> first among the <s>graha</s>s.'
And when these are cumulated, as much as is taken for each [deity's] purpose, that much is to be offered to that deity — and thus, by implication, the repetition of the sacrifice is necessitated.
If, however, even after being separately [taken], they were combined and offered to some [single] deity, then the separate takings and the deity-dedications would serve no perceived purpose.
And it has been said that when a perceived purpose is possible, the postulation of an unperceived one is not justified.
Therefore, where cumulation is inevitable, even the repetition of the principal is resorted to in accordance with the subsidiary elements.
But here, because of the absence of a valid reason for postulating repetition, and because the material of the <s>puroḍāśa</s> — not being restricted — is obtained in any of the prescribed substances, each independent <s>Śruti</s> about rice and <s>Śruti</s> about barley, as restricting [the choice] to a single purpose, deserves to be an alternative.
But for the <s>nāḍī</s>s, <s>purītat</s>, and <s>Paramātman</s> — being mutually independent — the possibility of having a single resting-place as their purpose [does not exist], such that there could be an alternative.
For the mere fact of being mentioned in the same case-ending does not establish single purpose, since even cumulated items are observed to be mentioned in the same case-ending: 'He sleeps on a couch; he sleeps in a palace.'
Therefore, since the mention in the same case-ending is inconclusive, determination must come from elsewhere.
And that has been stated by the author of the <s>Bhāṣya</s>: 'Even where the <s>nāḍī</s>s seem to be [mentioned] independently as the location of sleep'

body.text:
#suptisthānatvena śrāvayatītyādinā# /
sāpekṣaśrutyanurodhena nirapekṣaśrutirnetavyetyarthaḥ /
śeṣamatirohitārtham /
nanu yadi brahmaiva nilayanasthānaṃ tāvanmātramucyatāṃ kṛtaṃ nāḍyupanyāsenetyata āha- #apicātreti# /
apiceti /
samuccaye na vikalpe /
etadupapattisahitā pūrvopapattirarthasādhinīti /
mārgopadeśopayuktānāṃ nāḍīnāṃ stutyarthamatra nāḍīsaṃkīrtanamityarthaḥ /
pittenābhivyāptakaraṇo na bāhyānviṣayānvedeti taddvārā sukhaduḥkhābhāvena tatkāraṇapāṣmāsparśena nāḍīstutiḥ /
yadā tu tejo brahma tadā sugamam /
apica #nāḍyaḥ purītadvā jīvasyopādhyādhāra eva bhavatīti# /
ayamarthaḥ-abhyupetya jīvasyādheyatvamidamuktam /
paramārthatastu na jīvasyādheyatvamasti /
tathāhi-nāḍyaḥ purītadvā jīvasyopādhīnāṃ karaṇānāmāśrayo jīvastu brāhmāvyatirekātsvamahipratiṣṭhaḥ /
na cāpi brahma jīvasyādhāraḥ, tādātmyāt /
vikalpa tu vyatirekaṃ brahmaṇa ādhāratvamucyate jīvaṃ prati /
tathāca suṣuptāvasthāyāmupādhīnāmasamudācārājjīvasya brahmātmatvameva brahmādhāratvaṃ na tu nāḍīpurītādhāratvam /
tadupādhikaraṇamātrādhāratayā tu suṣuptadaśārambhāya jīvasya nāḍīpurītadādhāratvamityatulyārthatayā na vikalpa iti /

autsagikaṃ brahmasvarūpatvaṃ jīvasyāsati jāgratsvapnadaśārūpe 'pavāde suṣuptavasthāyāṃ nānyathayituṃ śakyamityarthaḥ /

na ceyamātmatādātmyaṃ vinā nāḍyādiṣu paramātmavyatirikteṣu sthāneṣūpapadyate /

tathāhi śrutiḥ-'yatra vā anyadiva syāttatrānye 'nyatpaśyet' iti /
ātmasthānatve tvadoḥ /
'yatra tvasya sarvamātmaivābhūtatkena kaṃ paśyedvijānīyāt' iti śruteḥ /
tasmādapyātmasthānavasya dvāraṃ nāḍyādītyāha- #apica sthānavikalpābhyupagame 'pīti# /
atra codayati- #nanu bhedaviṣayasyāpīti# /
bhidyata iti bhedaḥ /
bhidyamānasyāpi viṣayasyetyarthaḥ /

na tāvajjīvasyāsti svataḥparicchedastasya brahmātmatvena vibhutvāt /
aupādhike tu paricchede yatropādhisaṃnihitastanmātraṃ na jānīyānna tu sarvam /
