body.translated_text:
'[The Śruti] makes them heard' — and so on.
The meaning is: the <s>Śruti</s> that states [the <s>nāḍī</s>s] independently is to be guided by the <s>Śruti</s> that states [them] dependently.
The rest has transparent meaning.
Now, if <s>Brahman</s> alone is the resting-place, let that much alone be stated — what is the need for mentioning the <s>nāḍī</s>s? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Moreover, here...' (<s>api cātra</s>).
'Moreover' — [means] in cumulation, not in alternative.
[The fact that] this justification, together with the previous justification, establishes the point — this is the meaning.
The mention of the <s>nāḍī</s>s here is for the purpose of praising them as being useful for the instruction of the path — this is the meaning.
When the faculties, pervaded by bile, do not apprehend external objects, through that [non-apprehension] the absence of pleasure and pain — and hence non-contact with evil (<s>pāpman</s>), the cause of that [pleasure and pain] — constitutes the praise of the <s>nāḍī</s>s.
But when <s>tejas</s> (light/fire) [is equated with] <s>Brahman</s>, then it is easy [to understand].
'Moreover, the <s>nāḍī</s>s and <s>purītat</s> are the substrate of the <s>jīva</s>'s limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) alone' — thus.
The meaning is: This is said by accepting the <s>jīva</s>'s being contained [in a location]. But in reality, the <s>jīva</s> does not have the nature of being contained.
Thus: the <s>nāḍī</s>s and <s>purītat</s> are the locus of the <s>jīva</s>'s limiting adjuncts — the sense-organs (<s>karaṇa</s>s). But the <s>jīva</s>, by virtue of non-difference from <s>Brahman</s>, is self-established in its own glory.
Nor is <s>Brahman</s> the substrate of the <s>jīva</s>, because of their identity.
An alternative would require [positing] the difference of <s>Brahman</s> as a substrate for the <s>jīva</s>.
And thus, in the state of deep sleep, due to the non-functioning of the limiting adjuncts, the <s>jīva</s>'s <s>Brahman</s>-selfhood itself is [what is meant by] <s>Brahman</s> being [its] substrate — not the substrate-hood of the <s>nāḍī</s>s and <s>purītat</s>.
But as a substrate of merely the limiting adjuncts, for the purpose of initiating the state of deep sleep, the <s>nāḍī</s>s and <s>purītat</s> are the substrate of the <s>jīva</s> — and thus, since these are of unequal purpose, there is neither alternative nor cumulation as equals.
'Moreover, never for the <s>jīva</s>...' — thus.
The naturally given <s>Brahman</s>-selfhood of the <s>jīva</s>, in the absence of a sublation in the form of the waking and dream states, cannot be altered in the state of deep sleep — this is the meaning.
'Moreover, even those who adopt the alternative of locations must accept the state of deep sleep as characterized by the subsidence of particularized knowledge. And this [subsidence] is not possible in locations such as the <s>nāḍī</s>s and the like, which are other than the <s>Paramātman</s>, without identity with the Self.
For one stationed there [in the <s>nāḍī</s>s etc.], this <s>jīva</s>, having the conceit of being different from the Self, would necessarily possess particularized knowledge.
Thus the <s>Śruti</s> says: "Where there is, as it were, another, there one sees the other" (<s>yatra vā anyad iva syāt tatrānye 'nyat paśyet</s>).
But if stationed in the Self, there is no [such] defect — because of the <s>Śruti</s>: "But where for him everything has become the Self alone, then by what and whom would he see or know?" (<s>yatra tv asya sarvam ātmaivābhūt tat kena kaṃ paśyed vijānīyāt</s>).
Therefore, even on the assumption of alternative locations, the <s>nāḍī</s>s and the like are a doorway to the location that is the Self — so [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Moreover, even on the assumption of alternative locations...' (<s>api ca sthānavikalpābhyupagame 'pi</s>).
Here [the opponent] objects: 'But even of an object that is being differentiated...' (<s>nanu bhedaviṣayasyāpi</s>).
'That which is differentiated' (<s>bheda</s>) — i.e., 'even of an object that is being differentiated' — this is the meaning.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] resolves: 'Yes indeed, it would be so...' (<s>bāḍham evaṃ syāt</s>).
To begin with, the <s>jīva</s> does not have inherent delimitation, since — being of <s>Brahman</s>-nature — it is all-pervading.
But in the case of adventitious delimitation, [the <s>jīva</s>], stationed where the limiting adjunct is present, would not know only that much — but not everything.
For <s>Devadatta</s>, who does not know <s>Sumeru</s> due to [its] non-proximity, does not fail to know even what is proximate.

body.text: tasmātsarvaviśeṣavijñānapratyastamayīṃ suṣuptiṃ na samapradhānatayāganyedivaditi vadanvikalpamapyapākaroti- #naca vayamiheti# /

children.translated_text: Of the corpus of the <s>Veda</s>, which has been invested with the status of serving human purposes by the injunction of self-study (<s>svādhyāyādhyayana</s>), it is not fitting that even a single syllable should be without human purpose.

children.text: naca suṣuptāvasthāyāṃ jīvasya svarūpeṇa nāḍyādisthānatvapratipādena kiñcitprayojanaṃ brahmabhūyapratipādena tvasti /
children.translated_text: And in the state of deep sleep, the teaching that the <s>nāḍī</s>s and the like are the location of the <s>jīva</s> in its own form serves no purpose; but the teaching of [the <s>jīva</s>'s] becoming <s>Brahman</s> does serve a purpose.

children.text: tasmānna samapradhānabhāvena samuccayo nāpi vikalpa iti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, there is neither a cumulation of equals nor an alternative — this is the purport.
The rest is of ascertained meaning. //7//

body.translated_text: Therefore, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>], while stating that the deep sleep characterized by the cessation of all particularized knowledge is not [to be conceived] as of equal status [with the other locations], as with 'as if another' — thereby also removes the alternative: 'And we do not [say] here...' (<s>na ca vayam iha</s>).

children.translated_text: Nor is that [pot-space] difficult to discriminate [from supreme space], because its limiting adjunct — the pot — is [clearly] discernible.

children.text: evamanādyanirvacanīyāvidyopadhānabhedopādhikalpito jīvo na vastutaḥ paramātmano bhidyate tadupādyudbhavābhibhavābhyāṃ codbhūta ivābhibhūta iva pratīyate /
children.translated_text: Similarly, the <s>jīva</s> — whose difference is imagined through the limiting adjunct of beginningless, indescribable <s>avidyā</s> — does not in reality differ from <s>Paramātman</s>; and through the arising and subsiding of that limiting adjunct, it appears as if arisen and as if subsided.

children.text: tataśca suṣuptādāvapi abhibhūta iva jāgradavasthādiṣudbhūta iva /
children.translated_text: And thus, even in deep sleep and the like, [the <s>jīva</s> appears] as if subsided; and in the waking state and the like, as if arisen.

children.text: tasya cāvidyātadvāsanopādheranāditayā kāryakāraṇabhāvena pravahataḥ suvivecatayā tadupahito jīvaḥ suviveca iti //9 //
children.translated_text: And since its limiting adjunct — <s>avidyā</s> and its latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>s) — being beginningless, flows in the form of cause and effect, and since it is [clearly] discernible — the <s>jīva</s> conditioned by it is [also clearly] discernible. //9//

body.translated_text:
'It is the same one [<s>jīva</s>], because of <s>karma</s>, recollection, scripture, and injunction' — thus.
Although the <s>jīva</s> is not different from <s>Īśvara</s> and the rest, nevertheless, having intended the difference through the delimitation of limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>), [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] commences a new <s>adhikaraṇa</s>.
'It is the same one' — this is difficult to establish — thus.
'Whether it is the same one or another — or <s>Īśvara</s>' — this is presented merely as a possibility.
For it is not possible that [<s>Īśvara</s>], whose nature is eternally pure and liberated, would have a waking produced by <s>avidyā</s>.
For this very reason, it is not presented at the stage of deliberation.
Now, that which is a <s>karma</s> prescribed for a single person to be completed over two days and the like — [the claim that] there is recollection of it as performed on the previous day — [in expressing this,] the prefix 'anu' is meant to indicate recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>).
For this very reason, it is said: 'He is that very I' (<s>so'ham asmi</s>).
'Again, according to the regular course, back to [his] source, he runs' — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s> quotes].
<s>Ayana</s> is 'going'; going in a fixed manner (<s>niyamena gamanam</s>) is <s>nyāya</s> (regular course).
The <s>jīva</s>, according to the regular course, in deep sleep (<s>saṃprasāda</s>), runs — comes — from the state of waking to [his] source.
For one who is of tiger-origin (<s>vyāghrayoni</s>), falling asleep and coming to the state of waking, becomes a tiger only, not another species.
This is what was stated: 'There is neither tiger, nor lion [in deep sleep].' 'And if he were to arise there while asleep' — thus [the <s>Śruti</s> says].
For the <s>jīva</s> who is asleep arises in another body; and having gone to another body, he arises in the body connected with the sleeping <s>jīva</s> — and thus there is no loss of transactional usage in the other body — this is the meaning.
'Moreover, no <s>jīva</s> whatsoever is other than the Supreme' — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s> says].
Just as pot-space is not other than the supreme space.

body.text:
#sugdher'dhasaṃpattiḥ pariśeṣāt# /
viśeṣavijñānābhāvānmūrcchā jāgarasvapnāvasthābhyāṃ bhidyate punarutthānācca maraṇāvasthāyāḥ /
ataḥ suṣuptireva mūrcchā viśeṣajñānābhāvāviśeṣāt /
cirānucchvāsavepathuprabhṛtayastu supteravāntaraprabhedāḥ /
body.translated_text:
'Fainting is a half-attainment [of <s>Brahman</s>], by elimination' — thus.
Because of the absence of specific cognition, fainting (<s>mūrcchā</s>) differs from the waking and dream states; and because of subsequent recovery, it differs from the state of death.
Therefore, fainting is simply deep sleep, because of the non-difference in the absence of specific cognition.
But prolonged cessation of breathing, trembling, and the like are sub-varieties of sleep.

body.text:
tadyathā kaścitsuptotthitaḥ prāha sukhamahamasvāpsaṃ laghūni me gātrāṇi prasannaṃ me mana iti, kaścitpunarduḥkhasamasvāpsaṃ gurūṇi me gātrāṇi bhramatyanavasthitaṃ me mana iti /
na caitāvatā suṣuptirbhidyate /
tathā vikārāntare 'pi mūrcchā na suṣupterbhidyate /
tasmāllokaprasiddhyabhāvānneyaṃ pcamyavastheti prāptam /
evaṃ prāpta ucyate-yadyapi viśeṣavijñānopaśamena mohasuṣuptayoḥ sāmyaṃ tathāpi naikyam /
nahi viśeṣavijñānasadbhāvasāmyamātreṇa svapnajāgarayorabhedaḥ /
bāhyendriyavyāpārabhāvābhāvābhyāṃ tu bhede tayoḥ suṣuptamohayorapi prayojanabhedātkāraṇabhedāllakṣaṇabhedācca bhedaḥ /
śramāpanuttyarthā hi brahmaṇā saṃpattiḥ suṣaptam /
śarīratyāgārthā tu brahmaṇā saṃpattirmohaḥ /
yadyapi satyapi mohe na maraṇaṃ tathāpyasati mohe na maraṇamiti maraṇārtho mohaḥ /
musalasaṃpātādinimittatvānmohasya śramādinimittatvācca suṣuptasya sukhanetrādivikāralakṣaṇatvānmohasya prasannavadanatvādilakṣaṇabhedācca suṣuptasyāsuṣuptasya tvavāntarabhede 'pi nimittaprayojanalakṣaṇābhedādekatvam /

children.text: tasmāt suṣuptamohāvasthayorbrahmaṇā saṃpattāvapi suṣupte yādṛśī saṃpattirna tādṛśī moha ityardhasaṃpattiruktā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, even though in the states of deep sleep and fainting there is [in both cases] attainment of <s>Brahman</s>, since the attainment in deep sleep is not the same as that in fainting, it is called 'half-attainment.'
The 'halfness' is by virtue of the similarity and dissimilarity [between the two].

If this [fainting] were not a separate state, then since [it already differs from deep sleep], one would have to seek another explanation [for the difference] by dissolving [fainting into deep sleep].
But if there is non-difference [between them], no separate explanation is needed — thus is the purpose of the investigation. //10//

body.translated_text:
For example: someone risen from sleep says, 'I slept well; my limbs are light; my mind is clear.' Another says, 'I slept painfully; my limbs are heavy; my mind is confused and restless.'
Nor does sleep thereby become [essentially] different.
Similarly, even with the variation [of fainting], fainting is not [essentially] different from deep sleep.
Therefore, because of the absence of common recognition [of fainting as a separate state], it follows that this is not a fifth state — this being the prima facie conclusion.
This being the prima facie conclusion, [the established view] is stated: Although there is a similarity between fainting and deep sleep in the subsidence of specific cognition, there is no identity.
For the waking and dream states are not identical merely because of the similarity in the presence of specific cognition.
Rather, [they are distinguished] by the presence and absence of the activity of the external sense-organs. Similarly, fainting differs from deep sleep because of the difference in purpose, cause, and defining characteristic.
For the attainment of <s>Brahman</s> for the purpose of the removal of fatigue is deep sleep.
But the attainment of <s>Brahman</s> for the purpose of abandoning the body is fainting.
Although fainting may occur without death, nevertheless, without fainting there is no death — hence fainting is for the purpose of death.
Because fainting is caused by [being struck with] a pestle-blow and the like, while deep sleep is caused by fatigue and the like; and because of the difference in defining characteristics — the contraction of the pupils and the like [characterize] fainting, while a serene countenance and the like [characterize deep sleep] — and because between [genuine] deep sleep and [merely seeming] deep sleep, even when there is a sub-difference, there is identity because of the non-difference of cause, purpose, and defining characteristic.

body.text:
#na sthānato 'pi parasyobhayaliṅgaṃ sarvatra hi# /
avāntarasaṃgatimāha- #yena brahmaṇā suṣuptādiṣviti# /
yadyapi 'tadananyatvamārambhaṇaśabdādibhyaḥ' ityatra niṣprapañcameva brahmopapāditaṃ tathāpi prapañcaliṅgānāṃ bahvīnāṃ śrutīnāṃ darśanādbhavati punarvicikitsā atastannivāraṇāyārambhaḥ /
tasya ca tattvajñānamapavargopayogīti prayojanavān vicāraḥ /
body.translated_text:
'Not even from [the difference of] location (<s>sthāna</s>) [does] the Supreme [<s>Brahman</s> have] dual characteristics; for [<s>Brahman</s> is present] everywhere' — thus.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the internal connection: 'That <s>Brahman</s> with which [the <s>jīva</s> unites] in deep sleep and the like' — thus.
Although in [the <s>sūtra</s>] 'That non-difference, because of the words "origination" and the like' (<s>tadananyatvam ārambhaṇaśabdādibhyaḥ</s>), <s>Brahman</s> was established as being without phenomenal manifestation, nevertheless, because of observing many <s>Śruti</s>s with indicatory marks pointing to phenomenal manifestation, a doubt arises again; hence the commencement [of this <s>adhikaraṇa</s>] is for the purpose of removing that [doubt].
And the investigation is purposeful, since the knowledge of Its true nature is conducive to final liberation (<s>apavarga</s>).

body.text:
tatrobhayaliṅgaśravaṇādubhayarūpatvaṃ brahmaṇaḥ prāptam /
tatrāpi saviśeṣatvanirviśeṣatvayorvirodhātsvābhāvikatvānupapatterekaṃ svato 'paraṃ tu parataḥ /
naca yatparatastadapāramārthikam /
nahi cakṣurādīnāṃ svataḥpramāṇabhūtānāṃ doṣato 'prāmāṇyamapāramārthikam /
viparyajñānalakṣaṇakāryānutpādaprasaṅgāt /
tasmādubhayaliṅgakaśāstraprāmāṇyādubhayarūpatā brahmaṇaḥ pāramārthikīti prāpta ucyate-na sthānata upādhito 'pi parasya brahmaṇa ubhayacihnatvasaṃbhavaḥ /
ekaṃ hi pāramārthikamanyadadhyāripatam /
pāramārthikatve hyupādhijanitasya rūpasya brahmaṇaḥ pariṇāmo bhavet /
sa ca prākpratiṣiddhaḥ /
tatpāriśeṣyātsphaṭikamaṇeriva svabhāvasvacchaghavalasya lākṣārasavasekopādhirūpaṇimā sarvagandhatvādiraupādhiko brahmaṇyadhyasya iti paśyāmo nirviśeṣatāpratipādanārthatvācchutīnām /
saviśeṣatāyāmapi 'yaścāyamasyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ tejomayaḥ' ityādīnāṃ śrutīnāṃ brahmaikatvapratipādanaparatvādekatvanānātvayoścaikasminnasaṃbhavādekatvāṅgatvenaiva nānātvapratipādanaparyavasānāt, nānātvasya pramāṇāntarasiddhatayānuvādyatvādekatvasya cānadhigatervidheyatvopapatterbhedadarśananindayā ca sākṣādbhūyasībhiḥ śrutibhirabhedapratipānādākāravadbrahmaviṣayāṇāṃ ca kāsāṃcicchutīnāmupāsanāparatvamasati bādhake 'nyaparādvacanātpratīyamānamapi gṛhyate /
yathā devatānāṃ vigrahavattvam /

children.translated_text: And there are here hundreds of <s>Śruti</s>s that, by directly negating duality, have as their primary purport the teaching of non-duality.
And some <s>Śruti</s>s that state duality have as their purport the dissolution of that [duality] into [non-duality].

children.text: tasmānnirviśeṣamekarūpaṃ caitanyaikarasaṃ sadbrahma paramārthataḥ, viśeṣāśca sarvagandhatvavāmanītvādaya upādhivaśādadhyastā iti siddham /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that <s>Brahman</s> is ultimately without qualification, of a single form, of the sole essence of consciousness (<s>caitanya-ekarasa</s>), and real (<s>sat</s>); while the qualifications — 'possessing all fragrances,' 'being of the form of a dwarf,' and the like — are superimposed due to the force of limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>).
The rest is of transparent meaning. //11//

body.translated_text:
Therein — because of hearing of dual characteristics (<s>ubhayaliṅga</s>), the dual nature of <s>Brahman</s> is the prima facie conclusion.
Moreover, since being qualified (<s>saviśeṣatva</s>) and being unqualified (<s>nirviśeṣatva</s>) are contradictory, their being [both] intrinsic (<s>svābhāvika</s>) is untenable; hence one is intrinsic and the other is extrinsic (<s>parataḥ</s>).
And it is not [the case] that what is extrinsic is non-ultimate.
For the invalidity of the eyes and the like — which are intrinsically valid means of knowledge — arising from a defect is not non-ultimate.
Because then, the effect characterized as erroneous cognition would not be produced [at all].
Therefore, because of the validity of the scripture that has dual characteristics, the dual nature of <s>Brahman</s> is ultimately real — this being the prima facie conclusion, [the established view] is stated: Not even from the [difference of] location — i.e., from the limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) — is the dual-characteristedness of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> possible.
For one [characteristic] is ultimate, the other is superimposed.
If the <s>upādhi</s>-generated form were ultimate, <s>Brahman</s> would be subject to transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>).
And that has been refuted earlier.
Therefore, by elimination, just as the crystal gem — whose intrinsic nature is clear and bright — has its coloration through the limiting adjunct of the infusion of lac-dye, so too the [attributes of] 'possessing all fragrances' and the like, being <s>upādhi</s>-based, are superimposed upon <s>Brahman</s> — thus we understand. [This is] because the <s>Śruti</s>s have the purpose of teaching the unqualified nature [of <s>Brahman</s>].
Even among the <s>Śruti</s>s that teach the qualified nature, those such as 'And he who is in this earth, resplendent with light (<s>tejomaya</s>)' and the like have as their primary purport the teaching of the oneness of <s>Brahman</s>; and since oneness and plurality cannot coexist in one [entity], they culminate in teaching plurality only as an accessory to oneness. Since plurality is already established by other means of knowledge and is thus [merely] reiterated (<s>anuvādya</s>), and since oneness, being previously unknown, is fittingly the newly enjoined content (<s>vidheya</s>), and since [the <s>Śruti</s>s] directly teach non-difference through the more numerous [passages] that censure seeing difference — and since some <s>Śruti</s>s about <s>Brahman</s> with form have as their purport meditation (<s>upāsana</s>), which is accepted in the absence of a sublating [cognition], even though its meaning may be inferred from a statement whose purport lies elsewhere.
Just as the possession of bodily form by the deities [is accepted for meditation purposes].

body.text:
#atra keciddve adhikaraṇe kalpayantīti# /
kiṃ sāllakṣaṇaṃ ca prakāśalakṣaṇaṃ ca brahma kiṃ sallakṣaṇameva brahmeti prakāśalakṣaṇameveti tatra pūrvapakṣaṃ gṛhṇāti- #prakāśavaccāvaiyarthyāt# /
cakārātsacca /
avaiyarthyāt /
brahmaṇi sacchuteḥ siddhāntayati- #āha ca tanmātram# /
prakāśamātram /
nahi sattvaṃ nāma prakāśarūpādanyat, yathā sarvagandhatvādayo 'pi tu prakāśarūpameva saditi nobhayarūpatvaṃ brahmaṇa ityarthaḥ /
tadetadanenopanyasya dūṣitam /
body.translated_text:
'Here some postulate two <s>adhikaraṇa</s>s' — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s> says].
[The question is:] Is <s>Brahman</s> characterized both by Being (<s>sat</s>) and by Consciousness (<s>prakāśa</s>), or is it characterized by Being alone, or by Consciousness alone? Therein, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] takes up the prima facie view: 'Like light, and because of non-purposelessness' — thus.
The word 'and' [includes]: and Being (<s>sat</s>).
'Because of non-purposelessness' — [both are needed to avoid purposelessness of the <s>Śruti</s>s that teach each].
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] establishes the <s>siddhānta</s> with the <s>Śruti</s> about Being in <s>Brahman</s>: 'It says: That alone' — thus.
Mere Consciousness (<s>prakāśamātra</s>).
For Being (<s>sattva</s>) is not something other than the form of Consciousness; just as 'possessing all fragrances' and the like [are not different from <s>Brahman</s>]; rather, the form of Consciousness itself is Being — hence <s>Brahman</s> does not have a dual nature — this is the meaning.
Having presented this, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes it.

body.text:
sattāprakāśayorekatve nobhayalakṣaṇatvam /
bhede na sthānato 'pīti nirākṛtamiti nādhikaraṇāntaraṃ prayojayati /
paramārthastvabheda eva prakarṣaprakāśavaditi /
#sarveṣāṃ ca sādhāraṇe pravilayārthatve sati 'arūpavadeva hi tatpradhānatvāt' iti vinigamanakāraṇavacanamanavakāśaṃ syāt# /
evaṃ hi tasyāvakāśaḥ syādyāda kāścidupāsanāparatayā rūpamācakṣīran kāścinnīrūpabrahmapratipādanaparā bhaveyuḥ /
sarvāsāṃ tu pravilayārthatvena nīrūpabrahmapratipādanārthatve ukto vinigamanaheturna syādityarthaḥ /
#ekaniyogapratīteḥ prayājadarśapūrṇamāsavākyavadityadhikārābhiprāyam,#anubandhabhedāttu bhinno 'nayorapi niyoga iti /
#ko 'yaṃ prapañcapravilaya iti# /
vāstavasya vā prapañcasya pravilayaḥ sarpiṣa ivāgnisaṃyogāt /
samāropitasya vā rajjvāṃ sarpabhāvasyeva rajjutattvaparijñānāt /
na tāvadvāstavaḥ sarvasādhāraṇaḥ pṛthivyādiprapañcaḥ puruṣamātreṇa śakyaḥ samucchettum /
apica prahlādaśukādibhiḥ puruṣadhaureyaiḥ samūlamunmūlitaḥ prapañca iti śūnyaṃ jagadbhavet /
naca vāstavaṃ tattvajñānena śakyaṃ samucchettum /
āropitarūpavirodhitvāttvajñānasyetyuktam /
samāropitarūpastu prapañco brahmatattvajñāpanaparaireva vākyairbrahmatattvamavabodhayadbhiḥ śakyaḥ samucchettumiti kṛtamatra vidhinā /
nahi vidhiśatenāpi vinā tattvāvabodhanaṃ pravartasvātmajñāna iti vā kuru prapañcapravilayaṃ veti pravartitaḥ śaknoti prapañcapravilayaṃ kartum /
na cāsyātmajñānavidhiṃ vinā vedāntārthabrahmatattvāvabodho na bhavati /
maulikasya svādhyāyādhyayanavirodhereva vivakṣitārthatayā sakalasya vedarāśeḥ phalavadarthāvabodhanaparatāmāpādayato vidyamānatvāt /
anyathā karmavidhivākyānyapi vidhyantaramapekṣeranniti /
naca cintāsākṣātkārayorvidhiriti tattvasamīkṣāyāmasmābhirūpapāditam /
vistareṇa cāyamarthastatraiva prapañcitaḥ /
tasmāt 'jartilayavāgvā juhuyāt' itivadvidhisarūpā ete 'ātmā vā are draṣṭavya' ityādayo na tu vidhaya iti /
tadidamuktam- #draṣṭavyādiśabdā api tattvābhimudhīkaraṇapradhānā na tattvāvabodhavidhipradhānā iti# /
apica brahmatattvaṃ niṣprapañcamuktaṃ na tatra niyojyaḥ kaścitsaṃbhavati /
jīvo hi niyojyo bhavet, sa cetprapañcapakṣe vartate ko niyojyastasyocchinnatvāt /
atha brahmapakṣe tathāpyaniyojyaḥ, brahmaṇo 'niyojyatvāt /
atha brahmaṇo 'nanyo 'pyavidyayānya iveti niyojyaḥ /
tadayuktam /
brahmabhāvaṃ pāramārthikamavagamayatāgamenāvidyāyā nirastatvāt /
tasmānniyojyābhāvādapi na niyogaḥ /
tadidamuktam- #jīvo nāma prapañcapakṣasyaiveti# /
apica jñānavidhaparatve tanmātrāttu jñānasyānutpattestattvapratipādanaparatvamabhyupagamanīyam /
tatra varaṃ tattvapratipādanaparatvamevāstu tasyāvaśyābhyupagantavyatvenobhayavādisiddhatvāt /
evaṃ ca kṛtaṃ tattvajñānavidhinetyāha- #jñeyābhimukhasyāpīti# /
naca tacchakyaṃ vāpi yuktamityāha- #naca pramāṇāntareṇeti /
kiñcānyanniyoganiṣṭhatayaiva ca paryavasyatyāmnāye yadabhyupagataṃ#bhavadbhiḥ śāstraparyālocanayāniyojyabrahmātmatvaṃ jīvasyeti tadetacchāstrāvirodhādapramāṇakam /
athaitacchāstramaniyojyabrahmātmatvaṃ ca jīvasya pratipādayati jīvaṃ ca niyuktaṃ tato dvyarthaṃ ca viruddhārtha ca syādityāha- #atheti# /
darśapaurṇamāsādivākyeṣu jīvasyāniyojyasyāpi vastuto 'dhyastaniyojyabhāvasya niyojyatā yuktā /
nahi tadvākyaṃ tasya niyojyatāmāhāpi tu laukikapramāṇasiddhāṃ niyojyatāmāśritya darśapūrṇamāsau vidhatte /
idaṃ tu niyojyatāmapanayati ca niyuṅkte ceti durghaṭamiti bhāvaḥ /
#niyogaparatāyāṃ ceti# /
paurvāparyālocanayā vedāntānāṃ tattvaniṣṭhatā śrutā na śrutā niyoganiṣṭhatetyarthaḥ /
apica niyoganiṣṭhatve vākyasya darśapaurṇāmāsakarmaṇa ivāpūrvāvāntaravyāpārādātmajñānakarmaṇo 'pyapūrvāvāntaravyāpārādeva svargādiphalavanmokṣasyānandarūpaphalasya siddhiḥ /

children.translated_text: And thus, [liberation] would be impermanent and surpassable, like heaven — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Like the fruit of [ritual] action#.'
'#Moreover, in the <s>Brahman</s>-sentences#' —

For in teachings [about <s>Brahman</s>] — both with and without phenomenal attributes (<s>saprapañca</s> and <s>niṣprapañca</s>) — since the qualifications (<s>sādhyānubandha</s>) to be accomplished differ, the [claim of] a single injunction is unestablished.

But in the sentences about the <s>Darśa-Pūrṇamāsa</s> and the <s>Prayāja</s>s, although there is a difference in qualifications, nevertheless, because the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be accomplished) in the <s>adhikāra</s> (jurisdiction) portion does not differ, there is non-difference [of injunction]. //21//

body.translated_text:
If existence (<s>sattā</s>) and luminosity (<s>prakāśa</s>) are one, there would be no dual characterization.
If they are different, [the problem persists] even from [different] loci — this has been refuted, and hence no further <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic of inquiry) is prompted.
The ultimate truth, however, is that there is non-difference alone, like intense illumination.
'#And when all [Upaniṣadic passages] have the common purpose of [teaching] the dissolution [of the phenomenal world], the statement "Because it is formless, for that is its predominant [nature]" (<s>arūpavad eva hi tat pradhānatvāt</s>) — which provides the reason for determination — would have no scope#.'
For [the sūtra] would have scope only if some [passages] were directed toward meditation (<s>upāsanā</s>) and described form, while others were directed toward teaching formless <s>Brahman</s>.
But if all [passages] have the purpose of [teaching] dissolution and hence of teaching formless <s>Brahman</s>, the stated reason for determination would be inapplicable — this is the meaning.
'#Because of the understanding of a single injunction, [this is] like the sentence of the <s>Prayāja</s>s and the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>#' — this is stated with the intent of [showing them as parts of] a single <s>adhikāra</s> (jurisdiction).
But because of the difference in qualifications (<s>anubandha</s>), the injunctions of these two are also distinct.
'#What is this dissolution of the phenomenal world?#'
[Is it] the dissolution of the real phenomenal world, like [the dissolution of] butter through contact with fire?
Or [is it the dissolution] of the superimposed [phenomenal world], like the snake-nature [superimposed] upon a rope through the knowledge of the rope's true nature?
To begin with, the real phenomenal world — common to all, [consisting of] earth and the like — cannot be annihilated by a mere person.
Moreover, if the phenomenal world were uprooted root and all by supreme persons such as <s>Prahlāda</s>, <s>Śuka</s>, and the like, the world would become void.
Nor can what is real be annihilated by knowledge of reality.
Because knowledge [of reality] is opposed only to what is superimposed — this has been stated.
But the superimposed phenomenal world can be annihilated by those very sentences that are directed toward teaching the reality of <s>Brahman</s> and that produce the understanding of <s>Brahman</s>'s reality — and thus there is no need for an injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) here.
For not even by a hundred injunctions can one who has been prompted [by an injunction] — 'Engage in Self-knowledge!' or 'Accomplish the dissolution of the phenomenal world!' — accomplish the dissolution of the phenomenal world.
Nor is it the case that without an injunction of Self-knowledge, the understanding of <s>Brahman</s>'s reality from <s>Vedānta</s> passages does not arise.
Because the original (<s>maulika</s>) [injunction of] <s>Svādhyāya</s>-study — having the desired import of [generating] the understanding of fruitful meaning — already exists, directing the entire mass of <s>Veda</s>s toward [generating] the understanding of fruitful meaning.
Otherwise, the sentences enjoining ritual action (<s>karmavidhi</s>) too would require yet another injunction [to motivate their study].
And that there is no injunction of reflection (<s>cintā</s>) and direct realization (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>) has been demonstrated by us in the <s>Tattvasamīkṣā</s>.
And this point has been elaborated there in detail.
Therefore, just as 'One should offer with <s>jartila</s> [mixed with] barley and speech,' these [passages] such as 'The Self indeed is to be seen' (<s>ātmā vā are draṣṭavyaḥ</s>) and the like are injunction-like in form but are not injunctions.
This is what is stated: '#The words "to be seen" (<s>draṣṭavya</s>) and the like too are primarily directed toward orienting [the mind] toward reality, not primarily toward enjoining the knowledge of reality#.'
Moreover, the reality of <s>Brahman</s> has been stated as devoid of phenomenal multiplicity — therein no possible person-to-be-enjoined (<s>niyojya</s>) exists.
For the <s>jīva</s> would be the one to be enjoined; but if it belongs to the side of phenomenal multiplicity, who is the person-to-be-enjoined, since it [the <s>jīva</s>] has been annihilated?
And if it belongs to the side of <s>Brahman</s>, even then it is not to be enjoined, since <s>Brahman</s> is not subject to injunction.
If it be said that though non-different from <s>Brahman</s>, it appears as if different through <s>avidyā</s>, and hence is subject to injunction —
that is unjustified.
Because <s>avidyā</s> has been negated by the scripture (<s>āgama</s>) that teaches the ultimate reality of <s>Brahman</s>-nature.
Therefore, even because of the absence of a person-to-be-enjoined, there is no injunction.
This is what is stated: '#The <s>jīva</s> indeed belongs to the side of phenomenal multiplicity#.'
Moreover, if [the <s>Vedānta</s> passages] were directed toward enjoining knowledge, then — since knowledge would not arise from that [injunction] alone — the directedness toward teaching reality must be accepted.
Therein, it is better that the directedness toward teaching reality alone should stand, since it must necessarily be accepted and is established for both parties [in the debate].
And thus, the injunction of knowledge of reality is unnecessary — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Even for one who is oriented toward the knowable#.'
And that this [injunction] is neither possible nor reasonable — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Nor through another means of knowledge#.'
'#Moreover, what has been accepted by you#' — namely, by examining scripture that everything culminates in injunction alone — '#that the <s>jīva</s> has the nature of the non-enjoinable <s>Brahman</s>#' — this, being unopposed by scripture, is without evidence [against it].
'#If this scripture both teaches the <s>Brahman</s>-selfhood of the <s>jīva</s>, which is not subject to injunction, and also enjoins the <s>jīva</s>, then it would serve two purposes and contain contradictory meanings#' — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#If so#.'
In the sentences of <s>Darśa-Pūrṇamāsa</s> and the like, the injunctive status of the <s>jīva</s> — who in reality is not subject to injunction — is reasonable, because of the superimposed status of being subject to injunction.
For that sentence does not teach the <s>jīva</s>'s being subject to injunction; rather, relying on the status of being subject to injunction that is established through worldly means of knowledge, it enjoins the <s>Darśa-Pūrṇamāsa</s> sacrifice.
But this [<s>Vedānta</s> passage] both removes the status of being subject to injunction and enjoins — this is impossible. This is the purport.
'#And if [the passages are] directed toward injunction#.'
By examining the sequential context, the directedness of the <s>Vedānta</s>s toward reality (<s>tattvaniṣṭhatā</s>) has been heard, not the directedness toward injunction (<s>niyoganiṣṭhatā</s>) — this is the meaning.
Moreover, if the sentences were directed toward injunction, then — just as in the case of the <s>Darśa-Pūrṇamāsa</s> ritual, where the fruit of heaven and the like is accomplished through the intermediate operation of <s>apūrva</s> (unseen potency) — so too for the action of Self-knowledge, the fruit of liberation characterized by bliss would be accomplished only through the intermediate operation of <s>apūrva</s>.

#prakṛtaitāvattvaṃ hi pratiṣedhati tato vravīti ca bhūyaḥ /
adhikaraṇaviṣayamāha-dve vāva brahmaṇo rūpe iti# /
dve eva brahmaṇo rūpe brahmaṇaḥ paramārthato 'rūpasyādhyāropite dve eva rūpe tābhyāṃ hi tadrūpyate /
te darśayati- #mūrte caivāmūrte ca# /
samuccīyamānāvadhāraṇam /
atra pṛthivyaptejāṃsi trīṇi bhūtāni brahmaṇo rūpaṃ mūrtaṃ mūrcchitāvayavamitaretarānupraviṣṭāvayavaṃ kaṭhinamiti yāvat /
tasyaiva viśeṣaṇāntarāṇi-martyaṃ maraṇadharmakam /
sthitamavyāpi /
avacchinnamiti yāvat /
sat anyebhyo viśiṣyamāṇamasādhāraṇadharmavaditi yāvat /
gandhasnehoṣṇatāścānyonyavyavacchedahetavo 'sādhāraṇā dharmāḥ /
tasyaitasya brahmarūpasya tejo 'bannasya caturviśeṣaṇasyaiṣa rasaḥ sāro ya eṣa savitā sapati /
athāmūrtaṃ vāyuścāntarikṣaṃ ca taddhi na kaṭhinamityamūrtametadamṛtamamaraṇadharmakam /
mūrtaṃ hi mūrtāntareṇābhihanyamānamavayavaviśleṣāddhvaṃsate natu tathābhāvaḥ saṃbhavatyamūrtasya /
etadyadeti gacchati vyāpnotīti /
etattyaṃ nityaparokṣamityarthaḥ /
tasyaitasyāmūrtasyāmṛtasyaitasya yata etasya tyasyaiṣa raso ya eṣa gatasmin savitṛmaṇḍale puruṣaḥ /
karaṇātmako hiraṇyagarbhaprāṇāhvayastyasya hyeṣa rasaḥ sāro nityaparokṣatā ca sāmyamityadhidaivatam /
athādhyātmamidameva mūrtaṃ yadanyatprāṇāntarākāśābhyāṃ bhūtatrayaṃ rīrārambhakametanmartyametatsthitametatsattasyaitasya mūrtasyaitasya martyasyaitasya sthitasyaitasya sata eṣa raso yaccakṣuḥ sato hyoṣa rasa iti /
athāmūrtaṃ prāṇaśca yaścāyamantarātmannākāśa etadamṛtametadyadetattyaṃ tasyaitasyāmūrtasyaitasyāmṛtasyaitasya yata etasya tyasyaiṣa raso yo 'yaṃ dakṣiṇekṣan puruṣastyasya hyeṣa rasaḥ /
liṅgasya hi karaṇātmakasya hiraṇyagarbhasya dakṣiṇamakṣyadhiṣṭhānaṃ śruteradhigatam /
tadevaṃ brahmaṇa aupādhikayormūrtāmūrtayorādhyātmikādhidaivikayoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvena vibhāgo vyākhyātaḥ sattyacchabdavācyayoḥ /
athedānīṃ tasya karaṇātmanaḥ puruṣasya liṅgasya rūpaṃ vaktavyam /
etaduktaṃ bhati-mūrtāmūrtavāsanāvijñānamayasya vicitraṃ rūpaṃ liṅgasyeti /
tadevaṃ niravaśeṣaṃ savāsanaṃ satyarūpamuktvā yattatsatyasya satyamuktaṃ brahma tatsvarūpāvadhāraṇārthamidamārabhyate /
yataḥ satyasya rūpaṃ niḥśeṣamuktamato 'vaśiṣṭaṃ satyasya yatsatyaṃ tasyānantaraṃ taduktihetukaṃ svarūpaṃ vakyavyamityāha- #athāta ādeśaḥ#kathanaṃ satyasatyasya paramātmanastamāha- #neti netīti# /
etadarthakathanārthamidamadhikaraṇam /
nanu kimetāvadevādeśyaṃ nāparamastītyarthaḥ /
atraivamarthenetinā yatsaṃnihitaṃ parāmṛṣṭaṃ tanniṣidhyate nañā saṃnihitaṃ ca mūrtāmūrtaṃ savāsanaṃ rūpadvayam /
tadavacchedakatvena ca brahma /
tatredaṃ vicāryate-kiṃ rūpadvayaṃ savāsanaṃ brahma ca sarvameva ca pratiṣidhyate, uta brahmaivātha savāsanaṃ rūpadvayaṃ brahma tu pariśiṣyata iti /
yadyapi teṣu teṣu vedāntapradeśeṣu brahmasvarūpaṃ pratipāditaṃ tadasadbhāvajñānaṃ ca ninditam /
'astītyevopalabdhavyaḥ' iti cāsya sattvamavadhāritaṃ tathāpi sadbodharūpaṃ tadbrahma savāsanamūrtāmūrtarūpasādhāraṇatayā ca sāmānyaṃ tasya caite viśeṣā mūrtāmūrtādayaḥ /
naca tattadviśeṣaniṣedhe sāmānyamavasthātumarhati nirviśeṣasya sāmānyasyāyogāt /
yathāhuḥ-'nirviśeṣaṃ na sāmānyaṃ bhavecchuśaviṣāṇavat' iti /
tasmāttadviśeṣedhe 'pi tatsāmānyasya brahmaṇo 'navasthānātsarvasyaivāyaṃ niṣedhaḥ /
ata eva nahyetasmāditi netyanyatparamastīti niṣedhāt paraṃ nāstīti sarvaniṣedhameva tattvamāha śrutiḥ /
'astītyevopalabdhavyaḥ' iti copāsanāvidhānavanneyaṃ, na tvastitvamevāsya tattvam /
tatpraśaṃsārthaṃ cāsadbhāvajñānanindā /
yaccānyatra brahmasvarūpapratipādanaṃ tadapi mūrtāmūrtarūpapratipādanavanniṣedhārtham /
asaṃnihito 'pi ca tatra niṣedho yogyatvātsaṃbhansyate /
yathāhuḥ-'yena yasyābhisaṃbandho dūrasthasyāpi tena saḥ' iti /
tasmātsarvasyaivāviśeṣeṇa niṣedha iti prathamaḥ pakṣaḥ /
athavā pṛthivyādiprapañcasya samastasya pratyakṣādipramāṇasiddhatvāt, brahmaṇastu vāṅmanasāgocaratayā sakalapramāṇavirahāt, katarasyāstu niṣedha iti viśaye prapañcapratiṣedhe samastapratyakṣādivyākopaprasaṅgāt, brahmapratiṣedho tvavyākopādbrahmaiva pratiṣedhena saṃbadhyate yogyatvānna prapañcastadvaiparītyāt, vīpsā tu tadatyantābhāvasūcanāyeti madhyamaḥ pakṣaḥ /
tatra prathamaṃ pakṣaṃ nirākaroti- #na tāvadubhayapratiṣedha upapadyate śūnyavādaprasaṅgāditi# /
ayamabhisaṃdhiḥ-upādhayo hyamī pṛthivyādayo 'vidyākalpitā na tu śoṇakarkādaya iva viśeṣā aśvatvasya /
na copādhivigame upahitasyābhāvo 'pratītirvā /
nahyupādīnāṃ darpaṇamaṇikṛpāṇādīnāmapagame mukhasyābhāvo 'pratitirvā /
tasmādupādhiniṣedhe 'pi nopahitasya śaśaviṣāṇāyamānatāpratyayo vā /
na cetīti saṃnidhānāviśeṣātsarvasya pratiṣedhyatvamiti yuktam /
nahi bhāvamanupāśritya pratiṣedha upapadyate /
kiñciddha kkacinniṣidhyate /
nahyanāśrayaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ śakyaḥ pratipattum /
tadidamuktam- #apariśiṣyamāṇe cānyasminya itaraḥ pratiṣeddhumārabhyate tasya pratiṣedbhumaśakyatvāttasyaiva paramārthatvāpatteḥ pratiṣādhānupapattiḥ# /
madhyamaṃ pakṣaṃ pratikṣipati- #nāpi brahmapratiṣedha upapadyate# /
yuktaṃ yannaisargikāvidyāprāptaḥ prapañcaḥ pratiṣidhyate prāptipūrvakatvātpratiṣedhasya /
brahma tu nāvidyāsiddhaṃ, nāpi pramāṇāntarāt /
tasmācchabdena prāptaṃ pratiṣedhanīyam /
tathāca yastasya śabdaḥ prāpakaḥ sa tatpara iti sa brahmaṇi pramāṇamiti kathamasya niṣedho 'pi pramāṇavān /
naca paryudāsādhikaraṇapūrvapakṣanyāyena vikalpaḥ vastuni siddhasvabhāve tadanupapatteḥ /
na cāvāṅmanasagocaro buddhāvalokhituṃ śakyaḥ /
aśakyaśca kathaṃ niṣidhyate /
prapañcastvanādyavidyāsiddho 'nūdya brahmaṇi pratiṣidyata iti yuktam /
tadimāmanupapattimabhipretyoktam-'nāpi brahmapratiṣedha upapadyate' iti /
hetvantaramāha-brahma te bravāṇīti /
upakramavirodhāditi /
upakramaparāmarśopasaṃhāraparyālocanayā hi vedāntānāṃ sarveṣāmeva brahmaparatvamupapāditaṃ prathame 'dhyāye /
na cāsatyāmākāṅkṣāyāṃ dūratasthena pratiṣedhenaiṣāṃ saṃbandhaḥ saṃbhavati /
yacca vāṅmanasātītatayā brahmaṇastatpratiṣedhasya na pramāṇāntaravirodha iti tatrāha- #vāṅmanasātītatvamapīti# /
pratipādayanti vedāntā mahatā prayatnena brahma /
naca niṣedhasya tatpratipādanam, anupapatterityuktamadhastāt /
idānīṃ tu niṣprayojanamityuktaṃ 'prakṣālanāddhi paṅkasya' iti nyāyāt /
tasmādvedāntavācā manasi saṃnidhānādbrahmaṇo vāṅmanasātītatvaṃ nāñjasamapi tu pratipādanaprakriyopakrama eṣaḥ /
yathā gavādayo viṣayāḥ sākṣācchṛṅgagrāhikayā pratipādyante pratiyante ca naivaṃ brahma /
yathāhuḥ-'bhedaprapañcavilayadvāreṇa ca nirūpaṇam' iti /
nanu prakṛtapratiṣedhe brahmaṇo 'pi kasmānna pratiṣejha ityata āha- #yaddhi prakṛtaṃ prapañcitaṃ ceti# /
pradhānaṃ prakṛtaṃ prapañcasya pradhānaṃ na brahma tasya ṣaṣṭhyantatayā prapañcāvacchekatvenāpradhānatvādityarthaḥ /
tato 'nyadbravītīti neti netīti pratiṣedhādanyadbhūyo bravītīti tannirvacanam /
nahyetasmādityasya yadā nahyetasmāditi neti netyādiṣṭādbrahmaṇo 'nyatparamastīti vyākhyānaṃ tadā prapañcapratiṣedhādanyadbrahmaiva bravītīti vyākhyeyam /
yadā tu nahyetasmāditi sarvanāmnā pratiṣedho brahmaṇa ādeśaḥ parāmṛśyate tadāpi prapañcapratiṣedhamātraṃ na pratipattavyamapi tu tena pratiṣedhena bhāvarūpaṃ brahmopalakṣyate /
kasmādtyata āha- #tato bravīti ca bhūya iti# /
yasmātpratiṣedhasya parastādapi bravīti /
atha brahmaṇo nāmadheyaṃ nāma satyasya satyamiti tadvyācaṣṭe śrutiḥ-'prāṇā vai satyam' iti /
māhārajanādyupamitaṃ liṅgamupalaṅayati /
tat khalu satyamitarāpekṣayā tasyāpi paraṃ satyaṃ brahma /

children.translated_text: Thus, since beyond the negation [the <s>Śruti</s>] speaks of that [<s>Brahman</s>], it is not mere negation of the phenomenal world, but <s>Brahman</s> as a positive entity.

children.text: tadevaṃ pūrvasmin vyākhyāne nirvacanaṃ bravītīti vyākhyātam /
children.translated_text: Thus, in the former interpretation, [the phrase] 'then it speaks further' was explained as 'it gives the etymological derivation (<s>nirvacana</s>).'
But in this [latter] interpretation, it should be explained as: 'it speaks "the real of the real."'
The rest has transparent meaning. //23//

body.translated_text:
'#For [the <s>Śruti</s>] negates just this much of what was presented, and then speaks further.#'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the subject-matter of the <s>adhikaraṇa</s>: '#There are indeed two forms of <s>Brahman</s>#.'
There are exactly two forms of <s>Brahman</s> — two forms superimposed upon <s>Brahman</s>, which is in ultimate reality formless — for it is characterized by those two.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] shows them: '#The formed (<s>mūrta</s>) and the formless (<s>amūrta</s>)#.'
The emphatic particle is used in conjunction with the cumulative [conjunction].
Here, the three elements — earth, water, and fire — are the formed (<s>mūrta</s>) form of <s>Brahman</s> — 'formed' meaning solidified, having parts that have entered into one another, hard — this is the meaning.
Its other qualifiers are: 'mortal' (<s>martya</s>) — subject to the law of death;
'stationary' (<s>sthita</s>) — non-pervading,
i.e., delimited.
'Existent' (<s>sat</s>) — meaning distinguished from others, possessing distinctive properties.
Smell, viscosity, and heat are the distinctive properties that serve as the means of mutual differentiation.
Of this form of <s>Brahman</s> — consisting of fire, water, and food, with these four qualifiers — the essence (<s>rasa</s>), the quintessence, is the sun (<s>Savitṛ</s>) who rules.
Now the formless (<s>amūrta</s>): air and space — for these are not hard, hence formless. This is immortal (<s>amṛta</s>) — not subject to the law of death.
For the formed, being struck by another formed [entity], perishes through the separation of its parts; but such a state is not possible for the formless.
'That which goes' (<s>yat</s>) — meaning that which pervades.
'<s>Tya</s>' — meaning eternally invisible; this is the meaning.
Of this formless, of this immortal, of this '<s>yat</s>,' of this '<s>tya</s>' — the essence is the <s>Puruṣa</s> who is in the orb of the sun.
[This <s>Puruṣa</s>] consists of the instruments [of cognition], is called <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> and <s>Prāṇa</s>; His essence and His being eternally invisible are shared [by both] — this is the <s>adhidaivata</s> (cosmic) aspect.
Now the <s>ādhyātma</s> (individual) aspect: this very formed [aspect] — that which is the triad of elements constituting the body, other than <s>Prāṇa</s> and the internal space — this is mortal, this is stationary, this is existent. Of this formed, of this mortal, of this stationary, of this existent — the essence is the eye; for 'of the existent, this is indeed the essence.'
Now the formless: <s>Prāṇa</s> and the space within the self — this is immortal, this is '<s>yat</s>,' this is '<s>tya</s>.' Of this formless, of this immortal, of this '<s>yat</s>,' of this '<s>tya</s>' — the essence is the <s>Puruṣa</s> in the right eye; for His essence [is there].
For it is learned from <s>Śruti</s> that the right eye is the seat of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) consisting of the instruments [of cognition].
Thus the division of <s>Brahman</s>'s two conditioned [forms] — the formed and the formless, the individual and the cosmic — has been explained in terms of cause and effect, denoted by the words '<s>sat</s>' and '<s>tya</s>.'
Now the form of that <s>Puruṣa</s> who consists of the instruments, who is the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body), must be stated.
What is meant is this: the <s>liṅga</s>, being constituted of cognition suffused with the impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of the formed and the formless, has a variegated form.
Thus, having stated exhaustively the form of 'the real' (<s>satya</s>) together with its impressions, now — regarding that which was called 'the real of the real' (<s>satyasya satyam</s>), namely <s>Brahman</s> — this [discussion] is commenced for the purpose of ascertaining its essential nature.
Since the form of 'the real' has been stated completely, what remains — 'the real of the real' — its essential nature must be stated immediately after, as it is occasioned by that [previous statement] — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Now, therefore, the teaching#' — the declaration of the <s>Paramātman</s> who is 'the real of the real' — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states it: '#Not this, not this (<s>neti neti</s>)#.'
This <s>adhikaraṇa</s> is for the purpose of explaining the meaning of this.
Objection: what — is only this much to be taught and nothing further? — this is the meaning.
Here, by 'not' (<s>iti</s>) with this meaning, what is proximate and referred to is negated by the negative particle, and what is proximate is the twofold form — formed and formless — together with its impressions.
And <s>Brahman</s> is the delimitor of that [twofold form].
Here this is examined: Is the twofold form together with its impressions and <s>Brahman</s> — all of it — negated? Or is <s>Brahman</s> alone [negated]? Or is the twofold form together with its impressions [negated] while <s>Brahman</s> remains?
Although in various <s>Vedānta</s> passages the essential nature of <s>Brahman</s> has been taught, and the cognition of its non-existence has been censured,
and its existence has been ascertained through 'It is to be apprehended as existing alone' — nevertheless, <s>Brahman</s>, whose form is being and consciousness, is common to the formed and formless together with their impressions, while the formed, formless, and the like are its particulars.
And when each particular is negated, the universal cannot persist, because a universal without particulars is impossible.
As they say: 'A universal without particulars cannot exist, like the horn of a hare.'
Therefore, even when those particulars are negated, since the universal that is <s>Brahman</s> cannot persist, this is a negation of everything.
For this very reason, 'for there is nothing higher than this "not"' — since there is nothing beyond the negation, the <s>Śruti</s> declares that the reality is nothing but complete negation.
And 'It is to be apprehended as existing alone' should be construed as an injunction of meditation (<s>upāsanāvidhi</s>), not that its existence is its reality.
And the censure of the cognition of non-existence is for the purpose of praising that [meditation].
And whatever teaching of <s>Brahman</s>'s essential nature exists elsewhere — that too, like the teaching of the formed and formless forms, is for the purpose of negation.
And even though the negation is not proximate there, it is possible because of its fitness [to apply].
As they say: 'Through whatever connection a thing has [with another], even when distant, it is [connected] with that.'
Therefore, there is negation of everything without distinction — this is the first view.
Alternatively, since the entire phenomenal world (<s>prapañca</s>) of earth and the like is established by means of knowledge such as perception and the like, while <s>Brahman</s>, being beyond speech and mind, lacks all means of knowledge — the question is: of which should there be negation? In the case of negating the phenomenal world, there would be the unwanted consequence of invalidating all perception and the like; but the negation of <s>Brahman</s>, not entailing [such] invalidation — <s>Brahman</s> alone is connected with negation, because of fitness, not the phenomenal world, since it is the opposite [in fitness]. And the repetition [of <s>neti neti</s>] is to indicate its absolute non-existence — this is the middle view.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes the first view: '#The negation of both is not tenable, because of the unwanted consequence of the doctrine of the void (<s>śūnyavāda</s>)#.'
The intention is this: these conditioning adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>s) — earth and the like — are imagined by <s>avidyā</s>, not real particulars [of <s>Brahman</s>] like the redness of <s>śoṇaka</s>-cattle is of horse-ness.
Nor does the conditioned [entity] cease to exist or be cognized when the conditioning adjuncts are removed.
For the face does not cease to exist or be cognized when the conditioning adjuncts — mirror, gem, sword, and the like — are removed.
Therefore, even when the conditioning adjuncts are negated, there is neither the non-existence of the conditioned [entity] nor the cognition of it as [unreal] like a hare's horn.
Nor is it reasonable [to argue] that, since 'not' is equally proximate to everything, everything is negated.
For negation is not possible without being grounded in a positive entity.
Something is negated somewhere.
For a negation without a locus cannot be apprehended.
This is what was stated: '#And when nothing else remains as that in reference to which the other [entity] could be negated, since the negation of that [remaining entity] is impossible, and since that itself would end up being the ultimate reality, negation is untenable#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] rejects the middle view: '#Nor is the negation of <s>Brahman</s> tenable#.'
It is reasonable that the phenomenal world, attained through innate <s>avidyā</s>, is negated — because negation presupposes prior attainment.
But <s>Brahman</s> is not established through <s>avidyā</s>, nor through another means of knowledge.
Therefore, what is attained through scripture (<s>śabda</s>) should be negated.
But if so, the scripture that is the means of attaining it has <s>Brahman</s> as its purport — and that scripture is a valid means of knowledge regarding <s>Brahman</s> — so how can its negation also be authoritative?
Nor is an option [between affirmation and negation] possible — as in the prima facie view of the <s>paryudāsa adhikaraṇa</s> — regarding an entity whose nature is already established, because of the impossibility thereof.
Nor can that which is beyond speech and mind be beheld by the intellect.
And how can what cannot be beheld be negated?
But the phenomenal world, established through beginningless <s>avidyā</s>, being restated (<s>anūdya</s>), is negated with respect to <s>Brahman</s> — this is reasonable.
With this impossibility in mind, it was stated: 'Nor is the negation of <s>Brahman</s> tenable.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states another reason: '#I shall teach you <s>Brahman</s>#.'
Because of contradiction with the introduction.
For the <s>Brahman</s>-directedness of all <s>Vedānta</s> passages has been established in the first <s>adhyāya</s> through the examination of the introduction, reference, and conclusion.
And in the absence of an expectation [for further information], the connection of these [passages] with a distant negation is not possible.
And as for the [argument] that because <s>Brahman</s> transcends speech and mind, the negation of <s>Brahman</s> would not contradict other means of knowledge — to that [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#The transcendence of speech and mind also#.'
The <s>Vedānta</s> passages teach <s>Brahman</s> with great effort.
And negation is not such teaching — because of the impossibility [of negation serving as teaching], as stated above.
Now, however, it is stated that [negation as teaching] would be purposeless — by the maxim 'for washing [merely produces more] mud.'
Therefore, the transcendence of <s>Brahman</s> beyond speech and mind is not straightforward from the <s>Vedānta</s> statement [alone]; rather, this is the commencement of the method of teaching.
Just as cows and other objects are taught and cognized directly through 'horn-grasping' perception, <s>Brahman</s> is not [taught] in that way.
As they say: 'The ascertainment [of <s>Brahman</s> is] through the dissolution of the phenomenal expansion of differences.'
Objection: When what is contextually presented is being negated, why should <s>Brahman</s> not also be negated? — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#For what is contextually presented and elaborated#.'
The principal (<s>pradhāna</s>) contextual subject is the phenomenal world, not <s>Brahman</s> — because <s>Brahman</s>, being in the genitive case, is subordinate as the delimitor of the phenomenal world — this is the meaning.
'Then it speaks something other [than the negation]' — the explanation is: '<s>neti neti</s>' — from the negation, it speaks something else, something further.
'For there is nothing higher than this' — when this is explained as 'there is nothing higher (<s>param</s>) than <s>Brahman</s>, which is indicated by <s>neti neti</s>,' then it should be explained as: what is spoken beyond the negation of the phenomenal world is <s>Brahman</s> itself.
But when 'there is nothing higher than this' — with the pronoun referring to the negation — refers to the teaching (<s>ādeśa</s>) of <s>Brahman</s>, even then it should not be understood as mere negation of the phenomenal world; rather, through that negation, <s>Brahman</s> as a positive entity is indicated.
Why? — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Because it speaks further beyond the negation#.'
Because beyond the negation it still speaks.
Now, the name of <s>Brahman</s> — 'the name is: the real of the real' — the <s>Śruti</s> explains this: '<s>Prāṇā</s>s are indeed the real (<s>satya</s>).'
The <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body), which is compared to <s>māhārājana</s> (saffron) and the like, is indicated.
That [the <s>Prāṇa</s>s and the like] is indeed real (<s>satya</s>) relative to the rest; but the supreme reality beyond even that is <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text: #ubhayavyapadeśāttvahikuṇḍalavat# /

children.translated_text: By this, in the form of a serpent, there is non-difference.

children.text: kuṇḍalādirūpeṇa tu bheda ityuktaṃ tena viṣayabhedādbhedābhedayoravirodha ityekaviṣayatvena vā sarvadopalabdheravirodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: But in the form of coils, there is difference — thus it is stated. Therefore, because of the difference of the subject-matter, there is no contradiction between difference and non-difference. Or, because both are always perceived in the same subject-matter, there is no contradiction.

children.text: viruddhamiti hi naḥ kka saṃpratyayo na yatpramāṇenopalabhyate /
children.translated_text: For our conviction that '[something] is contradictory' does not arise with respect to what is apprehended by a means of knowledge.

children.text: āgamataśca pramāṇādekagocarāvapi bhedābhedau pratīyamānau na virodhamāvahataḥ savitṛprakāśayoriva pratyakṣātpramāṇādbhedābhedāviti //27 //
children.translated_text: And from scripture (<s>āgama</s>), which is a means of knowledge, difference and non-difference — even though perceived in the same object — do not bring about contradiction, just as difference and non-difference [are perceived] between the sun and its light from perception, which is a means of knowledge. //27//

body.translated_text: '#Because of the designation of both, like a serpent and its coils (<s>ahikuṇḍalavat</s>)#.'

body.text: prakārāntareṇa bhedābhedayoravirodhamāha-prakāśāśrayavadvā tejastvāt //28 //
body.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the non-contradiction of difference and non-difference in another way: 'Or like that which has light as its substrate — because of luminosity (<s>tejastvāt</s>).' //28//

body.text:
tadevaṃ paramatamupanyasya svamatamāha- #pūrvavadvā# /
ayamabhisaṃdhiḥ-yasya mataṃ vastuno 'hitvenābhedaḥ /
kuṇḍalatvena bheda iti,
body.translated_text:
Thus, having presented the ultimate view, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states his own view: '#Or as before (<s>pūrvavadvā</s>)#.'
The intention is this: in the view of one who holds that as a thing [i.e., as gold], there is non-difference, [but] as a bracelet, there is difference —

body.text:
sa evaṃ bruvāṇaḥ praṣṭavyo jāyate, kimahitvakuṇḍalatve vastuno bhinne utābhinne iti /
yadi bhinne, ahitvakuṇḍalatve bhinne iti vaktavyaṃ na tu vastunastābhyāṃ bhedābhedau /
nahyanyabhedābhedābhyāmanyadbhinnamabhinnaṃ vā bhavitumarhati /
atiprasaṅgāt /
atha vastuno na bhidyete ahitvakuṇḍalatve tathā sati ko bhedābhedayorviṣayabhedastayorvastuno 'nanyatvenābhedāt /
na caikaviṣayatve 'pi sadānubhūyamānatvādbhedābhedayoravirodha svarūpaviruddhayorapyavirodhe kka nāma virodho vyavatiṣṭheta /
naca sadānubhūyamānaṃ vicārāsahaṃ bhāvikaṃ bhavitumarhati /
dehātmabhāvasyāpi sarvadānubhūyamānasya bhāvikatvaprasaṅgāt /
prapañcitaṃ caitadasmābhiḥ prathamasūtra iti neha prapañcitam /
tasmādanādyavidyāvikrīḍitamevaikasyātmano jīvabhāvabhedo na bhāvikaḥ /
tathāca tattvajñānadavidyānivṛttāvapavargasiddhiḥ /

children.translated_text: But if this [difference] were ultimately real, its cessation through knowledge would not be possible.
And there is no means of liberation other than the knowledge of reality.

children.text: yathāha śrutiḥ-'tameva viditvātimṛtyumeti nānyaḥ panthā vidyate 'yanāya' iti /
children.translated_text: As the <s>Śruti</s> says: 'Having known That alone, one crosses over death; there is no other path for going [to liberation]' (<s>tam eva viditvā atimṛtyum eti nānyaḥ panthā vidyate 'yanāya</s>).
The rest is of transparent meaning. //29//

body.translated_text:
One who speaks thus is subject to the question: are serpent-hood and earring-hood (<s>ahitva-kuṇḍalatva</s>) [i.e., being a snake and being an earring, referring to the gold-snake/gold-earring example] different from the substance, or non-different?
If different, then one should say that serpent-hood and earring-hood are different [from each other], not that the substance is both different and non-different from them.
For nothing can be different or non-different by virtue of the difference and non-difference of something else — because of over-extension.
But if serpent-hood and earring-hood are not different from the substance, then what is the object-difference between difference and non-difference, since [difference and non-difference], being non-other than the substance, would be non-different [from each other]?
Nor [can it be said that] even though they have a single object, there is no contradiction between difference and non-difference because they are always experienced — for if there were no contradiction even between [things that are] contradictory in their very nature, where indeed would contradiction ever obtain?
Nor can what is always experienced — but unable to withstand scrutiny — be ultimately real (<s>bhāvika</s>),
because [if it could,] even the identification of the body with the self — which is always experienced — would absurdly become ultimately real.
And this has been elaborated by us in the first <s>sūtra</s> — hence it is not elaborated here.
Therefore, the difference of the <s>jīva</s>-state from the one Self is merely a sport of beginningless <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), not ultimately real.
And thus, upon the cessation of <s>avidyā</s> through the knowledge of reality, the attainment of liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) is established.

body.text:
#paramataḥ setūnmānasaṃbandhabhedavyapadeśebhyaḥ# /
yadyapi śrutiprācuryādbrahmavyatiriktaṃ tattvaṃ nāstītyavadhāritaṃ tathāpi setvādiśrutīnāmāpātatastadvirodhadarśanāttatpratisamādhānārthamayamārambhaḥ /
#jāṅgalaṃ#sthalam /
prakāśavadanantavajjyotiṣmadāyatanavaditi pādā brahmaṇaścatvārasteṣāṃ pādānāmardhānyaṣṭau śaphāḥ /
te 'ṣṭāvasya brahmaṇa ityaṣṭaśaphaṃ brahma /
ṣoḍaśa kalā asyeti ṣośakalam /
tadyathā prācī pratīcī dakṣiṇodīcīti catasraḥ kalā avayavā iva kalāḥ sa prakāśavānnāma prathamaḥ pādaḥ /
etadupāsanāyāṃ prakāśavān mukhyo bhavatīti prakāśavān pādaḥ /
athāparāḥ pṛthivyantarikṣaṃ dyauḥ samudra iti catasraḥ kalā eṣa dvitīyaḥ pādo 'nantatavānnāma /
so 'yamanantavattvena guṇonopāsyamāno 'nantatvamupāsakasyāvahatīti anantavān pādaḥ /
athāgniḥ sūryaścandramā vidyuditi catasraḥ kalāḥ sa jyotiṣmānnāma pādastṛtīyastadupāsanājjyotiṣmān bhavatīti jyotiṣmān pādaḥ /
atha ghrāṇaścakṣuḥ śrotraṃ vāgiti catasraḥ kalāścaturthaḥ pāda āyatanavānnāma /
ete ghrāṇādayo hi gandhādiviṣayā mana āyatanamāśritya bhogasādhanaṃ bhavantītyāyatanavānnāma pādaḥ /
tadevaṃ catuṣpādbrahmāṣṭaśaphaṃ ṣoḍaṣakalamunmiṣitaṃ śrutyā /
atastato brahmaṇaḥ paramanyadasti /
syādetat /
asti cet parisaṃkhyāyocyatāmetāvaditi /

children.translated_text: To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'There is the unlimited' (<s>amitam asti</s>).
Established by means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>).
But not [limited to] 'this much' — this is the meaning.
And the designation of difference is of three kinds: by way of substratum, by way of extension (<s>atideśa</s>), and by way of delimitation (<s>avadhi</s>). //31//

body.translated_text:
'From the Supreme, because of the designations of bridge (<s>setu</s>), measure (<s>unmāna</s>), connection (<s>saṃbandha</s>), and difference (<s>bheda</s>)' [BS 3.2.31].
Although it has been ascertained from the abundance of <s>Śruti</s> that there is no reality other than <s>Brahman</s>, nevertheless, because the <s>Śruti</s>s about bridge and the like appear at first glance to contradict this, this [discussion] is undertaken for the purpose of resolving them.
'<s>Jāṅgala</s>' means dry land.
'Luminous (<s>prakāśavat</s>), infinite (<s>anantavat</s>), resplendent (<s>jyotiṣmat</s>), having an abode (<s>āyatanavat</s>)' — these are the four quarters (<s>pāda</s>s) of <s>Brahman</s>. The halves of those four quarters are the eight hooves (<s>śapha</s>s) — those eight belong to this <s>Brahman</s> — hence <s>Brahman</s> is 'eight-hoofed' (<s>aṣṭaśapha</s>). 'Having sixteen parts' (<s>ṣoḍaśakala</s>) — it has sixteen parts.
Thus: east, west, south, north — these four parts, like limbs, [constitute] the first quarter called 'luminous' (<s>prakāśavān</s>).
In the meditation on this, one becomes chiefly luminous — hence [it is] the 'luminous quarter.'
Then, the other [four]: earth, intermediate space, heaven, ocean — these four parts constitute the second quarter called 'infinite' (<s>anantavat</s>).
This [<s>Brahman</s>], being meditated upon with the attribute of infinitude, brings infinitude to the meditator — hence the 'infinite quarter.'
Then, fire, sun, moon, lightning — these four parts constitute the third quarter called 'resplendent' (<s>jyotiṣmat</s>); from meditation on it, one becomes resplendent — hence the 'resplendent quarter.'
Then, the sense of smell, the eye, the ear, speech — these four parts constitute the fourth quarter called 'having an abode' (<s>āyatanavat</s>).
For these — smell and the rest — having their objects in scent and the like, become means of enjoyment by resorting to the mind as their abode — hence the quarter named 'having an abode.'
Thus, <s>Brahman</s> — four-quartered, eight-hoofed, sixteen-parted — has been disclosed by the <s>Śruti</s>.
Hence, there is something other than that <s>Brahman</s>, which is supreme.
One might object: if there is [something beyond], let its measure be stated through enumeration — 'this much [and no more].'

body.text:
sāmānyāttu /
jagatastanmaryādānāṃ ca vidhārakatvaṃ ca setusāmānyam /
yathā hi tantavaḥ paṭaṃ vidhārayanti tadupādānatvādevaṃ brahmāpi jagadvidhārayati tadupapādakatvāt /
tanmaryādānāṃ ca vidhārakaṃ brahma /

children.translated_text: Otherwise, the ocean — turbulent with waves, dense, powerful, overflowing with garlands of billows — would swallow up the sphere of the earth.
Or the submarine fire (<s>vaḍavānala</s>) — bristling with blazing flame-locks — would reduce the world to ashes.
Or the fierce wind would shatter the cosmic egg (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>) itself without any cause.
And thus the <s>Śruti</s>: 'Out of fear of It, the wind blows' (<s>bhīṣāsmād vātaḥ pavate</s>) and the like. //32//

body.translated_text:
'But because of the commonality [with a bridge]' [BS 3.2.32].
The commonality with a bridge consists in [<s>Brahman</s>] being the upholder of the world and its boundaries.
For just as threads uphold a cloth — being its material cause — so too <s>Brahman</s> upholds the world, being its source.
And <s>Brahman</s> is the upholder of its [the world's] boundaries.

body.text:
#buddhyarthaḥ pādavat# /
manaso brahmapratīkasya samāropitabrahmabhāvasya vāgghrāṇaścakṣuḥ śrotramiti catvāraḥ pādāḥ /
mano hi vaktavyaghrātavyadraṣṭavyaśrotavyān gocarān vāgādibhiḥ saṃcaratīti saṃcaraṇasādhāraṇatayā manasaḥ pādastadidamadhyātman /
ākāśasya brahmapratīkasyāgnirvāyurādityo diśa iti catvāraḥ pādāḥ /

children.text: te hi vyāpino nabhasa udara iva goḥ pādā vilagnā upalakṣyanta iti pādastadidamadhidaivatam /
children.translated_text: For these, being pervading, are perceived as attached to the belly of space, as it were, like the legs of a cow — hence they are its quarters; this pertains to the divine level (<s>adhidaivata</s>).

children.text: tadanena pādavaditi vaidikaṃ nidarśanaṃ vyākhyāya laukikaṃ cedaṃ nidarśanamityāha- #athavā pādavaditi /
children.translated_text: Having thus explained 'like the quarters' as a Vedic illustration, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states this worldly illustration: 'Or alternatively, "like the quarters" [means]...'
'Like that' —
Here too, [it is] for the purpose of facilitating the practice of meditation for those of dull intellect — this is the meaning. //33//

body.translated_text:
'For the purpose of [assisting] meditation, like the quarters [of an animal]' [BS 3.2.33].
Of the mind — which serves as a <s>pratīka</s> (symbol) for <s>Brahman</s> and upon which <s>Brahman</s>-hood has been superimposed — speech, smell, the eye, and the ear are the four quarters.
For the mind moves through its objects — things to be spoken, smelled, seen, and heard — by means of speech and the rest. Thus, due to the commonality of movement, [speech and the rest] are the quarters of the mind — this pertains to the individual level (<s>adhyātman</s>).
Of space (<s>ākāśa</s>), which serves as a <s>pratīka</s> for <s>Brahman</s>, fire, wind, the sun, and the directions are the four quarters.

children.translated_text: 'Because of the specific location, like light (<s>prakāśa</s>) and the like' [BS 3.2.34].

Due to the contact with the specific location of the limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) — the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) and the rest — the particular cognition (<s>viśeṣavijñāna</s>) that has arisen in waking and dream [states] subsides in deep sleep upon the cessation or suppression of the limiting adjunct.
Likewise, even the threefold designation of difference regarding <s>Brahman</s> is with reference to the difference of limiting adjuncts.

children.text: yathā saudhajālamārganiveśinyaḥ savitṛbhāso jālamārgopādhibedādbhinnā bhāsante tadvigame tu gabhastimaṇḍalenaikībhavantyatastena saṃbadhyanta evamihāpīti //34 //
children.translated_text: Just as the rays of the sun entering through the lattice-windows of a palace appear as different due to the difference of the lattice-window limiting adjuncts, but upon the removal of those [lattice-windows] become unified with the solar disc — so too here. //34//

body.text: syādetat /

children.text: ekībhāvaḥ kasmādiha saṃbandhaḥ kathañcidvyākhyāyate na mukhya evetyetatsūtreṇa pariharati- #upapattaśca# /
children.translated_text: Why is the unity [of the self with <s>Brahman</s>] here explained as a 'connection' in some roundabout way, and not as unity in the primary sense? — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] resolves this with the <s>sūtra</s>: 'And because of reasonableness' [BS 3.2.35].
For [the <s>Śruti</s>] '<s>svam apītaḥ</s>' (having gone to one's own [nature]) speaks of a connection with one's own essential nature (<s>svarūpa</s>).

children.text: svabhāvaścedanena saṃbandhatvena spṛṣṭastataḥ svābhāvikastādātmyānnātiricyata iti tarkapāda upapāditamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And if [one's own] essential nature has been touched [i.e., identified] as this connection, then — being natural (<s>svābhāvika</s>) and hence identical — it does not differ [from <s>Brahman</s>]. This has been demonstrated in the <s>Tarkapāda</s> (the section on reasoning) — this is the meaning.

children.text: tathā bhedo 'pi trividho vānyādṛśaḥ svābhāvika ityarthaḥ //35 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, even the threefold difference — or any other kind — is natural [i.e., non-ultimate, pertaining to the conventional level] — this is the meaning. //35//

body.translated_text: One might object:

children.translated_text: 'Likewise, because of the negation of the other' [BS 3.2.36].
This is explained by the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, which is easy [to understand]. //36//
'By this, the all-pervasiveness [of <s>Brahman</s> is established], from <s>āyāmaśabda</s> and the like' [BS 3.2.37].

children.text: brahmādvaitasiddhāvapi na sarvagatatvaṃ sarvavyāpitā sarvasya brahmaṇā svarūpeṇa rūpavattvaṃ sidhyatītyata āha- #anena setvādinirākaraṇena#parahetunirākaraṇenānyapratiṣedhasamāśrayaṇena ca svasādhanopanyāsena ca sarvagatatvamapyātmanaḥ siddhaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: Even when the non-duality (<s>advaita</s>) of <s>Brahman</s> is established, the all-pervasiveness — i.e., the pervading of everything, the form-possessing nature of everything through <s>Brahman</s>'s own essential nature — is not thereby established. Hence [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'By this refutation of the bridge and the like' — by the refutation of the other's position, by resorting to the negation of the other, and by the presentation of one's own proofs — the all-pervasiveness of the Self too is established.

children.text: advaita siddhe sarvo 'yamanirvacanīyaḥ prapañcāvabhāso brahmādhiṣṭhāna iti sarvasya brahmasaṃbandhādbrahma sarvagatamiti siddham //37 //
children.translated_text: When non-duality is established, this entire inexpressible (<s>anirvacanīya</s>) phenomenal appearance (<s>prapañcāvabhāsa</s>) has <s>Brahman</s> as its substratum — hence, because of everything's connection with <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Brahman</s> is all-pervading — this is established. //37//

body.text:
#phalamata upapatteḥ#siddhāntopakramamidamadhikaraṇam /
syādetat /
nityaśuddhabuddhamuktasvabhāvasya brahmaṇaḥ kuta īśvaratvaṃ kutaśca phalahetutvamapītyata āha- #tasyaiva brahmaṇo vyāvahārikyāmiti# /
nāsya pāramārthikaṃ rūpamāśrityaitaccintyate kintu sāṃvyavahārikam /
etacca 'tapasā cīyate brahma' iti vyācakṣāṇerasmābhirūpapāditam /
#iṣṭaṃ#phalaṃ svargaḥ /
yathāhuḥ-'yanna duḥkhana saṃbhinnaṃ naca grastamanantaram /
abhilāṣopanītaṃ ca sukhaṃ svargapadāspadam' iti /
#aniṣṭa#mavīcyādisthānabhogyaṃ, #vyāmiśraṃ#manuṣyabhogyam /
#tatra tāvatpratipādyate-phalamata īśvarā#tkarmabhirārādhitādbhavitumarhati /
atha karmaṇa eva phalaṃ kasmānna bhavatītyata āha- #karmaṇastvanukṣaṇavināśinaḥ#pratyakṣavināśina iti /
codayati- #sayādetatkarma# #syādetatkarma vinaśyaditi# /
upāttamapi phalaṃ bhoktumayogyatvādvā karmāntarapratibandhādvā na bhujyata ityarthaḥ /
pariharati- #tadapi na pariśudhyatīti# /
nahi svarga ātmānaṃ labhatāmityadhikāriṇaḥ kāmayante kintu bhogyo 'smākaṃ #bhavatviti# /
tena yādṛśamebhiḥ kāmyate tādṛśasya phalatvamiti bhogyameva satphalamiti /
naca tādṛśaṃ karmānantaramiti kathaṃ phalaṃ, tadapi svarūpeṇa /

body.translated_text:
'The fruit [comes] from That [<s>Īśvara</s>], because of reasonableness' [BS 3.2.38]. This <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic) begins with the established conclusion.
One might ask: how can <s>Brahman</s> — whose nature is eternally pure, awakened, and liberated — have lordship (<s>Īśvaratva</s>), and how can it be the cause of fruits? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Of that very <s>Brahman</s>, at the conventional (<s>vyāvahārika</s>) [level]...'
This is not thought of with reference to its ultimate nature, but with reference to the conventional.
And this has been demonstrated by us when explaining '<s>Brahman</s> is augmented by <s>tapas</s> (austerity)' (<s>tapasā cīyate brahma</s>).
'<s>Iṣṭa</s>' (desired) — the fruit is heaven.
As they say: 'That which is not mixed with suffering, not swallowed by what follows,
and brought about by desire — that happiness is the domain of the word "heaven" (<s>svarga</s>).'
'<s>Aniṣṭa</s>' (undesired) — that which is to be experienced in locations such as <s>Avīci</s> and the like. '<s>Vyāmiśra</s>' (mixed) — that which is to be experienced by humans.
'Therein, to begin with, it is established: the fruit is able to come from <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) who has been propitiated by [ritual] actions.'
But why does the fruit not come from the action itself? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Because action, being destroyed at every moment' — is perceptibly destroyed.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises an objection: 'One might say: this action...' — 'One might say: the action perishes.'
The meaning is: even a fruit that has been obtained may not be enjoyed — either because of unfitness to enjoy, or because of obstruction by another action.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] resolves: 'Even that is not settled [as a valid objection].'
For those who are eligible do not desire 'let heaven attain itself' but rather 'let it be an [object of] enjoyment for us.'
Hence, the nature of the fruit is as desired by them — and what is desired is the enjoyable alone as the real fruit.
And since the [desired] fruit is not [present] immediately after the action — how then [is it] a fruit [of action]? That too [must be answered with reference to] its own nature.
Moreover, heaven and hell are the most intense happiness and suffering — and [hence] there must necessarily be experience (<s>bhoga</s>) — by another name, an experience directed toward them.
Therefore, when something is fit to be experienced but is not experienced, it is concluded to be non-existent, like a hare's horn.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises an objection: 'But one might say: let the fruit not arise immediately after the action; rather, the fruit will arise from <s>apūrva</s> (the unprecedented potency) produced by the action.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] resolves: 'That too is not [tenable].'
It has been ascertained — through perception and scripture — that whatever is insentient, all of that, operates only when presided over by a conscious [entity].
Therefore, even by <s>apūrva</s>, which is insentient, [operation is possible] only when presided over by a conscious entity — not otherwise — this is the meaning.
And [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states that <s>apūrva</s> is not even established by valid means of knowledge: 'In its existence...'
