body.translated_text:
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>], having commenced with the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>), takes up the prima facie view: '<s>Dharma</s> (<s>Jaimini</s> [holds]) — for that very reason' — thus.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the <s>Śruti</s>: 'It is heard, to begin with' — thus.
One might object: The <s>Śruti</s>s such as 'One who desires heaven should sacrifice' and the like do not enjoin sacrifice as a means to the fruit.
For: if the sacrifices and the like themselves are the action, without a <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive force) distinct from them, still — they are not understood from their own words as having the nature of something to be accomplished in terms of 'before and after'; hence they do not require another thing to be accomplished, and therefore cannot be connected with heaven as another thing to be accomplished.
Even if a <s>bhāvanā</s> distinct from them exists, still — that [<s>bhāvanā</s>], even though requiring something to be accomplished [for its completion], cannot — abandoning the <s>bhāvya</s> (what is to be produced), i.e., the verbal root-meaning, which is the primary and antecedently given [content of its own words] — accept heaven and the like — which are qualifications of the person, conveyed by separate words — as its <s>bhāvya</s>.
Nor is it possible that in a single sentence, a connection with two things-to-be-accomplished [exists], since that would entail the splitting of the sentence.
Not only from the word [analysis] but also from the thing itself: the effort of the person — i.e., the <s>bhāvanā</s> — has as its direct <s>sādhya</s> (thing to be accomplished) the verbal root-meaning alone, not heaven and the like, since [the <s>bhāvanā</s>] does not pervade those.
But heaven and the like — being already accomplished entities denoted by the nominal words, and being qualifications of the person — are connected with the verbal root-meaning, which is the thing to be accomplished denoted by the verb, as means (<s>sādhana</s>) and subsidiaries (<s>guṇa</s>), by the principle 'what is already accomplished is taught for the sake of what is to be accomplished.'
And accordingly, [there is] the <s>sūtra</s> of [<s>Jaimini</s>] the sage: 'The connection of substances with the action is as subsidiaries.'
And thus, since the actions — sacrifice and the like — are not desired by the person because of being painful, and since the desired [goals] — heaven and the like — are not [directly] to be accomplished [by the person], the sacrifices and the like do not benefit the person; and since they are non-beneficial, the person does not desire them; and since he is unable [to perform them without desire], no eligible person is possible for them — and thus, to avoid the purposelessness demonstrated by the absence of an eligible person, the entire <s>Veda</s> has as its purport the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, which is eternal bliss with all suffering thoroughly wiped away, through the dissolution of the phenomenal world of difference.
For: everywhere in the <s>Veda</s>, the dissolution of some difference or other is understood. For example, 'One who desires heaven should sacrifice' — [this effects] the dissolution of the body-self identification.
For here, at first glance, an eligible person is understood who is distinct from the body and capable of enjoying the fruit in the other world.
Therein, when the eligibility is removed through the method described, even though [the person] is apprehended, being unable to withstand scrutiny, it remains only as a means [for the dissolution] — and by this sentence, the dissolution of the body-self identification is brought about by its sequel.
'By the milking of cows, one should offer the <s>praṇaya</s> for one desiring cattle' — here too, since at first glance an eligible person with eligibility is apprehended, [there is] the dissolution of the difference of eligible persons.
And prohibitive sentences directly — through the prohibition of activity — [and] injunctive sentences too — not [primarily] as commanding the activity of the <s>Sāṃgrahaṇī</s> sacrifice and the like through [injunctions like] 'One desiring a village should sacrifice with the <s>Sāṃgrahaṇī</s>' — but rather, through the instruction of an alternative means, they have the purpose of prohibiting the means that is in conformity with what is observed.
Just as [one says]: 'Do not eat poison; eat in his house instead.'
And thus, through the prohibition of activity impelled by passion (<s>rāga</s>) and the like, the scripture-hood of the scripture is also established.
But if [the <s>Veda</s>] permitted activity through the instruction of means, by nourishing passion, there would be the unwanted consequence of its not being scripture.
But by prohibiting that [passion-driven activity] and establishing meditation upon <s>Brahman</s>, the scripture would indeed be scripture.
Therefore, since the connection of <s>karma</s> with its fruit is without valid authority, the diverse fruits arise from <s>Īśvara</s> alone — who is beginninglessly assisted by the diverse <s>avidyā</s> — independently of <s>karma</s> — thus.
But then, what is the injunction? What here — how does it [function as] mere prompting? Because the injunction is merely prompting, and that [prompting] is tenable even without an eligible person.
For not everyone who prompts requires an eligible person — since wind and the like, which are prompters, do not require one — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>], wishing to remove this doubt, says: 'And therein, from the acceptance of being the object of an injunctive <s>Śruti</s>, sacrifice is understood as the producer of heaven. Otherwise, sacrifice would turn out to have no performer' — thus.
The intent is this: An injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) is an instruction (<s>upadeśa</s>).
As it is said: 'The knowledge of that [duty] is instruction.'
And instruction, in both worldly and scriptural usage, is well-known as being about an action that serves the purpose of the one being instructed.
For example: 'One who desires health should eat when the [previous meal] is digested.' 'This is a good path; please proceed by this.' But [an injunction] does not serve the purpose of the instructor — like a fire and the like — because there, the intention [of the instructor] is the motivator, and that [intention] is not possible in a non-human-authored [scripture].
And [the fact] that this instruction has as its domain an activity serving the purpose of the one being instructed — i.e., [an activity] whose scope is a favorable operation needed by the performer — has been established by us in the <s>Nyāyakaṇikā</s>.
And thus, in 'One who desires heaven should sacrifice' and the like, for the one desiring heaven, the sacrifices and the like are understood as the desired means.
Otherwise, they would not serve the one who wishes to accomplish [the goal].
This was stated by the sage [<s>Jaimini</s>]: 'But the non-productive [karma], because of serving that purpose' — thus.
If [the injunctions] had the purpose of mere prompting without the means needed by the performer, then <s>karma</s> — sacrifice and the like — would be non-productive.
The meaning is: it would not find one who wishes to accomplish [the goal].
Nor can these [karmas] — even though not directly the <s>bhāvya</s> (object-to-be-produced) of <s>bhāvanā</s> — be the <s>bhāvanā</s>'s object-of-purpose (<s>uddeśya</s>), endowed with the propriety of being the object of an injunction that specifies the means needed by the agent — by virtue of which [propriety], being non-beneficial to persons, they would not be objects of eligibility.
Because actions are not the locus of the person's positive regard (<s>cetanasamāhāna</s>), since they are painful.
But heaven and the like — because of the <s>bhāvanā</s>'s superimposition of <s>apūrva</s>-form desire (<s>kāma</s>) [upon them] —

children.translated_text: But when something must be postulated because the production of the fruit is otherwise inexplicable — then [it is postulated as:] 'Or, a prior state of the fruit' — thus.
'Of a non-variegated cause' — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s> adds].
[The remainder is:] if from <s>Īśvara</s> alone, without anything else — thus.

If the production of diverse [fruits] from <s>karma</s>s — good and bad — [were denied], there would be the consequence of [<s>Īśvara</s>] possessing passion (<s>rāga</s>) and the like — this is the intent. //40//

body.translated_text:
and because of being of the nature of delight (<s>prīti</s>).
Even though denoted by nominal words and being qualifications of the person, [heaven and the like] are understood as having the nature of <s>bhāvya</s> (thing-to-be-produced) characterized by being the <s>uddeśya</s> (purpose) of the <s>bhāvanā</s>.
And since the <s>sādhya</s>-ness of sacrifice and the like for <s>bhāvanā</s> — in the form of being the <s>bhāvya</s> of a <s>bhāvanā</s> engaged for the sake of the fruit — and the <s>sādhya</s>-ness of the fruit — in the form of being the <s>bhāvya</s> of a <s>bhāvanā</s> engaged for the sake of the fruit — are not of equal principal status, a single-sentence combination is possible. Because the mere <s>bhāvanā-bhāvya</s>-ness of sacrifice and the like is not incompatible even with [their being] the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>).
Otherwise, that [<s>bhāvanā-bhāvya</s>-ness] would be destroyed everywhere.
Because even the axe and the like have that same status in cutting and the like.
Since the fruit — though lacking direct pervasion by <s>bhāvanā</s> — is established everywhere through its being the purpose (<s>uddeśya</s>) of that [<s>bhāvanā</s>], the eligibility of one desiring heaven in the sacrifice and the like that accomplish heaven is established.
Nor can the injunctions of the <s>Sāṃgrahaṇī</s> sacrifice and the like — which pertain to objects not yet obtained — be either enumerative (<s>parisaṃkhyāyaka</s>) or restrictive (<s>niyāmaka</s>).
Nor, in the absence of eligibility, can the dissolution of body-self identity or the dissolution of the difference of eligible persons be established.
And when [the sentence] spontaneously yields [a meaning] at first glance, its purport is precisely that, not [a meaning] arrived at [only] derivatively.
When the purport of the sentence corresponds to the meaning that is spontaneously understood, it is not appropriate to [assign it] the purport of a derived [meaning].
Nor does this [interpretation] create any conflict with scripture.
Because the scripture is tenable as scripture even through the instruction of the means to heaven and the like.
For scripture-hood consists in conveying what is conducive to human welfare.
Since it conveys the welfare of both passionate and dispassionate persons, being all-encompassing, there is no conflict with that [definition].
Therefore, from the acceptance of being the object of an injunction, it is established that sacrifice produces heaven.
'Or, some state of the <s>karma</s>' — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s> adds].
[This means:] an intermediate operation of the <s>karma</s>.
What is stated amounts to this: The <s>sādhana</s>-ness (instrumentality) of <s>karma</s> toward the fruit that is heard [in <s>Śruti</s>] — to sustain that, there is an intermediate operation of that very [<s>karma</s>].
And it is not reasonable that there is [intermediate] operation when the [principal] operator exists, but not when it does not.
Even when the <s>Āgneya</s> and other [intermediate] offerings do not [yet] exist, [their] <s>utpatti-apūrva</s>s (production-unseen-potencies) have [such] intermediate-operation-hood, since [they serve] in generating the supreme <s>apūrva</s>.
And even when the act of drinking oil does not exist, the intervening stages of oil-transformation — [serving] the nourishment that is to be accomplished — have intermediate-operation-hood.
Therefore, the <s>apūrva</s> — being an effect of <s>karma</s> — is a reasonable intermediate operation when the fruit is to be produced by <s>karma</s>.

nahi jātu mṛtpiṇḍadaṇḍādayaḥ kumbhakārādyanadhiṣṭhitāḥ kumbhādyārambhāya vibhavavanto dṛṣṭāḥ /
naca vidyutpavanādibhiraprayatnapūrvairvyabhicāraḥ, teṣāmapi kalpanāspadatayā vyabhicāranidarśanatvānupapatteḥ /
tasmādacetanaṃ karma vāpūrve vā na cetanānadhiṣṭhitaṃ svatantraṃ svakārye pravartitumutsahate naca caitanyamātraṃ karmasvarūpasāmānyaviniyogādiviśeṣavijñānaśūnyamupayujyate, yena tadrahitakṣetrajñamātrādhiṣṭhānena siddhasādhyatvamudbhāvyeta /
tasmāttattatprāsādāṭṭālagopuratoraṇādyupajananidarśanasahasraiḥ supariniścitaṃ yathā cetanādhiṣṭhānādacetanānāṃ kāryārambhakatvamiti tathā caitanyaṃ devatāyā asati bādhake śrutismṛtītihāsapurāṇaprasiddhaṃ na śakyaṃ pratiṣedhdhumityapi spaṣṭaṃ niraṭaṅki devatādhikaraṇe /
laukikaśceśvaro dānaparicaraṇapraṇāmañjalikaraṇastutimayībhiratiśraddhāgarbhābhirbhaktibhirārādhitaḥ prasannaḥ svānurūpamārādhakāya phalaṃ prayacchati virodhataścāpakriyābhirvirodhakāyāhitāmityapi suprasiddham /
tadiha kevalaṃ karma vāpūrvaṃ vā cetanānadhiṣṭhitamacetanaṃ phalaṃ prasūta iti dṛṣṭaviruddham /
yathā vinaṣṭaṃ karma na phalaṃ prasūta iti kalpyate dṛṣṭavirodhādevamihāpīti /
tathā devapūjācmako yāgo devatāṃ naprasādayan phalaṃ prasūta ityapi dṛṣṭaviruddham /
nahi rājapūjātmakamārādhanaṃ rājānamaprasādya phalāya kalpate /
tasmāddṛṣṭānuguṇyāya yāgādibhirapi devatāprasattirutpādyate /
tathāca devatāprasādādeva sthāyinaḥ phalotpatterupapatteḥ kṛtamapūrveṇa /
evamaśubhenāpi karmaṇā devatāvirodhanaṃ śrutismṛtiprasiddham /
tataḥ sthāyino 'niṣṭaphalaprasavaḥ /
naca śubhāśubhakāriṇāṃ tadanurūpaṃ phalaṃ prasuvānā devatā dveṣapakṣapātavatīti yujyate /
nahi rājā sādhukāriṇamanugṛhṇannigṛhṇan vā pāpakāriṇaṃ bhavati dviṣṭo rakto vā tadvadalaukiko 'pīśvaraḥ /
yathā ca paramāpūrve kartavye utpattyapūrvāṇāmaṅgāpūrvāṇāṃ copayogaḥ /

children.translated_text: so too, in the propitiation of the principal [deity], the propitiation of the subsidiary [deities] — both the <s>utpatti</s>-propitiation and the [limb]-propitiation — is of use.
Just as, in the propitiation of a master, the propitiation of his ministers and his loved ones [is useful] — thus everything is the same, except for stubborn attachment [to one's own position].

children.text: tasmāddṛṣṭāvirodhena devatārādhanāt phalaṃ na tvapūrvātkarmaṇo vā kevalādvirodhato hetuvyapadeśaśca śrautaḥ smārtaśca vyākhyātaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, by non-contradiction with observation, the fruit [comes] from the propitiation of the deity — not from <s>apūrva</s> or from <s>karma</s> alone, because of contradiction. And the designation as cause — both <s>Śrauta</s> (Vedic) and <s>Smārta</s> (traditional) — has been explained.

children.text: ye punarantaryimivyāpārāyā phalotpādanāyā nityatvaṃ sarvasādhāraṇatvamiti manyamānā bhāṣyakārīyamadhikaraṇaṃ dūṣavibhāge bhāmatyāṃ tṛtīyasyādhyāyasya dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ //2 //
children.translated_text: But those who, thinking that the intermediate operation — namely, the production of the fruit — is eternal and common to all [deities], [interpret] the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>'s <s>adhikaraṇa</s> [differently] — [here ends] the second <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s> in the <s>Bhāmatī</s>, the elucidation [of the <s>Śārīraka-Bhāṣya</s>]. //2//

body.translated_text:
'But <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> [holds that the fruit comes] from the former [i.e., the deity], because of the designation as cause' — thus.
For a postulation that follows what is observed (<s>dṛṣṭānusārin</s>) is appropriate, not otherwise.
For indeed, clay, staff, and the like — unsupervised by a potter and the like — have never been seen as capable of producing a pot and the like.
Nor is there a counter-example from lightning, wind, and the like — which [operate] without [deliberate] effort — since those too, being objects of postulation [about a guiding intelligence], cannot serve as counter-examples to disprove [the need for supervision].
Therefore, insentient <s>karma</s>, or <s>apūrva</s>, unsupervised by a sentient being, is not independently capable of operating toward its own effect. Nor is mere consciousness — devoid of specific knowledge of the form, general applicability, and particular assignment of <s>karma</s> — of any use, such that [the opponent] could demonstrate the superfluousness [of <s>Īśvara</s>] through the supervision of the mere field-knower (<s>kṣetrajña</s>) lacking that [specific knowledge].
Therefore — just as it is firmly established through thousands of examples of the production of palaces, towers, gate-houses, and arches, that the production of effects by insentient [materials] is [preceded] by the supervision of a sentient being — so too, the consciousness of the deity, in the absence of a sublating [cognition], being well-known from <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, <s>Itihāsa</s>, and <s>Purāṇa</s>, cannot be denied — this too has been made clear, without reservation, in the <s>devatādhikaraṇa</s>.
And it is well-known in the world that a lord, when propitiated through gifts, service, salutations, folded-hands gestures, and praises — [all offered] with intense faith and devotion befitting [his station] — when pleased, bestows upon the worshipper a fruit befitting himself; and conversely, through hostile actions, [bestows] misfortune upon the adversary.
Therefore, here — [the view that] mere <s>karma</s>, or <s>apūrva</s>, being insentient and unsupervised by a sentient being, produces the fruit — this is contradicted by observation.
Just as, because it is contradicted by observation that <s>karma</s> which has perished [cannot] produce the fruit, [the <s>apūrva</s>] is postulated — so too here.
Likewise, [the view that] sacrifice, whose nature is the worship of a deity, produces the fruit without propitiating the deity — this too is contradicted by observation.
For worship whose nature is the propitiation of a king does not yield fruit without propitiating the king.
Therefore, in conformity with observation, even through sacrifice and the like, the propitiation of the deity is produced.
And thus, since the production of an enduring fruit from the deity's grace alone is tenable, there is no need for <s>apūrva</s>.
Likewise, even through inauspicious <s>karma</s>, the offense against the deity is well-known from <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>.
From that [offense], the production of an enduring undesirable fruit [follows].
Nor is it appropriate [to say] that the deity, in bestowing corresponding fruits upon performers of good and bad [deeds], possesses hatred or partiality.
For a king who rewards the righteous and punishes the wrongdoer is neither hateful nor partisan — similarly, the non-worldly <s>Īśvara</s> too.
And just as, when the supreme <s>apūrva</s> is to be produced, the <s>utpatti-apūrva</s>s (production-unseen-potencies) of the limbs (<s>aṅga</s>s) — the <s>Āgneya</s> and the like — are of use,

body.text: iti tṛtīyādhyāyasya tattvampadārthapariśodhanākhyo dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ #tṛtīyādhyāye tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ# /
body.translated_text:
Thus [ends] the second <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s>, called 'The Purification of the Referent of the Word <s>Tat</s> (That).'
The third <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s> [begins].

body.text:
#sarvavedāntapratyayaṃ codanādyaviśeṣāt# /
pūrveṇa saṃgatimāha- #vyākhyātaṃ vijñeyasya brahmaṇa iti# /
nirūpādhibrahmatattvagocaraṃ vijñānaṃ manvāna ākṣipati- #nanu vijñeyaṃ brahmeti# /
sāvayavasya hyavayavānāṃ bhedāttadavayavaviśiṣṭabrahmagocarāṇi vijñānāni gocarabhedādbhidyerannityavayavā brahmaṇo nirākṛtāḥ pūrvāparādītyanena /
naca nānāsvabhāvaṃ brahma yataḥ svabhāvabhedādbhinnāni jñānānītyuktam- #ekarasamiti /
dhanaṅ#kaṭhinam /
nanvekamapyanekarūpaṃ loke dṛṣṭaṃ, yathā somaśarmaiko 'pyācāryo māyulapitā putro bhrātā bhartā jāmātā dvijottama ityanekarūpa ityata uktam- #ekarūpatvācca# /
ekasmin gocare saṃbhavanti bahūni vijñānāni na tvanekākāraṇītyuktam- #anekarūpāṇi# /
rūpamākāraḥ /

tattadguṇopādhānabrahmaviṣayā upāsanāḥ prāṇādiviṣayāśca dṛṣṭādṛṣṭakamuktiphalā viṣayabhedādbhidyanta ityarthaḥ /
tata upapanno vimarśa ityāha- #teṣveṣā cintā# /
pūrvapakṣaṃ gṛhṇāti- #tatreti /
nāmnastāvaditi# /
asti 'athaiṣa jyotiḥ-etena sahasradakṣiṇena yajeta' iti /
tatra saṃśayaḥ-kiṃ yajeteti saṃnihitajyotiṣṭomānuvādena sahasradakṣiṇālakṣaṇaguṇavidhānam, utaitadguṇaviśiṣṭakarmāntaravidhānamiti /
kiṃ tāvat prāptam, jyotiṣṭomasya prakrāntatvādyajeteti tadanuvādājjyotiriti prātipadikamātraṃ paṭhitvā etenetyanukṛṣya karmasāmānādhikaraṇyena karmanāmavyavasthāpanāt, karmaṇaścānuvādyatvena tattantrasya nāmno 'pi tathaiva vyavasthāpanāt, jyotiḥśabdasya 'vasante vasante jyotiṣā' iti ca jyotiṣṭome yogadarśanāt nāmaikadeśena ca nāmopalakṣaṇasya lokasiddhatvādbhīmasenopalakṣaṇabhīmapadavat, athaśabdasya cānantaryārthasyāsaṃbandhitve 'nupapatteḥ, guṇaviśiṣṭakarmāntaravidheśca guṇamātravidhānasya lāghavāt, dvādaśaśatadakṣiṇāyāścotpattyaśiṣṭatayā samaśiṣṭatayā sahasradakṣiṇayā saha vikalpopapatteḥ, prakṛtasyaiva jyotiṣṭomasya sahasradakṣiṇālakṣaṇaguṇavidhānārthamayamanuvādo na tu karmāntaramiti prāptam /
evaṃ prāpta ucyate-bhavetpūrvasmin guṇavidhiryadi tadeva prakaraṇaṃ syāt /
vicchinnaṃ tu tat /
tathāhi saṃnidhāvapi pūrvāsaṃbaddhārthaṃ saṃjñāntaraṃ pratīyamānam 'anyāyaścānekārthatvam' iti nyāyādutsargator'thāntarārthatvātpūrvabuddhiṃ vyavacchinattyapūrvabuddhiṃ ca prasūta iti lokasiddham /
na jātu dehi devadattāya gāmatha devāya vājinamiti devaśabdāddevadattaṃ vājibhājamavasyanti laukikāḥ /
tathā copariṣṭāt 'yajeta' iti śrūyamāṇamasaṃbaddhārthapadavyavāyāttatkarmabuddhimanādadhat tatra guṇavidhānamātrāsamarthaṃ karmāntarameva vidhatte /
na caikatrānupapattyā lakṣaṇayā jyotiḥśabdo jyotiṣṭome pravṛtta ityasatyāmanupapattau lākṣaṇiko yuktaḥ /
nahi gāṅgāyāṃ ghoṣa ityatra gāṅgāpadaṃ lākṣaṇikamiti mīno gāṅgāyāmityatrāpi lākṣaṇikaṃ bhavati /
bhede 'pi ca prathamaṃ saṃjñāntareṇollikhite yajiśabdasāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ karmanāmadheyatāmātratāmāvahati natu saṃjñāntaropajanitāṃ bhedadhiyamapanetumutsahate /
tathā cāthaśabdo 'dhikārārthaḥ prakaraṇāntaratāmavadyotayati /
eṣaśabdaścādhikriyamāṇaparāmarśaka iti so 'yaṃ saṃjñāntarādbheda iti /

yathaiva kāṭhakādisamākhyā granthe prayujyanta evaṃ jñāne 'pi laukikāḥ /
na cāsti viśeṣo yato granthe mukhyāvijñāne gauṇī bhavet /
praṇayanaṃ ca granthajñānayorabhinnaṃ pravṛttinimittam /
tasmājjñānasyāpi vācikā samākhyā /
tathāca yadā jyotiṣṭomasaṃnidhau śrūyamāṇaṃ samākhyāntaraṃ tatpratikamapi karmaṇo bhedakaṃ tadā kaiva kathā śākhāntarīye viprakṛṣṭatame 'tatpratīkabhūtasamākhyāntarābhidheye jñāta iti /
tathā rūpabhedo 'pi karmabhedasya pratipādakaḥ prasiddho yathā 'vaiśvadevyāmikṣā vājibhyo vājinam' ityevamādiṣu /
idamāmnayate-'tapte payasi dadhyānayati sā vaiśvadevyāmikṣā' iti /
atra hi dravyadevatāsaṃbandhānumito yāgo vidhīyate /
tadanantacaraṃ cadamāmnāyate-'vājibhyo vājinam' iti /

kiṃ tāvat prāptam, dravyadevatāntaraviśiṣṭakarmāntaravidhau vidhigauravaprasaṅgāt karmāntarāpūrvāntarakalpanāgauravaprasaṅgācca na karmāntaravidhānamapi tu pūrvasminneva karmaṇi vājinadravyavidhiḥ /
na cotpattiśiṣṭamikṣāguṇāvarodhāttatra vājinamalabdhāvakāśaṃ karmāntaraṃ gocarayatīti yuktam /
body.translated_text:
'[The meditation is] the teaching of all <s>Vedānta</s>s, because of the non-difference in injunction and the like' (<s>sarvavedāntapratyayaṃ codanādyaviśeṣāt</s>).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the connection with the preceding [<s>pāda</s>]: 'The <s>Brahman</s> that is to be known has been expounded' (<s>vyākhyātaṃ vijñeyasya brahmaṇaḥ</s>).
Conceiving that the knowledge directed toward the reality of <s>Brahman</s> without limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>s) [is the sole topic], [the opponent] raises an objection: 'But is not the knowable <s>Brahman</s>...' (<s>nanu vijñeyaṃ brahma</s>).
For if [<s>Brahman</s>] had parts, then due to the difference of parts, the cognitions directed toward <s>Brahman</s> qualified by those parts would differ due to the difference of objects — hence the [claim that <s>Brahman</s> is] without parts was previously refuted, through [the argument] 'from the anterior and posterior [portions]' and the like.
Nor does <s>Brahman</s> have a manifold nature such that cognitions could differ due to the difference of natures — this has been stated: 'Of a single essence' (<s>ekarasam</s>).
'<s>Dhanaṅ</s>' means 'hard' [i.e., the essence is unitary and firm].
But [the opponent says:] even a single [entity] is seen in the world as having multiple forms — just as <s>Somaśarman</s>, though one, is [simultaneously] a teacher, a son of <s>Māyula</s>, a father, a son, a brother, a husband, a son-in-law, an excellent <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — thus having multiple forms. To this it has been said: 'And because of single-formedness' (<s>ekarūpatvāc ca</s>).
'Regarding a single object, many cognitions can arise — but not [cognitions] of many forms' — this has been said: 'Of many forms' (<s>anekarūpāṇi</s>).
'Form' (<s>rūpa</s>) means 'aspect' (<s>ākāra</s>).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] resolves: 'It is said: Regarding <s>Brahman</s> with qualities (<s>saguṇa</s>)' — thus.
The meditations (<s>upāsanā</s>s) directed toward <s>Brahman</s> as qualified by various qualities, and those directed toward <s>prāṇa</s> and the like — yielding seen and unseen fruits as well as liberation — differ due to the difference of objects — this is the meaning.
Hence, deliberation [about them] is fitting — so [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'Among these, this is the investigation' (<s>teṣv eṣā cintā</s>).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] takes up the prima facie view: 'Therein...' (<s>tatra</s>).
'Regarding the name, to begin with' (<s>nāmnas tāvat</s>) — thus.
There is [the <s>Śruti</s>]: 'Now this is the light (<s>jyotiḥ</s>) — with this, the sacrifice with a thousand [gifts as] <s>dakṣiṇā</s> should be performed.'
Therein, the doubt is: Does 'one should sacrifice' (<s>yajeta</s>), by being a restatement of the proximate <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> [sacrifice already known], prescribe a [new] qualification characterized by a thousand-<s>dakṣiṇā</s>? Or does it prescribe an altogether new ritual (<s>karmāntara</s>) distinguished by a different qualification of [involving] a deity and substance?
What, then, is the prima facie conclusion? Since the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is the [topic] in progress, 'one should sacrifice' (<s>yajeta</s>) is a restatement of that. [The word] '<s>jyotiḥ</s>' (light), having been cited as a mere nominal base, [is then] drawn back by 'with this' (<s>etena</s>), and through co-reference with the verb of sacrificing, is established as a name of the ritual. And since the ritual is what is being restated, and its name too — being connected to it — is similarly established. And [the word] '<s>jyotiḥ</s>' is observed to be applicable to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> [ritual] through [the passage] 'In every spring, with the <s>Jyotiḥ</s> [<s>Stoma</s>].' And since the identification of a name by a partial component of that name is well-known in the world — like the word '<s>Bhīma</s>' identifying [the person called] '<s>Bhīmasena</s>.' And since the word '<s>atha</s>' (now), meaning 'immediately after,' would be purposeless if there were no connection [with what precedes]. And since a mere qualification-prescription is lighter [i.e., involves less postulation] than the prescription of a new ritual distinguished by a [different] qualification. And since a <s>dakṣiṇā</s> of twelve hundred — being equally unspecified as to the manner of its origination as one of a thousand — can appropriately be an alternative with the thousand-<s>dakṣiṇā</s>. [Therefore,] this is a restatement of the very <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> in progress, for the purpose of prescribing the qualification of a thousand-<s>dakṣiṇā</s> — not a different ritual — this is the prima facie conclusion.
This being the prima facie view, the reply is given: The [argument about] qualification-prescription for the previous [ritual] would hold if that very context [of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>] were [still operative]. But that [context] has been broken.
Thus: even when in proximity, a different designation (<s>saṃjñāntara</s>) — which evokes a different [previously] unconnected meaning — is well-known in the world to sever the [previous] understanding by the principle 'an alternative [meaning] and multiplicity of meanings [are defects of a word]' (<s>anyāyaś cānekārthatvam</s>), generating a fresh understanding from its [own] meaning as a different term [from the preceding one].
Ordinary people never conclude from the word '<s>deva</s>' (god) in 'Give a cow to <s>Devadatta</s>; now give a horse to the god' that the god is <s>Devadatta</s> who receives the horse.
Likewise, the word 'one should sacrifice' (<s>yajeta</s>), being heard subsequently and being separated by an intervening word of unconnected meaning, does not generate the understanding [that it refers to] that [earlier] ritual, and being insufficient for a mere qualification-prescription, prescribes a different ritual altogether.
Nor is it the case that because in one [particular] instance [the word '<s>jyotiḥ</s>'] is used figuratively (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) [for the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>], it is [therefore always] figurative — for figurative usage is justified only when there is an impossibility [of the primary meaning]. For 'a settlement on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>' (<s>Gāṅgāyāṃ ghoṣa</s>) has a figurative usage of the word '<s>Gāṅgā</s>,' but that does not make [the word] '<s>Gāṅgā</s>' figurative in 'fish in the <s>Gaṅgā</s>' (<s>mīno Gāṅgāyām</s>).
Moreover, even [conceding] the difference [of rituals], since [the word '<s>jyotiḥ</s>'] is first marked by a different designation, the co-reference with the verb of sacrificing merely establishes its being a name of a ritual — but it cannot remove the understanding of difference generated by the different designation.
And thus, the word '<s>atha</s>' (now), meaning '[beginning of a new] topic,' illuminates the fact that [this is] a different context.
And the word '<s>eṣa</s>' (this), referring back to what is being [newly] introduced — hence this is a different [ritual], by virtue of the different designation.
Let there be a difference of ritual from the different designation; but what bearing does this have on the matter at hand? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: 'And there is here, in those prescribed in other <s>Vedānta</s>s...' (<s>asti cātra vedāntāntaravihiteṣu</s>).
Just as the designations '<s>Kāṭhaka</s>' and the like are applied to texts (<s>grantha</s>s), so too [they are applied] to cognitions (<s>jñāna</s>s) in ordinary usage. And there is no distinction such that [they are] primary in texts but figurative in cognitions. And the reason for their application (<s>pravṛttinimitta</s>) — [namely,] the fact of being composed [in a particular tradition] — is the same for both texts and cognitions. Therefore, cognitions too have verbal designations.
And thus, when a different designation heard in the proximity of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> — even when it is a <s>pratīka</s> (representative designation) of a ritual — distinguishes the ritual [from the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>], what need is there to speak of a cognition (<s>jñāna</s>) designated by a different name that is not even a <s>pratīka</s> of [the earlier meditation], belonging to a most remote other <s>śākhā</s> (Vedic branch)?
Likewise, a difference of form (<s>rūpabheda</s>) is well-known as indicating a difference of ritual — as in 'The <s>Vaiśvadevī</s> preparation of <s>ikṣā</s> (curdled milk); for the <s>Vājin</s>s, a <s>vājina</s> (horse-offering)' and the like.
This is what is [traditionally] recited: 'In heated milk, he brings curds — that is the <s>Vaiśvadevī</s> preparation of <s>ikṣā</s>.' For here, a sacrifice distinguished by [specific] substance and deity is prescribed.
Immediately following that, this is recited: 'For the <s>Vājin</s>s, a <s>vājina</s>.' Therein, the doubt is: Is <s>vājina</s> (the horse-substance) prescribed as a qualification in the previous ritual itself, or is a new, unprecedented ritual distinguished by a different substance and deity prescribed?
What, then, is the prima facie conclusion? Since the prescription of a separate ritual distinguished by a different substance and deity would involve the heaviness of [postulating additional] injunctions and the heaviness of postulating a different ritual and a different unprecedented [merit], it is not a prescription of a different ritual but rather a prescription of the <s>vājina</s>-substance in the previous ritual itself.
Nor is it correct [to argue] that because the original [<s>Vaiśvadevī</s>] <s>ikṣā</s>-substance, prescribed at the inception [of the ritual], occupies [all the qualificatory space], the <s>vājina</s>, finding no room, [must] bring about a different ritual.

body.translated_text:
Since in both sentences [the words] <s>āmikṣā</s> (curd preparation) and <s>vājin</s> (food-offering) arise simultaneously with the commencement of both sentences, and since both are equally being taught, <s>āmikṣā</s> does not have the status of being [already] taught [independently].
How then would the <s>karma</s> restricted by it [<s>āmikṣā</s>] not admit <s>vājin</s> [as part of the same rite]?
Nor is the connection of <s>āmikṣā</s> in '<s>Vaiśvadevī</s>' a Śrauta (directly heard) connection with the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, such that it would be stronger than the connection with <s>vājin</s> that is sentence-derived — because there is no difference in being sentence-derived, since the cognition of both depends on other words.
Indeed, when '<s>Vaiśvadevī</s>' is stated, we do not ascertain <s>āmikṣā</s> without depending on the word '<s>āmikṣā</s>.'
Or even granting that it is Śrauta, nevertheless the word '<s>vājibhyaḥ</s>' — through the etymological derivation that <s>vāja</s> means food, <s>āmikṣā</s> [is that food], and those who possess it [are <s>vājins</s>] — indicates the <s>Viśvedevas</s> as connected with that [food].
Although the word <s>vājin</s> is different from the word <s>Viśvadeva</s> — and the deity-status at the point of designation [belongs to] that very word by which the injunction [is expressed], not by another word, lest there be the absurd consequence that because of the identity of meaning of the words <s>sūrya</s> and <s>āditya</s>, the <s>Sūryāditya</s> rites would have a single deity — nevertheless, since <s>vājin</s> is remembered through [the suffix] <s>ini</s> as having the meaning of a pronoun (<s>sarvanāma</s>), and since what is proximate has the status of the pronoun's referent, and since the <s>Viśvedevas</s> are made proximate by the word <s>viśvadevā</s>, these [deities] are to be presented by the word <s>vājin</s> as preceded by that word — not independently like the words <s>sūrya</s> and <s>āditya</s>.
And thus, the word <s>vājin</s>, serving as an indicator (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) of that [deity], indicates the deity as qualified by <s>Viśvadeva</s> — hence there is no difference of deity from [the use of] a different word.
Consequently, the <s>vājin</s> offering, being enjoined for the <s>Viśvedevas</s> on the basis of the connection with <s>āmikṣā</s>, is not overridden by <s>āmikṣā</s> but is rather combined (<s>samuccīyate</s>) with it — thus it is not a separate rite; rather, a single rite equipped with [both] substances is enjoined by the two sentences — this being the prima facie conclusion, it is stated: This would be so if <s>āmikṣā</s> were not denoted by the <s>taddhita</s> (secondary derivative) suffix in '<s>Vaiśvadevī</s>.'
But since the <s>taddhita</s> [suffix '<s>asya</s>'] is remembered as having the meaning of a pronoun, and since the proximate qualified [noun] has the status of the pronoun's referent, the <s>taddhita</s> too operates there [in the proximate referent] alone, not in the <s>Viśvedevas</s> [directly].
Not in the relation [with them], nor in mere possessors of that relation.
Objection: If so, why do we not understand <s>āmikṣā</s> from the word '<s>Vaiśvadevī</s>' alone — why do we require the word '<s>āmikṣā</s>'?
Because the denotation of a word ending in a <s>taddhita</s> suffix is not complete [in itself], we require [another word] for its completion.
For a word whose denotation is complete is capable of producing the cognition of its meaning.
But this [<s>taddhita</s>-ending word], denoting a proximate qualifier, requires the proximity-establishing word '<s>āmikṣā</s>' for that proximity — so how would the consequence of cognizing <s>āmikṣā</s> without depending on the word '<s>āmikṣā</s>' arise?
Or how would there be non-dependence on it there?
And thus, even when there is dependence on another word, the word that, depending on another word, denotes [something] — being cognized through a first-occurring word that is authoritative — is Śrauta (directly scriptural) and stronger.
But what is cognized through the meaning of a word whose denotation is already complete — that, being sentence-derived through a final cognition, is weaker. And therefore, the word <s>vājin</s> — being somehow etymologically derived (<s>yaugika</s>), operating dependently — will indicate the deity that is subordinated to the <s>āmikṣā</s> substance ascertained from the <s>taddhita</s> suffix, the <s>vājin</s> substance that is unconnected with the prior rite and breaks away from the former together with its connections.
For what is contextually present (<s>prakṛta</s>) is the referent of the pronoun.
And what is principal (<s>pradhāna</s>) is called contextually present, not what is subordinate.
And when the weightiness of postulating an injunction according to valid means of knowledge must be accepted — because the valid means of knowledge has reality as its object —
therefore, just as here, because of the subsidiary [element] that is incompatible with the prior rite, there is a difference of rite, so too here the six-fire doctrine (<s>ṣaḍagnividyā</s>) is different from the five-fire doctrine (<s>pañcāgnividyā</s>), and similarly in the <s>Prāṇasaṃvāda</s>s (dialogues about <s>Prāṇa</s>), because of the excess or deficiency [of elements], there is a difference of <s>vidyā</s>.
Likewise, a particular <s>dharma</s> (practice) too serves to establish the difference of rites.
Thus: the <s>Taittirīya</s>s, who study the <s>Kārīri</s> passages, practice eating on the ground — others do not practice this.
Likewise, some who study [the section on] <s>Agni</s> bring a water-pot for the teacher — others do not bring [one].
Likewise, some who study the <s>Aśvamedha</s> [section] bring fodder for the horse — others do not bring [it].
Some [do not practice these]; some, however, practice yet another <s>dharma</s>.
And it is not reasonable that those very rites both require and do not require the benefit produced by eating on the ground and the like.
Therefore, it is understood that the rites in those <s>śākhā</s>s (Vedic branches) are different.
What is the relevance [of this] to the present topic? — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#There is also here#.'
The rest is: 'it does not exist for [followers of] other <s>śākhā</s>s.'
'#Thus, repetitions and the like too#.'
In [passages such as] '<s>samidho yajati</s>' (he sacrifices with fuel-sticks) and the like, the word <s>yajati</s> is repeated five times.
Therein, [the question is:] is there one ritual operation (<s>karmabhāvanā</s>), or are there five?
What is first arrived at? Since in the <s>śabdāntarādhikaraṇa</s> (the topic concerning different words), a difference of operation has been stated [to follow] from a difference of verbal root-meaning and qualifications (<s>anubandha</s>) — and since a difference of verbal root-meaning is impossible without a difference of verbal roots — the ritual operation enjoined by the first-occurring sentence '<s>samidho yajati</s>' is restated (<s>anūdyate</s>) by the subsequent sentences that are recurrences.
Nor is it a [genuine] non-restatement [i.e., a new injunction] due to absence of purpose — because what is established by a valid means of knowledge, even if purposeless, is not to be challenged.
And if there were a difference of ritual operation, there would be the absurd consequence of postulating multiple <s>apūrva</s>s — hence, [the conclusion is that] through the intermediary function of a single <s>apūrva</s>, it is one rite — this is what is arrived at.
This being arrived at, it is stated: For the sentences about <s>samidh</s> and the like are mutually independent.
Although all [sentences] deserve primacy, because of the impossibility of studying [them] simultaneously, they are studied in sequence.
But this sequence is not their motivating [factor].
For [a motivating sequence] would apply [only] if they were mutually dependent and formed a single sentence.
Therefore, since there is no primacy [of one over another], what is arrived at [as a conclusion] simply does not exist — so whose restatement is whose?
Because mere recurrence somehow lacks the capacity to override what is established by the rule (<s>utsarga</s>) — [namely,] the capacity characteristic of an exception (<s>apavāda</s>) that prompts what has not been prompted by the general rule.
For when a subsidiary [element] is heard, [and] to avoid the weightiness of enjoining the subsidiary-qualified rite, for the sake of the lighter [interpretation] of enjoining the subsidiary alone, the expectation of a restatement of the rite [arises] — therein recurrence is helpful.
Just as in the sentence '<s>dadhnā juhoti</s>' (one offers with curds), which is directed toward enjoining curds, when a recurrence is expected, the offering enjoined by '<s>agnihotraṃ juhoti</s>' (one offers the <s>Agnihotra</s>) is restated in its recurrent form.
But here there is no difference from a subsidiary [element], because the words <s>samidh</s> and the like — being names of rites (<s>karmanāmadheya</s>) — are not words denoting subsidiaries.

agṛhyamāṇaviśeṣatayā ca kiṃvacanavihitakiṅkarmānuvādena kasya guṇavidhitvamiti na vinigamyate /
na cāpūrvā nāma jyotirādivadvidhānasaṃbandhaṃ prathamamavagataṃ, yataḥ pūrvabuddhivicchedena vidhīyamānaṃ ka4ma pūrvasmātsaṃjñāto vyavacchindyāt /
kintu prathamata eva karmasāmānādhikaraṇyenāvagatāḥ samidādayastadvaśātkarmanāmadheyatāṃ pratipadyamānā ākhyātasyānuvādatve 'nuvādā vidhitve vidhayo na tu svātantryeṇa kasyacidīśate /
tasmāt svarasasiddhāprāptakarmavidhiparatvātkarmaṇyayamabhyāso bhāvanānubandhabhūtāni bhindāno bhāvanāṃ bhinatti yathā tathā śākhāntaravihitā api vidyāḥ śākhāntaravihitābhyo vidyābhyo 'bhyāso bhetsyatīti /
aśakteśca /

pratiśākhaṃ bhede tūpāsanānāṃ nāyaṃ doṣaḥ /
samāptibhedācca /
keṣāñcit śākhināmoṅkārasārvātmyakathane samāptiḥ /
keṣāñcidanyatra /
body.translated_text:
And since no specific [subsidiary] is apprehended, it cannot be determined whose subsidiary-injunction [is established] by the restatement of which rite enjoined by which word.
Nor is <s>apūrva</s> (unseen potency) something that is first cognized in its connection with the injunction, like <s>jyotis</s> (light) and the like, such that the rite being enjoined, by interrupting the prior cognition, would distinguish [itself] from the former through a denomination.
Rather, <s>samidh</s> and the like, being cognized from the very beginning through co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) with the rite, assume the status of rite-names (<s>karmanāmadheya</s>) by virtue of that [co-reference] — [and thus] if the verb is a restatement, they are restatements, and if the verb is an injunction, they are injunctions — but they do not independently govern anything.
Therefore, since [the sentences] are by their natural purport directed toward enjoining rites, this repetition — breaking apart the operations (<s>bhāvanā</s>) that are the qualifications (<s>anubandha</s>) of [each] rite — breaks apart the operation [into separate rites]. Just as [this principle applies here], so too <s>vidyā</s>s (meditations) enjoined in other <s>śākhā</s>s (Vedic branches) — the repetition will distinguish [them] from the <s>vidyā</s>s enjoined in [yet] other <s>śākhā</s>s.
And because of incapacity.
For a single person is not capable of consolidating a meditation that consists of all <s>Vedānta</s> cognitions, because of the impossibility of studying all <s>Vedānta</s>s — and if [one adopts] the consolidation of meaning not studied, there would be the absurd consequence of the purposelessness of the injunction to study.
But if there is a difference of meditations for each <s>śākhā</s>, this defect does not arise.
And because of the difference of conclusion (<s>samāpti</s>).
For some <s>śākhā</s>-followers, the conclusion [of the meditation] is in the exposition of <s>Oṃkāra</s>'s identity with all things.
For others, [the conclusion is] elsewhere.
