children.translated_text: Likewise, the connection with the fruit (<s>phalasaṃyoga</s>) — characterized by the attainment of supremacy and preeminence — is also the same.
The form (<s>rūpa</s>) too is the same.

children.text: yathā yāgasya yadekasyāṃ śākhāyāṃ dravyadevatārūpaṃ tadeva śākhāntareṣvapīti /
children.translated_text: Just as the form of a sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>) in terms of substance (<s>dravya</s>) and deity (<s>devatā</s>) in one <s>śākhā</s> is the same in other <s>śākhā</s>s as well,
so too, the form of the knowledge (<s>vedana</s>) — having as its object the supremacy and preeminence of <s>Prāṇa</s> — in one [<s>śākhā</s>] is the same in other <s>śākhā</s>s as well. //1//

body.translated_text:
Therefore too, there is a difference of meditations.
And the difference [is established] also from the observation of a different purpose.
Thus: 'One who has not performed the observance (<s>vrata</s>) does not study this' — from observing that one who has not performed the observance does not study, [it follows that] there is no meditation [for such a person].
[But] somewhere, from observing that one who has not performed the observance does study, meditation is understood [to be present].
Therefore, there is a difference of meditations.
Here [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the <s>siddhānta</s>: '#All <s>Vedānta</s> cognitions — because of the non-difference of injunction and the rest#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] explains this: '#The cognitions of all <s>Vedānta</s>s#' — the valid means of knowledge of all <s>Vedānta</s>s — '#the <s>vijñāna</s>s in each and every <s>Vedānta</s> deserve to be just those same ones#.'
The meaning is: those [cognitions] that are in one <s>Vedānta</s> are the same in other <s>Vedānta</s>s as well.
Because of the non-difference of injunction (<s>codanā</s>) and the rest.
By the word 'and the rest' (<s>ādi</s>), the connection-form (<s>saṃyogarūpa</s>) and designations (<s>ākhyā</s>) are included.
And here, '<s>codanā</s>' means the person's effort (<s>puruṣaprayatna</s>) — for it is the exertion of the person, since 'it is that which impels' (<s>codyate</s>).
Here indeed this [effort] operates upon the uninterrupted verbal root-meaning such as oblation (<s>homa</s>) and the like.
The person's effort that is delimited by the sacrifice (<s>tyāga</s>) addressed to a deity, and by the pouring (<s>āsecana</s>) and the like — that very same [effort], in another <s>śākhā</s>, as also here, having as its object the knowledge (<s>vedana</s>) of <s>Prāṇa</s>'s supremacy and preeminence — that very same [effort] is [present] in other <s>śākhā</s>s as well.

body.text:
#kañcidviśeṣamiti# /
yuktaṃ yadagnīṣomīyasyotpannasya paścādekādaśakapālatvādisaṃbandhe 'pyabheda iti /
yathotpannasya tasya sarvatra pratyabhijñāyamānatvādiha tvagniṣūtvapattigata eva guṇabheda iti kathaṃ vaiśvadevīvanna bhedaka iti viśeṣaḥ /
tamimaṃ viśeṣamabhipretyāśaṅkate sūtrakāraḥ- #bhedānneti cediti# /
parihāraḥ sūtrāvayavaḥ- #na ekasyāmapīti# /
pañcaiva sāṃpādikā agnayo vājasaneyināmapi chāndogyānāmiva vidhīyante /
ṣaṣṭhastvagniḥ saṃpadvyatirekāyānūdyate na tu vidhīyate /
vaiśvadevyāṃ tūtpattau guṇo vidhīyata iti bhavatu bhedaḥ /

children.translated_text: Alternatively, even for the <s>Chāndogya</s>s, a sixth fire is indeed recited.

children.text: athavā bhavatu vājasaneyināṃ ṣaṣṭhāgnividhānaṃ mā ca bhūcchāndogyānāṃ tathāpi pañcatvasaṃkhyāyā avidhānānnotpattiśiṣṭatvaṃ saṃkhyāyāḥ kintūtpanneṣvagniṣu pracayaśiṣṭā saṃkhyānūdyate sāṃpādikānagnīnavacchetuṃ, tena yeṣāmutpattisteṣāṃ pratyabhijñānāt /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, let the <s>Vājasaneyin</s>s have the enjoining of a sixth fire, and let the <s>Chāndogya</s>s not — even so, the number five is not enjoined, hence it is not [directly] taught at origination. Rather, the number, being taught for the purpose of collecting (<s>pracayaśiṣṭā</s>) [the fires] after they have been originated, is restated to delimit the constructed fires — and therefore, those that are originated are recognized [as the same across <s>śākhā</s>s].

children.text: apratyabhijñāyamānāyāśca saṃkhyāyā anuvādyatvenānutpattervidhīyamānasya cādhikasya ṣoḍaśigrahaṇavadvikalpasaṃbhavānna śākhāntare jñānabhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: And since the number, not being originated [as new, but merely] restated, is not recognized [as different], and since the additional [fire] that is being enjoined admits of an option (<s>vikalpa</s>) — like the <s>Ṣoḍaśi</s> cup — there is no difference of knowledge in another <s>śākhā</s>.

children.text: utpattiśiṣṭatve 'siddhe prāṇasaṃvādādayo 'pi prāṇasaṃvādādayo 'pi bhavanti pratyabhijñānādabhinnāstāsu tāsu śākhāsviti //2 //
children.translated_text: When [the doctrine of] being taught at origination is not established, the <s>Prāṇasaṃvāda</s>s and the like too are non-different across those various <s>śākhā</s>s, because of being recognized [as the same]. //2//

body.translated_text:
'#Some specific [difference]#.'
It is reasonable that the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [sacrifice], once originated, even when subsequently connected with the eleven-<s>kapāla</s> [offering] and the like, is non-different [across <s>śākhā</s>s].
Because that [sacrifice], once originated, is recognized as the same everywhere. But here the difference of subsidiary [elements] pertains to the very origination of the fire — so how is it not a differentiator, unlike in the case of <s>Vaiśvadevī</s>? — this is the specific [objection].
With this specific [objection] in mind, the <s>Sūtrakāra</s> raises the doubt: '#Because of difference, [some say] no#.'
The resolution, which is part of the <s>sūtra</s>: '#Not [so], because even in a single [<s>śākhā</s>]#.'
Exactly five constructed (<s>sāṃpādika</s>) fires are enjoined for the <s>Vājasaneyin</s>s as well, just as for the <s>Chāndogya</s>s.
The sixth fire is restated (<s>anūdyate</s>) for the purpose of differentiating the correspondences (<s>saṃpad</s>), but is not enjoined [as new].
But in the case of <s>Vaiśvadevī</s>, since a subsidiary is enjoined at the [point of] origination, let there be a difference.

body.text:
#svādhyāyasya tathātvena hi samācāre 'dhikārācca savavacca tanniyamaḥ# /
yairātharvaṇikagranthopāyā vidyā veditavyāṃ teṣāmeva śirovratapūrvādhyayanaprāptagranthabodhitā phalaṃ prayacchati nānyathā /

children.text: anyeṣāṃ tu chāndogyādīnāṃ saiva vidyā cīrṇaśirovratānāṃ phaladetyātharvaṇagranthādhyayanasaṃbandhādavagamyate /
children.translated_text: But for others — the <s>Chāndogya</s>s and the like — that very same <s>vidyā</s> yields fruit [only] for those who have performed the head-observance — this is understood from the connection with the <s>Ātharvaṇika</s> text.
And that connection [is understood] through the Vedic observance (<s>vedavrata</s>) — from the scriptural statement 'One who has not performed the observance does not study this.'

children.text: 'teṣāmevaitāṃ brahmavidyāṃ vadeta' iti vidyāsaṃyoge 'pyetāmiti prakṛtaparāmarśinā sarvanāmnādhyāyanasaṃbandhāvirodhādātharchavihitaiva vidyocyata iti /
children.translated_text: 'To them alone one should teach this <s>Brahmavidyā</s>' — even though the pronoun 'this' (<s>etām</s>), which refers to what is contextually present, is connected with <s>vidyā</s>, since there is no contradiction with the connection to [Vedic] study, the <s>vidyā</s> is said to be enjoined by the <s>ātharva</s> [<s>Upaniṣad</s>] itself.

children.text: savā homāḥ sapta sauryādayaḥ śataudanāntā śataudanāntā ātharvaṇikānāṃ ta ekasminnevārtharvaṇike 'gnau kriyante na tretāyām //3 //
children.translated_text: The seven <s>savā</s> libations beginning with the solar (<s>saurya</s>) and ending with the <s>śataudana</s> (hundred-rice) — these belong to the <s>Ātharvaṇika</s>s and are performed in the single <s>Ātharvaṇika</s> fire, not in the three fires (<s>tretā</s>). //3//

body.translated_text:
'#[The observance pertains to the] <s>Svādhyāya</s> (self-study), because of its being of that nature; for in [matters of] practice (<s>samācāra</s>) there is eligibility; and like a ritual, that restriction [applies]#.'
The <s>vidyā</s> whose means is the <s>Ātharvaṇika</s> (Atharva Veda) text — for those [who follow it], the text-understanding obtained through prior study accompanied by the head-observance (<s>śirovrata</s>) yields the fruit, and not otherwise.

body.text:
#vidyaikatvaṃ darśayati ca# /
bhūyobhūyo vidyaikatvasya vedadarśanādyatrāpi saguṇabrahmavidyānāṃ na sākṣādveda ekatvamāha tāsāmapi tatprāyapaṭhitānāṃ tadvidhānāṃ prāyadarśanādekatvameva /
tathāhyagryaprāye likhitaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhavedayamagrya iti buddhiriti /
yacca kāṭhakādisamākhyayopāsanābheda iti tadayuktam /
etā hi pauruṣeyyaḥ samākhyāḥ kāṭakādipravacanayogāttāsāṃ śākhānāṃ na tūpāsanānām /
nahyetāḥ kāṭhādibhiḥ proktā naca kaṭhādyanuṣṭhānamāsāmitarānuṣṭhānebhyo viśeṣyate /
naca kāṭhaproktānimittamātreṇa granthe pravṛttau tadyogācca kathañcillakṣaṇayopāsanāsu pravṛttau saṃbhavantyāmupāsanābhidhānāmapyāsāṃ śakyaṃ kalpayitum /
naca tadbhedābhedau jñānabhedābhedaprayojakau, mā bhūdyathāsvamāsāmabhedājjñānānāmekaśākhāgatānāmaikyam /
kaṭhādipuruṣapravacananimittāścaitāḥ samākhyāḥ kaṭhādibhyaḥ prāk nāsanniti tannibandhano jñānabhedo nāsīdidānīṃ cāstīti durghaṭamāpadyeta /
tasmānna samākhyāto bhedaḥ /
abhyāso 'pi nātra bhedakaḥ /
yuktaṃ yadekaśākhāgato yajatyabhyāsaḥ samidādīnāṃ bhedaka iti /
tatra hi vidhitvamautsargikamajñātajñāpanamapravṛttapravartanaṃ ca kupyeyātām 'śākhāntare tvadhyetṛpuruṣabhedādekatve 'pi nautsragikavidhitvavyākopa iti /
aśaktirapi na bhedahetuḥ svādhyāyo 'dhyetavya iti svaśākhāyāmadhyayananiyamaḥ /

children.translated_text: And therefore, the meanings pertaining to another <s>śākhā</s>, having been learned from other knowers of that <s>vidyā</s>, will be incorporated.
And completion (<s>samāpti</s>) — even when a single [subsidiary] connected with it is completed — is predicated of that [whole <s>vidyā</s>].

children.text: yathādhvaryave karmaṇi jyotiṣṭomasya samāpti vyapadiśanti-'jyotiṣṭomaḥ samāptaḥ' iti tasmātsamāptibhedo 'pi na sādhanamupāsanābhedasya /
children.translated_text: Just as in the <s>Adhvaryu</s> ritual, they predicate the completion of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>: 'The <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> is completed' — therefore, difference of completion too is not a means of [establishing] difference of meditations.

children.text: tadevamasati bādhake codanādyaviśeṣātsarvavedāntapratyayāni karmāṇi tāni tānyeveti siddham //4 //
children.translated_text: Thus, in the absence of an overriding [consideration], because of the non-difference of the injunction and the like, the cognitions (<s>vidyā</s>s) belonging to all <s>Vedānta</s> [passages] are those very same ones — this is established. //4//

body.translated_text:
'#And the Veda shows the oneness of the <s>vidyā</s>s#.'
Since the oneness of the <s>vidyā</s>s is seen in the <s>Veda</s> again and again, here too, regarding the <s>saguṇa</s> (qualified) <s>Brahmavidyā</s>s, the <s>Veda</s> does not directly state their oneness; [rather] since those [<s>vidyā</s>s], being for the most part recited in accordance with those [<s>Veda</s>s], and since their injunctions are for the most part seen [to be the same], their oneness alone [is established].
For thus: having seen a document written predominantly in the style of the foremost [category], the cognition arises: 'This must be foremost.'
And the [objection] that the <s>vidyā</s>s are different because of the designations '<s>Kāṭhaka</s>' and the like — that is unreasonable.
For these designations are man-made, pertaining to those <s>śākhā</s>s (Vedic branches) by virtue of their being the teachings of <s>Kaṭha</s> and the like, not to the meditations (<s>upāsanā</s>s).
For these [<s>vidyā</s>s] were not taught by <s>Kaṭha</s> and the like, nor is the practice of <s>Kaṭha</s> and the like distinguished from the practice of others.
Nor can it be postulated that these are designations of the meditations — merely because, from the fact of the text being commenced on account of being taught by <s>Kaṭha</s>, and from its connection therewith, the meditations too are somehow commenced through secondary designation (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) — since this is untenable.
Nor are the difference and non-difference of those [designations] the causes of the difference and non-difference of the cognitions — lest, from the non-difference of the [<s>vidyā</s>s'] own [natures], there be the oneness of cognitions belonging to a single <s>śākhā</s>.
These designations, caused by the teaching of persons such as <s>Kaṭha</s> and the like, did not exist before <s>Kaṭha</s> and the like — and the difference of cognition grounded in those [designations] did not exist [then] but exists now — this would lead to an impossibility.
Therefore, there is no difference on account of the designations.
Nor is repetition a differentiator here.
It is reasonable that the repetition of '<s>yajati</s>' (he sacrifices) within a single <s>śākhā</s> is a differentiator of <s>samidh</s>s (fuel-sticks) and the like.
For there, the character of being an injunction — the general [character] of making known what is unknown and instigating the uninitiated — would be vitiated. But in another <s>śākhā</s>, because of the difference of the studying persons, even when there is oneness [of the <s>vidyā</s>], there is no vitiation of the general injunctive character.
Nor is incapacity a cause of difference — [for the rule is] 'one should study one's own self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>),' [meaning] the restriction is to study one's own <s>śākhā</s>.

children.translated_text: Having anticipated a certain distinction, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] established [it] through the earlier system (<s>pūrvatantra</s>),
and for the purpose of establishing the meaning to be stated [later], the <s>sūtrakāra</s> states the meaning in this <s>sūtra</s>.

body.text:
cintāprayojanapradarśanārthaṃ sūtram- #upasaṃhāror'thābhedādvidhiśeṣavatsamāne ca# /
atraidamāśaṅkate-bhavatu sarvaśākhāpratyayamekaṃ vijñānaṃ tathāpi śākhāntaroktānāṃ tadaṅgāntarāṇāṃ na śākhāntarokte tasminnupasaṃhāro bhavitumarhati /
tasyaikasya karmaṇo yāvanmātramaṅgajātamekasyāṃ śākhāyāṃ vihitaṃ tāvnamātreṇaivopakārasiddheradhikānapekṣaṇāt /
apekṣaṇe cādhikamapi tatra vidhīyate /
naca vihitam /
tasmādyathā naimittikaṃ karma sakalāṅgavadvihitamapi aśaktau yāvacchakyamaṅgamanuṣṭhātuṃ tāvanmātrajanyenopakāreṇaupakṛtaṃ bhavatyevamihāpyaṅgāntarāvidhānādeva bhaviṣyatīti /
evaṃ prāpta ucyate-sarvatraikatve karmaṇaḥ sthite gṛhamedhīyanyāyena nopakārāvacchedo yujyate /
nahi tadeva karma sattadaṅgamapekṣate nāpekṣate ceti yujyate /
naimittike tu nimittānurodhādavaśyakartavye sarvāṅgopasaṃhārasya sadātanatvāsaṃbhavādupakārāvacchedaḥ kalpyate /

children.translated_text: If, when the aggregate of benefit from the <s>Prākṛta</s> (model sacrifice) is attained through injunction, the <s>ājyabhāga</s> (ghee-portions) injunction [introduces] a limitation of benefit even in the <s>Gṛhamedhi</s> [sacrifice] — [that would be one thing].

children.text: iha tu śākhāntare katipayāṅgavidhānaṃ tāni vidhatte netarāṇi parisaṃcaṣṭe /
children.translated_text: But here, in another <s>śākhā</s>, a few subsidiaries are enjoined — it enjoins those, but does not enumerate the others.
And it is not a mere enjoining of those [few] alone — like the <s>ājyabhāga</s>s — when the aggregate of that benefit is attained through injunction.

children.text: tasmāttattvena karmaṇāṃ sarvāṅgasaṅgama autsargiko 'sati balavati bādhake nāpavadituṃ yukta iti //5 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the conjunction of all subsidiaries with the <s>karma</s> is the general rule (<s>autsargika</s>), and in the absence of a strong overriding [consideration], it is not appropriate to make an exception. //5//

body.translated_text:
The <s>sūtra</s> is for the purpose of showing the purpose of the inquiry: '#The incorporation [of subsidiary elements is justified] because of non-difference of meaning, as in the case of supplements to an injunction, and when [the <s>vidyā</s>s are] the same#.'
Here this doubt is raised: granted that the <s>vidyā</s> recognized in all <s>śākhā</s>s is one, nevertheless the subsidiary elements mentioned in another <s>śākhā</s> should not be incorporated into that [<s>vidyā</s>] as stated in [yet] another <s>śākhā</s>.
For since the single <s>karma</s> (rite) — with whatever extent of subsidiaries is enjoined in one <s>śākhā</s> — accomplishes its benefit with just that much, there is no need for anything additional.
And if there were a need for more, more would be enjoined there.
But it is not enjoined.
Therefore, just as an occasional rite (<s>naimittika karma</s>), though enjoined with all its subsidiaries, when there is incapacity, achieves its benefit through the benefit generated by performing as many subsidiaries as possible — so here too, [the <s>vidyā</s>] will [function] through the non-enjoining of additional subsidiaries.
With this prima facie view established, the reply is given: when the oneness of the <s>karma</s> everywhere is established, a limitation of benefit by the principle of the <s>Gṛhamedhi</s> (householder's sacrifice) is not appropriate.
For it is not reasonable that the very same <s>karma</s> both requires its subsidiaries and does not require them.
But in the occasional rite, because of the necessity of performing it in accordance with the occasion, since the incorporation of all subsidiaries is not always possible, a limitation of benefit is postulated.

body.text:
#anyathātvaṃ śabdāditi cennāviśeṣāt# /
dvayā dviprakārāḥ prājāpatyā devāścāsurāśca /
tataḥ kānīyasā eva devā jyāyasā asurāḥ /
śāstrajanyayā sāttvikyā buddhyā saṃpannā devāḥ /
te hi dīvyanta iti devāḥ /
śāstrayuktyaparikalpitamatayastāmasavṛttipradhānā asurā asubhiḥ prāṇairanindriyairagṛhītaisteṣu teṣu viṣayeṣu ramanta ityasurā ata eva te jyāyāṃsaḥ /
yato 'mī tattvajñānavantaḥ kānīyasāstu devāḥ /
ajñānapūrvakatvāttattvajñānasya /
prāṇasya prajāpateḥ sāttvikavṛttyudbhavastāmasavṛttyabhibhavaḥ kadācit /
kadācittāmasavṛttyudbhavo 'bhibhavaśca sāttvikyā vṛttaiḥ /
seyaṃ spardhā /
te ha devā ūcuḥ, hanta asurān yajña udgīthenātyayāma asurān jayāmāsminnābhicārike yajña udgīthalakṣaṇasāmabhaktyupalakṣitenodgātreṇa karmaṇoti /
te ha vācamūcurityādinā saṃdarbheṇa vākprāṇacakṣuḥśrotramanasāmāsurapāpmaviddhatayā ninditvā atha hemamāsanyamāsye ūvamāsanyaṃ mukhāntarbilasthaṃ mukhyaṃ prāṇaṃ prāṇābhimānavatīṃ devatāmūcustvaṃ na udgāyeti /
tathetyabhyupagamya tebhya eva prāṇa udagāyat te 'surā viduranena prāṇenodgātrā no 'smān devā atyeṣyantīti /
tamabhidrutya pāpmanāvidhyannasurā yathāśmānamṛtvā prāpya mṛttvālloṣṭo vā vidhvaṃsata evaṃ vidhvaṃsamānā viṣvañco 'surā vineśuḥ /
tadetat saṃkṣipyāha- #vājasaneyaka iti# /
tathā chāndogye 'pyetaduktamityāha- #tathā chāndogye 'pīti# /
viṣayaṃ darśayitvā vimṛśati- #tatra saṃśaya iti# /
pūrvapakṣaṃ gṛhṇāti- #vidyaikatvamiti# /
pūrvapakṣamākṣipati- #nanu na yuktamiti# /
ekatrodgātṛtvenocyate prāṇa ekatra codgānatvena kriyākartrośca sphuṭo bheda ityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] resolves [the objection]: '#This is not a defect#.'

The recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) of the greater number of features [common to both versions] is [paramount]; whatever few features are not recognized should be interpreted through secondary designation (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>).

children.text: na kevalaṃ śākhāntare, ekasyāmapi śākhāyāṃ dṛṣṭametanna ca tatra vidyābheda ityāha- #vājasanetyake 'pi ceti# /
children.translated_text: Not only in another <s>śākhā</s> — even within a single <s>śākhā</s> this is observed, and yet there is no difference of <s>vidyā</s> there — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Even in the <s>Vājasaneyaka</s> itself#.'

children.text: bahutararūpapratyabhijñānānugrahāya comityanenāpi udgīthāvayavena udgītha eva lakṣaṇīya iti pūrvapakṣaḥ //6 //
children.translated_text: In support of the recognition of the greater number of features, by the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) too, what is to be indicated through a component of the <s>Udgītha</s> is the <s>Udgītha</s> itself — this is the prima facie view. //6//

body.translated_text:
'#If [it be said] that there is difference because of the word, [we say:] no, because of non-distinction#.'
The twofold, two-natured [beings] — the descendants of <s>Prajāpati</s> — are the gods and the demons.
Among them, the gods are indeed the younger ones, and the demons the older.
The gods are endowed with intellect that is <s>sāttvika</s> (pure) and born of scripture.
For they are called gods (<s>deva</s>s) because they play (<s>dīvyanti</s>).
The demons (<s>asura</s>s) are those whose thinking is not shaped by scripture and reasoning, who are predominantly of <s>tāmasa</s> (dark) disposition, and who delight (<s>ramante</s>) in various sense-objects through their <s>prāṇa</s>s (vital breaths) — [so called] because they [delight] through <s>asu</s>s (breaths) in ungrasped [objects] — hence they are <s>asura</s>s. And for that very reason they are the older ones,
because they possess the knowledge of reality [in a distorted sense], while the gods are the younger ones,
since the knowledge of reality is preceded by ignorance.
The uprising of <s>sāttvika</s> disposition and the suppression of <s>tāmasa</s> disposition [occurs] in <s>Prāṇa</s> (the individual soul), who is a child of <s>Prajāpati</s>, at certain times.
At other times, there is the uprising of <s>tāmasa</s> disposition and the suppression of <s>sāttvika</s> disposition.
This is the rivalry.
The gods said: 'Come, let us surpass the demons in the sacrifice through the <s>Udgītha</s>; let us conquer the demons' — meaning 'in this <s>Ābhicārika</s> (sorcery) sacrifice, through the <s>Udgātṛ</s> (chanter) indicated by the <s>Sāman</s> portion called <s>Udgītha</s>, through ritual action.'
'They addressed speech' — and so on: through this narrative, having censured speech, <s>Prāṇa</s>, eye, ear, and mind as being afflicted by the demonic evil, [the text says:] 'Then they addressed this oral <s>Prāṇa</s> — the chief <s>Prāṇa</s>, situated within the mouth (<s>mukhāntarbila</s>), [that is,] the deity identified with the vital breath — "You chant the <s>Udgītha</s> for us."'
Having agreed, <s>Prāṇa</s> chanted the <s>Udgītha</s> for them. The demons knew: 'By this <s>Prāṇa</s> as <s>Udgātṛ</s>, the gods will surpass us.'
They rushed at him and pierced him with evil — just as a clod of earth, having struck a stone, is shattered; just as a lump of clay is shattered — so the demons, shattering in all directions, perished.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] summarizes this: '#In the <s>Vājasaneyaka</s>#' — thus.
Similarly, in the <s>Chāndogya</s> too this is stated — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Similarly in the <s>Chāndogya</s> too#.'
Having shown the subject-matter, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] deliberates: '#There is a doubt#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] takes up the prima facie view: '#The oneness of the <s>vidyā</s>#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] objects to the prima facie view: '#But this is not reasonable#.'
In one [version], <s>Prāṇa</s> is spoken of as the <s>Udgātṛ</s> (chanter), and in another as the object of the <s>Udgāna</s> (chanting) — and the difference between the action and the agent is clear — this is the meaning.

body.text:
#na vā prakaraṇabhedātparovarīyastvādivat# /
bahutarapratyabhijñāne 'pi upakramabhedāttanurodhena copasaṃhāravarṇanādekasminvākye tasyaiva codgīthasya punajhapunaḥ saṃkīrtanāllakṣaṇāyāṃ ca chāndogye vājasaneyake pramāṇābhāvādvidyābheda iti rāddhāntaḥ /
#oṃkārasyopāsyatvaṃ prastutya rasatamādiguṇopavyākhyānamoṅkārasya# /
oṃkāra tathāhi-bhūtapṛthivyoṣadhipuruṣavāgṛksāmnāṃ pūrvasyottaramuttaraṃ rasatayā sāratayoktam /
teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ rasatama oṃkāra uktaśchāndogye /
#naca vivakṣitārthabheda iti# /
ekatrodgīthodgātārāvupāsyatvena vivakṣitāvekatra tadavayava oṃkāra iti /
tathā hyabhyudayavākye iti /
evaṃ hi śrūyate-'vivā etaṃ prajayā paśubhirardhayati vardhayatyasya bhrātṛvyaṃ yasya havirniruptaṃ purastāccandramā abhyudeti sa tredhā taṇḍulānvibhajedye madhyamāḥ syustānagnaye dātre puroḍāśamaṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapedye sthiviṣṭhāstānindrāya pradātre dadhaṃścaruṃ ye kṣodiṣṭhāstān viṣṇave śipiviṣṭāya śṛte carum' iti /
tatra saṃdehaḥ-kiṃ kālārādhe yāgāntaramidaṃ codyata uta teṣveva karmasu prakṛteṣu kālāparādhe nimitte devatāpanaya iti /
eṣa tāvadatra viṣayaḥ-amāvāsyāyāmeva darśakarmārthaṃ vedikriyāgnipraṇayanakriyā vratādiśca yajamānasaṃskāraḥ /
dadhyarthaśca dohaḥ /
pratipadi ca darśakarmapravṛttirityanuṣṭhānakramastāttvikaḥ /
yasya tu yajamānasya kutaścidbhamanibandhanāccaturdaśyāmevāmāvāsyābuddhau pravṛttaprayogasya candramā abhyudīyate tatredaṃ śrūyate-'yasya havirniruptam' iti /
tena yajamānenābhyuditenāmāvāsyāyāmeva nimittādhikāraṃ parisamāpya purastadahareva vedyuddharaṇādikarma kṛtvā pratipadi darśaḥ pravartayitavyaḥ /
tatrābhāyudaye kiṃ naimittikamidaṃ karmāntaraṃ darśāccodyata uta tasminneva darśakarmaṇi pūrvadevatāpanayanena devanāntaraṃ vidhīyata iti /
tatra havirbhāgamātraśravaṇāccaruvidhānasāmarthyācca karmāntaram /
yadi hi pūrvadevatābhyo havīṃṣi vibhajediti śrūyate tatastānyeva havīṃṣi devatāntareṇa yujyamānāni na karmāntaraṃ gamayitumarhanti kintu prakṛtameva karma taddhaviṣkamapanītapūrtadevatākaṃ devatāntarayuktaṃ syāt /
atra punastredhā taṇḍulān vibhajediti haviṣa eva madhyamādikrameṇa vibhāgaśravaṇādanapanītā haviṣi pūrvadevatā iti pūrvadavatāvaruddhe haviṣi devatāntaramalabdhāvakāśaṃ śrūyamāṇaṃ karmāntarameva gocarayet /
apica prāpte pūrvasmin karmaṇi dadhnastaṇḍulānāṃ cendrādidevatā saṃbandhaśca vidhātavyaḥ /
carutvaṃ cātra vihitaṃ nāstīti tadapiva vidhātavyam /
tathā prāpte karmaṇyanekaguṇavidhānādvākyaṃ bhidyeta /
karmāntaraṃ tvapūrvaṃ śakyamekenaiva prayatnenānekaguṇaviśiṣṭaṃ vidhātumiti nimitte karmāntarameva vidhīyate /
darśastu lupyate kālāparādhāditi prāpta ucyate-na karmāntaram /
pūrvadavatāto haviṣo vibhāgapūrvaṃ nimitte devatāntaravidhānāt /
carvarthasya cārthaprāpteḥ /
bhavedetadevaṃ yadā tredhā taṇḍulān vibhajediti taṇḍulānāṃ tredhā vibhāgavidhānaparametadvākyaṃ syādapi tu vākyāntaraprāptaṃ taṇḍulānāṃ tredhātvamanūdya vibhajedityetāvadvidhatte tatra vākyānyapanīte pūrvavat devatāsaṃbandhe haviṣastasminneva karmaṇyapratyūhaṃ devatāntarasaṃbandhaṃ vidhātuṃ śaknuvanti /
tathāca dravyamukhena prakṛtamukhapratyabhijñānāt devatāntarasaṃbandhe 'pi na karmāntarakalpanābhavitumarhati /
tataśca samāpte 'pi naimittikādhikārasiddhyarthaṃ tānyeva punaḥ karmāṇyanuṣṭheyāni /
naca dadhani carumiti carusaptamyarthayorvidhānaṃ tayorapyarthaprāptatvāt /
prakṛte hi karmaṇi taṇḍulapeṣaṇaprathanaṃ puroḍāśapākādi dadhipayasī ca prāptāni tatrābhyudayanimitte dadhiyuktānāṃ payoyuktānāṃ ca taṇḍulānāṃ vibhajediti vākyena pūrvadevatāpanayaṃ kṛtvā ye madhyamā ityādibhirvākyairdevatāntarasaṃbandhaḥ kṛtaḥ /
naca prabhūtadhipayaḥ saṃsaktairalpaistaṇḍulaiḥ puroḍāśakriyā saṃbhavati /
iti puroḍāśanivṛttau tadarthasya prathanasyāpi nivṛttiranivṛttastu pāko 'pavādābhāvāttathā cārthaprāptaścodyate /
bhavatu vā anekavākyakalpanam /
prakṛtādhikārāvagamabalādasyāpi nyāyyatvāditi /
tasmāttadevedaṃ karma na tu karmāntaramiti siddham /
paśukāmavākye tvapūrvakarmavidhirabhyudayavākyasārūpye 'pi /
'yaḥ paśukāmaḥ syātso 'māvāsyāmiṣṭvā vatsānapākuryādye sthaviṣṭhāstānagnaye sanimate 'ṣṭhākapālaṃ nirvapedye madhyamāstān viṣṇave śipiviṣṭāya śṛte caruṃ ye kṣodiṣṭhāstanindrāya pradātre dadhaṃścarum' iti /
atra hi amāvāsyāmiṣṭveti samāpte yāge paśukāmeṣṭividhānaṃ nātra pūrvasya karmaṇo 'nanuvṛtteryāgāntaravidhiriti yuktam /
#parovarīyastvādivat# /

children.translated_text: Just as, even though the <s>udgītha</s>-meditations are similar, the <s>udgītha</s>-meditation qualified by attributes such as being golden-hued, being like a stone (<s>aśman</s>), being [the sun's] seeing-capacity — as connected with the sun (<s>Āditya</s>) — is different from the <s>udgītha</s>-meditation qualified by the attribute of being greater-than-the-greatest (<s>parovarīyastva</s>) — so too this [case].

children.text: parasmāt paro varācca varīyāniti parovarīyānudgīthaḥ paramātmarūpaḥ saṃpannaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Greater than the great, and more excellent than the excellent' (<s>parovarīyān</s>) — the <s>udgītha</s> that has attained the nature of the supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>).
For this very reason, [it is called] 'infinite' (<s>ananta</s>).

children.text: paramātmadṛṣṭimudgīthe bhavayitum 'ākāśo hyevaibhyo bhūtebhyo jyāyān' ityākāśaśabdena paramātmānaṃ nirdiśati //7 //
children.translated_text: To cultivate the meditation on the supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) in the <s>udgītha</s>, [the <s>Śruti</s>] designates the supreme Self by the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' (space) in 'For space indeed is greater than these elements' (<s>ākāśo hy evaibhyo bhūtebhyo jyāyān</s>). //7//

body.translated_text:
'Or not, because of the difference of topic — like the <s>parovarīyastva</s> (greater-than-the-greatest) and the like' [BS 3.3.7].
Even though there is extensive mutual recognition [between the two meditations], because of the difference of introductions, and because the conclusion is described in conformity with that [introduction], and because in a single passage that very <s>udgītha</s> is repeatedly extolled, and because there is no valid evidence for figurative usage (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) in the <s>Chāndogya</s> [or] the <s>Vājasaneyi</s>, the difference of meditations is the established conclusion.
'Having introduced the meditativeness of <s>Oṃkāra</s>, the attributes such as being the quintessence (<s>rasatama</s>) and the like are explanatory elaborations of <s>Oṃkāra</s>.'
The <s>Oṃkāra</s> — for thus: of beings, earth, plants, the person, speech, <s>Ṛc</s>, and <s>Sāman</s>, each subsequent one has been declared as the essence (<s>rasa</s>) of the preceding. Of all of those, the <s>Oṃkāra</s> is declared in the <s>Chāndogya</s> as the quintessence (<s>rasatama</s>).
'And it is not the case that the intended meanings are different' — in one [passage], the <s>udgītha</s> and the <s>udgātṛ</s> (chanter) are intended as the objects of meditation; in the other, their component <s>Oṃkāra</s> [is intended].
For thus it is heard in the '<s>abhyudaya</s>-passage' (the passage on prosperity).
This is what is heard: 'He indeed conquers, thrives in progeny and cattle, and makes his rival decline — he whose <s>havis</s> (oblation) has been prepared when the moon rises [visibly] before [the sacrifice begins]. He should divide the rice grains into three portions: those that are medium, he should offer as an eight-<s>kapāla</s> <s>puroḍāśa</s> (cake) to <s>Agni Dātṛ</s> (the giver); those that are largest, he should offer as a curd-oblation (<s>dadhi-caru</s>) to <s>Indra Pradātṛ</s> (the bestower); those that are smallest, he should offer as a cooked-rice oblation (<s>śṛta-caru</s>) to <s>Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa</s>.'
Therein the doubt [arises:] is a separate sacrifice prescribed here when the [proper] time has passed, or is it, in those very prescribed rites, a substitution of different deities when the occasion [of untimeliness] arises?
The subject matter here is as follows: on the new-moon day itself, the preparation of the altar (<s>vedi</s>), the establishment of the fire, vows and the like for the consecration of the sacrificer [are performed]. And the milking is for the sake of curds. And the <s>Darśa</s> sacrifice commences on the first day [of the bright fortnight] — this is the actual procedural sequence.
But for a sacrificer who, due to some cause of confusion, has begun the procedure on the fourteenth day itself under the impression that it is the new-moon day — [if] the moon rises [visibly before the completion], then this [passage] is heard: 'He whose <s>havis</s> has been prepared [when the moon becomes visible].'
That sacrificer, for whom [the moon has] risen, having completed the occasional duties (<s>naimittika-adhikāra</s>) on the new-moon day itself, and having performed the altar-excavation and other preparatory rites on that very prior day, should commence the <s>Darśa</s> sacrifice on the first day.
Therein, when [the moon] rises [untimely], is a separate occasional rite prescribed — apart from the <s>Darśa</s> — or is a substitution of different deities prescribed in that very <s>Darśa</s> rite by removing the original deities?
In that matter, [the argument for] a separate rite: because only the share of the oblation is heard [specified], and because of the capacity of the <s>caru</s> (oblation) prescription.
For if the <s>Śruti</s> said 'he should distribute the oblations to the original deities,' then those very oblations — being connected with different deities — would not warrant [the postulation of] a separate rite; rather, the prescribed rite itself, [retaining] its oblation-material, would have its original deities removed and different deities connected.
But here, since the distribution of the oblation-material [rice] is heard through the statement 'he should divide the rice grains into three portions' — with the classification into medium and the like — the original deities are not removed from the oblation. Hence, since a different deity is heard [being prescribed] when the oblation is [still] occupied by the original deity, [the new deity,] having no scope [within the same rite], must indicate a separate rite.
Moreover, in the prescribed original rite, the connection of curds and rice grains with the deities <s>Indra</s> and the like must be enjoined [anew]. And the <s>caru</s>-nature (being a cooked oblation) is not [already] prescribed here — so that too must be enjoined.
Thus, in the prescribed rite, the multiple-attribute prescription would split the sentence.
But a separate, unprecedented rite can be prescribed with multiple attributes by a single effort — hence what is prescribed on the occasion is a separate rite alone.
And the <s>Darśa</s> is omitted because of the passing of the [proper] time — this being the prima facie view, it is said: it is not a separate rite.
Because, upon distributing the oblation from the original deities, different deities are prescribed on the occasion.
And because the purpose of the <s>caru</s> (cooked oblation) is obtained from the context.
This would be so if the statement 'he should divide the rice grains into three portions' were a sentence whose sole purpose was to prescribe the threefold division of rice grains. But [in fact, this sentence,] taking as stated [by other sentences] the threefold nature of the rice grains, prescribes only 'he should divide' — and therein, the sentences — having removed [the original deities] as before — are capable of prescribing the connection with different deities in that very rite without impediment.
And thus, since the prescribed [rite] is recognized by way of its material [offerings], even when a different deity is connected, there need not be a postulation of a separate rite.
And consequently, even after the occasional duties are completed, those very rites must be performed again for the purpose of establishing the eligibility [for the naimittika-adhikāra].
Nor is the prescription of '<s>caru</s>' in curds [a new prescription], nor of the locative 'in curds' [as instrumental] — because both are obtained from the context.
For in the prescribed rite, the grinding and spreading of rice grains, the baking of <s>puroḍāśa</s> and the like, curds and milk — are all [already] obtained. And therein, on the occasion of the <s>abhyudaya</s> (prosperity rite), by the statement 'he should divide the rice grains mixed with curds and those mixed with milk,' having removed the original deities, the connection with different deities is made by the sentences beginning with 'those that are medium' and the like.
And since a <s>puroḍāśa</s> cannot be made from small amounts of rice mixed with abundant curds and milk,
upon the negation of <s>puroḍāśa</s>, the spreading [of rice] — which serves it — is also negated; but the cooking (<s>pāka</s>) is not negated, because of the absence of an overriding rule. And thus, [the <s>caru</s>] is obtained from the context.
Or alternatively, let there be the postulation of multiple sentences.
Even that is justified, by the force of the understanding of the prescribed rite's scope.
Therefore, it is established that this is that very [same] rite and not a separate rite.
But in the '<s>paśukāma</s>-passage' (the passage on the desire for cattle), a separate rite is prescribed, despite the similarity with the <s>abhyudaya</s>-passage.
'He who desires cattle should, having sacrificed on the new-moon day, release the calves. Those that are largest, he should offer as an eight-<s>kapāla</s> <s>puroḍāśa</s> to <s>Agni Sanimate</s>; those that are medium, he should offer as a cooked-rice oblation (<s>śṛta-caru</s>) to <s>Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa</s>; those that are smallest, he should offer as a curd-oblation (<s>dadhi-caru</s>) to <s>Indra Pradātṛ</s>.'
For here, the prescription of the <s>paśukāmeṣṭi</s> (sacrifice for the desire of cattle) [comes] after the completion of the sacrifice, by 'having sacrificed on the new-moon day' — since the original rite does not continue here, the prescription of a separate sacrifice is justified.
'Like the <s>parovarīyastva</s> (greater-than-the-greatest) and the like' —

body.text: #saṃjñātaścettaduktamasti tu tadapi# /

children.translated_text: When the understanding of the meaning is clearer [from the text itself], the sameness of name is not a proof of non-difference — because it would lead to over-extension.
Moreover, upon examining the syllables of the <s>Śruti</s>, the cognition of difference is more intimate (<s>antaraṅga</s>) and independent (<s>anāpekṣa</s>).

children.text: saṃjñaikatvaṃ tu śrutibāhyatayā bahiraṅgaṃ ca pauruṣeyatayā sāpekṣaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: But the sameness of name — being external to <s>Śruti</s> — is extrinsic (<s>bahiraṅga</s>), and — being of human origin (<s>pauruṣeya</s>) — is dependent (<s>sāpekṣa</s>).
Therefore, being weak, it is insufficient to establish non-difference. //8//

body.translated_text: 'If [it be said that they are the same] because of the sameness of name — that has been stated; but there is also that [i.e., difference]' [BS 3.3.8].

body.text:
#vyāpteśca samañjasam /
adhyāso nāmeti# /
gauṇī buddhiradhyāsaḥ /
yathā māṇavake 'nivṛttāyāmeva māṇavakabuddhivyāpadeśavṛttau siṃhabuddhivyapadeśavṛttiḥ siṃho māṇavaka iti, evaṃ pratimāyāṃ vāsudevabuddhirnāmni ca brahmabuddhistathoṅkāga udgīthabuddhivyapadeśāviti /
apavādaikatvaviśeṣaṇāni coktāni /
ekārthe '
body.translated_text:
'And because of pervasion, [the interpretation is] coherent' [BS 3.3.9].
'Superimposition (<s>adhyāsa</s>) is' — thus.
A secondary (<s>gauṇī</s>) cognition is superimposition.
Just as in the case of a boy — when the usage and designation of 'boy-cognition' has not ceased — the usage and designation of 'lion-cognition' arises [as in] 'The boy is a lion' — so too, in an image, the <s>Vāsudeva</s>-cognition [is superimposed]; and in a name, the <s>Brahman</s>-cognition; and similarly in the <s>Oṃkāra</s>, the <s>udgītha</s>-cognition and its designation [are superimposed].
And the distinguishing features of sublation (<s>apavāda</s>) and unity have been stated.
Even for a single referent,

body.text:
pi ca śabdadvayaprayogo dṛśyate /
yathā vaiśvadevyāmikṣā vijñānamānandam /
vyākhyāyāṃ ca paryāyāṇamapi sahaprayogo yathā sindhuraḥ karī pikaḥ kokila iti /
vimṛśyānadhyavasāyalakṣaṇaṃ pakṣaṃ gṛhṇāti- #tatrānyatama iti# /
body.translated_text:
the employment of two words is seen — as in '<s>vaiśvadevī āmikṣā</s>' (the <s>vaiśvadeva</s>-curds) and '<s>vijñānam ānandam</s>' (knowledge, bliss).
And even in commentary, the co-employment of synonyms [is seen], as '<s>sindhuraḥ karī</s>' (elephant, elephant) and '<s>pikaḥ kokilaḥ</s>' (cuckoo, cuckoo).
Having deliberated, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] takes up the position characterized by non-determination (<s>anadhyavasāya</s>): 'Therein, one or the other...'

body.text:
siddhāntamāha-idamucyate- #vyāpteśca# /
pratyanuvākaṃ pratyṛcamupakrame ca samāptau cokāraḥ sardavedavyāpīti kiṅgato 'yamoṅkārastattadāpyādiguṇaviśiṣṭastasmai tasmai kāmāvāptyādiphalāyopāsyatvenādhikriyata ityapekṣāyāmudgīthapadeneti viśiṣyate /
udgīthapadenokārādyavayavaghaṭitasāmabhaktibhedābhidhāyinā samudāyasyāvayavabhāvānupapattestatsaṃbandhavayava oṃkāro lakṣyate, na punaroṅkāreṇāvayavina udgīthasya lakṣaṇā /
oṃkārasyaivopariṣṭāttu tattadguṇaviśiṣṭasya tattatphalaviśiṣṭasya copavyākhyāsyamānatvāt /
dṛṣṭaśca samudāyaśabdo 'vayave lakṣaṇayā yathā grāmo dagdhaḥ paṭo dagdha iti tadekadeśadāhe /
adhyāse tu lakṣaṇā phalakalpanā ca /
tathāhi āptyādiguṇakapraṇavopāsanādidamudgīthatopāsanaṃ praṇavasyānyat /
nacātrāpyādi upāsaneṣviva phalaṃ śrūyate /
tasmāt kalpanīyam /
udgīthasaṃbandhipraṇavopāsanādhikārapare vākye nāyaṃ doṣaḥ /
apica gauṇyā vṛtterlakṣaṇāvṛttirbalīyasī lāghavāt /
lakṣaṇāyā hi lakṣaṇīyaparatvaṃ padasya tasyaiva vākyārthāntarbhāvāt /
yathā gāṅgāyāṃ ghoṣa iti lakṣyamāṇasya tīrasya vākyārthe 'ntarbhāvo 'dhikaraṇatayā /
gaurvāhīka ityatra tu gosaṃbandhitīṣṭhanmūtrapurīṣādilakṣaṇayā na tatparatvaṃ gośabdasya /
apitu tatkakṣādhyavasitatadguṇayuktavāhīkaparatvamiti gauṇyā vṛtterdurbalatvaṃ tadidamuktaṃ-lakṣaṇāyāmapi tviti /
gauṇyapi vṛttirlakṣaṇāvayavatvāllakṣaṇoktā /
yadyapi vaiśvadevīpadamāmikṣāyāṃ pravartate tathāpyarthamedaḥ sphuṭataraḥ /
āmikṣāpadaṃ hi rūpeṇāmikṣāyāṃ pravartate /

children.translated_text: But the word '<s>vaiśvadevī</s>' applies to that very [curds] as qualified by [the ritual deity] <s>Viśvadeva</s>.

children.text: evaṃ hi vijñānāndayorapi sphuṭataraḥ pravṛttinimittabhedaḥ satyapi brahmaṇyaikārthye /
children.translated_text: Thus too, in the case of '<s>vijñāna</s>' (knowledge) and '<s>ānanda</s>' (bliss), the difference of the basis for usage is clearer, even though both [apply to] the single referent <s>Brahman</s>.
Nor [can it be said that this is like] a commentary [where synonyms are used together] — because both [words in the Vedic passage] have well-known meanings and different meanings.
The rest is of transparent meaning. //9//

body.translated_text:
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the established conclusion: 'Here it is said: And because of pervasion' [BS 3.3.9].
The <s>Oṃkāra</s> pervades the entire <s>Veda</s> — in each <s>anuvāka</s> (section), each <s>ṛc</s> (verse), at the beginning and at the end. And when the question arises — 'On what basis is this <s>Oṃkāra</s>, qualified by such-and-such attributes like <s>āpti</s> (attainment) and the like, prescribed as an object of meditation for such-and-such fruits like the attainment of desires and the like?' — it is specified by the word '<s>udgītha</s>.'
By the word '<s>udgītha</s>' — which denotes the different divisions of the <s>Sāma</s>-chant (<s>sāmabhakti</s>) composed of the components beginning with <s>Oṃkāra</s> — the <s>Oṃkāra</s> is indicated (<s>lakṣyate</s>) as a component of the aggregate, since an aggregate cannot become a component of itself. But the indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) is not of the aggregate <s>udgītha</s> by the [word] <s>Oṃkāra</s>.
Because subsequently, it is the <s>Oṃkāra</s> itself — qualified by such-and-such attributes and such-and-such fruits — that will be explained.
And the usage of an aggregate-word for a component is seen in figurative usage — as 'the village was burned' and 'the cloth was burned' when only a part thereof has been burned.
But in the case of superimposition (<s>adhyāsa</s>), there is [both] figurative usage and postulation of the fruit.
For thus: the meditation on <s>Praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃkāra</s>) with attributes such as <s>āpti</s> (attainment) and the like, being different from the meditation on <s>udgītha</s>, is another [meditation] apart from those of <s>Praṇava</s>.
And in these meditations — like [those concerning] <s>āpti</s> and the like — no fruit is heard [explicitly].
Therefore, [the fruit] must be postulated.
But in a passage whose purport is the meditation on <s>Praṇava</s> as related to <s>udgītha</s>, this fault does not arise.
Moreover, the figurative function (<s>lakṣaṇā-vṛtti</s>) is stronger than the secondary function (<s>gauṇī vṛtti</s>), because of economy (<s>lāghava</s>).
For in figurative usage, the word's referential thrust (<s>paratva</s>) is toward the indicated meaning, because that very [indicated meaning] is included within the sentence-meaning.
Just as in '<s>gāṅgāyāṃ ghoṣaḥ</s>' (the cowherds' settlement is on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>), the bank — which is the indicated meaning — is included in the sentence-meaning in the capacity of a location.
But in '<s>gaur vāhīkaḥ</s>' (the <s>Vāhīka</s> is a bull), [the word '<s>go</s>' (cow/bull)] indicates [a person] by virtue of the characteristic marks of cow-habitation — its standing, urine, dung, and the like — and the referential thrust of the word '<s>go</s>' is not toward that [person];
rather, it is toward the <s>Vāhīka</s> endowed with those qualities, ascertained within the scope of that [cow-related meaning]. Hence the weakness of the secondary function. This is what is stated: 'Even in the case of figurative usage, however...'
The secondary function too, being a part of figurative usage, is called figurative.
Although the word '<s>vaiśvadevī</s>' applies to the curds (<s>āmikṣā</s>), nevertheless the meaning-difference is clearer.
For the word '<s>āmikṣā</s>' applies to the curds by virtue of its form.

body.text:
#sarvābhedādanyatreti# /
evaṃśabdasya sannihitaprakārabhedaparāmarśārthatvātsākṣācchabdopasthāpitasya ca saṃnidhānācchākhāntaragatasya cānukramatayā(?) saṃnidhānābhāvānna kauṣītakiprāṇasaṃvādavākye prāṇasya vasiṣṭhatvādibhirguṇairupāsyatvamapi tu jyeṣṭhatreṣṭhatvamātreṇeti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ /
siddhāntastu-satyaṃ saṃnihitaṃ parāmṛśati evaṅkāro na tu śabdopāttamātraṃ saṃnihitam /
kintu yacchabdābhihitārthanāntarīyakatayā prāptaṃ tadapi hi buddhau saṃnihitaṃ saṃnihitameva /
yathā 'yasya parṇamayī juhūrbhavati' ityavyabhicāritakratusamanvayayā juhvopasthāpitaḥ kratuḥ /
tasmādupāsyaphalapratyabhijñānāttadavyabhicāriṇaḥ prakārabhedasyehānuktasyāpi buddhau saṃnidhānātprakṛtaparāmarśinaivaṅkāreṇa parāmarśo yukta iti siddhaṃ kauṣītakibrāhmaṇagatena tāvadevaṅkāreṇa śakyate parāmraṣṭum /

children.text: tathāpyabhyupetyāpi brūma ityāśayavatā bhāṣyakṛtoktam- #tathāpi tasminneva vijñāne vājasaneyibrāhmaṇagateneti /
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] — with the intention 'even conceding [the opponent's point], we still say' — states through the words of the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>: 'Even so, in that very knowledge, by [the word <s>evam</s>] occurring in the <s>Vājasaneyi Brāhmaṇa</s>...'
'The abandonment of what is heard' (<s>śrutahāni</s>) —

children.text: kevalasya śrutasya hāniritarasahitasya cākṣutasya kalpanā na cetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is neither the loss of what is heard alone, nor the postulation of what is unheard combined with the other — this is the meaning.
What is concealed is another [reading]. //10//

body.translated_text:
'Because of the non-difference of all [attributes], except where otherwise [stated]' [BS 3.3.10].
Since the word '<s>evam</s>' (thus) is for the purpose of referring back to the mode (<s>prakāra</s>) that is proximately present, and since what is directly presented by the word is proximate, while what belongs to another <s>Śākhā</s> — being [only] sequentially [related] — lacks proximity, in the <s>Kauṣītaki</s> <s>prāṇa-saṃvāda</s> (dialogue of the vital breaths) passage, <s>prāṇa</s> is not to be meditated upon with the attributes of being <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and the like [found in another <s>Śākhā</s>], but only with the attribute of being the chief and the best — this is the prima facie view.
The established conclusion is: it is true that the word '<s>evam</s>' refers back to what is proximate; but what is proximate is not merely what has been presented by a word.
Rather, what has been obtained as necessarily connected with the word's stated meaning — that too, being present in the intellect, is proximate.
Just as in 'he whose ladle is made of <s>Parṇa</s>-leaves [should perform the sacrifice]' (<s>yasya parṇamayī juhūḥ</s>), the sacrifice — presented by the word '<s>juhū</s>' (ladle) through the invariable concomitance of the ladle with the sacrifice — is [also] proximate.
Therefore, since the object of meditation and its fruit are mutually recognized [between the two passages], and since the mode-difference — though not stated here — is present in the intellect as invariably concomitant with that [recognized object], it is appropriate that it be referred back to by the word '<s>evam</s>' which refers to what is proximate. Thus it is established that even by the word '<s>evam</s>' occurring in the <s>Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa</s>, [the attributes from the other <s>Śākhā</s>] can be referred back to.

body.text:
ānandādayaḥ pradhānasya /
guṇavadupāsanāvidhānasya vāstavaguṇavyākhyānādvivekārthamidamadhikaraṇam /
yathaikasya brahmaṇaḥ /
saṃyadvāmatvādayaḥ satyakāmādayaśca guṇā na saṃkīryeran /
evāmānandavijñānatvādayo vibhutvanityatvādibhirguṇaiḥ pradeśāntaroktairna saṃkīryeran /
tatsaṃkare vā saṃyadvāmatvādayo 'pi satyakāmādibhiḥ saṃkīryeran /
nahi brahmaṇo dharmiṇaḥ sattve kaścidviśeṣa iti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ /
rāddhāntastu vāstavavidheyayorvastudharmatayā cānuṣṭheyatayā cāvyavasthāvyavasthe vyavatiṣṭhete /
vastudharmo hi yāvadvastu vyavatiṣṭhate /
nāsāvekatrokte 'nyatrānukto nāstīti śakyaṃ vaktum /
vidheyastu puruṣaprayatnatantraḥ puruṣaprayatnaśca yatra yāvadguṇaviśiṣṭe brahmaṇi coditaḥ sa tāvatyevāvatiṣṭhate nāvihitamapi guṇaṃ cotarīkartumarhati /
tasya vidhitantratvādvidheśca vyavasthānāt /
tasmādānandavijñānādayo brahmatattvātmatayoktā yatra yatra brahma śrūyate tatra tatrānuktā api labhyante /
saṃyadvāmādayaścopāsanāprayatnavidhiviṣayā yathāvidhyavatiṣṭhante na tu yathāvastviti siddham /

children.translated_text: As for <s>priyaśiras</s> (dear-headed) and the like — [their] being objects of meditation has been shown by superimposition as a reasoning principle.
The reasoning for that has been stated [in connection with] <s>saṃyadvāma</s> and the like.
<s>Moda</s> (joy) is mere delight.
<s>Pramoda</s> (intense joy) is heightened delight — these two are relative to each other, being increase and decrease. //11//

body.translated_text:
'<s>Ānanda</s> (bliss) and the like belong to the principal [<s>Brahman</s>].' This <s>adhikaraṇa</s> is for the purpose of distinguishing between the prescription of meditation on [<s>Brahman</s>] as qualified by [certain] qualities and the explanation of [its] real qualities.
Just as the qualities of a single <s>Brahman</s> — such as <s>saṃyadvāmatva</s> (being <s>Saṃyadvāma</s>) and <s>satyakāmatva</s> (being one whose desires are true) — are not intermixed,
so too, <s>ānanda</s> (bliss), <s>vijñānatva</s> (being consciousness), and the like should not be intermixed with qualities such as all-pervasiveness (<s>vibhutva</s>), eternality (<s>nityatva</s>), and the like, which are stated in other passages.
Or, if there were such intermixing, then <s>saṃyadvāmatva</s> and the like too would be intermixed with <s>satyakāmatva</s> and the like.
For there is no distinguishing feature in <s>Brahman</s> as the common substratum — this is the prima facie view.
But the established conclusion is: between what is real and what is to be enjoined, there is a fixed distinction by virtue of being a real property and being something to be practiced.
For a real property persists as long as the thing [itself] persists.
One cannot say that because it is stated in one place and not stated in another, it does not exist [there].
But what is enjoined depends on the person's effort, and the person's effort — being enjoined with respect to <s>Brahman</s> qualified by a certain number of qualities in a given [meditation] — remains confined to just that [number], and cannot include even an un-enjoined quality.
Because [what is enjoined] depends on the injunction, and the injunction has a fixed scope.
Therefore, <s>ānanda</s> (bliss), <s>vijñānatva</s> (consciousness), and the like — being stated as [belonging to] the very essence of <s>Brahman</s> — wherever <s>Brahman</s> is heard, there they too are obtained even if not [explicitly] stated.
But <s>saṃyadvāma</s> and the like — being the objects of the injunction of meditative effort — remain fixed according to the injunction, not according to the thing — this is established.

body.text:
#ādhyānāya prayojanābhāvāt /
indriyebhyaḥ parā hyarthā iti# /
kimatra sarveṣāmevārthādīnāṃ paratvaṃ pratipādayiṣitam, āho puruṣasyaiva tatpratipādanārthaṃ cetareṣāṃ paratvapratipādanam /
tatra pratyekamarthādiparatvapratipādanaśruteḥ śrūyamāṇatattatparatve ca saṃbhavati na tattadatikarme sarveṣāmekaparatvādhyavasānaṃ nyāṭyam /
na ca prayojanābhāvādasaṃbhavaḥ /

children.translated_text: because the statement of the superiority of each one individually has the purpose of <s>ādhyāna</s> (meditation [on each level]),
and because of the <s>Smṛti</s> [testimony] that the meditations on each of those [levels] are fruitful.
Thus the <s>Smṛti</s> [states]: 'Those who meditate on the senses dwell here for ten <s>manvantara</s>s;

those who meditate on the material elements, a full hundred; those who meditate on the presiding deities (<s>ābhimānika</s>s), a thousand;
those who meditate on the intellectual [self] (<s>bauddha</s>) dwell for ten thousand, free from affliction;
those who meditate on the Unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) dwell a full hundred thousand;
but having attained <s>Puruṣa</s> beyond qualities (<s>nirguṇa</s>), there is no reckoning of time.'
Since the authoritative division of the sentence [into multiple teachings] must be accepted, against the prima facie conclusion that these sentences teach the superiority of each one — objects and the rest — individually, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says:
'For the objects are higher than the senses' — this passage, to begin with, is understood as having the purport of teaching the reality of things (<s>vastu-tattva</s>), not as having the purport of enjoining meditation (<s>ādhyāna-vidhi</s>).
Because [meditation] is not heard [in the passage].
Therein, whichever [teaching] is directly seen to have purpose — the superiority of all [is directed toward] that [teaching].
And it is seen that the knowledge of the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s> [results in] the subsidence of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), which is the cause of all suffering and <s>saṃsāra</s>.
Because the arising of true knowledge (<s>tattva-jñāna</s>) has the characteristic of the subsidence of error (<s>viparyāsa</s>) — this is seen in each and every case.
But no purpose is seen for the cognition of the superiority of objects and the rest [taken individually].
And when a seen [purpose] is possible, the postulation of an unseen [purpose] is not appropriate.

body.translated_text:
'#For the purpose of meditation (<s>ādhyāna</s>), because of the absence of purpose.#'
'#For the objects (<s>artha</s>s) are higher than the senses#' — thus.
Here, the question is: Does this [passage] intend to teach the superiority of each and every one — objects and the rest — [over the preceding], or is the teaching of the superiority of the others [merely] for the purpose of establishing the superiority of <s>Puruṣa</s> alone?
Therein, the prima facie view is: since the <s>Śruti</s> teaches the superiority of each one — objects and the rest — individually, and since when each individual superiority as heard [in the text] is possible, it is not appropriate to force the conclusion that the superiority of all [levels] is [directed] toward a single [entity's] superiority.
Nor is there impossibility due to absence of purpose,

body.text:
bauddhā daśa sahasrāṇi tiṣṭhanti vigatajvarāḥ /
pūrṇaṃ śatasahasraṃ tu tiṣṭhantyanyaktacintakāḥ /
puruṣaṃ nirguṇaṃ prāpya kālasaṃkhyā na vidyate /
' iti /
prāmāṇikasya vākyabhedasyābhyupeyatvāt pratyekaṃ teṣāmarthādīnāṃ paratvaparāṇyetāni vākyānīti prāptaya ucyate-indriyebhyaḥ parā hyarthā ityeṣa tāvatsaṃdarbho vastutattvapratipādanaparaḥ pratīyate nādhyānavidhiparaḥ /
tadaśruteḥ /
tadatra yatpratyasya sākṣātprayojanavattvaṃ dṛśyate tatpratyayaparatvaṃ sarveṣām /
dṛṣṭaṃ ca viṣṇoḥ paramapadajñānasya nikhilānarthasaṃsārakāraṇāvidyopaśamaḥ /
tattvajñānodayasya viparyāsopaśamalakṣaṇatveta tatra tatra darśanāt /
arthādiparatvapratyayasya tu na dṛṣṭamasti prayojanam /
naca dṛṣṭe saṃbhavati adṛṣṭakalpanā nyāṭyā /

children.translated_text: Therefore, because of having a directly seen purpose, this passage is understood as having the purport of teaching the superiority of <s>Puruṣa</s>.
Moreover, even from [an examination of] what is near [in context], this alone is its meaning — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#And further, by the negation of the other (<s>para-pratiṣedha</s>)#.'

Now, [one might ask:] there is no injunction of meditation (<s>ādhyāna-vidhi</s>) here — then how is it said 'for the purpose of <s>ādhyāna</s>'? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#For the purpose of <s>ādhyāna</s>#' — [it means the passage serves this purpose even without an explicit injunction]. //14//

body.translated_text: And when [the passage] can serve as the means to the supreme human goal (<s>parama-puruṣārtha</s>), [interpreting it as serving] a subordinate human goal is not fitting.

'#And because of the word <s>Ātman</s>#.'
Because the nature of valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>s) is to convey what is not [otherwise] known, and especially of <s>Āgama</s> (scripture); and because scripture itself ascertains that the <s>Ātman</s> denoted by the word '<s>Puruṣa</s>' is difficult to know (<s>duradhigama</s>); and because in reality too it is difficult to know; and because objects and the like are easy to know — therefore, the statement of the superiority of objects and the rest has the purport of [establishing] the superiority of That [<s>Ātman</s>] — this is the meaning.

body.text:
#ātmaśabdācca# /
anadhigatārthapratipādanasvabhāvatvāpramāṇānāṃ viśeṣataścāgamasya, puruṣaśabdavācyasya cātmanaḥ svayaṃ śrutyaiva duradhigamatvāvadhāraṇādvastutaśca duradhigamatvādarthādīnāṃ ca sugamatvāttatparatvamevārthādiparatvābhidhānasyetyarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: [That is to say:] that is its purport (<s>tātparya</s>).
Moreover, even from the reference to another <s>Śruti</s> [passage], this alone [is established].

But if the superiority of objects and the rest were intended in its own right, the <s>Śruti</s> would not state what is required [only] by [another passage] — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#And further, "He attains the end of the road"#.' //15//

children.text: arthādiparatve tu svarūpeṇa vivakṣite nāpekṣitaṃ śrutirācaṣṭe ityāha- #apica so 'dhvanaḥ pāramāpnotīti# //15 //

body.translated_text: The special emphasis (<s>āśayātiśaya</s>) of the <s>Śruti</s> is like [the figure of speech called] <s>āśayātiśaya</s> (emphasis of intent).

'#The apprehension of <s>Ātman</s>, as in the other [<s>Upaniṣad</s>], because of what follows#.'
For in <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>, the creation of the world is known as presided over by the supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>) and as having both <s>Parameśvara</s> and <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> as creators. Here [in the <s>Aitareya</s>], this primary creation of the world — [described] without mentioning the creation of the great elements (<s>mahābhūta</s>s) — being perceived [as the work of] a subordinate lord (<s>avāntareśvara</s>), and the ascertainment of the oneness of <s>Ātman</s> before creation, [being taken] in relation to the subordinate lord —
because the creation of <s>Parameśvara</s> involves the great elements such as <s>ākāśa</s> (space) and the rest, while this [creation] is the reverse of that;
because that very one [<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>], in relation to a different modification, has fire-hood (<s>agnatva</s>), and also has the act of seeing (<s>īkṣaṇa</s>);
moreover, in this very <s>Aitareyaka</s>, in the preceding section, the creation of the world is stated as having <s>Prajāpati</s> as its agent —
following that [precedent] too, this alone is understood;
moreover, the activities such as 'From them he brought forth a cow' and the like, as stated in <s>Śruti</s>, are well-known specifically in connection with a self (<s>ātman</s>) that is distinct, [namely] <s>Paramātman</s> [as distinguished from <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>];
from that too, the subordinate lord alone is understood;
and the use of the word '<s>Ātman</s>' is seen here too — therefore, this is a discourse about the other [lower] self — having established this prima facie view, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says:
The apprehension of <s>Paramātman</s> is [what is intended] here, just as in the other creation passages such as 'From this <s>Ātman</s>, <s>ākāśa</s> (space) arose' and the like.
Therefore, from what follows — namely, 'He, this one, saw' (<s>sa aikṣata</s>), the hearing of creatorship preceded by seeing (<s>īkṣaṇa</s>) — and from the ascertainment [that the creator is] '<s>Ātman</s>' —
this is the intent: To begin with, the soleness before creation, the designation as '<s>Ātman</s>,' and creatorship — these primarily belong to <s>Parameśvara</s> here.
In the absence of a genuine impossibility [of this reading], it is not appropriate to interpret [the passage as referring to] another [entity].
Nor does the non-mention of the creation of great elements constitute a ground of impossibility.
Just as, in the creation that in reality belongs to <s>Brahman</s> and begins with <s>ākāśa</s> (space), the statement of creation beginning with <s>tejas</s> (fire) [found] somewhere [else] does not contradict [this] — as is seen from 'From this <s>Ātman</s>, <s>ākāśa</s> arose.'
[The opponent says:] 'After creating space and air' — that [mention of space and air] must be supplied there [too]. Here too, 'after creating the great elements' must be postulated.
Since knowledge — whose validity is established by [its appearance in] all <s>śākhā</s>s (Vedic branches) — requires effort when a heard [text] yields an unheard [implication], one should not treat lightly the creation's [supposed] nature of [beginning with] great elements merely because it is heard [elsewhere], thereby weakening [one's commitment to the text at hand].
Moreover, the mass of Vedic text — whose study depends on the injunction of <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study) and whose meaning, endowed with purpose, is acquired through the injunction of study — the more it attains a greater purpose, the more it is approved.
And its having <s>Brahman</s> as its object gives it the usefulness of being a means to the supreme human goal — this is not the case when its object is something else.
This is what is stated: '#And the particular mode of activity that is followed here#' — thus.
Nor is the creation of the world the activity of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>; rather, it is [the activity] of <s>Paramātman</s> who has entered into him — this has been stated right here.

body.text:
#ātmagṛhītiritaravaduttarāt# /
śrutismṛtyorhi lokasṛṣṭiḥ parameśvarādhiṣṭhitā parameśvarahiraṇyagarbhakartṛkopalabdhā seyamiha mahābhūtasargamanabhidhāya prāthamikī lokasṛṣṭirupalabhyamānāvāntareśvarakāryā prāgutpatterātmaikatvāvadhāraṇaṃ cāvāntareśvarasaṃbandhitayā gamayati /
pārameśvarasargasya mahābhūtākāśāditvādasya ca tadvaiparītyāt /
asti hi tasyaivaikasya vikārāntarāpekṣayāgnatvamasti cekṣaṇam /
api caitasminnaitareyake pūrvasminprakaraṇe prajāpatikartṛkaiva lokasṛṣṭiruktā /
tadanusārādapyetadeva vijñāyate /
apica tābhyo gāmānayadityādayaśca vyavahāraḥ śrutyoktā viśeṣavatsvātmaparamātmaṣu prasiddhāḥ /
tato 'pyavāntareśvara eva vijñāyate /
ātmaśabdaprayogaścātrāpi dṛṣṭastasmādaparātmābhilāpo 'yamiti prāpta ucyati-paramātmano gṛhītiriha yathā itareṣu sṛṣṭiśravaṇeṣu 'etasmādātmana ākāśaḥ saṃbhūtaḥ' ityādiṣu /
tasmāduttarātsa aikṣatetīkṣaṇapūrvakasraṣṭṛtvaśravaṇādātmetyavadhāraṇācca /
etadabhisaṃhitam-mukhyaṃ tāvat sargātprākkevalatvamātmapadatvaṃ sraṣṭṛtvaṃ ca parameśvarasyātra bhavataḥ /
tadasatyāmanupapattau nānyatra vyākhyātumucitam /
naca mahābhūtasṛṣṭyanabhidhānena lokasṛṣṭyabhidhānamanupapattibījam /
ākāśapūrvikāyāṃ vastuto brahmaṇaḥ sṛṣṭau yathā kkacittejaḥpūrvakasṛṣṭyabhidhānaṃ na virudhyate 'etasmādātmana ākāśaḥ saṃbhūtaḥ' iti darśanāt /
ākāśaṃ vāyuṃ sṛṣṭveti hi tatra pūrayitavyamevahāpi mahābhūtāni sṛṣṭveti kalpanīyam /
sarvaśākhāpratyayatvena jñānasya śrutisidvyarthamaśrutopalabdhau yatnavatā bhavitavyaṃ na punaḥ śrute mahābhūtāditve sargasya śaithilyamādaraṇīyam /
apica svādhyāyavidhyadhīnagrahaṇo vedarāśiradhyayanavidhyāpāditaprayojanavadarthamabhidadhāno yathā yathā prayojanādhikyamāpnoti tathā tathānumanyatetarām /
yathā cāsya brahmagocaratve paramapuruṣārthaupayikatvaṃ naivamanyagocaratve /
tadidamuktam- #yo 'pyayaṃ vyāpāraviśeṣānugama iti# /
naca lokasargo 'pi hiraṇyagarbhavyāpāro 'pi tu tadanupraviṣṭasya paramātmana ityatraivoktam /
body.translated_text:
Therefore, from the opening — '<s>Ātman</s> alone was this, as fire' (<s>ātmaivāgra</s>) — and from the reference in the middle to His activity, namely seeing (<s>īkṣaṇa</s>); and from the conclusion above, where the entire assemblage of differentiation is traced back together with the great elements to <s>Brahman</s> as its ground — the discourse's being about <s>Brahman</s> alone is ascertained.
Where there is mention of the form of <s>Puruṣa</s> and the like, that [passage] would have a different purport, since there is no other interpretive possibility — thus everything is clear.
Another interpretation:
The question is whether the passage beginning with <s>sat</s> (Being) [in the <s>Chāndogya</s>] and the passage beginning with <s>Ātman</s> [in the <s>Aitareya</s>] have the same meaning or different meanings.
Therein, since the word '<s>sat</s>' (Being) applies without distinction to both <s>Ātman</s> and non-<s>Ātman</s>, it does not mean '<s>Ātman</s>' but rather means the universal of existence (<s>sattā-sāmānya</s>) that pervades all things; and thus, because of the difference of opening [terms], [the two passages] have different meanings.
And the concluding statement '<s>sa ātmā tat tvam asi</s>' (That is the <s>Ātman</s>; thou art That) should be interpreted as a meditation-identification (<s>saṃpatti</s>) in accordance with the opening — [meaning] that universal of Being (<s>sat-sāmānya</s>) is to be identified with <s>Paramātman</s> as a meditative exercise;
and the 'knowledge of everything' [promised as the result] through knowledge of that [<s>sat</s>] is [explained by] the fact that the universal of existence (<s>sattā</s>), being a great universal, pervades the entire expanse of things — having established this prima facie view, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says:
The apprehension of <s>Ātman</s> by the <s>Chāndogya</s> [followers] too — just as by the <s>Vājasaneyin</s>s — [is established] from what follows: '<s>sa ātmā tat tvam asi</s>' (That is the <s>Ātman</s>; thou art That), the teaching of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>).
Granted that the phenomenal world (<s>prapañca</s>), which is other than <s>Ātman</s>, being inexpressible (<s>anirvacanīya</s>) as either being or non-being, is not [truly] existent; but existence (<s>sattva</s>) [belongs] to the root <s>Ātman</s> alone, since it alone is genuinely expressible (<s>nirvacanīya</s>) — therefore, '<s>Ātman</s> alone is <s>sat</s> (Being)' — thus.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states this while accepting [the opponent's premise].
Given the doubt — arising from the word '<s>sat</s>' denoting the universal of existence and from its application to each individual [thing] as well as to both <s>Ātman</s> and non-<s>Ātman</s> — the word '<s>sat</s>' is fixed upon <s>Ātman</s> alone in accordance with the concluding statement.
For the description of the conclusion should be in accordance with the opening whose meaning is settled, not [the other way, where] the conclusion [is used to describe an opening] whose meaning is doubtful.
Moreover, in [the case of] meditation-identification (<s>saṃpatti</s>), a fruit must be postulated,

children.translated_text: Thus, the ascertainment [of <s>Ātman</s> as the referent of '<s>sat</s>'] and all the rest would be untenable if [the passage] were not about <s>Ātman</s> — therefore, the <s>Chāndogya</s> [passage] too is about <s>Ātman</s> alone — this is established.
And here, in the prima facie view, the meditation on <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> [is implied]; in the established conclusion, however, [it is] the contemplation of <s>Brahman</s>. //16//

children.text: atra ca pūrvasmin pūrvapakṣe hiraṇyagarbhopāsanā siddhānte tu brahmabhāvaneti //16 //

body.translated_text: and the knowledge of a mere universal does not yield the knowledge of particulars.

'#The <s>kārya</s> (effect) — [it is] unprecedented (<s>apūrva</s>), because of the statement of its [nature as] effect#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the subject matter: '#The <s>Chāndogya</s> [followers] and the <s>Vājasaneyin</s>s#' — thus.
<s>Ana</s> (breathing) is <s>prāṇana</s> (vital breathing); <s>anaḥ</s> is <s>prāṇa</s> (the vital breath); making that <s>prāṇa</s> 'un-fired' (<s>anagna</s>) —
'#The contemplation of un-firedness (<s>anagnatā-cintana</s>)#' — thus.
Meditation (<s>manana</s>) is thinking, which means knowledge — and it has been stated that this [contemplation] extends up to <s>vyāna</s> (the diffusive breath).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the doubt: '#Is that...#' — thus.
Having grasped at first glance the position [that allows] both [interpretations], the prima facie advocate takes up the middle position: '#Or rather, it is the eating alone#' — thus.
If this is so, what is the purpose of the mention of <s>anagnatā</s> (un-firedness)? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#But that is for the purpose of praise (<s>stuti</s>) alone#' — thus.

yadyevamanagnatāsaṃkīrtanasya kiṃ prayojanamityata āha- #tasyaiva tu stutyarthamiti# /

ayamabhisandhiḥ-yadyapi smārtaṃ prāyatyārthamācamanamasti tathāpi prāṇopāsanaprakaraṇe 'vidhānāttadaṅgatvenāprāptamiti vidhānamarthavadbhavati, anṛtavadanapratiṣedha iva smārte jyotiṣṭomaprakaraṇe samāmnāto nānṛtaṃ vadediti pratiṣedho jyotiṣṭomāṅgatayārthavāniti /

children.translated_text: But actual consumption must be supplied [by implication], merely through some kind of fitness — this is the distinction.

children.text: kiñca chāndogyānāṃ vājasaneyināṃ cācamane prāyeṇācāmantīti vartamānāpadeśaḥ evaṃ yatrāpi vidhivibhaktistatrāpi jartilayavāgvavā vā juhuyāditivadvidhitvamavivakṣitam /
children.translated_text: Moreover, in the <s>ācamana</s> of the <s>Chāndogya</s> and <s>Vājasaneyin</s> [schools], 'they sip' — the present tense indicates [an already established practice]. Similarly, wherever the injunctive verbal suffix occurs, the injunctive force is not intended — like 'one should offer with barley gruel or [other offerings].'

[If they say:] 'they think' [shows it is already obtained] — but because of its having an unobtained meaning, it is an injunction, like 'he sacrifices with fuel-sticks' — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Moreover, they sip#.'
The rest has transparent meaning. //18//

body.translated_text:
The intention is this: although the <s>ācamana</s> (ritual sipping) based on <s>Smṛti</s> exists for the purpose of expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>), nevertheless, since it is not enjoined [specifically] in the context of <s>Prāṇopāsanā</s> (meditation on <s>Prāṇa</s>), and since it has not been obtained as a subsidiary thereof, the injunction is meaningful — just as the prohibition of speaking untruth, recited in the <s>Smṛti</s> context of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, 'one should not speak untruth,' is meaningful as a subsidiary of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the established view: '#With this prima facie view established#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] objects: '#But this <s>Śruti</s>#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] resolves: '#No#.'
The meaning is: the relationship of root and derivative (<s>mūla-mūlibhāva</s>) exists between those of equal purport, not between those of unequal purport.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] removes the seed of the prima facie view that was implicit: '#And this <s>Śruti</s> is not#.'
In the case of the two prohibitions against speaking untruth — one for the sake of the sacrifice and one for the person's sake — the absence of redundancy is reasonable.
But here, since <s>ācamana</s> based on <s>Smṛti</s> is enjoined as a subsidiary of all rituals generally, and since [the <s>Prāṇopāsanā</s>-related <s>ācamana</s>] is also a subsidiary of <s>Prāṇopāsanā</s>, it would be redundant with the all-encompassing <s>Smṛti</s>-based <s>ācamana</s> injunction, and hence purposeless.
Nor is there redundancy of the <s>Smṛti</s>-based [injunction] with this [<s>Śruti</s>-based one], because the former is all-encompassing and the latter has a specifically restricted scope.
Having set aside the middle view, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] sets aside the first view: '#For this very reason, there is not a dual injunction#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states another reasoning: '#And if there were a dual injunction#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] concludes: '#Therefore, it is already obtained#.'
'#And this is not a statement about non-fire-contact (<s>anagnatāvāda</s>)#.'
The meaning is: in the absence of something to be praised, praise is untenable.
Moreover, what is to be enjoined, being unobtained, would be praised by what is obtained through another means of knowledge.
But the intention of non-fire-contact (<s>anagnatā-saṃkalpa</s>) is not obtained from elsewhere so as to be the object of praise.
Nor is <s>ācamana</s> unobtained from elsewhere, so that, being something to be enjoined, it would be praised — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#And the intention of non-fire-contact itself#.'
Moreover, it is fitting that a single <s>karma</s> has a single purpose; multiple purposes are postulated for it only when, by the force of a stronger means of knowledge, it cannot be assigned elsewhere.
But when the intention (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) is enjoined as a different <s>karma</s>, this defect does not arise — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#And when this is so, of the one <s>ācamana</s>#.'
Moreover, because of the association with the injunction of contemplation (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>), what is appropriately [enjoined here] is the injunction of contemplation alone, not the injunction of <s>ācamana</s> — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Moreover, whatever this is#.'
For just as, since food that is limited to [the level of] dogs and the like cannot be actually eaten, the contemplation of food is enjoined — so here too, since the actual 'wearing' of water is impossible, contemplation alone is enjoined — this is understood from the association with the injunction of food-contemplation.
And although the absence of direct scriptural expression is equal for both contemplation and actual consumption, nevertheless, contemplation is directly apprehended as being produced by scripture, through being inseparable from what is indicated by scripture.

children.translated_text: Nor is the mention of qualities enjoined in one [version] purposeless in the other, because it serves the purpose of strengthening recognition.
Or, let it be a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) regarding this — for restatements need not necessarily have a purpose in every case.
Because mere restatement too is observed here and there.
Therefore, it is that very same meditation in the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> too — because of the incorporation of those qualities — this is established. //19//

body.translated_text:
3.3.10.19.
'#The same [meditation], thus, because of non-difference#.'
Here the prima facie view follows the principle of the repetition (<s>abhyāsa</s>) <s>adhikaraṇa</s>.
Since no distinction can be apprehended between the two <s>vidyā</s>-injunctions belonging to a single <s>śākhā</s>, and since there is no ascertainment of which is the restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) of which, and since the injunctive character — making known the unknown and instigating the uninitiated — is naturally established in both, there is a difference of meditations in both.
Nor is it [the case that] one is a restatement for the purpose of enjoining additional qualities — because the enjoining of additional qualities is observed in both, and because there is no reason for determination [of one over the other], and because there would be the unwanted consequence of not stating qualities that are common.
Therefore, as in [the principle of] 'he sacrifices with fuel-sticks' and the like, from the repetition, there is a difference of meditations — with this prima facie view established, the reply is given: there is identity of action, because of recognition of identity.
Nor is there a non-apprehension of distinction.
The injunction of the <s>karma</s> [belongs] where the greater number of qualities are enjoined; in the other [version], there is the enjoining of a few qualities through the restatement of that [karma].
Just as where there is a retinue of umbrella, flywhisk, banner, elephants, horses, spearmen, club-bearers, bow-bearers, sword-bearers, javelin-bearers, and foot-soldiers, there [one understands] 'this is the king' — but not where there are merely a few elephants, horses, and foot-soldiers — [there one understands it is] a minister of that [king]; so here too.

children.translated_text: If, even within a single <s>śākhā</s>, there is a mixing of the qualities enjoined there with the meditation — through the genuine recognition [of identity],

then, since the single '<s>Satya</s>' (the Real) is non-different [from itself] though present in the two orbs [of the sun and the eye], there would be the unwanted consequence of mixing even the two <s>Upaniṣad</s> [passages].
And 'of that' (<s>tasya</s>), being a reference to the contextually present [subject], [indicates] difference.

children.text: satyasya ca pradhānasya prakṛtatvādadhidaivamityasya viśeṣaṇatayopasarjanatvenāprastutvātprastutasya ca satyasyābhedātpūrvavadguṇasaṃkaraḥ //20 //

body.translated_text: '#Because of the connection, the same [applies] elsewhere too#.'

children.translated_text: For when one says 'bring the man with the staff,' a man without a staff but carrying a water-pot is not brought.

Therefore, the <s>Upaniṣad</s> teaching about '<s>Satya</s>' in its cosmic (<s>adhidaiva</s>) aspect cannot be the same as [the teaching about] that very [<s>Satya</s>] in its individual (<s>ādhyātma</s>) aspect.

children.text: yathā cācāryasya gacchato 'nugamanaṃ vihitaṃ na tiṣṭhato bhavati, tasmānnopaniṣadoḥ saṃkaraḥ kintu vyavasthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the injunction to follow the teacher when he is going does not apply when he is standing still — therefore, there is no mixing of the two <s>Upaniṣad</s> [passages], but rather a distinct arrangement.
This is what was stated: 'Because of the non-departure of the essential nature.' //21//

body.translated_text:
With this prima facie view established, the reply is given: '#Or not, because of a distinction#.'
True, where the connection of qualities is heard with the essential nature alone, there — since the essential nature is recognized [as the same], and since the qualities are connected with that alone.
But where the principal [subject] is understood together with a qualifier, there the connection of qualities is with that [subject] together with its qualifier, not with [the subject] without the qualifier, nor with [the subject] accompanied by a different qualifier.

children.translated_text: '#And [the <s>Śruti</s>] shows [this]#.'
From the extension (<s>atideśa</s>) too, it is exactly so — for if they were identical in reality, there would be no extension. //22//
