yā tu kācidādhidaivikī vibhūtiḥ śāṇḍilyādividyāyaṃ śrūyate tasmāstatprakaraṇādhīnatvāttāvanmātraṃ grahīṣyate naitāvanmātreṇa saṃbhṛtyādīnanukraṣṭumarhati /
tatraitatpratyabhijñānābhāvādityuktam /

children.translated_text: But the recognition [proposed] through the commonality of having <s>Brahman</s> as substrate would be over-extended.
Because there would be the unwanted consequence of the unity of a greater number [of <s>vidyā</s>s].
This is what was stated: '#<s>Saṃbhṛti</s> and the rest, however, are within the scope of the <s>Śāṇḍilya</s> and the like passages#.'

children.text: tasmātsaṃbhṛtiśca dyuvyāptiśca tadidaṃ saṃbhṛtidyuvyāptyapi cātaḥ pratyabhijñānābhāvānna śāṇḍilyādividyāsūpasaṃhriyata iti siddham //23 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>saṃbhṛti</s> and <s>dyuvyāpti</s> — this is '<s>saṃbhṛtidyuvyāpti</s> and also because of this' — because of the absence of recognition [of identity], they are not incorporated in the <s>Śāṇḍilya</s> and the like <s>vidyā</s>s — this is established. //23//

body.translated_text:
'<s>Saṃbhṛti</s> (plenitude) and <s>dyuvyāpti</s> (pervasion of heaven) — and also because of this.'
'The powers whose eldest is <s>Brahman</s> were gathered together; <s>Brahman</s>, O <s>Agni</s>, being the eldest, extended to heaven;
<s>Brahman</s> was born first among beings — who then is fit to compete with that <s>Brahman</s>?'
'Those whose eldest is <s>Brahman</s>' — those that were born [with <s>Brahman</s> as eldest].
Although in the various <s>vidyā</s>s such as <s>Śāṇḍilya</s> and the like, through the acceptance of the difference of abodes (<s>āyatana</s>), the individual (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) abode-nature of the qualities such as <s>saṃbhṛti</s> and the like, and the cosmic (<s>ādhidaivika</s>) nature — and thus the difference of abodes is apparent — nevertheless, since through the passage 'greater than heaven' and the like, the cosmic glory is recognized; and since in the <s>vidyā</s>s of the sixteen parts (<s>ṣoḍaśakala</s>) and the like no abode is heard; and since ultimately, through the commonality of having <s>Brahman</s> as their substrate, recognition [of identity] is possible — therefore the qualities such as <s>saṃbhṛti</s> and the like should be incorporated in the <s>Śāṇḍilya</s> and the like <s>vidyā</s>s and the <s>ṣoḍaśakala</s> and the like <s>vidyā</s>s — this is the prima facie view.
But the established view is: through hearing qualities common to each other, when one <s>vidyā</s> recognizes [identity and] incorporates even novel qualities not heard there — that [process applies]. But here, in the <s>Brahmavidyā</s> that has qualities such as <s>saṃbhṛti</s>, no hearing of qualities belonging to <s>Śāṇḍilya</s> and the like <s>vidyā</s>s exists.
And whatever cosmic glory is heard in the <s>Śāṇḍilya</s> and the like <s>vidyā</s>, since it is dependent on that context, only that much will be accepted — it should not thereby drag in <s>saṃbhṛti</s> and the like.
The reason given there is: because of the absence of recognition [of identity].

body.text:
#puruṣavidyāyamitra cetareṣāmanāmnānāt# /
puruṣayajñatvamubhayatrāpyaviśiṣṭam /
naca viduṣo yajñasyeti na sāmānādhikaraṇyasaṃbhavaḥ /
yajñasyātmetyātmaśabdasya svarūpavacanatvāt /
yajñasya svarūpaṃ yajamānastasya ca cetanatvādviduṣa iti sāmānādhikaraṇyasaṃbhavaḥ /
tasmātpuruṣayajñatvāviśeṣānmaraṇāvabhṛthatvādisāmānyāccaikavidyādhyavasāne ubhayatra ubhayadharmopasaṃhāra iti prāptam /
evaṃ prāpta ucyate yādṛśaṃ tāṇḍināṃ paiṅgināṃ ca puruṣayajñasaṃpādanaṃ tadāyuṣaśca tredhā vyavasthitasya savanatrayasaṃpādanam /
aśiśiṣādīnāṃ ca dīkṣādibhāvasaṃpādanaṃ naivaṃ taittirīyāṇām /
teṣāṃ na tāvat puruṣe yajñasaṃpattiḥ /
nahyātmā yajamāna ityatrāyamātmaśabdaḥ svarūpavacanaḥ /
nahi yajñasvarūpaṃ yajamāno bhavati /
kartṛkarmaṇorabhedābhāvāt /
cetanācetanayoścaikyānupapatteḥ yajñakarmaṇoścācetanatvāt /
yajamānasya cetanatvāt /
ātmanastu cetanasya yajamānatvaṃ ca vidvattvaṃ copapadyate /
tathā cāyamarthaḥ-evaṃ viduṣaḥ puruṣasya yaḥ saṃbandhī yajñaḥ tasya saṃbandhitayā yajamāna ātmā tathā cātmano yajamānatvaṃ ca vidvatsaṃbandhitā ca yajñasya mukhye syātāmitarachātmaśabdasya svarūpavācitve viduṣo yajñasyeti ca yajamāno yajñasvarūpamiti ca gauṇe syātām /
naca satyāṃ gatau tadyuktam /
tasmātpuruṣayajñatā taittirīye nāstīti tayā tāvanna sāmyam /
naca patnīyajamānavedavidyādisaṃpādanaṃ taittirīyāṇāmivi tāṇḍināṃ paiṅgināṃ vā vidyate savanasaṃpattirapyeṣāṃ vilakṣaṇaiva /
tasmādbhūyo vailakṣaṇye sati na kiñcinmātrasālakṣaṇyādvidyaikatvamucitamatiprasaṅgāt /
apica tasyaivaṃ viduṣa ityanuvādaśrutau satyāmanekārthavidhāne vākyabhedadoṣaprasaktirityarthaḥ /

children.text: api ceyaṃ paiṅgināṃ tāṇḍināṃ ca puruṣayajñavidyāphalāntarayuktā svatantrā pratīyate /
children.translated_text: Moreover, this <s>Puruṣayajña</s> <s>vidyā</s> of the <s>Paiṅgin</s>s and <s>Tāṇḍin</s>s, having a distinct result, is understood as independent.

But for the <s>Taittirīya</s>s, because of the hearing of 'of one who knows thus,' because of the reference to what was previously stated, and because of the <s>Śruti</s> declaring the result as belonging to that [previously stated ritual], there is subordination.

And the unity of an independent and a subordinate [<s>vidyā</s>] is not appropriate — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Moreover, the <s>ātmavidyā</s> (knowledge of the Self) together with renunciation (<s>saṃnyāsa</s>)#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] concludes: '#Therefore#.' //24//

body.translated_text:
'#In the <s>Puruṣavidyā</s> (knowledge of the cosmic person), on the other hand, because of the non-mention of the others#.'
The character of being a sacrifice-of-the-person (<s>puruṣayajña</s>) is common to both [versions].
Nor [can it be argued] that because [the text says] 'of the sacrifice of the knower,' co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) is impossible.
Because the word '<s>ātman</s>' in 'the self of the sacrifice' has the sense of 'essential nature.'
The essential nature of the sacrifice is the sacrificer (<s>yajamāna</s>), and because of his being sentient, [co-reference with] 'of the knower' is possible.
Therefore, because of the non-distinction of the <s>puruṣayajña</s> character, and because of the commonality of having death as the <s>avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath) and the like, when the oneness of the <s>vidyā</s> is decided, the incorporation of the qualities of both [versions] in both should occur — thus is the prima facie view.
With this prima facie view established, the reply is given: the manner in which the <s>Tāṇḍin</s>s and the <s>Paiṅgin</s>s accomplish the identification of the person with the sacrifice — and the identification of the three divisions of life-span with the three <s>savana</s>s (pressings),
and the identification of hunger and the like with <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) and the like — this is not the case for the <s>Taittirīya</s>s.
For them, there is no identification of the sacrifice with the person.
For the word '<s>ātman</s>' in 'the self is indeed the sacrificer' is not here used in the sense of 'essential nature.'
For the sacrificer is not the essential nature of the sacrifice,
because there is no identity of agent and action,
and because the identity of the sentient and the non-sentient is untenable — since the sacrificial action is non-sentient,
while the sacrificer is sentient.
But of the self (<s>ātman</s>), which is sentient, both sacrificer-hood and knower-hood are tenable.
And thus the meaning is: the sacrifice that belongs to the person who knows thus — its sacrificer is the self by way of that connection. And thus, the self's sacrificer-hood and the sacrifice's connection with the knower would be in the primary sense. But if the word '<s>ātman</s>' were used in the sense of 'essential nature,' then 'of the sacrifice of the knower' and 'the sacrificer is the essential nature of the sacrifice' would be in a secondary sense.
And when a primary meaning is available, a secondary meaning is not appropriate.
Therefore, since the <s>puruṣayajña</s> identification does not exist in the <s>Taittirīya</s>, there is no commonality on that basis.
Nor do the <s>Tāṇḍin</s>s or <s>Paiṅgin</s>s have the identification of wife, sacrificer, <s>Veda</s>, <s>vidyā</s>, and the like [in the same manner] as the <s>Taittirīya</s>s; the <s>savana</s>-identification too is of a different character for them.
Therefore, when there is greater dissimilarity, it is not appropriate to determine the oneness of the <s>vidyā</s> from a slight similarity — because of over-extension.
Moreover, when the <s>Śruti</s> 'of one who knows thus' is a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>), if multiple purposes were enjoined [for a single action], there would be the defect of splitting the sentence — this is the meaning.

body.text:
#vedhādyarthabhedāt# /
vicāraviṣayaṃ darśayati- #ātharvaṇikānāmiti# /
ātharvaṇikādyupaniṣadārambhe te te mantrāstāni tāni ca pravargyādīti karmāṇi samamnātīni /
saṃśayamāha- #kimima iti# /
pūrvapakṣaṃ gṛhṇāti- #upasaṃhāra evaiṣāṃ vidyāsviti# /
saphalā hi sarvā vidyā āmnātāstatsannidhau mantrāḥ /
karmāṇi ca samāmnātāni 'phalavatsannidhāphalaṃ tadaṅgam' iti nyāyādvidyāṅgābhāvena vijñāyante /
codayati- #nanveṣāmiti# /
nahyatra śrutiliṅgavākyaprakaraṇasthānasamākhyānāni santi viniyojakāni pramāṇāni, nahi yathā darśapūrṇamāsāvārabhya samidādayaḥ samāmrātāstathā kāñcidvidyāmārabhya mantrā vā karmāṇi vā samāmrātāni /

children.translated_text: And in the absence of a general connection, the mere proximity of a related [element] does not establish the possibility of serving its purpose.

children.text: naca śrutasvāṅgaparipūrṇā vidyā etānākāṅkṣitumarhati yena prakaraṇāpaditasāmānyasaṃbandhānāṃ saṃnidhirviśeṣasaṃbandhāyā bhavedityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Nor does the <s>vidyā</s>, being complete in its own subsidiaries as heard [in the text], have the need to expect these [mantras and rituals], such that their proximity — which has obtained only a general connection from the context — could serve to establish a specific connection — this is the meaning.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] resolves: '#Indeed, even though not being apprehended#' — thus.
Let there indeed be no expectation on the part of the <s>vidyā</s>s, which are fruitful and complete in their subsidiaries.

body.translated_text:
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] shows the subject of inquiry by the words '#because of the difference of purpose such as piercing and the like#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] shows the subject of inquiry: '#Regarding the <s>Ātharvaṇika</s>s#' — thus.
At the commencement of the <s>Ātharvaṇika</s> and other <s>Upaniṣad</s>s, various mantras and various rituals such as the <s>Pravargya</s> and the like are recited.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the doubt: '#Whether these#' — thus.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] takes up the prima facie view: '#These are to be subsumed under the <s>vidyā</s>s#' — thus.
For all the <s>vidyā</s>s that are recited are fruitful, and the mantras are in proximity to them.
And the rituals too are recited [there], and by the principle 'what is fruitless in proximity to what is fruitful is a subsidiary of that,' they are understood as subsidiaries of the <s>vidyā</s>s.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises an objection: '#But of these#' — thus.
For here, the valid means of assignment — <s>Śruti</s> (direct statement), <s>liṅga</s> (indicative mark), <s>vākya</s> (sentence), <s>prakaraṇa</s> (context), <s>sthāna</s> (position), and <s>samākhyāna</s> (designation) — are not present. For it is not the case that, just as — beginning with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new and full moon) sacrifice — the fuel-sticks (<s>samidh</s>) and the like are recited [as subsidiaries], so too — beginning with some <s>vidyā</s> — mantras or rituals are recited.

body.text:
mantrāṇāṃ tu svādhyāyavidhyāpāditapuruṣārthabhāvanāṃ karmaṇāṃ ca pravargyādīnāṃ svavidhyāpāditapuruṣārthabhāvānāṃ puruṣābhilaṣitamākāṅkṣatāṃ saṃnidhānādanyatārākāṅkṣānibandho raktapaṭanyāyena saṃbandhaḥ /
tatrāpi ca vidyānāṃ phalavattvāttādarthyamaphalānāṃ mantrāṇāṃ karmaṇāṃ ca /
naca pravargyādīnāṃ piṇḍapitṛyajñavatsvargaḥ kalpanāspadaṃ, phalavatsaṃnidhānena tadavarohāt /
#anumāsyāmahe saṃnidhisāmārthyāditi# /
idaṃ khalu nivṛttākāṅkṣāyā vidyāyāḥ saṃnidhāne śrutamanākāṅkṣāyā sākāṅkṣasyāpi saṃbaddhumasāmarthyāttasyā apyākāhkṣāmutthāpayati /
utthāpya caikavākyatāmupaiti /
asamarthasya copakārakatvānupapatteḥ prakaraṇinaṃ prati upakārasāmarthyamātmanaḥ kalpayati /
naca satyapi sāmarthye tatra śrutyā aviniyuktaṃ sadaṅgatāmupagantumarhatītyanayā paramparayā saṃnidhiḥ śrutimarthāpattyā kalpayati /
ākṣipati- #nanu naiṣāṃ mantrāṇāmiti# /
prayogasamavetārthaprakāśanena hi mantrāṇāmupayogo varṇitaḥ 'aviśiṣṭastu vākyārthaḥ' ityatra /
naca vidyāsaṃbaddhaṃ kañcanārthaṃ mantreṣu pratīmaḥ /
yadyapi ca pravargyo na kiñcidārabhya śrūyate tathāpi vākyasaṃyogena kratusaṃyogena kratusaṃbandhaṃ pratipadyate /
'purastādupasadāṃ pravargyeṇa pracaranti' iti /
upasadāṃ juhūvadavyabhicaritakratusaṃbandhatvāt /
yadyapi jyotiṣṭomavikṛtāvapi santyupasadastathāpi tatrānumānikyo jyotiṣṭome tu pratyakṣavihitāstena śīghrapravṛttitayā jyotiṣṭomāṅgataiva vākyenāvagamyate /
apica prakṛtau vihitasya pravargyasya codakenopasadvattadvikṛtāvapi prāptiḥ /
prakṛtau vā adviruktatvāditi nyāyājjyotiṣṭome eva vidhānamupasadā saha yuktaṃ, tadetadāha- #kathaṃ ca pravargyāditi# /
saṃnidhānādarthaviprakarṣeṇa vākyaṃ balīya iti bhāvaḥ /
samādhatte- #naiṣa doṣaḥ /
sāmarthye tāvaditi# /
yathā 'agnaye tvā juṣṭaṃ nirvapāmi' iti mantre agnaye nirvapāmiti pade karmasamavetārthaprakāśake /
śiṣṭānāṃ tu padānāṃ tadekavākyatayā yathākathañcidvyākhyānamevamihāpi hṛdayapadasyopāsanāyāṃ samavetārthatvāttadanusāreṇa tadekavākyatāpannāpi padāntarāṇi gauṇyā lakṣaṇayā ca vṛttyā kathañcinneyānīti nāsamavetārthatā mantrāṇām /
naca mantraviniyogo nopāsaneṣu dṛṣṭo yenātyantādṛṣṭaṃ kalpyata ityāha- #dṛṣṭaścopāsaneṣviti# /
yadyapi vākyena balīyasā saṃnidhirdurbalo bādhyate tathāpi virodhe sati /
na cohāsti virodhaḥ /
vākyena viniyuktasyāpi jyotiṣṭome pravargyasya saṃnidhinā vidyāyāmapi viniyogasaṃbhavāt /
yathā 'brahmavarcasakāmo bṛhaspatisavena yajeta' iti brahmavarcasaphalo 'pi bṛhaspatisavo vājapeyāṅgatvena codyate-vājapeyeneṣṭvā bṛhaspatisavena yajeteti /
atra hi ktvaḥ samānakartṛkatvamavagamyate dhātusaṃbandhe pratyayavidhānāt /
dhātvarthāntarasaṃbandhaśca kathaṃ ca samānaḥ kartā syāt /
yadyakaḥ prayogo bhavet /
prayogāviṣṭaṃ hi kartṛtvam /
tacca prayogabhede kathamekam /
tasmātsamānakartṛkatvādekaprayogatvaṃ vājapeyabṛhaspatisavayordhātvarthāntarasaṃbandhācca /
naca guṇapradhānabhāvamantareṇaikaprayogatā saṃbandhaśca tatrāpi vājapeyasya prakaraṇe samāmnānādvājapeyaḥ pradhānam /
aṅgaṃ bṛhaspatisavaḥ /
naca 'darśapūrṇamāsābhyāmiṣṭvā somena yajeta' ityatrāṅgapradhānabhāvaprasaṅgaḥ /
nahyetadvacanaṃ kasyaciddarśapūrṇamāsamya somasya vā prakaraṇe samāmnātam /
tathāca dvayoḥ sādhikāratayā agṛhyamāṇaviśeṣatayā guṇapradhānabhāvaṃ prati vinigamanābhāvenādhiṣṭhānamātravivakṣayā lākṣaṇikaṃ samānakartṛkatvamityadoṣaḥ /
yadi tu kasyāñcicchākhyāyāmārabhyādhītaṃ darśapūrṇamāsābhyāmiṣṭveti /
tathāpyanārabhyādhītasyaivārabhyādhīte pratyabhijñānamiti yuktam /
tathā sati dvayorapi pṛthagadhikāratayā pratītaṃ samapradhānatvamatyaktaṃ bhaveditarathā tu guṇapradhānabhāvena tattyāgo bhavet /
tasmātkālārtho 'yaṃ saṃyoga iti siddham /
siddhāntamupakramate- #evaṃ prāpta iti# /
hṛdayaṃ pravidhyetyayaṃ mantraḥ svarasatastāvadābhicārikakarmasamavetaṃ sakalaireva padairarthamabhidadhadupalabhyate tadasyābhidhānasāmarthyalakṣaṇaṃ liṅgaṃ vākyaprakaraṇābhyāṃ kramādbalīyobhyāmapi balavatkimaṅga punaḥ kramāt, tasmālliṅgena saṃnidhimapodyābhicārikakarmaśeṣatvamevāpādyate /
yadyapi copāsanāsu hṛdayapadamātrasya samavetārthatvam /
tathāpi taditareṣāṃ sarveṣāmeva padānāmasamavetārthatvam /
ābhicārike tu karmaṇi sarveṣāmarthasamavāya iti kimekapadasamavetārthatā kariṣyati /
naca saṃnidhyupagṛhīyāsūpāsanāsu mantramavasthāpayatīti yuktam /
hṛdayapadasyābhicāre 'pi samavetārthasyetarapadaikavākyatāpannasya vākyapramāṇasahitasyābhicārikātkarmaṇaḥ saṃnidhinācālayitumaśakyatvādevaṃ 'deva savitaḥ prasuva yajñam' ityāderapi yajñaprasavaliṅgasya yajñaṅgatve siddhe jaghanyo vidyāsaṃnidhiḥ kiṃ kariṣyati /
evamanyeṣāmapi śvetāśva ityevamādīnāṃ keṣāñcilliṅgena keṣāñcicchutyā #keṣāñcitpramāṇāntareṇa#prakaraṇeneti /
kasmātpunaḥ saṃnidhirliṅgādibhirvādhyate ityata āha- #durbalo hi saṃnidhiriti# /
prathamatantragator'thaḥ smāryate /
tatra tu śrutiliṅgayoḥ samavāye samānaviṣayatvalakṣaṇe virodhe kiṃ balīya iti cintā /
atrodāharaṇam-astyaindrī ṛk 'kadācanastarīrasi nendra' ityādikā śrutirviniyokī 'aindrayā gārhapatyamupatiṣṭhate' iti /
atra hi sāmarthyalakṣaṇālliṅgādindre viniyogaḥ pratibhāti /
śruteśca gārhapatyamiti dvitīyāto gārhapatyasya śeṣitvaṃ aindriyeti catṛtīyāśruteraindyā ṛcaḥ śeṣatvamavagamyate /
yadyapi gārhapatyamiti dvitīyāśruterāgneyīmṛcaṃ prati gārhapatyasya śeṣitvenopapatteḥ /
yadyapi caindrayeti ca tṛtīyāśruteraindrayā indraṃ prati śeṣatvanopapatteravirodhaḥ /
padāntarasaṃbandhe tu vākyasyaiva liṅgena virodho na tu śruteḥ /
tatra ca viparītaṃ balābalam /
tathāpi śrutivākyayo rūpato vyāpārabhedādadoṣaḥ /
dvitīyātṛtīyāśrutī hi kārakavibhaktitayā kriyāṃ prati prakṛtyarthasya karmakaraṇabhāvamavagamayata iti viniyojike /
kriyāṃ prati hi karmaṇaḥ śeṣitvaṃ karaṇasya ca śeṣatvamiti hi viniyogaḥ /
padāntarānapekṣe ca kriyāṃ prati śeṣaśeṣitve śrutimātrātpratiyete iti śraute /
so 'yaṃ śrutitiḥ sāmānyāvagato viniyogaḥ padāntaravaśādviśeṣe 'vasthāpyate /
so 'yaṃ viśiṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvalakṣaṇaḥ saṃbandho vākyagocaraḥ, śeṣaśeṣibhāvastu śrautaḥ,
body.translated_text:
But the mantras — whose capacity to serve human purpose has been brought about by the injunction of self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>) — and the rituals such as the <s>Pravargya</s> and the like — whose capacity to serve human purpose has been brought about by their own injunctions — being desirous of what is desired by persons, their proximity [to the <s>vidyā</s>s] generates the expectation of one or the other, and the connection is by the principle of the dyed-cloth (<s>raktapaṭanyāya</s>).
And therein too, the <s>vidyā</s>s — being fruitful — are what the fruitless mantras and rituals serve.
Nor can it be postulated that the <s>Pravargya</s> and the like have heaven [as their fruit] like the <s>Piṇḍapitṛyajña</s> (ancestral offering), because [the <s>Pravargya</s>] descends from [its connection with] what is fruitful in proximity.
'#We shall infer from the capacity of proximity#' — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s> says].
This is indeed what happens: the proximity [of mantras and rituals] to a <s>vidyā</s> whose expectation has ceased — being itself without expectation and being incapable of connecting with something that is [also] without expectation — generates expectation even in that [<s>vidyā</s>].
Having generated [expectation], it enters into a single-sentence unity [with the <s>vidyā</s>].
And since what is incapable [of generating benefit independently] cannot serve as an auxiliary, it constructs for itself the capacity to be of service to the principal [element] in the context.
And since, even when there is capacity, what is not assigned [to a purpose] by <s>Śruti</s> cannot attain subsidiary status — [therefore] by this chain [of reasoning], proximity constructs a <s>Śruti</s> through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises an objection: '#But these mantras do not#' — thus.
For the utility of mantras has been described as illuminating the meaning connected with the ritual performance — in 'But the sentence-meaning is undifferentiated' — [that is, the mantras illuminate the meaning of the ritual action].
But we do not apprehend in the mantras any meaning connected with the <s>vidyā</s>.
Even though the <s>Pravargya</s> is not heard [as commencing] any [new rite], nevertheless, through syntactic connection, it attains a connection with the sacrifice.
'After the <s>Upasad</s>s, they perform with the <s>Pravargya</s>' — thus.
Since the <s>Upasad</s>s have an unfailing connection with the sacrifice, [the <s>Pravargya</s> too is connected].
Even though the <s>Upasad</s>s exist in the modifications (<s>vikṛti</s>) of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> too, nevertheless there they are inferred, whereas in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> they are directly prescribed — hence, due to the swiftness of application [to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>], the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>-subsidiary-hood alone is understood from the sentence.
Moreover, the <s>Pravargya</s> — prescribed in the model sacrifice (<s>prakṛti</s>) — extends by the power of the injunction (<s>codana</s>) to the modifications [of that sacrifice] too, just as the <s>Upasad</s>s do.
Or, by the principle 'what is not mentioned [in the modification] is [to be taken from] the model sacrifice,' the prescription of the <s>Pravargya</s> together with the <s>Upasad</s>s in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> itself is appropriate — this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states: '#How then the <s>Pravargya</s> and the like#' — thus.
The intent is: a sentence, being stronger, overrides proximity by virtue of extending the meaning.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] resolves: '#This is not a defect. As for capacity, to begin with#' — thus.
Just as in the mantra 'I offer to you, <s>Agni</s>, what is pleasing' (<s>agnaye tvā juṣṭaṃ nirvapāmi</s>), the words 'to <s>Agni</s>' and 'I offer' illuminate the meaning connected with the ritual action.
But the remaining words, by virtue of forming a single sentence with those [words], are somehow explained.
Similarly here too, the word '<s>hṛdaya</s>' (heart), being connected with the meditation, — following its lead — even the other words, having entered into single-sentence unity with it, are to be interpreted somehow through figurative (<s>gauṇī</s>) and secondary (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) usage — hence the mantras are not devoid of connected meaning.
Nor is it the case that the assignment of mantras is not seen in meditations (<s>upāsanā</s>s), such that a completely unprecedented [practice] would need to be postulated — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#And assignment in meditations is observed#' — thus.
Even though a sentence, being stronger, overrides the weaker proximity — nevertheless, [this applies only] when there is a conflict.
But here there is no conflict.
For even the <s>Pravargya</s>, though assigned to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> by sentence, can also be assigned to the <s>vidyā</s> through proximity.
Just as the <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s> — 'One desiring spiritual radiance (<s>brahmavarcasa</s>) should sacrifice with the <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s>' — though having spiritual radiance as its fruit, is enjoined as a subsidiary of the <s>Vājapeya</s>: 'Having sacrificed with the <s>Vājapeya</s>, one should sacrifice with the <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s>.'
For here, the absolutive (<s>ktvā</s>) conveys same-agent-ness, since the suffix is prescribed in connection with the verbal root.
And the connection with a different verbal-root-meaning — how can the agent be the same?
[The agent can be the same] only if there is a single performance.
For agent-hood is [defined by] being engaged in a performance.
And how can that [agent-hood] be single when the performances differ?
Therefore, from the same-agent-ness, the single-performance-ness of the <s>Vājapeya</s> and <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s> [is established], and from the connection with a different verbal-root-meaning, [their relationship is established].
And without a principal-subsidiary relationship, single-performance-ness and connection are not possible — and therein too, the <s>Vājapeya</s>, being recited in the context, is the principal.
The <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s> is the subsidiary.
Nor does the objection arise that — in 'Having sacrificed with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, one should sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>' — there would be a principal-subsidiary relationship [between them].
For this statement is not recited in the context of either the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> or the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice].
And thus, since both [sacrifices] have equal ritual status, and since no specific distinction is apprehended, because of the absence of a basis for determining the principal-subsidiary relationship — the same-agent-ness is figurative, intended merely to convey temporal sequence [between the two].
But if it were read beginning with some <s>śākhā</s> as 'Having sacrificed with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>...' — even then, the recognition of [<s>Soma</s> as] equally independent, being a non-dependent reading, is appropriate.
When that is the case, the equal principal status of both — apprehended through [their] separate independence — would remain intact; otherwise, by a principal-subsidiary relationship, that [equal status] would be abandoned.
Therefore, this conjunction has temporal meaning — this is established.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] commences the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion): '#Having thus arrived at [the prima facie view]#' — thus.
This mantra — 'he pierces the heart' (<s>hṛdayaṃ pravidhyet</s>) — when taken at face value according to its natural meaning, is apprehended by all its words as expressing a meaning connected with an <s>ābhicārika</s> (sorcery) ritual — that [expressive] capacity, being its indicative mark (<s>liṅga</s>), [is] stronger than even sentence and context, which are successively stronger — how much more so than [mere proximity]! Therefore, by the indicative mark, proximity is overridden, and [the mantra's] subsidiary-hood to the sorcery ritual alone is established.
Even though the word '<s>hṛdaya</s>' (heart) alone has connected meaning in the meditations,
nevertheless, all the other words lack connected meaning [in that context].
But in the sorcery ritual, all words have connected meaning — so what will the single word with connected meaning accomplish?
Nor is it reasonable that proximity, having established [the mantra] in the meditations, fixes it there.
For the word '<s>hṛdaya</s>' — having connected meaning even in the sorcery ritual — when joined in a single sentence with the other words that are established [only] in the sorcery context, cannot be dislodged from the sorcery ritual by [mere] proximity, since it is supported by sentence-level authority.
Thus, just as 'O divine <s>Savitṛ</s>, impel the sacrifice' — [where] the indicative mark of impelling the sacrifice, establishing [the mantra's] subsidiary-hood to the sacrifice, is sufficient — what will the inferior proximity to the <s>vidyā</s> accomplish?
Likewise, regarding certain others — the '<s>śvetāśva</s>' (white horse) [mantras] and so on — some [are assigned] by indicative mark, some by <s>Śruti</s>, '#some by other means of valid knowledge#' — [namely] by context — thus.

body.text:
tasmādvākyalabhyaṃ viśiṣamapekṣya śrautaḥ śeṣaśeṣibhāvo liṅgena virudhyata iti śrutiliṅgavirodhe kiṃ liṅgānuguṇena gārhatvamiti dvitīyāśrutiḥ saptamyarthe vyākhyāyatāṃ gārhapatyasamīpe aindrayendra upastheya iti /
āho śrutyanuguṇatayā liṅgaṃ vyākhyayatām /
prabhavati hi svocitāyāṃ kriyāyāṃ gārhapatya itīndra indarteraiśvaryavacanatvāditi /
kiṃ tāvatprāptaṃ śruterliṅgaṃ balīya iti /
no khalu yatrāsamarthaṃ tacchutisahasreṇāpi tatra viniyoktuṃ śakyate /
yathā agninā siñcet pāthasā dahediti /
tasmātsāmarthyaṃ purodhāya śrutyā viniyoktavyam /
taccāsyā ṛcaḥ pramāṇāntarataḥ śabdataśca indre pratīyate /
tathāhi-viditapadatadarthaḥ kadācanetyṛcaḥ spaṣṭamindramavagacchati, śabdāccaindrayetyataḥ /
tasmāddārudahanasyeva dahanasya saliladahane viniyogo gārhapatye viniyoga aindrayāḥ /
naca śrutyanurodhājjaghanyāmāsthāyā vṛttiṃ sāmarthyakalpaneti sāmpratam /
samarthyasya pūrvabhāvitayā tadanurodhenaiva śrutivyavasthāpanāt /
tasmādaindrayendra eva gārhapatyasamīpa upasthātavya iti prāpte 'bhidhīyate-'liṅgajñānaṃ purodhāya na śrutervinayoktṛtā /
śrutijñānaṃ purodhāya liṅgaṃ tu viniyojakam' /
yadi hi sāmarthyamavagamya śruterviniyogamavadhārayetpramātā tataḥ śruterviniyogaṃ prati liṅgajñānāpekṣatvāddurbalatvaṃ bhavet /
na tvetadasti /
śrutirviniyogāya samarthyamapekṣate nāpekṣate sāmarthyavijñānam /
avagate tu tato viniyoge nāsamarthasya sa iti tannirvāhāya sāmarthyaṃ kalpyate /
tacchutiviniyogātpūrvamasti sāmarthyam /
na tu pūrvamagamyate /
viniyoge tu siddhe tadanyathānupapattyā paścātpratīyata iti śrutiviniyogātparācīnā sāmarthyapratītistadanurodhenāvasthāpanīyā /
liṅgaṃ tu na svato viniyojakamapi tu viniyokīṃ kalpyitvā śrutim /
tathāhi-na svarasato liṅgādanenendra upasthātavya iti pratīyate, kintvīdṛgindra iti tasya tu prakaraṇāmnānasāmartyāt sāmānyataḥ prakaraṇāpatitaidamarthyasya tadanyathānupapattyā viniyogakalpanāyāmapi śrautādviniyogātkalpanīyasya viniyogasyārthaviprakarṣācchutireva kalpayitumucitā na tu tadartho viniyogaḥ /
nahi śrutamanupapannaṃ śākyamarthenopapādayitum /
nahi trayo 'tra brahmaṇāḥ kaṭhakauṇḍinyāviti vākyaṃ pramāṇāntaropasthāpitena māṭhareṇopapādayanti, upapādayato vā nopahasanti /
śabdāḥ /
māṭharaśceti tu śrāvayantamanumanyante /
tasmācchutārthasamutthānānupapattiḥ śrutenaivārthāntareṇopapādanīyā, nārthāntaramātreṇa pramāṇāntaropanīteneti lokasiddham /
naca lokasiddhasya niyogānuyogau yujyete śabdārthajñānopāyabhūtalokavirodhāt /
tasmādviniyojikā śrutiḥ kalpanīyā /
tathāca yāvalliṅgādviniyojikāṃ śrutiṃ kalpayituṃ prakāntavyāpārastāvatpratyakṣayā śrutyā gārhapatye viniyogaḥ siddha iti nivṛttākāṅkṣaṃ prakaramamiti kasyānupapattyā liṅgaṃ viniyokīṃ śrutimupakalpyet /
mantrasamāmnānasya pratyakṣayaiva viniyogaśrutyopapāditatvāt /
yathāhuḥ-'yāvadajñātasaṃdigdhaṃ jñeyaṃ tātpramitsyate /
pramite tu pramātṛṇāṃ pramautsukyaṃ vihanyate' iti /
body.translated_text:
Therefore, with respect to the specific [meaning] obtained from the sentence, the Śrauta (directly scriptural) subsidiary-principal relation (<s>śeṣaśeṣibhāva</s>) is contradicted by the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>). Thus, in a conflict between <s>Śruti</s> and <s>liṅga</s> — should the second <s>Śruti</s> be interpreted in the locative sense, in conformity with the <s>liṅga</s>, as 'the <s>Aindrī</s> [<s>ṛc</s>] is to be addressed to <s>Indra</s> near the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [fire]'?
Or should the <s>liṅga</s> be interpreted in conformity with <s>Śruti</s>?
For '<s>Gārhapatya</s>' [can be explained as] <s>Indra</s>, who is capable of the appropriate action, from the root <s>indṛ</s> which denotes sovereignty.
What, then, is the prima facie conclusion? That the <s>liṅga</s> is stronger than <s>Śruti</s>.
Indeed, where [something] is incapable, even a thousand <s>Śruti</s>s cannot assign it there.
Just as 'one should sprinkle with fire, one should burn with water.'
Therefore, keeping capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>) in the forefront, the assignment should be made through <s>Śruti</s>.
And the capacity of this <s>ṛc</s> (verse) is cognized as pertaining to <s>Indra</s>, from another means of valid knowledge and from the word [itself].
Thus: one who knows the words and their meanings clearly understands <s>Indra</s> from the <s>ṛc</s> [beginning with] '<s>kadācana</s>' (sometimes), and from the word — because of '<s>Aindrī</s>' (belonging to <s>Indra</s>).
Therefore, just as the assignment of burning [ordinarily connected] with wood-fuel to water-[fuel would be absurd], so is the assignment of the <s>Aindrī</s> [<s>ṛc</s>] to the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [fire].
Nor is it correct [to say] that the postulation of capacity, by conformity with <s>Śruti</s>, adopts a secondary meaning — [this is] not appropriate.
Because capacity, being previously established, determines [the meaning of] <s>Śruti</s> in conformity with it.
Therefore — the <s>Aindrī</s> is to be addressed to <s>Indra</s> alone, near the <s>Gārhapatya</s> — this being the prima facie conclusion, it is stated: 'Keeping the knowledge of the indicatory mark in the forefront, <s>Śruti</s> does not have the function of assignment.
Keeping the knowledge of <s>Śruti</s> in the forefront, the indicatory mark is what assigns.'
For if the knower were to determine the assignment of <s>Śruti</s> [only] after ascertaining the capacity, then <s>Śruti</s> would be weak with respect to assignment, due to its dependence on the knowledge of the indicatory mark.
But this is not the case.
<s>Śruti</s> requires capacity for [the purpose of] assignment, but does not require the knowledge of capacity.
And when the assignment is [already] understood from <s>Śruti</s>, since what is incapable cannot [fulfill] that [assignment], capacity is postulated for the sake of carrying it out.
That capacity exists prior to the assignment by <s>Śruti</s>.
But it is not cognized prior [to the <s>Śruti</s>-assignment].
When the assignment is established, [capacity] is cognized afterwards because of the impossibility of [the assignment] being otherwise — thus the cognition of capacity, being subsequent to the assignment by <s>Śruti</s>, must be determined in conformity with that [<s>Śruti</s>-assignment].
But the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) does not assign of its own accord; rather, [it assigns only] by postulating a <s>Śruti</s> that assigns.
Thus: from the indicatory mark alone, 'this person should address [the <s>ṛc</s>] to <s>Indra</s>' — this is not naturally understood. Rather, [what is understood is merely] 'such is <s>Indra</s>.' But through the capacity of the mantra's being mentioned in the context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>), [and] through the impossibility of explaining otherwise the general relevance of what has fallen within the context — even when postulating the assignment from the indicatory mark, the assignment to be postulated [on the basis of the indicatory mark] is remote in [its] meaning, compared to the Śrauta assignment, and therefore <s>Śruti</s> alone is appropriate for postulation, not the assignment [based on the indicatory mark's] meaning.
For what is heard [directly in <s>Śruti</s>] cannot be established as inexplicable through [indirect] meaning.
For the sentence 'There are three <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s here — <s>Kaṭha</s> and <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>' — people do not explain it by [supplying] <s>Māṭhara</s> [as the third], who is brought in through another means of knowledge; or if one were to explain [it thus], people would not mock [the explanation].
Words [alone suffice].
But one who makes [others] hear 'And <s>Māṭhara</s>' — they accept.
Therefore, the impossibility of deriving the heard meaning must be resolved through another heard meaning, not through a mere [inferred] meaning brought in from another means of knowledge — this is established in common experience.
And it is not appropriate to challenge or question what is established in common experience, because that would contradict the common experience that is the basis for understanding word-meaning.
Therefore, a <s>Śruti</s> that assigns must be postulated.
And thus, for as long as the indicatory mark must labor to postulate an assigning <s>Śruti</s>, the assignment to the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [fire] is already accomplished by the directly perceived <s>Śruti</s> — and thus the expectation [for another assignment] has ceased and the context is completed — so on account of whose impossibility would the indicatory mark postulate an assigning <s>Śruti</s>?
Because the mantra's being mentioned [in context] has been explained by the directly perceived assigning <s>Śruti</s> itself.
As they say: 'As long as [something] is unknown or doubtful, the knowable is desired to be ascertained through a means of knowledge.
But when it is ascertained, the eagerness of the knowers for [further] ascertainment is arrested.'

body.text:
tasmātpratītaśrautaviniyogopapattyai mantrasya sāmarthye tadanuguṇatvena nīyamānaṃ prathamāṃ vṛttimajahajjaghanyayāpi neyamiti siddham /
liṅgavākyayoriha virodho yathā-'syonaṃ te sadanaṃ kṛṇomi ghṛtasya dhārayā suśeṣaṃ kalpyāmi /
tasminsīdāmṛte pratitiṣṭha vrīhīṇāṃ medha sumanasyamānaḥ' iti /
kimayaṃ kṛtsna eva mantraḥ sadanakaraṇe puroḍāśāsādane ca prayoktavya uta kalpyāmyanta upastaraṇe tasmintsīdetyevamādistu puroḍāśāsādana iti /
yadi vākyaṃ balīyaḥ kṛtsnau mantra ubhayatra, suśevaṃ kalpyāmītyetadapekṣo hi tasminsīdetyādiḥ pūrveṇaikavākyatāmupaiti yatkalpayāmi tasmintsīdeti /
atha liṅgaṃ balīyastataḥ kalpyāmyantaḥ sadanakaraṇe tatprakāśane hi tatsamartham /
tasmintsīdeti puroḍāśāsādane tatra hi tatsamarthamiti /
kiṃ tāvatprāptam /
liṅgādvākyaṃ balīya ityubhayatra kṛtsnasya viniyoga iti /
iha hi yattatpadasamabhivyāhāreṇa vibhajyamānasākāṅkṣatvādekavākyatāyāṃ siddhāyāṃ tadanurodhena paścāttadabhidhānasāmārthyaṃ kalpanīyam /
yathā devasyatvetimantre 'gnye nirvapāmīti padayoḥ samavetārthatvena tadekavākyatayā padāntarāṇāṃ tatparatvena tatra sāmarthyakalpanā /
tadevaṃ pratītaikavākyatānirvāhāya tadanuguṇatayā sāmarthyaṃ kḷptaṃ sanna tadvyāpādayitumarhati, api tu viniyojikāṃ śrutiṃ mantraḥ prayoktavya iti prāptam /
evaṃ prāpte ucyate-bhavedetadevaṃ yadyekavākyatāvagamapūrvaṃ sāmarthyāvadhāraṇamapi tu avadhṛtasāmarthyānāṃ padānāṃ praśliṣṭapāṭhitānāṃ sāmarthyavaśena prayojanaikatvenekavākyatvāvadhāraṇam /
yavanti padāni pradhānamekamarthamavagamayituṃ samarthāni vibhāge sākāṅkṣāṇi tānyekaṃ vākyam /
anuṣṭheyaścārtho mantreṣu prakāśyamānaḥ pradhānam /
sadanakaraṇapuroḍāśāsādane cānuṣṭheyatayā pradhāne /
tayośca sadanakaraṇaṃ kalpayāmyanto mantraḥ samarthaḥ prakāśayituṃ puroḍāśāsādanaṃ ca tasminsīdetyādiḥ /
tataśca yāvadekavākyatāvaśena sāmarthyamanumīyate tāvatpratītaṃ sāmarthyamekaikasya bhāgasyaikaikasminnarthe viniyojikāṃ śrutiṃ kalpayati /

children.text: tathāca śrutyaivaikaikasya bhāgasyaikatra viniyoge sati prakaraṇapāṭhopapattau na vākyakalpitaṃ liṅgaṃ viniyojikāṃ śrutimaparāṃ kalpayitumarhatītyekavākyatābuddhirutpannāpyābhāsībhavati liṅgena bādhanāt /
children.translated_text: And thus, when the assignment of each portion to one [particular act] is established through <s>Śruti</s>, and when the contextual reading (<s>prakaraṇapāṭha</s>) is explained [by this], the <s>liṅga</s> (indicatory mark) postulated from single-sentence-hood is not capable of postulating yet another assigning <s>Śruti</s> — and thus the cognition of single-sentence-hood, even though arisen, becomes apparent [only] — it is overridden (<s>bādhana</s>) by the indicatory mark.

children.text: yatra tu virodhakaṃ liṅgaṃ nāsti tatra samavetārthaikadvitripadaikavākyatā padāntarāṇāmapi sāmarthyaṃ kalpayatīti bhavati vākyasya viniyojakatvam /
children.translated_text: But where there is no contradicting indicatory mark, there the single-sentence-hood of words having their meaning jointly — whether of one, two, or three words — postulates the capacity of the other words as well, and thus the sentence has the power of assignment.
As in this very case, [regarding the words] '<s>syonaṃ te</s>' ('comfortable for you') and the like.
Therefore, it is established that the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is stronger than the sentence (<s>vākya</s>).

body.translated_text:
Therefore, it is established that [the mantra's] capacity — being led in conformity with that [directly perceived Śrauta assignment] — for the sake of supporting the perceived Śrauta assignment, should be taken in its primary meaning without abandoning [it], and [only if needed] should be led to a secondary meaning as well.
The example of the conflict between <s>liṅga</s> (indicatory mark) and <s>vākya</s> (sentence) is as follows: 'I make a comfortable seat for you; with a stream of ghee, I prepare it well.
Sit in it, O immortal one; remain firm. [Let] the essence of the rice [nourish you], O rejoicing one.'
Should this entire mantra be employed both in the preparation of the seat (<s>sadanakaraṇa</s>) and in the placing of the offering-cake (<s>puroḍāśāsādana</s>)? Or should [the portion up to] '<s>kalpayāmi</s>' ('I prepare') [be used] for the seat-preparation, and '<s>tasmin sīda</s>' ('sit in it') and so on for the placing of the offering-cake?
If the sentence (<s>vākya</s>) is stronger, the entire mantra [should be used] in both [acts], because '<s>tasmin sīda</s>' and the like, expecting [the antecedent] '<s>suśevaṃ kalpayāmi</s>' ('I prepare it well'), forms a single sentence with the preceding — [meaning] 'In what I prepare, sit in that.'
But if the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is stronger, then [the portion ending with] '<s>kalpayāmi</s>' [is used] for the seat-preparation — for it is capable of illuminating that [act].
'<s>Tasmin sīda</s>' [is used] for the placing of the offering-cake — for it is capable of [illuminating] that [act].
What, then, is the prima facie conclusion?
That the sentence (<s>vākya</s>) is stronger than the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>), and hence the assignment of the whole [mantra] to both [acts].
For here, since the single-sentence-hood is established — because of the expectation-bearing [nature] of the [words] being divided by co-occurrence with the <s>tat</s>-pronoun (that-word) — the capacity of their denotation must be postulated subsequently in conformity with that [single-sentence-hood].
Just as in the mantra '<s>devasya tve</s>' ('of the god, yours'), since the words '<s>agne nirvapāmi</s>' ('I offer to <s>Agni</s>') have their meaning jointly, and through the single-sentence-hood with that, the capacity of the other words is postulated as being directed toward that.
Thus, the capacity — postulated in conformity with the perceived single-sentence-hood, for the sake of upholding it — ought not to undermine that [very single-sentence-hood]; rather, the mantra should employ an assigning <s>Śruti</s> — this is what is arrived at.
This being arrived at, it is stated: This would be so if the determination of capacity were prior to the cognition of single-sentence-hood. But in fact, the determination of single-sentence-hood is based on the capacity of the words — [whose meanings are] jointly read — by virtue of their capacity, through the oneness of purpose.
Whatever words are capable of conveying a single principal meaning, [and] when separated are expectant [of completion] — those constitute a single sentence.
And the meaning to be accomplished (<s>anuṣṭheya</s>), being illuminated in the mantras, is the principal [meaning].
And the seat-preparation and the placing of the offering-cake are both principal as things to be accomplished.
And the mantra [portion ending with] '<s>kalpayāmi</s>' is capable of illuminating the seat-preparation, and '<s>tasmin sīda</s>' and so on [is capable of illuminating] the placing of the offering-cake.
And thus, for as long as the capacity is inferred on the basis of single-sentence-hood, the capacity that has been perceived [directly] — of each portion in each [respective] act — postulates an assigning <s>Śruti</s> for each.

body.text:
vākyaprakaraṇayorvirodhodāharaṇam /
atra ca padānāṃ parasparāpekṣāvaśātkasmiṃścidviśiṣṭa ekasminnarthe paryavasitānāṃ vākyatvaṃ, labdhavākyabhāvanāṃ ca punaḥ kāryāntarāpekṣāvaśena vākyāntareṇa saṃbandhaḥ prakaraṇam /
kartavyāyāḥ khalu phalabhāvanāyā labdhadhātvarthakaraṇāyā itikartavyatākāṅkṣāyā vacanaṃ prakaraṇamācakṣate vṛddhāḥ /
yathā 'darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeta' iti /
etaddhi vacanaṃ prakaraṇam /
tadetasmin svapadagaṇena kiyatyapyarthe paryavasite karaṇopakāralakṣaṇakāryāntarāpekṣāyāṃ 'samidho yajati' ityādivākyāntarasaṃbandhaḥ /
samidādibhāvanā hi svavidhyupahitāḥ puruṣe hitaṃ bhāvyapekṣamāṇā viśvajitryāyena vānuṣaṅgato vārthavādato vā phalāntarāpratilambhena darśapūrṇamāsabhāvanāṃ nirvārayitumīśate /
tasmāttadakāṅkṣāyāmupanipatitānyetāni vākyāni svakāryāpekṣāṇi tadapekṣitakaraṇopakāralakṣaṇaṃ kāryamasādya nirvaṇvanti ca nirvārayanti ca pradhānam /
so 'yamanayornaṣṭāśvadagdharathavatsaṃyogaḥ /
tadevaṃ lakṣaṇayorvākyaprakaraṇayorvirodhodāharaṇaṃ sūktavākanigadaḥ /
tatra hi paurṇamāsīdevatā amāvasyādevatāḥ samāmnātāḥ /
taśca na mitha ekavākyatāṃ gantumarhantīti liṅgena paurṇamāsīyāgādindrāgnīśabda utkraṣṭavyaḥ amāvāsyāyāṃ ca samavetārtatvātprayoktavyaḥ /
athedānīṃ saṃdihyate-kiṃ yadindrāgnipadaikavākyatayā pratīyate 'avivṛdhethāṃ maho jyāyo 'kātām' iti tannotākraṣṭavyamutendrāgniśabdābhyāṃ sahotkraṣṭavyamiti /
tatra yadi prakaraṇaṃ balīyastato 'panītadevatāko 'pi śeṣaḥ prayoktavyo 'tha vākyaṃ tato tatra devatāśabdastatraiva prayoktavyaḥ /
kiṃ tāvatprāptamapanītadevatāko 'pi śeṣaḥ prayoktavyaḥ prakaraṇasyaivāṅgasaṃbandhapratipādakatvāt /
phalavatī hi bāvanā pradhānetikartavyatātvamāpādayati /
tadupajīvanena śrutyādīnāṃ viśeṣasaṃbandhāpādakatvāt /
ataḥ pradhānabhāvanāvacanalakṣaṇaprakaraṇavirodhe tadupajīvivākyaṃ bādhyata iti prāptam /
evaṃ prāpta ucyate-bhavedetadevaṃ yadi viniyojyasvarūpasāmarthyamanapekṣya prakaramaṃ viniyojayet /
api tu viniyogāya tadapekṣaye 'nyathā pūṣādyanumantraṇamantrasya dvadaśopasattāyāśca notkarṣaḥ syāt /
tadrūpālocanāyāṃ ca tadyadeva śīghraṃ pratīyate tattadvalavadviprakṛṣṭaṃ tu durbalam /
tatra yadi tadrūpaṃ śrutyā liṅgena vākyena vānyatra viniyuktaṃ tataḥ prakaramaṃ bhaṅktvotkṛṣyate, piriśiṣṭaistu prakaraṇasyetikartavyatāpekṣā puryate /
atha svasya śīghrapravṛttaṃ śrutyādi nāsti tataḥ prakaramaṃ viniyojakam /
yathā samidādeḥ /

children.translated_text: Here, the quicker operation of the sentence compared to the context is being stated.
For in the context, sentences — whose own meanings are complete — show only the expectation of the relation of helped and helper.
But in a sentence, the connection of words is direct.

children.text: tataśca saha prasthitayorvākyaprakaraṇayoryāvatprakaraṇenaikavākyatā kalpyate tāvadvākyenābhidhānasāmarthyaṃ, yāvaditaratra vākyena sāmarthyaṃ tāvaditaratra sāmarthyena śrutistāvadiha śrutyā viniyogastāvatā ca vicchinnāyāmākāṅkṣāyāṃ śrutyanumāne vihate prakaraṇenāntarā kalpitaṃ vilīyanta iti vākyabalīyastvāttaddevatāśeṣaṇāmapakarṣa eveti siddham //
children.translated_text: And thus, when sentence and context have set out together — for as long as single-sentence-hood is postulated with the context, so long the capacity of denotation [is postulated] with the sentence; and for as long as the capacity [is established] elsewhere through the sentence, so long through that capacity a <s>Śruti</s> [is postulated] elsewhere; so long through that <s>Śruti</s> the assignment is [established] here; and so long, when the expectation has been severed, <s>Śruti</s> and inference are arrested — what is postulated intermediately by the context dissolves. Thus, because of the greater strength of the sentence, the extraction [pertains] only to the deity-word along with its remainder — this is established.

body.translated_text:
An example of the conflict between sentence (<s>vākya</s>) and context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>):
Here, the mutual expectation of words, by virtue of which they conclude in a single specific meaning, constitutes their sentence-hood (<s>vākyatva</s>). And the relationship of a sentence — having obtained [its] operation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) — with another sentence, by virtue of the expectation for a further action, constitutes the context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>).
The elders explain the context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) as the statement of the result-producing operation (<s>phalabhāvanā</s>) — [the operation] that has obtained its verbal-root meaning and the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) — expecting the procedural details (<s>itikartavyatā</s>).
As in: 'One who desires heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Darśa-Pūrṇamāsa</s>.'—
This statement is the context.
In this [context], when [the operation] has concluded in whatever extent of meaning through its own set of words, [and] expects a further action characterized by instrumental assistance (<s>karaṇopakāra</s>) — [there is] the connection with another sentence such as '<s>samidho yajati</s>' (he sacrifices with fuel-sticks) and the like.
For the operations (<s>bhāvanā</s>) of <s>samidh</s> and the like — qualified by their own injunctions — expecting a benefit for the person conducive to the attainable [fruit], are able to select the <s>Darśa-Pūrṇamāsa</s> operation [as their principal] through either the <s>Viśvajit</s> principle, or through association (<s>anuṣaṅga</s>), or through <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passages), or through the non-attainment of another fruit.
Therefore, these sentences — having fallen in [the context] when that [<s>Darśa-Pūrṇamāsa</s> operation] is expecting — expecting their own subsidiary action, having reached the action characterized by instrumental assistance expected by that [principal operation], they both consummate and select the principal.
This conjunction of the two is like one whose horse is lost and whose chariot is burnt.
Thus, the example of the conflict between the two — sentence and context, whose definitions [have been given] — is the <s>Sūktavāka</s> recitation (<s>nigada</s>).
For therein, the deities of the full-moon [offering] and the new-moon [offering] are listed.
And these cannot enter into a single sentence with each other — hence, by the indicatory mark, the word '<s>Indrāgnī</s>' should be extracted from the full-moon sacrifice and employed in the new-moon [sacrifice], being of joint meaning there.
Now the doubt arises: should what is cognized through single-sentence-hood with the <s>Indrāgnī</s> word — namely, '<s>avivṛdhethāṃ maho jyāyo 'kātām</s>' ('may the two increase; may they make great and greater') — also be extracted, or should [only] the <s>Indrāgnī</s> words be extracted together?
Therein, if the context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) is stronger, then even the remainder — stripped of the deity-word — should be employed [in the new-moon sacrifice]. But if the sentence (<s>vākya</s>) is [stronger], then the deity-word should be employed only there [where its sentence is].
What, then, is the prima facie conclusion? The remainder — even stripped of the deity-word — should be employed, because the context alone is what establishes the subsidiary-connection.
For the result-bearing operation (<s>phalabhāvanā</s>), being the principal, confers upon the procedural details (<s>itikartavyatā</s>) [the status of being] its subsidiaries.
By depending on that [principal operation], <s>Śruti</s> and the like establish the specific subsidiary-connections.
Therefore, when there is a conflict with the context — whose definition is the statement of the principal operation — the sentence that depends on it is overridden — this is the prima facie conclusion.
This being the prima facie conclusion, it is stated: This would be so if the context assigned without regard to the capacity of the form (<s>svarūpa</s>) of what is to be assigned.
But in fact, it requires that [capacity] for assignment — otherwise the extraction of the <s>Pūṣan</s>-invocation mantra and of the twelve-day (<s>dvādaśopasattā</s>) [offering] would not [take place].
And when examining that form — whatever is quickly cognized, that is strong; what is remote is weak.
Therein, if that form is assigned elsewhere by <s>Śruti</s>, indicatory mark, or sentence, then [it] breaks the context and is extracted. But with the remainder, the context's expectation of procedural details is fulfilled.
But if there is no <s>Śruti</s> and the like of its own that is quickly operative, then the context is the assigner.
As in the case of <s>samidh</s> and the like.

body.text:
kramaprakaraṇavirodhodāharaṇam /
rājasūyaprakaraṇe pradhānasyaivābhiṣecanīyasya saṃnidhau śaunaḥśepopākhyānādyāmnātaṃ, tatkiṃ samastasya rājasūyasyāṅgamutibhiṣecanīyasya /
yadi prakaramaṃ balīyastataḥ samastasya rājasūyasya, atha kramastato 'bhiṣecanīyasyaiveti, kiṃ tāvatprāptam /
nākāhkṣāmātraṃ hi saṃbandhahatuḥ /
gāmānaya prasādaṃ paśyeti gāmityasya kriyāmātrāpekṣiṇaḥ paśyetyanenāpi saṃbandhasaṃbhavādvinigamanābhāvaprasaṅgāt /
tasmātsaṃnidhānaṃ saṃbandhakāraṇam /
tathā cānayetyananaiva gāmityasya saṃbandho vinigamyate /
naca saṃnidhānamapi saṃbandhakāraṇam /
ayameti putro rājñaḥ puruṣo 'pasāryatāmityatra rājña ityasya putrapuruṣapadasaṃnidhānāviśeṣānmā bhūdavinigamanā /
tasmādākāṅkṣā niścayaheturvaktavyā /
atra putraśabdasya saṃbandhivacanatayā samutthitākāṅkṣasyāntike yadupanipatitaṃ saṃbandhyantarākāṅkṣaṃ padaṃ tasya tenaivākāṅkṣāparipūrteḥ puruṣapadena puruṣarūpamātrābhidhāyinā svatantreṇaiva na saṃbandhaḥ kintu pareṇāpasāryatāmityanenāpasaraṇīyāpekṣeṇeti /
satyapi saṃnidhāne ākāṅkṣābhāvādasaṃbandhaḥ /
tathā cābhāṇakaḥ-'taptaṃ taptena saṃbadhyate' iti /
tathā cākāṅkṣitamapi na yāvatsaṃnidhāpyate tāvanna saṃbadhyate /
tathā saṃnihitamapi yāvannākāṅkṣyate na tāvatsaṃbadhyata iti dvayoḥ saṃbandhaṃ prati samānabalatvātkramaprakaraṇayoḥ samuccayāsaṃbhavācca vikalpena rājasūyābhiṣecanīyayorviniyogaḥ śaunaḥśepopākhyānādīnāmiti prāptam /
evaṃ prāpta ucyate-rājasūyake kathaṃbhāvāpekṣā hi pavitrādārabhya kṣatrasya dhṛtiṃ yāvadanuvartate /
tathāca-'avicchinne kathaṃbhāve yatpradhānasya paṭhyate /
anirjñātaphalaṃ karma tasya prakaraṇāṅgatā ' iti nyāyādrājasūyāṅgatā śaunaḥśopopākhyānādīnām /
abhiṣecanīyasya tu svavākyopāttapadārthanirākāṅkṣasya saṃnidhipāṭhenākāṅkṣotthāpanīyā yāvattāvatsiddhākāṅkṣeṇa rājasūyenaikavākyatā kalpyate /
body.translated_text:
An illustration of the conflict between <s>krama</s> (sequence) and <s>prakaraṇa</s> (context):
In the <s>Rājasūya</s> context, in the proximity of the principal [rite], the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s> (consecration ceremony), the <s>Śaunaḥśepa-upākhyāna</s> (narrative of <s>Śunaḥśepa</s>) and the like are recited. The question is: is it a subsidiary of the entire <s>Rājasūya</s>, or of the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s> alone?
If <s>prakaraṇa</s> (context) is stronger, then [it belongs] to the entire <s>Rājasūya</s>; if <s>krama</s> (sequence) [is stronger], then to the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s> alone — what then is the prima facie view?
Mere expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>) alone is not the cause of syntactic connection.
For in 'Bring the cow, behold the palace' (<s>gām ānaya prasādaṃ paśya</s>), since the word 'cow' — which expects merely an action — could also be connected with 'behold,' there would be an absurd failure of determinate assignment.
Therefore, proximity (<s>saṃnidhāna</s>) is the cause of connection.
And thus, by proximity with 'bring' alone, the connection of the word 'cow' is determinately established.
But proximity too is not [by itself] the cause of connection.
In the [sentence] 'This son of the king, let the man be removed' (<s>ayam iti putro rājñaḥ puruṣo 'pasāryatām</s>), since the word 'of the king' (<s>rājñaḥ</s>) is equally proximate to both the words 'son' and 'man,' there should be indeterminate assignment — [which is absurd].
Therefore, expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>) must be stated as the cause of determinate cognition.
Here, for the word 'son' (<s>putra</s>) — which, being a relational term, has an arisen expectancy [for its correlate] — the word that is proximate and that expects another relatum, [namely 'of the king,'] has its expectancy fulfilled by that very [word 'son']. But the word 'man' (<s>puruṣa</s>) — denoting merely the form of a person and being independent — is not connected [with 'of the king'] but rather with another [word], namely 'let be removed' (<s>apasāryatām</s>), which expects [the specification of] what is to be removed.
Thus, even when proximity obtains, there is no connection in the absence of expectancy.
And thus the maxim: 'What is heated is connected with what is heated' (<s>taptaṃ taptena saṃbadhyate</s>).
Likewise, even what is expected, as long as it is not brought into proximity, is not connected.
Similarly, what is proximate, as long as it is not expected, is not connected — thus, since both [expectancy and proximity] are of equal strength with respect to connection, and since the simultaneous application (<s>samuccaya</s>) of <s>krama</s> and <s>prakaraṇa</s> is impossible, the prima facie view is that the assignment of the <s>Śaunaḥśepa-upākhyāna</s> and the like is alternatively to [either] the <s>Rājasūya</s> or the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s>.
With this prima facie view established, [the conclusion] is stated: in the <s>Rājasūyaka</s> [context], the expectancy of 'how it should be' (<s>kathaṃbhāva</s>) extends continuously from the <s>Pavitra</s> [rite] up to the <s>Kṣatrasya Dhṛti</s> (Sustaining of Royal Power).
And thus: 'When the sequential narrative (<s>kathaṃbhāva</s>) is unbroken, whatever action of unknown fruit is recited in connection with the principal [rite] — its subsidiary-hood to the <s>prakaraṇa</s> (context) [is established]' — by this rule, the subsidiary-hood of the <s>Śaunaḥśepa-upākhyāna</s> and the like to the <s>Rājasūya</s> [is established].
But for the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s> — which, through the meanings contained in its own sentence, has no expectancy [for additional material] — expectancy would have to be generated by proximity-recitation. And as long as [the expectancy must be generated], syntactic unity (<s>ekavākyatā</s>) is to be construed with the <s>Rājasūya</s>, whose expectancy is already established.

children.text: yāvaccābhiṣecanīyaikavākyatayā liṅgaṃ kalpyate tāvatkḷptaliṅgaṃ viniyokrīṃ śrutiṃ kalpyati yāvadvākyakalpitena liṅgena śrutiritaratra kalpte tāvatkḷptayā śrutyā viniyoge sati prakaraṇapāṭhopapattau saṃnidhānaparikalpitamantarā vilīyate /
children.translated_text: And as long as figurative identification (<s>liṅga</s>) is being construed for syntactic unity with the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s>, the already-construed <s>liṅga</s> [instead] construes a <s>Śruti</s> (scriptural statement) as the basis for assignment. And as long as a <s>Śruti</s> construed by <s>liṅga</s> from elsewhere construes [assignment] in the other [the <s>Rājasūya</s>], so long, with the assignment being established by the construed <s>Śruti</s>, the contextual recitation (<s>prakaraṇapāṭha</s>) is justified — and thereby all that was construed through proximity dissolves.
In the absence of a [valid] means of knowledge, [the proximity-based construal remains] at the level of mere conjecture (<s>pratibhā</s>).
And because for the <s>Rājasūya</s> — which is the subject of the context (<s>prakaraṇin</s>) — its proximity is always present to the intellect and [hence] need not be construed.

children.text: tasmātprakaraṇavirodhe kramasya bādha eva naca vikalpo durbalatvāditi siddham //
children.translated_text: Therefore, in conflict with <s>prakaraṇa</s> (context), <s>krama</s> (sequence) is indeed overridden — and there is no [mere] option, because of its weakness — this is established.

body.text:
kramasamākhyayorvirodhodāharaṇam-pauroḍāśika iti samākhyāte kāṇḍe sānnāṭyakrame ca śundhadhvaṃ daivyāya karmaṇa iti śundhanārtho mantraḥ samāmnātaḥ, tatra saṃdihyate kiṃ samākhyānasya balīyastvātpuroḍāśapātrāṇāṃ śundhena viniyoktavyaḥ, āho sānnāṭyapātrāṇāṃ śundhena kramo balīyāniti /
kintāvatprāptam /
samākhyānāṃ balīya iti pauroḍāśikaśabdena hi puroḍāśasaṃbandhīnītyucyante tānyadhikṛtya pravṛttaṃ kāṇḍaṃ pauroḍāśikam /
tataśca yāvatkrameṇa prakaraṇādyanumānaparamparayā saṃbandhaḥ pratipādanīyaḥ yāvatsamākhyayā śrutyaiva sākṣādeva sa pratipādita iti arthaviprakarṣeṇa kramātsamākhyaiva balīyasīti puroḍāśapātraśundhena mantraḥ prayoktavyaḥ na sānnāṭyapātraśundhana iti prāptam /
evaṃ prāpte 'bhidhīyate-samākhyānātkramo balavānarthaviprakarṣāditi /
tathāhi-samākhyā na tāvatsaṃbandhasya vācikā kintu pauroḍāśaviśiṣṭaṃ kāṇḍamāha /
tadviśiṣṭatvānyathānupapattyā tava saṃbandhaḥ kāṇḍasyānumīyate na tu sākṣānmantrabedasya /
taddhāreṇa ca tanmadhyapātino mantrabedasyāpi tadanumānam /
na cāsau saṃbandho 'pi śrutyaiva śeṣaśeṣibhāvaḥ pratīyate /
api tu saṃbandhamātram /
tasmācchatisādṛśyamasya dūrāpetamiti krameṇa nāsya spardhocitā /
tatrāpi ca sāmānyato darśapūrṇamāsaprakaraṇāpāditaidamarthyasya śaunaḥśepopākhyānādivaccārādupakārakatayā prakṛtamātrasaṃbandhānupapattiḥ /
mantrasya prayogasamavetārthasmāraṇena sāmavāyikāṅgatvāt /
tathāca yaṃ kañcitprakṛtaprayogagatamarthaṃ prakāśayato 'sya prakaraṇāṅgatvamaviruddhamiti viśeṣāpekṣāyāṃ sānnāṭyakramaḥ sānnāṭyaṃ prati prakaraṇādyanumānadvāreṇa viniyogaṃ kalpayitumutsahate na tu samākhyānam /
tasya durbalatvāt /
tathāhi-samākhyā saṃbandhanibandhanā sati tatsidhyarthaṃ saṃnidhimupakalpayati yāvattādvaidikena pratyakṣadṛṣṭena saṃnidhānenākāṅkṣā kalpyate /
yāvacca kḷptena saṃnidhānenākāṅkṣā kalpyate tāvaditaratra kḷptayākāṅkṣayaikavākyatā tāvaditaratraikavākyatayā kḷptayopakārasāmarthyam /
yāvaccātraikavākyatayopakārasāmarthyaṃ tāvaditaratra liṅgena viniyojikā śrutiḥ /

children.text: yāvadatra liṅgena viniyojikā śrutistāvaditaratra kḷptayā śrutyā viniyoga iti tāvataiva prakaraṇapāṭhopapatteḥ sarvaṃ samākhyānakalpitaṃ vicchinnamūlatvāttūyamānaśasyamiva nirbījaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: As long as there is a <s>Śruti</s> serving as the basis for assignment through <s>liṅga</s> here, so long there is assignment elsewhere through the construed <s>Śruti</s> — and just by that much, the contextual recitation (<s>prakaraṇapāṭha</s>) is justified. Hence, everything construed by <s>samākhyā</s>, being of severed root, becomes seedless — like grain that is threshed.
It should be understood that the section has the designation '<s>Pauroḍāśika</s>' because of the preponderance of mantras denoting <s>puroḍāśa</s> [within it].

'The disparity with respect to the meaning of <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) among <s>liṅga</s> (indicatory mark) and the rest is perceived as being caused by [the intervening factors of] one, two, three, four, five, and [other] obstacles.

body.translated_text:
An illustration of the conflict between <s>krama</s> (sequence) and <s>samākhyā</s> (designation):
In the section designated '<s>Pauroḍāśika</s>' (pertaining to the <s>puroḍāśa</s> cake), and in the <s>Sānnāṭya</s> sequential arrangement, the mantra 'Purify yourselves for the divine rite' (<s>śundhadhvaṃ daivyāya karmaṇe</s>) — a mantra for the purpose of purification — is recited. Therein the doubt arises: because of the strength of designation (<s>samākhyāna</s>), should [the mantra] be assigned to the purification of the <s>puroḍāśa</s> vessels, or is <s>krama</s> (sequence) stronger, [meaning it should be assigned] to the purification of the <s>Sānnāṭya</s> vessels?
What is the prima facie view?
Designation (<s>samākhyāna</s>) is stronger — for by the word '<s>Pauroḍāśika</s>' it is said '[these things] pertain to the <s>puroḍāśa</s>'; the section (<s>kāṇḍa</s>) that is undertaken with reference to those [<s>puroḍāśa</s>-related items] is '<s>Pauroḍāśika</s>.'
Consequently, whereas through <s>krama</s> the connection [of the mantra with the <s>Sānnāṭya</s>] must be established through a chain of inferences via <s>prakaraṇa</s> and the like, through <s>samākhyā</s> it is established directly by <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) itself. Hence, by virtue of the remoteness of meaning [in the case of <s>krama</s>], <s>samākhyā</s> alone is stronger than <s>krama</s> — [therefore] the mantra should be employed for the purification of <s>puroḍāśa</s> vessels, not for the purification of <s>Sānnāṭya</s> [vessels] — this is the prima facie view.
With this prima facie view established, it is stated: <s>krama</s> (sequence) is stronger than <s>samākhyā</s> (designation), because of the remoteness of meaning [in the latter].
For thus: <s>samākhyā</s> is not a direct verbal indicator of the connection; rather, it states the section as qualified by <s>puroḍāśa</s>.
From the impossibility of the section's being so qualified [without a connection], the connection of the section is inferred — but not [the connection] of the mantra directly.
And through the medium of that [inferred connection of the section], the connection of the mantra too — which falls within [the section] — is inferred.
And that inferred connection is not [directly] cognized by <s>Śruti</s> as a <s>śeṣa-śeṣin</s> (subsidiary-principal) relationship,
but only as a connection in general.
Therefore, [<s>samākhyā</s>'s] similarity to <s>Śruti</s> is far-removed, and it is not fit to compete with <s>krama</s>.
Moreover, here too — just as in the case of the <s>Śaunaḥśepa-upākhyāna</s> and the like, which through the <s>Darśa-Pūrṇamāsa</s> context have acquired a general purposiveness (<s>idamarthya</s>) — the impossibility of connecting [the mantra] with the <s>prakṛta</s> (model rite) alone [follows], because of its indirect subsidiary-hood (<s>cārād upakārakatā</s>).
For the mantra, through its function of recalling the meaning inherent in its actual employment (<s>prayoga</s>), has an inherent subsidiary-hood (<s>sāmavāyika-aṅgatva</s>).
And thus, since [the mantra], illuminating whatever meaning belongs to a contextual employment (<s>prakṛta-prayoga</s>), has an uncontradicted contextual subsidiary-hood, when a specific [assignment] is required, the <s>Sānnāṭya</s> sequence — being capable of construing assignment to the <s>Sānnāṭya</s> through inference via <s>prakaraṇa</s> and the like — prevails, but not <s>samākhyā</s> (designation),
because of its weakness.
For thus: <s>samākhyā</s>, being grounded in [the need to establish] connection, construes proximity to establish [that connection]. As long as [this process continues,] expectancy is construed through the Vedic proximity that is directly perceived.
And as long as expectancy is construed through the construed proximity, so long syntactic unity (<s>ekavākyatā</s>) [is established] elsewhere [i.e., in the <s>Rājasūya</s> context]. And as long as syntactic unity is construed elsewhere, so long the capacity for subsidiary service [is established]. And as long as the capacity for subsidiary service [is established] here through syntactic unity, so long a <s>Śruti</s> serving as the basis for assignment [is established] through <s>liṅga</s> (indicatory mark) elsewhere.

[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] justifies the proximity-recitation: '#Like the statement about the forest (<s>araṇyādi</s>) and the like#.' //25//

body.translated_text:
The [mantra] '<s>upahūta</s>' — by virtue of its indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) — is a permission-granting (<s>anujñā</s>) mantra, not [a mantra] for the act of granting permission (<s>anujñāpana</s>). And '<s>upahūyasva</s>' — by virtue of its indicatory mark — is a mantra for the act of granting permission, not for the permission [itself].
Here, having overridden <s>krama</s> (sequence) through <s>liṅga</s> (indicatory mark), the reverse subsidiary-hood is established.
For as long as syntactic unity is being construed by position (<s>sthāna</s>) through <s>prakaraṇa</s>, so long, having construed a <s>Śruti</s> through <s>liṅga</s>, the assignment is accomplished — hence [there is] the overriding of <s>krama</s> by the unconstrued <s>liṅga</s>-based <s>Śruti</s>.
Likewise here too, in the [matter of] assignment, the <s>vidyā</s>-based <s>krama</s> — which is separated by four [intervening steps] — is overridden by <s>liṅga</s>, which is separated [from the <s>Śruti</s>] by only one [step].
Although this matter has been demonstrated in the <s>Prathamatantra</s> (first system) itself, nevertheless [its] demonstration in a conflict [belongs] there; but here [the point is] the absence of conflict.
For the connection of the <s>Ābhicārika</s> (sorcery) rite through <s>liṅga</s> is not contradicted by the <s>krama</s>-based connection with the <s>vidyā</s>.
Nor is the conflict here one of [two different] assignments to [two different] assignees — for that [conflict] would apply even in the <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s> [case].
Rather, the conflict is only at the level of cognition, not at the level of reality — and that [cognition-level conflict] is equally [present] in the assignment to the <s>vidyā</s> as well.
Therefore, because there is no [real] conflict, the subsidiary-hood of the <s>Vedha</s> mantra to the meditation (<s>upāsanā</s>) — this is the stronger objection.
To that it is replied: 'It is not the case that the overriding of <s>krama</s> is stated by virtue of conflict with <s>liṅga</s>;
rather, in a domain where <s>liṅga</s> has already determined [the assignment], <s>krama</s> is incapable of generating a construal.'
For through the justification of contextual recitation (<s>prakaraṇapāṭha</s>) via <s>Śruti</s>, <s>liṅga</s>, <s>vākya</s> (sentence), and <s>prakaraṇa</s> (context), [a mantra that was] unassigned [gets] assigned through <s>krama</s> — [which operates] by the chain of construals: <s>prakaraṇa</s>, <s>vākya</s>, <s>liṅga</s>, <s>Śruti</s>.
But then, since the contextual recitation of the [already-]assigned [mantra] would become purposeless, [there is a problem].
When, however, the contextual recitation has been justified by <s>Śruti</s> and the rest, then — because [the construal via <s>krama</s>] has been exhausted — <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) [from <s>krama</s>] cannot generate its proper cognitive force (<s>pramā</s>), [and] due to the absence of [valid] cognition [from <s>krama</s>, its claim is void].
But in the <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s>, the <s>ktvā</s>-scriptural statement itself — being enjoined for the same-agent condition by virtue of the connection of the verbal root [with the agent] — even while assigning [the mantra] separately through the disjunction of combination (<s>saṃyoga-pṛthaktva</s>), [this <s>Śruti</s>] cannot be blocked by another <s>Śruti</s>, since it has its own [independent] cognitive force — this is the difference.
