For them, when there is the possibility of entering the body of the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic), the description of another meaning is indeed incongruous. //28//

body.translated_text:
But the destruction of merit and demerit is possible even while in the human body — since a competent cause, namely <s>vidyā</s> accompanied by <s>yama</s>, <s>niyama</s>, and the like, is unsuitable for destroying its effect [only after death], the destruction of merit and demerit while alive alone is established.
'At will' (<s>chandataḥ</s>) means 'of one's own accord,' 'by one's own wish.'
The practice of <s>vidyā</s> accompanied by <s>yama</s>, <s>niyama</s>, and the like is at one's own will.
'#Of that one#' — of the living person, not of the dead.
And the shedding of merit and demerit, being preceded by that [voluntary practice], would occur while alive alone.
Because a competent [cause] cannot be denied [its effect].
Thus, when the effect arises immediately after the cause, the tenable relationship of cause and effect [is established], and there is concordance with the <s>Tāṇḍin</s> and <s>Śāṭhyāyanin</s> <s>Śruti</s>s; otherwise, in the absence of independence [of the dead person], the discordance would have been stated.
By this, the non-contradiction of both is explained.

body.text:
#gaterarthavattvamubhayathānyathā hi virodhaḥ# /
yathā hānisaṃnidhāvupāyanamanyatra śrutamiti, tatrāpi kevalā hāniḥ śrūyate tatrāpi upāyanamupasthāpayatyevaṃ tatsannidhāveva devayānaḥ panthāḥ śruta iti yatrāpi sukṛtaduṣkṛtahāniḥ kevalā śrutā tatrāpi devayānaṃ panthānamupasthāpayitumarhati /
naca nirañjanaḥ paramaṃ sāmyamupaitītyanena virodhaḥ /
devayānena pathā brahmalokaprāptau nirañjanasya paramasāmyopapatteḥ /
tasmāddhānimātre devayānaḥ panthāḥ saṃbadhyata iti prāptam /
evaṃ prāptam ucyate-vidvān puṇyapāpe vidhūyanirañjanaḥ paramaṃ sāmyamupaitīti hi viduṣo vidhūtapuṇyapāpasya vidyayā kṣemaprāptimāha /
bhramanibandhano 'kṣemo yāthātmyajñānalakṣaṇayā vidyāyā vinivartanīyaḥ /
nāsau deśaviśeṣamapekṣate /
nahi jātu rajjau sarpabhramanivṛttaye samutpannaṃ rajjutattavajñānaṃ deśaviśeṣamapekṣate /
vidyotpādasyaiva svavirodhyavidyānivṛttirūpatvāt /
naca vidyotpādāyā brahmalokaprāptirapekṣaṇīyā /
yamaniyamādiviśuddhasattvasyehaiva śravaṇādibhirvidyotpādāt /
yadi paramārabdhakāryakarmakṣapaṇāya śarīrapātāvadhyapekṣeti na devayānenāstīhārtha iti śrutidṛṣṭavirodhānnāpekṣitavya iti /
asti tu paryaṅkavidyāyāṃ tasmārtha ityuktaṃ dvitīyena sūtreṇeti /
ye tu yadi puṇyamapi nivartate kimarthā tarhi gatarityāśaṅkya sūtramavatārayanti /
gaterarthavattvamubhayathā duṣkṛtanivṛttyā sukṛtanivṛttyā ca /
yadi punaḥ puṇyamanuvarteta brahmalokagatasyāpīha puṇyaphalopabhogāyavṛttiḥ syāt /
tathā caitena pratipādyamānāgatyanāvṛttiśrutivirodhaḥ /

children.text: tasmādduṣkṛtasyeva sukṛtasyāpi prakṣaya iti taiḥ punaranāśaṅkanīyamevāśaṅkitam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as demerit is destroyed, merit too [is destroyed] — and they should not have raised this doubt that is not [genuinely] a doubt.

children.text: vidyākṣiptāyāṃ hi gatau keyamāśaṅkā yadi kṣīṇasukṛtaḥ kimarthamayaṃ yātīti /
children.translated_text: For when the journey is impelled by <s>vidyā</s>, what doubt is this — 'If merit is exhausted, for what purpose does this one travel?'
For this journey is not grounded in merit, but in <s>vidyā</s>.
Therefore, the description given by the elder [commentator] alone is correct. //29//

body.translated_text:
'#The journey has purpose in both ways; otherwise there would be a contradiction#.'
Just as where shedding [of sins] is proximate, the approaching [of divine guides] heard elsewhere [is incorporated] — so there too, where mere shedding is heard, [the text] brings in the approaching as well; similarly, since the <s>Devayāna</s> (path of the gods) is heard in proximity to [the shedding], wherever the mere shedding of merit and demerit is heard, the <s>Devayāna</s> path too ought to be brought in.
Nor is there a contradiction with 'Stainless, he attains supreme equality' —
because the supreme equality of the stainless one is tenable upon the attainment of <s>Brahmaloka</s> via the <s>Devayāna</s> path.
Therefore, the <s>Devayāna</s> path is connected with mere shedding [of sins] — thus is the prima facie view.
With this prima facie view established, the reply is given: 'The wise one, having shaken off merit and demerit, stainless, attains supreme equality' — this states the attainment of well-being for the knower whose merit and demerit have been shaken off by <s>vidyā</s>.
The ill-being that is grounded in delusion is to be removed by <s>vidyā</s> characterized as knowledge of reality (<s>yāthātmyajñāna</s>).
That [ill-being] does not require a particular place [for its removal].
For the knowledge of the true nature of the rope, once arisen for the removal of the delusion of a snake in the rope, does not require a particular place.
Because the very arising of knowledge has as its nature the cessation of <s>avidyā</s>, which is its opposite.
Nor is the attainment of <s>Brahmaloka</s> to be expected for the arising of knowledge.
Because knowledge arises right here through hearing and the like for one whose <s>sattva</s> (mind) is purified by <s>yama</s>, <s>niyama</s>, and the like.
If [it is argued] that [the knower] awaits the fall of the body for the exhaustion of <s>karma</s> whose effects have already commenced (<s>prārabdha</s>) — then the <s>Devayāna</s> [path] has no purpose here — and because of the contradiction with what is seen in <s>Śruti</s>, it should not be expected.
But there is purpose [for the <s>Devayāna</s> path] in the <s>Paryaṅka-vidyā</s> — this has been stated by the second <s>sūtra</s>.
But those who introduce the <s>sūtra</s> with the doubt 'If merit too ceases, then what is the purpose of the journey?' —
[they explain:] the journey has purpose in both ways — through the cessation of demerit and through the cessation of merit.
But if merit were to continue, even after going to <s>Brahmaloka</s>, there would be a return here for the enjoyment of the fruit of merit.
And thus, there would be a contradiction with the <s>Śruti</s> of non-return, which is being taught in this [context].

body.text:
aniyamaḥ sarvāsāmavirodhaḥ śabdānumānābhyām /
prakaraṇaṃ hi dharmāṇāṃ niyāmakam /
yadi tu tannādriyate tato darśapūrṇamāsajyotiṣṭomādidharmāḥ saṃkīryeran /
naca teṣāṃ vikṛtiṣu sauryādiṣu dvādaśāhādiṣu codakataḥ prāptiḥ /
sarvatraupadeśikatvāt /
naca darvihomasyāprakṛtivikārasyādharmakatvam /
naca sarvadharmayuktaṃ karma kiñcidapi śakyamanuṣṭhātum /
na caivaṃ sati śrutyādoya'pi viniyojakāsteṣāmapi hi prakaraṇena sāmānyasaṃbandhe sati viniyojakatvāt /
yatrāpi vināprakaraṇaṃ śrutyādibhyo viniyogo 'vagamyate tatrāpi tannirvāhāya prakaraṇasyāvaśyaṃ kalpanīyatvāt /
tasmātprakaraṇaṃ viniyogāya tanniyamāya cāvaśyābhyupetavyamanyathā śrutyadīnāmaprāmāṇyaprasakteḥ /
tasmādyāsvevopāsanāsu devayānaḥ pitṛyāṇo vā panthā āmnātastāsveva na tūpāsanāntareṣu tadanāmnānāt /
naca 'ye ceme 'raṇye śraddhātapa ityupāsate' iti sāmānyavacanātsarvavidyāsu tatpathaprāptiḥ /
śraddhātapaḥparāyaṇānāmeva tatra tatpathaprāptiḥ śrūyate, na tu vidyāparāyaṇānām /
apicaivaṃ satyekasyāṃ vidyāyāṃ mārgopadeśaḥ sarvāsu vidyāsvityekatraiva mārgopadeśaḥ kartavyo na vidyāntare /
vidyāntare ca śrūyate /
tasmānna sarvopāsanāsu pathiprāptiriti prāptam /
evaṃ prāpte ucyate-'ye ceme 'raṇye śraddhātapa ityupāsate' iti na śraddhātapomātrasya pathiprāptimāhāpi tu vidyayā tadārohāntītyatra nāvidvāṃsastapasvina iti kevalasya tapasaḥ śraddhāyāśca tatprāptipratiṣedhādvidyāsahite śraddhātapasī tatprāpyupāyatayā vadan vidyāntarīlānāmapi pañcāgnividyāvidbhiḥ samānamārgatāṃ darśayati /
tathānyatrāpi pañcāgnividyādhikāre 'bhidhīyate-'ya evametādvidurye cāmī araṇye śraddhāṃ satyamupāsate' iti /
satyaśabdasya brahmaṇyevānapekṣapravṛttitvāt /
tadeva hi satyamanyasya mithyātvena kathañcidāpekṣikasatyatvāt /
pañcāgnividāṃ cetthaṃvittayaivopāttatvāt /
vidyāsāhacaryācca vidyāntaraparāyaṇānāmevedamupādānaṃ nyāṭyam /

children.translated_text: And because the downward course is heard for those who have fallen from both paths.
And there too, through fitness, the connection is indeed with the <s>Devayāna</s> path only.

children.text: etaduktaṃ bhavati-bhavetprakaraṇaṃ niyāmakaṃ yadyaniyamapratipādakaṃ vākyaṃ śrautaṃ smārtaṃ vā na syādasti tu tattasya ca prakaraṇādbalīyastvam /
children.translated_text: What is meant is this: the context would be the restrictor if there were no <s>Śrauta</s> (Vedic) or <s>Smārta</s> (traditional) statement teaching non-restriction — but there is such [a statement], and it is stronger than the context.

children.text: tasmādaniyamo vidyāntareṣvapi saguṇeṣu devayānaḥ panthā asakṛnmārgopadeśasya ca prayojanaṃ varṇitaṃ bāṣyakṛteti //31 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the non-restriction [applies] — the <s>Devayāna</s> path extends even to other <s>saguṇa</s> (qualified) <s>vidyā</s>s. And the purpose of the repeated teaching of the path has been explained by the author of the <s>Bhāṣya</s>. //31//

body.translated_text:
'Non-restriction, non-contradiction of all, from scripture and reasoning.'
For the context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) is the restrictor of the qualities.
But if that [context] is not respected, then the qualities of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, and the like would be mixed up.
Nor is their attainment in the <s>vikṛti</s> (modified) sacrifices — <s>Saurya</s> and the like, <s>Dvādaśāha</s> and the like — through injunction.
Because [they] are instructed everywhere.
Nor is the <s>Darvihoma</s> (ladle-oblation), being neither a <s>Prakṛti</s> (model) nor a <s>Vikāra</s> (modification), devoid of qualities.
Nor can any rite be performed with all qualities [combined].
Nor, when this is so, are the <s>Śruti</s> and the like assigning agents — for they too assign [qualities] only when there is a general connection through context.
And even where the assignment is understood from <s>Śruti</s> and the like without context, context must necessarily be postulated for the purpose of carrying out that [assignment].
Therefore, context must necessarily be accepted for the purpose of assignment and its restriction — otherwise, the <s>Śruti</s>s and the like would lack authority.
Therefore, only in those meditations in which the <s>Devayāna</s> or <s>Pitṛyāṇa</s> path is mentioned does [that path apply], not in other meditations — because of its non-mention [there].
Nor is there attainment of that path in all <s>vidyā</s>s from the general statement 'those who in the forest meditate on faith and austerity.'
For the attainment of that path is heard only for those devoted to faith and austerity, not for those devoted to <s>vidyā</s>.
Moreover, if this were so, the teaching of the path in a single <s>vidyā</s> [would apply] to all <s>vidyā</s>s — so the teaching of the path should be done in one place only, not in another <s>vidyā</s>.
But it is heard in another <s>vidyā</s> [as well].
Therefore, there is no attainment of the path in all meditations — thus is the prima facie view.
With this prima facie view established, the reply is given: 'Those who in the forest meditate on faith and austerity' — this does not state the attainment of the path for mere faith and austerity alone; rather, 'they ascend to that by <s>vidyā</s>' — herein, 'not the unlearned ascetics' — since the attainment of that [path] by mere austerity and faith alone is negated, by declaring faith and austerity accompanied by <s>vidyā</s> as the means of that attainment, [the <s>Śruti</s>] shows that those devoted to other <s>vidyā</s>s too have the same path as the knowers of the <s>Pañcāgni-vidyā</s>.
Similarly, elsewhere too, in the context of the <s>Pañcāgni-vidyā</s>, it is stated: 'Those who know this thus, and those who in the forest meditate on faith and truth (<s>satya</s>).'
Because the word '<s>satya</s>' (truth/reality) applies to <s>Brahman</s> alone without dependence [on anything else].
For that alone is real; other things have only relative reality due to their being ultimately unreal.
And because the knowers of the five fires are included precisely through their 'knowing thus.'
And because of the association with <s>vidyā</s>, this inclusion is appropriate only for those devoted to other <s>vidyā</s>s.

body.text:
#yāvadadhikāramavasthitigadhikārikāṇām# /
saguṇānāṃ vidyāyāṃ cintāṃ kṛtvā nirguṇāyāṃ cintayati /
nirguṇāyāṃ vidyāyāṃ nāpavargaḥ palaṃ bhavitumarhati /
śrutismṛtītihāsapurāṇeṣu viduṣāmapyapāntaratamaḥprabhṛtīnāṃ tattaddehaparigrahaparityāgau śrūyete /
tadapavargaphalatve nopapadyate /
apavṛktasya tadanupapatteḥ /
upapattau vā tallakṣaṇāyogāt /
apunāvṛttirhi tallakṣaṇam /
tena satyāmapi vidyāyāṃ tadanupapatterna mokṣaḥ /
phalaṃ, vidyāyāṃ vibhūtayastu tāstāstasyāḥ phalam /
apunarāvṛttiśrutiḥ punastatpraśaṃsārtheti manyate /
naca 'tāvadevāsya ciraṃ yāvanna vimokṣye 'tha saṃpatsye' iti śruterviduṣo dehapātāvadhipratīkṣāvadvasiṣṭhādīnāmapi prārabdhakarmaphalopabhogapratīkṣeti sāṃpratam /
yena hi karmaṇā vasiṣṭhādīnāmārabdhaṃ śarīraṃ tatpratīkṣā syāt /
tathāca na śarīrāntaraṃ te gṛhṇīyuḥ /
naca tāvadeva ciramityetadapyārjavena ghaṭate /
samarthahetusaṃnidhau kṣepāyogāt /
tasmādetadapi vidyāstutyaiva gamayitavyam /
tasmānnāpavargo vidyāphalam /

children.translated_text: And thus, the prima facie view [is established] by denying <s>apavarga</s>.

children.text: atra ca pākṣikaṃ mokṣahetutvamityāpātataḥ, ahetutvaṃ vetu tu pūrvapakṣatattvam /
children.translated_text: And here, the being a cause of liberation is only tentative at first glance; but the true prima facie position is the denial of [<s>vidyā</s>'s] being a cause [of liberation].
But the established conclusion is: Impelled by <s>Īśvara</s>, who has been pleased through the proper performance of <s>vidyā</s> (meditation) and <s>karma</s> (ritual action),
having completed their cosmic office (<s>adhikāra</s>), these [sages] attain the supreme abode.

body.translated_text:
'#[The fruits of meditation] continue as long as the entitlement lasts, for those who are entitled#.'
Having deliberated upon the <s>saguṇa</s> (qualified) <s>vidyā</s>, [the commentary] now deliberates upon the <s>nirguṇa</s> (unqualified) <s>vidyā</s>.
In the <s>nirguṇa vidyā</s>, <s>apavarga</s> (liberation) ought not to be the result.
For in <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, <s>Itihāsa</s>, and <s>Purāṇa</s>s, even for knowers such as <s>Apāntaratamas</s> and others, the assumption and relinquishing of various bodies is heard.
This is untenable if <s>apavarga</s> were the result.
Because for one who has attained liberation, that [rebirth] is untenable.
Or, if it were tenable, the defining characteristic [of liberation] would not apply.
For the defining characteristic of that [liberation] is non-return.
Therefore, even though <s>vidyā</s> is present, since that [non-return] is untenable, liberation is not the result; rather, the various powers (<s>vibhūti</s>s) are the result of <s>vidyā</s>.
And the <s>Śruti</s> of non-return is again for the purpose of praising that [<s>vidyā</s>] — so they think.
Nor is it proper [to argue] that from the <s>Śruti</s> 'so long alone is the delay until I shall be released; then I shall attain [<s>Brahman</s>],' just as the knower awaits the fall of the body, so too <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and the others await the exhaustion of the fruit of <s>prārabdha karma</s>.
For the <s>karma</s> by which the body of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and the others was commenced — [only] that would await [exhaustion].
And thus they would not assume another body.
Nor does 'so long alone is the delay' work out straightforwardly [in the opponent's view].
Because when a competent cause is present, its effect cannot be denied.
Therefore, this too must be explained as mere praise of <s>vidyā</s>.
Therefore, <s>apavarga</s> (liberation) is not the result of <s>vidyā</s>.

body.text:
nirguṇāyāṃ vidyāyāmapavargalakṣaṇaṃ śrūyamāṇaṃ na stutimātratayā vyākhyāyamucitam /
paurvāparyaparyālocane bhūyasīnāṃ śrutīnāmatraiva tātparyāvadhāraṇāt /
naca yatra tātparyaṃ tadanyathayituṃ yuktam /
uktaṃ hi 'na vidyau paraḥ śabdārtha' iti /
body.translated_text:
In the <s>nirguṇa vidyā</s> (meditation on the qualityless <s>Brahman</s>), the liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) that is heard [as its fruit] should not be explained as mere praise.
Because upon examination of the sequential order (<s>paurvāparya</s>), the majority of <s>Śruti</s>s have their purport ascertained here [in liberation] alone.
And it is not appropriate to explain away that in which the purport [of the texts] lies.
For it has been said: 'There is no meaning of a word higher than its injunctive [force].'

body.text:
naca viduṣamapāntaramaḥprabhṛtīnāṃ tattaddehasaṃtārātsatyāmapi brahmavidyāyāmanirmokṣānna brahmavidyā mokṣasya heturiti sāmpratam /
hetorapi sati pratibandhe kāryānupajano na hetubhāvamapakāroti /
nahi vṛntaphalasaṃyogapratibaddhaṃ gurutvaṃ na patanamajījanaditi pratibandhāpagame tatkurvanna taddhetuḥ /
naca na setupratibandhānāmapāṃ nimnadeśānabhisarpaṇamiti setubhede na nimnamabhisarpanti /
tadvadihāpi vidyākarmārādhanāvarjiteśvaravihitādhikārapadapratibaddhā brahmavidyā yadyapi na muktiṃ dattavatī tathāpi tatparisamāptau pratibandhavigame dāsyati /
yathā hi prārabdhavipākasya karmaṇaḥ prakṣayaṃ pratīkṣamāṇaścaramadehasamutpannabrahmasākṣātkāro 'pi dhriyate 'tha tatprakṣayānmokṣaṃ prāpnoti /
evaṃ prārabdhādhikāralakṣaṇaphalavidyākarmā puruṣo vasiṣṭhādirvidvānapi tatkṣayaṃ pratīkṣamāṇo yugutkrameṇa vā tattaddehaparigrahaparityāgau kurvanmukto 'pyanābhogātmikayā prakhyayā sāṃsārika ava viharati /
body.translated_text:
Nor is it correct [to argue] that — since knowers such as <s>Apāntaratamas</s> and the like transmigrate through successive bodies despite possessing <s>Brahmavidyā</s> (knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>), and hence do not attain liberation — <s>Brahmavidyā</s> is not the cause of liberation.
For even when there is an obstruction to the effect despite the cause being present, the non-production of the effect does not negate the causal status [of the cause].
For it is not the case that gravity — obstructed by the connection of the stalk with the fruit — did not [potentially] cause the fall; and when the obstruction is removed, [gravity] producing the fall is not [thereby proven to be] not the cause.
Nor is it the case that water obstructed by a dam does not flow toward lower ground; [and] when the dam breaks, they do not flow toward lower ground.
Similarly here too, <s>Brahmavidyā</s> — obstructed by the cosmic office (<s>adhikāra</s>) ordained by <s>Īśvara</s>, who has been won over through the propitiation of worship through <s>vidyā</s> and <s>karma</s> — although it has not [yet] bestowed liberation, will bestow it when that [office] is completed and the obstruction is removed.
Just as the direct realization of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahmasākṣātkāra</s>) arising in the final body — while awaiting the exhaustion of the <s>karma</s> whose ripening has already commenced (<s>prārabdhavipāka</s>) — is sustained [without immediately granting liberation], and then upon the exhaustion of that [<s>prārabdha</s>], attains liberation;
so too, the person — such as <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and the like — being a knower, yet engaged in <s>vidyā</s> and <s>karma</s> whose fruit is the cosmic office that has already commenced (<s>prārabdhādhikāra</s>), while awaiting the exhaustion of that [office], whether simultaneously or sequentially assuming and abandoning successive bodies, though liberated, moves about as if in <s>saṃsāra</s> through a manifestation (<s>prakhyā</s>) that does not involve [genuine] engagement.

body.text:
tadidamuktam- #sukṛtapravṛttameva hi te karmāśayamadhikāraphaladānāyeti# /
prārabdhavipākāni tu karmāṇi varjayitvā vyapagatānijñānenaivātivāhitāni /
na caite jātismarā iti /
yo hi paravaśo dehaṃ parityājyate dehāntaraṃ ca nītaḥ pūrvajanmānubhūtasya smarati sa janmavāñjātismarca /
gṛhādiva gṛhāntare svecchayā kāyāntaraṃ saṃcaramāṇo na jātismara ākhyāyataṃ /
#vyudya#vivādaṃ kṛtvā /
vyatirekamāha- #yadi hyupayukte sukṛtpravṛtte#prārabdhavipāke #karmaṇi karmāntara#maprārabdhavipākamiti /
syedātat /
vidyayāvidyādikleśanivṛttau nāvaśyaṃ niḥśeṣasya karmāśayasya nivṛttinaranādibhavaparasparāhitasyāniyatavipākakālasyāsaṅkhyeyatvātkarmaśayasyetyata āha- #na cāvidyādikleśadāhe satīte# /
nahisamāne vināśahetau kasyacidvināśo nāparasyeti śakyaṃ vaditum /
tatkimidānīṃ pravṛttaphalamiti karma vinaśyet /
tathāca na viduṣo vasiṣṭhāderdehadhāraṇetyata āha- #pravṛttaphalasya tu karmaṇa iti# /
tasya tāvadeva ciramiti śrutiprāmāṇādanāgataphalameva karma kṣīyate na pravṛttaphalamityavagamyate /
apica nādhikāravayāṃ sarveṣāmṛṣīṇāmātmatattvajñānaṃ tenāvyāpako 'pyayaṃ parvapakṣa ityāha- #jñānāntareṣu ceti# /
tatkinteṣāmanirmokṣa eva, netyāha- #te paścādaiśvaryakṣaya iti /
nirviṇṇā#viraktāḥ /
#pratisaṃcaraḥ#pralayaḥ /
apica svargādāvanubhavapathamanārohati śabdaikasamadhigamye vicikitsā syādapi mandadhiyāmāmuṣmikaphalatvaṃ prati /
yathā cārthavādaḥ-'ko hi tadveda yadamuṣmiṃlloke 'sti vā na veti' /
advaitajñānaphalatve mokṣasyānubhavasiddhe vicikitsāgandho 'pi nāstītyāha- #pratyakṣaphalatvācceti# /

children.text: advaitatattvasākṣātkāro hi avidyāsamāropitaṃ prapañcaṃ samūlaghātaṃ nighnandhoraṃ saṃsārāṅgaparitāpamupaśamayati puruṣasyetyanuvādapi sphuṭamupapatidraḍhimnaśca śrutirdarśitā /
children.translated_text: For the direct realization of the non-dual reality (<s>advaitatattvasākṣātkāra</s>), destroying root and all the phenomenal world superimposed by <s>avidyā</s>, pacifies the person's terrible burning agony of <s>saṃsāra</s> — even this restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) clearly demonstrates the <s>Śruti</s> that strengthens [this] rational demonstration.
And this is established from the experience of <s>Vāmadeva</s> and the like.

children.text: nanu tattvamasi vartasa iti vākyaṃ kathamanubhavameva dyotayatītyata āha- #nahi tattvamasītyasyeti# /
children.translated_text: Objection: How does the sentence '<s>tattvamasi</s>' ('You are That') indicate experience itself? — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#For this [sentence] "You are That" does not#.'
The meaning is: it is impossible for a statement in the present tense to have a future meaning, and impossible to supply [the elided word] 'dead' (<s>mṛta</s>). //32//

body.translated_text:
This is what was stated: '#For the <s>karmāśaya</s> (latent karmic impressions) that has already begun to operate — that alone [proceeds] for the purpose of yielding the fruit of the cosmic office#.'
But the <s>karma</s>s whose ripening has already commenced — setting those aside — the remaining [<s>karma</s>s] have been carried across (<s>ativāhita</s>) by knowledge alone, having departed.
Nor are these [sages] possessed of memory of past births (<s>jātismara</s>s).
For one who, being under another's control, abandons a body and is led to another body and remembers what was experienced in a former birth — he is one who has [undergone] birth (<s>janmavān</s>) and is a <s>jātismara</s>.
But one who moves from one body to another by his own will — like [going] from one house to another — should not be called a <s>jātismara</s>.
'#Having contended#' (<s>vyudya</s>) — having engaged in debate.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the difference: '#If, when the well-performed [<s>karma</s>]#' — the <s>prārabdhavipāka</s> (whose ripening has commenced) — '#has been enjoyed, another <s>karma</s>#' — i.e., one whose ripening has not yet commenced.
This could be [objected].
When through <s>vidyā</s> the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) such as <s>avidyā</s> and the like are eliminated, not necessarily all the <s>karmāśaya</s> (latent karmic impressions) are eliminated — because of the innumerable [<s>karma</s>s] spanning beginningless existence, whose time of ripening is undetermined, and which are mutually unsupportive — hence [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Nor, when <s>avidyā</s> and the other <s>kleśa</s>s have been burnt#.'
For when the cause of destruction is the same, it cannot be said that some are destroyed and not others.
Then what — would even the <s>karma</s> whose fruit has already commenced be destroyed?
And if so, the knower <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and the like would not sustain a body — hence [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#But the <s>karma</s> whose fruit has already commenced#.'
From the authority of the <s>Śruti</s> 'for that long indeed is the delay' (<s>tasya tāvadeva ciram</s>), it is understood that only the <s>karma</s> whose fruit has not yet commenced is destroyed, not the one whose fruit has commenced.
Moreover, not all <s>ṛṣi</s>s (sages) have knowledge of the Self-reality (<s>ātmatattva</s>) during their period of cosmic office — hence this prima facie view is also non-pervasive — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#And in the case of other kinds of knowledge#.'
Then is there no liberation for them at all? — No, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#They, afterwards, upon the exhaustion of [their] sovereignty#.'
'#Disenchanted#' (<s>nirviṇṇāḥ</s>) — i.e., detached.
'#Return#' (<s>pratisaṃcaraḥ</s>) — i.e., dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>).
Moreover, regarding that which does not ascend to the path of experience — regarding heaven and the like — that which is accessible only through scripture — there might be doubt, even for those of dull intellect, regarding its being a fruit in the other world.
As there is the <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory statement): 'For who knows whether there is [something] in the other world or not?'
But when the fruit of liberation is [constituted by] non-dual knowledge (<s>advaitajñāna</s>), being established through experience, there is not even a trace of doubt — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Because the fruit is directly perceptible#.'

body.text:
#akṣaradhiyāṃ tvavarodhaḥ sāmānyatadbhāvābhyāmaupasadavattaduktam# /
aṅaraviṣayāṇāṃ (?) pratiṣedhadhiyāṃ sarvavedavartinīnāmavarodha upasaṃhāraḥ pratiṣedhasāmānyādakṣarasya tadbhāvapratyabhijñānāt /
ānandādayaḥ pradhānasyetyatrāyamartho yadyapi bhāvarūpeṣu viśeṣaṇeṣu siddhastantryāyatayā ca niṣedharūpeṣviti siddha eva /
tathāpi tasyaivaiṣa prapañco 'vagantavyaḥ /
#nidarśanam /
jāmadagnye 'hīna iti# /
yadyapi śābare dattottaramatrodāharaṇāntaraṃ tathāpi tulyanyāyatayaidapi śakyamudāhartumityudāharaṇāntaraṃ darśitam /
tatra śābaramudāharaṇamastyādhānaṃ yajurvedavihitam-'ya evaṃ vidvānagnimādhatta' iti /
tadaṅgatvena yajurveda eva 'ya evaṃ vidvānvāravantīyaṃ gāyati ya evaṃ vidvānyajñāyajñīyaṃ gāyati ya evaṃ vidvānvāmadevyaṃ gāyati' iti vihitam /
etāni ca sāmāni sāmavedeṣūtpannāni /
tatredaṃ saṃdihyate-kimetāni yatrotpadyante tatrapyainevoccaiṣṭvena svareṇādhāne prayoktavyānyatha yanna viniyujyante tatratyenopāṃśutvena svareṇa 'uccaiḥ sāmnopāṃśu yajuṣā iti śruteḥ /
kiṃ tātprāptam /
utpattividhinaivāpekṣitopāyatvātmanā vihitatvādaṅganāṃ tasyaiva prāthamyāttannibandhana evoccaiḥsvare prāpta ucyate-guṇamukhyavyatikrame tadarthatvānmukhyena vedasaṃyogaḥ /
ayamarthaḥ-utpattividhirguṇo viniyogavidhistu pradhānaṃ, tadanayorvyātikrame virodhe utpattividhyālocanenoccaiṣṭvaṃ viniyogavidhyālocanena copāṃśutvaṃ so 'yaṃ virodho vyatikramastasminvayatikrame mukhyena pradhānena niyujyamānatvarūpeṇa tasya vāravantīyādervedasaṃyogo grāhyo notpadyamānatvena guṇena /
kutaḥ, viniyujyamānatvasya mukhyatvenotpadyamānatvasya guṇatvena tadarthatvādviniyujyamānārthatvādutpadyamānatvasya /
etaduktaṃ bhavati-yadyapyutpattividhāvapi cātūrūpyamasti vidhitvasyāviśeṣāt /
tanmātranāntarīyakatvācca cātabarūpyasya /
tathāpi vākyānāmaidaṃparyaṃ bhidyate /
ekasyaiva vidherutpattiviniyogādhikāraprayogarūpeṣu caturṣu madhye kiñcideva rūpaṃ kenacidvākyenollikhyate yadanyato 'prāptam /

children.text: tatra yadyapi sāmavede sāmāni vihitāni tathāpi tadvākyānāṃ tadutpattimātraparatā viniyogasya yājurvaidikaireva vākyai prāptatvāt /
children.translated_text: Therein, although the <s>Sāman</s>s are enjoined in the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, nevertheless the purport of those sentences is directed only toward their origination, because the assignment has already been obtained through the <s>Yajurvedic</s> sentences alone.

children.text: tathācotpattivākyebhyaḥ samīhitārthāpratilambhādviniyogavākyebhyaśca tadavagatestadarthānyevotpattivākyāni bhavantīti tatra yena vākyena viniyujyante tasyaiva svarasya sādhanatvaṃsaṃsparśino grahaṇaṃ na tu rūpamātrasparśina iti /
children.translated_text: And thus, since the desired purpose is not obtained from the origination-sentences [alone], and since it is understood from the assignment-sentences, the origination-sentences serve the purpose of those [assignment-sentences] — and therefore, the tone (<s>svara</s>) that belongs to the <s>Veda</s> where [the <s>Sāman</s>s] are assigned should be adopted, touching that [<s>Veda</s>'s] tone, and not [the tone] that merely touches the form [of the originating <s>Veda</s>].
The illustration given by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (<s>Śaṅkara</s>) should also be construed in exactly this way.

children.text: udrātṛvedotpannānāṃ mantraṇāmudgātrā prayoge prāpte adhvaryupradānake 'pi puroḍāśe viniyuktatvātpradhānānurodhenādhvaryuṇaiva teṣāṃ prayogo nodrātreti dārṣṭāntike yojayati- #evamihāpīti# //33 //
children.translated_text: When the mantras originating in the <s>Udgātṛ</s>'s <s>Veda</s> (<s>Sāmaveda</s>) are to be employed by the <s>Udgātṛ</s> (chanter) — [but] since they are assigned even in the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (offering-cake) that belongs to the <s>Adhvaryu</s> — in conformity with the principal [assignment], their employment is by the <s>Adhvaryu</s> alone, not the <s>Udgātṛ</s> — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] applies [this] to the illustrated case: '#Similarly here too#.' //33//

body.translated_text:
'#The negation-cognitions (<s>akṣaradhī</s>s), however, should be incorporated, because of commonality and the being-that-nature, like the <s>Upasad</s>s — so it has been stated#.'
The incorporation (<s>avarodha</s>) — i.e., the consolidation — of the negation-cognitions pertaining to <s>Akṣara</s> (<s>Brahman</s>), which belong to all <s>Veda</s>s, is [justified] because of the commonality of negation and because of the recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>) of <s>Akṣara</s> as being of that nature.
The meaning of 'Qualities such as bliss and the like [belong to] the principal [subject]' here is: although this is already established regarding positive (<s>bhāvarūpa</s>) qualifiers through the <s>tantrayukti</s> (principle of extension), the same is established for negation-form [qualifiers] as well.
Nevertheless, this very elaboration should be understood [as being offered for clarity].
'#An illustration.
In [the case of] <s>Jāmadagnya</s> — "lacking" (<s>ahīna</s>)#.'
Although in <s>Śabara</s>'s [commentary] the answer has been given with a different illustration, nevertheless, since the reasoning is the same, this [alternative illustration] too can be cited — hence a different illustration has been shown.
Therein, the illustration in <s>Śabara</s>'s [commentary] is: The establishment of the [sacred] fire (<s>ādhāna</s>) is enjoined by the <s>Yajurveda</s> — 'One who knows thus establishes the fire.'
As subsidiary to that, in the <s>Yajurveda</s> itself, [it is] enjoined: 'One who knows thus sings the <s>Vāravantīya</s> [<s>Sāman</s>]; one who knows thus sings the <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s> [<s>Sāman</s>]; one who knows thus sings the <s>Vāmadevya</s> [<s>Sāman</s>].'
And these <s>Sāman</s>s originate in the <s>Sāmaveda</s>.
Therein this doubt arises: Should these [<s>Sāman</s>s] be employed in the fire-establishment in the loud (<s>uccaiṣṭva</s>) tone — the tone [proper to the <s>Sāmaveda</s>] where they originate — or should they [be employed] in the soft (<s>upāṃśu</s>) tone proper to [the <s>Yajurveda</s>] where they are assigned, from the <s>Śruti</s> 'loudly with <s>Sāman</s>, softly with <s>Yajus</s>'?
What, then, is the prima facie conclusion?
Since the origination-injunction (<s>utpattividhi</s>), having prescribed [them] in the capacity of required means, has the priority of that [origination], the loud tone — grounded in that [origination-injunction] — being arrived at, it is stated: 'When there is a conflict between subsidiary and principal, the connection with the <s>Veda</s> should be [determined] through the principal, because it serves the purpose of that [principal].'
The meaning is this: the origination-injunction (<s>utpattividhi</s>) is the subsidiary, while the assignment-injunction (<s>viniyogavidhi</s>) is the principal. When these two conflict — the loud tone from the perspective of the origination-injunction, and the soft tone from the perspective of the assignment-injunction — this is the conflict, the crossing. In that crossing, the connection of the <s>Vāravantīya</s> and the like with the <s>Veda</s> should be understood through the principal — through their being-assigned nature — not through the subsidiary, through their being-originated nature.
Why? Because the being-originated nature serves the purpose of the being-assigned nature — i.e., the being-originated [exists] for the sake of the being-assigned.
What is being said is this: Although in the origination-injunction too the fourfold character [of injunctions] exists, because of the non-specificity of the injunctive nature,
and because the fourfold character is merely incidental to [the injunctive nature],
nevertheless, the purport (<s>aidaṃparya</s>) of the sentences differs.
Among the four aspects of a single injunction — origination (<s>utpatti</s>), assignment (<s>viniyoga</s>), jurisdiction (<s>adhikāra</s>), and application (<s>prayoga</s>) — only that aspect is highlighted by a particular sentence which is not obtained otherwise.

body.text:
#iyadāmananāt# /
'guhāṃ praviṣṭāvātmānau' ityatra siddho 'pyarthaḥ prapañcyate /
ekatra bhokrabhokrorvedyatā, anyatra bhokroreveti vedyabhedādvidyābheda iti /
naca sṛṣṭirupadadhātītivatpibadapiballakṣaṇāparaṃ pibantāviti netumucitam /
sati mukhyārthasaṃbhave tadāśrayaṇāyogāt /
naca vākyaśeṣānurodhāttadāśrayaṇam /
saṃdehe hi vākyaśeṣānnirṇayo naca mukhyalākṣaṇikagrahaṇaviṣayo viṣayaḥ saṃbhavati, tulyabalatvābhāvāt /
prakaraṇasya ca tato balīyasā vākyena bādhanāt /
tasmādvedyabhedādvidyābheda iti prāpta ucyate-dvāsuparṇatyatra ṛtaṃ pibantāvityatra ca dvitvasaṃkhyotpattau pratīyate tena samānatautsargikī /
pibantāviti dvayoḥ pibantā yā sā bādhanīyā, sā copakramopasaṃhārānurodhena na dvayorapi tu chatrinyāyena lākṣāṇikī vyākhyeyā /
yena hyupakramyate yena copasaṃsthite tadanurodhena madhyaṃ jñeyam /
yathā jāmitvadoṣasaṃkīrtanopakrame tatpratisamādhānopasaṃhāre ca saṃdarbhe madhyapātino viṣṇurūpāṃśu yaṣṭavyo 'jāmitvāyetyādayaḥ pṛthagvidhitvamalabhamānā vidhitvamavivakṣitvārthavādatayā nītāstatkasya hetorekavākyatā hi sādhīyasī vākyabhedāditi /
tathehāpi tadanurodhena pibadapibatsamūhaparaṃ lakṣaṇīyaṃ pibantāvityanena /
tathāca vedyābhedādvidyābheda iti /
apica triṣvapyeteṣu vedāntaṣu prakaraṇatraye 'pi paurvāparyaparyālocanayā paramātmavidyaivāvagamyate /

children.translated_text: If so, how then is the <s>jīva</s> (individual self) introduced [as a topic]? — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#With the intent of expressing identity (<s>tādātmya</s>)#.'

children.text: nāsyāṃ jīvaḥ pratipādyate kintu paramātmano 'bhedaṃ jīvasya darśayitumasāvanūdyate /
children.translated_text: The <s>jīva</s> is not the subject being taught here; rather, for the purpose of showing the non-difference of the <s>jīva</s> from the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self), the former is restated (<s>anūdyate</s>).
And because the <s>Paramātmavidyā</s> has non-difference as its object, there is no occasion for a debate about difference and non-difference.
Therefore, the oneness of the <s>vidyā</s> here is established. //34//

body.translated_text:
'#[The objection of] this-much-ness (<s>iyat</s>) — because of instruction (<s>āmanana</s>)#.'
'The two selves that have entered the cave' (<s>guhāṃ praviṣṭāv ātmānau</s>) — here an already-established meaning is elaborated.
In one [version], the knowability of both the enjoyer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>) and the non-enjoyer is [taught]; in the other, [only] that of the enjoyer — thus, from the difference in what is to be known, there is a difference of <s>vidyā</s>s — this is [the prima facie view].
Nor is it appropriate to construe '<s>pibantau</s>' ('both drinking') — like '<s>sṛṣṭi</s>' meaning 'He created' — as '<s>pibat-apibat</s>' ('one drinking, one not-drinking').
Because when a primary meaning is possible, it is not appropriate to resort to [such interpretation].
Nor [should one resort to it] in conformity with the remainder of the sentence (<s>vākyaśeṣa</s>).
For resolution [comes] from the remainder of the sentence when there is doubt — but a case involving the choice between primary and figurative meaning cannot be a case of doubt, because of the absence of equal force [between the two].
And because the context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>), being weaker, is overridden by the sentence (<s>vākya</s>), which is stronger.
Therefore, from the difference in what is to be known, a difference of <s>vidyā</s>s — this being the prima facie conclusion, it is stated: In '<s>dvā suparṇā</s>' ('two beautiful-winged [birds]') here and in '<s>ṛtaṃ pibantau</s>' ('both drinking the real') there, the dual number is cognized at the origination [of the passage], hence the commonality is natural (<s>autsargikī</s>).
'<s>Pibantau</s>' ('both drinking') — [this] dual [form] should be overridden. And [this overriding], in conformity with the introduction and conclusion (<s>upakramopasaṃhāra</s>), should be interpreted through figurative usage (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) — not [as applying] to both [birds], but by the '<s>chatrī</s>' principle (the 'umbrella-bearer' principle, where the attribute of one is ascribed to the pair), as figurative.
For by that by which [the passage] is introduced and by which it is concluded, the middle should be understood in conformity with that.
Just as, in a context that opens with the mention of the defect of <s>jāmitva</s> (consanguinity) and concludes with its resolution, the [statements] that fall in the middle — '<s>Viṣṇurūpa</s> should be sacrificed for the avoidance of <s>jāmitva</s>' and the like — not obtaining independent injunctive status, are led [to be interpreted] as <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory statements), since 'single-sentence-hood is indeed superior to sentence-splitting.'
Similarly here too, in conformity with the introduction and conclusion, '<s>pibantau</s>' should be taken figuratively as referring to the aggregate of drinking and not-drinking.
And thus, since there is no difference in what is to be known, there is no difference of <s>vidyā</s>s.
Moreover, in all three of these <s>Vedānta</s>s — in all three contexts — upon examination of the sequential order, what is understood is the <s>Paramātmavidyā</s> (knowledge of the Supreme Self) alone.

body.text:
#antarā bhūtagrāmavatsvātmanaḥ# /
kauṣītakeyakaholacākrāyaṇoṣastapraśnopakramayorvidyornaitarantaṇāmnātayoḥ kimasti bhedo na veti viśaye bheda eveti bhrūmaḥ /
kutaḥ-yadyapyubhayatra praśnottarayorabhedaḥ pratīyate, tathāpi tatsyaivaikasya punaḥ śruteraviśeśādānarthakyaprasaṅgādyajatyabhyāsavadbhedaḥ prāptaḥ /
na caikasyaiva tāṇḍināṃ navakṛtva upadeśe 'pi yathā bhedo na bhavati 'sa ātmā tattvamati śvetaketo' ityatra tathehāpyabheda iti yuktam /
bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatu, iti hi tatra śrūyate tenābhedo yujyate /
na ceha tathāsti /
tena yadyapīha vedyābhedo 'vagamyate tathāpyekatra tasyaivāśanāyādimātrātyayopādherupāsanādekatra ca kāryakaraṇavirahopādherupāsanādvidyābheda eveti prāpte pratyucyate /
naitadupāsanāvidhānaparamapi tu vastusvarūpapratipādanaparaṃ praśnaprativacanālocanenopalabhyate /
kimato yadyavam /
etadato bhavati-vidheraprāptaprāpaṇārthatvātprāptāvanupapattiḥ /
vastusvarūpaṃ tu punaḥpunarucyamānamapi na doṣamāvahati śatakṛtvo 'pi hi pathyaṃ vadantyāptāḥ /
viśeṣatastu vedaḥ pitṛbhyāmapyabhyarhitaḥ /

children.translated_text: Nor is there complete repetition (<s>paunaruktyam</s>).
In one [<s>vidyā</s>, the transcendence is of merely] hunger and the like, and in the other, [it is achieved] through the dissolution of the body-mind complex.
Therefore, the <s>vidyā</s> is one, because of recognition [of identity]. //35//

children.text: ubhābhyāmapi vidyābhyāṃ bhinna ātmā pratipādyate iti yo manyate pūrvapakṣaikadeśī taṃ prati sarvāntaratvavirodho darśitaḥ //35 //
children.translated_text: He who thinks that the Self taught by both <s>vidyā</s>s is different — being a partial holder of the prima facie view — against him, the contradiction with [<s>Brahman</s>'s] being the inner Self of everything has been shown. //35//

body.translated_text:
'#[The Self is] the inner [Self] of the aggregate of beings, just as of one's own Self#.'
Regarding the two <s>vidyā</s>s — introduced respectively by the questions of <s>Kahola</s> and <s>Cākrāyaṇa</s> in the <s>Kauṣītaki</s>, and by the question of <s>Uṣasta</s> — both recited in the <s>Antara</s> [section], the question is: is there a difference or not? We say: there is indeed a difference.
Why? Because — even though the non-difference of the question and answer is perceived in both — still, since the hearing again of that very same single [teaching] would be purposeless due to the absence of any distinguishing [content], a difference is warranted, just as in the repetition of '<s>yajati</s>' (he sacrifices).
Nor is it correct [to say] that — just as in the ninefold instruction of the <s>Tāṇḍin</s>s, 'That Self — thou art that, O <s>Śvetaketu</s>' — there is no difference [despite repetition], so too here there is non-difference.
For there [in the <s>Chāndogya</s>], it is heard: 'Please instruct me further, Revered One' — hence the non-difference is justified.
But here there is nothing of the kind.
Therefore, even though the non-difference of the knowable [<s>Brahman</s>] is perceived here, still — since in one [<s>vidyā</s>] the meditation is on that very [<s>Brahman</s>] through the limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) of merely the transcendence of hunger and the like, and in the other through the limiting adjunct of the absence of the body-mind complex — there is indeed a difference of <s>vidyā</s>s — this being the prima facie view, the reply is given:
This [passage] is not intended for the prescription of a meditation but rather for the exposition of the real nature of the entity — as is perceived by examining the question and answer.
What follows from this? This follows: since an injunction has the purpose of bringing about what has not [yet] been brought about, it is inapplicable when [the thing] is already established.
But the real nature of the entity, even when stated again and again, does not produce a defect — for the trustworthy speak what is salutary even a hundred times.
And especially, the <s>Veda</s> is to be honored even more than parents.

children.translated_text: '#If [it be said that] otherwise the difference would be inexplicable — [we say:] no, because it is like another instruction#.'
The true intent of the prima facie view of this [<s>sūtra</s>] has been shown.
The rest is easy [to understand]. //36//

body.text:
#vyatihāro virsiṣanti hītaravat# /
utkṛṣṭasya nikṛṣṭarūpāpatternobhayatrobhayarūpānucintanam /
api tu nikṛṣṭe jīva utkṛṣṭarūpābhedacintanam /
evaṃ hi nikṛṣṭa utkṛṣṭo bhavatīti prāptam /
evaṃ prāpta ucyate-itaretarānuvādenetaretarūpavidhānādubhayatrābhayacintanaṃ vidhīyate /
itarathā tu yo 'haṃ so 'sāvityetāvadevocyeta /
jīvātmānamanūdyeśvaratvamasya vidhīyeta /
na tvīśvarasya jīvātmatvaṃ yo 'sau so 'hamiti /
yathā tattvamasītyatra /
tasmādubhayarūpamubhayatrādhyānāyopadiśyate /

children.text: nanvevamutkṛṣṭasya nikṛṣṭaprasaṅga ityuktaṃ tatkimidānīṃ saguṇe brahmaṇyupāsyamāne 'sya vastuto nirguṇasya nikṛṣṭatā bhavati /
children.translated_text: But [one might object:] as stated, this would lead to the descent of the exalted [<s>Brahman</s>] into the lowly — to this [the reply is:] Does <s>Brahman</s>, which is in reality without qualities (<s>nirguṇa</s>), actually become lowly when meditated upon as <s>saguṇa</s> (qualified)?

children.text: kasmaicitphalāya tathā dhyānamātraṃ vidhīyatena tvasya nikṛṣṭatāmāpādayatīti cedihāpi vyatihārānucintanamātramupadiśyate phalāya na ti nikṛṣṭatā bhavatyutkṛṣṭasya /
children.translated_text: Meditation is prescribed for the sake of some fruit — it does not [actually] bring about the lowliness of [<s>Brahman</s>]. And if here too, the interchange-meditation is merely prescribed for the sake of a fruit, the exalted [<s>Brahman</s>] does not [actually] become lowly.
But the strengthening of identity — which is the residual [teaching] of the interchange — we do not disregard.

Just as the instruction of qualities such as '<s>satyakāma</s>' (one whose desires are true) and the like '#establishes the attributes of <s>Īśvara</s>#' — so it is established that the meditation on both natures in both [<s>Brahman</s> and <s>jīva</s>] is [prescribed]. //37//

body.translated_text:
'#The interchange — [we say that the text] intends [both], because it is like the other [case]#.'
The objection is: because of the descent of the exalted [<s>Brahman</s>] into the form of the lowly [<s>jīva</s>], the meditation on both forms in both [<s>Brahman</s> and <s>jīva</s>] should not [be prescribed].
Rather, only the meditation on the identity of the exalted form in the lowly <s>jīva</s> [should be prescribed].
For thus, the lowly becomes the exalted — this is the prima facie view.
This being the prima facie view, the reply is given: Through the restatement of each in the other and the prescription of each other's form, the meditation on both forms in both [<s>Brahman</s> and <s>jīva</s>] is prescribed.
Otherwise, only this much would be said: 'I am that' (<s>yo 'haṃ so 'sāv</s>).
The <s>jīva</s> would be restated, and its <s>Īśvara</s>-hood would be prescribed.
But the [reverse] — that <s>Īśvara</s> has <s>jīva</s>-hood — 'He who is that is I' (<s>yo 'sau so 'ham</s>) — [would not be stated].
As in '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' ('That thou art').
Therefore, both forms are taught in both for the purpose of meditation.

body.text:
#saiva hi satyādayaḥ# /
tadvai tadetadeva tadāsa satyameva sa yo haitanmahadyakṣaṃ prathamajaṃ veda satyaṃ brahmeti jayatīmāṃllokāñjita ityasāvasadya evametanmahadyakṣaṃ prathamajaṃ veda satyaṃ brahmeti satyaṃ hyeva brahma /
pūrvoktasya hṛdayākhyasya brahmaṇaḥ satyamityupāsanamena saṃdarbheṇa vidhīyate /
taditi hṛdayākhyaṃ brahmaikena tadā parāmṛśati /
etadeveti vakṣyamāṇaṃ prakārāntaramasya parāmṛśati /
tattādāgre āsa babhūva /
kiṃ tadityata āha-satyameva /
sacca mūrtaṃ tyaccāmūrtaṃ ca sattyam /
tadupāsakasya phalamāha-sa yo haitamiti /
yaḥ prathamajaṃ yakṣaṃ pūjyaṃ veda /
kathaṃ vedetyata āha-satyaṃ brahmetīti /
sa jayatīmān lokān /
kiñca jito vaśīkṛta inuśabda itthaṃśabdasyārthe vartate /
vijetavyatvena buddhisaṃnihitaṃ śatruṃ parāmṛśati-asāviti /
asadbhavennaśyet /
uktamartha nigamayati-ya evametaditi /
evaṃ vidvānkasmājjayatītyata āha-satyameva yasmādbrahmeti /
atastadupāsanāt phalotpādo 'pi satya ityarthaḥ /
tadyattatsatyaṃ kimatau /
atrāpi tatpadābhyāṃ rūpaprakārai parāmṛṣṭau /
kasmiṃnnālambane tadupāsanīyamityata uttaram-sa ādityo ya eṣa ityādinā tasyopaniṣadaharahamiti /
hanti pāpmānaṃ jahāti ca ya evaṃ vedetyantena /
upaniṣat rahasyaṃ nāma /
tasya nirvacanaṃ-hanti pāpmānaṃ jahāti ceti /
hanterjahātervā rūpametat /
tathāca nirvacanaṃ kurvanphalaṃ pāpahānimāheti /
tamimaṃ viṣayamāha bhāṣyakāraḥ- #yo vai haitamiti /
sanāmākṣaropāsanāmiti# /
tathāca śrutiḥ-'tadetadakṣaraṃ satyamiti sa ityekamakṣaraṃ tītyekamakṣaraṃ yamityekamakṣaraṃ prathamottame akṣare satyaṃ madhyato 'nṛtaṃ tadetadanṛmubhayataḥ satyena parigṛhītaṃ satyabhūyameva bhavati naivaṃvidvāṃsamanṛtaṃ hinasti' iti /
tītīkārānubandha uccāraṇārthaḥ /
niranubandhastakāro draṣṭavyaḥ /
atra hi prathamottame akṣare satyaṃ mṛtyurūpābhāvāt /
madhyato madhye 'nṛtamanṛtaṃ hi mṛtyuḥ /
mṛtyvanṛtayostakārasāmyāt /
tadetadanṛtaṃ mṛtyurūpamubhayataḥ satyena parigṛhītam /
antarbhāvitaṃ satyarūpābhyām /
ato 'kiñcitkaraṃ tatsatyabhūyameva satyabāhulyameva bhavati /
śeṣamatirohitārtham /
seyaṃ satyavidyāyāḥ sanāmākṣayopāsanatā /
yadyapi tadyatsatyamiti prakṛtānukarṣeṇābedaḥ pratīyate tathāpi phalabhedena bhedaḥ sādhyabhedeneva nityakāmyadiṣayordarśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeta yāvajjīvaṃ darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajeteti śāstrayoḥ satyapyanubandhābhede bheda iti prāpte pratyucyate-ekaiveyaṃ vidyā tatsatyamiti prakṛtaparāmarśādabhedena pratyabhijñānāt /
naca phalabhedaḥ /
tasyopaniṣadaharahamiti tasyaiva yadaṅgāntaraṃ rahasyanāmnopāsanaṃ tatpraśaṃsārthor'thavādo 'yaṃ na phalavidhiḥ /
yadi punarvidyāvidhāvadhikāraśravaṇābhāvāttatkalpanāyāmārthavādikaṃ phalaṃ kalpyeta tato jāteṣṭāvivāgṛhyamāṇaviśeṣatayā saṃvalitādhikārakalpanā tataśca samastārthavādikaphalayuktamekamevopāsanamiti siddham /
parakīyaṃ vyākhyānamupanyasyati- #kecitpunariti# /

children.translated_text: The <s>Vājasaneyaka</s> [passage] too pertains to the imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>) and the sun (<s>Āditya</s>), and the <s>Chāndogya</s> too — hence, because of the non-difference of the object of meditation, there is non-difference [of the <s>vidyā</s>].

children.text: tataśca vājasaneyoktānāṃ satyādīnāmupasaṃhāra ityatrārthe saiva hi satyādaya iti sūtraṃ vyākhyātaṃ tadetaddūṣayati- #tanna sādhviti /
children.translated_text: And thus, the incorporation of the [qualities] <s>satya</s> and the rest stated in the <s>Vājasaneyaka</s> [follows] — in this sense, the <s>sūtra</s> 'These are indeed the same — <s>satya</s> and the rest' has been explained [by others]. [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes this: '#That is not correct#.'
'#This [<s>vidyā</s>] has a connection with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> sacrifice through the <s>Udgītha</s>#' — thus.

Even when the ritual connection is non-different, because of the difference of [what is] to be accomplished (<s>sādhya</s>), there is difference — hence, because of the difference of <s>vidyā</s>s, there is no incorporation. //38//

body.translated_text:
'#These are indeed the same — <s>satya</s> and the rest#.'
'That indeed — that very thing — was <s>Satya</s> (the Real). He who knows this great adorable being (<s>yakṣa</s>), the first-born, as "<s>Brahman</s> is <s>Satya</s>" — he conquers these worlds; conquered is [his enemy]' — this is what the opponent cites.
The meditation on the previously mentioned <s>Brahman</s> called '<s>hṛdaya</s>' (heart) as '<s>Satya</s>' (the Real) is prescribed by this passage.
By the word '<s>tat</s>' (that), the <s>Brahman</s> called '<s>hṛdaya</s>' is referred back to.
By '<s>etad eva</s>' (this very), a different aspect of that [<s>Brahman</s>] — to be stated [subsequently] — is referred to.
'That was then — [it] existed (<s>āsa</s>).'
What was that? — to this [the text] says: '<s>Satya</s>' (the Real) — 'indeed.'
'<s>Sat</s>' is the gross (<s>mūrta</s>), '<s>ti</s>' is the subtle (<s>amūrta</s>) — [together] '<s>sattya</s>' (<s>Satya</s>).
The fruit for the meditator is stated: 'He who knows this' — thus.
Who knows the first-born adorable being (<s>yakṣa</s>) — the venerable [<s>Brahman</s>].
How does he know [it]? — to this [the text] says: 'As "<s>Brahman</s> is <s>Satya</s>."'
He conquers these worlds.
Moreover, conquered (<s>jita</s>) — made subservient. The '<s>inu</s>'-suffix has the sense of the word '<s>ittham</s>' (thus).
The enemy — present in the mind as something to be conquered — is referred to by '<s>asau</s>' (that one).
[He] would perish through the mode of non-existence (<s>asat</s>).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] concludes the stated meaning: 'He who knows thus' — thus.
Such a knower — why does he conquer? To this [the text] says: 'Because <s>Brahman</s> is indeed <s>Satya</s>.'
Therefore, from meditating on that [<s>Brahman</s> as <s>Satya</s>], the production of fruit too is real (<s>satya</s>) — this is the meaning.
Now, [one asks:] what is that <s>Satya</s>? What [does it amount to]?
Here too, the two forms are referred back to by the two words '<s>tat</s>' (that).
On what substrate should that [<s>Satya</s>] be meditated? — to this the answer [is given] by '<s>sa ādityo ya eṣa</s>' ('That is the sun, the one here') and so on, up to 'its <s>Upaniṣad</s> is "day after day."'
'It destroys evil and abandons [it] — he who knows thus' — [thus ending the passage].
'<s>Upaniṣad</s>' means 'secret teaching' — that is [its] name.
Its etymology is: 'it destroys evil and abandons [it].'
This is the form of [the verbal roots] '<s>han</s>' (to destroy) and '<s>hā</s>' (to abandon).
And thus, while giving the etymology, [the text] states the fruit — namely, the destruction of evil.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states this subject-matter: '#He who indeed knows this#' — thus. '#The meditation together with the name and the syllable#' — thus.
And the <s>Śruti</s> [says:] 'That indeed is the imperishable <s>Satya</s>: "<s>sa</s>" is one syllable, "<s>ti</s>" is one syllable, "<s>yam</s>" is one syllable. The first and last syllables are <s>satya</s> (real); in the middle is <s>anṛta</s> (unreal). This <s>anṛta</s> is enclosed on both sides by <s>satya</s>. It becomes predominantly <s>satya</s>. The <s>anṛta</s> does not harm one who knows thus.'
The '<s>ī</s>' appended to '<s>ti</s>' is for the purpose of pronunciation.
The consonant '<s>t</s>' without the appendage is to be considered.
For here, the first and last syllables are <s>satya</s> — because of the absence of the form of death [in them].
In the middle is <s>anṛta</s> — [meaning] <s>anṛta</s> (unreal), for <s>anṛta</s> is death.
Because of the similarity between death/<s>anṛta</s> and the consonant '<s>t</s>.'.
That <s>anṛta</s> in the form of death is enclosed on both sides by <s>satya</s>.
[It is] contained within [the syllables] having the form of <s>satya</s>.
Therefore, being powerless, it becomes predominantly <s>satya</s> — [meaning] it is indeed predominantly <s>satya</s>.
The rest is of transparent meaning.
This is the character of the <s>Satya-vidyā</s> as a meditation together with the name and syllable.
Even though through the contextual reference '<s>tad yat tat satyam</s>' (now, that which is <s>Satya</s>), non-difference is perceived, nevertheless — because of the difference of fruit — a difference [of <s>vidyā</s>s] is [warranted]. For just as, despite the non-difference of the ritual connection, the [two scriptures about] the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> — 'One who desires heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>' and 'One should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> as long as one lives' — despite the non-difference of the ritual connection, differ [as nityakāmya vs. nityakarma]. This being the prima facie view, the reply is given: this <s>vidyā</s> is one alone — because of the recognition [of identity] through the contextual reference '<s>tat satyam</s>'.
Nor is there a difference of fruit.
The passage 'its <s>Upaniṣad</s> is "day after day"' — this secondary portion, being the meditation on the name through the secret teaching — is a laudatory statement (<s>arthavāda</s>) for praising [the <s>vidyā</s>], not a prescription of the fruit.
But if — because of the absence of hearing the qualification of the eligible person in the <s>vidyā</s>-injunction — the <s>arthavādika</s> (laudatory) fruit were postulated, then — just as in the <s>Jāteṣṭi</s> [sacrifice], where — in the absence of an apprehended distinction — the postulation of a combined qualification is [made], so here too [the postulation of a] combined <s>arthavādika</s> fruit [is made] — and thus it is established that this is a single meditation endowed with the aggregate of all <s>arthavādika</s> fruits.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] presents the interpretation of others: '#Some, however#' — thus.

body.text:
#kāmādītaratra tatra cāyatanādibhyaḥ# /
chāndogyavājasaneyavidyayoryadyapi saguṇanirguṇatvena bhedaḥ /
tathāhi chāndogye-'atha ya ihātmānamanuvidya vrajanti etāṃśca satyānkāmān' ityātmavatkāmānāmapi vedyatvaṃ śrūyate /
vājasaneye tu nirguṇameva paraṃ brahmopadiśyate 'vimokṣāya brūhi' iti tathāpi tayoḥ parasparaguṇopasaṃhāraḥ /
nirguṇāyāṃ tāvadvidyāyāṃ brahmastutyarthameva saguṇavidyāsaṃbandhiguṇopasaṃhāraḥ saṃbhavī /
saguṇāyāṃ ca yadyapyādhyānāya na vaśitvādiguṇopasaṃhārasaṃbhavaḥ /
nahi nirguṇāyāṃ vidyāyāmādhāyātavyatvenaite coditā yenātrādhyeyatvena saṃbadhyerannapi tu satyakāmādiguṇanāntarīyakatvenaiteṣāṃ prāptirityupasaṃhāra ucyate /

children.text: evaṃ vyavasthita eṣa saṃkṣepo 'dhikaraṇārthasya-sāmyabāhulye 'pyekatrākāśādhāratvasyāparatra cākāśatādātmyasya śravaṇādbhede vidyayorna parasparaguṇopasaṃhāra iti pūrvapakṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus is this summary of the topic established: Even though there is extensive similarity, because of the hearing in one [<s>vidyā</s>] of [<s>Brahman</s> as] the substrate of <s>ākāśa</s> (space) and in the other of [<s>Brahman</s>'s] identity with <s>ākāśa</s> — [the prima facie view is that] because of the difference of the <s>vidyā</s>s, there is no mutual incorporation of qualities.

children.text: rāddhāntastu sarvasāmyamevobhayatrāpyātmopadeśādākāśaśabdenaikatrātmokto 'nyatra ca daharākāśādhāraḥ sa evokta iti sarvasāmyādbrahmaṇyubhayatrāpi sarvaguṇopasaṃhāraḥ /
children.translated_text: But the established conclusion is: there is indeed complete similarity in both, because in both the Self is taught. By the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' in one, the Self is spoken of; and in the other, the <s>daharākāśa</s> (small space [of the heart]) — its substrate is that very same [Self]. Therefore, because of the complete similarity, the incorporation of all qualities of <s>Brahman</s> in both [<s>vidyā</s>s is established].
But even when the <s>vidyā</s>s differ by virtue of [the distinction between] <s>saguṇa</s> and <s>nirguṇa</s>, the arrangement of the incorporation of qualities has been shown.
Therefore, everything is clear. //39//

body.translated_text:
'#Desire and the like [are incorporated] from the one into the other, and in that [<s>vidyā</s> too], because of abode and the like#.'
Even though the <s>Chāndogya</s> and <s>Vājasaneyaka</s> <s>vidyā</s>s differ because of [the distinction between] <s>saguṇa</s> (qualified) and <s>nirguṇa</s> (unqualified) —
for thus, in the <s>Chāndogya</s> it is heard: 'Those who, having known the Self here, depart — and these true desires' — the knowability of the desires too, like the Self, is heard.
But in the <s>Vājasaneyaka</s>, only the unqualified supreme <s>Brahman</s> is taught: 'Tell me for the sake of liberation.' Nevertheless, there is mutual incorporation of qualities between the two.
To begin with, in the <s>nirguṇa</s> <s>vidyā</s>, the incorporation of qualities connected with the <s>saguṇa</s> <s>vidyā</s> is possible only for the purpose of praising <s>Brahman</s>.
And in the <s>saguṇa</s> [<s>vidyā</s>], even though the incorporation of qualities such as sovereignty (<s>vaśitva</s>) and the like is not possible for [actual] meditation —
for these are not enjoined in the <s>nirguṇa</s> <s>vidyā</s> as [things] to be meditated upon, such that they could be connected here as [things] to be meditated upon — rather, their attainment is a necessary consequence of the attributes such as '<s>satyakāma</s>' (one whose desires are true) and the like — hence the incorporation is stated [in that sense].

body.text:
#ādāradalopaḥ# /
asti vaiśvānaravidyāyāṃ tadupāsakasyātithibhyaḥ pūrvabhojanam /
tena yadyapīyamupāsanāgocarā na cintā sākṣāttathāpi tatsaṃbaddhaprathamabhojanasaṃbandhādasti saṃgatiḥ /
vicāragocaraṃ darśayati- #chāndogye vaiśvānaravidyāṃ prakṛtyeti# /
vicāraprayojakaṃ saṃdehamāha-- #kiṃ bhojanalopa iti# /
atra pūrvapakṣābhāvena saṃśayamākṣipati- #tadyadbhaktamiti bhaktāgamanasaṃyogaśravaṇāditi# /
uktaṃ khalvetatprathama eva tantre 'padakarmāprayojakaṃ nayanasya parārthatvāt' ityanena /
yathā somakrayārthānīyamānaikahāyanīsaptamapadapāṃśugrahaṇamaprayojakaṃ na punarekahāyanyā nayanaṃ prayojayati /
tatkasya hetoḥ /
somakrayeṇa tannayanasya prayuktatvāttadupajīvitvātsaptamapadapāṃśugrahaṇasyeti /
tathehāpi bhojanārthabhaktāgamanasaṃyogātprāṇāhuterbhojanābhāve bhaktaṃ pratyaprayojakatvamiti nāsti pūrvapakṣa ityapūrvapakṣamidamadhikaraṇamityarthaḥ /
pūrvapakṣamākṣipya samādhatte- #evaṃ prāpte, na lupyeteti tāvadāha# /
tāvacchabdaḥ siddhāntaśaṅkānirākaraṇārthaḥ /
pṛcchati- #kasmāt /
uttaram-ādarāt# /
tadeva sphorayati- #tathāhīti# /
jābālā hi śrāvayanti-'pūrvo 'tithibhyo 'śrīyāt' iti /
aśrīyāditi ca prāṇāgnihotrapradhānaṃ vacaḥ /
'yathā hi śrudhitā bālā mātaraṃ paryupāsate /
evaṃ sarvāṇi bhūtānyagnihotramupāsate' iti vacanādagnihotrasyātithīnbhūtāni pratyupajīvyatvena śravaṇāttadekavākyatayehāpi pūrvo 'tithibhyo 'śrīyāditi prāṇāhutipradhānaṃ lakṣyate /
tadevaṃ sati 'yathāha vai svayamahutvāgnihotraṃ parasya juhuyādityevaṃ tat' ityatithibhojanasya prāthamyaṃ ninditvā #svāmibhojanaṃ#svāminaḥ prāṇāgnihotraṃ prathamaṃ prāpayantī prāṇāgnihotrādaraṃ karoti /
nanvātithitāmeṣā śrutiḥ prāṇahutiṃ kintu svāmibhojanapakṣa eva nābhojane 'pītyata āha- #yā hi na prāthamyalopaṃ sahate natarāṃ sā prāthamyavato 'gnihotrasya lopaṃ saheteti manyate# /
īdṛśaḥ khalvayamādaraḥ prāṇāgnihotrasya dharmiṇaḥ prāthamyadharmalopamapi na sahate śrutistadāsyāḥ kaiva kathā dharmilopaṃ sahata ityarthaḥ /
pūrvapakṣākṣepamanubhāṣya dūṣayati- #nanu bhojanārthā iti# /
yathā hi kauṇḍapāyināmayanagate agnihotre prakaraṇāntarānnaiyamikāgnihotrādbhinne dravyadevatārūpadharmāntararahitatayā tadākāṅkṣe sādhyasādṛśyena naiyamikāgnihotrasamānanāmatayā taddharmātideśena rūpadharmāntaraprāptirevaṃ prāṇāgnihotre 'pi naiyamikāgnihotragatapayaḥprabhṛtiprāptau bhojanāgatabhaktadravyatā vidhīyate /
na caitāvatā bhojanasya prayojakatvam /
uktametadyathā bhojanakālātikramātprāṇāgnihotrasya na bhojanaprayuktatvamiti /
na caikadeśadravyatayottarārdhātsviṣṭakṛte samavadyatītivadaprayojakatvamekadeśadravyasādhanasyāpi prayojakatvāt /
yathā jāghanyā patnīḥ saṃyājayantīti patnīsaṃyājānāṃ jāghanyekadeśadravyajuṣāṃ jāghanīprayojakatvam /
sa hi nāmāprayojako bhavati yasya prayojakagrahaṇamantareṇārtho na jñāyate /
yathā na prayojakapuroḍāśagrahaṇamantareṇottarārdhaṃ jñātuṃ śakyam /
śakyaṃ tu jāghanīvadbhaktaṃ jñātum /
tasmādyathā jāghanyantareṇāpi paśūpādānaṃ paraprayuktaśūpajīvanaṃ vā khaṇḍaśo māṃsavikrayiṇo muṇḍādivadākṛtirūpādīyate /
body.translated_text:
'#The non-omission, because of regard (<s>ādara</s>)#.'
In the <s>Vaiśvānara-vidyā</s>, the practitioner's eating before the guests is [prescribed].
Therefore, even though this inquiry does not directly pertain to the meditation, nevertheless, because of its connection with the prior-eating associated with that [meditation], there is relevance.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] shows the subject of inquiry: '#In the <s>Chāndogya</s>, having taken up the <s>Vaiśvānara-vidyā</s>#' — thus.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the doubt that motivates the inquiry: '#Whether the eating is omitted#' — thus.
Here, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises the doubt by [presenting] the absence of a prima facie objection: '#That which is food (<s>bhakta</s>) — because of the hearing of the conjunction with the arrival of food#' — thus.
This has indeed been stated in the first system (<s>Prathamatantra</s>) itself through [the principle] 'An accessory action is not the instigator [of another], because the bringing [of the material] serves another purpose.'
Just as the taking up of dust at the seventh step of the one-year-old [cow] being brought for the <s>Soma</s>-purchase is not the instigator [of a new rite] — it does not cause the bringing of the one-year-old cow [as a separate purpose].
For what reason?
Because the bringing of that [cow] is instigated by the <s>Soma</s>-purchase, and the seventh-step dust-taking is dependent upon that [bringing].
Likewise here too, because of the conjunction of the <s>prāṇāhuti</s> (oblation to the vital breath) with the arrival of food for the purpose of eating, [the <s>prāṇāhuti</s>] is not the instigator [of eating] when eating is absent — hence there is no prima facie objection — the meaning is that this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic) is without a prima facie view.
Having raised and [then] resolved the prima facie view, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states: '#When this [prima facie view] has been arrived at, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] first says: "it should not be omitted"#.'
The word '<s>tāvat</s>' (first) is for the purpose of removing a doubt about the established conclusion.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] asks: '#For what reason?#'
The answer: '#Because of regard (<s>ādara</s>)#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] elaborates that very [point]: '#For thus#' — thus.
For the <s>Jābāla</s>s declare: 'One should eat before the guests' (<s>pūrvo 'tithibhyo 'śrīyāt</s>).
And the word '<s>aśrīyāt</s>' (one should eat) is a statement whose principal [subject] is the <s>prāṇāgnihotra</s> (oblation to the vital breaths).
'Just as hungry children sit around their mother, so all beings attend upon the <s>Agnihotra</s>' — because of this statement, since the <s>Agnihotra</s> is heard as being depended upon by beings as guests, by syntactic unity with that [statement], here too 'one should eat before the guests' is indicated as having the <s>prāṇāhuti</s> (oblation to the vital breath) as its principal [subject].
This being so, having censured the priority of guest-feeding — 'It is as if one, without having offered one's own <s>Agnihotra</s>, were to offer another's' — '#the eating of the owner#' — the owner's <s>prāṇāgnihotra</s>, by making [it] first, shows regard for the <s>prāṇāgnihotra</s>.
But [one might object:] this <s>Śruti</s> enjoins the <s>prāṇāhuti</s> [only] in the context of hospitality, [specifically] in the case where the owner does eat — not even in the case of non-eating. To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#For that [<s>Śruti</s>] which does not tolerate the omission of priority, all the more so does it not tolerate the omission of the <s>Agnihotra</s> which possesses [that] priority — so it is understood#.'
Such indeed is this regard: the <s>Śruti</s> about the <s>prāṇāgnihotra</s> does not tolerate even the omission of the attribute of priority of the <s>dharmin</s> (the qualified entity [i.e., the <s>prāṇāgnihotra</s>]) — how much less would it tolerate the omission of the <s>dharmin</s> itself? — this is the meaning.
Having restated the prima facie objection, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes [it]: '#But [one might say:] because it serves the purpose of eating#' — thus.
Just as, for the <s>Kauṇḍapāyin</s>s, when the <s>Agnihotra</s> — which is incidental to a context — differs from the regular (<s>naiyamika</s>) <s>Agnihotra</s> in being devoid of specific attributes such as [particular] materials and deities, and — having a need for [those attributes] due to its similarity with what is to be accomplished — receives, by virtue of its having the same name as the regular <s>Agnihotra</s>, the transfer (<s>atideśa</s>) of the attributes of the regular <s>Agnihotra</s>, and thereby obtains [specific] attribute-forms — so too, in the <s>prāṇāgnihotra</s>, when milk and the like [which belong to] the regular <s>Agnihotra</s> are obtained [by transfer], the materiality of food (<s>bhakta</s>) — which belongs to the [actual] eating — is [separately] enjoined.
But this does not thereby make eating the instigator [of the <s>prāṇāgnihotra</s>].
This has been stated: just as the <s>prāṇāgnihotra</s> is not instigated by eating because of the lapse of the mealtime, [so too here].
Nor is [eating] non-instigating merely because of being a one-part material, [as in the case] 'he cuts off from the latter half for the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>' — because even a means that is a one-part material can be an instigator.
Just as the <s>Jāghanī</s> [cow] — which serves as a one-part material — instigates the <s>patnīsaṃyāja</s>s (wives' offerings): 'he offers the <s>patnīsaṃyāja</s>s at the last [cow]' — the <s>Jāghanī</s> is the instigator of the <s>patnīsaṃyāja</s>s which partake of the one-part material of the <s>Jāghanī</s>.
For that alone is non-instigating whose purpose cannot be known without the apprehension of the instigator.
Just as the latter half cannot be known without the apprehension of the instigating <s>puroḍāśa</s>.
But food, like the <s>Jāghanī</s>, can be known [independently].
Therefore, just as even without the <s>Jāghanī</s>, the taking up of an animal — whether instigated by another or as a dependent subsidiary (<s>upajīvana</s>) — or the form [of the animal] such as hornlessness (<s>muṇḍa</s>) and the like is adopted from a meat-seller in portions,

children.translated_text: so too food can be adopted [independently].

children.text: tasmānna bhojanasya lope prāṇāgnihotralopa iti manyate pūrvapakṣī /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the prima facie view holds that in the omission of eating, there is no omission of the <s>prāṇāgnihotra</s>.
But the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>'s [mention of] adopting with water is for the purpose of indicating the indispensability [of the <s>prāṇāgnihotra</s>]. //40//

#upasthite 'tastadvacanāt# /
taddhomīyamiti hi vacana kimapi saṃnihitadravyaṃ home viniyuṅkte tadaḥ sarvanāmnaḥ saṃnihitāvagamamantareṇābhidhānāparyavasānāttadanena svābhidhānaparyavasānāya tadyadbhaktaṃ prathamamāgacchediti saṃnihitamapekṣya nirvartitavyam /
tacca saṃnihitaṃ bhaktaṃ bhojanārthamityuttarārdhātsviṣṭakṛte samavadyatītivanna bhaktaṃ vāpo vā dravyāntaraṃ vā prayoktumarhati /
jāghanyāstvavayavabhedasya nāgnīṣomīyapaśvadhīnaṃ nirūpaṇaṃ svatantrasyāpi tasya sūnāsthasya darśanāttasmādastyetasya jāghanīto viśeṣaḥ /
yaccoktaṃ codakaprāptadravyabādhayā bhaktadravyavidhānamiti /
tadayuktam /
vidhyuddeśagatasyāgnihotranāmnastathābhāvādārthavādikasya tu siddhaṃ kiñcitsādṛśyamupādāya stāvakatvenopapatterna tadbhāvaṃ vidhātumarhatītyāha- #na cātra prākṛtāgnihotradharmaprāptiriti# /
api cāgnihotrasya codakato dharmaprāptāvabhyupagamyamānāyāṃ bahutaraṃ prāptaṃ bādhyate /
naca saṃbhave bādhanicayo nyāpyaḥ /
kṛṣṇalacarau khalvagatyā prāptabādho 'bhyupeyata ityāha-taddharmaprāptau cābhyupagamyamānāyāmiti /

yata evoktena krameṇātideśābhāvo 'ta eva sāṃpādikatvamagnihotrāṅgānām /
tatprāptau tu sāṃpādikatvaṃ nopapadyeta /
kāminyāṃ kila kucavadanādyasatā cakravākanalinādirūpeṇa saṃpādyate /
na tu nadyāṃ cakravākādaya eva cakravākādinā saṃpādyante /
ato 'pyavagacchāmo na codakaprāptiriti /

children.translated_text: But as for the observation of regard (<s>ādara</s>) [for the <s>prāṇāgnihotra</s>] — that is for the purpose of enjoining priority in the case where eating does [occur].

children.text: yasminpakṣe dharmānavalopastasmindharmiṇo 'pi na tvetāvatā dharminityatā sidhyatīti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the case (<s>pakṣa</s>) where the attribute [of priority] is not omitted, even the <s>dharmin</s> (the qualified entity [i.e., the <s>prāṇāgnihotra</s>]) is not [omitted] — but this does not thereby establish the permanence of the <s>dharmin</s> — this is the intent.

children.text: nanvatithibhojanottarakālatā svāmibhojanasya vihiteti kathamasau bādhyata ityata āha- #nāsti vacanasyātibhāraḥ# /
children.translated_text: But [one might object:] since the posteriority of the owner's eating to the guest's eating is enjoined, how is it overridden? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#The statement does not have excessive weight#.'
The meaning is: the specific rule (<s>viśeṣaśāstra</s>) does not have excessive weight [i.e., difficulty] in overriding the general rule (<s>sāmānyaśāstra</s>). //41//

body.translated_text:
'#When [the material] is present, that is to be used, because of the statement regarding that#.'
For the statement 'that is to be offered' (<s>tad dhomīyam</s>) assigns some proximate material to the oblation. Since the pronoun '<s>tad</s>' (that) cannot terminate its denotation without the apprehension of something proximate, [the statement] must be carried out with reference to [what is] proximate — [namely,] 'that which is the food that arrives first' (<s>tad yad bhaktaṃ prathamam āgacchet</s>).
And that proximate [material] — being food intended for eating — is not [a case where one can say] 'he cuts off from the latter half for the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>' [and hence use] food, water, or some other material.
As for the <s>Jāghanī</s> — the determination of the division of [its] parts is not dependent on the <s>Āgnīṣomīya</s> animal, since that [<s>Jāghanī</s>] is seen to be independent even at the slaughter-post. Therefore, there is a difference from the <s>Jāghanī</s> [case].
And as for what was said — that [the opponent proposes] an enjoining of food-materiality by overriding the material obtained through the injunctive transfer [from the regular <s>Agnihotra</s>] —
that is unreasonable.
Because the word '<s>agnihotra</s>' occurring in the injunctive statement has that status [i.e., of referring to the regular <s>Agnihotra</s>]; but the <s>arthavāda</s> (explanatory passage) — having taken up a certain similarity with what is [already] established — is tenable as eulogy, and does not warrant enjoining that status [upon the <s>prāṇāgnihotra</s>] — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Nor is there the attainment of the attributes of the regular (<s>prākṛta</s>) <s>Agnihotra</s> here#.'
Moreover, even if the attainment of attributes [from the regular <s>Agnihotra</s>] through injunctive transfer is conceded, a greater number [of attributes] that have been obtained would be overridden.
And when [preservation] is possible, an accumulation of overridings should not be resorted to.
The overriding of the <s>kṛṣṇala</s>-<s>caru</s> [i.e., the substitution in the <s>kṛṣṇala</s> oblation] is accepted as an unavoidable overriding — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#And even if the attainment of those attributes is conceded#' — thus.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] corroborates the absence of injunctive transfer: '#For this very reason, here too#' — thus.
Since by the method stated [above] there is no transfer (<s>atideśa</s>), for this very reason the subsidiary elements of the <s>Agnihotra</s> are <s>sāṃpādika</s> (brought about by creative construal, not by transfer).
But if there were attainment [through transfer], the <s>sāṃpādika</s> character would not be tenable.
For in a woman, beauty is creatively construed (<s>saṃpādyate</s>) through the form of the <s>cakravāka</s> [bird], lotus, and the like — [which is possible] because the face and the like lack [those qualities in reality].
But in a river, <s>cakravāka</s>s and the like are not creatively construed through [other] <s>cakravāka</s>s and the like — [because they are already present].
Hence we understand: there is no attainment through injunctive transfer.

#tannirdhāraṇāniyamastaddṛṣṭeḥ pṛthagdhyapratibandhaḥ phalam# /
yathaiva 'yasya parṇamayī juhūrbhavati na sa pāpaṃ ślokaṃ śṛṇoti' ityetadanārabhyādhītamavyabhicāritakratusaṃbandhaṃ juhūdvārā kratuprayogavacanagṛhītaṃ kratatvarthaṃ satphalānapekṣaṃ siddhavartamānāpadeśapratītaṃ na rātrisatravatphalatayā svīkarotīti /

parārthatvāt /
