children.translated_text: If [it were] mere <s>arthavāda</s>, its function would be extremely remote — [but] it is not so remote when [the statement] is directed toward the fruit.
But the cognition of fruit is not directly [obtained] from the reference to present accomplishment [alone].
For this very reason, in the <s>prayāja</s>s (preliminary offerings) and the like, there is no postulation of fruit from <s>arthavāda</s> through reference to present accomplishment.

children.text: phalaparatve tvasya na śakyaṃ prayājādīnāṃ pārārthyenāphalatvaṃ vaktumiti //42 //
children.translated_text: But when [the statement] is directed toward the fruit, it is not possible to assert the fruitlessness of the <s>prayāja</s>s and the like on the grounds of their serving another's purpose. //42//

body.translated_text:
'#There is no restriction in the determination of that [fruit], because that [independence] is seen; for separately, there is no obstruction — [this is about] the fruit#.'
Just as [in the statement] 'He whose ladle is made of <s>Parṇa</s>-leaves does not hear an evil report' — this, being studied without being commenced [for any particular sacrifice], having an invariable connection with a sacrifice, and being apprehended through the ladle as connected with the statement prescribing the sacrifice's performance, and being understood — through its reference to present accomplishment — as not requiring a [separate] fruit, does not accept [fruit] as its own [purpose], like the <s>Rātrisatra</s> (overnight sacrifice) —
so too the meditation connected with the <s>Udgītha</s> — which has an invariable connection with ritual action — being apprehended through the statement prescribing the ritual performance, is not sufficient to warrant the postulation of a fruit characterized by the attainment of all desires, as understood through its reference to present accomplishment.
Because of its serving another's purpose (<s>parārthatva</s>).
And thus, because of its being for the highest purpose.
And thus the sage's <s>sūtra</s> [from <s>Jaimini</s>]: 'In the case of material-refinement-actions (<s>dravyasaṃskāra-karma</s>), because of serving another's purpose, the hearing of fruit would be [mere] <s>arthavāda</s> (explanatory passage).'
This being so, when the prima facie view is that just as the restriction to [using] <s>Parṇa</s>-leaves in the sacrifice [applies], so too there is a restriction on meditation — the reply is: It is appropriate that the hearing of fruit for <s>Parṇa</s>-leaf [usage] is mere <s>arthavāda</s>.
For <s>Parṇa</s>-leaf nature, not being a substrate [for independent action], does not deserve to have a connection with fruit, like a sacrifice and the like.
Because of being of the nature of non-activity (<s>avyāpāra</s>).
And because only activity has [the capacity for] fruitfulness.
As they say: 'Because [fruit] is seen for what has [the capacity of] production.'
Nor is there a substrate — such as a sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>) connected with the model sacrifice (<s>prakṛta-kratu</s>) — that serves as the basis for [the <s>Parṇa</s>-leaf quality], as in the case of desirable taste (<s>svādiratā</s>), because the <s>Parṇa</s>-leaf quality is studied without being commenced [for a particular sacrifice].
Therefore, the connection of the <s>Parṇa</s>-leaf quality with a sacrifice must be made known through the sentence alone, via the medium of the ladle-connection.
And a sentence that is not directed toward that [fruit-connection] cannot make it known.
And thus, the sentence — being necessarily directed toward that [sacrifice-connection], being so directed — is also not able to convey the fruit-connection of the <s>Parṇa</s>-leaf quality,
because of the absurdity of sentence-splitting.
But for meditations, because their very nature is activity (<s>vyāpāra</s>), the connection with fruit is tenable on its own; hence the basing [of the meditation] on the <s>Udgītha</s> and the like does not contradict the injunction along with [a specific] fruit — because of being a qualified injunction (<s>viśiṣṭavidhāna</s>).
For a meditation enjoined as the means to a fruit, with the <s>Udgītha</s> as [its] instrument, does not bring about sentence-splitting.
Objection: the meditation is a refinement (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of the <s>Udgītha</s> — which is a subsidiary of ritual action — like sprinkling (<s>prokṣaṇa</s>) and the like; [this follows] from the accusative case-ending in [the word] '<s>udgītham</s>' (the <s>Udgītha</s> [as object]).
And thus, just as for refinements like anointing (<s>añjana</s>) and the like, the hearing of fruit is [mere] <s>arthavāda</s>.
This is not so.
For it is not the <s>Udgītha</s> that is the object of meditation here, but its component <s>Oṃkāra</s> — as has been stated above.
And <s>Oṃkāra</s> is not a subsidiary of ritual action, but a component of the <s>Udgītha</s> which is a subsidiary of ritual action.
And what is not directly useful is not sought [as a subsidiary].
Therefore, like [the statement] 'he offers with <s>saktu</s>s (barley-meal),' by the disjoining of the assignment [of <s>Oṃkāra</s> to ritual], the connection is: from meditation whose instrument is <s>Oṃkāra</s>, [comes] the fruit.
Therefore, just as the <s>Godohana</s> (cow-milking vessel) and the like — though based on a sacrifice — are impermanent because of their connection with [specific] fruits, so too the <s>Udgītha</s>-meditations and the like should be viewed [as having independent fruits].
The rest has been stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>.
'#This hearing of fruit is not mere <s>arthavāda</s>#' —

#pradānavadeva taduktam# /
tattacchutyarthālocanayā vāyuprāṇayoḥ svarūpābhede siddhe tadadhīnanirūpaṇatayā tadviṣayopāsanāpyabhinnā na cādhyātmādhidaivaguṇabhedādbhedaḥ /
nahi guṇabhede guṇavato bhedaḥ /
nahyagnihotraṃ juhotītyutpannasyāgnihotrasya taṇḍulādiguṇabhedādbhedo bhavati /
utpadyamānakarmasaṃyukto hi guṇabhedaḥ karmaṇo bhedakaḥ /
yathāmikṣāvājinasaṃyuktayoḥ karmaṇoḥ /
notpannakarmasaṃyuktaḥ /
adhyātmādhidaivopadeśeṣu cotpannopāsanāsaṃyogaḥ /
tathopakramopasaṃhārālocanayā vidyaikatvaviniścayādekaiva sakṛtpravṛttiriti pūrvapakṣaḥ /
rāddhāntastu-satyaṃ vidyaikatvaṃ tathāpi guṇabhedātpravṛttibhedaḥ /
sāyaṃprātaḥkālaguṇabhedādyathaikasminnapyagnihotre pravṛttibhedaḥ evamihāpyadhyātmādhidaivaguṇabhedādupāsanasyaikasyāpi pravṛttibheda iti siddham /
#ādhyānārtho#
body.translated_text:
'#The giving (<s>pradāna</s>) is as stated — thus it has been declared#.'
When the identity of essential nature between <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) and <s>Prāṇa</s> (vital breath) is established by examining the purport of the <s>Śruti</s>, the determination [of the meditation] being dependent on that [identity], the meditation concerning them too is non-different. Nor is there difference because of the difference of attributes — <s>adhyātma</s> (individual level) and <s>adhidaiva</s> (cosmic level).
For the difference of attributes does not [entail] the difference of the attribute-possessor.
For the <s>Agnihotra</s> — arising from 'he offers the <s>Agnihotra</s>' — is not made different by the difference of attributes such as rice-grains and the like.
For it is the difference of attributes conjoined with a [newly] arising action that differentiates the action —
as in the case of actions conjoined with <s>āmikṣā</s> (curds) and <s>vājina</s> (an offering) [respectively].
But not a difference of attributes conjoined with an [already] arisen action.
And in the <s>adhyātma</s> and <s>adhidaiva</s> teachings, there is conjunction with an [already] arisen meditation.
Likewise, by examining the introduction and conclusion, through the ascertainment of the oneness of the <s>vidyā</s>, there is only a single performance — this is the prima facie view.
But the established conclusion is: true, the <s>vidyā</s> is one; nevertheless, because of the difference of attributes, there is a difference of performances.
Just as, because of the difference of the evening and morning time-attributes, even in a single <s>Agnihotra</s> there is a difference of performances — so here too, because of the difference of <s>adhyātma</s> and <s>adhidaiva</s> attributes, even though the meditation is one, there is a difference of performances — this is established.
'#For the purpose of meditation#' —

body.text:
#hyayamadhyātmādhidaivavibhāgopadeśa iti# /
agnihotrasyevādhyānasya kṛte tadhitaṇḍulādivadayaṃ pṛthagupadeśaḥ /
#etena vratopadeśa iti# /
etenat tattvābhedena /
evakāraśca vāgādivratanirākaraṇārthaḥ /
nanvetasyai devatāyai iti devatāmātraṃ śrūyate na tu vāyustatkathaṃ vāyuprāptimāhetyata āha- #devatetyatra vāyuriti# /
vāyuḥ khalvagnyādīnsaṃvṛṇuta ityagnyādīnapekṣyānavacchinno 'gnyādayastutenaivāvacchinnā iti saṃvargaguṇatayā vāyuranavacchinnā devatā /
#sarveṣāmabhigamayanniti# /
militānāṃ śravaṇāviśeṣādindrasya devatāyā abhedātrayāṇāmapi puroḍāśānāṃ sahapradānāśaṅkāyāmutpattivākya eva rājādhirājasvarājaguṇabhedādyājyānuvākyāvyatyāsavidhānācca yathānyāsameva devatāpṛthaktvātpradānapṛthaktvaṃ bhavati /

children.translated_text: For in the case of offering together, the prescription of interchange would be untenable.
When there is sequential offering, the prescription of interchange is meaningful,
because it is precisely that kind of sequence that is intended.
The rest is easy to understand. //43//

body.translated_text:
'#For this is the teaching of the division into individual (<s>ādhyātma</s>) and cosmic (<s>ādhidaiva</s>) aspects#.'
Just as rice-grains and the like [are separate subsidiaries] for the purpose of meditation (<s>adhyāna</s>) on the <s>Agnihotra</s>, so this is a separate teaching [of the division into individual and cosmic aspects].
'#By this, the teaching of the observance (<s>vrata</s>) [is explained]#.'
'By this' — i.e., through the non-difference of the reality [being taught].
And the emphatic particle '<s>eva</s>' is for the purpose of negating the observance pertaining to speech and the like.
Objection: In [the <s>Śruti</s>] 'for this deity' (<s>etasyai devatāyai</s>), only 'deity' in general is heard, not <s>Vāyu</s> [specifically] — so how is the attainment of <s>Vāyu</s> [as the deity] stated? — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#The word "deity" here [refers to] <s>Vāyu</s>#.'
Indeed, <s>Vāyu</s> envelops <s>Agni</s> and the rest — thus, with reference to <s>Agni</s> and the rest, [<s>Vāyu</s>] is unlimitedwhile <s>Agni</s> and the rest are limited by him — hence, by virtue of the quality of absorption (<s>saṃvarga</s>), <s>Vāyu</s> is the unlimited deity.
'#Conveying all [of them] to agreement#.'
Since in the hearing [of the text], the combined [offering] is undifferentiated — and because <s>Indra</s>, the deity, is non-different [from the three <s>puroḍāśa</s>s addressed to him] — when the doubt arises whether the three <s>puroḍāśa</s>s (offering-cakes) should be offered together, [the answer is:] in the very origination-sentence, because of the differentiation of qualities such as 'king,' 'supreme king,' 'self-ruler,' and because of the prescription of the interchange (<s>vyatyāsa</s>) of the <s>yājyā</s> and <s>anuvākyā</s> [verses], the offerings are separate, in accordance with the separateness of the deities.

body.text:
#liṅgabhūyastvāttaddhi balīyastadapi# /
iha siddhāntenopakramasya pūrvapakṣayitvā siddhāntayati /
tatra yadyapi bhūyāṃsi santi liṅgāni manaścidādīnāṃ svātantryasūcakāni tathāpi na tāni svātantryeṇa svātantryaṃ prati prāpakāṇi /
pramāṇaprāpitaṃ tu svātantryamupodbalayanti /
na cātrāsti svātantryaprāpakaṃ pramāṇam /
na cedaṃ sāmarthyalakṣaṇaṃ liṅgaṃ yenāsya svātantryeṇa prāpakaṃ bhavet /
taddhi sāmarthyamābhidhānasya vārthasya vā syāt /
tathā pūṣādyanumantraṇamantrasya pūṣānumantraṇe, yathā vā 'paśunā yajeta' ityekatvasaṃkhyāyā arthasya saṃkhyeyāvacchetasāmarthyam /
na cedanamanyasyārthadarśanalakṣaṇaṃ liṅgaṃ tathā /
stutyarthatvenāsya vidhyuddeśenaikavākyatayā vidhiparatvāt /
tasmādasati sāmarthyalakṣaṇe viroddhari prakaraṇapratyūhaṃ manaścidādīnāṃ kriyāśeṣatāmavagamayati /
naca te haite vidyācita evetyavadhāraṇaśrutiḥ kriyānupraveśaṃ vārayati /
yena śrutivirodhe sati na prakaraṇaṃ bhavet, bāhyasādhanatāpākaraṇārthatvādavadhāraṇasya /
naca vidyayā haivaita evaṃvidaścitā bhavantīti puruṣasaṃbandhamāpādayadvākyaṃ prakaraṇamapabādhitumarhati /
anyārthadarśanaṃ khalvetadapi /
naca tatsvātantryeṇa prāpakamityuktam /
tasmāttadapi na prakaraṇavirodhāyālamiti sāṃpādikā apyete agnayaḥ prakaraṇātkriyānupraveśina eva mānasavat /
dvādaśāhe tu śrūyate-'anayā tvā pātreṇa samudraṃ rasayā prājāpatyaṃ manograhaṃ gṛhṇāmi' iti /
tatra saṃśayaḥ-kiṃ mānasaṃ dvādaśāhā daharantamuta tanmadhyapātino daśamasyāhnāṅgamiti /
tatra vāgvai dvādaśāho mano mānasamiti mānasasya dvādaśāhādbhedena vyapadeśādvāṅmanasabhedavadbhedaḥ /
nirdhūtāni dvādaśāhasya gatarasāni chandāṃsi tāni mānasenaivāpyāyantīti ca dvādaśāhasya mānasena stūyamānatvādbhede ca sati stutistutyabhāvasyopapatterdvādaśāhādaharantaraṃ na tadaṅgaṃ, patnīsaṃyājāntatvāccāhnāṃ patnīḥ saṃyājya mānasāya prasarpantīti ca mānasasya patnīsaṃyājasya parastācchuteḥ /
trayodaśāhe 'pyavayujya dvādaśasaṃkhyāsamavāyātkathañcijjaghanyayāpi vṛttyā dvādaśāhasaṃjñāvirodhābhāvāditi prāpte 'bhidhīyate-pramāṇāntareṇa hi trayodaśatve 'hnāṃ siddhe dvādaśāha iti jaghanyayā vṛttyonnīyeta /
na tvasti tādṛśaṃ pramāṇāntaram /
naca vyapadeśabhedo 'harantaratvaṃ kalpayitumarhati /
aṅgāṅgibhedenāpi tadupapatteḥ /
ata eva ca stutyastāvakabhāvasyāpyupapattiḥ /
devadattasyeva dīrghaiḥ keśaiḥ /
patnīsaṃyājāntatā tu yadyapyautsargikī tathāpi daśamasyāhno viśeṣavacanānmānasāni grahaṇāsādanahavanādīni patnīsaṃyājātparāñci bhaviṣyanti /
kimiva hi na kuryādvacanamiti /
eṣa vai daśamasyāhno visargo yanmānasamiti vacanāddaśamāharaṅgatā gamyate /
visargo 'nto 'ntavato dharmo na svatantra iti daśame 'hani mānasāya pramarpantīti daśamasyāhna ādhāratvanirdeśācca tadaṅgaṃ mānasaṃ nāharantaramiti siddham /

children.translated_text: Thus, here, the author of the <s>Dharma-Mīmāṃsā Sūtra</s>s (<s>Jaimini</s>) has stated that the <s>Mānasa</s> is a subsidiary of the tenth day of the <s>Dvādaśāha</s>.
The revered <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (<s>Śaṅkara</s>) [states that] it is also a subsidiary of the tenth day of the <s>Daśarātra</s> (ten-night sacrifice).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states this on the strength of another <s>Śruti</s>: '#Just as in the <s>Daśarātra</s>, on the tenth day, the <s>Avivākya</s>#.'
'<s>Avivākya</s>' is the name of the tenth day. //44//

body.translated_text:
'#Because of the preponderance of indicatory marks (<s>liṅga</s>), for that is stronger — that too#.'
Here, the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion) treats the introduction (<s>upakrama</s>) as the prima facie view and then establishes [its own position].
Therein, although there are many indicatory marks suggesting the independence of the <s>manaścit</s> (mind-piled) [fires] and the like, nevertheless they are not independently capable of establishing independence.
Rather, they strengthen independence that has been established by a [valid] means of knowledge.
But there is no means of knowledge here that establishes independence.
Nor is this an indicatory mark of the capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>) type, such that it could independently establish [independence].
For that capacity would pertain either to the denotation or to the meaning.
As the capacity of the <s>Pūṣan</s>-invocation mantra pertains to the invocation of <s>Pūṣan</s>; or as the capacity of the singular number in '<s>paśunā yajeta</s>' ('one should sacrifice with an animal') pertains to the meaning — the capacity of the number to delimit the thing numbered.
Nor is this an indicatory mark of the observation-of-a-different-purpose (<s>anyārthadarśana</s>) type, [which could establish independence] in the same way.
Because it is directed toward the praise of <s>vidyā</s>, being a single sentence with the injunction's object [and hence] having [its] purport directed toward the injunction.
Therefore, in the absence of an indicatory mark of the capacity type that could oppose [the context], the context establishes the <s>manaścit</s> and the like as subsidiaries of ritual action (<s>kriyāśeṣatā</s>).
Nor does the emphatic <s>Śruti</s> 'these are indeed constructed by <s>vidyā</s> alone' (<s>te haite vidyācita eva</s>) prevent [their] entry into ritual.
Because in a conflict with <s>Śruti</s>, the context would not apply — [but] the emphatic [particle] is for the purpose of negating external means [of construction].
Nor can the sentence 'These are indeed constructed by <s>vidyā</s> for one who knows thus' — which establishes a connection with the person — override the context.
This too is an observation of a different purpose.
And it has been stated that such [observation] does not independently establish [independence].
Therefore, it too is not sufficient for contradicting the context — and thus these fires too, though constructed [mentally], enter into ritual action through the context, just like the <s>Mānasa</s> [libation].
Regarding the <s>Dvādaśāha</s> (twelve-day sacrifice), the <s>Śruti</s> states: 'With this vessel I take for you the ocean-[like], the juicy, the <s>Prājāpatya</s>, the <s>Mānasa</s> (mental) cup (<s>graha</s>).'
Therein the doubt arises: Is the <s>Mānasa</s> [cup] a separate rite independent of the <s>Dvādaśāha</s>, or is it a subsidiary of the tenth day that falls within [the <s>Dvādaśāha</s>]?
Therein — since speech is the <s>Dvādaśāha</s> and mind is the <s>Mānasa</s>, and since the <s>Mānasa</s> is designated as different from the <s>Dvādaśāha</s> — the difference [between them] is like the difference between speech and mind — [this is the prima facie view].
And since the <s>Chandas</s>-metres of the <s>Dvādaśāha</s> — drained of their essence — are nourished by the <s>Mānasa</s> alone, and since the <s>Dvādaśāha</s> is being praised by the <s>Mānasa</s>, when there is difference, the relationship of praiser and praised is tenable — [hence] it is a separate rite, not a subsidiary of that [<s>Dvādaśāha</s>].
And because the days end with the <s>Patnīsaṃyāja</s> (wives' sacrifice), and after performing the <s>Patnīsaṃyāja</s> they proceed to the <s>Mānasa</s> — since the <s>Mānasa</s> is heard as coming after the <s>Patnīsaṃyāja</s>.
Even [if counted as] a thirteenth day, by separating [it from the twelve] and [yet] through some connection with the number twelve — even through a secondary meaning — since there is no contradiction with the designation '<s>Dvādaśāha</s>' — this being the prima facie conclusion, it is stated: When the thirteen-ness of the days is established through another means of knowledge, '<s>Dvādaśāha</s>' (twelve-day) could be explained through a secondary meaning.
But there is no such other means of knowledge.
Nor can the designation as different establish it as a separate rite.
Because that [designation as different] is tenable even through the difference of part and whole.
And for that very reason, the relationship of praiser and praised is also tenable.
Just as [when praising] <s>Devadatta</s> with his long hair.
As for the ending with the <s>Patnīsaṃyāja</s> — although this is the general rule (<s>autsargikī</s>), nevertheless, because of the specific statement regarding the tenth day, the <s>Mānasa</s> [rites of] cup-taking, placing, and offering will come after the <s>Patnīsaṃyāja</s>.
For what can a [specific] statement not accomplish?
'This indeed is the emission (<s>visarga</s>) of the tenth day — namely, the <s>Mānasa</s>' — from this statement, the subsidiary-hood to the tenth day is understood.
Since 'emission' (<s>visarga</s>) means 'end,' and since a <s>dharma</s> that has an end [is part of] what has an end, it is not independent — and from the indication of the tenth day as the locus [with the words] 'on the tenth day they proceed to the <s>Mānasa</s>' — it is a subsidiary of that [tenth day], not a separate rite — this is established.

children.translated_text: '#And because of the extension (<s>atideśa</s>)#.'

children.text: nahi sāṃpādikānāmagnīnāmiṣṭakāsu citenāgninā kiñcidasti sādṛśyamanyatra kriyānupraveśāt /
children.translated_text: For the constructed (<s>sāṃpādika</s>) fires have no resemblance whatsoever with the fire built with bricks (<s>iṣṭakācita</s>), apart from [their shared] entry into ritual action.
Therefore, from this too, [the <s>manaścit</s> fires] are not independent — this being the prima facie conclusion, it is stated. //46//

body.text:
#vidyaiva tu nirdhāraṇāt# /
mā bhūdanyeṣāṃ śrutavidhyuddeśānāmanyārthadarśanānāmaprāptaprāpakatvameteṣu tvaśrutavidhāyuddeśeṣu 'vacanāni tvapūrvatvāt' iti nyāyādvidhirunnetavyaḥ /
tathā caitebhyo yādṛśor'thaḥ pratīyate tadanurūpa eva sa bhavati /
pratīyate caitebhyo manaścidādīnāṃ sāntatyaṃ cāvadhāraṇaṃ ca phalabhedasamanvayaśca puruṣasaṃbandhaśca /
na cāsya godohanādivatkratvarthāśritatvaṃ yena puruṣārthasya karmapāratantryaṃ bhavet /
naca vidyācita evetyavadhāraṇaṃ bāhyasādhanāpākaraṇārtham /
svabhāvata eva vidyāyā bāhyānupekṣatvasiddheḥ /
body.translated_text:
'#It is <s>vidyā</s> alone, because of ascertainment (<s>nirdhāraṇa</s>)#.'
Let it be that other [indicatory marks] — which have a heard injunction as their object and are [merely] observations of a different purpose — do not independently establish [independence]. But in these [cases of the <s>manaścit</s> fires], which have no heard injunction as their object, by the principle 'statements are [to be treated as] unprecedented injunctions' (<s>vacanāni tv apūrvatvāt</s>), an injunction must be derived.
And thus, whatever meaning is cognized from these [statements], the meaning takes a form conforming to that [injunctive reading].
And what is cognized from these is: the perpetuity of the <s>manaścit</s> and the like, the emphatic restriction, the correlation with a distinct fruit, and the connection with the person.
Nor does this, like cow-milking and the like, have the character of being dependent on the ritual purpose (<s>kratvārtha</s>), such that the person-serving character would be subordinate to the ritual.
Nor is the emphatic statement 'constructed by <s>vidyā</s> alone' for the purpose of negating external means.
Because the independence of <s>vidyā</s> from external [means] is already established by its very nature.

body.text:
tasmātpariśeṣānmānasagrahavatkriyānupraveśaśaṅkāpākaraṇārthamavadhāraṇam /
na caivamarthatve saṃbhavati /
dyotakatvamātreṇa nipātaśrutiḥ pīḍanīyā /
tasmācchutiliṅgavākyāni prakaraṇamapodya svātantryaṃ manaścidādīnāmavagamayantīti siddham /
anubandhātideśaśrutyādibhya evameva vijñeyam /
te ca bhāṣya eva sphucāḥ /
yaduktaṃ pūrvapakṣiṇā kratvaṅgatve pūrveṇeṣṭakācitena manaścidādīnāṃ vikalpa iti /
tadutalyakāryatvena dūṣayati-naca satyeva kriyāsaṃbandha iti /
apica pūrvāparayorbhāgayorvidyāprādhānyadarśanāttanmadhyapātino 'pi tatsāmānyādvidyāpradhānatvameva lakṣyate na karmāṅgatvamityāha sūtreṇa- #pareṇa ca śabdasya tādvidhyaṃ bhūyastvāttvanubandhaḥ# /
sphuṭamasya bhāṣyam /
asti rājasūyaḥ 'rājā svārājyakāmo rājasūyena yajeta' iti /
taṃ prakṛtyāmananti aveṣṭiṃ nāmeṣṭim /
āgneyo 'ṣṭākapālo hiraṇyaṃ dakṣiṇetyevamādi tāṃ prakṛtyādhīyate /
yadi brāhmaṇo yajeta bārhaspatyaṃ madhye nidhāyāhutiṃ hutvābhighārayedyadi vaiśyo vaiśvadevaṃ yadi rājanya aindramiti /
tatra saṃdihyate-kiṃ brāhmaṇādīnāṃ prāptānāṃ nimittārthena śravaṇamuta brāhmaṇādīnāmayaṃ yāgo vidhīyata iti /
tatra yadi prajāpālanakaṇṭakoddharaṇādi karma rājyaṃ tasya kartā rājeti rājaśabdasyārthastato rājā rājasūyena yajeteti rājyasya kartū rājasūye 'dhikāraḥ /
tasmātsaṃbhavantyaviśiṣeṇa brāhmaṇakṣatriyavaiśyā rājyasya kartāra iti siddhaṃ sarva evaite rājasūye prāptā iti 'yadi brāhmaṇo yajeta' ityevamādayo nimittārthāḥ śrutayaḥ /
atha tu rājñaḥ karma rājyamiti rājakartṛyogāttatkarma rājyaṃ tataḥ ko rājetyapekṣāyāmāryeṣu tatprasiddherabhāvātpikanematāmarasādiśabdārthāvadhāraṇāya mlecchaprasiddhirivāndhrāṇāṃ kṣatriyajātau rājaśabdaprasiddhistadavadhāraṇakāraṇamiti kṣatriya eva rājeti na brāhmaṇavaiśyayoḥ prāptiriti rājasūyaprakaraṇaṃ bhittvā brāhmaṇādikartṛkāṇi pṛthageva karmāṇi prāpyanta iti na naimittikāni /
tatra kiṃ tāvatprāptaṃ, naimittikānīti /
rājyasya kartā rājetyāryāṇāmāndhrāṇāṃ cāvivādaḥ /
tathāhi-brāhmaṇādiṣu prajāpālanakartṛṣu kanakadaṇḍātapatraśvetacāmarādilāñchaneṣu rājapadamāndhrāścāryāścāvivādaṃ prayuñjānā dṛśyante /
tenāvipratipatrvipratipattāvapyāryāndhraprayogayoryavavarāhavadāryaprasiddherāndhraprasiddhito balīyasītvāt /

children.text: balavadāryaprasiddhivirodhe tvatanmūlāyāḥ pāṇinīyaprasiddheḥ 'virodhe tvanapekṣaṃ syāt' iti nyāyena bādhanāttadanuguṇatayā vā kathañcinnasvanakulādivadanvākhyānāmātraparatayā nīyamānatvādrajyasya kartā rājeti siddhe nimittārthāḥ śrutayaḥ /
children.translated_text: But when there is a conflict with a strong <s>Ārya</s> usage, since the <s>Pāṇinian</s> usage — which is rooted in that [<s>Ārya</s> usage] — overrides by the principle 'In a conflict, [the stronger] should be independent [of the weaker],' and since [the dissenting usage] is led — in conformity with that [<s>Pāṇinian</s> usage] — to be directed merely toward the <s>anvākhyāna</s> (illustration), like <s>nasvana</s>, <s>kula</s>, and the like — when it is established that '<s>rājan</s>' means 'the one who performs ruling,' the <s>Śruti</s>s are indicative of occasion.
And thus, the word '<s>yadi</s>' ('if') too would have its straightforward [conditional] meaning — this is what is arrived at.

children.text: evaṃ prāpta ucyate-'rūpato na viśeṣo 'sti hyāryamlecchaprayogayoḥ /
children.translated_text: This being arrived at, it is stated: 'There is no difference in form between <s>Ārya</s> and <s>Mleccha</s> usages.
But from the Vedic remainder of the sentence, a distinction has been shown there.'

body.translated_text:
Therefore, by elimination (<s>pariśeṣa</s>), the emphatic statement is for the purpose of negating the doubt about entry into ritual action, just like the <s>Mānasa graha</s> (mental libation).
Nor, when this meaning is possible,
should the <s>Śruti</s> of the particle [<s>eva</s>] be strained to have a merely illuminative (<s>dyotaka</s>) function.
Therefore, <s>Śruti</s>, indicatory mark, and sentence — overriding the context — establish the independence of the <s>manaścit</s> and the like — this is established.
From the qualifications (<s>anubandha</s>), extension (<s>atideśa</s>), <s>Śruti</s>, and the like — it should be understood in exactly this way.
And these are clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> itself.
What the prima facie opponent said — that when [the <s>manaścit</s> fires] are subsidiaries of ritual, there would be an option (<s>vikalpa</s>) with the previous brick-built [fire] because of equal effectiveness —
that [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes through [the argument of] equal effectiveness: '#Nor, when there is indeed a connection with ritual action#.'
Moreover, since in both the earlier and later portions [of the text], the predominance of <s>vidyā</s> is observed, what falls in the middle too — by similarity to those — is seen as predominantly <s>vidyā</s>-oriented, not as a subsidiary of <s>karma</s> — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says through the <s>sūtra</s>: '#And the word, by virtue of being of that nature through the subsequent [context], the qualification (<s>anubandha</s>) [is established] because of preponderance#.'
The <s>Bhāṣya</s> on this is clear.
There exists the <s>Rājasūya</s> [sacrifice]: 'A king desiring sovereignty should sacrifice with the <s>Rājasūya</s>.'
That [<s>Rājasūya</s>] is listed as the model (<s>prakṛti</s>) — namely the <s>Iṣṭi</s> called <s>Aveṣṭi</s>.
'An <s>Āgneya</s> (to <s>Agni</s>) [offering-cake] on eight potsherds; gold is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee)' — and so on is studied as its model (<s>prakṛti</s>).
'If a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> were to sacrifice, he should place a <s>Bārhaspatya</s> (offering to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>) in the middle and, having offered the oblation, should sprinkle [the consecrated substance]; if a <s>vaiśya</s>, a <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (offering to the <s>Viśvedevas</s>); if a <s>rājanya</s> (kṣatriya), an <s>Aindra</s> (offering to <s>Indra</s>).'
Therein the doubt arises: Is the hearing of '<s>brāhmaṇa</s>' and the like for the purpose of indicating an occasion (<s>nimittārtha</s>) [i.e., restricting the rite to particular <s>varṇa</s>s], or is a separate sacrifice being enjoined for <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s and the like?
Therein — if the word '<s>rāja</s>' (king) means one who performs the action of ruling (<s>rājya</s>) — [which involves] protecting subjects, removing thorns [of society], and the like — then from '<s>rājā rājasūyena yajeta</s>' ('a king should sacrifice with the <s>Rājasūya</s>'), the one who performs ruling has eligibility for the <s>Rājasūya</s>.
Therefore, since <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s, <s>kṣatriya</s>s, and <s>vaiśya</s>s can all equally be performers of ruling without distinction, it is established that all of them are eligible for the <s>Rājasūya</s> — and hence 'if a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> were to sacrifice' and the like are <s>Śruti</s>s indicating an occasion (<s>nimittārtha</s>).
But if [the word '<s>rāja</s>'] means 'kingship (<s>rājya</s>) is the <s>karma</s> (function) of a <s>rājan</s>' — then from the connection of the agent with the <s>karma</s> [of ruling], when the question arises 'Who is the <s>rājan</s>?' — since among the <s>Ārya</s>s there is no established usage [of '<s>rāja</s>' restricted to one <s>varṇa</s>], just as the <s>Andhra</s> usage [is consulted] for ascertaining the meaning of words like <s>pika</s>, <s>nema</s>, <s>tāmarasa</s>, and the like — so the <s>Andhra</s> established usage of the word '<s>rāja</s>' in the <s>kṣatriya</s> caste alone serves as the criterion for its determination — hence only the <s>kṣatriya</s> is the <s>rājan</s>. And since <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s and <s>vaiśya</s>s are not eligible [for the <s>Rājasūya</s>], breaking the <s>Rājasūya</s> context, separate rites for <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and other agents are arrived at — hence [the <s>Śruti</s>s] are not [merely] indicative of occasion.
What, then, is the prima facie conclusion? That they are indicative of occasion.
For regarding '<s>rājya</s> is the <s>karma</s> of a <s>rājan</s>' — there is no dispute between the <s>Ārya</s>s and the <s>Andhra</s>s.
Thus: when <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s and the like who protect subjects are seen [bearing] the insignia of golden staff, parasol, white fly-whisk, and the like, both <s>Andhra</s>s and <s>Ārya</s>s are seen applying the word '<s>rāja</s>' without dispute.
Therefore, even in the absence of a disputed usage, and even when there is a dispute, the <s>Ārya</s> usage, being stronger than the <s>Andhra</s> usage — like [the words] <s>yava</s> (barley) and <s>varāha</s> (boar) — [prevails].

body.text:
tadiha rājaśabdasya karmayogādvā kartari prayogaḥ kartṛprayogādvā karmaṇīti viśaye vaidikavākyaśeṣavadabhiyuktatarasyātrabhavataḥ pāṇineḥ smṛternirṇāyate prasiddhirāndhraṇāmanādirādimatī cāryāṇāṃ prasiddhirgogāvyādiśabdavat /
naca saṃbhāvitādimadbhāvā prasiddhiḥ pāṇinimsṛtimapodyānādiprasiddhimādimatīṃ kartumatsahate /
gāvyādiśabdaprasiddheranāditvena gavādipadaprasiddherapyādimattvāpatteḥ /
tasmātpāṇinīyasmṛtyanumatāndhraprasiddhibalīyastvena kṣatriyatvajātau rājaśabde mukhye tatkartaryatajjātau rājaśabdo gauṇa iti kṣatriyasyaivākārādrājasūye tatprakaraṇamapodyāveṣṭerutkarṣaḥ /

children.translated_text: The word '<s>yadi</s>' ('if') conforms to the [contextual] construction — it does not have the power to explain away an unprecedented injunction when one exists.
For that very reason they say: 'If [you prefer] the abandonment of the word "<s>yadi</s>" — [then at least] the postulation of an ellipsis [should be acknowledged].'

children.text: iyaṃ ca rājasūyādadhikārāntarametayānnādyakāmaṃ yājayediti nāstītikṛtvā cintā /
children.translated_text: And this deliberation is undertaken with the assumption that there is no other eligibility (<s>adhikāra</s>) besides the <s>Rājasūya</s> [in the text] '<s>annādyakāmaṃ yājayet</s>' ('one should have the one desiring food-sovereignty sacrifice').

But in this [other] eligibility, since the three <s>varṇa</s>s — desiring food-sovereignty — are eligible by being arrived at [through the injunction], the hearing of '<s>brāhmaṇa</s>' and the like as indicating occasion is indeed irresistible. //47//

body.translated_text:
Thus, here — whether the word '<s>rāja</s>' is used in the sense of the agent by virtue of the connection with the <s>karma</s> [of ruling], or in the sense of the <s>karma</s> by virtue of the usage regarding the agent — in this matter, from the <s>Smṛti</s> (grammar) of the more learned <s>Pāṇini</s>, which is like the Vedic remainder of the sentence, the established usage is determined. The established usage of the <s>Andhra</s>s is beginningless, while that of the <s>Ārya</s>s has a beginning — like the words <s>go</s> (cow), <s>gāvya</s>, and the like.
Nor can an established usage whose beginning is suspected [to exist] — merely by overriding the <s>Pāṇinian Smṛti</s> — make the beginningless usage one that has a beginning.
Because of the absurd consequence that, since the established usage of the words <s>gāvya</s> and the like is beginningless, the established usage of the words <s>go</s> (cow) and the like would also have a beginning.
Therefore, since the <s>Andhra</s> usage — endorsed by the <s>Pāṇinian Smṛti</s> — is stronger, the word '<s>rāja</s>' primarily denotes the <s>kṣatriya</s> caste. When used for one who is not of that caste, the word '<s>rāja</s>' is figurative (<s>gauṇa</s>). Hence, the extraction of the <s>Aveṣṭi</s> from the <s>Rājasūya</s> context — [establishing it as a rite] of the <s>kṣatriya</s> alone by the letter '<s>ā</s>' [in the word <s>rājā</s>] — [is established].

body.text:
eka ātmanaḥ śarīre bhāvāt /
adhikāraṇatātparyamāha- #iheti# /
samarthanaprayojanamāha- #bandhamokṣeti# /
asamarthane bandhamokṣādhikārābhāvamāha- #na hyasatīti# /
adhastanatantroktena paunaruktyaṃ codayati- #nanviti# /
pariharati- #uktaṃ bhāṣyakṛteti# /
nasūtrakāreṇa tatroktaṃ yena punaruktaṃ bhavedapi tu bhāṣyakṛtetyatratyasyaivārthasyāpakarṣaḥ pramāṇalakṣaṇopayogitayā tatra kṛta iti /
yata iha sūtrakṛdvakṣyatyata eva bhagavatopavarṣeṇoddhāro 'pakarṣasya kṛtaḥ /
vicārasyāsya pūrvottaratantraśeṣatvamāha- #iha ceti# /
pūrvādhikaraṇasaṃgatimāha- #apiceti# /
nanvātmāstitvopapattaya evātrocyantāṃ kiṃ tadākṣepeṇetyata āha-ākṣepapūrvikā hīti /
ākṣepamāha- #atraike dehamātrātmadarśina iti# /
yadyapi samastavyasteṣu pṛthivyaptejovāyuṣu na caitanyaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ tathāpi kāyākārapariṇateṣu bhaviṣyati /
nahi kiṇvādayaḥ samastavyastā na madanā dṛṣṭā iti madirākārapariṇatā na madayanti /
ahamiti cānubhave deha eva gaurādyakāraḥ prathate /
na tu tadatiriktaḥ tadadhiṣṭhānaḥ kuṇḍa eva dadhīti /
ata evāhaṃ sthūlo gacchāmītyādisāmānādhikaraṇyopapattirahamaḥ sthūlādibhiḥ /
na jātu dadhisamānādhikaraṇāni madhurādīni kuṇḍasyaikādhikaraṇyamanubhavanti sitaṃ madhuraṃ kuṇḍamiti /
na cāpratyakṣamātmatattvamanumānādibhiḥ śakyamunnetum /
na khalvapratyakṣaṃ pramāṇamasti /
uktaṃ hi-'deśakālādirūpāṇāṃ bhedādbhinnāsu śaktiṣu /
bhavānāmanumānena prasiddhiratidurlabhā' iti /
yadā ca upalabdhisādhyanāntarīyakabhāvasya liṅgasyeyaṃ gatistadā kaiva kathā dṛṣṭavyabhicārasya śabdasyārthāpatteścātyantaparokṣārthagocarāyā upamānasya heturbhāṣyakṛtā vyākhyātaḥ /

children.translated_text: <s>Ceṣṭā</s> (activity) is the action directed toward the attainment and avoidance of what is beneficial and harmful.

children.text: sa ca śarīrādhīnatayā dṛśyamānaḥ śarīradharma evaṃ prāṇaḥ śvāsapraśvāsādirūpaḥ śarīradharma eva /
children.translated_text: And that [activity], being observed as dependent on the body, is a property of the body alone; similarly <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), in the form of inhalation and exhalation, is a property of the body alone.

children.text: icchāprayatnādayaśca yadyapyāntarāḥ tathāpi śarīrātiriktasya tadāśrayānupalabdheḥ sati śarīre bhāvāt antaḥ śarīrāśrayā eva, anyathā dṛṣṭahānādṛṣṭakalpanāprasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text: And desire, effort, and the like — although internal — nevertheless, since no substrate distinct from the body is perceived for them, [and] since they exist when the body exists, they are grounded in the body alone as their substrate; otherwise, there would be the fallacy of abandoning what is observed and postulating what is unobserved.

children.text: śarīrātirikta ātmani pramāṇābhāvāccharīre ca saṃbhavāccharīre ca saṃbhavāccharīramevecchādimadātmeti prāpta ucyate- //53 //
children.translated_text: Since there is no means of valid knowledge for a self distinct from the body, and since [these properties] are possible in the body — [this being] the prima facie conclusion that the body alone, possessing desire and the like, is the self — it is stated: //53//

body.translated_text:
One [self exists], because of [its] being in the body.
[Śaṅkara] states the purport of the topic: '#here#' (<s>iha</s>).
He states the purpose of the demonstration: '#bondage and liberation#' (<s>bandhamokṣa</s>).
He states the absence of the topic of bondage and liberation in the absence of demonstration: '#for without [a self] existing#' (<s>na hyasati</s>).
He raises the objection of redundancy with the topic stated in the earlier section: '#but#' (<s>nanu</s>).
He resolves it: '#it was stated by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>#' (<s>uktaṃ bhāṣyakṛtā</s>).
It was not stated by the <s>Sūtrakāra</s> so as to constitute redundancy; rather, the drawing out (<s>apakarṣa</s>) of this very meaning stated here was done by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> there, for the purpose of its utility in the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge).
Because the <s>Sūtrakāra</s> will say here itself — therefore the venerable <s>Upavarṣa</s> made the drawing out of [this meaning].
He states that this inquiry is supplementary to both the earlier and later sections: '#and here#' (<s>iha ca</s>).
He states the connection with the preceding topic: '#moreover#' (<s>apica</s>).
Objection: Let the proofs of the existence of the self alone be stated here — what need is there for the objection? To this he says: '#for [the demonstration] is preceded by objection#' (<s>ākṣepapūrvikā hi</s>).
He states the objection: '#here some, who view the body alone as the self#' (<s>atraike dehamātrātmadarśinaḥ</s>).
Even though in the elements — whether aggregate or discrete — earth, water, fire, and air — consciousness is not observed, nevertheless in [those elements] transformed into the form of the body, it will arise.
For it is not the case that ferments and the like, [merely because they are] not intoxicating when aggregate or discrete, do not intoxicate when transformed into the form of liquor.
And in the experience 'I,' it is the body alone that appears in the form of a fair-complexioned person and the like,
not something distinct from it that is its substrate — like 'curd is [nothing but] the pot.'
Hence the co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) in [expressions] such as 'I am stout, I walk' is explained — of 'I' with 'stout' and the like.
Never do 'sweet' and the like, which are co-referential with curd, experience co-referentiality with the pot — as in 'the pot is white and sweet.'
Nor can the reality of the self, being imperceptible, be established by inference and the like.
For indeed there is no imperceptible means of valid knowledge.
As it has been said: 'Given the differences of place, time, and the like, and [correspondingly] different powers, the establishment of [things'] existence through inference is extremely difficult.'
And when this is the status of the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>), whose invariable concomitance (<s>nāntarīyakabhāva</s>) is to be established through perception — then what need be said of verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>), which has observed deviation, or of presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>), or of analogy (<s>upamāna</s>), which operates in the domain of the absolutely imperceptible? The reason has been explained by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>.

body.text:
#vyatirekastadbhāvābhāvitvānna tūpalabdhivat# /
nāpratyakṣaṃ pramāṇamiti bruvāṇaḥ praṣṭavyo jāyate kuto bhavānanumānādīnāmaprāmāṇyamavadhāritavāniti /
pratyakṣaṃ hi liṅgādirūpamātragrāhi nāprāmāṇyameṣāṃ viniścetumarhati /
nahi dhūmajñānamivaiṣāmindriyārthasannikarṣādaprāmāṇyajñānamudetumarhati /
kintu deśakālāvasthārūpabhedena vyabhācirotprekṣayā /
na caitāvānpratyakṣasya vyāpāraḥ saṃbhavati /
yathāhuḥ-nahīdamiyato vyāpārānkartuṃ samarthaṃ saṃnihitaviṣayabalenotpatteravicārakatvāditi /
tasmādasminnanicchatāpi pramāṇāntaramabhyupeyam /
apica pratipannaṃ pumāṃsamapahāyāpratipannasaṃdigdhāḥ prekṣāvadbhiḥ pratipādyante /
na caiṣāmitthaṃbhāvo bhavatpratyakṣagocaraḥ /
na khalvete gauratvādivatpratyakṣagocarāḥ kintu vacanaceṣṭādiliṅgānumeyāḥ /
naca liṅgaṃ pramāṇaṃ yata ete sidhyanti /
na puṃsāmitthaṃbhāvamavijñāya yaṃ kañcana puruṣaṃ pratipipātayiṣato 'navadheyavacanasya prekṣāvattā nāma /
apica paśavo 'pi hitāhitaprāptiparihārārthinaḥ komalaśaṣpaśyāmalāyāṃ bhuvi pravartante /
pariharanti cāśyānatṛṇakaṇṭakākīrṇām /
nāstikastu paśorapi paśuriṣṭaniṣṭasādhanamavidvān /
na khalvasminnumānagocara-pravṛttinivṛttigocare pratyakṣaṃ prabhavati /
naca parapratyāyanāya śabdaṃ prayuñjīta śābdasyārthasyāpratyakṣatvāt /
tadeva mā nāma bhūnnāstikasya janmāntaramasminneva janmanyupasthito 'sya mūkatvapravṛttinivṛttiviraharūpo mahānnarakaḥ /
parākrāntaṃ cātra sūribhiḥ /
body.translated_text:
'#But [the self] is distinct [from the body], because of the non-existence [of consciousness etc.] in the absence of that [self] — not like perception#.'
One who says 'there is no imperceptible means of valid knowledge' should be asked: How have you ascertained the non-validity of inference and the like?
For perception, grasping only the form of the inferential mark and the like, is not capable of determining their non-validity.
For it is not the case that from the contact of the sense-organ with the object — as in the cognition of smoke — a cognition of their non-validity can arise.
Rather, [such a claim arises] through the supposition of deviation based on differences of place, time, and condition.
And perception cannot have such extensive scope.
As they say: 'For this [perception], arising from the power of the proximate object, is incapable of performing such extensive operations, because of its non-deliberative nature.'
Therefore, even unwillingly, one must accept another means of valid knowledge.
Moreover, discerning people explain to the doubting and the unaware by setting aside the already-understood person [and addressing the issue directly].
And the mental states of these [other persons] are not within the scope of your perception.
For indeed these [mental states] are not perceptible like 'whiteness' and the like; rather, they are to be inferred from marks such as speech, gestures, and the like.
And if the inferential mark is not a valid means of knowledge, then those [mental states] by which they are established [cannot be known].
Without knowing the mental states of people, for one who wishes to persuade any person whatsoever — whose words carry no weight — there can be no discernment.
Moreover, even animals, seeking the attainment of the beneficial and the avoidance of the harmful, proceed upon ground that is soft with green grass,
and avoid [ground] that is marshy and covered with thorns and thistles.
But the <s>Nāstika</s> (materialist) is [like] an animal even to an animal — one who does not know the means to the desired and the undesired.
For indeed, in this domain — the domain of activity and withdrawal accessible to inference — perception does not prevail.
Nor would [the materialist] employ speech for the purpose of persuading others, since the meaning conveyed by words is imperceptible.
Then let the materialist indeed have no future birth — in this very birth there awaits him a great hell in the form of muteness, [the cessation of] activity and withdrawal.
And the wise have exerted themselves extensively on this matter.

body.text:
atyantaparokṣagocarāpyanyathānupapadyamānārthaprabhavārthāpattiḥ /
bhūyaḥsāmānyayogena copamānamupapāditaṃ pramāṇalakṣaṇe /
tadatrāstu tāvatpramāṇāntaraṃ pratyaśramevāhaṃpratyayaḥ śarīrātiriktamālambata ityanvayatirekābhyāmavadhāryate /
yogavyāghravatsvapnadaśāyāṃ ca śarīrāntaraparigrahābhimāne 'pyahaṅkārāspadasya pratyabhijñāyamānatvamityuktam /
sūtrayojanā tu na tvavyatiriktaḥ kintu vyatirikta ātmā dehāt /
kutastadbhāvābhāvitvāt /
caitanyādiryadi śarīraguṇaḥ tato 'nena viśeṣaguṇena bhavitavyam. na tu saṃkhyāparimāṇasaṃyogādivatsāmānyaguṇena /
tathāca ye bhūtaviśeṣaguṇaste yāvadbhūtabhāvino dṛṣṭā yathā rūpādayaḥ /
nahyasti saṃbhavaḥ bhūtaṃ ca rūpādirahitaṃ ceti /
tasmādbhūtaviśeṣaguṇarūpādivaidharmyānna caitanyaṃ śarīraguṇaḥ /
etenecchādīnāṃ śarīraviśeṣaguṇatvaṃ pratyuktam /
body.translated_text:
Even <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), though its domain is the absolutely imperceptible, arises from a meaning that cannot be explained otherwise.
And <s>upamāna</s> (analogy) has been established by [its] extensive commonality as a means of valid knowledge in the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s>.
Now, let there be other means of valid knowledge for the time being — [the question is:] the 'I'-cognition apprehends something distinct from the body — this is ascertained through positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s>).
Even in the dream state, when there is the assumption of another body, the 'I'-sense is recognized as having the same locus [as before] — this has been stated, [namely] that the substrate of the ego is recognized [across states].
The construction of the <s>sūtra</s> is: not non-distinct, but rather the self is distinct from the body.
Why? Because of the non-existence [of consciousness] in the absence of that [self].
If consciousness and the like were properties of the body, then they should be specific properties [of the body]. But they should not be general properties like number, magnitude, conjunction, and the like.
And thus, those which are specific properties of the elements are observed to persist as long as the elements persist — such as form (<s>rūpa</s>) and the like.
For there is no possibility of an element being devoid of form and the like.
Therefore, because of the dissimilarity with form and the like, which are specific properties of the elements, consciousness is not a property of the body.
By this, the [claim of] desire and the like being specific properties of the body is also refuted.

body.text:
prāṇaceṣṭādayo yadyapi dehadharmā eva tathāpi na dehamātraprabhavāḥ /
mṛtāvasthāyāmapi prasaṅgāt /
tasmādyasyaite adhiṣṭānāddehadharmā bhavanti sa dehātirikta ātmā /
adṛṣṭakāraṇatve 'bhyupagamyamāne tasyāpi dehāśrayatvānupapatterātmaivābhyupetavya iti /
vaidharmyāntaramāha- #dehadharmāśceti# /
svaparapratyakṣā hi dehadharmā dṛṣṭā yathā rūpādayaḥ /
icchādayastu svapratyakṣā eveti dehadharmavaidharmyam /
tasmādapi dehātiriktadharmā iti /
tatra yadyapi caitanyamapi bhūtaviśeṣaguṇastathāpi yāvadbhūtamanuvarteta /
naca madaśaktyā vyabhicāraḥ /
sāmarthyasya sāmānyaguṇatvāt /
apica madaśaktiḥ pratimadirāvayavaṃ mātrayāvatiṣṭhate tadvaddehe 'pi caitanyaṃ tadavayaveṣvapi mātrayā bhavet /
yathā caikasmindehe bahavaścetayeran /
naca bahūnāṃ cetanānāmanyonyābhiprāyānuvidhānasaṃbhava iti ekapāśanibaddhā iva bahavo vihaṅgamāḥ viruddhādikriyābhimukhāḥ samarthā api na hastamātramapi deśamatipatitumutsahante /
evaṃ śarīramapi na kiñcitkartumutsahate /

children.text: nānātve hi nānyenopalabdhe 'nyasya puruṣasya smṛtirupapadyata ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For if [the perceiver and the rememberer were] different, the memory of one person regarding what was perceived by another would not be tenable — this is the meaning.
He restates an already-refuted point for the purpose of [offering] another refutation: '#but what was said#' (<s>yattūktam</s>).

children.text: yo hi dehavyāpārādupalabdhirutpadyate tena dehadharma iti manyate taṃ pratīdaṃ dūṣaṇam- #na cātyantaṃ dehasyeti# /
children.translated_text: One who thinks that perception arises from the operation of the body and therefore is a property of the body — against him this refutation [is directed]: '#and not absolutely of the body#' (<s>na cātyantaṃ dehasya</s>).
He concludes the topic at hand: '#therefore, [the self is] beyond reproach#' (<s>tasmādanavadyam</s>). //54//

body.translated_text:
<s>Prāṇa</s> (vital breath), activity, and the like — although indeed properties of the body — are nevertheless not produced by the body alone.
Because [otherwise] they would apply even in the state of death.
Therefore, that [entity] by whose superintendence these become properties of the body — that is the self distinct from the body.
If [the cause of these properties] is accepted as an unseen force (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>), since even that unseen force cannot be grounded in the body, the self alone must be accepted.
He states another point of dissimilarity: '#and the properties of the body#' (<s>dehadharmāśca</s>).
For the properties of the body are observed to be perceptible both to oneself and to others — such as form and the like.
But desire and the like are perceptible only to oneself — this is [their] dissimilarity from the properties of the body.
Therefore, from this too, [they are] properties of [something] distinct from the body.
Therein, even if consciousness too were a specific property of the elements, it should nevertheless persist as long as the elements persist.
Nor is there a counter-example through the power of intoxication.
Because the power [of intoxication] is a general property.
Moreover, the power of intoxication resides in each constituent part of the liquor in a [certain] measure — similarly, consciousness in the body too should exist in its constituent parts in a [proportional] measure.
And thus many [consciousnesses] would be conscious in a single body.
And since the mutual conformity of intention among many conscious [entities] is impossible — like many birds tied to a single string, who though capable, facing mutually contradictory actions, cannot fly even a hand's distance —
so too the body would not be capable of doing anything.
Moreover, mere co-presence (<s>anvaya</s>) alone cannot determine the relation of property and property-bearer.
Lest space [be deemed to have] every property, due to its co-presence with everything.
Rather, [the determination is] through both co-presence and co-absence (<s>anvayavyatirekābhyām</s>).
And the co-absence (<s>vyatireka</s>) here is doubtful.
And thus, he says that mere co-presence alone is the prover: '#moreover, when [the body] exists#' (<s>apica sati hi tāvat</s>).
Wishing to state another refutation — the non-difference of elements is [like] form and the like; [consciousness] is not something other than the four elements — thus the transformation of elements alone is consciousness, not something other than the elements, by which [there would be] a contradiction with the thesis 'earth, water, fire, and air — these are the realities' — this is the meaning.
What is being said is this: the evolution of the world is of the four elements alone, and there is no other reality whose transformation would be form and the like or any other transformation.
By the arguments stated here, the [claim of consciousness] being a property of the body has been refuted. Nevertheless, wishing to state yet another argument, he says: '#if then#' (<s>cettarhi</s>).
The properties of the elements — form and the like — being insentient (<s>jaḍa</s>), are observed to be objects (<s>viṣaya</s>) alone, never subjects (<s>viṣayin</s>).
Nor should it be said that some objects too will become subjects.
Because of the contradiction of an operation upon itself.
Nor does this problem arise regarding perception (<s>upalabdhi</s>), because of the acceptance that it is self-luminous (<s>svayaṃprakāśa</s>), being non-insentient.
And this has been demonstrated previously.
He construes the <s>sūtra</s>-portion 'like perception' (<s>upalabdhivat</s>): '#just as of this#' (<s>yathaivāsyā</s>).
The distinctness [of the self] from the body is also established from the means of valid knowledge that apprehend perception.
Because of the ascertainment of the distinction [of perception] from the insentient properties of the elements, by means of the self-luminous cognition, [there is] the ascertainment of distinctness.
Granted then that perception is distinct from the elements and independent — still, there is no means of valid knowledge for the self — to this he says: '#and perception is itself the nature of the self#' (<s>upalabdhisvarūpa eva ca na ātmā</s>).
For one who does not know [otherwise], the difference of perceptions is not experienced — hence it must be accepted on the basis of the difference of objects.
And it has been demonstrated that the manifestation of objects distinct from perception is impossible.
And it has been demonstrated [by us] in the <s>Brahmatattvasamīkṣā</s> that there is no means of valid knowledge that apprehends the difference of objects.
And this being so, since the object-nature and its differences are extremely difficult to establish, the talk of difference of perceptions based on difference of objects is far removed.
Therefore, the subjecthood (<s>upalabdhṛtva</s>) of perception too is not ultimately real,
but is superimposed by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance).
Therein, even in the state of <s>avidyā</s>, perception is non-different — he says: '#I saw this#' (<s>ahamidamadrākṣam</s>).
Not only from ultimate non-difference [does] eternality [follow], but from conventional non-difference too, eternality alone [follows] — this is the meaning.
'#And because of the tenability of memory and the like#' (<s>smṛtyādyupapatteśca</s>).

children.translated_text: Nor in this way is there injury to <s>Śruti</s> through proximity — for if one were to override the meaning presented by <s>Śruti</s> through displacement, then one would indeed injure the <s>Śruti</s>; but that is not the case here.

For the general and the particular — denoted and indicated by the <s>udgītha</s>-<s>Śruti</s> — are not overridden; since from the acceptance of those belonging to one's own <s>śākhā</s>, the non-acceptance of those belonging to another <s>śākhā</s> [does not follow].
As they say: 'Having taken the universal and the particular here as denoted by <s>Śruti</s>,

children.text: kṛṣṇādi yadi muñcāmaḥ kā śrutistatra pīḍyate' //
children.translated_text: if we release the black [cow] and the like — which <s>Śruti</s> is thereby violated?'

body.translated_text:
'#But [the meditations] that are subsidiaries [of rituals] are not [combined] across <s>Śākhā</s>s (Vedic recensions), for [they are taught] in each <s>Veda</s> [separately]#.'
Due to the differences of <s>svara</s> (accents) and the like, the <s>Udgītha</s> and the like differ in each <s>Veda</s>.
But the meditations (<s>pratyaya</s>s) that are subsidiary to them are enjoined differently in each <s>Śākhā</s> (recension).
Therein, a doubt arises: Do the meditations enjoined in a given <s>Veda</s> belong only to the <s>Udgītha</s> and the like enjoined in that very <s>Veda</s>, or do those meditations apply also to the <s>Udgītha</s> and the like enjoined in other <s>Veda</s>s?
What then is the prima facie conclusion?
'One meditates on the syllable <s>Om</s> as the <s>Udgītha</s>' — through the word '<s>Udgītha</s>,' the <s>Udgītha</s> in general is understood.
And since that [general <s>Udgītha</s>], being without qualification, is untenable, when a specific qualification is sought, the specific [<s>Udgītha</s>] enjoined in one's own <s>Śākhā</s> (recension), being proximate, satisfies the expectation — and [thus] does not require [reference to] the <s>Udgītha</s> of another recension.

evaṃ prāptam /
evaṃ prāpta ucyate-udrīthāṅgavavaddhāstu pratyayā nānāśākhāsu prativedamanuvarteranna pratiśākhaṃ vyavatiṣṭheran /

children.translated_text: There is no valid means [of knowledge] for restriction.
Nor can mere proximity override [it].
And to confine a <s>Śruti</s> — which, through the medium of its general [meaning], extends to all specifics — to just one [specific] would itself be a violation.
Therefore, the cognitions pertain to all <s>udgītha</s>s. //55//

body.translated_text:
This being the prima facie view, the reply is stated:
Having thus arrived at [the prima facie view], the reply is given: The cognitions (<s>pratyaya</s>s) pertaining to the <s>udgītha</s> and its subsidiaries should follow [the pattern of] each <s>Veda</s> across the various <s>śākhā</s>s, not be confined to each <s>śākhā</s> individually.
Because of the non-specificity of the general <s>Śruti</s> such as '<s>udgītha</s>' and the like. What is thereby stated is this: It is appropriate [to argue] that in 'bring a white cloth' and the like, the <s>Śruti</s> of 'cloth' — though operating without specificity — is overridden by the proximate [qualifier] '<s>Śruti</s> of white.'
Because the co-occurrence (<s>samabhivyāhāra</s>) of words is for the purpose of conveying a qualified meaning.
Otherwise, that [co-occurrence] would be inexplicable.
Nor is it the case that — since words convey a qualified meaning without first evoking their own meaning — the evocation of their own meaning, prompted by [their role in conveying] the qualified meaning, is unable to override its own prompter.
Let it not be the case that — because of the absence of a prompter for overriding — there is no evocation of their own meaning either. Thus, it is appropriate that even a <s>Śruti</s> operating without specificity be confined to just one specific [meaning].
But here, the <s>udgītha</s>-<s>Śruti</s> conveys the qualified meaning without specificity.

children.translated_text: We understand as contradicted that which is not apprehended through a valid means of knowledge.
And it is apprehended that mantras and the like belonging to another <s>śākhā</s> have a connection with rituals belonging to [yet] another <s>śākhā</s>.
Likewise here too — from this observation, there is no contradiction.
And this has been shown by the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, which is easy [to understand]. //56//

body.translated_text: There is no contradiction, just as with mantras and the like.

#bhūmnaḥ kratuvajjyāyastvaṃ tathāhi darśayati# /
vaiśvānaravidyāyāṃ chāndogye kiṃ vyastopāsanaṃ samastopāsanameveti /

children.translated_text: is for the purpose of praising the principal [meditation].
And it is established that fruitfulness belongs to the aggregate meditation alone.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>], having presented the partial interpretation, refutes it: '#Some, however, here#' — thus.
When single-sentence-hood is possible, sentence-splitting is irregular — hence such an interpretation of the <s>sūtra</s> is not fitting — this is the meaning. //57//

body.translated_text:
'#The superiority [belongs to the meditation on] the aggregate (<s>bhūman</s>), as in the case of a sacrifice, for thus [the <s>Śruti</s>] shows#.'
In the <s>Vaiśvānara-vidyā</s> of the <s>Chāndogya</s>, [the question is:] should [<s>Vaiśvānara</s>] be meditated upon in parts or only as a whole?
Therein, since there is the <s>Śruti</s> of meditation on each [part] individually — 'Heaven alone, O king' and so on — and since the hearing of fruitfulness pertains to each part individually, and since fruitfulness is also heard for the aggregate meditation, the meditation is possible in both ways.
Nor [can it be argued] that — just as in the <s>Vaiśvānarīyeṣṭi</s> (offering to <s>Vaiśvānara</s>), although the hearing of individual fruits [occurs in statements like] 'He whose [cake is of] eight potsherds' and the like — those are mere <s>avayujyavāda</s>s (laudatory statements about parts), while only 'He should offer the twelve-potsherd [cake]' has fruitfulness — so here too [only the aggregate meditation should be fruitful].
For there, 'He should offer the twelve-potsherd [cake]' has the <s>Śruti</s> of an optative-mood (<s>vidhibhakti</s>) [injunction], whereas 'He whose [cake is of] eight potsherds' and the like are in the present-tense form.
Nor is there [there] a postulation of injunction because of the statement being unprecedented (<s>apūrva</s>) — since the <s>avayujyavāda</s> can also be explained as praise.
But here, since the present-tense form is undifferentiated in both the aggregate and the individual [meditations], and since — in the absence of an apprehended distinction — the postulation of an injunction and the postulation of a fruit differ [for both cases];
and since censure — [expressed] at the beginning of the aggregate meditation — is tenable even with respect to individual meditation;
[therefore,] just as [the rule] 'the dark one should eat the <s>āśvāhuti</s> offering' [allows] both kinds of meditation — this being the prima facie view, the reply is given: The superiority belongs to the aggregate meditation alone, not to the individual meditation.
Even though the present-tense form is undifferentiated in both, nevertheless, upon examination of the sequential order, the purport directed toward the aggregate meditation is understood.
For the sentence in which [the passage] culminates — that is its meaning.
For thus: <s>Prācīnaśāla</s> and the others, being unsettled regarding the <s>Vaiśvānara-vidyā</s>, came to <s>Aśvapati Kaikeya</s>.
And they had presented their respective individual-part meditations.
Therein, <s>Kaikeya</s>, having first censured each individual meditation, consolidated [the teaching] into the aggregate meditation by removing [the partial ones].
And thus, for the sake of obtaining single-sentence-hood and avoiding sentence-splitting, the purport of the passage is seen to be directed toward the aggregate meditation alone.
Therefore, the enumeration of many fruits
