children.translated_text: '#Nor, in this view, are the qualities beginning with <s>satyakāma</s> and the like [that are] common#' — thus.
Certain qualities indeed are common to certain <s>vidyā</s>s — hence, if there were oneness of <s>vidyā</s>, they would have to be repeated.
Because of having been stated in one [<s>vidyā</s> already].

children.text: vidyābhede tu na paunaruktyamekasyāṃ vidyāyāmuktā vidyāntare noktā iti vidyāntarasyāpi tadguṇatvāya vaktavyā anuktānāmaprāpteriti //58 //
children.translated_text: But when the <s>vidyā</s>s are different, there is no redundancy — [for] what is stated in one <s>vidyā</s> is not stated in another; hence, for the other <s>vidyā</s> to also have that quality, it must be stated [there] — since what is not stated would not be obtained. //58//

body.translated_text:
'#Because of the difference of word and the like#.'
Having taken the difference of <s>vidyā</s>s as established, the subsequent body of inquiry has been developed.
But now, the question to be investigated is: regarding all the <s>vidyā</s>s pertaining to <s>Īśvara</s> — are they non-different or different? And likewise regarding those pertaining to <s>Prāṇa</s> and the like.
But [one might object:] Just as the <s>apūrva-bhāvanā</s> (unprecedented productive force) — denoted by the verbal suffix — is different even when the person does not know [the difference], because of its being determined by the verbal-root meaning, and because that [verbal-root meaning] — sacrifice and the like — being different, [the <s>bhāvanā</s>s] are different due to the difference of the verbal-root-meaning connection that qualifies the model-meaning, sacrifice and the like —
since only that [<s>bhāvanā</s>] which is connected with that [specific meaning] is perceived —
so too, even when there is formal non-difference of the knowable <s>Īśvara</s> in the <s>vidyā</s>s, because of the difference of the attribution of such-and-such qualities as '<s>satyasaṃkalpatva</s>' (having true will) and the like, there is a difference of <s>vidyā</s>s — hence there is no occasion for a doubt about non-difference.
[The reply is:] It is correct that because of the difference of connections, there is a difference of the <s>apūrva-bhāvanā</s>s, which are of the nature of effects.
But here, since <s>Brahman</s> has an established form, and since the qualities such as <s>satyasaṃkalpatva</s> and the like — being dependent on that [<s>Brahman</s>] — are also established as the same everywhere in the <s>vidyā</s>s, [there is non-difference].
For a person of broad chest, <s>cakora</s>-like eyes, a <s>kṣatriya</s> youth, of <s>Duśyavana</s>'s lineage — taught in one [place] — when taught elsewhere as lion-faced, bull-shouldered — does not abandon [the attributes of] <s>cakora</s>-like eyes and the like. For the entity is not divided with each instruction.
Because of its being in the same state everywhere.
Or, if it were not in the same state, it would not even be that [same entity].
For an entity is not subject to optionality.
Therefore, because of the non-difference of the knowable, [the conclusion that] the <s>vidyā</s>s are different — this being the prima facie view, the reply is given:
This would be so if the meditation-sentences were directed toward the entity [itself]. But [in fact] they prescribe a meditation-<s>bhāvanā</s> (productive force of meditation) directed toward that [entity].
And that [<s>bhāvanā</s>] is of the nature of an effect.
Even though the meditation-<s>bhāvanā</s> depends on the meditation for its determination, and the meditation depends on the object of meditation for its determination, and the object of meditation — <s>Īśvara</s> and the like — has an established form, nevertheless, its becoming an object of meditation — [occurring] sometimes, by someone, in some form — is itself unsettled.
Just as a single woman's body — being made an object by someone as something to eat, by another as something to approach, by another as offspring, by another as a mother, by another as something to be ignored — is dependent on the person's desire.
So here too, the meditations — being dependent on the person's desire — do not transcend the character of being enjoinable.
Nor do the meditations differ because of the difference of qualities by which [<s>Brahman</s>] is meditated upon — [just as meditations do not differ because qualities differ].
Nor — as in the <s>Agnihotra</s>, where after prescribing the meditation, the qualities such as curds, rice, and the like are prescribed [separately] — is there here a separate prescription of qualities such as <s>satyasaṃkalpatva</s> and the like, such that there would be a single-scripture-ness.
Rather, the meditations are understood at their very inception as qualified by such-and-such qualities.
Therein, in the absence of an apprehended distinction, the difference of all [meditations] is equal.
Nor is the incorporation of all qualities prescribed in all <s>śākhā</s>s practicable — therefore, there is difference.

body.text:
#vikalpo 'viśiṣṭaphalatvāt# /
agnihotradarśapūrṇamāsādiṣu pṛthagadhikārāṇāmapi succayo dṛṣṭo niyamavāṃsteṣāṃ nityatvādupāsanāstu kāmyatayā na nityāstasmānnāsāṃ samuccayaniyamaḥ /

children.text: tena samānaphalānāṃ darśapūrṇamāsajyotiṣṭomādīnāmiva na niyamavānvikalpaḥ phabhūmārthinaḥ samuccayasyāpi saṃbhavāditi pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, for those [meditations] having the same fruit — like the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and the like — there is optionality without restriction; and for those desiring an abundance of fruit, cumulation too is possible — this is the prima facie view.

Since these meditations have as their goal the direct realization (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>) of the object of meditation, and since — when the direct realization of the object of meditation is achieved through a single meditation — the fruit is obtained from that [single meditation] alone, there is no need for another meditation.
And since direct realization does not admit of degrees — being in the same state even through a thousand means — and since the attainment of the fruit is through that [realization] alone,

children.text: upāsanāntarābhyāse ca cittaikāgratāvyāghātena kasya cidupāsanāniṣpatteriha vikalpa eva niyamavāniti rāddhāntaḥ //59 //
children.translated_text: and since the practice of another meditation would obstruct the one-pointedness of mind, preventing the completion of any [meditation] — therefore, here, optionality alone with restriction is the established conclusion. //59//

body.translated_text:
'#There is optionality, because of the non-distinction of the fruit#.'
In the <s>Agnihotra</s>, <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, and the like — even though each has a separate qualification (<s>adhikāra</s>) — cumulation (<s>samuccaya</s>) is seen; [and] they have the restriction [of being] obligatory (<s>nitya</s>). But the meditations, being desire-motivated (<s>kāmya</s>), are not obligatory — hence there is no restriction of cumulation for them.

children.translated_text: '#But the desire-motivated [meditations] may be cumulated as one wishes, or not — because of the absence of the previous reason#.'

children.text: yāsūpāsanāsu vinopāsyasākṣātkāraṇamadṛṣṭenaiva kāmyasādhanaṃ tāsāṃ kāmyadarśapaurṇamāsādivatpuruṣecchāvaśena vikalpasamuccayāviti sāmpratam //60 //
children.translated_text: In those meditations where — without the direct realization of the object of meditation — the desired goal is accomplished through <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit) alone, for them — like the desire-motivated <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and the like — optionality and cumulation depend on the person's wish — this is correct. //60//

body.text:
#aṅgeṣu yathāśrayabhāvaḥ# /
tannirdhāraṇāniyamastaddṛṣṭeḥ pṛthagdhyapratibandhaḥ phalamityatropasanāsu phalaśruteḥ parṇamayīnyāyenārthavādatayopāsanānāṃ kratvarthatvena samuccayaniyamamāśaṅkya puruṣārthatayaikaprayogavacanagrahaṇābhāve samuccayaniyamo nirastaḥ /
iha tu satyapi puruṣārthatve kasmānnaikaprayogavacanagrahaṇaṃ bhavatīti pūrvoktamarthamākṣipan pratyavatiṣṭhate /
yadyapi hi kāmyā etā upāsanāstathāpi na svatantrā bhavitumarhanti /
tathā sati hi kratvarthānāśritatayā kratuprayogādbahirapyamūṣāṃ prayogaḥ prasajyate /
naca prayujyante tatkasya hotoḥ /
kratvarthāśritānāmeva tāsāṃ tattatphaloddeśena vidhānāditi /
evaṃ cāśrayatantratvādāśritānāṃ prayogavacanenāśrayāṇāṃ samuccayaniyamenāśritānāmapi samuccayaniyamo yukta itarathā tadāśritatvānupapatteḥ /
sa ca prayogavacana upāsanāḥ samuccitanvaṃstattatphalakāmanānāmavaśyaṃbhāvamākṣipati tadabhāve tāsāṃ samuccayaniyamābhāvāditi manvānasya pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ /
rāddhāntastu yathāvihitoddiṣṭapadārthanurodhī prayogavacano na padārthasvabhāvānanyathayitumarhati /
kintu tadavirodhenāvatiṣṭhate /
tatra kratvarthānāṃ nityavadāmnānāttathābhāvasya na saṃbhavānniyamenaitāntsamuccinotu /
kāmāvabaddhāstūpāsanāḥ kāmānamanityatvānna samuccayena niyantumarhati /
nahi kāmā vidhīyate yena samuccīyerannapi tūddiśyante /
mānāntarānusārī coddeśo na tadvirodhenoddeśyamanyathayatī /

children.translated_text: For if so, the indication would be inexplicable.
Therefore, because of the non-permanence of desires, even the meditations tied to them are non-permanent.

children.text: nityānityasaṃyogavirodhāt satyapi tadāśrayāṇāṃ nityatve idameva cāśrayatantratvamāśritānāṃ yadāśraye satyeva vṛttirnāsatīti /
children.translated_text: And because of the contradiction between the permanent and the non-permanent joining together — even though the bases [i.e., the rituals] to which [the meditations] are dependent are permanent — the dependency of the dependents amounts to this: they operate when the basis is present, not when it is absent.

children.text: na tu tatra vṛttireva nāvṛttiriti tadidamuktam-āśrayatantrāṇyapi hīti //61 //
children.translated_text: But [it does not mean] that they must operate [whenever the basis is present] and cannot not-operate — this is what was stated: 'For even those dependent on the basis...' //61//

body.translated_text:
'#In the subsidiaries, [the arrangement is] according to the nature of the basis#.'
'The determination of that is not a restriction; seeing that, [there is] separate non-obstruction; the fruit [comes] from the <s>Śruti</s> of fruit in the meditations' — herein, having suspected — from the <s>parṇamayī</s> (made of <s>Parṇa</s> leaves) principle — that the meditations, because of their fruitfulness being mentioned and because of their <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory) nature, are for the purpose of the ritual (<s>kratvarthatva</s>), [and hence] there should be a restriction of cumulation — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] has rejected the restriction of cumulation because of [the meditations'] being for the person's purpose, [and] because of the absence of a single-performance statement.
But here, even when [the meditations] are for the person's purpose, [the question is:] why is there no single-performance statement? — [the opponent,] objecting with this previously stated point, stands firm.
For even though these meditations are desire-motivated, they cannot be independent.
For if so, since — [being] not dependent on the ritual purpose — the performance of these [meditations] even outside the ritual performance would follow.
But they are not performed [outside the ritual]. Why not?
Because they are prescribed for such-and-such fruit-purposes as dependent on such-and-such ritual purposes.
And thus, since — being dependent on the basis — the dependents, through the single-performance statement of the bases, have a restriction of cumulation, the dependents too should have a restriction of cumulation — otherwise their dependency would be inexplicable.
And that single-performance statement — stating that the meditations are cumulated — implies the inevitability for those who desire such-and-such fruits. In its absence, since there would be no restriction of cumulation for them — this is the prima facie view.
But the established conclusion is: The single-performance statement, conforming to the objects prescribed and indicated [in the text], cannot alter the nature of those objects.
Rather, it stands without conflicting with that [nature].
Therein, the ritual-purpose [meditations] — being mentioned as obligatory — cannot have that [obligatory] character not exist; hence let them be invariably cumulated.
But the meditations — being tied to desires, and desires being non-permanent — cannot deserve to be restricted by cumulation.
For desires are not prescribed — they are merely indicated.
And indication, following other valid means [of knowledge], does not alter the indicated [object] in contravention of that [other valid knowledge].

body.text: #samāhārāt /

children.translated_text: '#From the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s seat, [the <s>Adhvaryu</s>] corrects even the <s>Udgītha</s> that has gone wrong#' — thus.
The word '<s>api</s>' [means] 'even the <s>Udgītha</s> that has gone wrong, being of a different kind.'

children.text: vedāntarohitapraṇavodgīthaikatvapratyayasāmarthyāddhotṛkarmaṇaḥ śaṃsanādudrātā pratisamādadhāti kiṃ tadityata āha durudrīthamapi vedāntarodite caudrātre karmaṇi utpannaṃ kṣatam /
children.translated_text: By the power of the cognition of the unity of <s>Praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃkāra</s>) and <s>Udgītha</s> — disclosed in the <s>Vedānta</s> — the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s ritual act of recitation (<s>śaṃsana</s>) corrects [the error]. What is that [error]? — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: [He corrects] even the <s>Udgītha</s> that has gone wrong — [meaning] the defect (<s>kṣata</s>) that has arisen in the <s>Udgāna</s> (chanting) ritual — the ritual that is disclosed in the <s>Vedānta</s>.
Having said thus, 'of [the <s>Brahman</s>] stated in the <s>Vedānta</s>, the cognition' and so on should be construed. //63//

body.translated_text: '#Because of correction (<s>samāhāra</s>)#.'

children.translated_text: '#And because of the <s>Śruti</s> of the commonality of qualities#.'
The explanation of this <s>sūtra</s> is both by way of positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) and by way of negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>).
The rest has an obvious meaning. //64//

body.text: iti śrīvācaspatimiśraviracite śārīrakabhagavatpādabhāṣyavibhāge bhāmatyāṃ tṛtīyādhyāyasya tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ //3 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the third <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s> in the <s>Bhāmatī</s>, the elucidation of the <s>Śārīraka-Bhāṣya</s> of the Blessed Master [<s>Śaṅkara</s>], composed by the venerable <s>Vācaspati Miśra</s>. //3//

body.text: #tṛtīyādhyāye caturthaḥ pādaḥ# /
body.translated_text: '#The fourth <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s>#.'

body.text:
#puruṣārtho 'taḥśabdāditi bādarāyaṇaḥ# /
sthitaṃ kṛtvopaniṣadāmapavargākhyapuruṣārthasādhanātmajñānaparatvamupāsanānāṃ ca tattatpuruṣārthasādhanatvamadhastanaṃ vicārajātamabhinirvartitam /
samprati tu kimaupaniṣadātmatattvajñānamapavargasādhanatayā puruṣārthamāho kratuprayogāpekṣitakartṛpratipādakatayā kratvarthamiti mīmāṃsāmahe /
yadā ca kratvarthaṃ tadā yāvanmātraṃ kratuprayogavidhināpekṣitaṃ kartṛtvamāmuṣmikaphalopabhoktṛtvaṃ ca na caitadanityatve ghaṭate kṛtavipraṇāśākṛtābhyāgamaprasaṅgādato nityatvamapi, tāvanmātramupaniṣatsu vivakṣitam /
ito 'nyadanapekṣitaṃ viparītaṃ ca nopaniṣadarthaḥ syāt /
yathā śuddhatvādi /
yadyapi jīvānuvādena tasya brahmatvapratipādanaparatvamupaniṣadāmiti mahatā prabandhena tatra tatra pratipāditaṃ tathāpyatra keṣāñcitpūrvapakṣaśahkābījānāṃ nirākaraṇe tadeva sthūṇanikhanananyāyena niścalīkriyata ityasti vicāraprayojanam /
tatra yadyapi prokṣaṇādivadātmajñānaṃ na kañcitkratumārabhyādhītam, yadyapi ca kartṛmātraṃ nāvyabhicāritakratusaṃbandhaṃ kartṛmātrasya laukikeṣvapi karmasu darśanādyena parṇatādivadanārabhyādhītamapyavyabhicaritakratusaṃbandhajihūdvāreṇa vākyenaiva kratvarthamāpadyate tathāpi yādṛśa ātmā kartāmuṣmikasvargādiphalabhogabhāgī dehādyatirikte vedāntaiḥ pratipādyate na tādṛśasyāsti laukikeṣu karmasūpayogaḥ /
teṣāmaihikaphalānāṃ śarīrānatiriktenāpi yādṛśatādṛśena kartraupapatteḥ /
āmuṣmikaphalānāṃ tu vaidikānāṃ karmaṇāṃ tamantareṇāsaṃbhavāttatsaṃbandha evāyamaupaniṣadaḥ ka4teti tadavyabhicārāttānyanusmārayajjuhvādivadvākyenaiva tajjñānaṃ parṇatāvatkratvaidamarthyamāpadyata iti phalaśrutirarthavādaḥ /
taduktam-'dravyasaṃskārakarmasu parārthatvātphalaśrutirarthavādaḥ syāt' iti aupaniṣadātmajñānasaṃskṛto hi kartā pāralaukikaphalopabhogayogyo 'smīti vidyāvācchraddhāvānkratuprayogāṅgaṃ nānyathā prokṣitā iva vrīhayaḥ kratvaṅgamiti /
priyādisūcitasya ca saṃsāriṇa evātmano draṣṭavyatvena pratijñāpanādapahatapāpmatvādi tu tadviśeṣaṇaṃ tasyaiva stutyartham /
na tu tatparatvamupaniṣadām /
tasmātkratvarthamevātmajñānaṃ kartṛsaṃskāradvārā na punaḥ puruṣārthamiti /
etadupodbalārthaṃ ca brahmavidāmācārādiḥ śrutyavagata upanyastaḥ /
na kevalaṃ vākyādātmajñānasya kratvarthatvam /
tṛtīyāśruteśca /
na tvetatprakṛtodgīthavidyāviṣayaṃ yadeva vidyayeti sarvanāmavadhāraṇābhyāṃ vyāpteradhigamat /

children.text: yathā ya eva dhūmavāndeśaḥ sa vahvimāniti /
children.translated_text: just as [in the inference:] 'whatever place has smoke, that has fire.'

children.text: samanvārambhavacanaṃ ca phalārambhe vidyākarmaṇoḥ sāhityaṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: And the statement of joint commencement (<s>samanvārambha</s>) shows the conjunction of <s>vidyā</s> and <s>karma</s> in the production of the fruit.

children.text: tacca yadyapyāpneyādiyagaṣaṭkavatsamapradhānatvenāpi bhavati tathāpyuktayā yuktyā vidyāyāḥ karma pratyaṅgabhāvenaiva netavyam /
children.translated_text: And although that [conjunction] could be one of equal principality — like the group of six sacrifices beginning with <s>Āpneya</s> — nevertheless, by the reasoning stated [above], <s>vidyā</s> is to be led to subsidiary-hood alone with respect to <s>karma</s>.

children.text: vedārthajñānavataḥ karmavidhānādupaniṣado 'pi vedārtha iti tajjñānamapi karmāṅgamiti //1 //
children.translated_text: Since ritual action is enjoined for one who knows the meaning of the <s>Veda</s>, and the <s>Upaniṣad</s>s too are the meaning of the <s>Veda</s>, knowledge of them too is a subsidiary of ritual. //1//

body.translated_text:
'#The human goal (<s>puruṣārtha</s>) — because of the word "<s>ataḥ</s>" (therefore) — so [holds] <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>#.'
Having established that the <s>Upaniṣad</s>s have as their purport the knowledge of the Self (<s>ātmajñāna</s>) — which is the means to the human goal called liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) — and that the meditations (<s>upāsanā</s>s) are the means to their respective human goals, the lower series of investigations has been brought to completion.
But now we inquire: Is the <s>Upaniṣad</s>ic knowledge of the reality of the Self a human goal (<s>puruṣārtha</s>) by virtue of being the means to liberation? Or is it for the sake of ritual (<s>kratvartham</s>) by virtue of presenting the agent required by the injunction of ritual performance?
And when it is for the sake of ritual, then only so much as is required by the injunction of ritual performance — agent-hood and the capacity to enjoy the fruit in the other world; and since this is not possible if [the self] were impermanent — because of the unwanted consequence of the loss of what has been done and the incurrence of what has not been done — [the self's] eternality too — just that much is intended in the <s>Upaniṣad</s>s.
What is beyond this — what is not required [by ritual] and what is contrary [to it] — would not be the meaning of the <s>Upaniṣad</s>s.
For example, [attributes like] purity (<s>śuddhatva</s>) and the like.
Although it has been demonstrated at length in various places that the purport of the <s>Upaniṣad</s>s is to teach the <s>Brahman</s>-hood of the <s>jīva</s> through its restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>), nevertheless, here — in the refutation of certain seeds of the prima facie view's doubts — that very [conclusion] is firmly established by the principle of 'driving in the post' (<s>sthūṇānikhanana-nyāya</s>) — hence there is a purpose for this inquiry.
Therein, although — like the sprinkling (<s>prokṣaṇa</s>) and the like — knowledge of the Self was not studied as commencing any particular ritual; and although mere agent-hood — not being invariably connected with ritual, since mere agent-hood is seen even in worldly actions — by which, like the <s>parṇa</s>-leaf and the like, even though not studied as commencing [a ritual], it becomes subsidiary to the ritual through the sentence [establishing] its invariable ritual-connection — still, the kind of Self that is the agent, the enjoyer of fruits such as heaven and the like in the other world, distinct from the body and the like, as taught in the <s>Vedānta</s>s — such [a self] has no utility in worldly actions.
Because for those [worldly actions] that have this-worldly fruits, agent-hood is possible even by someone who is not distinct from the body.
But for rituals yielding other-worldly fruits, [the self] being impossible without it [i.e., without being distinct from the body], this <s>Upaniṣad</s>ic connection [of the self with ritual] is precisely through its invariability with respect to [ritual] — and reminding [the agent] of that, like the <s>juhū</s>-ladle and the like, that knowledge becomes subsidiary to ritual through the sentence itself, like the <s>parṇa</s>-leaf and the like — hence the [<s>Upaniṣad</s>ic] declaration of the fruit is an <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory statement).
This has been said: 'In the case of actions involving the consecration of substances, because of serving another's purpose, the declaration of the fruit would be an <s>arthavāda</s>.' For the agent consecrated by <s>Upaniṣad</s>ic self-knowledge — [thinking] 'I am fit for the enjoyment of other-worldly fruits such as heaven' — with faith imbued with <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), [becomes] a subsidiary of ritual performance — not otherwise — just as sprinkled rice-grains [become] a subsidiary of ritual.
And since the Self indicated by [attributes such as] '<s>priya</s>' (dear) and the like — the self of the <s>saṃsārin</s> (transmigrating being) — has been pledged as what is to be seen (<s>draṣṭavya</s>), [the attributes] such as '<s>apahatapāpmatva</s>' (freedom from evil) and the like are merely qualifications of that [self], for the purpose of praising it.
But they are not the purport of the <s>Upaniṣad</s>s.
Therefore, self-knowledge is for the sake of ritual alone, through the door of consecrating the agent — not for the human goal [of liberation].
And for corroborating this, the conduct and the like of the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> — as known from <s>Śruti</s> — have been cited [by the opponent].
Not only from the sentence [does] the ritual-subsidiary-ness of self-knowledge [follow];
but also from the <s>Śruti</s> of the third [person form].
Nor is this [<s>Śruti</s>] restricted to the <s>Udgītha-vidyā</s> (meditation on the <s>Udgītha</s>) that is the current topic — because of the pervasion [established] by the pronoun and the emphatic particle in '<s>yad eva vidyayā</s>' ('whatever indeed by knowledge'),

children.translated_text: '#And because of the restriction (<s>niyama</s>)#.'
Easy [to understand]. //7//

body.text:
#siddhāntayati-adhikopadeśāttu bādarāyaṇasyaivaṃ taddarśanāt# /
yadi śarīrādyatiriktaḥ kartā bhoktātmetyetanmatra upaniṣadaḥ paryavasitāḥ syustataḥ syādevaṃ, na tvetadasti /
tāstvevaṃbhūtajīvānuvādena tasya śuddhabuddhodāsīnabrahmarūpatāpratipādanaparā iti tatra tatrāsakṛdāveditam /
anadhigatārthabodhanasvarasatā hi śabdasya pramāṇāntarasiddhānuvādena /
tathā caupaniṣadātmajñānasya kratvanuṣṭhānavirodhinaḥ kratusaṃbandha eva nāsti /
kimaṅga punaḥ tadavyabhicārastataśca kratuśeṣatā /
tathāca nāpavargaphalaśruterarthavādamātratvamapi tu phalaparatvameva /

children.text: ata eva priyādisūcitena saṃsāriṇātmanopakramasya tasyaivātmano 'dhikopadidikṣāyāṃ paramātmanātyantābheda upadiśyate /
children.translated_text: For this very reason, when the wish is to teach additionally about that very Self — indicated by '<s>priya</s>' (dear) and the like as a <s>saṃsārin</s> (transmigrating being) at the commencement — its absolute non-difference from <s>Paramātman</s> (the Supreme Self) is taught.

children.text: yathā samāropitasya bhujagasya rajjurūpādatyantābhedaḥ pratipādyate yo 'yaṃ sarpaḥ sā rajjuriti /
children.translated_text: Just as the absolute non-difference of the superimposed snake from the rope-form is taught: 'What is this serpent — that is [in fact] a rope.'
Just as evidence has been cited for <s>vidyā</s>'s subsidiary-hood to <s>karma</s>, evidence for [<s>vidyā</s>'s] independence from <s>karma</s> has [also] been stated.
Therein, the evidence for <s>karma</s>-subsidiary-hood admits of being otherwise explained; but the evidence for <s>vidyā</s> being independent does not admit of being otherwise explained. //8//

body.translated_text:
'#[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] establishes the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion): "But because of the additional teaching, <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> [holds] thus, for that is observed"#.'
If the <s>Upaniṣad</s>s had concluded with just this much — that the agent and enjoyer is a Self distinct from the body and the like — then it would be so [i.e., self-knowledge would be for the sake of ritual].
But this is not the case.
Rather, they — through the restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) of such a <s>jīva</s> — have the purport of teaching its nature as pure, awakened, quiescent <s>Brahman</s> — this has been communicated again and again in various places.
For the natural tendency of a word as a valid means of knowledge is to convey what is not [otherwise] known, [which would be undermined] by mere restatement of what is already known through another valid means.
And thus, since <s>Upaniṣad</s>ic self-knowledge is contradictory to the performance of ritual, its connection with ritual does not exist at all.
How much less [can one speak of] its invariable connection with [ritual], and hence its being subsidiary to ritual.
And thus, the <s>Śruti</s> declaring liberation as the fruit is not a mere <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory statement) but has liberation as its very purport.

children.translated_text: '#[The pervasion is] not universal#.'
The pervasion too is with reference to the <s>Udgītha-vidyā</s> alone — because it alone is the current topic — not with reference to all [<s>vidyā</s>s] without exception.

children.text: yatha sarve brāhmaṇā bhojyantāmiti nimintritāpekṣayā teṣāmeva prakṛtatvāt //10 //
children.translated_text: Just as 'Let all the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s be fed' — [refers] to the invited ones alone, because they alone are the current topic. //10//

body.text: #vibhāgaḥ śatavat# /

children.translated_text: Easy [to understand].

children.text: avibhāge 'pi na doṣa ityāha- #na cedaṃ samanvārambhavacanamiti# /
children.translated_text: Even if there were no division, there would be no defect — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Nor is this a statement of joint commencement#.'
The <s>vidyā</s> pertaining to the <s>saṃsārin</s> (transmigrating being) is '#enjoined#' — like the <s>Udgītha-vidyā</s>.
And [<s>vidyā</s>] is also prohibited — as in the case of [pursuing] knowledge through false scriptures (<s>asacchāstra</s>). //11//

body.translated_text: '#The division (<s>vibhāga</s>) is like [that of] a hundred#.'

body.text: #adhyayanamātravata eva karmavidhirna#tūpaniṣadadhyayanavataḥ /

children.text: etaduktaṃ bhavati-yadadhyayanamarthāvabodhaparyantaṃ karmasūpayujyate yathā karmavidhivākyānāṃ tanmātravata evādhikāraḥ karmasu nopaniṣadadhyanavataḥ tadadhyayanasya karmasvanupayogāditi /
children.translated_text: What is stated amounts to this: the study that is useful for ritual — extending to the comprehension of meaning — as in the case of the sentences prescribing ritual action — for one who has just that much [study] alone is there eligibility for rituals, not for one who has studied the <s>Upaniṣad</s>s, since such study has no utility in rituals.

children.text: adhyayanamātravata eveti mātragrahaṇenārthajñānaṃ vā vyavacchinnamiti manvāno bhrāntaścodayati- #nanvevaṃ satīti# /
children.translated_text: Thinking that the word 'merely' (<s>mātra</s>) in 'one who has merely studied' excludes the knowledge of meaning, the mistaken [opponent] objects: '#But then, in that case#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>], revealing his own intent, resolves: '#We do not [mean that]#.'
The word 'merely' (<s>mātra</s>) is with reference to the study of the <s>Upaniṣad</s>s, not with reference to the comprehension of meaning — this is the meaning. //12//

body.translated_text: '#The injunction of ritual action is for one who has merely studied — not for one who has studied the <s>Upaniṣad</s>s#.'

children.translated_text: '#Not [contradictory], because of the non-specification#.'
'Performing actions indeed here' — [this <s>Śruti</s>] pertains to one who is subject to <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — this is the meaning. //13//

body.text: vidyavadviṣayatve 'pyavirodho vidyāstutyarthatvādityāha- #stutayo 'numatirvā# //14 //
body.translated_text: Even if [the <s>Śruti</s>] pertained to one who possesses <s>vidyā</s>, there would be no contradiction, because it would be for the purpose of praising <s>vidyā</s> — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#[The <s>Śruti</s>s are] praises or permissions#.' //14//

children.text: apica vidyāphalaṃ pratyakṣaṃ darśayantī śrutiḥ kālāntarabhāviphalakarmāṅgatvaṃ vidyāyā nirākarotītyāha- #kāmakāreṇa caike# /
children.translated_text: Moreover, the <s>Śruti</s> — showing the fruit of <s>vidyā</s> as directly perceptible — refutes <s>vidyā</s>'s subsidiary-hood to ritual, [which would involve] a fruit [occurring only] at a later time — thus [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#And some [teach] by free will (<s>kāmakāra</s>)#.'
<s>Kāmakāra</s> (free will) means wish (<s>icchā</s>). //15//
'#And the dissolution (<s>upamarda</s>)#.'

By [the <s>sūtra</s>] 'because of the additional teaching,' [attributes such as] purity (<s>śuddha</s>), awakening (<s>buddha</s>), and quiescence (<s>udāsīna</s>) and the like of the Self have been stated.
But here, the dissolution of the entire division of action, instrument, and fruit [is stated]. //16//
'#And for the <s>ūrdhvaretasa</s>s (celibates), [there is eligibility], because the word [says so]#.'
Easy to understand. //17//

body.text:
#parāmarśaṃ jaiminiracodanā cāpavadati hi# /
siddha ūrdhvaretasāmāśramitve tadvidyānāmakarmāṅgatayāpavargārthaṃ syāt /
āśramitvaṃ tveṣāmanyārthaparāmarśamātrānna sidhyati /
vidhyabhāvāt /
smṛtyācāraprasiddhiśca teṣāṃ pratyakṣaśrutivirodhādapramāṇam /
nindati hi pratyakṣā śrutirāśramāntaraṃ 'vīrahā vā eṣa devānām' ityādikā /
pratyakṣaśrutivirodhe ca smṛtyācārayoraprāmāṇyamuktaṃ 'virodhe tvanapekṣaṃ syādasati hyanumānam' iti /
tadetatsarvamāha- #trayo#
body.translated_text:
'#[<s>Jaimini</s> holds that the] reference (<s>parāmarśa</s>) [to other life-stages is merely] for another purpose — [<s>Jaimini</s> holds this] because the injunction (<s>codanā</s>) overrides (<s>apavadati</s>)#.'
When the eligibility of the <s>ūrdhvaretasa</s>s (lifelong celibates) for the [other] life-stages (<s>āśrama</s>s) is established, then the <s>vidyā</s>s belonging to them — not being subsidiary to <s>karma</s> — would serve the purpose of liberation (<s>apavarga</s>).
But the eligibility of these [celibates] for the other life-stages is not established merely from the reference [to those stages] being for another purpose.
Because of the absence of an [explicit] injunction.
And the well-known establishment [of these life-stages] through <s>Smṛti</s> and traditional practice is not a valid authority, because of the conflict with direct <s>Śruti</s>.
For the direct <s>Śruti</s> censures the other life-stages: 'He is indeed a slayer of the gods' (<s>vīrahā vā eṣa devānām</s>) and the like.
And when there is a conflict with direct <s>Śruti</s>, the non-authoritativeness of <s>Smṛti</s> and traditional practice has been stated: 'When there is a conflict, [<s>Smṛti</s>] should be disregarded, for inference [applies only] in the absence [of direct <s>Śruti</s>].'
All this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states: '#Three branches of <s>dharma</s>#'

body.text:
#dharmaskandhā ityādinā /
anadhikṛtaviṣayā veti# /
andhapaṅgavādayo hi ye naimittikakarmānadhikṛtāstānpratyāśramāntaravidhiriti /
#apicāpavaditi hi# /
na kevalamanyaparatayā parāmarśasyāśramāntaraṃ na labhyate api tvāśramāntaranindādvāreṇāpavādādapītyarthaḥ /
syādetat /
bhavatveṣa parāmarśo 'nyārthaḥ /
ye ceme 'raṇya ityādibhyastvāśramāntaraṃ setasyatītyata āha- #ye ceme 'raṇya iti# /
asyāpi devapathopadeśaparatvānnaitatparatvamityarthaḥ /
na cānyaparādapi sphuṭatarāśramāntarapratyata ityāha- #saṃdigdhaṃ ceti# /

children.text: nahi tapa eva dvitīya ityatrāśramāntarābhidhāyī kaścidasti śabda iti /
children.translated_text: For in '<s>tapa eva dvitīya</s>' ('austerity indeed is the second [branch]'), there is no word at all that designates another life-stage.

children.text: nanvetameva pravrājina iti vacanādāśramāntaraṃ setsyatītyata āha- #tathaitameveti# /
children.translated_text: Now, from the statement '<s>nanv etam eva pravrājinaḥ</s>' ('Indeed, these are the <s>parivrāj</s>s [wandering renunciants]'), the other life-stage will be established — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#And that very statement#.'
This too has the purport of praising [the status] in the world.

children.text: adhikaraṇārambhamākṣipya nāsti pratyakṣavacanamitikṛtvā cinteyamiti samādhatte- #nanu brahmacaryādeveti# //18 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara</s>], having raised the objection against the commencement of the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> [by noting] that there is no direct statement [of other life-stages], resolves [it by saying] that [it] should be investigated — '#But [the <s>Śruti</s> says:] "from <s>brahmacarya</s> alone"#.' //18//

body.translated_text:
'#and so on. "Or for those not eligible"#.'
For those who are not eligible for the regular (<s>naimittika</s>) <s>karma</s>s — such as the blind, lame, and the like — the injunction of the other life-stages [is intended].
'#Moreover, [the injunction] overrides (<s>apavadati</s>)#.'
Not only is the reference [to other life-stages] not obtained as [establishing] the other life-stages because of being for another purpose, but moreover, through the door of censuring the other life-stages, there is also an overriding — this is the meaning.
One might object: let this reference be for another purpose; but from [the <s>Śruti</s>s] '#those who in the forest#' and the like, the other life-stages will be established — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Those who in the forest#.'
This too has the purport of teaching the path of the gods (<s>devapatha</s>) — not the purport [of establishing] that [life-stage] — this is the meaning.
Nor does [this passage] clearly convey the other life-stages even incidentally — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#And it is doubtful#.'

body.text:
#anuṣṭheyaṃ bādarāyaṇaḥ sāmyaśruteḥ# /
bhavatvanyārthaḥ parāmarśastathāpyetasmādāśramāntarāṇi pratīyamānāni ca nāpākaraṇamarhanti /
evaṃ tānyapākriyeranyadyasmānna pratīyeran /
pratīyamānāni vā śrutyā bādhyeran /
na tāvanna pratīyante /
tathāhi-trayo dharmaskandhā iti skandhatritvaṃ pratijñātam /
tatra skandhaśabdo yadyāśramaparo na syāditi tu samūhavacanastato dharmāṇāṃ yajñādīnāṃ prātisvikotpattīnāṃ kimapekṣya tritvamaṅkhyā suvyavasthāpyeta /
ekaikāśramopasaṃgṛhītāstvāśramāṇāṃ tritvācchakyāstritve vyavasthāpayitumityāśramatritvapratijñopapattiḥ /

children.text: tatra yajñādiliṅgo gṛhāśrama eko dharmaskandho brahmacārīti dvitīyastapa iti ca, tapaḥpradhānāttu vānaprasthāśramānnānyaḥ, brahmasaṃstha iti ca pāriśeṣyātparivrāḍiti vakṣyati /
children.translated_text: Therein, the householder's life-stage (<s>gṛhāśrama</s>) — characterized by sacrifice and the like — is one branch of <s>dharma</s>; '<s>brahmacārī</s>' is the second; and '<s>tapas</s>' (austerity) — since the forest-dweller's (<s>vānaprastha</s>) life-stage is characterized by the predominance of <s>tapas</s>, there is no other [branch beyond these three]; and '<s>brahmasaṃstha</s>' (one established in <s>Brahman</s>) — by the method of elimination, [this refers to] the <s>parivrāj</s> (wandering renunciant) — as [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] will state.

children.text: tasmādanyaparādapi parāmarthādaśramāntarāṇi pratīyamānāni devatādhikaraṇanyāyena na śakyante 'pākartum /
children.translated_text: Therefore, even though the reference is for another purpose, the other life-stages — being perceived from that reference — cannot be set aside, by the principle of the <s>devatādhikaraṇa</s> (topic of deities).

children.text: naca pratyakṣaśrutivirodho vīrahā vetyādeḥ pratipannagārhasthyaṃ pramādādajñānādvāgnimudvāsayituṃ pravṛttaṃ pratyupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: Nor is there a conflict with direct <s>Śruti</s> — because [the <s>Śruti</s>] 'He is a slayer' and the like can be explained as pertaining to one who, having already entered the householder's [life-stage], through negligence or ignorance, is inclined to extinguish his [sacred] fires.

children.text: evañca avirodhe siddhavatparāmarśādaśramāntarāṇāṃ śāstrāntarasiddhiṃ vā kalpayiṣyāmo yathopavītavidhipare vākye 'upavyayate devalakṣmameva tatkurute' ityatra nivītaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ prācīnāvītaṃ pitṛṇāmiti śāstrāntarasiddhayornivītaprācīnāvītayoḥ parāmarśa iti //19 //
children.translated_text: And thus, when there is no conflict, from the reference to [the life-stages] as established facts, we shall postulate that the other life-stages are established through another scripture — just as in the sentence whose purport is the injunction of the sacred thread (<s>upavīta</s>), 'He puts on the sacred thread; that which belongs to the gods he makes thus' — therein, '<s>nivīta</s>' (the human-style wearing) for humans and '<s>prācīnāvīta</s>' (the ancestral-style wearing) for the ancestors are established through another scripture, and are referred to [in this passage]. //19//

body.translated_text:
'#[The other life-stages] are to be observed (<s>anuṣṭheyam</s>) — so [holds] <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>, because of the <s>Śruti</s> of equality#.'
Let the reference be for another purpose; nevertheless, the other life-stages — being perceived [in the text] — do not deserve to be set aside.
They could be set aside only if they were not perceived;
or if, [even when] perceived, they were overridden (<s>bādhyeran</s>) by [another] <s>Śruti</s>.
To begin with, they are not unperceived.
For thus: 'Three branches of <s>dharma</s>' — the threefold division of branches (<s>skandha</s>s) has been asserted.
Therein, if the word '<s>skandha</s>' (branch) were not about life-stages (<s>āśrama</s>s) but were a collective term, then — with reference to what — could the threefold division of <s>dharma</s>s such as sacrifice and the like or of the individual-specific births be well-established?
But [the <s>dharma</s>s] subsumed under each life-stage — because of the threefold [division of] life-stages — can be established as three — hence the assertion of a threefold division of life-stages is vindicated.

body.text:
#vidhirvā dhāraṇavat# /
yadyapi brahmasaṃsthatvastu tiparatayāsya saṃdarbhasyaikavākyatā gamyate /
saṃbhavāntyāṃ caikavākyatāyāṃ vākyabhedo 'nyāpyaḥ /
tathāpyāśramāntarāṇāṃ pūrvasiddherabhāvātparāmarśānupapatteḥ, aparāmarśe ca stuterasaṃbhavena kiṃparatayā ekavākyatāstvitī tāṃ bhaṅktvā dhāraṇavadvaramapūrvatvādvidhirevāstu /
yathā 'adhastātsamidhaṃ dhārayannanudravedupari hi devebhyo dhārayati' ityatra satyāmapyadhodhāraṇenaikavākyatāpratītau vidhīyata evoparidhāraṇamapūrvatvāt /
tathoktam 'vidhistu dhāraṇe 'pūrvatvāt' it /
tathehāpyāśramāntaraparāmarśaśrutirvidhareveti kalpyte /
saṃprati parāmarśe 'pītareṣāmāśramāṇāṃ brahmasaṃsthatā saṃstavasāmarthyādeva vidhātavyā /
na khalvavidheyaṃ saṃstūyate tadarthatvātsaṃstavasyetyāha- #yadāpīti# /
atrāvāntaravicāramārabhate- #sā ca kiṃ caturṣviti# /
vicāraprayojanamāha- #yadi ceti# /
nanu anāśramyeva brahmasaṃstho bhaviṣyatītyata āha- #anāśrayamitveti# /
tatra pūrvapakṣamāha- #tatra tapaḥśabdeneti# /
ayamabhisaṃdhiḥ /
yadi tāvadbrahmasaṃstha iti padaṃ pratyastamityāvayavārthaṃ parivrājake 'śvakarṇādipadavadrūḍhaṃ tadāśramaprāptimātreṇaivāmṛtībhāva iti na tadbhāvāyā brahmajñānamapekṣeta /
tathāca nānyaḥ panthā vidyate 'yanāyeti virodhaḥ /
naca saṃbhatyavayavārthe samudāyasaktikalpanā /
tasmādbrahmaṇi saṃsthāsyeti /
brahmasaṃsthaḥ /
evañca caturṣvāśrameṣu yasyaiva brahmaṇi niṣṭhatvamāśramiṇaḥ sa brahmasaṃstho 'mṛtatvametīti yuktam /
tatra tāvadbrahmacārigṛhasthau svaśabdābhihitau tapaḥpadena ca tapaḥpradhānatayā bhikṣuvānaprasthāvupasthāpitau /
bhikṣurapi hi samādhikaśaucāṣṭagrāsībhojananiyamādbhavati vānaprasthavattapaḥpradhānaḥ /
naca gṛhasthādeḥ karmiṇo brahmaniṣṭhatvāsaṃbhavaḥ /
yadi tāvatkarmayogaḥ karmitā sā bhikṣorapi kāyavāṅmanobhirasti /
atha ye na brahmārpaṇena karma kurvanti kintu kāmārthitayā te karmiṇaḥ /
tathā sati gṛhasthādayo 'pi brahmārpaṇena karma kurvāṇā na karmiṇaḥ /
tasmādbrahmaṇi tātparyaṃ brahmaniṣṭhatā na tu karmatyāgaḥ /
pramāṇavirodhāt /
tapasā ca dvayorāśramayorekīkaraṇena traya iti tritvamupapadyate /
evañca trayo 'pyāśramā abrahmasaṃsthāḥ santaḥ puṇyalokabhājo bhavanti yaḥ punareteṣu brahmasaṃsthaḥ so 'mṛtatvabhāgiti /
naca yeṣāṃ puṇyalokabhāktvaṃ teṣāmevāmṛtatvamiti virodhaḥ /
yathā devadattayajñadattau mandaprajñāvabhūtāṃ saṃprati tayoryajñādattastu śāstrābhyāsātpaṭuprajño vartate iti tathehāpi ya evābrahmasaṃsthāḥ /
puṇyalokabhājasta eva brahmasaṃsthā amṛtatvabhāja ityavasthābhedādavirodhaḥ /
tathāca brahmasaṃstha iti yaugikaṃ padaṃ prakṛtaviṣayaṃ bhaviṣyati /
yathā āgnepyāgnīdhramupatiṣṭhata ityatra viniyuktāpi prakṛtaivāgneyī gṛhyate /
naca viniyuktaviniyogavirodhaḥ /
yadi hyatrāgnotyupadiśyeta tato yathā pratītā tathoddiśyate /
viniyuktā ca pratītirbhavediti viniyuktaviniyogavirodhaḥ /
iha tu āgnīdhropasthāne sā vidheyatvena viniyujyate /
na tūddiśyate /
vidheyatvena ca viniyoge āgneyīpadārthāpekṣaṇātprakṛtātikrame pramāṇābhāvāt /
tāvatā ca śāstropapatternāprakṛtānāmapi grahaṇasaṃbhavaḥ /
naca yātayāmatayā na viniyogaḥ /
vācasteme sarveṣāmeva mantrāṇāṃ viniyogādanyatrāpyaviniyogaprasaṅgāt /
tathehāpi prakṛtā evāśramā buddhiviparivartinaḥ parāmṛśyante nānuktaḥ parivrāḍeveti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ /
rāddhāntamupakramate- #tadayuktam /
nahi satyāṃ gatau vānaprasthaviśeṣeneti# /
yathopakrāntaṃ tathaiva parisamāpanamucitam /
yatsaṃkhyākāśca ye prasiddhāste tatsaṃkhyākā eva kīrtyante iti cocitam /
na tu satyāṃ gatāvutsargasyāpavādo yujyate /
aśādhāraṇenaikaikena lakṣaṇenaikeka āśramo vaktumupakrānta iti tathaiva samāpanamucitam /
na tu sādhāraṇāsādhāraṇābhyāmupakramasamāptī śrliṣyete /
naca tapo nāma nāsādhāraṇaṃ vānaprasthānāmityata āha- #tapaścāsādhāraṇa iti# /
na khalu parākādibhiḥ kāyakleśapradhāno yathā vānaprasthastathā bhikṣuḥ satyapyaṣṭagrāsādiniyame /
naca śaucasantoṣaśamādayastapaḥ pakṣe vartante tatra vṛddhānāṃ tapaḥprasiddherasiddheḥ /
ata eva vṛddhāstapaso bhedena śaucādīnācakṣate-'śaucasantoṣatapaḥsvādhyāyeśvarapraṇidhānāni niyamāḥ' iti /
siddhasaṃkhyābhedeṣu ca saṃkhyāntarābhidhānamaśliṣṭamityāha- #catuṣṭvena ceti /
apica bhedavyapadeśo 'treti# /
traya eta iti kiṃ bhikṣurapi parāmṛśyate kintvā bhikṣuvarjaṃ traya eva /
na tāvantraya iti bhikṣusaṃgrahe tadvarjanamete traya ityatra vartuṃ śakyam /
eva iti prakṛtānāṃ sākalyena parāmarśādbhikṣusaṃgrahe ca na tasya puṇyalokatvamabrahmasaṃsthātvābhāvādbhikṣoḥ /
tena tasya brahmasaṃsthasya sadā puṇyalokatvamamṛtatvaṃ ceti virodhaḥ /
triṣu ca brahmasaṃsthapade yadeti saṃbandhanīyam /
bhikṣau ca sadeti vaiṣamyam /
tadidamuktam- #pṛthaktve ceti# /
pūrvapakṣābhāsaṃ smārayati- #kathaṃ punarbrahmasaṃsthaśabdo yogāditi# /
tannirākaroti- #atrocyata iti# /
ayamabhisaṃdhiḥ /
satyaṃ yaugikaḥ śabdaḥ sati prakṛtasaṃbhave na tadatipattyāprakṛte vartitumarhati /
asati tu saṃbhave mā bhūtpramādapāṭha ityaprakṛte vartayitavyaḥ, darśitaścātrāsaṃbhavo 'dhastāditi /
eṣa hi brahmasaṃsthatālakṣaṇo dharmo bhikṣorasādhāraṇa āśramāntarāṇi tatsaṃsthānyatatsaṃsthāni ca bhikṣustatsaṃstha ityeva /
tatsaṃsthatā hi svābhāvaṃ vyavacchindantī virodhādyastatsaṃstha eva tatrāñjasī nānyatra /
#śamadamādistu tadīya iti# /
svāṅgamavyavadhāyakamityarthaḥ /
brahmasaṃsthatvamasādhāraṇaṃ parivrājakadharmaṃ śrutirādarśayatītyāha- #tathāca nyāsa iti brahmeti# /
sarvasaṅgaparityāgo hi nyāsaḥ sa brahmā kuta ityata āha- #brahmā hi paraḥ# /
ataḥ paro brahmeti /
kimapekṣya paraḥ saṃnyāsa ityata āha- #tāni vā etānyavarāṇi tapāṃsi nyāsa evātyarecayaditi# /

children.translated_text: What is being said is this: <s>nyāsa</s> (renunciation), characterized by the complete abandonment of all desires (<s>eṣaṇā</s>) out of devotion to <s>Brahman</s>, is <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: tathā cedṛśaṃ nyāsalakṣaṇaṃ brahmasaṃsthatvaṃ bhikṣorevāsādhāraṇaṃ netareṣāmāśramiṇām /
children.translated_text: And thus, such a definition of <s>nyāsa</s> (renunciation) as being-established-in-<s>Brahman</s> is distinctive of the <s>bhikṣu</s> (mendicant) alone, not of the members of other <s>āśrama</s>s.

children.text: brahmajñānasya śabdajanitasya yaḥ paripākaḥ sākṣātkāro 'pavargasādhanaṃ tadaṅgatayā parivrājyaṃ vihitam /
children.translated_text: The maturation (<s>paripāka</s>) of knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> born from verbal testimony — namely, direct realization (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>) — is the means to liberation (<s>apavarga</s>); as a subsidiary to that, the life of renunciation (<s>parivrājya</s>) has been enjoined.
But [this does] not [mean] that one who is not entitled [to renunciation may take it up] — this is the meaning. //20//

body.translated_text:
'#Or [it is] an injunction, like [the case of] holding#.'
Although the single-sentence-hood (<s>ekavākyatā</s>) of this passage is understood by its having 'being established in <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>brahmasaṃsthatva</s>) as its purport,
and although when single-sentence-hood is possible, sentence-splitting should not be resorted to,
nevertheless — since the prior establishment of the other <s>āśrama</s>s (stages of life) is not available, the reference [to them] is untenable; and when there is no reference, praise is impossible — [the question arises:] with what purport can there be single-sentence-hood? Breaking that [single-sentence-hood], it is better — like [the case of] holding — that it be an injunction alone, because of its being unprecedented (<s>apūrva</s>).
Just as in 'holding the fuel-stick below, he utters [the mantra]; above, for he holds it for the gods' — although single-sentence-hood with the holding-below is cognized, the holding-above is enjoined alone because of its being unprecedented.
Thus it has been stated: 'But it is an injunction regarding holding, because of its being unprecedented.'
Similarly here too, the <s>Śruti</s> referring to the other <s>āśrama</s>s is construed as an injunction.
Now, even if there is reference, the being-established-in-<s>Brahman</s> of the other <s>āśrama</s>s must be enjoined by the very force of the praise.
For indeed what is not to be enjoined is not praised, since praise serves the purpose of that [injunction] — he says: '#even if#' (<s>yadāpi</s>).
He begins a subsidiary inquiry here: '#and whether in all four#' (<s>sā ca kiṃ caturṣu</s>).
He states the purpose of the inquiry: '#if indeed#' (<s>yadi ca</s>).
Objection: One who is not in any <s>āśrama</s> will be established in <s>Brahman</s> — to this he says: '#being without an <s>āśrama</s>#' (<s>anāśramitva</s>).
Therein he states the prima facie view: '#therein, by the word "<s>tapas</s>" (austerity)#' (<s>tatra tapaḥśabdena</s>).
The intent is this:
If the word '<s>brahmasaṃstha</s>' (established in <s>Brahman</s>) is conventionally fixed (<s>rūḍha</s>) — like the words '<s>aśvakarṇa</s>' and the like — to mean the renunciant (<s>parivrājaka</s>), without analyzing its component parts, then by the mere attainment of [the renunciant] <s>āśrama</s> alone, one would attain immortality, and knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> would not be required for that [attainment].
And thus there would be a contradiction with 'there is no other path known for going [to liberation].'
Nor, when the component meaning (<s>avayavārtha</s>) is possible, should the postulation of a conventional fixed meaning (<s>samudāyaśakti</s>) be made.
Therefore, [the compound means] 'one who will be established in <s>Brahman</s>' —
'<s>Brahmasaṃstha</s>' (established in <s>Brahman</s>).
And thus, among the four <s>āśrama</s>s, whichever <s>āśramin</s> (member of an <s>āśrama</s>) has steadfastness in <s>Brahman</s> — he, being established in <s>Brahman</s>, attains immortality — this is fitting.
Therein, the <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student) and the <s>gṛhastha</s> (householder) are denoted by their own [respective] words; and by the word '<s>tapas</s>' (austerity), the <s>bhikṣu</s> (mendicant) and the <s>vānaprastha</s> (forest-dweller) are indicated, as austerity is predominant [in their stages].
For the <s>bhikṣu</s> too, because of the regulations of heightened purity, the rule of eating [only] eight morsels, and the like, is predominantly characterized by austerity, like the <s>vānaprastha</s>.
Nor is it impossible for the <s>gṛhastha</s> (householder) and the like, who are performers of ritual action (<s>karmin</s>), to be steadfast in <s>Brahman</s>.
If engagement with ritual action constitutes being a <s>karmin</s>, then that [engagement] exists for the <s>bhikṣu</s> too, through body, speech, and mind.
But if those who perform action not as an offering to <s>Brahman</s> but out of desire for [worldly] ends are the <s>karmin</s>s,
then the <s>gṛhastha</s> and the like too, performing action as an offering to <s>Brahman</s>, are not <s>karmin</s>s.
Therefore, steadfastness in <s>Brahman</s> means having one's ultimate purpose in <s>Brahman</s>, not the abandonment of action.
Because [abandonment] contradicts the authoritative texts.
And by unifying the two <s>āśrama</s>s [<s>bhikṣu</s> and <s>vānaprastha</s>] under the word '<s>tapas</s>' (austerity), the number three — 'three' — is justified.
And thus, the three <s>āśrama</s>s, while not established in <s>Brahman</s>, partake of meritorious worlds; but whoever among them is established in <s>Brahman</s>, he partakes of immortality.
Nor is there a contradiction [in saying that] those very ones who partake of meritorious worlds [also attain] immortality.
Just as <s>Devadatta</s> and <s>Yajñadatta</s> were [once] of dull intellect, [but] now <s>Yajñadatta</s> has become sharp-witted through the study of the <s>śāstra</s>s — similarly here too, those very ones who were not established in <s>Brahman</s> and partook of meritorious worlds, those very ones, [now] established in <s>Brahman</s>, partake of immortality — there is no contradiction because of the difference of states.
And thus, the word '<s>brahmasaṃstha</s>' will be derived [etymologically] (<s>yaugika</s>), having its referent in the subject at hand.
Just as in 'one attends the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> (fire-hall) with the <s>Āgneyī</s> (verse addressed to <s>Agni</s>)' — even when assigned [to a specific use], only the contextually relevant <s>Āgneyī</s> is taken.
Nor is there a contradiction between the assigned [verse] and [its] assignment.
For if the <s>Āgneyī</s> were being taught here [for the first time], then as it was cognized, so it would be designated.
And the cognition would be of what is [now being] assigned — hence there would be a contradiction of the assigned and the assignment.
But here, it is assigned for the purpose of the <s>Āgnīdhra</s>-attendance as something to be enjoined.
It is not [merely] designated.
And when the assignment is as something to be enjoined, since [it] depends on the referent of the word '<s>Āgneyī</s>,' and since there is no authoritative basis for going beyond the contextually relevant [verse],
and since the scripture is explained just by that much, there is no possibility of taking the non-contextual ones as well.
Nor is the assignment [prevented] because of [the verse] being 'used up' (<s>yātayāma</s>).
Because of the <s>Vācastoma</s> — since all mantras are assigned [in it] — the absurd consequence of non-assignment elsewhere too would follow.
Similarly here too, only the <s>āśrama</s>s that are contextually relevant — those that revolve in the [present] intellectual context — are referred to, not the unmentioned <s>parivrājaka</s> (renunciant) alone — this is the prima facie view.
He begins the established conclusion: '#that is unjust.
For when there is a [clear] path, [one should not identify the <s>vānaprastha</s>] with a particular [<s>āśrama</s>]#' (<s>nahi satyāṃ gatau vānaprasthaviśeṣena</s>).
As [the enumeration] was begun, so should the completion be fitting.
And it is fitting that those who are of a [specific] number and are well-known are enumerated as being exactly of that number.
But when there is a [clear] path of the general rule (<s>utsarga</s>), its exception (<s>apavāda</s>) is not appropriate.
[Since] each <s>āśrama</s> was begun to be stated with its own distinctive characteristic — the completion should be in exactly that way.
But the introduction and conclusion should not be mixed — [one] with a shared [characteristic] and [another] with a distinctive one.
Nor is austerity (<s>tapas</s>) not distinctive of the <s>vānaprastha</s>s — hence he says: '#and austerity is distinctive#' (<s>tapaścāsādhāraṇam</s>).
For the <s>bhikṣu</s> (mendicant) is not predominantly characterized by bodily mortification through the <s>Parāka</s> and other [penances] in the way the <s>vānaprastha</s> is, even though there is the rule of eight morsels and the like.
Nor are purity (<s>śauca</s>), contentment (<s>santoṣa</s>), self-control (<s>śama</s>), and the like included in the category of austerity — because the well-known understanding of austerity among the elders does not support [such inclusion].
For that very reason, the elders speak of purity and the like as distinct from austerity: '<s>śauca</s> (purity), <s>santoṣa</s> (contentment), <s>tapas</s> (austerity), <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study), <s>Īśvarapraṇidhāna</s> (devotion to the Lord) — these are the <s>niyama</s>s (observances).'
And to state a different number when the numbers are well-established is incongruous — he says: '#and with the number four#' (<s>catuṣṭvena ca</s>).
'#Moreover, a separate designation here#' (<s>apica bhedavyapadeśaḥ atra</s>).
'These three' — does the <s>bhikṣu</s> also get included, or is it three excluding the <s>bhikṣu</s>?
To begin with, if 'three' includes the <s>bhikṣu</s>, then the exclusion — 'these three' — cannot function here.
'Indeed' (<s>eva</s>) — because of the reference to the entirety of those contextually relevant, and because if the <s>bhikṣu</s> were included, he would not have meritorious-world [status], since the state of not-being-established-in-<s>Brahman</s> does not exist for the <s>bhikṣu</s>.
Hence, for that one who is established in <s>Brahman</s>, the constant state of meritorious-world [status] and immortality would be contradictory.
And among the three, the relative pronoun 'whoever' (<s>yad</s>) should be connected with the word '<s>brahmasaṃstha</s>'; and for the <s>bhikṣu</s>, [it would have to be] 'always' (<s>sadā</s>) — and that is incongruous.
This is what was stated: '#and in the separateness#' (<s>pṛthaktve ca</s>).
He recalls the semblance of the prima facie view: '#but how can the word "<s>brahmasaṃstha</s>" [be taken] etymologically?#' (<s>kathaṃ punarbrahmasaṃsthaśabdo yogāt</s>).
He refutes that: '#it is said here#' (<s>atrocyata</s>).
The intent is this:
Indeed, the word is etymological (<s>yaugika</s>); [but] when the contextually relevant meaning is possible, it should not transgress that [context] to apply to something non-contextual.
But when [the contextual meaning] is not possible, lest [the text] be a careless reading (<s>pramādapāṭha</s>), it should be applied to the non-contextual — and the impossibility [of the contextual meaning] has been shown above.
For this property characterized as being-established-in-<s>Brahman</s> is not shared [equally] among the <s>āśrama</s>s — the other <s>āśrama</s>s may or may not be established in that; [but] the <s>bhikṣu</s> is established in that alone.
For being-established-in-that, excluding one's own nature [of worldly engagement], being contradictory [to it] — the one who is established in that, [the word applies] directly there alone, not elsewhere.
'#But <s>śama</s> (tranquility), <s>dama</s> (self-restraint), and the like are his own#' (<s>śamadamādistu tadīya</s>).
The meaning is: [these are] his own subsidiary [practices], not an obstruction [to his being established in <s>Brahman</s>].
The <s>Śruti</s> shows being-established-in-<s>Brahman</s> as a distinctive property of the renunciant — he says: '#and thus, <s>nyāsa</s> (renunciation) is <s>Brahman</s>#' (<s>tathāca nyāsa iti brahma</s>).
For the complete abandonment of all attachments is <s>nyāsa</s> (renunciation); [and] that is <s>Brahman</s> — how? To this he says: '#for <s>Brahman</s> is the highest#' (<s>brahmā hi paraḥ</s>).
Therefore, the highest is <s>Brahman</s>.
In what respect is [<s>nyāsa</s>] the highest — to this he says: '#these indeed are the lower austerities; <s>nyāsa</s> (renunciation) alone surpasses [them]#.'

#stutimātramupādānāditi cennāpūrvatvāt# /
yadyatra saṃnidhāna upāsanāvidhirnāsti tataḥ pradeśāntarasthito 'pi vidhivyabhicāritatadvidhisaṃbandhenodgīthenopasthāpitaḥ sa eṣa rasānāṃ rasatama ityādinā padasaṃdarbheṇaikavākyabhāvamupagataḥ stūyate /
nahi samabhivyāhṛtairevaikavākyatā bhavatīti kaścinniyamaheturasti /
anuṣaṅgātideśalabdhairapi vidhyasamabhivyāhṛtairarthavādairekavākyatābhyupagamāt /
yadi tūdgīthamupāsīta sāmopāsītetyādividhisamabhivyāhāraḥ śrutastathāpi tasyaiva vidheḥ stutirna tūpāsanāviṣayasamarpaṇapara omityetadakṣaramudgīthamityanenaivopāsanāviṣayasamarpaṇāditi prāpte 'bhidhīyate-na tāvaddūrasthena karmavidhivākyenaikavākyatāsaṃbhavaḥ /
pratītasamabhivyāhṛtānāṃ vidhinaikavākyatayā stutyarthatvamarthavādānāṃ raktapaṭanyāyena bhavati /
na tu stutyā vinā kācidanupapattirvidheḥ /
yathāhuḥ-'asti tu tadityatireke parihāraḥ' iti /
ata eva vidherapekṣābhāvātpravartanātmakasyānuṣaṅgatideśādibhirarthavādaprāptyabhidhānamasamañjasam /
nahi kartrapekṣitopāyāmavagatāyāṃ prāśastyapratyayasyāsti kaścidupayogaḥ /
tasmāddūrasthasya karmavidheḥ stutāvānarthakyam /
body.translated_text:
'#If [it be said that these are] mere praise, because of being taken up [from elsewhere] — no, because of being unprecedented#.'
If there is no injunction of meditation (<s>upāsanā</s>) in this proximate context, then even [a meditation injunction] situated elsewhere — connected with a proximate <s>Udgītha</s> through an injunction whose [original context] deviates from it — having entered into single-sentence-hood with the passage 'this is the quintessence of essences' and the like, is praised.
For there is no determining reason that single-sentence-hood occurs only with what is directly co-stated.
Because single-sentence-hood is accepted even with <s>arthavāda</s>s (laudatory statements) that are not co-stated with an injunction but obtained through connection (<s>anuṣaṅga</s>), extension (<s>atideśa</s>), and the like.
But even if the co-statement of an injunction — such as 'one should meditate on the <s>Udgītha</s>' or 'one should meditate on the <s>Sāman</s>' — is heard, even so, it is praise of that very injunction, not directed toward presenting the object of meditation — since the object of meditation has already been presented by '<s>Om</s> — this syllable is the <s>Udgītha</s>' alone — this being the prima facie conclusion, it is stated:
To begin with, single-sentence-hood with a ritual injunction situated far away is not possible.
The <s>arthavāda</s>s (laudatory statements) become praise-purposed through single-sentence-hood with a cognized co-stated injunction, by the principle of the 'red cloth' (<s>raktapaṭanyāya</s>).
But there is no impossibility of the injunction without the praise.
As they say: 'But that [sentence] exists — the resolution is in its exceeding [the injunction].'
For that very reason — because of the absence of any need from the injunction, which is of the nature of prompting — the statement that <s>arthavāda</s>s are obtained through connection (<s>anuṣaṅga</s>), extension (<s>atideśa</s>), and the like is incongruous.
For when the means desired by the agent has been known, the cognition of excellence has no use whatsoever.
Therefore, for a ritual injunction situated far away, there is purposelessness in [being connected with] praise.

body.text: tenaikavākyatānupapatteḥ saṃnihitasya tūpāsanāvidheḥ kiṃ viṣayasamarpaṇenopayujyatāmuta stutyeti viśaye viṣayasamarpaṇena yathārthavattvaṃ naivaṃ stutyā bahiraṅgatvāt /

children.translated_text: For that [praise] is [resorted to] only as a last resort.
Therefore, it is established that [these passages] serve the purpose of meditation (<s>upāsanā</s>).
'<s>Kuryāt</s> (one should do), <s>kriyeta</s> (it should be done), <s>kartavyam</s> (it is to be done), <s>bhavet</s> (it should be), <s>syāt</s> (it would be) — the fifth [form].
This would be, in all <s>Veda</s>s, the fixed characteristic of an injunction (<s>vidhi</s>).'

body.translated_text: Hence, since single-sentence-hood [with a distant ritual injunction] is untenable — but for the proximate meditation injunction, the question is: should [the passage] serve the purpose of presenting the object [of meditation], or of praise? In this matter, the passage serves its purpose through presenting the object — not through praise, since [praise] is extrinsic.

body.text:
' bhāvanāyāḥ khalu kartṛsamīhitānukūlatvaṃ vidhirniṣedhaśca karturahitānukūlatvam /
yathāhuḥ-'kartavyaśca sukhaphalo 'kartavyo duḥkhaphalo 'kartavyo duḥkhaphalaḥ' iti /
etaccāsmābhirupapāditaṃ nyāyakaṇikāyām /
kriyā ca bhāvanā tadvacanāśca karotyādayaḥ /
yathāhuḥ-kamabhvastayaḥ kriyāsāmānyavacanā iti /
ata eva kṛbhvastīnudāhṛtavān /
sāmānyoktau tadviśeṣāḥ pacedityādayo 'pi gamyanta iti tatra kuryādityākṣiptakartṛkā bhāvanā /
kriyeteti ākṣiptakarmikā bhāvanā /
kartavyamiti tu karmabhūtadravyopasarjanabhāvanā /
evaṃ daṇḍī bhaveddaṇḍinā bhavitavyaṃ daṇḍinā bhūyetetyekadhātvarthaviṣayā vidhyupahitā bhāvanā udāhāryāḥ /

children.translated_text: And this [root] '<s>bhavati</s>' (becomes) is [used] in the sense of coming into being (<s>janman</s>).

children.text: yathā kulālavyāpārādghaṭo bhavati bījādaṅkuro bhavatīti prayuñjate /
children.translated_text: Just as [people] use [it in]: 'From the potter's activity, the pot comes into being (<s>bhavati</s>)'; 'From the seed, the sprout comes into being (<s>bhavati</s>).'
But [people] do not use: 'From the seed, the sprout exists (<s>asti</s>).'
Therefore, '<s>asti</s>' (exists) is [used] in the sense of existence (<s>sattā</s>), not in the sense of coming into being (<s>janman</s>). //21//

body.translated_text:
The conformity of <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive force) to what is desired by the agent is an injunction (<s>vidhi</s>); and a prohibition (<s>niṣedha</s>) is [its] conformity to what is undesired by the agent.
As they say: 'What is to be done has a pleasant fruit; what is not to be done has a painful fruit; what is not to be done has a painful fruit.'
And this has been demonstrated by us in the <s>Nyāyakaṇikā</s>.
Action (<s>kriyā</s>) is <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive force), and the words expressing it are <s>karoti</s> (does) and the like.
As they say: the roots <s>kṛ</s> (do), <s>bhū</s> (be), and <s>as</s> (exist) denote action in general.
For that very reason, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] has cited <s>kṛ</s>, <s>bhū</s>, and <s>as</s> [as examples].
When the general is stated, its specific instances — '<s>pacet</s>' (one should cook) and the like — are also understood. Therein, '<s>kuryāt</s>' (one should do) — <s>bhāvanā</s> with an implied agent.
'<s>Kriyeta</s>' (it should be done) — <s>bhāvanā</s> with an implied object.
'<s>Kartavyam</s>' (it is to be done) — <s>bhāvanā</s> in which the substance that constitutes the object is subordinate.
Similarly, '<s>daṇḍī bhavet</s>' (one should be a staff-bearer), '<s>daṇḍinā bhavitavyam</s>' (one must be a staff-bearer), '<s>daṇḍinā bhūyeta</s>' (one should become a staff-bearer) — these are examples of <s>bhāvanā</s> directed toward a single verbal root-meaning (<s>dhātvarthā</s>), qualified by an injunction.

body.text:
#pāriplavārthā iti cenna viśeṣitatvāt# /
yadyapi upaniṣadākhyānāni vidyāsaṃnidhau śrutāni tathāpi 'sarvāṇyākhyānāni pāriplave' iti sarvaśrutyā niḥśeṣārthatayā durbalasya saṃnidherbādhitatvātpariplavārthānyevākhyānāni /
naca sarvā dāśatayīranubrūyāditi viniyoge 'pi dāśatayīnāṃ prātisvikaviniyogāttatra tatra karmaṇi yathā viniyogo na virudhyate tathehāpi satyapi pāriplave viniyege saṃnidhānādvidyāṅgatvamapi bhaviṣyatīti vācyam /
dāśatayīṣu prātisvikānāṃ viniyogānāṃ samudāyaviniyogasya ca tulyabalatvādiha tu saṃnidhānāt śruterbalīyastvāt /
tasmātpāriplavārthānyevākhyānānīti prāpta ucyate-naiṣāmākhyānānāṃ pāriplave viniyogaḥ /
kintu pāriplavamācakṣītetyupakramya yānyāmnātāni manurvaivasvato rājetyādīni teṣāmeva tatra viniyogaḥ, tānyeva hi pāriplavena viśeṣitāni /
itarathā pāriplave sarvāṇyākhyānānityetāvataiva gatatvātpariplavamācakṣītetyanarthakaṃ syāt /
ākhyānaviśeṣaṇatve tvarthavat /

children.translated_text: Therefore, in conformity with the specified [narratives], the word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>) is relative to those — not an expression of totality.

children.text: yathā sarve brāhmaṇā bhojayitavyā ityatra nimintrātāpekṣaḥ sarvaśabdaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as in 'all <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s should be fed,' the word 'all' is relative to those who have been invited.

children.text: tathā copaniṣadākhyānānāṃ vidyāsaṃnidhirapratidvandīṃ vidyaikavākyatāṃ so 'rodīdityādīnāmiva vidhyekavākyatvaṃ gamayatīti siddham /
children.translated_text: Similarly, the proximity of the <s>Upaniṣad</s> narratives to <s>vidyā</s> — being uncontested — leads to single-sentence-hood with <s>vidyā</s>, just as [the proximity of] 'he wept' (<s>so 'rodīt</s>) and the like [leads to] single-sentence-hood with an injunction — this is established.

children.text: pratipattisaukaryāccetyupākhyānena hi bālā apyavadhīyante yathā tantropākhyāyikayeti //23 //
children.translated_text: And because of the ease of comprehension — for even children are engaged [in learning] through narratives, just as through the illustrations in a treatise (<s>tantropākhyāyikā</s>). //23//

body.translated_text:
'#[If it be said] that they are for the purpose of the <s>Pāriplava</s> (recurrent narrative) — no, because they are specified#.'
Although the <s>Upaniṣad</s> narratives are heard in proximity to <s>vidyā</s>, nevertheless — since by the <s>Śruti</s> 'all narratives [are to be recited] in the <s>Pāriplava</s>,' the word 'all,' having the meaning of totality, overrides the weaker proximity — the narratives are for the purpose of the <s>Pāriplava</s> alone.
Nor should it be said that just as in the assignment 'one should recite all the <s>Dāśatayī</s>s' — even though there is a collective assignment of the <s>Dāśatayī</s>s, the individual assignment of each [<s>Dāśatayī</s>] to each particular ritual does not conflict — so too here, even though there is a <s>Pāriplava</s> assignment, the subsidiary-hood to <s>vidyā</s> will also follow from proximity.
Because in the <s>Dāśatayī</s>s, the individual assignments and the collective assignment are of equal force; but here, <s>Śruti</s> is stronger than proximity.
Therefore — the narratives are for the purpose of the <s>Pāriplava</s> alone — this being the prima facie conclusion, it is stated: The assignment of these narratives is not to the <s>Pāriplava</s>.
Rather, beginning with '<s>pāriplavamācakṣīta</s>' ('one should recite the <s>Pāriplava</s>'), those [narratives] that are listed — such as '<s>Manu Vaivasvata</s> was a king' and the like — their assignment alone is there [in the <s>Pāriplava</s>], for those alone are specified by the <s>Pāriplava</s>.
Otherwise, if 'all narratives in the <s>Pāriplava</s>' were sufficient [by itself], '<s>pāriplavamācakṣīta</s>' would be purposeless.
But if [this phrase] serves as a qualifier of the narratives, it is purposeful.

body.text:
#ata eva cāgnīndhanādyanapekṣā# /
vidyāyāḥ kratvarthatve sati tathā kratūpakaraṇāya svakāryāya kraturapekṣitaḥ /
tadabhāve kasyopakāro vidyayeti /
yadā tu puruṣārthā tadā nānayā kraturapekṣitaḥ svakārye nirapekṣāyā eva tasyāḥ sāmarthyāt /

children.text: agnīndhānādinā cāśramakarmāṇyupalakṣyante tadāha- #agnīndhanādīvyāśramakarmāṇi vidyayā svārthasiddhau nāpekṣitavyānīti# /
children.translated_text: And by 'fire-kindling and the like,' the <s>āśrama</s>-duties (<s>āśramakarma</s>) are indicated — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Fire-kindling and the like means the <s>āśrama</s>-duties; [they] are not to be depended upon by <s>vidyā</s> for the accomplishment of its own purpose#.'
They are not to be depended upon for the accomplishment of [<s>vidyā</s>'s] own purpose — but not [not depended upon] for [<s>vidyā</s>'s] own origination.
And this additional [point] will be stated further below.
And it is with the intention of stating this additional [point] that the purpose of this prior <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic) has been stated. //25//

body.translated_text:
'#For this very reason, there is no dependence on fire-kindling and the like#.'
If <s>vidyā</s> were to serve the ritual purpose (<s>kratvārtha</s>), then, for the sake of assisting the ritual in its own [subsidiary] function, the ritual would be required [by <s>vidyā</s>].
In the absence of that [ritual purpose], for whose assistance would <s>vidyā</s> [need the ritual]?
But when [<s>vidyā</s>] serves the person's purpose (<s>puruṣārtha</s>), then by it the ritual is not required, because of the capacity of [<s>vidyā</s>] itself, which is independent in its own function.

body.text:
3.4.5.26.
adhikavivakṣyeti yaduktaṃ tadadhikamāha- #sarvāpekṣā ca yajñādiśruteraśvavat# /
yathā svārthasiddhau nāpekṣyante āśramakarmāṇi evamutpattāvapi nāpekṣyeranniti śaṅkā syāt /
naca vividiṣanti yajñenetyādivirodhaḥ /
nahyeṣa vidhirapi tu vartamānāpadeśaḥ /
sa ca stutyāpyupapadyate /
apica catasraḥ pratipattayo brahmaṇi /
prathamā tāvadupaniṣadvākyaśravaṇamātrādbhavati yāṃ kilācakṣate śravaṇamiti /
dvitīyā mīmāṃsāsahitā tasyādevopaniṣadvākyādyāmācakṣate /
mananamiti /
tṛtīyā cintā /
santatimayī yāmācakṣate nididhyāsanamiti /
caturthī sākṣātkāravatī vṛttirūpā nāntarīyakaṃ hi tasyāḥ kaivalyamiti /
tatrādye tāvatpratipatti viditapadatadarthasya viditavākyagatigocaranyāyasya ca puṃsa upapadyete eveti na tatra karmāpekṣā /
te eva ca cintāmayīṃ tṛtīyaṃ pratipattiṃ prasuvāte iti na tatrāpi karmāpekṣā /
sā cādaranairantaryadīrghakālasevitā sākṣātkāravatīmādhatta eva pratipattiṃ caturthīmiti na tatrāpyasti karmāpekṣā /
tannāntarīyakaṃ ca kaivalyamiti na tasyāpi karmāpekṣā /
tadevaṃ pramāṇataśca prameyata utpattau ca kārye ca na jñānasya karmāpekṣeti bījaṃ śaṅkāyām /
evaṃ prāpta ucyate-utpattau jñānasya karmāpekṣā vidyate vividiṣotpādadvārā 'vividiṣanti yajñena' iti śruteḥ /
na cedaṃ vartamānāpadeśatvātstutimātramapūrvatvādarthasya /
yathā yasya parṇamayī juhūrbhavatīti parṇamayatāvidhirapūrvatvānna tvayaṃ vartamānāpadeśaḥ, anuvādānupapatteḥ /
tasmādutpattau vidyayā śamādivat karmāṇyapekṣyante /
tatrāpyevaṃviditi vidyāsvarūpasaṃyogādantaraṅgāṇi vidyotpāde śamādīni, bahiraṅgāṇi karmāṇi vividiṣāsaṃyogāt /
tathāhi-āśramavihitanityakarmānuṣṭhānāddharmasamutpādastataḥ pāpmā vilīyate /
sa hi tattvato 'nityāśuciduḥ-khānātmani saṃsāre sati nityaśucimukhātmalakṣaṇena vibhrameṇa malinayati cittasattvamadharmanibandhanatvādvibhramāṇām /
ataḥ pāpmanaḥ prakṣaye pratyakṣopapattidvārāpāvaraṇe sati pratyakṣopapattibhyāṃ saṃsārasya tāttvikīmanityāśuciduḥkharūpatāmapratyūhaṃ viniścineti /
tato 'sminnanabhiratisaṃjñaṃ vairāgyamupajāyate /
tatastajjihāsāsyopāvartate /
tato hānopāyaṃ prayeṣate paryeṣamāṇaścātmatattvajñānamasyopāya iti śāstradācāryavacanāccopaśrutya tajjijñāsata iti vividiṣopahāramukhenātmajñānotpattāvasti karmāṇamupayogaḥ /
vividiṣuḥ khalu yukta ekāgratayā śravaṇamanane kartumutsahate /
tato 'sya 'tattvamasi' itivākyannirvicikitsaṃ jñānamutpadyate /
naca nirvicikitsaṃ tattvamasīti vākyārthamavadhārayataḥ karmaṇyadhikāro 'sti /
yena bhāvanāyāṃ vā bhāvanākārye vā sākṣātkāre karmaṇāmupayogaḥ /
etena vṛttirūrapasākṣātkārakārye 'pavarge karmaṇāmupayogo dūranirasto veditavyaḥ /
tasmādyathaiva śamadamādayo yāvajjīvamanuvartante evamāśramakarmāpītyasamīkṣitābhādhānam /
viduṣastatrānadhikārādityuktam /
dṛṣṭārtheṣu tu karmasu pratiṣiddhavarjamanadhikāre 'pyasaktasya svārasikī pravṛttirupapadyata eva /
nahi tatrānvayavyatirekasamadhigamanīyaphale 'sti vidhyapekṣā /
ataśca 'bhrāntyā cellaukikaṃ karma vaidikaṃ ca tathāstu te' iti pralāpaḥ /

children.translated_text: But <s>śama</s>, <s>dama</s>, and the like — having been adopted for the origination of <s>vidyā</s> — continue in the subsequent states naturally, even without being required.

children.text: upapāditaṃ caitadasmābhiḥ prathamasūtra ite neha punaḥ pratyāpyate /
children.translated_text: And this has been demonstrated by us in [the commentary on] the first <s>sūtra</s> — hence it is not reiterated here.

children.text: tasmādvividiṣotpādadvārāśramakarmaṇāṃ vidyotpattāvupayogo na vidyākārya iti siddham /
children.translated_text: Therefore, through the door of producing the desire to know, <s>āśrama</s>-duties have utility in the origination of <s>vidyā</s> — not in the effect of <s>vidyā</s> — this is established.
The rest has transparent meaning. //26//

body.translated_text:
3.4.5.26.
Regarding what was said — that there is an additional [point] to be stated — that additional [point] is now stated: '#All [<s>āśrama</s>-duties] are required, because of the <s>Śruti</s> about sacrifice and the like, as with the horse#.'
Just as <s>āśrama</s>-duties are not required for the accomplishment of [<s>vidyā</s>'s] own purpose, so too [the doubt arises:] they would not be required even for [<s>vidyā</s>'s] origination.
Nor is there a contradiction with '<s>vividiṣanti yajñena</s>' ('they seek to know through sacrifice') and the like.
For this is not an injunction but a statement about a current [practice].
And that [current practice statement] is also explicable as praise.
Moreover, there are four cognitions (<s>pratipatti</s>s) regarding <s>Brahman</s>.
The first arises merely from hearing the <s>Upaniṣad</s> sentences — which [people] call '<s>śravaṇa</s>' (hearing).
The second is accompanied by reasoning (<s>mīmāṃsā</s>), arising from those very <s>Upaniṣad</s> sentences — which they call '<s>manana</s>' (reflection).
The third is contemplation (<s>cintā</s>) — continuous [in nature] — which they call '<s>nididhyāsana</s>' (meditation).
The fourth is the modification (<s>vṛttirūpā</s>) that possesses direct realization (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>), and liberation (<s>kaivalya</s>) is its inevitable [consequence].
Therein, the first two cognitions are possible for a person who knows the words and their meanings, who knows the scope and principles of sentence-meaning — hence there is no requirement of <s>karma</s> for those.
And those very [two cognitions] give rise to the third cognition — the contemplative (<s>cintāmayī</s>) — hence there too there is no requirement of <s>karma</s>.
And that [third cognition], when cultivated with reverence, continuity, and for a long time, produces the fourth cognition — that which possesses direct realization — hence there too there is no requirement of <s>karma</s>.
And liberation is the inevitable [consequence] of that [fourth cognition] — hence there too there is no requirement of <s>karma</s>.
Thus, from the standpoint of the means of knowledge, the object of knowledge, the origination [of knowledge], and the effect [of knowledge], there is no requirement of <s>karma</s> for knowledge — this is the seed of the doubt.
This being arrived at, it is stated: There is indeed a requirement of <s>karma</s> for the origination of knowledge — through the door of producing the desire to know (<s>vividiṣā</s>) — from the <s>Śruti</s> '<s>vividiṣanti yajñena</s>' ('they seek to know through sacrifice').
Nor is this mere praise because of being a statement about a current [practice], since the meaning is unprecedented.
Just as '<s>yasya parṇamayī juhūr bhavati</s>' ('one whose ladle is made of <s>Palāśa</s> leaves') — [this is] an injunction of being made of <s>Palāśa</s>, because of the unprecedented [nature of the content], and is not a statement about a current [practice] — because the construction as a restatement is untenable.
Therefore, for [<s>vidyā</s>'s] origination, <s>karma</s>s are required by <s>vidyā</s>, just like <s>śama</s> (tranquility) and the like.
Therein too, because of the connection with <s>vidyā</s>'s essential nature in [the phrase] '<s>evaṃvit</s>' ('one who knows thus'), <s>śama</s> and the like are proximate (<s>antaraṅga</s>) in producing <s>vidyā</s>; <s>karma</s>s are remote (<s>bahiraṅga</s>), because of their connection with the desire to know (<s>vividiṣā</s>).
Thus: from the performance of the obligatory <s>karma</s>s prescribed for one's <s>āśrama</s>, <s>dharma</s> (merit) is produced; from that, <s>pāpman</s> (sin) dissolves.
For that [sin] — in the presence of <s>saṃsāra</s>, which is truly impermanent, impure, and sorrowful and non-self — taints the mental substance (<s>cittasattva</s>) through the delusion characterized by [the misperception of saṃsāra as] permanent, pure, pleasant, and self — because delusions are grounded in <s>adharma</s>.
Hence, upon the destruction of sin, when the covering is removed through the door of direct perception and rational demonstration, one ascertains — through perception and reasoning — without obstruction the true nature of <s>saṃsāra</s> as impermanent, impure, and of the nature of suffering.
From that, dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) — designated as non-delight — arises toward this [<s>saṃsāra</s>].
From that, the desire to abandon it arises.
From that, one seeks the means of abandonment; and while seeking, having learned from scripture and the teacher's words that knowledge of the Self's reality is the means, one desires to know it — thus, through the door of bringing about the desire to know, there is utility of <s>karma</s> in the origination of Self-knowledge.
Indeed, one who desires to know, being concentrated and one-pointed, is able to engage in hearing and reflection.
From that, from the sentence '<s>tattvamasi</s>' ('You are That'), indubitable knowledge arises for him.
Nor does one who ascertains with certainty the meaning of '<s>tattvamasi</s>' have eligibility for <s>karma</s>,
such that <s>karma</s> would be of use in the cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) or in the effect of cultivation, namely direct realization (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>).
By this, the usefulness of <s>karma</s> in liberation — which is the effect of the modification (<s>vṛtti</s>) that is direct realization — should be understood as thoroughly refuted.
Therefore, just as <s>śama</s>, <s>dama</s>, and the like continue throughout life, so too <s>āśrama</s>-duties — [to say this] is an unexamined claim.
Because of the knower's non-eligibility for [<s>karma</s>] there — this has been stated.
But regarding <s>karma</s>s that have visible results (<s>dṛṣṭārtha</s>), even for one who is not eligible [for Vedic karma], and who is unattached, there is a natural (<s>svārasikī</s>) engagement — avoiding what is prohibited.
For where the fruit is ascertainable through positive and negative concomitance, there is no need for an injunction.
And therefore, [the statement] 'If through delusion, let worldly and Vedic <s>karma</s> be yours' is mere prattle.

body.text:
sarvānnānumatiśca prāṇātyaye taddarśanāt /
prāṇasaṃvāde sarvendriyāṇāṃ śrūyate /
eṣa kila vicāraviṣayaḥ-sarvāṇi khalu vāgādīnyavajitya prāṇo mukhya uvācaitāni kiṃ me 'nnaṃ bhaviṣyatīti, tāni hocuḥ /
yadidaṃ loke 'nnamā ca śvabhya ā ca śakunibhyaḥ sarvaprāṇināṃ yadannaṃ tattavānnamiti /
tadanena saṃdarbheṇa prāṇasya sarvamannamityanucintanaṃ vidhāyāha śrutiḥ-'na ha vā evaṃvidi kiñcanānannaṃ bhavati' iti /
