sarvaṃ prāṇasyānnamityevaṃvidi na kiñcinānannaṃ bhavatīti /
tatra saṃśayaḥ-kimetatsarvānnābhyanujñānaṃ śamādivadetadvidyāṅgatayā vidhīyata uta stutyarthaṃ saṃkīrtyata iti /
tatra yadyapi bhavatīti vartamānāpadeśānna vidhiḥ pratīyate /
tathāpi yathā yasya parṇamayī juhūrbhavatīti vartamānāpadeśādapi palāśamayītvavidhipratipattiḥ pañcamalakārāpattyā tathehāpi pravṛttiviśeṣakaratālābhe vidhipratipattiḥ /

children.text: stutau hi arthavādamātraṃ na tathārthavadyathā vidhau /
children.translated_text: For in [mere] praise, there would be only <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory statement) — not as meaningful as when [it is] an injunction.

children.text: bhakṣyābhakṣyaśāstraṃ ca sāmānyataḥ pravṛttamanena viśeṣaśāstreṇa bādhyate /
children.translated_text: And the general scripture on what is fit and unfit to eat is overridden by this specific scripture.

children.text: gamyāgamyavivekaśāstramiva sāmānyataḥ pravṛttaṃ vāmadevavidyāṅgabhūtasamastantryaparihāraśāstreṇa viśeṣaviṣayeṇeti prāpta ucyate-aśakteḥ kalpanīyatvācchāstrāntaravirodhataḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the general scripture on permissible and impermissible sexual relations is overridden by the specific scripture that prescribes the avoidance of the <s>Stainīya</s> (adultery) as a subsidiary of the <s>Vāmadeva-vidyā</s> — this being the prima facie conclusion, it is stated: Because of the impossibility [of eating everything], because it is to be postulated [only when possible], and because of the conflict with other scriptures,
'All this is the food of <s>Prāṇa</s>' — this is a hymn of meditation (<s>cintanasaṃstava</s>).

body.translated_text:
'#And the permission of all foods — [only] when life is in danger, because of the scriptural indication of that#.'
In the <s>Prāṇasaṃvāda</s> (dialogue about <s>Prāṇa</s>), [the supremacy] of all the sense-organs is heard.
This is indeed the subject of inquiry: all [the organs] — speech and the like — having been conquered by <s>Prāṇa</s>, the chief [vital breath], said: 'These — what will be my food?' They replied:
'Whatever food there is in the world — up to [what is eaten by] dogs, up to [what is eaten by] birds — the food of all living beings, that is your food.'
Thus, by this passage, having prescribed the meditation 'all is the food of <s>Prāṇa</s>,' the <s>Śruti</s> says: 'For one who knows thus, nothing whatsoever is not food.'
'All is the food of <s>Prāṇa</s>' — for one who knows thus, nothing is not food.
Therein the doubt arises: Is this permission of all foods, like <s>śama</s> and the like, enjoined as a subsidiary of this <s>vidyā</s>, or is it merely mentioned for the purpose of praise?
Therein, although from the present-tense statement '<s>bhavati</s>' ('becomes'), no injunction is cognized,
nevertheless, just as from '<s>yasya parṇamayī juhūr bhavati</s>' ('one whose ladle is made of <s>Palāśa</s>') — even from a present-tense statement — the cognition of an injunction of <s>Palāśa</s>-wood-ness is obtained through the method of the 'five <s>mala</s>s' (<s>pañcamalakāra</s>), so too here, when a specific activity-prompt (<s>pravṛttiviśeṣakara</s>) is obtained, the cognition of an injunction [results].

body.text:
na tāvatkauleyakamaryādamannaṃ manuṣyajātinā yugapatparyāyeṇa vā śakyamattum /
ibhakarabhakādīnāmannasya śamīkarīrakaṇṭakavaṭakāṣṭhāderekasyāpi aśakyādanatvāt /
na cātra liṅ iva sphuṭatarā vidhipratipattirasti /
naca kalpanīyo vidhirapūrvatvābhāvāt /
stutyāpi ca tadupapatteḥ /
naca satyāṃ gatau sāmānyataḥ pravṛttasya śāstrasya viṣayasaṃkoco yuktaḥ /
tasmātsarvaṃ prāṇasyānnamityanucintanavidhānastutiriti sāmpratam /
śakyatve ca pravṛttiviśeṣakaratopayujyate nāśakyavidhānatve /
prāṇātyasya iti cāvadhāraṇaparaṃ prāṇātyaya eva sarvānnatvam /
tatropākhyānācca sphuṭataravidhismṛteśca surāvarjaṃ vidvāṃsamavidvāṃsaṃ prati vidhānāt /
na tvanyatreti /
#ibhyena#hastipakena #sāmisvāditā#nardhabhakṣitān /
sa hi cākrāyaṇo hastipakocchiṣṭānkulmāṣānbhuñjāno hastipakenoktaḥ /
kulmāṣāniva maducchiṣṭamudakaṃ kasmānnānupibasīti /

children.translated_text: When thus addressed, he refused that water because of the fault of [it being] leftover.
And he stated the reason for this:
'Without these [grains] I would not have lived, I would not have survived — [so] I ate these <s>kulmāṣa</s>s.'

children.text: kāmo ma udakapānamiti svātantryaṃ me udakapāne nadīkūpataḍāgaprāpādiṣu yathākāmaṃ prāpnomīti nocchiṣṭodakābhāve prāṇātyaya iti tatrocchiṣṭabhakṣaṇadoṣa iti maṭacīhateṣu kuruṣu glāyannaśanāyayā munirnirapatrapa ibhyena sāmijagdhānkhādayāmāsa //28 //
children.translated_text: 'But drinking water is at my discretion' — meaning: 'I have freedom regarding water-drinking; I can obtain [water] at will from rivers, wells, ponds, and the like' — thus, since there was no danger to life in the absence of leftover water, there is the fault of eating leftovers there. And so the sage, in the <s>Kuru</s> country afflicted by drought (<s>maṭacīhata</s>), weakened by hunger, eating shamelessly, ate what was half-eaten by the elephant-keeper. //28//

body.translated_text:
To begin with, the food up to [what is eaten by] jackals [and other animals] cannot be eaten by a human being — either simultaneously or sequentially.
Because even one [type of] food among the foods of elephants, camels, and the like — such as <s>Śamī</s> [thorns], <s>Karīra</s> [thorns], <s>Kaṇṭaka</s> [thorns], <s>Vaṭa</s> [bark], and wood — is impossible to eat.
Nor is there here a clear cognition of an injunction, as [clear] as in the case of the <s>liṅga</s> (phallus) [worship].
Nor should an injunction be postulated — because of the absence of unprecedented [content].
And because even praise can explain that [statement].
Nor, when there is a [viable] interpretation, is it appropriate to contract the scope of the general scripture.
Therefore, '[this is] a prescription of the meditation "all is the food of <s>Prāṇa</s>" as praise' — this is correct.
And when [eating everything is] possible, [the permission] serves as a specific activity-prompt, not as a prescription of the impossible.
'When life is in danger' (<s>prāṇātyaye</s>) — the emphatic [reading] means: the all-food [permission] applies only when life is in danger.
And therein, from the narrative (<s>upākhyāna</s>) and from the clearer remembered rule (<s>smṛti</s>), [it is] enjoined for both the learned and the unlearned, excepting liquor.
But not elsewhere.
'#<s>Ibhya</s>#' — a keeper of elephants (<s>hastipaka</s>). '#<s>Sāmi</s>-eaten#' — half-eaten [by him].
For that <s>Cākrāyaṇa</s> [sage], while eating <s>kulmāṣa</s>s (parched grains) that were leftover from the elephant-keeper, was addressed by the elephant-keeper:

body.text:
#vihitatvāccāśramatarmāpi# /
nityāni hyāśramakarmāṇi yāvajjīvaśruternityehitopāyatayāvaśyaṃ kartavyāni /
vividiṣantīti ca vidyāsaṃyogādvidyāyāścāvaśyaṃbhāvaniyamābhāvādanityatā prāpnoti /
nityānityasaṃyogaścaikasya na saṃbhavati, avaśyānavaśyaṃbhāvayorekatra virodhāt /
naca vākyabhedādvāstavo virodhaḥ śakyo 'panetum /

children.translated_text: Therefore, there is simply no determination [possible] here — this is the prima facie conclusion.
By this, [the sūtra] 'But for one [entity having] both [aspects], there is separateness of connection' is anticipated [as the resolution].

children.text: evaṃ prāpte 'bhidhīyate-siddhe hi syādvirodho 'yaṃ na tu sādhye kathañcana /
children.translated_text: This being the prima facie conclusion, it is stated: This contradiction would apply if [the entity in question were already] established; but not at all if it is [still] to be accomplished.
When the self's attainment is dependent on the injunction, the abiding as prescribed is the [correct] view.

body.translated_text:
'#And [the obligation extends to] the <s>āśrama</s>-duties, because they are enjoined#.'
For the obligatory <s>āśrama</s>-duties (<s>nityakarma</s>) — being necessarily to be performed because of the <s>Śruti</s> 'as long as one lives' — must inevitably be performed.
And through [the Śruti] '<s>vividiṣanti</s>' ('they seek to know'), because of the connection with <s>vidyā</s>, and because <s>vidyā</s> has no fixed certainty of [when it will] arise, non-fixity (<s>anityatā</s>) [of the obligation] follows.
And the conjunction of what is fixed (<s>nitya</s>) and what is non-fixed (<s>anitya</s>) in a single [entity] is not possible — because of the contradiction of necessary and non-necessary arising in one [and the same thing].
Nor can the real contradiction be removed by splitting the sentences.

body.text:
siddhaṃ hi vastu viruddhadharmayogena bādhyate /
na tu sādhyarūpaṃ yathā ṣoḍaśina ekasya grahaṇāgrahaṇe /
te hi vidhyadhīnatvādvikaspete eva /
na punaḥ siddhe vikalpasaṃbhavaḥ /
tadihaikamevāgnihotrākhyaṃ karma yāvajjīvaśruternimittena yujyamānaṃ nityehitopāttaduritaprakṣayaprayojanamavaśyakartavyaṃ, vidyāṅgatayā ca vidyāyāḥ kādācitkatayānavaśyaṃ bhāve 'pi 'kāmyo vā naimittiko vā vikṛtya niviśate' iti nyāyādanityādhikāreṇa niviśamānamapi na nityamanityayati, tenāpi tasmiddheriti saṃyogapṛthaktvānna nityānityasaṃyogavirodha ekasya kāryasyeti siddham /
sahākiratvaṃ ca karmaṇāṃ na kārye vidyāyāḥ kiṃ tūtpattau /
kor'tho vidyāsahakārīṇi karmāṇīti /
ayamarthaḥ-satsu karmasu vidyaiva svakārye vyāpriyate /
yathā 'sahaiva daśābhiḥ pūtrairbhāraṃ vahati gardabhī' iti sātsveva daśaputreṣu saiva bhārasya vāhiketi /
#avidhilakṣaṇatvāditi# /
vihitaṃ hi darśapaurṇamāsādyaṅgairyujyate na tvavihitam /
grāhakagrahaṇapūrvakatvādaṅgabhāvasya vidhaiśca grāhakatvāt /
avihite ca tadanupapatteḥ /
catasṛṇāmapi ca pratipattīnāṃ brahmaṇi vidhānānupapatterityuktaṃ prathamasūtre /
draṣṭavyo nididhyāsitavya iti ca vidhisarūpaṃ ni vidhirityapyuktam /

children.translated_text: But the causal role [of <s>karma</s>] toward the origination [of <s>vidyā</s>] — through purification of <s>sattva</s> (being), via the door of generating the desire for knowledge (<s>vividiṣā</s>) — has been established earlier.
And because the fruit of <s>vidyā</s> — namely liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) — is not something to be accomplished; for that [liberation] has the character of abiding in one's own essential nature.

children.text: naca svaṃ rūpaṃ brahmaṇaḥ sādhyaṃ nityatvāt /
children.translated_text: And the essential nature of <s>Brahman</s> is not something to be accomplished, because of [its] eternality.
The rest is of transparent meaning. //32//

body.translated_text:
For an established entity is overridden by the conjunction of contradictory attributes.
But not [an entity] of the nature of something to be accomplished — as in the case of [the single <s>Ṣoḍaśi</s>] cup, where both taking and not-taking [are enjoined].
For those [alternatives], being dependent on injunction, are indeed optional.
But in an established [entity], optionality is not possible.
Thus, here, the single ritual called <s>Agnihotra</s> — being conjoined with the perpetual (<s>nitya</s>) [obligation] through the evidence of the <s>Śruti</s> 'as long as one lives' — has the purpose of destroying the accumulated sins and must necessarily be performed; and as a subsidiary of <s>vidyā</s> — since <s>vidyā</s> is occasional, even when it need not [always] occur — by the principle 'whether desire-motivated or occasional, [the rite] enters [the principal] by modification,' even while entering through a non-permanent qualification, it does not make the permanent [rite] non-permanent; because of the separateness of conjunction with that [non-permanent qualification] too, there is no contradiction of the permanent and non-permanent conjoining in a single effect — this is established.
And the co-operative-hood of <s>karma</s>s is not in the effect of <s>vidyā</s> but in its origination.
What is meant by [saying] '<s>karma</s>s are cooperatives of <s>vidyā</s>'?
The meaning is this: when <s>karma</s>s are present, <s>vidyā</s> alone operates toward its own effect.
Just as 'the she-donkey, together with her ten foals, carries the burden' — she, together with her ten foals, alone carries the burden.
'#Because of not having the character of an injunction#' — thus.
For what is enjoined is conjoined with subsidiaries — the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and the like — but not what is not enjoined.
Because subsidiary-hood presupposes the prior cognition of a receptor, and injunctions are [the source of] that receptive cognition.
And in what is not enjoined, that [receptive cognition] is inapplicable.
And it has been stated in the first <s>sūtra</s> that none of the four cognitions (<s>pratipatti</s>s) can be enjoined regarding <s>Brahman</s>.
'One should see, one should contemplate' (<s>draṣṭavyo nididhyāsitavyaḥ</s>) — even though these have the form of injunction, they are not injunctions — this too has been stated.

body.text:
#sarvathāpi ta evobhayaliṅgāt# /
yathā māsamagnihotraṃ juhvatīti prakaraṇāntarātkarmabheda evamihāpi 'tametaṃ vedānuvacanena brāhmaṇā vividiṣanti yajñena' itikratuprakaraṇamatikramyaśravaṇātprakaraṇāntarāttadbuddhivyavacchede sati karmāntaramiti prāpta ucyate-satyapi prakaraṇāntare tadeva karma, śruteḥ smṛteśca saṃyogabhedaḥ paraṃ yathā 'agnihotraṃ juhuyātsvargakāmaḥ' 'yāvajjīvamagnihotraṃ juhuyāt' iti tadevāgnihotramubhayasaṃyuktam /
nahi prakaraṇāntaraṃ sākṣadbhedakam /
kintu ajñātajñāpanasvaraso vidhiḥ prakaraṇaikye sphuṭatarapratyabhijñābalena svarasaṃ jahyāt /
prakaraṇāntareṇa tu vighaṭutapratyabhijñānaḥ svarasamajahatkarma bhinatti /
iha tu siddhavadutpannarūpāṇyeva yajñādīni vividiṣāyāṃ viniyuñjāno na juhvatītyādivadapūrvameṣāṃ rūpamutpādayitumarhati /
naca tatrāpi naiyamikāgnihotre māsavidhirnāpūrvāgnihotrotpattiriti sāṃpratam /
homa eva sākṣadvidhiśruteḥ /
kālasya cānupādeyasyāvidheyatvāt /

children.text: kāle hi karma vidhīyate na karmaṇi kāla ityutsargaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the general rule is: <s>karma</s> is prescribed in [relation to] time, not time in [relation to] <s>karma</s>.

children.text: iha tu vividiṣāyāṃ vidhiśrutiḥ na yajñādau /
children.translated_text: But here, the injunctive <s>Śruti</s> pertains to the desire for knowledge (<s>vividiṣā</s>), not to sacrifice and the like.
And those [sacrifices and the like] are merely restated as already established — hence, from [their being] a single <s>karma</s>, the separateness of conjunction is established.
Setting aside <s>Smṛti</s>, the indicatory mark has been stated. //34//

body.translated_text:
'#In every way, these very same [rituals], because of the twofold indicatory mark (<s>ubhayaliṅga</s>)#.'
Just as — 'They offer the <s>Agnihotra</s> for a month' — from a different context, there is a difference of <s>karma</s>; so too here, from the different context of 'The <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s seek to know this through the study of the <s>Veda</s>, through sacrifice' and the like — since [these sentences] go beyond the ritual context — from the different context, when the cognition of [the same <s>karma</s>] has been severed, [the conclusion that this is] a different <s>karma</s> — this being the prima facie view, the reply is given:
Even though the context is different, the <s>karma</s> is the same — because of <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>. The separateness is only of conjunction — just as 'One who desires heaven should offer the <s>Agnihotra</s>' and 'One should offer the <s>Agnihotra</s> as long as one lives' — that very same <s>Agnihotra</s> is conjoined with both.
For a different context is not a direct differentiator.
Rather, the injunction — whose natural function (<s>svarasa</s>) is making known what is unknown — would, when the context is the same, abandon its natural function by the force of the clearer recognition [of identity].
But when the context is different, since recognition is disrupted, [the injunction] — not abandoning its natural function — differentiates the <s>karma</s>.
But here, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] — assigning the already-established sacrifice and the like — in their arisen form — to the desire for knowledge (<s>vividiṣā</s>) — does not produce an unprecedented form of them, as [is done] in 'they offer' and the like.
Nor is it correct [to say] that even there, in the regular (<s>naiyamika</s>) <s>Agnihotra</s>, the month-prescription is not a production of an unprecedented <s>Agnihotra</s>.
Because the <s>Śruti</s> directly prescribes the oblation (<s>homa</s>) itself.
And because the time, being something not to be taken up [as a new element], is not prescribable.

body.text:
#antarā cāpi tu taddṛṣṭeḥ# /
yadi vidyāsahakārīṇyāśramakarmāṇi hanta bho vidhurādīnāmanāśramiṇāmanadhikāro vidyāyām, abhāvātsahakāriṇāmāśramakarmaṇāmiti prāpta ucyate-nātyantamakarmāṇo raikkavidhuravācakravīprabhṛtayaḥ /
santi hi teṣāmanāśramitve 'pi japopavāsadevatārādhanāditi karmāṇi /
karmaṇāṃ ca sahakāritvamuktamāśramakarmaṇāmupalakṣaṇatvāditi na teṣāmanadhikāro vidyāsu /
#janmāntarānuṣṭhiterapi ceti# /
na khalu vidyākārye karmaṇāmapekṣā /
apitu utpāde /
utpādayanti ca vividiṣopahāreṇa karmāṇi vidyām /
utpannavividiṣāṇāṃ puruṣadhaureyāṇāṃ vidhurasaṃvartaprabhṛtīnāṃ kṛtaṃ karmabhiḥ /

children.text: yadyapi ceha janmani tatheha janmanyāśramakarmotpāditavividiṣa eva vidyāyāmadhikṛto netara ityanāśramiṇāmanadhikāro vidhuraprabhṛtīnāmityata āha- #dṛṣṭārthā ceti# /
children.translated_text: Even though [one might argue that] in this very birth, one whose desire for knowledge has been generated by <s>āśrama-karma</s>s in this very birth alone is eligible for <s>vidyā</s>, and not otherwise — and hence those without a life-stage, such as <s>Vidhura</s> and the like, would be ineligible — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#And because the fruit is directly perceptible#' — thus.
The directly perceptible fruit of <s>vidyā</s> is the cessation of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance).
And that [cessation], being established through [the method of] agreement and difference (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>), does not require a restriction [on eligibility] — this is the meaning.
'Prohibition' (<s>pratiṣedha</s>) [means] obstruction; 'its absence' — this is the meaning. //36//

body.translated_text:
'#And even one who is in an intermediate [state] — because that is seen#.'
If <s>āśrama</s>-<s>karma</s>s (rituals belonging to life-stages) are cooperatives of <s>vidyā</s>, then — for those who are without a life-stage (<s>anāśramin</s>), such as <s>vidhura</s>s (widowers) and the like — there would be no eligibility for <s>vidyā</s>, because of the absence of the cooperatives, namely <s>āśrama-karma</s>s — this being the prima facie view, the reply is given: <s>Raikva</s>, <s>Vidhura</s>, <s>Vācakravī</s>, and the like are not entirely without <s>karma</s>.
For even though they are not in any [particular] life-stage, they have <s>karma</s>s such as recitation (<s>japa</s>), fasting (<s>upavāsa</s>), worship of deities (<s>devatārādhana</s>), and the like.
And the cooperative-hood of <s>karma</s>s was stated with reference to <s>āśrama-karma</s>s as merely representative [examples] — hence they are not ineligible for the <s>vidyā</s>s.
'#And because of the performance in a previous birth too#' — thus.
For <s>karma</s>s are not required [as cooperatives] for <s>vidyā</s>'s effect.
Rather, [they are required] for [<s>vidyā</s>'s] origination.
And <s>karma</s>s generate <s>vidyā</s> through the offering of the desire for knowledge (<s>vividiṣā</s>).
For <s>Vidhura</s>, <s>Saṃvarta</s>, and the like — preeminent among persons, in whom the desire for knowledge has arisen — <s>karma</s>s have [already] done their work.

children.translated_text: If even those without a life-stage (<s>anāśramin</s>s) are eligible for <s>vidyā</s>, then what is the need for the life-stages involving excessive exertion? — anticipating this [objection], [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#But from these, the other [life-stages] are superior, because of the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>)#.'
One who is healthy should adopt a life-stage.

children.text: daivātpunaḥ patnyādiviyogātaḥ satyanāśramitve bhavedadhikāro vidyāyāmiti śrutismṛtisaṃdarbheṇa vividiṣanti yajñenetyādinā jyāyastvāvagateḥ śrutiliṅgātsmṛtiliṅgāccvāgamyate /
children.translated_text: But due to providential [misfortune] — such as separation from wife and the like — when there is a genuine absence of a life-stage, there may be eligibility for <s>vidyā</s>. And from the passage of <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>, beginning with 'they seek to know through sacrifice' and the like — since the superiority [of the life-stages] is understood from the <s>Śruti</s>-indicatory mark and the <s>Smṛti</s>-indicatory mark — [this] is comprehended.

children.text: tenaiti puṇyakṛditi śrutiliṅgam, anāśramī na tiṣṭhetetyādi ca smṛtiliṅgam //39 //
children.translated_text: 'By that he goes to the realm of merit' — this is the <s>Śruti</s>-indicatory mark; 'one who is without a life-stage should not remain [so]' and the like — this is the <s>Smṛti</s>-indicatory mark. //39//

body.text:
#tadbhūtasya tu nātadbhāvo jaiminerapi niyamātadrūpābhāvebhyaḥ# /
ārohavatpratyavaroho 'pi kadācidūrdhvaretasāṃ syāditi mandāśaṅkānivāraṇārthamidamadhikaraṇam /
pūrvadharmeṣu yāgahomādiṣu /
rāgato vā gṛhastho 'haṃ patnyādiparivṛtaḥ syāmiti /

children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] explains the restriction: 'For thus — "#absolutely, of the selves#"' — thus.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] explains the absence-of-that-form — [meaning] the absence of parity with ascent: '#For thus, "having completed <s>brahmacarya</s>"#' — thus.

children.text: abhāvaṃ śiṣṭācārābhāvaṃ vibhajate- #na caivamācārāḥ śiṣṭā iti# /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] elaborates the absence — [meaning] the absence of the practice of the learned (<s>śiṣṭācāra</s>): '#And those who conduct themselves thus are not among the learned#' — thus.
The rest is of transparent meaning. //40//

body.translated_text:
'#But for one who has attained that [state of renunciation], there is no reversal to a non-that-state — [so holds] <s>Jaimini</s> too — because of the restriction, and because of the absence of that form#.'
This <s>adhikaraṇa</s> is for the purpose of removing the feeble doubt that — just as there is ascent [to higher life-stages], so there might sometimes be descent for the <s>ūrdhvaretasa</s>s (lifelong celibates).
In the earlier <s>dharma</s>s — sacrifice, oblation, and the like —
or [one might think:] 'Through passion, I might become a householder, surrounded by a wife and the like.'

body.text: #na cādhikārikamapipatanānumānāttadayogāt# /

children.text: prāyaścittaṃ na paśyāmīti naiṣṭhikaṃ prati prāyaścittābhāvasmaraṇānnairṛtagardabhālambhaḥ prāyaścittamupakurvāṇakaṃ prati /
children.translated_text: 'I do not see an expiation' — from this <s>Smṛti</s>-statement of the absence of expiation for the lifelong celibate (<s>naiṣṭhika</s>), the <s>nairṛta-gardabhālambha</s> (the rite involving a <s>Nirṛti</s>-donkey) is the expiation for the <s>upakurvāṇaka</s> (the temporary student).

children.text: tasmācchinnaśirasa iva puṃsaḥ pratikriyābhāva iti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, like a person whose head has been severed, there is no remedial action — this is the prima facie view.

children.text: sūtrayojanā tu-na cādhikārikamadhikāralakṣaṇe prathamakāṇḍe nirṇītam 'avakīrṇipaśuśca tadvadādhānasyāprāptakālatvāt' ityanena yatprāyaścittaṃ tanna naiṣṭhike bhavitumarhati /
children.translated_text: But the construction of the <s>sūtra</s> is: The expiation that has been determined in the first <s>kāṇḍa</s> (book), which pertains to qualification (<s>adhikāra</s>) — [by the <s>sūtra</s>] 'And the animal for one who has broken his vow (<s>avakīrṇin</s>), likewise, because the time for fire-establishment has not arrived' — that expiation cannot apply to the lifelong celibate (<s>naiṣṭhika</s>).
Why? — Because from the inference of falling — [implied by] the <s>Smṛti</s> 'he has ascended to the lifelong [vow]' — there is the impossibility of expiation for that [lapse]. //41//

body.translated_text: '#And the [sin] pertaining to the qualification (<s>adhikārika</s>) — [there is] no expiation — because of the inference from falling, [and] because of the impossibility of that#.'

body.text:
upapūrvamapītyeke bhāvamaśanavattaduktam /
śrutistāvatsarasato 'saṅkacadvṛttirbrahmacārimātrasya naiṣṭhikasyopakurvāṇasya cāviśeṣeṇa prāyaścittamupadiśati sākṣāt /
prāyaścittaṃ na paśyāmīti tu smṛtiḥ /
tasyāmapi ca sākṣātprāyaścittaṃ na kartavyamiti prāyaścittaniṣedho na gamyate, na paśyāmīti tu darśanābhāvena so 'numātavyaḥ /
body.translated_text:
'Some [say] that even a minor [lapse] — like eating [forbidden food] — has that [status of irremediability]; that has been stated.'
The <s>Śruti</s>, to begin with — proceeding generally and without restriction — prescribes expiation directly for the <s>brahmacārin</s> in general — for both the lifelong (<s>naiṣṭhika</s>) and the temporary (<s>upakurvāṇa</s>) — without distinction.
'I do not see an expiation' — this, however, is <s>Smṛti</s>.
And even in that [<s>Smṛti</s>], 'An expiation should not be directly performed' — a prohibition of expiation is not directly conveyed; rather, through the expression 'I do not see,' it must be inferred from the absence of observation.

body.text:
tathā ca smṛtirniṣedhārtheti anumāya tadarthā śrutiranumātavyā /
śrutistu sāmānyaviṣayā viśeṣamupasarpantī śīghrapravṛttiriti /
smārtaṃ prāyaścittādarśanaṃ tu yatnagauravārtham /
etaduktaṃ bhavati-kṛtanirṇejanairapi etairna saṃkhyānaṃ kartavyamiti /
sūtrārthastu-upapūrvamapi pātakaṃ naiṣṭhikasyāvakīrṇitvaṃ na mahāpātakamapirevakārārthe ata eke prāyaścittabhāvamicchantīti /

children.translated_text: When the teachers disagree, in the absence of a specific [deciding factor], there should be equality [of the views].

children.text: śāstrasthā yā vā prasiddhiḥ sā grāhyā śāstramūlatvāt /
children.translated_text: Or, the well-known position that is grounded in scripture should be accepted, because of [its] having scripture as its root.
And it has been established that the well-known position favoring expiation has scripture as its root.
The rest is easy [to understand]. //42//

body.translated_text:
And thus, having inferred that the <s>Smṛti</s> has the purpose of prohibition, the <s>Śruti</s> [which prescribes expiation] should be inferred [as applying more narrowly].
But the <s>Śruti</s>, being general in scope, and — when approaching a specific [case] — having quicker application [is stronger].
But the <s>Smṛti</s>'s statement of the absence of expiation is for the purpose of [indicating] the gravity of the effort [required for purification].
What is stated amounts to this: even after performing these purificatory [rites], one should not be counted [among the worthy].
But the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is: Even a minor (<s>upa</s>-) transgression is, for the lifelong celibate, a fall (<s>avakīrṇitva</s>) — not a great sin (<s>mahāpātaka</s>) — the word '<s>api</s>' [here] has the sense of 'only'; hence some [teachers] hold that there is [room for] expiation.

body.text:
3.4.12.43.
yadi naiṣṭhikādīnāmasti prāyaścittaṃ tatkimetaiḥ kṛtanirṇejanaiḥ saṃvyavahartavyamuta neti /
tatra doṣakṛtatvādasaṃvyavahārasya prāyaścittena tannibarhaṇādanibarhaṇe vā tatkaraṇavaiyarthyātsaṃvyavahāryā eveti prāpta ucyati- #bahistūbhayathāpi smṛterācārācca# /
niṣiddhakarmānuṣṭhānajanyameno lokadvaye 'pyaśuddhimāpādayati dvaidham lokadvaye 'pyaśuddhirapanīyate prāyaścittairenonibarhaṇaṃ kurvāṇaiḥ /
kasyācittu paralokāśuddhimātramapanīyate prāyaścittairenonibarhaṇaṃ kurvāṇairihalokāśuddhistvenasāpāditā na śakyāpanetum /
yathā strībālādighātinām /
yathāhuḥ-'viśuddhānapi dharmato na saṃpibet' iti /

children.text: tathā ca 'prāyaścittairapaityeno yadajñānakṛtaṃ bhavet' kāmataḥ kṛtamapi /
children.translated_text: And thus: 'The sin that is committed unknowingly is removed by expiations' — [and] even [sin committed] intentionally.

children.text: bālaghrādistu kṛtanirṇejano 'pi vacanādavyavahārya iha loke jāyata iti /
children.translated_text: But a killer of a child and the like — even though purified — is, by scriptural injunction, one with whom association in this world is not [to be had].
And the injunction is 'killers of children' and the like.
Therefore, everything is clear. //43//

body.translated_text:
3.4.12.43.
If there is expiation for the lifelong celibate (<s>naiṣṭhika</s>) and the like, then [the question is:] should one associate with these persons who have performed purificatory [rites], or not?
Therein — since the non-association is [due to the] fault committed, and since that [fault] is destroyed by expiation, and if [the fault is] not destroyed, the performance [of expiation] would be purposeless — they are indeed to be associated with. This being the prima facie view, the reply is given: '#But [they are] excluded in both ways, because of <s>Smṛti</s> and traditional practice#.'
The sin generated by the performance of a prohibited action produces impurity in both worlds — [i.e.,] a twofold [impurity] in both worlds is removed by expiations that effect the destruction of sin.
But for some, only the impurity pertaining to the other world is removed by expiations that effect the destruction of sin — the impurity in this world, produced by the sin, cannot be removed.
As in the case of those who have killed a woman, a child, and the like.
As they say: 'One should not dine even with those who are purified according to <s>dharma</s>.'

children.translated_text: '#[The meditations belong to] the sacrificer (<s>svāmin</s>), because of the <s>Śruti</s> of the fruit — so [holds] <s>Ātreya</s>#.'

children.text: prathame kāṇḍe śeṣalakṣaṇe tathākāma ityatrartviksaṃbandhe karmaṇaḥ siddhe kiṃ kāmo yājamāna utārtvijya iti saṃśapyārtvijye 'pi karmaṇi yājamāna eva kāmo guṇaphaleṣviti nirṇītamihi tvevañjātīyakāni cāṅgasaṃbaddhāni upāsanāni kiṃ yājamānanyevotārtvijyānīti vicāryata iti na punaruktam /
children.translated_text: In the first <s>kāṇḍa</s> (book), in the section on the subsidiary relation (<s>śeṣalakṣaṇa</s>), when the [topic] '<s>tathākāma</s>' [is discussed] — when the connection of <s>karma</s> with the priests (<s>ṛtvik</s>s) is established — the question is: whose is the desire [for the fruit] — the sacrificer's (<s>yajamāna</s>) or the priests'? And it was determined that even in a ritual performed by the priests, the desire [for the fruit] in secondary fruits belongs to the sacrificer alone. But here, the investigation is of a similar kind: do the meditations connected with the subsidiary [rites] belong to the sacrificer alone or to the priests? — hence this is not a mere repetition.

children.text: tatropāsakānāṃ phalaśravaṇādanadhikāriṇastadanupapatteryajamānasya ca karmajanitaphalopabhogabhājo 'dhikārādṛtvijāṃ ca tadanupapattervacanācca rājājñāsthānīyātkkacidṛtvijāṃ phalaśruterasati vacane yajamānasya phalavadupāsanaṃ tasya phalaśruteḥ taṃ ha bako dālabhyo vidāñcakāretyāderupāsanasya ca siddhaviṣayatayānyāyāpavādasāmarthyabhāvādyājamānamevopāsanākarmeti prāpta ucyate- //44 //
children.translated_text: Therein, since the fruit is heard [as belonging to] the meditators, and since for one who is not eligible [as a meditator] that [fruit] would be inapplicable; and since the sacrificer — being eligible as one who partakes of the fruits generated by <s>karma</s> — [would qualify]; and since for the priests, that [fruit] would be inapplicable; and since, from scripture — which occupies the position of a king's command — the hearing of the fruit [pertains] to certain priests; but in the absence of [such explicit] scripture, the meditation — being fruitful for the sacrificer — and the <s>Śruti</s> of its fruit — [and since, from passages like] '<s>Baka Dālbhya</s> knew thus' — [which show that] the meditation has an already-established [person] as its domain, and hence the capacity for overriding by exception (<s>anyāyāpavāda</s>) is absent — the meditation-ritual belongs to the sacrificer alone — this being the prima facie view, the reply is given: //44//

body.text: #ārtvijyamityauḍulomistasmai hi parikrīyate# /

children.translated_text: From the narrative (<s>upākhyāna</s>), to begin with, the meditation is understood as belonging to the <s>Udgātṛ</s> (chanter).
When that strong overriding [evidence] is present, [any evidence to the contrary] must be explained otherwise.

children.text: na cartvikkartṛka upāsane yajamānagāmitā phalasyāsaṃbhavinī tena hi sa parikrīyastadgāmine phalāya ghaṭate /
children.translated_text: Nor is the transfer of the fruit to the sacrificer impossible when the meditation is performed by the priest — for he is hired [precisely] for that [purpose], and [it] is fitting that the fruit goes to [the one who hired him].
Therefore, the narrative should not be reinterpreted merely because of a difficulty — this is the established conclusion. //45//

body.translated_text: '#It belongs to the priests (<s>ṛtvik</s>s) — so [holds] <s>Auḍulomi</s> — because [the sacrificer] is hired for that [purpose]#.'

body.text:
tasmādbrāhmaṇaḥ pāṇḍityaṃ nirvidya niścayena /
labdhvā bālyena tiṣṭhāsedbālyaṃ ca pāṇḍityaṃ ca nirvidyātha muniramaunaṃ ca maunaṃ ca nirvidyātha brāhmaṇa iti /
yatra hi vidhivibhaktiḥ śrūyate sa vidheyaḥ /
bālyena tiṣṭhāsedityatra ca sā śrūyate na śrūyate tu maune /
tasmādyathātha brahmaṇa ityetadaśrūyamāṇavidhikamavidheyamevaṃ maunamapi /
na cāpūrvatvādvidheyaṃ, tasmādbrāhnaḥ pāṇḍityaṃ nirvidyeti pāṇḍityavidhānādeva maunasiddheḥ pāṇḍityameva maunamiti /
athavā bhikṣuvacano 'yaṃ muniśabdastatra darśanāt 'gārhasthyamācāryakulaṃ maunaṃ vānaprastham' ityatra /
tasyānyato vihitasyāyamanuvādaḥ /
tasmādbālyamevātra vidhīyate maunaṃ tu prāptaṃ praśaṃsārthamanūdyata iti yuktam /
bhavedevaṃ yadi paṇḍitaparyāyo muniśabdo bhavet /
api tu jñānamātraṃ pāṇḍityaṃ jñānātiśayasaṃpattistu maunaṃ tatprasiddheḥ /
āśramabhede tu tatpravṛttirgārhasthyādipadasaṃnidhānāt /
tasmādapūrvatvānmaunasya bālyapāṇḍityāpekṣayā tṛtīyamidaṃ maunaṃ jñānātiśayarūpaṃ vidhīyate /
evaṃ ca nirvedanīyatvamapi vidhāna āñjasaṃ syādityāha- #nirvedanīyatvanirdeśāditi# /
kasyedaṃ maunaṃ vidhīyate vidyāsahakāritayetyata āha- #tadvato vidyāvataḥ saṃnyāsino#bhikṣoḥ /
pṛcchati- #kathamiti# /
vidyāvattā pratīyate na saṃnyāsitetyarthaḥ /
uttaran #tadadhikārāt#bhikṣostadadhikārāt /
taddarśayati- #ātmānaṃ viditveti# /
body.translated_text:
Therefore: 'The <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, having become disenchanted with learning (<s>pāṇḍitya</s>) — with firm resolve —
should abide in child-like simplicity (<s>bālya</s>); and having become disenchanted with both <s>bālya</s> and <s>pāṇḍitya</s>, he becomes a <s>muni</s> (sage); and having become disenchanted with both non-silence and silence (<s>mauna</s>), he becomes a [true] <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.'
For wherever a prescriptive verb-ending (<s>vidhivibhakti</s>) is heard, that [action] is what is to be enjoined.
And in 'he should abide in <s>bālya</s>' (<s>tiṣṭhāset</s>), it is heard; but it is not heard with respect to <s>mauna</s> (silence).
Therefore, just as '<s>atha brāhmaṇaḥ</s>' ('now [he becomes] a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>') — having no heard injunction — is not something to be enjoined, so too <s>mauna</s>.
Nor is it something to be enjoined merely because of being unprecedented — because <s>mauna</s> is established from the very injunction of <s>pāṇḍitya</s> (learning), since <s>pāṇḍitya</s> itself is <s>mauna</s>.
Alternatively, the word '<s>muni</s>' here denotes a mendicant (<s>bhikṣu</s>), since it is seen [used in that sense] there — 'the householder's life, the teacher's house, <s>mauna</s> [denotes] the forest-dweller's life' — in that [passage].
Being enjoined elsewhere, this is a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) of that [injunction].
Therefore, <s>bālya</s> alone is enjoined here, while <s>mauna</s> — being [already] established — is restated for the purpose of praise — this is fitting.
This would be so if the word '<s>muni</s>' were synonymous with '<s>paṇḍita</s>' (learned one).
But in fact, <s>pāṇḍitya</s> is mere knowledge, while <s>mauna</s> is the attainment of a superlative degree of knowledge — because that is the well-known [meaning].
But the usage [of '<s>muni</s>'] in the sense of different <s>āśrama</s>s is due to the proximity of words like '<s>gārhasthya</s>' (householder's life) and the like.
Therefore, because of its being unprecedented — compared to <s>bālya</s> and <s>pāṇḍitya</s> — this third [element], <s>mauna</s> in the form of a superlative degree of knowledge, is enjoined.
And thus, the designation as something [from which one should become] 'disenchanted' (<s>nirvedanīya</s>) too would be straightforward in the [context of the] injunction — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Because of the designation as something to be transcended#.'
For whom is this <s>mauna</s> enjoined, as an auxiliary to <s>vidyā</s>? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#For one who possesses that — i.e., for one who possesses <s>vidyā</s>, the <s>saṃnyāsin</s>#' — the mendicant (<s>bhikṣu</s>).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] asks: '#How?#'
The meaning is: what is perceived is the possession of <s>vidyā</s>, not the [status of] <s>saṃnyāsin</s>.
The answer: '#Because of his eligibility for that#' — i.e., the eligibility of the mendicant.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] demonstrates this: '#Having known the Self#.'

body.text:
sūtrāvayavaṃ yojayituṃ śaṅkate- #nanviti# /
pariharati- #ata āha-pakṣeṇeti# /
vidyāvāniti na vidyātiśayo vivakṣitaḥ /
api tu vidyodayāyābhyāse pravṛtto na punarutpannavidyātiśayaḥ /

children.translated_text: And thus, it is possible that in his case, optionally, the perception of difference [may arise at times] — this is the meaning.
The injunction and the like — the injunction being the principal — that [injunction] is the principal — this is what is meant.

children.text: ata eva samidādirvidhyantaḥ sa hi vidhiḥ pradhānavidheḥ paścāditi /
children.translated_text: For this very reason, the injunction of fuel-sticks (<s>samidh</s>) and the like falls within [the scope of] the injunction — for that injunction comes after the principal injunction.
Therein, even when the [explicit] injunction is not heard, because of [the content's] being unprecedented, an injunction should be resorted to — this is the meaning. //47//

body.translated_text:
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>], wishing to construe a component of the <s>sūtra</s>, raises a doubt: '#But surely#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] resolves: '#Hence [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: "optionally" (<s>pakṣeṇa</s>)#.'
By 'possessing <s>vidyā</s>' (<s>vidyāvān</s>), a superlative degree of <s>vidyā</s> is not intended.
Rather, [it means] one who is engaged in the practice [leading] to the arising of <s>vidyā</s> — not one in whom the superlative degree of <s>vidyā</s> has already arisen.

children.text: nanu yadyayamāśramo bālyapradhānaḥ kasmātpunargārhasthyenopasaṃharatīti codayati- #evaṃ bālyādiviśiṣṭeti# /
children.translated_text: Now, if this <s>āśrama</s> (life-stage) has <s>bālya</s> (child-like simplicity) as its principal [characteristic], why then does [the <s>Śruti</s>] conclude with the householder's life-stage? — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises this objection: '#Thus, [the life-stage] distinguished by <s>bālya</s> and the like#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] reads out the answer: '#But because of completeness (<s>kṛtsnabhāva</s>), the summation is through the householder#.'

children.text: chāndogye bahulāyāsādhyakarmabahulatvādgārhasthyasya cāśramāntaradharmāṇāṃ ca keṣāñcidahiṃsādīnāṃ samavāyāttenopasaṃhāro na punastena samāpanādityarthaḥ //48 //
children.translated_text: In the <s>Chāndogya</s>, because of the abundance of <s>karma</s>s achievable through much effort in the householder's life-stage, and because of the inclusion (<s>samavāya</s>) of certain <s>dharma</s>s of the other life-stages — such as non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>) and the like — the summation is through that [householder's stage]; but it does not mean that [the <s>vidyā</s>] is completed [only] through that — this is the meaning. //48//

children.text: evaṃ tadāśramadvayopanyāsena kkacitkadāciditarābhāvaśaṅkā mandabuddheḥ syāditi tadapākaraṇārthaṃ sūtram- #maunavaditareṣāmapyupadeśāt# /
children.translated_text: Thus, since from the mention of only those two life-stages [householder and renunciant], a person of dull intellect might suspect that the other [life-stages] are absent somewhere or at some time, for the purpose of removing that [doubt], the <s>sūtra</s> is: '#Like <s>mauna</s> (silence/contemplation), for the others too, because of the teaching#.'

children.text: vṛttirvānaprasthānāmanekavidhairevaṃ brahmācāriṇo 'pīti vṛttibhedo 'nuṣṭhātāro vā puruṣā bhidyante, tasmāddvitve 'pi bahuvacanamaviruddham //49 //
children.translated_text: The modes of living of the forest-dwellers (<s>vānaprastha</s>s) are of many kinds; similarly, of the <s>brahmacārin</s>s (celibate students) too — thus, the modes of living differ, or the persons who practice [them] differ; therefore, even when there are [only] two [life-stages mentioned], the plural [in the <s>sūtra</s>] is not contradictory. //49//
'#Without making [it] manifest, because of the coherence (<s>anvaya</s>)#.'

children.text: bālyeneti yāvadbālacaritaśruteḥ kāmacāravādabhakṣatāyāśacātyantabālyena prasiddheḥ śaucādiniyamavidhāyinaśca sāmānyaśāstrasyānena viśeṣaśāstreṇa bādhanātsakalabālacaritavidhānamiti prāpte 'bhidhīyate-vidyāṅgatvena bālyavidhānātsamastabālacaryāyāṃ ca pradhānavirodhaprasaṅgādyattadanuguṇamaprauḍhendriyatvādi bhāvaśuddhirūpaṃ tadeva vidhīyate /
children.translated_text: 'In <s>bālya</s>' — this being so, since the <s>Śruti</s> speaks of the conduct of a child (<s>bālacarita</s>), and since <s>kāmacāra</s> (acting by whim) and eating anything (<s>bhakṣatā</s>) are well-known as extreme child-like behavior, and since the general scripture (<s>sāmānyaśāstra</s>) enjoining the rules of purity (<s>śauca</s>) and the like is overridden by this specific scripture — [one might conclude that] the injunction is of the entire conduct of a child. Against this prima facie view, it is stated: Since <s>bālya</s> is enjoined as subsidiary to <s>vidyā</s>, and since the entire conduct of a child would involve the unwanted consequence of contradicting the principal [<s>vidyā</s>], what is enjoined is only that which is conducive to it — namely, the purity of disposition (<s>bhāvaśuddhi</s>) characterized by the non-maturity of the senses and the like.

children.text: evaṃ ca śāstrāntarābādhenāpyupapattau na śāstrāntarabādhanamanyāpyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti //50 //
children.translated_text: And thus, when the explanation is possible without overriding another scripture, the overriding of another scripture should not be resorted to. //50//

body.text:
#aihikamapyaprastutapratibandhe taddarśanāt# /
saṃgatimāha- #sarvāpekṣā ceti# /
kiṃ śravaṇādibhirihaiva vā janmani vidyā sādhyate utāniyama iha vāmutra veti /
yadyapi karmāṇi yajñādinyaniyataphalāni teṣāṃ ca vidyotpadasādhanatvena vidyotpādasyāniyamaḥ pratibhāti /
tathāca garbhasthasya vāmadevasyātmapratibodhaśravaṇāt 'anekajanmasaṃsiddhastato yati parāṃ gatim' iti ca smaraṇādāmuṣmikatvamapyavagamyate /
tathāpi yajñādīnāṃ prameyāṇāmapramāṇatvācchravaṇādeśca pramāṇatvātteṣāmeva sākṣādvidyāsādhanatvam /
yajñādīnāṃ sattvaśuddhyādhānena vā vidyotpādakaśravaṇādilakṣaṇapramāṇapravṛttivighnopaśamena vā vidyāsādhanatvām /
śravaṇādīnāṃ tvanapekṣāmāmeva vidyotpādakatvam /
naca pramāṇeṣu pravartamānāḥ pramātāra aihikamapi cirabhāvinaṃ pramotpādaṃ kāmayante kintu tādātvikameva prāgeva tu pāralaukikam /
nahi kumbhalādidṛkṣuścakṣuṣī samunmīlayati kālāntarīyāya kumbhadarśanāya kintu tādātvikāya /
tasmādaihika eva vidyotpādo nāniyatakālaḥ /
śrutismṛtī ca pāralaukikaṃ vidyotpādaṃ stutyā brātaḥ /

children.translated_text: [The intent of those passages is:] Such indeed are <s>śravaṇa</s> and the like — necessarily fruitful — that they produce <s>vidyā</s> even at a later time.

children.text: evaṃ prāpta ucyate-yata evātra vidyotpāde śravaṇādibhiḥ kartavye yajñādīnāṃ sattvāśuddhidvāreṇa vā vighnopaśamadvārā vopayogo 'ta eva teṣāṃ yajñādīnāṃ karmāntarapratibandhāpratibandhābhyāmaniyataphalatvena tadapekṣāṇāṃ śravaṇādīnāmapyaniyataphalatvaṃ nyāṭyaniyataphalatvaṃ nyāṭyamanapahatavighnānāṃ śravaṇādīnāmanutpādakatvādaviśuddhasattvādvā puṃsaḥ pratyanutpādakatvāt /
children.translated_text: Against this prima facie view, it is stated: Since the sacrifices and the like — whose utility in the arising of <s>vidyā</s> through <s>śravaṇa</s> and the like is either through the purification of <s>sattva</s> or through the removal of obstacles — have fruits that are not fixed in time due to the obstruction or non-obstruction by other <s>karma</s>s, therefore <s>śravaṇa</s> and the like too — being dependent on those [sacrifices and the like] — appropriately have fruits that are not fixed in time, since <s>śravaṇa</s> and the like, when obstacles have not been removed, are non-productive, or because [they are] non-productive for a person whose <s>sattva</s> is impure.

children.text: tathāca teṣāṃ yajñādyapekṣāṇāṃ teṣāṃ cāniyataphalatvena śravaṇādīnāmapyaniyataphalatvaṃ yuktamevaṃ śrutismṛtipratibandho na stutimātratvena vyākhyeyo bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: And thus, since [<s>śravaṇa</s> and the like] depend on the sacrifices and the like, and since both have fruits that are not fixed in time, the <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s> [statements about the] obstruction [to immediate knowledge] should not be explained away as mere praise.

children.text: puruṣāśca vidyārthinaḥ sādhanasāmarthyānusāreṇa tadanurūpameva kāmayiṣyante tadidamuktam-abhisaṃdherniraṅkaśatvāditi //51 //
children.translated_text: And persons seeking <s>vidyā</s> will desire [the fruit] in accordance with the capacity of their means, proportionate to that — this is what is stated: '#Because of the unrestricted nature of the intention#.' //51//

body.translated_text:
'#[The fruit is] in this life too, when there is no obstruction by what is not relevant — because of the observation of that#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the connection: '#And the consideration of all [subsidiary means]#.'
[The question is:] Does <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) arise in this very birth through <s>śravaṇa</s> (hearing) and the like, or is there no fixed rule — [it could be] here or hereafter?
Although the sacrifices and the like yield fruits that are not fixed [in time], and since their being the means to the arising of <s>vidyā</s> implies that the arising of <s>vidyā</s> too has no fixed [time] —
and thus, from the hearing [in <s>Śruti</s>] of the Self-realization of <s>Vāmadeva</s> while still in the womb, and from the <s>Smṛti</s> 'Having been perfected through many births, he then attains the supreme goal' — the other-worldly [occurrence of <s>vidyā</s>] too is understood.
Nevertheless, since the sacrifices and the like — being objects of knowledge (<s>prameya</s>) — are not [themselves] valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), and since <s>śravaṇa</s> and the like are valid means of knowledge, the latter alone are the direct means to <s>vidyā</s>.
The sacrifices and the like are means to <s>vidyā</s> either through the purification of <s>sattva</s> (the quality of goodness) or through the removal of obstacles to the operation of <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means) characterized by <s>śravaṇa</s> and the like, which generate <s>vidyā</s>.
But <s>śravaṇa</s> and the like have the capacity to produce <s>vidyā</s> independently [of external aids].
And persons who are engaged in valid means of knowledge do not desire a production of knowledge (<s>pramotpāda</s>) that occurs at a distant future time — even in this life — but desire it immediately; how much less [do they desire it] in the other world.
For one who wishes to see a pot does not open his eyes for the purpose of seeing the pot at some later time, but for [seeing it] immediately.
Therefore, the arising of <s>vidyā</s> is in this life alone, not at an indeterminate time.
And the <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s> [statements about] other-worldly arising of <s>vidyā</s> are spoken by way of praise.

body.text:
#evaṃ muktiphalāniyamastadavasthāvadhṛtestadavasthāvadhṛteḥ# /
yajñādyupakṛtavidyāsādhanaśravaṇādivīryaviśeṣātkila tatphale vidyāyāmaihikamuṣmikatvalakṣaṇa utkarṣo darśitaḥ /
tathā ca yathā sādhanotkarṣanikarṣābhyāṃ tatphalasya vidyāyā utkarṣāvevaṃ vidyāphalasyāpi mukterutkarṣanikarṣau saṃbhāvyete /
naca muktāvaihikāmuṣmikatvalakṣaṇo viśeṣa upapadyate brahmopāsanāparipākalabdhajanmani vidyāyāṃ jīvato mukteravaśyaṃbhāvaniyamātsatyapyārabdhavipākakarmāprakṣaye /
tasmānmuktāveva rūpato nikarṣotkarṣau syātām /
apica saguṇānāṃ vidyānāmutkarṣanikarṣābhyāṃ tatphalānāmutkarṣanikarṣau dṛṣṭāviti mukterapi vidyāphalatvādrūpataścotkarṣanikarṣau syātāmiti prāpata ucyate-na muktestatra tatraikarūpyaśruterupapatteśca /
sādhyaṃ hi sādhanaviśeśaṣādviśeṣavadbhavati /
naca muktirbrahmaṇo nityasvarūpāvasthānalakṣaṇā nityā satī sādhyā bhavitumarhati /
naca savāsananiḥśeṣakleśakarmāśayaprakṣayo vidyājarnmaviśeṣavān, yena tadviśeṣānmokṣo viśeṣavānbhavet /
naca sāvaśeṣaḥ kleśādiprakṣayo mokṣāya kalpate /
naca cirācirotpādānutpādāvantareṇa vidyāyāmapi rūpato bhedaḥ kaścidupalakṣyate tasyā apyekarūpatvena śruteḥ /

children.translated_text: But in the case of <s>saguṇa</s> (qualified) <s>vidyā</s>, through the addition and removal of various qualities, a gradation of its effect — the fruit — is reasonable.

children.text: na cātra vidyātvaṃ sāmānyato dṛṣṭaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: And here, [the case of <s>saguṇa</s>] <s>vidyā</s>-hood [serving as] a generally observed [analogy] does not apply.
Because [the analogy is] overridden by scripture and the reasoning derived from it, [and hence] is stale (<s>kālātyayāpadiṣṭa</s>) [i.e., inapplicable].

children.text: tasmāttasyā muktyavasthāyā aikarūpyāvadhṛtermuktilakṣaṇasya phalasyāviśeṣo yukta iti //52 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, because of the ascertainment of the uniform nature of that state of liberation, the non-differentiation of the fruit characterized as liberation is fitting. //52//

body.translated_text:
'#Similarly, there is no fixed rule regarding the fruit of liberation — because of the ascertainment of that state, because of the ascertainment of that state#.'
Indeed, from the special potency of <s>śravaṇa</s> and the like — which are the means to <s>vidyā</s> and are assisted by sacrifices and the like — a gradation (<s>utkarṣa</s>) in their fruit, <s>vidyā</s>, characterized by its being in this life or the next, has been shown.
And thus, just as there is gradation in <s>vidyā</s> through the gradation of its means, so too a gradation in the fruit of <s>vidyā</s> — namely, liberation (<s>mukti</s>) — is conceivable.
But no distinction characterized by this-worldly or other-worldly [occurrence] is tenable in liberation — because of the fixed rule that, when <s>vidyā</s> arises in a birth obtained through the maturation of meditation on <s>Brahman</s>, liberation-while-living (<s>jīvanmukti</s>) necessarily follows, even though the <s>karma</s> whose ripening has already commenced (<s>prārabdhavipāka</s>) has not been exhausted.
Therefore, the gradation in liberation would have to be in its essential form.
Moreover, since the gradation of <s>saguṇa</s> (qualified) <s>vidyā</s>s [leads to] a gradation of their fruits — this being observed — and since liberation too is a fruit of <s>vidyā</s>, a gradation in its essential form is conceivable — against this prima facie view, it is stated: No, because of the <s>Śruti</s> ascertaining the uniform nature of liberation everywhere, and because of logical consistency.
For something to be accomplished (<s>sādhya</s>) can be affected by the specificity of its means.
But liberation — being the eternal abiding in <s>Brahman</s>'s own nature — being eternal, cannot be something to be accomplished.
Nor does the complete destruction — together with its latent impressions (<s>savāsana</s>) — of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), <s>karma</s>, and latent karmic deposits (<s>āśaya</s>) vary [in nature] based on different births of <s>vidyā</s>, such that liberation would vary on account of [such] variation.
Nor does a partial destruction of afflictions and the like suffice for liberation.
Nor is any difference in the essential form of <s>vidyā</s> discernible — between [arising] sooner or later, or arising or not arising — because of the <s>Śruti</s> of its uniform nature.

body.text: iti śrīvācaspatimiśraviracite śārīrakabhagavatpādabhāṣyavibhāge bhāmatyāṃ tṛtīyādhyāyasya caturthaḥ pādaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s> in the <s>Bhāmatī</s>, the elucidation of the <s>Śārīraka-Bhāṣya</s> of the Blessed Master [<s>Śaṅkara</s>], composed by the venerable <s>Vācaspati Miśra</s>.

body.text: iti tṛtīyādhyāyasya nirguṇavidyāyā antaraṅgasādhanavicārākhyaścaturthaḥ pādaḥ ____________________________Adhyāya 4____________________________ /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s>, called 'The Investigation of the Inner Means of <s>Nirguṇa Vidyā</s> (the Meditation on the Qualityless [<s>Brahman</s>]).'

body.text: #atha caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ (bhāmatī)#
body.translated_text: '#Now the fourth <s>adhyāya</s> (<s>Bhāmatī</s>)#.'

children.text: nābhyarthyā iha santaḥ svayaṃ pravṛttā na cetare śakyāḥ /
children.translated_text: The worthy ones need not be entreated here — they proceed on their own; nor can the others [be helped],
for whom the indigestion (<s>arocaka</s>) — incurable, caused by the bile of envy (<s>matsara</s>) — [persists]. //1//

body.text: śaṅke saṃprati nirviśaṅkamadhunā svarājyasaukhyaṃ vahannendraḥ sāndratapaḥsthiteṣu kathamapyudvegamabhyeṣyati /
body.translated_text: I fancy that now <s>Indra</s>, bearing without apprehension the bliss of his sovereignty, will somehow find alarm among those who are established in intense <s>tapas</s> (austerity) —

body.text: yadvācaspatimiśranirmitamitavyākhyānamātrasphuṭadvedāntārthavivekavañcitabhavāḥ svarge 'pyamī niḥspṛhāḥ //2 //
body.translated_text: for those who, deluded regarding the discernment of the meaning of <s>Vedānta</s> — [now] made perfectly clear by this commentary composed by <s>Vācaspati Miśra</s> — are freed from [their] delusion of existence (<s>bhava</s>), and are without desire even for heaven. //2//

body.text:
#āvṛttirasakṛdupadeśāt# /
sādhanānuṣṭhānapūrvakatvātphalasiddherviṣayakrameṇa viṣayiṇorapi tadvicārayoḥ kramamāha-- #tṛtīye 'dhyāya iti# /
muktilakṣaṇasya phalasyātyantaparokṣatvāttadarthāni darśanaśravaṇamanananididhyāsanāni codyamānānyadṛṣṭārthānīti yāvadvidhānamanuṣṭheyāni na tu tato 'dhikamāvartanīyāni pramāṇābhāvāt /
yatra punaḥ sakṛdupadeśa upāsītetyādiṣu tatra sakṛdeva prayogaḥ prayājādivaditi prāpta ucyate /
yadyapi muktiradṛṣṭacarī tathāpi savāsanāvidyocchedenātmanaḥ svarūpāvasthānalakṣaṇāyāstasyāḥ śrutisiddhatvādavidyāyāśca vidyotpādavirodhitayā vidyotpādena samucchedasyāhivibhramasyeva rajjutatvasākṣātkāreṇa samucchedasyopapattisiddhatvādanvayavyatirekābhyāṃ ca śravaṇamanananididhyāsanābhyāsasyaiva svagocarasākṣātkāraphalatvena lokasiddhatvāsakaladuḥkhavinirmuktaikacaitanyātmako 'hamityaparokṣarūpānubhavasyāpi śravaṇādyabhyāsasādhanatvenānumānāttadarthāni śravaṇādīni dṛṣṭārthāni bhavanti /
na ca dṛṣṭārthatve satyadṛṣṭārthatvaṃ yuktam /
body.translated_text:
'#Repetition (<s>āvṛtti</s>) [is required], because of the instruction being repeated#.'
Because the attainment of the fruit is preceded by the practice of the means, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the sequential order of the two investigations concerning the object and the knower, in the order of the object: '#In the third <s>adhyāya</s>#.'
Since the fruit characterized as liberation is extremely remote [from ordinary experience], the seeing (<s>darśana</s>), hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>), reflection (<s>manana</s>), and meditation (<s>nididhyāsana</s>) that serve that [liberation] — being enjoined for an unseen purpose — should be performed only as much as prescribed, and should not be repeated beyond that, because of the absence of a [scriptural] authority [for further repetition].
But wherever there is a single instruction — 'one should meditate' (<s>upāsīta</s>) and the like — there, the performance should be only once, like the subsidiary rites (<s>prayāja</s>s) and the like — against this prima facie view, it is stated:
Although liberation is of an unseen [character], nevertheless — since liberation, characterized as the abiding in one's own nature of the Self through the destruction of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) together with its latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), is established through <s>Śruti</s>; and since <s>avidyā</s>, being contradicted by the arising of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), [undergoes] complete destruction through the arising of <s>vidyā</s> — just as the delusion of a snake [superimposed on a rope undergoes] complete destruction through the direct realization of the rope-nature — this being established through logical consistency; and since, through positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>), the practice of <s>śravaṇa</s>, <s>manana</s>, and <s>nididhyāsana</s> alone is established in the world as having direct realization of its own object as its fruit; and since the directly perceptible experience (<s>aparokṣānubhava</s>) of the form 'I am the sole consciousness free from all suffering' is also inferred as having the practice of <s>śravaṇa</s> and the like as its means — therefore <s>śravaṇa</s> and the like have a directly seen purpose.
And when the purpose is directly seen, [the inference of] an unseen purpose is not fitting.

body.text: na caitānyanāvṛttāni satkāradīrghakālanairantaryeṇa sākṣātkāravate tādṛśānubhavāya kalpante /

children.translated_text: And here, knowledge that falls short of direct realization (<s>asākṣātkāravat vijñāna</s>) is not capable of destroying <s>avidyā</s> that is accompanied by direct [perceptual] experience.

children.text: na khalu pittopahṛtendriyasya guḍe tiktatāsākṣātkāro 'ntareṇamādhuryasākṣātkāraṃ sahasreṇāpyupapattibhirnivartitumarhati /
children.translated_text: Indeed, for one whose senses are afflicted by [an excess of] bile (<s>pitta</s>), the direct perception of bitterness in sugar (<s>guḍa</s>) — without [the corrective] direct perception of its sweetness — cannot be removed even by a thousand logical arguments.

children.text: atadvato narāntaravacāṃsivopapattisahasrāṇi vā parāmṛśato 'pi thūtkṛtya guḍatyāgāt /
children.translated_text: Even one who considers a thousand logical arguments — or the words of others who do not share [the bile-affliction] — still spits out and discards the sugar.

Thus, since <s>śravaṇa</s> and the like have a directly seen purpose, and since meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) and <s>upāsanā</s> (contemplative worship) — being determined to involve repetition — are known from common experience [to require repetition], repetition (<s>āvṛtti</s>) alone is established. //1//

body.translated_text: And these [<s>śravaṇa</s> and the like], without being repeated with earnestness (<s>satkāra</s>), long duration (<s>dīrghakāla</s>), and continuity (<s>nairantarya</s>), are not sufficient for producing direct realization (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>) and the corresponding experience in one who has [not yet achieved] such direct realization.

body.text:
adhikaraṇārthamuktvā nirupādhibrahmaviṣayatvamasyākṣipati-- #atrāha bhavatu nāmeti# /
sādhye hyanubhave pratyayāvṛttirarthavatī nāsādhye /
nahi brahmānubhavo brahmasākṣātkāro nityaśuddhasvabhāvādbrahmaṇo 'tiricyate /
tathāca nityasya brahmaṇaḥ svabhāvo nitya eveti kṛtamatra pratyayāvṛtyā /
tadidamuktam--- #ātmabhūtamiti# /
ākṣeptāraṃ pratiśaṅkate #---sakṛcchrutāviti# /
ayamabhisaṃdhiḥ--
body.translated_text:
Having stated the purpose of the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic), [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises the objection that [this meditation] pertains to <s>nirupādhi-Brahman</s> (unconditioned <s>Brahman</s>): '#Here it is said: let it be so#' — thus.
For the repetition of cognition (<s>pratyayāvṛtti</s>) is purposeful when the experience is [something] to be accomplished (<s>sādhya</s>), not when [it is already] accomplished (<s>asādhya</s>).
For the experience of <s>Brahman</s>, the direct realization (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>) of <s>Brahman</s>, does not differ from <s>Brahman</s> whose nature is eternally pure.
And thus, the essential nature of eternal <s>Brahman</s> is itself eternal — hence repetition of cognition is pointless here.
This is what is stated: '#[Because the realization] is identical with the Self (<s>ātmabhūtam</s>)#' — thus.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises a counter-doubt against the objector: '#Upon hearing once (<s>sakṛcchrutāv</s>)#' — thus.
The intention is this:

body.text:
na ca brahmātmabhūtastatsākṣātakāro 'vidyāmucchinanti tayā sahānuvṛtteravirodhāte /
virodhe vā tasya nityatvānnāvidyodīyeta kuta eva tu tena sahānuvarteta /
tasmāttannivṛttaye āgantukastatsākṣātkāra eṣitavyaḥ /
tathāca pratyayānuvṛttirarthavatī /
ākṣeptā sarvapūrvoktākṣepeṇa pratyavatiṣṭhate #---na āvṛttāvapīti# /
na khalu jyotiṣṭomavākyārthapratyayaḥ śataśo 'pyāvartamānaḥ sākṣātkārapramāṇaṃ svaviṣaye janayati /
utpannasyāpi tādṛśo dṛṣṭavya bhicāratvena prātibhatvāt /
#brahmātmatvapratītiṃ#brahmatmasākṣātkāram /
punaḥ śaṅkate-- #na kevalaṃ vākyamiti# /
ākṣeptā dūṣayati #---tathāpyāvṛtyānarthakyamiti# /
vākyaṃ cedyuktyapekṣaṃ sākṣātkārāya prabhavatitathā sati kṛtamāvṛtyā /
sakṛtpravṛttasyaiva tasya sopapattikasya yāvatkartavyakaraṇāditi /
punaḥ śaṅkate #---athāpi syāditi# /
na yuktivākye sākṣātkāraphale pratyakṣasyaiva pramāṇasya tatphalatvāt /
te tu parokṣārthāvagāhinī sāmānyamātramabhiniviśate natu viśeṣaṃ sākṣātkuruta iti tadviśeṣasākṣātkārāyāvṛttirupāsyate /
sā hi satkāradīrghakālanairantaryasevitā satī dṛḍhabhūmirviśeṣa sākṣātkārāya prabhavati kāminībhāvaneva straiṇasya puṃsa iti /
ākṣeptāha #--na /
asakṛdapīti# /
sa khalvayaṃ sākṣātkāraḥ śāstra yuktiyonirvā syādbhāvanāmātrayonirvā /
na tāvatparokṣābhāsavijñānaphale śāstrayuktī sākṣātkāralakṣaṇaṃ pratyakṣapramāṇaphalaṃ prasotumarhataḥ /
na khalu kuṭajabījādvaṭāṅkuro jāyate /
naca bhāvanāprakarṣaparyantajamaparokṣāvabhāsamapi jñānaṃ pramāṇaṃ vyabhicārādityuktam /
ākṣeptā svapakṣamupasaṃharati-- #tasmādyadīti# /
ākṣeptākṣepāntaramāha #---naca sakṛtpravṛtte iti# /
kaścitkhalu śuddhasatvogarbhastha iva vāmadevaḥ śrutvā ca matvā ca kṣaṇamavadhāya jīvātmano brahmātmatamanubhavati /
tato 'pyāvṛttiranarthiketi /
ataścāvṛranarthikā yanniraṃśasya grahaṇamadrahaṇaṃ vā na tu vyaktāvyaktatve sāmānyavaśeṣavatpadmarāgādivadityata āha #--api cānekāṃśeti# /
samādhatte -- #atrocyate--bhavedāvṛtyānarthakyamiti# /
ayamabhisandhiḥ---satyaṃ na brahmasākṣātkāraḥ sākṣādāgamayukttiphalamapi tu yuktyāgamārthajñānāhitasaṃskārasacivaṃ citameva brahmaṇi sākṣātkāravartīṃ buddhivṛttiṃ samādhatte /
sā ca nānumānitavahmisākṣātkāravatprātibhatvenāpramāṇaṃ tadānīṃ vahnisvalakṣaṇasyaparokṣatvātsadātanaṃ tu brahmasvarūpasyopādhirūṣitasya jīvasyāparokṣatvam /
nahi śuddhabuddhatvādayo vastutastato 'tiricyate /
tasmādyathā gāndharvaśāstrārthajñānābhyāsāhitasaṃskāraḥ sacivena śrotreṇa ṣaḍjādisvaragrābhamūrcchanābhedamadhyakṣeṇekṣate evaṃ vedāntārthajñānāhitasaṃskāro jīvasya brahmasvabhāvamantaḥkaraṇeneti /
#yastatvamasīti sakṛduktameveti# /
śrutvā matvā kṣaṇamavadhāya prāgbhavīyābhyāsajātasaṃskārādityarthaḥ /
#yastu na śaknotīti# /
prāgbhavīyabrahmābhyāsarahita ityarthaḥ /
#nahi dṛṣṭe 'nupapannaṃ nāmeti# /
yatra parokṣapratibhāsini vākyārthe 'pi vyaktāvyaktatvatāratamyaṃ tatra mananottarakālamādhyāsanābhyāsanikarṣaprakarṣakramajanmani pratyayapravāhe sākṣātkārāvadhau vyaktitāratamyaṃ prati kaiva katheti bhāvaḥ /
tadevaṃ vākyamātrasyārthe 'pi na drāgityeva pratyaya ityuktam /
tatvamasīti tu vākyamatyantadurgrahapadārthaṃ na padārthajñānapūrvake svārthe jñāne drāgityeva pravartate /
kintu bilambitatamapadārthajñānamativilambenetyāha #---apica tatvamasītyetadvākyaṃ tvaṃpadārthasyeti# /
syādetat padārthasaṃsargātmā vākyārthaḥ padārthajñānakrameṇa tadadhīnanirūpaṇīyatayā kramavatpratītiryujyate /
brahma tu niraṃśatvenāsasṛṣṭanānātvapadarthakamiti kasyānukramema kramavatī pratītiriti sakṛdeva tadgṛhyeta na vā gṛhyatetyuktamityata āha #---yadyapi ca pratipattavya ātmā niraṃśa iti# /
niraṃśo 'pyahamaparokṣo 'pyātmā tattaddehādyāropavyudāsābhyāmaṃśavānivātyantaparokṣa iva /
tataśca vākyārthatayā kramavatpratyaya upapadyate /
tatkiṃmiyameva vākyajanitā pratītirātmani tathāca na sākṣātpratītirātmanyanāgataphalatvādasya ityata āha #---tattu pūrvarūpamevātmapratipatteḥ#sākṣātkāravatyāḥ /
etaduktaṃ bhavati ---vākyārthaśravaṇamananottarakālā viśeṣaṇatrayavatī bhāvanā brahma sākṣātkārāya kalpate iti vākyārthapratītiḥ sākṣātkārasya pūrvarūpamiti /
śaṅkate #--satyamevamiti# /
samāropo hi tatvapratyayenāpodyate na tatvapratyayaḥ /
duḥkhitvādipratyayaścātmani sarveṣāṃ sarvadotpadyata ityabādhitatvātsamīcina iti balavānna śakyo 'panetumityarthaḥ /
nirākaroti #---na /
dehādyabhimānavaditi# /
nahi sarveṣāṃ sarvadotpadyata ityetāvatā tātvikatvam /
dehātmābhimānasyāpi satyatvaprasaṅgātso 'pi sarveṣāṃ sarvadotpadyate /
uktaṃ cāsya tatra tatropapatyā bādhanamevaṃ duḥkhitvādyabhimāno 'pi tathā /
body.translated_text:
Nor does the direct realization of <s>Brahman</s> — which is identical with <s>Brahman</s>'s own Self — destroy <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), because there is no contradiction between [that realization] and <s>avidyā</s>'s continuation.
Or, if there were a contradiction, then — because of [that realization's] eternality — <s>avidyā</s> would never arise; how then could it continue alongside [that realization]?
Therefore, for the removal of <s>avidyā</s>, an adventitious (<s>āgantuka</s>) direct realization must be sought.
And thus, the repetition of cognition is purposeful.
The objector stands by all the previously stated objections: '#Not even with repetition (<s>na āvṛttāv api</s>)#' — thus.
For indeed, the cognition of the meaning of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> [ritual] sentence — even if repeated a hundred times — does not generate direct perceptual knowledge (<s>sākṣātkāra-pramāṇa</s>) in its own domain.
Even [a cognition that has] arisen — being of such a [merely inferential] nature — [lacks authority], because of its unreliable character (<s>vyabhicāritva</s>) and hence its being [mere] intuition (<s>prātibha</s>).
'#The cognition of <s>Brahman</s>'s selfhood (<s>brahmātmatva-pratīti</s>)#' — [means] the direct realization of <s>Brahman</s>'s selfhood.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises another doubt: '#Not merely the sentence [alone]#' — thus.
The objector refutes: '#Even so, the repetition is purposeless#' — thus.
If the sentence, requiring reasoning (<s>yukti</s>), is capable of [producing] direct realization, then — that being the case — repetition is pointless,
because that very [sentence-with-reasoning], having been applied just once with its supporting rationale, accomplishes everything that needs to be accomplished.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises yet another doubt: '#But even so, it might be#' — thus.
Reasoning and the sentence are not [capable of producing] the fruit of direct realization, because direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) alone is the [valid] means of knowledge whose fruit is that [direct realization].
But those [sentence and reasoning] — grasping only [things] remote in nature (<s>parokṣa</s>) — apprehend only the general (<s>sāmānya</s>) [aspect], but do not directly realize the particular (<s>viśeṣa</s>). Hence, for the direct realization of that particular, repetition (<s>āvṛtti</s>) is to be practiced.
For that [repetitive practice] — when cultivated with reverence (<s>satkāra</s>), for a long time, and without interruption — becomes firmly grounded and is capable of [producing] the direct realization of the particular — just as the contemplation of a beloved woman [produces a vivid mental image] for a man infatuated [with her].
The objector says: '#No. Even [with practice] repeated many times (<s>asakṛd api</s>)#' — thus.
For this direct realization must either arise from scripture and reasoning, or from contemplation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) alone.
To begin with, scripture and reasoning — whose fruit is a cognition that appears remote (<s>parokṣābhāsa</s>) — cannot produce [a result of] the nature of direct perceptual knowledge (<s>pratyakṣa-pramāṇa-phala</s>), which is the defining character of direct realization.
For indeed, a <s>vaṭa</s>-sprout does not arise from a <s>kuṭaja</s>-seed.
Nor is the knowledge that arises at the culmination of contemplation — even though it appears direct (<s>aparokṣāvabhāsa</s>) — a [valid] means of knowledge, because of unreliability (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) and the like — this has been stated.
The objector summarizes his position: '#Therefore, if [it is so]#' — thus.
The objector raises another objection: '#And not even when [the sentence] has been applied just once#' — thus.
For a certain [person] of purified <s>sattva</s> — like <s>Vāmadeva</s> while still in the womb — having heard [the teaching], reflected upon it, and having contemplated for a [single] moment, directly experiences the selfhood of the individual soul as <s>Brahman</s>.
Hence, even [further] repetition for him is purposeless.
And moreover, repetition is purposeless because the apprehension or non-apprehension of what is without parts (<s>niraṃśa</s>) is [all-or-nothing] — it is not [amenable to] degrees of clarity and obscurity, like a general [cognition] with a remainder [to be specified], as in [the case of] a ruby or the like — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Moreover, [<s>Brahman</s>] has many aspects (<s>anekāṃśa</s>)#' — thus.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] resolves: '#Here it is said: The purposelessness of repetition would obtain#' — thus.
The intention is this: True, the direct realization of <s>Brahman</s> is not directly the fruit of scripture and reasoning; rather, the mind itself — assisted by the latent impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) deposited by the knowledge of the meaning of scripture and reasoning — assumes a mental modification (<s>buddhivṛtti</s>) that operates as direct realization with respect to <s>Brahman</s>.
And that [modification] is not — like the direct realization of [a fire that is merely] inferred — invalid (<s>apramāṇa</s>) due to [being mere] intuition (<s>prātibha</s>). [For] at that time, [in the case of inferred fire,] the particular nature (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) of fire is [indeed] directly present (<s>aparokṣa</s>). But [in the case of <s>Brahman</s>], it is the eternally-present directness (<s>aparokṣatva</s>) of the Self — which is the <s>jīva</s> [as] conditioned by limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhiruṣita</s>) — of the essential nature of <s>Brahman</s> [that is at stake].
For [qualities such as] being eternally pure, awakened, and the like do not in reality differ from that [Self].
Therefore, just as one who has the latent impressions deposited by the knowledge of the meaning of the science of music (<s>gāndhārva-śāstra</s>), assisted by the ear, perceives directly the distinctions of <s>ṣaḍja</s> and other notes, <s>grāha</s>s, and <s>mūrchanā</s>s — so too one whose latent impressions have been deposited by the knowledge of the meaning of the <s>Vedānta</s> [perceives] the <s>Brahman</s>-nature of the <s>jīva</s> through the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>).
'#He for whom "<s>tat tvam asi</s>" — stated just once#' — thus.
The meaning is: having heard, reflected, and contemplated for a [single] moment — due to the latent impressions generated by practice in previous births.
'#But he who is unable#' — thus.
The meaning is: one who lacks the practice of <s>Brahman</s>-contemplation from previous births.
'#For indeed, nothing that is seen is untenable (<s>nahi dṛṣṭe 'nupapannaṃ nāma</s>)#' — thus.
Where — even in the meaning of the sentence that appears remote (<s>parokṣa</s>) — there are degrees of clarity and obscurity, there — in the stream of cognitions generated by the progressive cultivation of contemplation (<s>ādhyāsanābhyāsa</s>) after reflection, up to the point of direct realization — what question is there about degrees of clarity? — this is the purport.
Thus it has been stated that even for the meaning of the sentence alone, the cognition does not [arise] instantly.
But the sentence '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' — whose word-meanings are extremely difficult to grasp — does not quickly produce knowledge of its own meaning that is preceded by the knowledge of the word-meanings.
Rather, because the word-meanings are most delayed, [the sentence-meaning knowledge arises] with great delay — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Moreover, this sentence "<s>tat tvam asi</s>" — [the meaning of] the word "<s>tvam</s>" (you)#' — thus.
One might say: the sentence-meaning, being constituted by the relation of word-meanings, is [naturally] of sequential cognition because of its dependence on the sequential cognition of word-meanings — this is fitting.
But <s>Brahman</s>, being without parts (<s>niraṃśa</s>) and hence not having a meaning constituted by a plurality of word-meanings, either is grasped all at once — [in which case] it is grasped — or is not grasped — [in which case] why should there be a sequential cognition of it? Hence it should be grasped all at once, or not at all — having said this, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] replies: '#Even though the object to be known — the Self — is without parts#' — thus.
Even though the Self is without parts and directly present (<s>aparokṣa</s>), through the superimposition and removal of various [attributes] such as body and the like, it is as if [it were] with parts and extremely remote.
And thus, the sequential cognition of the sentence-meaning is tenable.
Then what? — is this very cognition generated by the sentence the cognition of the Self? And thus — is there no direct cognition (<s>sākṣāt-pratīti</s>) of the Self as [something] of unattained fruit? — To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#But that is merely the preliminary form (<s>pūrvarūpa</s>) of the cognition of the Self#' — of [the cognition] that possesses direct realization.
What is being said is this: the contemplation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) — endowed with three qualifications [reverence, duration, continuity] — that follows the hearing and reflection on the sentence-meaning, is capable of [producing] the direct realization of <s>Brahman</s>. Hence the cognition of the sentence-meaning is [merely] the preliminary form of direct realization.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises a doubt: '#True, this is so#' — thus.
For superimposition (<s>samāropa</s>) is removed by the cognition of reality — [but] the cognition of reality [itself] is not [removed by anything].
And the cognition of suffering and the like arises in the Self for everyone at all times — hence, being unsublated (<s>abādhita</s>), it is correct and [therefore] strong, and cannot be removed — this is the meaning.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes: '#No. Just as the identification with the body and the like (<s>dehādyabhimānavat</s>)#' — thus.
For it is not the case that [a cognition's] arising for everyone at all times [makes it] ultimately real.
Because the identification of the body with the Self (<s>dehātmābhimāna</s>) would then absurdly become ultimately real — for it too arises for everyone at all times.
And its sublation (<s>bādhana</s>) by reasoning has been stated in various places — similarly, the identification with suffering and the like [is also sublated].

body.translated_text:
For of the Self — whose nature is eternally pure and awakened — suffering, grief, and the like, which have the character of arising and perishing, cannot belong to the Self.
Nor are they attributes [of the Self], because of the impossibility of their being attributes of [entities] that are entirely different from it. For indeed, a cow is not an attribute of a horse. And because the [supposed] connection [between them] too is unable to withstand scrutiny — [whether that connection be examined] through separateness and non-separateness, or through the presence and absence of the connection [itself].
And because difference and non-difference — being mutually contradictory — cannot coexist in a single [entity].
All this has been presented in the second <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter).
This is what is stated: '#Just as [what is] perceived as external to consciousness — like the body and the like#' — thus.
And moreover, the [attributes of] suffering and the like do not have identity [with the Self] — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#And in deep sleep and the like#' — thus.
One might say: Why is the acceptance of repetition specifically for the purpose of experience [i.e., direct realization]? — since '<s>draṣṭavyaḥ</s>' (is to be seen), '<s>śrotavyaḥ</s>' (is to be heard), and the like enjoin repetition pertaining to a subject-matter other than the meaning of the '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' sentence — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Moreover, not [a subject-matter] other than the meaning of the "<s>tat tvam asi</s>" sentence#' — thus.
'The Self is indeed to be seen (<s>ātmā vā are draṣṭavyaḥ</s>)' and the like enjoin seeing (<s>darśana</s>) pertaining to the Self.
And no seeing of the Self other than the meaning of the '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' sentence is taught [in the <s>Upaniṣad</s>s].
That by which [a passage] is introduced (<s>upakramyate</s>) and by which it is concluded (<s>upasaṃhriyate</s>) — that is the sentence-meaning.
Having introduced with '<s>sad eva somyedam</s>' ('Being alone, O dear one, was this') and concluded with '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' — that alone is the sentence-meaning.
Therefore, one who, wishing to prescribe repetition elsewhere [i.e., for another subject-matter], obstructs the principal [teaching] by means of the subsidiary.
For the groom — being the one intended by the [marriage] ritual — is the principal, [i.e.,] the recipient (<s>saṃpradāna</s>).
Him they do not obstruct by the subsidiary, namely the ritual of marriage.
Objection: But since the <s>Vedānta</s> sentence is primarily injunctive (<s>vidhipradhāna</s>), it does not have the existing reality (<s>bhūtārtha</s>) as its primary [purport]; rather, the existing reality is conveyed as subsidiary to that [injunction].
As they say, expounding the <s>Śābara</s> statement: 'The injunction (<s>codanā</s>) indeed [conveys] what exists, what is present' — 'The injunction, while conveying the action to be performed (<s>kārya</s>), conveys the existing reality and the like as subsidiary to that [action]' — anticipating this objection, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#And for one who is engaged in this [practice], [the understanding] "I am the eligible person"#' — thus.
To begin with, that the <s>Vedānta</s>s culminate in existing reality (<s>bhūtārtha</s>) and are not directed toward the injunction of action — this has been demonstrated in '<s>tattu samanvayāt</s>' ('But that, because of the coherence [of the <s>Vedānta</s> texts]')

children.translated_text: [stated] there.

On the contrary, if [the <s>Vedānta</s> sentences] were directed toward injunction, they would produce a cognition that is opposed to liberation — and hence would themselves be an obstacle to liberation — [so] only this excess [of absurdity] has been stated here.
