body.translated_text:
'#They accept [it] as the Self, and they teach [it as such]#.'
Even though the <s>Śruti</s>s such as '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' and the like teach the <s>Paramātman</s>-hood of the individual in <s>saṃsāra</s>, nevertheless — since the definite ascertainment of their duality [is established] through their conjunction with contradictory attributes such as being-free-from-evil (<s>apahatapāpmatva</s>) and not-being-free-from-evil — and since the <s>Śruti</s>s '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' and the like can also be explained as <s>pratīka-upadeśa</s> (instruction on symbols), just like 'the mind is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>mano brahma</s>), 'the sun is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>ādityo brahma</s>), and the like — this [teaching] is merely a <s>pratīka-upadeśa</s> (instruction on a symbol).
Nor is it correct [to argue] that — just as when serpent-hood superimposed [on a rope] is restated (<s>anūdya</s>) and rope-hood is prescribed for the object present before one — so too, having restated the <s>jīva</s>-hood of the self-luminous [consciousness], <s>Paramātman</s>-hood is prescribed.
For superimposition of a different particular [identity] is reasonable with regard to a present object that has been apprehended in a general form but whose particular [nature] has not been grasped.
But here, for the self-luminous [consciousness] — which is a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) without qualification, and whose luminosity is self-dependent — there is nothing ungrasped in its form. Hence, in the non-grasping of what particular could what other particular be superimposed?
Therefore, since the superimposition of <s>jīva</s>-hood upon <s>Brahman</s> is impossible, the <s>jīva</s> is [merely] a <s>jīva</s> and <s>Brahman</s> is [merely] <s>Brahman</s> — thus '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' is merely a <s>pratīka-upadeśa</s> — this is the prima facie view.
With this prima facie view established, the reply is given: It is <s>Śvetaketu</s>'s own Self that is to be known as the supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>) — not a <s>Parameśvara</s> distinct from <s>Śvetaketu</s>.
For if [they were] different, there would be the consequence of figurative usage (<s>gauṇatva</s>) — and figurative usage is not appropriate when the primary meaning is possible.
Moreover, in a <s>pratīka-upadeśa</s>, a single statement [suffices]; but [here] the censure of the [dualistic] view of difference is perceived.
For in repetitive [teaching], there is an abundance of meaning — not a paucity. [A paucity would make the identification] extremely far-fetched as figurative.
Therefore, from examining the sequential context (<s>paurvāparyalocanā</s>), the <s>Śruti</s> is perceived as directed toward [the teaching that] the <s>Paramātman</s>-hood of the <s>jīva</s> is real (<s>vāstavī</s>).
[One might object:] because of the conflict with other means of knowledge, the <s>Śruti</s> lacks authority here.
But there is no conflict with other means of knowledge — all this has been demonstrated in the first <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter).
Moreover, even for the [Self] that is without parts (<s>niraṃśa</s>), because of the superimposition of the manifold phenomenal world (<s>prapañca</s>) — constituted by beginningless, indescribable <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and its various impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) — the [Self] is as if with parts. And because of the non-grasping of some aspect, there is as if a delusion (<s>vibhrama</s>). But in ultimate reality, there is no such thing as delusion, nor is there such a thing as <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration).

natu tatvamasītyādāvahaṅkārāspadamupāsyamavagamyate /
kintu sarpatvānuvādena rajjutatvaśjñāpana ivāhaṅkārāspadasyāvacchinnasya pravilayo 'vagamyate /
kimato yadyevam /
etadato.bhavati---pradhānībhūtānāṃ na pratīkānāmucchedo yukto naca taducchede vidheyasyāpyupapattiriti /

children.translated_text: Moreover: '#and because the self-nature of <s>Brahman</s> is [already established]#.'

children.text: nahyupāsanavidhānāni jīvātmano brahmasvabhāvapratipādanaparaistatvamasyādisaṃdarbhairekavākyabhāvamāpadyante yena tadekavākyatayā brahmadṛṣṭyupadeśeṣvātmadṛṣṭiḥ kalpeta bhinnaprakaraṇatvāt. tathāca tatra yathālokapratītivyavasthito jīvaḥ kartā bhoktā ca saṃsārī na brahmeti kathaṃ tasya brahmātmatayābrahmadṛṣṭyupadeśeṣvātmadṛṣṭirupadiśyatetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
For the injunctions of meditation do not enter into single-sentence-hood with the passages like '<s>tattvamasi</s>' ('You are That') and the like, which are directed toward establishing the <s>Brahman</s>-nature of the <s>jīvātman</s> (individual self) — because they belong to different contexts. Therefore, it cannot be that by such single-sentence-hood the self-view (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>) would be constructed in the instructions of <s>Brahman</s>-view.
And thus, therein, the <s>jīva</s> — as established through ordinary worldly cognition — is an agent, an experiencer, and a transmigrator, not <s>Brahman</s>. How then would the self-view be taught for him in the instructions of <s>Brahman</s>-view? — this is the meaning.
'#And therefore, because of the equality of the meditator with the <s>pratīka</s>s#.'

children.text: yadyapyupāsako jīvātmā na brahmavikāraḥ, pratīkāni tu manaḥprabhṛtīnibrahmavikārastathāpyavacchinnatayā jīvātmanaḥ pratīkaiḥ sāmyaṃ dṛṣṭavyam //4 //
children.translated_text: Even though the meditating <s>jīvātman</s> (individual self) is not a transformation of <s>Brahman</s>, while the <s>pratīka</s>s — mind and the like — are indeed transformations of <s>Brahman</s>, nevertheless, the equality of the <s>jīvātman</s> with the <s>pratīka</s>s should be understood in terms of [their shared] delimited nature. //4//

body.translated_text:
'#Not in a <s>pratīka</s> (symbol), for it is not that [self]#.'
Just as the pure <s>Brahman</s> whose nature is liberation, as stated in the <s>śāstra</s>, is meditated upon by the <s>jīva</s> (individual self) as its very self — 'I am <s>Brahman</s>,' 'You are That, O <s>Śvetaketu</s>' and the like — for the reason that the <s>jīvātman</s> (individual self) is truly of the nature of <s>Brahman</s>, and because of the <s>Śruti</s> declaring non-duality;
and just as the <s>jīvātman</s> is, as it were, a reflection of <s>Brahman</s> in the mirror of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — so wherever the instruction of viewing [things] as <s>Brahman</s> is given, as in 'the mind is <s>Brahman</s>,' 'the sun is <s>Brahman</s>' and the like — everywhere one should think 'I am the mind' and the like, [seeing] the primary selfhood of <s>Brahman</s> [in these].
And the identity of mind and the like with <s>Brahman</s> is justified through their being transformations (<s>vikāra</s>) of <s>Brahman</s>,
just as pots, lids, water-pots, and the like, being transformations of clay, are of the nature of clay.
And thus, since in such <s>pratīka</s>-instructions (instructions regarding symbols), the dissolution of a certain transformation is occasionally understood, [these instructions] have their purport in the dissolution of the entire phenomenal diversity — this being the prima facie conclusion, it is stated:
To begin with, just as through 'I am <s>Brahman</s>' and the like, the selfhood of <s>Brahman</s> is taught for the locus of the ego-sense (<s>ahaṅkārāspada</s>), it is not the case that through 'the mind is <s>Brahman</s>' and the like, the locus of the ego-sense is [taught] for mind and the like; rather, [what is taught is] that these are to be meditated upon as <s>Brahman</s>.
Objection: Since the locus of the ego-sense is of the nature of <s>Brahman</s>, in mind and the like — which are to be meditated upon as <s>Brahman</s> — one should also meditate on them as the locus of the ego-sense.
No.
Because in such [passages] the word 'I' (<s>aham</s>) is not heard.
But if [one argues that] by treating the locus of the ego-sense as having <s>Brahman</s>-nature, the meditation of other transformations of that [<s>Brahman</s>] too — such as space (<s>ākāśa</s>) and the like — as the locus of the ego-sense would follow, just as in the case of its reflection.
Therefore, whatever is prescribed to be meditated upon as having merely that [particular thing's] selfhood — that should be understood as having merely that selfhood, by the principle 'the verbal instruction extends exactly as far as the statement goes.'
Nothing more should be supplied — because of the absurd consequence of over-extension.
Nor is the dissolution of the entire phenomenal world the purpose of every class of sentences.
For if that were the purpose, the mention of mind as the <s>pratīka</s> (symbol) would be meaningless — [instead] one should say '<s>viśvam</s>' (the universe), as in 'all this is indeed <s>Brahman</s>.'
Nor is it fitting that the mention of 'mind' serves to indicate the totality [of things].
Because when a primary meaning is possible, figurative usage (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) is inappropriate.
And because [otherwise] there would be the absurd consequence that 'the sun is <s>Brahman</s>' and the like would be purposeless.
'#For the meditator [does not identify himself with] the <s>pratīka</s>s#.'
Either from experience or from <s>Śruti</s>, there is no apprehension of mind and the like — the <s>pratīka</s>s — as one's self — and neither of these two [bases] exists — this is the meaning.
'#Because of the absurd consequence of the non-existence of the <s>pratīka</s>s#.'
Objection: Just as the delimited locus of the ego-sense [realizes its identity with] the undelimited <s>Brahman</s>, resulting in the annihilation [of its limited nature], so too will it be for the <s>pratīka</s>s — to this he says: '#and in the annihilation of the own-nature of names and the like#.'
For here the <s>pratīka</s>s are intended as principal — as objects to be meditated upon through identification with the locus of the ego-sense.
But in '<s>tattvamasi</s>' ('You are That') and the like, the locus of the ego-sense is not apprehended as an object of meditation.
Rather, just as in [the case of] illuminating the rope-nature by restating the serpent-nature, the dissolution of the delimited locus of the ego-sense is understood.
What follows if this is so?
This follows: the annihilation of the <s>pratīka</s>s, which have become principal, is not appropriate; nor, if they are annihilated, is the tenable establishment of what is to be enjoined [possible].

body.text:
#brahmadṛṣṭirutkarṣāt# /
yadyapi sāmānādhikaraṇmubhayathāpi ghaṭate tathāpi brahmaṇaḥ sarvādhyakṣatayā phalaprasavasāmarthyena phalavatvātprādhānyena tadevādityādidṛṣṭibhiḥ saṃskartavyamityādityādidṛṣṭayo brahmaṇyeva kartavyā na tu brahmadṛṣṭirādityādiṣu /
na caivaṃvidhe 'vadhṛte śāstrārthe nikṛṣṭadṛṣṭinorkṛṣṭa iti laukiko nyāyo 'pavādāya prabhavatyāgamavirodhena tasyaivāpoditatvāditi pūrvapakṣasaṃkṣepaḥ /
satyaṃ sarvādhyakṣatayā phalādātṛtvena brahmaṇa eva sarvatra vāstavaṃ prādhānyaṃ tathāpi śabdagatyanurodhena kvacitkarmaṇa eva prādhānyamavasūyate /
yathā 'darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajeta svargakāmaḥ', 'citrayā yajeta paśukāmaḥ' ityādau /
atra hi sarvatra yāgādyārādhitā devataiva phalaṃ prayacchatīti sthāpitaṃ tathāpi śabdataḥ karmaṇaḥ karaṇatvāvagamane phalavatvapratūte- prādhānyam /
kvacidravyasya yathā vrīhīnprokṣatītyādau /
taduktaṃ ----'yaistu dravyaṃ saṃcikīrṣyate guṇastatra pratīyate' iti /
tadiha yadyapi sarvādhyakṣatayā vastuto brahmaiva phalaṃ prayacchati tathāpi śāstraṃ brahmabuddhyā'dityādau pratika upāsyamāne brahma phalāya kalpate ityabhivadati kiṃvādityādibuddhyā brahmaiva viṣayīkṛtaṃ palāyetyubhayathāpi brahmaṇaḥ sarvādhyakṣasya phaladānopapatteḥ śāstrārthasaṃdehe lokānusārato niścīyate /
tadidamuktam-- #nirdhārite śāstrārtha etadevaṃ syāditi# /
na kevalaṃ laukiko nyāyo niścaye heturapi tu ādityādiśabdānāṃ prāthamyena mukhyārthatvamapītyāha #---prāthamyācceti# /
iti paratvamapi brahmaśabdasyāmumeva nyāyamavagamayati /
tathāhi ----svaravṛtyā ādityādiśabdā yathā svārthe vartante tathā brahmaśabdo 'pi svārthe vartsyati yadi svārtho 'sya vapavakṣitaḥsyāt /
tathācetiparatvamanarthakaṃ tasmāditinā svārthātpracyāvya brahmapadaṃ jñānaparaṃ svarūpaparaṃ vā kartavyam /
naca brahmapadamādityādipadārtha iti ,pratūtipara evāyamitiparaḥśabdo yathā gauriti me gavayo 'bhavaditi /
body.translated_text:
'#The <s>Brahman</s>-view [is to be superimposed on the symbols], because of [<s>Brahman</s>'s] superiority#.'
Although co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) works both ways, nevertheless — because <s>Brahman</s>, being the superintendent of all, has the capacity to bestow fruits and is thus fruitful — it is that [<s>Brahman</s>] primarily that should be refined through the views of the sun and the like; hence the sun-views and the like should be superimposed on <s>Brahman</s> alone, not the <s>Brahman</s>-view on the sun and the like.
Nor, when the scriptural meaning has been thus determined, can the worldly maxim 'the inferior [is superimposed] on the superior' serve as an objection — because of the conflict with scripture, and because that [maxim] itself has been refuted [in the case of conflict with scripture] — this is the summary of the prima facie view.
True, because of [<s>Brahman</s>'s] being the superintendent of all and bestower of fruits, the real preeminence (<s>prādhānya</s>) everywhere belongs to <s>Brahman</s> alone; nevertheless, in conformity with the force of the words, sometimes the preeminence of <s>karma</s> (ritual action) alone is ascertained.
Just as in 'One who desires heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>,' 'One who desires cattle should sacrifice with the <s>Citrā</s>' and the like.
For in all these cases it has been established that the deity — propitiated through sacrifice and the like — alone bestows the fruit; nevertheless, since from the words [of the <s>Śruti</s>] <s>karma</s> is understood as the instrument, [and since] the fruitfulness [of <s>karma</s>] is understood [from the injunctive form] — [<s>karma</s> has] preeminence.
Sometimes it is the substance (<s>dravya</s>) [that has preeminence], as in 'He sprinkles the rice-grains' and the like.
Thus it has been said: 'But for those who wish to specify the substance, the quality (<s>guṇa</s>) is understood therein.'
So here too, even though — because of [<s>Brahman</s>'s] being the superintendent of all — it is truly <s>Brahman</s> alone that bestows the fruit, nevertheless the scripture declares that when the <s>pratīka</s> (symbol) — the sun and the like — is meditated upon with <s>Brahman</s>-view, <s>Brahman</s> produces the fruit; or [alternatively], when <s>Brahman</s> itself is made the object through the sun-view and the like, [<s>Brahman</s>] produces the fruit — since in both ways the bestowal of fruit by <s>Brahman</s>, the superintendent of all, is tenable, when there is doubt about the meaning of scripture, it is determined in accordance with worldly [usage].
This is what was stated: '#When the meaning of scripture has been determined, this alone would be so#.'
Not only is the worldly maxim a reason for determination, but also the primacy of the sun and the like [words] having their primary meaning — he says: '#and because of the primacy#.'
The [word] '<s>iti</s>' being posterior [i.e., appended to '<s>brahma</s>'] also conveys this very maxim.
For just as by their natural force (<s>svaravṛtti</s>) the words 'sun' and the like denote their own objects, so too the word '<s>Brahman</s>' will denote its own object — if its own meaning were not displaced [by the construction].
And thus, the [word] '<s>iti</s>' being posterior would be purposeless. Therefore, by means of '<s>iti</s>,' displacing the word '<s>Brahman</s>' from its own meaning, it should be made to refer to knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) or to its own nature [as predicate].
And the word '<s>Brahman</s>' does not mean the referent of the word 'sun' and the like — rather, the [word] '<s>iti</s>' being posterior has its purport in [establishing] a particular cognition, just as in 'The <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) was like a cow to me.'

body.text: tathāca ādityādayo brahmeti pratipattavyā ityartho bhavatītyāha--- #itiparatvādapi brahmaśabdasyeti# /

children.translated_text: The rest has transparent meaning. //5//

body.translated_text: And thus the meaning is: 'The sun and the like are to be cognized as <s>Brahman</s>' — he says: '#because of the word "<s>Brahman</s>" being posterior to "<s>iti</s>"#.'

children.translated_text: '#And the sun-views and the like are subsidiaries [of ritual], because of [their] tenability [as such]#.'
'#Or alternatively, the <s>Udgītha</s>-views and the like would necessarily be superimposed on the sun and the like#.'

children.text: satsvapi ādityādiṣu phalānutpādādutpattimataḥ karmaṇa eva phaladarśanātkarmaiva phalavat /
children.translated_text: Even though the sun and the like exist [as objects], since the fruit does not arise [from them alone], and since the fruit is observed only from <s>karma</s> (ritual action) which possesses the capacity to produce [fruit] — <s>karma</s> alone is fruitful.

And thus, if the sun-views and the like were to take <s>karma</s> in the form of the <s>Udgītha</s> and the like as their object, then [those <s>karma</s>-forms] would be overpowered by the sun-views and the like.

body.text:
evañca karmarūpeṣvasatkalpeṣu kutaḥ phalamutpadyeta /
ādityadiṣu punarudgīthādidṛṣṭāvudgīthādibudyopāsyamānā ādityādayaḥ karmātmakaḥsantaḥ phalāya kalpiṣyanta iti /
ata eva ca pṛthvyagnyorṛksāmaśabdaprayoga upapanno yataḥ pṛthvyāmṛgdṛṣṭiradhyastāgnau ca sāmadṛṣṭiḥ /
sāmni punaragnidṛṣṭau ṛci ca pṛthvīdṛṣṭau viparītaṃ bhavet /
tasmādapyetadeva yuktamityāha--- #tathācāyameveti# /
upapattyantaramāha--- #apica lokeṣviti# /
evaṃ khalvadhikaraṇanirdeśo viṣayatvapratipādanapara upapadyate yadi lokeṣu sāmadṛṣṭiradhyasyeta nālyatheti /
pūrvādhikaraṇarāddhantopapattimatraivārthe brūte--- #prathamanirdiṣṭeṣu ceti# /
siddhāntamatra prakramate--- #ādityādimataya eveti# /
yadyudgīthādimataya ādityādiṣukṣipyeraṃstata ādityādīnāṃsvayamakāryatvādudgīthādimatestatra vaiyarthyaṃ prasajyeta /
nahyādityādibhiḥ kiñcitkriyate yadvidyayā viryavattaraṃ bhavatītyādityamatīnāmupapadyate udgīthādiṣu saṃskārakatvenopayogaḥ /
codayati--- #bhavatu karmasamṛddhiphaleṣvevamiti# /
yatra hi karmaṇa- phalaṃ tatraivaṃ bhavatu yatra tu guṇātaphalaṃ tatra guṇasya siddhatvenākāryatvātkarotītyeva nāstītyatra vidyāyāḥ kva upayoga ityarthaḥ /
pariharati--- #teṣvapīti# /
na tāvadguṇaḥ siddhasvabhāvaḥ kāryāya phalāya paryāptaḥ, mā bhūtprakṛtakarmāniveśino yatkiñcitphalotpādaḥ, tasmātprakṛtāpūrvasaṃniveśinaḥ phalotpāda iti tasya kriyamāṇatvena vidyayā vīryavattaratvopapattiriti /
#phalātmakatvāccādityādīnāmiti# /
yadyapi brahmavikāratvenādityodgīthayoraviśeṣastathāpi phalātmakatvenādityādīnāmastyudgīthā dibhyo viśeṣa ityarthaḥ /
dvitīyanirdeśādapyudgīthādīnāṃ prādhānyamityāha--- #api comitīti# /
svayamevopāsanasya karmatvātphalavatvopapatteḥ /
nanūktaṃ siddharūpairādityādibhiradhyastaiḥ sādhyabūtatvamabhibhūtaṅkarmaṇāmityata āha--- #ādityādibhāvenāpi ca dṛśyamānānāmiti# /
bhavedetavaṃ yadyadyāsena kramarūpamabhibhūyeta /
api tu māṇavaka ivāgnidṛṣṭiḥ kenacittīvratvādinā guṇena gauṇyanabhibhūtamāṇavakatvāttathehāpi /
nahīyaṃ śuktikāyāṃ rajatadhīriva vahnidhīryena māṇavakattvamabhibhavet /
kintu gauṇī /
tatheyamapyudgīthādāvādityadṛṣṭirgauṇīti bhāvaḥ /
#tadetasyāmṛcyadhyūḍhaṃsāmeti tviti# /
anyathāpi lakṣaṇopapattau na ṛksāmetyadhyāsakalpanā pṛthvyagnayorityarthaḥ /
akṣaranyāsālocanayā tu vaniparītamevetyāha--- #iyamevargiti# /
'lokeṣupañcavidhaṃ sāmopāsīta' iti dvitīyānirdeśātsāmnāmupasyatvamavagamyate /
tatra yadi sāmadhīradhyasyeta tato na sāmānyupāsyeran api tu lokāḥ pṛthivyādayaḥ /
tathā ca dvitīyārthaṃ parityajya tṛtīyārthaḥ parikalpayeta sāmneti /
lokeṣviti saptamī dvitīyārtheṃ kathañcinnīyate /
akāre gāvo vāsyantāṃ prāvāre kusumānītivat tenoktanyānurodhena saptamyāścobhayathāpyavaśyaṃ kalpanīyārthatvādvaraṃ yathāśrutadvitīyārthānurodhāya tṛtīyārthe saptamī vyākhyātavyā /
lokapṛthvyādibuddhyā pañcavidhaṃ hiṅaraprastāvoṅkārodgīthapratihāropadravanidhanaprakāraṃ sāmopāsīteti nirṇīyate /
nanu yatrobhayatrāpi dvitīyānirdeśo yathā khalvamumevādityaṃ saptavidhaṃ hiṅkāraprastāvoṅkārodgīthapratīhāropadravanidhanaprakāraṃ sāmopāsīteti, tatra ko vinigamanāyāṃ heturityata āha #---tatrāpīti# /

children.text: tatrāpi samastasya saptavidhasya sāmna upāsanamiti sāmna upāsyatvaśruteḥ sādhviti pañcavidhasya /
children.translated_text: Even there, since the meditation is on the entire sevenfold <s>Sāman</s>, from the <s>Śruti</s> teaching the object-hood of the <s>Sāman</s>, it is good that [the same applies] to the fivefold [<s>Sāman</s>].
And the 'goodness' (<s>sādhutva</s>) of this is [its being in accordance with] <s>dharma</s>.
And thus the <s>Śruti</s>: 'One who acts well becomes good.'

children.text: hiṅkārānuvādena pṛthivīdṛṣṭividhāne hiṅkāraḥ pṛthivīti prāpte viparītanirdeśaḥ pṛthivī hiṅkāraḥ //6 //
children.translated_text: When the injunction of the earth-perception is made through the restatement of <s>Hiṅkāra</s> — [although] '<s>Hiṅkāra</s> is earth' is what is expected — the reverse indication is [given]: 'Earth is the <s>Hiṅkāra</s>.' //6//

body.translated_text:
And thus, when <s>karma</s>s — [which are the real entities here] — are [merely] imagined [in the form of objects like <s>Āditya</s>], how would a fruit be produced [from them]?
But when in <s>Āditya</s> and the like, the perception of <s>Udgītha</s> and the like is [superimposed], then <s>Āditya</s> and the like — being meditated upon through the cognition of <s>Udgītha</s> and the like — being of the nature of <s>karma</s> (ritual action), will be postulated as [productive] of fruit.
And for this very reason, the use of the words '<s>ṛc</s>' and '<s>Sāman</s>' for earth and fire [respectively] is justified — because the perception of <s>ṛc</s> is superimposed on earth, and the perception of <s>Sāman</s> is superimposed on fire.
But if the perception of fire were [superimposed] on <s>Sāman</s>, and the perception of earth on <s>ṛc</s>, the reverse would occur.
Therefore, from this too, this alone is fitting — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#And thus, this very [conclusion]#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states another argument: '#Moreover, in the worlds#.'
Thus indeed, the indication of the topic (<s>adhikaraṇanirdeśa</s>) — which is directed toward establishing the object-hood [of <s>Āditya</s> etc.] — is justified only if the perception of <s>Sāman</s> is superimposed on the worlds, and not otherwise.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the tenability of the established conclusion of the prior <s>adhikaraṇa</s> even in this very meaning: '#And in the things first indicated#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] commences the <s>siddhānta</s> here: '#The views of <s>Āditya</s> and the like alone#.'
If the views of <s>Udgītha</s> and the like were cast into <s>Āditya</s> and the like, then — since <s>Āditya</s> and the like do not produce anything by themselves — the view of <s>Udgītha</s> and the like there would be purposeless.
For <s>Āditya</s> and the like do not do anything that would become more powerful through <s>vidyā</s> — hence the use of the <s>Āditya</s>-views as refiners (<s>saṃskārakatva</s>) in <s>Udgītha</s> and the like is justified.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises an objection: '#Let it be so in the case of fruits accomplished by <s>karma</s>#.'
Where the fruit [comes] from <s>karma</s>, there let it be so; but where the fruit [comes] from the subsidiary (<s>guṇa</s>), there — since the subsidiary is already established [and] not something to be accomplished — [the expression] 'makes' does not apply — so where is the use of <s>vidyā</s>? — this is the meaning.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] resolves: '#Even in those#.'
To begin with, the subsidiary in its established nature is not sufficient for the effect, the fruit — lest any random fruit be produced without the participation of the model (<s>prakṛta</s>) <s>karma</s>. Therefore, the production of the fruit belongs to [the subsidiary] as participating in the model <s>apūrva</s> (unseen potency) — and since it is [thereby] being 'made' [effective], the tenability of being made more powerful through <s>vidyā</s> [holds].
'#And because <s>Āditya</s> and the like are of the nature of fruit#.'
Although, being modifications of <s>Brahman</s>, there is no distinction between <s>Āditya</s> and <s>Udgītha</s>, nevertheless, in their being of the nature of fruit, <s>Āditya</s> and the like are distinct from <s>Udgītha</s> and the like — this is the meaning.
From the second [case] indication too, the primacy of <s>Udgītha</s> and the like [is established] — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Moreover, from the word "<s>api ca</s>"#.'
Because meditation (<s>upāsanā</s>) is itself <s>karma</s> (action), and hence the tenability of its being fruit-bearing.
Objection: It was said that by being superimposed on <s>Āditya</s> and the like — which are of established form — the to-be-accomplished nature of <s>karma</s>s is overwhelmed — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Even though seen as having the nature of <s>Āditya</s> and the like#.'
This would be so if the actual [ritual] form were overwhelmed by the superimposition.
But [it is] rather like the perception of fire in a young boy (<s>māṇavaka</s>) — [where] the boy-hood is not overwhelmed because of some quality such as intensity and the like, and [the fire-perception] is figurative (<s>gauṇī</s>); similarly here too.
For this is not like the cognition of silver in mother-of-pearl, or like the cognition of fire [erroneously perceived], where the boy-hood would be overwhelmed.
Rather, [it is] figurative (<s>gauṇī</s>).
Similarly, this perception of <s>Āditya</s> and the like in <s>Udgītha</s> and the like is figurative — this is the import.
'#That this [perception of <s>Sāman</s>] is superimposed on this <s>ṛc</s>#.'
Even when the figurative usage is tenable through another analysis, there should be no postulation of superimposition [of the form] '<s>ṛc</s> and <s>Sāman</s>' upon earth and fire — this is the meaning.
But when examining the placement of syllables, [the result] is the reverse indeed — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#This very one is the <s>ṛc</s>#.'
From the second [case] indication in 'In the worlds, one should meditate on the fivefold <s>Sāman</s>,' the object-hood of the <s>Sāman</s>s [in relation to meditation] is understood.
Therein, if the perception of <s>Sāman</s> were superimposed [on the worlds], then the <s>Sāman</s>s would not be what is meditated upon; rather, the worlds — earth and the like — would be.
And thus, abandoning the accusative meaning, the instrumental meaning would be postulated — 'by means of <s>Sāman</s>.'
The locative in 'in the worlds' (<s>lokeṣu</s>) is somehow led to the accusative meaning.
Just as 'Let the cows be tied up in the enclosure; let the flowers be gathered in the shawl' — thus, in conformity with [<s>Śaṅkara</s>'s] stated analysis, since the locative must in any case be postulated as having a different meaning in both interpretations, it is better that the locative be explained in the instrumental sense, in conformity with the accusative meaning as directly heard.
It is determined that: with the cognition of the worlds — earth and the like — one should meditate on the fivefold <s>Sāman</s> in its aspects of <s>Hiṅkāra</s>, <s>Prastāva</s>, <s>Oṃkāra</s>, <s>Udgītha</s>, <s>Pratihāra</s>, <s>Upadrava</s>, and <s>Nidhana</s>.
Objection: But where there is a second [case] indication in both [texts] — as in 'One should meditate on that very <s>Āditya</s> as the sevenfold <s>Sāman</s>, in its aspects of <s>Hiṅkāra</s>, <s>Prastāva</s>, <s>Oṃkāra</s>, <s>Udgītha</s>, <s>Pratihāra</s>, <s>Upadrava</s>, and <s>Nidhana</s>' — there, what is the reason for determination? — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Even there#.'

body.text:
#āsīnaḥ saṃbhavāt# /
karmāṅgasaṃmandhiṣu yatra hi tiṣṭhataḥ karma coditaḥ tatra tatsaṃbaddhopāsānāni tiṣṭhataiva kratavyā /
yatra tvāsīnasya tatrapāsanāpyāsīnenaiveti /
nāpi samyagdarśane vastutantratvātpramāṇatantratvāñca /
pramāṇatantrā ca vastuvyavasthā pramāṇaṃ ca .....nāpekṣata iti tatrāpyaniyamaḥ(?) /
yanmahatā prayatnena vinopāsitumaśakyaṃ yathā pratīkādi , yathā vā samyagdarśanamapi tatvamasyādi,tatraiṣā cintā /
tatra codakaśāstrābhāvādaniyame prāpte yathā śakāyata ityupabhandhādāsīnasyaiva siddham /
nanu yasyāmavasthāyāṃ dhyāyatirupacariyate prayujyate kimasau tadā tiṣṭhato na bhavati na bhavatītyāha /
āsīnaścāvidyamānāyāso bhavatīti /
atirohitārthamitarat //7 // //8 // //9 // //10 //
body.translated_text:
'#[One should meditate] while sitting, because of the possibility#.'
Regarding meditations connected with ritual subsidiaries — where one is enjoined to perform the ritual while standing, there the meditations connected with that [ritual] too should be performed while standing alone.
But where [the ritual is performed] while sitting, the meditation too [should be performed] by one who is sitting.
Nor [is there restriction] in the case of right knowledge (<s>samyagdarśana</s>), because it depends on the reality (<s>vastutantra</s>) and on the means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇatantra</s>).
And the determination of reality depends on the means of knowledge; and the means of knowledge does not depend on [posture] — hence there too there is no restriction.
Regarding what cannot be meditated upon without great effort — such as a <s>pratīka</s> (symbolic meditation) and the like, or even right knowledge [of sentences] such as '<s>tattvamasi</s>' ('You are That') and the like — here this deliberation [applies].
Therein, when non-restriction is arrived at due to the absence of an enjoining scripture, from the qualifying clause 'as one is able,' [the conclusion] is established for one who is sitting alone.
Objection: In whichever state one meditates — being addressed [by the injunction] and engaged [in the practice] — could that [meditation] not also occur while standing? — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says:
And one who is sitting is free from fatigue.
The rest has transparent meaning. //7// //8// //9// //10//

body.text:
#yatraikāgratātatrāviśeṣāt# /
same śucau śarkarāvahnivālukāvivarjita ityādivacanānniyame siddhe digdeśādiniyamamavācanikamapi prācīnapravaṇe vaiśvadevena yajetetivadvaidikārambhasāmānyātkvacitkaścitadāśaṅkate /

children.translated_text: The teacher, out of friendly compassion, then states this:
Wherever the mind achieves concentration, there alone should one engage the cultivation [of meditation].
Because of non-distinction.
For here there is no specific scriptural statement, as in the case of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> and the like — therefore. //11//

body.translated_text:
'#Wherever there is concentration (<s>ekāgratā</s>), there — because of non-distinction#.'
When the restriction [of place] is established from the statement 'On even, clean [ground], free from gravel, fire, and sand' and the like, someone — from the general similarity with Vedic undertakings [such as] 'One should sacrifice the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> facing east on a slope' — suspects a restriction of direction, place, and the like, even though unscriptural.

body.text:
#ā prāyaṇāttatrāpi hi dṛṣṭam# /
adhikaraṇaviṣayaṃ vivecayati -- #tatra yāni tāvaditi# /
avidyamānaniyojyā yā brahmātmapratipattistasyāḥ /
śāstraṃ hi niyojyasya kāryarūpaniyegasaṃbandhamavabodhayati tasyaiva karmaṇyaiśvaryalakṣaṇamadhikāraṃ taccaitadubhayamatīndriyatvādbhavati śāstralakṣaṇaṃ pramāṇāntarāprāpye śāstrasyārthavattvādbrahmatvapratītestu jīvanmuktena dṛṣṭatvānnāstīha tirohitamiva kiñcaneti kimatra śāstraṃ kariṣyati /
nanvevamapyabhyudayaphalānyupāsanāni tatra niyoganiyojyalakṣaṇasya ca kramaṇi svāmitālakṣaṇasya ca saṃbandhasyātīndritvāttatra sakṛtkāraṇādeva śāstrārthasamāptauprāptāyāmupāsanapadavedanīyāvṛttimātrameva kṛtavata uparaṃmaḥ prāptastāvataiva kṛtaśāstrārthatvāditi prāpte 'bhidhīyate--savijñāno bhavatītyādiśruteryatra svargādiphalānāmapi karmaṇāṃ prāyaṇakāle svargādivijñānāpekṣakatvaṃ tatra kaiva kathātīndriyaphalānāmupāsanānām /
tāni khalu āprāyaṇaṃ tattadupāsyagocarabuddhipravāhavāhitayā dṛṣṭenaiva rūpeṇa prāyaṇasamaye tadbuddiṃ bhāvayiṣyanti /
kimatra phalavatprāyaṇasamaye buddhyākṣepeṇa nahi dṛṣṭe saṃbhavatyadṛṣṭakalpanā yuktā /
tasmādāprāyaṇaṃ pravṛttā vṛttiriti /

children.translated_text: This is what was stated: '#The cognitions indeed are these#.'

children.text: tathā ca śrutiḥ sarvādīndriyaviṣaya--'sa yathākraturasmāllokāt praiti tāvatkraturhāmuṃ lokaṃ pretyabhisaṃbhavati' iti /
children.translated_text: And the <s>Śruti</s> regarding all sense-objects [confirms]: 'As one's intention (<s>kratu</s>) is when departing from this world, with that very intention one arrives in the other world upon death.'
'<s>Kratu</s>' means a specific intention (<s>saṃkalpaviśeṣa</s>).
And <s>Smṛti</s>s have also been cited. //12//

body.translated_text:
'#Until death (<s>āprāyaṇa</s>), because even there it is observed#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] distinguishes the subject of the <s>adhikaraṇa</s>: '#Therein, those that are#.'
[Regarding] the cognition of <s>Brahman</s>-selfhood (<s>brahmātmapratipatti</s>), where there is no person-to-be-enjoined (<s>niyojya</s>) —
For scripture teaches the person-to-be-enjoined the connection with an enjoined duty in the form of what-is-to-be-done (<s>kāryarūpa</s>); it teaches that very person the eligibility (<s>adhikāra</s>) characterized by mastership (<s>aiśvarya</s>) in <s>karma</s>; and both of these, being supersensory (<s>atīndriya</s>), are the domain of scripture as a means of knowledge, [since they] cannot be reached by other means of knowledge, and scripture is meaningful [precisely because of this].
But the cognition of <s>Brahman</s>-hood — having been seen [directly] by the <s>jīvanmukta</s> (one liberated while living) — there is nothing hidden here, as it were — so what will scripture accomplish here?
Objection: Even so, the meditations (<s>upāsanā</s>s) that have worldly prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>) as their fruit — [there too] the connection of injunction-and-person-to-be-enjoined, and the connection characterized by mastership (<s>svāmitā</s>), being supersensory — for those, upon the attainment of the completion of the scriptural purpose through a single performance, there being the prima facie conclusion of ceasing [after] merely the modification (<s>vṛtti</s>) — the cognitive state indicated by the word '<s>upāsanā</s>' (meditation) — performed [once], because the scriptural purpose is fulfilled by just that much — this being arrived at, it is stated: From the <s>Śruti</s> '<s>savijñāno bhavati</s>' ('one becomes possessed of knowledge') and the like — where even for <s>karma</s>s having heaven and the like as their fruits, the dependence on the cognition of heaven and the like at the time of death (<s>prāyaṇa</s>) [is taught] — how much more so for meditations whose fruits are supersensory!
Indeed, those [meditations], being sustained in the continuous flow of cognition directed toward their respective objects of meditation until death, will — in their directly observed form — intensify that cognition at the time of death.
What further fruit is there through the drawing forth of cognition at the time of death? — For when what is directly observed is possible, the postulation of something unobserved is not appropriate.
Therefore, the modification (<s>vṛtti</s>) continues until death.

body.text:
#tadadhigama uttarapūrvārdhayoraśleṣavināśau tadvyapadeśāt# /
gatastṛtīyaśeṣaḥ sādhanagocaro vicāraḥ /
idānīmetadadhyāyagataphalaviṣayā cintā pratanyate /
tatra tāvatprathamamidaṃ vicāryate kiṃ brahmādhigame brahmajñāne sati brahmajñānaphalānmokṣādviparītaphalaṃ duritaṃ bandhanaphalaṃ kṣīyate na kṣīyata iti saṃśayaḥ /
kiṃ tāvatprāptaṃ , śāstreṇa hi phalāya yadvihitaṃ pratiṣiddhaṃ cānarthaparihārāyāśvamedhādi brahmahatyādi cāpūrvāvāntaravyāpāraṃ kiṃ tadapūrvamuparate 'pi karmaṇyatra sukhadukhopabhogātprāṅgāvirantumarhati /
sa hi tasya vināśahetusdabhāve kathaṃ vinaśyediti /
tyākasmikatvaprasaṅgāt śāstravyākopācceti /
adattaphalaṃ cetkarmāpūrvaṃ vinaśyati karmaṇa eva phalaprasavasāmarthyabodhakaśāstramapramāṇaṃ bhavet /
naca prāyaścittamiva brahmajñānamadattaphalānyapi karmapūrvāṇi kṣiṇotīti sāmpratam /
prāyaścittānāmapi tadaprakṣayahetutvāt tadvidhānasya cainasvinarādhikāriprāptimātreṇopapattāvupāttaduritanibarhaṇaphalākṣepakatvāyogāt /
ata eva smaranti nābhuktaṃ kṣīyate karmeti /
yadi punarapekṣitopāyatātmā prāyaścittavidhirna niyojyaviśeṣapratilambhamātreṇa nirvṛṇotītyapekṣitakāṅkṣāyāṃ doṣasaṃyogena śravaṇāttannibarhaṇaphalaḥ kalpeta /
tathāpi brahmajñānasya tatsaṃyogenāśravaṇannaduparitanibarhaṇasāmarthye pramāṇamasti mokṣavāt /
tasyāpi svargādiphalavaddeśakālanimittāpekṣayopapatteḥ /
śāstraprāmāṇyātsaṃbhaviṣyatyasāvavasthā yasyāmupabhogena samastakarmakṣaye brahmajñānaṃ mokṣaṃ prasoṣyati /
yogādhdyairva vā divi bhuvyantarīkṣe bahūni śarīrendriyāṇi nirmāya phalānayupabhujyarddhena yogasāmarthyena yogī karmāṇi kṣapayitvā mokṣī saṃpatsyate /
sthite caitasminnarthe nyāyabalādyathā puṣkarapalāśa ityādivyapadeśo brahmavidyāstutimātraparatayā vyākhyeya iti prāpta ucyate--vyākhyāyetaivaṃ vyapadeśo yadi karmavirodhaḥ syānna tvayamasti /
śāstraṃ hi phalotpādanasāmarthyamātraṃ karmaṇāmavagamayati na tu kutaścidāgantukānnimittataḥ prāyaścittādestadapratibandhamapi /
tasya tatraudāsīnyāt /
yadi śāstrabodhitaphalaprasavasāmarthyamapratibaddhamāgantukena kenacit karmaṇā tatastatphalaṃ prasūta evāti na śāstravyāghātaḥ /
nābhuktaṃ karma kṣīyataiti ca smaraṇapratibaddhasāmarthyakarmābhiprāyaṃ /
doṣakṣayoddheśena cāparavidyānāmasti prāyaścittavadvidhānamaiśvaryabhalānāmapyubhayasaṃyogāviśeṣāt /
yatrāpi nirguṇāyāṃ paravidyāyāṃ doṣoddheśo nāsti tatrāpi tatsvabhāvālocanādeva tatprakṣayaprasavasāmarthyamavasīyate /
nahi tatvamasivākyārthaparibhāvanābhuvā prasaṃkhyānena nirmṛṣṭanikhilakartṛbhokktṛtvādivibhramo jīvaḥ phalopabhogona yujyate /
nahi rajjavāṃ bhujaṅkasamāropanibandhanā bhayakampādayaḥ sati rajjutatvasākṣātkāre prabhavanti, kintu saṃskāraśeṣātkiñcitkālamanuvṛttā api nivartanta eva /
amumevārthamanuvadanto yathā puṣkarapalāśa ityādayo vyapadeśāḥ samavetārthāḥ santo na stutimātratayā kathañcidvyākhyānamarhanti /
nanūktaṃ saṃbhaviṣyanti sāvasthā jīvātmano yasyāṃ paryāyeṇopabhogādvā yogarddheḥ prabhāvato yugapannaikavidhakāyanirmāṇenāparyāyeṇopabhogādvā jantuḥ karmāṇi kṣapayitvā mokṣī saṃpatsyata ityata āha--- #evameva ca mokṣa upapadyata iti# /
anādikālapravṛttā hi karmāśayā aniyatakālavipākāḥ kramavatā tāvadbhogena kṣetumaśakyāḥ /
bhuñjānaḥ khalvayamaparānapi saṃcinoti karmāśayāniti /
nāpyaparyāyamupabhogenāsaktaḥ karmāntarāṇyasaṃcinvānaḥ kṣeṣyatīti sāmpratam /
kalpaśatāni kramakālabhogyānāṃ samprati bhoktusāmarthyāt /
dīrghakālaphalāni ca karmāṇi kathamekapade kṣeṣyanti /
tasasmānnānyathā mokṣasaṃbhavaḥ /
nanu satsvapi karmāśayāntareṣusukhadukhaphaleṣu mokṣaphalāt karmaṇaḥ samudācarato brahmabhāvamanubhūyātha labdhavipākānāṃ karmāntarāṇāṃ phalāni bhokṣyanta ityāha-- #naca deśakālanimittāpekṣā iti# /
nahi kāryaḥ sanmokṣo mokṣo bhavitumarhati brahmabhāvo hi saḥ /
naca brahma kriyate niyatvādityarthaḥ /
parokṣatvānupatteśca jñānaphalasya /
jñānaphalaṃ khalu mokṣo 'bhyupeyate /
jñānasya cānantarabhāvinījñeyābhivyaktiḥ phalaṃ, saivāvidyocchedamādadhatī brahmasvabhāvasvarūpāvasthānalakṣaṇāya mokṣāya kalpate /

children.translated_text: For thus the directly perceptible purpose of knowledge would be [established].

children.text: apūrvādhānaparamparayā jñānasya mokṣaphale kalpyamāne jñānasya parokṣaphalatvamadṛṣṭārthatvaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: If the liberation-fruit of knowledge were postulated through the chain of producing <s>apūrva</s> (unseen potency), [then] knowledge would have a non-perceptible fruit and a non-directly-seen purpose.
And when a directly seen [purpose] is possible, the postulation of a non-directly-seen [purpose] is not fitting — this is the meaning.
Therefore, upon the attainment of <s>Brahman</s> — when <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge arises — upon the establishment of non-duality, the destruction of sin is established. //13//

body.translated_text:
'#Upon the attainment of that [<s>Brahman</s>], the non-clinging and destruction of the earlier and later halves [of <s>karma</s>] — because of that designation#.'
The investigation of the third [<s>adhyāya</s>], the remainder of which pertains to the means, has come to an end.
Now the reflection on the fruit-topic belonging to this [fourth] <s>adhyāya</s> is continued.
Therein, to begin with, this is first investigated: Upon the attainment of <s>Brahman</s> — when <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge arises — is the sin (<s>durita</s>) that has a fruit contrary to liberation — namely, the fruit of bondage — destroyed or not? — this is the doubt.
What, then, is the prima facie conclusion? That which has been prescribed by scripture for the purpose of a fruit, and that which has been prohibited for the avoidance of misfortune — sacrifice (<s>aśvamedha</s>) and the like, or killing a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (<s>brahmahatyā</s>) and the like — [each] has an intermediate operation in the form of <s>apūrva</s> (unseen potency). Does that <s>apūrva</s>, even when the <s>karma</s> has ceased, deserve to cease before yielding its fruit of pleasure and pain?
For in the absence of a cause of its destruction, how would it be destroyed?
Because there would be the consequence of causelessness, and because of the disruption of scripture.
For if the <s>apūrva</s> of <s>karma</s> were destroyed without having given its fruit, the scripture that reveals the capacity of <s>karma</s> to produce its fruit would become non-authoritative.
Nor is it correct [to say] that <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge, like <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation), destroys even <s>karma</s>-potencies that have not yet given their fruit.
Because the <s>prāyaścitta</s>s too are not causes of the destruction of that [accumulated <s>karma</s>]; and because the injunction of <s>prāyaścitta</s> is tenable merely through the obtainment of the sinner's eligibility [for further ritual action], [it has] no capacity to imply the destruction of the accumulated sin as its fruit.
For this very reason, they declare: 'Unexperienced <s>karma</s> does not decay.'
But if the injunction of <s>prāyaścitta</s> — having the nature of a means that is required [for something further] — does not exhaust itself merely by obtaining the specific person who is to be enjoined, then — when the required expectation [is present] — from the hearing of [its] connection with the fault, [the injunction] may be postulated as having the destruction of that [fault] as its fruit.
Even so, there is no valid authority for the capacity of <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge to destroy accumulated sin — since [that knowledge] is not heard in connection with that [sin] — unlike liberation.
Because even that [liberation] could be explained as depending on time, place, and occasion — like heaven and other fruits.
[One could argue:] By the authority of scripture, there will arise that state [at some point] in which, through the exhaustion of all <s>karma</s> by sequential experience, <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge will bring forth liberation.
Or alternatively, by means of <s>yoga</s> and the like, the <s>yogī</s>, having created many bodies and sense-organs in heaven, earth, and the atmosphere, and having experienced the fruits sequentially, or — by the power of <s>yoga</s>-perfection — having simultaneously created manifold bodies and thereby experiencing [the fruits] non-sequentially, having exhausted the <s>karma</s>s, will attain liberation.
And when this position stands by the force of reasoning, the designations such as 'like a lotus-leaf' and the like should be explained as having the mere purport of praising <s>Brahmavidyā</s> — this being the prima facie view, the reply is given:
The designations could be explained thus if there were a conflict with <s>karma</s>. But there is no such [conflict].
For scripture reveals only the mere capacity of <s>karma</s>s to produce their fruits — not also the non-obstruction of that [capacity] by some adventitious cause such as <s>prāyaścitta</s> and the like.
Because of [scripture's] indifference toward that [question].
If the fruit-producing capacity revealed by scripture is unobstructed by any adventitious <s>karma</s>, then it produces its fruit — there is no disruption of scripture.
And the <s>Smṛti</s>-statement 'Unexperienced <s>karma</s> does not decay' is with reference to <s>karma</s> whose capacity has not been obstructed.
And there is an injunction of the lower <s>vidyā</s>s (<s>aparavidyā</s>s) for the purpose of destroying sins, like <s>prāyaścitta</s> — because there is no distinction in the conjunction with both [sin-destruction and worldly fruits] — even for the <s>vidyā</s>s that have sovereignty and the like as their fruits.
And even where — in the <s>nirguṇa</s> (unqualified) supreme <s>vidyā</s> — there is no explicit mention of sin-destruction, even there, from the very examination of its essential nature, the capacity to bring about the destruction of that [sin] is ascertained.
For the <s>jīva</s> (individual self) — whose entire delusion of being an agent, an experiencer, and the like has been wiped away by the <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s> (contemplative reflection) born of the thorough cultivation of the meaning of the sentence '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' ('That thou art') — is not suited for the experience of [karmic] fruits.
For the fear, trembling, and the like caused by the superimposition of a snake on a rope do not arise when the direct realization of the rope-nature is present; rather, even though they may persist for a short while due to residual impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), they indeed cease.
The designations such as 'like a lotus-leaf' and the like — echoing this very meaning — being connected with their [literal] meaning, do not deserve to be explained somehow as mere praise.
But [one might object:] it was said that there will arise that state of the <s>jīva</s> in which — through sequential experience, or through the power of <s>yoga</s>-perfection by simultaneously creating manifold bodies for non-sequential experience — the being, having exhausted the <s>karma</s>s, will attain liberation. To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#And thus liberation is tenable [only in this way]#.'
For the latent karmic deposits (<s>karmāśaya</s>s) accumulated since beginningless time — having indeterminate times of ripening — cannot be exhausted by sequential experience.
For even while experiencing [some], this [being] accumulates other latent karmic deposits.
Nor is it correct [to say] that, through non-sequential experience, being detached, not accumulating further <s>karma</s>s, [the being] will exhaust [them].
Because of the capacity to presently experience [fruits] that [would otherwise] require hundreds of cosmic cycles of sequential time.
And how will <s>karma</s>s whose fruits extend over long periods be exhausted in a single step?
Therefore, liberation is not possible in any other way.
But [one might object:] even when the other latent karmic deposits — whose fruits are pleasure and pain — exist, [the being], having experienced the <s>Brahman</s>-state from the <s>karma</s> whose fruit is liberation, which is operating — will then experience the fruits of the other <s>karma</s>s whose ripening has been obtained. To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Nor is there a dependence on time, place, and occasion#.'
For liberation, being something to be accomplished, cannot [truly] be liberation — for it is the state of <s>Brahman</s>.
And <s>Brahman</s> is not produced, because of [its] eternality — this is the meaning.
And because of the consequence that the fruit of knowledge would be non-perceptible (<s>parokṣa</s>).
For liberation is accepted as the fruit of knowledge.
And the fruit of knowledge is the manifestation of the knowable that occurs immediately [upon knowing] — and that very [manifestation], effecting the destruction of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), serves as liberation characterized by the abiding in one's own essential nature as <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text:
#itarasyāpyevamasaṃśleṣaḥ pāte tu# /
adharmasya svābhāvikatvena rāgādinibandhanatvena śāstrīyeṇa brahmajñānena pratibandho yuktaḥ /
dharmajñānayostu śāstrīyatvena, jyotiṣṭomadarśapaurṇamāsavirodhānnocchedyocchettṛbhāvo yujyate /
pāpnamanaśca viśeṣato brahmajñānocchedyatvaśruterdharmasyana taducchedyatvam /
viśeṣavidhānasya śeṣapratiṣedhanāntarīyakatvena lokataḥ siddheḥ /
yathā devadatto dakṣiṇenākṣṇā paśyatītyukte na vāmena paśyatīti gamyate /
ubhe hyevaiṣa ete taratīti ca yathāsaṃbhavaṃ, brahmajñānena duṣkṛtaṃ bhogena sukṛtamiti /
'kṣīyante cāsya karmaṇi' iti ca sāmānyavacanaṃ 'sarve pāpmānaḥ' iti viśeṣaśravaṇātpāpakarmāṇīti viśeṣe upasaṃharaṇīyam /
tasmādbrahmajñānādduṣkṛtasyaiva kṣayo na sukṛtasyeti prāpte pūrvādhikaraṇarāddhānto 'tidiśyate /
no khalu brahmavidyā kenacidadṛṣṭena dvāreṇa duṣkṛtamapanayatyapi tu dṛṣṭenaiva bhoktṛbhoktavyabhogādipravilayadvāreṇa taccaitattulyaṃ sukṛtepīti kathametadapi nocchindyāt /
evaṃ ca satina śāstrīyatvasāmyamātramavirodhaheturanahi pratyakṣatvasāmānyamātrādavirodho jalānalādīnāṃ /
naca sukṛtaśāstramanarthakamabrahmavidaṃ prati tadvidherarthavatvāt /
evamavasthite ca pāpmaśrutyā puṇyamapi grahītavyam /
brahmajñānamapekṣya puṇyasya nikṛṣṭaphalatvāttatphalaṃ hi kṣayātiśayāt /

children.translated_text: For liberation is not thus [characterized], because of [its] unsurpassability and eternality.
And this word '<s>pāpman</s>' has a directly seen usage in the <s>Veda</s> for both merit and demerit.

children.text: tadyathā puṇyapāpe anukramya sarve pāpmāno 'to nivartaneta ityatra /
children.translated_text: For example: having enumerated both merit and demerit, [the <s>Śruti</s> says:] 'All <s>pāpman</s>s (evils) turn away from him' — in that [passage].
Therefore, the non-clinging and destruction of both merit and demerit without distinction is established. //14//

body.translated_text:
'#For the other [i.e., merit] too, likewise, there is non-clinging; but [it may also be known] from falling#.'
The obstruction of demerit (<s>adharma</s>) — which is of a natural character and is grounded in passion (<s>rāga</s>) and the like — by scriptural <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge is reasonable.
But between merit (<s>dharma</s>) and knowledge — both being scriptural — the relationship of what-is-to-be-destroyed and the destroyer is not fitting, just as between the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [which do not conflict].
Moreover, since the <s>Śruti</s> specifically states that sin (<s>pāpman</s>) is destroyed by <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge, [it follows that] merit (<s>dharma</s>) is not destroyed by it.
Because the specific mention [of sin alone] is well-known in the world as necessarily implying the negation of the remainder.
Just as, when it is said '<s>Devadatta</s> sees with the right eye,' it is understood that he does not see with the left.
And [the <s>Śruti</s>] 'He crosses over both of these' — [should be interpreted] as applicable to each: sin is [crossed over] by <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge, and merit by experience.
And the general statement 'all his <s>karma</s>s are destroyed' — from the specific hearing 'all sins (<s>pāpmānaḥ</s>)' — should be drawn into the specific [meaning]: the <s>karma</s>s that are sinful [are destroyed].
Therefore, from <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge, only sin is destroyed, not merit — this being the prima facie view, the established conclusion of the previous <s>adhikaraṇa</s> is extended.
<s>Brahmavidyā</s> does not remove sin by some unseen (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) means; rather, [it does so] by the directly seen means of the dissolution of the experiencer, the experienced, and experience itself. And this is the same for merit too — so how would it not destroy that [merit] also?
And when this is so, the mere sameness of being scriptural is not a reason for non-conflict — for the mere general sameness of being perceptible does not [establish] non-conflict between water and fire and the like.
Nor is the scripture [enjoining] merit rendered purposeless — because that injunction has purpose with respect to one who is not a knower of <s>Brahman</s>.
And when the matter stands thus, by the <s>Śruti</s> about '<s>pāpman</s>' (sin), merit too should be included.
Because merit, in relation to <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge, has an inferior fruit — for that fruit is characterized by destruction and surpassability.

body.text:
#anārabdhakārya eva tu pūrve tadavadheḥ# /
yadyadvaitajñānasvabhāvālocanayottarapūrvasukṛtaduṣkṛtayoraśleṣavināśau hanta ārabdhānārabdhakāryayoścāviśeṣeṇaiva vināśaḥ syāt /
kartṛkarmādipravilayasyobhayatrāviśeṣāt /
tannibandhanatvācca vināśasya /
naca saṃskāraśeṣātkulālacakrabhramaṇavadanuvṛttiḥ /
vastunaḥ khalvanuvṛttiḥ /
māyaivādinaśca puṇyapāpayoścamāyāmātravinirmitatvena māyānivṛttau na puṇyāpuṇye na tatasaṃskāro vastusantīti kasyānuvṛttiḥ /
naca rajjau sarpādivibramajanitā bhayakamapādayo nivṛtte 'pi vibhrame yathānuvartante tathehāpīti yuktam /
tatrāpi sarpāsatve 'pi tajjānasya satve tajjanitabhayakampādīnāṃ tatsaskārāṇāṃ ca vastusattvena nivṛtte 'pi vibhrame 'nivṛtteḥ /
atra tu māyā na tajjaḥ saṃskāro na tadgocara iti tucchatvātkimanuvarteta /
na saṃskāraśeṣo na karmetyaviśeṣeṇārabdhakāryāṇāmanārabdhakāryāṇāṃ ca nivṛttiḥ /
naca tasya tāvadeva ciraṃ yāvanna vimokṣye 'tha saṃmapatya iti śruterdehāpratīkṣārabdhakāryāṇāṃ yuktā. nahyeṣā śrutiravadhibhedavidhāyinyapi tu kṣipratāparā /
yathā loka etāvanme ciraṃ yatsanāto bhuñjānaśceti /
nahi tatra snānabhojane avadhitvena vidhīyate kitu kṣapīyastā pratipādyate. ubhayavidhāne hi vākyaṃ bhidyetāvadhibhedaḥ ciratāceti prāpte 'bhidhīyate--yadyapyadvaitabrahmatatvasākṣātkāro 'nādyavidyapadarśitapruñcamātravirodh itayā tanmadhyapatitasakalakarmaviredhī /
tathāpyanārabdhavipākaṃ karmajātaṃ drāgityeva samucchinatti na tvārabdhavipākaṃ saṃpāditajātyāyurvitatapūrvāparībhītasukhaduḥkhopabhogapravāhaṃ karmajātam /
taddhi samudācaradvṛttitayetarebhyaḥprasuptavṛttibhyo balavat /
anyathā devarṣīṇāṃ hiraṇyagarbhamanūddālakaprabhṛtīnāṃvigalitanikhilakleśajālāvaramatayā paritaḥ pradyotamānabuddhisatvānāṃ na jyogjīvitā bhavet /
śrūyate caiṣāṃ śrutismṛtītihāsapurāṇeṣu tatvajñatā ca mahākalpakalpamanvantarādijīvitā ca /
na caite mahadhiyo na tadīyasamastaphalopabhogapratīkṣā satyapi tatvasākṣātkāre /
tāvadeva ciramiti na ciratā vidhīyate. api tu śrutyantarasiddhāṃ ciratāmanūdya dehapātāvadhimātravidhānaṃ tadetadabhisaṃdhāyaucityamātratayāha bhagavān bhāṣyākāraḥ--- #na tāvadanāśrityārabdhakāryaṃ karmāśayamiti# /
na cedaṃ na jātu dṛṣṭaṃ yadviredhisamavāye viroddhyantaramanuvartata ityāha--- #akartrātmabodho 'pīti# /
yadā loke 'pi virodhinoḥ kiñcitkālaṃ sahānuvṛttirupalabdhā tadehagamabalāddīrghakālamapi bhavatīti na śakyā nivārayitum /
pramāṇasiddhasya niyogaparyanuyogānupapatteḥ /
tadevaṃ madhyasthanapratipādya ye bhāṣyakāramāptaṃ manyate tān pratyāha--- #apica naivātra vivaditavyamiti# /
sthitaprajñaśca na sādhakastasyottarottaradhyānotkarṣeṇa pūrvapratyayānavasthitatvāt /
niratiśayastu sthitaprajñaḥ /
sa ca siddha eva /
naca jñānakāryā bhayakampādayaḥ,jñānamātrādanutpādāt /
body.translated_text:
'#But it is only the [<s>karma</s>] whose effect has not yet commenced (<s>anārabdhakārya</s>) that [is destroyed], because of the termination [of the body being the limit] of the previous [<s>karma</s>]#.'
If, upon examining the nature of non-dual knowledge (<s>advaitajñāna</s>), both subsequent and prior merit (<s>sukṛta</s>) and demerit (<s>duṣkṛta</s>) [undergo] non-attachment and destruction — then indeed, the destruction of both <s>karma</s>s whose effects have commenced (<s>ārabdha</s>) and those whose effects have not commenced (<s>anārabdha</s>) should occur without distinction.
Because there is no distinction between the two regarding the dissolution of agent-hood, action-hood, and the like.
And because the destruction is grounded in that [dissolution].
Nor is there a continuation due to residual impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), like the spinning of a potter's wheel.
For continuation belongs to a [real] thing.
But since merit and demerit are beginningless <s>māyā</s> (illusion) and are fabricated by <s>māyā</s> alone, upon the cessation of <s>māyā</s>, neither merit nor demerit, nor their impressions, are [real] things — so whose continuation [could there be]?
Nor is it reasonable [to argue] that — just as fear, trembling, and the like generated by the delusion of a snake on a rope continue even after the delusion has ceased — so too here.
For even there, although the snake is unreal, since the cognition of it is real, the fear, trembling, and the like generated by it, and their impressions — being real things — do not cease even when the delusion ceases.
But here, <s>māyā</s> is [unreal]; the impression born of it is [unreal]; it has no [real] object — hence, being void, what could continue?
There is neither residual impression nor <s>karma</s> — hence there is cessation of both <s>karma</s>s whose effects have commenced and those whose effects have not commenced, without distinction.
Nor is the <s>Śruti</s> 'For him the delay is just so long until he is freed; then he merges' [an obstacle] — [it is] appropriate [even when] the <s>karma</s>s whose effects have commenced do not await the [death of the] body. For this <s>Śruti</s> does not prescribe a distinction of termination [limits], but rather has the purport of [expressing] swiftness.
Just as in the world [one says]: 'So long is my delay as [it takes me] to bathe and eat' — therein, bathing and eating are not prescribed as termination [limits], but rather the swiftness [of the delay] is conveyed. For if both [a termination-limit and swiftness] were prescribed, the sentence would be split [into two distinct meanings] — 'distinction of limit' and 'swiftness' — against this prima facie view, it is stated:
Although the direct realization of non-dual <s>Brahman</s>-reality (<s>advaitabrahmatattvasākṣātkāra</s>) — being contradictory to the entire phenomenal world projected by beginningless <s>avidyā</s> — is contradictory to all <s>karma</s> that falls within that [phenomenal world],
nevertheless, it quickly cuts off the aggregate of <s>karma</s> whose ripening has not yet commenced (<s>anārabdhavipāka</s>), but not the aggregate of <s>karma</s> whose ripening has already commenced (<s>ārabdhavipāka</s>) — [<s>karma</s>] that has [already] produced the stream of experience of happiness and suffering, which has been made into [a sequence of] 'before' and 'after' by the birth, lifespan, and [resultant] experience [it has] brought about.
For that [<s>ārabdha karma</s>], being of actively operative function (<s>samudācaradvṛtti</s>), is stronger than the others, whose function is dormant (<s>prasuptavṛtti</s>).
Otherwise, the divine sages (<s>devarṣi</s>s) — <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, <s>Manu</s>, <s>Uddālaka</s>, and the like — whose <s>buddhi-sattva</s> shines forth on all sides due to their minds being free from the entire web of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) — would not have long lives.
But it is heard in <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, <s>Itihāsa</s>, and <s>Purāṇa</s> that these [sages] possess knowledge of reality and also have lifespans lasting great <s>kalpa</s>s, <s>kalpa</s>s, <s>manvantara</s>s, and the like.
And these great-minded [sages] do not [refuse liberation because they are] awaiting the full enjoyment of all their fruits — even though direct realization of reality has [already] occurred.
'The delay is just so long' — this does not prescribe the duration [of embodiment]. Rather, restating the duration established through another <s>Śruti</s>, it prescribes only the termination [limit as] the fall of the body — this is the intent, stated by the venerable <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (<s>Śaṅkara</s>) with appropriateness alone: '#Not without relying on the <s>karmāśaya</s> (latent karmic deposit) whose effect has commenced#.'
Nor is the following unobserved — that in the co-existence of contradictories, [one of] the contradictories continues — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Even the knowledge of the Self as non-agent#.'
Since even in the world the co-existence of contradictories for some time is observed — all the more so can it be [observed] for a long time, due to the force of the body-connection — and [hence] cannot be prevented.
Because it is impossible to challenge something established through a valid means of knowledge.
Having thus demonstrated the middle position, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] addresses those who regard the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> as authoritative: '#Moreover, there is no need to dispute here at all#.'
And one who is <s>sthitaprajña</s> (of steady wisdom) is not a practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>) — because, due to the progressive elevation of meditation, his previous cognitions are unsettled.
But one who is <s>sthitaprajña</s> is [one whose wisdom is] unsurpassed.
And he is already an accomplished one (<s>siddha</s>).
Nor are fear, trembling, and the like effects of knowledge — because they are not produced from mere knowledge alone.

body.text:
sarpāvacchedohi tasya bhayakampādihetuḥ /
sa cāsanna nirvacanīya iti kuto vastusataḥ karyotpādaḥ /

children.translated_text: Nor is the effect — fear, trembling, and the like — a [real] thing either.
Because that too is inexpressible (<s>anirvacanīya</s>), being unable to withstand scrutiny.
And from something inexpressible, the production of something [equally] inexpressible is not untenable.
For 'as is the demon (<s>yakṣa</s>), so is the offering (<s>bali</s>)' — thus everything is clear. //15//

body.translated_text:
For the delimitation [of consciousness] as a snake is the cause of fear, trembling, and the like.
And that [delimitation] is unreal, inexpressible (<s>anirvacanīya</s>) — so from where would an effect arise from something that is [ontologically] a real thing?

body.text:
#agnihotrādi tu tatkāryāyaiva taddarśanāt# /
yadi puṇyasyāpyaśleṣavināśau hanta nityamapyagnihotrādi na kartavyaṃ yogamārūrukṣuṇā /
tasyāpītarapuṇyavadvidyayā vināśāt /
'prakṣālanāddhi paṅkasya dūrādasparśanaṃ vara'miti nyāyāt /
naca vividiṣanti yajñena dāneneti mokṣalakṣaṇaikakāryatayā vidyākarmaṇoravirodhaḥ /
sahāsaṃbhavenaikakāryatvāsaṃbhavāt /
nahyetamātmānaṃ viduṣo vigalitākhilakartṛtvādiprapañcavibhramasya pūrvottare nitye kriyājanye puṇye saṃbhavataḥ /
tasmādvividiṣanti yajñeneti vartamānāpadeśo brahmajñānasya yajñādīnāṃ vā stutimātraṃ na tu mokṣamāṇasya muktisādhanaṃ yajñādividhiriti prāpta ucyate /
--satyaṃ na vidyayaikakāryatvaṃ karmaṇāṃ parasparavirodhena sahāsaṃbhavāt /
vidyotpādakatayā tu karmaṇāmārādupakārakāṇāmastu mokṣopayogaḥ /
naca karmaṇāṃ vidyayā virudhyamānānāṃ na vidyākāraṇatvaṃ, svakāraṇavirodhināṃ kāryāṇāṃ bahulamupalabdheḥ /
tathāca vidyālakṣaṇakāryopāyatayā kāryavināśyānāmapi karmaṇāmupādānamarthavat /
tadabhāve tatkāryasyānutpādena mokṣasyāsaṃbhavāt /

children.text: evañca vividiṣanti yajñeneti yajñasādhanatvaṃ vidyāya apūrvamarthaṃ prāpayataḥ pañcamalakārasya nātyantaparokṣavṛttitayā jñānastutyarthatayā kathañcidvyākhyānaṃ bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: And thus, 'They seek to know through sacrifice' — since the fifth-case ending (<s>pañcama lakāra</s>), which conveys the sacrificial means to <s>vidyā</s>, teaches an unprecedented meaning, [this statement] will be explained somehow — not as having the function of a completely remote [metaphorical] usage for the purpose of praising knowledge.

children.text: tadanenābhisamadhinoktaṃ -- #jñānasyeva hi prāpakaṃ satkarama praṇaḍyā mokṣakāraṇamityupacaryate# /
children.translated_text: This is what is stated with this intent: '#For it is <s>satkarma</s> (good action) alone that, as the means to knowledge, is figuratively (<s>upacāra</s>) called the cause of liberation#.'

children.text: yata eva na vidyodayasamaye karmāsti nāpi parastādapi tu prāgeva vidyāyāḥ, ata eva cātikrāntaviṣayametatkāryaikatvābhidhānam /
children.translated_text: Since at the time of the arising of <s>vidyā</s>, <s>karma</s> does not exist, nor does it [exist] after [<s>vidyā</s>], but only prior to <s>vidyā</s> — for this very reason, this statement about the single-effect-ness [of <s>vidyā</s> and <s>karma</s>] pertains to what has been transcended.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] elucidates this: '#For one who knows <s>Brahman</s>#.' //16//

body.translated_text:
'#<s>Agnihotra</s> and the like, however, are [to be performed] for the sake of that [knowledge] alone — because of the observation of that#.'
If even merit undergoes non-attachment and destruction — then indeed, even the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like, which are perpetual [obligations], should not be performed by one who aspires to ascend the path of <s>Yoga</s>.
Because even their [merit], like that of other meritorious [actions], is destroyed by <s>vidyā</s>.
'For rather than washing off mud, it is better not to touch it at all' — by this principle.
Nor is there non-contradiction between <s>vidyā</s> and <s>karma</s> by virtue of having liberation as a single effect, [as suggested by] 'They seek to know through sacrifice and charity' —
because the single-effect-ness is impossible due to the impossibility of co-existence [of <s>vidyā</s> and <s>karma</s>].
For one who has known this Self — whose delusion of the entire phenomenal world of agent-hood and the like has dissolved — cannot [coherently] have either prior or subsequent merit, which is perpetual and born of action.
Therefore, 'They seek to know through sacrifice' — this present-tense usage is mere praise of either <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge or sacrifice and the like, not an injunction of sacrifice and the like as means to liberation for one who is seeking liberation — against this prima facie view, it is stated:
True, <s>karma</s> does not have a single effect with <s>vidyā</s>, because of the impossibility of co-existence due to their mutual contradiction.
But let <s>karma</s>s — which are remote aids, being productive of <s>vidyā</s> — have utility for liberation.
Nor is it the case that <s>karma</s>s, being contradicted by <s>vidyā</s>, cannot be the cause of <s>vidyā</s> — because effects that are contradicted by their own cause are abundantly observed.
And thus, since <s>karma</s>s are means to the effect characterized by <s>vidyā</s>, the employment of <s>karma</s>s — even though they are destroyed by [their own] effect — is purposeful.
Because in the absence of that [<s>karma</s>], the non-production of its effect [<s>vidyā</s>] would make liberation impossible.

children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara</s>], wishing to introduce another <s>sūtra</s>, asks: '#But what is the subject of this?#'
The answer is the <s>sūtra</s>: '#Moreover, even from others — for some [<s>śākhā</s>s have such statements] — of both [merit and demerit]#.'

children.text: kāmyakarmaviṣayamaśle,vināśavacanaṃ śākhāntarīyavacanaṃ ca tasya putrā dāyamupayantīti //17 //
children.translated_text: The statement about non-attachment and destruction pertains to optional (<s>kāmya</s>) <s>karma</s>s; and the statement from another <s>śākhā</s> is: 'His sons receive his inheritance.' //17//

body.text: #yadeva vidyayeti hi# /
body.translated_text: '#Whatever indeed [one does] with knowledge#.'

body.text:
asti vidyāsaṃyuktaṃ yajñādi ya evaṃ vidvānyajetetyādikam /
asti ca kevalam /
tatra yathā brāhmaṇāya hiraṇyaṃ dadyādiyukte viduṣe brāhmaṇāya dadyātra brāhmaṇabruvāya mūkhāyeti viśeṣapratilambhaḥ tatkasya hetostasyātiśayavatvāt /

children.translated_text: Similarly, sacrifice and the like conjoined with <s>vidyā</s> are superior to [those] devoid of <s>vidyā</s> — hence it is that [conjunction with <s>vidyā</s>] alone that serves as the means to the supreme <s>vidyā</s>, through the door of the destruction of accumulated sins — not the other [<s>karma</s> devoid of <s>vidyā</s>].

children.text: tasmādvividiṣanti yajñenetyaviśeṣaśrutamapi vidyāsahite yajñādāvupasaṃhartavyamiti prāpte 'bhidhīyate--yadeva vidyayā karāti tadevāsya vīryavattaramiti tarabarthaśrutervidyārahitasya vīryavattāmātramavagamyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, although 'They seek to know through sacrifice' is heard without specification, it should be applied to sacrifice and the like that are conjoined with <s>vidyā</s> — against this prima facie view, it is stated: From the <s>Śruti</s> 'Whatever indeed one does with knowledge, that alone is more potent' (<s>yadeva vidyayā karoti tadevāsya vīryavattaram</s>), and from the comparative suffix (<s>tarap</s>), only a [relative] greater potency [is understood] for [<s>karma</s>] devoid of <s>vidyā</s>.
And [such greater potency] is not possible for something that is utterly inefficacious in every way.

children.text: tasmādastyasyāpi kayāpi mātrayā paravidyotpādopayoga iti vidyārahitamapi yajñādi paravidyārthinānuṣṭheyamiti siddham //18 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, even [<s>karma</s>] devoid of <s>vidyā</s> has, in some measure, utility for the arising of the supreme <s>vidyā</s> — hence sacrifice and the like devoid of <s>vidyā</s> too are to be performed by one who seeks the supreme <s>vidyā</s> — this is established. //18//

body.translated_text:
There exists sacrifice and the like conjoined with <s>vidyā</s> — [as in] 'One who knows thus should sacrifice' and the like.
And there exists [sacrifice] by itself [without <s>vidyā</s>].
Therein, just as [in the statement] 'One should give gold to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>' — when conjoined [with the specification] 'to a learned <s>brāhmaṇa</s>' — there is a specific gain compared to [giving] to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-in-name-only, a fool — the reason [for the specific gain] being its superior potency.

children.translated_text: '#But by experiencing the others, having exhausted [them], he merges [with <s>Brahman</s>]#.'

children.text: anārabdhakārya ityasya nañaḥ phalaṃ bhogena nivṛttiṃ darśayatyanena sūtreṇa /
children.translated_text: The word '<s>na</s>' (not) in '<s>anārabdhakārya</s>' ([<s>karma</s>] whose effect has not commenced) — this <s>sūtra</s> demonstrates the cessation [of that <s>karma</s>] through experience.

children.text: asya tūpapādanaṃ purastādapakṛṣya kṛtamiti neha kriyate punaruktibhayāt //19 //
children.translated_text: But the justification of this [point] has been accomplished earlier by anticipation — hence it is not done here again, for fear of repetition. //19//

body.text: iti śrīvācaspatimiśraviracite śārīrakabhagavatpādabhāṣyavibhāge bhāmatyāṃ caturthasyādhyāyasya prathamaḥ pādaḥ samāptaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the first <s>pāda</s> of the fourth <s>adhyāya</s> in the <s>Bhāmatī</s>, the elucidation of the <s>Śārīraka-Bhāṣya</s> of the Blessed Master [<s>Śaṅkara</s>], composed by the venerable <s>Vācaspati Miśra</s>.

body.text: #caturthe 'dhyāye dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ# /
body.translated_text: '#The second <s>pāda</s> of the fourth <s>adhyāya</s>#.'

body.text:
#vāṅmanasi darśanācchabdācca# /
athāsmin phalavicāralakṣaṇe vāṅmanasi saṃpadyata ityādivicāro 'saṃgata ityata āha-- #athāparāsu vidyāsu phalaprāptaya iti# /
aparavidyāphalaprāptyarthadevayānamārgārthatvādutkrāntestadgato vicāraḥ pāramparyeṇa bhavati phalavicāra iti nāsaṃgata ityarthaḥ /
nanvayamutkrāntikramo viduṣo nopapadyate 'na tasya prāṇā utkrāmantyatraiva samavanīyante' iti śravaṇāttatkathamasya vidyādhikāra ityata āha-- #samānā hi vidvadaviduṣoriti# /
viṣayamāha-- #astīti# /
vimṛśati-- #kimiheti# /
viśayaḥ saṃśayaḥ /
pūrvapakṣamāha-- #tatra vāgeveti# /
śratilakṣaṇāviśaye saṃśaye /
siddhāntasūtraṃ pūrayitvā paṭhati-- #vāgvṛttirmanasi saṃpadyate iti# /
vṛttyadhyāhāraprayojanaṃ praśnapūrvakamāha #kathamiti# /
uttarādhikaraṇaparyālocanenaivaṃ pūritamityarthaḥ /
tattvasya dharmiṇo vācaḥ pralayavivakṣāyāṃ tviha sarvatraiva paratreha cāvibhāgasāmyātkiṃ paratraiva viṃśiṣyādavibhāga iti na tvatrāpi /
tasmādihāvibhāgenāviṃśiṣato 'tra vṛttyupasaṃhāramātravivakṣā sūtrakārasyeti gamyate /
siddhāntahetuṃ praśnapūrvakamāha-- #kasmāditi# /
satyāmeva manovṛttau vāgvṛtterupasaṃhāradarśanāt /
vācastūpasaṃhāramadṛṣṭaṃ nāgamo 'pi gamayitumarhati /
āgamaprabhavayuktivirodhāśca /
āgamo hi dṛṣṭānusārataḥ prakṛtau vikārāṇāṃ layamāha /

children.text: na ca vācaḥ prakṛtirmano yenāsminniyaṃ līyate /
children.translated_text: But the mind is not the material cause (<s>prakṛti</s>) of speech, such that speech would dissolve into it.
Therefore, with the intent of non-distinction between the function and its possessor, the word 'speech' (<s>vāk</s>) should be interpreted as [referring to] its function.
And it is possible for the function of speech to dissolve in the mind, even though [the mind] is not the material cause of speech.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says, because this is observed in various [cases]: '#The arising and suppression of the function#.' //1//

body.translated_text:
'#Speech [merges] in the mind — because of observation and because of the word [of <s>Śruti</s>]#.'
Now, in this [<s>pāda</s>] dealing with the investigation of the fruit [of <s>vidyā</s>], the inquiry 'speech merges in the mind' and the like seems out of place — hence [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#But in the other <s>vidyā</s>s, for the attainment of the fruit#.'
Because the departure (<s>utkrānti</s>) [of the soul] serves the purpose of attaining the fruit of the inferior <s>vidyā</s>s through the path of the gods (<s>devayāna</s>), the inquiry pertaining to that [departure] is, by extension, an inquiry about the fruit — hence it is not out of place — this is the meaning.
But surely, this sequence of departure is not tenable for one who possesses [<s>nirguṇa</s>] <s>vidyā</s> — because of the <s>Śruti</s> 'His <s>prāṇa</s>s do not depart; right here they are gathered together.' Then how is this the domain of <s>vidyā</s>? To this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#For [the process] is the same for the knower and the non-knower#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the subject: '#There is#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] deliberates: '#Is it that here#.'
The subject and the doubt [have been stated].
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the prima facie view: '#Therein, speech itself#.'
[This relates to] the doubt concerning the <s>Śruti</s>'s characteristic [meaning].
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>], having completed the <s>siddhānta</s> <s>sūtra</s>, reads: '#The function (<s>vṛtti</s>) of speech merges in the mind#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the purpose of supplying the word '<s>vṛtti</s>' (function), preceded by a question: '#How?#'
The meaning is: through the consideration of the subsequent <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, [the <s>sūtra</s>] has been thus completed.
When there is the intent of [teaching] the dissolution of the entity (<s>tattva</s>) — the substrate, namely speech — since the non-differentiation [of speech from its substrate] is equally [present] here and hereafter, everywhere, why would [the <s>Śruti</s>] specify non-differentiation only in the hereafter and not here too?
Therefore, since [the <s>Śruti</s>] does not specify non-differentiation here [in this world], the intent of the <s>sūtrakāra</s> [is understood as pertaining] to the withdrawal of the function (<s>vṛtti</s>) alone — this is apprehended.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the reason for the <s>siddhānta</s>, preceded by a question: '#Why?#'
Because the withdrawal of the function of speech is observed [to occur] only when the function of the mind [still] exists.
But the withdrawal of speech [as a substance] is not observed [at the time of dying], and scripture too cannot convey it.
Because of the conflict with reasoning that derives from scripture.
For scripture teaches the dissolution of modifications in their material cause (<s>prakṛti</s>).

children.translated_text: '#And for this very reason, all [the senses] follow [the mind]#.'

children.text: yata eva prakṛtivikārabhāvābhāvanmanasi na svarūpalayo vāco 'pi tu vṛttilayaḥ, ata eva ca sarveṣāṃ cakṣurādīnāmidriyāṇāṃ satyeva savṛttike manasi vṛtteranugatirlayo na svarūpalayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since there is no dissolution of the essential nature (<s>svarūpa</s>) of speech and the like in the mind — which lacks the relation of material cause and modification — but rather a dissolution of [their] function alone, for this very reason, of all the sense-organs — eye and the like — what follows [the mind] is the dissolution of function when the mind together with its function [still] exists, not the dissolution of [their] essential nature.

children.text: vācastu pṛthak grahaṇaṃ pūrvasūtre udāharaṇāpekṣaṃ na tu tadeveha vivakṣitamityarthaḥ //2 //
children.translated_text: But the separate mention of speech in the previous <s>sūtra</s> was required as an example — and it is not that very same [separate mention] that is intended here — this is the meaning. //2//

body.text:
#tanmanaḥ prāṇa uttarāt# /
yadi svaprakṛtau vikārasya layastato manaḥ prāṇe saṃpadyate ityatra manaḥsvarūpasyaiva prāṇe saṃpattyā bhavitavyam /
tathā hi manaḥ iti nopacārato vyākhyānaṃ bhaviṣyati /
saṃbhavati hi prakṛtivikārabhāvaḥ prāṇamanasoḥ /
annamayaṃ hi somya mana ityannātmatāmāha manasaḥ śrutirāpomayaḥ prāṇa iti ca prāṇasyābātmatām /
prakṛtivikārayostādātmyāt /
tathā ca prāṇo manasaḥ prakṛtiriti manaso vṛttimataḥ prāṇe laya iti prāpte 'bhidhīyate-- satyam, āpo 'nnamasṛjanta iti śruterabannayoḥ prakṛtivikārabhāvo 'vagamyate /

children.translated_text: But not [dissolution] of the two that are transformations of that [<s>tejas</s>] — namely <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) and <s>manas</s> (mind).

children.text: khayoniprāṇāḍikayā tu mitho vikārayoḥ prakṛtivikārabhāvābhyupagame saṃkarādatiprasaṅgaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: But if mutual transformation-hood (<s>prakṛtivikārabhāva</s>) were accepted between the two [<s>prāṇa</s> and <s>manas</s>] — both being transformations — through the series beginning with space as the source and <s>prāṇa</s> and the like, there would be the absurd consequence of intermixture (<s>saṃkara</s>).

children.text: tasmādyo yasya sākṣādvikārastasya tatra laya ityannasyāpsu layo na tvabvikāre prāṇe 'nnavikārasya manasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, only that which is a direct transformation of something dissolves into that [source] — thus food dissolves into water, but not mind, which is a transformation of food, into <s>prāṇa</s>, which is a transformation of water.

children.text: tathā cātrāpi manovṛttervṛttimati prāṇe layo na tu vṛttimato manasa iti siddham //3 //
children.translated_text: And thus, here too, it is established that the function of mind dissolves into <s>prāṇa</s>, which possesses function — but not the mind that possesses function [dissolves as an entity]. //3//

body.translated_text:
'#That mind [merges] in <s>Prāṇa</s> (the vital breath), because of what follows [in the <s>Śruti</s>]#.'
If the dissolution of a modification in its own material cause [is the rule], then in 'the mind merges in <s>Prāṇa</s>,' the essential nature of the mind itself should merge in <s>Prāṇa</s>.
For thus, 'mind' would not be interpreted figuratively.
For the relation of material cause and modification is possible between <s>Prāṇa</s> and mind.
For the <s>Śruti</s> [says]: 'The mind, O dear one, is made of food' — thus declaring the food-nature of the mind; and 'The <s>Prāṇa</s> is made of water' — thus [declaring] the water-nature of <s>Prāṇa</s>.
Because of the identity of material cause and modification.
And thus, <s>Prāṇa</s> is the material cause of the mind — hence the dissolution of the mind, which possesses function, in <s>Prāṇa</s> [is expected] — against this prima facie view, it is stated: True, by the <s>Śruti</s> 'Water created food,' the relation of material cause and modification between water and food is understood.

body.text:
#so 'dhyakṣe tadupagamādibhyaḥ# /
prāṇastejasīti tejaḥśabdasya bhūtaviśeṣavacanatvādvijñānātmani cāprasiddheḥ prāṇasya jīvātmanyupagamānugamāvasthānaśrutīnāṃ ca tejoddhāreṇāpyupapatteḥ /
tejasi samāpannavṛttiḥ khalu prāṇaḥ /
tejastu jīvātmani samāpannavṛtti /
tadvārā jīvātmasamāpannavṛttiḥ prāṇa ityupapadyate /
tasmāttejasyeva prāṇavṛttipravilaya iti prāpte 'bhidhīyate--- sa prakṛtaḥprāṇo 'dhyakṣe vijñānātmanyavatiṣṭhate tattantravṛttirbhavati /
kutaḥ-- upagamānugamāvasthānebhyo hetubhyaḥ /
tatropagamaśrutimāha-- #evamevemamātmānamiti# /
body.translated_text:
