'#That [<s>prāṇa</s> dissolves] in the superintendent [i.e., the <s>jīvātman</s>], because of [the <s>Śruti</s>s about] approaching and the like#.'
Since '<s>prāṇa</s> [dissolves] in <s>tejas</s> (fire/light)' — and since the word '<s>tejas</s>' denotes a particular element, and since it is not well-known [as a term] for the <s>vijñānātman</s> (cognizing self), and since the <s>Śruti</s>s about the <s>prāṇa</s>'s approaching, following, and abiding in the <s>jīvātman</s> can also be explained by extracting [the role of] <s>tejas</s> [as an intermediary] —
for indeed, <s>prāṇa</s> has its function terminated in <s>tejas</s>,
and <s>tejas</s> has its function terminated in the <s>jīvātman</s>,
and through that [<s>tejas</s> as intermediary], it is tenable that <s>prāṇa</s>'s function terminates in the <s>jīvātman</s>.
Therefore, the dissolution of <s>prāṇa</s>'s function is in <s>tejas</s> alone — this being the prima facie conclusion, it is stated:
That <s>prāṇa</s> under discussion dissolves in the superintendent (<s>adhyakṣa</s>), the <s>vijñānātman</s> (cognizing self) — it becomes dependent on its governance.
Why? Because of the reasons of approaching, following, and abiding.
Therein, he cites the <s>Śruti</s> about approaching: '#Thus indeed this self#' (<s>evamevemamātmānam</s>).

body.text:
anugamanaśrutimāha-- #tamutkrāmantamiti# /
avasthānaśrutimāha- #savijñāno bhavatīti ceti# /
vijñāyate 'neneti vijñānaṃ pañcavṛttiprāṇasahita indriyagrāmastena sahāvatiṣṭhata iti savijñānaḥ /
codayati-- #nanu prāmastejasīti śrūyata iti# /
adhikāvāpo 'śabdārthavyākhyānam /
pariharati-- #naiṣa doṣa iti# /
yadyapi prāṇastejasītyatastejasi prāṇavṛttilayaḥ pratīyate, tathāpi sarvaśākhāpratyayatvena vidyānāṃ śrutyantarālocanayā vijñānātmani layo 'vagamyate /
na ca tejasastatrāpi laya iti sāmpratam /
tasyānilākāśakrameṇa paramātmani tatvalayāvagamāt /
tasmāttejograhaṇenopalakṣyate tejaḥ sahacaritadehabījabhūtapañcabhūtasūkṣmaparicārādhyakṣo jīvātmā tasmin prāṇavṛttirapyetīti /
codayati-- #nanu ceyaṃ śrutiriti# /

children.text: tejaḥsahacaritāni bhūtānyupalakṣyantāṃ tejaḥśabdenādhyakṣe tu kimāyātaṃ tasya tadasāhacaryādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: let the elements accompanied by <s>tejas</s> be indicated by the word '<s>tejas</s>' — but what [basis] is there for [including] the superintendent (<s>adhyakṣa</s>), since he is not accompanied by those [elements]?
He resolves it: '#That in the superintendent#' — [meaning:] of the superintendent too [it is established by the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>so 'dhyakṣe</s>'].

children.text: yadā hyayaṃ prāṇo 'ntarāle 'dhyakṣaṃ prāpyādhyasaṃparkavaśādeva tejaḥprabhṛtīni bhūtasūkṣmāṇi prāpnoti tadopapadyate prāṇastesīti /
children.translated_text: For when this <s>prāṇa</s>, in the intermediate [state], having reached the superintendent (<s>adhyakṣa</s>), attains the subtle elements beginning with <s>tejas</s> by virtue of its connection with the superintendent — then it is tenable [to say] '<s>prāṇa</s> [dissolves] in <s>tejas</s>.'
He gives an illustration for this very [point]: '#Just as one [going] from <s>Srughna</s>#.' //4//

body.translated_text:
He cites the <s>Śruti</s> about following: '#Him departing#' (<s>tamutkrāmantam</s>).
He cites the <s>Śruti</s> about abiding: '#He becomes endowed with <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness)#' (<s>savijñāno bhavati</s>).
That by which things are known is <s>vijñāna</s> — the aggregate of sense-organs together with <s>prāṇa</s> of five functions — he abides together with that, hence 'endowed with <s>vijñāna</s>' (<s>savijñānaḥ</s>).
He raises an objection: '#But is it not heard that <s>prāṇa</s> [dissolves] in <s>tejas</s>?#' (<s>nanu prāṇastejasīti śrūyate</s>).
[This is] an explanation of the meaning that involves an additional [element] not [directly] conveyed by the words.
He resolves it: '#There is no fault in this#' (<s>naiṣa doṣaḥ</s>).
Although from '<s>prāṇa</s> [dissolves] in <s>tejas</s>' the dissolution of <s>prāṇa</s>'s function in <s>tejas</s> is understood, nevertheless — since <s>vidyā</s>s are common to all <s>Śākhā</s>s (Vedic recensions) — by examining other <s>Śruti</s>s, the dissolution in the <s>vijñānātman</s> (cognizing self) is understood.
And it is not appropriate [to say] that <s>tejas</s> too dissolves there [in the <s>vijñānātman</s>].
Because the real dissolution of that [<s>tejas</s>] is understood [as occurring] in the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) through the sequence of air and space.
Therefore, by the mention of <s>tejas</s>, what is indicated (<s>upalakṣita</s>) is the <s>jīvātman</s> who is the superintendent of the subtle elements of the five <s>bhūta</s>s (elements) — which are the seeds of the body, accompanied by <s>tejas</s> — [and it is] into him that the function of <s>prāṇa</s> too enters.
He raises an objection: '#But this <s>Śruti</s>...#' (<s>nanu ceyaṃ śrutiḥ</s>).

body.text:
sūtrāntaramavatārayituṃ pṛcchati-- #kathaṃ tejaḥsahacariteṣviti /
naikasmindarśayato hi# /
atra bhāṣyakāro 'numānadarśanamāha-- #kāryasya śarīrasyeti# /
sthūlaśarīrānurūpamanumeyaṃ sūkṣmamapi śarīraṃ pañcātmakamityarthaḥ /
darśayata iti sūtrāvayavaṃ vyācaṣṭe-- #darśayataścaitamarthamiti# /
praśnaprativacanābhiprāyaṃ dvivacanaṃ śrutismṛtyabhiprāyaṃ vā /
aṇvyo mātrāḥ sūkṣmā daśārdhānāṃ pañcabhūtānāmiti /
śrutyantaravirodhaṃ codayati-- #nanu copasaṃhṛteṣu vāgādiṣviti# /
karmāśrayateti pratīyate na bhūtāśrayatetyarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: He resolves it: '#It is stated here#' (<s>atrocyate</s>).
The <s>graha</s>s (seizers) are the sense-organs; the <s>atigraha</s>s (over-seizers) are their [respective] objects.

The dependence of <s>karma</s>s [on the <s>jīva</s>] is in the capacity of being the impeller (<s>prayojaka</s>); [the dependence] of the elements is in the capacity of being the material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) — thus there is no contradiction.

children.text: praśaṃsāśabdo 'pi karmaṇāṃ prayojakatayā prakṛṣṭamāśrayatvaṃ brūte sati nikṛṣṭa āśrayāntare tadupapatterityāha-- #praśaṃsāśabdādapi tatreti //6 //
children.translated_text: The word 'praise' (<s>praśaṃsā</s>) too indicates that the dependence on <s>karma</s> — being the impeller — is the primary [form of] dependence, while there exists a secondary [form of] dependence [on the elements] — since [the latter] can be established — he says: '#From the word "praise" too, therein#.' //6//

body.translated_text:
In order to introduce another <s>sūtra</s>, he asks: '#How [is it established that the subtle body includes elements] accompanied by <s>tejas</s>?#'
'#For [the <s>Śruti</s>] shows in not just one [element]#.'
Here the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (<s>Śaṅkara</s>) states the inferential demonstration: '#Of the body, which is the effect#.'
The meaning is: the subtle body too, corresponding to the gross body, is to be inferred as composed of five [elements].
He explains the <s>sūtra</s>-portion 'shows' (<s>darśayataḥ</s>): '#And of [the <s>Śruti</s>] that shows this meaning#.'
The dual number [in the <s>sūtra</s>] is either with reference to the question and the answer, or with reference to <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>.
'<s>Aṇvyaḥ mātrāḥ</s>' — subtle [are] the measures, i.e., the subtle [forms] of the ten halved [elements], that is, of the five <s>bhūta</s>s (elements).
He raises an objection from a conflicting <s>Śruti</s>: '#But when speech and the like have been withdrawn#' (<s>nanu copasaṃhṛteṣu vāgādiṣu</s>).
The meaning is: [the <s>Śruti</s>] seems to indicate that [<s>prāṇa</s>] depends on <s>karma</s> (action), not on the elements.

body.text:
samānā cāsṛtyupakramādamṛtatvaṃ cānupoṣya# /
atrābhṛtatvaprāptiśruteḥ paravidyāvantaṃ pratyetaditi manvānasya pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ /
#viśayānānāṃ#saṃdihānānāṃ puṃsām /
codayati-- #nanu vidyāprakaraṇa iti# /
pariharati-- #na svāpādivaditi# /
paravidyayaivāmṛtatvaprāptyavasthāmākhyātuṃ tatsadharmāśca tadvidharmāścānyā apyavasthāstadanuguṇatayākhyāyante /
sādharmyavaidharmyābhyāṃ hi sphuṭataraḥ pratipipādayiṣite vastuni pratyayo bhavatīti /
na tu viduṣaḥ sakāśādviśeṣavanto 'vidvāṃso vidhīyante yena vidyāprakaraṇavyākhyāto bhavedapi tu vidyāṃ pratipādayituṃ lokasiddhānāṃ tadanuguṇatayā teṣāmanuvāda iti /
evaṃ prāpte 'bhidhīyate--- #samānā caiṣotkrāntirvāṅmanasītyādyā vidvadaviduṣoḥ# /
kutaḥ-- #āsṛtyupakṛmāt# /
sṛtiḥ saraṇaṃ devayānena pathā kāryabrahmalokaprāptirāsṛterākāryabrahmalokaprāpteḥ /
ayaṃ vidyopakrama ārambhaḥ prayatna iti yāvat /
tasmādetaduktaṃ bhavati-- neyaṃ parā vidyā yato nāḍīdvāramāśrayate /

children.translated_text: Rather, this is the lower <s>vidyā</s> (<s>aparā vidyā</s>).

children.text: na cāsyāmātyantikaḥ kleśapradāho yato na tatrotkrāntirbhavet /
children.translated_text: And in this [lower <s>vidyā</s>], there is no absolute burning away of the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>s) — hence there would be no departure [through the <s>nāḍī</s>s in the case of the higher <s>vidyā</s>].

Therefore, through the power of the lower <s>vidyā</s>, this teaching about the differentiation of departure — which seeks immortality as the relative state of non-dissolution in the elements (<s>bhūtasaṃplava</s>) — is established as serving the person's purpose (<s>puruṣārtha</s>).
From the root '<s>uṣ</s>' (to burn) preceded by the prefix '<s>upa</s>' (<s>dāha</s> — burning), the usage '<s>upoṣya</s>' (having burnt/reached) is derived. //7//

body.translated_text:
'#And the departure is the same; and without reaching immortality#.'
Here, one who thinks that the <s>Śruti</s> about the attainment of immortality pertains to the knower of the higher <s>vidyā</s> — [this constitutes] the prima facie view.
'#Of diverse ones#' — of people who are in doubt.
He raises an objection: '#But [this is] in the context of <s>vidyā</s>#' (<s>nanu vidyāprakaraṇe</s>).
He resolves it: '#Not so, as in sleep and the like#' (<s>na svāpādivat</s>).
In order to describe the state of attainment of immortality through the higher <s>vidyā</s> alone, other states too — those that share characteristics with it and those that differ from it — are described in conformity with it.
For through similarities and dissimilarities, the understanding of the thing intended to be taught becomes clearer.
But it is not the case that persons who are distinct from the knower — the ignorant — are being enjoined [to do something], such that [the passage] would be explained as belonging to the context of <s>vidyā</s>; rather, for the purpose of teaching <s>vidyā</s>, those [states] that are well-known in the world are restated in conformity with it.
This being the prima facie conclusion, it is stated: '#The departure is indeed the same — [the process beginning with] speech [dissolving] into mind and the like — for the knower and the ignorant alike#.'
Why? '#Because of the beginning with departure (<s>sṛti</s>)#.'
<s>Sṛti</s> means 'going' — the attainment of the <s>Brahmaloka</s> that is an effect, through the <s>Devayāna</s> (path of the gods); '<s>āsṛti</s>' means 'up to the attainment of the <s>Brahmaloka</s> that is not an effect.'
This is the beginning, the commencement, the endeavor of <s>vidyā</s>.
Therefore, what is being said is this: this is not the higher <s>vidyā</s>, because it takes recourse to the channel of the <s>nāḍī</s>s (subtle channels).

body.text:
#tadāpīteḥ saṃsāravyapadeśāt# /
siddhāṃ kṛtvā bījabhāvāvaśeṣaṃ paramātmasaṃpattiṃ vidvadaviduṣorutkrāntiḥ samarthitā /
saiva saṃprati cintyate /
kimātmani tejaḥprabhṛtīnāṃ bhūtasūkṣmāṇāṃ tatvapravilaya eva saṃpattirāhosvidbījabhāvāvaśeṣeti /
yadi pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ,
body.translated_text:
'#Because of the designation of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) upon that approach (<s>āpīti</s>)#.'
Having established the departure (<s>utkrānti</s>) of both the knower and the ignorant — with the attainment of the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) in seed-form (<s>bījabhāvāvaśeṣa</s>) — that very [attainment] is now being examined.
Does the attainment (<s>saṃpatti</s>) of the subtle elements beginning with <s>tejas</s> in the self consist in their real dissolution into it, or does it retain a seed-form (<s>bījabhāvāvaśeṣa</s>)?
If the former view [holds],

body.text: notkrāntiḥ /

children.translated_text: But if the latter [view holds], then departure follows from that.

children.text: tatrāprakṛtau na vikāratatvapravilayo yathā manasi na vāgādīnām /
children.translated_text: And therein, there is no real dissolution of transformation into [something that is] not its [direct] material cause — just as there is no [real dissolution of] speech and the like into mind [which is not their direct cause].

children.text: sarvasya ca janimataḥ prakṛtiḥ parā devateti tattvapralaya evātyantikaḥ syāttejaḥprabhṛtīnāmiti prāpte 'bhidhīyate-- 'yonimanye prapadyante śarīratvāya dehinaḥ /
children.translated_text: And since the ultimate material cause (<s>prakṛti</s>) of everything that has originated is the Supreme Deity (<s>parā devatā</s>), the absolute dissolution of <s>tejas</s> and the like [elements] would be [only] into that — this being the prima facie conclusion, it is stated: 'Some enter a womb for embodiment,
others enter a stationary [state] — in accordance with [their] <s>karma</s> and [their] knowledge.'

body.translated_text: there is no departure (<s>utkrānti</s>) [i.e., no rebirth would follow].

body.text:
' ityavidyāvataḥ saṃsāramupadiśati śrutiḥ seyamātyantike tattvalaye nopapadyate /
na ca prāyaṇasyaivaiṣa mahimā vidvāsamavidvāṃsaṃ vā pratīti sāṃpratamityāha-- #anyathā hi sarvaḥ prāyaṇasamaya eveti# /

children.translated_text: The injunctive scripture concerning <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and the like would be purposeless — since, upon absolute dissolution at death, there would be no rebirth.
And the scripture of liberation too [would be purposeless] — since every creature would attain liberation effortlessly, through death alone.
Not only would the scriptures be purposeless, but liberation through mere death is also unreasonable — he says: '#[Because of] false knowledge#' (<s>mithyājñāna</s>).
The meaning is: without the cessation of the cause [i.e., false knowledge], the cessation of that which is caused by it [i.e., <s>saṃsāra</s>] is not tenable. //8//

body.translated_text:
Thus the <s>Śruti</s> teaches <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) for one who possesses <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — and this is untenable if there were absolute dissolution into reality.
And it is not appropriate [to say] that this is merely the glory of death itself — whether for the knower or the ignorant — he says: '#For otherwise, every [being] at the very time of death#' (<s>anyathā hi sarvaḥ prāyaṇasamaya eva</s>).

body.text:
athetarabhūtasahitaṃ tejo jīvasyāśrayabhūtamutkrāntamaddehāddehāntaraṃ vā saṃcaratkasmādasmābhirna nirīkṣyate /
taddhi mahattvādvānekadravyatvādvā rūpavadupalabdavyam /
kasmānna mūrtāntaraiḥ pratibadhyata iti śaṅkāmapākartumidaṃ sūtram-- #sūkṣmaṃ pramāṇataśca tathopalabdheḥ# /
cakāre bhinnakramaḥ /
na kevalamāpītestadavatiṣṭhate /
tacca sūkṣmaṃ svarūpataḥ parimāṇataśca svarūpameva hi tasya tādṛśamadṛśyam /
yathā cākṣuṣasya tejaso mahato 'pi adṛṣṭavaśādanudbhūtarūpasparśaṃ hi tat /
parimāṇataḥ saukṣmyaṃ yato nopalabhyate yathā trasareṇavo jālasūryamarīcibhyo 'nyatra pramāṇatastathopalabdhiriti vyācaṣṭe-- #tathāhi nāḍīniṣkramaṇa iti# /
ādigrahaṇena cakṣuṣṭo vā mūrdho vā anyebhyo vā śarīradeśebhya iti saṃgṛhītam /

children.translated_text: He states the reason for [its] non-obstruction: '#because of [its] transparency#' (<s>svacchatvāt</s>).
And this too is comprehended under subtlety alone.

children.text: yathā hi kācābhrapaṭalaṃ svacchasvabhāvasya na tejasaḥ pratidhātam /
children.translated_text: For just as a glass or a cloud-sheet cannot obstruct <s>tejas</s> (light), which is transparent by nature,
so too [does] the entire class of objects [fail to obstruct] this [subtle body]. //9//

body.translated_text:
Now, if the <s>tejas</s> (fire-element) together with the other subtle elements — serving as the basis of the <s>jīva</s> — having departed from this body, travels to another body, why is it not observed by us?
For it should be perceivable as having form (<s>rūpavat</s>), either because of its large size or because of being composed of many substances.
Why is it not obstructed by other material objects? — To remove this doubt, this <s>sūtra</s> [is stated]: '#[It is] subtle, and in measure too — because of the observation of that [subtlety]#.'
The [particle] '<s>ca</s>' is out of sequence.
Not only does it continue to exist upon that approach (<s>āpīti</s>),
but it is subtle — both in its own nature and in its measure. For its own nature is indeed such — invisible.
Just as visible <s>tejas</s> (fire/light), though large, [can be invisible] — because through the power of <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit), its form and touch are unmanifested.
The subtlety in measure, due to which it is not perceived — just as atoms (<s>trasareṇu</s>s) [are not perceived] apart from sunbeams [coming through] a lattice — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] explains 'the observation of that' (<s>tathopalabdhi</s>): '#For it is observed exiting through the <s>nāḍī</s>s (channels)#.'
By the word 'and the like' (<s>ādi</s>), [it is indicated that the departure is] from the eye, or from the crown of the head, or from other parts of the body.

children.translated_text: '#[There is] no crushing, therefore#.'
And for this very reason — because of the subtlety characterized as transparency, [which is] another name for non-attachment (<s>asaktatva</s>). //10//
'#And the tenability of this alone [explains] this warmth#.'
<s>Upapatti</s> (tenability) means attainment.

children.text: etaduktaṃ bhavati-- dṛṣṭaśrutābhyāmūṣmaṇo 'nvayavyatirekābhyāmasti sthūlāddehādatiriktaṃ kiñciccadāmātsūkṣmaṃ śarīramiti //11 //
children.translated_text: What is being said is this: Through the observed and heard positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>) of warmth, it is established that there exists something beyond the gross body — a subtle body that is always [associated with the <s>jīva</s>]. //11//

body.text:
#pratiṣedhāditi cenna śārīrāt# /
adhikaraṇatātparyamāha-- #amṛtatvaṃ cīnupoṣyetyato viśeṣaṇāditi# /
viṣayamāha-- #athākāmayamāna iti# /
siddhāntimatamāśaṅkya tannirākaraṇena pūrvapakṣī svamatamavasthāpayati-- #ataḥ paravidyāviṣayātpratiṣedhāditi# /
yadi hi prāṇopalakṣitasya sūkṣmaśarīrasya jīvātmanaḥ sthūlaśarīrādutkrāntiṃ pratiṣedhecchrutiḥ tata etadupapadyate /

children.translated_text: But this is not the case.

children.text: na tasmātprāṇa utkrāmantīti hi tadā sarvanāmnā pradhānāvamarśinābhyudayaniḥ śreyasādhikṛto dehi pradhānaṃ parāmṛśyate /
children.translated_text: In '<s>prāṇa</s>s do not depart from him' — at that time, by the universal term [referring to all <s>prāṇa</s>s], the principal [referent] being the embodied self (<s>dehin</s>) who is entitled to both prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>) and the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>), it is the principal [self] that is being referred to.

children.text: tathā ca tasmāddehino na prāṇaḥ sūkṣmaṃ śarīramutkrāmantyapi tu tatsahitaḥ kṣetrajña evotkrāmatīti gamyate /
children.translated_text: And thus, [the meaning is:] from that embodied self, not the <s>prāṇa</s> [as] the subtle body departs — rather, the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field) himself, together with that [<s>prāṇa</s>], departs.

children.text: sa punaratikramya brahmanāḍya saṃsāramaṇḍalaṃ hiraṇyagarbhaparyantaṃ saliṅgo jīvaḥ parasminbrahmaṇi līyate tasmātparāmapi devatāṃ viduṣa utkrāntirata eva mārgaśrutayaḥ, smṛtiśca mumukṣoḥ śukasyādityamaṇḍalaprasthānaṃ darśayatīti prāptam //12 //
children.translated_text: And he — the <s>jīva</s> with his characteristics (<s>saliṅga</s>) — having traversed through the <s>Brahma-nāḍī</s> the realm of <s>saṃsāra</s> extending up to <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, dissolves in the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>. Therefore, for the knower too there is departure beyond even the [supreme] deity — hence the <s>Śruti</s>s about the path [apply]. And the <s>Smṛti</s> too shows the departure of the <s>mumukṣu</s> (seeker of liberation) — the bright one (<s>śuka</s>) — toward the orb of the sun — this is the prima facie conclusion. //12//

body.translated_text:
'#If [it be objected] that [there is] a negation, [we say:] not so, because [the negation pertains to] the embodied [self, not the departure]#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the purport of the topic: '#Because of the qualifier "and without reaching immortality"#.'
He states the subject: '#Now, the one who is without desires#' (<s>athākāmayamānaḥ</s>).
Having assumed the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion) and refuting it, the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> (prima facie opponent) establishes his own view: '#Therefore, because of the negation [stated] in the context of the higher <s>vidyā</s>#.'
For if the <s>Śruti</s> were to negate the departure of the <s>jīvātman</s> — who is indicated by <s>prāṇa</s> and accompanied by the subtle body — from the gross body, then this [prima facie view] would be tenable.

body.text:
evaṃ prāpte pratyucyate-- #spaṣṭo hyekeṣām# /
nāyaṃ dehyapādānasya pratiṣedhaḥ /
api tu dehāpādānasya /
tathā hi -- ārtabhāgapraśnottare hyekasminpakṣe saṃsāriṇa eva jīvātmano 'nutkrāntiṃ parigṛhya na tarhyeṣa bhṛtaḥ prāṇānāmanutkrānteriti svayamāśaṅkya prāṇānāṃ pravilayaṃ pratijñāya tatsiddhyarthamutkrāntyavadherucchvayanādhmāne bruvanyasyocchvayanādhmāne tasya tadavadhitvamāha /
śarīrasya ca te itiśarīrameva tadapādānaṃ gamyate /
nanvevamapyastvaviduṣaḥ saṃsāriṇo viduṣastu kimāyātamityata āha-- #tatsāmānyāditi# /
nanu tadā sarvanāmnā pradhānatayā dehi parāmṛṣṭaḥ tatkathamatra dehāvagatirityata āha-- #tatsāmānyaditi# /
nanu tadā sarvanāmnā pradhānatayā dehī parāmṛṣṭaḥ tatkathamatra dehāvagatirityata āha-- #abhedopacāreṇa# /
dehadehinordehiparāmarśinā sarvanāmnā deha eva parāmṛṣṭa iti pañcamīpāṭhe vyākhyeyam /
ṣaṣṭhīpāṭhe tu nopacāra ityāha-- #yeṣāṃ tu ṣaṣṭhīti# /
api ca prāptipūrvaḥ pratiṣedho bhavati nāprāpte /
aviduṣo hi dehādutkrāmaṇaṃ dṛṣṭamiti viduṣo 'pi tatsāmānyāddehādutkramaṇe prāpte pratiṣedha upapadyate na tu prāṇānāṃ jīvāvadhikaṃ kvacidutkramaṇaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yena tanniṣidhyate /
apicādvaitaparibhāvanābhuvā prasaṃkhyānena nirmṛṣṭanikhilaprapañcāvabhāsajātasya gantavyābhāvādeva nāsti gatirityāha-- #naca brahmavida iti# /

children.text: apadasya hi brahmavido mārge padaiṣiṇo 'pi devā iti yojanā /
children.translated_text: The construction is: even the gods who seek a path do not [find a path] for the knower of <s>Brahman</s> who has no destination (<s>apada</s>).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises an objection: '#But the journey too#' — thus.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] resolves: '#This [journey] is for one [still] embodied, by the power of <s>yoga</s>#' — thus.
By the power of the lower <s>vidyā</s> (<s>aparavidyā</s>). //13//

body.translated_text:
With this prima facie view established, the reply is given: '#For some [<s>Śākhā</s>s it is] explicit#.'
This is not a negation of [departure] from the embodied self (<s>dehin</s>) as the source (<s>apādāna</s>),
but rather of the body as the source.
For thus: in the question and answer of <s>Ārtabhāga</s>, in one interpretation, having accepted the non-departure of the <s>jīvātman</s> (individual self) who is a transmigrator, [<s>Yājñavalkya</s>] himself raises the doubt 'Then this one is not sustained, because the <s>prāṇa</s>s do not depart'; having declared the dissolution of the <s>prāṇa</s>s, [and] for the purpose of establishing that, while stating the swelling and inflation as the limit-indicator of departure, he says 'of that one whose swelling and inflation [occur], that is the limit-indicator.'
'And of the body, yours' — thus the body alone is understood as the source.
But [one might say:] even so, let this be for the ignorant transmigrator; but what does it establish for the knower? — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Because of the similarity with that#' — thus.
But [one might object:] at that time, by the pronoun [he/that], the embodied self (<s>dehin</s>) was primarily referred to; how then is the understanding of the body [obtained] here? — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Because of the similarity with that#' — thus.
But [one might object:] at that time, by the pronoun, the embodied self (<s>dehin</s>) was primarily referred to; how then is the understanding of the body [obtained] here? — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#By figurative identification (<s>abhedopacāra</s>)#.'
In the reading with the ablative case (<s>pañcamī</s>), this should be explained [as follows]: by the pronoun — which refers to the embodied self — the body alone is [figuratively] referred to, through the figurative identification of body and embodied self.
But in the reading with the genitive case (<s>ṣaṣṭhī</s>), there is no figurative usage — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#But for those [who read] with the genitive#' — thus.
Moreover, a negation is preceded by [something's] being prima facie established — not [applied] to what is not prima facie established.
For the departure of the ignorant from the body is observed — hence, because of the similarity [of the knower] with that [ignorant person], when departure from the body is prima facie established for the knower too, the negation is tenable. But nowhere is the departure of the <s>prāṇa</s>s beyond the <s>jīva</s> [as their limit] observed, such that it would be negated.
Moreover, for the knower of <s>Brahman</s> — whose entire phenomenal appearance has been effaced by the <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s> (contemplative reflection) born of the thorough cultivation of non-duality — since there is nowhere to go, there is no journey — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#And for the knower of <s>Brahman</s>#' — thus.

body.text:
#tāni pare tathāhyāha# /
pratiṣṭhāvilayanaśrutyorvipratipattervimarśastamapanetumayamārambhaḥ /
tāni punaḥ prāṇaśabdoditānīndriyāṇyekādaśa sūkṣmāṇi ca bhūtāni pañca /
#brahmavidastasminneva parasminnātmanīti# /
ārambhabījaṃ vimarśamāha-- #nanu gatāḥkalā iti# /
ghrāṇamanasorekaprakṛtitvaṃ vivakṣitvā pañcadaśatvamuktam. /
atra śrutyorviṣayavyavasthayā vipratipattyabhāvamāha--- #sā khalviti# /

children.translated_text: The conventional (<s>vyavahāra</s>) [usage] is worldly. This <s>Śruti</s> depends on the conventional means of knowledge.
It does not depend on the ultimate means of knowledge.

children.text: itarā tu evamevāsya paridṛṣṭuḥ ityādikā vidvatpratipattyapekṣā tāttvikapramāṇāpekṣā /
children.translated_text: But the other [<s>Śruti</s>] — 'Thus indeed of this seer' (<s>evam evāsya paridṛṣṭuḥ</s>) and the like — depends on the ultimate means of knowledge, since it concerns the cognition of the knower.
Therefore, because of the domain-distinction, there is no conflict between the two <s>Śruti</s>s. //15//

body.translated_text:
'#Those [<s>prāṇa</s>s] dissolve in the Supreme — for thus [the <s>Śruti</s>] declares#.'
Because of the conflict between the <s>Śruti</s>s about the establishment [of the <s>prāṇa</s>s in the body] and [their] dissolution, this inquiry is undertaken to remove [the conflict].
Those [entities] denoted by the word '<s>prāṇa</s>' are the eleven subtle sense-organs and the five subtle elements.
'#Of the knower of <s>Brahman</s>, in that very supreme Self#' — thus.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the seed of the inquiry — the doubt: '#But the <s>kalā</s>s (parts) have gone#' — thus.
Having expressed the single-origin-ness of the sense of smell and the mind, the number sixteen is stated.
Here [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the absence of conflict through the domain-distinction of the two <s>Śruti</s>s: '#That indeed#' — thus.

body.text:
#avibhāgo vacanāt# /
nimittāpāye naimittikasyātyantikāpāyaḥ /
avidyānimittaśca vibhāgo nāvidyāyāṃ vidyayā samūlaghātamapahatāyāṃ sāvaśeṣo bhavitumarhati /
body.translated_text:
'#Non-differentiation, because of the [<s>Śruti</s>] statement#.'
When the cause (<s>nimitta</s>) ceases, the effect (<s>naimittika</s>) ceases absolutely.
And differentiation is caused by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — [hence] when <s>avidyā</s> is destroyed root and all by <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), [differentiation] cannot remain with any residue.

body.text: tathāpi pravilayasāmānyāt sāvaśeṣatāśaṅkāmatimandāmapanetumidaṃ sūtram //16 //
body.translated_text: Nevertheless, to remove the extremely dull doubt about [its] remaining with a residue — [a doubt arising] from the general [observation of] dissolution [in other cases] — this <s>sūtra</s> [is stated]. //16//

body.text:
#tadokograjvalavaṃ tatprakāśitadvāro vidyāsāmarthyāttaccheṣagatyanusmṛtiyogācca hārdānugṛhītaḥ śatādhikayā# /
aparavidyāvido 'viduṣaścotkrāntiruktā /
tatra kiṃ vidvānavidvāṃścāviśeṣeṇa mūrdhādibhya utkrāmatyāho vidvānmūrdhasthānādeva, apare tu sthānāntarebhya iti /
atra vidyāsāmarthyamapaśyataḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ /
tasyopasaṃhṛtavāgādikalāpasyocciktamiṣato vijñānātmanā oka āyatanaṃ hṛdayaṃ tasyāgraṃ tasya jvalanaṃ yattatprakāśitadvāro viniṣkramadvāro vidvānmūrdhasthānādeva niṣkrāmati nānyebhyaścakṣurādisthānebhyaḥ /
kutaḥ-- vidyāsāmarthāt hārdavidyāsāmarthyāt /
utkṛṣṭasthānapratilambhāya hi hārdavidyopadeśaḥ /
mūrdhasthānādaniṣkramaṇe ca notkṛṣṭadeśaprāptiḥ /

children.translated_text: But [one might ask:] even when departing from other openings, why does [the soul] not attain an exalted world? — to this [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#And because of the practice of recollecting the path that is subsidiary to that [<s>vidyā</s>]#.'

children.text: hārdavidyāśeṣabhūtā hi mūrdhanyā nāḍī gatyai upadiṣṭā /
children.translated_text: For the <s>nāḍī</s> (channel) going to the head, being subsidiary to the <s>vidyā</s> that resides in the heart, is taught for the purpose of the journey.

children.text: tadanuśīlanena khalvayaṃ jīvo hārdena sūpāsitena brahmaṇānugṛhītastasyānusmaraṃstadbhāvamāpanno mūrdhanyayaiva śatādhikayā nāḍya niṣkrāmati /
children.translated_text: And this <s>jīva</s>, by virtue of practicing [the recollection of] that [channel], being favored by <s>Brahman</s> in the heart — which has been well-worshipped — and remembering It, having attained Its nature, departs through that very <s>nāḍī</s> going to the head — the one that is more than a hundred [in number].

children.text: hṛdayādudgatā hi brahmanāḍī bhāsvarā tālumūlaṃ bhittvā mūrdhānametya raśmibhirekībhūtā ādityamaṇḍalamanupraviṣṭā tāmanuśīlayatastayaivāntakāle nirgamanaṃ bhavatīti //17 //
children.translated_text: For the <s>brahmanāḍī</s> (the channel of <s>Brahman</s>), luminous, having arisen from the heart, having pierced the root of the palate and reached the head, having become one with the rays [of the sun], enters the solar disc. For one who practices [the recollection of] that [channel], departure at the time of death occurs through that very [channel]. //17//

body.translated_text:
'#[The soul goes out] through the opening of the head — the self-luminous flame of that [<s>Brahman</s>], the door illuminated by that [flame], by the power of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), by the practice of recollecting the path that is subsidiary to that [<s>vidyā</s>], and being favored by [<s>Brahman</s>] in the heart, through the <s>nāḍī</s> (channel) that is more than a hundred [in number]#.'
The departure (<s>utkrānti</s>) of the knower of the lower <s>vidyā</s> (<s>aparavidyā</s>) and of the ignorant has been stated.
Therein, the question is: does the knower and the ignorant depart without distinction from the head and the other [openings], or does the knower depart from the head-opening alone, while the others [depart] from other openings?
Herein, the prima facie view belongs to one who does not see the power of <s>vidyā</s>.
For [the soul] that has withdrawn its aggregate of speech and the other [faculties], desiring to depart with the <s>vijñānātman</s> (cognizing self) — the abode (<s>oka</s>), the seat, is the heart; its tip (<s>agra</s>), its luminous flame (<s>jvalana</s>) — that which illuminates the door [of departure]; through the door illuminated by that [flame], the knower departs from the head-opening alone, not from the other openings such as the eye and the rest.
Why? — Because of the power of <s>vidyā</s> — the power of the <s>vidyā</s> that resides in the heart.
For the instruction of <s>vidyā</s> residing in the heart is for the purpose of attaining an exalted destination.
And if one does not depart from the head-opening, there is no attainment of an exalted destination.

children.translated_text: '#Following the rays [of the sun]#.'

children.text: rātrāvahani cāviśeṣeṇa raśmyanusārī sannādityamaṇḍalaṃ prāpnotīti siddhāntapakṣapratijñā //18 //
children.translated_text: Without distinction between night and day, following the rays, [the soul] reaches the solar disc — this is the statement of the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>). //18//

body.text:
pūrvapakṣamāśaṅkate sūtrāvayavena-- #niśi neti cet# /
sūtrāvayavāntareṇa nirākaroti--- #na saṃbandhasya yāvaddehabhāvitvāddarśayati#pramāṇāntarātpratīyate /
darśayati caitamarthaṃ śrutirapyaśeṣeṇa /
amuṣmādādityātpratāyante raśmayanta āsu nāḍīṣu sṛptā bhavanti ya ābhyo nāḍībhyaḥ pratāyante #a#vistāryante te raśmayo 'muṣminnāditye sṛptāḥ /
#pratāpādikāryadarśanāditi# /
ādigrahaṇena candrāpaḥ saṃgṛhyante /
candramasā khalvaṃmayena saṃbadhyamānānāṃ sūrīṇāṃ bhāsāṃ candrikātvam /
tasmādapyasti niśi sauryaraśmipracāra iti /
ye tyāhuḥ-- sa yāvatkṣipyenmanastāvadādityaṃ gacchediti nirapekṣaśravaṇādrātrau prete nāsti raśmyapekṣeti /
tānpratyāha--
body.translated_text:
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises the prima facie view through a portion of the <s>sūtra</s>: '#If [it be said that] at night, [it is] not [possible]#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes through another portion of the <s>sūtra</s>: '#No, because the connection [of rays with the <s>nāḍī</s>s] lasts as long as the body endures — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] shows [this]#' — it is known from another means of valid knowledge.
And the <s>Śruti</s> too shows this meaning completely:
'From that sun rays extend; they become inserted into these <s>nāḍī</s>s. Those that extend from these <s>nāḍī</s>s' — are spread out — 'those rays become inserted into that sun.'
'#Because of the observation of the effects such as heat (<s>pratāpa</s>) and the like#.'
By the word 'and the like,' the moon and water are included.
For the lustre of the rays — belonging to the sun — when connected with the moon, which is of watery nature, becomes moonlight.
Therefore, even at night there is the operation of the solar rays.
As for those who say: 'As quickly as the mind goes, so quickly does one go to the sun' — [meaning that] from this <s>Śruti</s> [heard] without qualification, for one who departs at night there is no dependence on rays — to them [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says:

body.text:
#yadi ca rātrau preta iti /
nahyetadviśiṣyādhīyate '#dhyetāraḥ /
ye tu manyante vidvānapi rātriprāyaṇāparādhena nordhvamākramata iti tānpratyāha-- #atha tu vidvānapīti# /

children.text: nityavatphalasaṃbandhena vihitā vidyā na pākṣikaphalā yukteti /
children.translated_text: <s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge), being enjoined with a connection to fruit that is [treated as] permanent (<s>nityavat</s>), is not appropriate [to have] a fruit that is merely occasional (<s>pākṣika</s>).

children.text: ye tu rātrau pretasya viduṣo 'harapekṣāṃ sūryamaṇḍalaprāptirācakṣate tanmatamāśaṅkyāha--- #athāpi rātrāviti# /
children.translated_text: As for those who state that for the knower who has departed at night, the attainment of the solar disc requires waiting for daytime — having raised that view, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#But even if at night#' — thus.
For [the <s>Śruti</s>] has declared the journey without any [such] dependence, according to all the qualifications stated [in the text].
And [such] dependence cannot be cognized, because of the conflict with [the text's] qualifications. //19//

body.translated_text:
'#If [it be said that one who] departs at night#' — thus.
For this [<s>Śruti</s>] is not recited with any such specification — [i.e.,] the reciters [do not read it that way].
As for those who think that even a knower, by the fault of departing at night, does not ascend upward — to them [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#But even if a knower#' — thus.

body.text:
#ataścāyane 'pi dakṣiṇe# /
ata evetyuktahetuparāmarśa ityāha-- #ata eva codīkṣānupapatteriti# /
pūrvapakṣabījamāha-- #uttarāyaṇamaraṇaprāśastya iti# /
apanodamāha-- #prāśastyaprasiddhiriti# /

children.translated_text: Therefore, by the force of the reason referred to by the word 'hence,' death in the <s>uttarāyaṇa</s> is praiseworthy for the ignorant; but for the knower, there is no distinction [between the two solstices], because of the power of <s>vidyā</s>.

children.text: viduṣo 'pi ca bhīṣmasyottarāyaṇapratīkṣaṇamaviduṣa ācāraṃ grāha- yati 'yadyadācarati śreṣṭhastattadevetaro janaḥ' iti nyāyāt /
children.translated_text: And even the waiting for the <s>uttarāyaṇa</s> by <s>Bhīṣma</s> — who was a knower — [served to] teach the practice for the ignorant, by the principle 'Whatever the best [person] does, other people [follow] that.'

children.text: āpūryamāṇapakṣādityādyā ca śrutirna kālaviśeṣapratipattyarthā, api tvātivāhikīrdevatāḥ pratipādayatīti vakṣyati /
children.translated_text: And the <s>Śruti</s> 'during the waxing fortnight' (<s>āpūryamāṇapakṣāt</s>) and the like is not for the purpose of specifying a particular time, but rather [the commentary will state that it] teaches the escorting deities (<s>ātivāhikī devatā</s>s).
Therefore, there is no conflict. //20//

body.translated_text:
'#For this very reason, even in the southern course (<s>dakṣiṇāyana</s>)#.'
'For this very reason' — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refers back to the previously stated reason: '#For this very reason, because of the untenable waiting#' — thus.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the seed of the prima facie view: '#The praiseworthiness of death in the <s>uttarāyaṇa</s> (northern course)#' — thus.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the refutation: '#The praiseworthiness is not well-known [as applying to the knower]#' — thus.

body.text:
sūtrāntarāvataraṇāya codayati-- #nanu ca yatra kāle tviti# /
kāla evātra prādhānyenocyate na tvātivāhikī devatetyarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: '#And for the <s>yogin</s>s, [the time-distinction] is remembered — and these are <s>Smṛti</s>-based [teachings]#.'

children.text: smārtīmupāsanāṃ pratyayaṃ smārtaḥ kālabhedaviniyogaḥ pratyāsatteḥ na tu śrautīṃ pratītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: This <s>Smṛti</s>-based assignment of time-distinctions pertains to the <s>Smṛti</s>-based <s>upāsanā</s> (meditation), because of its proximity — not to the <s>Śrauta</s> (Vedic) [meditation] — this is the meaning.

children.text: atra yadi smṛtau kālabhedavidhiḥ śrautau cāgnijyotirādividhistatrāgnyādīnāmātivāhikatayā viṣayavyavasthayā virodhābhāva uktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, if the <s>Smṛti</s> contains an injunction of time-distinction and the <s>Śruti</s> contains an injunction of fire, light, and the like, then — [since] fire and the like are [understood as] escorting [deities] — the absence of conflict through domain-distinction has been stated.

children.text: atha pratyabhijñānaṃ tathāpi yatra kāla ityatrāpi kālābhidhānadvāreṇātivāhikya eva devatā uktā ityavirodha eveti //21 //
children.translated_text: But if there is recognition [of the same path in both], even so — in 'at whatever time' and the like — even through the medium of mentioning time, it is the escorting deities alone that are stated — hence there is no conflict at all. //21//

body.translated_text:
To introduce the next <s>sūtra</s>, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises an objection: '#But the <s>Śruti</s> "at whatever time"#' — thus.
Here, time is stated as the principal [factor], not the escorting deity — this is the meaning.

body.text: iti śrīvācaspatimiśraviracite śārīrakabhāṣyavibhāge bhāmatyāṃ caturthasyādhyāyasya dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ //2 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the second <s>pāda</s> of the fourth <s>adhyāya</s> in the <s>Bhāmatī</s>, the elucidation of the <s>Śārīraka-Bhāṣya</s>, composed by the venerable <s>Vācaspati Miśra</s>. //2//

body.text: #caturthe 'dhyāye tṛtīyaḥ pāṭhaḥ#
body.translated_text: '#The fourth <s>adhyāya</s>, the third <s>pāda</s>#.'

children.translated_text: '#By the path of light (<s>Arcirādi</s>) — because of the well-known [teaching about it]#.'
Because of being situated in different contexts, because of being connected with different meditations,
the paths, being mutually independent — [this follows] also from the determination of speed. //

children.text: gantavyamekaṃ nagaraṃ prati vakreṇādhvanā gatimapekṣya ṛjunādhvanā gatistvarāvatī kalpyate /
children.translated_text: With respect to a single destination — [just as] one who goes to a [single] city by a crooked road, hastiness is construed [relative to] one going by a straight road.
But when there is a single path, with respect to whom would there be hastiness?

children.text: atha taireva raśmibhirityavadhāraṇaṃ nopapadyate pathyantarasya nivartanīyasyābhāvāttasmātparānapekṣā evaite panthāna ekabrahmalokaprāptyupāyā vrīhiyavāviva vikalperanniti prāpte pratyucyate- ekatve 'pi patho 'nekaparvavasaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: But [one might say:] the emphatic determination 'by those very rays' is untenable because there is no other path to be excluded. Therefore, these paths — being independently [taught as] means for attaining the single <s>Brahmaloka</s> — would be alternatives, like rice and barley — with this prima facie view, the reply is: even though the path is one, because of the possibility of multiple stages (<s>parva</s>s),
because of the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of recognition, there is no multiplicity, [and] the heaviness [of such a view would be avoided]. //

body.text:
saparvā hi panthā nagarādikamekaṃ gantavyaṃ prāpayati nābhāgaḥ /
tatra kimete raśmyaharvāyusūryādayo 'dhvanaḥ parvāṇaḥ santo 'dhvanaikena yujyante, āho yathāyathamadhvānamapi bhindantīti saṃdehe 'bhede 'pyadhvano bhāgabhedopapatterna bhāgibhedakalpanocitā, gauravaprasaṅgāt /
ekadeśapratyabhijñānācca viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvopapatternānekādhvakalpanā / athaitaireva raśmibhirityavadhāraṇaṃ na tāvadarthāntaranivṛttyarthaṃ tatprāpakaireva vākyāntarairvirodhāt, tasmādanyānapekṣāmasyāvadhārayatīti vaktavyam /
na caikaṃ vākyamaprāptamadhvānaṃ prāpayati tasya cānapekṣatāṃ pratipādayatītyarthadvayāya paryāptaṃ, tasmādvidhisāmarthyaprāptamayogavyavacchedamevakāro 'nuvadatīti yuktam /
#tvarāvacanaṃ ceti# /
na khalvekasminneva gantavye pathibhedamapekṣya tvarāvakalpyate kintu gantavyabhedādapi tadupapattiḥ /
yathā kaśmīrebhyo mathurāṃ kṣipraṃ yāti caitra iti tathehāpyanyataḥ kutaścidgantavyādanenopāyena brahmalokaṃ kṣipraṃ prayātīti /

children.translated_text: '#Many path-stages are [mentioned] in the <s>Arcirādi</s> <s>Śruti</s>#' — thus.

children.text: ayamarthaḥ-ekatvātprāptavyasya brahmalokasyālpaparvaṇā mārgeṇa tatprāptau saṃbhavantyāṃ bahumārgopadeśo vyarthaḥ prasajyate /
children.translated_text: The meaning is this: since the destination — <s>Brahmaloka</s> — is one, and since attainment of it via a path with few stages is possible, the teaching of many paths would be purposeless.
Because a conscious [being] would not engage [in a longer path when a shorter one is available].

children.text: tasmādbhūyasāṃ parvaṇāmavirodhenālpānāṃ tadanupraveśa eva yukta iti //1 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is fitting that the stages that are fewer should be subsumed within the greater number [of stages mentioned in another <s>Śākhā</s>] without contradiction. //1//

body.translated_text:
For a path with stages leads to a single destination like a city — not [merely] a portion [of it].
Therein, the doubt is: are these rays, day, bright fortnight, sun, and the like portions of the path that are combined with a single path, or do they each separately constitute a distinct path?
When there is doubt, even though the path is one, since the distinction of portion-differences is tenable — the construal of a difference of the whole [path] is not appropriate, because of the absurdity of over-complexity.
And because of the recognition of a common element, the relationship of qualifier and qualified being tenable, there is no construal of multiple paths.
Now, the emphatic 'by those very rays' — this does not serve to exclude another [path], because it would conflict with other sentences [describing the same path] that lead to the same [destination]. Therefore, what it establishes is the non-dependence [of this path on any other path] — this is what must be said.
And a single sentence cannot both establish an un-established path and convey its non-dependence — hence it is not sufficient for both purposes. Therefore, the emphatic particle simply restates the already-established [fact of] non-conjunction [with another path], by the force of the injunction — this is fitting.
'#And because of the statement about speed#' — thus.
For hastiness is not construed merely by reference to a difference of paths when the destination is one; rather, it is tenable even from a difference of destinations.
Just as 'from Kashmir, <s>Caitra</s> quickly goes to Mathurā' — so here too, 'from some other starting-point, by this means, one quickly goes to <s>Brahmaloka</s>.'

children.translated_text: '#<s>Vāyu</s> (wind) [is to be placed] after the year (<s>abda</s>), because of both non-specification and specification#.'
'In the absence of <s>Śruti</s> and the like, the sequence of recitation is the determinant.
And <s>Vāyu</s> is heard only as the cause of upward ascent.' //

body.text: ' 'sa vāyumāgacchati tasmai sa tatra vijihīte yathā rathacakrasya khaṃ tena sa ūrdhvamākramate' iti hi vāyunimittamūrdhvākramaṇaṃ śrutaṃ na tu vāyunimittamādityagamanaṃ 'sa ādityaṃ gacchati' ityādityagamanamātrapratīteḥ /

children.translated_text: And the pronoun 'through that' — being connected without expectancy with the immediately preceding action of upward ascent — is not fit to be connected also with the action of going to the sun.

Nor is there any inconsistency without [the mention of] the going to <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) by that [soul], such that [the mention of <s>Āditya</s>] — though unconnected with this [text] — would need to be annexed.

children.text: tatrāgnilokamāgacchati sa vāyulokamityādisaṃdarbhagatasya pāṭhasya kvacinniyāmakatvena kḷptasāmarthyādagnivāyuvaruṇakramaniyāmakaśrutyādyabhāvāditi prāpte pratyucyate- ūrdhvaśabdo na lokasya kasyacitpratipādakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therein, the reading found in the sequential passage 'He reaches the world of <s>Agni</s>, he [reaches] the world of <s>Vāyu</s>' and the like — having its established capacity as a determinant in some [texts] — [would suggest that] in the absence of a <s>Śruti</s> or the like that determines the sequence of <s>Agni</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s>, [the order is undetermined] — against this prima facie view, the reply is given: The word 'above' (<s>ūrdhva</s>) does not denote any particular world.
With reference to the distinction of that [world], the qualification by <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) is fitting.

body.translated_text: 'He reaches <s>Vāyu</s>; [<s>Vāyu</s>] opens up for him like the opening of a chariot-wheel; through that he ascends upward' — thus the upward ascent caused by <s>Vāyu</s> is heard, but not the going to the sun caused by <s>Vāyu</s>, since 'He goes to the sun' conveys only the going to the sun [without specifying <s>Vāyu</s> as cause].

body.text:
bhavedetadevaṃ yadyūrdhvaśabdātkaścillokabhedaḥ pratīyeta sa tūparideśamātravācī lokabhedādvināparyavasyaṃllokabhedavācināditye vyavasthāpyate /
tathā cādityalokagamanameva vāyunimittamiti śrautakramaniyame, pāṭhaḥ padārthamātrapradarśanārtho na tu kramāya prabhavati śrutivirodhāditi siddham /
vājasaneyināṃ saṃvatsaraloko na paṭhyate chāndogyānāṃ devaloko na paṭhyate tatrobhayānurodhādubhayapāṭhe māsasaṃbandhātsaṃvatsaraḥ pūrvaḥ paścimo devalokaḥ /
nahi māso devalokena saṃbadhyate kintu saṃvatsareṇa /

children.text: tasmāttayoḥ parasparasaṃbandhānmāsārabhyatvācca saṃvatsarasya māsānantarye sthite devalokaḥ saṃvatsarasya parastādbhavati /
children.translated_text: Therefore, because of the mutual connection of those two [months and year], and because the <s>saṃvatsara</s> begins from the months — when the <s>saṃvatsara</s> is established as immediately after the months, the world of the <s>devas</s> comes after the <s>saṃvatsara</s>.

children.text: tatrādityānantaryāya vāyoḥ saṃvatsarādityasya sthāne devalokādvāyumiti paṭhitavyam /
children.translated_text: Therein, for the purpose of [placing <s>Vāyu</s>] immediately after <s>Āditya</s> — in place of [the sequence] '<s>saṃvatsara</s>–<s>Āditya</s>' — it should be read as 'from the world of the <s>devas</s> to <s>Vāyu</s>.'
The <s>sūtra</s> '<s>vāyum abdāt</s>' ('to <s>Vāyu</s> from the year') is indeed expressive of this very [meaning] here too.

children.text: tathāpi saṃvatsarātparāñcamādityādarvāñcaṃ vāyumabhisaṃbhavantīti chāndogyapāṭhamātrāpekṣayektaṃ, tadidamāha- #vāyumabdāditi tviti# //2 //
children.translated_text: Even so, [the statement] 'they reach <s>Vāyu</s> — [which is] beyond the <s>saṃvatsara</s> and below <s>Āditya</s>' is stated with reference merely to the reading of the <s>Chāndogya</s> [text]. This is what [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#To <s>Vāyu</s> from the year — thus#.' //2//

body.translated_text:
This would be so if from the word 'above' (<s>ūrdhva</s>) some distinction of world were understood; but that [word], being merely denotative of the upper direction, culminating without [implying] a world-distinction, is settled as [referring to] <s>Āditya</s> which [alone] denotes a world-distinction.
And thus, when the scriptural sequence-determination is [established] — namely, that the going to the world of <s>Āditya</s> alone is occasioned by <s>Vāyu</s> — the textual order [in other recensions] serves merely to indicate the items, and does not have the power to [determine] sequence, because of the conflict with <s>Śruti</s> — this is established.
Among the <s>Vājasaneyins</s>, the world of <s>saṃvatsara</s> (the year) is not mentioned; among the <s>Chāndogyas</s>, the world of the <s>devas</s> is not mentioned. Therein, in accordance with both [recensions], when both are included in the reading — because of <s>saṃvatsara</s>'s connection with the months, the <s>saṃvatsara</s> comes first, and the world of the <s>devas</s> comes after.
For the month is not connected with the world of the <s>devas</s>, but rather with the <s>saṃvatsara</s> (year).

children.translated_text: '#<s>Varuṇa</s> is above the lightning, because of the connection#.'
In the <s>arcirādi</s> (path beginning with light) path, [the station of] the lord of waters (<s>Varuṇa</s>) is after the lightning,
because of the connection with that [lightning]; and similarly, <s>Indra</s> and the others are considered to be after the lord of waters.
The placement of the newcomers [i.e., stations not found in all recensions] at the end is established because of the absence of a [specific] position [for them].
And thus, <s>Indra</s> and the others — being newcomers — are read as [coming] after the lord of waters. //3//
'#[They are] <s>ativāhika</s>s (conductors), because of the indication of that [in scripture]#.'
Because of their resemblance to path-markers (<s>mārgacihna</s>), <s>arcis</s> (light) and the others are merely markers;
or they could be realms of experience (<s>bhogabhūmi</s>) for the sustainer, the <s>jīvātman</s>, because of [their being called] 'worlds' — [and hence] they are not <s>ativāhika</s>s (conductors).

body.text: arcirādiśabdā hi jvalanādāvacetaneṣu nirūḍhavṛttayo loke /

children.text: na caiṣāṃ tvāvadhikānāmiva niyamavatī saṃvahanasvarūpā svatanantrakriyā buddhipūrvā saṃbhavatyacetanānām /
children.translated_text: And for these [entities] — being non-sentient, unlike those who have authority (<s>āvadhika</s>) — a rule-governed, independent, intentional activity of the nature of conducting [souls] is not possible.
Therefore, because they are denoted by the word 'world' (<s>loka</s>), we hold that they are merely realms of experience (<s>bhogabhūmi</s>) for the sustainer, the <s>jīvātman</s>.
Moreover, from [the ablative in] '<s>arciṣaḥ</s>' ('from light'), an ablative [sense of departure] is understood,

children.text: na heturnāguṇe hetau pañcamī dṛśyate kvacit //
children.translated_text: and the fifth case [ablative] in the sense of cause is never seen with respect to a non-quality [i.e., a substantive].

body.translated_text: For the words '<s>arcis</s>' (light) and the like have their well-established usage in the world for non-sentient [entities] such as fire and the like.

body.text:
jāḍyādbaddha ityādiṣu guṇavacaneṣu jāḍyādiṣu hetupañcamī dṛṣṭā /
na cārcirādiśabdā guṇavācino yena pañcamyā teṣāṃ vahanaṃ prati hetutvamucyate /
apādānatvaṃ cācetaneṣvapyastīti nātivāhikāḥ /

children.text: na cāmānavasya puruṣasya vidyudādiṣu voḍhṛtvadarśanādarcirādīnāmapi voḍhṛtvānnāmānavaḥ puruṣo voḍhā śrūyate /
children.translated_text: Nor — just because the <s>amānava puruṣa</s> (non-human person) is seen as a conductor from the lightning and the like — should <s>arcis</s> and the others also [be considered] conductors; for the <s>amānava puruṣa</s> alone is heard as the conductor.
From the fact that [only] he is heard [as conductor], we understand that — like the lightning and the like — <s>arcis</s> and the others do not have the role of conductor.

children.text: tasmādbhogabhūmaya evārcirādayo nātivāhikā iti prāpte pratyucyate -saṃpiṇḍakaraṇānāṃ hi sūkṣmadehavatāṃ gatau /
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>arcis</s> and the others are merely realms of experience (<s>bhogabhūmi</s>), not <s>ativāhika</s>s (conductors) — against this prima facie view, the reply is given: For the souls (<s>saṃpiṇḍakaraṇa</s>s), who possess subtle bodies, in their journey (<s>gati</s>),

children.text: na svātantryaṃ na cāgnyādyā netāro 'cetanāstu te //
children.translated_text: there is no independence; nor are <s>Agni</s> and the others — being non-sentient — their guides.

body.translated_text:
In [expressions like] '<s>jāḍyād baddhaḥ</s>' ('bound by dullness') and the like — which are quality-denoting words — the causal ablative is seen with respect to <s>jāḍya</s> (dullness) and the like.
But the words '<s>arcis</s>' (light) and the like are not quality-denoting, such that their causality with respect to conducting would be stated by the ablative.
And the ablative [sense of departure from a place] exists even for non-sentient [entities] — hence [they are] not <s>ativāhika</s>s (conductors).

body.text:
īdṛśī hi niyamavatī gatiḥ svayaṃ vā prekṣāvato 'prekṣāvato vā prekṣāvatprayuktasya /
na tāvadvigalitasthūlakalevarāḥ sūkṣmadehavantaḥ saṃpiṇḍitakaraṇagrāmā utkrāntimanto jīvātmāno mattamūrcchicavatsvayaṃ prekṣāvanto yadevaṃ svātantryeṇa gaccheyustadyadyarcirādayo 'pi mārgacihnāni vā śamīkāraskarādivadbhogabhūmayo vā sumeruśailalāvṛttādivadubhayathāpyacetanatayā na nayanaṃ pratyeṣāmasti svātantryam /
na caitebhyo 'nyasya cetanasya netuḥ kalpanā sati śrutānāṃ caitanyasaṃbhave /
naca parameśvara evāstu neteti yuktam /
tasyātyantasādhāraṇatayā lokapālagrahādīnāmakiñcitkaratvāt /
tasmādvyavasthita eva parameśvarasya sarvādhyakṣatve yathā yathātvaṃ lokapālādīnāṃ svātantryamevamihāpyarcirādīnāmātivāhikatvameva darśanānusārācchabdārtha iti yuktam /
body.translated_text:
For such a rule-governed journey is [performed] either by one who is sentient on his own, or by one who is non-sentient, or by one who is non-sentient but directed by a sentient being.
To begin with, the <s>jīvātman</s>s — who have departed [from the body], whose gross body has dissolved, who possess subtle bodies with their sense-organs gathered together — are not, like intoxicated or unconscious persons, independently sentient such that they could travel on their own. Even if <s>arcis</s> and the others are either path-markers — like <s>śamīkāra-skara</s> (boundary stones) and the like — or realms of experience — like Mount <s>Meru</s>, <s>Śaila</s>, <s>Lāvṛtta</s> and the like — in either case, being non-sentient, they have no independence with respect to guiding.
Nor is it proper to postulate some other sentient guide, when sentience is possible for those [<s>arcis</s> etc.] that are heard [in scripture].
Nor is it proper [to say] that the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>) alone is the guide — because, due to His being exceedingly general [i.e., the universal superintendent], the world-protectors (<s>lokapāla</s>s), planets, and the like would be rendered ineffectual.
Therefore, when it is well-established that the Supreme Lord has universal superintendence, just as the world-protectors and the like have their respective independence, so too here the <s>ativāhika</s>-hood (conductor-nature) of <s>arcis</s> and the others alone — in accordance with the scriptural evidence — is the meaning of the words. This is fitting.

body.text:
imamevārthamamānavapuruṣātivāhanalakṣaṇaṃ liṅgamupodvalayatītyuktam /
#anavasthitatvādarcirādīnāmiti# /
avasthitaṃ hi mārgacihnaṃ bhavatyavyabhicārānnānavasthitaṃ vyabhicārāditi /
arciṣa iti ca hetau pañcamī nāpādāne /
guṇatvaṃ cāśritatayā /

children.translated_text: Nor should the restriction [that the ablative cannot express cause for non-qualities] be maintained according to the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> convention, because of its conflict with common usage.
Moreover, [the statement] 'they reach <s>arcis</s>' expresses merely a connection [between the soul and <s>arcis</s>].
When the word [expressing] a general [relation] is in expectation of a specific [determination], clearly,
that general [meaning] is determined by whichever specific word [is present in the context].

body.translated_text:
The indication (<s>liṅga</s>) characterizing the <s>amānava puruṣa</s> (non-human person) as a conductor strengthens this very meaning — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Because of the non-fixedness of <s>arcis</s> and the others#.'
For a path-marker is fixed — because of non-deviation — not non-fixed, [which would involve] deviation.
And [the ablative] '<s>arciṣaḥ</s>' ('from light') is in the causal [sense], not the sense of departure from a place.
And the quality-hood [of <s>arcis</s>] is [established] through its dependent nature [i.e., as an attribute of the fire-stations].

body.text: yathā brāhmaṇamānaya bhojayitavya iti tadviśeṣāpekṣāyāṃ yadā tatsaṃnidhāvupanipatati padaṃ kaṇṭhādi(?) tadā tenaitanniyamyate evamihāpīti //4 // //5 //
body.translated_text: Just as in 'Bring a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, [he] is to be fed' — when a specific [<s>brāhmaṇa</s>] is expected, whatever word such as '<s>kaṇṭha</s>' etc. (?) falls in its vicinity, by that [word] this [general meaning] is determined — so too here. //4// //5//

children.translated_text: '#By the <s>vaidyuta</s> (lightning-born [person]) alone [they are conducted] from there, because of the <s>Śruti</s> regarding that#.'

children.text: vidyullokamāgato 'mānavaḥ puruṣo vaidyutastenaiva na tu varuṇādinā svayamuhyate /
children.translated_text: The <s>amānava puruṣa</s> (non-human person), who is <s>vaidyuta</s> (born of lightning), having arrived at the world of lightning — by him alone, not by <s>Varuṇa</s> and the others, [the soul] is conducted on its own.
Because of the <s>Śruti</s> regarding that — because [only] he is heard in scripture as conducting on his own.

children.text: varuṇādayastu tatsāhāyake vartamānā voḍhāro bhavantīti ca vaiṣamyaṃ na voḍhṛtve iti sarvamavadātam //6 //
children.translated_text: But <s>Varuṇa</s> and the others — being engaged in assisting him [the <s>vaidyuta puruṣa</s>] — are [also] conductors; and thus the difference lies not in their conductor-nature [per se, but in their independence] — all this is clear. //6//

body.text: pāṭhakramādarthakramo balavānitiyathārthakramaṃ paṭhyante sūtrāṇi- #paraṃ jaiminirmukhyatvāt# /

children.translated_text: [The statement] 'He leads them to <s>Brahman</s>' is under investigation.

children.text: kiṃ paraṃ brahma gamayatyāhosvidaparaṃ kāryaṃ brahmeti /
children.translated_text: Does he lead [them] to the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, or to the non-supreme, effected (<s>kārya</s>) <s>Brahman</s>?
Because of [the word <s>brahma</s> being used in its] primary sense, because of the attainment of immortality (<s>amṛta</s>), and also because of the context [dealing with] the Supreme —
<s>Jaimini</s> held that the destination [reached] through the <s>arcirādi</s> path is the Supreme [<s>Brahman</s>] alone.

body.translated_text: Since the order based on meaning is stronger than the order based on [mere] textual sequence, the <s>sūtra</s>s are read in accordance with the order of meaning: '#<s>Jaimini</s> [holds that the destination is] the Supreme [<s>Brahman</s>], because of [the word <s>brahma</s> being used in its] primary [sense]#.'

body.text:
brahma gamayatītyatra hi napuṃsakaṃ brahmapadaṃ parasminneva brahmaṇi nirūḍhatvādanapekṣatayā mukhyamiti sati saṃbhave na kārye brahmaṇi guṇakalpanayā vyākhyātumucitam /
api cāmṛtatvaphalāvartirna kāryabrahmaprāptau yujyate /
tasya kāryatvena maraṇadharmavattvāt /
kiñca tatra tatra parameva brahma prakṛtya prajāpatisadmapratipattyādaya ucyamānā nāparabrahmaviṣayā bhavitumarhanti prakaraṇavirodhāt /
na ca parasmintsarvagate gatirnopapadyate prāptatvāditi yuktam /
prāptepi hi prāptiphalā gatirdṛśyate /
yathaikasminnyagrodhapādape mūlādagramagrācca mūlaṃ gacchataḥ śākhāmṛgasyaikenaiva nyagrodhapādapena nirantaraṃ saṃyogavibhāgā bhavanti /
na caite tadavayavaviṣayī na tu nyagrodhaviṣayā iti sāmprataṃ tathā sati na śākhāmṛgo nyagrodhena yujyate /
nyagrodhāvayavasya tadavayavayogāt /
evaṃ dṛśyamānānāmapi tadavayavānāṃ na yogastadavayavayogāttadantena krameṇa tadavayaveṣu paramāṇuṣu vyavatiṣṭhate /
te cātīndriyā iti kasminnu nāmāyamanubhavapaddhatimadhyāstāṃ saṃyogatapasvī /
tasmādakāmenāpyanubhavānurodhena prāpta eva prāptiphalatvāvagatireṣitavyā /
tadbrahma prāptamapi prāptiphalāyāvagategocaro bhaviṣyati /
brahmalokeṣviti ca bahuvacanamekasminnapi prayogasādhutāmātreṇa gamayitavyam /
lokaśabdaścālokane prakāśe vartayitavyo na tu sanniveśavati deśaviśeṣe /
tasmāt parabrahmaprāptyarthaṃ gatyupadeśasāmarthyādayamartho bhavati /
yathā vidyākarmavaśādarcirādinā gatasya satyalokamatikramya paraṃ jagatkāraṇaṃ brahma lokamālokaṃ svayaṃ prakāśakamiti yāvat /
prāptasya tatraiva liṅgaṃ pralīyate na tu gatimevaṃbhūtāṃ vinā liṅgapravilaya iti /
ata eva śrutiḥ- puruṣamāṇāḥ puruṣaṃ prāpyāstaṃ gacchanti /

children.text: tadanenābhisandhinā paraṃ brahma gamayatyamānava iti mene jaiminirācāryaḥ /
children.translated_text: With this intention — [namely that] 'the <s>amānava</s> [person] leads [them] to the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>' — <s>Jaimini</s>, the teacher, held [this view].
'#<s>Bādari</s> [holds that the destination is] the effected [<s>Brahman</s>], because journey to it is logically possible#.'
<s>Bādari</s>, the seer of reality, saw [thus]: The journey — which consists in reaching what was not previously reached — [leads to] the effected (<s>kārya</s>) [<s>Brahman</s>],
because it can lead to <s>Brahman</s> that is not [yet] attained, not to the Supreme [<s>Brahman</s>], since [the Supreme] is [already] attained, being the Self of the universe.

body.translated_text:
For in [the statement] 'He leads [them] to <s>Brahman</s>,' the neuter word '<s>brahma</s>' — being established in its primary sense (<s>nirūḍha</s>) only with reference to the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> — is primary due to its non-dependence [on any secondary interpretation]; and when the primary meaning is possible, it is not appropriate to interpret it as [referring to] the effected (<s>kārya</s>) <s>Brahman</s> through figurative usage (<s>guṇakalpanā</s>).
Moreover, the non-returning characterized by the fruit of immortality (<s>amṛtatva</s>) is not fitting upon the attainment of <s>kārya Brahman</s> — because, being an effect, it is subject to destruction.
Furthermore, in various [passages] where the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone is the topic, the statements about reaching the abode of <s>Prajāpati</s> and the like cannot be about the non-supreme <s>Brahman</s>, because of the conflict with the context.
Nor is it correct [to argue] that journey (<s>gati</s>) to the all-pervading Supreme [<s>Brahman</s>] is impossible because it is [already] attained.
For journey whose fruit is attainment is seen even to [what is already] attained.
Just as, for a monkey on a single banyan tree, going from root to top and from top to root — conjunctions and disjunctions with that one banyan tree occur continuously.
Nor are these [conjunctions and disjunctions] concerning its parts rather than the banyan [as a whole] — [for] if that were so, then the monkey would not be connected with the banyan [itself].
[This is] because the part of the banyan has conjunction with [another] part of it.
Likewise, even for those parts that are observed — there is no conjunction [of them with the whole], because of the conjunction with [their own] parts — [and this regress] terminates step by step in the atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>s), which are parts of those [parts].
And those [atoms] are beyond the senses — so in what, pray tell, would this practitioner of conjunction (<s>saṃyogatapasvī</s>) take his stand on the path of experience?
Therefore, even involuntarily, in accordance with experience, the attainment whose fruit is [simply] attainment must be accepted even for what is [already] attained.
Thus, <s>Brahman</s> — even though [already] attained — will be the object of the cognition (<s>avagati</s>) whose fruit is attainment.
And the plural in '<s>brahmalokeṣu</s>' ('in the worlds of <s>Brahman</s>') should be explained merely by the grammatical correctness of usage even for a single [world].
And the word '<s>loka</s>' should be understood in the sense of 'illumination' (<s>ālokana</s>), 'light' (<s>prakāśa</s>), not in the sense of a particular region characterized by spatial location.
Therefore, from the capacity of the teaching of journey for the purpose of attaining the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, this meaning follows:
Just as one who has traveled through the <s>arcirādi</s> path by the power of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) and <s>karma</s> (action) — having transcended <s>Satyaloka</s> — reaches the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the cause of the universe, the world [in the sense of] illumination, self-luminous — this is the purport.
Upon reaching there, the <s>liṅga-śarīra</s> (subtle body) dissolves; but without such a journey, there is no dissolution of the subtle body.
Hence the <s>Śruti</s>: 'Being of the measure of a person (<s>puruṣamāṇāḥ</s>), having reached the Person (<s>puruṣa</s>), they set [like the sun].'

body.text:
tattvamasivākyārthasākṣātkārātprākkila jīvātmāvidyākarmavāsanādyupādhyavacchedādvastuto 'navacchinno 'vacchinnamivābhinno 'pi lokebhyo bhinnamivātmānamabhimanyamānaḥ svarūpādanyānaprāptānarcirādīṃllokāngatyāpnotīti yujyate /
advaitabrahmatattvasākṣātkāravatastu vigalitanikhilaprapañcāvabhāsavibhramasya na gantavyaṃ na gatirna gamayitāra iti kiṃ kena saṃgatam /
tasmādanidarśanaṃ nyagrodhasaṃyogavibhāgā nyayagrodhavānaratadgatitatsaṃyogavibhāgānāṃ mitho bhedāt /
naca tatrāpi prāptaprāptiḥ karmajena hi vibhāgena niruddhāyāṃ pūrvaprāptāvaprāptasyaivottaraprāpterutpatteḥ /
etadapi vastuto vicārasahatayā sarvamanirvacanīyaṃ vijṛmbhitamavidyāyāḥ samutpannādvaitatattvasākṣātkāro na vidvānabhimanyate /
viduṣo 'pi dehapātātpūrvaṃ sthitaprajñasya yathābhāsamātreṇa sāṃsārikadharmānuvṛttirabhyupeyate evamāliṅgaśarīrapātādviduṣastaddharmānuvṛttiḥ /
tathācāprāptaprāptergatyupapattistaddeśaprāptau ca liṅgadehanivṛttermuktiḥ śrutiprāmāṇyāditi cet /
na /
paravidyāvata utkrāntipratiṣedhāt 'brahmaiva sanbrahmāpyeti na tasmātprāṇā utkrāmanti atraiva samavanīyante' iti /
yathā vidyābrahmaprāptyoḥ samānakālatā śrūyate- 'brahma veda brahmaiva bhavati' 'ānandaṃ brahmaṇo vidvānna bibheti' 'tadātmānameva vedāhaṃ brahmāsmīti tatsarvamabhavat' 'tatra ko mohaḥ kaḥ śoka ekatvamanupaśyataḥ' iti paurvāparyāśravaṇāt paravidyāvato muktiṃ prati nopāyāntarāpekṣeti lakṣyate 'bhisaṃdhiḥ śruteḥ /
body.translated_text:
For prior to the direct realization (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>) of the meaning of the sentence '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' ('That thou art'), the <s>jīvātman</s> — though in reality undivided, [yet] appearing as if divided due to the delimitation by the limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>karma</s>, <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impressions), and the like — and though in reality non-different from the worlds, [yet] considering himself as if different — reaches the worlds of <s>arcis</s> and the like, which are other than his own nature and not [previously] attained, through journey — this is fitting.
But for one who has directly realized the truth of non-dual <s>Brahman</s> — for whom the delusion of the appearance of the entire phenomenal world has dissolved — there is nothing to be reached, no journey, and no conductors — so what is connected with what?
Therefore, the analogy of the banyan tree is inapplicable — because the conjunctions and disjunctions of the banyan tree, the monkey, and its journey in the banyan are mutually different [from the case of <s>Brahman</s>].
Nor is there attainment of what is [already] attained even there [in the banyan analogy] — for through a conjunction produced by <s>karma</s>, when the prior attainment is obstructed, it is the attainment of what was [temporarily] unattained that arises as the subsequent attainment.
This too — being in reality incapable of withstanding scrutiny — is entirely indescribable (<s>anirvacanīya</s>), a manifestation of <s>avidyā</s>; one who has directly realized the truth of non-duality does not entertain [such notions].
Even for the knower — prior to the fall of the body — [who is] established in wisdom (<s>sthitaprajña</s>), just as the continuation of <s>saṃsāric</s> attributes is accepted as mere appearance, so too for the knower — until the fall of the <s>liṅga-śarīra</s> (subtle body) — the continuation of those attributes [is accepted].
And thus, the logical possibility of journey — [as] attainment of what was not [previously] attained — [holds]; and upon reaching that place, the cessation of the subtle body constitutes liberation — [this is established] from the authority of <s>Śruti</s> — if [one argues] thus;
No — because of the denial of departure (<s>utkrānti</s>) for the knower of the supreme <s>vidyā</s>: 'Being <s>Brahman</s>, he merges into <s>Brahman</s>; his <s>prāṇa</s>s do not depart — they are resolved right here.'
Just as the simultaneity of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) and attainment of <s>Brahman</s> is heard in <s>Śruti</s> — 'He who knows <s>Brahman</s> becomes <s>Brahman</s> itself,' 'The knower of the bliss of <s>Brahman</s> fears nothing,' 'He knew the Self: "I am <s>Brahman</s>" — he became all this,' 'What delusion, what sorrow is there for one who sees oneness?' — since no temporal sequence is heard [between knowledge and liberation], it is indicated that for the knower of the supreme <s>vidyā</s>, liberation does not depend on any other means — this is the intention [of <s>Bādari</s>], from the <s>Śruti</s>.
