body.translated_text:
And this is fitting.
For indeed, when <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) has been uprooted without remainder by the direct realization of <s>Brahman</s>-hood of the <s>jīvātman</s> (individual self) — [arising] from the contemplation (<s>paribhāvanā</s>) 'This universe is indeed <s>Brahman</s>, I am <s>Brahman</s>' — there is no distinction between what-is-to-be-reached and the one-who-reaches for the knower. In its absence, how would he proceed on the <s>arcirādi-mārga</s> (path beginning with light)?
Nor does the continuation of <s>saṃsāric</s> attributes, even as a mere shadow, serve as an impetus for proceeding there — because of the spontaneous nature of such continuation.
For one devoid of faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), <s>karma</s>s directed toward visible purposes may or may not bear fruit.
But regarding <s>karma</s>s directed toward unseen purposes — what need be said about their fruit? — this was stated in the first <s>sūtra</s>.
Nor is the meditation on the <s>arcirādi-mārga</s> instructed for the non-knower for the purpose of attaining <s>Parabrahman</s> — and if so, [then] just as in other <s>karma</s>s such as the <s>nitya</s> (obligatory) rites and the like, his engagement therein too would be fitting at present.
Because [this position] cannot withstand the dilemma:
Is this [meditation on the path] a means of attaining <s>Parabrahman</s> independent of the higher knowledge (<s>paravidyā</s>), or dependent on it?
To begin with, it is not independent — because of the direct negation of any other path than the knowledge of <s>Parabrahman</s>: 'Having known That alone, one crosses over death; there is no other path for going [to liberation].'
But if dependent on the higher knowledge, then [the question arises:] does this meditation on the path assist the effect of knowledge, or the origination of knowledge?
To begin with, it does not [assist] the effect of knowledge — because of the impossibility of [their] coexistence, since [they] are mutually contradictory in having duality and non-duality as their respective domains.
Nor [does it assist] the origination of knowledge, like sacrifice and the like — because [the <s>Śruti</s>] is heard as directly being a means of attaining <s>Brahman</s>: 'It leads these [beings] to <s>Brahman</s>.'
But sacrifice and the like, through conjunction with the desire to know (<s>vividiṣā</s>), have their subsidiary role in the origination of knowledge from the <s>Śruti</s> [that teaches them].
Therefore, in accordance with the many <s>Śruti</s>s cited and because of [logical] tenability, the word '<s>Brahman</s>' — since the primary meaning is impossible — should be led by secondary indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) to the <s>apara-Brahman</s> (lower <s>Brahman</s>), on account of the proximity [of the term] '<s>Brahman</s>' [to the lower <s>Brahman</s>].
And thus, the plural in 'in the worlds' (<s>lokeṣu</s>) is fitting — because the <s>kārya-Brahmaloka</s> (created <s>Brahman</s>-world) [has parts].
But for the supreme [<s>Brahman</s>], being without parts, even through that [expression] the [plural] is not fitting.
And the word 'world' (<s>loka</s>) is conventionally established in a realm of enjoyment possessing a specific spatial arrangement, like a dwelling and the like — it cannot somehow be explained as [meaning] 'light' through etymological derivation.
Therefore, the venerable <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> is one who sees correctly; <s>Jaimini</s> is one who sees incorrectly — this is established.
The prolific disputations of those without valid authority — [such as:] 'The qualities of an all-pervading substance are themselves all-pervading,' 'Consciousness, bliss, and the like — the qualities of the qualified <s>Paramātman</s> — are qualities that are both different and non-different [from their substance],' and the like — even though restated for refutation, [these views] bring upon themselves [the status of] being without valid authority from our perspective — hence [they are] disregarded.
The construction of the text is: '#Because of being the inner Self (<s>pratyagātmatvāt</s>) of the travelers (<s>gantṝṇām</s>)#' — '<s>pratyak</s>' means that which goes toward each [individual], i.e., the inner reality; <s>Brahman</s> is that; because of being the Self of that [<s>Brahman</s>], of the travelers — the <s>jīvātman</s>s — thus.
'#But figurative (<s>gauṇī</s>) elsewhere#' — thus.
For even [a usage that is] etymologically derived (<s>yaugikī</s>) is figurative (<s>gauṇī</s>) insofar as it depends on the quality [that motivates] the derivation.
'#Connection with a pure limiting adjunct (<s>viśuddhopādhisaṃbandha</s>)#' — thus.
The imaginations (<s>kalpanā</s>s) such as 'consisting of mind' (<s>manomayatva</s>) and the like are effects (<s>kārya</s>).
Being effects, they are impure; yet being causes of the highest good, they are pure.
<s>Pratisaṃcara</s> means the great dissolution (<s>mahāpralaya</s>); <s>pratipattyabhisaṃdhi</s> — <s>pratipatti</s> means 'going' (<s>gati</s>), since the root <s>pad</s> has the meaning of motion; <s>abhisaṃdhi</s> means 'purport' (<s>tātparya</s>).
Of that <s>Brahman</s> whose name (<s>nāman</s>) — whose designation — is '<s>yaśas</s>' (glory) — thus.
'#By breaking the previous sentence (<s>pūrvavākyavicchedena</s>)#' — thus.
The <s>Śruti</s>-sentence is stronger than the context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>).
'#Even in <s>saguṇa-Brahman</s> (qualified <s>Brahman</s>)#' — thus.
The meaning is: for the purpose of praise (<s>praśaṃsā</s>).
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises an objection: '#Surely, even for one who has gone [to <s>Brahmaloka</s>], there is a real destination (<s>gantavyatā</s>) — being qualified by a different place#' — thus.
The illustration of the <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan) tree and the man has been provided.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes: '#No. Because all specific attributes of <s>Brahman</s> have been negated#' — thus.
The purport is this: Just as a banyan tree — being a whole with parts — is subject to modification and is conjoined and separated by contacts and separations born of <s>karma</s> arising from origination and destruction — but this <s>Paramātman</s>, in whom the entire manifold of difference has been negated, being eternally unchanging (<s>kūṭasthanitya</s>), cannot be a partaker of contact and separation like a banyan tree.
But imagined (<s>kālpanika</s>) contact and separation are fitting only for the imagined <s>kārya-Brahmaloka</s> (created <s>Brahman</s>-world), not for the supreme [<s>Brahman</s>].
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises a doubt: '#Because of the <s>Śruti</s> [declaring <s>Brahman</s>] to be the cause of the origination, sustenance, and dissolution of the universe#' — thus.
For the state of being the cause of origination and the like is not possible for one who does not undergo modification — therefore [<s>Brahman</s>] undergoes modification — thus.
And being so, its real state of being a destination (<s>gantavyatva</s>) is fitting — this is the meaning.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes: '#No. Because of the <s>Śruti</s>s that negate specific attributes#' — thus.
The negation of specific attributes — being fruitful through the cessation of all suffering such as grief and the like — [serves] the purpose of the human goal (<s>puruṣārtha</s>).
But the teaching of origination and the like is fruitless.
Therefore, what is taught in the proximity of what is fruitful is stated for the purpose of that [fruitful teaching] alone — this is the reasoning.
And the <s>Śruti</s>: 'That you should desire to know' (<s>tadvijijñāsasva</s>).
Therefore, by both <s>Śruti</s> and reasoning, this scripture (<s>āmnāya</s>) is primarily directed toward establishing <s>Brahman</s> devoid of all specific attributes — not primarily directed toward establishing origination and the like.
Therefore, the going [to <s>Brahman</s>] is not ultimately real.
Moreover, this going cannot withstand rational examination — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#And in the imagination of going#' — thus.
The two alternatives of otherness and non-otherness are the positions of parts (<s>avayava</s>) and modifications (<s>vikāra</s>).
'#Or absolutely other#' — [meaning] completely [other].
But why is absolute non-otherness not imagined? — to this he says: '#Because of absolute identity#' — thus.
For pots and the like — being of the nature of clay by their essential character — are entities that are transformations pervaded by that [clay]; in the absence of that [clay], they do not exist — like a <s>śiṃśapā</s> [tree] in the absence of tree-hood — thus.
'#And because of the stability of that which possesses modifications and parts#' — because of the immovability of <s>Brahman</s>, going — which has the character of <s>saṃsāra</s> — is not fitting in conjunction with modifications and parts.
For what is of a stable nature cannot be unstable.
And even in [the position of] otherness-cum-non-otherness, because of the impossibility of one [entity possessing] contradictory [properties] — this is the purport.
'#But if the <s>jīva</s> is absolutely other than <s>Brahman</s>#' — thus.
And so, even though <s>Brahman</s> does not transmigrate, the <s>saṃsāra</s> of the <s>jīva</s> can be imagined — thus.
Having raised this alternative, he refutes it: '#He is atomic (<s>aṇu</s>)#' — thus.
'#Because of the middling size (<s>madhyamaparimāṇatva</s>)#' — thus.
Because of the observation that things of middling size — pots and the like — are impermanent.
'#No. Because the unity is not primary (<s>mukhya</s>)#' — thus.
Because of the impossibility of difference and non-difference — which are contradictory — [coexisting] in a single [entity], the difference of objects [follows] from the difference of cognitions (<s>buddhivyapadeśa</s>).
Because of being inseparably connected (<s>ayutasiddha</s>), what is said to be non-different is said figuratively — hence its unity is not primary — this is the meaning.
Moreover, in the positions of [the <s>jīva</s>s] being parts of <s>Brahman</s>, modifications [of <s>Brahman</s>], or absolutely different [from <s>Brahman</s>] — since transmigration (<s>saṃsāritā</s>) would be real — upon liberation, since their essential nature would be destroyed, there would be the absurd consequence of the annihilation of the <s>jīva</s>s.

brahmavivartatve tu brahmaivaiṣāṃ svabhāvaḥ pratibimbānāmiva bimbaṃ taccāvināśīti na jīvavināśa ityāha- #sarveṣveteṣviti# /

But when [the world is understood as] the apparent transformation (<s>vivarta</s>) of <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Brahman</s> alone is the essential nature of these [<s>jīva</s>s] — just as the original (<s>bimba</s>) is [the essential nature] of reflections (<s>pratibimba</s>) — and that [<s>Brahman</s>] is indestructible; hence there is no destruction of the <s>jīva</s>s — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#In all these [positions]#.'
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] presents another view in order to refute it: '#But what is prattled by some#' — [namely, the view that] without <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge, '#the obligatory and occasional (<s>nityanaimittika</s>) [rites]#' [alone suffice for liberation].
Just as a fever caused by phlegm — when the accumulated phlegm is depleted through specific treatments and the like, and when the causes of further phlegm-production such as curd and the like are avoided — [the fever,] though pacified, does not recur;
so too, bondage caused by <s>karma</s> — when the accumulated <s>karma</s>s are depleted through experience — subsides.
And when the causes of further bondage — [namely] the other <s>karma</s>s — are not performed, due to the absence of a cause, the absence of the effect [follows] — hence, in the absence of bondage, liberation is established by its own nature, like health.
And for the eradication of accumulated sin, through the performance of obligatory and occasional <s>karma</s>s, the misfortune (<s>pratyavāya</s>) caused by sin does not arise.
And when misfortune does not arise, one whose mind is at ease does not perform prohibited acts — thus.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes this: '#That is wrong. Because of the absence of valid authority#' — thus.
Scripture is indeed the valid authority here, and it teaches only the knowledge of the Self as the means of liberation for the one who is to be liberated — not the aforementioned conduct.
Nor does reasoning prevail here — because of <s>saṃsāra</s>'s being beginningless, and because the karmic deposits (<s>karmāśaya</s>) — being innumerable and having indeterminate times of ripening — cannot be exhausted through experience — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] says: '#Nor can this even be reasoned about#' — thus.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] raises an objection: '#It may be so#' — thus. '#The obligatory [rites]#' — thus.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] refutes: '#That is not so, because of the absence of conflict#' — thus.
For if the obligatory and occasional <s>karma</s>s were to exhaust merit just as [they exhaust] demerit, then the instructions for optional <s>karma</s>s (<s>kāmyakarma</s>) would become futile — like poured-out handfuls of water.
For there is no one in the four <s>varṇa</s>s and four <s>āśrama</s>s who does not perform obligatory and occasional <s>karma</s>s.
Therefore, these [obligatory rites] do not conflict with merit — thus.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states an additional argument: '#Nor from the performance of obligatory and occasional [rites]#' — thus. '#Nor in the absence of right knowledge (<s>samyagdarśana</s>)#' — thus.
For one who has right knowledge, being dispassionate (<s>virakta</s>), while avoiding optional and prohibited [acts] — even when [sins] befall through inadvertence — destroys them by that very right knowledge.
And at the maturation of knowledge, he does not perform [sins] at all. But one who lacks knowledge, even if skillful, performs [sins] through inadvertence.
And having performed [them], he is unable to destroy [them] — this is the distinction.
'#Nor when the <s>Brahman</s>-selfhood accessible through knowledge is not accepted#' — thus.
Agency (<s>kartṛtva</s>) and experiencership (<s>bhoktṛtva</s>) — which imply action and experience — if these are the essential nature of the Self [as] ascertained and not superimposed, then they cannot be removed.
For an entity (<s>bhāva</s>) cannot be removed from its essential nature — because there would be the absurd consequence of the destruction of the entity.
Nor can experience (<s>bhoga</s>) that has a real essential nature be rendered non-existent — for indeed, even <s>Indra</s> cannot make blue into non-blue. This is what was stated: '#Because of the irremovability of essential nature#' — thus.
But what is superimposed — being indescribable (<s>anirvacanīya</s>) — its [apparent] essential nature can be removed through the knowledge of reality, just as [the appearance of] a snake [is removed] through the knowledge of the reality of a rope — this is the purport.
The one who does not know this [teaching] raises an objection: '#It may be so. [Agency and experiencership] are the effects of agency and experiencership#' — thus.
[<s>Śaṅkara</s>] — without revealing his own position — resolves [the objection] in the manner stated: '#That too is not so#' — thus.
Because of the eternality of the causal connection of agency, experiencership, and their associated powers — at some point their operation will occur, from which pleasure and pain will be experienced — thus the apprehension [arises]. Hence, whence comes the certainty of <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute isolation/liberation)? — this is the meaning.
Having raised [this objection] — though it has been refuted many times before — [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] presents it again for the strengthening of conviction, and refutes: '#Even though not different from the Supreme#' — thus.
The rest has transparent meaning. //7// //8// //9// //10// //11// //12// //13// //14//

children.translated_text: '#[<s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> holds that <s>Brahman</s>] leads [them] — because [the meditation is] not based on a <s>pratīka</s> (symbol); because of the defect in both [alternatives]; and because of the <s>tatkratu</s> [principle]#.'
Those who are not <s>Brahman</s>-meditators (<s>abrahmakratu</s>) go [to other destinations] as [taught] through the <s>pañcāgnividyā</s> (doctrine of five fires);
<s>Pratīka</s>-meditators will likewise go to <s>Brahmaloka</s>.

body.text:
santi hi mano brahmetyupāsītetyādyāḥ pratīkaviṣayā vidyāḥ /
tadvanto 'pyarcirādimārgeṇa kāryabrahmopāsakā iva gantumarhanti 'aniyamaḥ sarvāsām' ityaviśeṣeṇa vidyāntareṣvapi gateravadhāraṇāt /
na caiṣāṃ parabrahmavidāmiva gatyasaṃbhava iti /
naca brahmakratava eva brahmalokabhājo nātatkratava ityapyekāntaḥ /

children.translated_text: Because even non-<s>Brahman</s>-meditators — namely, knowers of the <s>pañcāgni</s> (five fires) — attain that [<s>Brahmaloka</s>].

children.text: na caite na brahmakratavo mano brahmetyupāsītetyādau sarvatra brahmānugamena tatkratutvasyāpi saṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: Nor are these not <s>Brahman</s>-meditators — because in 'One should meditate on the mind as <s>Brahman</s>' and the like, everywhere, through the accompaniment of <s>Brahman</s>, the status of being <s>tatkratu</s> (meditators on That) is also possible.

children.text: phalaviśeṣasya brahmalokaprāptāvapyupapatteḥ, tasya sāvayavatayotkarṣanikarṣasaṃbhavāditi prāpte pratyucyate- uttarottarabhūyastvādabrahmakratubhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Because the specific fruit of attaining <s>Brahmaloka</s> too is fitting — since that [world], being composite (<s>sāvayava</s>), admits of degrees of excellence and inferiority — thus being the prima facie conclusion, the reply is given: Because of the progressively greater [proximity to <s>Brahman</s>], because of the status of not being <s>Brahman</s>-meditators,
<s>Pratīka</s>-meditators — being atomic [in their scope of meditation] — [<s>Brahman</s>] would not lead [them] to <s>Brahmaloka</s>.

body.translated_text:
For there are <s>vidyā</s>s (meditations) pertaining to <s>pratīka</s>s (symbols), such as 'One should meditate on the mind as <s>Brahman</s>' and the like.
Those who possess these [<s>pratīka</s>-meditations] too deserve to go by the <s>arcirādi-mārga</s> (path beginning with light), just like the meditators on <s>kārya-Brahman</s> (created <s>Brahman</s>) — because the going has been ascertained for other <s>vidyā</s>s too without distinction, [from the <s>Śruti</s>:] 'There is no restriction [of the path] for all [<s>vidyā</s>s].'
Nor is there an impossibility of going for them, as there is for knowers of <s>Parabrahman</s>.
Nor is it the case that only <s>Brahman</s>-meditators (<s>brahmakratu</s>) alone attain <s>Brahmaloka</s> and not non-<s>Brahman</s>-meditators (<s>atatkratu</s>) — [for] that too is not a fixed rule.

aiśvaryaśrutayastu saguṇavidyāvipākāvasthāpekṣā muktyabhisaṃdhānaṃ tu tadavasthāsatteryathāruṇadarśane saṃdhyāyāṃ divasābhidhānam //16 //

body.text:
'āpnoti svārājyaṃ' 'sarve 'smai devā balimāvahanti' 'sarveṣu lokeṣu kāmacāro bhavati' ityādiśrutibhyo viduṣaḥ parabrahmaṇa ivānyānadhīnatvamaiśvaryamavagamyate /
nanvasya brahmopāsanālabdhamaiśvaryaṃ kathaṃ brahmādhīnaṃ na tu svabhāvaḥ /

na ca viduṣāṃ parameśvarādhīnaiśvaryasiddhitvāttadgatamaiśvaryaṃ yena laukikā iva rājāno mahārājādhīnaḥ svavyāpāre vidvāṃsaḥ parameśvarādhīnā bhaveyuḥ /
na khalu yadadhīnotpādaṃ yasya rūpaṃ tattadrūpādūnaṃ bhavatīti kaścinniyamaḥ /
tatsamānāṃ tadadhikānāṃ ca darśanāttathā hyantevāsī gurvadhīnavidhaḥ tatsamastadadhiko vā dṛśyate /
duṣṭasāmantāśca pārthivādhīnaiśvaryāḥ pārthivānspardhamānāstānvijayamānā vā dṛśyante /
tadiha niratiśayaiśvaryatvāt parameśvarasya mā nāma bhūvanvidvāṃsastato 'dhikāstatsamāstu bhaviṣyanti /

children.text: tadete svatantrāḥ santastadvyāpāre jagatsarjane 'pi pravarteranniti prāpte pratyabhidhīyate-nityatvādanapekṣatvāt śrutestatprakramādapi /

body.text:
jagatsargalakṣaṇaṃ hi kāryaṃ kāraṇaikasvabhāvasyaiva hi bhavatu āho kāryakāraṇasvabhāvasya /
tatrobhayasvabhāvasya svotpattau mūlakāraṇāpekṣasya pūrvasiddhaḥ parameśvara eva kāraṇamabhyupetavya iti sa evaiko 'stu jagatkāraṇam /
tasyaiva nityatvena svakāraṇānapekṣasya kḷptasāmarthyāt /
kalpyasāmarthyāstu jagatsarjanaṃ prati vidvāṃsaḥ /
na ca jagatsraṣṭṛtvameṣāṃ śrūyate /
śrūyate tvatrabhavataḥ parameśvarasyaiva /
tameva prakṛtya sarvāsāṃ tacchrutīnāṃ pravṛtteḥ /

children.text: apica samapradhānānāṃ hi na niyamavadaikamatyaṃ dṛṣṭamiti yadaikaḥ sisṛkṣati tadaivetaraḥ saṃjihīrṣatītyaparyāyeṇa sṛṣṭisaṃhārau syātām /
tatrāgantukānāṃ kāraṇādhīnajanmaiśvaryāṇāṃ gṛhyamāṇaviśeṣatayāsamatvānnityaiśvaryaśālinaḥ sa eva teṣāmadhīśa iti tattantrā vidvāṃsa iti parameśvaravyāpārasya sargasaṃhārasya neśate //17 //
yataḥ parameśvarādhīnamaiśvaryaṃ tasmāttato nyūnamaṇimādimātraṃ svārājyaṃ na tu jadatsraṣṭṛtvam /
tathā pādo 'sya viśvā bhūtānīti vikāravarti rūpaṃ tripādasyāmṛtaṃ divīti nirvikāramāha rūpam //19 //

body.text:
darśayataścāpare śrutismṛtī nirvikārameva rūpaṃ bhagavataste ca paṭhite /
etaduktaṃ bhavati-yadi brūṣe saguṇe brahmaṇyupāsyamāne yathā tadguṇasya niravagrahatvamapi vastuto 'stīti niravagrahatve viduṣā prāptavyamiti tadanena vyabhicārayate /

children.text: yathā savikāre brahmaṇyupāsyamāne vastutaḥ sthitamapi nirvikārarūpaṃ na prāpyate tatkasya hetoḥ, atatkratutvādupāsakasya /
tathā tadguṇopāsanayā vastutaḥ sthitamapi niravagrahatvaṃ nāpyate /
upāsakasya tadakratutvaṃ ca niravagrahatvasyopāsanavidhyagocaratvādvidhyadhīnatvāccopāsanāsu puruṣasvātantryābhāvātsvātantrye vā prātibhatvaprasaṅgāditi //20 //

body.text:
#bhogamātrasāmyaliṅgācca# /
na kevalaṃ svārājyasyeśvarādhīnatayājagatsarjanam, sākṣādbhogamātreṇa tena parameśvareṇa sāmyābhidhānādapi vyapadeśaliṅgāditi /
bhūtānyavanti prīṇayantīti bhojayantīti yāvat /
sūtrāntarāvatāraṇāya śaṅkate- #nanvevaṃ sati sātiśayatvāditi# /

children.text: saha parameśvarasyātiśayena vartata iti viduṣa aiśvaryaṃ sātiśayam /
yacca kāryaṃ sātiśayaṃ tacca yathā laukikamaiśvaryam /
tathāca kāryatvādantavatprāptamiti tacca na yuktamānantyena tadviduṣāṃ tatra pravṛtteriti //21 //
children.translated_text: And thus, since it is an effect, the prima facie conclusion is that it is finite — but that is not fitting, because those who know that [<s>Brahman</s>] engage in it [meditation/knowledge] on account of its infinity. //21//

body.text:
ata uttaraṃ paṭhati- #anāvṛttiḥ śabdādanāvṛttiḥ śabdāt# /
kimarcirādimārgeṇa brahmalokaprāptānāmaiśvaryasyāntavattvaṃ tvayā sādhyate /
āhosviccandralokādiva brahmalokādetallokaprāptirmukterantavattvam /
tatra pūrvasmin kalpe siddhasādhanam /
uttaratra tu śrutismṛtivirodhaḥ /
tadvidhānāṃ ca kramamuktipratipādanāditi /
tattvamasivākyārthaikopāsanāparān pratyāha- #samyagdarśanavidhvastatamasāmiti# /
dvidhāvidyā tamaḥ /
body.translated_text:
Therefore, he reads the reply: '#Non-return — from the scriptural word; non-return — from the scriptural word#.'
Is it the finiteness of the sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>) of those who have attained <s>Brahmaloka</s> through the <s>arcirādi</s> (path beginning with light) that you are trying to establish?
Or is it the finiteness of the liberated one — [meaning] a return from <s>Brahmaloka</s> to this world, as from the world of the moon?
In the former alternative, it is [the fallacy of] proving what is already established.
In the latter, there is a contradiction with <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>.
And because the scriptures of that kind teach gradual liberation (<s>kramamukti</s>).
Addressing those who are devoted exclusively to the meditation on the meaning of the sentence '<s>tattvamasi</s>' ('You are That'), he says: '#For those whose darkness has been destroyed by right vision#' (<s>samyagdarśanavidhvastatamasām</s>).
<s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance) is the darkness — of two kinds.

children.translated_text: The direct realization of <s>Brahman</s> without limiting adjuncts (<s>nirupādhi</s>) is the vision of reality (<s>tattvadarśana</s>).

children.text: na caitannirvāṇaṃ svarūpāvasthānalakṣaṇaṃ kāryaṃ yenānityaṃ syādityāha- #nityasiddheti# //22 //
children.translated_text: And this <s>nirvāṇa</s> (liberation), characterized as abiding in one's own nature, is not an effect — such that it would be impermanent — he says: '#eternally established#' (<s>nityasiddha</s>). //22//

Having vanquished the hosts of champions of rival doctrines, transcending the substratum of all <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), by the path of reasoning from the ocean of the <s>Veda</s>s, the nectar of <s>Brahman</s> is attained.

children.text: so 'yaṃ śāṅkarabhāṣyajātaviṣayo vācaspateḥ sādaraṃ saṃdarbhaḥ paribhāvyatāṃ sumatayaḥ svārtheṣu ko matsaraḥ //1 //
children.translated_text: This composition of <s>Vācaspati</s>, whose subject matter is born from the <s>Bhāṣya</s> of <s>Śaṅkara</s> — let the wise reflect upon it with care. What envy is there regarding one's own welfare? //1//
For those who, having crossed the ocean of ignorance, seek the reality of <s>Brahman</s>,
their heart's desire has been fulfilled by me — the helmsman of the boat of right conduct (<s>nīti</s>). //2//
That which through the <s>Nyāyakaṇikā</s>, the <s>Tattvasamīkṣā</s>, and the <s>Tattvabindu</s>,
that which through the treatises on <s>Nyāya</s>, <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, <s>Yoga</s>, and <s>Vedānta</s>, //3//
the great merit I have accumulated — its abundant fruit
has been offered [here]; and by this, may the Supreme Lord be pleased. //4//
He who, by a mere raising of his brow, created a fame inaccessible even to the minds of other kings,
whose caravans of wealth were filled with gold and iron, and who was himself learned in the <s>śāstra</s>s — //5//
The lords of men wish to imitate his conduct but are unable to do so.
For that king of illustrious fame, the glorious <s>Nṛga</s>, this treatise was composed by me. //6//

body.text: #iti śrīvācaspatimiśraviracite śaṅkarabhagavatpādabhāṣyavibhāge bhāmatyāṃ caturthasyādhyāyasya caturthaḥ pādaḥ samāptaḥ# /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth <s>pāda</s> (quarter) of the fourth <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter) in the <s>Bhāmatī</s>, the division of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> of the Blessed Lord <s>Śaṅkara</s>, composed by the venerable <s>Vācaspati Miśra</s>.
